title: Another good performer from OontZ
text: This is an updated version of the original OontZ Angle Bluetooth speaker, but with the additional feature of being splash-proof. Like the original, it provides nice sound when linked to your phone, iPod, or other Bluetooth device. The water resistance is due to covering the buttons and ends with a somewhat hard plastic coating to prevent moisture intrusion; it's not meant to allow the speaker to be submerged. Performance-wise, it's the same as my other, Original, OoontZ. Bluetooth setup is the same as are the various controls for synching, volume, and track selection. Also like the original, charging is via a mini-USB jack plugged into any USB power source such as your computer. The jack appears to be sealed also. So far, getting it slashed in the shower hasn't caused any issues. The water does appear to get into the grill a little, but a little shake seems to get most of it out. No way to tell if there are any materials inside the grill that the water could affect long term, but I suspect not. Only con: there is no ring or hook (or a place to attach a ring or hook) to allow you to attach the speaker to the shower wall. Right now I'm putting it on a small wire shelf that suctions to the wall; an OK solution.

text: I just got mine, plugged it to charge and it was done in a couple of hours. Assuming they sent it with some battery life as they said it can take up to five hours when it’s dead and mine was done in under three. First, it DOES work with Alexa. I just did it. You download their app and it couldn’t be easier. I was playing music from my Amazon account prior to doing this though. What may confuse people is that you have to hit the bar at the bottom on the app screen after you log into your Amazon account & then she comes to life. She interrupted my music to tell me the weather as requested and when I asked her to return me to my music, she did. And she did NOT start it. I thought that was cool. I do not use the premium feature on Amazon music either. Just the free version. So far I am pretty impressed with this little speaker. It pairs very readily to an iPhone 11. You can adjust the volume from the speaker, from your phone, or via Alexa. I love having options. I did NOT want to have to go to the speaker every time I wanted to do this. I am not comfortable speaking to sound quality just yet as I haven’t used it enough to do that. I did crank up Fleetwood Mac’s The Chain outside and as it got louder the bass felt a little weak, but honestly, for its size, it was filling up my decent sized yard pretty well & the range was good. I’m heading up north with it in a few days so we’ll see how it does up there and I’ll update! I’m happy I’ll have this with me👍

title: WOW!!!
text: This speaker is better than what our 48 inch TV can put out. I read the reviews and saw how many people were happy with it but I wasn't expecting it to be so crisp. The volume goes louder than I would ever play it in my home but I can see this being amazing in a crowded loud room. Let alone a shower. The bass is perfect, it's just a really good little speaker. I have a feeling well be getting a lot of use out of it. We've had other speakers before but they end up collecting dust because they were cheap and the sound quality was the same as a smart phone. I mean, the cheap ones aren't even comparable to this. Bluetooth connecting was seamless. For instance, I have a Bluetooth receiver in my car even after years of using it it takes 30 seconds to pair even with a remembered device. My husband pressed the pair button on his phone and it instantly paired. Although, if you do have some trouble pairing, you can always use the auxiliary cord included. The battery powers this speaker for a long time depending on the sound level. I would say it should be okay for at least 5 hours on full blast. My only minor complaint is that there aren't forward/back buttons on the speaker itself. Aside from that, I am very impressed with this speaker. I would recommend this to anyone with a tight budget who needs a speaker for the shower, travel, dorm, office, etc. Update June 2019: I had to update the review just to add that my family has used this on a weekly basis, it has served through countless showers, poolside or on the beach, camping/ traveling for the past few years. This is truly a great product for the price and it's more than held up to everything we've thrown at it. I has little signs of wear and tear and the battery life is amazing. I see there's a deal right now for around $20, so I'll probably purchase another one. For the price I think this particular speaker at this price is the best bang for your buck. . Update July 2021: This STILL works! It is basically retired as new technology has come out and I have acquired several more BT speakers (like a dozen). But WOW! This speaker is amazing and just continues to function with decent sound. I have seen other reviews where they get totally beat up and still manage to operate. This has to be one of the best values in budget speakers!

title: Excellent for Audiobooks!
text: This is an excellent speaker for listening to audiobooks. The sound quality is rich and deep, which helps you hear the voices even if they are muffled or high-pitched. The buttons are soft and easy to push and locate. It also has a decent speaker phone. The small size and flexibility (horizontal or vertical) make it easy to set anywhere as I move around. Since the the volume between the speaker and the phone are independent there is a great deal more flexibility with volume. It can be very loud when I’m gardening. And very quiet when I’m falling asleep. The sleep timer also comes in very handy. After the timer turns off my audiobook, the speaker turns off after 15 minutes of no activity. Awesome! It’s very comfortable to carry around. I also love that it’s Bluetooth connection signal is quiet and pleasant. The water resistance is also very handy if I need to touch it while doing the dishes. I highly recommend this speaker for audiobook listeners!

title: Not user friendly, ANKOR is better
text: I bought both the Oontz and the Ankor, and in using them, the Ankor is much, much better. WHY? Because, on the Oontz--though they have a little sticker where the power button is--you're constantly turning the thing round and round to find the on button. With the Ankor, the power button sits on the top left, and you can just reach over and feel it and turn it on. Also, the Oontz DOES NOT REMEMBER DEVICES, so every time I use it with my iPhone, then use it with my iPad, I have to go through settings again and set up the bluetooth. That might not sound like much, but in actual usage, here I am, flipping the thing round and round to turn it on, then I'm waiting for it to sync, then it's not syncing, then I have to push the sync button, then it makes me go through settings again, then wait again for it to sync, and YIKES! Three full minutes of minutiae! And the Ankor remembers all my devices. PLUS, in the car, I can use the Ankor and just feel for the on button without taking my eyes off the road. UPSHOT: Ankor makes a better device in the actual day-to-day usage...good things: it's compact (so is Ankor), the sound is nice (Ankor, ditto), but it's just a bit too cumbersome to be great. Hope that helps! Here is the Ankor I bought for 27.99

title: Sounds good but does not work with my Phones
text: I like the speaker and it sounds good and at loud volumes there is very little distortion. It connects very easily to both my phones and tablet. A nice feature is you can answer the phone by pushing the Bluetooth button on the speaker and it will pause the audio source. Callers on the other end say they had no trouble hearing me and it was clear without echo or static. It is splash proof only if you make sure you keep the rubber door on the charging port closed. Now for the dislikes. The main problem I have is it sounds good connect to my Surface tablet but when connected to my Cell phones, a Lumia 950 and a 950XL it cuts out repeatedly. This does not matter if I have the speaker next to or at any distance from the phones. I can overlook the other faults of this speaker but the cell phone issue make it worthless for my primary use. Maybe I got a defective unit but I am at a lost to the reason it works very well when connected to my computer and not the phones. Because of this glitch I am returning the speaker. I do not recommend this speaker if you have Lumia phones at this time. My other gripe is the rubber on the ends of the speaker are a dust magnet which you can clearly see in the photos. There is no way to keep the speaker looking good. I have another waterproof speaker and it does not exhibit the problem of dust collection. I had high hopes for the OontZ Angle since I have been using an OontZ Curve also made by Cambridge Sound Works for over 2 years without a single problem. In my humble opinion the OontZ Curve sounds a little better than OontZ Angle but not being splash proof it does not meet my needs at this time. I have been looking for a smaller splash proof speaker to take with me while traveling and I will have to continue my search. If this review helped you or not in you buying decision please let me know. Thanks for reading

text: Right out of the box, the speaker is beautiful. The nice minimal branding of the coke design in the front of the speaker and the classic coke logo on the back. It really is a nice looking speaker. The only problem is the sound quality. The lack of any quantifiable amount bass is astounding in a modern bluetooth speaker. This speaker leans to more of the mids and highs and with certain songs it distorts like crazy, which is a shame. Also, with the way the speaker is built. If you are not fully facing the speaker the volume drops considerably. The only reason I am considering keeping it is because of how it looks. It really is beautifully designed. Plus it being waterproof is great too. But the sound quality makes me want to immediately return it.

title: This version was lacking but the Angle 3 Plus version is terrific - for me
text: I was very disappointed after reading so many positive reviews. This unit was to be primarily used in my bathroom with my Iphone 6 while I get ready for work. It was to replace a JBL Charge I'd had for a few years and no longer would hold a charge. The sound is strong, but tinny. No real depth or strong bass notes. I played several songs and really, really wanted it to work. Finally, I just gave up. Now, the reason I gave it 2 stars is that it would be perfect for spoken-word use. It paired up fairly quick and the size is simply perfect for portability. And it is very attractive. So I decided to give the Angle 3 Plus a shot for $7.00 more. Wow - what a difference! Sounds great, bass is perfect for the size, and I couldn't be happier. Bottom line is that the choice is totally subjective on the part of the listener but, for the money, the Cambridge Angle 3 Plus is the way to go.

title: Why is this getting such good reviews?! Much better for the money!
text: I needed a small blue tooth speaker because the Echo Dot sound quality just wasn't cutting it and i would like to add music to whatever room I am working in that may not have a device. I have an Echo Dot 2nd and 3rd gen. The 2nd gen is tinny and the 3rd way too bass centric and boomy, but still better than this speaker. The sound quality doesn't blow me away, in fact, it is pretty bad. Not enough bass and not much of an improvement over my Echo Dot Mini 2nd Gen. Wow, this is so disappointing. The speaker paired easily with my phone and laptop, but had an issue pairing with the Alexa app via blue tooth. The controls are a pain to see in low light. As long as you keep your expectations super low you will be happy. ----Update----- Lost another star after buying the Doss Touch speaker for $4 more. The Doss has MUCH better sound quality and paired to Echo Dot instantly. The Oontz seems to be having difficulties with Alexa. Probably going to return this and buy the upgraded version of the Doss 20W because I am much more impressed with that speaker as a whole. The sound quality on the Doss is more balanced and it has True Wireless Stereo so both can be used simultaneously. At first it was about being an upgrade to the Echo Dot sound quality, but now it's about better sound with every device. I was never happy with the sound on the Oontz to begin with and now it's completely unacceptable after trying a much better speaker within the same price range.

title: Poor reliability stemming from charge port issues
text: This is my second Oontz Angle 3 and though it was sold as a 3rd generation device, the motherboard is clearly marked “ V 0.2”, so I am unsure what I have. I give this a one star rating as it is my second Angle 3 from Amazon and the second to develop charging issues literally two weeks after the wambly 90 day warranty ended. The first one just stopped working and would not accept a charge...no lights, nothing. This time, the unit charges but the red power/charge light will not go off and the unit runs until it discharges fully in a couple of days. I followed the reset procedure with no improvement (first unit did not respond as it will not take a charge). The device has good sound and easily connects to Apple and Android Bluetooth devices. Unfortunately, don’t expect this unit to outlast quarantine as it is unlikely to do so. Oontz Customer service has yet to respond to my email, but it sounds like these units are prone to charge port failure, which is my guess here.

Obviously the tower is much better in the speaker department. However, I did find that there is a cordless speaker you can buy to go with your 2nd gen dot that is an improvement and still at lower price point than the tower when combined with the cost of the dot. (Mokcao cordless speaker - amazon sells it too) Because the dots are so reasonably priced we have them in all 3 major rooms and use the cordless speaker to drop one dot in and take it outside to our sunroom when we like. Over all, I am pleased with both my tower AND dots... but probably will stick to dot purchases in the future because of the price point. I would say if you've been on the fence, the dot is well worth a try. It's very easy to set up, you will need to download the app, also easy to follow step by step setups. Once you're hooked up you will be amazed at how often you use Alexa. At our house she helps me keep track of where I am supposed to be every day... timers... night time meditation... the occasional argument and even plays games with us as well as much needed comedic relief. It may not be "necessary" to have Alexa, but I am always surprised at how often we use her assistance. It's nice and worth it to us. I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.

title: Dot, Tap, Tower?
text: We have all three of the Echo products: The Dot, The Tap, and the original Echo. The Dot works very similarly to the original Echo. You say the wake word, you give a command or question, it responds. It does have a speaker itself, but it doesn't get as loud as the original Echo or the Tap. All of the devices will sync together in one Amazon app, but they all still work independently. Meaning, if I set an alarm on the Dot, only the alarm on the Dot goes off. But with the app on my phone, I can access all the devices in the one place. The Original Echo is better for larger areas. the Dot is ideal if you already have a sound system you would like to connect the Dot to, or small spaces like bathrooms or bedrooms. The Dot is great for kids. My daughter has it in her room so she can ask it how to spell words and such. The Tap is an entirely different beast, in my opinion. No wake word. Touch and talk. But it works via Bluetooth and wifi for on the go use using your cellular device. The Echo Dot does not come with a remote. Like the Original Echo, it needs to be plugged into the wall and needs wifi. (The Tap has a chargeable battery.) They are all great devices, though Amazon still has some work to be done on them. Each has a different place where it is the ideal choice, so which you should choose really depends on your needs.

title: Echo Dot (Not)
text: This was purchased as a gift. I, the writer of this review, am the recipient of the gift. After about a year of "monkeying around" with this piece of technology, I have unplugged it and relegated it to a drawer. It simply doesn't work consistently. It often " has trouble connecting to the internet", even though nothing has changed. It often gets the voice commands wrong, or just doesn't respond. When it is working, (we use it mostly to stream music to a sound bar that I bought just to use with the dot by Blue tooth connection), it will often just quit, or pause and restart. I have had several conversations with the help desk at Amazon, and although very pleasant, the solution always seems to be the same. Turn it off and reinstall it. Not doing that any more. The WiFi is one room away, and lap tops, tablets and smart phones all work just fine in this room and others through out the house. It is sad, because this seemed like a great solution to get some music into this room without blasting it from several rooms away, but alas, it is a bust. Some of the things that it did, like the "this day in history" were fun, or the jokes she would tell were so silly that they were just funny, but that doesn't make the Dot worth the time, effort, or money. Save your money and buy a Blue tooth speaker for your phone. You'll be glad you did.

title: We want an Alex!

Come on, Amazon. Don't any women work in your product development department? I'm sure Chris Hemsworth would lend (sell) you his voice. Give us women some options, please! title: Thank you for updates!
text: Update: since my last review, I stopped playing music. Why don’t I just subscribe? Because I didn’t want to and I felt we shouldn’t be charged if asking to play a song we don’t know is free or not. My son activated it asking to play a song and Alexa told me it was only available with amazon music and asked if I’d like to subscribe. So I’m glad that amazon updated this to actually let you know that it’s not free if you aren’t subscribed. Thx! UPDATE: apparently u get charged if u activate music. Not only the monthly charge but every time u play music? I canceled when I saw the charges the first time but then I got charged again (over the next several months). The customer service couldn’t tell me exactly what the random charges were other than they were echo charges. I don’t like surprise charges. I feel like we should be able to activate services and not have them automatic or easily activated without knowledge. Apparently if you ask Alexa to play music, and it’s not free, you won’t know and will get charged. AMAZON STAFF: This needs to be fixed! ZERO stars if I could. I really love this dot. It’s my first Alexa product. I ordered two and finally put up the 2nd one later, in our living room. I haven’t explored ALL features but i was pretty excited about the “Drop in” feature... BUT it wasn’t that great. The sound is horrible. I dropped in from my bedroom to the living room and it sounds like a bad phone call on speaker where reception keeps cutting in and out. :( I wanted to purchase the Echo’s with a screen but I’m worried the sound will be just as bad! For other uses, I’m loving it so far! Bummer about the drop in feature. I was hoping to use this feature often to call home to talk to my son when I’m at work to check on him...

title: My New Buddies, Alexa and Echo Dot
text: I have two Dots, Alexa and Echo, and have been using them for about two months. In order to get the most out of them I have had to rethink how I do things, but I am learning more all the time. I have had to rethink how I ask some things, and try to find more practical skills that fit my lifestyle. They are great to find definitions and spellings of words, info on events and people, making shopping lists and to do lists, keeping up with my appointments, playing my Prime music, and Alexa deals. Some of the skills are fun like facts on President's, strange laws still on the books (it is illegal to shoot buffalo from second story hotel rooms!), cat facts, dog facts, timer, alarm, and many others. I have set up my Daily Flash Briefing for news and weather,for a word for the day, and who was born/died on this day. It is nice to listen to as I make my bed. There are at least 100 "Easter Eggs" which are questions or statements to get Alexa to say funny stuff. We got a kick about how ugly her Christmas sweater was. We bought a tp- plug to have Alexa control a difficult to reach lamp, and it works great. My most favorite skill is having Alexa make my shopping list, then when I am in the store I just check items off. The list shows up in the Alexa App on my phone. I believe that home computerization is the future and the Dot is an inexpensive way to get started. Someday the house of the future will have centralized computerization built in and we will not need the little Dots. Until then I am a very happy with Alexa and Echo. Yes, I did purchase each Dot a little speaker in order to hear music better.

Well, after watching a video of someone sitting peacefully on their couch, giving Alexa commands (turn on this device, turn off that device, turn the lights down to 30%, play Christmas music, etc). I was sold!!! So far I only have one light set up, our bedroom light. Our light switch is by the door and it's the only source of light there is in that room, so at night it's a pain to shut it off, and then shuffle around to bed in pitch blackness. Now with Alexa I can climb into bed with the lights on, and once I'm settled I tell her to "turn bedroom light off" and she does! I use the smart plug at the moment, but I plan to get the smart bulbs that dim at some point. Overall, it's a cute little device. title: Good for Parties
text: It's a "party" speaker and you can get a lot of noise out of this little package. I use it in a living room to play spotify while i read. At lower volumes it's just adequate, a little muddy in mid and treble, weak on bass. There is no bass/treble adjust and the online JBL app is only for conjoining speakers. Online equalizers seriously diminish sound quality. Result, for quieter applications, this speaker is only adequate, not great. Also I cannot see the volume controls in dim light (black on black) and cannot feel them either. The speaker makes a gratuitously loud and annoying sound on startup. It easily pairs with bluetooth on phone and tablet, which is what I wanted, but after reading the reviews, I was disappointed with the mediocre sound. I'll keep the speaker for travel, but I'm looking for a higher quality bluetooth OR Wifi speaker for everyday home use.

title: Randomly turns off even when plugged into power source and fully charged
text: We got this as a gift and are impressed with the easy connectivity with iPhone and sound quality. BUUUUT we use this to play 1 song continuously throughout the night in the baby's room. If you know anything about babies, it's that once something is ingrained in a routine, if there is ANY disruption they go beserk. So randomly, every 1-2 days, the speaker will just decide to shut down. Then it becomes mission impossible to sneak into her room without waking her, extract speaker, turn it BACK on, hook it BACK onto iphone, RESTART music, and somehow sneak it back into the baby's room without waking her. It also doesn't help that EVERY time you turn it on/off, it makes this stupid "BOOM" sound. The sound quality is so good that it's enough to wake a village. There is NO way to turn off this "BOOM" sound. It claims that battery life 12 hours, which is also false. 10 months ago when she was first born, we used this as a BRAND NEW speaker to play music through the night and it lasted for like 8 hours MAX. If you're just looking for a speaker to use here and there this is good enough, but if you're looking for one that you can RELY on and doesn't give you a heart attack every 2-3 days, look elsewhere.

title: Bad Sound, No Settings, Worthless App
text: You might think that you'd get a premium product for the price, but no, this is actually a cheap low-end throwaway part of JBL's lineup. There is a feature on by default which (aggressively) boosts the base, which I think hides the terrible sound quality. I know, these are small speakers, but still, I expected a lot more. from the price and brand. THERE ARE NO EQ SETTINGS that might help to overcome the poor quality. When you install the JBL Portable application, the interface is practically bare -- you can change the name of the speaker (oh yes, very important feature) and the behavior of some buttons, and that's it. Other JBL models use the same app, but have more settings. So if you want EQ settings, you could try those. I'm at a loss to understand how there could be so many positive reviews here.

title: Amazing speaker for the size and cost
text: Pretty amazing little speaker for $80. I had tried three other portable Bluetooth speakers before settling on the Flip 4: the Bose SoundLink Color II (good, but lacks the crisp highs), the Bose SoundLink Micro (good for its size, but overall too muffled sounding on many tracks), and the JBL Charge 3 (bass was too dominant). The Flip 4 proved to be the "sweet spot" for me -- best combination of clear, crisp, balanced sound; amazing sound IMO for its relatively small size. But still provides a nice punchy bass! Also, as a true stereo speaker (two drivers vs one on the Flip 5, for instance) you get a slight but noticeable separation of "sound stage" instruments. Highly recommended. Thinking of getting a second one.

title: Going on 3 years, and still going strong!
text: I bought this in September 2017, and it's still going strong. This is my 2nd JBL Bluetooth speaker, I also had a 2015 Xtreme which I eventually sold. JBL sound is the best! Nice high and bass range, less in the middle. It gets relatively loud, although it's not going to be enough for a backyard BBQ or pool party. This little speaker has been a workhorse, and is incredibly durable, which is why I decided to write a review after having it for almost 3 years. I use it daily for conference calls (while working from home during COVID-19) and can also bring it outside for use in the hot tub, since it's waterproof. I couldn't ask for a better speaker for daily use. The battery has not diminished - it goes for several days without needing a charge. When it does need a charge, it only takes about 30 minutes to fully refresh. Pairing is so simple - once paired to a device, it instantly remembers once it's powered on. I couldn't ask for a better personal Bluetooth speaker!

title: I'm a fan.
text: I went and compared 3 similar portable speakers with each other (same price of around $100 each): JBL Flip 4 - Best quality sound of the 3 (amazing quality - very similar to Bose Soundlink Mini) - No noticeable crackle at max volume with high treble in music - Strongest/deepest bass (my table was shaking on max volume) - Very loud max volume Ultimate Ears WONDERBOOM - Smaller than JBL 4 but larger than Bose Micro - Crackling at max volume for some songs with high treble (Was not expecting this) - Bass is not as strong (very slight bass) - Very loud max volume (similar to JBL 4) Bose SoundLink Micro Bluetooth - Smallest of the 3 - Max sound was at 75% that of JBL 4/Ultimate Ears - Sounds "muffled" and not clear (quality is not even close to that of Bose Soundlink Mini) - Exposed charging slot (is this really waterproof?) Overall - I would pick JBL (amazing quality & very similar to Bose Soundlink Mini, but waterproof!) and Ultimate Ears for portability (75 % size of JBL 4). The Bose Micro, although very small, had really poor quality sound for the price (most disappointing).

title: Returned an Oontz to buy this instead -- was the right decision
text: I initially tried to save some money and bought an Oontz (forget which model, it was about half the price, though, so this might not be comparing apples to apples) triangle-shaped speaker. It arrived, and honestly it sounded so horrible I assumed it must be defective and returned it. I'm not really a sound snob, but that speaker sounded awful. Everything was distorted and mushy, even at medium volumes. So, after reading that basically everybody thought the JBL speakers sounded better, I decided to order this one. So far, I'm super happy. What sounded distorted and mushy on the Oontz sounds clear and warm on the JBL, even at louder volumes. The JBL does sound the tiniest bit tinny or hollow, but that is just me being critical, it doesn't bother me at all. Honestly I was surprised at how good the speaker sounded. As for volume, we had an older, cheaper Barricade speaker that we took to the tennis court, but unless we were right near the speaker, we couldn't enjoy the music (i.e. when we were both at opposite baselines of the court, neither of us could hear the music clearly). With this speaker, even at half volume, the music is nice and clear on the court. I take it into the garage when I'm "working" on "projects" and it's more than beefy enough to fill the space even at lower volumes. We have ~600 sq foot living / dining room and I think 1 of these would be enough to comfortably listen in that space. Battery charge -- I haven't had this very long, but I've listened to it for about 8 hours so far and haven't yet needed to recharge. Can't really comment on that, other than I'm happy if I need to throw this on the charger once a week or so, which seems to be the case.

title: Auto Sleep & Volume Controls Are A Pain In The Butt
text: When I first got this unit I was not very happy with it but I decided to have a cooling off period before writing a review and I'm glad I did because I'm now very happy with it and realize it was just a matter of getting used to the button functions. I still think that it is a poor design that everything operates from the volume buttons, but the sound and unbelievable battery life kinda make up for things. It is built very solidly and has a nice rubber grip on the bottom that keeps it from sliding. The SD card slot works well and is easy to insert and remove the card. The unit fits very well in a standard size cup holder and the FM radio function works okay but is not static free even with the supplied antenna. There is no volume display indicator, you just keep rapidly pushing the + or - until it beeps, and if you are too slow the unit will go to the next track rather then change the volume and that is a HUGE pain in the butt when you are in the middle of listing to a podcast from the SD card and that happens because there is no way to go forward or backward by 10 seconds so you have to start ALL OVER AGAIN to whatever you were listening to. It takes about 21 extremely firm thumb presses before you reach maximum volume, so after about 6 months, you are probably going to wind up with carpal tunnel syndrome. Overall though, I’m happy with this purchase. Thanks for reading, and I hope this helps.

title: Nice and Compact. Not great quality sound. Cuts off and needs to be cycled on and off.
text: I love how small this speaker is. Fits in my bag easily, the battery lasts quite a while, and the sound is good enough for one or two people to listen to at a comfortable volume. It falls short in a couple of areas - one is predictable. The volume is limited, and if you go above a certain point it often sounds less than perfect. But that is a limitation of the size and power, and if you want to avoid it, go bigger. The other is more of an annoyance. The speaker has a physical on / off toggle (vs a momentary button). Which is convenient. But because people won't turn it off consistently, it goes to sleep after a while, or a short drop of connection. And it doesn't stay in a low power mode waiting for reconnect - no, it goes off so you can't reconnect to it without moving the physical toggle off and then on again. This is not obvious or intuitive, and is irritating if you are going to use it for a bit, take a break, go back to it, etc. Not a big deal for continuous usage, but in a lot of situations it will time it while sound is paused for a phone call or something. And that is just a pain. I don't have similar issues with other small bluetooth speakers, so I'm not sure why this one was done that way. But it is my least favorite feature of an otherwise decent little speaker.

At home, I dumped all my scuba stuff into the bathtub to get washed and... yep, forgot about the speaker inside the fin. It soaked for an hour before I remembered and pulled it out. Yikes! I dumped out the soapy water, rinsed it off, and then set it out to dry. I let it dry for a week and then tried it out. It connected right to my device and played music like nothing had ever happened. Amazing! Well worth the price for a nice travel size speaker.

title: You won't believe the quality of sound!!!
text: Purchased for my wife for Mother's Day. It is awesome- she LOVE it. So much so we purchased a second one for her to use as a teacher in her kindergarten class. Unbelievable sound from such a little package!!

title: Five Stars

title: Great speaker for the size.

title: Great Speaker in a Small Package
text: I've been very happy with all the Anker products I've purchased over the past few years, and this little speaker is no exception. It's basic, functional, and affordable. At home I use it with a Raspberry Pi and my amateur radio equipment. I work at a large regional theatre and we use Anker speakers ,including this model, whenever we need compact, wireless sound playback. The batteries last a long time, the quality is always good, and the electronics for Bluetooth and other features don't get in the way of the simple Aux input.

title: Big sound for small speaker, good bass and highs, no distortion

title: Does not auto-connect to my pc and volume control does not work

Also, the volume controls on my PC will not control the speaker volume. I've had several other BT speakers and all of them allowed me to control the volume. This thing is a piece of useless junk.

title: Great little speaker, but has volume flaws
text: Pros: Compact, quick connectivity, great sound, features & customer service (Anker). Cons: Anker confirmed this model had no volume memory - factory default is max volume when turned on each time. When iPhone is connected via Bluetooth, it rings at max volume through this speaker when phone is in silent mode. Sadly I will be returning this model due to the volume issues. After consulting with Anker, they claim the Soundcore Mini 2 should not have these volume & ringing issues, so I’ll give that model a try & cross my fingers “2” is a charm!

title: One Flaw

title: It's a great little speaker!
text: I listen to podcasts and long form acoustic effects like storms on my phone. I used to have a Motorola Z4 that famously had "mods" that could be purchased to add giving it extra features, one of which is a JBL stereo speaker. I miss that phone a great deal and if I still had it, honestly I would not have bought this speaker. However, those phones have gone by the wayside. I now have a Samsung S21 that cannot come close to the acoustic perfermance I was used to, hense my purchase of this little Anker bluetooth speaker. It goes a long way toward improving the tinny sound of my phone. The 2.5" driver does have a great deal more depth, volume, and presence than the .125" diameter speakers in my phone making it bearable to listen to but sacrificing the stereo seperation I would like. So until a phone comes along offering acceptable sound quality, one must, at least, buy an ultra portable speaker like this little Anker to get us by. I think it is a little expensive but Anker does make quality products in my opinion, so I can recommend it.

title: Good sound for a small speaker
text: This speaker is exactly what I was looking for. It sits on my desk while I work. For the level of volume I need it really does have great quality of sound. Nice base and sharp tones. Even at max volume it sounds decent. Its light enough to throw in a hydration pack when I go on hikes too. Connects quickly and easily. If you’re looking to get big sound for a party or something like that then this is not the speaker for you. This is after all is a small speaker. I hesitantly took away one star because it starts up at max volume every time it connects. Not that big of a deal but would be nice to not have to turn it down every time.

I still find it very annoying that the speaker goes to sleep, even when plugged in, if you pause the audio for more than 10 minutes.

Phone calls sound great but you probably should invest a bit more if you want to be heard well by others. Updating: Taking off a star because speaker has a habit of unexpectedly discharging. It has an auto power-off feature so I don't know why I sometimes find the batter flat even though I've not used it much. Maybe a button is accidentally getting pushed. Charging is a bit of a pain since it is is micro USB and orientation matters and you sometimes try to plug the charger into the micro SD card slot.

I haven't used it for extensive periods of time yet, so I am not sure how great the battery life is, but I love that it's small, wireless and easy to use!

I never write reviews but this is the best portable blue tooth speaker I’ve owned that wasn’t made by Dr Dre... 1. It’s affordable. Any other speaker for this price is a piece of trash don’t waste your money. 2. The base is decent, the volume goes up really loud and it can be heard on the beach over ambient sounds which is an important feature for someone who is active. 3. You can control the volume, song and blue tooth connectivity, as well as a few other features directly from your speaker so you don’t have to take out the phone when you want to change a song or turn it down, or turn it up if it happens to be your jam, etc. super helpful. 4. It’s actually light for the quality of speaker that it is, so you can just toss it in a backpack or shoulder bag and it’s doesnt impact the weight too much. 5. It’s also really compact about the size of my fist (I’m a tiny person.) 6. Battery life is amazing and you can track it on your iPhone... also it shuts off on its own to save battery as well. I came on here to buy a new one and decided to write a well earned review. I’ve had mine for about a year and a half and the only reason I’m replacing it is because I think I got some sand in it so it doesn’t sound as great as it once did, but as much as I’ve put this bad boy to use I don’t mind spending the $25 every two years to freshen it up.

title: Was Surprised by this device.
text: First of all this is an excellent value for the price. I was very surprised by the sound quality and how easy it was to connect. It's small, but sounds as good as device costing twice as much. No, it is not going to be audio-file quality, but I didn't buy it for that. I bought it to play in the background while busy doing something else, or relaxing and reading. In other words for times when the music is secondary. I have a high quality system to listen to music when I want to really focus on the music. This one, I use to play mp3, not flac, not CDs, not vinyl. I'm not counting on focusing on the music while using this. For the price it could be 5 star if it weren't for two failings. First it gives you a USB charging cord, but not a charging transformer. It would be nice to have one. Second, I don't like the location of the on off switch and volume controls. I'm sure this is just a function of internal design, but it would be nice is the the power switch was below the power light, and the volume controls were right next to the power light. I use this at night sometimes and I hate having to turn on the flashlight to find the power switch. Though I can feel to find the volume control. This isn't a big problem though and over all it seems like a good solid device. Features that would be nice. Since it has a microphone and can be used to answer the phone, it would be great if the microphone could also be used to activate the "hey Siri" or "google voice" functions. But that's a lot to ask for a $17 speaker.

title: Great sound, plus FM Radio and Micro SD. Best little speaker there is!
text: I wanted a portable speaker I could carry in my coat pocket, and I am very pleased with this unit. For the price I paid, this little speaker is great. The sound is absolutely beautiful, with good bass. I totally overlooked the fact that there was an FM radio built in. The radio is a bit of work to first set up, but you must let it do the auto tuning and let it finish. Once that is done, using the radio is a breeze. Hold the volume buttons to tune up or down, to change volume, just press and let go quickly. It's that easy. The MicroSD card is a bonus as well as I can take music on the go without depleting my phone battery. I haven't tried the SD card yet, though. Battery life seems to be good, for the amount time I have used it so far. I've also discovered I can use this as a speakerphone when I get a phone call. I was listening to music from my phone and I got a phone call. It played through the speaker and I was able to talk back through the tiny pinhole microphone. I am very happy with this purchase. The speaker does a lot for a little money, and it sounds great, too.

title: Great little speaker
text: We purchased this speaker to use with Pandora, and it works beautifully. The sound quality is beautiful, the battery lasts a long time, and it paired with my phone readily. I'm glad we have it.

title: Great Introduction To The World Of Bluetooth Mini-Speakers
text: I bought this during a sale and was instantly impressed with the sound and especially the bass, which I found fairly impressive for such a small speaker. It is not huge, window-rattling bass at all, but you generally do not find even this much bass in these smaller Bluetooth speakers. Overall, the sound separation is quite good although I would prefer a bit more brightness or high end, but that is just me. However - within a week I had some issues with the device. I could not get more than a half hour to 3 hours of play from it even after charging it for hours. I contacted Anker and they were extremely helpful in sending a replacement. Good thing too, as eventually this device completely stopped working right before I sent it back. The replacement has been working much better (updated as of 3/2/2018), although it seems to not do as well with the Bluetooth when I move it to another room - it sputters a bit more than the 1st device did. In general though I am very happy with the device. It is not super high-end, so don't expect audiophile sound. But if you want to crank some music and impress your friends with such a small speaker, this is more than adequate and you would even be able to host a small dance party with it, using music from your Kindle or phone. As others have mentioned, there is that auto shut-off issue that can be a bit annoying. In other words, the speaker will shut off after a few minutes of non-usage and you have to turn it off and on again. However, I understand why the company designed it that way (to save power), so best to just deal with it. Overall, I am very happy with this purchase and I use this speaker every single day. It has been a great introduction to the world of Bluetooth mini-speakers. Eventually I would like to get a higher-end device, but for right now, this is more than sufficient for my needs.

title: Great sound and mobility

title: I love all Anker products
text: I love all Anker products....They have become my go-to for battery back up chargers to cables and now to portable wireless bluetooth speakers. The sound is what i expected for the price point, nothing spectacular but all that I need to play background music while i am at work or to listen to a movie on my ipad mini. Perfect. Thanks Anker.

title: Nice upgrade over the original Soundcore.
text: The Soundcore 2 is a nice upgrade over the original. The original was nice and sounded okay. But its only real redeeming points for me was its amazing battery life, small size and clear mid tones. I eventually gave the original soundcore away. The Soundcore 2 on the other hand is nicer in everyway. The audio quality has gone way up. Highs are no longer harsh, mids are clear and lows are much improved. You also get a nice bit of bass added in to, Anker decided to double the power output from two, three watt speakers to two, six watt speakers and alap added a passive radiator which really improved the capabilities of this speaker. At lower to mid volumes it sounds similar to my JBL flip 3. Overall build quality has been improved, the buttons are now more positive feeling, the LED light placement has also been changed for the better (never liked the LED behind the grill). Overall this is a great upgrade over the original soundcore in everyway except call quality which still stinks unfortunately, the built in Microphone is not good and causes you to sound muffled unless you speak directly into the speaker. Anker needs to work on this because its not acceptable, I also own the Sound Core Boost which also has the same issue.

title: Great sound and easy to pair!
text: Great sound for my computer without built in speakers. I just needed it to hear typical sounds, stereo, nothing special. It is way overkill for my use, but it is nice to know I could use it outside if I needed.

title: Great speaker!
text: excellent sound quality and not to hard to connect blue tooth. Still, being able to use a cable is a very nice extra ability which I will take advantage of when the cable arrives.

title: Battery life poor
text: I was so excited about this new anker speaker , everything about is amazing except the battery life . The old one stayed charged for a week, this one barely a day .

title: Just as good as my Jambox
text: It sounds as good as my Jambox speaker, which is about the same size. I was hoping it would handle the bass a little better (less distortion) but they're basically the same. Satisfied overall, with the quality of the build and audio.

title: Soundcore’s a great speaker for the money
text: Would not pair after a week bought Sony xb10. Much better speaker. UPDATE- Anker contacted me and sent me their most updated speaker, the boost. What a stand up company. I am very pleased with them and the speaker. That is how a company should be. Thank you Anker.

title: Totally worth the price
text: This speaker is easily the best Bluetooth out there for this price. The sound is great, the Bluetooth range is decent but maybe not as advertised. Well worth the price. Battery lasts a LONG time.

title: Good bass for a small speaker
text: I’m pleasantly surprised by how much bass this has, considering the size of it. Sounds a lot better than the Oontz Angle 3 I’m replacing.

title: Very nice sounding portable speaker
text: The biggest thing I like about this speaker is that I can plug my mp3 player into it.

title: Lacks bass
text: Buit well and looks great, overall sound quality is good but don't get this product if you're looking for something with more punchy bass.

title: Great speaker at a affordable price
text: Set up was easy and it came partly charged. Love how loud and powerful it sounds. A great Bluetooth speaker for the price.

title: Dynamite comes in small packages!
text: Great sound! Amazing battery life and water proof, what more can one ask for? How about a great price, and they nailed it worth every penny! Would recomend this to anyone that wants a worry free listening experience!

title: Great little speaker
text: Pretty great sound for the price. Wish it had come with the aux cable and case. Would have been willing to pay a little more for that. Nice speaker! Anker makes great products.

title: Good value
text: The Soundcore 2 is a solid product that I have mixed feelings on. I think that the price is fair, bluetooth connection is very solid with my Pixel XL, the weather sealing makes it a fine bathroom device, and battery life is excellent. I don't like the sound though, it's very mediocre sound quality overall - too bassy and not very quality bass - and I had to send the first one back due to a speaker buzzing. You get what you pay for, but it's not going to be better than more expensive options.

title: Really great sound for the price
text: Really great sound for the price, works great right out of the box. We liked it so much my wife bought one as well.

title: easy to operate
text: Honestly, I expected this speaker to be larger in size, but that doesn't matter and the sound isn't affected. It's loud, easy to operate, and connects easily to other Bluetooth sources (my phone and laptop). Decent battery life. Easily portable. Good product--not disappointed!

title: Remarkable Speaker
text: I was amazed at the sound coming out of this little speaker. It sounds as good as the Boze at a fraction of the price.

title: Great product for the price
text: Bought this for my husband as one of his Father's day gifts. I wanted to get him a blue-tooth speaker to and use when he takes our son to practice baseball. This wasn't expensive and plays very well despite the price.

title: Really Nice Speaker
text: Got it for a gift. Didn't get to mess with it too much, but from what I heard, the sound out of it seems pretty nice, and the Bluetooth paired pretty quickly. The person I got it for seems to really like it too. Have no real complaints.

title: Great sound for the money
text: I bought these for my two teenage kids. They have enjoyed them for about five months with no issues. The size is about right to take in a backpack and they seem to stay charged for a long time. We have owned other Anker products with no problems as well.

title: The sound and quality are great. I have it connected to my Echo Dot ...
text: The sound and quality are great. I have it connected to my Echo Dot (bluetooth) and can take it outside, or on the other side of the house, with not disruptions. I will buy more. The only reason I gave it 4 out 4 stars was becasue it doesn't automatically shutdown when the Echo Dot is stopped. I know the Dot keeps the bluetooth connection but it would be nice for the Anker to detect no sound and shutdown. I forget to tuen it off and need to recharge the next time I use it. Otherwise everything is great and I will but more.

title: Good Value & Sound!
text: Very happy with product! It has great sound and is definitely comparable to more expensive brands.

title: Excellent small speaker!
text: I ordered the basic version of this and it did not work. I took a chance on a Soundcore 2 and I am delighted. It can go amazingly loud for a very small speaker. Sound is good but do not expect pounding bass.

title: Made the right choice!!!!
text: I was overwhelmed by the amount of options, but due to thorough feature lists on each speaker choice I was able to figure out the features important to me to look for and narrowed it down to a few then used other features to determine the best deal between those. Battery life was my number one, this speaker is 24hrs! Scratch resistant material was another, this speaker has a neoprene coating Waterproof was another, this speaker is. It’s also 12watts another feature to look for. Shockingly there are $40 speakers with only 6 watts which leads to cracking and distortion in the sound. I didn’t need lighting effects that just drain the battery anyway and this one doesn’t have that. I use it for hd tv shows and movies and the sound is crisp and clear! Setup literally took 2 secs! Didn’t even read directions. Just turned it on then selected it in my blue tooth menu on my tablet.

title: [Upgraded] Anker Soundcore 2 Portable Bluetooth Speaker with 12W Stereo Sound, Bluetooth 5
text: This is an amazing product. I love the volume and portability. I use it in my exercise room and listen to music via my iPhone. It's completely changed my exercise routine. I'm also a musician and I've used this speaker to play music that I play along with via a flute. It works very well and I'm very pleased. Many people have commented their amazement at the volume of such a small speaker. I love the portability as I used to carry around a much bulkier system and now I only need my phone and speaker! I highly recommend!

title: Good but battery not as advertised
text: It’s a fine purchase if you don’t already have a portable Bluetooth speaker, but the battery doesn’t last any longer than what I have now. It says 10hrs in the description but I was getting six. Even after I totally drained and recharged it didn’t change. Thus returning.

title: Great sound from small speaker.
text: Great sound wish I had bought it for myself. Plan on getting one soon.

title: Exactly what I wanted!
text: A fantastic speaker all-around. Easily connects to Bluetooth and the sound quality is fantastic. It's also nice and compact. Would definitely recommend purchasing this speaker.

title: EXCELLENT BT SPEAKER!!
text: Outstanding BT speaker for the money! Would certainly buy again and would highly recommend. Only concern is that volume control is not variable, but in steps. Would prefer variable.

title: Impressive
text: I received this as a gift and am really impressed with the sound quality from such a small box!

title: Best portable bluetooth speaker for the price!
text: Great little speaker. Easily transporter, sleek design. For the price the sound quality is truly outstanding, it's very rich and all music sounds great through it. I would definitely buy it again and recommend to anyone looking to purchase a reasonably priced portable bluetooth speaker. In comparison to my $100 JBL Flip 2, the sound quality, design, and overall performance is just as good if not better. Great product! Don't be discouraged because it's made by Anker (not generally known for audio products).

title: battery died
text: I was satisfied with this speaker, but battery almost died after 1.5 years of rare use (about 10 hours a month). Yes, battery of batteries' giant manufacturer company's speaker died. Speakers turn on only for several seconds and then turns off. The only way it works is when it is plugged in for charging. If it has lasted for 5-7 years I wouldn't write 1 star review, but 1.5 years in such a rare use is inadmissible.

title: A superb bluetooth speaker.
text: The Soundcore 2 portable speaker is superb. At its price point there is no bluetooth speaker that would match its sound quality especially in the mid and high frequencies. The mid- range frequencies might be lean to some people but is perfectly acceptable to me. The high frequencies could use a little reduction in brightness for my taste but small speakers tend to be like this. The low frequencies taper off below around 100 Hz but again at this speaker category it is acceptable. I can hear lower frequencies up to about maybe 60 Hz but not at the output I prefer. I initially had an issue with the music spontaneously reducing in volume but it was fixed with a replacement speaker that they sent me ASAP. Customer service is very professional and in my opinion this is the other half of what makes a product valuable to a consumer. You can be sure that customers satisfaction is first on their list when handling product issues. They definitely handled my issues with care and consideration. The battery life is especially satisfying since it is good for up to 24 hours of playtime. Speakers costing up to 4 times as much will only play up to a third of its battery life. I also own a Bose soundlink mini. When taking this speaker to the beach or backyard this becomes a significant benefit. It will definitely last a full day. The speaker size and portability is also ideal because it is light and durable yet solidly built and does not feel inexpensive. I intend to fully enjoy this product for all the good listening that it offers. I definitely would recommend this speaker to others considering a bluetooth speaker with superb capabilities.

title: Sound quality.
text: This is the best Bluetooth speaker for the money that I have used. You wont believe the sound from a compact speaker system.

title: Good speaker but no 24 hour battery life.
text: I've had my speaker for about a month now, I wanted to really test it out before reviewing it. The sound is very good considering the size. It is a dense brick of a speaker, with a decent amount of weight. I bought this to be used as my everyday speaker to use when working in the yard or most other times I'm outside and want some entertainment. My previous speaker, Motorola Sol republic Deck, is still going strong, but it has been assigned mainly to my disc golf bag, I like that it's carrying case has a clip and is sound permeable. I've had the Deck for 2+ years, and it gets about 6-8 hours of battery life. When I read the reviews for the Anker, 24 hrs of battery sounded amazing, I hate it when the battery dies halfway through a task. The reality is, I have gotten about 6 hrs of battery life consistently, with a mix of music and podcasts, I do freely admit it is usually listened to at or near it's loudest. Overall I am happy with the sound from the speaker, but not so much with the battery life.

title: Great personal speaker
text: It's a great little speaker with wide sound range for its size. Battery last a long time. Perfect for intimate backyard encounters where you want good quality sound in an extremely small package. I found the Bluetooth range adequate for my deck size. I did have to contact customer support for an issue on my end that they helped resolve with some of the best custom support I've seen in a long time.

title: Good, not great
text: We got this speaker for trips to the beach, picnics, the pool, etc. I didn't want/need something really loud as we don't want to be disrespectful of people near us, but it is not quite loud enough. We had a 10 year old Pyle speaker we had been using. It was heavy and had a good, not great battery life and sound quality. It is just as loud as this one, while only being about half an inch wider and a quarter inch taller. This speaker is much lighter, but unfortunately doesn't have a hook to attach a carininer or bungee to. Sound quality is great. Haven't had a chance yet to put the battery life to the test. We'll probably keep this one to replace a smaller speaker in one of the kid's bedrooms, but we'll need to seek out something louder for outdoor use. For the price, it is a very good speaker and works well indoors, when there isn't a party. If you want to use it indoors, then by all means by it.

title: Fantastic Sound
text: Very impressed with the sound quality out of such a small box. Purchased one each for my (2) kids; they really like it too and that is equally important as my 2¢.

title: Very portable, good sound
text: I take this from room to room and outback to have music for my toddler, sound is great and seems like A sturdy unit.

title: Does the job
text: Why spend twice or three times as much on a speaker when this does the job? It’s a lot of punch in a small package. If you want a dependable basic speaker this is definitely the way to go. Outperforms it’s price point.

title: We use this at night when we go to bed...

I also use it when I get a live feed from twitter on my phone, makes it easier to listen. Definitely will recommend this.

title: The price is great for for this powerful speaker
text: This is the perfect little speaker for your summer outings. It's compact and it's not too heavy. I recommend it because the sound is fantastic. The bass is not too harsh which is a plus.

title: Amazing little unit is like a tiny boombox!

Only thing we wish it had was an FM tuner, but it doesn’t. No matter - it’s a great little unit, so after the first one we bought for work, we turned around and bought a second one for our home.

title: Easy to keep it everywhere.

title: Great speaker!
text: This little speaker is great! Perfect for the bathroom. Connected flawlessly with DOT. Simple to use and battery last for sometime.

title: Great quality
text: I purchased this speaker for a road trip and was thrilled at the water resistance and longevity of the battery life. The sound quality is pretty good and about what I expected. The battery life isn’t quite as long as I hoped for with the listed 24 hour battery life. Overall functionality is definitely easy and user friendly to work with.

title: Great for the price
text: Considering waterproof, sound quality, ease of pairing, range, and overall sound, this thing is great. It is missing some features, like easily toggling between bluetooth devices (on some I've used previously, you can easily cycle through these by pressing the bluetooth button until you arrive at the one you want). This one seems to just remember what you'd paired it to the last time it was on, so, particularly in the case of my computer (macbook) I have to pair it every time I want to use it, which is a little bit of a pain. I could be missing something, though, in that regard. Sound is not gigantic, but it's very "clean" which is more important to me. As I say, the range is phenomenal and I can have a device around corners and many feet away with no interruption, which is wonderful. Smaller than anticipated, which is fine (about the size of a burrito...like, a "smaller than Chipotle" burrito). Battery life seems excellent so far. As other reviewers have said, there is a mildly irritating "chime" noise when you hit volume up and it is maxed out - not unlike the "you can't do that" sound on older (98/2000/XP/7?) Windows systems. It interrupts what you're listening to for like entirely too long, which I get is just a hard thing to implement from a software standpoint in terms of making that shorter. That and the inability to toggle devices easily are probably my only two gripes. Happy listening!

title: Works great for watching videos on my cell phone in noisy environments

Then used the two pairing them to my Echo and placing in stereo mode. Had to connect only ONE to echo and then set up stereo between both speakers pressing the blue-tooth button. Worked well. Took a little practice to get them connect in stereo initially. Sound and speaker volume are great - no tinny or vibrating sound from speakers when on highest volume.

title: Poor sound, dies quickly
text: This product didn’t have the sound quality that I’d hoped for. It also doesn’t have an automatic shut off function so it dies very quickly, and doesn’t seem to hold a charge well. I definitely would not recommend.

title: Great speaker at an amazing price!!!!!
text: In full disosure I received this item free from the manufacturer. That said here's my experience with this item. I took this speaker on a vacation to the lake. Camping, boating and swimming were in the agenda and having a Bluetooth speaker was great. We easily synced this speaker to 3 different phones during the trip. The buttons are oversized and raised, which makes adjustments in little to low light fairly easy. While on the boat it got wet several times and still had amazing sound quality. Over the course of 2 days this speaker was ran for several hours and still had a small charge at the end of the trip. It was dropped, in the sand, in the mud and had beverages spilled on it and it never missed a beat! Overall this speaker is the best bang for your buck. I have purchased JBL and Bose Bluetooth speakers as gifts. While the sound quality of this Anker isnt quite up there with Bose it's also a quarter of the price. I'd take 4 of these over 1 Bose anyday.

title: Love this speaker

title: Powerful little speaker
text: This little speaker is great for enhancing the sound of virtual meetings. I use it with Zoom & Teams meetings. My laptop computer is so weak that even at full volume I can barely hear soft spoken people. This Anker Soundcore 2 has great clarity and I can hear even the most soft spoken person. I can carry it into other rooms and not miss a moment of my meetings. It's the perfect size (6in long x 2.25in tall x 1.75in deep) for my small home-office desk that's only 23.5in wide x 17.25in deep. I feel I got great value and quality for the money. I did a lot of comparing and it had very good ratings on several, not just a couple, but several sites. I highly recommend.

text: The speaker has a delay in it so that the words are not in sync with the lips when I'm watching someone on YouTube. That is super annoying. beyond that, the battery life is significantly less then the Anker soundcore 1. That being said, Anker went above and beyond to keep me a satisfied customer.

title: Amazingly Small and Amazingly Loud
text: This is my first mini portable Bluetooth speaker. I was previously going to buy the original Soundcore, but it just happened the day I was looking online version 2 came out. I picked up 2 of them, one for me and 1 for my wife. The picture doesnt do justice when you realize how small this speaker really is in person. The bass from it sounds great and the battery life is amazing. Pairing my cell phone was so simple. Why did I only give it 4 stars though? I got 2 big complaints. 1. Why no USB C connector? Its 2017, all devices should now be using USB C instead of MicroUSB. At the very least they could had added both ports. 2. The side door is slightly difficult to grip and open. I understand its made like that to keep the water out, but its a little to firm. I do want to give a major Shout-Out to Anker though. About 4 days after I bought my 2 speakers they had them on sale (I guess for an initial new product sale). Anyways I emailed them and they promptly refunded me the difference on both speakers. Very good customer service.

title: Very annoyed for the price paid
text: Sound cuts out a lot even when the phone is within a couple feet and I constantly have to re-pair which is really frustrating. The charging port cover is also extremely hard to pry open. title: For music, it rocks!
text: I have an older truck with just an am/fm radio. I wanted to listen to podcasts and music from my phone in the truck but not install a new radio. This little dude was the right gadget for the time and place. He just fits right in there in my dash, or on my desk or the counter in the kitchen and plays all the things just fine. Battery life has been over a week with my 20 minute commute and other times I listen throughout the day. I'd definitely trend for these kinds of purposes.

title: Great small speaker. Good sound for its size.
text: This is a great little speaker. Has really good sound for its size. Very good battery life as well. There are more expensive speakers available that have better sound quality - but this one is really good for the price.

title: Have two
text: This is the second one I’ve purchased. My husband uses one in the garage and on his fishing boat. I bought a second one to keep at our lake house to use there, and on our other boat. The sound quality is great and it’s the perfect size to take along anywhere.

title: Long lasting music
text: Soundcore2 arrived yesterday with 70% battery life. Played it immediately and have these initial observations. Battery life is amazing so far. 3 hours of playing music at roughly 70% volume reduced battery from 70% to 60% battery life. The claims of 24 hours of playback between charges appears accurate. Speaker enclosure is surprisingly small, portable and not toy like feeling. Sound quality is very good for the size of the enclosure. Mid range frequencies are emphasized; vocals, guitars, pianos are very detailed. Low bass is not present and high frequencies like drum cymbals are faded. This is WITHOUT the speaker drivers being broken in. At maximum volume the sound is clean, there is no distortion from the speakers trying to produce bass it cannot or a harshness in the high frequencies. The result is extremely portable, clean music reproduction in like 80% of the human audible range with a respectable maximum volume and infrequent charging. Pretty much what I was hoping for. Knew it charged via micro usb, that kinda sucks but carrying a cable from a since upgraded phone is light. Product so far has met my expectations. Update 5/5/22 After playing music through the speakers for 7 hours each day this week, the drivers have broken in and 'opened up" more to the higher frequencies. Cymbals are present and not faded like when the speakers were brand new. It's the bottom like 10% of audible range that's missing IMO. Going from 4 to 5 stars.

title: Sound quality is very clean at all levels.
text: I really like mine. Sound quality is very clean at all levels. Battery life is very long and charging time is fast.

title: Works fine, sound quality is good and it keeps charge ...
text: Works fine, sound quality is good and it keeps charge for a very long time. Use it to listen to audiobooks and podcasts on long car drives.

title: Great product
text: I can't say anything to make this a better buy. For $40???!!! are you kidding me. Now this is value. The folks that are having issues with bluetooth connection just don't know how to connect bluetooth that well. A friend bought one because I showed him mine, and he called because he couldn't connect it. I worked with him for 1/2 hour or more and finally told him to bring it over the next time we had beers. I had no trouble whatsoever. I told him perhaps he had another bluetooth device and it had connected to it. I would recommend the first time you hook it up to do it away from your home where there aren't six iPhones, an iPod, two amplifiers, etc. that all use bludtooth. It can only service one device at a time. I KNOW you can get better sound for more money, but for $40 I don't think you'll beat this speaker.

title: Disappointed by quality (2-stars) || Update: Anker Customer Service is the best! (5-stars)
text: Update (original 2-star review below): Anker customer service saw my review and reached out very quickly to offer to replace the device. They assured me this should not happen, and shipped a replacement free of charge and without any forms or requiring I send the old one back. This is the reason I keep purchasing Anker products and don't buy cheaper stuff - with any other company, I'd have to contact them myself and argue with someone, pay fees, and fill out forms, but Anker is proactive about their customer satisfaction and knows how to keep people coming back. ---------------------------- After less than a year, I'm pretty disappointed in the build quality of this product. The painted mesh on the front of this speaker has been rusting profusely. It started after just a few months and I hoped it wouldn't get too much worse, but the rust just keeps spreading, and the paint is beginning to flake off too. I'm a big fan of Anker products, and have bought dozens for myself and others, but this just doesn't meet the quality I've come to expect. This is an otherwise very good product, and I haven't exposed anything beyond some light splashes of tap water (it sits on a high shelf in my shower where it barely gets any water at all) so I can't imagine how much worse it must fare in wetter conditions.

title: Volume control is great
text: I often have trouble clearly hearing sound from various computer sites. I have been very happy with the performance in this regard so far. There may need to be some additional settings to allow me to use the speaker effectively on Zoom calls. It will work for awhile and then, after a few minutes, I can hear the other participants but they can no longer hear me until I disconnect the speaker. As I said, it may be operator error because it works very well otherwise.

title: Bluetooth connectivity
text: The Good: Well made. Rubberized matte finish feels secure in the hand when moving around, and looks nice. Very rich sound quality given the size and price. Excellent ergonomic control layout. The Bad: I purchased this primarily for watching stream services on my laptop. The bluetooth connection paired easily enough, but slowly moves out of voice sync rendering it unusable after a few minutes. (Prior to purchasing this Anker Soundcore 2, I was using a cheaper Irulu brand speaker which is intended mainly for my tablet. I have zero delay problems with that unit regardless of device). I've been working around the sync issue by using the optional headphone jack, but probably would have chosen another product had I been aware of the bluetooth delay issue.

title: Solid, with solid sound and solid battery life.
text: Really like these speakers (I have 4!). I have them scattered around the house and turn them on and off as I migrate from room to room. Turn one off and the next one on, and it automatically connects to my phone and resumes my podcast where I left off in the former room. Had an issue with one (after buying two at the same time), and the company took care of it immediately! GREAT customer service! Just replaced it after a short phone call (they did verify my purchase, but I didn't have to send anything in), and the replacement arrived in just a few days—quick ship! Haven't timed the battery life [difficult, given the way I use them], but several hours is not unrealistic. While I was an audiophile in a former era of my life, I no longer am quite so demanding regarding sonic quality. That said, these more than meet my requirements for great sound. It just occurred to me that these are probably just heavy enough to use as hand-weights when jogging! If your phone supports dual bluetooth connections, you could then jog with dual stereo "surround sound"!

title: Amazing quality sound, long batter life and long range connectivity...Anker delivers again!
text: Another Anker gem. I am so glad I found this company. Every item I have purchased, wither for myself or as a gift, has been reasonably priced and of high quality. The sound is fantastic, and not just for a portable Bluetooth speaker. The feel is robust and sturdy. I haven't tested its water resistance, but by the feel of its rubbery housing and the protective flap, I imagine it would live up to its rating. Other things that make it a winner: I have left it downstairs out on the patio and walked up a flight of stairs all and down a long hallway with my phone, and heard no complaints about music being disrupted. It also feels like I never have to charge it as the battery life is extensive. I purchased a previous model for my boyfriend's parents, and the minimal charging needs of that unit were also a hit. Thanks Anker, keep up the good work!!

title: Good sound for music/podcasts - but terrible for phone calls
text: Update: I've owned this speaker for just over 2 years and it has stopped working. Why doesn't anybody make products that last anymore? This throw-away economy is a big part of global warming and climate change. I use this speaker mostly to play music, podcasts or other audio content from both my smartphone and my laptop and it works great for that. I'm not much of an audiophile so I won't go into more detail. Other reviews are a lot better at that. But what this speaker *doesn't* do is handle phone calls. I mostly use Skype, and with my old speaker, I could grab a phone call coming in on my computer without issue. But now, I have to disconnect the speaker in order to take the call. I don't know why this is, but at least a half-dozen people I've tried to talk to have given me the same feedback. And with my cell phone it's even worse. I'm not downgrading my review because of it, since it's a darn good little speaker for what it's intended to do. But just in case you, like me, were hoping it would do double duty ... it doesn't.

title: Solid speaker with one BIG flaw
text: This is a solid speaker with one big, fatal flaw. First, the positives. Well constructed. Compact size. Nice tactile feel of the buttons. Easy initial Bluetooth pairing with my iPhone 6s. Sound quality is decent. A bit tinny and lacking in bass, but the clarity is very nice, especially if you're a treble-head. But there's also a MAJOR flaw in this speaker that must be addressed: The Soundcore 2 will not automatically switch between previously paired devices on startup. It only will connect automatically to the LAST device with which it was paired. Example: My son used the SoundCore 2 in the bathroom, pairing it with his iPhone 6s. I then took the Soundcore 2 -- to which I already had paired earlier in the day -- and it would not recognize my phone. The only way the Soundcore 2 would recognize my phone after being paired with my son's phone is if I entered the Settings on my phone, told my phone to Forget This Device for the Soundcore 2, shut off my Bluetooth, turned Bluetooth back on, waited for my phone to recognize it and re-pair. This is a big pain in the butt if you have multiple devices connected to this speaker. I recommend the Soundcore 2 if you're using it with only one device. It's solid little speaker that delivers excellent value and decent sound. But if you plan on sharing it with others or pairing it with more than one device, do not buy this product.

text: Good sound quality, but lacks in every other feature. Within a couple weeks of this arriving, it stopped pushing audio for phone calls, as though the mic blocked its ability to play audio. I have problems with audio changing volume constantly as though it has some auto-leveling feature that doesn't work properly. The skip button is a pain, since it takes double clicking the play button, which often ends up simply pausing rather than skipping. You have to get the clicks in just the right timing. Finally, there is no way to skip backwards without triggering Google Now and telling it to skip by voice. I'm returning this ASAP.

title: An excellent value
text: The only other Bluetooth speaker system I've owned would be the Deck by Sol Republic. The deck had okay performance once you could get your devices paired with it (long story, but the short version was that it didn't want to pair with any of my devices.) This Anker speaker system paired immediately with everything that I used. Overall, the sound quality is at least what one should expect. Unless you drive it at top volume, everything comes through crystal clear. There is a bit of distortion at high volumes, but for the size and the price, it's well within my expectations. I will also note that while it is advertised to get "better bass," you shouldn't expect it to thump. I'm very pleased with the device (and it's a wonderful addition to our kitchen/dining room!)
