title: Great for good patio sound without disturbing the neighbors...
text: I'd love to crank up a really high-wattage wireless speaker on my patio and just flood the whole back yard with the sounds I'm enjoying while bbq'ing. But my neighbors and cars passing on the street behind my house would likely call the police and I would end up embarrassed and fined. The Anker Soundcore 2 Portable Bluetooth Speaker (12 watts) is perfectly designed for backyard patios like mine. The volume is a little more than adequate. All my neighbors and passersby on the street behind me see is an old hippie rockin' to something in his head, cuz the sound doesn't reach them. Very good buy considering quality and price.

title: Audio quality is very good
text: I originally bought Anker SoundCore mainly for listening to audio books and online videos. I liked the products except for the buttons which were basically black-on-black embossing on top. They are hard to see even under normal lighting and I complained it. Anker customer service responded and offered Anker SoundCore 2 to try out. Upon receipt, I compared two products not expecting much difference in audio quality. I am pleasantly surprised that SoundCore2 has much better audio quality (deep bass and louder sound). The difference is very clear. (I used "We are the World" song on YouTube to compare audio quality.) SoundCore 2 has the same button design (black-on-black embossing) which was my original complaint with SoundCore, but the buttons are bigger in size and more pronounced, which make it a little easier to see. Still I would have preferred it if the button outlines have either different color (white maybe?) or are lit when touched or something. SoundCore 2 has status lights on top which is a big plus in that you can see them from a little distance. SoundCore 2 has a cover for charging ports while SoundCore does not. To me, this cover is simply an inconvenience rather than an improvement because I use it at home and I have to open and close it every time. (I left it open.) However, if you carry it around with you in the car or in the back pack, the cover will be useful to keep from dust etc. With a price difference of so little between SoundCore and SoundCore 2, I would go with SoundCore 2 definitely. Anker has solid products at a very good price point. And most of all, their customer service is superb.

title: Great sound small size
text: Best sound out of a small speaker. Love it so much bought another for my brother in law.

title: Awesome
text: Everything is great especially battery life. I love this speaker.

title: Seems well made. hefty.
text: So, I like Anker stuff. This unit seems to be fairly hefty, an indication of some good magnets in the speakers and maybe a decent sized rechargeable battery. Bluetooth connected instantly with my iphone after I asked it to find the unit. The buttons and feel of the unit are good. The sound quality is pretty good considering it's smaller than I expected. Not a ton of bass but enough, and the sound presence is for a smaller area. No distrotion at higher volumes. I'm using it as a speaker for a small flatscreen TV in a camper. Good enough for that of course. Music... Nice and portable for the picnic table but don't expect overly in depth sound. The sound is very good quality just not big. I'm thinking that this unit is higher quality and better sound than a lot of other units of this size and price. I've had a couple others and tried some in the stores. This is the one that stood out in this price/size range.

title: Great for music, bad for videos
text: For this price the sound quality is awesome, easy to connect, and I have splashed it and gotten it dirty with no issue. However, there is a delay in the audio, so if you use this to watch any video or movie the words will come in after their mouths move. I attempted to use the aux input instead to reduce this delay, but the speaker continually defaults to bluetooth connectivity and will not accept data through the aux. There is no way to manually turn off bluetooth pairing on the speaker, the instruction manual only tells you to plug in an aux cable.

title: Warning! Dark arts involved!!
text: This review is a warning. I will take no responsibility for whatever grim tidings may befall you if you ignore my words and purchase this product. You see, I purchased this little soundbar in good faith, with innocent expectations. Little did I know that I was entering into a contract with a company that clearly is meddling in dark magic. I worry now that this little device may be corrupting my soul as I type this. Because dark magic is the only thing that can explain the sound that emanates from this tiny little contraption. When looking the other way, this is a pair of full size speakers with a subwoofer, and it is pumping out full-bodied sound that fills a room. Yet when I look back, it instantly transforms back into a tiny little box. Or perhaps it is the evil magic used to create this device that is casting an illusion of smallness in order to deceive me. Either way, I suspect demons must be involved somehow. When this speaker is playing and you pick it up, you can feel the sinister power within it, thumping against your palm. It's as though the evil creatures trapped inside, forced to create such powerful and rich sounds, are struggling to break free and enter this world -- possibly to rule us all with sonic authority. Do not purchase this product if you value your sanity, because your brain will simply not be able to comprehend how so much sound can come from such a tiny source. Like myself, you may then begin to suspect the truth of the dark forces Anker has summoned to create this glorious product and you will slowly become a slave to its seductive sound quality. This is all part of their plan. You have been warned.

title: Really Good Value for the Price

Never have any bluetooth connection issues, and the battery last sufficiently long enough. I use this thing quite often and enjoy it. I play all kinds of things through this speaker: Classical music, rock, jazz....everything except country and rap (seriously, how are those even a thing!?). I also play podcasts. I'm impressed with the sound quality. I consider it a good buy and would be sad if it died on me.

The Anker speaker was EXTREMELY easy to pair to my TV and easy to reconnect when I turn it on/off as well. When I was using the TV speakers, you could hear the TV blaring in the hallway, now as soon as you get to the doorway you can't hear the TV anymore. Anker is one of my favorite brands for accessories and this simple-to-use speaker doesn't disappoint. I can hear the dialogue and music perfectly next to my head.

title: Great little BT speaker!
text: I am very happy with this little speaker. I use it in all sorts of ways, including playing music from my phone via Bluetooth and hooking it up to my 22" TV mounted in my van via the audio out port (see picture). The audio quality is far superior compared to my TV's speakers and makes for a much more enjoyable TV/movie experience. The battery life is good and charging is a breeze. The BT connects easily to all of my BT devices. The size vs. sound quality is excellent and is a good match for van dwellers like me. I've always had good luck with Anker products and find this speaker to be another excellent choice with surprising sound quality for the size. One interesting feature is that even though I may have the speaker connected via a cable to my TV, if I play music from my phone, the BT overrides the cable input. Kind of nice so I don't have to unplug the speaker from the TV if I'd rather listen to music with the TV still on and connected.

title: Buy it but read up about the Bluetooth pairing problem
text: I had given this five stars but I'm knocking two stars off because of the Bluetooth pairing issue. Each time you want to pair it up with a new device, you have to forget it on the old device and then add it to the new device and so on for every new device. . So, there are three different devices I would use it with, I have to disconnect it, forget it and then add it to the new device. That is kind of a pain in the butt to do. If you have only one device you're going to Pair it with, then this wouldn't be an issue. So, I give it five stars for everything but the pairing situation. Other than that, this is a good speaker. ------------ I'll keep this short and sweet: Buy this thing. It is worth the money. This is the first Bluetooth speaker I have owned and I was impressed once I turned it on and got it going. Granted this is not a $1000 sound system, but for $40, it's a damn good deal. This sounds excellent in a room about 25 x 30 or smaller. I actually bought this for my daughter, she is 12, for Christmas and I wanted to charge it up and have it ready for her. I was going to buy myself a more expensive Bluetooth speaker, but I'm deciding to keep this one and buy her one. Do your due diligence and read other reviews, watch YouTube videos, etc., but if you want a good sounding speaker and don't want to pay more than $43, buy this one. One negative, it seems to show fingerprints on the top of it. You can easily spend $40 on a good dinner and a couple of drinks, now you can have a good Bluetooth speaker.

title: Easiest sound system for patio or deck!
text: Bluetooth connection to Pandora, gives full range of music choices. It doesn’t get any better! It’s small, sturdy, strong clear sound that sits flat on hard surface under the table or chair (keep in the shade). Packs away in its included carry tote for travel. Comes with its own charging wire

title: Excellent Bluetooth Remote Speaker
text: I bought this speaker to replace an older one (from a different maker) that had died. I like the Anker product line, and this proved to be the same...reliable. It pairs very easily with my phone, and the buttons on top of the speaker work as labeled. Minimal need to refer to the user manual. At times, I wish it was a bit louder, but it does the job. A very nice portable (rechargeable) speaker, at a very fair price.

title: The Reviews on this great little speaker are all true. Excellent!
text: The reviews all are true. This compact little speaker is well made, well designed, functions easily and battery life and plug in ability are perfect for small parties or condos!

title: Impressive for its size and cost.
text: With its portability, and the fact that it’s water proof, it makes a great travel speaker.

title: Disappointed
text: I like the Anker brand of cables and other offerings, so I bought this with no hesitation. Anker is a solid brand. Imagine my disappointment when the sound came out fuzzy and like it was coming through a long tube. There are no adjustments for fine tuning, you get what you get. If there was a basic treble and bass dial, you'd be cranking up the treble on this speaker to get more clarity. After using this speaker the tiny little speaker on my cell phone didn't sound so bad! It was much clearer. I was hoping for much more from the Soundcore 2.

title: This little speaker is a must-have.
text: I can't believe how much quality sound this little speaker produces. The Bluetooth range is amazing and the battery life is as advertised. It's easy to use and very well built!

title: awesome bass, 'long battery life
text: I wasn't expecting too much from a speaker not only under $50, but under $40. Boy was I surprised. Clear sound, awesome bass, 'long battery life, nuff said.

title: Sound is AMAZING!
text: I purchased the Anker PowerCore 13000 portable phone battery which I am completely happy with. When my 9 year old bluetooth speaker began to die, I naturally wanted to try Anker. I am so happy I did. My old speaker was good (I thought it was great) until I heard the Soundcore 2. I am not a techy person so I can't begin to describe the highs and lows, base put out and stuff like that. I can tell you once the volume is all the way up on my phone or tablet, and I then control it through the speaker, the sound is amazing. Clearly, I made the right choice.

title: I wish I had bought two of them
text: I bought this BT speaker on a whim - it was offered on a 'deal of the day' for $17 and change. It's great. much heavier than it looks and sound is great, even when cranked up. It has that 'rubberized' finish which will no doubt turn gooey and sticky and have to be scrubbed down with rubbing alcohol. A warning about this rubberized finish should be required on all products that are made with it.

title: Doesn't Match Anker Quality
text: Im generally a huge fan of Anker products and have purchased numerous items from them over the last year. However. This speaker is not good. The sound quality is terrible when using an aux cord. I get a lot of static unless I'm connected via bluetooth. I purchased it as a speaker connected to my laptop at work. Since our IT folks disabled bluetooth, I have to use the aux cord. I have since stopped using this speaker because of the static and replaced it with a free speaker I picked up at a vendor fair. It's cheap quality but sounds much better than the Anker.

title: Love it
text: Love this thing. Won’t blow your hair back with the volume but for its size it is amazing.

title: Anker Soundcore 2 Portable Bluetooth5 Speaker with 12W Stereo Sound,
text: Anker Soundcore 2 Portable Bluetooth5 Speaker with 12W Stereo Sound, works great for the money

title: better than though
text: like this it was compact , sound was good, and kept in office just right

title: The only drawback is the loud "connected alert"
text: For the money, I find this to be a great quality speaker. Bass is strong. Treble is clear. The voice could be louder but I won't complain because the volume capability is great. Battery life is what it claims to be. Evidently, if you use it at 100% volume the battery wont last as long but it is still an easy 8 hour+ battery regardless. It can charge while playing, too. The only thing I dislike is that you cannot control or mute the loud turn on/off and connected alert...it can wake people up :) For the money invested, this is a great value

title: Nice little speaker.
text: Above average sound, average battery life and very good build quality.

title: A speaker so nice i've bought it twice
text: My first one took a tumble and stopped working, but other than that human error these speakers work perfectly! The battery lasts far longer than I could have imagined.

title: Awesome little speaker!
text: It has really astounding audio and bass for its size! I love that it is water proof. I have been using it for about 3 weeks (30-40 minutes a day) and it still has about 30% battery left. I only wish it had a battery indicator directly on the unit because the one on the phone's Bluetooth indicator is not super accurate.

title: ... had it for less than an hour but I LOVE it! So easy to set up
text: I've only had it for less than an hour but I LOVE it! So easy to set up. Sounds fantastic. Sooooo glad I went with this instead of paying a ton for the one I was originally going to get.

title: Excellent speaker!
text: I bought this as a birthday gift for my husband. He loves music and loves how this speaker sounds and how easy it is to use. It’s durable and always out on the golf cart with us, in his shed, or out wherever we are working. Great battery life, simple to use, great sound.

title: Excellent upgrade from the older Anker product we had
text: This product is excellent for the price range it is sitting in. My wife uses it for music. I use it for audiobooks. We are both pleased with it. It's sleek, somewhat heavy, durable, water resistant, sound quality is much better than what I'd expect for the price, battery lasts quite a long time, bluetooth connectivity is simple and easy, and the volume gets much louder than I need it to. I can be washing dishes or doing other noisy chores and hear my books with great clarity over the ambient noise and sound. I do not have to strain to hear at all. Would buy again.

title: Great Speaker
text: I’ve never had a bad product from Anker. This is a great speaker.

title: They stand behind their product and made it right, very happy!
text: Although I initially had technical difficulty, Anker responded promptly and made it right. They went above and beyond in rectifying the problem, and clearly stand behind their product. I'm very happy with the replacement they provided 👍

title: What an impressive speaker!!
text: We take this to the beach with us and are amazed at the sound quality.

title: High quality sound, You get what you pay for
text: Great sound and value. Upgrading from JBL Flip 2 and original jawbone jambox. Was looking in the $30-60 range but ended up choosing the flip5 since the flip 2 has never failed me. The sound is waaaay better than both Flip2 and OG jambox. I use it on my Lanai, perfect sound for all types of music. Hip hop, rap, country, alternative, classic rock, classical, electronic, show tunes all sound great. You can cheap out, or you can go high end with the smart higher end speakers (Sonos, bose, etc). but I think this is best mix of quality and value if you just want a high quality sounding speaker to pairnto your device.

title: Sounds amazing!

I don't regret this purchase :)

title: TOP NOTCH SPEAKER Excellent value
text: This is a nice unit. The item was well packed for shipping. No damage noted at all. The unit came almost fully charged and topped up in 10 min on a charger. The fit and finish of the item is top notch. I was amazed by how easily the speaker paired with my phone “IPhone 10R”. Just went to settings-Bluetooth and it was rite there and paired up after permission. For its size the sound is rich and fills the room well. The function buttons are nice, low key with a quality feel when actuated. I usually get the brand that begins with a B when accoutrement of this type is acquired. That being said I must say that this JBL product is on par with any of the other quality choices.

title: BEST ON THE MARKET
text: this bluetooth speaker always has and always will be the best bluetooth speaker on the market. they last extremely long periods of time between each charge and the sound quality is amazing. the bass is also insane and the sound carries so you can use this to play music for a large space. this speaker is definitely worth the price!

I promise it will be worth the investment.

text: I was going to go with an echo or Alexa but when I read about how you will have to acquiesce all of your privacy for it, I decided on a JBL FLIP. Super happy with it. It's easy to take with me camping, traveling and also my backyard. Well made, get's loud, great little speaker.

title: Quality

title: Great midsize speaker
text: I had compare it to several others in a store before I was considering buying one. This speaker didn’t sound like the Bose, but it didn’t have the price tag either. The flip sounded better than most of the others I tested that day. I considered the JBL Charge, but didn’t need to charge my phone with it. I have used it a few times in my garage to work on my antique truck and a few times in my shop. I have used it in my home office and wonder how much better it sounds in stereo, but I got this to move and listen where I’m working. It was also great while helping my wife cook and clean up for Christmas. The range pretty seems good, the volume is good enough for me, the bass is very nice. I can’t comment on the battery as I haven’t used it long enough to drain it. Overall, I like it and i‘d recommend it.

title: Good sound for travel
text: Sound delivery is a little less than I expected. Slightly boomy. I wish there were a way to EQ the sound on the unit rather than EQ on the source. That said, its quite adequate for travel and I would recommend it for that purpose. For frequent home use, I'd recommend maybe a step up from this.

title: Great sound, tricky to connect
text: Got this bluetooth speaker to use on our deck because of the excellent rating, not on the price. The sound quality is very good and will suit our needs though I was hoping it would go a little louder. The only downside was connecting it to my Alexa Echo. After trying to connect it with no luck I went to the internet to find a solution. Found some good instructions, but to no avail still no connection. Not until it was suggested in one video to shut down the Alexa app and restart it. After I did that the speaker connected right away. Had it connected right away from the beginning it would have been set up in less than 5 minutes and would have given it 5 stars. Update: Forgot that the max volume is controlled by the Alexa and not the speaker. Have to put Alexa at max volume if you want to get max volume out of the speaker. Now it's more than loud enough and at max volume the sound is crisp and clear for a little speaker.

title: great sound
text: This is a great small portable speaker. The sound is amazing. I compared it to a coworkers Bose speaker and the JBL sound was superior, especially the bass. Battery life longer than the Bose too.

title: Awesome speaker
text: Great investment. Sounds and works great! Being used in my boat

title: Love the yellow
text: Bought it for myself , good sound, easy to keep track of when traveling and bc nobody else has one this color.

title: Great!

text: The setup and sound is amazing its so loud. Took it out of town with me and played it every one loved the bass. And now since my car radio went out this is what i use in the car... lol

title: My Son Loves it
text: He's in the Army and take this on ruck marches with his platoon. They all love it - great sound and great portability.

title: Battery life is great
text: Bought this speaker for my husband for his birthday. The speakers sound is great; the sound travels nicely when we leave it on the patio and play in the yard. I charged it full a few days ago, using it a couple hours each day and its battery still has power. Love the color and glad my husband like it!

title: Impressive sound in a very small package.
text: I was replacing a larger Jambox that I had for 10 years. (It still works!) The Flip 5, shockingly, sounds just as good. The sides of the speaker pulse with the bass beat. Very cool. And since I play it in the shower it’s great that it’s water proof. It paired with my iPhone 12 very easily. The only surprising thing is that the speaker doesn’t send the battery life info to the iPhone. My old Jambox did that. Aside from that oversight, I highly recommend this speaker.

title: Amazing sound for a small inexpensive device...
text: Surprisingly good... I got it primarily for the shower. My 3 yr old iPhone is now absorbing water from shower vapor. I put it on a high shelf so there is not direct exposure to water. But, that no longer works, so part of my screen fogs. This device allows me to keep the phone on a bathroom cabinet with zero exposure to moisture. And, the sound is 10X better. The software that is recommended appears to only be good to link several Flip 5s together. Something I would never use. Other software to change the sound, or ?, would be better. That may exist, but it is not in the excellent Quick Start Guide. Actually, there is almost nothing to this device. No radio, no other player; you simply connect it to any other external device that uses Bluetooth. For me, that is my iPhone. What could make it better? Perhaps, a zipper shutting case for protection during travel. It does have an excellent hard foam surround if someone thinks to keep it. But, it looks more like part of the packaging that you would throw away. This is small, easy to use, excellent sound quality, and looks to me to be the best buy for my usage.

title: After Two and a Half Months, Sound is Cutting Out - Don't Waste Your Money on Overpriced Junk!
text: This is, with the exception of a pair of headphones, by far the most money I've paid for a Bluetooth sound device. And, after barely 2.5 months, the sound is getting wonky. It keeps cutting out while i'm using it and to say that I'm disappointed would be a HUGE understatement! I cannot believe that this is happening. The other two Bluetooth speakers I own are years old and cost a fraction of this. Suffice to say, this is the last JBL product I will buy.

title: Love this speaker!
text: This speaker is fantastic. The sound is amazing and the battery lasts longer then any other portable speaker we've purchased (which is SEVERAL). I listened to this speaker all day while I painted the house and I was shocked that it never died. We also take this speaker out on our boat and it's a great size for portability and music sounds great. I highly recommend.

title: DO NOT BUY
text: Worked great for two months. Now it cuts itself off after 25 minutes even with a full battery. Amazon refused to exchange or refund. DO NOT BUY. JBL is garbage. Buy another brand. You’re welcome.

title: Very good

title: Nice to hear the music
text: Delivered quickly. I am very happy with my JBL Flip-5 speaker. The sound is surprising for the size! I connect my i-phone, or my laptop and it sounds great. I haven't had the time to try it out on the boat, but plan to. My friend and my son have a larger version, but I am very pleased with this one - I can take it about anywhere. I have recommended my brother to get one.

title: MUST HAVE FOR SHOWER SPEAKER USERS
text: For years now I have been using a cheap speaker in the shower to listen to music. I personally can’t shower without music. This speaker was a LIFE CHANGER. It’s 10x louder with 100x more bass, I stay connected to the Bluetooth without any cutouts or problems from all the way across my apartment, plus it’s completely waterproof so I don’t have to worry about the water splashing on it in the shower. If you shower listening to music, you really have to buy this speaker. I got it at a slight discount but it is well worth the $120 normal price tag.

title: Fantastic portable waterproof speaker
text: Got this waterproof speaker in the green for someone as a Christmas gift. They love it. Perfect size and good sound. Should you have more than one you can connect them to play in different rooms or what not. Highly recommend.

title: Works great... until it doesn't
text: I bought this to replace the JBL Flip 4 I loved that my teenager begged me for. I thought "hey, go for the upgraded model for yourself!" and trusted the brand and went with the Flip 5. This speaker has never been put through the wringer. In fact, we've used it about a dozen times just on our patio. All of a sudden, just after the 1 year manufacturer warranty period, it doesn't turn on and won't charge. What a disappointment! I purchased the extended warranty through Amazon and will be trying to get this replaced. Depending on how that experience goes, my review may change, but that remains to be seen.

title: Great little speaker!
text: I saw that the Flip 5 was currently on sale, and I was considering sending that info to others. I have a pair, and rather enjoy them. I'm usually listening at pretty low volume, so I get way more than the 12 hours noted. I didn't realize how good the sound quality was until I ended up needing to use my work laptop for music briefly. But I also take it outside on walks near a busy street. I can crank it up and hear it over all the commotion (and not feel too bad, since there's not a ton of foot traffic for me to be bothering others with my music). PartyBoost has been a mixed bag. It's great to have multiple speakers going! But stereo mode doesn't seem to work right, the connection seems to hiccup here and there, and it occasionally gives a high pitched chirp or a low blub. As a single speaker, it's a great travel companion! But the main reason I am writing this review? While looking at the features list way up top, it says there's a 3.5mm headphone jack. and I am here to say "THE FLIP 5 DOES /NOT/ HAVE A HEADPHONE JACK." I hope someone in charge of the listing sees this review and removes that from the list, before someone gets upset about that. My only other complaint is something that I have never seen a bluetooth speaker able to overcome. There's a lag between video and audio if you're watching anything and using the flip 5 as your speaker. One thing that would be great to have that 3.5mm jack for, but it's pretty rare for me to actually want that anyway. Not all that worried about it.

title: Returned for Refund
text: I need a low-profile speaker to fit under my monitor, so I thought the JBL Flip 5 would work for me - but it doesn't. The sound quality is better than your average speaker, but not as good as Bose. But sound quality isn't why I'm returning this speaker. First of all, the product description said the Flip 5 has a 3.5mm audio jack, but this is not true. The Flip 5 is Bluetooth only. I figured I'd give it a try, but this speaker literally will not work for me. The sound sometimes starts lagging behind the video, and I have to un-pair and re-pair the speaker. Sometimes the speaker just starts powering down randomly, and I have to un-pair and re-pair the speaker. Now it doesn't even want to power back up. I'm done. I'm gonna go find a speaker that still uses a 3.5mm audio jack.

title: I take it everywhere. Love it
text: Great sound quality and battery life. I connect with ease every time. I've had JBL in the past. My main purpose for this speaker was the golf course. I use it on the course 3-4 times a week and often at home. Love it. I purposely bought the red so I wouldn't accidentally leave it behind anywhere. Easy to see. It's a chore to switch between them because you have to remove it completely from your Alexa device if you want to switch over to phone. The party boost with other speakers is wishful thinking. The connection to other speakers drops out half the time, is sometimes spotty and skips around. Sometimes the speakers aren't even at the same spot in the song. Forget about the stereo mode - it's just adding one more part to an already-struggling machine. Overall, a good little speaker with sound that I think is equivalent to similar size Bose speakers. Here's my review: PROs: Size, ease of use, decent bass at 50%, ability to pair two of same speaker, color options CONs: Can get screechy at 75% and loses its bass. Battery life is maybe 6 hours at 75% though does turn itself off to save battery. At $90 there are many other speakers that are better, but someone on here convinced me to buy another to pair with. That turned out to be a bad idea. It's a hassle to get them both to pair and after some time, speaker 2 will cut off even at 6 ft between each. Here's the loss of a star, they are at different volumes and you have to take off the control from your phone to fix it, but when you take back control with your phone, it goes back to one louder than the other. Bottom line, research Tribit and Trelab for speakers as good for half the price. Or spend the $ on Klipsch for good audio engineering, not waterproofness.

title: How to Eliminate Echoing/Feedback
text: So far so good, it requires a rather long 12 hours to charge, and it does not come with a charger, luckily I had one to charge it overnight. It can charge from a USB port, for me charger was easier. This puppy pairs quickly with newer devices and tablets but has a few glitches pairing with older PCs. Unfortunately both the Playback speaker and the Microphone were enabled causing feedback and echoing. To eliminate the echo when using on laptop you'll have to disable the Bluetooth Microphone, so that only the Bluetooth Speaker is enabled. Having both enabled causes echoing and feedback. Fastest way to sync to your device: When you turn on DOSS SoundBox the companion file called "DOSS SoundBox should pop up on your computer. The DOSS SoundBox pop up window helps you CONNECT and DISCONNECT the speaker. It can get glitchy, if it doesn't connect or disconnect when you wish then turn speaker off and on again, or close the DOSS SoundBox file and reopen the file. Moving the speaker closer to the device will boost the signal strength. If you can't find the file then search your computer for the Start Menu folder: Windows\Start Menu\Programs\BT Devices\DOSS SoundBox Alternate way to sync to your device: Right click the Sound icon, select Playback Devices. Right click on Speakers Bluetooth Audio Device and select the Recording tab. Right click on Bluetooth Microphone and select "Disable." When idle for 10 minutes it turns itself off, but then it often won't pair correctly if you turn it back on. The fix for that on the PC is to open the DOSS SoundBox pop up window and click "DISCONNET" then click "CONNECT" to get it to pair correctly. Longer way is to go to Bluetooth Settings; Manage Bluetooth Settings; click DOSS SoundBox; then "Remove Device." Turn your PC's Bluetooth off and then on again if it doesn't unpair the DOSS SoundBox. Once it's unpaired, then turn the DOSS SoundBox on again the PC go back to Bluetooth Settings; Manage Bluetooth Settings and on the DOSS SoundBox item click "Pair" to sync the speaker back to your PC.

title: A Cheap But Quality Wireless Bluetooth Speaker
text: As a non-audiophile and first time Bluetooth speaker owner, I can personally attest this thing sounds amazeballs. It fills my 1100 sq ft apartment with crisp, clear sound throughout. I could not detect any distortion EXCEPT when the speaker was placed at maximum volume and only at maximum volume; if I set it to max and then back off a smidgen the distortion goes away. The unit itself is very compact and has that feeling of heft that implies quality production. Certainly, in running my hands over the external surfaces of the unit, everything felt like it fit together snugly. I could not easily dislodge anything or cause it to rattle. The housing causes no distortion, likely due to thickness of material, hence the heft. The controls are very sleek and responsive. The icons are intuitive and using the center blue circle as a haptic touch interface implies modernity as does everything else about the device. I have not used it for voice calls so I cannot speak to the quality of that feature. It is likely safe to assume similar sound performance when using AUX or the TF card. As I do not have a TF card I did not test that feature so cannot speak to it's performance either. I noticed in the instructions it states it works with Alexa, apparently as a wireless microphone/speaker. I do not have Alexa, so did not test. All in all, I am very happy with my purchase. It is exactly what I wanted - A quality but cheap and very functional wireless Bluetooth speaker. I am not an audiophile and am usually happy with most speaker setups.

title: Bose should be better than 'Meh.'
text: I was SO impressed with the mini version of this line of speakers. A ton of clear, rich sound that you don't really expect from something so small! It sits low with the speaker pointing straight up, and you get plenty of bass response from whatever it's sitting on. It seemed to completely fill the room without being overpowering, and it was hard to pinpoint where the sound was coming from. Full 360! Sorta magical! So when the 'I WANTS' finally got me, I splurged the few extra bucks to get the larger version. Should be even better, right? Nope. It's VERY directional. You've got maybe a 45deg range directly in front of the speaker, preferably at eye level if you hope to hear any of the high end. Too far to the side or behind? Dead wood. I spent 10 minutes trying to orchestrate the perfect natural acoustic scenario for the thing before finally plopping it down on its back. Maybe it would behave like its little brother? Nope. Slight improvement, but my 7 yr old Sony SRSX3 sounds better without making me rearrange the furniture. Don't be dumb like me. Get the little one.

title: Mine quit too......
text: UPDATE! Contacted BOSE. They tried to get mine to work by giving me instructions. Still wouldn't turn on. (The extra warranty I paid for is not in effect until mnfr warranty expires so had to call Bose direct.) So they sent me a new charge cable but that took 2 months because they said it was on backorder. That didn't work so I had to call again and they said they'd send me a new unit. The new unit lasted 2 months and now it won't turn on or show power or anything. SO..... contacting Bose again....... I wanted a small bluetooth speaker for my mail truck. Several coworkers have Bose products and i love the sound so i found this one. I read reviews that said it suddenly stopped working but i thought, "Hey, this is Bose and i've trusted them forever!" so i bought it. Luckily i bought the extended warranty too (Just in case those reviews were right!) Turns out they were. Speaker had a full charge this morning and 5 songs later it just stopped. Won't turn on, won't charge, no light, nothing. So now i've started the replacement process......BTW, the sound is GREAT for the small size! And charge lasts about 6 hours.

title: Don't get the Bose hype
text: I've never been a big fan of Bose products. Way overpriced, mediocre sounding, and very base heavy. I though this would be a good compact, loud speaker for outdoors and beach. And for those purposes it is, but the sound quality is not great for what it costs. In typical Bose fashion, they emphasize trying to create very strong sounding bass from small devices but it lacks clear highs and is overwhelmed by very muddy sounding bass.. It can get loud but without some distortion. It's a nice speaker for the beach, but not worth this price. I put it up against multiple other speakers that were a fraction of the cost and the Bose was my least favorite sounding.

text: I bought several Bose speakers and headphones as gifts in the past. I did buy Bose headphones for me and very happy with them. But as speakers I felt they were a little overpriced and over rated. Then I decided to get these to be used while traveling. In summary I am very impressed with the sound (amazing). They added a rubber texture to these new models and they improved the handling of them. I have professional speaker monitors at home for listening but these sound natural, flat response (no artificial bass or treble boost) and room fulling perfect for travel companion. I do not know how Bose does it but I cannot believe the sound you get from such a small unit. They are well worth every penny.

title: She said it's a godsend
text: Used this speaker to produce "white noise" for sleeping. Use your smartphone or other computer to load up fan/white noise from youtube, and connect to bose using 3.5mm audio cable (not Bluetooth ). I say don't use Bluetooth for thisinstance because occasionally there can be a break in the transmission, which can disturb your sleep. The fullness and richness of bose sound technology will engulf you in Pleasant saturating white noise and ensure undisturbed sleep. Whether you have a wheezing (perhaps from bronchitis or the like) that keeps u up at night, or in my mothers case, a clicking in her ear everytime she took a breath (she recently suffered some ear trauma ), this will undoubtedly smooth out the rough edges and let you get to sleep at night. Triple A++ for this bose speaker. A godsend, as she can finaly rest and get to sleep at night. Thank you Bose!!!

title: Broken after using 2 times, cheap quality
text: I received this Bose Soundlink Color Bluetooth II as a present. Used it right after I received it and it seemed ok. So I charged the battery and then used it on a birthday party about a year ago. Then I turned it off and put it back into the box. Now 1 year later, I took it out of the box and hooked it up to the charger over the weekend. It briefly comes on, says "battery low" and then turns itself off. This thing does not even work when the power cord is plugged in. It seems that the battery broke, just by not using it and then the entire unit is broken because it cannot function without the battery working. This Bose Soundlink Color Bluetooth II does not provide any option to exchange the battery. It is made in Mexico and the quality appears to be very cheap. Bottom line, Bose keeps their "expensive" name and then uses super cheap stuff underneath to make more profit. It is not serviceable and essentially a "throw-away" product. This should be my last Bose product. Very disappointing - For those reasons listed above, Bose can no longer be recommended! For reference I attached lifecycle pictures: The unit as it was when new, then disassembled from the rubber shell to show the cheap core, the bottom label for information, then in the trash bag (where it belongs).

title: A great little - BIG speaker
text: I was really amazed at the sound! A tiny speaker the size of a soda can that creates a wonderful sound environment. I have it hooked to my Echo dot and the sound clarity is really good! And the bass coming out of the top is pretty precise. It's not the thundering bass but the correct one (to my ears). Takes up really a very small space. Set up was very easy. Pressed a button to pair it with Echo using Bluetooth. My phone and Echo both picked it up really quick. Can't really tell if it's going to work in long distance but I have no reason to doubt what the manufacturer is claiming. The only issue I had was figuring out how to use the volume buttons. I assume it's a quick press to lower or increase the volume but it's actually a long press. And then I am not sure how long to hold down the button to increase and decrease since there's no visual cue. But once I found the right volume it's OK. I can control the actual volume from the source as well. I got the black one so it sits very nicely behind a few Knick Knacks and not really visible. The sound is "surround" so it's not directional. I have not paired it up with a twin to test out the stereo effect. But that's not how I intend to use this speaker anyways. Very happy with this purchase. Kudos to the engineers for putting together such a nice speaker!

title: Surprisingly musical, but rarely capable of stereo
text: Initially, the MusicBaby Bluetooth operation was the best I've experienced yet and the speakers connected easily and reliably to my Win11 laptop and my Samsung tablet. After a few months of use, the speakers simply quit connecting to each other and it is either mono or nothing. Now, if I expect to hear stereo, I have to switch off my computer's Bluetooth, delete the MusicBaby speakers from the connected devices, start the two speakers simultaneously, restart the computer Bluetooth, reinstall the MusicBaby speakers. Pretty disappointing. Sound-wise, the speakers are far better than they sound be considering the size and cost. Totally pleasant and more bass than they have any right to possess, at moderate volume. They are fairly easy to overload with bass content, but they are also the size of a 12oz beer can. Great outdoor party speakers, loud enough to hear but not so loud as to dominate conversation. Really crisp midrange and decent high end (at least around 8kHz or so). I positioned the speakers on either side of my firepit (see picture) and the diffusion created by the shape of the firepit really illustrated the principle to some of my acoustics students last summer. The battery longevity is amazing. I have yet to run them down to nothing and I've listened to these speakers for most of a day a few times.

title: I miss my Bose
text: I purchased this to replace a Bose Soundlink Mini that cost 6 times what this speaker does. The sound quality on the Musibaby is decent enough, it’s no Bose, obviously, but it is much better than the iPad I pair it with. Which brings me to the things that annoy me about it, and I feel others should consider. They may or may not be an issue for you. First, this speaker can only pair with one device at a time. If you want to pair it to something else, the original device must be told to “forget” the Musibaby. This annoys me, as I got to taking my Bose being connected to my phone, laptop, and iPad simultaneously for granted. It’s not a huge deal, but it’s there. Second, the design is such that picking the speaker up often leads to inadvertent button presses. The buttons do strange things, at least when watching YouTube on my iPad. Pressing + , which one might assume is Volume up, skipped a video, and - did the opposite. YouTube has these buttons, I don’t need or want this functionality on my speaker. Get used to adjusting volume with the paired device rather than the speaker. I have not and don’t intend to test the waterproof / sand proof claim. I’m happy with the purchase so far. There are just those irritating issues which anyone considering this speaker should consider.

text: I got two of these in December 2017: one as a gift to me, and I bought one for my girlfriend. Both are the exact same model, but one is black and one is white. Otherwise, identical. The black one has been plugging along nicely for a year and a half now, but the white one conked out just over the one-year mark last December. I contacted Oontz, and the company offered me a one-time option to replace it for $4.99 or send mine in for repair. I paid the five bucks and got a new one. Well, that "new" white one has now conked out in the exact same manner as the first: one minute it's streaming music just fine, then there's some intermittent cutting out, and then---nothing. I de-paired and re-paired multiple phones and Bluetooth devices, and they all connect to the black one, but not the white one. This replacement lasted just over 6 months and was not used nearly as often as the black one. I contacted Oontz again and THIS time the one-time option for replacement is $9.99...which on one hand is generous and shows the company supports its products, but on the other, feels like an escalating membership fee for a product replacement service. At $15 in, I'd be almost halfway to just buying a brand-new Oontz, and while I can't prove it, given the short life of the replacement, I suspect those "new" speakers are refurbished (and not necessarily in a comprehensive, long-lasting way). So I decided to skip the replacement fee and I'll be looking for another brand of Bluetooth speaker.

title: Latency and middle of the road sound by default
text: When starting these up, the sound from this is comparable to your garden variety computer speaker. The output is not very good. Way too much high frequency treble. The bass isn't deep. Its manufactured kind of sound to pull it in those directions. When I fired up two flat response range studio monitors, the unadulterated sound in those revealed how poor these sound by default. However, because these are driven by Bluetooth from a computing device, these shine when using a software audio equalizer. After using one, I was quite impressed with the sound. The Bluetooth range is good. I can have my laptop located in the house playing music and carry this outside to the backyard 60 feet away. No disconnection, no disruption. If I took it out to my front yard, I was limited to less than 30 feet with it cutting in and out. This, likely due to line of sight. Bluetooth has wireless audio latency. Syncing video and audio isn't a good application of this. This is what makes the technology disappointing. I can put this right next to my Bluetooth enabled laptop Then, play a YouTube music video. The lips of the singer never match what you will hear. I even did a Ooontz firmware upgrade that didn't improve this situation either. The only way to fix this is to have the video source implement a delay so what you see syncs with the audio. This would require the video player to have this delay in. This also has to be a system wide solution, not application specific. For it should work across YouTube and all your applications, system wide. With this in mind, Bluetooth sucks for watching videos w/audio. Though I can use RCA connection, one of the reasons why I bought this was to get rid of cabling across my desk. While the product does emit Bluetooth audio and is perfectly suited for non video application syncing, Bluetooth, due to its low power consumption, makes this not possible. One needs to use wired RCA jack (provided) with your computing device to eliminate this latency. Thus, making the wireless application useless in my use case.

Sound was just adequate, the volume controls, power on off and ports hard to find in the dark. I needed a flashlight to find them. Thought it would be much louder than the others. AND IT WAS, but not by much. And here once again, I like sitting on my backporch at night with Moroccan lamps lit, beautiful mesmerizing light casting beautiful mural on ceiling but does not produce much light. title: GREAT speaker with AWFUL Bluetooth audio latency.
text: I should have bought the Angle 3 Plus. I decided to go with the Ultra because of its 14w output vs. the 10w of the Plus. The Plus had thousands of glowing reviews and was constantly mentioned as the best Bluetooth speaker you could buy for around $30 but the Ultra is apparently inferior in one key regard: Audio Latency (aka, "delay" or "lag"). When connected via Bluetooth, there is a very noticeable delay in the audio - no big deal if you only intend to listen to music but horrible if you want to watch a movie or play a game. People's mouths will not sync up at all to the sound you're hearing. There is a firmware update which improves the delay from 1-2 seconds to maybe 250-300ms (estimating here) but it's still noticeable. And there is 0 delay when you plug in the Aux cable... but that defeats the purpose of a Bluetooth speaker! The sound quality is fantastic, it's very loud with an appropriate amount of bass. But it's frustrating having to keep it tethered to my device. I think I'm going to return it and purchase an Angle 3 Plus.

title: Great sound, great portability, battery life is awesome but...
text: These are great and I recommend them. It's just that sometimes it takes a while for them to pair and I always have to manually activate "dual stereo" mode. It took a moment to figure out that the main speaker (any one I choose) should be the one being adjusted all the time. For instance, if you want to "dual pair" pick the main speaker playing to press and hold the key (not the silent, inactive speaker). If you want to "dual stereo" also remember which speaker is the main one and press and hold the button for about 5 seconds. I ended up labeling them to remember which is which. Also powers off after a while and doesn't power back on until power button is pressed on both of them. Kind of a pain when you want to start playing however once you do, they have great range - I'm able to use one on one side of a 1400 sq ft house and the other upstairs on the complete opposite end. The sound does well outdoors with one speaker and indoors with one as well. They are very cute and fit any shelf or surface and produce excellent sound quality for such small speakers. title: Get One!
text: I've owned three different Bose products; the Wave (cd & radio) music system, the Bose sound dock for iPod, and the Bose Wave Radio. Bose is known by audiophiles as "entry-level." They all sound great, and a LOT depends upon your audio source. That being said, I was in the market for a bluetooth speaker that is portable; that I can take with me on outings. I looked at Bose again, and none of them were below a hundred U.S. dollars. I just didn't feel comfortable handing out that much money. So I started searching for the highest-rated bluetooth speakers, with most reviewers. I happened upon the Oontz bluetooth units. A lot of people have them. People were giving them 4 and 5 stars out of 5. I looked at the price. The earliest unit sells for $25. The latest unit, just shy of $40. Heck of a lot less than a hundred bucks for a Bose, so I decided to give the Angle 3 Ultra a try. I opened the box, charged up the unit, bluetoothed it, and listened to the quality, and in the back of my head, remembering the sound from my Bose units. Again, it all depends on the source audio. My hearing is quite acute and sensitive. I can pick out conversations in a busy office. I work in one. I listen to Jazz....Django Reinhardt, Stacey Kent, Dave Koz, Benny Goodman, Vince Guaraldi. I also listen to "some" Classical; "some" Hip-Hop, lots of R&B, lots of 50's & 60's R&R, and all periods of Rock. I guess you can say I'm eclectic. I know what I like, and I can feel what the artist is communicating through his music. Okay, enough of that. Here's my impression of the Angle 3 Ultra: It's as good as my Bose Sound Dock. The Angle 3 Ultra isn't as distinct and separate as the Bose Wave by 2 points out of 10. That's pretty darn close. And a lot of it depends upon the source audio. If you listen to an un-remastered Django Reinhardt track, or any other monaural source, the Angle 3 Ultra is easily equal to my three Bose stereos. I think that's all I need to say to give you my FYI. Get one! Thanks for reading my review. Peace & Love.

title: Sounds good for it's size. Bonus points for design, water resistance, battery, durability.
text: This speaker sounds good for it's size. For it's size...Is that a caveat? Sure it is, but it's absolutely true. The sound, especially the bass, doesn't shake your foundations or rattle your windows, but it sounds better than what one would expect from an approximately 6"x3"x3" box running 14 watts into 2 small drivers, plus a passive bass radiator. Is it room filling? Depends on what you mean by that. Yes it will fill the room with sound, but not the bass to match the clean room-filling highs and mids. In fact the sound is processed by the speaker's circuitry to limit output if the speaker anticipates it will be distorted. Sometimes this washes out tones from the lows/bass whereas a different speaker without this electronic limit would play at full volume albeit with some modest distortion. The result is that the Oontz always sounds clean but I often found myself trying to push volume up -- if only because it 'seems' like the Oontz could be pushed harder. Overall sound quality 9/10. Sound power 7/10. The design and size are brilliant. It's small and I believe weighs less than a pound. Very easy to transport. Rubbery exterior, rounded edges, tough grilles, playable in vertical or horizontal orientation, tacky rubber feet and the rubberized exterior keep it from damaging surfaces or slipping. Looks and feels durable. Large control keys for play/pause, volume, forward/back and pairing. Stated to be rain proof. Probaby won't test that, but a great feature. Battery life is stated to be very long. I've not needed to recharge after playing at max volume for 6+ hours. Additional design features: Blue tooth pairing is super straightforward. Mini-plug audio input. Can be paired with a second Oontz. Overall design/features: 10/10 Overall. Yes, I'd like more power/volume but it's a mini-sized speaker, not going to happen. If you're looking for a good/great sounding speaker with a small footprint, long battery life, and excellent overall design boasting rain/weather resistance and apparently high durability, look no further. The volume limiting circuity may have you jamming the volume up on your paired device or on speaker itself (to no avail) just because it sounds so clean it leaves you wanting more..

As far as bluetooth goes, it works great with iPhone 6 and above, but you do have to remember to disconnect the device. Pre-iPhone 6 - you'll need to use the 3.5 mm audio cable; it's like connecting headphones. Only real cons and these are minor, but I'd like to see longer cables, especially the charging cable and they should include an outlet adaptor otherwise you end up having to use your iPhone adaptor. I'd also like to see the carrying case packaged with it. Updated Review: I iiked this speaker so much, I decided to purchase a second speaker. I still remain very pleased. Pairing with the existing speaker is very easy. You first have to pair as Left and Right Channel. Then, you can configure for dual stereo. It only takes a couple of minutes to pair. Of switching back and forth is very easy. I use the speakers with both my iPhone 6s and iPhone 11 Pro without issue. I've now purchased two of these speakers so obviously, I do like the product and very pleased. I would like to see a bit more volume, a slight update from my original review now that I've had one for several months. I would like to see a Bass control. These speakers have some Bass and it's enough to move the speaker. I'd also like to see an option that allows for connecting more than 2 speakers. Beyond that, still a great product and worth buying.

It only took a few minutes to decide that the few dollare more for this pair was well worth it. Some may wonder if they can operate as left speaker and right speaker. YES! title: Great for multiple speaker connections.
text: They sound decent for their size. I bought them for an office event where we wanted the same music streaming in multiple rooms. I bought two pairs and was easily able to get all 4 speakers connected and streaming. However, I found that the connection was better with 3 speakers rather than 4. Sound starts to cut in-and-out with 4 speakers and you also cannot gain as much distance from each other. 3 speakers seemed to be the sweet spot where you could separate them enough while having a solid connection. The description says "100ft wireless range" but I found it to be more like 50 ft with two speakers and decreasing distance the more speakers you add. Overall it did its job well and I recommend it for any budget method of creating an environment with multiple sound sources.

title: Much Better Than It Should Be Based On Size and Price, Very Convenient
text: We have many vintage audio systems, both in service and in closets, some of which I built in the deep past. To be sure, this device doesn't play in the same league as Altec 605B's. But I'm chagrinned in saying that we use it as much as the classic equipment because of its portability. We use it in the kitchen or out on the patio, or carry it from room to room if the day's tasks require migration. It sounds pretty great - certainly clear and of wide frequency range. (Note: my hearing is certainly not what it once was.) One may find it sounds better (always a subjective judgment) if it is placed against a hard surface (wall, closed window, etc.). We maintain a paid subscription to Spotify, so the digital files are high res (and yep, we have Bluetooth receivers on all the old systems). We have yet to run the battery down, even during a long evening (claimed life is 20 hours). It shuts off after some period of idleness. Bought this one as a gift based on our admiration for the one we own. There are surely alternatives out there, but this one is a great choice.

title: Sound first, everything else second.
text: I've tried other JBL bluetooth speakers in past years. To be clear, I've tried many dozens, listened for hours, tested, usually reviewed, and I've kept the ones that I think have something special, good sound. I thought after a few more generations JBL may have figured out how to nail together a decent thing. I was wrong. Buy a Bose Soundlink Mini. Listen to it. Figure out how to do better than that. It has half the volume of this thing and sounds indisputably bigger, better. JBL, don't cry. Bose also completely beefed it with their own new-generation "Revolve" speakers. They had spectacular speakers in the Soundlink III and especially, the brilliant and nonpareil Soundlink Mini, and decided to make the awful Revolve speakers. They may get a notch louder, and sound like muddy garbage. But it's round, and that makes it better for parties. Congratulations, we've discovered Idiocracy. Sony is even worse leading the charge into irrelevance, starting with the SRS-X5 and "improving" it by making the SRS-XB40. Great bass for a speaker its size, if only great sound was produced by bass alone. It doesn't produce any midranges or treble. Speakers by idiots, for idiots. Anyway, JBL has never made a great bluetooth speaker, so I suppose a 4th generation speaker that still sucks isn't really giving anything up. I just want the world to know that this speaker just ain't great. There's better, richer, more articulate deep and mid bass in the Bose Soundlink Mini, at half the size. It's not waterproof, and I suppose, people who need speakers with round cabinets probably also need to listen to music around pools most of the time, and can't figure out any effective way to prevent their speakers from falling in, so... maybe the JBL is great. For a certain type of person.

title: In Sum: Charge 3 is clearer and truer, Charge 4 is louder and "bassier"
text: I have both of these speakers, and I like them both. Here's the long and short of it so you don't have to research a million reviews. The Charge 4 is larger, louder, and has more bass. I like this one because I don't care about the miniscule differences in quality of mid/high/low that won't be noticed anyways since this is a speaker for pools, parties, etc. The Charge 3 is smaller, less expensive, and has a "truer" sound where the quality comes across as slightly, but noticeably, higher. It's not as loud and doesn't have as much bass as the Charge 4, which sounds noticeably less authentic than the Charge 3. Unless you're a tech guy, the deal with drivers, mono vs. stereo, etc. doesn't matter all that much. Do you want a louder, bassier speaker that can be heard from a further distance, on a bike ride, around a campfire, etc.? Get the Charge 4 Do you want a truer, more authentic sound at a lesser price? Get the Charge 3.

text: If you're like me, you're considering this for a mix of relatively low cost (you can find cheaper for sure) with a decent average customer review and supposedly great sound. Well, if you're into mega-bass, it's definitely a great option. For me, I would prefer something with a big more accuracy and while I don't expect a lot out of a speaker this size and at this price point, this is definitely heavy on the bass side for me. The EQ mode is difficult to figure out, so it may have a correction that I'm missing, but that just highlights an issue I have with it in general - I find the controls to be non-intuitive. I also struggle with "Which side is up?". some port of speaker surface has to be on the ground/table/etc.. If you put it on end, then that's going to be the bass side of things (no pun intended). If you put it on the side where it might role, you block less sound, but also don't give it a stable perch. That said, it worked out of the box, puts out decent sound volume, connected relatively easily once you figure out how to get into pairing mode (not that hard), and doesn't cost a lot. It is not a purchase I regret, but definitely isn't a purchase I would make again.

title: Louder, but sound quality takes a step back from the Charge 2+
text: I have owned the JBL Flip, JBL Charge and the JBL Charge 2+ and use the heck out of them. With each generation, they get a little bigger, sometimes add new features, and usually add an improvement in sound quality. I listen to Rock, Jazz, Classical, and Electronic music, as well as podcasts and sometimes a movie from my tablet when traveling. The Charge 3 is definitely a lot louder, but, to me, the sound quality is nowhere near as rich and full as the Charge 2+. For a portable, battery-operated Bluetooth speaker, one must have reasonable expectations - the Flip and Charge met my expectations, and the Charge 2+ definitely exceeded them. I was excited to check out the Charge 3, but was pretty disappointed - limited bass and treble - just a lot of over-emphasized mid-range. It's a noticeable step backwards. My listening habits usually have me fairly close to the unit, usually outside on the deck or in the same room as the unit, often a hotel room. I've never needed the Charge 2+ to be louder than it was capable of. If all you want is loud, and are willing to sacrifice sound quality, the Charge 3 may be the right unit for you. Additionally, I've got to say, I'm not a fan of the coarse fabric-like cover/texture of the Charge 3 (same as the JBL Extreme). It just isn't aesthetically or tactile-ly pleasing to me. Finally, there is one element of the Charge 3 that I really like - the larger rubber base prevents accidental rolling when bumped or set down slightly off center. Pros: + Loud! - louder than my other JBLs + Speakerphone capability + Great battery life that can be used to charge your phone or tablet if needed + Can use two for even louder stereo sound Cons: - A good bit larger than the Charge 2+ - Sound quality takes a hit in my opinion - midrange is over-emphasized - Fabric grill isn't pleasing in my opinion - No case included

title: JBL Charge3 review
text: I have been listening to the JBL Charge3 for about a month now. I work as a low voltage tech and have this on job sites with me. It has great bass, the mids are fine, the highs are not very crisp though. The speaker is loud I can here it quite well from 50 to 75 feet away indoors. However it is a directional speaker so if you are behind it, the sound is not as great as being in front of the speaker. It pared easily with my galaxy-6, my co-workers and I linked two of these Charge3's together and it sounds pretty darn good. Tried to link a third but it would not link 3 together. All in all it is a hefty speaker that should last. I have not tested the float ability, but it does withstand the rain very well. I would give it 5 stars but the directional system, with no tweeters just doesn't warrant 5 stars, sorry JBL. P.S. I wish it had a place for a lanyard or carabiner.

text: For the past few months I've been looking at higher priced units. As much as I love 80's Rock, $300.00 and up is a fairly substantial outlay for a Bluetooth speaker. This is a quality product that provides a pleasantly balanced listening experience. The Bass is good on this product but not outstanding. I would like to hear a bit more thump. But in all fairness, I believe JBL did a nice job balancing sound directed at the masses. Instrumentation though the mid range is very satisfying and the highs are clean and crisp even with artists that really rip the high notes. If you like a booming Bass that rattles the windows on your car this product may not be for you. But if your looking for a quality well made speaker with very satisfying sound, the Charge 3 is not a bad choice. I highly recommend it.

text: Disclaimer: Paid full Amazonian price for this. Pros: Big powerful sound; Water Resistant (play in the rain or dock side), Long Battery Life, Charge 2 gadgets at same time (I bring a lightning cable and a micro-USB to charge the phones for my friends in need while partying outside), one of the few wireless Bluetooth speakers that do well outside; connect 2 together to double up; durable and well designed. Cons: Fairly large...borderline too big to be portable, has a proprietary charger (which I hate), the power access is covered by a zipper which seems awkward, a little pricey for most, but in my opinion is a steal when compared to other similar priced products, even far more expensive options. In Conclusion: You can't go wrong with these. I have 2....I love them. If you are an audiophile...don't expect to have super accurate sound (wireless bluetooth speakers rarely excel in this), but the sound is great especially if you love music with some bass. I would check out the Charge 3 for those concerned about size, or the AIWA Exos-9 if you want something that sounds great, but alot less portable. I couldn't be happier with this product, if you are even considering it...get it....you will only regret not doing so.

I am finding myself agreeing with the other reviewers, the mid range for vocals and instrumentals seems lossy and lacking in detail (comes out very flat). The charge 2 I bought my mom, to my ears by comparison has superb sound reproduction for vocals, and bass in the charge 2 was a bit overbearing but it was a better product overall compared to this one. I bought my mother a charge 2, I regret not taking it back when it was offered. >.> Play a wide variety of genre in this you'll see what myself and others mean - Adele, Apocalyptica, Slipknot, Fly Leaf, Five Fingered Death Punch, Nadia Ali, Daft Punk (Tron), Enya ETC :) . Then listen to them on a charge 2, I think you'll agree with the findings. Compared to my high end surround sound system from Onkyo pretty much everything else sounds bad in comparison. :D I purchased this item for it's water resistant properties, I was planning on using one or more of these to for some temporary audio on the go for my motorcycle and traveling. I think the Charge 4 upgrade is not worth the extra $$ in comparison to this model. PROS Great sound in a small package! It also gets decently loud and has a considerable amount of bass for it's size. The price is reasonable for the quality. One charge lasts a long time. I regularly use this speaker during the week and maybe charge it once every 10 days or so. It lasts hours and hours on higher volumes on a single charge. You can turn the charging cable around and actually charge your phone or other device from the speaker's battery too. There are indicator lights to let you know how much juice is left. CONS It's a hair heavier than I'd like. I've taken it with me on trips, and it adds a noticeable amount of weight to a shoulder bag let's say. That's probably the price we pay for good battery life though. Also, I wish it had better controls. You can adjust the volume and play/pause on the speaker itself. In my application, it doesn't quite do as well I hoped it would. I like to mount this speaker on the handlebars of my sportster, behind the windshield, for music while riding. The problem I have is I can only hear it up to about 60-65 mph. I have noticed since purchasing it, I literally do not leave my house without it. I take it along in the tractor while working on the farm, I take it into the garage while working in there, and I even take it in the shower. The battery life is awesome at 20 hours rated. I very rarely have to charge it. I do wish there was a little protection on the ends for the passive radiators. I'm worried ill poke a hole through those one way or another. Other than that and the volume I can't complain. Great product and I look forward to years of use. In my honest opinion, Bose better step up their game on the Soundlink Color because sound quality isn't everything when it comes to a real world portable speaker. title: Do NOT buy if you plan on linking them together!
text: I had the Pill+ and the UE Megaboom. Charge 3 seems to be louder than Pill and bout the same as the Megaboom. Bass response is better on the Charge 3 then the other two by far. For the price point I figured I could buy TWO of these and use the Connect app to "link" them together in either Stereo or Party. Stereo mode sounds excellent...when it works! This is a known issue. Your device only pairs with ONE speaker, the other speaker(s) connect to each other. While there is no lag between them, the speaker(s) that are NOT paired to your device drop out constantly. Also please read about the Connect+ feature. This is a firmware update that can be done on your Charge 3 but ONLY speakers that have Connect+ capability can be used. You cannot link an Xtreme with a Charge 3 that has the Connect+ firmware. Before purchasing any JBL speakers be sure they are compatible with Connect...otherwise you are going to have speakers that can ONLY be used separately like myself. ---UPDATE---2/5/18 I have been in contact with JBL. After about 5 emails of back-and-forth they "kind of" admitted this is an issue they are working on. They have no ETA on a fix or what the fix will be (firmware or hardware). It was like pulling teeth to have them say their is an issue. They offered an exchange but I'm not sure how that is going to help me with a feature that doesn't work?! Also, JBL will NOT cover anything purchased from an UNAUTHORIZED dealer so beware. Look at Authorized Dealers on their website. There is a specific section for Amazon.

title: Great size, great sound
text: I wasn't sure what to expect, but this sounds really good and works well with an iPhone8. Connects immediately, and doesn't sound tinny. It's loud, too, so if you want to hear music while you're taking a shower, you can leave it on the counter. Very pleased with this purchase.

title: Good speaker that comes with no tools!
text: I have a Sony portable Bluetooth speaker. It is tiny and the sound is too! So reading the reviews, JBL came up frequently—no matter what speaker product I was looking at. That's a big bold recommendation right there. So I ordered it and I’m pleased with it. Good bass sound. Volume is good—which was my complaint against the Sony speaker. I cld turn it all the way to and it still wouldn’t be loud enough. With this JBL, I have sufficient volume with room to turn it higher—plenty of room left. Sound quality is very good. There is depth to speaking and musical voices. No feedback. Very, very compact; easily portable. Easily paired. But no directions come with it and no charger cord comes with it. Being an excellent product doesn’t give JBL a pass on providing the ancillary equipment needed to operate their product. Is the product worth it? Only if you already have the charger and know how to pair Bluetooth products. If you don’t, it’s not worth having to buy one on general principle: a charger should come with the speaker along with the directions. That’s just SOP.

title: Love this little speaker

title: Great Bluetooth Speaker, with one problem that has been fixed
text: Love this speaker, I am a huge fan of Anker and I was not disappointed with the Boost. However the first one I purchased failed within it’s warranty period and Anker quickly replaced it. Now the 2nd one has failed in the same way. The USB micro plug fails. Because the micro is a one way plug and the recessed port on the Boost it is not the easiest thing to get it in the right way, especially in the dark. This puts a lot of strain on the jacks mounts on the PCB. With repeated fumbling the Jack fails. Thus a perfectly good BT speaker cannot be charged. I also have the larger Anker Motion it uses the much, much better “C” connector I will never have a problem with it. Thankfully Anker has updated the Boost to a “C” connector. The USB mini Boost model 4 stars, with the “C” it would be 5 Stars. Make sure the Boost you get has the “C” connector.

title: Probably a good $20 speaker, Too bad it costs $80
text: I only briefly tested the sound quality and found it acceptable but not exceptional. The issue is the unit is supposed to be first fully charged and either it does not charge or the status lights are defective. I first contacted Amazon who in turn tried to contact Anker.. The first red flag is Anker is unavailable until NOON on EDT! Second red flag is they don;t appear to be responsive even after they open. This delay gave me time to try to research the issue solo. Turns out that charging seems to be a pretty common issue with this unit. And it seems that changing to a better quality charging cable often resolves the problem, although it did not in my case. So, we have an $80 speaker which apparently comes with an inferior charging cable. NICE! You expect this kind of thing with a $16 speaker but certainly not at this price If you can put any faith in the charging lights I received the speaker with 3/4 full charge. Over seven hours and two cables later, still not fully charged. I only tried the speaker briefly. It did connect easily to Bluetooth. The sound quality seemed pretty good but volume was far below expectation and below other speakers I have that cost 1/4 the Anker price. Oddly, it also seemed to disable the volume control on my Sony Walkman Digital Player. With my Bose, Pill and cheap Phillips Bluetooth speakers both the volume control on the speaker and the Sony work independently. When connected to the Anker, ONLY the Anker volume control works. I got fooled by the good reviews on this thing and trusted this no-name product as maybe an unknown premium speaker. Trust me, the only thing premium about this speaker IS the price..

title: It's okay. But don't expect anything fabulous.
text: This speaker is alright. I bought it at $50 after reading many reviews comparing it to Bose speakers. Being a very big Bose fan, I figured I'd try it, to leave at work. If it ends up disappearing or damaged, it's not a huge loss, albiet still annoying. Owning more Bose speakers than I care to admit, because they are fantastic, I can assuredly tell you the sound quality on this Anker does not come close. Primarily at higher than medium volume. Anything higher than 40-50% volume and forget it. Distortion is present and it is not enjoyable. The good news is that at low volume, this speaker does sound decent, and does a good job with mildly low frequencies. So if you're happy with low volume, then you'll likely enjoy this speaker. But, as mentioned, it will never replace any of my Bose products. For the price, I'd say give it a try. But if you spend hours a week (or day) listening to music, or are not worried about losing your speaker, spending more would be worth the extra cost. Additionally, after having used the speaker for a while, it does have strange charging habits. The last charging light will simply blink continuously, even after more than 24+ hours of charging, and never indicate a full charge. If I unplug the cord, then plug it back in, it then fulls show charge.

title: **UPDATE 2** *UPDATE* Ok But Not Awesome - Battery Has Died
text: UPDATE 2: Little over a year and the battery no longer holds a charge. I will contact Anker as I remember this speaker having a two year warranty. UPDATE: I got the original speaker replaced, as I suspected, the battery was bad. Also, the original speaker had other issues causing the distortion and clipping with the BassUp. The replacement speaker sound very good at higher levels with BassUp turned on, although a little bass heavy. and unnatural. I use this for mostly low-level listening and it sounds very good. I have a bunch of Bluetooth speakers and got this one specifically for my car, where I listen at low levels, so I'll keep it. If I was expecting it to fill a small room, it would be going back. Sound is nice and the BassUp works well up to half volume.. Anything above half and you get clipping and it sound degrades drastically. I do have a concern that when I received the speaker, the battery was completely dead, LiPo's really don't like that. It took several hours to reach a full charge and it seems to run out of power quite quickly so the battery may be damaged from the discharge. Time will tell.

title: WOW
