title: Much improved over the old Anker Premium.
text: This speaker is much improved over the old Anker Premium BT speaker. Everything from design layout to the speakers battery life BT connection and most importantly its sound quality are all welcome upgrades. This speaker is rated at 20 watts like the old Anker Premium. But this speaker hits harder and now has a more balanced sound signature. Highs are no longer muffled. Lows are now controllable which is nice. This speaker is also water resistant unlike the old one. Good if you're by a pool or something, Battery life is also way better then the old Premium. Overall Ankers new line of audio products obliterate their previous offerings in most aspects. But they are in need of improvement as a speakerphone. I own the Sound Core 2, Sound Core Boost and the Anker SoundBuds Slim +. The boost and soundcore 2 both have poor built in microphones, people say I sound muffled on them. But the Sound Buds Slim people can hear me fine. Having said that these newer Anker products are all vast improvements compared to their previous offerings. I also a few JBL BT speakers the flip 3 and the Charge 3. These Anker Speakers give those higher end speakers a good run for money! Even the Sound Buds + give my much higher priced JBL reflect minis a run for the money. Sound quality, battery life and call quality is very similar to my Anker Sound Buds +.

title: Great product

title: Best BT speaker I've ever had

title: KIA one year later!
text: Reupdate 2019: After one year of using this speaker it no longer charges. Works well plugged in. I would not recommend or buy again. Update review.... Anker went out of their way to send me a replacement that was updated. The new unit works perfectly and I am 100% satisfied. Anker is the bar when it comes to customer service!! I wanted to love it but the battery life was a deal breaker! I use Anker brand power cells all the time and love them, but I have NO luck with their flashlights. I gave this speaker a chance and the sound quality lived up to its reputation. The only thing I noticed was that when up louder than 75% the bass was drowned out by distorted treble and mids. At 75% the sound was excellent! The problem for me is that leaving the volume at 75% I only got 3 1/2 hours of battery life! I get more than that from an off-brand Costco special. For me, this was deal-breakeraker, had the speaker lasted 6-7 hours I would have gladly kept it! Sorry Anker, I still love you though.

Overall, I’m pretty impressed with these little speakers, especially since I got two for cheaper than one of the speaker brands I usually buy.

title: Anker SoundCore Boost 20W Bluetooth Speaker with BassUp Technology
text: Bought it as a Xmas gift for my son but when He is out I use it also. Very great sound in a small portable size.

title: Sound is good but not superior
text: I spent a lot of time researching bluetooth speakers and the bottom line remains that you really need to listen to them before buying. That said, you obviously can't do that buying from Amazon so I picked the Boost out of all the options. First, it came quickly but for the life of me I could not get the little door open on the side to access the charging port. I finally got it open with a pair of pliers. (Keep trying; try pliers.) It paired immediately with my iPhone 7 Plus. No problem there. As for the sound, it's okay but not what I expected. The bass boost is audible if you listen when it's changed but not something I would miss if was turned off (I wouldn't be able to tell). It fills a medium sized living room well enough but it's just not "rich and full" like I think you would get with a larger speaker (perhaps the Anker Motion + 30w speaker). I'm not an audiophile but I know and appreciate good sound when I hear it and I try to buy decent stereo equipment for exactly that reason. Bottom line with the 20w Anker Soundcore Boost is I would tell a friend to keep looking and listening. It's only a "deal" if it sounds good.

title: Can’t beat it for the price. And it is REALLY good sound.

title: Insane Bass
text: The amount of bass coming from this tiny speaker is mind-boggling. I'm very satisfied with the product and would recommend it strongly. The bass boost feature comes in handy when listening to different genres of music. Update Unfortunately, the speaker died after a couple months of use. For the first time, I'm disappointed with Anker. At first, the speaker wouldn't work unless it was plugged in so I assumed it must be an issue with the battery. A few days after that, it stopped working completely. It simply won't switch on.

title: Sadly not as reliable as the older Soundcore2 speaker
text: I bought this to replace my six year old Anker Soundcore 2, which was extremely reliable and durable. I was excited about this newer model, for a few reasons - 1) I'm getting rid of my Micro-USB devices and replacing them with USB-C, 2) the battery life of my old Soundcore 2 was starting to wean, 3) the new Soundcore Boost would be louder and have better bass response than my Soundcore2. The sound quality and battery life of the Soundcore Boost are definitely great, but I do have some serious gripes about this upgraded model. The main gripe is that the Bluetooth connectivity is pretty crappy. Mine could just be a lemon, but it frequently cuts out for very short periods and almost sounds like a CD is skipping. I've tested this indoors, outdoors, and by placing my phone at varying distances from the speaker. Toggling Bluetooth on/off on my phone seems to fix the issue, but I never ONCE had this problem with the old Soundcore2. My other gripe is that the buttons on the top are really difficult to use. On the older Soundcore2, the buttons were at least embossed (raised) which made them much easier to see. On this model, they're flat black, just like the rest of the speaker, so it's VERY difficult to see the buttons unless the light is really good. I probably sound old complaining about this, but I don't know why they made it this way. The sound quality itself is great, and the volume is quite loud for a portable speaker. I'd give this more stars if it weren't for the Bluetooth connectivity issues.

title: Love it

title: UPDATE: New speaker works/sounds great | Problem, side and rear speakers DON'T work at all.
text: UPDATE 1 (11NOV2017) (+4 stars, new rating is now 5-stars): Anker quickly sent a replacement speaker. I tested it for a few days, and man, I must say that the new speaker works and sounds great. The surround sound produced is amazing, closely resembling a movie theater. Don't get discouraged by the 12-hr battery life. The speaker has a built-in feature that automatically turns the speaker off (to conserve) battery life, if no sound is sent to the speaker after a certain amount of time (length unknown), thus making your speaker utilization extend well past a 12 hour period of time. It is extremely well made and durable, and excellent quality, which is a norm for Anker. Hats off to you Anker, you've once again surpassed the competition by providing a quality product, for a decent price, along with excellent service. That truly is a recipe for success. Job well done Anker, job well done indeed. ORIGINAL REVIEW: Big Problem... Side and rear surround speakers DON'T work at all. No audio whatsoever comes out of them. Only the front speakers (located at the Anker logo) work, but sound very scratchy. What's going on Anker? I know you make great quality products, but surely, this speaker that you sent to me is defective and unusable. Anker, please take this defective speaker back, and sent me a fully functional one, so that I too can enjoy a great sounding speaker that everyone seems to be talking about.

text: This is a good little Bose speaker, although not nearly as booming as others have said. It’s got a decent sound, which differs depending on how you situate it. The front and back speakers omit different sounds. One more bassy, one more treble. Considering this, it is a big con that this speaker doesn’t stand on straight. The edges are all rounded. Bose literally just needed to make the bottom flat to solve this problem but…nope. It has a silicon strap on the back so you can attach to things like a bike handle or shower hook (waterproof, total bonus) but the strap only fits around thin bars. Very thin. The app is easy to use. Speaker connects to two devices at once. Good battery life, but uses the charger smaller than USB-C which is stupid. Controls for volume, advancing tracks (or going back) are all simple. I haven’t used this for phone calls so can’t comment on mic. But I’d rather carry my phone than this boxy speaker so not sure why I’d even want that feature. PROS …Decent sound …waterproof …East-to-use controls …battery life CONS …Decent sound…not great sound…sound gets muffled/distorted depending on which way you set it down …doesn’t stand up on its own …silicon strap doesn’t fit around a lot of things …stupid tiny charger

text: I went and compared 3 similar portable speakers with each other (same price of around $100 each): JBL Flip 4 - Best quality sound of the 3 (amazing quality - very similar to Bose Soundlink Mini) - No noticeable crackle at max volume with high treble in music - Strongest/deepest bass (my table was shaking on max volume) - Very loud max volume Ultimate Ears WONDERBOOM - Smaller than JBL 4 but larger than Bose Micro - Crackling at max volume for some songs with high treble (Was not expecting this) - Bass is not as strong (very slight bass) - Very loud max volume (similar to JBL 4) Bose SoundLink Micro Bluetooth - Smallest of the 3 - Max sound was at 75% that of JBL 4/Ultimate Ears - Sounds "muffled" and not clear (quality is not even close to that of Bose Soundlink Mini) - Exposed charging slot (is this really waterproof?) Overall - I would pick JBL (amazing quality & very similar to Bose Soundlink Mini, but waterproof!) and Ultimate Ears for portability (75 % size of JBL 4). The Bose Micro, although very small, had really poor quality sound for the price (most disappointing).

title: This is a TRUE portable speaker!!!
text: I've owned Bose "portable speakers" in the past. I've also owned lesser known brand portable speakers in the past. After a year of use, I have to say this is the first TRUE portable speaker I have used. We've had it to the beach, Miami, Cruise Ships, biking, kayaking, you name it! The bluetooth connection is amazing. It connects to my phone almost instantly. I'd say 1 second after turning it on. It also alerts you and tells you what device it is connected to. This is really helpful if you've connected it to multiple devices and they are by each other. It'll also connect to multiple devices. The range you can walk away from it with your phone is very impressive too. The battery last a long time. It has a little light indicator to let you know where the battery is. It'll also tell you when you first turn it on. I've used it for hours and hours without needing to charge it. I've also forgotten to charge it before heading out and it still works like a champ! The sound. Wow! It sounds great and it gets really loud without losing quality. On the beach I have zero problem hearing it over the sound and other people's music/talking. I could crank it up even more if I wanted half the beach to hear. Portability. This is where it really shines. It has a rubber strap on the back that allows it to wrap around poles or other objects to keep it attached. I've only had it fall off a few times. I've wrapped it to bike handles, kayak handles, beach umbrella poles, you name it! It's small enough I can just throw it in a bag and run! I really like this speaker and use it all the time! The price point is also perfect for what you get. Not too expensive but still has that Bose quality feel and sound! I'd highly recommend this if you want something you can throw into your bag and run around with!

title: AMAZING LITTLE SPEAKER!
text: I bought this primarily for biking, which can become a little boring. It fits tightly to the handlebar, and stays on, so far, though I ride only on paved trails and streets, not sure it would handle any radical mountain biking (just hope the silicone strap doesn't break). I stream Sirius XM from my phone, which is in a rack bag, on the back of the bike, and has no problem maintaining a connection, was a breeze to set-up, too, with the Bose app I downloaded. It has powerful, clear sound, for a speaker of its size, quite impressive. It is supposed to last 6 hours, at a full charge, playing at moderate volume (I run mine a little louder, to overcome highway noises and such, so get only about 4 hours, actual, which is still fine). It is ease to charge with the included USB cable to a computer, and I also purchased an AC (wall) plug and DC (auto) plug, that connects to the USB for charging, for ultimate convenience in any situation (these are very cheap and available at Wal-Mart). There are also several hard shell cases designed to fit it on Amazon, and I have one on order, though the speaker itself is encased in silicone, and looks pretty rugged, According to Bose, it is waterproof, sandproof and shockproof, so really great for most outdoor uses. There are many cheaper bluetooth speakers, for sure, but I saw nothing comparable in quality, versatility or durability at Best Buy, where I purchased it (same price as Amazon), and they had at least 25 or 30 others, by many different manufacturers. I hope it lasts a long time, but I bought the extra 2 year warrantly from Best Buy for only $25.00, so I know I am good for at least 3 years (comes with a 1 year warranty from Bose). I highly-recommend this speaker.

title: Tiny yet Powerful
text: First off, I love Bose products. I own 2 pairs of headphones and a set of desktop speakers from the company. When I went and picked up the Bose SoundLink Micro speaker, I actually wasn't expecting much. I kind of collect small Bluetooth speakers and have had my fair share of good ones, and bad ones. I was absolutely BLOWN AWAY by this speaker. I have put it through various tests ranging from Podcasts to Heavy Metal to Rap to Indie to Classical. All of it. Every single time, I was amazed by just how much this speaker was able to muster. I do these little tests to each small Bluetooth speaker I pick up. Mostly as a hobby. Few things I have noticed are that this speaker sounds a bit better if you have it laid flat on a table and not hooked to something. I know it's made to hook onto things, but...whatever. The way that it's made is the cause for this. It sounds fantastic clipped to something as well, but just better on a table. The majority of this is made of a soft rubber/silicone, as well as the thicker strap that lets you loop (I can't really think of a better word for it) it onto things. Underneath has slightly thicker rubber and an open space that has some of the speaker exposed (though it's still waterproof). This is the reason it sounds a bit better on a table. The sound isn't really base heavy, it's fully balanced. The device also charges very quickly and I find it lasting more than 6 hours on a full charge. Sometimes 7 or 8 hours depending on what one is listening to. I'd say the best ones to pick this up for are high schoolers and college students, also hikers and people that enjoy traveling. This speaker is more than capable of filling up a decent sized space with crisp, clear sound. I've used it in my bedroom and my living room and I've had friends shocked that full music is coming out of this little thing. Pick this up and you won't regret it in the least. I can't say enough good things about this product.

text: EDIT: was 5 stars, now it’s only 3 at most. Not sure if it’s the charger or the actual speaker, but it stopped charging. It’s only been 3 months! Too bad because it was perfect. **Tip! Once you've turned the speaker on, if the constant blue light bothers you, push the on/off button quickly and it'll go off. Don't push it for too long or you'll turn the speaker off!** Anyway, I love this little speaker. I received it a couple days ago and, though it seems pretty self explanatory, I was a bit annoyed that the instructions were very poor at best. If you're having any issues or need any explanation on how to use you speaker, I'd suggest you check out the review by 'Purchaser' that was posted on on October 9, 2017. He/She did a wonderful job explaining the features. Anyway, though some have had a few issues, my speaker's sound is clear, crisp and not tinny at all. I've used it up to about 3-3.5 hours without any issues of it losing it's battery life. I used it one time and left it in my studio without turning it off (it turns off automatically after about 5 minutes of downtime) and without charging it. I went back the next day and still got a couple hours of playing time out of it. One thing that needs to be mentioned is that I was using it one day and had it up pretty loud (I use it in my art studio), unbeknownst to me, the bass was so strong that it made the speaker slowly move towards the edge of the counter I had it set on... it went over the edge and fell to the concrete floor! Luckily, there was just a minor dent and it still works perfectly. So just a warning that when you use it, you're mindful of where you set it. Either way, I highly recommend this speaker. Great value for the price.

title: Excellent Sound Quality .. A Few Limitations
text: We use the Lenrue Bluetooth Speaker primarily for playing music. It's small size makes it ideal for moving it from room-to-room throughout our house. It has excellent sound quality for such small a unit. It has four control buttons on the bottom of the unit. A MODE button that allows you to select one of three operational modes (BLUETOOTH, AUXILIARY or PHONE). As with a lot of similar electronic units the User's Guide leaves quite a bit to the imagination. Our first attempt to use the unit was successful, however, we found the battery dead when we returned to use the unit a second time. It turned out that you must keep the on-off button depressed until the unit plays its power-off tune. This holds true for all of the control buttons. (e.g. To increase or decrease the volume you must hold the volume control down until the satisfactory sound level is reached. All control buttons are located on the bottom of the unit so you need to turn it over to select the available options. The four button symbols on the bottom of the unit are small and very hard to read because they are simply depressions in the plastic button. I found that going over the depressions with a permanent marker made them very easy to see. While the unit produces excellent sound, our primary reason for purchasing it was to amplify sound during phone calls made via our Android cellphone through use of it's PHONE mode. I do not recommend use of this unit for this purpose. While we had excellent sound quality on phone calls made and received, everyone complained about the poor quality of the sound on their end.

text: 7/22 Update: I received an email from someone claiming to be with the company telling me they will give me an Amazon gift card in exchange for a positive review. I truly hope this is a scam and not from a representative of the company because this is terrible and extremely dishonest. I reported this to Amazon and if you receive a similar offer, don't click the link in the email and please contact Amazon immediately. I purchased this during a lightening deal on May 28th which was a fantastic deal. The 1st week it worked great and the volume was very loud. Keeping in mind that I only used it three times since I purchased it. On the days that I did use it, I was able to sit it on a table downstairs in the living room, walk upstairs to my office (which is directly above the living room) and could hear it loud and clear. Yesterday, (6/9) I noticed the volume was significantly lower than the last time I used it. In fact, it is the same as my cell phone and will not get any louder. I decided to test it out and connected it to my tablet and the results were the same. I really liked the size and the rose color, and it connected quickly to my cell phone and my tablet, but it is useless if the volume is the same as my phone. If that is the case, I may as well listen to my phone. Unfortunately, I have to return the product and will look for another speaker but this time, I'll go ahead and pay more 💲💲 and hope for the best. 😏

title: Quality that doesn't last--too many issues to be usable
text: *Updated* After having this bluetooth speaker for a few months, I can no longer recommend it. Very often now, there is an audible and extremely irritating buzzing sound emitted from the speaker when I play music from it. I have tried moving it away from other devices in case it is because of interference, but no luck. It does not always buzz, but when it's not buzzing, it's cutting out. The workable distance used to be at least 15-20 feet without barriers. If I start inching toward 10 feet, it will just stop playing for long periods of time, and then pick up again randomly without the speaker or my phone being moved. Finally, if I turn the volume on my phone down even one notch while I am sending audio to the speaker, the speaker will mute when it moves to the next song/track until I turn my phone back up. This is the case even if my phone is at a high volume and turned down only one or two levels. It will keep happening even if I never turn it down again, forcing me to max the volume out when I really don't want to. The volume buttons on the speaker appear to do nothing when I try adjusting volume that way. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- I am pleased with this item. It arrived on time and is aesthetically pleasing in my office. Some reviewers have complained that it is difficult to sync with their devices. Although, my item did not come with instructions of any kind, it was a fairly simple process. Just hold down the center power button until it flashes blue, look through bluetooth ready devices on your phone/tablet, and select the item titled Sync. The sound is slightly tunnel-like, but that may be because of where I have it placed. I would strongly recommend for this price point.

title: Honest and realistic take on this speaker. Excellent for low level listening.
text: This Tribit speaker is well balanced and puts out great sound for it’s small size. I picked this one up, after watching Oluv’s review on YouTube. He was able to work with Tribit and improve the sound, via a firmware upgrade. It’s important to note: make sure you have the latest firmware installed. I was able to confirm with Tribit that I have the correct firmware. If you have PO number 170629003 on the speaker, you’ll need to upgrade the firmware. The firmware can be found on Tribit’s website, under “Product Guides”. Just follow the easy instructions to upgrade. If your packaging is white and orange, you should have the latest firmware. Always check the PO, just to be sure. Just a firmware tip, before you evaluate the speaker. I have another smaller speaker for low level listening. I can compare this with and that’s the Xiaomi Mi. The Tribit sounds just as good, if not slightly better and it does get louder. It appears to have better stereo separation than the Xiaomi Mi. It also has a well balanced bass. The bass is there and noticeable at low level listening. I was listening to Princess Freesia at volume step 1,2 and 3 in iOS. The music was well balanced and full. If you’re looking for JBL Charge 2 bass/thump here, you’ll be disappointed. It’s a well balanced speaker. It’s not a thumping type speaker. It can get louder and fill a room. I can hear it throughout my 700 sq ft condo. The speaker is well made and it claims to be ip7 waterproof. Haven’t tested that. It comes with a USB cable. The volume level is in sync with iOS and there is a battery level indicator in iOS. There is no indicator on the speaker, just a warning when it’s low (red blinking led). I’m very pleased with the speaker. Just make sure you have the correct firmware and the sound should be more balanced and distortion free. I posted several pictures showing the front, top, bottom and back of the speaker.

title: Not going to be my beach speaker
text: I compared Tribit XSound Go ($30) vs Tribit MaxSound Plus ($50) vs Eduplink M6 ($30). All 3 had a deal, both Tribits had a coupon and the M6 was on a lightning deal. MaxSound Plus is far superior to the XSound Go, now the MaxSound Plus is almost twice the price. But it feels only slightly heavier than the Go, and only slightly larger. If you need the speaker to be smaller I'd recommend looking into the very small options out there. The bass boost and audiobook options on the MaxSound Plus make the sound quality shine compared to the XSound Go. Eduplink M6 is a 360° speaker so comparing to Tribits Stormbox ($100+) would be better but the M6 is priced around XSound Go. The sound isn't as clear as the Tribit MaxSound Plus. The bass also doesn't compare to MaxSound Plus which has bass boost capabilities. The M6 is far lighter than either of the Tribit speakers by far. It feels half the weight of the MaxSound. But it is slightly bigger than the MaxSound. -XSound Go is the smallest of these 3 speakers. -MaxSound Plus is the loudest -MaxSound Plus has the most clarity -M6 will float -M6 is 360° so it sounds the same on every side -M6 has RGB lighting effects "party lights" -M6 arrived with a cosmetic defect -All 3 have a cover for the charge port, USB-C -Tribit cover is easier to open, better design -All 3 have auxiliary port -All 3 say 20+ hours of battery life. It took me 3 days to drain the MaxSound Plus. I'm leaning towards keeping the Eduplink M6 because I need a beach speaker. The XSound Go doesn't stand a chance in this race. The real comparison is between M6 and MaxSound Plus. Both are plenty loud enough, MaxSound Plus has better clarity and much better bass. The M6 feels half the weight, the woven material on the M6 and silicone ends make me think it will do better keeping the sand out. The front of the MaxSound Plus has holes and if the speaker is knocked in the sand I fear it may get sand on the drivers. The M6 was almost half the price. The M6 feels like you could throw it and withstand damage better, pure speculation.

text: I've been looking for a portable bluetooth speaker that sounds good and is portable. Just received Tribit XSound Go today, and really surprised at the size, portability, and build quality. I can’t say about the claim of 24 hour battery life, but I’m optimistic. The thing I’m surprised is the sound quality for its small size. It has two speakers and a passive radiator, and they produce clear and balanced sound, the base is there but not muddled or overpowering like Sony XB 10. Good sound quality for its size and purpose. I have tried other bluetooth speakers like Sony XB10, Anker Soundcore Motion Q., Ontz, Insignia, JBL Flip 2, but I like the clear and balanced sound with adequate presence of bass of Tribit and will be keeping it. Update after 3 months: bought another one but it was producing hissing sound, Amazon did a quick replacement, but the replacement is producing crackling sound from one of the speaker, so need to return it too. So good sound, reasonable price, but uncertain as to the quality of it.

title: It's gooooood
text: I bought this and the Maxsound Plus. Honestly, I liked this better than the Plus even though it is half the price and smaller. Sure there isn't as much bass, but it has a nicer soundstage, is more clear, and sounds great. Go with this one. It's on sale right now for like $26. Worth it!

title: After about a year, the micro-USB connection is dying.
text: Pretty good sound, good price, but after almost a year the micro-USB connection (for charging it) is getting loose so that it will only charge if I put pressure on it, like from setting some weight on the connection--not good. Was satisfied until this problem, but it's not worth it for it lasting only a year.

title: Good battery life. Good sound. Good shower speaker.
text: It’s a very good quality speaker; my daughter uses it in the shower for three weeks. She has used it quite a bit without needing to charge it yet, and she loves the sound quality.

title: Good buy
text: Battery life is sick... Sounds great as long as your not too far away from it. Bass is there, but wont travel very far. Sounds good overall for a BT compact speaker. It’s the perfect size for my needs at work. Bought on for my daughter, and she loves it. She takes it into the shower and places it on the window with no moisture issues to speak of. Long term could be an issue, but for the price, any longevity will be worth it for me.

title: very good
text: This speaker works great, has good clarity, volume, and battery life. Setup was quick and easy. My old speaker worked good, but would drop its connection frequently. I have not had that problem with this speaker.

title: It produces a great quality clear sound
text: The range of the sound of music is awesome & clear.

title: Not the best sound quality.
text: I have the Google Home speaker in my kitchen and I always use that to listen to music in my kitchen. I bought this to take with me to other rooms throughout my house and I noticed that it doesn’t hold a candle to my Google Home speaker. It serves its purpose, but the sound quality is just ok.

title: Big thing comes in small package they was talking about this speaker
text: Surprisedly loud for it’s size Go for personal use and good for small children 👶🏿. For me personally I’ll go with the upper tier of tribit you won’t be disappointed

title: XSound Go vs. XSound Surf
text: I couldn't decide between the XSound Go and XSound Surf and ordered both. After testing both next to each other, I can definitely say that the XSound Go sounds much better especially at higher volumes. So even though this is a bit more expensive, I kept the XSound Go and returned the Surf. Its a good speaker for under $30 price range. The Bluetooth range is not much and definitely not what is advertised. I would say 20-25 ft max. Have only used it for 2-3 days so can't say much about battery or other things yet. I'll update it later if something comes up.

title: Used to like it - 5 months old and broken
text: I purchased this is December, it is now 5 months old and I hardly use it. I brought it out for a gathering and it sounds like the speaker is blown. I'm Very disappointed because at first, this speaker was Awesome and well worth the money. Now I know why its cheaper. The life on it is short. FYI, I Never crank it for respect of my neighbors.

title: Great sound for a little $
text: Just got my Tribit speaker and set it up in less than 10 seconds! I'm using it in my work office and although it's a small space, I'm really impressed with the rich sound from this bluetooth speaker. It's by far the best sounding speaker I've heard for under $100, much less under $50! I'm now considering getting a second one for my home office as my main stereo receiver is on the fritz - its sound is that satisfying. Note - I am a real "hooman", based in the US, and I'm an unrepentant music snob. So this is a real product review (which I seldom write).

title: Big sound for a little cutie of a speaker 🔊
text: I bought this speaker thinking I would use it as my computer speaker. It worked for that purpose sound-wise but I decided that it was impractical to use a battery driven powered speaker after I accidentally left it on all night and it was dead the next morning leaving me speakerless in the morning until I charged it up. So now it is a great speaker I am using for listening to music, easy to carry around, nice looking. My husband has used the larger one for a few years and loves it so I knew I would probably like it, even though smaller. And I do. Excellent sound!

title: Great value
text: Connects super easily and offers good quality sound. I probably use 1x-2x a week for about anywhere from 20 min to 2 hr total (this is on the high end). Believe it or not, I’ve charged it no more than 3x since purchasing it in July. Unbelievable.

title: They work OK and help with an iPad so that you can turn up the volume. Too much bass for my taste.
text: They are OK. I use them with my iPad because the speker on the iPad is tinny and too quiet. There is way more bass than I would like. I tried to adjust the equalizer on the iPad, but it did not seem to help.

title: Great all-purpose bluetooth speaker, especially for the price
text: I bought this last summer and it has been a fantastic companion through two moves, trips to the beach, bicycle rides, and too many showers to count. I use it as my primary speaker for my computer when I'm home (via the 3.5mm connection), as well as a bluetooth speaker for my phone. For a transient student, it couldn't be more perfect, and it will continue being an excellent on the go speaker. THE 3.5MM CONNECTION Easy to use, and can be paired with a bluetooth device simultaneously (the bluetooth audio take priority, so if you get a notification it will mute the 3.5mm connection momentarily). If it is also plugged into USB, the speaker won't automatically turn off (which I like!). BLUETOOTH Easy to pair and, for me, the battery level indicator for the latest android update works perfectly. Range feels pretty good, but I haven't pushed it. I haven't had any connection losing problems, and it will automatically pair with my phone when I get home. WATERPROOF I literally bring this into the shower with me (on bluetooth) and it's been fully submerged in water with no problems. Dries relatively quickly as well and I'm able to plug it back in on my desk with no issue. SOUND The sound is crisp and clear, though a bit bass heavy for my personal taste. It's powerful for its size, but don't expect home theater quality. It has great all-purpose sound for a small space or when out and about. I used it once to get voice directions while biking somewhere, and it worked okay, but sometimes even on max volume would get drowned out by cars. I don't like turn by turn directions while biking generally, so I never tried it out again. Overall probably one of the best deals out there for a waterproof bluetooth speaker.

title: Great speaker! Excellent value.
text: I love my Tribit! The sound quality is excellent. Easy to connect. The charge lasts forever. I only use it occasionally (a couple of hours a week, maybe) and I have not had to recharge it once yet (have had it a few months). I am going to see how long I can go without charging. Very pleased with this speaker!

title: Best Bluetooth speaker for price out there
text: I’m sure many people these days have gone through their fair share of Bluetooth speakers. This one is by far the best one I’ve had out of the probably 10-15 I’ve had in the past, especially for this price point. The sound is amazing, the volume also goes up to a decent decibel for the size of the speaker. The quality of the speaker of itself seems pretty sturdy and made well. It is very easy to connect with from many different devices. The battery life is okay, but if you’re wanting something to last you multiple days when used constantly you should just get something that plugs into an outlet and not something wireless. Overall I love this speaker! Would buy it again in a heartbeat and buy it for gifting purposes as well.

title: worth it
text: This is a nice speaker for the price. The only issue we have is that the volume does not stay consistent and I have to keep adjusting it.

title: Amazing value for the price
text: I use this speaker when listening to music from my iPhone and I love it! The sound is outstanding and it is a great value for the price! I would definitely recommend it!

title: Great Sound Quality
text: Very happy with this little gem! Purchased the speaker to use outside on our deck or in the pool area. Great sound. Very happy :)

title: Bass heavy
text: The sound is okay at best. It's very heavy on bass and if it gets wet the sound turns to utter mud due to water blocking the mesh cover. It's acceptable for open areas but in more closed environments the over the top bass really makes it an underwhelming experience. I do not recommend for a shower/bath speaker unless you have a very open room. On the plus side, the device is solidly built and feels nice. It's functions very well with Bluetooth connectivity and battery life is great. I've only charged it once since purchasing. Can't accurately say if it is indeed "24h" as no one will realistically run speakers that long. Has auto power off as well so if you use it in bed like I do, it won't drain the battery.

title: Not bad! Buttons need work.
text: Been using the trivet for about a week now with both my moto G7 phone and hp laptop and I really like it. Sound isn't top quality but for the price it is a good deal. Had a few connectivity issues at first but nothing consistent and it seems to be connecting pretty quickly now. My only complaint is the control buttons on top. They are completely flush and same black as the rest of the device, nothing is raised, no distinguishing colors. You have to tilt it so the light catches the markings to see them. I prefer raised buttons so you can just feel for the one you need. Bad design IMO. Other than that, I'm happy with it.

title: 3 YEAR REVIEW: Excellent!
text: We bought this speaker in 2019 and it went strong until its death this December. We used it constantly outside, inside, in the care etc and it never failed us. Highly recommend. Ordering another for the next 3 years!

title: Beyond expectations
text: I wanted something small but not too small. I wanted something with great sound. I wanted something that would connect hassle free. I got all my wants. If you're on the fence about this product, buy it. My husband had a similar speaker by Sony. I tried repeatedly to connect my iphone to it and we couldn't figure out why I wasn't able to connect. Frustrated, I scanned all the reviews here and decided on this one. Glad I did. I'm very happy.

title: Sound On the Go
text: Great little speaker with some impressive battery so far. The bass is a high light and the price was just right. Good feel too.

title: Battery stopped re-charging after five weeks
text: Do use it every day. Good sound. Unfortunately the battery went bad 5 weeks after buying, would not re-charge. My friend did the same thing.

title: Love this speaker.
text: Love this speaker! I live in a small apartment. I don't have room for a bunch of audio equipment. This speaker has great tone. I can listen to opera loud with no distortion. I just got it, so I hope the battery life is true. I tried two other cheaper Bluetooth speakers, but they both stopped working fairly quickly. Listening right now!

title: Great sound quality, particularly for the price, but not waterproof.
text: I loved this little speaker. It had excellent sound quality, excellent battery life, but I bought it specifically for its waterproof rating. In Minnesota, we love to float down rivers on inner tubes. I took this little speaker with me on my last float down the river. It spent the entire time in a waterproof bag (not dangling in the river, like most of my friends' speakers, like the JBL) playing music. It worked great, but the moisture condensation from the sun in the bag must've got to it, because that was the last time it ever played (and yes, the charging cover was sealed tight on it). I tried to charge it and the light went red for a bit and then disappeared and it never played again. Loved it, but do not recommend near water. Not waterproof. *EDIT* I contacted the company after writing this review and they offered an immediate replacement/refund at no cost, no questions asked, which was excellent customer service. Adding a star. :)

title: Just the thing for poolside sound!
text: Good audio, especially with the extra bass. Bought it primarily for use poolside since it’s waterproof but so far it’s seen major duty in my workshop. But the pool is nearly at summer temp so we’ll soon be putting it to good use around the pool 😊

title: Can't beat it for the price
text: While it's not the greatest bluetooth speaker in the world, it sounds many times better than the other speakers I've bought around this price and some that were even more expensive. Easy to recommend.

title: Very good sound for the price
text: The battery lasts for the entire day and the sound is very crisp, good bass

title: Best used as a speaker for a TV with crappy sound.
text: The sound GREAT! The range is CRAP! I have a Sounsblaster Roar that I use as my primary BT speaker for outside. This thing sounds like a mini version of that, but I literally have to be in the same room as the speaker to use the BT. 3 STARS.

title: Really good, really expensive.
text: I don't particularly care for coconut, but this is good stuff if you can afford it.

title: Exactly what I was looking for
text: It came appropriately packaged. It arrived on time. The battery life is great. Keep in mind it is not something I use all day everyday. The sound is pretty full and bass is pretty good as well (doesn't have the tin can sound). When I turn it on it immediate connects to my phone, no effort, no issues. I use it in the bathroom while I shower and in all other environments. Would recommend.

title: Love this!
text: Love this speaker! Unobtrusive, easy to connect to and a clear crisp sound. No unique funky power cord to keep up with, uses an easy to find charger.

title: Too much bass for me.
text: Easy to use. Good volume. Too much bass for me. Guess I should have read the description huh?

title: to small for me
text: not what I ordered, decided to keep, turned out okay

title: Proof that size doesn't always matter
text: When I first open the very well package speaker I was sure I was going to be disappointed because of it's small size. Then I blue toothed it to my phone and played some Ottmar Liebert. The sound was so clear and clean I couldn't believe it. So I decided to try some Lynyrd Skynyrd and was equally impressed. I haven't used enough to comment on the batty life but if it is anything like the quality I will buying some off these as gifts. A truly great product especially for the price.

title: Even though it supposed to be waterproof, try not getting water in it
text: Brought this on vacation to Punta Cana. Sound quality is great until you bring it in the water but I’m just assuming because water gets inside of it. Connecting to the Bluetooth isn’t fast and took a while but overall, it did the job. Happy with the purchase :)

title: Best Speaker!
text: Have had this for a little more than a month now & absolutely love it. Awesome sound quality for a small speaker, nice & loud. Use this at work & sound remains great for my 12 hour shift. Great charge quality & love that I can also use an auxiliary cord with it!

title: Shower speaker with good sound...
text: Great speaker and use it everyday in the shower. Battery lasts a while..unsure how long. I usually charge every 3rd or 4th day. Recommend....

title: Simple, Clear, and Powerful
text: I recently moved into an apartment and decided to not set up the Denon stereo component system I had had for years. Thought I'd try this Bluetooth unit instead. I am amazed at how well it produces stereo sounds. Some of my recordings are of birds singing and other nature sounds, and although this unit is in one place, I hear the birds far off to the left and right -- a truly enveloping sound. And using Bluetooth means I don't have to make the connections with my Airport Express, as I have done in the past to play music from my mobile devices. Very pleased with this. An exceptional value at this price.

title: I like it!
text: It is very user friendly not too big and the sound is very clear. I love using it on my golf cart.

title: Great bluetooth speaker
text: I have used this on vacation many times. I like my music at the beach and pool and this speaker has worked fantastic. Battery life has stayed constant and I have had the speaker for a few years now. I would buy another if this one ever quits working. Or I drop it in the pool or ocean.

title: Poor volume control and no safety certification
text: Pros: Great sound Cons: Not UL Listed or even ETL Listed. No safety certification. Volume increments are way too big. Can't ever achieve the volume I want, and don't see myself ever using more than 25-30% of the max volume. It goes from too soft to too loud. In addition, the volume varies across different uses and apps.

title: Very happy with the sound
text: It is inexpensive and I am very happy with this speaker. I think it sound great.

title: What am I hearing?! Update edit
text: I will simply leave this one thing about this speaker and go from there... Put a UE, Bose, Harmon Kardon case on this and it's selling at this form factor for $150-$200. I have been into high end audio for awhile so I needed a small speaker to lug around and not worry about maybe taking a fall here and there. I didn't expect this sound quality at this price or even double the price. This is just slightly longer than my cell phone and is easily held in one hand, so a small form factor. The sound is truly incredible in clarity and level of bass coming from the small unit. Don't waste your money on a name brand because this little thing is quite the value and will rival speakers up to $200 in the BT realm. Edit: I purchased another for different portable use, got one of the blue ones. For some reason the blue one seems to have a hotter treble range, maybe I'm comparing a brand new speaker to a well used one but not sure.

title: Quit charging after a year and a half.
text: I would love to give this speaker five stars, but after a year and a half it will no longer charge- it seems like the USB connections are loose. Otherwise, I love everything about this speaker.

title: re edit 8/29
text: re edit 8/29/22 speaker wont charge now after two months...emailed customer service...no response thus far June 1, I love love love my speaker...its in a 15x30 room...its really really loud. I was able to connect my cpu and my phone to it...Just ordered another one so I can have on the go...Its great sound like a Bose speaker, great bass...Im highly impressed.

title: Replaced a Sony
text: It turns out that you're not supposed to leave a bluetooth speak IN THE HOT TUB FOR A MONTH. Who'd have guessed that? Anyhow, this one replaced a nice Sony Bluetooth speaker. This one cost a lot less, and works fine. The audio quality isn't as good, but considering the price, this is a great product. Seems to be waterproof, and it works well.

title: Finally FULL SOUND
text: This is my third Bluetooth speaker. I use them camping so I need tough, waterproof and decent battery life, what I've always sacrificed was sound. Not that the others were bad they were just a little tinny and small. The Tribit is full balanced sound, tough and waterproof and yes I dunked it.

title: It’s only 6 Watts the seller was good and I received a quick return and refund
text: This speaker had very little power. You almost have to be right next to it to hear the music. It’s only 6 Watts the seller was good and I received a quick return and refund. Be cautious of Watts when buying speakers. Minimum should be 10 Watts.

title: Amazing Speaker!
text: Wow! Every time I turn this thing on I'm blown away at the sound it produces. For its size and price you can't do any better. Amazing speaker!

title: Big Bang for the buck
text: This small but mighty little speaker has an awesome sound for its six. I haven’t had the chance to test how water/splash proof it is, but the battery life is awesome!

title: Sound distorts quickly as volumes rise.
text: Very little bass from this, and sound quality suffered as volume got even moderately high.

title: Excellent speaker for the price
text: I bought this speaker and an Echo Dot (on sale) for around the same price. I like the Tribit MUCH better. Personal opinion, of course. The sound quality is at least as good and it is rechargeable, instead of having to be plugged in. But, the real Echo Dot deal breaker for me is that it is constantly announcing that it is connected to my iPhone. ("Thanks. I know that. And if I don't hear my music, I'll check my settings. Shut up.")

title: My audiophile ears are amazed!
text: I read dozens of reviews and a few comparisons of speakers under $50, and this one really shines, sounding better than name brand speakers well over $50. My primary goal was to find the one with the best sound quality. I am an audiophile now living in a nursing home, so I needed something really tiny, but with sound quality that would not disappoint me, and it had to be very inexpensive. This speaker completely blows me away! The detail! The full spectrum including bass is there without an artificial booster! Listen to some acoustic guitar by Tommie Emanuel so you can appreciate the realism. When used in a small room or personal space (even on your lap), it provides hours of enjoyment. And with a 24 hour battery charge life, I only have to charge it every 3 or 4 days. It will not produce sound as loud as a party boom box or a P.A. system. It is 6" long and has 12 watts powering 2 little 2" drivers and a passive radiator between them that enhances the bass. Given this, it provides adequate volume and fullness of sound for personal listening. And accuracy and realism that continues to bring joy to my audiophile ears! 10/15/20 Update: I dropped the 1st one with the charge cord in it and the micro usb port got damaged to where I couldn't get it to charge. My bad. So, I bought a new one that I am going to be more careful with. WOW! It is upgraded, has Bluetooth 5.0 so it is quicker linking up, and a usb type C charge port which seems sturdier. Still the most flat, blended and yet detailed sound!

title: Good or better than most
text: Big sound, great for the patio while barbecuing or just watching the sunset.

title: Great sound for the price
text: I got this to replace an older amazon basics speaker that stopped holding a charge. I did my research and read reviews. I am not disappointed. This is a low cost, high quality speaker. The sould is full and rich. I primarily use it with my laptop when I am streaming shows. Two minor complaints. (1) If you pause the show and step away for a few minutes, it is quick to time out and turn off, and (2) when I turn it on it sometimes takes 15 to 30 seconds to connect with this weird transition where there is no sound from the computer or the tribit.

title: Bang for your buck!
text: Bass is amazing, great sound quality also! Whenever I show my friends they want one too! A great stereo for a great price. I can’t even tell a difference between this and some other high end speakers

title: Great sound!!!
text: Sounds awesome! Very very impressive for a small speaker. We can take it camping, boating, on the side-by-side, golf cart, outside or anywhere. Very pleased. One of my favorite purchases from Amazon. Highly recommend

title: Great sound, cheap price.
text: I’m using this speaker in a smallish office with a MacBook Air and the size and sound are almost perfect for my application. If I had one complaint it’d be the sound isn’t great at very low volume. Take it up a few notches and that’s where it shines. I only wish it had a carrying case and possibly an AC adapter but that’s asking a bit much and I imagine it’d raise the price considerably.

title: Great little speaker for personal use!
text: Excellent quality, especially for this price! I listen to podcasts and love the voice quality. Music is very good too but don’t expect Bose quality at this price point. For doing work around the house it’s great. Just not a big party.

title: Great sounding speaker for price
text: I wasnt expecting such a great sounding speaker for the price I paid. Highly recommend!

title: Good sounding
text: Just got it yesterday so can't comment on battery life but the sound is amazing, even has base. I was using a Anker speaker before but this is so much better sounding.

title: Really Great speak for the price, worth a lot more.
text: I read a lot of reviews before choosing this speaker. I was still amazed when I turned it on. Incredible full sound and loud. I had it only at medium setting and it filled several rooms. The music sounds full and very clear. And one charge lasts all day. Definitely THE speaker to get. No need to spend more money.

title: This is a great speaker for the price.
text: Excellent clarity with quality sound and range. Very glad I purchased this to listen to music and podcasts.

title: This speaker rocks!!!!!!
text: This speaker rocks!!!!!! It pairs in seconds & sounds great!!!!! It really helps me, because I'm losing hearing in one ear, but at the same time I'm also extremely sensitive to sound & this Tribit gives out such a rich sound, that it doesn't hurt my ear. I can now hear much better on my phone, etc. Love it!!!!!!!

title: Great sound for a little speaker.
text: This speaker performs well and the sound is very good for it's size. The bass actually makes it vibrate. However, I have found that sometimes when I have it connected to charge on my laptop, and it's connected by cable to play also, I hear low beeping when the sound is low. It could be that the connection to my laptop is the problem, though, as it goes away if I unplug the charge cord. The Bluetooth works well and unlike the other Bluetooth small speakers I have, this one can charge and play at the same time. I like the shape and weight of it and the carry strap too. I wish it had an SD card slot like my old one, but for the price, I think it's a good buy.

title: Great sound quality and it’s very loud.
text: This speaker is literally the best speaker I ever owned. It’s way better than the JAM speakers. It’s very loud and the sound quality is legit. It’s half the price of the jam speakers too

title: Great sound
text: For the price, this is a really good portable blue tooth speaker. The sound is crisp and not muddied. Sounds quite lovely. The Speaker is not very large, about the length of a larger model smart phone. Also has connection range between the kitchen and living room in my house, of about 26 or so feet (walked with my phone playing music to the kitchen and speaker continued to read my phone). Comes with a micro USB cable so you can charge it via plug (initial charge of 5 hours). Battery not included, if you want to use them. The “cover” to the USB charger was a little hard to open; you may need a metal object or string nails to unclasp it (minor quibble though). Overall nice design & feel.

title: Great little speaker
text: Great product and sound for the price. We now own two!

title: First 1.5h of use has been great so far.
text: Update 13 months later (March 2022): I am no longer able to charge it. It does that thing we may have all experienced at some point in our lives where the device only charges if I hold the charging cable *just* right. I've tested with several different cables and outlets and I believe that the issue is the actual charging port on the device. Apparently Tribit offers a 1 year warranty. I am 1 month past that. Not sure if it's worth repurchasing the same speakers or if I should go for something more expensive. I just got this today. Will update my review later if needed. It came 60% charged. I was able to use it right out of the box. I played Halsey’s Manic album all the way through twice. I used it on the kitchen counter while cleaning. I also hung it up in the shower (comes with a lanyard) and listened to it there. It has been lovely so far, both in sound quality and in aesthetics. It looks durable and sleek - doesn’t look cheap at all. Really glad to have gotten this quality at this price. Additional notes: - This product feels heavier than I expected. Not so heavy that it’s inconvenient, in my opinion. But I did wonder if my shower hook (one of those vacuum suction cups) would be able to carry it. It did. - No rewind or fast forward buttons. This is done by two and three presses on the play button. This isn’t unusual - my AirPods work that way as well as the accessibility shortcuts on my iPhone. I don’t adore multi tap controls in general. Works fine on this device. Just a matter of preference.

title: Great little Bluetooth speaker
text: Very happy withe the product. The sound quality is good with nice high volume.

title: Not loud enough for large outdoor places
text: I gave 4 stars only because it isn't loud enough for outdoors except in small areas. It's great for doing housework or just listening but you better get the next size up wattage for loudness. It does have a very nice sound quality and it's nice that it is small and lightweight enough I can carry it in my apron pocket when working outside if I need to. All in all a good buy as it was on sale black Friday for $20 cant beat that. I doubt I would pay much more than that tho, maybe $30

title: Decent Sound - Terrible Controls - Deceptive Photo
text: Perhaps someone can explain the point of black buttons on a black device. Anyone? Obviously people do not wear eyeglasses in the shower. 75% of adults use some sort of vision correction. 64% wear glasses (11% wear contacts). Why manufacture a device that will be difficult for two-thirds of consumers to use? The bluetooth connectivity and sound quality become irrelevant when the device is so hard to use. Moreover, this fails to maintain a stable bluetooth connection from an unobstructed source about 20 feet away. As always, your mileage may vary.

title: Amazing!
text: I just received this speaker yesterday, and I am in love! The sound is seriously so good, and the price is amazing. The high, mid, and bass are all really clear. Bluetooth connectivity is really easy, too. I honestly like this speaker just as much as my mom’s Bose bluetooth speaker.

title: A Keeper
text: I saw this reviewed as a budget Bluetooth portable speaker and for 20 bucks I thought I could not go wrong. I grabbed it on a flash sale and it is incredibly powerful and clear. I couldn’t be happier. The size is great if you wanna carry it around as a personal speaker but don’t let the sizeDissuade you from picking up this little gem. I have to say I am pleasantly surprised and it’s a keeper. I liked it so much I went back to grab one for my daughter but the price bumped back up to $30 so I’ll wait till it comes back on sale.

title: Solid sound for the price
text: This is a really solid speaker for the price. Compares pretty well to the lower priced JBLs. My only complaint is not particular to this speaker but the speaker grate cover. If you plan on throwing it in a beach bag sand jams into the metal grate holes. So now I have some sand bouncing around inside and some sand jammed into the holes. Synthetic cloth would have been ideal.

title: Sounds okay but the range is horrible
text: I bought this to listen to while painting. It sounds great for the price. Unfortunately the range is pretty poor. I had to pack it from room to room or it would cut out with just one wall between it and my phone. Even if I have a direct line of sight thru a doorway it still seemed to cutout. Outside if I'm more than 15' away it starts losing signal. I ended up just having to sit my phone next to it. Sounds good and battery life is decent, but next time I'll look for one with better range.

title: Oh yeah Daddy likes

title: A TINY MARVEL!
text: I've been using this Tribit speaker for a good few weeks now. I was pleasantly surprised by how heavy it was when I got it all unwrapped and unboxed. I'm old, so I still subscribe to the idea that if it's heavy, (it doesn't matter what "it" is) it's either expensive or of fine quality or both. Well the Tribit certainly wasn't expensive. My last Bluetooth speaker was very inexpensive, the sound was mediocre at best and it finally gave up the ghost by refusing to charge. I surmised that the repair charge would be more than it was worth so now I have a small white paperweight. The Tribit is the replacement and there is no comparison. Stunning sound from such a small device and just the right amount of bass. I suppose well balanced would be the words to use. It is definitely of fine quality. I'm delighted with my purchase and can't recommend it highly enough.

title: Will pair with only one device at a time; sounds horrible
text: In full disclosure, I must admit that I miss my Bose Bluetooth speaker. Their acoustics are impeccable. The "Tribit XSound Go Bluetooth Speakers" only cost a fraction of my Bose speaker. I first purchased the "DOSS Touch Wireless Bluetooth" which is in the same price range; I returned that product because it lacked bass and was unimpressive overall. The Tribit, however, has plenty of bass for such a small speaker. Ironically, the problem that I have is the treble! I think it is an inherent problem with smaller speakers and not this particular device. I have installed an equalizer on my computer which mitigates some of the problems and makes the speaker sound very acceptable. The pros: • The speaker is loud! It is perfect for a jam session in your bedroom. I'm not sure it is suitable for large or multi rooms. • The quality is good, and the speaker looks like a million bucks. • It has an excellent microphone that works well with phone calls and even to interact with Siri or Cortana. • The Play button allows one to answer, reject or end a call. It also can play or pause a song. Finally, it allows you to skip a music track forward or backward. The cons: • While the bass is fairly impressive, the treble is slightly overriding. • The battery does not nearly last for 24 hours if you like to blast music as I do • The speaker can only be paired to one device at a time. If you are listening to music on the computer and the phone tries to connect, the speaker will sometimes disconnect from all devices. The speaker does have an av input one could connect to the computer but obviously, the speaker would no longer be completely portable. This could be a deal breaker for many. After comparing this speaker with others in its price range, I realize that this speaker has such poor sound quality that I could never recommend it to anyone.

I have the Tribit attached to the monitor via the AUX input (as my display does not have internal speakers). I should say the Tribit's sound is superior to any computer monitor (with internal speakers) or low end TV I've encountered to-date. I have not decide whether to buy a second Tribit for the full stereo experience (they can be paired so one speaker becomes the left-hand-side and the other the right-hand-side). May be overkill for the bath experience! You do need to provide your own usb-c charger but like most people, I suspect, I had several lying around the house. For portable use I might find the 5 hour recharge time to be slow (my phone with a similar size battery does a fast-charge in under an hour). Overall, the ergonomics, simplicity and sound quality make this a good buy. I will probably buy another for my workshop as I like background music (connected by bluetooth to my phone). title: Balanced sound for jazz; switching sources is a bit of a pain
text: After a lot of research on the many top contenders for best blue tooth speaker, I answered the question this way - how large did I want the device to be in my life. Since I have a component based hi-fi system and wasn't looking to compete with it, the answer was 'not large'. So that narrowed down the choices to a few in the price range of the Tribit. A couple of youtube videos helped in which the Xsound Go sounded less tinny and shrill than the others. I listen mostly to jazz in various formats and have to say it's sound has been balanced for the purpose. Since neither my iPhone 6SE and Lenovo T470S have great sound, the Xsound Go does the job which is provides much more listening pleasure out of these two sources. Pairing it to the iPhone took less than 5 seconds. Pairing it to the Lenovo laptop after that proved to be more of a puzzle, it would simply not see the device. Prompt customer service assistance from Tribit helped me figure it out. Once paired to a source, it cannot be paired to a second source (even if the first one has it's bluetooth turned off) unless you reset the Xsound Go. The way to do that is to turn it on and press the (-) and (+) buttons together for 5 seconds until you hear it beep. Then turn bluetooth on at the second source and search for / pair it. Do the reverse to get it paired back to the first source, but you may have to 'forget' the device first and re-pair it fresh. Fortunately I won't have to do it often, but it made me realize that a bluetooth speaker than can pair two devices at one time is a real convenience.

Compared to the Clip 4, its carabiner is junk (hard to use and too small and fiddly) and it does not get as loud (important for my application). Also, the music does not sound as good (quality of music was not my main concern). So, the pros for the Clip 4 are that the carabiner is very nice, large, and integrated into the casing. And it gets noticeably louder, which is a big deal for me. The quality of music is also noticeably better than the $18.99 no-name, so many will want the Clip4 over el-cheapo. Also, the Clip4 looks very nice (not super important, but I'm not complaining about that). If you are geeky, you might enjoy having a Aux port on the no-name as it frees you from using Bluetooth, which can bring its own problems. To me, the Clip4, as $80 retail, it way too expensive. Even at $50, which is what I paid, it is still way overpriced by my standards. I think $30 is a fair price for this thing. Since I just received the speaker, I can’t review the battery life yet. If I can, i will edit the review. As for Bluetooth distance, it is better than expected. title: Mostly an improvement over JLB Clip 3, but with an annoying step back
text: The Clip 4 is a good improvement over Clip 3, except with one annoying step back. Pros: The design is more slender and less circular, which gives it a bit more downward directional gravity when hanging from the clip. The actual clip mechanism itself seems sturdier, and larger too. My Clip 3's clip broke within a few weeks, and my Clip 4's clip is still going strong after a few months. The overall aesthetic is more appealingly stylish. The grey option has a cool 90s vibe that I really dig. The bluetooth signal/range seems a bit better, and the sound quality seems better. Cons: The Clip 3 power/bluetooth buttons were caved into the side of the speaker, which made it next to impossible for those buttons to be accidentally pressed. The Clip 4, unfortunately, decided to make those buttons just like every other button on the speaker (raised above the surface); which, unfortunately, means it's a LOT easier to accidentally bump the power button and unintentionally turn off the unit. And it happens. A lot. Overall, I like the Clip 4 more than the Clip 3, though only marginally (mainly because of the aggravating power button design). Hopefully they keep all the new improvements and fix the power button when they come out with the Clip 5.

Bottom line, when you go to take a shower in the morning, you unplug it and put it in the shower, only to discover that it, in fact, did not charge overnight, and no sound comes out. The battery lasts for something like 8 hours, so that means that either you're diligent about turning it off or you have to charge it every day. It's a shame that Oontz wasn't willing to spend the extra $.05 or so to get a better jack for the power connection. I was fully charging it after I used it and then after a couple of days of being off, the speaker would need to be fully charged again before I can use it. I reached out to the company because I thought surely this unit had a defective battery. The company confirmed what I am experiencing. "It seems like the problem is that the speakers were kept and not used for several days and gets drained too fast when used again. Please know that even if the speaker is not used, it's battery would still be consumed but in a small fraction. This means, the fully charged battery from 2 days ago will not have the same amount of battery if used after 2 days even though you didn't turn it on along those days. It's a bit complicated but what's clear is that batteries still drain even if not used but only in small percentage. Hope this answers your question!"

But the Oontz does it the right way, allowing you to step up or down the volume quickly as needed without having to pull out your phone, go to the app playing the audio, etc, in order to change the volume. I can see a use case for both styles/methods, since most of the time I just set the Bluetooth speaker at max and control from the phone, but I like and prefer this control setup, it's quicker when I need it to be. I have trouble understanding speech if there's too much background noise, so this control scheme is way better for me. With the Oontz if my wife says something to me that I miss when I'm rocking out, I can silence or at least turn it down to a low enough volume to have her repeat it in like 1 second, vs 5-10 seconds or even longer (a relative ETERNITY. Sit silent for 10 seconds before responding while having a conversation with someone and you'll see, it's very sub-optimal, ruins the rhythm of the conversation, and causes them to contemplate how much more conversations are going to suck as I get older and my hearing gets worse) with the long-press volume control method. And at $16, it's a slam dunk, and would make a great gift. Thanks Oontz!

title: Exceeded my expectations
text: After reading reviews on the Oontz Angle Solo and several other competing speakers, based on reviews, I settled on the Oontz (BTW, I bought it on Amazon at a super sale price). I was looking to replace an early-model Bluetooth mini speaker from another manufacturer that I used for travel. That speaker was unreliable in its Bluetooth connection, the controls were wacky, the soft-touch finish had become sticky and, most importantly, it just didn’t sound good. After having traveled with the Oontz Angle Solo for 11 days, I’m ready to add my review to the others. For a speaker I intended to use for travel, this one ticked all my boxes: 1) The small size is perfect; 2) The case is rigid and sturdy enough that I’m not concerned it will get crushed or broken—very solid construction; 3) Bluetooth connection with my phone is consistent and reliable—turn it on and it connects right away and stays connected across the room; 4) The controls are straightforward and easy to understand; and 5) The sound is clear with good overall tone, reasonable bass for a speaker this size and it can play pretty loud. [I worked in the home audio industry for many years and I think I can most assuredly attest that this is a good and good-sounding product considering its price and size. I have other speakers for serious listening]. Plus it can be paired with another Oontz speaker for left-right stereo or dual speaker sound. I have not yet tried the speakerphone feature. For what I paid, it would be hard to beat the Angle Solo. I like it so much that when I saw the Oontz Angle 3 reduced on Amazon, I bought one. I intend to use it as the left speaker (control speaker) with the Angle Solo as the right at my desk. I’m thinking the extra bass from the larger Angle 3 will enhance the stereo sound. I’ll report on this in a review of the Angle 3.

title: Better in my car than its installed speakers
text: I have gone through many Bluetooth speakers and had yet to listen to one that had such depth of sound as this Bose SoundLink Revolve. I know it's not the first Bose SoundLink Bluetooth speaker, but it's my first and it blows away all the others that gather dust around here. Visually similar to my Amazon Echo, I had to let Alexa know that she has a competitor in my home but reassured her that she is still loved. I can't talk to this Bose, but each time I turn it on, a generated female voice alerts me to the battery life remaining and what device it's pairing with. Setup took only a minute, the manual is only a few words and diagrams, and after a full battery charge, it's still going after daily use for what seems like dozens of hours. I'm serious, I have not plugged it back in yet because I want to see what happens when the battery nears death. I did not want to wait to write this review because I'm so impressed with the audio that is generated from this little speaker that can also withstand being carried outside without harm. Of course, I'm not willing to test it in the rain, but have to say that my neighbors could not believe the music was coming from this little black speaker.

title: Bose Sound in a sleek 360 degree bundle of joy

As you unpack this little 2 pound wonder, you find the charging cord and charger and instructions. First thing I did, was plug this baby into an outlet and start charging it up. Before you use it, download the Bose Connect app for iPhone or android app, which will unlock the pairing feature and access future updates. You will see the charge on the speaker on the very top by the on off button. On the top of the speaker, you will see a Bluetooth pairing button and symbols to show if it is connected or not. One charge will yield about 12 hours of play time. On the top, you will see the speaker also has NFC capability. You will also see buttons for volume. The sound is what you would expect from Bose. Loud, clear and lots of bass. Oh, one more thing, the speaker is water resistant so you can have it outside. This was very easy connect to my iPhone.

title: Just tried this out at a big box store before purchasing here...
text: I compared the Revolve with the Soundlink Color II--from low volume to high across jazz, hip hop, classic rock, and electronic. I've owned Bose for over a decade--all wired speakers. And I kept buying Bose because I like the warm, full-bodied, balanced sound. However, I want to get away from wires so have been looking into BT speakers. After bad luck with Anker's much-praised Soundcore Motion+ speakers (stereo BT connection), I thought I'd have better luck with a higher quality brand. No such luck. The Soundlink Color II sounded, to me, like a toy. Loud, yes, but 2-dimensional and astringent. The Revolve was a definite step up from the Soundlink Color II, but compared to my Companion MusicMonitor series, the Revolve lacked nuance and warmth. I'm not paying MORE for worse sound quality AND all the BT connection issues others report and I've had with most of my BT speakers/headphones. Worse yet, when the battery on these BT speakers dies, there's no easy way to replace it. My MusicMonitors are STILL working great over a decade after I bought them. And no BT speaker I've tried comes close to the MusicMonitor wired speakers in a small (300 sf) space. I took the MusicMonitors with me overseas on my last long-term work assignment. Baggage workers damaged them (small dent on one of the speakers' metal grill). But the sound quality, to me, remains unmarred. That's reliability. Others have suggested that BT speakers are great for convenience and NOISE, but not sound quality. So, they argue, you should save money on "quality" BT speakers and just go for reliability, ease of connection, and economy. I'm still looking for an economical pair of BT speakers for white noise, but I'll be sticking with wired speakers for sound quality. Two stars for the Revolve's 360-degree soundstage. Too bad I didn't like the sound quality enough to part with $200 + tax.

title: The Bose Quality I’ve come to expect
text: I purchased this speaker to use primarily for educational presentations. For years a had a OONTZ Angle, which was fine, but did not have the power and projection needed for a hotel-type break out room where there are 30 or so in attendance. I wanted Bluetooth capability AND also the ability to hard-wire in with a 3.5mm sound cord (sold separately). I also purchased the charging dock and have only used that once. The sound is fantastic. Used it today in a breakout session and everyone heard the video I was playing. CONS - it is a little tricky to figure out the BT and the Aux Power. I tested it at home to make sure both worked, but it took a while to get it off of BT and toggle over to Aux. You have to tap on the buttons very quickly. I easily paired it with my iPad and the voice commands will tell you when it is paired and with what device. Then I tried a corded connection with an Mac Book Pro - it wanted to stay on BT! I had to turn BT off of my iPad and then it allowed me to jump on to what they call the USB connection, although that was really the 3.5mm. Once plugged and that aux button is lit, I received no sound. I found out later that I had to tap it one more time and then it played fine. So the instructions that come with it aren’t the best, so I advise you to do a little trial and error practicing first. Even though this was an issue, I consider it a “beginner” issue and did not penalize the review. Now I know what to do going forward. The 3.5mm option is very important to me. For presenters, sometimes you are asked to use the laptop that is already set up. Today was such a case, the BT was turned off on the Dell laptop. The owner was not around, I couldn’t get the speaker and the laptop to complete a BT handshake, so I did a corded connection and it worked perfectly after I figured out the tapping sequence! Bose sound was incredible. This is a sturdy speaker, about the size of an “Alexa” speaker. I am very pleased with the purchase.

title: Good value for my intended purpose
text: The primary purpose of this speaker is to have something louder than my phone in the shower, around the pool, or at the beach. For the price, it is a good solution. Battery life and portability appear excellent. Very easy to connect and it can get fairly loud without significant distortion. In terms of tonal quality it’s not bad. Very mid-range heavy. I typically find myself using an in-app EQ to boost the highs to get more clarity. It’s a small speaker so don’t expect any bass. At the beach with constant ambient noise, this works. Biggest drawback is poor Bluetooth reception. 10-15ft and it starts dropping out badly and it’s even worse if your body is in between the phone and the speaker. I don’t have a big pool but i can’t be on one side with my iPhone 11Pro and have a clear, consistent connection to the speaker. If Bluetooth reception were stronger, this would be 5-stars for value. But again, for having a little music while sitting with a friend at the beach, it works well enough. For the price, I’d recommend it as a good value.
