title: A+ for customer service!!
text: The first speaker I received came defective. It wouldn’t hold a charge and refused to turn on. I decided to contact the seller directly via email, and I expressed my concerns to them. Without hesitation, the seller offered to send me out a replacement device at no cost to me. They also replied in a timely fashion, and the replacement device arrived very quickly. Great customer service! Now for the device itself: It is very loud. Much louder than I expected, which is awesome. The sound quality itself is very good as well. Clear sounding music. It is very easy to operate and to pair via Bluetooth. The new device holds a charge for a long time, and I haven’t seemed to have any issues. I want to buy another so I can pair both of them together and have even louder sound. Now for my one complaint: Even though this device is advertised as “waterproof”, take that lightly. If you continue reading in the description, it states that is is more water-resistant than anything. I am happy I read that before using the device, as I assumed when I first bought it that I could use it in the shower. To cut the risk of ruining the device, I hang it outside of the shower where it is in reach in case I want to change what I’m listening to, but that way it’s safe from possible damage. Overall, I am beyond pleased with the device, and more importantly the seller. If you have a problem, try communicating as it can get you very far. Stuff happens. Sometimes things come defective. It’s how it’s handled that matters. I think this speaker is way above the other ones I’ve tried.

title: You can do better
text: This thing fell apart one piece at a time. First, the suction cup was so ill-fitting to the device that it broke. We emailed the company for a replacement suction cup but it never came. Next, it uses a flimsy proprietary charging plug which stopped working unless bent to just the right spot. Ultimately because it had no suction cup it got too wet in the shower and died completely. It has an absolutely obnoxious beep when the battery is getting low -- unrelenting and every few seconds. Completely unnecessary. It was good for a year then it slowly fell apart. Sometimes you get what you pay for and I'm not sure if that's even the case with this product. I'll be getting something that is a little more rugged for the bathroom. UPDATE: The company swiftly addressed my review and sent a replacement. It appears they recognized the charger as an issue and changed it to a USB connection versus the poor proprietary design. Also improved is the button feel and the alert sounds (although still extremely pervasive and obnoxious with constant beeping when battery is low). Unfortunately, the suction cup failed after the second use and the device fell about four feet into the tub and the unit broke completely. Something with a suction cup design absolutely needs to survive an average fall without having pieces rattle around internally. I have emailed the company to zero response.

text: This is a great product. It was a bit difficult to get the plastic box around it open, and it left my hand a little scratched. The packaging looked very nice. It will glow red until it is fully charged. It was easy to turn on and pair with my phone. The suction cup appears strong and durable. Only complaint about the suction cup, is it seems like it should hold the product a little bit closer to the wall. Makes it look like it might fall, despite it actually having a very tight suction to the wall. The sound quality is fantastic. And the volume goes from very soft to very loud. It does not seem to distort the sound as it gets louder. I wish that it had separate volume buttons from the forward and back buttons. It was a little bit tricky to realize how long you had to push the power button to get it to turn off but once you get used to the difference of the noise it makes it helps you to understand. There are two tones but the power button will make, one is to pair it with your phone and the other is the noise it makes when it is powering down. text: [[ASIN:B00MITLPX2 SoundBot SB571 Bluetooth Wireless Speaker 12W Output HD Bass 40mm Dual Driver Portable Speakerphone for 12Hr Enhanced Music Streaming & HandsFree Calling, Built-in Mic, 3.5mm Line-In]] I was in the market for a decent bluetooth wireless speaker for light use in the office or in the bathroom and wasn't expecting a whole lot for 20 dollar bluetooth speaker but I was extremely impressed by the sound quality! The speakers were surprisingly loud but sound quality was not affected at all by the volume. For the price point on these speakers, these speakers are a steal! The only thing that I don't like is the loud female voice that announces (screams) the status of the speakers whether it's paring or connecting. Also, when you've maxed out the volume or turned the volume all the way down, theres's this extremely loud beeping noise that lets you know that you're at the end of the volume range. It isn't a major deal when you've maxed out the volume but when you're trying to lower the volume to a lower volume but get surprised by this loud high pitch noise, it sorta defeats the purpose. Other than those minor issues, I would totally recommend these speakers to anyone looking for a good bluetooth wireless speaker without the spending a pretty penny for it.

title: Really good, with only minor issues.
text: Excellent product. It's perfectly waterproof and it has a nice volume (the volume control is separate from the device you link it to). I use it every day when taking a shower. The battery seems to last pretty long too. It's also much sturdier than it looks. I lost count of how many times it dropped to the floor because I didn't stick it carefully to the wall, and yet it not only hasn't broken, but it has nary a scratch. It does have a couple of minor issues, though. There's a bit of a delay between the speaker and the device. This isn't really noticeable when you're just listening to music, but if you're doing any other activity (like playing a game) it'll be more evident. There's also a small delay for the sound to start when pressing the "Next" button, so when you click on it the next song will start one or two seconds in. Also, for some reason the "Previous" and "Next" buttons don't work all the time. I don't know if this is a problem with the speaker or some compatibility issue with my phone or the audio app I'm using, though. Overall, still really satisfied with the speaker. It's worth much more than its actual price.

title: Not appropriate for husbands.
text: I purchased this because I believed its sound would overpower road noise and because the reviewers have it at 4+ stars. On the plus side: I have been able to get good volume and quality sound from this unit at various times. The microphone seems to work well. The trouble is with the connection. Bluetooth hasn't connected at all. And when connected with the provided 3.5mm cord it makes a terrible static sound. So, either the company threw in a cheap connector cord, or the unit itself is bad. Since I paid for it I'm going to get another cord but I'm a bit miffed that I have to do this when it should work fine right out of the box. Another complaint: a female voice says "pairing" when the unit is linking up with the source. And it doesn't sound like "pairing," it sounds more like "bear ring," or even worse "baring" as in taking off one's clothes! The first time I use it to call my wife (hands free in the car) it said this and my wife asked, "Who's that?" Sheesh! Is this what I need?? A female voice?! Why not an innocuous beep or something?? Also, the next time I used it, it interrupted my call to my mother twice by saying "pairing" and I had to explain to her what that sound was. I'm not sure why it even bothers saying "pairing" when it's connected directly to the source. Not a deal-breaker per se, but irritating. I'm giving two stars and not one because I still hope that the company merely gave me a bad electrical cord but made a decent speaker. We'll see. Post-Script: I hate giving bad reviews! The two problems I described don't seem like insurmountable issues: (1) make sure the connector cord isn't a lowball construct and (2) make sure an audio indicator doesn't interfere with the use of the product (and doesn't sound like a robotic streetwalker). I bet the company which makes this product could fix these idiosyncrasies with minimal effort.

title: Love this thing.
text: I absolutely love this product. Every time I shower and its never let me down. Holds a good charge and totally water resistant.

title: This is a very good unit for the price
text: This is a very good unit for the price. I am able to connect all my devices to it (iPhone, iPad & MacBook Pro) without any issues. Battery life is good, and sound is decent. Unfortunately, occasionally the unit freezes up and I get a horrible continuous loud noise. I can not turn off the unit or lower the volume. I just have to wrap it in a towel, to deaden the sound, and hide it in a remote section of the house until the battery dies. Unfortunately, this had taken up to six hours. Which, in a way, is a nice testament to how long the battery can last. Once charged up, the unit is back to useability again. For the price, the unit is hard to beat. It lives in the shower and has shown no sign of any issues being drenched every day.

title: Stopped working after a month
text: This worked fine for what I needed it for, but a little over a month after I got it now it keeps giving me a dial tone? Im just using it to play music, not make calls and there are no incoming calls, but every few seconds the music stops and there is a dial tone so now it’s now usable and of course it’s just days after the return/exchange window has closed

title: Works amazing outdoors

Impressed with playback and the many features of the speaker. It came with a micro usb and aux cable, which is handy. Speaker is easily portable and lightweight, small enough to fit just about anywhere.

The ONLY thing I wish, which it's not even a complaint, was that the charge lasted longer. It actually lasts quite a bit of time (hours at least) but I am just a lazy person and hate having to recharge it. Haha. I would buy this product over and over again. I researched speakers forever because I wanted a decent one but didn't want to shell out a ton of money especially when I wasn't sure how well it was going to work and I am SO GLAD I chose this one. Honestly, I would probably have even paid more for it because I love it so much. I love my laptop but it's sometimes I wish it was louder so I mostly use this speaker when I watch movies and listen to music on my laptop and it's perfect for that. 10/10 would buy again.

title: Great Sound - Update 11/6/2016
text: Okay speaker for around $20. Sound is impressive and this small speaker can get loud. It does distort at higher volume levels and the speakerphone is pretty bad. We bought it for use in the bathroom so we don't need the loud volumes or speakerphone ability so it works great for us. It does pair with multiple devices, but you can only listen to one device at a time. The battery life is great and we have only charged it twice in the last month and we use the speaker daily. Range is not that great, when I first tested it out, if i moved my phone at all, I would get drops and static and my phone was less then a foot away (the speaker did have a full charge). It does sound really good for an inexpensive speaker. You can even hear many lower bass tones, you just can't feel them. The speaker does provide a nice full sound and is a nice upgrade from the small 5 watt speaker we were using previously. Update 10/3/2016: Customer service contacted me and had me send in the defective product. We got the second speaker last week and it is just as bad as the first one. No range, frequent drops of the signal and the battery seems worse then the previous one. I am changing my rating to 1 star and hopefully customer service will contact me and give me a refund for a terrible product. Update 11/6/2016: The company sent me a third speaker and I am happy to say this one works fine. I am upgrading my review from 1 star to 3 stars for their customer service and finally getting me a speaker that works correctly.

Hers cost a lot more, but the sound quality is the same. Also, this is a bit smaller than her Sony, but the sound is big. You're not going to get the sound of a home stereo system, but it will fill any bedroom or desk area with more sound than you need. Good bass, good vocal clarity, good price.

title: This is a good speaker.
text: My son was looking for a new Bluetooth speaker and I went to several stores looking at them and just was not happy with the high prices they were looking for and the minimal selection they offered. A quick search led me to the sound bot Bluetooth speaker. We ordered the speaker and it arrives quickly. It was packaged well and arrived safe and secure. My son was excited and plugged it in quickly to ensure it was fully charged. It really puts out a nice quality sound with no feedback and he can even turn the volume up quite a bit as kids do. He has now been using his soundbot for a little while and has had no problems at all. It holds a charge for a good long time and he is very happy with this purchase. I was very happy with the price when you take into consideration the speaker and the time it will hold the charge in comparison to the items that were available when I went to stores. I would definitely purchase this item again if I had the need and I would definitely recommend this soundbot speaker to others.

I can still hear the music while in the shower with the exhaust fan on without cranking the volume up loud enough to disturb my neighbors, and still leave my phone in the bedroom charging. No, I can't use the call feature while in the shower, but I really don't see an urgent need to talk on the phone whilst bathing. I can see using this in the kitchen or outside while gardening. I'd like to see how it works as a hands free phone speaker/mic in the car... my parents have vehicles that do not have the feature and this is simple enough they may be able to use it.

title: Excellent Budget Speaker!
text: We bought this as a Christmas gift for our teen daughter. She in a phase where she has LED lighting all throughout her bedroom and behind her bed. I noticed this on sale and decided to try it (she has been "borrowing" a similarly sized BT speaker of mine for months). I figured with the neat lighting effect on this it would be a win-win and I could finally have mine back. Well it worked great! I actually unboxed the speaker to test it before gifting it and everything checks out. It has decent sound performance, bass-boost enhancement (via button on top), and controls on top including changing the light effect. I think DOSS did a great job with this product and it checks all the boxes for a solid budget-friendly small BT speaker. It's also super easy to connect and seems to have decent battery life judging by the fact I hear it almost constantly every evening :). Plus, it goes really well with the vibe of her room and she absolutely loves it! I would highly recommend this product! Update 7/19/21: The charging port ended up bent on this a couple of months ago. My teen might have been rough on it and I don't consider it to be any fault of DOSS. However, I purchased the 24W tubular-style DOSS portable speaker and it did not live up to expectations. If you are considering both speakers I would recommend this one!

title: Quality control problems
text: I am not interested in the gimmicky lights which probably add to the cost. I guess party people enjoy them. The sound on this is ok. It makes the sound coming from my Echo Show less boomy. I listen to music, podcasts and my Audible and Kindle books on this. For the books, I really find the sound much better without all the bass from the Echo. I had to send the speaker back because I kept getting the sound of telephone busy signals every few minutes. This does not happen with my UE Boombox when connected. The other problem was that when I went to raise the volume with the + button it would advance the music to the next music selection instead of raising the volume. My Tribit got tossed in the trash because it would no longer hold a charge after a few months. I didn’t bother calling them. I usually return things to Amazon within the 30 day warrantee. I probably should not have tossed it but I got angry that it stopped working so quickly. So now I will continue my search for a hard working decent sounding Bluetooth wireless speaker. I don’t expect concert hall quality for under $100 but I do expect something well made and that will not have problems after a couple of months.

title: Decent sound box, great seller
text: This fits the bill for what I wanted. But I wish there was a way to cut the light sound feature off Good sound quality and good battery life. And the overall quality is good as well But I would give the company that sells this through Amazon an A+ Five Stars for customer service. My model died after 7 months. There is a one year warranty, and after contacting the company by email they list with the sellers information, telling them about the problem- (would no longer take a charge-) and sending a short video as per their request, they promptly sent me a brand new one. They were quick, courteous and kept me informed all along the way! Now I have a new one at no cost to me. Thank you, Wonders- Tech!

title: Enjoyable Sound - Surprising Service - Functioning Party Speakers!
text: *Update* Service Team responded very fast with firmware to fix. Still not sure if I can mix and match and use either speaker at will but until I need to I won't. The sound is good. There is a much better review, pretty much the bass boost is a gimmick. Leaving it off provides a more natural sound without lossy compression. Haven't tried BT calling but it answered the one time I was connected. All in all, enjoyable audio. Perfect for setup teardown at tradeshows. That's what I use these for. AV industry installation/servicing. I love the stereo pair, brings a much needed breadth solo BT speakers couldn't hope to provide alone. Was skeptical on the sync but it's spot on. Bonus* My Samsung S9 just rolled out Dual Audio for BT so if you want to preserve the Stereo channels per both speakers you can do that too! Thank you Doss for the direct responses and the fully functioning speakers again! Never sent these back, Doss helped me out directly with excellent service. 5-Stars would come with an improved DAC. You can tell a lot of compression happens at the lower volume levels. 5-Stars would also come if I was confident in this current pairing to stick. Maybe I'll update again. How about a Stereo Pair Sub?? Huh Doss? What do you think? It'd be silly but I bet it'd sell. Accessory Subwoofer!

title: Great customer service

Sound quality is really muffled; it's a little less so without the bass boost, but then is tinny. Best little bluetooth speaker I've found is the Skullcandy Shrapnel.

title: Initial impression... Fantastic sound and appears to be very well built
text: I've been using a Doss DS-1168 Bluetooth speaker for 8 years or so , in my opinion, it proved itself to be a quality product. So I wanted another Doss Bluetooth speaker... and I'm not disappointed. I immediately connected it to my cellphone and it connected without any fuss, and then I connected it to my Asus Zenbook notebook computer, again, without fuss. Sound is incredible. If I had a complaint, it would be that there doesn't seem to be a way to turn off the mood lights on the front. If we listen to sleepy time music in bed, we really don't want disco lights lighting up the room. --- EDIT... you can turn off the rhythmic lights by holding down the Extra Bass button for 3 seconds... this is not noted in the User Manual.

title: Awesome Little Speaker with Big Sound
text: I am always leery of purchasing low priced Bluetooth speakers as that route in the past has burned me with tinny sounding speakers that aren't suitable for listening to anything but an audio book, if that. I was looking for something small and powerful that was wireless for my bathroom to replace a tower speaker that was always in the way and also had an unsightly cord draped across the wall. I am absolutely thrilled with the quality of this speaker. The sound is vibrant and it carries rich bass tones. It will never pack the punch of a 200w PA speaker, but it suffices for a small area. My bathroom is 15' x 10' and it it more than ample to fill the space with sound. I only use it a few times a week for about 30 minutes at a time. Thus far it has remained charged for 3 weeks without a charge. I am certain with more use it would require more frequent charging, but in my experience it is a great addition to my home and I would buy another if the need arose. I spent hours researching and looking for the right output wattage. If you are on the fence about it, researching and reading reviews, bite the bullet and order this thing. You won't be disappointed!

title: It's OK

title: Update. Woah......

I listen to traditional 80s country mostly so these speakers have not been pounded by heavy bass. Kind of a let down as I was really excited about these when I first got them (one for me and one for my son). ............ After contacting support they sent me a new one!!! GREAT people. OK I admit it, I was a bit tipsy when I ordered this. I have been using my Bose Acustamass radio thingie for a bluetooth speaker for a long time and it has crapped out. Bose has shrugged their shoulders on my $600.00 radeo.. Too bad , so sad.... So having read the reviews on this I gave it a try and WOW am I impressed. I am a Bruno Mars, Salsa, Zumba king of guy and the horns, drums, percussion of these speakers is amazing!!! WAY the hell better than my Bose unit and way more acomodating space wise. i put the original unit in the kitchen and will order another for my master bath. This is amazing sound for fifty bucks. AMAZING. WAY better then my Bose unit. The frequency range on this is amazing and the build is solid, tight and quality. I am so impressed I can't even tell ya! Having said this first and foremost to all potential buyers of this product, the information I'm conveying here is honest, and as a consumer who paid a decent amount of money for these speakers expects to receive what is being advertised about this product. So, if bettery life is important to you, and perhaps a top concern in your buying decission, then take from this review, and all other reviews, all pros and cons about this product in order to help you make the best buying decission possible. Now, other than the poor battery life I'm experiencing with my speakers (I did purchase a pair for stereo sound) is that these speakers sound really great, and the build quality seems to be very good. These things are pretty solid, and they shipped very fast, and were packaged extremely well. Perhaps my speakers regarding the battery life may be defective units, and your purchase might perfectly well give you near or exactly 20 hours of usage. Best of luck in your search for bluetooh wireless speakers.

title: My Kid Loves It
text: When moving into our new house a few months ago, I found an old Jambox and synced it with my phone to let my toddler carry around and listen to music. As an 18 month old she dropped it half a dozen times in a week, and the micro usb connection stopped working. So for Christmas we bought her the DOSS Soundbox. It's hold up super well. She loves carrying it around the house and yard dancing and looking at the flashing light. She still drops it all the time, but this one has taken the beating much better. The only knock I have on it is that the bluetooth range isn't great. It starts to get wonky sounding (skipping and staticky) if I am more than about 10' from the speaker, and disconnects entirely at about 20', and it's worse if the connection has to travel through a wall.

title: Works fine if you want one. Pairing system is absolute crap

text: Tried to like their Motion Plus, and it was very good sounding BUT, lacked any "deep" bass. AND for the price I thought I could do better, and I DID. The Soundcore Motion Boom was only marginally bigger but the amount of deeper bass was evident. If you're technically inclined, the bass isn't really deep but has a large "hump" at around 100Hz, and rolls off sharply at about 80Hz. But for a portable speaker that's a bit bigger than a large sub-sandwich, the bass is impressive none the less. Play time was at an impressive 24+hrs, as I had the opportunity to really work it out over a period of a few days initially. Haven't really tried to torture it with rain/weather but that really isn't necessary, is it? If you want something compact with big sound, check it out and crank your music!

As loud as the bass is, for larger spaces at higher volumes you do have to drop the bass boost to avoid distortion. Use speaker placement in corners to help overcome this limitation. This has more than enough volume to fill a 4,000 sq ft room I tested it in. I am really tempted at picking up a second one while the sale price is still in effect for full stereo separation using the pairing mode. A full 10 amp hour battery will keep this running long enough and gives you USB for charging your other small USB powered devices, cell phone, tablet etc. Bottom line if you are a bass head on a budget, buying this is a no brainer! The only thing Anker needs to do to make this more perfect is add a couple tweeters for improved high end response/clarity and a 3.5mm input port.

title: Really great sound for the price. A couple of things kept me from giving it five stars though.
text: I’ve had this for three months now, and here are my thoughts. First off, this sounds amazing! I love Anker products. I have used their keyboards, charging cables, wall chargers, and headphones. I’ve had my, Anker Soundcore Life 2 Neo headphones, for almost three years now. I’m pretty picky about sound quality, but also on a bit of a budget. Back in 2020, my husband got me the headphones, which I thought I would keep for a few months, and replace with something better. Three years later, and I’m still happy with them, so I thought, i’ve been happy with all of my other purchases from this company, especially my headphones, this has great reviews, so why not take a chance on this speaker? Oh. It was on sale too! That also helped me decide. Last week was the Super Bowl, and my husband and I listened to the game on the speaker. It sounded great! I listen to a wide variety of music, and so far, this speaker has performed pretty well. I’m also surprised at how long the battery lasts in this thing. Now, here are a couple of things that I don’t like about this speaker. First of all, unlike with the headphones that I have, where you can skip backwards and forwards through the tracks, you’re not able to do this with the speaker. That’s kind of inconvenient if my phone is in a different room, and I’d like to skip a track or something. The only other complaint that I have about this speaker is, I wish that it was easier to adjust the sound, and the equalizer. I wish that there were buttons to do it on the speakers, or Sliders that were easier to use with voiceover through the app. I am totally blind, and if you don’t like the presets, it’s kind of hard to get it adjusted just right. Thanks to the reviewer who posted a diagram of how it should be adjusted for optimum sound, my husband, who is cited, was able to do it for me through the app. Overall, I am very pleased with this speaker. I’m glad I didn’t waste big money on a Bose. My daughter has one, and I think this little speaker sounds better than her way more expensive one.

text: Okay, so let me start with the positives: Battery life? Excellent. I charged it once when I bought it, and about 15 total hours of use later, still going strong. Connectivity? I have very little faith in suction cups, but slap this bad boy on a wet wall and it won't move. Now for the one downside, the reason I docked a star. Sound quality. For this price point, I expected better. Bass is not a replacement for quality. It sounds a bit tinny, and while much louder than my Google Pixel 4a, the sound quality isn't any better. I'd even say it's a bit worse. It's good enough quality to listen to in the shower I suppose, but I'd gladly use this speaker all the time if it sounded better. And while it is waterproof and I held it under the shower to test this, getting it wet makes the sound even worse. It won't damage the speaker, but it will hurt the sound quality until it dries out. The water droplets make it sound a bit muffled and vibrato-y. Overall, I'd say I'm happy with it for what I paid through a lightning deal, but I wouldn't have been happy to pay full price; I would have returned it, honestly.

title: Pairs Perfectly With Nvidia Shield
text: This speaker is not going to blow anyone away with robust bass and crystal high notes but it is well designed. It sounds better when it has its back to a wall. This is advertised as waterproof in contrast to water resistant. It has a snug plug over the charging outlet. At this point, every device should have a type "C" adapter so that you don't have to figure out which side is which when you plug it in. This has the old Android outlet with its polarized arrangement. I suppose that I should mention that the suction cup is mediocre. While it is large in diameter it is not very deep. Thing like this really need a lever to tighten the attachment of suction cup to wall. Mine fell off the wall. The good news is that it still worked just fine. Connectivity and range are excellent. I had a similar product for a few years and it recently died. RIP. What I particularly like about this speaker is that the controls are in the front and the large white icons are prominent enough for me to make sense of without my glasses. Each button has two functions; long press and short press. You really want to RTFM. If you have an Nvidia Shield running Kodi you are going to love this thing. Once paired it connects automatically whenever you turn on the speaker redirecting the output from the my sound center. Turn the thing off and the music comes back to my living room speakers. All the controls work as expected.

title: Not great. Get the Omaker M4 instead.
text: This speaker is OK, but not great by any means when compared to others in it's price range. I have a few wireless bluetooth speakers but decided to give this a try for a dedicated shower speaker that would stick to the wall. To my surprise, it does stick to the shower wall really well; ours hasn't fallen off once yet. Problem 1: Sound quality. It's not every loud and the sound quality isn't great. It's "passable" I'd say, but it didn't impress me. Problem 2: Speaker phone volume. So I didn't honestly expect to use the speaker phone functionality unless it was an emergency, but I was disappointed to find out how very quiet it is. It's much quieter than the music even after I made sure the volume was turned up the whole way. I had to stand with my ear right up to it. Pretty much not usable for this function. My recommendation: Just get something like the Omaker M4 instead. It's also waterproof, it's a few bucks cheaper, and it sounds way better. The Omaker doesn't have a suction cup, but if you have a shelf in your shower to sit it on you'll be just fine.

title: Great for kids who love music.
text: I have a non-verbal teenage son with a severe developmental disability + autism who loves music. He likes kids toys like baby einstein and I wanted to get him something more age appropriate because he's 16 now. Unfortunately, he puts EVERY toy/electronic in the shower and we have to keep them locked up or they are ruined in just a few days. I bought this for him for his 16th birthday and he carries it with him constantly. I charge it overnight and it's ready to go the next day. I have a google play account set up with his favorite music and I connect it via bluetooth from my chromebook. This allows him to carry it around wherever he goes in the house, I can tell exactly where he is at all times and on a few occasions when I could not find it after he fell asleep, I was able to have our iphone pair with it, called the iphone and it rang through the speaker so we could locate it. It has an amazingly long battery life and only once did he burn the power all the way down, and that was on a night I forgot to recharge. This is, by far, the best present he has ever gotten. He loves it and no longer plays with the toddler music toys. When offered a choice, he always picks this speaker. He takes it in the bath and shower and it still plays. It is absolutely waterproof. I feel like this is the best purchase I have made in his entire life. I edited this to add: Ifox has the absolute BEST customer service of anyone I've ever dealt with on Amazon.

title: Okay sound quality, with a few design flaws
text: I ordered this speaker as a replacement for: IPX7 Waterproof Shower Speaker - Bluetooth Compatible - **Lifetime Guarantee** - Perfect for the Shower, Pool, Bath, Beach, Boat, Car, or Outside - iP Sold by: Home Products Direct I'm not going to spend the time researching the how or why, but the two speakers, though with a different logo and sold by "different manufacturers" are clearly the exact same. The are packaged the exact same. The little instruction booklet is the exact same. The tones, buttons, etc., are all the exact same. The IPX7 by "Home Products Direct" was DOA--music crackled and gurgled nonstop. I have used this new speaker once, and sound quality was fine. Of course, when the speaker was the "loudest it could get," I was able to get louder sound by turning up my paired phone as loud as it would get. This meant I could hear the music clearly, even with the shower running, if I walked into another room on the same floor and even downstairs some, so it's plenty loud. My only 3 complaints are as follows: (1) if the speaker is touched while playing, audio quality sometimes crackles or skips. It's as if this and the IPX7 are super sensitive to touch. I think now perhaps the IPX7 was jostled in shipping and that's why it worked so poorly. Thus, I worry how long this iFox Creations speaker will last if it gets touched or bumped, e.g., by a shampoo bottle. (2) the volume up/down buttons are also the skip buttons, and they are very sensitive. To volume up/down, the user must long-press. The device is really finicky about what constitutes a long press, and it's easy to accidentally skip a tune you love and are just trying to turn up. (3) the suction cup is not of good quality. The speaker slides down the wall with the lightest touch. I'm very concerned it could fall and therefore "jostle" the speaker too hard and ruin audio quality permanently. Forty dollars isn't expensive for convenience, but if this speaker won't remain in place, it's not going to last very long, and I'll be really disappointed.

title: Just.......WOW!
text: When I first opened the box, I kind of doubted that this compact bluetooth speaker was worth $50. But, after I got it fully charged (which didn't take long) and connected to my phone (super easy), I opened my graphic equalizer app and then started my favorite Pandora station. I cannot say enough about how surprised and pleased I am about the sound quality! The bass is thumping! The treble is crisp and clear! I have other BT speakers this size and none of them even come close to the quality! This Miatone TWS BT speaker is awesome! Note: because the sound comes out both sides and both ends, you need to keep the control panel at the top (or the bottom). Otherwise, you lose some of the sound quality. So, propping it up in the right position is essential to getting the best quality sound. I had to knock off one star on the portability factor for one thing; it's a perfect cylinder with no flat edge to keep it from rolling away. And, placing it on end will muffle part of the bass, as both ends have that wonderful bass speaker in them. I guess you can make sure that you place it either on a perfectly flat surface or if it's on a slope, that the included cord is underneath like a 'wheel chock'. But, overall, that's just a minor oversight. I still have to give this amazing little BOOMBOX five stars, because of the quality of construction and the amazing sound. I have JBL's this size that don't sound as good. Super happy with this purchase. Highly recommend.

I don't know why they include the audio cable at all - it almost never works. The phone recognizes that there's something plugged in, but no sound comes out of the speaker at all. Every once in a while it will decide to cooperate, but that's maybe one out of 10 attempts. The bluetooth connection is better, but still not good. You really have to fiddle with the settings to make it work. Like repeatedly turn bluetooth on and off, then switch the output from phone to speaker and back, until it finally works. Highly frustrating. What's the worst about it though, is the sound quality. It's horrible. Muffled and garbled, it sounds like it's coming from underwater. Maybe for crappy music it's okay, but I want to use this as an amplifier to my phone for Skype calls, and speech comes through really poorly and hard to understand. To make things even worse, it turns out that in addition to a speaker, this stupid thing also has a microphone, and when you connect it, it automatically turns off your phone's microphone and switches to the speaker's for input, and guess what - the microphone is just as bad as the speaker is! The other side can't hear me well at all either, and we just garble back and forth at each other. WHY the hell does it need a mic?!?!? And why does it force its mic over my phone's?? Unlike with output, with input I can't choose one mic over the other. This little POS makes the choice for me and leaves me no other option. I hate it and want to stomp it into pieces. Do not buy.

I believe I paid $75 each for the Motion Booms, and they are FAR superior to the Charge 5. The Motion Boom has a cleaner, much punchier sound, that is louder, smoother, and is EQ adjustable with the Soundcore app. If you directly compare the Charge 5 to the Soundcore Motion Boom, you will do the same thing I did… return the Charge 5. Don’t waste your money on the Charge 5. You will be much happier with the Soundcore Motion Boom. It is the best speaker under $100 and may be the best under $200.

I get occasional bluetooth drop outs, even when the phone is sitting just inches away. Also, bluetooth is your only option. That might not be a big deal for some, but if you walk away from the speaker with the phone in your pocket, the connection will drop. If you want to use this on your deck, patio, or garden, than a Wi-Fi speaker is a much better method. If you want to hard-wire this, you can't.

title: Beautifully built, thoughtfully designed, but Audio distortion not good.
text: First off, this thing looks reaaaalllly good. Impressive industrial design and built quality. Easy to use. Bluetooth range is SHOCKINGLY good. I took it to a company picnic and went to play some cornhole over 100 ft away with phone in my pocket. Not 1 single drop out. That alone lead to 2 people at the picnic to lock into Amazon and buy one on the spot. Battery last for just about any length party you have in mind. Now to the bad: Even moderate volume contains significant distortion. I do have a picky ear but I just cant get my head around how much distortion in mid range and upper base range exists. I expected more from JBL at this price point. The base response seems fleeting and over emphasized in narrow frequency ranges to try to trick the ears into hearing sufficient bass. I blame that on the absolute waterproof nature of the speaker. The design is portless to prevent water intrusion, so the only design option was to add passive radiators 0n the sides to enhance base. These are a compromise in audio compared to a port. With the Woofer handling all base and midrange frequencies and then also trying to drive two large passive radiators is just too much for it to handle without playing havock with lower mid range distortions. Many people wont care or notice. Unfortunately I do.

text: I had the phone playing tunes when the BT first connected and I was shocked at the sound. I expected smartphone speaker quality but louder. It actually has some bass... enough to vibrate against the table a bit. Sound is so good I'm not docking a star for the false advertising. Current listing for the IMW257 clearly states... "To play from Chromebooks, Windows 7-8 systems, TVs and non-Bluetooth devices use the included 3.5mm audio cable connected to the AUX-IN jack" If you care about that (and I had plans for that jack) IT'S NOT THERE on this model. I verified that they sent the same model as the listing... it's just a bad description copied from one of their older models I suspect. You lift the rubber flap and you have the charging port only. That said... awesome sound and super handy as a shower speaker so you can keep your phone dry while you podcast in the shower. Perfect for travel with the tiny size. Good for a pool or hot tub. When it gets wet you can see the bass vibrate the water drops. Can't speak to the battery life yet, but if it's remotely close to the promised 6hrs, I'm good. You get a sticker and a cheap plastic clip... nice thought. I'll replace with a keyring and a better clip. Got this on a Lightning deal on Cyber Monday and I'm kicking myself for not getting two. title: Don't buy unless you like loud automated women!
text: I did not buy this product at Amazon, but I am so upset with Altec Lansing's poor customer service, that I feel I should warn potential buyers. I bought this for my husband for Christmas. When we powered it on for the first time, there was an incredibly high volume voice welcoming us to Altec Lansing and informing us that the device is charging. The sound is great and it is everything-proof, which is what I wanted. We both assumed the voice message was a one time thing when we powered up for the first time. Oh no. That annoying voice lets you know at full volume when its connected and charging and when its not. It welcomes you to Altec Lansing when you turn it on and it tells you to enjoy. Great, thanks. It is at full volume, so, unless everyone is awake, I'm afraid to unplug it when I need the charger for another device or if I want to plug it in to charge. Forget turning it on if anyone is still asleep! I'm not a techy person, but even I understand what the light means on my other devices when it comes on after plugging it in. It's charging!!! Effective and quiet! Why would anyone need this feature? Without the packaging I didn't think I could return it to Best Buy (little did I know I could have, but only by 1/15), so I emailed Altec Lansing to see if this feature could be disabled or if maybe, just maybe, they'd accept a return and let me buy another one of their bluetooth speakers without this unnecessary voice feature. No reply to my email to their customer service in 13 days and no reply to the post I made to their facebook page. That really is terrible customer service. I should know by now to shop exclusively at Amazon; I would've seen the other reviews and I probably would've been able to return it beyond a 15 day time period too.

text: I've had this speaker for about a year now. I love it. I use it in my office cubicle. The wireless component comes in handy. And the Bluetooth pairing is easy to use. The only issue I have with this speaker is that, when you turn it on, it literally yells at me at the highest volume, "Welcome to Altec Lansing, powering on." It's so loud and nothing I can do will lower the volume, both before or during the powering on. If I walk away with my phone (when I'm streaming music from) for more than an hour, it powers of--even if plugged in. That wouldn't be such an issue if I didn't have to power it back on and have it blast at the highest volume: WELCOME TO ALTEC LANSING, POWERING ON. It's ridiculous. I can't find a way to make it not be so loud, so I bring the speaker to a filing cabinet, push the power on button, then close the door while it powers on at the highest volume! Ugh. text: This is tough rating this speaker. For the money, it's very good. Compared to my better speakers, it's just acceptable. If I didn't own a Harmon Kardon Go+Play, I might agree with the majority of reviews. The problem is... I do own a Go+Play... plus I have a JBL Xtreme (original) and a JBL PartyBox 100. Compared to the Go+Play, all other speakers pale in comparison. It's just a phenominal speaker. The PartyBox 100 has better bass and is louder, but the overall sound can't compete with the Go+Play either. Back to the W-King... it's great for $65. It's actually kind of hard to believe you can get a speaker of this size, battery life, and sound for $65. I purchased it mainly due to Oluv's review. I just had to see what it sounded like. I will keep it, even though I have much better speakers. The W-King will be great to put in the golf cart when I want something pretty loud, or when I am going somewhere and I don't want to worry about it. The sound... well... overall it's pretty closed. It is not a spacious sound like the others I have mentioned. The bass is pretty good, but is not getting low enough to compete with the HK Go+Play. Interestingly, it does complete pretty well with the Xtreme, since the extreme doesn't get very low (below 70 hz). It's pretty bright. The W-King's highs are very good. With the "EQ" button on, it gets pretty loud, but it sounds best under 70% volume. At 100% it is slightly distorted. It does get plenty loud at 70%. Overall, it is very nice and sounds very good. I just can't give it 5 stars, I would give it 4 and 1/2 stars if I could.

text: [[VIDEOID:c018a1681487f3b634afc70a7e6038af]] I tried a handful of other speakers including the fugoo XL 360 which was my second favorite to this W-KING speaker. I'm using this on a PWC, jet ski. I used 3x 40 in straps to secure it in place and it doesn't budge. I can hear the music with perfect clarity going over 50 mph. It says IPX5 but so far I've had it in the rain, soaked in salt water and it's pretty darn rugged. Had it fall off the back of my truck about 45 mph and the thing still works great! When you get to max volume it simply makes a beeping sound, more like a pleasant tone letting you know you're at max volume. Other speakers would lower the volume all the way and then crank it back up to let you know you're at max volume (very annoying). There's audio spectrum analysis videos out there on YouTube showing that the EQ button mainly boosts the sound, some say it's outdoor mode. It definitely makes it louder outdoors! You can tell you're in this mode because the light on top will blink at a rate around one second on and off. I had this thing playing for about 5 hours steady (max volume + EQ "outdoor" mode) and it was still around 80% battery which is indicated by the three LED lights on top. Assuming when I get to 78% or below one of the three lights will turn off and show only two. Best part is I can remove two of the straps and the third is left as the new handle (I the factory strap off).

title: Best audio discovery I've made in a long time
text: I discovered the W-KING D8 while reading an Amazon customer review of another speaker. The person mentioned several speakers he had tried, and that this was his favorite. Based on the reviews of the D8, I ordered it. I couldn't be happier. I have quite a few bluetooth speakers, almost all of which cost more than the D8, and if I did not know the prices of them, I would guess the D8 was the most expensive. The D8 is a very impressive speaker, made even more impressive by its affordable price. It has huge power, yet good fidelity. The D8 is ruggedly built, looks and feels built like a tank, and has great styling. It is easy to pair and use. I agree with several reviewers who said it would be nice if the strap were removable. I love the strap when on the go, but at home it gets in the way somewhat. I have not yet tried pairing two together. After I have tried this feature, I will update this review. Summing up, I couldn't be happier with my W-KING D8. Update: I could not get NFC to work. I could not get TWS to work. If anyone has successfully used NFC or TWS with this speaker, I would appreciate a description of the steps you used. Even though I am disappointed by the NFC and TWS failures, I still give this speaker a 5-star rating. That's how much I love the D8!

title: Mixed Results
text: I ordered this for the higher wattage and on my primary phone, it does get quite loud; but on my Dex device, it's maxed out is equivalent to about 50% volume on a 10W speaker. I used a dB meter that was about 6ft away with the speaker pointed towards the meter. At max volume on my main phone (fold3) and at 150% volume, I was getting a consistent mid-90s dB for melody and lyrics, with peaks up to 109dB. On my other device (Note 10+), also at 150%, it was pulling about 70 dB on TV dialogue. I did try testing it with a volume booster, and even with only 110% (on top of the 150%) it was beginning to distort. I played the TV audio for about 16hrs at moderate and 8hrs on low, and it was reading as still having 70% battery. But after only a few hours of moderate-high volume music, that 70% was gone and it died. The sound quality is quite good with a warm tone. The highs are clear and the bass is better than I expected for there not to be a dedicated bass cone. Despite appearances, I think the best use for this will be background music - not too loud will keep it playing all day & night and it will provide a much cleaner and richer sound than a small speaker at similar volume.

title: This is one of the best bluetooth speakers a person could buy for under a $100.
text: After using this speaker for over a month now, I determined what I think about it. So sound quality is really good, sound is crisp and clear with barley any noticeable hissing unless I put my ear up against it. The bass is one of the best things about this speaker. It's nice and bassy but not boomy, it's just right. Since this speaker has tweeters it has really good highs that I didn't think was possible for a speaker in this price point. Mid range is just as good as well. This is literally a full range speaker. I do love how it has passive radiators on the back of the speakers that vibrate whenever heavy bass is playing, it gives it that classic boombox feeling. Now onto the battery life. Surprisingly enough, I haven't even charged this speaker yet since I bought it, yea crazy I know. This is probably cause I only use it for 30 minutes at a time every other day but still very good battery. This speaker is very loud, in fact I keep it about less then half way so I don't damage my hearing. I have it paired with my echo dot and it works flawlessly. What other speaker for $70 are you gonna find that performs just as good as this one? Honestly it's pretty darn good for the amount that it's worth. Think about it, most bluetooth speakers such as the JBL Flip series and Charge series or UE Boom speakers which cost over $100 and they aren't as powerful as this speaker. Yes there is the W-King speaker that cost around $60 but after looking at youtube review comparisons and various amazon reviews, it seems results are mixed. Some people say one is louder while the other has better bass or the other one is more crisp. You decide for yourselves but for me this a bargain. I'm never buying those overpriced JBL speakers again when you can get something just as good if not better for less money, it's a no brainer. Good speaker for the money.

Anyway, my BOOM finally has pretty serious battery life issues so before wanting to drop another 100-200 dollars on a BT speakers I figured I’d try some, return the ones I do not like. I came across this speaker during a deal for less than $60 bucks. I feel it’s price point accurately depicts this speaker. The bass sounds great but at higher volume levels, you can tell the volume gets limited during notes with more bass. My BOOM is louder, probably 2X but it was also much more expensive. The benefit of the Bugani speaker is that is also acts as a power bank - which is awesome! Makes for playing music longer periods of time easier if you’ve got a dying battery on your phone. Note that it will also deplete the BT speakers battery. I’m pretty sure the back of the unit where it looks like “woofers” are false. But the overall design and quality is definitely up to par (maybe more so in some cases) with their normal asking price! Great speaker that is also water resistant which means it’ll do great at the beach, or rainy days on your patio. It’s also much less heavier then you’d think it would be.

title: Amazing sound quality!
text: Outstanding sound quality in a portable package. Obviously, with BT speakers, you're only going to get a certain amount of sound compared to the size. So, yes, this is a little larger than the kind of BT speaker you can toss in your backpack, but, it's more than worth it. I've read many reviews on this before buying it, and it's truly one of the best speakers out there in this price range. I have more expensive brands, and they do NOT sound better than this. I already have smaller, more portable speakers, but I wanted something louder. I also got a big one from another brand, and, while it is louder, the sound quality is not as good. This is just a terrific blend of volume and quality. Excellent bass, mids and highs, and impressive stereo separation considering the design. I love the build and textures on it, and it really feels to be a quality unit. At high volume, it pulls back the highs and mids a bit, to avoid distortion, and I'd say this is not so much of a party boom box, as it is ideal for a bedroom or office area where you can appreciate the sound quality, which is warm and rich. Don't get me wrong, it will pump plenty of sound, but it just really shines more at about 70% volume, where the audio wizardry can be heard. I even tried some Dolby tests on it, and, as I say, the sound stage is very impressive. Just nothing not to like here, and, honestly, I'm strongly tempted to get a second one, since it sounds so good. I can only imagine the bliss of two of these, paired. I'm really happy with this speaker! Highly recommend!

Another attractive quality about this speaker is that you have back and forward buttons that seem to be lacking on almost all of the Bluetooth speakers I have had over the years. So why 3 stars? If your going to listen to music loud all the time, this is a great speaker for that. The problem starts when your not blasting it at 100% -- you loose all bass and vocals are amplified so much they overpower the rest of the spectrum. I tried both modes (indoor / outdoor) of the speaker but could not notice any difference at lower volumes. I feel like the EQ curve should have been dynamic based on the volume like so many other speakers have.

text: First of all, I took the product as it is, not as it should be. Comparing it with others of course makes little sense. So we'll look at its strengths and downsides, for me. The sound is not very loud, not ideal for high volumes as the output tends to break up. This is not a party device, but rather for mild to moderate volume levels. Don't crank up the knob (very nice control) if you want to avoid unpleasant sound. There is no light, and I like that for nighttime listening and falling asleep as there's no light to interfere with my sleep, unlike my DOSS unit. I use the micro SD feature as this doesn't drain the battery as fast as using a Bluetooth connection. What makes the micro SD input so nice is the presence of the small screen where you can choose which folder to play, and you have control over random and linear play. The unit is actually very small, but not water-resistant even, so handle this with care. There's a strap that comes in handy for carrying this device. For the price and the features for which I chose this, I would say I'm quite happy with what it has.

title: Yes, you can organize your music in sub-folders!!
text: This device at this price point is really amazing. Easy to use, great sound... I was ready to buy a couple more of them when I experienced an issue. I had 900 songs on an SD card in a certain order but when I put the card in the player, the order was scrambled. Also, other folks had mentioned that you CANNOT have sub-folders. What a pain. 900 songs and no way to easily access them except by going forward or backward 900 times - or so I thought. Tonight, I fell upon the fix and it's crazy but it worked. Previously, I had selected "copy" and "paste" off the windows menu when transferring my songs to the SD. This gave me the scrambled results. Now, I temporarily moved the files to my PC in different sub-folders. I then deleted the existing files off the SD drive and formatted the drive. In other words, I started fresh with a "new" SD card. THE TRICK: Next, instead of selecting the words "copy" and "paste" off the menu, I used CTRL C to copy and CTRL V to paste the entire file which contained many sub-folders. I read somewhere that doing this ensures they get on the root drive of the SD card. Works perfect!!! I can now choose what sub-folder to listen to, rather than having 900 songs in no particular order. If you want a different sub-category for each album, it works! text: I bought two speakers to get stereo (they call it TWS). Just could not get the speakers to pair with each other to achieve TWS. Wrote to the manufacturer and got a quick response. Per their instructions we tested the speakers and they passed. What we found was this -- during the process of pairing the speakers with each other to achieve TWS, you must click the master speaker twice. IF YOU CLICK TOO SLOWLY, it will not work. When you get to that point in the process, make sure you click twice very quickly and the speakers will pair with each other easily. The sound is then legitimate stereo. I was very impressed with the response of the manufacturer and I love the speakers.

title: Surprisingly good
text: I have been using a JBL charge 3 for a few years and absolutely love it great at home in the yard and on camping trips. Recently I wanted a similar product in my room to set up as stereo speakers. Being more expensive and needing to buy 2 to achieve the stereo effect getting 2 more JBLs were not in my price range. I took a chance buying 2 of these Trelab speakers at half the price. While the sound is warmer and the bass is just a hair better on the JBL the trelab had a more powerful output for noticeable more volume (i know JBL has newer versions of the Charge speakers that are higher wattage but I'm comparing to the older charge 3 since its what I own). So here are my opinions. You lose the ability to charge mobile devices since the trelab doesn't have a USB output. The trelab is smaller so you get adequate but lowered bass performance. The stereo feature works Just as well and is as easy to set up as the JBLs link function. The price is also half of JBL for nearly the same performance. My only minor quibble is that for some reason the controls do not act as the manual implies when charging. It's good that the speakers can be charged while in use, however, I noticed that connection to Bluetooth or stereo link is unpredictable while connected to the charger. To avoid frustration power up, connect to Bluetooth or the other speakers, then reconnect the charger to avoid frustration. Also these speakers cone with cables but no charger, JBL cones with both. But honestly, I don't see this as a problem since most people already have too many USB adapters at home so id rather not pay more to receive equipment I already have ... Cables only are fine with me.

title: Voice prompts are irritating & unnecessary.

I do not recommend this (or similar, which there are many, under different brand names) products. Don't waste your money on this speaker. Sound quality is decent, but there are better alternatives out there. 2022 update: Battery life has dropped significantly but still sounds the same and the ridiculous voice prompts on start up still irritate me. It's still usable but battery life makes me want to replace it. That and the voice prompts. For comparison, I bought a JBL Flip 4 at the same time. The JBL is about done. It shuts down at half battery and has developed a bass crackle. Neither of these speakers have ever been dropped and have been used indoors.

If I'm in a conference call or not sure where the charging cable is, I have to drop everything and look for it, or lose my ever loving mind, or bury the speaker under towels in the closet until I have time to address the situation. title: Nice speaker - great sound, can use micro-SD card!
text: I haven't used a whole ton of bluetooth speakers, but I have used several & this is the very first one that I've encountered that enables use of a micro-SD card to play offline music & I think that is a pretty cool feature. Can also stream music via bluetooth or connect via a 3.5mm stereo cable to a MP3 player or other source. Sounds great overall. No annoying giant logos painted on the device, which is a big plus in my opinion. I am an old guy with failing eyesight & the print within the included manual is tiny. With help from a magnifying glass and good light, I was able to figure out the controls easily enough. I did accidentally discover a seemingly undocumented operation - when paired with my iphone, it can be used to take calls - double-pressing the power button will redial the last number called on the device. I did not find that documented in the manual - not a big thing, but good to know. I do wish the "party lights" could be permanently disabled until manually turned back on, but that setting defaults to "party lights on" upon power-up. It is an easy single-press of an hour-glass shaped button on the controls to turn the lights on and off. The party lights are kind of cool - they sort of flash/change in time with the music, and while I'm not sure what is being sensed when they change, but I'm guessing it must be a frequency-based sensor of some sort. The lowest volume setting is a bit high for my preference for indoor/office use, but then again, this is a waterproof bluetooth speaker designed for use outdoors, so it makes some sense that it would be on the loud side. It is an attractively designed speaker & has good bass response. The tweeter portion of the speaker seems quite directional to my ears, so you may have to experiment with it a bit to find the orientation that is best for you. All in all, this is a very good speaker. Recommended!

title: And the winner is, this M6Pro
text: My new favorite budget bluetooth speaker, but with a couple caveats. I recently reviewed a Tronsmart speaker “Portable Bluetooth Speaker, Tronsmart Trip Wireless Waterproof Speaker with 10W Output, Bluetooth 5.3, IPX7 Waterproof, 20H Playtime, Built-in Mic”. I was happy with how it performed for its size, budget class, and intended purpose. However, this EDUPLINK M6Pro, although not as compact and slightly more expensive than the Tronsmart (by thirteen bucks at time of this review), the M6 does indeed provide better sound quality. Pros: - Produces noticeable bass with treble and midrange sounding clear and undistorted. - The party light effect is nice - not too distracting and can be turned off, but pleasant to use at night. - Like many bluetooth speakers on the market, you can pair this speaker with another identical one if you care. The grill seems plenty sturdy along with the strap. - It has a TF card slot, which I did not test, but presume you can play music directly from a card. - Battery life at mid volume was at least 3 hours with party lights going. I turned it off after 3 hours, so I can’t yet state how long it could play before needing a recharge. - Uses type C usb for charging. Cons: - With the controls facing upright, the speaker wants to roll around until it is stopped by the carry strap attachment point, which then means the controls are facing down. - With controls facing up, the treble and mid range will sound muffled as those speakers, inside the barrel, will be facing down. Initially I was unhappy with the sound quality until I reoriented the speaker and figured that out. The internal speakers are not readily visible through the grill, so hard to tell which way they face. - It would be nice if somewhere on the housing/barrel, there were dedicated flat spots to keep this from rolling and also to help make proper orientation obvious, albeit with controls facing down, but I can live with that. If a super compact speaker is more important than a little more bass and marginal overall better sound quality, I would steer towards the Tronsmart. Otherwise, I think this M6 will make most people very happy. I think it is a very good value.

text: This isn't a high-end speaker, and an audiophile would sneer at it. I'm reviewing this as a decent sound quality durable speaker. In that regard it works the way it's supposed to. The device pairs seamlessly. Pairing, volume, and "outdoor boost" volume controls work correctly. Battery life is as advertised although the louder outdoor setting significantly reduces it. Since I only have one of these I was unable to try the two-speaker stereo pairing, but since this worked well I might get another at some future point. The device really is sturdy, waterproof, and dustproof. My wife and I played catch with it for a couple minutes. No problems. I rolled it in potting soil which is pretty dusty. No difficulties, and it washed off easily. Then I turned it on and tossed it in the bathtub. It floated, just as advertised. I will admit it sounded a little odd, but that's to be expected. It performed just fine and showed no signs of damage from its immersion. I must hasten to say that I used the rubber cover for the USB port. I am not sanguine about the port's function if it got wet. So, it's a good bluetooth speaker with decent sound. It stands up to abuse that an outdoor speaker should. Quite pleased with the product.

It has no audio input jack, so you are forced to try to connect through Bluetooth. That is unfortunate, because the Bluetooth connectivity is quite unreliable. Sometimes it will pair and connect, but sometimes not. If you manage to get it connected, you soon discover that it has a "battery saver" automatic shutoff that turns it off EVEN WHEN IT IS CONNECTED TO THE CHARGER. So if you pause a movie to go to the toilet or answer a phone call, you come back to it to find that the game of trying to get it to connect starts all over. You would be much better off spending your money on a ZoeeTree speaker. They have better sound quality, reliable Bluetooth connectivity, usable control buttons on top, audio input jack, two (2) different USB charging ports, and they DO NOT shut themselves off when on external power. Unfortunately mine was fragile: my wife broke BOTH of the USB ports by pushing the connectors in too forcefully.

title: Great Sound in a Small Package
text: I've had the TriBit Max Sound Bluetooth speaker for around 2 weeks now and I have to say that I am impressed. It paired with my iphone XR immediately and reconnects when turned back on. The sound is what sets this apart from others I have listened to. It is a very pleasant balance that is very clear and not blaring. I mostly listen to an eclectic mix of music and radio broadcasts at low to medium volume in my kitchen and on my front porch, but it can crank it out loud enough to fill a large patio or a basement. I keep the bass boost on as it seems to improve the sound quality which is amazing. I can't speak to its durability, but it looks and feels sturdy. The battery life is pretty impressive too. It lasted longer than the 20 hours it advertised, and it charged fully connected to an ac outlet in under 4 hours. I haven't tested it for water resistance, and I don't plan to. If it fails because it accidently gets wet, I'll update. The strap that comes attached to it comes in handy. The small size makes this thing very portable. If you are in the market for a great sounding, portable Bluetooth speaker, Tribit Max sound should be seriously considered. The few extra dollars spent were well worth it.

title: Finally, the "Sweet Spot"
text: After trying out several different makes/models of small Bluetooth speakers, I think I have finally found the "sweet spot" in this amazing little Tribit speaker. The sound quality is excellent, with a relatively flat frequency response that doesn't overemphasize bass (as many portable bt speakers seem to do). The loudness is sufficient to fill small to medium size rooms. You have the option of turning off the "extra bass" button, e.g., for quieter listening in evening hours or for purely acoustic music -- although I think leaving X-bass on as default generally delivers the fullest, richest sound. For the price (about $60 including tax), this speaker is pretty amazing. For me, the sound it produces rivals that of much more expensive offerings from Bose, JBL, and Harman Kardon. (I listen to a mix of classic rock, indy folk, instrumental jazz, and the occasional classical piece.) Of course, sound preference is highly subjective. But if you're looking for a great, inexpensive bt speaker with well balanced bass, mids, and highs, I highly recommend this Tribit unit.

title: Nice sound, but not very portable or stable
text: I like the sound of this speaker - it does a great job for a small speaker and replaces a flakey Anker SoundCore speaker that stopped taking a charge. This Tribit puts out more realistic sound and better bass response than the Anker. But then, it cost almost $20 more. What I don't like about the Tribit is that it is bulky and oddly shaped. This makes slipping it into my duffel bag or backpack. Where the Anker Soundcore is rectangular and fits in along side of books and other carryables, this Tribit is rounded on the ends and the back. This may be what allows the Tribit to produce better sound - more room for larger speakers - but it also makes for a somewhat unstable flat bottom to rest on. It is also heavier - coming in at 21.5 ounces vs 12.5 ounces for the Anker. Now, when I'm sitting around my home office listening to a podcast or doing a conference call, this extra size and weight don't matter - the better sound of the Tribit makes it all worthwhile. But when I'm on a trip and simply want to slip some better sound for watching movies on my phone or listening to the news when waking up in a strange hotel room, the Anker's size and weight are a better travel companion. Too bad their batteries are wimpy.

title: The Little Speaker That Could
text: There is always a moment that everyone's lives where they realize what they have found is enough. It is the feeling you get when you first walked into your house, or when car shopping... That feeling where you think this was designed for only me. The Maxsound Plus gave that feeling when I first played it. It was at the bridge of the Popular song: 'Versace on the Floor' by Bruno Mars it struck me that this is easily the best $56.00 I have ever spent. The musicality of this little speaker is nothing short of amazing. The bass is exceptional. The highs and mids are great. Listening to this magical piece of tech took me back to when I was little and wanted a computer, it is all I wanted, but my parents could not afford it. The Processor was 600Mhz (blazing fast at that time), the HD stored 9.51Gb (very good memory), it had a 32x CD-ROM drive and a floppy drive. NOW my Samsung phone is maybe 5 times faster, stores 128gb in a package 30X smaller. What I am alluding to is the fact that there comes a time in every electronic where the regular person can afford something that is very close in quality to a device more expensive... that time is now here for Portable Audio.... Tribit, from the bottom of my heart, I thank you! My brother/roommate has a Bose SoundLink Mini II so I have a direct comparison. My advice is buy the Maxsound Plus and spoil yourself with a nice dinner with the $100 you saved by not buying the Bose.

title: Really good replacement for my old analog clock radio
text: Let me start with the Cons of the radio, or actually, the instructions. They are cram packed, so you may have to bring a magnifying glass [so, this is more of a complaint against the instructions and not the radio itself]. But once you do take the time to read the instructions, you'll find this clock has a lot of neat features. Now for the Pros... I just love how it starts off at a very low volume and slowly gets louder and louder. It's not a "hi, I'm on at full volume", instead, it starts off nice and low. The second thing I like is the M-F wake time can be different than Sat/Sun time. I set the M-F for 6AM... The sat/sun is set for 7AM [or you can turn off Sat/Sun]. The snooze button is your standard 9 minute snooze and right in the front middle top of the clock radio. I waited to write this review, and yes, it automatically changed for Daylight savings. I did not have to touch anything, it automatically moved the clock time forward an hour. I like a very dim setting, and yes, the clock goes all the way down to very dim. On bright, it can light up the night, so I'm happy with the range. The radio is digital and is fine. I don't need a perfect sound with bass, etc... It's a clock radio, it's small, it's not going to have amazing sound. For it's size, I will say it does sound good. But I'm not using the radio to play all day long, I'm using it to wake me up and once I'm up, the radio goes off. If your expectations are that it's a clock radio, with digital display, that automatically stays on the correct time, this is a great match.

title: Clear and powerful sound, easy to operate!!!
text: I've only had this for about a week. Boy, is it fantastic. It worked as soon as charging it for a few hours, every time so far. I LOVE it. I should have known Bose wouldn't let me down (like Jams and Jams2 did). Pros: Just turn it on. A female voice will tell you what the speaker is connected to. An example would be my Kindle - Turn on the speaker, then turn on your Kindle. Swipe to wireless settings then bluetooth on the Kindle. You will see the name "Bose" speaker under the bluetooth section. Tap it and the speaker will say it is now connected to your Kindle. I love it. I did the same with my IPod. No problem. It can connect with two devices simultaneously, but I only use one device at a time. The unit is very substantial weight and won't get knocked over easily at all. There are four little rubber pads under the device which help to click to slick surfaces. There are speaker or sound holes front and half of the back of the unit. The control touch pads are on top of the device. Has a round auxiliary "in" as well as the Power in, cord provided. Rechargeable battery inside - no more throwing away batteries (love, it's green) The sound is extremely clear, words and notes distinct. Cons: The sound is just a bit on the tinny side. I have downloaded apps for more bass boost and volume to both devices. However, I still cannot get that deep, tone that I'm used to with our Bose stereo. But it's still very acceptable. If you turn it up you will definitely rattle your windows and perhaps knock off some plaster from the walls. It's that powerful. Can you imagine if you had two of these? Wooo, middle of the concert sound! Enjoy. So far, so near to perfect.

title: I'm not a fan of tons of features; instead, I like the ones I have to work well. NOTE: "Press and hold" means 5 seconds.
text: The Bose SoundLink speaker was up, paired with my phone (iPhone 4s), and playing tunes in about five minutes (most of which was opening the packaging)! Here's what I love about this speaker: It's simple. Very simple. I'm not a fan of tons of features; instead, I like the ones I have to work well. This speaker delivers! Everything I've tried has worked well: charging the speaker, pairing, stopping and starting music, and adjusting the volume on both the speaker and via my phone. Really, what else do I need a speaker to do?!? NOTE: if you want to make calls, this speaker isn't the one for you. It doesn't have a microphone to take sound IN. Sound comes only OUT. My Usage Notes: To check remaining battery charge, the instructions tell you to "press and hold" the power button. The "press and hold" time on my speaker is about five seconds which is a long time to press and hold a button (not a long time in reality, of course). I haven't been able to check battery life without turning the speaker off; however, a voiced warning will come from the speaker when the battery starts to get low, so I don't feel a lot of need to do a bunch of checking the remaining charge. One tiny complaint: I notice a very slight emphasis on s, d, f, z, and t, etc. sounds with this speaker. You know, that hissing/breathing sound when the radio isn't perfectly tuned? It's slight, slight, slightly present in this speaker, Not enough to remove a star, but enough that my very picky ears noticed it. If hissing/breathing sounds in music is a pet peeve of yours, you're probably going to notice it in this speaker. The effect gets more noticeable as you turn the volume up. I love this thing! It's making it so much more enjoyable to listen to content from my phone!

title: The epitome of planned obsolescence. You’ll only get a couple of years out of this speaker
text: The sound quality is good, the fit and finish are good, the user interface is good. I own the previous generation of the Soundlink speaker but the problems are the same with the current generation. I also cannot speak about their other portable speaker, but I would imagine they are designed in a similar way. Bose clearly intended for this product to become useless as soon as the battery had exceeded it’s working life and no longer takes a charge. It is the absolute perfect example of planned obsolescence. in my case it worked well for about two years. The case is sealed with tamper proof screws (who are they trying to prevent from tampering with the speaker) and the battery is soldered into place. This device was clearly designed to make it as difficult as possible for the user to service even for a simple dead battery. I would almost be OK with that approach, except Bose also refuses to provide service for this device despite the fact that it was still available for purchase a year ago. I don't understand how they can charge exorbitant prices and expect to maintain a reputation for high quality when they've designed a device and implemented policies for that device which render it unusable after just a couple of years. I find it disturbing that they make throw away speakers and then charge high prices for them. No more Bose for me.
