title: BOSE Soundlink Color vs. SONY SRSX33
text: A friend brought this speaker to the beach and upon first hearing, I was enamoured with the sound. At first, I thought the music coming from a car that was passing by. Imagine my surprise when my buddy pulled this out and I realized the music was coming from that?! Holy cow. I was sold! I went to Best Buy to check it out. That's when the reality set in. I paired my iPhone to this speaker and upon closer inspection, I found the bass sound very muddy. I'm not an audiophile by any means, but even I was able to detect this flaw. As so happens, the Sony products were displayed next to it SRSX33 was sitting nearby. I didn't really pay any attention to the Sony before but I figured, why not try it? At this point, I was reserved to not buying the Bose after all. So I paired my iPhone with the Sony and and was pleasantly surprised to find the sound coming from it to be clearer and tighter than the Soundlink Color. And this from a smaller, more compact product and cheaper to boot. At this point it was a no-brainer. The quality of the Sony sold me. (Disclaimer: I also compared the Soundlink Mini II against this Sony and found the Mini better in all aspects. However, at twice the price. If you have $200 to burn, get the Soundlink Mini II. If you want to keep it around $100, the Sony SRSX33 is a solid winner).

title: Great sound and super easy to set up and manage with voice prompts!
text: This 1.25 pound bluetooth speaker has great sound, both high and low range, at comfortable listening volumes (soft enough to converse over to loud enough that we have to turn it down for conversation). There is some distortion at the highest volume, and I think most of my other audio devices will get louder, but that isn't a problem for me, since I never turn them up that loud. I think the coolest thing about it is that there are voice prompts. As with many of the bluetooth speakers, there are only a few buttons -- on/off, bluetooth (used to add devices or 'forget' previously added ones), an auxiliary input, and volume up or down. The process for adding bluetooth connections can be kind of confusing but the voice prompt makes it super easy, no more digging out the manual! The voice prompts can be switched from English to Spanish to French to German to Italian, to Portuguese to Dutch to Polish to at least three more that I can't interpret. And the speaker comes with a micro-USB to USB cord that can be used with the included wall plug to charge the speaker or to connect the speaker to the computer for software upgrades, which, Bose intimates, will probably support more languages. However, if the voice prompts aren't your cup of tea, you can disable them! I like the vertical orientation of the speaker both for space utilization and sound coverage. The re-chargeable battery provides enough juice to play for 8 hours at "normal" volumes, according to Bose, and low battery will be signaled by changes from green to amber then red LED. The Bluetooth is supposed to link at distances of up to 30 feet but I believe I'm seeing a bit more than that. Bose does note that if you're using your smartphone as the audio source, and you get a call, the speaker will go silent for the duration of the call and then pick up when the call ends. Handy for listening, but wouldn't work as a "speakerphone." Interestingly, the speaker comes with receptacle for a 3.5mm jack so that you can connect it to sources that don't support bluetooth, which is great for my old Sandisc player.

text: I am in LOVE with Bose! I purchased this at my local Best Buy because they were on sale and I splurged on them, and I'm glad I did! I feel like I'm hearing my music for the first time. Kitchen when I'm cooking or doing dishes, office when I'm working or surfing the web, bedroom when I'm folding laundry/exercising/cleaning, etc... You can pair it with multiple devices, but obviously only stream from one device at a time. I have it paired with my phone, tablet, and my husbands phone and tablet. If you get a phone call you can answer it and speak with the caller through the Bluetooth speaker. You can also use the speaker itself, or the item your streaming music from, to adjust volume levels, change song, pause, etc... The package comes with the speaker, USB cable, and power adapter. This give you the option to charge your speaker from your laptop USB port, or use the adapter and charge from an outlet on the wall. The battery lasts up to eight hours, but it depends on the volume level. I find that the louder and more bass the song has, the quicker the battery drains. Oh and speaking of bass, man does this little speaker deliver a big punch! I would recommend to anybody and everybody that likes to listen to music. Yes you can save money buy purchasing a cheaper speaker, but don't deprive yourself from the awesomeness that is BOSE!

PORTABLE: Obviously it's not huge, because of that I was able to take it on vacation with us half way around the world to use in the hotel etc. It fits in some of my shorts pockets (maybe not jeans, but most cargo shorts etc). Which opens up the options about where you can take it without it being a pain. CHARGE: I don't know how long it actually lasts because it's never died from one use. title: You'll Be Impressed!
text: Great sound in a tiny package. I was hesitant to spend the money on the larger SoundLink so I opted for the SoundLink Color first. It works great and sounds awesome. It's definitely small enough to put in a backpack for a day at the park or beach. It's plenty loud for typical daily use, and the bass is particularly impressive for such a small speaker. The battery lasts a long time too. I do notice that if you're not either directly in front of the speaker or within a few feet left or right of it that it can sound a little flat. I've also noticed that certain frequencies don't quite sound right. I'm not sure if it's a lack of stereo (since it's just one speaker), but on a couple of tracks with heavy synths, it just sounds a little dull. Still, I love it. This isn't meant to replace your hifi system. We use it in the kitchen most of the time. My son loves to dance while we cook dinner! The only drawback I have noticed is that I can't use the video function on my phone while I'm playing music (via Bluetooth, to the SoundLink Color). I think this might be due to the fact that the SoundLink Color allows you to answer calls and the microphone is therefore "owned" by the SoundLink Color while connected via Bluetooth. The Bluetooth range could be a bit better as well, but it's typical of other Bluetooth devices that I own. You'll definitely notice sound degradation if you take your device around 15 feet away from the speaker. My house is old though. Maybe it's all the lead paint!

Overall, this little speaker is loud, rich in sound, sports a nice bass, and is stylish and fits in with other household items and appliances! I love it and would definitely recommend it for anyone looking for a relatively inexpensive, super-awesome Bluetooth speaker!

title: I'd give 6 stars if I could! Simply fantastic!
text: This is truly amazing. I'm glad I didn't splurge for the next higher Bose model because at home this is ALL you will need (and then some). We have the heavier, silver $200.00 model at our Surgical Office and patients exclaim over the spend coming from "that tiny speaker" in the lobby and easily heard into all 4 surgical rooms. So I already knew the other version was excellent and decided to get a more portable, lower-priced model for at home. We use our cell phones to stream satellite radio, mp3s, and even YouTube videos to it through Bluetooth and are AMAZES how clear and fantastic the sound is! Considering that dome of the Mp3s and especially YouTube videos are recorded in lower quality, you'd expect it to sound terrible on a good speaker, but it doesn't. We have seamlessly paired cell phones, really old iPods, and our older, cheaper tablets with this speaker with zero connection issues. I think the sound on the Bose Colors is just as good as the higher priced model and can discern no real difference. It's easily loud enough for parties, to hear from many rooms away, and the battery seems to last us at least 8 hours minimum. We've never had it die on us and need recharging, so the limit is hard to say. Don't be fooled by the plastic outer casing on this speaker. It doesn't feel cheap. It's heavy and very sturdy and surrounding seams and buttons are smooth and quality as well. It's attractive and charging is no problem. We pick it up and take it all around the house. I would spend even more on this product than it cost. Nothing better than Bose out there. My only wish is that the unit itself had a basic remote control for powering the device off and on. It would be nice to just switch it off and save battery power while listening to music in bed and getting sleepy. You can still just turn off your Bluetooth device to go to sleep, but then the speaker power is still on. Anyway, I can't think of a single con for this and would give it 6 stars if I could. I'll be buying all of the colors and giving these to loved ones as the "best gift you didn't know you wanted".

text: [[VIDEOID:aedbd047bdcee111326af43f1b70c93c]] After experimenting with several small speakers to use with my Echo Dot, I became enamored with the Doss Soundbox Touch because it had the best overall sound quality compared to other speakers in its price range. Naturally, I couldn't wait to try the Doss Touch Plus when it came up for review. It is larger than my original Doss Soundbox, and I was expecting the same well rounded dynamic range with a little more volume. This speaker paired effortlessly with all of my devices. The touch controls are my favorite. It not only gives this speaker a sleek modern look, but they also make it a breeze to change functions effortlessly. It's like swiping my phone screen between apps and I have become spoiled by not having to push or press anything. It sounds like a small thing, but once you live with it you will find anything that that requires more effort to be an inconvenience. The Soundbox Plus boasts an increased battery life when using it without the light feature. The light show is fun, but it's not a big draw for me since I use this near my computer monitor and it's somewhat distracting. The sound quality is decent, but it is not what I had expected. It has larger drivers and moves more air, so there is increased volume but the sound quality degrades and becomes too bright. I hear mostly the mid and high ranges with slightly muddled bass. However, at a lower volume, the sound quality improves and becomes more balanced. I love the touch control features, and it's attractive enough for use in every room. As a side note, Doss customer service is second to none. The best I have ever experienced outside of Amazon's support team. ** If you found this review to be helpful at all, please take a moment and click the button below to let Amazon know. Thank you so much 😊 **

First of all it is easy to pair, and the volume dial is like a iPod- you “dial” up or down on a circle controller. It has buttons to kip or repeat songs. title: A++ purchase worthy of writing a review!
text: I have purchased so many different wireless speakers because they just haven’t been loud enough to really be work writing a review! That was until this one, this lil guy is loud with incredible base & battery life. Not to mention it’s a cute light up speaker which changes color with each sound. This was a worthwhile purchase worthy of a review. Mind you I buy thousands of amazon products annually & rarely write reviews!! Way to go DOSS!

title: A huge step up from the DOSS SoundBox
text: I have the DOSS Soundbox speakers. I was really happy with the performance on those given that I have a pretty small & cozy house. However, they weren’t great for audiobooks as we cleaned. I could never get it loud enough or place the speakers in such a way that it was easy to hear the book. I always felt like I was straining to hear the story and shushing everyone. No straining to hear with the SoundBox Plus. Everyone could easily hear the story over the breakfast cereal crunches. If you are wondering if you should get the SoundBox or SoundBox Plus, definitely get the SoundBox Plus. It is worth the extra sound quality, volume, and range. In fact, I have some sensory sensitive kiddos and the SoundBox Plus was the first time I’ve ever been asked to turn the music down! The pink color is so much fun and it’s just what my pink loving kid wanted. The lights are fun and give the everyday a festive air. I love that it’s not just functional, it’s cute and decorative too.

title: Doss it all
text: [[VIDEOID:405b2ad1539406fa6a281229246ed359]] Doss has impressed me with their speakers; and that's not something easily done. But without the light feature on, you will save your battery from overheating. but if there are any defects, amazon will replace defects in the equipment, free of charge. Fortunely they understood and sent one day shipping for defective model I received. Tip: keep the cords attached to the device or label them with tape to stop cord confusion. Notes: Device was at 70-80% when video was made. When fully charged, device reaches over 80 decibals. Touch surface allows for a hassle in carrying across short distances. Accident selection, mode or random button can be pressed. Only one side has the RGB feature. without using the RGB feature allows for longer/louder sessions. Turning off this feature is optional.

title: A DOSS Bluetooth speaker that acts like a jerk. It is defective.
text: Since I was having so many problems with the standard DOSS Bluetooth Speaker, I decided to invest in the next highest price DOSS Bluetooth speaker. Is it worth it? NOOOOOOO. Not at all. If a man made machine can be a jerk, this speaker is definitely a jerk. Let me tell you about it. You have set the volume to a reasonably low volume so that it is great for your hearing pleasure, but won't disturb your neighbors upstairs. You click on a video you want to watch. The volume is now at 100% instead of the 8% you set it at. So you stop the video, and adjust the volume again. Hit play. Volume is now at 58%, not 8%. Another example is your volume control is working fine through several videos. You are working on something on your work surface and reach for a part. Your hand has come within 3-5 inches of the speaker. The speaker shoots up immediately to 100% or down to 0%. Either way, you have to adjust the volume again which may take a full minute or more until you get this unpredictable machine to stay at the 8% volume level that you have chosen because that's all you need. I have no comment on audio quality since the machine has been a first class problem on the number one issue: VOLUME. Next, battery life: I plugged the rechargeable battery in immediately as soon as I took it out of the box. How quickly does it charge up? I wouldn't know. After 5 hours, the little green light NEVER came on. The funky lights: Unnecessary use of the built in battery. Manual: Non existent. Not provided by company. You are on your own. USB charging cord: Short but reasonable length in comparison to other Bluetooth devices. 3.5 Auxillary cord: Very short. Also, even if the auxiliary cord is plugged into your laptop and the DOSS speaker, you can actually continue using your Bluetooth earbuds. What's up with that. I see no advantage to purchasing this speaker.

title: All good in a small package
text: I listen mostly to jazz in the background while I’m reading or on the web, usually at low volume - sometimes rock at louder volumes. I’ve bought any number of blue tooth speakers, as a hobby I suppose, always in search of that nirvana sound. They’ve ranged from really small Fugoo units (with unbelievably good sound) to paired floor standing auditorium behemoths that will blow your contacts out. IMO, the UE Boom 3’s are not only a good value, they are superlative in sound from low to high ranges at easy and medium volume. Great for voice, too, e.g. podcasts. I have 2 paired and will likely buy another pair (stereo is nice) for another room. I recently tried the UE Megablast and they don’t hold a candle to to crispness and range of the Boom 3’s. They’re loud and have some nice control features but for sound, IMO the 3’s are the best by far, and uncannily the least expensive of over 10 other brands, up to $300. Unless you’re filling a large room with loud music I’d say the Boom is the best speaker in it’s portable class. Enjoy, and don’t worry about missing any sound - you’ll pleasantly hear it all!

title: Beware this device cannot do deep base
text: I know it's a little speaker and I shouldn't expect booming bass from it, but that's not the problem. The problem is that any bass tones below 90 Hz aren't low power, they don't exist ... at all. Everything below 90Hz is just gone, like a high-pass filter. Classical music sounds retarded when you can't even hear the cello or kettle drums. Rap sounds even more retarded, like the entire percussion track has been removed from the recording. I don't know how people enjoy listening to music on these things. I can only guess that it's the same type of people who can't tell the difference between a low-quality 128 kbps MP3 and a lossless FLAC file.

title: Great portable sound system!
text: This is a great portable sound system (boom box). The unit measures 4.25x7.5x12.5" and weighs 6 pounds 1.1 ounces. The handle is rigid and possibly removable. There is another unit like this that has a flexible strap. The 3.5mm jack can connect directly to a cellphone or tablet or computer. When the 3.5mm plug is inserted into the unit, the Blue Tooth connection will end. The Blue Tooth connection works well with little latency. There is a micro Secure Digital card slot that I haven't tried yet. To power up the unit: Press & hold the Power Button for 2 to 3 seconds. The Power Button LED will begin to flash Blue (searching for Blue Tooth connection). Turn on cellphone, etc, and locate Blue Tooth and choose W-King. Power Button LED should turn and stay solid blue. You are now connected via Blue Tooth. Press and hold the Power Button for 2 to 3 seconds. Power Button LED should turn solid red. The LED should then turn off after a few seconds. The unit is now off. There are 2 equalization modes. I might search and install an equalization app on my cellphone in the future for more frequency control. The volume is LOUD. Be sure to fully charge the internal battery. The unit has a 3-stage battery level indicator. After charging for10 hours, my unit was still flashing on the 3rd level. After using my unit for 10 hours, the level is still indicating 3 bars and are solid (not charging). text: As another review has stated, "It's OK." I'm an audiophile. It's not good enough to purchase a second unit for wide stereo reproduction. title: Great Speaker
text: A decent little speaker. It is loud. I tried the default bass up setting and wasn't impressed. However, after trying the custom equalizer settings, you can get a bit more of a punch out of it if you try placing it in different areas. Bass seems hit or miss. title: Disappointing sound
text: I got this speaker to use with my laptop since laptops aren't know for their audio quality. I also like using the speaker with my phone when I'm in the shower/bathroom, and have used an Anker cube for that for literally years. I expected this to be a huge upgrade, but right off the bat the audio quality is very lacking in the high-end. Bass? There's tons. I love a lot of bass and find there can be too much sometimes. I don't know how some people claim there's no bass. Midrange is OK, a little hollow sounding. But highs are almost non-existent. If I put the speaker up to my ear, I can hear the tweeters doing their thing, but either the fall-off is high or volume of them is just lacking. I can sort of compensate for it with the app and the EQ, but I have no such control over it using my laptop (unless I use the EQ in Foobar.) Also with the laptop I notice it doesn't play sounds instantly; it seems to take a second or so to start playing, so Windows sounds are generally never heard. Or if I play music, I can see the graph in Foorbar going, but nothing coming from the speaker for a second or two. I've tried it with all kinds of music, all in FLAC format. I'd say it sounds about as good as my Bose Wave Radio that's like 18 years old now. It's certainly no slouch with the bass or volume, but the clarity just isn't there for me. Most of the time if I cover the tweeters with my hands, I can't tell the difference in the sound. Another note on the bass.. it entirely matters where you put the speaker. Outside, yeah it's not going to make the windows of your house rattle. But put it on a flat surface, especially near the corner of the room and it's amazingly capable.

title: Incredible Speaker
text: Went from a Gen 1 UE Boom to this. Slightly less portable, but it blows away the UE Boom in every other category. Happy with it across the board.

title: Good little speaker. Hearty bass, and EQ can be adjusted for jazz and vocals.

title: works well mostly
text: There are a couple annoying things but it mostly works fine. Even if it's on and synced, when you start to play something it cuts off the first second or two. This is OK if you're watching longer videos or listening to music continuously but I also study languages and often the sample is too short to even register on something like memrise. Sound quality is good. It will sync to multiple devices but if it's connected and they both are trying to play something they will fight over who gets the speaker so sometimes you have to disconnect manually. For example, if I'm watching videos on my computer and my synced phone starts to play an ad on a game. Do not recommend using the on-board mic, everyone tells me they can't hear me if it accidentally/automatically gets used for teams calls.

title: Highly recommended
text: I orderd one of these two weeks ago and was impressed enough to buy another for stereo playback. I can't really assess battery life on these since I've only had them for a short time but the first one lasted maybe 6hrs at moderate to slightly loud volumes. Way better than my UE Megaboom. Bluetooth range is somewhat limited at around 12-15ft. Sound quality is better than that of the Megaboom as well. At high volumes however these things quickly become very strident so be prepared to play with the manual EQ function on your device. I'm using Soundcore app and it works fine but I couldn't imagine ever listening to these without bass boost or EQ as the treble on some music is way too hot. The speakers are easily recognized by my device. Stereo function twixt the two Motion+ is a breeze *even if I did have to go to YouTube for instructions because none were provided*. And after the initial connection the two speakers instantly connect to each other. In stereo mode these things, set about 6ft apart, image beautifully. And while volume increases with two of these, it isn't a 'doubling of output' as stated on their advertising, since double output power will only net you a 3db increase in total volume, but it's still significant compared to just one. After a few years of listening almost exclusively to one Bluetooth speaker at a time it's so cool to hear a stereo pair with such quality at this price point and portable too.

title: Solidly built, great sound, in a perfect package
text: I love this thing! First off, I think it looks good. I like that one can see the speakers through the grill, while feeling confident that said speakers are well protected, since themesh is metal not fabric. This will make wiping it down easier, too. I hate fabric speaker covers, they're dust magnets and a pain to clean. The sound: Remarkable! Especially for such a small sized unit. Honestly, it looks bigger in the photos, and it's the perfect size for any shelf or table. The sound is so crisp and clear, yet you can honestly feel the bass, and that's not even with the Bass boost enabled. The Soundcore app is easy to use and gives you access to an EQ mixer, as well as a range of presets. I use the EQ mixer, and you can clearly hear the difference as you adjust. It's also clearly well made. The unit feels hella solid and it's surprisingly heavy, which is a good thing! You're not likely to find great quality sound and quality construction in a plastic, lightweight speaker. This bad boy has a metal body and feels solid AF. My only knock would be that the control buttons on top of the unit are unlit, and the same color (black) as the rest of the unit, making it difficult to see which button is which. But this is really pretty minor, given that most of us will use the soundcore app or our music app, to adjust the controls instead of manually with the hard to read buttons. Also, once you learn which does what, it's a non-issue. I highly recommend this speaker for anyone who wants a high quality portable speaker with excellent sound-for-size/price. You cannot go wrong, and Anker is a quality company with excellent customer service, so you can buy with confidence.

title: Pleasantly surprised.
text: Wow. This sounds great. It easily outperforms similar products twice this price. I've heard great things about the Anker Soundcore line of products, and now I'm a fan.

title: Awesome quality.
text: This product is very solidly built and sounds great. I have several Anker products and I'm happy with all of them this one is really great.

title: Very interesting speaker...
text: This is a very interesting speaker. It is very bright and detailed. Compared to several others from Bose, Sony and JBL, it is much more refined. Many of the others I own now sound muddy. I love the Soundcore app. It works very well and makes a huge difference to the final sound. Highs are amazing. Mids are a bit overstated, and bass response is very accurate. This is not a Bose, JBL, or Sony with exaggerated boomy bass. If you want boomy, you may not be happy with this speaker. If you like to hear the high hats or tambourine for example, you will absolutely love this speaker. I love the fact that the focus on this speaker is the sound. No light show or crazy design, just a speaker that 100% focused on an accurate sound. It gets loud but it is not as loud as others have made me expect. It provides very similar volume to the JBL Charge 3 or the Sony XB30. Low volume provides a nice wide sound with good bass as well. To sum it up, if your taste is all about the bass, you may not be happy. I personally think there is excellent bass response, but there are many more powerful speakers out in the same price range, like the W-King, that really thump bass. None of these I have heard can compare in regards to overall sound in my opinion. Don’t get me wrong, this speaker cannot compete with my Harmon Kardon Go+ Play, but it is much cheaper and much more portable.

So If I am around 6 feet around the Motion+, its quite amazing, I could feel the music. BUT if you step outside of that zone - everything immediately dies down. The sound doesn't reach far. I had the speaker in one part of the room I was maybe 20ft away. I turned it up higher to hear it, but my wife was yelling at me to turn it down (she was near it) but I could barely hear it from my end. I walked up closer it was way louder. title: Big sound small speaker

title: A great computer speaker in Bluetooth clothing!
text: All the reviews were right.. - The speaker does not turn off and can be left plugged in (I don't use the Battery) - The speaker has great crossovers. The bass it can't handle is controlled so the speaker never sounds like it is going to die. Messes with the soundstage but soundstage is not what this is for. - Has a great soundstage. Sound is "wide" enough for the entire song. You will "see" the separation of the instruments and vocals with great recordings sound better than bad recordings. That is an impressive accomplishment at this pricing. - Ease of use of any of the top brands. Seem-less bluetooth and smart to grab the analog signal when plugged in and vice versa when phone reconnects. That is nice. - Made very well. Seems like it could travel and such although mine is perfect peaking through the bottom of my 2 monitors with no obstruction. - This is the perfect active speaker when desktop space is premium and you have 2 monitors. It fits quite nicely and seems made for it. - Bass will not shack the desk but the music is full and it sounds bigger than it is... once the volume is at 25%. So happy with the purchase. So thankful that Amazon has this available. I really have been looking for this solution for years. Hope you give it a try. Cheers!

title: Awesome!!

title: Worth Every Penny. Get two. Seriously. I should have.
text: edit (12/1/2020): The battery isn't holding the charge as long as it did while new, only getting around 6-8 hours at MEDIUM volume. The rest of my review stands... this speaker sounds amazing. I am impressed with it almost daily. I was thoroughly unimpressed initially. Then I adjusted the equalizer and WOW! Blown away. Impressive. Completely blows away my JBL Charge 3 with better mids, better highs and WAY better lows. For the price, I wish I had found this first. Wow, Anker. What you’ve done for this price is amazing. Update: More than a week in and the drivers are broken in nicely after mostly listening at low and medium volume. You can tell they’ve settled in because the bass is amazingly low and responsive as all heck. I’ve had the JBL Charge 3 for a year and the sounds never matured like this has. I’m blown away. It makes me WANT to listen to music. The highs, the mids and the lows all play well together, especially at volume. I want a second one in red now. Maybe if Anker wish to donate. ;) Adjust the EQ and be happy. Tip: as with most speakers, this beauty loves being in a corner or just near a wall. It ABSOLUTELY loves to be about 3 - 3.5ft (about 1m) off the floor. It produces sound much bigger than expected for size.

title: Great sound for the price

title: Outperforms more expensive wireless speakers
text: I bought two of these and paired them to get stereo. The red one was about $90, which is about $15-20 less than blue or black. The sound is incredible. I listen to all kinds of music, classical, classical vocal, classic rock, jazz, electronic, pop, etc. Regardless of the type of music, the Sound Cores+ perform beautifully. The voices on Pergolesi's Stabat Mater are clear with not a hint of strain in the high frequencies. Midrange frequencies are also rendered with accuracy and clarity, never sounding nasally or overwhelming the bass. The bass is tight and deep. Listen to the acoustic bass in the Diana Krall's Like Someone in Love. Overall a clear, accurate, and spacious sound. They show up much more expensive wireless speakers such as the Audioengine HD4. Overall the sound is astounding for small, wireless speakers. Unlike so many Bluetooth products, I gave yet to experience a drop in over 24 hrs of listening. An incredible value at the asking price. The only debit is pairing them for stereo sound. The manual isn't accurate about the colors of the Bluetooth light. It says it goes blank, but one stays white and the other stays blue. And it's a bit hard to know when they've paired. Regardless, they do pair flawlessly. The stereo sound stage is excellent. If you're in the market for reasonably priced, great sounding portable wireless speakers, try the Soundcore Motion+ out. You won't be disappointed.

text: I got this used from the Amazon warehouse for around $85. I also bought 2 Earfun Ubooms for $25 each (as it was on a sale and normal price is around $50). The sound quality of Anker Soundcore Motion+ is excellent. At first I thought I got a bad unit and probably that's why they returned it. However, after connecting to my Samsung S9+, downloading the app and updating the firmware the sound just changed dramatically. I don't use the bass button (which is basically the EQ setting with lows (bass) turned up all the way. I used my own custom EQ setting and the sound quality is on point for the price range. One thing to note was that initially it wouldn't connect to Windows 10. Follow these instructions and you should be able to do it, I was. The issue is that the device shows up as "other devices" and not an "audio device". 1) Delete the Soundcore speaker from Windows 10 device list. 2) Hold the Bluetooth button and Volume up + button for 5 seconds or so. 3) Wait for the Soundcore Motion+ to appear as a device. 4) Pair again and now it should work. This speaker has great sound quality, is well built, has features like app to fine tune performance, has plenty of bass and loudness, all for under $100. The only one feature that's missing is reverse charging and acting as a power bank for cellphones.

title: A projector for your pixel dreams
text: When I was a kid I had the opportunity to learn on PET computers, these big monsters with keyboards larger than their tiny green screens. The keys were solid and had a heavy tactile feel. Graphics were out of the question -- the only graphics were ASCII-based. But you could play some cool text-based role-playing games anyway. That sums up with Ditoo. The Ditoo works a lot like the other Divoom products in that it's a pixel-based screen. Any animation you can think of with pixels, you can recreate on the Ditoo. It's functionality is also similar: alarm clock, speaker, and social media notifications. You can just as easily use this as a replacement for your alarm clock if you're so inclined (if you're not already using your phone). That said, this is only as good as the content you put on it, and that requires the app. It's essentially a projector of sorts for your pixel dreams. With the addition of a lever -- I don't remember THAT on our PET machines!

title: Cute, Setup takes some getting used to

A lot of users create their own gifs so you won't have to figure it out. However, I wish the app search engine was a little more robust. It takes me a while to find gifs I like and searching for keywords is quite difficult. And I wish the setup was a little more user friendly. Also, I wish the start up volume matched the audio volume. I set my audio volume to only 1 bar (one above mute) but when I turn on the device, the volume is at full blast which is annoying. Other than that, a great buy. Hopefully you can get it on sale or get a coupon. The speaker is great quality and well built. Battery life is meh (depending on brightness, volume setting and if you're playing audio or not.)

text: The lil Ditoo packs a lot of value in a small package. Good sound and large array of applications. Device available in several colors. The Divoom phone app offers Design, Animations, Text Editor, Pixel Coloring, DJ Mixer, Voice Memo, Chat, Alarm, Sleep Time, Planner, Games, Stopwatch, Celebration Days, Countdown Meter, Noise Meter, Scoreboard, Notifications, Weather, Voice Commands, Internet Radio, and a clock. App is easy to use to create 16x16, 32x32, or 64x64 pictures or animations (note - the Ditoo can only display 16x16). Upload to a community of users - download the shared designs or use them as inspiration to create your own. My favorite apps are the Sleep Timer with 24 white noise options, Noise Meter, and Internet Radio. This includes a handful of games that can be controlled from the Ditoo or from your phone. I do find the controls on the Ditoo itself a little unwieldy, but can also control from your phone. Overall a solid choice - I would purchase again.

title: Great Bluetooth Speaker at Reasonable Price
text: I bought this speaker for use in my office. I mostly listen to classical music, but sometimes other things, depending on the time of day. The speaker sounds great for acoustic stuff, like classical guitar, but playing Elton John at higher volume also sounded pretty great. I took it home where I could play it at a higher volume and listened to a symphony with my wife and kid. My kid continued to play with his blocks and did not seem enthusiastic. Then again, he's only 8 months old. My wife, on the other hand, could not believe how good this speaker sounded. The only downsides seem to be inherent problems with any speaker like this. There is very little separation because the size of the unit is small. Also, while the low end sounds good, it obviously lacks the oomph you'd get from a real speaker set with a powerful amplifier driving much larger speakers. Until someone figures out how to hack physics, that's completely normal and not at all a defect in this speaker. Finally, although it claims to be waterproof (to an extent), I have not tested it, and do not plan to. The buttons all appear to be sealed, and the charging port has a tight-fitting rubberized cover. While I can't say for sure how waterproof it is, I will be taking this on trips to the beach and will not really be worrying much about sand, random splashes, or rain.

text: [[VIDEOID:83b10e5b0e120bdb0ddb07776117ab4a]] When opening the Tribit XBoom packaging, my initial reaction was that the XBoom is a solidly built speaker and it’s suited for rugged environments. It’s also waterproof, so you can take it by the pool. There’s a USB cable and silicone carrying strap included as well. Rugged good looks don’t matter without pleasing sound. What I really like about this manufacturer is, they listen to their customers. There’s a reviewer on YouTube, clavinetjunkie, who’s an audiophile. He gave this company some recommendations to tweak the sound signature of the speaker. You now have a great sounding omnidirectional speaker. The XBoom sounds fantastic, to go along with it’s rugged functional looks. I recorded a short video clip, with non copyrighted music called “Fade” by Alan Walker. This may not be the best quality, since it’s a phone recording, but it gives you an idea of the nice bass the speaker has. The speaker was placed on the floor while recording. I also posted a few photos as well. Hope this helps. ***** UPDATE after several days of usage: Battery life has been excellent. Build quality is awesome. Nothing cheap looking about this speaker. Sound is well balanced and not boomy. By boomy, I mean a one note boom that overwhelms the sound. I own a JBL Charge 2 and it has that boomy sound, that detracts from overall sound signature. The treble of this speaker has sparkle and the bass is there, but does not dominate the sound. The speaker is omnidirectional, so it functions better placed in the middle of a room. This way the sound is projected in all directions, as you move around. If you listen to XBoom in your room, you can adjust the speaker so one side is pointing in your direction. With this speaker, it’s important how you place it in your specific listening environment. ******Update #2: I got another XBoom and used the daisy chain feature, where you can connect multiple speakers. It’s a simple process to connect the additional speakers. You can then place the speakers in different locations to expand the reach of your music. Really cool feature.

text: I bought this to use on my patio to do workouts in my pool or relax in my hot tub. title: Great Speaker, Better Customer Service
text: I've been through a handful of Bluetooth speakers and did hours of research before landing on this gem. I'm a self proclaimed audiophile on a budget (aka not at all), so I look for audio quality at the best value and I have find THE speaker. I listen to a wide variety of music, but most of the music I listen to requires close listening with balanced audio. I want the frequency to be flat, the highs to be clear, and the low end to have punch, even at lower volumes. This speaker checks all of those boxes. I have two, one for home and travel and another at the office. Obviously at the office I can't be bumping music like I'm in an abandoned warehouse so it's important that I get good sound quality at lower volumes which is rare to find in speakers in general, let alone a budget Bluetooth one. The two drawbacks are higher volume and battery life. This speaker is loud enough for a small get together, but not loud enough to be played to multiple people outdoors who are all talking, but I knew this already. The battery life unfortunately is shorter than the advertised length, but that only means that it lasts as long as the average speaker that I've owned, so also not a big issue. The customer service though.. I contacted Tribit several times with what I assume are very niche problems. Not only did I receive timely responses, I continued this correspondence until my issues were resolved. Fantastic speaker and company. If they created a higher tier speaker, I would buy it in a heartbeat.

title: Great but could be excellent with a few refinements
text: I'm going to echo many of the comments already posted here. Sound quality isn't as good as Bose SoundLink but it gets close for less than 1/3rd the price, and this unit is built to take a beating, unlike the Bose. I'm surprised and impressed with its sound and volume abilities, gonna be great for while I'm working outside with tools running. Compact, heavier than expected but feels rock solid. The ability to charge a battery while on AC power would have been nice but no biggie to me. Where I think DeWalt came up a little short is there could have been onboard cord storage for AC or at least a phone charge cord, it should have a nutsert in the bottom so it can be attached to a camera or laser tripod, and depending on what battery is used my phone can slip out the back end of the tray, which has a waterfall edge. I glued some semi-sticky drawer lining material in that tray so the phone wouldn't slide as easily. Waterproof would have been a plus too for taking it out boating and on sand bars. I have a BT unit about the same price as this one that's waterproof, floats and can be tripod mounted but it doesn't have this sound quality or volume.

It has decent volume and doesn't get too distorted at full blast. The BT range is where it shines. This box is designed so that you can connect to your phone and keep it on you while you work around the shop. I don't like having to abandon my phone to have tunes while I'm working. What I don't like... I wish it were louder. It's intended for a shop environment so it really can't be too loud. A few more watts would be good. As I mentioned above the full volume does start to distort a bit depending on the source audio. I know it wasn't advertised, but I had hopes... it'd be nice if it could charge a battery while on AC power.

title: Very Good Bluetooth Option
text: The best part about the DEWALT 20V MAX Bluetooth Speaker was connecting it. Setup was a breeze and it connected to my iPhone instantly. I mostly use it in our garage and generally play Pandora from my iPhone. I've used it on our back patio a few times as well. The sound is good, not great, but good. It doesn't have as much base as I'd like, but it does sound nice and is plenty loud. The wireless range is very good as well. I’ve walked at least 100 feet away with no dropouts. Most of the time I have it plugged in, but I have run it for several hours on a DeWalt 18v battery. Afterwards I've checked the LED charge indicator light on the battery and it still shows fully charged, so this unit seems to draw very little power. I've charged my iPhone via the DeWalt's USB port and it worked fine. I like that it's very portable, doesn't weigh a lot and seems very rugged. It doesn't look or sound like a high-end, audiophile Bluetooth speaker that'll impress your friends, but it's a great option if that's not important to you. If you're not concerned about pulsing bass and just want an easy to set up and listen to speaker for your smart phone, this is a great option. Recommended. 👍

title: Great- If you don't care about the sound quality or your money.
text: Look, I get it, it's a job site speaker, I have one, and if you are just listening to talk radio or the news, it's fine. For anything else, it really just sounds like shit- it's extremely flat throughout the entire frequency spectrum. Nothing pops- no highs, no mids, no lows. It's just blah. Even if you are using Spotify or something, and you EQ it out as best you can, it really just sounds fairly bad. The speakers are garbage, plain and simple. You'd be better off with an Amazon Echo and a battery, because the difference in sound quality would be exponentially better. I guess the reason people like this is because it's yellow, and you can use DEWALT batteries. Woohoo. That just means you have a $100 battery sitting in a $100 (shit) radio, instead of in your $2-300 tool, making you money at a job site. This makes sense how? I can get a $100 BT speaker that has a built in battery that will play all day and sound far better, and for $200, since that's really what you have invested if you are using a DEWALT battery, I can get something that would absolutely destroy this thing. (Too bad I wasn't thinking like this when I saw it Lowes and bought it) On the positive side, the battery life with 20V LiPo batteries is great (I mean, duh, why wouldn't it be?), and you can bang it around, and it's water resistant, and it will charge your phone with the USB port/cable while you are streaming to it- but obviously you have to leave your phone there. It does have a headphone jack, so you can plug something like your ancient phone into it- but again, that means your phone is tethered to the speaker. You still aren't going to hear it over hammering, air compressors, or heavy machinery running at a job site. I just think you'd be better served with something else, like a good pair of headphones.

To make that worse, it will beep at you every 10? minutes to let you know it's looking to pair with a device until you manually turn it off. It's actually quite annoying. Re-pairing to my phone after my wife's phone was connected is an ordeal. Putting it in pairing mode doesn't just allow me to connect to it. I have to first Forget the device from my Bluetooth settings, then since the device doesn't show up in my iPhone's list of bluetooth devices in pairing mode, I have to turn off bluetooth, turn on bluetooth, wait for it to show up, then connect. Doing this every time we want to stream from a different device? Forget about it. Strangest Bluetooth experience I've ever had.

Yet, when my podcast doesn't run on weekends, by Monday battery is totally dead even if it got a full charge on the previous Thursday and it was run for only 20 minutes on Friday. I honestly can't recommend getting this speaker. Stupid me got the carrying case too. UPDATE (Feb. 2, 2019) After seeing my review, Anker contacted me. Their reps went out of their way to help me and ended up replacing my speaker. New speakers works just fine. Super happy. My updated rating (from 2 to 4) is for their customer service. However, I would much prefer that Anker has better quality control. I always buy their brand, but more than once, I've had issues with devices not working. title: A good compact stereo bluetooth speaker
text: I own the A3143 Premium Stereo Bluetooth speaker (2x10W=20W) which sounds great, but it doesn't have a microphone or the longer battery life of this lower-cost A3102 SoundCore speaker (2x3W=6W). The features and sound characteristics are different, but which is the better choice depends on personal preference. To me based on sound quality alone, the A3143 wins hands down. The bass is stronger (more power is required to drive the lower frequencies than the higher frequencies), but I also find overall frequency response to be more balanced and accurate for instruments and vocals. For either speaker, I'd recommend using an EQ app to set the frequency response and spatial effects to your preference (I use Bass EQ from Coocent). Interestingly, the maximum volume level for both the A3143 and this A3102 SoundCore are about the same. The A3102 has a brighter sound overall. The A3102 is good as a general purpose speaker, and it is excellent to use with a cell phone. The A3102 microphone (which the A3143 doesn't have) and speaker quality for voice calling are crisp and clear. My dad who can't hear very well often could not understand me on my cell phone handset or its speakerphone, but had no problem when I used the A3102. So for long battery life, good overall music speaker, and particularly for use as a microphone/speakerphone for voice calls, A3102 is a good choice. For best music reproduction, the A3143. For either, Anker's quality and customer support are among the best in the industry.

text: I bought this speaker for use in my office and have only one complaint: it's a little too loud at the lowest setting on my iPhone. The sound on this little speaker is very good. It's a small speaker - don't expect deep bases and great range. But for a portable little speaker, the sound is great. The sound is not "tinny." I wouldn't call it "rich" either, though. It is very good for the size and price of this speaker. Battery life is awesome. Helping battery life is the auto-off, which is great since this is something I typically forget. Biggest complaint is the volume control. Because this is on my desk at work, I generally don't want it overly loud. The lowest volume when controlled from my iPhone, though, is still a little too loud at times. For whatever reason, I can only go down to volume level two on the iPhone when paired with this speaker; at level one, the volume cuts out entirely. I have tried turning the speaker around and turning its face down on the desk to lower the volume but those have drawbacks too. So, if you want a portable speaker for what most people want out of it -- volume -- it's great. If you're looking for a speaker that has good volume control on the low-end, this one may not be for you.

title: Competes directly with Bose SoundLink Mini Bluetooth Speaker II, for a fraction of the price.
text: Anker's speaker seems to have been designed to directly compete with Bose SoundLink Mini Bluetooth Speaker II. Do a search on Amazon with this ASIN: B00WK47VEW. I've critically listened to both devices. I'm really impressed that Anker has put Bose to shame for their ridiculous price. It's astounding how alike these two high-quality devices sound over a full range of music types and volume. Pairing with the device was easy, and the connection has remained rock-solid for hours and hours. Anker has created a personal speaker that can fill a small room with quality sound, that's for sure. There are no boomy/rumbling lows or thin/grating highs. What a delightful surprise. Also, Amazon's Alexa Dot sounds mighty sweet when paired to this speaker. It would really be great if Anker and Amazon could work out a bundle price for the pair.

But it has great durability. I have an 11 month old who loves music, so I let him carry it around while music is playing and even with his slobber, there isn't any water damage or anything. title: It's a Sound Purchase
text: Like an idiot I spilled a glass of wine right into my Echo dot and now it sounds like it's underwater. Rather than taking the time to rip apart the Dot to clean it out, and since I was looking for an inexpensive Bluetooth speaker already, I purchased the Anker SoundCore speaker. Right out of the box, this Anker speaker feels really solid. I am not sure, but it seems to be built from metal and hardened rubber. The instructions that come with it are minimal, but after about 10 minutes I was able to decipher it in its entirety. Basically, I pressed "on" button for a couple of seconds to turn it on, then through my Alexa app, I paired my Dot with it. Took all of 1 minute tops. The sound from this speaker is very good for the price. My kids have a Bose Soundlink Mini Bluetooth speaker and that sounds incredible compared to this Anker. However the Bose costs about $200 and should sound better. For the price of this Anker, the sound is quite acceptable. The highs are present and there is just enough bass to feel it. It won't rattle the windows, but it is great for the price point. I pumped the volume up to the max on the speaker and on the Dot and had no distortion whatsoever. The sound remained clean, clear, and quite loud. If you don't need the top of the line sound, I highly recommend this. I use it mainly for audiobooks, news, etc. So this works perfectly for me. But this is still great for listening to music as well.

title: Lack of useful instructions and failure to connect via Bluetooth
text: I'll be the first to admit that Bluetooth and me have a rocky relationship. I have owned many an Apple Bluetooth keyboard and mouse and have always had more than my fair share of connection difficulties. This might make sense if it was just one computer or one phone, but I have 2 iPhones and 3 Apple computers. 2 iMacs and on Mac Mini. The Anker SoundCore was discoverable on one iMac computer but none of the other devices. The one iMac would not play thru the Anker SoundCore speaker since it seemingly doesn't work with Spotify wirelessly. Only via audio cable. I already have nice speakers tethered to my iMac. The whole reason for the Anker SoundCore was to take my tunes into the bathroom while I shower and shave, in my garage when I'm working on cars or projects, or by my pool. It's also possible that I didn't hold the various buttons for the prescribed number of seconds or in the right prescribed order, but when the "Getting Started" instructions give such comprehensive detail (being facetious) in setting up and using this confounding piece of tech that seems to have more in common with a puzzle than a Bluetooth speaker, I am Audi5000, baby!

title: I've never owned a portable speaker with such good battery life
text: Out of every portable device I have owned, speaker or otherwise, everything is great until the battery runs out and you're stuck charging the device for the next couple of hours. My Anker Speaker mostly live sin my kitchen, and is probably playing for a couple of hours most nights of the week (at probably around 1/2 volume since that can be a factor in determining power draw). I have probably had to charge my speaker less than once a month in the past 3-4 months. I charged it once in September, and once in mid December, and given by my bluetooth battery indicator its hovering right around 70% right now. I swear by the battery life of this speaker above all other features, its always surprising after weeks and weeks of off/on use when I see the little red light blink indicating its low on battery. Another related detail, I have owned my speaker for roughly 3 years now, having bought it just when I started college in 2016. Even after all this time, it has no signs of faulting and continues to be my most reliable electronic device I own. Oh and sound quality is good too, much better base than any speaker I have had up until this point. Even still, it can sound a little bit "mid - heavy", especially at a slight distance, so I'm sure if you were an audiophile you would find something not to like about it. For a casual listener like myself however, its been a phenomenal little speaker that I can't recommend enough.

title: LOVE IT!! Fantastic sound!!
text: LOVE LOVE LOVE this wireless Bluetooth portable speaker. The sound is much clearer and more powerful than the 3 others I tried, including the Bose Soundlink Revolve Plus which sells for $250+. Regarding the term "portable" - this speaker is larger and heavier than most portable speakers on the market, and I do NOT use it outside. For my needs, which is to have great-sounding music in any room, within the confines of my apartment, it is perfect. While it is not multi-directional sound, like the Bose Soundlink Revolve+, the sound quality is so superior, it renders that feature unimportant. For now, I have one of the HK Onyx Studio 4 wireless speakers, but I plan to buy another one, and two will link together to give true stereo sound. Still, even with just one, it is fantastic. The only small criticism I have is the way the volume buttons are difficult to locate/see. It requires good light and/or "feeling around" for them on the top of the speaker to find them. My fix: I set the speaker's volume up to the highest level, and then use my iPhone (or my laptop, if I'm paired to that) to control the volume - which works very well.

title: Good quality sound in a portable package
text: I went on a trip aboard a small cruise ship last year and they had the Onyx 3 onboard for us to use... was impressed with it then whether on the ship or on any of the small islands we visited. Again, recently I stayed in a nice hotel in Singapore whose suites had the Onyx 3 in them, and that did it for me. It just sounded so good. So I bought the successor, the Onyx 4. Though I had some minor concerns about this being a knock-off, given the good price, it sure seems to be the genuine article in every way, from packaging to documentation to (most importantly) performance. Sounds terrific, syncs up effortlessly, and even came with several different plugs to use, which is great for me since I live overseas. The adapter itself is universal voltage, which I knew, but didn't expect the bonus of four different plugs being included, which precludes the need to use a plug adapter. The plugs included were North American, European 2-pin, UK 3-pin, and Australian angled 2-pin. I've been very pleased with the sound quality and battery life. With two woofers and two tweeters, plus good porting, the Onyx 4 delivers nice bass and excellent room-filling sound overall, in a portable unit (weighs about 2kg/4.5 lbs). There are so many Bluetooth speakers out there, it's hard to know which is the 'best', but the HK Onyx 4 sure does a fine job for my needs.

text: I saw this at Best Buy at around $450. I was worried this would be a knock-off at $148. So worried that I registered the product before I even took it out of the box for a test run. Once it was charged, I was able to pair it with my Amazon Echo Dot (2nd gen). Sound quality is superb, very crisp and clear. The power light glows a steady white when it is on and fully charged. There are two buttons for volume up and volume down. Battery lasted over 5 hours so far at medium volume. My understanding is the louder the volume, the shorter the battery life. Also, when the power light starts blinking rapidly, it means it's time to recharge the battery. Also, I was told to ALWAYS use the power cord and charger that came with the speaker to recharge the speaker. Do not just used any charging cable you happen to find.

title: Sound quality is fine, but not exceptional.
text: I liked the idea of a surround sound speaker that rests on one's shoulders. The plastic speaker yoke is fairly comfortable and light. It would be somewhat in the way if I was doing exercises involving lifting my arms a lot. There is a speaker just behind and in front of each ear. I believe there is a microphone located on the front inner right side. The controls are on the front outside right of the yoke, and it's easy to feel the difference between the buttons. There are four buttons: a power button, a plus button, a minus button, and a mode button. Below these buttons is the USB port for the power cord and a slot for a SD memory card. The mode button allows you to select between playing a Bluetooth connection, the memory card, or FM radio. The plus or minus buttons control the sound volume or skip songs (previous/next). Charging is done with a USB cord, and an LED light indicates when charging is done. Charging only takes an hour or two. The sound quality is okay, but not exceptional. The bass sounds fine, but it doesn't sound truly low. It wasn't difficult to pair the speakers with Bluetooth on my smart phone or computer, but there's a static sound that comes out of the speakers when playing music or listening to audiobooks. I don't hear the same static sound when using Bluetooth headphones so I assume it's these speakers. I was disappointed that the sound quality wasn't better, but it is nice to sometimes listen to music while being mobile without having headphones on.

title: Suprisingly Decent, with a few flaws, made me want a Bose
text: My expectations for this was pretty low, but it ended up sounding surprisingly decent, not incredible, but not bad. The build and materials of the device is sturdy, but cheap looking and feeling. Buttons and ports all seem a bit cheap, but nothing has broken yet. Bluetooth functions well, range is about average, battery life is good. It stays on fairly well if I do not move too much, but it will shift around a bit when on the rowing machine. Has USB C, that was surprising with such a cheap device. It has a few irritating flaws, it is always triggering the assistant on my tablet, because the assistant button on the device is the power button, so If the power button is held down to power off the device it will trigger the assistant first. Also putting a built in radio on a device like this is just stupid, it would have to have an antenna to even work and who uses a radio anymore anyway? Sometimes I accidentally press the mode button and get blasted by radio static. I never tried to use the SD card, so no comment on that. Overall I recommend it if you want to try out this style of device, it is surprisingly usable. It really made me want to try out the Bose, but I can't afford a $200 speaker right now.

title: Good value for the money, could have a better user interface.
text: Pleasantly surprised that the FM radio reception is better than my 3M work headphone radio. The sound quality is OK, fair for music, good for voice (talk radio). Bending over and moving around a lot, they can and will fall off, but so far they have survived every fall. My biggest disappointment is that it takes too many steps to turn on the radio. (1) long press of the power button. (2) comes up in blue tooth mode, one short button press of mode button to switch to FM. (3) Radio comes in loud, long press on volume down/radio tuning button to decrease the volume to a reasonable level. Doesn't sound like much, but after a while it seems tedious. I also wish that the a long press was not needed to adjust the volume up or down. An accidental short press will change the radio station -- an annoyance. For me, I want to adjust the volume a lot more often than change the radio station. What would be nice, of course, is if this gadget remember the last mode and volume setting when you turn it back on. At least it remembers the last radio station.

With this collar and the speakers directly under each ear, she is able to hear and understand so much better. I did need a blue tooth adapter to plug in to the TV. But I needed it for the speaker I bought previously too and was able to use the same one. I'm not sure if all TVs would need one. But my TV is not very new. This has helped her hear better and made being in the room with her more enjoyable for the rest of us. This is a GREAT product. I would have given it 5 stars except there is a slight delay in the sound compared to the sound coming directly from the TV which makes it annoying to use the TV speaker for anyone else at the same time Mom is using this speaker collar. But overall this was a great solution for the my elderly mother watching TV with other people nearby and it was a great price/value.

The v4 fits in better and takes up less space than the v3 did, so it's perfect for a computer desk where you may not be able to mount it or have a lot of space to place it. The light ring on the bottom is less intrusive at night than the the light ring placed on top of the v3. I'm not crazy about the look of the design, but it's got its high points. The rest is just like the v3. They're both great devices regardless. However, it's better to buy the v4 because the support for it will last longer. title: Nothing but praise
text: For the price, I doubt you can do any better than the Soundbox XL. It's the second one I bought. The first one still works just fine (about 1 1/2 years old). But I purchased this second one for my wife. I love good, deep bass. Of course, that's a challenge for small speakers. But the sub-woofer with the XL valiantly tries hard to pump out the low notes, and usually does well. I've had zero problems with both units. The one caveat I have is this: They do vibrate when being played loudly and will dance across hard surfaces. So be careful in that regard. Still...even though the first one I bought fell off some tabletops a few times...it still works fine. Oh yes...one more thing...the TF / SD card is a great feature. I don't think I'd consider another bluetooth speaker that didn't have one. I enthusiastically recommend the Soundbox XL.

title: Coming from a serious sound snob.....
text: Update March 2020: I ordered the "Newer version" of the SoundBox XL... (the SoundBox Pro)....... and immediately sent it back. The numbers and description made it look like that one was better............ but, hearing it first hand.... I sent it back. So I ordered this one again (the SoundBox XL).... and I can't wait to get it. ********* Update... Feb 2020 - I just need to say........ 2 days ago, my beautiful speaker that I loved so much (yes, this Doss one...) fell off my desk and the quality immediately dropped to a fraction of what it was............. So I re-ordered, got it today, and I noticed that the amazon box was a bit banged up........ and my first thought was.... if my first speaker took one dive onto the ground and then wasn't usable anymore for me................. WHY WASN'T THIS AMAZON BOX LABELED "FRAGILE"??.... So.... I opened it up........ turned it on........ and immediately knew I needed to send it back. Moral of the story........ If your Doss speaker doesn't sound incredible right out of the box.......... I'm willing to bet it hit the ground too hard at some point on it's delivery to you............... because my first one..... lol I can't even believe how much I appreciated the sound quality from it........... Maybe needless to say, I have to return this one. ********************* July 2019 I love this speaker. I've been through so many speakers and headphones, it really is ridiculous........ but high quality, bass bumping, crystal clear sound is one of the most important things in the world to me....... And I'm very happy with this speaker. I also bought the DOSS Traveler....... and though that one is radically different (I mean... it's a LOT smaller...).... I use my big one to play music, and my baby one to play podcasts....... at the same time........ so I get the best of both worlds. I'm learning while listening to music that makes me happy. If you're really picky about high-quality sound that will make you MOVE though...... definitely get the big one instead of the travel version. I'm very happy with this brand, and both speakers.

title: Incredible low frequency response for a Bluetooth speaker
text: I've tested many Bluetooth speakers from Sony, Cambridge soundworks, and anker, and have listened many demos of speakers online recorded with binaural microphones and the only other speaker with comparable sub-bass range is the Harman kardon onyx studio 4,which costs twice as much and is arguably less capable than this speaker. This speaker has been tested to produce audible sub-bass down to 20-ish hz. As for personal taste i prefer a brighter eq tuning that makes midrange and vocals more prominent but i wouldn't say this speaker has suppressed midrange.It has a neutral tuning which should appeal to more people. And in any case one can download an eq app to change the characteristics. I just don't find those apps convenient and i wish Bluetooth speakers would provide the eq functionality in the speakers themselves accessible from a smartphone app. But none do so that's not a criticism of this speaker. The only downside of this speaker is the tradeoff for deeper sub bass, it's bigger and heavier than a truly portable Bluetooth speaker. You can't haveboth ways though and i think most people will prefer err on the side of better audio quality. Highly recommended, but first test the speaker at Oluv's Gadgets (you have to use headphones!). Disclaimer: i have no affiliation with oluv's site, but you absolutely have to know about it if you're looking at Bluetooth speakers (in fact, i don't like his reviews. he's a pseudo-audiophile with imo poor taste in music and a huge bias for bass-boosted speakers, but his speaker comparison tool is just oustanding). Another disclaimer is that I tend to listen to these speakers at low to moderate volume with only one or two people in the room. I haven't tested them for party use or at max volume. In summary, i would recommend this speaker to someonewho misses having an audio system with subwoofer but doesn't have the space or budget for that and is not looking to blast the volume of their music.

title: Boom boom boom
text: [[VIDEOID:3876182f7d75736f3c756ffed2d78b3]] This box has quite a bit going for it. I think it fair to focus on the pros and cons of this unit. Pros, Searching for bass from a portable speaker? Search no more, this has more Bass than any of the multitude of portable speakers I've ever heard or owned. Low distortion, even nearing Max volume. No rattles or buzzes except to the objects laying around it, (sincerely, it shakes the entire king size bed I own like a built-in bed massage) Simple to use. Good BT, with decent range. As you increase volume, it digs in its heels and pushes even harder instead of just distorting like most other units. Well constructed, the positive click on the buttons is a nice bonus, very tactile. The entire unit has a solid look and feel. No matter the volume level it produces excellent bass, so you can listen to it on low but still get the feel for the music as the punch is still there. Cons, Heavy on the mid-range, and you will need an equalizer to help tweak that out, a picture of the equalizer settings I use attached. Heavy as a brick, (and larger too) Battery life is short, adding an additional 18650 battery would help here tremendously. But this is to be expected considering the amount of bass and pure volume it produces, you got to put some juice in to get some sound out, and the 2200 milliamp hour battery could really use some help. It needs a little space to sing, it can easily fill a typical room with sound and Bass, it's awfully loud in a more confined space. That being said the unit is designed for bass lovers, it works well across all spectrums of music but is geared more towards Rock/Hip Hop thumping music, but it's still plays all other styles very well. You should buy it, I have paid a heck of a lot more for far more inferior products, it belts out far more bass and volume then even the higher end units.

text: This small unit puts quality sound out there well beyond its size, and if you buy a single unit, it connects simply to any Bluetooth. Just pair it to a phone or computer, and it works after you've pressed the Bluetooth button on the speaker. But … if you're impressed enough to get a second speaker to hear all in stereo, you'll need some advice, which you'll not get from Ultimate Ears. Do not first connect one or both speakers to your phone and then later connect them to your computer to test things out because the speakers have a tiny little brain and seem to remember what they've been connected to in the past and get confused when Bluetooth pairings have been left on. To connect the speakers to your phone, remove all other Bluetooth connections to the speakers. Play music on your phone. Switch one speaker ON (it becomes the master speaker … consider marking it somehow), and ensure the other is OFF. Pair this speaker to your phone by pressing the Bluetooth button on the master speaker. It should fire up. Now switch ON the second (slave) speaker. To connect the slave speaker to the master, press the '+' and Bluetooth buttons simultaneously on the 'master' for 5 secs or so until the master says 'tum-tum-tum' and its Bluetooth light flashes, which says I am ready to pair. Now press the Bluetooth button twice fairly quickly on the slave speaker… like click.click not click ….. click (if it pairs with the master, its Bluetooth light should flash … if not … double press the slave speaker's Bluetooth button again). When its Bluetooth button flashes, leave the slave speaker alone. It will connect in 10 secs or so. If you switch a paired computer on while playing from your phone, the music will stop because the computer screws up the Bluetooth connection between the phone and the speaker, and the speaker becomes confused. If confused switch both speakers off, disconnect Bluetooth pairings that are not needed, and repeat the process.

title: The BEST portable bluetooth speaker for your money...
text: WOW. First, I was very impressed with the sound quality right out of the box. Crystal clear and no distortion even at max volume. Take it a step further, the app has tuning capability to tailor your speaker to your use...this is where I was floored. Adjusting the base, mid, treble were extremely easy and if you are a novice or a tuner scares you, they have built-in listening profiles for you to chose from to take that fear of not knowing what you are doing, away. The 360 degree sound actually emits very very saturating sound no matter where you are in reference to the speaker. I previously had a Big Jambox for 7 years and it was great with 360 degree sound. This MegaBoom 3 beats the Big Jambox in my opinion. The app is very lite, super simple and allows you to change the name of your speaker...customization to you. The battery life blew me away. I charged it to 100% and left music on 3 nights in a row, 6-8 hours at a time and the app displayed 42% battery life. Truly 30+ hours of continuous battery life in this small and sleek speaker. Charging is a breeze and quick. The ONLY thing I didn't like about this speaker is the Micro-USB charging port/cable. It really needs to be USB-C with today's technology. Maybe -.1 star lol. The look, feel and design are all gorgeous. It doesn't weigh a lot, its super compact and portable. I bought the carrying case for protection and travel...I suggest you do the same so it lasts and looks great for many years. Bottom Line: Spend the little extra on the MegaBoom 3, you will not be disappointed!!!

title: The Megaboom isn't kidding - this thing packs a punch!
text: The Ultimate Ears Megaboom isn't kidding - this thing packs a punch! At just nine inches tall, this speaker has a voice as big as my larger (non-portable) table speaker. And it isn't just loud - it's got a deep, delicious sound that hits all the notes. It's simple and easy to use and waterproof, so I am not nervous using it around the tub, pool and while cooking (ever spilled wine on a speaker? Not good). And it floats! USE There's a little trap door in the back where you plug the speaker in to charge, three buttons on the top that you can access by feel, and two volume buttons on the front. There's also a little nylon ring where you can hook this speaker up or hang it. It's really pretty simple to use. The power button doubles as a navigation button and then there's the Bluetooth button. Charging is pretty straightforward, but you can also buy a dock for the Megaboom so you don't even have to deal with lifting the flap and plugging it in. Connecting a device is easy, it takes seconds. SOUND Oh my - the sound is impressive. Clear on the highs, rich in the middle, delicious bass. For a portable speaker, I was blown away. It easily fills by 10-foot ceiling rooms. Outdoors it can get a little lost if you are in a loud area, but that's to be expected. You can "party" the speaker up, so you can easily amp up the sound if you need. RANGE Range is pretty great. I can go anywhere in my home without losing signal, and even out into the yard. BATTERY Around the house, I use this a few hours a day and charge it once a week. I get probably 20 hours on one charge with the volume in the middle. Once you turn this all the way up,I only get about 4 hours. Charging is fairly quick, I have juiced it back up in an hour. APP The app is easy to use, it has a little EQ and the utility to connect (Party Up) the speaker to other speakers. The app works like it should and is intuitive. I'm super impressed with this speaker. Unless you are listening on full volume, it lasts a long time, sounds great and is totally portable.

title: "Auto Off" Can Be Disabled!
text: I was looking for a good bluetooth speaker to go with my Echo Dot. One tech article I read about this Bose speaker stated that the speaker would turn itself off unless the Dot was connected to it via an aux cable. Before I ordered this speaker I contacted Bose in order to find out if the "Auto Off" could be neutralized. Bose told me to press and hold the Bluetooth and Volume + buttons at the same time. A voice will prompt and confirm the auto off setting is now off. To reinstate Auto Off hold the same buttons down and the speaker will tell you that Auto Off is reinstated. These directions are not included with the speaker. I ordered this Bose Sound Link Mini Bluetooth Speaker II and found the auto off directions to work beautifully. I LOVE THIS SPEAKER! The sound is wonderful. It hooked up easily through the Alexa app to my Echo Dot, and we had clear lovely sounding music playing Christmas Eve night and Christmas morning. Since the Dot and this speaker do not need to be attached to each other I can move the speaker all over the house. I leave the speaker sitting on its charging base all the time and have not had any adverse reactions. When completely depleted of power the battery took about a couple of hours to recharge. I did not have to reset any of its settings other than to make sure the Bluetooth was on, and then tell the Dot to reconnect -- easy. If you are even just a semi-audiophile I think you will really like/love this little speaker.

The Bose also has a premium feel to it, being made of slick metal rather than plastic which also gives it a bit of heft. I found the "voice" which tells you the charge level and the device it's connected to pretty annoying after a while, but I'm sure there are others out there that would appreciate this feature. I also didn't care for the mushy feeling buttons up top, I felt like they could break easily if someone put too much pressure on them. Unfortunately, mine stopped working properly after only two months. It wouldn't turn on unless it was connected to its charging cradle, even if it had a full charge. That kind of defeats the purpose of it being portable. I called Amazon and they were great, letting me return the speaker.
