title: Bose Soundlink Mini 1 vs Mini 2: Mini 1 is still he Clear Winner!
text: I've been a very happy owner of the Bose Soundlink mini 1 for a couple of years now, so when a nephew asked for it, I decided it was time for an upgrade to the Mini 2. Though I had seen a couple of Youtube reviews that noted the noticeable inferior sound quality of the Mini 2, given the new features (longer battery life for one), I decided to purchase the Mini 2 from Amazon. To my big disappointment, it was immediately noticeable that the Mini 2's sound quality was inferior to the Mini 1. I'm not an audiophile, but having been used to the Mini 1, it was a big letdown. On the same day, I ordered the Mini 1 from Amazon. When the Mini 1 came, I played them both from the same set of Spotify songs. The Mini 1 was clearly superior, specifically the depth of the bass at lower volumes. I would have wanted to keep the Mini 2 with its new features, but to me, it was too big a letdown that I decided to keep the Mini 1. I cannot imagine why Bose would redesign the Soundlink Mini 1 and sacrifice sound quality, which is why it was the best bluetooth speaker in the first place. The Mini 1 probably still is. My recommendation: If you haven't owned a Mini 1, you could go for the Mini 2. If you've owned a Mini 1 -- don't go for a Mini 2, you will be disappointed. Clearly people are still buying the Mini 1. It is still priced at about a $5 discount from the Mini 2!

text: This little speaker is really rather remarkable. As a matter of fact when you consider the size and sound output it isn't so much a speaker as a sound machine. Room filling sound...? I would say maybe. Depends on the song or style of music you're listening to. Heavy bass lines get muted some...diluted. Jazz, classical, new age, ambient...do very well. Heavy rock, not so much. I have found the Samsung[[ASIN:B016DG1YKO Samsung WAM1500/ZA Radiant 360 R1 Wi-Fi/Bluetooth Speaker]] does a very credible job of recreating rock music with driving bass lines and melodic electric guitar (Joe Satriani, Robin Trower...). As a personal speaker with uber-portability capabilities from what I've read and what I've listened to this is probably the best all around portable bluetooth portable speaker available today. Build quality is outstanding. It feels solid and refined like many of the Apple products. The cradle complements the design flawlessly and works exactly as it should. Sit the speaker on the cradle it makes an audio tone to confirm your connected and the pilot light blinks until fully charged then it glows solid blue. I'll update post once I use it outside.

text: This device has seriously blown me away. The sound is INCREDIBLE - especially for its size! We also have a Sonos system in our house and have often taken that device out to our backyard patio to enjoy our music collection while we relax outside in the summer. I have to say - since purchasing the Bose, the Sonos has remained inside. :D The simplicity, small form factor, and ability to have just the right volume of music at our patio table for entertainment purposes just couldn't be better. I also recently used the device, paired with my iPhone, to listen to my music and better hear the GPS navigation instructions from one of my iPhone apps while driving a rental car. One Y-connector for the cigarette lighter is all I needed to power both my phone and the Sonos for continuous use during the long drive. The grippy base made it a breeze to set right on the dash, without having to worry about it sliding around. And with the newly added speakerphone feature for calls, it was the perfect solution while on the road, away from the conveniences of my own car (with handsfree, GPS, and phone connected everything). It would be hard to imagine someone not being impressed by the quality and features of this little beauty. I'm so happy I pulled the trigger on this - well worth the investment, IMHO.

title: Works great... until it dies a slow death
text: This speaker sounds great and works really well, until it gets a little age on it. Just do a search for the orange/yellow battery light issue for these and you’ll find a TON of people having battery problems after a few months to a couple of years. Once you try in vain to update the firmware, reset the unit, etc... it’ll finally give up the ghost and the battery light will turn red. At that point it’s a paperweight. It won’t respond at all and won’t work even when plugged into AC power. Bose, of course, will offer to replace the battery and extend your warranty by 1-yr for $75 as they state that the battery has “exceeded expectations”, LOL in my opinion it totally failed to even meet expectations for a premium product. Mine died after just over a year of use, so $200 up front and $75 every year and a half for a battery for the privilege of listening to this little speaker is pretty ridiculous IMO. There are other speakers out there that sound just as good (or better) for the same price or less. I ended up purchasing a Sony SRS-XB20 that has very comparable sound to the Soundlink Mini II for less than what Bose wanted for just a battery. So the Bose is great while it works... just don’t expect to get more than a year or two out of it before it dies.

text: If you're just looking for loud, there are plenty of other bluetooth speakers that can get loud. You don't need a lot of cash to get loud. It's been used in my house to listen to music while taking a shower (it stays out of the shower of course), to listen while cleaning around the house, and even just hanging out on the patio. It has no trouble filling a room. With some streaming music services reaching up to 320kbps right now, the quality is very good. I haven't run into any battery performance issues. I've had it off the dock for a few hours at a pretty loud volume without it dying on me. When I was done with it, I just placed it back onto the dock. No worrying about plugging it in. The calling feature is nice too. When getting a call, it will pause the music and speak the name or number of the caller. Just push the button on the speaker and you can speak through it. I can hear others well through it, and they tell me they hear me normally. Overall, it's a nice little unit.

title: This speaker is just awesome. The audio quality is excellent
text: This speaker is just awesome. The audio quality is excellent, especially considering the form factor. If you are a hardcore audiophile, then I'm sure you can find issues to focus on here - but for a small, portable speaker you're not going to do much better. This sound quality is what we've come to expect from Bose, and this product is no different. It's loud and clear, with solid bass. Music just sounds awesome on this speaker, it's top notch. It's almost shocking how great it sounds considering that the speaker is so tiny. The overall design is simple and solid. The construction is excellent, as you hold the SoundLink it just screams out "well built". Visually I like the design very much, but the look is simple and understated. If you're looking for something flashy, then you might want to look elsewhere. The small form factor makes this really easy to take on the go - you can definitely easily carry it in a backpack or even in your jacket pocket or purse. It is pretty heavy though, much more dense than you'd think by just looking at it. It's a brick! I've paired it with multiple phones and my iPad, and the bluetooth setup has gone off without a hitch. I've moved around the house a bit without losing my connection, but when I walked outside to test the range it did drop connection. One thing to point out, is that I've used bluetooth speakers in the past that seem to just randomly drop the connection from time to time, but the SoundLink hasn't done that to me at all yet. Very refreshing! The battery life has been very good in my tests, lasting around 9 hours before running out of juice on me. The only thing that would prevent me from recommending this product to everyone is that the $200 price tag is fairly steep. If you're looking for a high quality product though, and are willing to spend $200 then I'm sure you'll be very happy with this one.

title: All about that bass...
text: ...is a clever hook line for a pop song, and a crummy way to approach music. Legendary for its ability to pump actual deep bass (as opposed to low midrange) out of such a small box, this wildly overpriced unit (although on par with equally $-inflated units from Beats, Jambox etc) certainly sells by the boatload - but is it actually a good speaker? Not to my ears. The bass is exaggerated to the point of eliminating any clear detail in the mids & highs. I currently have, in addition to a couple other BT speakers, this and the Soundlink Color - and the Color sounds 10x superior to my ears, a larger clearer sound. No, the Color doesn't have anything like the bass coming out of the Mini when fed a FLAT eq'd signal but it has the ability to pump out low end just fine when it's dialed up in your EQ. [You DO know that your phone has an equalizer, don't you? Look it up. If it's old enough to not have one, which is unlikely, just grab one from your app store for free.] FATAL flaw that seems overlooked: Your Mini's battery is low, so you set it on the charging dock (or plug in the charger) overnight, like you'd do with your phone or other devices, right? Guess what? You're ruining the battery! That's right, once the battery reaches 100%, instead of simply having a charging-shutoff in the circuit, it continues to try and charge and the battery is gradually damaged to the point where it will no longer hold a charge. That's the case with my unit which I bought used - play it for 20 minutes and I'm at 40% battery. The other factor about the Color we like is that fact that it's semi- water resistant. The charge port & aux input on the side aren't covered (a piece a tape would remedy that) but the top mounted controls are sealed and waterproof. It would definitely survive being out in the rain for a bit. Everyone loves it when demo'd in the store or compared to countless other units in Youtube videos, just because of the bass. Big deal, I want ALL the music.

title: Very pretty- instructions unclear. Read on to find out how to play out of 2 speakers simultaneously!
text: My mom ordered 2 of these thinking she'd be able to play music out of both of them at the same time from her iPhone. They come in the mail and we cannot figure out how to do this at all, and the instructions that came with them were unclear, as well as what we found online. After a few hours of trial and error, this is what we figured out: Pair both of the speakers to the iPhone Make sure *one* of the speakers in connected (the other may not show anymore/doesn't have to be connected) On the *connected* speaker, press the play and + buttons simultaneously (a sound will play) On the other speaker, press the play and + buttons simultaneously (the same sound will play with some additional beeps) Play music and they should work! This worked best for us when only one iPhone was connected/paired with the speakers at a time. Hope this helps someone else!

title: Looks great, sounds OK
text: The LED flames are very cool and the overall aesthetic design is very nice. However, the sound quality is just OK. Mids and Highs are pretty crisp and clear, but but the bass is very limited, and there is no sub-bass at all. If you're looking for background music and a nice centerpiece on a small covered outdoor table (like in a Gazebo) or to use it in place of a Tiki torch, it would work really well for that. However, if you want lots of full sound for a larger area or are looking for some bass in your music, you may not be entirely satisfied. It does have a 1/4" tripod mount on the bottom if you want to mount it on a more stable base, or perhaps elevated with an articulating tripod, which I think is a nice option. In conclusion, I will definitely use it in my gazebo, but I would have paid extra for a larger speaker with more bass. For a few more inches in each direction they could have added a resonant chamber or passive radiator to bring out more bass...or better yet, just used a beefier driver altogether. My son has a JBL Charge 3 that is approximately the same size and shape and absolutely blows the bass out of the water on this thing. On the other hand, the LED flames on this are pretty cool and will look really nice in our gazebo...

text: I ordered the 'DOSS SoundBox Pro+ Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with 24W Impressive Sound, Booming Bass, Wireless Stereo Pairing, Mixed Colors Lights, IPX5 Waterproof, 15 Hrs Battery Life, 66 ft Bluetooth Range -Grey' for my oldest daughter as she keeps "borrowing" my wireless Bluetooth speaker and rarely gets it back to me. At first my daughter was not so impressed with the speaker, but after using it now for a while, she stated that she loves the grey color, the light effects and the sound quality. Also a nice little surprise with this speaker is that you can ad music to your own SD card (up to 32GB) and install it directly into, and play it through the unit. title: Exceeded my expectations with clean balanced sound and undistorted bass.
text: [[VIDEOID:4c60e87ead4c44abcba14a2d6daa5b1e]] When I test speakers I play the type of music that is meant for headphones because of the meticulous care taken when mixing the recordings. I don't expect headphone quality, but I do expect balanced sound and on occasion, a little extra "undistorted" bass. I do like my bass and the Doss Soundbox Pro+ did not disappoint. The bass was punchy and clean without being overwhelming. Not only did this fill my living room with clear, undistorted sound, but I could hear it two rooms away without it sounding too bright or boomy at max volume. I am not sure if this would be loud enough to blast through a large room filled with noisy people, but it's perfect for smaller gatherings and apartments that share common walls with neighbors. I mostly use this with my computer, so the even though the lights are fun, they're a bit distracting near my screen, and I was able to turn it off by holding the "extra bass" button for a few seconds. This speaker paired quickly with all of my devices, and the sound quality exceeded my expectations, I highly recommend it. ** If you found this review to be helpful at all, please take a moment and click the button below to let Amazon know. title: Nicely designed, good sound and a good value
text: This is a nicely designed, nice-sounding bluetooth speaker. It's similar in size to my Bose Soundlink and Jabra Solemate speakers. It was incredibly easy to sync this speaker with my tablet. That's not always the case with bluetooth speakers and ear buds but in this case my tablet found the speaker immediately and instantly synced up. The instructions are a little tough to read with my old eyes, lol, but they do cover the all the controls and features. Most prominently, the speaker has options for multi-colored lights that display and pulse according to the music. They're cool looking, especially in the dark, but I'm not sure that I'd use them often. The good news is the lights are easily turned off at the push of a button. There's a button to boost the bass too. It works but even boosted the bass is not on par with the output from my other speakers. Given that the 15 hr. battery life is based on no lights and standard bass I'm unlikely to use either feature too often. The controls are pretty easy once you understand them. For example, sound (up/down) used the same buttons as next track/last track. It just depends on whether you push once (sound) or press and hold the button (track selection). The unit is water resistant (don't submerge it but it will survive splashing) and the ports for aux input and usb charging are covered on the back. Plus there's an added feature to play music off of an SD card. Finally, I haven't done this but you can also apparently sync another speaker for true stereo sound. (It has to be the same model, though.) I've always been partial to Bose and I love my Soundlink. I don't think any of my other speakers match up to it head-to-head, even though they both have really good sound on their own. But for the money, for the water repellant case, for the option to pulse lighting, and for the overall sound too I think this is a really good speaker and a good value.

title: Excellent sound quality and loud
text: The DOSS SoundBox Pro Plus is the latest in the line of DOSS bluetooth wireless speakers. In the box you will get a small instruction manual, a double ended 3.5mm microphone jack for plugging your phone directly in and of course the speaker itself. The speaker has a rubberized feel to it. This is in part due it being waterproof and will also help if you take it to the beach for example to stop it getting all scratched with the sand. The DOSS speakers will let you pair together more than one if you own a couple or more although to be honest you don't really need to as the speaker is very loud for being only 24 watts. Sound quality is excellent with very nice, floor shaking bass and the treble isn't tiny at all. You even get an extra bass button on top if you need more. DOSS have done an excellent job with regards to the sound quality. The front panel will change/cycle through colors based on the frequency of the music being played giving you different hues of white, blue and purple. On top you will find some basic controls (on/off switch, play/pause, skip forward etc.) although for the most part you will actually run this from your phone. Battery life is also impressive with this speaker easily lasting all day before needing recharged. Size wise, the DOSS is inline with most wireless speakers and is easily carried around or placed in a bag. Pairing your phone (or other bluetooth device like the Sony Walkman mp3 player) is extremely easy and quick and you will be up and running in a couple of minutes. Overall the biggest thing you will notice about this DOSS Pro Plus is the sound quality and just how loud it actually is. An excellent bluetooth speaker.

title: Unexpectedly high quality in a retro package
text: Yes, the obvious should be stated: this unit is just as heavy and built-like-a-tank as you'd expect, given the musical heritage on which it is modeled. They could have left it at that, and made a nice little replica unit that executes basic Bluetooth functions and sits on a bookshelf. But Marshall went further. Even though the three pots on top are just "spinners" with no detents or stops, they feel solid and smooth. The power switch is a strongly-sprung, "pull-on/pull-off" solid knurled metal affair. And, though I don't want to take it apart to find out, I suspect the case itself is vinyl-clad wood, sitting on four rubber feet screwed into the case like the good Lord intended. The attention to detail is much more lavish overall than I expected. The associated control app can be used to adjust the speaker remotely—it's important to note, though, that you don't EVER have to use the app once the speaker is set up. It is mainly for toggling among modes, and applying EQ across five bands. While (at least using iOS) you have some control over the track currently playing, Marshall wisely expects that you might have your own music player to do this. I was amused that the pots make up for a lack of orientation by lighting up a series of LEDs arranged radially. These LEDs indicate the state of the controls in real time, whether using the physical controls on the speaker or making changes through the app. The app also allows you to set the brightness of the LEDs; a helpful touch. Marshall includes power cords for U.S. and UK electrical outlets. You need to go online for any instructions beyond how to power on the unit. But pairing is simple, and two other methods are included for adding input to this speaker, making it a rudimentary sound system. I wasn't expecting this level of quality; I honestly thought it would be more of a novelty item. But this is no novelty, and in fact is one nice speaker.

title: Emberton vs JBL Flip 4 vs Bose Soundlink 2
text: Indoors: Each unit sounds very different depending on where it is located. For the Emberton, it sounded a little too bassy in most locations and the mids and highs sounded drowned out because of that. The Bose also sounded a little too bassy but was more even on the mids and highs. In particular, the highs sounded great indoors. In certain spaces indoors, the Bose might have had the most even sound but only when standing right in front of the speaker. The JBL Flip 4 did not go as low in frequency response to the others however there was more clarity in the mids and had a more stereophonic sound. The Flip 4 in most cases sounded too bassy indoors (and I don't mean low bass but mid-bass). The Emberton sounded as one of the best when placed in the middle of the room. Outdoors: The Emberton was definitely the loudest and had the most bass and sounded better outdoors and had the best low frequency response as well as loudness. In some cases again, the bass drowned out the mids and highs. I liked the JBL Flip 4 outdoors for having a stereophonic sound and clarity in the mids and highs however the bass did not extend as low as the other 2. The Bose did not sound too good outdoors (worst of the 3 outdoors) and sounded the best indoors in particular situations. The Bose outdoors also did not perform well when not standing right in front of the speakers while the other 2, you can get pretty good response at different angles. As far as loudness and bass, the Emberton blew the other 2 away, but did not have the stereo spaciousness or mid/high clarity of the JBL.

title: My favorite speaker I’ve ever owned!
text: I would have given this speaker 5 stars just for the sound quality and volume capabilities (it’s astounding for the size) but the process of connecting devices is a bit clunky at times, and it won’t always play audio on things such as Twitter videos. So if I’m listening to music and want to watch something a friend sent me, I have to pause the music, disconnect the Bluetooth, play the video through my phone, then reconnect to the Bluetooth, which sometimes means I have to go push the button on the speaker again to make it discoverable. It’s enough of a flaw that I couldn’t ignore it. It can be frustrating. But it’s so light and small, the battery lasts forever, and it is built to LAST. And I have to reiterate how good the sound quality is. Makes JBL’s best sound like trash. I bought them both and played them side by side and it wasn’t even close. Anyone who says JBL’s comp models sound the same or better would probably be happier with the original music canisters from the turn of the century. The tinny, muffled, distant sound is frankly quite similar. If they got the Bluetooth connectivity figured out on this model and maybe made it so it takes less time to turn the speaker on/off, and if they included a carrying strap in the design of the next edition, this speaker would be absolutely unparalleled in every category.

title: Impressive omnidirectional sound
text: While this is not the very best sounding portable speaker that I have heard, it is exceptionally good and is perhaps the best overall buy in this price range. The highs and midrange on this unit are beautifully crisp and clean. It does a fantastic job with electric guitar or classical strings down through cello. Compared to the Sony portable speakers, like the SRS-XB22S, this speaker does not handle lows very well. In general, the lows have little punch and the deepest lows are simply missing. If you like dance music you will love the highs and midrange but if you expect a solid baseline you will be disappointed. That is truly sad because this is hands down the best omnidirectional little speaker I have heard. While there is some degradation in sound quality as you walk around the unit it is very good compared to all other speakers in this price range. So, if you want a great sounding omnidirectional speaker and you don't plan on throwing dance parties this is an excellent buy.

title: Compact Size with Excellent Sound
text: [[VIDEOID:c8d9d00f0b6394614ae8a991ce291d96]] If I’m being honest, this was a complete impulse buy. It came up on my Amazon feed and I was slightly interested at the time. Fast forward to a camping trip where we spent a lot of time outside of our camper and it was clear that this speaker would have been useful. I totally ordered it at that point. What sold me was the suction cup and the water resistance, which is what you need when sitting outside of your camp trailer. I received the speaker about a week ago and have been using it quite a bit around the house (haven’t gotten it into the wild yet). What I can tell you is this thing sounds great. Decent highs and mids, and you can kind of feel the bass. Pretty impressive given the size. Speaking of size, It’s much smaller than I thought. It’s about a third of the height of a soda can and about 30% larger in diameter than said can. Connecting to bluetooth was pretty straight forward, but setting the time and finding radio stations took a bit. Here’s what I did. -Setting time: Hold the play/pause button until the time blinks. Volume up will then change the hours. Play/Pause again will change to minutes then volume up to change the minutes. Play/Pause to finish. -Scanning for radio stations: Use “M” button to get to FM. Hold the volume up button until device starts scanning for stations. Once you get through the setup, the device is easy to use. One thing to note, is it only has military time (at least that I could figure out). That’s not an issue for me, but could be for somebody else. I did “test” the waterproofness (is that a word?), and it seemed to work fine. I put a clip of my test in the included video. Pros: -Small size -Strong suction cup (removable) -Water resistant -Excellent sound -FM stations -Water resistant Cons: -Didn’t get good FM reception in my basement (upstairs/outside fine) -Setup takes a bit Overall, this speaker is good quality and I’m satisfied with my purchase (thanks Amazon). I can’t wait to show this off on my next camping trip.

title: Bottom line: It sounds really good!
text: I have an older smaller USB speaker that I like but is lacking in bass. This Tamproad looked like an upgrade so based on reviews I bought it for $35. The sound is clean, that is most important to me. There is bass, but not what you would expect from the looks of that center driver. Moderate bass adds richness to the sound, but don't expect any thumping. I ran a bass test on it and it really fell off below 100hz. One thing I found annoying straight off is the blue light ring around the bass cone. Hurting my eyes at night, the blue is too cold. Noticing there are four screws holding the front of the speaker on, I took the front face off and easily disconnected two white wires on the board= no more ring light and this will only help the battery last longer. (see image) Another thing is that the remote raises volume to 14 but no higher. However, the volume knob does go much higher than the remote, in fact this little box will get loud and stay clean sounding. Blutooth always connects with my iphone 8 but you have to get past the cringy status voices "blutooth connect-duh successfully". FM works for what that's worth. The battery charges quickly and lasts for at least 3 hours nonstop. I haven't tried a flashdrive or media card in it, I just want it for wireless connection. It does work brilliantly for that. Yes, a good sound upgrade over what I had. EDIT 2/23: so two years in this speaker has worked flawlessly, it connects via blutooth to my iPhone every time. Flashdrive works every time. I've put it to use as my traveling guitar amp-acoustic guitar with a Rushhead preamp using an 1/8" stereo cord to the aux speaker input. Nice clear sound with the limitation that it only gets loud enough, you won't rock the local open mic night with it. I've taken the time to review this twice because it is a reliable tool for my music needs. Top recommendation!

Even if I'm watching a movie on my laptop, I pair it to this and it has a variety of uses - mediation for the more serene vibe, pounding house music for a party vibe. It does it all and all you have to do is take it out the box, pair it and get to rockin. It's on the bigger side but still remains very portable and it is the perfect gift for ANYONE, especially yourself!

title: Awesome Sound!
text: Sony SRS-XB43 EXTRA BASS Wireless Portable Speaker IP67 Waterproof BLUETOOTH and Built In Mic for Phone Calls, Black (SRSXB43/B) My family really loves this speaker. The sound is great for a portable Bluetooth speaker. I really fills up the backyard during pool parties. The bass is a bit lackluster. I thought it would be a bit punchier considering the size of this speaker. It pairs easily with my iPhone and my Alexa devices. The battery life is great too, we went all day and it way still jamming. It also can be used to charge your phone, which is pretty convenient. The gimmicky thing is the light show. I don't really think its necessary and doesn't really add anything to this speaker. Fortunately the lights can be turned off. As far as being portable, it kind of is. It's big and while its easy to move around the house, I wouldn't carry it out on a hike or any where I would have to carry it for long distances.

title: No the best, no the worst
text: I hardly write reviews anymore, but in the case of the Sony XB43 I will do an exception. I bought these speakers (I bought 2 of them) because of the Sony name brand. It has always been a good brand for sound. The sound quality is ok, its not the best or the worst. I am sure you can get a higher definition in a BOSE or SONOS but the price point is the lowest for the XB43. Hence, my review of this speaker. I bought these speakers in an Amazon Epic Deal, which cut the price to $148.00 from the regular price of $248.00. In my opinion the speakers are really good at $148.00 but you can find better at $248.00. Why the four stars if I bought them at $148.00? because you can turn them OFF from your phone (Sony music APP) but not ON. When you have one, it is not a problem, but when you set them as a pair (which you can and it is the reason of buying two of these) you have to go to both speakers to physically turn them ON, which is not cool since I have them set up in different rooms. If you can turn them OFF, why not also turn them ON.

title: Worth the Upgrade
text: I've typically bought $100 or less speakers in the past, but I decided I wanted a richer sound from my portable speaker, so I splurged for the XB43. I'm glad I did because the sound quality over cheaper speakers makes it worth it. Size-wise, the XB43 is pretty big compared to what I've owned before. It's a bit over a foot long, and is pretty heavy. I guess that's what it takes to produce good sound though. The XB43 connects to my laptop or phone quickly upon powering on. So far I've used my speaker for over 10 hours, and the speaker says I have about 50% battery remaining. If you want to preserve the battery, you can leave it plugged into an outlet. Sound-wise, it's a massive upgrade over $100 speakers. It has solid bass (but don't expect subwoofer deepness) and it balances the highs and lows well. I've cranked it up while playing some modern pop, and there's no distortion. It can definitely get pretty loud for its size.

title: Low expectations smashed ... a very nice little unit.
text: I was not expecting much. What I was hoping for is a bike speaker that would allow me to ride my bike while still being able to hear the sounds around me for safety purposes. This works pretty darn well. The sound is a lot better than one might expect, and it is easy to set up and use. The only real problem I have with it, or that I don't like about it is that the controls are in black along the side of the unit, so as you ride you cannot really distinguish what control is what ... on/off, louder/softer or Bluetooth pair? Very difficult to adjust while riding, which we probably should not be doing anyway, but to turn it up or down should not be so difficult. Also trying to turn the volume down you hold the (+) or (-) buttons down, which are also the FF or FR controls and it really doesn't work well for that. I end up just putting the volume on maximum and varying the volume on my phone, or device. Works particularly well on my bike where I can listen to music or podcasts without shutting out the ambient noise of traffic or what is going on around me. All in all it is very good, as good as any other more expensive alternative, but not quite perfect. I would buy it again or recommend it to others and rate it at a 4/5.

title: Loud and clear...did I mention loud
text: This is my initial review of the product, as I just got it yesterday. It's simple and easy to use. I love that in a product. No having to read the instruction manual if you've used BT devices before. It even had a good 80% charge on it when I got it so I was immediately able to use it. This thing is loud and has very clear audio. I'm surprised at how much volume this thing puts out without distorting. Especially for it's size. It's like a football that's slightly larger. I actually thought I had it on full blast, but the speaker was on like 75% and my phone's volume was 100%. So there was more room for volume. I tried various audio sources and the only time the audio wasn't good...was when the source wasn't good. So it's not the speaker. I'm not a fan of the "outdoor" EQ mode. It literally just strips the bass and makes the highs and mids clearer. People complaining that this thing needs an EQ...just download one for your phone, computer, or device. I would like to see an app that allows control of this for the speaker, but for the price and what this thing can do...I'm not complaining. The Bluetooth 5 works well even at a distance. I tested it, and it's more than anyone should ever need distance wise. It also didn't cut out during the few hours of testing. The weight is nice. It's not heavy, but doesn't feel at all cheap. It even has a "seatbelt" material for the carry strap which is nice This is my first BT speaker, but I'm super impressed. Maybe an audiophile can pick it apart...but I haven't found anything that upsets me or makes me feel like I didn't get my money worth. Update. Dropping the stars to 3. The 3.5mm port pushed in(broke) a little more than a year after I bought it...which is crazy considering it's only been plugged in like that 4-5 times. Super unhappy about it since I was going to use this as a speaker as a PA for my guitar pedal. Not happy about it.

title: Good sound, but FM tuner feels like an afterthought
text: I bought this for my barn bc although I stream my music via my phone and bluetooth, others in the barn prefer to use the radio. The sound quality is good and it works great with bluetooth. But if you're going to use the radio, find one station and don't change it. There's no display to indicate the numbers on the 'dial,' and there's no way to save a station into memory (like the numbered buttons on car radios). It's easy to adjust the volume by the + and - buttons when using the bluetooth function, but you have to be VERY careful adjusting the radio volume because the same buttons are used to change the station - you have to touch the button in EXACTLY the right way to change the volume without accidentally changing the station. It's like they decided at the last minute to add FM tuner function but didn't really think about the usability of the device for that function. That said, I'm keeping it because the sound is good and it was very reasonably priced. I just don't change the radio station.

He also mentioned he loves using his iPad to play easy listening music on his other speaker but using that speaker means he needs to stay inside because it's not portable. Hearing this, my wife and I looked at each other and said we need to get him this Bose speaker. He can ditch the radio and listen to his easy listening music on his back porch and enjoy the weather. I took it up to him, showed him how to use it. I had to explain a few times how he can select an app on his iPad and listen to it on the speaker but he got it. title: pros and cons
text: I will start this review by saying that I honestly do love this speaker But at the same time I can easily see why others might not. This is NOT the speaker that you simply grab and throw in the bag and go. This speaker is rather large and surprisingly VERY heavy. The sound quality is nice but the bass is only ok in my opinion. I have another speaker which is made by Amazon that cost about $50 that has the exact same sound quality. It is loud but as with this bass, ive heard others that are louder and cost much less. I will start with the app that the instructions tell you that you need to download. It states that it is for updates, but all I saw is that it is used for is linking multiple speakers together. I wanted this speaker because we spend alot of time out by the pool and at the river during the summer. I knew that I wanted something that was water proof for both of those settings so I was happy to give this one a try. For the pool and sitting stationary, it would be perfect. One use that I can see us using this speaker would be for travel baseball games. It is loud enough that you would be able to hear it from a distance. As I said earlier... some will love this speaker and think that it is absolutely worth it. Others will not. title: Take this, Noisy Neighbor

His house is right in back of mine, and in addition to letting his dog bark all night and doing loud yard work early on weekends, he frequently hosts backyard pool parties. As in nearly every weekend. All day his kids and others screech and splash while the Noisy Neighbor blasts music so loudly I can sing along in my house with the windows closed. I don't mind his taste in music--just that it's so loud and persistent. But now I have this speaker. I can send my teens outside with their friends, or my husband and I can bring the boombox with us when we're outdoors, and we can blast our playlists (Bosnian reggae-punk, perhaps?) loud enough to drown out the neighbor. The sound quality is fantastic and the charge lasts a long time. The boombox, although a good size, isn't too heavy, and it's easy to carry. We don't have to worry if it gets splashed from our pool. And it syncs easily with all of our devices. You don't have to have a Noisy Neighbor to enjoy this speaker, but it sure does help.

text: Update: It has been almost a year since I bought this Antimi "gray color" player. The device still works just as great as the day I bought it. I use it practically every day in MP3 or tuner (radio) mode. Love the device. I maintain the 5 star rating. The battery just doesn't die on this device. I use it mostly to listen to talk radio at home while I work under quarantine. After work I switch over to music either contained on a micro SD card, or through a plugged in USB flash stick containing music MP3 files, as I work on projects around the house or garden. The sound quality through the built in speakers, and also when I pipe it to a bigger powered speaker for music listening is excellent. I have not tested the Bluetooth functionality but all in all I am more than satisfied with this Antimi player. Note that this picture shows a red LED readout. The device I have has an amber readout. Also the Chinese female voice that announces the mode I have selected is a bit difficult to understand for some mode (ex. radio mode is supposed to be announced as "tuner mode" but sounds like "turner mode"). Music mode is announced as "music mode" whether the micro SD card is being read or the USB flash stick is being read. But these are trivial issues and do not affect my 5 star rating. Update: I've used this produce practically every day since purchasing it in March 2020. During weekdays, while working from home due to COVID-19 I listen mostly to radio, for many hours on end. On weekends I listen to music played from SD/TF cards or USB drives. The device has never failed me, plays for many hours on end on battery power, and even if connected to an external amplifier and speaker system, delivers excellent sound quality. In a nutshell, the device gets exercised everyday and has never failed me. I even brought this device up to Canada for 3 weeks and used it every single day to belt out the MP3 tunes on my memory sticks as I worked on my late mom's property. This Antimi player has never failed me. Audio quality is great, battery life is superb, and when connected to a good quality amplified speaker system this nicely built player will blow your mind.

title: I have tried Sonos, Marshall, Sony and Bose and Bose WINS!
text: I was specifically looking for a smart speaker with Google and Alexa built in. I tried the Sonos - One (Gen 2) and I really do prefer that sound over this Bose 500 . The Sonos was not as loud as the Bose but delivered a clearer, crisper sound with sharp clear Bass. Where the Bose 500 was more mid range and deeper Bass. Both units produced great sounds. The only issue I had with Sonos is that it does not have Bluetooth. That was a deal breaker, otherwise I would have chosen it over Bose. The next unit I tried was the Marshall - Uxbridge Smart Speaker and it is a great unit and great sound, but not very much Bass. The smart capabilities are great but however, it is lacking a deep punch in sound. I tried the Sony XB402M Smart Speaker and simply put-Don't waste your money on it. It is a great little unit for what it does but does not compare in sound quality to Bose or Sonos and falls short in bass by an immeasurable amount. I then tried this Bose 500-I was amazed at how great it sounds. It has Bluetooth and Google and Alexa integration that is wonderful. Yet, like most other 3rd party smart speakers, you don't get 100pct of the smart capabilities but the only one I found is asking Alexa to connect to my phone. It won't do that on the Bose and only tested it on Sonos and Sonos lacked even more abilities than the Bose. When using Google as the smart assistant, there was no issue with asking it connect to my phone. In overall sound, the two top choices are the Sonos and Bose. Until Sonos updates to Bluetooth, I would pass it up and choose the Bose. Also, there are no issues of it connecting to Wi-Fi as people report. A lot of tech issues are a result of people not knowing what to do. They may be on an unstable wifi and having spotty connection issues, etc. So many variables to consider. Don't buy into those negative reviews on connections for this Bose unit, It is more likely their user error.

title: Forget it about for Apple Music. You MUST use Airplay.
text: Fantastic speaker. Much better sound and microphones than the Echo Studio. HOWEVER, this is not the same thing as an Echo talking over bluetooth to a powered speaker. The Alexa version is (I assume deliberately) crippled. For example, I have the Apple Music skill installed, which works fine on a normal Echo. This device, however, ignores the skill and refuses to play Apple Music. The only way to listen to Apple Music is to stream from your phone using Airplay (or, I assume, bluetooth, but I haven't tried that). Given how awful the Apple-music skill is, this may or may not be an issue for you. The iPhone music app is way better, but if you want Alexa to play a specific album or song by name, you'll have to get an Amazon Music subscription on top of your Apple Music subscription. Given that there's no easy way to transfer your collection from Apple to Amazon, this is a big deal. You lose a lot by moving, so you need both services. Unfortunately, there are no good choices for a decent Alexa speaker. The Echo Studio is not quite as good quality as the Bose, but it is an Echo, so supports skills (though the AppleMusic skill is extremely minimal). The Echo doesn't support AirPlay, though, so you're stuck with the skill. The Bose speaker does support AirPlay, but doesn't support skills properly, and if you want to request music by name, you'll have to have an Amazon-Music subscription on top of the Apple Music subscription. The Sonos One has the same problems.

title: Only Pairs with same firmware bluetooth speakers
text: 2 Bitty boomers can sync together and you get true stereo, but the spiderman black and gold suit has a different version of the firmware as Iron Man and Red suit Spiderman. You can tell they’re different because the gold suit Spiderman BBs only beep when you double tap the pairing button. While the Iron Man and Red suit BB make a echo-ey couple of notes. They do not pair because of this. Unfortunately, there no way to tell which firmware one has because I’m not sure if they released multiple version of the same product. With that caveat, on with the review: The Good: The bitty boomer is small and light, so it fits in any pocket. Rugged: I’ve dropped them quite a few times only pavement (why they come with a carrying strap), but they don’t take any damage. You can stick one in each pocket and walk around like a human boom box, and live like you’re in a movie with a soundtrack. They’re inexpensive. They sound pretty decent—a lot better than my phone’s speakers—but not as good as something higher up the bluetooth speaker food-chain like a UE Boom 2: this speaker can’t touch it sound quality and battery wise. The only thing is, I can’t carry around 2 UE Booms in my pockets. The Bad: As above: the Bitty Boomers don’t pair with some other BBs. The batteries do not last as long as they should: I got less than a year’s good life, using it almost everyday for 9 months. Now, the battery on the oldest one only lasts about an hour and a half: down from the advertised 4 hour battery life. Bottom Line: I ended up buying 2 sets of these because I had to buy a second with the same firmware, after already owning 3 with the one with low battery shelved. Would I buy it again? Yes, despite the battery wear. I suggest you buy 2 together to increase the odds of them pairing off the bat.

title: What am I missing here - why such high marks??
text: I'm sorry but I just don't see, or rather hear, the appeal. I received my PLAY:1 Compact "wireless" Smart speakers two days ago. They run wirelessly through your home router via WiFi, but they must be plugged in to an outlet, as there is no battery option and the cords aren't very long. For me, the fact that they must be plugged in is a problem. They won't work where I was hoping to put them. Their sound quality is a mixed bag. The mid's especially around the voice range are pretty good as is mid high frequencies. The highs are okay but they shine best in the mid range. However, the mid low range is very disappointing, almost non existent, and the base is a muddy mess that's hardly detectable over the mid range frequency. I purchased two of these speakers in order to have stereo sound - and it made a big difference - but please know that my comments above regard the two speaker stereo sound arrangement.. A single PLAY:1 is a very sad experience, at least for me. I'm a bit of an audio file - truly just a bit - but the single speaker was unable to provide anything close to a satisfying sound experience. The app that must be downloaded to your phone in order to play the speaker(s) has something called a "graphic equalizer," which consists of a slide for base response and a slide for treble. Does anyone consider that a graphic equalizer?? It also has a button for "Loudness," which is "on" by default, and provides somewhat of an extra punch to base and low mid frequencies. Because of their need to be plugged into a wall socket and their over all poor dynamic range, I must return these speakers. A full half of the music is missing, the bottom half. I have my two stereo PLAY:1's in a 10' X 10' bedroom and I find their sound inadequate in even such a small space. I had a sub woofer, I may be giving a different review. Low mids would probably still be missing but, who knows, the over all sound experience may be pleasing enough with a sub woofer. If you need the 1's, get a sub woofer or expect nice mid's and high notes, with the treble turned up a bit, at the expense of everything else.

title: Great Sound, Great Functionality...Easy to Setup and Use.
text: I discounted the Sonos system for a long time as just another poor-sounding, flaky-connection wireless speaker system. Finally, when Sonos created the Play 1 and Bridge package I gave one a try as a "kitchen radio", replacing an iPad and Jambox speaker. We liked it so much we quickly bought two more for other rooms in the house. The sound is very, very good. No, it doesn't compare to the sound of a Denon receiver and high-end speaker system, but for 99% of our use it's just great. The speakers also appear to be very solid and well built. Best of all, the setup is extremely easy, You plug the bridge into your router and an outlet and press a button, plug your speaker into an outlet and press another button and within a minute you're up and running. The wireless connection has been flawless and other than Google's refusal to work with Sonos the music sources available cover just about everything. You control the system through apps that are available for Android, iOS, Windows and Mac, but once you have made your musical selection you don't have to keep the device running. I will say that the user interface on the apps could use a little work, but there's no lack of functionality. With our three speakers I can have them playing three separate music sources, two and one, or all the same thing. If you want true stereo sound, put two speakers in the same area and select "stereo pair". All in all, I couldn't be more pleased with Sonos.

title: The Haters are Full of It
text: The haters are either full of it, or they don't know what they're getting themselves into. When Logitech announced that they were discontinuing their SqueezeBox line, I started looking for a replacement. It took me a while before I resigned myself to Sonos, but I am glad I did, and I wish I had sooner. I have a Play:1, a Play:5 and a Connect and I couldn't be happier. Setup is a breeze. The first device I configured was the Connect and it was super easy. Subsequent devices are even EASIER. Seriously, you press two buttons at once, and you're done. The only thing that would be easier is someone doing it for you. The Play:1 is surprisingly awesome, and it has great sound from a small form factor (or even a larger one!). The Play:5 sounds even better, and it actually does fill a large room with high quality sound. The Connect is awesome in its own right, but since it funnels its sound through your existing audio receiver it's not fair to comment on its sound quality directly - it's definitely a high-quality device though. The only drawback is that Sonos devices are rather expensive... Anyway, if you can afford a Sonos system and you want a whole-home audio system, you owe it to yourself to give Sonos a try. I expect it to give me years worth of audio enjoyment.

text: I had been using a Bose Soundlink Mini bluetooth speaker for listening to music in the kitchen. This unit sounds great, but I thought it would be nice to make the jump to a nicer category of system and save the Soundlink for situations that require portability. After reading a bunch of reviews (I'm not an impulse buyer), I ordered a Sonos Play:1 and a Sonos Boost (I wanted the separate network just for music). These were super easy to setup, and the Play:1 sounded fantastic. I was so pleased with the sound that I ordered another one right away so I could set it up for stereo. This was also very easy. My wife and I have the Sonos controller app installed on our phones, and I also have the Sonos controller app installed on my laptop. It's very easy to play music from our music libraries, online radio stations, and Pandora stations (other music sources are available, but we're happy with Pandora). Because of the quality of sound and location of the speakers, we can easily hear the music clearly without cranking it up. The sound carries well, and yet we don't have any trouble carrying on a conversation over the music. Very nice. And if we do crank up the volume, well, these speakers are capable of way more volume than we'd probably ever use. Very happy with this purchase, and I recommend it highly.

title: The sound quality is really quite good, even though it is not producing stereo sound
text: This is my second Sonos product. The first was the Playbar and now I added the Play 1. The sound quality is really quite good, even though it is not producing stereo sound. It is able to get quite loud without distortion. I use it both indoors and outdoors and in both locations it's great. I like the play 1 so much that I think I need another one for more areas of my house. Like others have said, this is a solid feeling product. It is humidity resistant too, so for anyone that like to have music on while in the shower, you can use it there. The only Sonos issue I have had, which is kind of big in my book, is that of failing to play music. From everything I have been able to trouble shoot, it appears to be interference on my wireless system. For those you know wireless channel, Sonos only operates on either 1, 6, or 11. Unfortunately, my wireless router likes to enjoy those channels too; thus interference. The problem is on the SONOS operation. During the setup process Sonos will choose the channel with the least interference but after setup, it will not auto switch to another channel if interference occurs. My wireless router, does auto switch and when Sonos isn't playing, those three channel (1, 6 and 11) make the router happy. The problem is when I choose to play music through Sonos and now they are both on the same channel; sonos won't play. The fix; you will need to plug in the sonos product directly in to your router and change the channel in the advanced settings or you will always have to keep one sonos product(play 1,3,5, playbar, boost, etc) hardwired to your router If i just focus on the Sonos play 1 and leaving out my wireless problem, this product is fantastic. Sonos really does produce a great product and I would recommend them to anyone with a house with internet and the want to not run speaker wire all over the place.

title: Sonos is a great system, but know these things for setup
text: I just added this Play:1 to my apartment, in which I already have a Play:3. Obviously, Sonos sounds amazing and the experience of multiroom audio is really cool--seriously having more than one of these is really where it starts to shine. But, there are some things you should know if you live in a crowded area. Sonos only supports wifi bands 1, 6, and 11! What that means is that if you're in a crowded area and your router is on default settings, it switches to the least crowded band, often one that Sonos doesn't support. I am tech savvy, had Sonos for a year and was disappointed because it never had a stable connection. Once I changed my router settings and locked it to one of the bands, Sonos has connected quickly and stayed connected like a dream. But, they really don't make this clear during setup at all. As reviewers have mentioned at length, the sound is amazing. It's simply the best (simplest, sleekest, most integrated) way to get multiroom audio in your home or apartment in my opinion. The app is ok, but could use some work. Once I found out I could play music through Sonos directly from the Spotify app, I hardly even bother with the Sonos app anymore. Pros: - Great sound - Really well integrated system - Sleek looking speakers - Open ecosystem with practically all music services Cons: - Limited wifi bands--check your router! - App interface could be improved If Sonos made Wifi setup more clear and improved their app, it would be perfect! But it's still great once you learn those tricks.

text: Gave an extra star for sound quality. Almost useless for podcasts. Got an app on your phone like Coast to Coast am, this speaker system will never let you listen to it because it won't stream things from your phone. Just ridiculous to me that they didn't include that option. On their list of apps you can get Stitcher Radio, but not regular Stitcher. I can wirelessly stream anything on phone in the car by way of older and much less expensive technology than Sonos, but this system only allows you to listen to the almost entirely music oriented redundant stations on their list. Sometimes you can find apps but the Sonos makes no distinction between podcast or music so that if you want to add a podcast to your favorites list it only saves that one particular podcast, i.e. date xx hour xx, without giving you access to say hour 2 of said podcast after listening to hour 1, and finding hour 2 then becomes an easter egg hunt. With apps like regular Stitcher, which Sonos doesn't support, you can save podcasts and it will automatically download the podcast and organize it by date and hour for you and play the next 1 in succession automatically. Really disappointed with this system. I am removing it, and going back to my streaming speaker which costs a fraction of what this did. If you only listen to music and don't care about having to deal with a clunky menu system where subfolders abound than perhaps this is for you.

title: I am a fan of Sonos!
text: I got this as a gift, but my "gifter" got it from Amazon...With that being said, this is my review of the Sonos play1 - Firstly "sound", for the size of this device, the sound is amazing; it's a little over half the size of a 1/2 gallon milk carton. This little speaker superbly makes me enjoy my music. The clarity of each note and the solid bass makes me feel every note. The "Truplay tuning" tunes the speaker to adapt to the dimensions of the room. The speaker almost disappears in the room and you wouldn't notice where the sound is coming from; it just fills the room. It takes a little while for the tuning to auto-adapt, but it's worth the small wait. My first time with a Sonos product, but I am now a fan! Now here's the reason for only 4 stars: this speaker DOES NOT fill every niche and need. It does not have Bluetooth and there are no inputs if you'd like to use this as a computer speaker replacement or to boost the sound on a LCD television. It must be connected to a wireless network and will only play music from its dedicated Sonos App. The App allows streaming from major music services like Amazon music etc. I have Amazon prime music so needing a subscription service was never an issue, but perhaps may be for someone with no internet and no subscription music service, this could spell disaster. The only source of music for the speaker would then be locally from either an Android or IOS device. However, in comparison to Bluetooth, this speaker does not lag at all when connecting to the device; music play is nearly instantaneous. In conclusion: sound quality is a definite 5 star rating, I will be exploring other Sonos products now because the sound quality is amazing. One star is knocked off because of this speaker's has limited range of usage. I would have liked to pair this speaker with my iPad and watched a YouTube video or something like that, but it's just not within this speakers range. You'd just have to "buy up". Just know what you're getting when buying this product.

text: I have several parts that cause me to dink a couple of stars on this and overall I am happy with the unit, the back end architecture is where it is falling short for me. Let's get the speaker quality out of the way first... it looks really nice, fit and finish is great, and I really like it over the Bose that I was considering as well. Connection was easy and overall it was painless to get it setup. Sound quality is a bit lacking for me as I find it bit hollow, but we will revisit that as the drivers breaks in over the next month. First I am going to dink it at least one star. I run behind a VPN on one network and do not have a choice-- so with that all of my apps from each service that I will mention work absolutely fine and have zero issues connecting... XM radio, Slacker, Pandora, Amazon Music... all are unable to connect through the Sonos App. That is unacceptable as far as I am concerned if the app works on my phone, it should work through theirs. Second is volume control. I know some other people have noted this, but honestly if you are using your phone (iPhone 7+ in my case) when a call comes in it should make sure the overall volume is lowered to a point....especially if you're jammin' and have it cranked up everywhere. My workaround will be to simply use my iPad to do it all at some point and it keeps my phone out of the loop. That is where I sit right now and if they improve their back end architecture... that will go a long way. The volume thing is also easy for the to do and only time will tell.

title: Moderately Invested in Sonos when they Pulled the Plug
text: See my review for Sonos Connect from 2014 which was my entry into this eco system - it was GLOWING and is still my most used Sonos unti. The Play:1 is something I bought to expand that system and since I've purchased a second Play:1 and a Sonos ONE (with voice, google/alexa, integration) as well as Bridge. Plenty has been written about these smaller Sonos speakers - they're fantastic for what they are, if a bit expensive - but it's the ecosystem you're buying into and investing in over time. Well today that came crashing down, and I'll just paste my update to Connect review here because it is directly applicable, as that issue now affects every single bit of Sonos in my home: ***** I'm updating this review for (applicable to ALL Sonos products) for no other reason than to voice my displeasure in Sonos in recent 2 years culminating in their decision to deprecate this model (removing support and updates from it) and not only that, but leaving it connected to the rest of my Sonos system which I've built since this original :Connect purchase in 2014 will render all those devices unsupported and unable to be updated as well (all Sonos devices must run on the same release version on a given Sonos network) effectively crippling the system. My option: remove it and take a 30% discount on "trade-in" for the new Sonos "Port", which involves Sonos remotely bricking the Connect device so it can be used for nothing but landfill, or simply removing it myself and trying to sell an unsupported device. Even better, the "updated" Sonos Port which replaces the Connect not only is devoid of added features I'd once hoped to see in a model refresh, but it is actually a downgrade in some respects, removing features that were present in the Connect (play/pause and vol control are gone, as is the TOSLINK optical output). It was a brilliant 6 years, but I'll be transitioning away if this is the direction the company is truly taking. A gigantic disappointment. I've been slowly adding to my system over time and had several more Sonos purchases in the queue. No longer.

title: Caution: setup is not so simple if you want to use it with Alexa
text: This product is not "Plug and Play." The setup is very cumbersome if you want this product to work with Alexa. As of 1/30/18, I had to do the following to make it work: (1) download Sonos app from the app store and go through their setup; (2) also download Sonos app from Alexa skills (this is a SKILL app) and enable it; (3) make sure that the Sonos device is identified in the correct "Room" (e.g., [Kitchen]) in Sonos and Alexa apps; and lastly, when you talk to Alexa, be sure to include the Device Location in the command you give -- as in "Alexa, Play "MUSIC name" in [Kitchen]." If your command does not include the location, the speaker will not work. The speaker quality is great, but the setup is a hassle -- and what bugs me more than anything else is that the stupid quick setup instruction that comes with the product states none of those steps!

I was initially disappointed and thought, before I was going to make major changes to my PC, I would be sending this back. The support team I dealt with was very reassuring they would find and correct the problem. Of course, my problem was something a bit more perplexing to them. Even turning off the Zone Alarm made no difference. They said they have had problems with certain anti-virus/firewalls before, but this was something of a first for them. A quick word of advice if anyone else has problems setting the SONOS PLAY1, uninstall your anti-virus/firewall and try to do the setup again. If that works then reinstall your anti-virus again. text: Growing up in an audiophile home I was very quick to scoff at the Sonos products. But like most young men, I had a young lady start hanging around and my large Klipsch speakers with a “confusing” receiver had to leave the living room. Little did I know that Sonos products were an easy, user friendly, and surprising high quality sounding solution. I bought the Beam first to help keep my setup clean and was so impressed I added two of these Play1s as my surrounds! Setup was a breeze (no running speaker wires a breath of fresh air) and once I tuned the system I was very impressed with the sound.

title: Love it
text: We love the sonos system. So easy and works great! Super versatile.

title: Think SONOS is too expensive, think again!
text: I love my SONOS system. I have 3 different devices. A play:5 which we use as a bedroom TV speaker and for music. I have a ZonePlayer (to hook up to my surround sound) for blasting music and I have this little (not that little really) guy in the kitchen. Each one I bought my wife called my an idiot. Each time after a week, she agreed she's wrong (I didn't get it on tape though) and says she loves them. She uses them more than I do. We have started to use this one more than the others for music. It has great sound for a little system. It's very crisp and clean sound. Very high end, in my opinion. The speaker looks great. I know this whole system seems a little expensive but you cannot compare it to a speaker by itself and you cannot compare this to any other "wireless" speaker system. This system is a high quality speaker, combined with a good amp and a great little multi-media computer. Just stream in some Pandora, play your favorite track off of Amazon or steams music from one of your computers. The house will fill up with speakers and music before you know it. Last, the setup is just stupid easy. I hooked the ZonePlayer and Play:5 into the router (my house is almost completely wired now) and only this Play:1 is wireless. The system is very responsive and you control them from your phone, tablet or computer. If you are thinking about it, just get one. You won't regret it and music will come back into your life in a big way.

title: Awesome
text: Awesome. Have has the whole set up for over 5 years and LOVE it. I use the app on my phone and on my PC. Waiting for an out door model...

title: Bumpin' Beats
text: Sonos products are expensive but worth it! This little speaker sounds great and fits basically anywhere. There are lots of wall mounting options available, or you can just set it on a table somewhere. The software works really well and they update it frequently. There are apps for Android, iOS, PC, and OSX; Not sure about linux. The volume level and clarity on this speaker are excellent, but it has very little low-end bass - to be expected for a single cone speaker of this size. I have my SONOS system on an Apple Airport Extreme wifi network, and it has always worked flawlessly.

title: Great "Alarm Clock"
text: OK, I use my Smartphone as my Alarm clock. I bought this unit and hooked Tasker up to it. Sound is great and I like that I can control it from any device once I start it, i.e. smartphone, tablet, laptop. I am now looking into stronger set of units for my living room.

title: Quality is top notch
text: This is the third speaker we have purchased and have loved them all. Terrific sound and easy to use. The speakers can sync or all play something different. Would recommend them to anyone any day.

title: Amazing Sound in a Compact Design
text: I've had my Play:1 speaker for several months and it absolutely rocks! For such a compact design, it offers amazing sound quality. I have one speaker for my downstairs living area (approximately 1,100 sq.ft) and this speaker easily fills up the room with crisp, clear music at only half volume. The integration with Amazon Prime Music and iTunes is great - I'm able to easily access my playlists and stream music. The iPhone interface is intuitive and I can quickly adjust the volume, skip songs, and add new music. The only 'difficulty' I've had is explaining to my parents how the music streams to the speaker ;-)

title: Another Great Sonos Product!
text: I needed a good speaker for my home office. I already own several Sonos products, so was happy to see that they now have a bookshelf speaker offering. The sound that comes out of this speaker is amazing. Good, deep bass and crisp highs. If you're looking for a good entry to the world of Sonos, this is a great choice. If you want to use this in a bigger room, I'd definitely recommend one of their larger speakers. You won't be disappointed.

title: Wow!
text: I don't know how I went so long without this. I bought an echo dot and streamed music on it all the time every day. That was it's primary purpose. I guess I bought the echo alone because I wasn't sure if I'd like it, but I used it all the time. I decided it was time to buy a nice speaker for it. I didn't realize how badly I needed one until this arrived and I got it set up. It's night and day, the sound out of this is fantastic! It's much smaller than I anticipated (about 6.5" tall, 4.75" wide), but it carries a powerful punch. I haven't had to turn it up even half way yet, as it's plenty loud, the bass is quite pounding, and the high end sounds clean and crisp. I love this speaker! On the bonus, plus side, you can stream music through it from your other music accounts (Google, Apple, Audible, Bandcamp, to name a few and not to mention whatever device you're using as a controller), and I didn't know this before buying it--that was a very pleasant surprise! It's almost made my echo dot obsolete. You can control everything through Alexa on whatever device you have, but you can also use your smart phone as a controller for the Sonos, which is how I primarily use it. All in all, this is fantastic. I really like it and highly recommend it. This is one of my favorite purchases of 2018. I can't say enough good things about it and I don't have anything negative to say. It's time for you to get one too!

title: Great Sound!

title: Amazing speakers
text: Purchased 3 of these speakers (an thinking of getting a 4th) and the Bridge after talking to a local Apple Store employee, who has them and recommended them as great wireless HiFi speakers. I placed 2 speakers on opposite ends of the first floor and one upstairs and the sound is amazing! I love the ability to control the music queue from my iPad and iPhone, and the signal was strong enough to add and change playlist while I was outside on the back porch. Great quality, clear and no issues to date with any dropping, static, etc. The ability to group the speakers throughout the house and play the same music is also incredibly useful. I did not have any issues setting these up, but do note you should download the Sonos App before you do anything else. You will need it to get these set-up and synched. Sonos App works well and is able to access my iTunes playlists. Updated addition: You will definitely need to purchase the bridge - unless you want to plug the speakers directly into your WiFi device (not practical). I am up to 4 speakers in the house now and am contemplating a 5th. [Not sure how the neighbors will feel about that!] Love the sound and the ability to queue up music from my iPad or iPhone no matter where I am. Like another reviewer noted, the app could be improved by adding options for skipping, advancing, etc. on the songs. Overall highly satisfied with these speakers.

title: Great sound, affordable whole house speaker
text: I love my Sonos. These Sonos plays are affordable and let you get music in every room.

title: As advertised and received when promised.
text: I purchased two of these, along with the soundbar and sub. It produces a great, room filling sound. Very easy to set up and you can easily change settings with a desktop, smartphone or tablet. My only problem is I can't get it to play my iTunes library or playlists, but I've heard their customer service is great so i'll be working that out soon.

title: small speaker with a big PUNCH!
text: wow. The Play:1 speaker exceeded my expectations. I actually went into Best Buy to buy this speaker, and tested them all out. Yes, the Play 5 obviously has a richer sound to it, but the Play 1 is very powerful. I ended up buying 2 Play 1's for my master bedroom and the sound is beautiful. I also paired them as an L and R speaker so they are like one stereo. I like how you can mess with the equalizer on the app to adjust your music. I like alot of bass with my music and I'm very surprised on how much bass these little things can punch. I turned the bass all the way up on the equalizer and I can feel the speaker vibrate than a normal little speaker would. These things can get very loud too. They are even great for moving them downstairs if you have a party with alot of people. also FYI- Sonos used to make their speakers where you were required to buy Bridge in order to pair a speaker with your internet. You do not need this anymore if you only choose to have ONE speaker in your house. You can buy one speaker and set it up wirelessly without any problems. BUT like most people who want to pair up 2 or more speakers into their system like I did, you will have to buy Sonos Boost. It basically connects all your speakers wirelessly. Some might find this to be a turn down, but it really is worth the money. The Boost helps the wifi connection between the speakers so that there are no dropped connections with music stopping or any of that. I so far have had no problems with my music playing. The app and speaker works flawlessly. Another plus is it supports a ton of music applications. I use Spotify the most, but it also has Pandora, Beats Music, SiriusXM, Rhapsody, Google Play Music, iHeartRadio, Last.FM, MLB gameday audio, 7digital, 8tracks, Amazon Cloud Player, Aupeo, Bandcamp, Batanga, Calm Radio, Concert Vault, Daytrotter, DAR.fm, hearts of space, hotelradio.fm, Murfie, Radionomy, rara.com, Rdio, RUSC, Shuffler.fm, Slacker, Songza, Stitcher SmartRadio, and The Hype Machine. (just looked through my list on my app and that is all of them). Overall, great little speaker that is perfect for any room. It can play really loud music with amazing quality. Would definitely recommend.

title: Best speakers on the planet.
text: I was given this as a gift by my husband who demanded we have better speakers in the house - ones that didn't require we plugged into and limited our mobility and music changing. I like the fact that you can pause/play, change the volume on the speaker, and with the latest software release you can change songs too!

title: Expensive, and not really that amazing.
text: I like the sound, but I really wanted more. This is a very expensive unit, especially considering that this is the bottom of the line. I would have gone with Bose, but I have a SmartThings z-wave hub, so I tried Sonos. The sound is fine, clear, but each unit is mono, you need two for stereo, and they are expensive. Also, they are supposed to work with your music on a Mac, but I could only the Sonos to connect to my MacBook Pro, not to my mini. The mini is where all my music is, so that was a bust. Research on the Sonos site seems to show many people with the same problem. Sonos, pay attention, why aren't you fixing this? Unlike a Mac and Apple TV, you cannot "push" the music to the Sonos. Sonos won't take airplay output. The Sonos has to connect to the music library and pull the music. Also, Sonos is supposed to pull music from Amazon Prime, but beware, it is only the music you purchased, not all the the Prime music.

title: Amazing Sound Quality
text: While having some work done on my house, unfortunately one of the workmen walked off with my former blue tooth speaker. I was going to buy the same thing to replace it when my painter (of all people!) recommended that I get a Sonos instead. He was so right about that! This sounds absolutely amazing! I can't get over the sound quality! The only drawback is that you must keep it plugged in, there's no wireless component to it. It's intended to either be used as a stand alone item, or can be used in conjunction with the other products they offer. This is the only one I have. It does not hook up to the TV, and that would have been something useful, but they do have a sound bar for TVs (very pricey!). When you first set it up through the app on your phone that you just download from the app store, it walks you through a specific set up for that particular room. I did that for my home office, but I still use it in many other rooms and even outside. I didn't go through the set up for any of the other places, and it still sounds wonderful! You have to remember to go through the app for it to play on the Sonos (versus just hitting play on your phone with other speakers), but your music on your phone shows up with no additional effort. You can also play Pandora from it. I'm really happy with this purchase!

title: Incredibly impressed with this awesome speaker, great bass for music
text: I really love this speaker. I already have two sets of Bose earbuds, so I already had the Bose app downloaded to my phone. It was easy to pair and didn't have any issues getting set up. I don't control it through the app, I just control it through the buttons on the speaker itself or just by turning the music on my phone on or off. I wanted a simple speaker that I didn't need to worry too much about so that I could listen to podcasts and music in the shower, or when working in my vegetable greenhouse this summer. So far it's been great! The battery life has been longer than expected, the sound quality is absolutely amazing for listening to music and has great bass, not any kind of tinny sound at all, and the unit itself seems thoughtfully designed and built to last. It's got a nice weight to it and doesn't want to tip over. I really appreciate after having a bunch of Chinese made brands in the past, that this one is just straight up quality, everything works, it's easy to deal with, etc. I haven't truly tested the water resistant capability of it, but after two weeks of showering with it just outside the shower and bringing it into the sometimes drippy or humid greenhouse, it still doing great. Overall the Bose quality shines through in this item and I've been really thrilled with it for my purposes.
