text: Coming from the UE Boombox the UE Megaboom was such a disappointment. The UE Megaboom is a loud, water resistant speaker, able to fill an entire room with sound. It has high gains but the bass is rather flat and there was a lot of distortion when the volume was raised. I liked the app that allowed for EQ settings. Sadly, if you use the AUX port the volume doesn't get much louder, the volume is actually lower for some weird reason. The tweeters are on the top of the Megaboom and the bass drivers on the bottom. You can't lay it sideways and if you want to use the aux or charge at the same time you have to flip the Megaboom upside down. title: Love my MegaBoom
text: I bought this from a Sprint store when it first came out two years ago - i've used it almost daily since then. I love this thing. It travels with me a lot. My only complaint after two years is that the charge port is a little fiddly now and i have to jiggle the cord to keep it charging. Not a big problem yet since it holds a charge for soooooo very long. I get longer battery life that is listed when I keep the volume at about 50% (which since I live in an apartment is my typical volume level). I can go for a day or two before I need to charge it. Keep in mind I use this all day every day. i even listen to music while I sleep. I rarely watch TV because I prefer to listen to music. I originally purchased the MegaBoom over the Boom due to the volume of this thing. It has great sound either all the way up outside or down low for sleeping or use in hotel rooms. However, I have found that it doesn't sound as good at top volume as it does at low volume. I think I may have messed up the speakers when I kept the volume too high for too long but I should be able to do that correct? Anyway, that doesn't detract from my 5 star rating because this thing does everything I want it to and it sounds great to me. However, for a pool party with lots of people I have a different party speaker that sounds better at the highest volume for long periods of time. The lowest volumes have great sound quality and I have absolutely nothing negative to say about that. I'm thinking about buying another MegaBoom because I bought a Boom due to the smaller size and wanted to use it in hotel rooms but I don't care for the sound quality nearly as much so therefore I rarely use it.

title: Do Not Purchase UE products...if you value your money
text: I purchased my UE Megaboom in 2017. I really liked the sound from the device. All worked as expected until the second year of ownership. I used my Megaboom probably twice a week for about 2 hours at a time if I averaged it out. One day while attempting to re-charge the device, it failed to connect or show charging. I decided to let it sit overnight and see. Nothing happened and the device would not charge. I went online to research the problem and/or solution and wouldn't you know it... very common problem with this company's devices. Worst of all, they refused to do anything for me as my one year warranty had expired. I do not expect 20 years from electronic devices, however, more than two years under light and normal wear should be expected. Especially when the device costs more than $170.00. I just ask that you do your research ahead of time on not only the device, but also the reputation of the company behind it. If they won't stand behind a product which they are fully aware of having problems, then we shouldn't keep giving them support by purchasing faulty products. I won't be buying from UE in the future.

title: Returned as didn't charge; new unit does charge. But verdict is flimsy micro-USB charging port.
text: Mine arrived quickly and I downloaded the free app for iPhone. From there I updated the firmware which took about 2 min total for the reboot. Then, played some music from my phone, and tested the volume. Everything was great and even cranked up from the phone's volume rocker is was clear and bass was heavy. The downside? It showed 40% charge off the get go (actually the app doesn't say the %, but the + and - can be pressed to announce it) and then plugged in the yellow charger to the wall and the yellow micro-USB cable to the Megaboom, but no LED light came on and the app didn't change to show it was charging. Checked the cable with another charger and a Kindle for my kid, and that worked so the cable is fine. Tried the 12V charger on an old Sony Handycam and it charged fine. So the unit itself is the issue and it was sent back. Update on 8-9-16: New unit arrived (1 day shipping) and charges out of the gate. Ok, I will diligently blow on the cable and charging port before re-sealing the bottom cover when it's done charging. These are fragile on the unit so perhaps dust-off would be good.

title: Best OUTDOOR speaker there is!
text: First off, I love Bose. I have many Bose items, but Bose Speakers are not made to be outdoors. They do not have 360° sound, they are not water proof and they are not shock proof. So many times I would put my SoundLink on my patio table and it would appear dusty at the bottom, even though my table is pretty clear. I would also CONSTANTLY have to move it for better placement. Bose Soundlink's are made for indoors where they are 2nd to NONE! They sound phenomenal.... But for outdoor use, I AM OBSESSED WITH MY MEGABOOM!! I set in on the ground near the leg of my gazebo and forget all about it. I don't have to worry about my 2 dogs running into it and breaking it since it is VERY durable. I don't have to worry about re-positioning it depending on where I am at in the yard due to it's 360° design. The bluetooth signal strength is A LOT better than my Bose, so I don't have to worry about walking too far off and the speaker going out until I come back. I don't have to worry about sudden rainfall ruining it since it is COMPLETELY water proof. It also sounds very good (not as good as Bose) and gets even louder than my Bose. I don't have to worry about battery life (much better than the Bose). If you want an indoor, stationary speaker that sounds amazing, get the Bose. If you want something made for the outdoors, get the Megaboom!

text: I was looking for a good quality bluetooth speaker. I was mainly considering: The UE BOOM 2 and Soundlink Mini II. I decided to go with the UE Megaboom because I did not want a small super portable speaker however I did want something I could take places occationally. The Soundlink Mini II has probably clearer sound however it is not as loud and it is not rugged. After spending 200+ on a speaker I did not want it to be too delicate. I am completely satisfied with with the MEGABOOM and I totally recommend it. The range is great the battery life is amazing and the sound is just good. It is loud and it has very punchy bass. It has an EQ which allows you to personalize the sound to your linking. If you are looking for a speaker that is very small portable and rugged with OK sound (not too bassy) -> UE BOOM 2 If you are looking for a speaker that has very good, bassy and warm sound and it is portable but more likely will stay on a desk/table most of its time -> Soundlink Mini II ( KEEP in mind the mini III is probably going to come out on June 4th - That is when the mini and mini II came out and the mini II has already been discounted). The sound is good but not as loud. If you don;t care too much about size but you want powerful rugged sound with good bass -> UE MEGABOOM. ( I don't think UE has plans to release the UE MEGABOOM 2 because it has just released UE ROLL 2 and the MEGABOOM is not on sale) so it is safe to buy right now.

title: Powerful speakers with a great battery life in a portable size.
text: What comes in the box? AC Adapter Micro USB cable Speaker The packaging is reusable as a carrying or storage box. The UE Megaboom by Logitech is a very powerful speaker system. I have purchased this speaker based upon reading reviews prior to purchasing. The battery life is incredible, and it exceeds the battery life of anything in its class. It is simple to operate and pair with your Bluetooth enabled device. The large volume buttons are easy to handle and adjust, especially with wet hands. The construction is solid and it is waterproof. The access ports for the input jack and the Micro USB cable are sealed. At the bottom, there is a hook that makes for a good way to hang the speakers out of your way. It is about as tall as my Kindle Fire HDX 8.9 is tall. The size is similar to an Arizona Tea or 40 ounce beer can. This has some serious girth and weight so it is stable for outdoor use in wind. The sound quality is incredible. It has a covers bass, midrange and treble equally well. The bass is more vibrant than average speakers. I plan to acquire a second speaker to get more of a stereo effect outdoors. However, the sound coming from this single speaker is nothing short of immersive in an enclosed room. Placing it close to a wall, allows the sound to reflect back towards you giving a unique effect, also. There is an app available through the Apple App store but I do not see an advantage unless I have a pair of these speakers. So I just ordered a second speaker for the purpose of a stereo effect. Once I get my second speaker, I will update the review. For its size, it is the best in its class for similar sized speakers. It is very powerful, and there is no distortion even with the maximum volume level for any genre of music.

For $299 I gave this a lot of thought but I took the plunge and OMGosh, I was blown away by the sound of the UE Megaboom. High tones, mid-range, lower tones and the bass...all were outstanding. I played the following songs...immediately: Old Smokey Robinson, The Winans (contemporary gospel), Michael Jackson, Drake, Reba McEntire, soundtrack from Les Miserables, Andrea Bocelli and then I let it rip with some classic Earth Wind and Fire. I mention the artists to express that the UE Megaboom embraces any music genre with great clarity and range. Syncing to my iPhone took no more than 5 seconds. I also downloaded the Megaboom application to my cell phone. I haven't played with that much yet but the download was easy breezy. I own several speakers which I have pictured to just say that this is not my first day at the bluetooth speaker rodeo :-) All I know is what I like and I don't think one has to be a musician to know what sounds good. This speaker sounds great to my ears, so all I can to you is...Buy this speaker It is expensive but well worth the money. Sit back and enjoy what has now become my favorite bluetooth speaker. Kudos to Logitech!

title: BEST $$ SPENT

But you can download app from computer with windows7 and that's what I'm going to do to get the updates from UE. The sound from this small speaker fills a large great room,kitchen, and master bedroom....and sound quality is better to my ears hi,medium, to low,and lots of bass without distortion compared to the Bose Soundlink Mini. I purchased both to compare bass. Mega boom blows the Bose away! Sound is loud! And you don't need to fiddle with the EQ. The MegaBoom comes factory set and to me it's perfect and needs no tweaking. I listen to Madonna for workouts and Frank Sinatra and Tony Bennett as well as Rod Stewart for easy listening. Clarity of the words in songs are crisp and clear. I will not be using outside even though it's waterproof. But will use on screened porch but using low volume because of neighbors. Love the casing and ease of turning speakers volume up or down. title: Best portable speaker for the money, bar none!
text: Couldn't be happier with this purchase! I have used many portable speakers in the past, and I can say that this one is by far the best, not only in its price range, but when compared to speakers that are considerably more expensive. Does it sound better than anything on the market? Of course not, but for $30, it just can't be beat. Sound is surprisingly rich, and the volume is pretty high-- I rarely have any reason to turn it up all the way. For a speaker with such a small form-factor, it has a vast array of options. You can fill up a flash drive or SD card with music and you're good to go! Plus, the battery is easily accessible, so you can buy an extra one to take along in case you won't be able to plug it into a power source. Best of all, you can actually charge your portable device via the built-in USB port-- who needs a 40-pin iPod/iPhone dock when you can use a 3.5mm headphone jack and a USB charging cable? I guess you could spend $150 on a fancy speaker with bluetooth and a direct dock, but audio-over-bluetooth is never going to sound as good as a direct 3.5mm connection, and it's going to cost considerably more. Build quality is solid as well-- I've packed this thing in my suitcase and sent it around the world and it still looks brand-new. Battery life is great too (never timed it, but it lasts many hours on a single charge). Like all rechargeable batteries, the length of the charge diminishes with use, but replacement batteries are cheap and easy to swap out. I just can't say enough good things about this product. For thirty bucks, you've got nothing to lose!

text: OK. well obviously this device isn't intended to help babies go to sleep, but by my word it works very well for this purpose! With this device I can load up any music (he seems to prefer noisy stuff) and set it to play right near him. In low light he likes to stare at the blue LEDs visible around the controls. The big volume knob is nice too, I usually start it out on a moderate volume and decrease it to something low once he starts to doze. I recommend getting a very small USB drive for this thing, and just change up the songs as you want. You can of course alternately use it with your MP3 player or anything with an audio jack. I've read some reviews that the audio input jack can fall off inside if you cause a sideways pulling motion on the cord so I'm careful when ever I plug it in. The battery life is pretty good for how loud is can get and the audio quality is very impressive with nice bass for a device this small. Best of all, the battery is replaceable in case it ever dies, or if you wanted you could buy more batteries and take a few with you if you were going some place without power. Overall this device has been well worth it for me. I also use it while doing chores around the house, it's a nice way to listen to music on the move and not wear earplugs.

title: Excellent sound for the size and price but poor mechanicals
text: This thing sounds great for its size, better than typical PC speakers. The drivers are 1.5 inches across and the magnets behind them are almost that big. The speaker enclosure is decent quality particle board, not plastic. I really like the traditional analog volume control. (Up and down buttons suck.) I used the 3.5 mm "aux" analog stereo input jack. The first time I tugged on the patch cord, the connector inside the cube cracked loose from the PC board and it stopped working. If I'd gotten it replaced it would still have a weak link connector, so I took it apart to repair it. The connectors are all surface mounted and the audio connector has no extra pads or tabs for mechanical stability. The other three connectors are better. Should have used a through hole audio jack. There's a fourth pin on the connector to detect a plug, so it may be hard to find a proper replacement. I'll update this review if I get that far. I'd recommend this thing for its size, sound quality, and function. But beware the audio input jack is *very* delicate. Use just enough force to insert and remove your patch cord. Don't put *any* strain on the cord when it's plugged in there. I should also note the volume control knob is loose on the control shaft, so they glued it there. What a shame to wrap a state of the art lithium battery, surprisingly good speakers, and all that fancy silicon in such poor mechanical finish.

During the night we some light rain showers and the speakers were exposed to the rain. One speaker is just fine, however, the other speaker malfunctioned, the flickering light will NOT turn off. No matter how long I hold the button or how many times I push the button the light stays on. It will stay on until the battery dies. It took a long time to drain the battery, about 24 hours. Afterwards, I recharged the unit and light did not come on by it’s self. The speaker sat unused for 4-5 days since being recharged. I just walked by it and the light was back on and of course I cannot turn it off. So it will continue to flicker until the battery dies again. The speakers still sound just like they did out of the box, so no damage to that part of the unit. I will update again when I hear back from the seller

title: I'm continually impressed.
text: I bought this bad boy almost six months ago and when I initially purchased it, I had some buyers remorse because I didn't want to spend that kind of money on a Bluetooth speaker. But then it arrived in the mail. Immediately after I opened it, the buyers remorse was just a faint memory. The build quality is excellent. Metal parts, rubber bumpers on the sides, and a rubber gasket around the io ports in the back? Say less. Then I got it charged and paired to my phone. OMG the sound quality. For speakers that size, this little guy sounds immaculate. The bass is rich, the highs are crisp, and the mids aren't muddy. It also gets REALLY loud; I'm not sure I've even turned it up all the way before. Halfway is usually plenty, even when working in a large sound stage. Buy it if you can, you won't regret it for long.

title: New Tech Continues To Impress
text: I’ve gone through a lot of portable stereo’s in my life. Just by saying that shows my age. The last one I purchased before the new reign of Bluetooth speakers was the JVC Kaboom Box. It was pretty amazing in it’s day. I haven’t found a portable since and that JVC wasn’t very portable in the first place. However, this reminds me a lot of the JVC. It’s so small, yet so powerful! The JVC was probably the same price as this JBL Xtreme 3 and sounds just as loud with the same bass, maybe a bit deeper. For me, this way way worth it. There is one con. The louder it gets, it seems that it looses the bass. You can kinda get this back with the app using the equalizer, but at about 75-80% volume is where it happens. Which is super loud. You might be able to hear the bass if you’re farther away. Bass is a much longer sound wave. So the closer you are, you may not be able to hear it over the volume of the treble and mids. This speaker is really loud and going above 50% is kinda overkill inside a normal to small room anyway. At that level, it sounds amazing! That’s why I only dropped it by one star. Overall, I am very impressed how technology has evolved and has gotten such huge sound in such a small device! Very impressed and well worth the price to me.

title: Good value in a basic power bank
text: In using this initially, I've learned some things about how they rate power banks. My Motorola Power G phone has a 5000 mAh so you'd think this bank would charge it twice. Turns out more like once a a bit more. These are rated on their internal battery capacity; here 10,000 mAh. But this is at 3.7V and charging is at 5.12V. So 10,000 mAh @ 3.7V becomes 7,200 at 5.12V. And the boost function in the charger is only about 85% efficient, so it is actually more like 6,100 mAh delivered. That's still fine for our use, but it could be an unexpected surprised for others, like me, who don't realize how these devices' capacities are represented. But knowing what I know now, I'd buy it again at this price.

title: Great Power Bank!!
text: I had ordered another power bank from a different seller and immediately returned it, as it was HUGE. This Anker one is exactly what I was looking for! Something small enough to toss in my purse for times when I have no access to electricity and my iPhone battery is dying. It is slightly smaller than a deck of cards and slightly thicker. Not too heavy as these things go. It came with a surprisingly nice drawstring pouch with enough room to store the power bank and the included charging cord for it. I separately purchased an Anker 1 ft long lightening cable, which also easily fits in the pouch - perfect for keeping it all together and taking it along anywhere! When the power bank arrived there were 2 lights lit, meaning it was at 50% power. I plugged it in to my computer and left it over night, which was probably more time than necessary to get it at 100% (4 lights). Next, I tried it out charging my iPhone 6S. It worked perfectly!!! Seemed to charge at the rate of a little less than 1% per minute. I went from 60% power on my phone to 100% in a little over an hour. The power bank stayed completely cool the entire time. And, I still have 4 lights showing on the power bank! I am definitely happy with this purchase and look forward to never having a dead phone battery again! The only thing that would make a great product even better was if there were ports to charge 2 items simultaneously. I would definitely recommend this for anyone, though!

This means that if you bought new Anker chargers, and cables, you cannot use them with this power brick. Basically if I want to travel with anker products, to charge two products (phones/tablets/laptops): 1 gen 2 GaN charger which has two USBC ports 1 power bank 4 USB cables, two USBC to USBC and two USB type A to USBC. text: Typical Anker quality but you have to be aware of what it takes to charge this brick. There are 2 micro usb input plugs and three standard USB output plugs. THE POWERCORE 26800 cannot be charged completely with an ordinary standard usb charger (1.5 or 2.0 amp output). It requires 2 standard wall chargers and 2 usb to micro cables plugged into PowerCore simltaneously to get the 4.0 amps required for all 4 charging lights to show complete charge. I have left a single 2.0 amp samsung phone wall charger plugged in for more than 24 hours and just get past 2 led lights to 3... never to 4. I did purchase a wall charger that has dual output ports at 3.0 amp and 1.5 amp ... which gets the job done with 2 cables. Be aware.. almost all new wall chargers have USB-C outputs... and your drawer full of old usb to micro cords won't work without an additional adaptor... good luck finding USB-c to Micro USB cable... I am satisfied with the power supplied just wish I had known about the high amps required to charge... Next time I would buy 2 smaller power banks vs this big one

title: A mighty charging power bank
text: I love my new power bank! Oh I do! It's sleek, smooth, naturally portable, durable, reliable and I am enjoying a freedom from hunting for outlets at the airport, at a large conference gathering, or needing to adapt to less-than-comfortable wall outlets in a hotel room simply because my 10' charging cable is still too short to reach my laptop. While at the home front, I can go camping or hiking knowing I will not run out of power for six months between charges!! That's incredible!! I've seen the comments on how long it takes to charge the power bank and I admit, I did hesitate to buy it, but I'm so glad I went through with it! When I received my new Anker power core, the instructions clearly stated to use attach both charging cables that came with the Anker power core, into a multi-connection wall charger. The power bank came with almost a 50% charge capacity and that was pretty pleasing to me already. I decided to see how long it took to reach each cell level (there are 4 indicator lights that blink until that cell "fills up" before moving on to the next flashing indicator light.) To move from 25% to 50% took 20 minutes. To move from 50% to 75% took 3hrs, and to move from 75% to 100% took 3.5hrs, totaling 6hrs 50min. In other words, or charged up overnight and this charge will last 6 months. Would you wait 8 hours to charge your Anker power core on two charging cables twice a year? 😏 Right! I would too! I also love the light carrying pouch that comes with the power bank. It's smooth curves make it easy to carry and won't harm your bag or even your hands with sharp boxy edges. It's a great joy to me to have this kind of charging freedom. I can even charge my phone and laptop at the same time! Or charge my tablet and laptop. If I was to play devil's advocate, I would first have to see how the power bank performs with different cables, if it can charge my laptop faster, for instance. If this product gets upgraded to include a fast charging port or even 3 ports I'll be buying that one as well. This is a great product.

Not always convieniet to find an outlet and this charger stays with me while charging. I've never used more than a third of the charge contined in this battery. One of my better purchases. Another great Anker purchase. I've had consistent quality from Anker. I don't use it very often, but when I have needed it, especially during power outages, it has saved me. Holds it's charge for months on end. As to those who say it takes too long to charge, please note, that the typical charger is 2A (2,000ma). 26800/2000=13.4 hours for a full charge from completely discharged! That's physics! Likely fire or explosion if it charged at double or more than 2A. However, there are two charger inputs so you can safely cut charge time in half, still much longer than most people are used to. Big battery=long charge time. Good trade-off.

title: A great battery to have with lots of depth
text: It's all about POWER! A great battery to have with lots of depth.

I use this for camping. We typically play music for hours around the camp fire. There's no power at the site, so there's no good way to charge a Bluetooth speaker and people's cellphones after multiple days up there. I was able to keep a nearly dead speaker running for hours through the night as well as a cellphone running YouTube, and then another cellphone the next day, and only got down to 2 out of 4 battery indicator lights. This was after hours of charging all 3 devices up to the full amount while they were still being used, not charging idle devices. My casual assessment of this is that you could charge a handful of basic devices for two full nights with heavy usage. Downside is that there is no port for modern super fast chargers (the smaller USB-C connections on both ends that most phones are switching to); just old school USB-A and A Mini ports. My buddy had the newer cable and couldn't charge his phone. Same with me, so I had to pick up a USB-A to USB-C cable to charge my Samsung S20 and JBL Charge 4 speaker. It comes with a charging cable for itself which is A Mini into the device. This is a slight inconvenience swapping cables if you have all USB-C chargers sitting around your house. There are multiple ports so you could charge several devices at the same time. Just be aware of and prepare for the proper cables/connections. It comes with a mesh bag that has a drawstring enclosure which is a small but nice feature if you're bringing this outdoors where it could get knocked around or fall. It doesn't offer a high degree of protection but better than nothing. I believe this is just a bank of vape style batteries in a black plastic case. For the price of a little over 50 bucks, compared to the pricier, larger battery boxes, this is perfect for a weekend camping trip or to have handy if the power goes out at home. It was definitely worth the investment for how I use it and I'm glad I didn't spend $100+.

title: Great battery that balances power and size
text: This is the second product in Anker’s PowerCore line that I have been given for review. After reviewing several Anker products, both purchased and sent for evaluation, I have only good things to say. They are well designed, built, and priced at a great value. The new PowerCore line of batteries come in a matte plastic finish which won’t show fingerprints as the Astro line does. If you’re looking for an external battery its so that you can keep your devices charged as needed when a wall outlet isn’t convenient. This is a great balance between a single port battery and a larger battery like the PowerCore 16000. The PowerCore 10400 can charge two devices at once but isn’t as large or heavy as the 16000. Its roughly the size of a billfold wallet which means you can put it in your pocket if needed. I prefer the shorter, more square like shape since it fits perfectly in an interior pocket in my bag. As with other PowerCore batteries it can charge some devices more quickly with its ability to put 2A of power through one port. If you need to charge two larger devices at once this can do it, but one device won’t charge fast as this battery maxes out at 3A total output. For most days this would be more than adequate and won’t take up a lot of space or add weight to a bag. I used to keep two Anker Astro E1 5200 mAh batteries in my bag but this single battery replaces that. The PowerCore 10400 comes with a quality USB cord and a small bag to store and protect the battery in. It has a bright LED light strip to let you know how much life is left in the battery between charges. It is a higher capacity battery so it does take a decent amount of time to charge. I would suggest letting it charge overnight if you expect heavy usage the next day. Anker has continued to impress me with their products and their customer service responded quickly and appropriately when I did have an issue long ago. I was supplied this sample for test and evaluation, and I promise that my review is fair and honest.

title: Fine for Phones and Tablets, FAILS for Smaller Devices, but Support Will Take Care of You!
text: This unit packs quite a bit of charging capacity - with that, I am very pleased. However, its load sensor circuit fails to stay on when charging small items (bluetooth headset, bluetooth earbuds) that consume very little amperage. It shuts off prematurely, not allowing smaller items to charge. This is due to the flawed design of its current sensor circuit. My prior portable charger (by EZO Power) featured an on/off button - when pressed, the unit provided power, period... and I could charge small devices without it cutting off prematurely. Unfortunately, Anker has failed in its design of the current sensor in this product. Jan 2017 Update: Anker made many attempts to contact me (even during the holidays, which made me difficult to get). The offered a full return, partial credit, or a smaller unit to charge small items. They also told me (in kinder words) that the description of their unit makes it clear it's intended for larger electronics, not for small items like bluetooth earbuds or wifi hotspots. I accepted a partial credit (one-third of the amount they proposed - because I felt it was partially my fault for not reading carefully), and I am upping this from 3 to 4 stars, because of their excellent customer service.

title: It's a decent battery for the money
text: This battery is pretty big, and I'm glad that I got the deal on it that I did. That being said, it's not the smallest physical size battery in the 10000 mAh charge size class. It's also heavy, but I think that's just the weight of the battery itself. The battery takes forever to completely charge, especially if you use a traditional 1A phone charger or your laptop's USB port. But even with a 1.5 or 2 A charger, it takes longer to charge up than I would like. Sometimes, this battery seems to discharge really fast - faster than it really should. There are only four indicator lights to show charge level, and they often will drop (say, from 3 to 2) and then go up again later. I'm not sure that they're really any good. If they are, then the batter drains too fast. If they aren't, then they're annoying. I wish there was a better way to check charge level. There are 2 USB ports for charging your device - 1 that adapts power output to the current your device can handle, and the other a dumb 1A (1.5A?) charger. The traditional port works great and I use it for basically all of my charging. When I use the adaptive port, it causes my devices to heat up to an unpleasant level. I've tried this with my iPad Air, my Beats Studio Wireless headphones, and my iPhone 6 Plus. All of the devices heated up noticeably when using the adaptive port, and heat is bad for the internal batteries of these devices. I experience no noticeable heat issues with the traditional port. Overall, it's a decent battery for the money. But there are better batteries out there. EDIT: Raised 1 star for the customer service of Anker.

title: Great Portable Battery From Anker
text: The Anker PowerCore 10400 is a great little portable battery pack. Because it is a 10400mAh battery, it does have some weight to it, but it is easy to carry around. It has a nice black, matte finish that provides plenty of grip while still looking nice. In addition to getting the PowerCore battery pack, you’ll find in the frustration-free box a nice padded travel/storage bag and a Micro USB charger to charge your PowerCore. Its real easy to start using your new PowerCore, mine came with about a 75% charge, so I was able to plug the cable right in and start using it to charge my devices. There are two ports to charge your phone from, and one port to charge the PowerCore itself. There is one button on top that, when pressed, gives you the current battery level of the PowerCore via a indicator light on the front. I like to use the PowerCore for a few different things. Mainly, its great for travel. It has enough battery to charge my LG V10 fully and more than once. This makes it a great device for in-car use, where the car power ports aren’t enough. It can also be handy around the house, when I need a charge, but don’t have an outlet nearby. The best part about this is how fast it charges. Because of the massive battery and Anker PowerIQ technology, this charges my phone as fast as if my phone was charging from an Anker PowerPort with PowerIQ technology! This makes it so much more worth getting! If you are looking for a moderate sized battery pack, this is a great one to get. It is a worthwhile investment over the smallest battery packs available. Anyone can benefit from this product! Overall, I’m really impressed with this product. Its super easy to use, works great, and is great to have on hand for unusual situations! I would most certainly recommend this or similar Anker battery packs to anyone!

title: Thus far, the best portable charger
text: You may ask yourself: if I already have a charging case, why would I need such a portable charger? You'd have to carry an extra cable, find a place to put it on your person, etc etc. Let me start off by saying that I DID happen to be upon that dilemma! I was bestowed a sample of Anker's slim battery case for the iPhone 6, and while I did love it and there was little interference with my every day life, there was that 5% that just wanted more portability and lightweight picture taking. In a recent trip, I decided to take off the battery case and let the phone breathe a little, while allowing my hands to take on less weight for scenic pics and numerous selfies. I still had qualms about running out of power, so I brought along the powercore 5000 and the traditional lightning cable. This portable charger is ridiculously small for the amount of power that it packs (about 1.5-2 iPhone 6s charges). I put it in my left pocket with the cable and completely forgot that it was there (even during a hike with slim fit shorts, mind you). Once I needed the power, I just popped it out, connected it, and left everything in the same pocket (side note: I did feel the phone and charger and cable in the shorts; it's not THAT slim!). The build feels very premium, as expected from a powercore product line. It's portable enough to put in a backpack or back pocket and serves the needs of most users. Extreme power users, I'm assuming people who play Pokemon Go 18 hours a day, might need something with more juice, but for the rest of us Facebook posters, vacay picture takers and snapchatters, this should work perfectly. This is a grade A product, and I'm always excited to see what Anker comes up with next. As always, I was supplied a sample for test and evaluation, and I promised that my review is fair and honest.

title: The Anker PowerCore 5000 is the perfect size for on the go charging
text: The Anker PowerCore 5000 is the perfect size for on the go charging. It has a 5000mAh battery and charges devices at a faster rate than other battery chargers I have used in the past. The PowerCore feels premium in the hand and fits easily into a front pocket or cargo pocket. It also comes with a carrying case and micro USB charger. I was able to get about 1.75 charges for my Moto X Pure 2015 but mileage may vary depending on the device you are charging. If you are looking for a backup battery for your phone or tablet you can go wrong with the Anker PowerCore 5000.

title: Compact battery with plenty of power
text: Anker does an excellent job of offering several different battery capacities in a wide range of form factors. Having purchased an Anker PowerCore+ mini almost 2 years ago and then an Anker Astro E1 shorlty after that, this new Anker PowerCore 5000 is a mix of both of those devices. Similar shape to the mini with the capacity of the E1. I’ve also had the luck of sampling several other Anker products as well and can say that Anker continues to deliver great products. The prices listed on Amazon compared to what you would pay for similar devices at another retail store are astounding. More than double the cost for the same amount of battery and you don’t get the same warranty that Anker offers either. The PowerCore 5000 is tube shaped, approximately 4.25” in height, and 1.25” in diameter. Both those measurements are slightly more than the product description lists. Still plenty portable and light enough to have in a pocket or easily store in a bag without taking up space or adding weight. As a portable power source it does a great job. It outputs enough power to provide a quick power boost to keep what you need powered to the end of the day. My daughter used this with her iphone while she played a new game that is a huge battery drain. Kept her going without having to worry about her phone dying. The battery itself is encased in a matte finish plastic. It may be susceptible to some scratching if just tossed in a bag but Anker provides a soft bag to store battery in while not in use. Like all Anker products that I have used it feels like a premium product without premium pricing. I can without hesitation recommend this battery to those who need it. Its great if you have several devices that may need charging at once or over a long period of time and small enough that you can always bring it with just in case. I did receive this product for testing and evaluation but promise that this review is fair and honest. As I wrote earlier, I have also purchased several Anker products besides the ones I have received for reviews and will continue to do so in the future.

text: To start off I want to say that I got this product to review with my unbiased opinion. When you first get the package it is a nice small package that is the typical white and teal color box. Or if you have an iphone, you can also keep that cord in it as well. - This little battery actually has 3 power indicator lights. I personally like it better when it has 4, but the fact that it has lights is actually rather uncommon with these smaller batteries. - It has enough charge to charge a phone at least one time. I have the Samsung S7 active with a 4000 mah battery. So, this battery can only charge it one time. But, it could get you through those rough times when you just don't have enough power to make it. Or if you have a phone that does alot. It can give it that little kick that it needs to keep going. - trying to keep it short, I'll make this the last pro. It has charge IQ in it. This is one of my favorite features. Charges all devices safely and quickly. I almost refuse to buy any anker products without this feature. Cons - The exterior of this battery is plastic. Most of the other anker batteries that I have seen and own all have metal exterior. So, I was little disappointed about that. - There are only three charge indicator lights. It is a great feature, but I do think 4 is better to gauge off of. There is not a lot of negative things to say about this little guy. It is not something that I would take for a weekend of camping. But, it is something that I would take to a day in the beach (I actually did this, and it worked very well.) It is a nice reliable product to give you phone a full charge to keep you going. I hope that this review has helped you out to decide if this is the battery for you.

text: I received this as an Evaluation from Anker. It arrived with 66% charge according to the 3 light indicators, I plugged it in and it took about an hour to get to full charge from that point. I'm a klutz so I knocked it off of the desk and it dropped about 4 feet to the floor and it didn't show any signs of scratches or cracks. The build quality is awesome, it doesn't feel like I'm going to break it. I work with a few people so I tested charging various phones... a Samsung S4 took an hour to charge from 65%-100%, I dug out an iPhone 4 that was completely drained in 8 minutes it had a 10% charge, after an hour it had 45% and was completely charged after 2 hours 20 minutes Then I hooked it up to a Nokia 830 and in 2 hours and 30 minutes went from 47% to 100% charge Then I hooked up another Nokia 830 and in an hour it went from 17% to 38% charge before the PowerCore 5000 ran out of charge I hooked it up to a USB power brick and charged it up through an outlet which took 4 hours and 30 minutes. I travel a lot as I'm in IT as well as a photographer and always get the question on where they can charge, now I toss them this little device and they stare at it for a couple of minutes while watching it power their device. It is a good size product, the diameter is about the size of a soda bottle cap and about 4 inches long, a little smaller than an empty toilet paper roll It came with a little pouch which protects it as it bounces around in my backpack. It has 1 input and 1 output the output is 2A and includes the charging cable, if you want to charge it from the wall you will need a USB power adapter, Anker sells those too. I would recommend this to anyone that travels, or is not able to leave their phone in one spot to charge.

title: No fake battery states it's the real deal!
text: TL:DR @ bottom but do yourself a favor and read the entire review, it has some VERY important info Most battery banks will say they are 10,000 or more mAh but they aren't... In fact most are half of what they claim. I know, I bought a bunch and opened them up and read the info right off the battery. This one and other's from this brand are legit. This small bank packs 2 batteries to hit it's advertised numbers. It also recharges fast if you have a 45w charger but even a regular one will do fine. It has the best soft plastic I've ever felt... It's like suede and so smooth. The power indicator is pretty accurate but I recommend calibration when you first get it. So let it reach room temp if it's cold outside (takes 2 hours) then drain the bank until it has no charge left which means the little flashlight won't turn on and charge something until the bank won't charge it anymore then unplug, wait 15 min and plug something back into it just to make sure. After that charge the bank to 100% and leave it plugged it once it hits 100% for another hour then discharge it it's dead and repeat. Id do this maybe once every 6 months because it's not good for a lithium battery to have 0% charge but calibration is important too. So this thing is excellent. It charges everything and anything and does so quickly. The only downside and I mean ONLY downside is the sad excuse for a flashlight. They might as well remove it. Its a single led so it's essentially as bright as a single small Christmas light. Other than that it's excellent and this brand has replaced Anker as my go to battery bank. Oh.. Anker failed the capacity test. This bank has amazing capacity, it's small and it's got a fantastic price. Just do yourself 1 favor and try to buy it directly from their Amazon store so you know you aren't getting a fake. TL;DR A must buy! Amazing value, amazing capacity. Nice carrying bag.

text: Just received this portable charger. First impression is - it's heavier weight and larger dimensions (length, thickness, not necessarily width) than I anticipated. I wouldn't carry (nor would it fit) in a mens pants pocket - it would have to be in a backpack or separate shoulder-like carry pouch. I think it's too big for any of my fanny packs. Is it portable? Yes, but not that compact. I bought it mostly for its usb-c port (since my Apple snuck that in on my ipad pro and none of my other power packs are compatible) and that it's rated to recharge it about 3 cycles (well suited for a long intercontinental air flight or multiple days without a wall outlet) plus a little power remaining for my iphone 6s plus. I used my ipad pro charger (18w) as it's usb-c and this power pack comes naked (no power adapter/cords). Arrived with 1-2 out of 4 battery led lights lit, and a full top-off took about 8-9 hours which fits right in to about what I read on-line. Probably from ground zero I'd plan 11 hours. What I need to figure out now is how it fits into my 'travel light' approach as that's why I have an ipad pro for remote work while mobile rather than a laptop pc brick. I will probably have to leave this unit in the car due to its weight and size, ready for a charge but not within arm's reach unless I'm on a road trip. Will it fit into my thin shoulder ipad pro accessories pocket? Yes, horizontally not vertically. But its far heavier and thicker than the tablet it's to server, sort of like a sumo wrestler protector for an acrobat. Hmm, so this sucker better charge when it's called on or the brick it is will be downgraded from 4 to 1 star in no time flat. This is a '30' model, the next lower is '20' but its dimensions are about the same (but weight about 0.5 lbs more) so I decided to gamble on its capacity as the size differential wasn't substantial between the models but about double the rated charge capacity. So I went for it. More later.

title: It's a monster
text: I bought this for my trip over seas. First off this thing is massive and weights a ton. I was expecting it to be a little smaller and lighter. Pros: 1. High capacity for lots of use. I was able to charge my Note 20 Ultra multiple times during my trip before needing to charger the powerbank. Great for an all day use powerbank or even for a weekend get away trip. 2. Have different ports and you can charge more than 1 device at a time. Great if you need to charge your phone, tablet, or wireless head phones at the same time. Cons: 1. Too big for airline travel. I think most airlines allow max 100Wh battery and this powerbank comes in at 111Wh which is over the limit. While in the US I was able to go through all the check points with no issues, but got stopped in Asia due to the size. Luckily with the airline I used allowed a slightly larger battery to be carried on board so I was able to get through and not have to donate my powebank to the tsa agent. Some tsa might consider it as a standalone battery and some may consider it as a portable device with a battery like a computer. 2. Really long charge time. First charge took literally the whole day to charge. Even after use depending on how much you use the powerbank and using a super fast charger to charge it still takes all day to fully charge. Sucks if your traveling and always on the move. Wish there was a faster charging option available. 3. No real manual on how the different port functions or which port to use. Or how the power button works. If I hold down the power button for a long time the led lights changes color and I'm not really sure what that does. 4. This thing weights a ton and massive. 5. No faster charging option. While there are 2 ports that allow fast charging for devices that can do fast charge, having a super fast charging will make this even better. More cons than pros but overall it's a good powerbank. Just be aware of the size and if that doesn't matter you can't really beat the price point for a 30,000mah powerbank. Simple and works.

My 5 year old Anker charging banks are still going strong! I recommend them over this brand. After review: the company contacted me without being asked. They sent me a replacement unit and it operates as it should. I only knocked one star for the experience but I still love the design and size of the battery, we'll see how it does over time.

text: We have two of these on our boat. The solar panel is tiny (one watt), so leaving it out in the sun to charge will only get you a little power. This works really well since we have 150 Watt solar panel for our boat. I can charge my phone to 100% at least three times off one fully charged battery. Our battery has lasted two years so far. The charge holds for at least a week or more. As an aside, solar panels, charge controllers, and batteries have become so cheap, I was thinking of getting a solar panel and charge controller along with a couple of batteries for our frequent home power outages, so I can keep my electronics charged up during power outages at home!

title: Very heavy and takes hours to recharge an iPhoneX
text: Not sure if mine is defective but it takes many hours to charge my iPhone X. Note in case it’s not clear from the pictures, you can charge one phone wirelessly but the other two phones need to be plugged in with your own charging cables to the two usb outlets. Instructions say to charge and completely use up the battery of the device at LEAST 3 times with the first charge being plugged into the wall and not via solar. However, when this solar charger gets down to the last battery bar, you’ll notice that when you try to wirelessly charge or charge with the USB port, that it will initially start charging, but within a minute, it will shut off. So beware that it’s not like your phone where you can use it till it’s completely empty. The led lights still work at that point though. It’s been really hard to completely discharge the device because when it’s on its last battery bar, it won’t charge my phone. I’ve been waiting for the device to run out of battery on its own but it’s been two days that it still has one bar left. Main problems: 1. POTENTIALLY NOT WATERPROOF: Included Instructions say not to get this wet, even though it’s marketed as water proof. The rubber orange flap that covers the USB ports is very flimsy in that I’m not convinced its a very tight waterproofed seal when closed. I am comparing this to my Olympus waterproof camera and Pelican waterproof phone case, which both have very tight seals for any ports. 2. WEIGHT: this thing is half the thickness of a brick and weighs about the same as a brick. It’s not something you’d want to take backpacking or in a purse. It’s more of a for-emergency-situations tool. Instructions recommend you utilize it at least every three months. 3. DURATION OF RECHARGE: It takes a long time (like overnight) to recharge itself even when plugged into a wall charger. 4. EFFICIENCY: It takes at least twice as long to charge my iPhoneX than my other wireless charging pads at home.

The QI wireless charger is extremely efficient and worked great with my Samsung S10. They could've put a better compass and karabiner belt clip because the one they included was completely worthless but I wouldn't hang it from a molle pack or anything anyway. I mounted mine in a molle pouch with an open face where the solar panel goes. That way I can attach it to my web and go and it'll still charge when my pack is in the sun. The f;ash light is just sufficient but I don't need the extra bells and whistles, I prefer it do it's main job better then trying to serve as multiple things anyway. On its 3.0 USB connection it can turbo charge my Moto z2 force quicker compared to my 15 watt wall charger, even though the amp app says it's charging slightly lower than my wall charger around .4 watts less, not sure what's happening there but it could be that it's a cleaner and safer power coming from it. Went from 20% to full charge in 50 minutes so roughly an hour to charge most Android phones that support quick charge. Connected an iPhone 4 and in the USB 3.0 it charged from 0 to 20% in 20 minutes. Then I charged an iPhone 7 from 0 to 20%, it took quite long, 30 minutes to be exact, so iPhones don't charge quick so far in the tests I made, and wasn't able to monitor amps and volts, the wireless charging might be better but I cannot test it at the moment. This solar charger I charged it fully before I started the tests and so far it did not went below 1 out of the 4 full charge indicator, meaning it still has juice to continue, and I did blocked the solar cells so it didn't absorbed additional energy. So far so good. One thing I'd recommend is make the little door where it opens that seals thecharging ports to be more solid cuz I'm sure if I pull it, it will break. Other than that seems really good to have. Solar absorbtion seem to work at any time, charges while laying just there or while charging something, it has a green indicator.

text: This is the largest of three portable chargers I own (both in size and capacity). It's big and heavy, but I've carried it in a pocket on several occasions and it's perfectly manageable. A backpack might be preferable if you plan to carry one anyway or you're a fan of skinny jeans. I can't say how quickly this charger will bring a completely dead phone up to 100%, but I've been very pleased with my usage so far. I generally get three nearly-full charges out of it WHILE the phone is in constant use. I made note of the specifics once: With the charger at full charge, and with my phone in use, it brought my phone from 5% to 95% percent while dropping from 100% to 61%. The next day, it brought my phone from 11% to 100% while dropping from 61% to 22%. On the third day, I charged my phone from 18% to 100%, which took the charger from 22% to 1%. Additionally, I have carried the charger with me on multi-hour excursions in which the phone is in constant use (pokemon go, mostly) and have never had battery usage outpace charger replenishing. It always regains charge, even while the phone is in use. My smallest battery charger often manages to only maintain my current charge level (ie if I plug the phone it at 22%, it's stay around 22% with the small charger. That's not bad for your smartphone, but if you're going to try to charge tablets and stuff, you're not going to get full charges, generally. As always, it's an Anker product, so it's built tough. I dropped mine on concrete by accident (in its bag) and it smashed an earbud that was next to it, but it didn't take any damage that I've detected. I can't overemphasize the convenience of having a two-in-one charger and power bank. I also like that recharging this one is as easy as plugging it into a wall -- or, if you want, you can charge it with a micro-USB cable. Yeah. It's exactly what I expected. This would be a great gift for someone going on a trip in the USA/Canada/wherever those outlets are used.

text: I considered whether to go 4 or 5 stars on the Fusion 5000, it essentially replaces your OEM transformer bricks and gives you a walk away power source at the very small expense of a larger size and weight. So when you switch from the wall tap to portable mode, if you're using it to power a non-battery powered device, your device will shut off when you unplug the Fusion 5000 from a wall outlet. It's not a deal killer by any means, just be aware for example if you using it for an Alexa Dot, you'll have pause briefly to reboot the Dot. Positives abound: 2 outputs, folding tines, solidly built, Power iQ technology, USB input for recharging the Fusion when outlet not available, power meter display. I'd suggest upgrading the next version to uninterrupted, and add a larger sibling, perhaps a 10,000, for those that want it may be out there..

But, once in a while, I need to have a battery back up when I cannot plug-in. It has worked beautifully in these situations, charging my iPhone and my Apple Watch fully from being nearly depleted. I know some of the reviews have said it may not have as much energy as other back up batteries, but for me, this is exactly what I wanted: mostly a wall adapter with sort of an "emergency" back up battery. I think if you just need a wall adapter, I would get something else, or if you just needed a back up battery, I would also probably pick something else. You should know this item takes just about 2hr 45min to fully charge while using a super fast 30w charger. The google pixel is done like in 40min. It’s also bigger in person than how you see it in the pictures. I tested this battery in two different ways to see how much juice I get out of it. Phone for this test will be a brand new iPhone 13 mini. 13mini 20% to 80% uses %25 from the jwalker from a full charge state so 100>75=%60 for 13mini Battery randomly went down from 75 to 73 while not in use 73>33=%50+ for 13mini J walker lost one percent 33>32 during idle/not in use. 33>8=% for iPhone 13 mini (29%>47%) Once the battery reached 8%, it died. So in total for this battery in this test I got 128% in battery use. —— In this exam we took the jwalker at 99% with the iPhone 13 mini at 3% and began to charge it to see how much battery would jwalker use in order to get the 13mini to 75% iPhone 13 mini 3%>80%=36% from j walker. This product is definitely bad. The jwalker in less than 2 minutes goes from 99% to 90%. Meanwhile the 13 mini only went from 3% to 4% iPhone 13 mini 0%>53%=64% from j walker. Once j walker 20% charge it just completely died. The total charge here for the 13 mini is 133% which is %5 higher than the previous exam. I have come to conclusion that this battery is not 6,000 mah as it claims to be. It seems to be more of about 2500-2700 mah since the iPhone 13 mini is 2438 mah Happy shopping

title: Great for recharging while on the go with one potential Gotcha
text: When camping I have been dragging around a car portable battery jumper box because it had 2 cigarette lighter ports to charge phones with. It was heavy and cumbersome and takes up lots of space in the tent. With this charger I can accomplish the same job in 1/20th the space. The charger unit is about the same size as my HTC One X+ phone. I can run the phone while connected to the battery to preserve its battery and extend usability for days. I have used it for a few days now with my phone but have only tried using it to charge two phones briefly. It seems to do the job fine though neither was completely drained so I don't have a gauge on how well it would work from a drained state. I was unable to charge my tablet with it because my tablets supplied cable only charges from the wall plug, not a USB port (no fault of this devices) so you might want to confirm that capability of your mobile device before purchasing for a specific purpose! I would have to spend a few dollars to get that functionality via a new cable. The one GOTCHA: I did note that when my phone fully charged after about 15-20 minutes it stopped charging. The phone was no longer receiving power from the battery so if you left it alone for hours on end it could potentially charge up and drain down again. I left it fully charged and then saw the charge light o the phone go off for about an hour and never saw it come back on again. Pushing the battery status button on the charger or disconnecting/reconnecting the cable got it going again. I DO NOT KNOW if this behavior is the result of the way this charger works or my phone or if it will do that with every phone?! Overall I am very pleased with this purchase because now I can run the phone on an extended outing or away from power without hesitation or concern that it end up dead before my trip is over.

title: Not perfect but it’s a good value for the money
text: The power bank holds a lot of charge and it has four USB A ports you can use for charging devices. It also had two input ports: a USB C port and a micro USB port that can only be used to charge the power bank. It also has a solar panel on one side but it barely works and may take days of continuous sun exposure to charge the power bank this way (if it works at all). The back side has a large LED light that can turned on by double clicking the power button and can also be used to send an SOS light signal by flashing on and off. I was disappointed by the very badly translated instructions it came with. They are almost impossible to understand. I basically had to figure most things out myself by trial and error. The other disadvantage is the very long charging time required (about 17-18 hrs). The solar and light panels make it very thick which reduces its portability. I think it would be better if it came without the solar panel (since it doesn’t really work) so it would be thinner. Overall a good value for the money especially because of the light panel which is very useful in addition to the large charge capacity.

title: Versatile Power Bank
text: This is a nice power bank with unique capabilities. The product description indicates that all outputs can be used concurrently. This isn’t exactly true. With the USB-C PD output connected to and charging a laptop PC via its USB-C PD port, the PD output quits charging the laptop when a phone is placed on the wireless charging pad. Interestingly, both outputs work concurrently when the PD port is connected to another phone. I inquired about this discrepancy and never received a practical response. Several reviews indicate that the capacity of this power bank is apparently less than what’s claimed when the charging pad is used. In general, Qi wireless charging has an overall energy transfer efficiency of ~65 %. When this is considered, the claimed capacity of the product appears accurate.

title: Great Compact Charger
text: This is a very small but capable charger. It is well build and is the smallest 10,000mAh charger I have tested. I have been using this charger for a month now and I can say it has been very reliable. It doesn’t lower its output current as it gets close to being fully drained and is comparable to a wall charger for phones that don’t use more than 18w. I really like it ability to charge the power bank using something similar to Samsung AFC. The only downside I have notices is that the PD charge controller is limited to 2.4A instead of the 3A stated on the product and in the manual. I would say most people wouldn’t notice this and most device would likely switch to a higher voltage at that point. You can only see it when charging the device with USB Type C cables using a 3A capable charger. The cable provided is nice and usable, but I wish it came with a USB Type C to Type C cable in addition to the Type A to Type C cable provided. Capacity: The usable capacity of the charger is about 6,500mAh or a more usable number of 33Wh. I would look more at (Wh) for a fair comparison because many modern devices charge at different voltages which affects the mAh observed. It can charge a standard phone at least 2 times with the potential to do a third time on some phones. Packaging: Good and compact although it can be tricky to get the charger out. The packaging was also activating the charger because of how snug of a fit it was. Overall: I would recommend this to anyone looking for a good and small portable charger. It would be great for both Android phone users as well as the iPhone crowd.

title: Small power bank, easy to carry around. Charge and recharge fast.
text: My 2-year's old cellphone starts showing a sign of aging. The run time after each full charge is getting shorter now. The phone is still working great with 6GB memory and 128G storage. Instead of spending big money on a new phone, I think a power bank is a more economic way in this case. I don't want to carry a big and heavy power bank. After a search, I bump into this new, smaller power bank with 10000Amh capacity from AINOPE...and price is also very good. Upon receiving it, the power bank is indeed small, very easy to carry it in the pocket (really no complaints about the size of it). It has 3 output ports, so I can charge 3 devices at the same time. It has one mini USB input port for charging. The USB-C port can be used for charging my phone, or for recharging the battery itself. After 1 week's usage, it charges my phone fast. Also, it is recharged fast when using a wall-adaptor (not included in this package) with 2.4A current output. Most of the power banks use 4-bar to show the status of the power bank. This AINOPE power bank is using a digital numerical number to show the exact status of the power bank. I like this feature also. All in all, I am happy with this power bank, except one thing. The button (for checking the battery status) is not recessed. So, the button is always pressed un-intentionally. I am able to convert and use a laptop camera cover to shield the button. So, the button does not get pressed un-intentionally. By the way, it comes with 2 USB-C cables. The package does not include a wall-adaptor for charging this power bank. And, the package does not include any carrying pouch.

title: Good Power pack for a Quest headset
text: I got this to extend the run time for the Oculus Quest. Day one of use and it is encouraging. The pack takes its time to charge up to full, but when pared to the Quest it will run it and charge it at the same time. It delivers more power than the quest will use. If the Quest is sleeping or off, it will charge it much faster than on its own charging cable. The combo easily managed a 3 hour session and had 77% power on battery and over 70% on the headset. You have to check it every so often because if the headset hits 100%charge the pack will turn off and stop charging. I originally thought I might be able to wear it on my arm with a phone holder like runners use, but it is way to heavy. Easily fits in a fanny pack positioned in the back and you don’t notice the weight. It seems to run cooler than the battery pack I was previously using. The instructions are a joke and poorly translated. If you want to try and read it you will either need a good magnifying glass or take a picture with your phone and expand it. You won’t learn much, but feel free. As others have mentioned, there seem to be a couple versions in the reviews with slightly different cable connections. So far haven’t found any combo that speeds up charging the pack itself. It would be nice to have instructions that explain things. Giving it a 4 for now, as the terrible paperwork was just off putting. Will update once I have more time with it. Update: My slow charge time was based on a standard USB wall plug. Stick it on a higher amp plug and you will not be waiting forever. I don’t think it is a strong as it is billed, but it works well and more compact than others at its power point. If I have the stamina, this block will keep the Quest going for multiple hours at a time. It will outlast me and with the new power plug it is ready to go again after an overnight charge. No more 15 hr charging sessions.

title: Good Value, Nice Display of Percentage, But Seems to Drain Fast
text: I have another 20,000mAh portable charger that I put to the test against this 26800 version. Before I get to the differences I saw there, let me first say that I really like the touch of having the percentage charged indicator on this charger. I am used to having flashing dots to tell me approximately how charged the device is, but having an "exact" number is nice. However, maybe that's where the problem lies. The 26,800 version (this one) seems to drain faster with the same technology as does my older 20,000 mAh battery pack. In fact, I tested it with charging a tablet and a phone from ~50%. The 26,800 was down to 41% after filling up the phone. We know that 50% of an iPhone is not over 14,000mAh, so that was odd. I tried two other times. It was down to 50% the second time and 55% the third. So what do I take from that? Maybe I need to charge it a few times for it to maximize throughput? I don't know. That said, I do LIKE this charger and think that it is a decent backup, especially at the price point. Maybe a good way to think of it is that you can get a 15,000 mAh pack for under $30?

Only odd thing is that (OUT4) is black and OUT3 and OUT2 are blue. 18 month warranty, register online. Normal precautions with this device, avoid dropping and it's not water proof, also don't leave in extreme heat. A device at this size is great for using with any backpack that has the built in charging cord. Normally I keep this in my camera gear bag. title: Not Even Close to Accurate
text: Everything appears to work fine with the Mi Fit. It can be taken in a pool, it connects well to the app, it can track sleep, it has great battery life, the screen can be seen in daylight, there is a good amount of data. It has pretty much all of the features I wanted. But none of that matters when the HR monitor is ridiculously inaccurate. The pedometer also is inaccurate but it's at least a bit closer and less important. The HR monitor would jump from reading 47 to 98 within a minute when my position didn't change. Even at peak exercise, it read my HR as so low that it didn't think I was putting in any effort. But, I still assumed it must be close enough until I had to go to the ER for what turned out to be AFib. I was connected to a heart monitor and my Mi Fit would be reading me at 50HR when I was actually at 135. And it never really got any closer to accurate. When I was released to go home, I used my wife's Amazon Halo band so we could track my heart rate. It read it very consistently and similar to what I was when I left the hospital. I put my Mi Fit on my other wrist to compare and it was still about 50 beats per minute lower than reality. I think this is extremely dangerous especially considering I now have a heart condition I need to keep track of at 35 years old. I have immediately discarded this band and will never use it again. If the heart rate reading is important to you and your health, I suggest you do not get this product. If you just want a cheap digital watch that gives you a vague picture of your steps, then I think this would work fine. Because so many of the features rely on the HR data, you won't be able to trust much of anything is accurate.

How many people playing badminton are really concerned about their testing heart rate ?? The blood pressure monitoring is way off as you can see from the photos, 125/64 with a calibrated sphygmomanometer & 142/84 with the watch, but I didn’t really expect an accurate blood pressure from a watch anyway.
