text: I have a Google pixel phone and this watch is amazing. I had Fitbit for several years and they would disconnect. I have had this watch for several months now and had zero connectivity issues. The only complaint is the battery life. I keep it on battery saver, so it lasts a little longer but I still get my notifications. I love the features on it, too (steps, HR, stress level, water intake, workouts).

title: Good looking but has serval bugs
text: I use the watch with non-galaxy Android smart phone. The watch has good looking style. Overall, the functionalities are good. However, the most annoying bug is that whenever the phone went to airplane mode and turn off airplane mode, the watch won't reconnect. It will require user to reset (clear everything) the watch in order for it to reconnect to the phone. It might be a software bug but not sure if Samsung will cooperate with other phone company to fix this issue.

title: Great watch
text: Love this galaxy 4 watch, the only downfall is 2 to 3 days battery life!!

title: Nothing special
text: The size of the watch was a good size. The band was comfortable. However, I didn't like the keyboard and I never knew when the battery was running low. It was not easy to navigate!

title: Nice upgrade from my other smart watch
text: This samsung galaxy 4 44mm watch is probably smarter than I am. It has so many features that I still haven't used them all. My favorite of those features are sleep tracking, being able to read and send text messages. Also surprisingly it connects to my Ring doorbell and Ring app. It doesn't show the Ring video, just a thumbnail, but it let's you know there is someone at your door. That blew me away when I found that out after I bought the watch. The drawbacks for this watch are I get a contact rash when I wear it to long. The rash is under the watch itself as well as the band so changing the band wouldn't make a difference. I googled about the watch and rashes and apparently it is a thing that is happening to other people too. The other thing is I have to charge the watch every other day, but it charges in about an hour so that's not so bad. Overall it is a great smart watch and I am happy with my purchase.

title: No
text: Battery not that great compared to my 5 year old watch. No physical bezel to navigate. No integration with google assistant. Not compatible with many old phone apps for some reason

title: Decent.
text: I expected more freedom of customization and the ability to select which step tracker I use. I don't like that I can't sync my steps to my phone just because I prefer Google Fit over Samsung Health.

title: Great watcg
text: This paired easily with my Android phone. It is lightweight and easy to read. My hands are a little big for some of the apps but a stylus works great. I suggest watching some You Tube videos as tutorials for the watch.

title: This watch looks great
text: I love my new watch. It is an extension of my phone and very easy to use.

title: Horrible battery life
text: Can't make it a day without the watch going into battery saving mode

title: Not what I hoped for
text: Not the fault of the product. I am constantly frustrated in their sleep monitor. If you're just lying quietly, they assume you're asleep, which really skews the readings. As a 50 year insomniac, I will tell you that when I wake up during the night, the last thing I want to do is be terribly active so the damned watch realizes I'm awake. I WANT to go back to sleep, so I lie quietly hoping sleep will come and embrace me once again. I wouldn't buy this again, but it nice that my watch now has my baby girl's hooding ceremony on the face when I want to see the time.

title: Fitness tracker apps for phone and watch did not work!
text: I was unable to get the apps for the phone or the watch to work. For sleep all it would tell me is the hours sleep, everything else was just blank. For heart rate just high low and a small chart on the watch that you cant really tell anything from. The phone app was no better. I was very disappointed with this product. it really seems like it was just half baked. lots of very important details like battery life and app design were horrible.

title: Terrible fitness watch
text: It's been disappointing from day one of getting this watch. As a galaxy phone user, I decided to upgrade from a 7 year old watch to this, thinking it can only be better. I was so wrong... Bugs that I've noticed so far: 1. Always on display is dim, so when running outside in the sun you can't see anything. There's no way to make it brighter, you have to touch the watch/raise wrist to turn it back on, rendering AOD worthless 2. GPS is slow and inaccurate. Example: running 100m sprints, according to the watch, my top speed was 10mph - yes, 10!!! This is my max out of 8 x 100m sprints. I run 10k at 10mph pace. 3. There is no heart rate zone training in the app. Old watch has it 4. Can't adjust your heart rate zones. My maximum heart rate is much higher than the watch has by default which makes all of my zones wrong. My old watch can be adjusted 5. My old watch has a mode where you race vs your previous run. Not GW4 6. It loses my heart rate all the time when using 'Other workout' One more thing, Samsung health app shows a graph of your workout with time on the X axis. However, you can't tell what exact minute and second the point on the graph refers to. It'd be great to be able to see that (needless to say, my 7 year old watch has that functionality). I was thinking about returning the watch from the beginning but was trying to find solutions to those issues. Now my 30 days are over and it seems these are the worst 150 bucks I've ever spent. Samsung just seem to be a decade behind true sports watch companies. I'll try to get rid of this and get a Pilar/Fitbit/etc., I know those work as they are supposed to. I do NOT recommend this watch

title: I feel robbed
text: I seriously hate this piece of crap. I have to charge it twice in every 24 hour period. So how can anything it tracks be even close to accurate. My Fitbit needed a charge every third or fourth day and I trusted its accuracy. You should be ashamed, Samsung.

title: worse battery life than prior models...
text: I don't have too many apps on this watch, about the same as the previous watch I traded in. I have to re-charge after 12 hours of use. My other watch lasted all day. I do like it's slimmer and has some extra features. The band is useless to me to struggle with tucking it under. I replaced it with my old watch band that has a buckle.

title: Poor range with phone
text: First of all, let me just say I'm comparing this watch to an Apple Watch. Not really much comparison, Apple has it hands down. I recently switched to a Samsung Phone. I like the phone, but strongly dislike the watch. The range to the phone has to be so close, why even bother . . . This morning I was on the elliptical machine for a little over a mile (30 minutes) and I just noticed a little while ago my watch said 531 steps. How can that be??? My apple watch gave me credit for a workout and it counted towards my steps. This watch isn't as user friendly as the Apple watch either. Oh, and I didn't rate the sleep tracking because I've never used it, so can't say if it's good or bad for that. For those who are looking for something comparable to the Apple Watch, this watch isn't for you. For those who have never had an Apple watch, maybe this will work for you, not sure.

title: I’m so disappointed!
text: I’ve tried several smartwatches because I really want one. I haven’t had much luck with getting what I want in a watch. I decided to just spend the money and get this watch because I have a Samsung phone. I was sure this would do everything. I am unable to read messenger messages which is a big thing for me. Also the different settings don’t always work. I have the touch screen set to wake when touch and the lifting my wrist setting and neither works. I have to switch it on every time which is a pain because I don’t want it to be on all the time. The battery already runs down quickly. Doesn’t even make it a whole day. Also, if you change a setting on your watch it also changes the setting on your phone. This watch is not at all what I expected and I even researched it. Update: after several people looking at it I finally got messenger to work. That was frustrating but I guess my advice would be don't give up it can be done.

title: Already Returned
text: I was so excited about this watch! I had it fully charged before I went to bed and Power Saver was on and it was already at 83% battery when I got up. I refuse to spend my life charging a watch.

title: Unreal! Meaning really good!
text: Much more than I was expecting in a "watch". I'm familiar with an iWatch but Galaxy 4 is way beyond that. Very satisfied except now I'm more curious than ever about the Neely announced Galaxy 5

title: Useful but poor battery life
text: I got the watch on a prime day deal so I thought for a discount I'll give it a try. I would never pay $300+ unless function and battery life gets better. The watch is useful but not needed. I use most for silent notifications when I get text messages and calls. It is nice to have an Google on your wrist. Health functions are neat but I question their accuracy. Battery life is bad, 8-12 hours. Overall it's good smartwatch as far as smartwatches go. I would recommend for someone that's really busy and can't get to their phone for things easily.

title: SAMSUNG GALAXY WATCH 4
text: Samsung Galaxy Watch 4 have great reviews. Amazon sold this watch without a warning that this watch won't work with iPhone. Samsung has now confirmed saying that you won’t be able to pair an iPhone with the Galaxy Watch 4. I will ask Amazon for compensation for wasting my time and keeping my money. It is an ethical issue for selling something that won't work, waste customers' time and keep customers' money.

title: Garbage
text: Don't waste your money. Buggy and laggy. Raise my wrist and swipes are not recognized. This junk is going back.

title: I already had Active 2, this one is better
text: The big takeaway is in the review's headline; the Galaxy Watch 4 is, IMHO, the best watch -- and best value -- Samsung has made to date. Mine has the 44mm bezel, as opposed to my Active 2's 40mm bezel; considerably larger display, and I think it looks better on my wrist. New features my other watch doesn't have, and possibly the health-related features are a little faster to measure/report. All this comes at a cost, though. Battery life per charge is shorter, barely two days versus 3-pluf for the Active 2. That's still roughly twice as long as the battery life of my daughter's Apple Watch. And if I forget to recharge ... well, I can always switch to my other watch, which is fully charged and turned off (so it doesn't discharge).

title: Wow! Totally recommend.
text: So, to be honest I read every single review about this smart watch. The biggest con that I was hung up on was the battery life. Instead of listening to everyone else I decided to take the plunge. I am glad I did! Listen, every day was charge our phones so what's the big deal that the watch only lasts a day as well? Unless you got a dud then that's an issue. I recommend this watch 100%. It does everything I want and more.

title: Looks and feels great but...
text: Day 1 we are at 1 star and I will tell why.... Pros: - Looks and feels like a quality smart watch. - Super responsive screen and the display appears to be top notch. - Samsung wearable app is clean and easy to setup. Cons: - requires you to download the Samsung health app but the app setup is garbage. It guides you towards enabling 2fa but either errors out or closes the app. - you have to have a Samsung phone in order to use the ecg function. Smart watches can be super gorgeous and built with the best specs, but if the required apps lead to a negative customer experience then the product is no good.

title: Does not pair with Iphone
text: I bought this with the intention of pairing it with my iphone after purchasing i realized it doesn't work with iphone. Luckily i was due for an upgrade so I purchase a different phone. Works well as it should.

title: Poor battery life
text: Watch is great with one flaw - its battery life. The battery could last a day with LTE off, however, when it's set to auto it could only last for six hours or less in stand by mode! If you make a few calls the watch gets overheated very quickly, I regret getting the LTE version because of the poor battery, it kind of defeats the purpose of having a data line if I have to keep LTE off.

title: Loving my watch!
text: I was using a diff smart watch and decided to upgrade to this one. Being able to change the face to all the health tracking like sleep(snore detection), ecg, heart rate, all that combined into 1 app..being able to select what you see on the face..able to play YouTube thru the watch(with subscription) connect earbuds to it..I love everything it can keep up with..reminders from your calendar, calls, texts..highly recommend this watch! I have the brightness down so it looks really dark but its just my settings..

title: Disappointing and infuriating
text: My Fitbit Versa 2 was becoming wonky, so I took the advice of my local cellular store and got the Samsung Galaxy 4. It fails at counting steps and I can never get it to accurately log my elliptical workout. It counts less than half of the normal daily steps that my Fitbit did. Or I may find that as of 3pm, it has counted 40 steps. And it changes my settings, so I’m always fiddling with the app to fix. I have an Android, but not a Samsung, so some stuff, like ECG, doesn’t work. Wish I had just waited and switched everything to Apple - phone, watch, etc. Update after 5 months, lowering to 1 star, will try to get a refund. I hate this watch The battery runs out and it goes blank with little notice. This is when it’s been charging all night, dead within 3 hours. I put it on the charger and it gives me a caution symbol which apparently doesn’t have a purpose other than to let you know something is wrong. I’ve researched and done everything possible to extend battery life. It may possibly be the extra charger I bought, they are reported to be picky about after market chargers. Then, the times I can get it to wake up, it says “charging paused” and I can’t get it off airplane mode! Oh, yeah, one of the “extend battery life” directions is to disable the continuous display, and also not have the “raise to wake” setting enabled. How about I just pull out my phone to check the time? Lots of stories like this for this watch. Thinking about replacing it with the cheapest, crappy plastic watch I can find at Target - just to have a reliable time piece on my wrist. Update: why am I still fighting with this thing? Because it should work? To make sure it’s not user error? I started charging only with the OEM cable to resolve those issues. That worked until today when I ran out of battery in mid-afternoon. What??!! Then there are the repeated voicemail notices, long after I listened and deleted them all. And not connected to WiFi? Greyed out? Possibly needs a factory reset? You know, I like tech. I work in tech. But that also gives me a short temper with stuff that’s unreliable. 😡

title: Very nice screen, battery life isn't great
text: Nice watch, everything worked well. The battery did not seem to last more than a day which isn't what i wanted. If you're okay with that and don't want to track your sleep it might be good for you. It does charge pretty quick.

title: Chips easily even with protection
text: Contacted Amazon in Aug 2022 that was going to contact Samsung for replacement. I never heard back from Samsung regarding the issue of replacement. Would like Samsung to contact me to resolve issues.

title: My husband loves it!
text: Christmas gift for the hubby and he loves it! Great fit, lots of functionality and keeps him more apt to responding to texts!

title: Best yet
text: Best smart watch yet. Great size, brightness and all the apps.

title: Best of breed
text: This is my third Samsung Watch and it is light-years ahead of it's older cousins. The difference between 1 and three wasn't that great; between 3 & 4 is huge. I'll let Amazon go over the features but my favorite small improvement is the watch band. The end of the band slips behind the clasp side and is completely hidden and out of the way. Both working with my hands and exercising the traditional band always slipped out or was in the way. It's the little things and their fixes that take my breath away

title: Watch itself is good, but battery life is short
text: Watch itself is good, but battery life is short. can barely last 16 hours in daily use if using it to track multiple activities in a day, it will die with in 5-8 hours

title: Comfortable, cute!
text: This watch was super easy to get up n running. This is my third samsung watch. I hope this one's battery cover doesn't fall off due to summer humidity here in Brooklyn? Battery life isn't the best. It literally lost 25% of its power within 4 hours. I just had to recharge watch after 12 hours. No Bueno.

title: Battery Lasted only 2 hours at a time
text: I was disappointed with this watch. The battery was the worst. I'd charge it to 100%, but then the battery would be drained after only 2 hours! I had all my notifications, screen turns on when raising my arm, etc. turned off too. The app wasn't that great and didn't even have the option to prompt me to get up and move or to drink water. You could track water in the Samsung Health app, but not through the watch or watch app.

title: Great watch!
text: I use with my Samsung Note20 & it does what I need, which is mainly texting, since I work with a doctor & can't be on/have my phone but want my family to have a way to get in touch with me. I can make & receive calls, when needed, and can check my heart, which is nice, since I have SVT. It has a lot of other perks, like activity & food monitoring, as well as sleep, but I don't use them. I'd recommend this watch for those who need it for simple things, like myself, or those who like a little more. The app it connects to is also great.

title: Excellent watch
text: I really like that this watch is lightweight and comfortable to wear. Some of my other smart watches were so heavy that I ended up not wearing them as much as I wanted to. The integrated sensors help me monitor my health and I'm extremely happy with this purchase.

title: doesn't hold a charge
text: This is a beautiful looking watch but essentially not usable. If I remove it from charger and leave on desk it gets totally drained.

title: Stylish and Cool
text: I bought this for my wife and she absolutely loved it. Very stylish with neat features. I have one as well and wear it all the time. There is always room for improvement but we are happy with these watches.

title: Great watch, no google assistant.
text: The biggest problem with this watch is that one of the buttons is mapped to Bixby and cannot be changed, you cannot change it to google assistant currently so you are forced to use Bixby for voice, the digital bevel is not very good in my experience but you can disable it and use it like any other smart watch. It has lots of great and unique features but doesn't do any of them to a high degree of accuracy, if you are really into health equipment then this watch will not be the best choice, but for an average consumer like me the fitness tracking and health features are great to have.

title: Not perfect
text: I like it. It works way better than my fitbit. This watch has yet to track my sleep and the battery dies super fast.

title: Love this watch!
text: This is my third Galazy watch and it's my favorite! I've got a Galaxy Watch 3 Classic and Galaxy Active. To me it's faster and easier to use than the Watch 3. I love being able to customize the watch face with a picture of my dog! I'm not crazy about the battery life, I like to have the watch always on, but I've got two other watches to wear when this needs charging. I can usually get 8 - 12 hours out of a charge and would get more if I didn't have it in the "always on" mode, but it's the look that I like. Not sorry I bought this, it's a beautiful watch.

title: Best android watch of 2021
text: This watch is the best of 2021. Affordable and easy to sync. Just a heads up this watch and the galaxy watch 4 classic are only compatible with Samsung devices. Will not work with other Android phones or Apple devices for those thinking of buying. Battery life is great I work 9-5 by the time I arrive home I have least 60% left. I recommend using the facer app. Tons of face watches to choose from free.

title: Garbage
text: battery life is non existent, all of the sensors that tell you pertinent information have to be turned off to get more than a day. wear app is bunk, Samsung does nothing to help when your app stops functioning and instead blames your phone if its not one of theirs. the ability to text is not worth this much headache. im going back to fitbit

title: Love the watch 4
text: I already owned a Galaxy Gear S2 which has served me well. Was torn between the watch 4 and the classic. Glad I chose the watch 4. Much lighter and sleek design. The watch itself is a huge improvement over the old S2 and Tyson. More apps and better response overall.

title: 40mm vs 44mm
text: Just returned this 40mm watch because the battery life is AWFUL. I have a Galaxy 2 and this was a downgrade. What I didn't realize, is that my Galaxy 2 was a 44mm size which also means it has bigger battery than the 40mm. If you don't mind the watch only holding a charge for a day, get the 40, but if you want a 2-3 day charge, get the 44mm. I returned this and bought a 44. Otherwise, all the features are pretty standard with my old Samsung with a few little upgrades

title: Disappointing
text: Very disappointed in this so-called smart watch. Continued to wear my Fitbit on the same wrist and it counted 2-3 times more steps than this watch. AND this watch has to be charged daily… what a pain! But I did like I could make a phone call and that it had fall detection.

title: Its the Best ever
text: I Love EVERYTHING about this watch it is amazing, I always wanted one , and now I know why. I couldn't live without it.

title: Great PRIME DAY purchase!
text: Love the watch. Still getting used to all the features, but I love it!

title: Vast Improvement
text: I used to have a Fitbit Versa 2 which was ok, but I saw this and thought it would be great to have since I have an S8 phone. Well, wasn't I surprised when my daughter got me the Galaxy watch for this past Christmas. I am still discovering all the cool things it does and what an improvement it is over the Fitbit. It IS like having my phone on my wrist. But, yes....the battery life is the pits. I figure if you are expected to use the watch to its full potential, the least Samsung could do is give you a better power source. I do like the magnetic charger and it charges very quickly.....you just have to charge it every day. Having said this, I still marvel at all the things this little watch can do. I love it!

title: Great watch but battery is not desirable
text: I got this watch from the Samsung website and tried it on and not going to lie, you need Samsung apps and probably a Samsung phone to get the full potential of this device. I have a galaxy device so can't relate to other phone users but all the health apps and connection are Samsung's. This comes with Weed OS 3 but cannot connect it to the Wear app by Google. Pros: -Good sleep tracking, I can't say how accurate it is but I come from a MI fitband and they both agree my sleep is not good -Responding to text messages is much easier as you can install Gboard and other Google play applications. -It had health monitoring such as blood oxygen, heart rate, sleep tracking, ECG, and body mass composition. If you have a galaxy device it even had snore detection. Cons: - It's still an unmature software and although it's probably the best Wear OS device out there so far when it comes to software, it still has a long way to go. - Battery on this device is about a day and it's the reason I would recommend the 44mm version as I was able to get close to two days.

title: It an tell you so many things about your body
text: My only complaint / concern was the watch box was 'unsealed' and the owners guide was missing

title: Battery life needs improvement
text: Great watch, great features, battery life need to be better. Currently only able to squeeze about 30 hours out of the watch. The sleep feature doesn't do much as I need to charge the watch when I sleep. Samsung plz for the love improve this.

title: Watch Face is ridiculous
text: The watch screen cracked after 40 days of wear, even with a screen protector. I am highly disappointed with the screen as it did not receive any impacts outside of a normal desk job. My FitBit lasted over 4 years with no issues, this barely lasted 4 weeks! So now $125 later to fix the screen, I am scared to wear it. ***Even better-apparently if you purchase through Amazon, the warranty is only 30 days if anything else goes wrong. Wish that would have been stated prior to me wasting $175 dollars buying it

title: Good quality. well made.
text: Not enough bluetooth capacity. I can't walk through my house to the bedroom or it loses bluetooth connection. Had to order a second one to replace the 1st one purchased as the screen went totally haywire during set up. Pretty tech savvy but couldn't get it fixed. Seems to be a common issue. Been using the 2nd one for a month and love it.

title: Very Frustrating
text: If you love spending hours searching every forum trying in vain to figure out why your watch won't pair to your phone after your 6,748,435 attempt, then you'll love this watch!

title: Worst customer service and warranty.
text: Watched was a great product until it stopped working. Set it on the charger for about thirty minutes after it died. When I went to turn it back on the screen wouldn't come on, but I could tell it was on because it was vibrating for phone calls and messages. The backside looked like the battery leaked acid out. Being only 8 months old Samsung told me it was still under warranty and sent me to a repair shop about 40 minutes away, who told me that they cannot repair watches, which Samsung knows but sends people to anyways, and I'd have to send it to Samsung. The day Samsung received the watch they sent me a bill for $176 saying it was out of warranty. I called and they said it had liquid damage (if you google,many people have been told the same thing when it breaks) and was no longer powering on. The watch has never been in the shower or pool, only in rain which it is supposedly water resistant up to 200' of water. It also powered on before sending it to them. I argued with them and Mikayla in the repair department said they would have a second person look into it and call back in 48 hours. 4 days later I recieved an email saying the watch was being returned unfixed and I never received a call back so I called and was told it was set for exchange. Talked to someone in the case management department and they said the price was going to be refunded. I asked how long and they said once the paperwork it accepted, then asked me to confirm my contact so they could START the paperwork. They never contacted me to start the paperwork, so I'm sure they were hoping I wouldn't call back and are still trying to stall. They told me to call back if I hadn't heard anything by Thursday, so I will be calling then.

title: Disappointed
text: Repeatedly disconnected from my S21. Returned it after 1 day.

title: Only one problem
text: What a great watch, but battery life truly is terrible. It doesn't even last the day and that's with not having always on watch face and not checking it often. Really a shame

title: Mostly great
text: My first ever smart watch. Battery life is fine. I get up to a day with change maybe with regular use, 2 days and change with the battery saver. The heart rate monitor is super close to whatever the treadmill I'm on says, so I'll give it a pass here. I don't know how much I trust the body comp measurement, but if it's accurate I need to improve! Performs well. Slightly confusing with swapping between in-use apps. Other than that just a good watch overall. Heads-up, you need to download the Samsung wearables app and an extra plugin for the watch to set everything up. Other than that it's straightforward.

title: A total DISAPPOINTMENT!!
text: This thing is absolutely frustrating. You want to create a nice watch at a high price point and you can't even wear it for a full work day! But you want to say it can track sleep and fitness? The battery doesn't even last 8 hrs!! I have a Fosil and that I have to charge daily so I'm used to that, but it atleast makes it to the end of the night after I'm off work. Unless you get this on sale and a very low price, or don't have a life where you can constantly charge it. I do not recommend 😡

title: Love, Love, Love this Smartwatch!
text: Easy to set up and use. Comfortable to wear. Charges quickly. Has a really good sleep app. Records your snoring, which is both a good and bad thing. 😳 Love that you can set the watch face with your four favorite apps. I just tap the screen to start the hiking app, see my step counter, and view my texts and calls. Clear, bright, easy-to-read watch face, which is a big factor for me. Easy to see and answer texts, even has voice mode. Has sensors that track heart rate, blood pressure, stress level, and blood oxygen level with a touch of a button. Has calculator, calendar, alarm, and timer. Exercise apps track time, distance, mph, heart rate, and will show a map of your route when you’re done. Battery lasts a bit over a day. TIP: To extend battery life, be sure to regularly tap the app icon and close the ones you’re not using. Can’t say enough good things about this Smartwatch.

title: Good watch
text: Good watch, more apps you add the less the battery

title: I love it!
text: I love my watch! I've used it with my galaxy s21 ultra. I have used it with my boxing workouts and with a wraps and a 12oz glove it hasnt had any issues. Heart rate was checked manually as well. It has worked well at tracking my sleep and recording snoring episodes (husband had a kick listening to it) I use this to manage spotify while working out. Take messages and calls with a vibration and knock noise. You can only record heart beats with a samsung phone. It has recorded my body fat,water, skeletal muscle as well. I have it tracking my menstrual cycle as well. It lasts 3 days without always on display. With it on only 2 days. The band is ridged sport in black. I would recommend the extreme sport for boxing though. Will purchase later. I haven't had any problems with sensitivity or bezel. I have also used the keyboard on the watch which is nice but I would rather speech to text and it has been flawless. No misheard words! I haven't used swimming mode yet. I love it!

title: I love this device
text: I'm totally addicted to this device. I do not know what I did without it before. If you love your samsung phone, you must have this watch.

title: Upgrade from 2 to 4
text: I have had Galaxy watches for years - my 2's back cover fell off and it was almost 3 years old. I wanted an upgrade and I enjoy the new options they offer in the 4. I am still getting use to the device but I really like it so far. I am not a tech snob but a "typical middle 30's person" with some IT background and this is very sufficient for everyday needs and assistance. I love my watch!

title: never got it to pair with our Goggle Pixel phones
text: never got it to pair completely with our Goggle Pixel phones. It would pair and launch then error and start the process over again.

title: Not durable
text: I wear this for medical reasons, not as durable as I had hoped

title: I love my watch
text: I love Samsung products. Watch did not disappoint. Love it

title: Burned and Disappointed
text: I bought this Samsung watch recently as my previous Samsung watch was on it's last leg. My previous watch (Active) lasted a long time and had no issues. I ended up returning the watch for a few reasons. 1) main reason is the watch triggered burn marks on my wrists. Pic included. 2) battery life is a joke. It required charge in less than 24 hours. Even on battery saving mode, it was used up super quickly. Avoid this product at all costs. That is coming from a huge fan of Samsung.

title: Love it! Great Value!
text: I replaced my 2 with this one. Nice upgrade! Great Value and Price. Best Deal out there!

title: After a few months screen displays only static. Battery life was very short when brand new

title: The only Android watch you need!!
text: I love this watch! I have the 44mm. I also had the 40mm for awhile until I switched to the bigger model. The battery life is better on the 44mm and the screen is better but only because it's bigger. That's the only two differences between the two. The Watch 4 is fast and good looking. Speaker on it is great for a watch. I mean everything works awesome. There really is nothing I dislike about this watch. Probably the best smart watch I've ever owned. I highly recommend this watch to any Android user. Do note that the ECG and Blood pressure monitor will only work if you have a Samsung phone. The Blood pressure monitor only works in certain countries so depending on where you live if you don't have a Samsung phone the only thing you're really missing out on is the ECG feature. Calls sound great on the watch. Messages on the watch work perfect with Google Messages and GBoard installed. Still no Google Assistant at this time so only the mostly useless Bixby is available. The screen is plenty bright for use in bright sun. I'll say it again; this is THE ANDROID WATCH TO BUY! You won't be disappointed. One more thing, battery life. The battery will last you through the day no problem on both models, smaller and bigger but not much more than a day. Maybe 2 days without AOD on. And the new Wear OS is great. Also, battery life will probably seem bad the first day you use it but give it a few days and somehow some way the battery life improves quite a bit. I give this watch 5 stars and absolutely recommend it!

title: Stylish & Functional
text: When buying a smartwatch there's three things I look at: 1. Does it look good? - I bought the black 40mm version and it looks slick. The black rubber wristband is comfortable and didn't irritate my skin when sweating. 2. How's the battery life? - Obviously this depends upon use and connectivity. I have everything off (wifi, location, HR tracking, etc.) except for Bluetooth so that I can receive work notifications. For 8 hours of Bluetooth it uses about 35%-40% of the battery. Whenever you have a phone call or play media on your phone, the watch will sync and drain the battery faster. 3. Does it have the functions I want/need? - For me, yes. I just need a good looking watch that connects to my phone and has its own location for tracking my bike rides.

However, the Galaxy watch is close enough where it's just about as good. That being said, the five Pro is definitely better and it is the first Wear OS watch as good as an Apple Watch in my opinion.

title: Fabulous watch priced right!
text: I love this watch! The soft wrist band is vastly more comfortable than my previous watch. The screen is brighter in the sun. I like the square shape so the time shows on a single line instead of two. The old watch died when I pulled the strap off to charge it and it pulled the USB connector out of the watch itself. I was extremely pleased to see the magnetic coupler to charge this one. Note that it must exit under the watch on the side WITHOUT the button. You don't want to reverse the polarity. The image makes it clear which way to put it, but I saw no text instructions to that effect. I was pleased to be able to download the manual, which is much more readable than the sheet that comes with it. I have not crosschecked with an arm band BP test, but based on my knowledge of what to expect, I think this watch is far more accurate than the old one for BP and pulse rate. And this one does far more stuff with my phone than the old one did. And the price is right! You won't find a better watch anywhere for anywhere near this price! I do wish the battery lasted longer, as I was used to charging it once a week, and this one they say lasts five days. But a larger battery would make the watch larger and heavier, So I guess it's a trade-off. And this one is at least much less stressful to actually perform the charge.

title: Resets itself/looses data. HORRIBLE documentation
text: For some reason, it seems that the $100 price point is the dividing line for Amazfit products being decent/working well, and not. To explain..... I have purchased 3 Amazfit watches, starting with this one. There are issues and disappointments with all of them, however, this particular watch worked OK for about 4 days/nights, then it would randomly reset itself, and in the process delete all data it had accumulated. That was what made me return it. A couple of very annoying things with this particular watch.... 1. SP02 has no automatic feature/setting. Meaning that the only way it will take a reading is if you do it manually. 2. The zepp app that is required with these watches is annoying because each watch displays a bit differently on the app, due to various watches having given functions or not. But the real annoyance is syncing data, which seems to have a mind of its own.... if I try to make it sync sometimes it will, and other times not. 3. DO NOT believe the claims on battery life! With the features I wanted turned on, the best I could get was 2 days/nights on a charge! 4. Finally, ALL of the Amazfit products I've purchased have absolutely horrible documentation! The included manual is very ambiguous, and you can't figure out how anything works using it. I had to search the web and comb through far too many YouTube videos to find the information needed. The amount of time and effort wasted searching for "how to" information is enough cause a 1 star rating! Many online reviews rate this watch as "Best Cheap Smart Watch"...... but I'd highly recommend either going with another brand at this price point, or higher price points in this brand. Go with their GTR or S or higher. I think their GTR/S 2e is the best bang for the buck, although it has the same faults and horrible documentation as the rest.

title: Handy, good-looking, convenient.
text: This is my first Amazfit product, so I cannot really comment on how well it works in comparison to other watches by the same manufacturer. But - it is affordable, looks very good, and works well out of the box. I was in need of a smart watch with a GPS tracker that would work with or without a mobile phone. This model checks all these boxes: the GPS works without a mobile phone nearby and seems very accurate. After completing a walking route that I know very well (and know the distance too), the GPS tracker measured my speed, distance walked, and mapped the walk very accurately (giving me the same numbers that I get by using my mobile phone GPS with apps like MapMyWalk or Strava). Its heart rate monitor is accurate too, but its oxygen (SpO2) meter seems to be inaccurate (I believe other reviewers also mentioned this). Other observations: system updates are very quick (take about 2-3 minutes only). The Zepp app is reasonably easy to use and quite intuitive - one needs to go to "Profile" and then to "My Devices" (or "Add a Device") to add the watch and sync it with the app. Battery life appears to be quite good and the watch will keep charge for days. Charging is quick and takes about 1.5 to 2 hours (from the battery being down to 20% or below). The image is bright with vivid colors (becomes somewhat dim if the sun is strong) and the touch screen is responsive. The watch is very easy to use and there are plenty of options to cover many outdoor activities. Overall - the Bit U Pro is among the most affordable GPS-enabled smart watches out there and, more importantly, it is well-made and offers lots of value.

Body temp: It is only manually entered and only in Celsius not Fahrenheit. It translates it to F on the chart after you enter in C. No option to select your preference under Profile/Settings/Units. title: Good deal. I like the face-display choices.
text: For the money, this is very useful. First,it is an accurate watch that I don't have to reset. It tells me the battery status, time, day and date without having to scroll. But what I really like it that it shows who is calling my iPhone without having to pull the phone out of it's holster when I am shopping. Also, if I receive a message, it shows the message. On the down side, I can't get it to display my all-day pulse rate in graph form on my computer. Same with my night time sleep stages. Doesn't display on my PC in graph form. It will show a "skyscraper" type sleep display on my iPhone, but it isn't as good as my Fitbit display on my PC. Oh, and the battery lasts much longer than my Fitbit. Follow up after two weeks: After wearing the watch for a while, the skin on my wrist, under the watch band, was red and peeling. One other buyer on this list had the same problem. I replaced the band with one of the “Barton” brands, listed on Amazon. It has a rubbery feel and is much more comfortable. The skin problem is now solved.

title: It's great unless you sweat, I got a burn on my wrist one day
text: I'm not if it's just my skin but on a sweaty workout the optical sensors burned my skin. It wasn't a rash, because I recently switched to a non-silicone band and around the house, going for a walk it was seriously great. But now I'm afraid to wear it because of the quarter size burn on the top of my wrist that is still recovering

title: Complicated
text: I could never get the watch to set the face that I wanted. It took ab ITT person 30 minutes to getbthings started from the suggested web page...

title: Good Starter Watch - Misses Steps
text: The watch is lightweight and the GUI is very nice with a great number of watch faces. The battery life is impressive - lasting 5-7 days. GPS tracking is quick overall. My only compliant (thus the reason for the Medium rating) is that the step counter freezes on multiple occasions thus missing steps.

title: Best fitness tracker for the money.
text: This is a great fitness tracker. I got one for each of my preteen kids for an Easter gift. First of all, it was a huge hit; they love them. They love competing over step counts and what not and they enjoy diving into all of the fitness metrics. But the Bip U Pro is also a very capable fitness tracker for an adult. I typically wear a Garmin Instinct and the BipU Pro compares very well to the Garmin. It is not quite as robust or as rugged/durable as the Instinct, but it is every bit as capable in terms of tracking workouts, sleep, heart rate, etc... I wore my Instinct on one wrist and the Bip U Pro on the other to compare them on a few workouts (swimming, jogging, biking) and they were nearly exactly the same. In fact the Bip U Pro seemed to be a couple of seconds quicker with my heart rate readings. Now it's really just a fitness tracker; not really a smartwatch. If you keep that in mind, a less than $70, you will not be disappointed.

title: Battery goes on and on
text: Love all the fitness and sleep features. App is super easy to use. Best part is that I only have to charge every 5-6 days on average. Highly recommend!!

title: Great battery life
text: Awesome watch...battery life is on point. Didn't like the "real smart watch" experience. This is more of a fitness tracker...you get call and text notifications and what not. Didn't care for the app much but ill deal with it since I like the watch...if you want more of a fitness tracker than a smart watch buy this u won't regret it.

title: Good quality for the money
text: I've had this watch for about two weeks now and like it. The strap is comfortable and there are more than a dozen watch faces to choose. It took a couple of days to get used to how to operate the watch (finding the workouts and finding where to change the brightness) but now it is second nature. The step count seems to be accurate as is the heart rate. I haven't used the sleep function so I cannot comment on that. The best thing is that it has a strap with a buckle rather than the type of strap with the post that snaps into a hole and that always seems to come loose. All in all, a good quality watch of this type.

title: If you want/need O2 measurements - don't buy
text: My Cardio Doctors want me top watch my O2 and Heart Rate at 3 hour intervals as a part of a Senior Cardio Study at Duke. I had seen Smart Watch claims of Heart Rate and O2 Monitor Capability. This is the 2nd Smart Watch I've tried. If O2 monitoring with a Smart Watch is your goal, don't' bother. Heart rate was occasionally he same, but occasionally 4 or more off, as both of my Finger Oximeters and my Bluetooth Blood Pressure/Heart Rate Monitor, but O2 on the "Bip U Pro" was a waste of time. It frequently read 99% and other times was in the 80's. If O2 monitoring is among your goals, don't bother with a smart watch. Duke Cardio folks echo the same opinion re O2 monitoring with ANY Smart Watch.

title: Won’t capture text messages.
text: Okay for the price. Does the minimum. No blood pressure.

title: Way less than an I Watch.
text: I love the watch. My daughter said I should get to keep me moving and check my health. It Alexa compatible but I haven’t used that yet. I matched the Spo2 and heart rate to my PT’s meter and it was the same on one and off by 1 on the other. So far I’m happy.

title: Great, but for one issue.
text: Everything works great, except for it won’t receive text/iMessage notifications. I get all of the unimportant app notifications, phone calls work, but no Text or iMessage. Otherwise, the health tracking seems to work well, syncing and setting it up were simple. The only issue is the notifications. Decent quality, inexpensive alternative to an Apple Watch etc.

title: Great watch
text: Bought this for my teenager. She wanted an Apple Watch but I wouldn’t spend the money. I got her this and she is over the moon and loves it.

title: It's ok
text: I bought the model because it includes the voice assistant Alexa The voice assistant doesn't work that well. There are many misses and even when she manages to activate something, a message is received that there is an error connecting to the server

title: you won't even know you're wearing it!
text: battery life is outstanding, great fit on my wrist, band is perfect, and changing watch faces is pretty cool!

title: A Good Intro Fitness Tracker (B rating) *Not a Smart Watch*
text: I have been using this fitness tracker watch for about a month now and I give it a B rating for quality and function. It gets about 7 days of use before I need to charge it and easily synch with my iPhone for recording data/updates. The silicone band is comfortable and doesn't cause me irritation or noticeable as I wear it all day. The waterproof is good for showering, swimming, and I have free dove down to about 20 ft with no problems or issues. I am 6'2" and about 220 lbs and it fits my wrist just fine, Issues: - The watch face scratches very easily (get a screen protector) - If your arm isn't moving it won't count steps. (Hands in pockets or pushing a shopping cart equals no steps) -I have been standing at my desk for a half-hour, walking around the office, and the watch will say I need to stand and move around. - Display is hard to read with some of the face options. Whish I could customize the things to show and were on the screen. - Limited and weird activity options for working out. 3/4 of the activities aren't anything that I will use. What I like: - Battery life is good but GPS will drain it faster when bike riding, running, or other sports. - Easy to use menus and synch with iPhone. - GPS seems to be accurate and works in a variety of locations with coats and gloves. - Lightweight and comfortable - PAI, Blood Pressure, O2 are accurate.

title: Pros and cons
text: Battery last about 4 days with high activity. Charger is a little difficult to deal with but understand it is a cheap watch, so cut money wherever they can. The watch band is sturdy, but caused rashes. I am a leather-skinned man so I was surprised. The app is good but difficult to setup. The Amazon function is cool but limited. Best part of the watch is sleep tracking, but the longer you wear the watch the more the rash happens. I only recommend this watch for sleep tracking or daily, but do not wear as a constant.

title: He loved it ❤️
text: I gifted this watch to my dad for Xmas 🎁 and he loved it. He’s a health freak and I thought this would be a perfect gift for him since he’s been wanting a watch so this was perfect for him and I was right

title: Doesn’t work worth beans!
text: Got this for my husband. I’ve had a variety of fitness watches and have had very little difficulty setting them up. I charged it up and tried to program it. Could not get it to talk to his phone or set up the blue tooth. None of the features were working. Just was a real piece of junk.

title: Curiosity
text: I have used this long enough to write an honest review. I absolutely love it. It holds up and if you wear correctly works very well.

title: Super reasonable price for a feature laden watch
text: First I didn't put any stars in the mobile app line above as I'm not really sure what was being asked. I use this with my phone all the time and the sync seems perfect. As mentioned this was very reasonably priced and has given me really every feature I was hoping for. Watch is comfortable, charges quickly but goes for days without charging. It has completely opened my eyes when it comes to my sleep patterns. Very interesting. The watch comes with a number of nice looking faces and I've found a couple that suit my needs perfectly. I had previously bought a lower cost watch –still $35 more than this one. It started to malfunction very quickly. Sure wish I'd come across this one first. I'd gladly buy again and have considered getting a more expensive model from this brand as they have some really good looking ones.

title: I absolutely love this watch & health monitoring.
text: [[VIDEOID:3f91b5d709eda579049417e59647cd60]] The only problem I have (that really isn't that bad) is that the watch faces in the store are kind of dull. I wanted to crate my own watch face but all it had on it was the time. I wanted to be able to add my steps on there, the date & day. There was a watch face that I like so I sync it & the heading of the watch face said Los Angeles & I couldn't change it. I would also like to see a better variety of digital watch faces that are fun for girls; like butterflies, hummingbirds, dragonflies etc. Even lightening, fireworks, flashy colors. That is a suggestion but I am very happy with my watch!!

title: Didn't know i needed this but love it!
text: I had looked at many fitness watches and never thought they were worth the cost. Saw this one and decided for the price I'd try it. Well I love it and have been wearing it every day for the past 2 weeks. Fitness settings and notifications are very nice and work well. Battery is awesome and one full charge lasts about two weeks! Wish it would've came with an instruction booklet but found it online. Set up not too bad but probably depends on user's smart phone. I highly recommend it!

title: Love
text: I don’t use this for sleep tracking, but I do love all the other features. The interface and app are user friendly. I love the music function for your phone.

title: Watch is a piece of junk
text: The watch failed when daylight saving time occurred with no technical support. The watch is absolutely worthless.

title: Great watch
text: Very nice surprise to find a reasonably priced watch that does what it said it would do! I use to have 3 of the Garmin family watches that all died after 4-8 years and were costly to replace to do the things I wanted like Dpo2 levels etc! But like this watch allot and display is great and the app I find very user friendly!

title: One of the best options for a full-featured SmartWatch with decent battery life
text: While I miss my four week battery life from the original BIP watch with the always on display, this watch does well on battery considering all the features that are turned on. I have almost all the features enabled and my average battery charging is about every 4 days. Overall, it's a very impressive feature set now with the heart rate monitoring and the blood oxygen level sensors. The Zepp app continues to be the biggest weakness for all the amazfit watches. The new version is a little better but it often crashes when syncing with the watch.

title: This Smart watch is perfect for my husband!
text: This Smart watch is perfect for my husband! He has the patience of an inchworm and therefore most smart devices he is unable to utilize. This watch is very simple and once connected just measures everything on a daily basis, even your stress level! He loves it!

title: Wouldn't sync to phone
text: I bought this as a gift for Father's Day and the watch wouldn't sync up to my dad's iPhone 12. I thought he was just having trouble because he is not extremely technologically savvy, however it refused to sync up when I tried as well.

title: Great fitness tracker at a great price.
text: This is an adequate fitness tracker. Nothing too fancy, just does the job. Battery life is reasonable too. Tracks sleep, steps and various fitness routines fairly well. The app is pretty good too, displays everything you might want. Floors, elevation is the only thing missing from it.

title: A great walking companion!
text: I’ve had this for almost two weeks now and I’m really enjoying it! It took a few days to get used to sleeping with a watch on but I’ve gotten used to it now and barely even notice it! It is pretty accurate at tracking my steps, sleep, and heart rate. I like that it can use gps to track my exercise outside. It’s a very useful tool to have while exercising or just doing daily activities!

title: Excellent value.
text: Great watch for tracking steps and blood oxygen, etc. The weather app tends to freeze but otherwise , great product.

title: Tracker that tracks!
text: This tracker is fantastic! Battery life is impressive. Had it a week, Saturday to Saturday battery was at 48%. Sleep and nap tracking is great. Only second tracker I've ever owned, so I can't say how it compares to others but this thing is amazing. I've already recommended it to my friend.

title: Silly people
text: Watch works perfect! Read the reviews before buying, people complaining that the weather tracker is low... Just change the measurement from C° to F° :)

title: Needs to charge faster
text: This is an okay device for what it is. Actually, a good value for the price. Pro: HR and SPO2 are very accurate when compared to specific devices. Con: Software is lousy. They don't pay attention to issues raised. They, do stupid things like ask for feedback, then tell you to open a ticket. JUST FWD THE INFO! Recharge takes a loooong time! Doesn't do BP. Claims waterproof, then tells you to not wear it in the shower.??!?!!! Although, many workout options, there are no options to record day-to-day strenuous work. Recommend for those on a budget. WOULD NOT buy their upscale version nor their newer ones that do nothing more. Still junk software.

title: Going To Make It Work
text: Purchased this watch inorder to receive call and text message notifications, mostly when I’m at work and away from my phone. It was easy to set up and connect to the Zepp app. Just have to read and follow instructions carefully. Call notifications hit without a problem but my text messages only hit every now and then. Not consistently. I have an Android (an LG Risio3 with an Android8 software). I emailed Amafit customer service and went back and forth since July to figure out what the issue was. It seems that my phone system isn’t compatible even though it’s usually compatible with Androids. Basically, I need a new phone. Amazfit customer service was incredible and followed through. Love my watch and will definately hunt for a new phone inorder for my text messages to consistently hit my watch.

title: This is a fantastic sports watch!
text: I love this watch. I’ve had 2 fitbits and they died in less than a years time. The battery life is so much better on this watch! I’ve had it for a little bit now and feel like it lives up to what I wanted. It tracks everything I need it to track as far as my fitness.

title: Love love love this smart watch!
text: I love this smart watch!!!! It does everything I could want. The only thing I wish it had was different faces than what it has, but it does have several to pick from. More holiday faces would be nice. I can get my heart rate, track my sleep, my oxygen saturation level and also tells me the time in other states where my kids live. Very good watch and I love it!

title: Not bad. Some days better than others
text: I was originally going to give this 5 stars, as it seemed like it was tracking amazingly in the first few weeks, and I was DELIGHTED to find something so accurate at this price. However, about 3 or 4 weeks in, the accuracy dropped. Some days it has been as much as 80 to 100 beats off when I am doing indoor cycling. Maybe 20 to 30 beats off at lower cardio levels when doing yoga, or warming up (I check manually)-- and then sometimes fairly close again. Could be a connection issue, but I have not been changing anything, so it feels like a roulette wheel. So, useful info, but know that if you are really depending on accurate numbers, you may not get them. Try to be more about consistent habits and awareness of your PRE.

title: Alexa what?
text: It says this has alexa built in, however the app on my watch cannot find the device. I have tried NUMEROUS times and it just can't see it. The watch tells me to go to my mobile app and allow it.....can't cause it can't find it!

title: Love the software not the hardware
text: Overall I love this watch and it's ability to control my alexa devices at home What I don't like The alexa feature is annoying to get to And cuts off randomly The little band part feel off mine and made it come off easily and when it comes off and drops it breaks easily even with a screen protector. I've bought about 6 variations of these because they don't stay on my arm!!!

title: Great watch
text: I walked all summer and I love it kept track of my miles and everything I do, plus I get text on it, for the price its a awesome watch, I wear it everyday and feel lost without it.

title: Don't SCAN QR code
text: When attempting to download app per enclosed manual to scan the QR code for step by step instructions, instead unwanted games where added to my phone with intro charge of $1.65 per month and $5.99 each month until cancelled. Downloaded multiple games apps to my cellphone. Had to cancel my card. The Amazfit is now Zepp which is not mentioned on the product or Amazon. Big hassle getting my card cancelled and reissued. I thought I was purchasing a reputable product with the Amazon name. This one is being returned.

title: Birthday Gift ... Daughter can't say enough about how much she loves it
text: Birthday Gift ... Daughter can't say enough about how much she loves it

title: The set-up took longer than I expected but…
text: It took me three days to figure out how to get text and calls on my watch, but now that I’ve got it all set up, I love it!

title: I love this watch!!
text: Although it required more time for me to get it right, I am pleased with the results. I can answer my mobile phone via the watch...but the phone cannot be to far away. It keeps track of multiple body measurable functions. I also set an alarm for certain events. It has far more features that I have taken the time to use.

title: Feels like junk and cheaply made.
text: Why even bother buying additional bands when the bottom part of the watch where the bands attach is the color of the watch? So for example a green watch with a blue band . Or black band.. you're stuck with whatever color you bought the watch in.. meh meh meh. Less than basic of a smartwatch.

title: Did not live up to what I was looking for
text: I wanted to get notifications like texts from my phone but I never did. Maybe because I have an iphone but it said it should work. Also the weather was only in Celsius and could figure out how to change that. The battery life was pretty good but the main features I was looking for didn't live up to what I wanted so I returned this.

title: App is unusable
text: If this is your first smartwatch, then congratulations... you will probably think this is a wonderful purchase. But if you've had a Fitbit or AppleWatch or Samsung Watch before, then you will immediately discover the lower quality of the Zepp app that you must install to use this Amazfit watch. I had a Fitbit Versa for years before trying out this Amazfit watch and I was impressed with the look and feel of the watch, but after using the Zepp app.... (it even had some Chinese in the app, and there was a weird (Chinese version?) name for Alexa). I couldn't take it and returned the watch.

title: Long lasting battery.
text: It has many face dials to use but none with the time in large numbers. I love how long the battery lasts. It went two weeks the first time I used it. Some of functions like BP don’t work for me.

title: Heart rate monitoring not good for biking...
text: I really would have liked to keep this watch. The screen is gorgeous, bright colors, lots of different watch faces (although a lot of them are a bit too busy for me). It is light weight, comfortable to wear. Great battery life (a few days when you use it for exercise (GPS) a lot). The app isn't too bad either (although syncing is very slow sometimes). It does easily sync to Strave (including heart rate data). It is convenient to see text messages and WhatsApp pop up when I am biking. The main reason I bought it for was the heart rate monitoring during my biking exercises. Just walking or sitting it works fine. But when biking (either road or mountain biking) it can be way off. Sometimes it works fine, but sometimes it is much too low or much too high. I think sometimes it is double counting or skipping ever other beat... For example, going downhill on a MTB pretty relaxed it is apparently often the most strenuous according to the watch, with HR of 170! Or I am huffing and puffing and the heart rates is only 85 or so! I have a Halo band as well, wearing both at the same time to compare, the heart rate on that works much better, but it doesn't sync to Strava unfortunately. I returned the watch, so sad...

title: Love this watch
text: This is my third "smart" watch. My first was a Samsung fitness watch, which was much more expensive and worked okay until I got my new Samsung phone. Then it wouldn't stay connected to my new phone and I wasn't receiving most notifications. I switched to a cheap Wyze watch. That watch could track steps, but the notification function was poor and the texts could barely be read. I'll give that watch to one of my grandchildren to use as a toy. I bought this watch when Amazon offered a discount through their Treasure Truck. Although setting up the watch took a while and lots of persistence on my part (it is not intuitive, some of the setting menus are hard to find), I finally got it all set up. I've had the watch about 10 days now and I just love it. It's very lightweight and unobtrusive. I don't know if the steps, heart rate, etc. are perfectly accurate, but they're good enough for my purposes (none of my watches or pedometers have ever been perfectly accurate). I love the Zepp app that goes with the watch because it gives me very detailed information about my workouts. I find that very motivating, especially tracking the cadence of my walks. I find that I'm working harder just because I can now measure my effort with more details. Also, I love the PAI (physical activity intelligence) system. I'd never heard of it before, but it calculates your activities using your heart rate, steps, etc. and based on your age. I love getting credit for working hard. Although I've always tracked my daily steps, now I can get "points" for going faster or getting my heart rate up higher. I love this! I haven't used it to track my sleep, I just take the watch off at night. After 9 days I finally charged the watch (it was at 28%). My Samsung had to be charged every day (the Wyze watch lasted a long time, but it was fairly useless). Overall, I would recommend the watch highly.

title: Why does it need an app?
text: I wanted a tracker with a good or hopefully better battery than every fitbit, pebble or other tracker I've tried yet. This was offered through the treasure truck and no where did I see that you needed to install an app for it to be useful. I hate when I want to buy a self sufficient product without having to install an app for it to be useful. I sent it back. People don't pay attention to the permission you allow these apps to have, for instance the need for access to my contacts, no, not going to happen unless it's an app such as a messenger or something like that. Or access to my camera or my files, nope not happening.

title: Not worth the price
text: Does not connect to I phone easily. I could get the texts to connect at all. Most the features only work occasionally.

title: Great value
text: This watch does more than the other brand i used to have and its much cheaper. I can even receive texts on it which is so convenient

title: Great purchase
text: I got this as a gift for my mom. She wanted something similar to an Apple Watch and this is. The only difference is apple is obviously more expensive and this watch has a way longer battery life! She wears it everyday and she loves it! Would recommend!

title: Decent, but connecting it to Amazon is a pain.
text: Decent, but connecting it to Amazon is a pain. I want to use it to have a nice-looking interactive watch, but I have to make sure it's connected via the app at all times, and it refreshes a lot, so the connection goes in and out a lot. Not the best purchase, but it's worth 99 bucks if you want a cool-looking e-watch. I'd save up for one that syncs to your phone and is more compatible with devices you use.

title: Better than the most expensive
text: Pros: Comfortable Lightweight Secures on wrist so doesn't pop off like others Free watch face background designs Customizable apps Easy app to install on phone Read text messages Read app notifications Caller ID when you get a call Can silence or ignore call with just a press of a button Charges quickly Tracks just about anything you need Alexa feature is super easy to use Silent alarm Gives weather (I can view up to 7 day forcast) Controls music (Spotify at least) Sleep monitoring Cons: Product specific charger ....not much else bad to say

title: Not a good fitness watch.
text: This fitness watch was far more trouble than it was worth. It kept stopping a lot and even worse - it could not take an accurate pulse. It's pretty much garbage. 🤨🤐

title: The Alexa does not work
text: I've spoken with Alexa support as well as Amazfit support. This feature just does not work on the Amazfit GTS 2 Mini, nor on the GTS 2. I tried both watches. The mini is the perfect size for me. I have tiny wrists and this takes up most of the area. I wear the band on the last hole. The sage color is really unique. However, as with all Amazfit watch bands, (I used to wear an Amazfit Lite until the face fell off) you'll only get at the most a couple of month's wear before the loop stops holding onto the strap. It's cheapo plastic, and it stretches out. As far as the functions, I use it mostly for the notifications and pilates. I'm pretty stoked it has that as an indoor exercise option.

title: Great Watch
text: I have been a loyal Fitbit user since the introduction of the Fitbit One. I wore out several and recommend and purchased several for friends over the years. I started having sync problems. I put up with it. When the screen popped off the watch body, I decided I need a new watch. My Fitbit was less than 2 years old and paid over $200 when it first came out. I am impressed with the new Amazfit GTS 2 Smartwatch. I am still learning how to use it. So many features. The only complaint, the instruction manual is written for someone that has better than average eyes. So far I highly recommend this Smart Watch.

title: Very good watch.
text: The watch is very good and not to difficult to set up.Features are more then adequate for keeping fit.

title: What more do you want?
text: Let me preface by saying I decided long ago that smartwatches are basically notification engines that can also keep you from having to constantly take your phone out. Also, they do some health tracking. If you see a smartwatch as anything other than that, this review probably isn't going to make sense to you I've owned, a AppleWatch, a TicWatch, a Galaxy Watch, an Amazfit BIP and this watch. I've used both iOS and Android. I do not understand why you would need anything more than what this watch offers. 14 (legit) day battery life. Bright, easily readable screen. Bluetooth notifications. Easy setup, and lots of watchfaces. What more do you want? Sure, the novelty of being able to take a call on my watch was neat (Galaxy Watch). It's just a gimmick/novelty. Yeah, being able to get emails on my watch while leaving my phone on a different floor in my office was neat. It just increased my anxiety about not being able to respond well (iWatch). The TicWatch was neat, but at the end of the day, the battery died after less than a day of use. The Amazfit Bip was amazing, but the screen left something to be desired. Then comes this watch, and seriously, what else do you want? I will buy this watch a 1000x over any other smartwatch. It's light, gorgeous screen. Good heath monitoring, with nice integrations to health apps. It's not perfect, but jeez...it's $90? You wanna spend $500 on another watch, it's your money, but dollar for dollar, you can't beat this watch.

title: A good watch not perfect
text: The watch in nice and it functions with many options. I did not like that I need to lift my hand twice to see the hour and I did not like many erroneous continuous readings of my heart rate.

title: A good option
text: If you can't afford or won't pay the price of a more expensive watch. Great for workouts and other physical activity. The Sleep Tracker leaves much to be desired; for instance, it reports that I'm sleeping one hour per night when I'm actually getting a full 8 or 9 hours. The other functions seem to work fine. The battery life on this watch is incredible - one charge lasts for about 10 days of normal use.

title: Easy to use
text: I love this watch. It is easy to use and very comfortable. And the face size is perfect as I have a very small wrist. And for all the things the watch does the price is awesome. I love this watch.

title: My first Smart Watch!!
text: I hope I can learn how to use this for everything I want to do!! So far, I'm understanding some of it, but its not letting me connect to Alexa and we are Prime members, have Alexa devices throughout our home, so I'm not understanding why I can't get this on my watch. I wish they'd put a manual in with the watch so people like me, not tech savvy, could fully understand everything this Smart watch does. But I'm still giving it a high rating because its made by Amazon and I trust their technology!!

title: FOR ONCE. MORE FOR LESS MONEY
text: Wanted to wear it awhile before reviewing. This is GREAT. Wore it to Dr. Office. All stats matched. Being able to use Alexa was a HUGE bonus. The watch faces you can change to are really nice.

title: Overall good
text: Battery backup is amazing! I have turned off heartbeat and oxymeter and it lasts around 30 days. When I had tested the oxymeter, it would sometimes say "reading failed". Step tracking works almost as same an Apple watch.

title: Wonderful ! *UPDATED*
text: I am really liking this watch! The last one I got was a bit cheaper but it was really awful so I decided to take it back. This watch works a lot smoother and has much better options for me ! I mostly need it as a timer, alarm and notifications and it does all these things ! I got a better strap for it as well :) *UPDATED* Now that I've owned this for several months, I have to say that the connection between the watch and my phone isn't very good. For no reason it wont show my notifications at times, I really wish this didn't happen, especially since I usually have important things pop up on my phone. I have to constantly every day go back to the app to reconnect it and sometimes that doesn't last very long (also it doesn't even let me know if its been disconnected..) this is really frustrating, I am not sure if something like this can be fixed on their side. Really disappointed. Had to change my rating because of this.

title: After 4 months I still love it.

title: Not as good as advertised

text: Update: I may be looking elsewhere for another watch as this one is just way too bright when it lights up. And every time I move my are or turn over at night it lights up. title: Works well
text: SLEEP TRACKING: - Seems to be accurate; but it does give a low sleep score if you sleep in and wake up couple of times in between. Compared to Fitbit, I didn't like this way of sleep tracking. Amazfit also give high sleep score even if your sleep is shorter than 7 or 8 hours, but certain ratios are met on deep sleep etc... personally doesn't seems to be that great method. CALORIES COUNTED: seems to be accurate, but it only counts only the calories burned due to activity, where as a Fitbit seems to be counting even idle calorie burned, to me, Amazfit method seems to be more favorable. BATTERY LIFE: There is always a disclaimer that whatever the maximum advertised life will not be achieved in practice. With some extra features enabled and mobile notifications enabled, I get 7 days give or take, which is better compared to the Fitbit HR I had which only gave 5 days MOBILE NOTIFICATIONS: Seems to be working 99.9% of the time. This is an improvement I had compared to my old Fitbit. STEPS COUNTED: Seems to be excluding some erroneous counting that my old Fitbit did. But it still counts “steps” that are just hand movements. So, I still don’t fully trust, nor is my focus on the step count. HEART RATE: Seems to be accurate and comparable to many smart watches I used. MOBILE APP: Seems to be okay, filled with all sorts of features and functions, which I don’t use very much. The app gives a ton of colorful and useful watch faces. GOALS: Activity, Stress level, Weight, BMI, Blood Oxygen level, “Physical Activity Index”, etc., … there are several features, seems to be nice, but I seldom use it and won’t be able to compare as much. OVERALL: for the price, pretty good deal, compared to big branded smart watches.

title: Defective Item, charged a re-stocking fee
text: My fault to have this item for MORE than the 30 day return window. From day 1 it lacked proper battery life. We purchased 2 of these at the same time with the difference being the COLOR of the band. The other one, works beautifully. The app sucks, but the watch itself is great. This one however, the battery life lasts for a mere 3-4 days. We have taken our time to complete the restart, tried a few times. Followed all of the product support suggestions and lastly finally tried the hard factory reset. Once completed we charged this and the other one at the same time for the same amount of time. Both pulled off the chargers at the same time, all settings were exactly the same. in little more than 24 hours the pink band watch was at 96% battery life remaining. This black band watch was at 70% battery life remaining. Do you see the issue here? Defective product. So I contacted customer service which was an entire chaotic mess of awfullness. They accidentally started the return on the wrong watch, they cannot do replacements, so I had to contact back and the advisor was oblivious to the actual issue of just correcting WHICH watch the return was for. I asked for a supervisor 4 times and received nothing, so I had the customer service call me to explain and get this moving. Hallalejuh it was taken care of, only for me to find that they took a 30% restocking fee off of my refund. A refund I am receiving because they sold a DEFECTIVE product. What? Now I know what you are thinking, I was outside of my 30 day return period and I should have gotten in touch with them sooner. You are right, I should have, so I will suck up the ridiculous 30% and then likely purchase a different product with a service plan in case anything else happens. Not worth the crap I just went through on this bad boy. Don't buy it, or if you do, make sure it is perfect straight out that box!

I am impressed with the information one can gather on the phone app. The alarm does not provide very strong vibration, so I've slept through several early morning "wake-ups" (and set up a back-up alarm on my cell phone). Considering that the Samsung watch died before it was completely paid for under Samsung's financing program, and the estimated cost of repairing the Active 2 was almost twice the cost of this watch, the choice was a no-brainer. This as a very attractive watch and has excellent battery life. I charged the watch 3 days ago and have nearly 70% charge still left. My old Samsung's battery lasted at best for 2 days. It will be interesting to see how long this new watch lasts. It is supposed to be designed for swimming, which I do regularly. My experience with other swimming watches has been big disappointments. My Fit-Bit ($180) only lasted a year; the replacement lasted only 8 months. My Samsung ($270) lasted about a year and a half. The watch is slim, lightweight and very comfortable to wear. I have the 40mm version and it looks appropriately sized on my 15cm/6" wrist. The only thing that is a little disappointing is the display. It looks sub-par while inside, even with the backlight (which causes a weird blueish/purpleish background on the screen), but looks really good outside in daylight. I have considered the Venu just for the amoled screen, but I think I'm just going to keep this watch because it is a little bit smaller and does everything that I want it to. title: Rounds pace to the closest 5 seconds
text: Decent watch but annoying that the watch rounds the pace and lap pace to the nearest 5 seconds. Per Garmin, many Garmin watches that feature a running activity profile will display a rounded pace, which is calculated by rounding the current pace value to the nearest 5 seconds. For seconds 1 and 2, the watch will round down and 3 and 4 will round up. For example, a current pace of 7:32 will display a pace of 7:30 and a pace of 7:33 will show a 7:35 pace. This is done in order to present a value to the runner that is not constantly changing every second of the activity. I called garmin about the "issue" but it was beyond the 30 days to switch devices...so consider this your warning. :) The customer service rep I spoke with today (07/07/2020) was very nice but sadly couldn't really help me out.
