text: "Back from whence it came." I have the original Samsung Galaxy 46mm watch. Some of this review is comparative. The first problem I encountered is that, to upload music, one must install a separate computer program (Samsung uploads from the Android app on the phone). There is no Linux version from Garmin and the program will not run in WINE. That rendered the watch useless to me although, apparently, one can store content from streaming services like Spotify. Nevertheless I want MY stuff; classical music that is normalized and high quality. Another issue, and again this is comparative, is that the Samsung turning bezel has a clear advantage over swipe-only on such a small platform. In other words a Samsung watch allows one to select items by turning the bezel which can then be touched for activation. The Garmin requires swipe-scrolling which is an adventure. In the process I found myself inadvertently selecting items as the watch has a hard time differentiating between a touch to swipe and a touch to select. Compared to a phone, this is a very tiny screen. I found the readability of the Samsung screen to be a bit better and sharper. I had ordered a Watch-4 directly from Samsung. The order was botched. I allowed my anger to replace my judgment. At least for me the Samsung is a far better choice. I am going to reorder. As always, your mileage may vary.

title: A good product but battery life is short and sleep tracker is a mystery
text: Garmin does GPS really well. Tracking walks, bike rides, etc. GPS is dead on. There are a wealth of watch faces that can be downloaded and the ones I have tried are very easy to read. Steps, stairs, distance are dead on. Heart rate can be iffy when compared to either manual measurement or with chest strap HRM. This probably due to HR and Pulse Ox being measured optically in the space between the Ulna and Radius. The sleep tracking feature is a bit of a mystery as the data returned seems off from what I am experiencing. Judges are still out on this feature. I like the concept but not sure I trust the data. The battery life, in my experience, is not very long when using GPS during walks, biking etc. and Pulse Ox only during sleep is about three days. I turn off the phone connection unless I am syncing data. Granted I may be missing something on the GPS setting and it is on all the time. For example, I put the watch on at about 5PM yesterday turned off phone app and after taking a 20 minute walk and sleeping w/ pulse Ox on by 10AM today the battery was down to 81%. UPDATE: GARMIN CUSTOMER SERVICE IS REPLACING THE WATCH AT NO COST TO ME DUE TO BATTERY ISSUE. A FEW EMAILS AND QUESTIONS ANSWERED AND NEW ONE ON THE WAY. While I am not overly annoyed with the "Badges" popping up, I find it a pretty useless "feature". The Garmin Express connection to the Garmin Connect data is impressive! A bit overkill for a slogger like me but if you want do dissect your training this combo probably will give you everything you need.

title: Tracking Sleep Problem Finally Solved

When I got this watch with oxygen tracking I noticed it got data all night and day long. I had several "yellow" sections during the night. Green being "okay". I talked to my doctor and he suggested a sleep study. When I got back the result I was shocked to discover I had severe sleep apnea. I got a CPAP machine and first night this watch recorded spot on my total sleep for the night. Rem, Deep, Light, got up once and total time all registered. If you are like me and have tried Fitbit, Garmin, Wirthings, etc and don't get a sleep register, you should talk to your doctor. Its changed my life.

text: The battery life is advertised as being better than my old forerunner but it doesn’t even compare. I’m finding my vivo is needing to be charged every 3-4 days if I record a run or another activity with GPS (not using music). Really disappointed. My forerunner would last anywhere between 5-7 days even with GPS. If I hadn’t purchased at such a sale price during prime day, I’d be trying to ditch the watch. Otherwise, it feels nice and works well. It often disconnects with my phone so if you’re really wanting a smart watch, this isn’t it.

title: Not great for sleep tracking
text: Wanted this for sleep tracking and O2 sensor but not pleased with these functions so far. Sleep tracking isn't great and O2 isn't that accurate. All other functions of the watch are great though so I shouldn't rate it so poorly.

title: Garmin fan
text: I've worn a Garmin for 10+ years. I use mine for running (5k-marathons) and enjoy that it has Bluetooth. As far as GPS goes I feel a Garmin is top of the line. The battery life is good for a runner; no problem in finishing a marathon. This is my first non-Forerunner Garmin that I've had and I will say the Forerunner has better battery life and I find myself charging at least once a week. According to my friends with Apple watches they are amazed I can go that long on a single charge. There is music connectivity but I don't utilize it. My biggest gripe with this watch is that the watch face doesn't have "seconds". I work in patient care and so that feature is a huge deal for me. You are able to have a stopwatch but it isn't as convenient for me to have to swipe to see it. I like that it tracks HR as this helps with my training. Other features such as sleep, stress level, weekly activity minutes, stair counter, step counter, calories burned are really not that useful to me. There is a function called "battery burn" which I actually find really inaccurate. As a runner/crossfitter it will show my battery depleted more on days that I walk versus on the days that I run/crossfit heavily. Overall I would recommend this watch. I really miss the "seconds" being shown on the watchface, also that this doesn't have as good of battery life as my last Garmin.

title: Nice features, but inconsistent tracking of performance
text: I have gone through 2 of these watches. The first did a poor job of tracking steps. I compared it to a fitbit and a replacement version of this watch and it was consistently 10-15% behind in steps. The replacement however never picks up heartbeat correctly during activity. I have tried numerous positions and tightnesses. The only thing that seems to work is carrying it in my hand. Not only inconvenient, but not particularly confidence inspiring.in the numbers. Too bad, I liked the features and wanted to like this watch, but at fails at it's most important tasks.

title: Not accurate
text: I was a fitbit user since 2014 and only wanted to make the switch bc the heart rate monitors kept burning my wrist. I bought this with careful consideration and I fully regret it. The steps are not accurate. The activity tracking is not accurate. I just ran an intense mile on my treadmill and it only registered as me running .14 of a mile. When I use it with my recombinant bike it loses time. I start them at the same time and I a straight 45mins to one hour and it will lose 5-10 mins somehow. I have UA gps tracking running shoes and when I run outside it doesn't match up to this Garmin ....this Garmin loses .25 mile on my run. I am constantly having to edit my activities. Sleep tracking is ok. It does not register unscheduled sleep times that u manually put it. So if I want to nap it doesn't log it. I feel like fitbit is way more accurate with sleep and the app is way better. I really regret this expensive purchase. The mobile app doesn't go into as much detail as fitbit. Battery life is pretty decent. Would NOT purchase again. Would NOT recommend. Oh and if you are doing an intense sweaty workout the HR monitor does not read right. You have to stop what you are doing to take it off and wipe wrist and watch off several times during 45 min workout. Was reading 75 and wiped off and went up to 160 during workout. It's not very efficient stoping during a class to get a correct HR

title: Love it!
text: I love that I do not have to charge it all the time. About once a week I put it on the charger and it's good to go.

title: Great Battery Life
text: A bit pricy. The watch is pretty. The battery life is excellent - I get several days (sometimes a week) with a full charge and it only takes 20 mins or so to get a full charge. The face is a bit bigger than I like. I am a petite woman and it sort of overwhelms my arm. I like that I can put different watch faces on the dial. I find the widgets hard to use. It seems to be very accurate with steps, exercise, and sleep. Would I buy it again? I just don't know. New and better out every day - so probably not. But it is good for now.

title: Impressive
text: I dont necessarily like big watches so I opted for the 4s. That was a mistake. a definite pitfall of buying stuff on the internet. Other than that the watch works as well as could be expected. The new feature that I especially like is the body battery. Even though its not always correct I check the reading often. Yes yes yes

title: Flawed
text: I can't recommend this smartwatch for monitoring your heart rate or using it in colder weather. I purchased the watch to monitor my heart rate when I exercise and let me know when my heart rate is too high. While I can set an bpm threshold, it doesn't give me an alert when the threshold is exceeded. The watch also doesn't seem to work well in colder weather. When I am inside and the temperature is above 60 degrees F, the watch responds quickly to taps/slides. However, when I am outside and the temperature is below 40 degrees F, it often doesn't respond at all or responds very slowly. The accompanying Android web application seems to work well for the most part, but has some serious deficiencies. It asks for permission to access my calendar, phone and calendar. I'm not using any features of the watch that should require these permissions so I haven't granted them. The Android app then regularly complains that it needs these features -- constantly at all times of day or night. The app should be updated so the features that need these permissions are disabled, not harass me with constant alerts about missing permissions.

title: Great features but very buggy
text: I had 2 different versions of the Samsung smart/activity watches, the Samsung activity metrics were always wrong. So I got this Garmin watch, it was cheaper and the focus was more activity tracking over smart features. The Garmin Watch started out great and the health app was better than Samsung's. The smart features were also surprisingly good(displaying email, text and calls from my phone). The safety features are great allowing my husband to easily track my whereabouts in real time when I am out walking, hiking, or biking. But within weeks the watch started acting up. I went for a published 7 mile hike and my watch showed only 5 miles. I climbed 2 floors but the watch showed 10 floors. I climbed 20 floors and the watch showed 0 floors and needed to be reset and then restarted.... the watch congratulated me on achieving my water goal for the day when I had not logged any water yet for the day. I really love this watch and the app when it works but I am always having to reset the watch to factory defaults or uninstall and reinstall the app. Also the GPS seems weak, the signal takes a long time to connect and disconnects easily in wooded areas. At this point I have had the watch only about 1 month. The watch face scratched on day 1 which never happened in over 1 year on the Samsung watch. I still prefer this Garmin over the Samsung.

title: It's decent. Might some bugs that need fixed with research
text: If you get an error downloading a play list "unable to upload certificates", fully restart the watch by holding the top right button, ignoring any messages until the screen turns black. Then turn the watch back on and try again. Garmin was very helpful in guiding me since I couldn't find an answer online. The music from the watch to my Galaxy earbuds is spotty on my left wrist but ok on my right.

title: Great fitness watch
text: I have tried many various trackers. I love working out and love new tech toys so always like to try out fitness watches. As of April 2020 I think the best tracker is the Fenix6 Pro, I love that its beast of watch amazing battery and look. However its very expensive which is why I ended up returning it, just couldn't justify its price to keep it. I ended up with the VA4 as result. Now If I had never tried the Fenix I would say VA4 is the best and amazing BUT to my surprise I fell in love with button operation of the fenix and now really hate touch screen on my fitness watches, never realized how laggy touch screen was til you try the buttons. Overall for the money this watch does it, it doesn't do anything to the extreme of fenix but its enough for most people. battery life is decent, better then venu which I also tried. I love that it pairs with external HRM since wrist is not really accurate in my use - I mainly weight train. For cardio or bike riding I found spot on with my External HRM. Its large but yet very comfortable, I was able to sleep with it and not notice it. touch screen is little laggy you really notice when you try out the fenix. Overall its probably garmins best value watch.

title: Excellent product, performs as described.
text: I wish I could give it 4.5 stars instead of 4. I take 1/2 points off because some things are not very intuitive and take a bit longer to figure out. Namely music and a setting up a few sensors. Aside from that I'm very satisfied with my purchase. I wear my watch 24x7 for up to 4 days before charging. Its advertised as longer but i keep all my sensors on and collecting data which uses up battery life. My favorite feature is being able to hear music and tracking my location without my phone. Some things to keep in mind: 1) After setting up the music app (Amazon in my case) you have to setup WIFI on the watch and it wont update your music/playlists until you start charging it. It may state that in the manual but I didn't see it. I own MP3 music and opted to just download it to the watch itself. 2) Some sensors, like the Oxygen Sensor have to be turned on from the Watch. I spent time looking for it in the mobile app but its not there. Once setup everything appears in the mobile. 3) The Garmin website does a fantastic job of reporting your health statistics as does the mobile app. 4) It can take up to 30 seconds to get GPS signal so add that in to your pre-workout steps 5) They sych great with my Apple Ipods and I can control skipping to the next song by double tapping however sound can only be controlled from the watch. 6) For much faster initial software updates I would recommend to install the Desktop app and update the watch from there. 7) Its a bit cumbersome at first but learn the shortcuts, like holding down the A button for quick menu Overall I really like my watch and somehow has become an excellent motivator to help me improve on my health activities. I just like to see the progress on the graphs. :)

title: Does not work as advertised
text: Purchased exclusively due to the ability to load music from Spotify onto the watch... Which it is supposed to do, but did not in practice for me. I picked this product initially because I had very little interest in full smart watch capability. However, I wanted to be able to run without carrying my phone while listening to music or a podcast. In working through the issue I went online to find a solution. Found that music sync issues have been a systemic issue since the release of the alleged capability. Customer service was subpar and needed me to go through multiple complicated steps in order to offer any solution. Including creating and then uploading files into a computer... Despite never using a computer with the watch Was also disappointed by what felt like limited capacity as far mapping runs. For example, zero capacity to load a route onto the watch and use it to follow through a neighborhood or something like that. As far as exercising with it, the different options also feel limited. No HIIT option was available. The heart rate was synced very close to the one I use at Orange Theory. To continue the limitations, the battery life I experienced over several days of use was far less than advertised. Was only able to get the watch on a single wifi network. Returned and bought an Apple Watch SE for only about $60 more. Songs loaded immediately upon the first attempt. Not entirely sure it can navigate without a phone, but it can do the primary task I wanted.

title: Altimeter doesn't work
text: I really liked this watch, it did a better job of tracking heart rate and other data better than my fitbit charge 2. After around a week, I realized it wasn't tracking floors climbed. Some floors descended, but rarely any floors climbed. This is a complete deal breaker for me for hiking. At this price point, that should be an easy metric. Unfortunately, returned and am now awaiting the new release of fitbit.

title: Not worth it
text: Overpriced. Wouldn't connect to WiFi or Spotify out of the box. Takes a solid minute, or more, to connect to gps. After 5 days, Bluetooth stopped working. Tried contacting support and received the response that they were busy. Returning.

title: Good watch. Upgrade from vivo3
text: I had a Garmin vivo 3, this one is pretty similar with some niftier tracking updates. Purchased this after my 3 stopped holding charge and so far I really like it. The face is less sensitive than the 3 (good thing) and I like the sleep trending.

title: My wife loves the stress monitoring feature
text: It has several useful features for women and the touch is great. I've been using Garmin products for over 6 years and I like the way they keep up with technology while maintaining their quality.

title: Bubs gift smart watch
text: Great watch, it looks great works awsome track alot of items and works great with mobile app.

title: Expensive for a watch died twice in 12 months
text: Garmin sent me a refurbished watch after it stopped working after 7 months. It again stopped charging at 5 months later. Time to return to Polar.

title: Not worth the money.
text: I purchased the watch and was really upset with the product. First of all the watch colors are washed out and dull. The music functionality Spotify and Amazon music so not work. This is know to Garmin and are working on a fix to this problem. This was what I wanted with the watch - to run and have Spotify music playing. Really poor watch overall and would not recommend it.

title: Good simple activity tracker
text: Great activity tracker that does what I want. Tracks many activities like walk, hike, bike, rowing, skiing, and more that I haven't used. Good heart rate monitor, decent O2 (will drain battery). Bonus of apps and add ons available for additional health tracking. Also basic phone notifications/responses.

title: Battery drains quickly
text: I took it off of the charger at 100% and it was down to 82% after syncing with my Amazon music...

title: Incredible
text: Incredible battety life for what it does (at least with variable HR tracking). Might as well be waterproof. Sometimes Health related notifications can be delayed, but very accurrate from my understanding. TLDR: Worth its price, as advertised.

title: Awesome
text: My third garmin product and the favorite one so far. I wish there were better looking watch faces.

title: Great watch!
text: I bought this watch to replace my Fitbit Sense that died. I didn't want to invest in another Fitbit product as their quality of life isn't great. My husband and I have had to replace the watches so many times in the past 3 years. This Garmin watch is amazing! There are so many functions that my old watch didn't have. Also, the battery life is pretty good too. It lasts about 4 to 5 days for me before I have to charge it again. One thing that I don't like about the Vivoactive 4s is that it doesn't have a lot of colors, so there will be always a blue tint for the backlight. I found that it helps to lower the backlight to 10% instead of keeping it at the default 30%. After I lowered the backlight to 10%, it has helped a lot especially when I'm trying to install watchfaces. I don't recommend turning it off completely because then you won't be able to see your watch at all when it's dark. Also, the watch's Bluetooth functionally works really well. I paired it with my wireless earbuds easily. However, the Spotify app for the watch doesn't work very well, so it's a little disappointing. Other than these two cons that I've experienced, I still love this watch a lot.

title: Vivoactive 4S
text: I just love everything about this watch this is my 2nd watch an I would recommend you buy a case cover or face gard to the face of your watch an to check the watch band an to add the warranty. Some how my watch came off, my wrist and landed on are concrete when out by are pool and I didn't notice it until my grandson said Nana is that your watch an to my surprise it was an when I picked it up an looked at it the face of my watch was cracked. We got the warranty on it an after spending 2 days and many hours on the phone and was told they would email us the shipping label to send the watch back we waited a few days an had to spend a few more hours on the phone an this time we received a direct # incase we had to call them back. But in the end we received a refund an ordered a new one an received it from Amazon with in 7 hours after we placed order. So I would highly recommend the warranty and face gaurd or watch gaurd. But over all I'm happy with it

title: Upgrade
text: Love this watch. Garmin is always top notch. Durable and looks good. This is an upgrade from the forerunner. Works so well

title: Substandard performance and components
text: The 1st watch lasted 9 months and was replaced under warranty (shipping my expense) with the same unit. The 2nd watch died in under 1 month (paid shipping) The 3rd watch lasted just under 4 months. (Garmin would not warranty) Watch Use - 24/7 - Exercise 7 days a week Music: 1 - Played intermittently at best. When using GPS or a Workout app it played at 60% intermittent. Useless feature. I tried multiple earbuds that worked on other devices without issues. GPS: 1 - Took 5+ minutes to synch and if you missed the window it resets. Highest resolution (poll rate) of GPS was greater than 20m (70') - That is terrible Heart Rate: 0 - Worked fine until about 100BPM. Then it was off significantly. It would show a HR of 130 as 180-200. It would often just show cadence instead of heartrate when running. Steps: 3 - Only worked if arm swings were exaggerated. If you moved around with minimal arm motion it would not track even 1 step. Stairs: 0 - Track less then half the stories if moving slow. Would not track any if you moved quickly as you would do when exercising. Blu-tooth: 1 - won't synch, drops synch, cuts out constantly. Was difficult to synch to even Garmin components (have a chest HR monitor as watch HR sensor is junk) Battery: 3 - lasts as tested in other reviews Screen: 2.5 (large version) - resolution & brightness decent in moderate light, bad in bright light, touch screen was terrible. I would looked into any other brand. The internal components of this watch are low end and not compatible even with each other. (GPS and Blu-tooth are in same band!)

title: Works well, I guess
text: There are a lot of features it would be easy to miss unless you read through the manual and set it all up. I used to have an earlier Garmin with a two year watch battery so switching to charging it all the time means I have down days every couple weeks when I forget to charge it. The charging cable is specific to the watch so I only have one and am afraid of misplacing it, which again prevents more frequent charging because I don't bring it with me. I'm sure there's a spare charger I could buy. It's one more thing to remember to bring while traveling. I don't like the watch band. The silicone leaves an impression in my skin and the metal of the clasp irritates my skin. I'll have to replace it. The sleep tracking is completely different than the earlier model I had. I'm not sure if it's more accurate or not. I don't know how the watch can claim to know I'm in REM sleep. Anyway, still learning the watch.

title: Sleep tracking is terrible
text: I really like how this watch looks but the deal breaker for me is the TERRIBLE sleep tracking. I will be returning it and going back to my old smart watch until Garmin figures this out.

title: Replaced my Vivoactive 3 and am not thrilled
text: My vivoactive 3 battery life was weak and it kept having issues with syncing (Silly me!). I loved the watch and all it did, was looking into the new watch as i saw it was smaller (which i really wanted a smaller watch) and the being able to play music. I made the purchase. I'm not that amazed. Battery life does last longer, the screen itself is nicer with its bedeviled edges...but they made it much "thicker" meaning it stands off my wrist even more. So i traded the larger watch face for a much taller watch. The band is smaller though, that is a plus. Another really annoying thing which i hated about FIT BIT the heart rate monitor sticks up more. It has a bump which digs into my arm making it much more uncomfortable. This is why i loved my old one so much, it wasn't raised. I wish garmin would not have done this, i looked at tons of watches and knew i hated the fit bit due to this, Had i know i would not have bought the new one. If you are picky like me, this is a deal breaker. The color is ok, i should have waited for the white to come back in stock. The pink is ehhhh not great for red skin toned freckles, plus i don't love gold, but this was my own fault. NOW for the annoying bit. What in the world is going on with the app garmin?! I bought this new watch (stupidly) thinking it would help with the syncing issues i was having. My last watch had taken serious beatings and been attacked my an Aussie a handful of times so i assumed it was my fault. Nope wrong. Garmin is having massive issues with the iphone app syncing all the date from my watch. I have to log in each time i open the app and reinstall my watch each time. The first month i just thought well, they will fix it, i contacted garmin and they explained it was the new iphone update causing the issues and they would fix it. 3..4...5....updates later. It still wont work. I am a super huge fan of gramin products but i am starting to loose faith here.

title: Really great watch.
text: watch does everything that is advertised by garmin. Highly recommend it. Taking the place of my vivoactive 3.

title: Top notch price for a low-end watch
text: 3 returns. Kept the 4th one. Steps are a estimate at best. Heart rate very inaccurate. Stress level on point. Especially when you realize you paid a grip for this watch. But for $190 I can deal. Garmin venu sq Is a better deal.

title: Screen resolution quality is laughable
text: The screen resolution quality is laughable for a device available in 2020. It looks something like the first color cell phones came out. The pictures in the listing and in the Garmin website are misleading. I was looking to upgrade my fitbit versa 2 and the screen makes it a considerable downgrade! The watch itself is not user friendly. You need two separate apps to use this watch: one for the tracking, one for watch faces and apps. The screen isn't very sensitive, but in certain screens it is! It's more expensive than the versa and the Samsung Active 2 which i ultimately ended up getting. The side of the watch case is silicone so it looks cheap. The only plus is that it's one of the smallest smart watches out there at 40mm. But the Samsung is also a 40 and it's cheaper too. Also this was shipped by Beach Camera and i have to pay $5 to shop back to return it. Why? That's why i pay for prime.

title: Love it
text: I love my watch. Received it as a gift and I am very happy with it.

title: It's ok but could be much better
text: I bought this to replace an old Huawei watch because I was tired of charging the battery every day. The battery on this lasts much longer. With full time oxygen sensor off, it will last several days, but only a couple days when it's on. Sleep tracking is terrible. My old watch was much better. For example one night I was up for an hour in the middle of the night; went to bathroom watched an hour of tv etc and the watch said I was awake for 1 minute only. Also editing watch faces or creating a new one is terrible. You can change font\color but it only changes the minute (not the hour) and the day but not the month. It's the same on my daughter's vivo4 too. The watch is good the app is not and the watch should be better.

title: Better than my Vivoactive 3 in a few ways
text: I would have given a 4.5 rating but half star increments are not an option on Amazon for some reason. So to my thoughts. The watch dial at 45mm is slightly nicer to have than my 3 and it’s dial face diameter. The added features to the 4 like Pulse Ox, exercise demo by cartoon like person, body battery and respiration count are nice to have. The 4 does not to date drop connection and have to do a total re-sync and sometimes uninstalling the app to recognize the watch. I had that happen about 5-6 times in my owning the 3 in several months. Overall, I am glad for my wanting the extra features over the 3 and purchasing the 4. I liked the 3, don’t get me wrong. I just wanted some of the extra features. If one does not need the added features over a 3 then the money difference is enough to stay with a 3. But if you are a tech junkie and need those to add to the already great 3, then purchase the 4.

title: Present for the GF for work out tracking - win!
text: Chicks dig it - so you've got that going for you if you buy it. Secondly - it works well - no issue after a month of ownership. Battery seems to last as long as stated without issue. GF enjoys all the features and it looks good too! We got a stand charger, different color bands and clear screen protectors to finish the buy - would recommend!

title: Accuracy needs to improve
text: Mostly, I like the watch. Here's a pros/cons breakdown: Pros: — Stylish, looks good. — Battery is pretty good. Sometimes it drains only 10%/day, sometimes more. — Lots of different modes for tracking different workouts. I've only tried a few so far. — Good waterproofing. Not sure about diving/swimming, but no issues showering with the watch. — The Android app and syncing are good and intuitive. — Looks/feels pretty rugged. Cons: — Some tracking is inaccurate. I live in a 2-storey house, so I go up and down all day long. Sometimes it tracks the number of floors accurately, but sometimes it just ignores/skips them. — Heart rate monitoring is mostly pretty accurate, but sometimes it isn't. I was jogging with a rate of about 140, but the watch was showing just 97bpm. Though, mostly it's pretty close. A lot of it depends on how tight/loose the band is. — GPS is mostly good, but regularly it veers off noticably. It also takes at least 30 seconds to acquire a GPS signal, which is annoying when you're trying to start a workout. — Similarly, sleep tracking is mostly good, but sometimes off. I had a night where I kept waking up all the time, but it showed me sleeping the whole time. — Proprietary charging cable instead of usb-c. No wireless charging. Overall, I'm happy with the watch. Thought, some improvements would be nice.

title: My 2nd Gamrin smartwath/fitness tracker
text: Started with one of the simipliar ones. A Vivosmart. This was a HUGE upgrade. So many more things. This tracks way more than my vivosmart, and with the customizable faces and addon-widgets (like local weather radar by the hour), makes it much more than a watch or fitness tracker. GarminPay works at places that accept other device payments. VERY handy when you just dont want to get your wallet out or touch the payment pad. Battery life is very good if you don't use the PulseOX all day. Garmin also has the best tracking app. They are able to pack a ton on info it, and make it easy to navigate and digest. My wife got one, and while it took her awhile to adjust (never having had something like this before) she loves it and it's been very helpful in helping her make lifestyle adjustments.

title: Accuracy, precision and excellent fit!
text: Like them very much. I can install my personal photo as wallpaper screen (but pic will not be perfect quality). Very convenient to use

title: I think I expected more of this watch
text: The size is perfect but I didn’t like the performance 🙄

title: Love It
text: I own a couple of the their watches, I love it

title: Not intuitive, returns are not free
text: I grew up with smartphones, but I have to turn to Google to figure out how to do every little thing. The watch also appears to need to be updated on a weekly basis. Sleep tracking doesn't seem accurate to me. I can be awake for a half hour and it still says I'm sleeping. Lastly, I found it annoying that you have to wait for the gps to load before starting my run. I've ended forgetting a few times to go back and press start once it gets the gps signal, leading to my run not being tracked. Lastly, the claim of free returns is a lie. If you want to go to UPS store like normal returns, you have to pay over $7. "Free return" is only if you're willing to drive over 20 minutes to a specific location, which defeats the whole point of having free shipping.

title: Pretty sure this watch was used :S
text: I have only had it for a day so I won't do a full review of the functionality, just some things I noticed. Considering this wasn't a refurbished purchase, I think it's good to know. When I opened my amazon box, the box this watch was in already had broken seals. When I plugged in the watch to allow it to charge, there was data on it, and I couldn't sync it to my phone. After resetting it, data was gone, and I was able to sync it. It's highly suspicious because if I had to pay for the watch, I'd like it to be new. I'm worried it's got some wear and tear or maybe someone returned it for a good reason. We'll see!

title: Worth it
text: For a runner it's pretty good. Tracking for gps is solid, not perfect, but accurate enough for long distances. I use the Amazon music app, and it has been a game changer. It does not do well with sweat or water loss tracking. Has all kinds of faces to play around with. Band is very comfortable. Had a faultly charging cord, but Amazon replaced it pronto. If you are not an apple person, its a viable option.

title: A bit larger than expected
text: The watch is a bit larger and thicker than I expected but I'm getting used to it. After installing the app, it was pretty to set up. I used a Fitbit Alta for years but it recently died so got this to replace the Alta. The battery doesn't last as long but it's easy to recharge and does a lot more than the Alta. One of my favorite features is the ability to set an alarm directly on the watch and not have to sync it through an app. I'm still trying to figure out all the options.

title: Great watch
text: I'm loving my watch. Just have 2 things I don't love, one is that the battery's life is very short (I had read about it, so I already knew). The other thing is that the wrist band is very small. I have a medium- large wrist, and it feels quite tight. I'm trying to buy a larger band, but I think they only make this size. I love how it tracks everything and suggests workouts.

title: Not as shown as in the photo
text: I bought this Garmin Vivoactove smart watch for my wife. When my wife turned on the watch and saw how it looks, she was disappointed. My Amzfit smartwatch display was brighter and more colorful, with dark black background, than the Garmin. This watch looked discolored with a dark gray background. This watch for us is too expensive for what it offers compared to other smart watches on the market. We thought that since it was a Garmin, it would look great. What a disappointment.

title: overall good watch
text: The app takes a little gets used to-there is alot of information to digest. The battery life is ok...not great. I do find that because of where the buttons are when I'm doing certain workouts (pull ups, barbell work) i will hit it with my wrist and it will start and stop...that's my only complaint....that could be adjusted by wearing it higher up I guess.

title: Poor battery life, not worth for that money
text: Battery dies very fast. Its not working for 7-8 days. Steps not accurate, think you can buy better featured smart watch for this price

title: Excellent fitness tracker
text: So far I've really enjoyed this fitness tracker. I'm not an athlete but I am trying to do a better job of being active, especially since I spend a lot of time working at my computer. This garmin tracker reminds me to be more active and it congratulates me when I am. It also makes it more fun to go for a bike ride when I know I can easily turn on the GPS and it will track my route and my stats. I find it very motivating to be more active when I know I can have fun reviewing my stats afterwards.
