text: With all the options out for watches that double as smartwatches and fitness watches, I settled on this one for really 2 reasons. First, its from Garmin so you can expect that the GPS functions are going to be spot on. In that regard this watch is solid. The GPS is automatic as soon as you tell it that you are going to work out and it acquires quickly and its accurate. All you have to do is hit the single button on the side once, and select your activity. It usually locks in after about 10-15 seconds and off you go. This is critical for someone like me that pushes a stroller, steps never count right if you don't have GPS. Second huge thing with this watch is the music function. I hate carrying my phone when i run and now, I don't! I set up spotify in a few minutes, downloaded 3 playlists (about 200 songs) and I'm good to go for my whole run. It makes it easy to hook to bluetooth and lets me either leave my phone behind when running or pull up a weight training app. The only drawback at all is that for the first about 2 minutes, it can have tiny skips if you are also running GPS, probably something to do with the watch not quite keeping up initially. All in all this has been a great purchase and at a cost less than other options. We liked it so much, my wife got one too!

title: had to return the first one, second one works perfectly, works great as both a smartwatch and a sports watch
text: This is a combination smartwatch and sports watch. The smartwatch features are not as smart as the Google or Apple products, but I still get notifications, text messages, and caller ID synced from my phone, which are the main feature that I want from a smartwatch. A full week of battery life per charge is tremendously better than Apple and Google. The sports features are much more accurate and better thought out than Apple and Google. I use this watch to record my runs and bike rides. Most of the time, I don't even use my Garmin bike computer any more since the watch is accurate enough, though I still use the bike computer for turn-by-turn directions on some routes. These Garmin watches are also better looking (to me) than the Apple or Google watches. I really don't see any reason to buy Apple or Google watches instead of Garmin (at least for now). I had problems with the first Garmin vivoactive 3 that I received. For some reason, it didn't sync with my smartphone very well and only half my notifications arrived on the watch. After a couple of weeks fighting with the watch I returned it (no questions asked) for a new one and the second watch works perfectly. I read in the Garmin forums that notification syncing problems are very common with this product. My advice is not to fight with your watch, since you are going to lose. If syncing doesn't work, then just return it for a new one.

title: Watch band is too short for me to even wear
text: I like the watch. It does what I need it to. I just wish the bezel was bigger so I could read it better. Most importantly the strap is so short I can’t even wear it. I have to shop for a replacement band. So, a good watch but not so much if you have a big wrist. I’m disappointed. I looked at the dimensions, I just didn’t realize. But for what it cost I sure wish it had come with a strap I could use!

title: Great watch!
text: Love this watch! It's very comfortable and looks nice! I have it in rose gold with a white band. Enjoy having a fitness watch and not a smartphone on my wrist. Seems pretty accurate.

title: easier to operate
text: my wife has always liked garmin products. this item looks good but is kind of difficult and frustrating to use. we will keep trying.

title: Very nice and easy to use.
text: Easy to use different settings. Easy to see face. Also easy to transfer data to iPhone.

title: Love it! User friendly / customizable
text: I absolutely love my new watch. It is exactly what I was looking for. I have a galaxy note 8 phone that easily paired with the watch. Not required to pair with a phone fyi. I customized the face so that it shows the date and time digitally and even the accent color; which I can change as often as I'd like. You can choose the time frame that you receive notifications and what notifications you want to receive; which you can change at any time. There are many you tube videos that help explain other features. I cannot say how much I love this watch. The battery life is great too. I have to charge it about every 3 days or more sometimes depending on how many apps/notifications I've received.

title: Heart rate monitor is surprisingly accurate
text: I am surprised by how accurate the heart rate monitor is on this watch. I had read reviews about inconsistencies, but it's working great for me. Battery life is great, lasts about a week. The only draw back I've experienced is not being able to upload my runs to "Map my Run". No scoffing, I chose it over Strava way back in the day, so I have a long history with it. Just wish these watches interacted better with 3rd party running applications.

title: Expensive piece of garbage
text: I was really excited about getting a Garmin. I wanted a smart watch, but I'm not really an Apple-person, so I took a lot of time to deliberate between all of the non-Apple options and decided to go with Garmin - mostly because I liked that it had a GPS function and I wanted to start running again. I have to say, I'm really disappointed. I attend bootcamp-style workouts on a regular basis. Before I made the switch to Garmin, I had a Polar heart rate monitor (the kind w/ the chest strap). During those workouts, I would usually clock in heart-rates upwards of 185 and 600-800 calories burned per session.... when I got this Garmin, I noticed the heart rate wasn't nearly as close (it would say in the 130s, which was ridiculous given the kind of workouts I was doing) In addition to the questionable HR/Calories burned calc, out of nowhere 2 weeks ago, the Garmin started counting stairs that I never even actually climbed. As an example, it's 10:30 am right now, and according to my VA3, I've climbed 32 flights of stairs, which I KNOW I haven't. I have tried Garmin's suggestion to remedy the issue, but so far no luck. The GPS is pretty solid, though, so I guess it has that going for it. Bottom line, this is, unfortunately, an expensive piece of garbage. I'm sad that I wasted so much money on it.

title: I just upgraded from Vivoactive HR to Vivoactive 3, and I am very impressed!
text: I use this for golf and my exercise routines, and was impressed that they are more seamless with tracking my health and scores. The golf function now tracks putts, GIRs and drive accuracy in addition to score and handicap analysis. Garmin appears to be hearing suggestions and improving their software. I loved my Vivoactive HR, and this is a superior watch, so if I do not supplement this review, it will continue to be 5*s.

title: Overall great watch
text: I love this watch! The battery will last for a few days. The sleep tracking is overall pretty good. I have only had difficulties with it once or twice. The steps challenge on the app is also a fun way to engage with your friends and motivate you to get moving more.

title: Good but poor heartrate accuracy
text: I really like the look and fit of the watch. My only issue is that it does not accurately measure my heartrate during exercise. I keep the sensors clean. For the price, and being an exercise watch I expect it to always be accurate. Awaiting response from Garmin to address.

title: One of my favorite new toys, glad I upgraded
text: Love it so far. Accuracy seems to be about as good as it can get, and it doesn’t record nearly as many false steps as my old Garmin (that thing would record over 1000 steps just driving down a dirt road!). Only negatives so far are that the band isn’t quite right - one notch is too tight, next one is just a bit too big - and it will sometimes start activities by itself. Not huge deals but mildly annoying.

title: Perfect size for women and great running watch with fun smart features.
text: Bought this to track my running. It is pretty accurate. Maybe off by a little intermittently but not enough for me to care. Its touch screen is very responsive and easy to use when running. I can easily change my music with out losing my pace. I love the different watch faces you can down load. Battery life is pretty good. Usually lasts about 3-4 days before needing to charge. In all a great looking watch not too big for my smaller wrists and great for running also.

title: Garmin Fumbles
text: My initial impressions - First, I should say I have been pretty happy with my Vivoactive HR since getting it well over a year ago. It needed a couple of improvements so I was looking forward to the upgrade. One thing that didn't need fixing was the band, but Garmin decided to move from a comfortable band that was easy to hold the watch with when taking it off/putting it on. To a thin, cheap feeling piece of crap band. It's also shorter than the short version that was on the VAHR. Horrible move by Garmin and that alone might be enough to return the thing. I would have rather they shipped it without a band and allowed me to use the bands from the VAHR, but they also reduced the width so they won't fit. The pairing process is as problematic as every other Garmin watch. It seemed to pair, except the watch didn't think so and kept trying. I think this is as much a Bluetooth problem as it is the watch. It's a poor system that the Bluetooth SIG still hasn't figured out how to make it user friendly. After about ten attempts I got it to pair up with my phone. It would find and connect and then I'd type in the code and the app/watch would lock up on the initial sync, but eventually it relented. There are many apps that are not compatible with the VA3, so be warned as loading a non-compatible app can lead to problems...especially fast battery drain.

title: It would be a great $100 watch
text: The watch was what i expected, which i consider a good thing. It was super easy to set up, looks good and feels natural on my wrist, the Garmin apps are reliable and offer a lot of good additional features. I only wish the screen was a little brighter, and would really love it if it had an AMOLED screen (like some cheaper alternatives do). I’d say this watch is worth $100, asking anymore and it starts to get overpriced in my opinion for today’s smart watch standards.

title: Overall very happy with the watch
text: Much better for sport, in my specific case swimming in comparison to the Galaxy sport of last year

title: Good deal!
text: I bought this because it’s the cheapest watch you can get that enables Spotify offline. Been using for 2 weeks now and I’m enjoying it. Had some issues during the start up: couldn’t connect to spotify and it got stuck during software update via WiFi. I had to hook it up to the pc to update the software , which was a bit of a hassle. But after that, it work fine. Sometimes during the run there are some small cuts in the BT connection, let’s see how it will perform in the long run

title: Froze on me the first day
text: I had to send this back because it ended up freezing on me the very first day I received it. I set it up and it was working throughout the day and when I sat down towards the evening to work on adding OTHER workouts to track it froze and never came back to the main screen. I couldn't shut it down to start it over. What a disappointment.:(

title: Great for about 2 years
text: I have really loved this watch for the most part. It has helped me to track running (treadmill and outside), cycling (stationary and moving), and swimming both in a pool and in a pond (put your watch under your swim cap!). Not to mention hiking, kayaking, and many other misc. activities. I like the way it looks and I like the various watch faces you can install. The app and web site are really nice. Sleep monitoring and all-day heart monitoring are great. Note that I never use the music feature, so you can skip that (get the VA3 rather than the VA3m). Here's my main problem: The barometric altimeter was very inaccurate from day 1 and, after 2 years, died completely. Without it, your runs and rides look like they are on the flat until you "fix" them online with the "elevation correction" option. This fix can't be set as a default (so far as I can tell-- seems strange) and is only available online, not in the Garmin App. So it gets a bit tiresome. However, the corrected elevation is actually MORE ACCURATE than the barometric altimeter, so in a weird way, this is an improvement.

title: Great Product
text: Love this watch. Perfect for both exercise and wearing around. It functions perfectly for workouts and runs as well as a just throughout the day.

title: heart rate is inaccurate
text: The heart rate (HR) function is horrible. I can workout for 60 minutes in cardio and the watch tells me my average HR is 90 - 100. I will wear a chest strap and the HR average is 125-135. The watch has basically become a step counter. So frustrating. I do like that it works great in the pool and this is the only reason I'm keeping it. I tried the Versa in the pool... Fried immediately.

title: SO happy I switched
text: I had previously purchased 3 different fitbits with my last one being the fitbit versa all of which I liked when I had them but all three broke and/or malfunctioned within a year of purchase. I was pretty upset I was constantly spending money on fitbit and had heard great things about Garmin from some friends of mine. I have had the vivoactive for 5 months now and have had no issues and have been very pleased with it. My job requires me to have a classic watch face with a seconds hand so I can track vitals if a athlete goes down on the field. The Garmin offers the classic watch face that is always visible on screen as well as many other option and the ability to customize if you want. The watch face is also very easy to see in all conditions (even on sunny days) I love that the watch is water proof and can say the watch is durable in all conditions. I have no quite figured out the strength feature on the watch yet and have found that it doesn't always count reps correctly but thats not a deal breaker for me since I can go in and change that manually if I want. I have also not tried the snowboard feature yet will definitely update when I have. Overall, I would highly recommend this product.

title: Best part is I got it ON SALE!
text: This watch does as advertised. I considered a Garmin bicycle computer but glad I got this instead. Plus bike computer won’t give me distances to the pin on golf course. And all this for just over a couple hundred bucks. Features too numerous to list! This thing is suppose to be able to count swim laps. There are other smart watches out there, but I’m glad I got a vivoactive 3. PROS: Good battery life (5 days) tho GPS when biking or golfing reduces that significantly. Easy to use touchscreen, no need to push buttons. Garmin Connect app on phone provides lots of data, including sleep patterns. Heart rate monitor is pretty accurate even during exercise. CONS: Training for overall features could be better. Not as convenient to view as a fixed larger screen on handlebars but face can be customized to display desired stats in bigger figures. Watch does not make climbing hills against the wind any easier! LOL

title: Not at all a legitimate sports watch...
text: Received as a gift, and unfortunately having to return it as it nowhere near meets my expectations. As an outdoorsman (hiking/hunting/camping/fishing/mountaineering/etc), this piece simply doesn't cut it. It's not a legit sports watch, and instead has the feel of a premium fitness tracker that would disintegrate in a few years under daily use. Here's the rundown: PROS -Lightweight -Decent battery life -HR tracking seems good -Eliminates need for phone for music playback CONS -Cheap build/plastic casing. Band is so thin it did not inspire confidence for any outdoor activities of substance. -Display contrast controls are lacking. To get good visibility you have to turn up brightness to 70%+, which degrades battery life. -Glass face is not scratch resistant and in fact is a scratch magnet. No tempered glass protectors available due to curved face (must use a plastic film). -Small, round profile looks like a toy on a man's wrist. Not rugged or professional in appearance. -User Interface is laggy and clunky; would benefit from push button navigation instead of touch screen. -Terrible syncing with Garmin Express (May have been a faulty unit, but 3 different computers would not sync when directly connected by USB cable). Inability to sync made this product unusable in the long-term unless I was to be satisified with it "out of the box" (i.e. no watch face upgrades, app downloads, etc). If you're looking for a replacement to an iWatch, this might be a decent option. I have similar feelings about the iWatch as I do the Vivoactive 3 Music, but the build on the iWatch is far more attractive and substantial. IF YOU ARE LOOKING FOR AN OUTDOOR/SPORTS WATCH, DO NOT BUY! Ultimately the music playback is a fun gimmick, but not really necessary as many people carry their phones with them anyways for safety. Going for a Garmin Fenix 3 HR instead like I should have from the beginning.

title: Fails with Bluetooth
text: It loses so much because of the unreliability of the smartphone connectivity. Maybe it's better on a Samsung product but the iPhone connectivity is poor at best. Multiple resets (on/off with the Bluetooth) and maybe reliable sync 40% of the time. Simply unacceptable. Update, January 2019: Still not a reliable device for connectivity. It simply does not work as a 'smart' device when it can not do the simplest of tasks like connect. Step tracker, pulse monitor seem fairly accurate.

title: Cool watch, great brand!
text: Overall quality is superb. Tracks your steps, movements and calories burned. It can be hard to tell time, especially when lights are dim. It's my favorite watch so far.

title: Disappointed considering the brand
text: Mediocre performance on heart rate. Switching between various modes is not easy. Screen is sensitive to touch so your recording can be paused very easily by accident. Also, not pairing with iPhone after initial installation of Garmin Connect. Compass function works only during activities. Same with Altimeter. Not sure what Garmin is trying to accomplish with releasing such unrefined gadget. Plus the annoying buzz telling you that you have achieved your goal! I just did a trail marathon and did not know how to stop this gold cup showing on the screen at random times telling me I achieved my goal... Reminds of old Reader Rabbit learning games.

title: Great so far!!!
text: This replaced a Garmin VivioActive HR which was only a few yrs old. I like the size of this one...easy to read the screen and easy to change screens. Nice having so many watch faces to choose from, Band is comfortable, and the battery seems to last around 6-7 days. I have not turned on the GPS. No real complaints thus far.

title: Great product
text: So far it been wonderful my husband hasn’t taken it off but to charge he loves it

title: Sent watch back twice in year warranty period.
text: I had to send back for warranty twice during the 1 year warranty period. 1. The first RMA was due to the button not working and vibration no longer working 2. The second was due to the watch not longer vibrating. This time, it would vibrate on power up but not due to timers or notifications.

title: What a watch
text: This was a gift to my husband and he loved it. He enjoys seeing the emails and text come across it. as well as it keeping track of his steps, sleep and heart rate.

title: Love this watch/tracker
text: I really love the Garmin vivoactive hr. I had to replace my older rectangular one after 3 years with this newer model and it did not disappoint. It looks much sleeker and has all the same great functions. I love that of all the trackers I’ve had this one has a constant lit up watch face. I can adjust the brightness to save battery. I love being able to change watch faces easily although initially the app did not work for some faces that I wanted. It seems garmin updated and it works better now. My battery lasts 2 days if I use the watch with Bluetooth and gps for runs or rides. I love the swimming mode. As with all wrist heart rate devices, I find it is fairly accurate while working out, but is not as accurate when I begin to cool down and recover from exercise. It registers way too high a heart rate for a good 5-10 min during cool down which then will over estimate the calorie burn. I also had great service from both the Garmin people directly and the Amazon insurance I purchased. I will continue to use Garmin for my fitness and everyday watch needs!

title: Great smart watch
text: Great smart watch. Has many face options and add ons you can download from the app. The app is useful also with tracking lots of different things. Easy to use.

title: Love and upset
text: Love: I used two tracking systems at first and to see the accuracy and this watch is excellent. I also love the ease of use. Upset: 5 months later the text messages are not coming through. I've checked my phone, the connect app as well as the watch and its not receiving text messages any more. The user manual was useless. I'm still receiving calls on the watch. It doesn't make scene.

title: Excellent upgrade from original VA
text: Great so far! Comfortable and great build quality. I was worried about the durability of quick release bands on a sports watch—but the Garmin quick release band uses a sturdier pin with a stiffer spring, so not worried about it falling off while mountain biking through a rock garden. No battery drain if using watch faces that were updated since the va3 release date. Also, turned off gestures because the backlight was turning on while driving. Looks stunning in all black version. Vibration is weaker than original VA, so the alarm doesn’t wake me up (not gonna dock a star for that). I just created some swim and bike workouts. Can’t wait to take it in the pool and cycling! Update 11/29/2017: I have to say the scratch resistant coating is pretty good. I’ve scraped the watch on metal locker sheet metal edges, painted brick walls, and metal edges under work benches and the watch still looks brand new. It is also pretty inconspicuous, so I didn’t get any flack at work for dropping big bucks on a watch. Battery life is 6 days with brightness at 10%, swimming 3x a week for 30 minutes each. Using SC7 watch face that is pretty awesome imo. HR and stress tracking working well, very interesting to see this info. Update 3/3/2018 Working great still, battery life a solid 5 days at least. Interestingly, the physical stress data showed when I had the flu. Normally I am in the ‘resting’ state when sleeping, but when I was sick, my physical stress reading never went below medium stress even while sleeping. Sleep app said I was in deep sleep, even though my stress level was high at that time of the night. The same is true if I have a few too many drinks, the stress meter is high during sleep. It’s no wonder I feel like crap the next day! Also used it downhill skiing, and it detected starting runs and stopping runs automatically. No issues, and very cool to see my routes on the map later. Also neat to see max speed, elevation change, etc. displayed on the watch while on the hill. No regrets here at all, Garmin has made a solid product here.

title: Fantastic product! B
text: This is my third Vivoactive watch - one was cracked canyoning in Scotland - should have known that jumping off rocks into a pool and repelling down a waterfall might be a bad idea for any watch - my next Vivoactive is fine - gave it to my husband because I LOVe the look of the Vivoactive 3 and now I love everything about it!!!! It’s amazing - honestly - this watch is worth every penny! I’ve used it golfing, running, swimming and walking - indoor and out. It is easy to use and tracks so much - buy it!!!!!

title: Love My New Garmin
text: I love this watch! Out of all the fitness trackers I've had this has been my favorite. Easy to use. I love that I can put music on it and not worry about bringing my phone along. I can't speak as to how well it will hold but these last few weeks I've enjoyed it. Also, it is very comfortable despite being on the bigger size. Light weight so it's not weighing your arm down. The graphite blue and rose gold is a beautiful combo too.

title: Wasn't my favorite
text: I was on the hunt for something that would replace my apple watch since I switch to android. You really can't do much with this watch other than fitness. To me it seemed to be too boring and plain for the price that its selling for. I do gotta say the battery life on this watch was awesome and I also liked that you can locate your phone off of this watch.

title: Great little watch for tracking your biometrics
text: The GPS, heart rate, sleep tracking, and activity tracking works great. I sync these biometric data to an advertising database and allow corporations to send me products based on my biological state. For instance, I can get pharmaceuticals auto-ordered to calm or excite me without even realizing that I need them. There are future add-ons that will allow new agencies to track your biological responses and tailor Russian propaganda to elicit better responses from your parasympathetic nervous system. I suspect this will greatly increase the effectiveness of electioneering and mass cultural shifts. I welcome this brave new world.

title: Great fitness watch with tons of features
text: Really happy with this watch! I had a Pebble for years but when that ended I tried two different Android Wear watches and wasn't really thrilled with either. I bought this after reading many reviews and one of the main attractions was the 5 day battery life. I use the Bluetooth for music frequently and it is seamless. The fitness tracking works pretty well, and the Garmin app is great. I've had a few compliments on the watch and had people ask what it is because it's not square or overly large like some other watches.

title: great while it lasted
text: loved the watch for first yr. shortly after that, issues started arising. not holding a charge as long under same conditions. as the second yr of use progressed the watch got more buggy. I was constantly resetting it back to factory per Garmin support, seemed to fix things for a while, but that is a pain in the rear. you have to re-establish all your associations and connections. well. 18 months later, the watch has completely died. wont charge, wont do anything except find its way to the trash. I am mad that I cant even get 2 yrs of use out of a $250 device, but I guess this is what our world is today, cheaply made devices designed to get you to buy the latest greatest device every 18 months. what's next? subscription service on watches. I wont be buying Garmin again. I will buy something cheap and throwaway for $50.00 and feel bad when it craps out.

title: Nice, cute watch - has drawbacks though
text: I really like the look of this watch, which is why I was interested initially. As for features, compared to my old Fitbit, there are some good and bad aspects. For the good, I like the watch faces much more. There is a lot more customization available in general and I like that I can pick what works for me. As for the bad, I am pretty tech savvy, but it took me a while to figure out how to check my notifications. Also, the app freezes a lot.. Battery life seems pretty similar between the two. Maybe Garmin's is a little less since the watch face is always lit, but I do like that part. Update: I wasn't sure if it was just a one time glitch, but since getting the watch I have had to update my widgets once every couple weeks - if not more. Somehow the widgets will change order or get uninstalled. It is super annoying and then I have to go back into the app to edit it. I don't like the scrolling feature on the side of the watch. It will get triggered by my skin or clothes and then mess up things on the app. Sometimes the watch face will change and then if I want to get my old face back I have to re-install it again, which shouldn't be necessary. Also, I use the alarm function and really like it, but the button shouldn't turn off the alarm. The button is easier to hit than looking on the screen to hit snooze or cancel so the button should really be the snooze alarm. You want the cancel button to be harder than snooze as an alarm to really make sure people wake up. That's why on iPhone's the snooze button is huge, but the cancel one is small.

title: Great Fitness Tracker
text: Really like this Garmin fitness tracker. Very straightforward and functional. I was a Fitbit user for several years but have grown increasingly dissatisfied with their reliability and frequent dropping of exercises. So far haven't had this issue with the Garmin (except for human error). Battery life is decent. I've gone up to 4-days between charging on my "lazy" weeks. However, if you exercise daily and track exercises with the GPS then expect to charge up the watch for at least 30-45 minutes afterward as GPS drains the battery fairly rapidly. All-in-all this is a great product and fills all of my needs in a fitness watch.

title: Unimpressive.
text: I only wore this watch for 24 hours, and had to charge it twice. It also wouldn't download 75% of the watch faces I wanted from the iq store, just showed an error screen. I've had several Samsung watches, one ticwatch, and by comparison this watch is a bit sad. I really wanted a watch more geared to fitness, so even though the screen was not nearly as impressive as my frontier, I was going to give it a try (even though it was a bit like going from hd color back to black and white). I'm just not willing struggle with problems from day one. I'll go back to my frontier, or upgrade to a new one..

title: Great for running
text: This watch is perfect, I run and it is very accurate. Has many different options to add.

title: I like it.
text: I like it and its pretty accurate. I dont use all the features. I just walk and ride a bike because I have bad knees and I am 73.5 yrs old. I dont even need it. I guess the stimulus money persuaded me to buy it. I play golf but I have not used that feature yet, I will though. It does all kinds of things but I dont use them. It tells me to move when I sit on the couch. It gives me a pic of a Trophy when I reach my walking goals that the app set for me according to my age and physicality. I dont need it like I said, but I like it and use it. I have not looked at the app statistics on line yet. It records your progress and activity. It works well, pairs easily with the android phone and with the computer app. Garmin items are pretty reliable, not like some cheap ones I tried. Previous to this watch, I have had 2 Garmin golf watches, still have one and no problems.

title: Not great
text: For some reason this watch (black) repeatedly stops working. My white one works perfectly. We have tried trouble shooting it so many time and it will work ok for a very short period of time before it wont connect to our phones or keep time properly.

title: Don’t waste your money
text: I wanted to like this. The battery life stinks. It says it’ll last 7 days plus. Mine will last 2. Very very disappointed

title: Best fitness watc
text: I have tried many fitness watches. I prefer fitness first, smart second. For long time my favorite watch was the Microsoft Band 2. I did like the Vivoactive HR but was butt ugly. I tried S2, S3, polar360, atlas, various fitbits, forrunner235 Overall I rank this as the best fitness watch available. Pros: Looks nice every fitness feature needed Smart watch capabilites, see Texts and even reply. Constant on display. Battery life (not as good as advertised) Cons Price Strap not very fitness friendly, sweat and moisture get trapped underneath. short charging cable. I use this for mostly weightlifting. It does that rep counting feature which is pain, because you cant turn it off and its really useless to me. I wear it with wahoo chest strap. I like to track my workout calorie burn to add to my rest of the day. I did try using it for golfing and its not as good as MS Band2. The band would actually track my swings/strokes and keep score. This basically just tells you distance and you have fiddle with it to add score, real pain if you wear a glove. I also find the side swipe feature a joke, wish i can turn it off. Its touchscreen so why do i need it? I constantly hit it with my hand on accident. So overall id say its great watch, i'm happy with it. It is best fitness watch I have used.

title: Great watch / Mediocre GPS accuracy
text: Coming of the original Vivoactive this watch is in improvement in every way except what matters most to runners and bikers: GPS accuracy. My 5 mile runs become 4.85 and 3.1 miles become 3. You could say this wouldn't be a big deal, because it could be in the margin of error, until you look closely at the maps. Like other reviewers mention my road runs look like I was running through backyards and cutting through houses. The VA original would do this from time to time but for the most part it was pretty spot on and was very close to the measured 5ks that I run every few weeks. If you are on any leaderboards/ladders be prepared to drop a couple notches. This is a major downer for me because this is the reason I go with Garmin over Fitbit or other competitors. The watch faces and usability is a huge improvement over the original and the heart rate appears to be spot on. I used it while having an EKG and it matched my resting heart rate. Battery life is about 15% per day with about 10% per hour GPS use drain. I bought this black Friday and have been running with it for over 1 1/2 weeks. I'm keeping it in hopes that the location accuracy improves with firmware updates but right now it is significantly worse than my VA original and a bit worse than my iPhone used to be. *Changed from 3 to 1 stars because the battery has been cutting out after 40%. I might a lemon but the customer service wants me to jump through hoops before they will do anything. I have already jumped through those hoops because I have been following the issues and workarounds in the forums.

title: Poor Screen Resolution and Quality
text: I returned this watch because the screen resolution is terrible. I read that it is low quality in exchange for longer battery life. The trade off isn't worth it for me. I am just fine charging my watch at the end of the day and I value good screen resolution. If you prefer longer battery life to screen quality, this will work well for you.

title: Wife told me that this is way better than the apple watch regarding fitness and keepoing track ...
text: Wife told me that this is way better than the apple watch regarding fitness and keepoing track of t=her activities. She had issues with the music from the apple watch. She loves this one.. So now we are a garmin family

title: Wife loves it
text: I bought this as a gift for my wife and she absolutely loves it. Keeps track of her daily steps, sleep cycle, and calories burned. She also likes the yoga setting on it as an exercise that you can get from the app.

title: GPS comes up short
text: After the first couple of mountain bike rides the GPS is tracking about 10% less than two apps on my phone. The heart rate is also running low compared to a chest strap monitor but I was not expecting it to be accurate on a mountain bike ride when I don't like adjusting the strap tight enough to keep it tight to my wrist. The touch screen response is good and navigating through the pages of apps responds quickly however the overall default layout is not as convenient or intuitive as I would like. If I get more accurate GPS tracking with more uses comparing it to other devices I'll update my rating.

title: My favorite thing is that it's completely waterproof and I can ...
text: At first I wasn't sure about this watch, but have started liking it more and more each day. My favorite thing is that it's completely waterproof and I can shower/swim with it without any worry. I have been unable to get the GPS function to work yet, so if you're looking for that option as a "deal breaker", I wouldn't bet on it...other than that everything is great. Love the look, design, and feel. Much better than the FitBit which is what I used for many years in the past.

title: Accurate, music 👌, fair battery life
text: Garmin fitness watches in my opinion are superior to others on the market. They are accurate, battery lasts a long time, durable, and this holds music. If you have Spotify premium, you're able to download playlists right to this watch and listen while working out without a phone! Gamechanger for sure. This also connects relatively easily to bluetooth headphones. Without listening to music and using this to track 3-15 or 20 minute walks a day plus other features such as sleep and steps, the battery lasts about 5-6 days. While listening to music on those walks the battery probably only lasts 4 days. However, the battery charges super fast and is easy to throw on the charger for 10-20 minutes before using if the battery is low.

title: PERFECT TRACKER
text: I needed to buy a 2nd one after I left my original one at the movie theater. I didn't even consider buying another brand of fitness tracker watch. The shape is perfect b/c it looks like a casual watch. The App is amazing & the tracking is great. Only thing is that the Garmin watches with multiple buttons on the side are a little too expensive for my liking. Wish this had more than just one button

title: Much better than a Fitbit
text: Replaced a very buggy Fitbit Charge 3 with this watch. The screen is great, the tracking is accurate, and so far the watch does exactly what I expect. Very happy with the purchase. Do yourself a favor and look at Garmin before you jump into the Fitbit world.

title: non
text: A wonderful watch but there are only three languages ​​and I tried to add another language and there is not yet.

title: Glitchy and warranty is questionable
text: First the good: Got this for myself for my birthday in July. I LOVE the look of it and intended to use it for hiking, so the GPS was an important feature. In two months, I’ve had the GPS fail on me twice. So, not perfect, but could be worse. I’m content with it. Now the not so good: The worst thing to me is that the software and sync is pretty glitchy. I’ve had several days that heartrate, sleep, and activity data don’t sync. They’re displayed on the watch, but don’t make it to the app and I’ve had to hard reset, which means lose the data in the watch, and then need to re-do all the customizing. Essentially I’ve had to factory re-set every three weeks, which I feel is a little much for a brand new device. I’ve been chatting and on the phone with garmin support several times, and they agreed this is a warranty issue, and sent me an RMA number. Super happy with that, until i read it indicates that I will be getting a refurbished watch. I have had a brand new vivoactive 3 for under 2 months and the warranty replacement is refurbished? I wouldn’t have spent full price on a new one LESS THAN 60 days ago if I wanted refurbished! I’m going to have to think about whether or not i want to go that route. The battery life is average since I customized my watch face. Not a picture, just some additional features compared to the standard (pretty lame) face. I guess that cuts battery life in half. I think you can expect users to customize their watch face, so stop marketing it as a long battery life and instead be straight-forward about the real situation.

title: HR sensor is accurate, overall great value for money
text: Great watch all around. Cheap and gets you all necessary features like HR, steps, GPS and the great Garmin app.

title: Great watch
text: I have had the watch for a month now. I took off my Apple Watch and have been wearing this. I love the look of it, the replaceable bands, it seems so much more accurate for me as a runner, it does send me my texts and my phone calls (can’t answer from the watch though like you could Apple Watch), and I usually charge 2 times a week. I don’t like that it disconnects from my phone a little too often. I loved the pinging feature on my Apple Watch when I couldn’t find my phone and this one has the feature too but always seems to be disconnected from my phone when I need to use it. Overall a good change though, I would recommend and will continue to use over my Apple Watch

title: convenient mp3 player for running
text: I use this Garmin Vívoactive 3 Music Smartwatch for running. The GPS accuracy is good. The heart-rate monitor is a great feature. But I mostly bought it for the convenience of listening to music while running. It holds a lot of mp3 files and sounds great connected to my Phaiser BHS-530 Bluetooth Headphones (

title: What I like about it water proof and it looks like a ...
text: So far with no gps use the watch last 6-7 days without a charge. What I like about it water proof and it looks like a watch. Has a lot of functions. Seems to be fairly accurate. For the person just looking for HR, calls, and steps this much does much more and you might be better off with something similar. Interface and app is pretty good but not as easy as Fitbit

title: Love this fitness smart watch!
text: This fitness smart watch is an upgrade for me from other Garmin product. I love it. Battery life is about 5 days without GPS usage and with occasional GPS usage is about 3 days.

title: Great watch
text: This watch is pretty much perfect. Had the Galaxy active. Didn't like it. Hard to see numbers while running. This watch is customizable. The RUN app numbers are large enough to see clearly and the GPS is accurate and fast. Absolutely love it.

title: Buggy and unreliable
text: I am so bummed about this watch. I like the way it looks and the interface isn't hard to use. After some annoying troubleshooting, I was able to get it to sync with my phone and show me notifications. However, I have had issues with recording activities, which is the entire reason I purchased the watch. First, I was in the middle of a long ride when I looked down and noticed the watch was no longer recording. I looked at my activities and the ride was saved. The only way to save a ride is by stopping recording, pressing "done," and then pressing "save." I definitely did not complete that three-step process while riding my bicycle. Then, I finished a ride and completed the three-step process to save it, but the ride is nowhere to be found. It either never saved or deleted itself somehow. I wanted to use this watch for tracking my running and cycling but when recording gets messed up it makes it all feel kind of pointless. Now I'm thinking of returning it and going back to the old days of not even worrying about how far I rode.

title: This is a fantastic fitness watch, but not a smart watch
text: The good: Battery life! Screen visible in any lighting conditions Garmin connect app is better than Fitbit Very customizable Looks expensive The bad: Doesn't auto-detect workouts Takes way too long to connect to GPS Altimeter doesn't seem to be accurate Not a lot of people on Garmin connect The battery life is awesome! I've been using GPS about 4 times a week for about an hour each time, and the battery lasts about 6 days. It also charges super fast. Maybe an hour, depending on the power source. I charge mine in my car so it takes longer, but once I'm down to about 30%, I'll throw it on the charger while I drive home, and I'll get to about 85% during a 30 minute commute. This watch looks really nice. I had the Fitbit versa before this, and it was a nice watch, but this one looks way more modern and expensive. The screen colors are dull and the resolution is low, but it is always visible in any light, which is amazing! You can check your texts, which comes in handy, but responding won't really be useful here. I wish it auto-detected workouts (if it does, it isn't very good at it because it hanst done so for me). It takes quite a while to find GPS (about a minute, as opposed to 5 seconds with my Fitbit versa). It doesn't count flights of stairs accurately.

title: Great smartwatch
text: I like to been able to change the watchfaces, sometimes is not as accurate with the footsteps, but all the rest works fine. I love that it looks good with any clothes!

title: Big and Bulky
text: I upgraded from the VivoActive to the VivoActice3. I wish I wouldn't have. I do not like how big and heavy the 3 is. I also have to lock the screen because it is so sensitive to everything. The battery life is not near as long as the original. I know it is partly because the HR monitor. I turned the HR monitor off and that has helped the battery life, however, I do not feel like the watch is as accurate with it off. The original's battery life is around 7 days and this 3's battery life is 1 day if the HR monitor is on and about 2-3 days with the HR monitor off. I have to wear the 3 higher up on my wrist because the side buttons are so sensitive and it is so bulky. The band is also 4mm wider than the original. It makes it less feminine and uncomfortable. I bought an aftermarket band to make it look more feminine. I like Garmin because of the map features. I bike and hike often so I like to see all the stats. I would switch back to the original VivoActive in a heartbeat.

title: I love love love this watch!
text: Some of the reviews scared me but I decided to full-send anyways. I got the white and gold and it is SOOOOO CUTEEEE!!! I get compliments all the time, and I have had it for like 4 months now and the band is still white! I bought glass screen protectors which are a must if you don't want to scratch your brand new watch (in my photo you can see I have chipped the one I have on there). The watch GPS loads in under a minute usually and seems pretty accurate, but when I run on the track (which I know the exact distance), it gets slightly off. That is kinda to be expected though and it is definitely muuuuuccchhhh more accurate than my phone. My boyfriend has an apple watch and even after 6miles they might only have a .3 difference (which I don't think is much of a big deal, I prefer to run for time rather than distance anyways and the watch helps me know my effort level). The other awesome thing is you can choose all of your displays. How they look, what order they are in, and which ones you want on there or not. And you can choose to have it flipped any direction for right and left hand. It doesn't turn off like an apple watch so the seconds don't disappear if you are trying to plank or count heart rate or something (I am a nursing student and its helpful for taking vitals). You can also connect your account to "My Fitness Pal" or "Stava" or whatever else you like to use. I exercise a lot so my battery dies in like 3 days, but I think it can last like 5 without recording things. It charges really fast though, so sometimes I just let it charge while I am showering or making lunch or something. It is waterproof and I wear it swimming all the time! And you can read full emails/texts on it (but not respond). It takes a little while to figure out how everything works, but then it is easy to use! I WOULD DEFINITELY RECOMMEND buying this one rather than spending $500 on a newer one because it works great.

title: Hubby loves it
text: Got this for the hubby to upgrade from his vivo fit 1 he’s love all the features and that it looks like a regular watch

title: Bands are too short to fit average fit male
text: I'll update this if Garmin comes clean about to the band only fitting small medium to small wrists and replaces the band. If you're a male, or woman with medium sized wrists, then this watch won't fit you without spending at least $30 (up to $60 for a large) for a new band. Nothing in the product description says you have to be 5'8" and 140lbs to buy this item. I own other Garmin wearables and feel seriously deceived on this one. Merry Christmas, Garmin!!!!!

title: Garmin watches are great
text: I got this for my dad and he is loving it. I have a different model and love it as well. My dad likes how this one fits and all that can be used for.

title: Do NOT get this watch! Runners beware!!!
text: This watch is the absolute WORST! For the first month is was fine, however after six months I have a glitch or an issue every time I pick it up to use it! My Spotify music mysteriously disappears, it won’t connect to any of my Bluetooth headsets(I have three different pairs, and they are all different brands so I don’t want to hear it’s my headphones) and sometimes it won’t turn on at all. It freezes and glitches anytime I run over 20 minutes which results in me having to reset it and it loses my run details. Super annoying! DO NOT BUY!

title: Great watch, subpar battery life
text: Battery life is nowhere near what it should be... however, I am more than satisfied with everything else about this watch.

title: Excellent battery life
text: Six months later and I still LOVE this watch!!! The battery lasts 5 days or more between charges. I love that I can edit the text replies I have available for use. This is a great watch!

title: Great watch
text: First of all it looks really good. Second the functionality of it is great. It supports all kinds of sports and had some apps that you can download from garmin connect.

title: Awesome sport watch.
text: Okay where does one begin? I bought this GPS sport watch over a few other brands to mainly have a sync ready HR to run with my cycling computer which is a Xplova X5 Evo. I bought new and not refurbished and the first one worked three days then would not read certain functions, mainly HR. So I returned it for a new replacement. The new one has worked flawlessly now. I love the preloaded apps and mainly only use cycling to sync up with my cycling computer. It works like a charm. Now there ar ed detractors of a wrist HR reader as not being accurate but neither is a chest strap. They are just somewhat in the area to give you a somewhat picture of HR while exercising and that is okay. I also love this watch does VO2 reading ( once again not as accurate as traditional methods to measure) but still gets you in a ballpark. My step measurement is spot on as you measure how many steps (normal stride) to cover 20 feet as the method I used. It is spot on. The most impressive feature is the screen does not wash out in direct sunlight. In fact, it is more readable in direct sunlight unlike most electronic screens. Plus being a 20mm watch band there are many replacement bands as well. Charging time you ask???? Extremely quick and usually from like 25% to 100% is around 45 minutes. I am getting about 4 days of mixing GPS activity with regular functions which to me is very good. Claimed is about 7 days regular use and 14 hours constant GPS functionality. Worth the money being a older version being the Vivoactive 4 has been out about two years and this model going on 3-4? Most definitely at the price of almost half. Highly recommended if you need a basic but somewhat expandable sport watch that you can also swim in. I will update this review in a year or sooner if it fails for no reason. So why 4 stars? I would have given 4.5 stars but Amazon does not have half star ratings. Nothing is ever really a 5 star but simple products.....this watch could improve on a few things.

title: What you see, isn't exactly what you get.
text: After one month, my VA3Music is going back to Garmin for a warranty exchange. My watch faces keep disappearing, and when tech support chatted with me, they said something about the IQ isn't registering correctly. Also, those brilliant and vibrant colors all the pics show.....nada. Check out my pictures vs their pictures. Yes, the lighting may appear different, but the pics of mine are accurate in appearance and subdued color appearance of the watch face. Tech did not think anything was wrong with the colors. I would probably be happier if what I saw in all the adds and articles I saw during my research was what I got. In appearance alone, the colors look cheap and that does a disservice to this device and Garmin. Not an intuitive interface. There is a learning curve to this device. I was still learning when I had to send it back. I will try again.....in the estimated 10-14 days, it will take for the replacement to arrive. Battery life seemed to be just under a week, but I was not doing anything other than monitoring my normal routine. The silicone band keeps giving me a heat or friction rash. I may end up changing bands all together if I can't get a fit that works against that. I will try to update later if anything significant occurs with my replacement. > Update - 02/08/2019: Actually took the watch outdoors into bright light. NOW you get to see the colors advertised. Indoors (even daytime or well-lit areas), when you have to use the backlighting, is when you get the blueish purple colors. I still hold by my earlier 3-Star. It would be a 4 if the colors were anywhere visible or vibrant indoors. No reason I can see why they shouldn't. Also, I am finding that the included silicone band is causing heat or dry rashes around my wrist. I sleep with a silicone mask on my CPAP, so it is not an allergic reaction. Will be looking for a leather or metal band next.

title: Mine broke in less than 5 days
text: I loved my watched when I 1st got it! It was my 1st smart watch I ever had. I was impressed w the stress level and how light weight it was. I am disappointed tht the battery life went to crap after I downloaded some apps. Then shortly stopped working. Green light wouldn't register my stress levels. I called the company and they said it was a rare occurrence. They tried their very best to fix it via phone. We did an update and everything possible. They were super friendly on the phone. But I was in the end sad tht I had to return it and didn't get to show it off. I ended up not buying this product again because I liked the features on the Samsung galaxy watch more. Seems like a phone but on ur wrist. More to do n functions. I hope I like my new watch when I get home to try it.

title: Frustrating
text: Most frustrating piece of technology I have ever owned. Too many issues to even list here. Never ever will I buy a Garmin again.

title: Looks Nicer than it Works
text: This watch was a huge disappointment. I’ve been using other fitness watches over the years, but this was my first “smart” watch. Disappointments: 1. The screen resolution is nothing like what you see on the online pictures. 2. Navigating through the watch menus is somewhat frustrating i did eventually get used to it but I still think there needs to be more development here. Perhaps I’m used to the “not so smart” watch I’ve been using for years. 3. Sync’ing doesn’t always sync and may take a while. Oddly enough, the data transfer is rather small in size (kbs), but the sync status bar seems to hang incomplete. I sometimes get “Uninstall error” when trying to delete a watch face, widget or data setting. 4. Interesting how it can measure my HR without actually touching my body. How does that technology work? 5. HR readings are iratic. Sometimes high when I’m at rest, other times low when I’m doing high intensity work. I’ve compared this watch with my Polar M400 (been using for years) and they are almost never in sync. Enough to question whether I bought a dud or not. Really wanted this to work. I’ve been wearing a strap HR monitor for years (Polar M400 and others previously) and have been able to train successfully for events with confidence. Even then, straps have issues too (I.e. battery life and replacement, strap wear and tear, strap point of contact issues), but I’m not sure Garmin got the wrist based measurement right. I’m returning this one and gonna get the Polar Vantage M to see if it is any better. BTW...the pictures I posted are side by side comparison while on a spinning cycle. I had been questing the reading of the Garmin so I decided to compare it against my M400 sometime into my cycling routine. I did this multiple times and even reset the Garmin to be sure...still iratic readings.

title: I expected more
text: Honestly the sensors on this thing are complete garbage. The step tracking is far from accurate, heart rate monitor is off as much as 40 bpm sometimes, and when conparing to gps run tracking on my phone it's off as much as .5 miles in a 6 mile run sometimes, on a distance i know to be exactly 6 miles. Handy for a general idea of things, but don't expect any real accuracy. First smart/fitness watch I've ever had and I'm pretty underwhelmed after 5 months +/- of use.

title: Have bluetooth pairing issues
text: I expected more from garmin, I choosen the Garmin because I though it was good brand. The watch have a lot of trouble to pair with my Jaybird headphones and my wife bose headphones. Each time I want to listen to music I need to try to pair the headphones several times until it works. Also while paired it just disconnects and you need to repeat the process. I checked the headphones with my phone and there is no pairing issues, so the watch is the faulty one. I bought the Vivoactive 3 Music to listen to music but it was a waste of money if it doesn't pair with any headphone.

title: Nice-looking watch, and the app is better
text: I got a Garmin watch to pick up running as a lockdown hobby. The Garmin app has training plans for 5k, 10k, and half marathon. I successfully completed a half marathon in September. The watch+app took all the planning out of it and just gave me workouts to complete. The battery life is also nice. I charge it every ~3 days when training and using the GPS, or once a week if not using the GPS. This lets me wear it at night to monitor how long I'm sleeping. What I like about the vivoactive 3 is that it has these serious features for running, but it also looks stylish. I've gotten compliments on my white/rose gold watch.

title: Had two Vivoactive 3s die, each in under a year
text: Got the Vivoactive 3 because I wanted to track exercise and didn't want to spend the money on an Apple Watch or more expensive Garmin watch. The first one died after about ten months. The first thing I noticed was the watch was taking longer and longer to track my heart rate while exercising, and I was getting drop outs. It also began to show weird HR spikes when I wasn't exercising, reading 120+ bpm when I was sitting down, reading. Within a couple weeks it completely stopped tracking my heart rate with any accuracy while exercising: it would read 50-70 bpm below where I knew my heart rate was. I contacted Garmin support and did everything they asked: reset the watch, made sure I was following directions, made sure the band was the right tightness, sent them screenshots, etc. They were unable to diagnose the problem and sent me a replacement. It failed in exactly the same way: about ten months in I started to see it take longer and longer to latch onto my heart rate, and then it, too, stopped tracking my heart rate while riding my bike. If you read the Garmin forums you'll see this isn't an isolated problem. I replaced it with and Apple Watch SE and the difference is night and day. The watch feels like a single, solid piece of hardware, the software is polished, and the syncing is easy. After these two watches, and my Garmin head unit, failed I'm done with Garmin products.

title: Love this watch
text: I had a Garmin Forerunner 25 for about 4 years. I really enjoyed it. But, I started having issues with it syncing with my phone, etc. I did quite a bit of research and decided to go with this Garmin Vivoactive 3. It's much lighter and more comfortable that the Garmin Forerunner 25. The functionality is much more extensive on the Vivoactive 3. I have used it on the treadmill, which hasn't been real accurate. It was under by about .25 mile. I also used it for a walk and that seemed pretty accurate. I am looking forward to using it while golfing and swimming.

title: Would recommend
text: I love this watch. Not over priced like Apple or Samsung and it works just fine with either. I especially love that it’s waterproof. No tracker is going to be exact, but this one comes pretty close. Definitely recommend.

title: Great GPS smartwatch choice!
text: My wife and I each have one of these watches. They're really great. Reliable, sturdy, and Garmin GPS works excellently as expected. I've used a TomTom GPS watch and Samsung Frontier S3 in the past. This Garmin is head and shoulders above those. The smart watch features are just the right amount. The Samsung watch I had had a bunch of useless apps that just drained the battery and didn't work too well anyway. The battery life on this watch is great. For just normal use I can probably get close to a week out of it. When running daily I'll probably charge it every 4 days. And it charges really fast!

title: GPS not accurate otherwise ok
text: I've been using my iPhone to track my running and play music to my bluetooth headset. With this watch, I don't need to bring the phone with me to go running anymore. I put in 100s of running music mp3 onto the watch, no streaming. But very soon I notice the GPS is not accurate at all, actually much worse than the iPhone, even for the runs in the suburban trails, it lose tracking of satellite often. The worse part is the pace, it is way off. I don't understand how the mileage is roughly correct, but the pace is way off it's own mileage calculation, and the pace tends to be much slower than my running - ok, maybe this will motivate you to run faster:) The Garmin connect software is very easy to use, provides a lot of data. I used to pay a lot of attention to them early on, now I don't look as much now. I still wear the watch to sleep, I don't take it off at all until it needs charging. Very light and comfortable. And the heart rate mostly works. That's why I haven't returned the watch, even though GPS not working well, sigh..

title: gift my sister
text: birthday gift to my sister and she adore it so much

title: Holds music and has a great heart rate monitor built in.
text: Upgraded from Garmin Forerunner 235 just for the ability to store music internally. The watch does so crunches many additional analytics. The HR monitor has better software so accuracy while sleeping and awake are better. Music works great. My only downside is literally too many options. I'm just a recreational runner who runs road/trail races and some obstacle course races. This watch has a lot going on but after customization can be scaled back. Absolutely love this watch.

title: Love
text: Love that I can wear this in water. Comfortable and easy to use.

title: Update does now work with Moto Phones.
text: Update issue with Garmin and Lenovo fixed. Now able to sync with Moto phone. Yay! I read that garmin has not fixed issues with lenovo on their website, I thought they may have fixed this by now so i contacted customer service and and asked and they said that is not an issue and as I was speaking with them I seen that it still is an issue on their website and the customer service was quick in trying to tell me it was my phone with the issue and that they can't do anything about it. I quickly responded that I found more information on their website regarding this then what they are telling me. So Moto is lenovo and the garmin does not stay connected, it disconnects and reconnects all dy long making the battery life shorter. I bought this knowing this was an issue but thinking its a big company they will have it fixed in no time. But it was never fixed and I can use the watch. I am not going to purchase a new phone that isnt moto just for my watch to work. But it was a bummer that their customer service at garmin was quick to write my issue as my fault. Also I helped a friend move a couple of weeks ago and her new place is up several stairs I walked these stairs no joke at least 35 times, and my garmin only recorded my going up stairs one time and never descending from those stairs. I had spent a lot of time researching this purchase before I even purchased it, I looked at others I looked at prices I looked at features, I spent a couple months researching and thought I nailed it with this Garmin but sadly was disappointed. I am back on the search for a fitness tracker and Looking into other brands and going to their website to read more about compatibility with phones and the features.

title: So glad I went with this one
text: I love this watch! It looks fancy and can look like a real watch with all the apps that a activity tracker has. I wear mine everyday and night. Love seeing my sleep schedule, HR and steps, plus getting all my phone notifications.

title: Love this watch.
text: I really love this watch...looks great and the features are excellent. Since I use the treadmill I'm not sure if the treadmill app is correct...I just use the Garmin app on my phone!

title: Fell short on the smartwatch side
text: I really wanted to love it. I really did. Lets preface this review with what I was hoping to get out of it - A fitness-focused watch that moonlights as a smartwatch. Overall I was unimpressed with the smartwatch features. Syncing it to my Google Pixel, the notifications it receives and displays are very limited. There isn't much you can do about that, but it didn't really feel like there was much to it. Also, they were often delayed by 10 minutes. My phone was always in my pocket near the watch, not sure if this was just a lemon or if it is something to do with the watch itself. The screen was also pretty underwhelming. In comparison to what the fitbit iconic looks like, the garmin falls short. The iconic is more crisp and bright, the vivoactive is more pixel-y and dull. What I was most interested in were I was pretty happy with the battery life. It would be nice if you could extend the battery life by the fitness tracking aspects of it. It takes some customization to get it to do what you really want - I could not figure out how to threshold the activity tracking so that just normal walks to and from places weren't counted as exercise. I ended up turning the automatic tracking off. The rep-counting was not accurate at all. Punching in data retrospectively was difficult as well. If I wanted to say I did squats with 150 pounds, I would have to sit there and wait for the numbers to go up one by one if logging it through the watch. Swimming with the watch was great, I love that you can track SWOLF scores through the app. However when the watch is submerged it becomes difficult to operate and the touch sensitivity is pretty whacko. turning constant HR off, but that is not possible. Overall, the basic features of the watch are fine but very difficult to control with swipes and the 1 button on the side. The cons didn't justify the $300 price tag, so it was returned. Maybe once there have been some software updates and it has been on the market longer I will re-evaluate.

title: Expensive Plastic Toy
text: The watch itself is too light and cheaply made to justify the cost. A Samsung watch is made better and costs less. I love Garmin, just not this Garmin.

title: Switched from Fitbit
text: The Garmin mobile app has some great features and seems to sync better with My Fitness Pal which is great. The software is subpar compared to Fitbit though. Vivoactive 3 step counter is way off and it doesn’t matter how many flights of steps I use during the day, the Garmin doesn’t register them correctly. Thought Garmin was supposed to be a leader in GPS technology- guess not? It is really aggravating to look at my end of day stats to see I’ve gone down 7 flights of steps but never up a flight. Guess Garmin thinks I’m on a stairway to hell. Thanks Garmin, thanks a lot. Update a year later (07/14/19) Bumped from 2 to 4 stars. I’ve put this watch through a lot and it is way more durable than I thought. If you are rough and tumble I recommend getting a screen protector. I managed to scratch mine on a sharp piece of metal. I’ve since learned you can adjust your stride length which has helped with my step count, but the stair counter still stinks. Mostly updating with a higher rating because this watch has lasted and because the third party apps add an endless amount of function Fitbit can’t even compete with.

title: If you like Purple, this watch is for you!
text: Default color for everything is an ugly purple. The screen is very pixelated and looks dated. Won't stay connected to WiFi and won't download music (downloaded 2 or 3 apps to do this on my phone). Returning. Purchased for music + GPS. But absolutely cannot stand that I can't change from PURPLE on everything. Connected to 3 wifis and says connected just fine; when you try to download songs on the spotify app (have to download a garmin app, garmin connect, and then a spotify sub-app in the garmin app); the music still won't download and it "loses" wifi connection. Go to the Garmin site: The software is not user friendly. The watch is well over a 1/4" high, and the entire width of my wrist. Would not recommend purchasing this watch. The Huawei proband 3 (bought for $55 on Amazon) worked 100% of the time, was never more than a couple hundred feet different than my phone GPS; and had a long battery life. I walked about a mile yesterday with the watch on; and the watch logged that I walked 11 steps total. For $200 I would expect it at least performed stated functions. I was able to connect it to headphones, and 3 wifi networks (although it randomly loses all 'memory' of them all or some especially when trying to download songs).

title: I love this watch for the price
text: I love Garmin products. This watch is perfect for every day wear. Light weight and It so easy to change the faces. I also use a Garmin 920 for triathlons but not for the office.

title: Good watch with fluff features.
text: While I like the device, I would probably recommend its predecessor due to: + the battery life being significantly shorter. + the firmware not being as solid as the former + the extra useless features such as the payment feature. I can't believe how little the battery lasts compare to the former. Maybe they have left the radio on for the payment feature even when one isn't using it? Not sure. Also, one does not have much control over the watch face other than the few faces they have which is sad noting how much data one gets by using an analog look versus a digital one. Maybe there are custom ones available? But this is such a simple thing to fix: make the digital clock smaller so more read outs can fit. The band is a bit small for my wrist which of the two vendors I tried for getting a device, neither of them knew of alternate sizes like historically were available. Anyway, I think the activity checking throughout the day is better as it does it more than just once a day like is predecessor, but it still pressures you to keep moving after you achieve your goals. The new firmware seems to help with getting the backlight to work a bit better which doesn't eat up as much battery, but even still it needs work.

title: Not perfect but a great little device
text: It's been about 2 weeks since I purchased this sweet little watch. I am just you typical "I just wanna count my steps, track my workouts, and track my sleep so I can work on being a healthier me" everyday person. This watch has been great so far. It is truly waterproof but it is touch screen so it freaks out a little bit when submerged which is expected. It does a great job at tracking all the various activities I do. I love that it has a yoga and a weight lifting option. The device does have its flaws. It likes to give me credit for flights of stairs I haven't climbed sometimes and sometimes counts extra or misses my steps, but overall it gives me an idea of where I'm at health wise and that is exactly what I wanted out of it. I would recommend it to anyone looking to do the same!

title: So far, so good!
text: This is my first smartwatch so I can't compare it to anything else yet. So far I'm happy with how well the watch itself works. It seems to track everything properly. I took it for a walk and am pleased with the ease of use when scrolling through the menu. The menus are also completely customizable which is awesome. I do think the phone apps, Garmin Connect and IQ Store could be better. You must download a PC app called Garmin Express as well in order to sync it properly and get firmware updates. So it feels like it would be nice if there was one central place to go for syncing, updates, and app downloads instead of having to install 3 separate things. Garmin should work on streamlining their services. Also many of the watchfaces they advertise are from third party developers who require payment through PayPal for use of their watchfaces, so that's something to think about. I also purchased the GlassShield screen protector for this and am happy with how it fits. It is applied to the watch in my photo. I previously had a Fitbit, and I was less than pleased with it when I had it only a year and the band fell apart. Here's hoping this one is better made.

title: Heart rate and steps are extremely inaccurate.
text: My resting heart rate is 72. Walked for 30 min. Apple phone app says I walked over 4,000 steps. Garmin 550. Garmin heart rate while walking says 70-126. I kept a steady pace except for when I stopped to check my heart rate. It was about 120 beats each time (give or take 4). I did turn it around so the sensor was on the inside of my wrist. That was the only time my pulse was over 100. But it was mostly at 70-94 that way. Sleep... says my heart rate was 74. I am a peaceful sleeper. Pro of watch - I could put my own picture as a background. Watch came charged at 64%. By the next morning (about 14 hours later it needed to charge). It did charge to 74% within an hour (didn't keep exact time). Sending this back today. Very disappointed, guess I'll have to join the fitbit craze!

title: Looks great, not accurate at all
text: It’s a nice looking watch, and functional enough for what I need, considering I got it for $84. I got it mostly for fitness tracking, which it okay, but not amazing at. I’m not worried about small inaccuracies, so I’m not disappointed, but based on first two uses at the gym: Distance measurement isn’t very accurate on the treadmill. It overshoots mileage by about .15 miles per mile versus the treadmill readout. It asks me to calibrate after every workout, so maybe it’s learning and will adjust accordingly. (Edit: Nope.) The step counter seems to be pretty close. HR monitor seems undershot. Every other monitor I’ve used, even Garmin’s VivoFit, and the various gym treadmills, pegs me at 170-175bpm full-out. With the VivoActive 3, I’m lucky to break 160. Unless my heart has become substantially stronger suddenly, it seems inaccurate. The strength app is intuitive and easy for manually recording your reps and sets, but it does a terrible job of sensing an accurate number of reps on its own. If you’re making shorter motions, it barely recognizes that you’re moving. Always underestimates by at least five reps, but usually more. I haven’t tested it to it’s potential yet, so I may update. ***Update - June 2021*** The heart rate monitor is basically worthless for gym activites. It takes sometimes 20 minutes to finally display anything close to an accurate HR, then it just makes up whatever it wants in that realm. I specifically bought this watch for use as a HR monitor and assumed Garmin would be at least semi-reliable. Not this time. The only thing this watch does well outside of telling time is look good. Otherwise every smart watch I have ever used outperforms it in basic functionality and accuracy. The battery was advertised by Garmin to last up to 13 days, but my absolute max without bluetooth or any widgets running is three, possibly four.

title: Impressed so far!

The Garmin Connect app is great and we are loving that we can be each other's "Connections" and track and challenge each other's progress. Battery life has been great so far. I took mine out of the box and charged it on 12/30, and have just under half the battery remaining on day 4, 1/2 (about 40%).

title: 48 hours in - so far great!
text: It has taken me 2+ years and on my third watch to find one that works well and I enjoy wearing! Everyone and everything I read told me to get an Apple watch, but I couldn't bring myself to spend $300+ for a watch. What I was looking for - a watch that could be worn for all occasions: fitness, every day life, work, events, night life, etc. A watch that easily could tell time, send me text and phone notifications, and track my fitness (steps, sleep, and heart rate). This watch does all of that and more, and so far I could not be more pleased. At first I thought the size would be too big - but it works well for my wrist, and is so light that the size isn't noticeable. It appears to be syncing quickly and accurately, tracking accurate steps, etc. I am starting day 3 of my watch and battery is only at 75% - very impressed! I will give it a few weeks and come back to provide an update. So far - couldn't be more impressed with Garmin and this watch!

title: Fashionable Sports Watch with Battery Issues
text: I really like the sports tracking aspect of this watch - I have had no trouble with it at all. And, I really like that while on the big side, it is nice enough looking that I feel comfortable wearing it to work. The downside, and why I wouldn't necessarily recommend this watch is the BATTERY! First, I get about TWO days out of a charge - with exercising at least once a day and the screen on bright enough so these middle-aged eyes can see it. Which I wouldn't really mind if I could just hook it up at the same time every day and charge it and know I am ready to go. BUT, with the battery saving feature, you can only charge it when it gets below a certain point. So, I find myself constantly monitoring the watch to make sure it doesn't die, but is low enough to charge. This is a super pain when I have a big race coming up - 1/2 or full marathon...I have to figure out how to run it down enough so I can charge it for the race, but if I'm off by 1% then it won't charge and I won't have enough juice to get through a long run (and for me we are talking 5+ hours for a marathon, only fair to mention that). So that just drives me nuts. Hey Garmin - a manual override for charging would be really helpful if you are out there listening!!!
