title: Not good enough. NOT suitable for cyclists.
text: Not suitable for cyclists. Suffers a tremendous amount of dropped connections and OHR misreadings. As explained to me by the support team, when the OHR misreads (due to light leak, or the skin moving underneath the device), the HR drops to 70 bpm and slowly, gradually climbs back up to about 130 unless it can correct itself. This artificially deflates heart rate analytics which can throw off your TRIMP, TRSS and caloric burn estimates. What's more, the battery life is nowhere near what is advertised. It should have the same capacity as that of the VAHR, but I am getting 25-33% the duration of time between charges with the same activity levels as with my VAHR. Brightness settings, backlight duration, and all the various battery saving adjustments have been made to no avail. I cannot recommend this product for serious athletes at this price point, especially with no music integration. Garmin was poised to conquer the triathlon market with the Vivoactive lineup, but this one is an utter flop. Shame, because it is a beautiful piece of hardware. As it stands, it is probably suitable as a casual fitness tracker like a Fitbit, but without Fitbit, Apple, or Nike's strong social networks that would draw the casual crowd. It's beautiful. It works, kind of. It DOES NOT do the job it needs to be doing for the audience it lends itself to. In all ways other than aesthetics, this is a complete downgrade from the VAHR.

title: Easy to Use!
text: This is my 3rd smart watch. I have had a Kate Spade and Michael Kors one. Those both used Wear OS. In comparison to those watches, I like this one better. It did require me to download more apps on my phone such as Galaxy Wearable. This watch is easy to use. There are 2 controls. The Michael Kors one had 2 controls, too, but their location was always accidently getting bumped which sometimes caused it to restart when I didn't want it to. I have never accidently bumped these buttons. The strap that comes with it barely fits my wrist, but there's an extra longer one that comes with it. It comes with a charger. The watch claims to stay charged for days. Well, technically that's true. I find that it lasts for 2 days so every other day I need to recharge it. My former watches both had to be charged every night, so I am pleased that this lasts a little longer. As far as the fitness aspect, this is better than my other ones. The step tracking seems to be more parallel to what I used to get from my Fitbit. The other smart watches were always really low in my step count which frustrated me. It tracks heart rate and stress levels. You can track fitness routines. The messaging feature is good, but I find it a little more difficult to reply to texts than my other watches. It gives you some quick replies, but I don't like the choices as much as the other ones. Also, I find it more difficult to customize my text replies with the actual typing. Overall, I do like this more than the other ones.

text: Update: 8/21/2020- so the battery has been draining VERY quickly the last few weeks. It charges to 100% but then by 4 hours it's at a 43% charges with it just being on my wrist with nothing really running. I've reset the watch, made sure it has the latest updates and turned off a lot of the necessary bloat but no luck. Not sure what to do with it at this time. 6/21/2020: Arrived without a scratch on the watch or band. Charger and extra watch band was also included. Definitely like new. I do have a skinny wrist and I've had a 42mm smartwatch prior (which to me was the perfect size) so putting on a 40mm made it seem "small" even on my skinny wrist. But I found that adding a watch cover "bulked it" up just enough for me so I'm happy! I cannot stand any of the Samsung related health apps. Honestly I'm only using this watch for running so Im only using the UA app and cell phone-less usage of music. A note but you need to disconnect the phone from the watch so that the watch is operating on its own IF you are wanting to use the watch for music. I run without my phone and didn't realize that if you don't disconnect the watch from the phone (you can do this via the app on the phone), the watch thinks it's still tethered to the phone and the music will play to the extent that the connection to the phone lasts. title: Good Watch, Poor Battery
text: Very nice watch. The screen is very responsive, moves fluidly. App selection is nice. This is my first smart watch. I primarily wanted a smart watch with lots of app options, this has them all. Lots of options and it syncs nicely with all my Samsung apps on my S9+. The battery on the first day lasted a mere 5 hours from 100% (initial charge) to 8%. However, this was spent doing initial setup, watch software updates, browsing through many, many apps, using the browser and pretty much continuously using the watch. I suspect that over time as I only use it for time and notifications I'll get more life out of it. There are 3 battery modes: default, power saving, and watch only. These would have extended my 8% battery time from 2hr to 8hr, and watch only: 3days, according to the watches estimate. So if you're crunched for battery life, you can extend it using these methods. My initial impressions are good. I also did 2 small workouts and they seemed to track well. I'm not looking for medical grade accuracy, just to compare my heart rate resting and to workout. I also wanted to keep track of my steps while I didn't have my phone on me. This works perfectly for this. I'll edit and update my review over time as this is an initial impression review.

text: I put off getting one because its not really a "need" but im so glad I caved and got it. It works like a charm. I can wear it in the shower or at the gym and always know whats going on so I don't have to look at my phone as much. No downside.

title: Smart Watch for Seniors
text: Product does what it was designed, for the price. Perfect starter watch for seniors (HR) or smart watch beginners.

title: Atrocious battery life, mediocre performance
text: You would be lucky to get an hour out if this. I bought it for running (it has Spotify offline so I don't need to bring my phone): With MapmyRun, Spotify, and my Bluetooth headphones in, I can get two 30 min runs out of it. Do NOT buy if you're planning to do any excercise for more than an hour. The device itself is also pretty sluggish. Not terrible given its mostly single purpose for me, but the experience wasn't great as a watch in general. But mostly I am just confused as to why Samsung released a product aimed at activity and included such a weak battery.

title: Just stopped charging one day.
text: One day the work wouldn't turn on or charge, using chargers that had worked previously. It stopped working past the return due date so now I just have a dead watch that I can't return.

title: This is the best value for the money
text: Love everything about this watch. Bought 2 Fitbit Versa watches and sent those back for horrible bluetooth for music. These are excellent and flawless. Love the sleep tracker, step tracker, heartbeat monitor, stress tracker, and music player! Battery life is not as bad as I thought reading reviews. Just charge it for an hour or two a day and it's good to go. Would be nice if it lasted longer, but everything else about the watch is perfect!

title: This watch is great for those who are active and those who aren't
text: I'm a generally active person-- I swim and run on the treadmill. My old watch (a Ticwatch Pro) doesn't hold a candle to this watch. No watch is more precise when swimming, it accurately depicts my current workouts without any input from me, and it reminds me to be a bit active when I've been sitting a while. Plus, notifications are great, and it works with my Galaxy S10 perfectly. The battery lasts 2 to 3 days and charges in an hour or two. I would recommend this watch to any android user, especially at the price point it's currently at.

title: Warranty does not cover the damage to my watch
text: My watched stopped working after 10 months. They denied to repair it under the warranty, because it is an international product!!!.

title: The good, the bad, and the obviously wrong
text: I bought the Galaxy Active for two reasons: my Withings HR Steel was undercounting my calories burned, and I wanted to cycle and run without my phone. I really dislike square watches (Apple Watch and most fitness trackers), and I hate bulky watches (all Android watches and the rest of the Samsung line up). The Active looks great, especially when you replace the band for something nicer, and it is feature packed. Not as many apps as the Apple Watch or even Wear OS, but certainly has a functional app store that covers most of the bases. Unfortunately this watch has glaring flaws. While my HR Steel was under counting my calories, the Active is all over the place. Sometimes it will track 600 calories for a brisk 4 mile walk, other times the exact same route will track 350 (more in line with reality but still off), however it seems to be pretty accurate with cycling calories (6 mile cycle at about 300 calories). The worst part about the watch is Spotify. It works fine for songs, but it is horrible for podcasts. The watch just refuses to download full episodes no matter how long I wait. It is infuriating for audio to cut off at 30 minutes or 40 minutes in a one hour long podcast that I chose for my run. In fact this problem is so frustrating that I am planning on returning the watch. I clear downloads after every run, I have plenty of space available, wifi turned on a fast connection, but the app will not download the full episode EVER. Regardless of podcast length and file size, it will only bring 50-80% of the content.

title: Stylish easy to use and reliable!
text: The Samsung Galaxy smartphone watch is the most reliable for notifications and activity. I love the feature that detects a workout. That reminds me to track specific activities. Step counter and heart rate monitoring are excellent and accurate. Easy to use for first time smart watch users.

title: Good except the battery life is horrible
text: I was worried at first but the step counter is fairly accurate to other devices, apps such as facebook or messenger alert on the watch but open on your phone, you can open, read, and reply to texts on the watch itself... it's pretty incredible except the battery life doesn't even last a full 10 hours which is what I needed since I'm in surgery for a majority of that time. Really bummed they advertise a few days of battery when you're lucky to get even a few hours. I got this because I needed the battery life as I work in surgery and cannot take my phone out.

title: Complicated
text: Very complicated to use. The responsiveness of the tough screen and where you go when swiped is anybody's guess. A highly magnified screen occasionally appears and the only way I've found to get rid of it is to re-boot the watch. Battery life is the worst I've ever encountered from any electronic product. Typically has to be charged every morning and every evening under normal use. Accuracy is questionable. I have a two story house and it never shows the number of stairs climbed. I guess I am comatose as my heart rate is so slow I must be. Steps taken are questionable. I've taken the exact same route to a designated spot and so far the number is steps taken varies by several hundred. Big negative is no blood pressure measurement. Sleep history shows I've had a good night's sleep only 6% of the time. I wake up 20 to 50 times a night and have deep sleep for just 1 or 2 minutes a night. According to this tracker I'm on the verge of death. The only redeeming factor is the watch faces. Either the built in ones or customize your own. Disappointed as I've always trusted Samsung and their products.

title: Great Watch
text: Bought this for my daughter for her birthday. She has been wanting a watch to track her steps and have a watch. We are a Samsung family and she deserved a great gift. Having a Samsung S2 watch, I knew of several ways to save battery life and to set up the watch. Battery Life: So far she is hitting about 60% by the end of the day as she uses. I have the screen brightness set to 5 or 6. I also taught her how to turn on and off the "Wake up gesture" which can activate while walking, running, or moving around, which can drain the battery life. Set Up: Unfortunately, that took a little bit longer than I had planned. However, that was my fault, not the watches. I simply pulled it out, turned it on, and then worked on connecting it to my daughter's Samsung Note 8. I did not pull out the directions or even look at them. Even still, I knew the basis of what needed to be done. I muddled through it and had it connected in about 10 minutes. (Probably could have cut that in half if I had looked at the directions) The rest dealt with Samsung Health. After getting an account set up for my daughter, the watch seamlessly integrated with the phone with no issues. Overall: I am happy with the watch and most importantly, my daughter loves it. I prefer the turning dial on the S2 so, if I were to get a new watch now, it would be the Samsung Watch 42mm version because the Samsung Watch Active does not have that satisfying, turning, dial on the face.

title: Good price and good unit
text: Have the original galaxy gear and it still works this unit definitely is worth the purchase if your are just looking for simplicity such as health ,sleep,heart,and apps.

title: Zero stars

title: It's a great device, but software is very buggy
text: Basic time, weather and notifications - that's all that is working reliably. It's like 10% of what is really advertised. Half of the times the watch itself cannot remember WiFi Connection, doesn't connect to your WiFi by default, you have to always click Connect to point manually. That leads to a lot of problems with apps like Strava and Spotify that need connection. They just don't sync! Applications won't install. There's always trouble when you switch phones. You manage your watch with Samsung Galaxy App on iOS. It often doesn't work as a connection provider either. The app says the Watch is connected, the watch says it's connected but there's no Internet on the Watch. So more problems with Strava, Spotify and all apps that need Internet connection. Samsung Health syncs 50% of the time. It says "No wearables detected". The only thing that Samsung Support recommended is restarting Watch, Bluetooth and iPhone. Really? It never helped. Bixby voice assistant works but often fails. Exactly when you need it it's not available - endless spinning logo. When new update comes out Watch looses Bluetooth connection with iPhone. So you have to reset the watch and reinstall EVERYTHING from scratch. All the software, apps, all the settings - Samsung Wear application cannot remember and transfer them. I wear this for months and software updates never fixed anything. If this is "Samsung quality" I'm out! Will never buy anything from that company again. Ever.

title: A clean-looking watch, but features are disappointing

Comes with wireless charging pad and an extra-long watchband for those who cannot fit into the basic watchband. Includes a heart rate monitor which is helpful, though not as accurate as a real medical instrument. Cons: Instructions are not very detailed; to use various special functions, one needs to study and research answers online and do lots of trial-and-error. Battery life is about 12 hours. It does have a Power-Saving setting which much extends the battery time, but then the watch face is dimmed and monochrome (no colors).

title: Watch is great but only work for a year

title: A thin functional watch with smart features
text: I bought this because it's relatively smaller/thinner plus it offers heart rate and blood pressure tracking (BP comes later). I also like gadgets. I play with the watch a lot so I'm only getting 36 hours on the battery (plan on charging daily). It's thin and fits under my dress shirt cuff. I've worn this for a few days 24/7 (including, to bed, as well as the shower & gym). It's very comfortable (no itching or rubbing) and performs well. The heart rate tracker is pretty accurate (give it time to adapt to changes in activity) and compares to the heart rate readings I get from the machines in the gym. I was doing my income tax on Sunday and the watch detected and notified me that I was stressed - and offered to walk me through deep breathing exercises (clever). I like that I can set the notification feature to only allow texts to show on the watch. If it's important I'll respond on my phone (not the watch). And I like that the notification stops when it detects me sleeping (so it doesn't wake me up). The only difficulty I had was: after setting up the watch and updating the software I had to 'reset' the watch in order to get the wake up feature to function. The Samsung web site chat/help box was very helpful. It comes with two straps. The longer strap is encased in a form fitting cover that fits so well you may not realize there's a strap inside. It's easy to change straps.

title: Nice Watch

title: Samsung Galaxy sport

title: Great watch, terrible battery life

title: Love this watch

They said this is because the damage was caused by water intrusion, even though there was only water intrusion in this case was due to a manufacturing defect! So be warned, the watch is "waterproof" but if the one you get isn't it's not Samsung's fault and they wont pay for it!

title: Warranty Repair
text: Watch is well within the warranty period at 8 months old. Love the watch. Well, until today when the magnetic charger pulled the quarter size plate off the back of the watch. Warranty repair is a nightmare. Instead of just sending me the miniscule grommet they use to attach the back plate to the watch, they want the watch mailed in to repair. No time line for repair and return. Unacceptable. Perfectly good watch gone for how long? BTW, the first question that the service rep at 1800samsung asked when I indicated the plate had come off was "did it happen while you were falling". Please, even if I fell off a cliff, the back plate is between my arm and the watch and it wouldn't have come off. Part of the reason to send it in is so "we can examine the watch and make sure it wasn't mishandled to cause the damage." Ok, I get that. But if was actually broken, sending me the grommet would not fix it. I asked to talk to a supervisor who connected me to Samsung Parts, unbeknown to me so I could buy the part! Which of course, Samsung Parts didn't have, as they don't stock parts for watches! So I asked where the repair department gets parts. "Well, they have them". OK, so why can't they send me the part. "That's not how it works. You have to send the watch in". I asked the supervisor to think outside the box and contact the repair shop and just ask if they would send it. Nope, no can do. This sounds like a short discussion, but with the interminable hold times, took 2 hours. I asked to talk to her supervisor, and hung up the phone after being on hold for 30 minutes. So for the price of a small grommet and some forward thinking, I will never buy another Samsung watch or phone. Who needs this kind of hassle? My guess is if I just superglue it back on, it won't be waterproof and it will probably void the warranty. I guess I don't care as the warranty is not doing me any good. BTW, I did not buy this on Amazon, impulse buy at COSTCO. So Amazon will not show me as a verified buyer. But is registered with Samsung.

title: Super cute and incredibly convenient

Sometimes I want to skip the song that's playing on my Bluetooth so I have to move positions or just listen to the song I don't care for. With this watch I can check my messages, see who's calling, and skip or turn up a song without moving positions! It's also waterproof so I don't have to worry about water from my job or sweat messing up my watch. Thanks! Great price and definitely made my job more toleratable

title: Great app: Sleep, steps, stress tracking!
text: [[VIDEOID:62d754a7ac76cfb6104dd7271d16b4ce]] I bought a watch that looked pretty much the same as this one after hours of sifting through reviews for similar ones and it was absolute garbage. After returning it, this one was my last hope to find an affordable option that included sleep tracking and I am so glad I tried again!! I honestly just wanted the step counting to work and had a very minor hope that the sleep tracking would be semi-accurate but I was beyond excited to find that ALL of the functions work exceptionally well and sync with my phone effortlessly!! It helps me so much to track my sleep and stress so I can actually fix it and make better habits or at least know why I feel crummy. The pedometer works wonderfully and I've compared it to my coworkers apple watches and it seems very similar. I didn't even know what an apple watch looked like before but people have mistaken this watch for one many times so if that's something you care about it's a bonus! It charges lightning fast and I keep it on all the time just alternating wrists and positions to let my skin breathe. I've had it on working 50hrs a week for about 4 months in the restaurant industry (10,000-25,000 steps a day) and I've washed my hands with it on and smashed it against things and it's still good as new! I don't know when I'll ever have to replace it since it seems very durable and reliable, but if I'm ever in the market for a new watch again I will DEFINITELY be getting this one!

title: Awesome device bye fitit

I would really like to have some more watch bands maybe turquoise or white or beige with some gold flick

title: Too big
text: The watch that does too much? In the drive to be all things to all people, this watch is simply too complicated. But that's not the fatal flaw. The size is simply too huge. title: Returned. Not enough features.

title: Best in line of fitness trackers with expensive look

The resulting training status and recommendations end up being wrong and misleading. I don't understand how a serious company can sell such a bad product.

title: Happy with the Fenix 6 Pro Solar
text: I have had Garmin watches for the past 15 years. This is the best one yet. It measures everything and can be tailored. I am glad I did not get the 6X, as this one looks plenty large on my narrow wrists. The band is quality rubber. I added a Road ID to it. Plenty of data.

title: It is not touchscreen
text: I’m still finding new things this watch can do. Guess I should’ve read the instructions more thoroughly. Mainly use for working out and travel. The color works with just about everything.

title: Nice smartwatch, completely happy with my purchase
text: I did pass for Montblanc Summit, Casio Amazfit T-Rex Pro and GTR2 and definitely Garmin will be my only and last smartwatch, 100% recommended

title: Does not connect to apple rings
text: My review is more about the Garmin watch software than about the watch itself. Garmin is great at creating hardware. The watch functionality is not up to speed for what technology is out there right now. If you would have put this watch on my wrist without telling me what year it was created, I would have guessed it was from 2013. For as expensive as this watch is, it really lacks in in functionality. The screen clarity and color is not at all like in the advertisement. The watch is not touch screen. The only way to record a weight lifting activity is to configure each workout and set with number of reps in the Garmin app before your workout. It is supposed to automatically track your reps, but this feature barely works. Even with an exercise of moving your arms it is not accurate at all. I didn’t keep this watch long enough to do any long runs outside, but from what I’ve read there are connection issues. Sure this watch has lots of data tracking, but their ability to visualize the data for the user is subpar at best. Apple has really mastered this, as well as the apps like strava that work with it. With Garmin, I cannot get most data to flow into apple health. It is frustrating that I cannot share my data with my friends who have apple watches anymore. Using this watch requires more work and set up to get the data you want than it’s really worth. With so much potential, it is disappointing to see how much Garmin missed the mark. Returned and went back to Apple.

title: I am a bit disappointed
text: I have wanted to upgrade to this watch since it came out. I have a Garmin 3HR that I have been wearing for several years and decided I needed to upgrade. So, I did. So, to make this short but effective, here are my thoughts. Pros: The watch face is amazing. The added information that the 6X offers over the 3HR is much better and easier to access. The overall size of the 6X is NOT significantly bigger than the 3HR as many have noted, but the readable screen is larger. The GPS is spot on and I consider the maps and GPS to be excellent. Cons: Price. (we all know this). The wrist heart rate readings are not at all accurate and are inconsistent. My experience was that while walking on a flat surface, the reading went suddenly to high aerobic (green zone) from low (grey zone) withing 10 feet. With this in mind I went for a moderately strenuous hike and wore a chest HRM. After hiking for 2 miles the watch sent a message saying that an external HRM had been connected. Really? 2 miles later? The bottom line is that a$800.00 watch should not be this glitchy. The 6X has been out long enough to have worked the bugs out. At this point, I have enough time to send it back, but I will wait a little longer. I am very disappointed in Garmin.

title: Quality watch
text: Bought the watch as a Christmas present for myself and have been using it for just a few weeks now. Overall I am quite impressed with the watch. It is very accurate in terms of the GPS and other measurements. One of the things that I really like is that when I am exercising in the gym none of the features gets inadvertently activated like what happens with my Apple Watch. Other than the price, the one small issue that I have with it is that the watch face background only comes in black or white whereas I wish there were other colors. Apart from that I am satisfied with the purchase.

title: Best Garmin I’ve purchased.
text: There’s no review I could write that is any better than DC Rainmakers reviews so I’m not going to try. However, this is by far the best Garmin I have ever had. I’ve used the Forerunner - 305, 310xt, 920xt and this one is multiple levels above all of those. Definitely read the book on this one as there are a lot of features you won’t know about if you don’t.

title: Awesome, high quality, high function watch
text: This watch - and the apps that go with it are outstanding. First the watch. The build of the watch is very high quality and rugged. Next the features - there are so many features it can be overwhelming to start with. You can find provided widgets and apps that cover any sort of activities you can think of. The data that you get helps you understand your workouts better and can drive you to more workouts and more accomplishments. The data is uploaded to an app where it is even more easily understood, with daily, weekly and longer summaries and graphs, and to a webpage where you can more easily edit how the screen works for you. The amount of technology packed into this watch, and the ability to tailor it to your activities is just amazing. Also amazing is the battery life and the charge time. The battery will las well over a week, and charge time I think is around an hour from near full depletion. I wish my phone had anywhere near this life and charge time.

title: Forces automatic updates, HR indicator inaccurate, GPS is lost.
text: Literally no one in the history of ever likes automatic forced updates. So please Garmin, Windows, et all stop it I'm just sitting here and my heartrate fluctuates between 65 and 75. GPS has no idea where I am. =========================================================== Update 10/26/2022 I was a little unfair in the first review. The heartrate monitor isn't quite as accurate as others. I somewhat wish I held out for the Fenix 7 with chest strap. The GPS signal isn't very strong, so it's lost sometimes indoors or under heavy tree cover. I think this is understandable given it's a watch and probably more likely used as a backup gps than a navigation unit. I actually used the gps a few days ago because the trail was poorly marked and I forgot my phone so in that regard I'd say it served its purpose. Forced updates are still annoying though but I'm the type of person that if something breaks, I want to be able to blame myself not other things. Some people may appreciate it.

title: I expected a little more than straight up utility, but there is where it wins big.
text: Overall this is an excellent watch... Functionally. I was expecting a lack luster display, but it still was a bit of a gut punch paying for premium quality in this day in age. Screen is reminiscent of a 2009 cell phone instead of a 2021 watch. Still the watch looks decent indoors with retro illumination just not in backlit or outside. My old ANT+ HR monitor paired flawlessly and loaded up songs and golf courses with ease. I also paired my Soundcore earbuds without issue and can play pause and increase volume on the buds. I have only had the watch for a day but the level of customization is excellent and the number of sensors/accessories it supports is awesome. The sleep tracking, "body battery", ect I see as gimmicky. The charger is a travesty. It is a fairly large, proprietary plug that sticks into the back of the watch. The included cord is too short to be useful in a way that makes me think they want to sell you a longer one. You have to tilt the watch awkwardly on its side to charge it or let it rest on its face, which makes it feel like an afterthought rather than a well thought out, engineered, polished device. I mean for this being the 6th iteration in the fenix series and having many other series under their belt I guess I expected a little more than straight up utility, but there is where it wins big.

title: Everything fine except battery life.
text: I have owned the Garmin Instinct for two years and it gets a full 2 weeks on a charge with my routine indoor workouts (no GPS). This Fenix has the same battery rating but does not go near as long as my Instinct with identical usage. At best 8-10 days. Either the claims are overrated or I got a defective or old watch that has sat on a shelf for 3 years!

title: LOVING IT!
text: I have had a Garmin Fenix 3 HR since the first days it was released and have worn it daily. I have never had an issue, I am a gadget freak and this is my most reliable gadget. Always worked, GPS very reliable, etc. It was still in perfect condition and working order, but decided to upgrade to the 6x Sapphire and am glad I did. Screen resolution is better, battery staggeringly long, heart rate/sleep tracking is improved, maps, spotify offline, etc. Amazing product. Get one, you will not regret it. Get the 6x as well, not the 6 pro. I returned the pro to get the 6x (which is the same size as the HR) - the extra screen real-estate is huge (as well as memory.)

title: The Fenix 6X Pro Solar is a really amazing device-- or not, updated 11/30/21
text: I find the features pretty amazing, especially all of the feedback data I receive. It's really motivating to have that real time data on your runs. However, I primarily chose this device because I'm training toward running ultras and wanted to have the best battery life and the best tracking capabilities on trail runs. Also using it for cycling and kayaking. Haven't quite figured out how to make the most of it in the gym for strength training but I'm still very happy with it. UPDATE: After nearly two years, I do not recommend this device nor the brand. Most of the sensors stopped working within a few weeks and I was never able to discover out how to get ahold of Garmin to return it or get it repaired. I wanted to get readings for pace, elevation, cadence, blood O2, steps, etc. But I get either inaccurate or nil readings. The pace reading is spotty as the GPS drops out frequently. Given the cost, I'm not going to dump it and in this condition I can't sell it. I've lived with it as is and got a HR monitor to go across my chest. It's really a $200 watch that cost me $1000.

title: Don’t Rely on the HR Monitor
text: Love the look and and feel like it’s pretty intuitive. The screen is easy to read and has all of the data I need for running and hiking. One warning: do not rely on the heart rate monitor, especially in the cold. At rest, it seems ok, but as soon as I start running, it spikes and seems to report 20-30 BPM over my HR strap. I know most wrist based HR monitors are less accurate, but this is way off. If HR is important to you, spend a few more bucks and get a strap. Everything else on the watch is great.

title: 6x pro dollar
text: Love the 6x solar , bought to replace my 6 pro , size is great , I can see everything, especially useful hiking / using maps . Comfortable. No complaints

title: Difficult pair with iPhone XR
text: Difficult pair with iPhone XR Blue tooth. Need pair mutable times every day. so frustrating. find same problem reviews here, If you have iPhone XR, Don't buy it.

title: Addicted to Garmin
text: I took the plunge and bought the most recent holy grail from Garmin. I love it and especially the lightweight titanium. I look at these purchases as an investment in health since I'm always working out outdoors and skip the gym membership. I actually use the suggested daily workout and can see how effective it is w/r to improving fitness. I like the larger screen. I use the topo in the Rockies quite often while on trail and it's useful for tracking route when it's covered in snow.

title: Overall, great watch for fitness/activity tracking; had the awful Vivosport for a couple of weeks.
text: I had the Vivosport... it was awful. Upgraded to this watch and it is way more accurate. The Vivosport shouldn't even exist IMO. I had auto-exercise recognition enabled and it was constantly turning on due to the inaccuracy of the sensors... shame on Garmin for even putting the product out. Nothing about it is accurate. Not an issue with the Fenix 6 Sapphire Ti. The Fenix 6 Sapphire Ti edi works great overall, looks great in casual and professional dress. I appreciate the included Ti band and flat-headed screw-driver to adjust the band. I've owned Apple watches in the past, I prefer the Fenix 6 because of the reflective display (don't care for OLED burnin on Apple watches and 2 year obsolescence... Fenix watches last about 6 years give or take). The Fenix 6 watches offer way more sensors than the iWatch while the iWatch is more of an iPhone extension... didn't really need that for my usage case... fitness and overall health is my priority... the iWatch doesn't even offer an oxygen saturation sensor... the EKG feature on the iWatch is far from accurate unfortunately but like that Apple is pushing towards an overall health/well-being focus. The Fenix 6 Sapphire Ti option includes the Ti band and silicone bands... good stuff. Aesthetically, I like the two tone design of the Ti version... I refuse to purchase the DLC option... Ti will patina and be less obvious with wear and tear over time on the bezel. DLC will have high-contrast scratches since it has a coating on it that is different than the raw metal. I debated between this watch and the Tactix Delta Solar (sapphire glass). I went with the Fenix 6 Sapphire Ti due to aging more gracefully, more practical size for my usage, looks great in professional attire, and lighter weight.

title: Upgrade worth extra cost
text: I’ve been a Garmin wearer for many years. Glad I upgraded to Fenix 6s. Lots of features and battery life is excellent.

title: Great rugged watch
text: I have small wrists and still went with the 6X and glad I did. The watch is big but comfortable. I wanted the 6X for more horsepower and battery. I don't regret my decision at all. The Garmin Connect app is a breeze to work with.

title: Great multi-sport watch
text: I've been running for over 40 years and have owned 7 of the Forerunner models, from the 100 series to the 945. While the 945 is a great watch, this one appears to be even better. Compared to the 945, the screen is more scratch resistant and the display seems to have more vibrant color. In terms of size the 6S weighs a few grams more than the 945 and the 6S is a bit thicker. Not really noticeable once you're wearing it. I haven't had it long enough to assess battery life.

title: Totally buggy, typical garmin
text: This thing is so buggy it is unreal. I own a number of garmin products and I'm pretty close to abandons garmin completely. It is inconsistent, data doesn't feed into garmin connect, the watch rarely gives a hr over 82 even if my heart rate is 160. Won't send respiration or spo2 data to garmin connect. Garmin needs hire some software developers who know what they are doing instead of hacking different things together.

title: I like it a lot but in accurate optiocal HRM
text: I overall like the watch. It's a bit substantial on the wrist but also quite good looking in a subdued way IMO. The biggest issue for me that the optical HRM is quite inaccurate compared to others watches I have (e.g. Garmin VivoActive3 Music). To get accurate heart rate I really need a strap (the HRM PRO which also has running dynamics) further adding to the already high price point. Fortunately I already had the latter strap. I like the button press User Interface (UI) much better than the touch UI of others. However since the watch has so much functionality ironically results in the UI being complex, the paths through the UI to many of the controls are often long and not obvious. Of course you can look at the user manual to find the sequence of button presses but that is not practical when you are running. If the price is a problem one could consider the ForeRunner 245 which also has running dynamics. You will lose some function but the latter is a very effective running watch, Again, I recommend the Garmin Pod at least (or better the HRM PRO) for the running dynamics.

title: Great! Lightweight and precise!
text: Everything is as expected with Garmin. My only gripe is that the screen looks faded, the resolution is so 1990....but, it gets the job done.

title: Not a touchscreen. But that's why I like it.
text: Hit this watch on doors frequently and it still looks great. Very sturdy construction. There is definitely a learning curve on figuring out all this watch can do. The app works good, not great, but works. Battery life is phenomenal! will go at least 2.5 weeks on a single charge.

title: Amazing

Also, this is a bigger heavier than the 735XT and I don't think the default band is ideal. Looking for a better band, open to suggestions!

title: Great
text: I have had this product over a year, and I love it. There is some much you can do with it and it does what it needs to very well! Great stuff.

title: Everything a trail runner would want

Love to play music from it, download GPX files onto it and link with Strava. I've dropped it so many times, no scratches or problems. I've taken this on about 100+ miles of runs and I have friends asking me about it. It's amazing. So many features you can download to it. I'd buy again and again.

title: My Upgrade

title: Loving it
text: This watch is awesome! It has a bunch of features and sensors. It syncs with the app nicely + an online dashboard. There's tons of data to comb through. Battery life is 21 days on a full charge and it recharges really fast. Notifications come through from my phone which is more handy than I was expecting. Overall, I love this watch so far!

title: Love it
text: This was the best price I could find. It is fantastic and has lots of features. I love it

title: Best tracking watch ever
text: Bought Fenix 6X pro. Simply, the best tracking/sport watch i ever had. Battery Life is Impressive.

title: One Year Review
text: Have had this watch for about a year and must say that the Sapphire glass is no joke - tough as nails and not visible scratches after a year. Have hiked, climbed, done auto repair, everything with this watch on and holding up great. Get about 9 days battery life with moderate use and without any battery saver on (that makes it longer). Have some alternate leather bands I use at night and switching bands takes literally seconds. Have downloaded multiple faces that I can change on my mood. Have used it for golf and it is really good. Checked accuracy against a laser distance meter and it is spot on +/- a foot or 2. Has pre-loaded courses which makes it easy to keep score with it and hole layout, etc. Use it daily for walks/runs and have it linked to an iPhone and it syncs extremely well allowing messages and notification on the watch. I bought the S version to get a little smaller face so it does not look like a huge on my arm and mostly stays out of the way when doing things like auto repair and other tasks around the house. Expensive but for what it does it remains a good buy in my view.

title: Good
text: Been using if for a 3 months and I love it. Especially the internal gps tracks all my training and. Which they had better bands like my gshock. But doesn't damage easy. I should have gotten the solar but I'm happy with it

title: Awesome watch
text: Love everything about it so far. The comfort and battery life are fantastic. Im pretty ruff on my watches and its holding up just fine.

title: Great watch
text: I am very satisfied with the functions and the battery life. For sure, the best watch for sports and to support your aims in a journey for healthy.

title: Extraordinary
text: This is a great product hands down. It provides lots of information that helps keep track of your health. I wear it all the time, night and day, and use it mainly for bike training. I’m staring to use it for running as well. It has multiple sport activities you can use it for, it is very versatile. And battery life is amazing. It can last up to 14 days without a recharge!

title: Good, but not great, especially at this price
text: This is my second smart watch. My first was a Series 2 from a very popular brand named after a fruit. This watch exceeds that first watch in some ways and comes up short in others. I wear this watch all the time but the main reason I bought it is for tracking workouts and running. Pros: The battery lasts a really, really long time. I've had this watch for almost a month and today is the third time I've charged it. The GPS is highly accurate. The music continues uninterrupted during outdoor runs, and the Bluetooth connectivity with my wireless headphones is always very strong. The interface is easy to see. The heart rate monitor appears very accurate, as does the pedometer. Replacing the metal wristband with the rubber wristband was easy and the rubber one fits my wrist very securely and moves very little while working out. Cons: interface looks and feels outdated; navigating between apps is clunky and difficult. Syncing Spotify playlists takes forever; and the Pulse Ox feature has never worked. Bottom line: There's more good than bad to this watch, but I would not recommend it at this price. I'm content with it and will keep it, but if I could do it again I'd go a different route and save the money.

title: The sports watch that claims to do everything.... And actually, it does.
text: I previously owned the ForeAthlete 45S, and loved it. When I bought it, I said nothing will make me replace this sports watch. I lied. The Fenix 6X Pro is everything I will ever need. I realized the shortcomings with the 45S, but I was able to compensate for them. Not anymore. I am still discovering things about the 6X Pro.

title: Fenix line just keeps getting better.
text: I chose the 6 Pro Sapphire, for the demands I put on my watch when out in the mountains and wilderness. I need something I can count on, especially for training, stats, and navigation. Yes it is expensive, but I haven't found any other watch that can take a beating, and keep me alive. iWatch 6, would be my second choice.

title: Love this Watch!
text: I've now had it for over a year. It's about time I make a review post. Primary Uses: Running, Swimming, Biking Secondary Uses: HR Monitoring, Sleep Tracking Tertiary Use: Finding my Phone Likes: 1 - Does great for all the things I use it for. 2 - Battery life is impressive for how much I use it. 3 - Lots of options for how to use and different watch faces. 4 - Solid GPS tracking 5 - App is helpful for workout recording. 6 - Incredibly scratch resistant. I'm rough on my stuff and still don't have a scratch on it. This is amazing. Haven't Tried: Garmin pay. Music. Could be Better: Slightly larger than my previous watch, which had 50% of the functionality and less accurate GPS and HR monitoring. Summary: I love this watch

title: Amazing
text: This is a review from a suunto owner that switch to Garmin for a change. I can honestly said that I should have change long time ago. Watch is way easier and better the suunto. I haven’t try all the program and settings but the functionality is amazing. The solar power is awesome. For all the Garmin owner I call Garmin to ask them if the installation of the screen protector will affect the solar power, they reply that the watch has been tested with an without screen protector and same result appear. The only thing to be awere is that the screen is completely transparent and not tinted. Amazing watch and glad to be part of the new Garmin family

title: Most awesome
text: Glad I went with the 6x. Got the 6 but then realized with getting older, running races, and navigating the 6x is the way to go. Just bigger and easier to see. One less thing to deal with, see, try to figure out. Watch- show me the way ..... Still getting used to it but totally awesome. It is big and takes a while to get used to but so many features. everyday wearing is fine but if you have to do projects you will want to take it off - just too big and gets in the way. Went from Vivoctive to 6x and a little confusing for the first week it is easy now. just button based and not touchscreen. Map and music downloading takes a little to get used to but like anything, it takes time. No issues on updates, functionality or usage. HR on activities seems a little more accurate with a strap probably due to arm movement, sensor, sweat but that is only minor if you were focused on HR zones during the workout. When I see a high number I just go by does it really feel like I at that BPM or perceived effort? if I do I just adjust. Other than that I just keep running.

title: I give it a mixed review
text: For me, the jury is still out. I have not worn an electronic watch in over 20 years but thought I'd give it a try. I like that it is Garmin and maps are integral and well executed. The watch has more features than anyone can use, although the pdf manual does not provide adequate instructions on all of the capabilities. You just have to play with the watch. I have no idea how long the learning curve is, to learn some of the more esoteric capabilities. What I like least is daytime use, but indoors, provides a very dim display unless you hit the backlight, a nuisance. I could turn gesture on all of the time although I wonder about the battery impact. I have tried all of the onboard faces and a few of the iqConnect faces, with the same issue on all of them. The customizable faces make for a big plus though. Not a lot available for the 6x yet. If it were not for mapping and navigation, I would send this back as it is very slanted to fitness stuff, which I do not need. I will probably grow into this, but I would not recommend it unless you are already accustomed to a fitness watch.

title: Battery life is amazing, Tech equally so
text: I've had this watch since initial release late 2019. I am astonished by the battery life of this watch and its durability. I've banged the watch face along counter edges, mountain rock, fallen hard in gravel and the watch face is a still good as new. Garmin has a fantastic 'Connect' app to show metrics and this watch takes advantage of all of it, showing everything you need on a wide screen. I have shut off battery draining aspects like Pulse Ox and I average 19 days of battery with 24/7 use, including my workouts. When I am not feeling great, I'll turn pulse ox on for overnight use only as needed. My next comment is a 'con' but it's the trade off I understood and accepted before I bought the watch. To get 19+ days on a single battery charge the screen is much darker than you expect in person. Its nothing like the advertising. The IQ app has many nice watch faces that turn your screen into some of the most amazingly fitness detailed screens you will find, or turn into a high end mechanical watch face for meetings or fancier occasions.

title: Powerful watch - wish it were slightly slimmer and had touch screen options
text: I had a Fenix 5s, then switched back to Apple Watch, then decided I missed all the advanced metrics so tried the new Garmin Venu 2S. I loved the Venu's slimmer profile and touchscreen, but decided I wanted advanced metrics on performance and training load, so sprung the extra $300 for the Fenix 6S. I wish I could meld the 2 watches together, but alas... I am a dedicated, slightly obsessive runner (4-6 days/running each week - I'd do more, but I get injured) but not a particularly talented one. So, not winning any races, but I enjoy the challenge of always trying to improve, and I also bike, swim (sometimes), and do yoga several times each week. I tend to "overdo" it so wanted a watch that would help me make better choices. This watch definitely does that - it has been telling me my training load is too focused on moderate-to-high intensity and I need more lower-aerobic runs or bikes to balance out. Pros of 6s: - Awesome advanced metrics on workout load with suggestions on what to do each day to continue to be "productive." - Lactate threshold test (with a chest strap not included) to determine HR zones - Battery life with "always on" display gets 4-5 days even with frequent workouts, music, etc. - sleep tracking metrics - body battery - pretty enough to wear to work with the upgraded watch band - on-watch workouts, routes, maps and navigation (very useful when I run in other cities) - fast and reliable GPS - HR metrics seem legit Cons: - still a bit bulky but comfortable once you get used to it - no touch screen - expensive even with the $150 off original prices

title: Seemingly worse than the previous
text: Had a Garmin VivofitHR that spit the bit after 18 months, and after making sure that I could return this if not satisfied via Amazon Chat, I decided to give the line another shot. I'm a technical trail runner and not a triathlete, so this watch will see outdoor use 12 months a year in all manner of Midwest weather, and the only water would be a shower or a soak in the hot tub lol. I like the design, as a round face seems more like a watch than a tracker, and that's was about it. The band feels like it'll break each time I take it off or put on. The "Side Swipe" feature was being triggered when I would flex my wrist or during random movements. Tried switching it from righty to lefty. Still no good, so I turned that feature off. Now the side button has been triggered numerous times when lifting or sleeping. I've woken up several times to the GPS being triggered while I was tossing or turning, and drained a majority of the battery life. Which brings me to another issue. Two short runs of an hour each on successive days drain the battery from 100% to under 15%, which is ridiculous. The previous Garmin was good for at least 3 solid runs before needing a charge, and this won't go 2 days. This is going back this week, and may try to bag a Fenix 5 on sale at AMZN in the future. GPS was solid, as it's a Garmin after all, but after that, I'm not pleased.

title: It's reliable and I love it
text: I bought this watch in 2019, and I just wanted to drop in and say that it's still going strong, and I'm continually delighted to find more ways to use my watch to improve my life and my fitness. The sleep tracking is about 90% accurate, and the heart rate monitor is about 95% accurate (compared with my pulse oximeter). The battery lasts about 3 days, depending on howany activities I track (e.g., I don't bring m charger when I go out of town to visit family for the weekend, but I do if I'm going hiking or something like that). The mobile app is fine, the only issues I've had with it have been issues with Garmin's servers. That is a downside, data from the watch has to go to Garmim before updating the app. It works perfectly 99.9% of the time, it's only been down twice in the three years I've been using it. The newer model has a more responsive touch screen and some other features that are nice, but I'm delighted with the durability and consistency of this watch. I used to say I'd use it until it breaks, but I'm starting to feel like it never will, and I'm very happy with that. It's been a great complement to and motivator for my active lifestyle goals.
