title: faded display
text: I received the Vivoactive 3 today but I'm already sending it back. I can't speak to the features- but the displays on the screen were so faded that I just couldn't live with the watch. It may have been defective- the watch faces didn't look like what I see online. It was as if the visuals were made out of faded construction paper- and no real black. If this is the way the watch really looks, no way is it worth the money.

title: Five Stars
text: IT HAS EVERYTHING THAT I NEED! AS AN ULTRA RUNNER THE BATTERY LIFE IS EXCEPTIONAL

title: Runners best friend for information
text: Great upgrade from my Garmin 220. I use it every day and night! I'm an avid runner and recommend it to everyone. Paired with Garmin Connect and it will give you any all information you want to know about your runs.

title: This smart watch is awesome
text: I've used quite a few smart watches for my workouts. I started indoor rowing and Garmin was the only watch that had the appropriate features to capture the most from my indoor rowing, without being hooked up to the rower. I also like the strength workout feature where you build a workout and can tap your way through the sets/reps. The mobile app to support the workouts has good detail with which muscles I am working and even volume.

title: I had to change a lot of settings
text: So the battery was awful, until I changed a ton of settings and now we're lasting ~5 days. Garmin has never been the best sleep tracker, but this watch does as well as Garmin can do. Where Garmin does best is activity tracking, which is really what I want it for. I LOVE the ability to choose your watch face, I needed a second hand on an analog clock and military time somewhere on the face and was able to find that without too much trouble.

title: Good Watch, Long Battery Life
text: I bought the Samsung Gear S2 Classic renewed, about a month before I bought this Garmin watch (received it Dec. 12), but the S2 needed charging twice - sometimes more - per day. I love the look of the Gear S2, but it has to go. It's annoying to have it die while I'm out and about or when I have to charge it twice while at work. This Garmin watch is much better. I do not have to charge it every day. It did freeze yesterday and refused to respond to touch or charging. I left it at home, and when I came back from work (8:00-7pm), it vibrated when I picked it up and the battery was at 0%. Weird. The night before, it was at 97%. Anyway, I charged it, wore it to bed, and now at 10:40AM, it's at 93%. All the monitors/counters seem accurate. The sleep monitor, however, is a bit off. I think it calculates your sleep based on heartrate and movement. It says I'm asleep before I get into bed sometimes, or if I'm in bed relaxing and watching YouTube. Also, I think that as soon as you open up the App, it says you're awake (obviously), but it will not count any sleep after that if it's less than three hours. It didn't register my two-hour naps either. I do like the watch, and I will keep it. I hope it doesn't freeze and stop working again.

title: Not Impressed
text: The watch comes with sad default watch faces. The Garmin IQ app is full of apps but the Apps don’t work! Contact support and they say its the 3rd party apps in a round about way. Many people in the support forums have the same issues. Many asking questions nobody answering them. Support leaves a lot top be desired. This is my 1st Garmin will probably be my last.

title: Poor watch - does not work for me., I HATE it. Update: HATE worse than ever...
text: UPDATE: No way to DISABLE the MOVE alert!!! Absolutely no way! Garmin support told me I should apprec8iate it! Told them they were a bunch of kid-Snowflakes and the only Garmin products i like are GPS Nav items. Watch is pure S**T in my view. Notwithstanding my wife's giving me this as a present, it's going on my bureau and I will take back my 1440 Timex. Original review follows: (It won't show as 'verified purchase' because my wife got it on her Amazon account as a gift for me...but I am still writing this review. Watch is very poor. Does not work with my iPhone 8, no sync with - well - anything. GPS doesn't work. Can't figure how to get it from continually telling me to "MOVE'. Poor product. Could not recommend. Won't set time when crossing time zones. (Must set manually!) NOTHING I can find to recommend it. Actually it is pure crap and I would NEVER recommend it. Worst Garmin experience and I have been a user of GPSs for many, many years. How do i turn the MOVE vibrator off? What a stupid item!

title: Promising. but constant resetting and now a rash
text: I've had the VivoActive 3 for 10 months, daily wear. Predominant sport is swimming. The VA 3 is better than many prior versions, but still not there. An aggravation is that it constantly drops settings, everything from the style of the watch dial to each and every widget. Would still have been 4 stars, except that eight months into it I started developing a recurring, itchy rash under the watch face (see photo). Over-the-counter cortisone cream (and not wearing the watch) fixes it, but rash returns the minute the watch does. I've never had a metal allergy reaction in my long life, and keep the watch back clean, so this is irritating (literally and metaphorically). On to next smart watch.

title: Great watch. Full Stop, a great wearable
text: This is really an impressive little watch. My first wearable, was a much larger, less sophisticated unit. Although my first wearable is still being sold. this watch is a combination of a good accelerometer, really good battery, and some great software.the most amazing part, this watch was able to differentiate between a pull up and a muscle up movement. That is some smart accelerometer design. The watch even correctly guessed my way to within one tenth of a pound. This is one heck of a good fitness watch, it really just does so much.

title: So Far so Good
text: Received the watch yesterday and chose NOT to pair with my phone and instead will just sync with my computer...which is a great option that many smart phones don't allow (as they require syncing) Maybe i will later but for right now, no thanks. The watch was easy to set up and looks great. i have the Analog face (even though its digital) and that gives it some elegance. The back light isn't great (nor was it on my tomtom that i'm replacing, but the sleek design and look are huge positives. when it was trying to locate satellites it kept flashing from underneath the watch face so i may want to take this off to call satellites when running. since i chose to get digital time from the satellite, i wonder if it will periodically space through my wrist. hmm don't like that so we'll see. i'll take it out for a run and update after....but so far so good.

title: Do not waste your money & time!
text: [[VIDEOID:1ce3edb76ffb3a80323446874b8f84bd]] This listing appears to ship units that were previously returned by customers and (poorly) repackaged as new! Received a unit in a box that appeared to be scratched a bit. Did not pay attention the first time. Started using it. The battery drains quickly and does not hold even two days of charge. Very light usage with backlight disabled! Watch faces freeze and need the unit to be power cycled for it to work again. Requested a replacement. The replacement unit came in a box that showed even more signs of wear and the unit did not even have the protective film on the screen. And to top it all - the unit does not even power up!!! It stays stuck at the blue triangle Garmin logo until the battery is completely discharged!!! Been a loyal Garmin customer for several years now and will need to find another brand this time! Even more disappointed with Amazon!

title: Not too big, good battery life
text: If you want a sports smartwatch that isn't too big for your wrist, this is a great option. Another great feature is that the battery life is more than one day. The only drawback from my perspective so far is that navigating the options (although somewhat easy for simple/intermediate things) is not so easy for more advanced things - including personal configurations. Also tough in my perspective is using the phone app - it isn't super intuitive and clumsy at first in my opinion. Once you get through the initial specific desires, the watch does seem quite complete in terms of features.

title: Easy to use watch optimized for Fitness Tracking
text: This is a replacement for a first generation Vivoactive that I recently broke. (It worked for about 5 years) and would still be functioning had I not dropped the watch face on concrete, and as it had no protection, it broke. This has more functionality and is easier to use - I am much more of a cyclist than a runner, but it seems to track that well enough (And better than the first Generation). Scrolling through it is easy and largely intuitive. In some ways its easier to use than the current generation of Apple watches, which my wife just got. While its more flexible, to see the weather on an Apple requires you to go to the app screen, scroll through them to get to the weather app - and this you just scroll the main screen. This watch does an excellent job tracking fitness activities, and as you can easily change the watch faces (And if you are using a TPU watch protector they can be had in multiple colours) so you can use this watch for everything from dress to daily activities.

title: Great value fitness watch with GPS
text: The Garmin Connect app is fantastic and, for general use as a GPS tracker, this Vivoactive is a great value. You get what you pay for though, and this is no Apple Watch. Garmin will occasionally break their app, and, although the GPS was extremely accurate for almost two years, a recent update caused the GPS to have a lot more variability (that is, it suddenly, inexplicably, was off by over a mile after the change to daylight savings time this year -- prior to that it recorded accurately within feet on the same ride for over a year). However, in general, it functions well and has a great battery life. The number of features you get for the price, and with a really stellar app, the value is hard to beat. The app connects with others such as MyFitnessPal, Strava, Virgin Pulse, etc. so you can get a great range of fitness and calorie tracking with shared data.

title: Garmin is synonymous with quality GPS.
text: Bought this for my husband for Christmas. It is probably "too much" watch for him, but it's got a lot of helpful features, besides step count and heart rate. Look carefully at the description and decide whether you need something with a LOT of bells and whistles. I cycle, so I USE the GPS. My husband doesn't. There's a less expensive ($25) watch by Letscom that works well for basic information.

title: Very excellent product as Garmin do fir all its products
text: Garmin product Nithing more to say that it is a very excellent product

title: Love it
text: Great running watch. The only thing I do not like is the battery life. I think it's just the smart watch function chews up a lot of battery life. Still a great watch my favorite garmin yet...

title: Face colors are not as shown in the marketing pictures.
text: Have had Fitbit for several years and I thought that I'd try a Garmin since it had all the capabilities as the Fitbit. The Fitbit, although rated for swimming crashed and burned the first time I went in the water with it. Concerning the Garmin, what a disappointment. Mainly purchased it because the water rating seems more definitive than the Fitbit. The colors on the Garmin watch face are various shades of grey. Not the vibrant colors depicted in the pictures. Black is not an option. The optional faces that can be downloaded have a charge for them if they are not Garmin.

title: Overall Great watch
text: Tracks all my activity, and the type of activity I engaged in. Tracks my pulse, and provides me with alerts and messages from my phone. I elected not to activate the phone call connection.

title: Get a model with buttons instead
text: Overall I like this much better than any of the Fitbits I have owned, but if I had to do it over again, I would get one of the models with buttons rather than the touch screen. Long sleeves reek havoc with the touch screen, and for the most part apps don't recognize touching specific spots, you get basic swipes and a general tap. The one screen that does have specific hot spots to touch doesn't work very well.

title: I'm so over this watch...
text: Bad. When I first got the watch I had high hopes. Unfortunately for me I was in la la land. For the record Garmin does not count stairs, the blogs are full of people trying to divine the Garmin algorithm (alltitude, must be over 12 feet per flight, hand must be in motion (no railing)) on and on. Some people run up and down multiple flights and end up with 1 flight measured In my year I never got more than 1 per day up, never a down, and I live in a 3 level home. One apologist offered up that standard American home flight were either no high enough or the angle to gradual. Garmin support thought maybe the air holes are clogged. But enough on flights, sleep measurements are laughable. Sometimes they don't register at all, other times 2 hours or 4. You can edit the start and stop and usually gain some sleep data but its never enough to be real. After the first month, I stopped looking at it. You do get a stress number, who knows what it means, apparently I'm rarely stressed for more than minutes a day. Not sure what that means or how to use this number or even how its derived. Called Garmin and got enough words, but no explanation of what it means. The Good Heart rate works, graph is nice. GPS works but drains the battery wicked bad. Steps when cross referenced with the GPS seem pretty accurate. If you use the "event" Walk a fairly cool representation of your walk shows up on you phone on the App. It charges fast and holds a charge for 3-4 days. The app interfaces with other fitness aps The Strange Many of the events, swimming, cycle, etc seem disconnected from reality. I'm guessing Garmin is using a simple time x calories x heart rate (and some average of the sport) to come up with a result. If anything its a highly dubious number. The lock on the touch screen can be turned off during normal wear. Many times in the morning I wake up with a totally different watch face. The battery cable plug barely connects to the watch. You have to be super careful putting the watch down with the cable attached cause it falls out. Very frustrating...

title: Worked great for a few years. Died suddenly with no warning.
text: I loved the watch's long battery life and simple features. It worked well. Until it didn't.

title: Durable product with good battery life.
text: I bought this as a gift for my girlfriend. She wears it daily, it has lasted through many workouts, hiking & camping trips, and general daily use. The glass has not scratched over a year later. It does have a sensitive touch screen so keeping it locked kept it from lighting up at night or replying to texts randomly when showering. It lasts on a single charge multiple days to almost a week depending on the settings.

title: It does it's minimal amount of things well
text: Let's just rip to the core here: the watch has serious issues connecting to its application. I used it with a Windows phone and an iPhone. Sucked both times. I'm done with this product line. As a stand alone, the watch is fine, if that's all you want. It's not all I wanted in this price range.

title: Easy to set up and happy to use
text: It's been an ongoing process to find a replacement for my last Garmin that unfortunately died while on vacation. But I am pleasantly surprised by this one. Arrived very quickly also! Not too thick, very lightweight, many face options available. Easy set up on app. I suspect I'll be very happy for many cycles, runs, sleeps to come!

title: Poor battery, will not last
text: I have owned this smartwatch for a year now and the battery life makes it nearly unusable. If I don't charge it daily it will die on me during the next use. I am quite disappointed that for the price this didn't last longer.

title: Garmin Watch
text: I'm enjoying my new Garmin. I really didn't need anything fancy, since I have a Garmin on my bike already.

title: Returning in under 24 hours. Absolutely Horrible
text: This watch is unusable. The process of originally connecting my watch was smooth and painless. Today, however I attempted to download a new watch face, which took an inordinate amount of time for how small the watch face is (~100MB). To get it to show up on my actual watch, I needed to unpair the watch from my phone, forget the device entirely, reconnect the watch, then power it off and then on again. This whole process took so much of my time just to get a few new features to show up. Then I used the watch during a lifting workout and it says that it tracks your sets. I did 12 reps of an exercise and the watch said 7. It isn't accurate and isn't helpful, and I wish it just worked like an Apple Watch where it said you're in a workout and it tracks your heart rate, steps, etc for that specific time frame and logs it. Also, I walked on the treadmill for 1.1 miles and the watch said I walked for under 1/2 a mile. It also registered my heart rate during the walk on the treadmill at 86, but sitting on the couch right now it says 98. So something is very off with this and it just all happened within the first day of owning it, so there is no way I can justify the price point of this watch and I can't recommend it for literally anyone.

title: refurbised watch not perfect
text: watch is not as good as the one it replace- it keeps losing connect with phone and battery doesnt last as long. called amazon - they asked me to call garmin and garmin wants me to set up a computer and cell phone to download more apps then remove device and help troubleshoot- i just want phone to work as well as the previous one i do not want to spend a day troubleshooting

title: Great watch
text: I have had my vivoactive 3 for just a little over a week and all I can say is, I love it. Easy to use, accurate, and works well with my phone and MyFitnessPal.

title: Ditch the ****bit and go Garmin
text: Fantastic tool, great user interface and software, well worth the money in my opinion. I do a lot of MTB riding and it's great.

title: Best watch I've owned
text: My 4th smartwatch, first was a zenwatch, 2nd was a Pebble, 3rd was a withings. With the Garmin I get better screen, good battery life, light weight, cool faces, great tracking. I'm getting 6 to 7 days battery life.

title: ok but low battery life
text: good at what I was looking for but the battery life is a little low. Only lasts a few days.

title: Tough, accurate, customization
text: I really like this watch mostly because you can customize it to your liking. One thing I did not like about the watch was that it does not have the body battery tracking. Everything else on the watch is very nice I like that you can control the volume of your music and change tracks on the watch One thing I did notice that it does not seem to connect to Bluetooth at a long range so you got to be pretty close to your phone to be controlling the music. If you use it for swimming or in the shower sometimes the water does change the watch faces and start selecting buttons. Battery life seems decent about 15% a day is one of averaging. It seems like a pretty tough and durable watch prone to scratches or any damage like that I use it during work and it seems to do the job.

title: Easy to set up
text: Great Watch. Lots of features Still learning all of them. Very pleased so far.

title: Great product
text: I really liked my vivosmart 4 but I had 2 bands break & you can't replace them. This one has a replaceable band and a few upgrades. Love the connection to my phone so I can read notifications and text messages and see who is calling. I would recommend this product to anyone .

title: My 14 year old loves it
text: My son is 14, a freshman in his high school cross country team. He loves this watch. Wears it everyday.

title: Battery life is not great. It is quite easy to use.
text: It works quite well and the Connect app is good. Floor counts are not usually very accurate. This is the previous version of this product so I bought it for a very good price on Amazon. I would not pay the typical overpriced Garmin price for the current version though. Garmin makes great equipment but their prices are sky high. The GPS works quite well but drains the battery fast. Overall I am happy with my purchase for the price I paid.

title: Worst Watch I'v ever purchased
text: HRM doesn't work, reading 97 when it is 162. I checked on both wrists, inside and outside, multiple times and multiple different days vs ANT chest strap to my Suunto Ambit2 and the Garmin always gives completely inaccurate readings. Also, will not connect to Google Pixel Phones nor to my computer using Garmin Express via the cable. Complete waste of money. I had another Garmin watch 6 years ago and it didn't work properly either, shut off randomly after only 9 months of use. I've had a Suunto Ambit2 for 5 years and it works great, figured I'd try Garmin and Wrist based HRM, complete fail, I highly recommend you look elsewhere if you want a product that actually works. This would easily be returned if not for Covid-19. Last Garmin product I ever purchase.

title: Vivoactive 3 OK
text: The Vivoactive 3 is light weight and looks like a normal watch. I 86 so many of the fitness apps I don't use, bought it mainly for the heart &sleep apps plus the golf. The Golf seems to read a little long but is quick to locate golf course. The real downside for me was the learning curve with Golf app and the heart rate to sync with my phone. Overall I like the watch.

title: A realy nice smart watch.
text: Love this watch. It helps you track your fitness profile through the day and also gives you access to a load of activity trackers. Reminds you about calender appointment, incoming phone calls and messages. One of the great things is that it is easy to customize the alerts you get so you are not inundated with information. I have not tried swimming with it yet, but I do wear it in the shower with no adverse effects so far. The battery life is good, it takes 3 days to get down to roughly 40% and recharges in about 15 mins. Of course the GPS functions (e.g. tracking a golf game or bike ride) eat up the battery charge..... duh.....

title: I really like my Garmin
text: I picked this Garmin specifically because it is waterproof and I can use the SUP app for kayaking. This watch replaced my Vioactive HR and took some getting used to. I do need to make sure the Garmin has a full charge before hiking or using the SUP mode. After 10 plus miles of either activity, the battery is pretty drained. The touch screen does take some getting used to. The watch will light-up unexpectedly when something touches it. Like, rolling over trying to get to sleep. The hiking app would shut down during a hike without me realizing it because the screen was touched by something. After several frustrating trips, I figured out how to lock the screen during events. Problem solved. Overall I am very happy with the smartwatch and I would purchase it again.

title: I love it! it looks nicer and feels way better ...
text: I love it! it looks nicer and feels way better than Fitbitc... Fitbit. My only issue is the workout setup feature. I use this watch for strength training and high intensity cardio but it only captures sets. I hope they can update this. Also the face clocks could use more variety.

title: Great smart watch and fitness tracker. A little short on the battery life
text: It's a great smart watch. As garmin watches it has great fitness features. The only downside is the battery life, using it while sleeping consume 10% of the battery. I have a garmin instinct tha has eternal battery, and maybe is because of that then the vivoactive 3 seems to have less battery life

title: Fantastic watch
text: Bought the Vivoactive 3 as a replacement for my trusty Forerunner 10.... I am in love with this watch!

title: Another dud from Garmin
text: This is my 2nd attempt to try a Garmin watch and like the previous one it's just pretty junk. Within 2 weeks it failed to sync to the app, making it useless, and then stopped charging as well. It looks great and has alot of fun and useful features but when they only last a few weeks then what is the point?

title: Good battery and live pace info
text: Great battery and charging, I usually let it charge for an hour while I work each day. No need to have the backlight on most of the time. The live pace and GPS are reasonably accurate for what I need. GPS does drain the battery a lot, about 20-30% for an hour or so run I think. For a bare bones GPS running watch this should do the trick.

title: Works great, exactly what I expect
text: 3rd Garmin device, I've owned. Always well built and the companion app works well. Small issue I have is that my step goal hasn't seemed to translate, even though it's set in my profile correctly and on older devices correctly.

title: This is a great upgrade for me
text: I LOVE this watch! I had the Garmin Forerunner 230 for a couple of years, and my wife surprised me with this Vivoactive 3 for Christmas. I couldn't be happier! It is much easier to use to control my music, I like that the side of the case is touch-sensitive to also control the watch, but not overly so. This watch does so much more than the 230 that I like all of its functionality. I wish the battery life was a bit better, as I have to recharge every week or so when the 230 used to go a month at a time. But for all of the functionality I can't really complain.

title: works but that gps
text: all features work just fine except that gps signal-lock time varies pretty wildly, anywhere from several seconds to over 2 minutes. and i'm running in only 3 different locations around town. following all instructions (including the GLONASS) does not make much difference. it is definitely hit-or-miss but standing around 2 minutes before running can seem like eternity. if it does not improve in a more consistent and predictable fashion, i will have to look for something else. that's a shame since i do like the watch otherwise. it is comfortable to wear and its functions are informative. oh, the heart monitor works for me as well as the online storage of all my activities.

title: Purchased for my dad who doesn’t like iPhone/Apple Watch
text: Purchased for my dad who doesn’t like iPhone/Apple Watch. Perfect for somebody who wants to track their steps and a few other basic features it has been very durable and reliable a lot tougher than a Fitbit very simple straightforward interface

title: Happy so far
text: I have had less then a week but am happy so far. Syncs with My Fitness Pal.... Its hard to figure out but once you do it works well. The app is very important and it looks like this app has a lot in it.

title: So much information!
text: It has been working as described, and there is so much information to be had from this device. I find the app easy to use.

title: Garmin is the best!
text: I love this watch. I have tried many of these smart watches/ activity trackers and this has been the best along with the app. You will really appreciate this watch.

title: Vivoactive 3
text: Great watch Accurate HR Accurate GPS Some functions difficult to figure out how to access; manual not always accurate

title: Ehhh is what I would say
text: I came from a gear sport and wanted to like the watch, the lack of updates OTA, needing to update over usb, the UI is very sluggy and ugly with the colors that are so bland, its not a good smart watch, its an okay fitness watch, i think it tried to do too much, just feels ugly to use and have on wrist, pros- it is light, and has good tracking, cons are its not easy on the eyes, not as durable, and laggy

title: We recommend it!
text: Great watch to play golf. The battery doesn’t last as long as a previous version but we recommend it. Looks very nice.

title: Good gift.
text: My nephew choose this one for his gift. He likes it

title: Easy to use, but short battery life
text: I am glad I purchased this watch as it helps me stay more focused on fitness. The pros are the ease of use, the GPS option with maps, the many types of activities (beyond running, walking, and biking) loaded into the watch and the app (which tracks hydration, weight, and etc. It works with the watch and downloads all your data by bluetooth. I have an older Samsung phone and it works great!). The biggest con is the short battery life; I have followed all of the suggestions for conserving the battery, but still must charge this watch every two or three days (I do not wear it all day, I turned off heart rate monitor and turned down the brightness to 10%...this does help somewhat). I still like the watch and do not regret the purchase.

title: Stopped working after 4 months
text: Stopped working after 4 months. It does do anything anymore. Don't buy

title: Wouldn't count stairs. Called, bs about don't hold ...
text: Wouldn't count stairs. Called, bs about don't hold the hand rail or skip steps, finally not really meant to count steps in a house, suppose to be in a stadium outside. Very disappointing. I had the fitbit it was to replace on at the same time, it got the the 100 flights right both times, Garmin did 49 and 65. Sent it back. Don't know how it does other things but won't do flights of stairs.

title: Great gadget so far.
text: To rate this watch is a very complex thing since there is so many things it can do. I haven’t used it to it’s full potential especially the GPS. The first few weeks I almost returned it because the battery life was horrible. 2 or 3 days max in one charge. I did some research and followed a few things to save battery and now the last charge it lasted 10 days (no gps, sleep tracking, etc) only as a step counter. As soon as my knee heals up I will start using the rest of the gadgets.

title: Not a great running watch
text: I wish I had just purchased a simpler GPS watch that achieved it’s basic functions well. The elevation sensor is totally useless. I googled how to fix it and found message boards full of complaints that the elevation sensor on the vivoactive 3 just doesn’t work. The distance function is slow to acquire satellites and seems inaccurate on the actual distance of runs. Even though I turned off the goals function, the watch still randomly buzzes throughout the day telling me to move more or that I’ve accomplished some random goal. It may be that if you’re more interested in a smart watch and don’t care about the basics of a running watch, this is a great budget choice. Otherwise, I’d look elsewhere.

title: Awesome so far
text: I have had fit bits, but they were not very durable. None of them last more than a year. My daughter has had her Forerunner25 for two years with no problems. This watch is much more powerful than either of those watches. Good: 1. Lots of different activities (running, golf, cycling, etc) 2. Screen is customizable 3. Bluetooth connectivity to iPhone and app 4. Battery life so far 5. Different types of workouts - Mixed intervals, 1/4 mile repeats, run/walk 6. Mapping a courses 7. Heart monitor 8. real time mile pace Bad 1. I really dislike the band. I'm use to the a velcro band. Silcone band does not breath like velcro band. I haven't found a decent velcro band, yet. 2. Stairs walked is not very accurate Could be better 1. I really wish they had customizable interval workouts. 2 minutes hard run : 1 min slow jog, etc

title: Best Gift Ever
text: It was the best Christmas gift to give him. He thoroughly loves all the features it has to offer.

title: Awesome Fitness Watch!!!
text: My dad absolutely loves this watch my siblings and I got for him this Christmas he never takes it off!!! Great buy!!!

title: I use it as a display for my cgm and for that it works just fine
text: I kind of like the watch long battery life. The screen is not the brightest but I use it mainly as a display for my cgm which works great

title: Helpful and easy to use
text: My husband loves this watch! So easy to keep up with texts and emails. Also helpful listening to podcasts.

title: Great product
text: Love it! Great battery life tough exterior only thing I wish it would let you text to talk but you can preset responses so that's helpful .

title: Perfect for the newbie Triathlete!
text: As much as I wanted to go all out with the most expensive Garmin watch - it just didn't make sense. This however, is the perfect watch for my budget and training needs! I love the step counting, exercise mode selection, and that this watch can do indoor AND outdoor swims! As a newbie Triathlete this is perfect for getting your feet wet into the fitness watch world without diving off the deep end for the price. The heart rate data is the data that is most important to me since I purchased this watch. The stress measure capability seems a little weird. Even when I'm feeling super stressed - my measurements are very low. However, it is a good indicator of when I'm not feeling well. For instance, I get random shoots of pain in my leg from some old burns - and when I feel the random pain - it shows as a jump in stress on my watch.... Which is the only way providing visual proof of the random pain I get. This watch band does irritate my skin slightly, but most watches do. Sometimes I just have to take a break from wearing it as needed.

title: Great upgrade in the Garmin family!
text: I love this watch! I had the Vivosmart 4 prior, but had an allergic reaction to the band. I'm so happy I switched to this watch! The band is replaceable, which is nice. The watch face is bold, pretty, and has excellent features.

title: avarage smart watch
text: had some problems from begging and was refunded. Think you can buy for that price better functional watch. not really recommended

title: Perfect fitness companion
text: I love it! So much information from my workouts. Plus it can handle a bit of a beating and I only have to charge it every 4-5 days. The waterproofing is fantastic, I can't say how many electronic fitness things I've sweated to death. But not a garmin!

title: Grossly Inaccurate HR Monitor
text: Received this watch as a gift. I wanted to lkke it, however, after 2 weeks of trial and error I am going back to my polar watch. The garmin has many great features and customization options. I know wrist based heart rate monitors are not a 100% accurate way to read the HR. The garmin was severely flawed and even worse than my expectations. At times during my workout my heart rate would dip below my resting heart rate despite the rigorous body weight and plyometric workout that I was doing. I did 2 weeks of workouts expecting these issues to be anomolies, however it was consistently inaccurate. It will be returned immediately.

title: Nice watch for the price
text: I really like this watch. It is unfortunate that it’s not compatible with the running dynamic foot pod but otherwise it’s been extremely motivational in helping me keep track of my running program. The battery lasts pretty long and charges in less time it takes for me to shower. It hasn’t scratched yet and I wear it all day hiking and running around.

title: Don’t wait to pair as it may not.
text: Bluetooth function does not work. Tried ALL fixes suggested by Garmin, still no connection. Return window has now just closed, so…thanks Amazon. Update: finally paired after a session with tech support. The PC app is really unusable. The watch itself maybe merits 2 stars, its very basic and balky. Ok for hubby’s needs but I was expecting better from Garmin.

title: Great watch
text: Just needed a watch to count steps in addition to date and time. This does so much more! Love the sleep mode that actually tells you how much rem sleep you are experiencing! Not too complicated, and easy to add to ipad. Highly recommend!

title: Good looking watch
text: Nice looking watch with clear display. Have used for workouts at health club. Accurate heart rate on elliptical, although took a little time to get up to speed. Weightlifting reps function not sensitive/accurate but wasn't going to use feature, just timer function to space between sets and record workout good. Got a round of winter golf in to test and worked accurately. Too cold to test bicycle function (have garmin speed and cadence sensors). Notifications and music functions work well. Bluetooth connection a little shaky at times around condo but acceptable. Battery life is OK for 3 days with workouts, not the best. Had a Vivoactive HR for four years till capacitive touchscreen went bad. The HR battery would last 5 days. The Vivoactive 3 is an upgrade to the HR in style, responsiveness, and readability. All works well with Connect app on android phone to monitor/record workouts. My concern is battery life, especially once start biking with GPS on, will update in future. Overall VA 3, battery life pending, a nice upgrade from VA HR at a reasonable price, considering the newest version VA 4 would cost $170 more (double cost of VA 3).

title: Disappointing heart rate tracking
text: Disappointed. In-acitivty heart rates are ridiculous. During strength training, it consistently rates my heart rate very low, around a third or my real heart rate. I've tried different activities, putting it instead in cardio or yoga, but the same result. Ranks my heart rate between 60 and 85 when counting my heartbeats myself puta my heart rate closer to 110-140. Heart rate is the main reason I wanted this watch, but it's terrible with this. Outside of activities, it raks my heart rate OK, but often too low or too high, such as saying my heart rate is 130 when I'm just walking at the office, or saying my heart rate is 55 when I'm sitting at my computer. WTF Garmin?? I'm not buying the chest strap for an additional $100 just to get this pice of garbage to work as it should put of the box. My 4 year old Samsung watch was better at heart rate tracking than you.

title: Don't Waste Money on the Warrantee
text: My first Garmin lasted over three years and Ioved it.. it went through a lot with me. This watch only worked a little over one year. The real slap in the face is, I bought the extra warrantee and they sent a refurbished watch which isn't covered. I had a lot of trouble getting it to sync with my phone, it does not hold a charge for a full day, and there are other issues. Don't waste your money on the warrantee.

title: Not happy vivoactive 3 owner.
text: I’ve had all sorts of problems with item and Garmin just keeps telling me to turn it off and on. Also had me put it back to default settings and reconnect to phone. Still have short battery life, sleep doesn’t work, readings all over the place. I’ve lost my faith in the product, and in manufacturer.

title: Not Worth It
text: This watch is crap. The step counter and stairs counter are way off. I've gone up 19 flights of stairs and it's only counted 4. I wore pedometer at the same time to compare....I'm at 13K steps on my pedometer and only 5k steps in this watch. It's being returned. Too bad because the app for it is great.

title: Very disappointed
text: Very disappointed. Says you can text on the watch. But only can do pre recorded responses.

title: Garmin is the best
text: I switched from Fitbit. I had 3 Charges and 1 Ionic none were durable. I am just a regular person trying to be healthy not a athlete by any stretch of my imagination. The Garmin is beautiful. I love that it is round. The information it provides is straightforward and relevant. The watch face options are great. The ease of use is great. For the first week I wore my Ionic and my Vivoactive 3 for comparison. The stats were consistent even with the sleep, however the stress monitor was awesome. At the end of the week, I put my Ionic in the drawer.

title: Battery life much less than advertised.
text: Compaired to my cheap amazfit boo this has alot of potential because of the apps. However instead of 30 days of battery life an heavy gps usage from the bio I get 2 or three days. I can pick up calls and send messages though. Been living with a while now. Battery life is still only 3-4 days but liking the bike and running data provided so going up to 4 stars. The Bluetooth link to the phone isn't the best either. Disconnects often and so far no way to get ride of the annoying notification when it disconnects.

title: Love it!
text: After wearing the narrow Vivofit and Vivosmart HR for several years, I decided to give this one a try, although I wasn't sure if I'd like the bigger, bulkier watch. The deciding factor when my Vivosmart died was cost. I could get this Vivoactive 3 with all the Bluetooth capabilities the Vivosmart didn't have for only about $25 more. I decided it was worth it, and I was right. The watch and the app allow me to do so much more than the Vivosmart HR and the Vivofit before that. I can sync it with my phone so that I can see texts or answer/deny calls. I'm still learning how to use some of those functions. I'm very glad I decided to give this one a chance.

title: This is a high quality product, well worth the money!
text: This item was received as described & on time. This was purchased as a gift for my son. He is very pleased with it and enjoys all of it’s functions. I highly recommend this item!

title: Can not update
text: Can not update because I do not have a computer with the newest operating system.... would have never thought it would be a issue

title: Randomly shuts off
text: It randomly shuts off on its own no matter how full the battery is. I miss steps because I don't know it's off.

title: No longer measures heart rate - buggy
text: Loved it for six months, then they did a software update and it stopped measuring heart rate which is why I bought it. Reset it, worked for 2 days, then stopped. Not happy.

title: perfect for outdoor sport - inconvenient for everything else
text: + cycling - tones of data and accurate recording + hiking - tones of data and accurate recording + running - - tones of data and accurate recording + golf - it seems to be designed for golfers - golf course maps … + battery - it works easily for 3-4 days with GPS activities and longer without GPS - Sleep tracking is just terrible - it does NOT have any way to track a nap - or more than one sleep at night. So if you wake up at the middle of the night for over 10 minutes, it does not track your second round. you canNOT adjust sleep goal. anything less than 8 hrs does are treated equally - interface: the only way to turn the display off is to wait until the pre-set time. - Interface - it has an interactive face, but it doesn't use it to its potentials at all. you can adjust the main watchface or select from some options. Beyond that, for all the other information you have to scroll up/down one at a time. There is no interactive watchface where you can touch the screen to go to the specific info you want to see now - calories in/out - yo can add calories in through sister apps. Garmin shows an updated calories out- but the watch does not show calories in. the phone interface shows the remaining calories based on your goal, not your current activity bottom line, unlike many other devices, you can't see what you've burned and what you've taken in together. -music. it uses the music on your device, which is fine, except that it works only with a few apps. I ended up keeping it for the sport features. But if that's not your priority, consider other devices.

title: Overall Really Happy
text: I bought the VA3 about a two/three days back for my son and he loves the watch, love that he can customize the different watch faces, battery life is great, fitness tracking features (steps, HR, GPS) are spot on, the built-in activities work really well. From a full charge, he tracked 4 walks, 2 runs, and 2 cardio workouts and still got 80% battery. Overall, my son is happy and I am really happy and would highly recommend VA3.

title: This is a Watch.. yes.. this is great watch
text: This is a Watch.. yes.. this is great watch. I tried Apple Watch and Fitbit before and stayed with this. It is not overloaded with so many functions like Apple Watch. If you want fancier one with sound and reply to your message notifications then you will get disappointed. Best part of this Watch is it never makes a sound!!! Only vibrations so less distractions. Battery life is too good. Overall a worth by imo

title: battery usage bar is not on main creen
text: great product yet battery display is not on main screen

title: So far so good.
text: Day #1 so review is brief.. but I'm digging it so far..

title: Some accuracy problems
text: Love the watch - despite the fact that the HR monitor is not accurate sometimes. I shaved all the hair off my wrist and that seems to help (no, I am not a gorilla). Also, I have no idea if the sleep tracking is accurate, but I hope it isn't. It's all over the map

title: Not long lasting
text: Watch not even 2 years old and wearing down. Next stop maybe Apple or Samsung.

title: very comfortable
text: love the durability. I do lots of farm work with this on including dealing with my horses. it takes a beating and stays acurate

title: The Garmin vivoactive 3 was recommended by a friend and this watch has exceeded my ...
text: The Garmin vivoactive 3 was recommended by a friend and this watch has exceeded my expectations! There are still features I'm learning but the battery life is excellent and I'm testing it out for accuracy on the heart rate monitor.

title: Good ass watch
text: I picked up this watch on sale because I’ve been wanting a smart watch for awhile. Initially I was looking at a Apple Watch, but am fairly active and outdoorsy, and the battery life is what drove me to look elsewhere and I picked up a Garmin on the recommendation of my mother who is a runner. I have had this watch for a few weeks, and I’m impressed. I have borrowed a friends Apple Watch, and while this may not be as feature heavy, it’s fine for me, and I honestly enjoy the more activity focused apps on here anyways, and anything more complex is honestly best done on my phone. With notifications, there isn’t a lot of interaction, but it’s handy, and I prefer the soft vibration, rather than loud ringtones or alerts from my phone. Again while it isn’t as feature heavy in terms of apps, it has different priories as a fitness app, where I find it excels. The battery life is great, and with a plain watch face will last about 10 days, and with more complex watch faces you can expect that to drop to about 5, which isn’t a big deal since the watch charges pretty quickly. I use a more complex face when I’m out and about, and a simpler one when at home or at night to save battery a bit while still getting about 7 days. I read some people have issues with heart rate, but it’s pretty accurate, I compared it with a monitor at a doctors visit and it was pretty dead on. Sometimes the stress tracker can act up a little bit though, and you need to sit still for awhile or have the watched pretty tight, which is a little annoying but not too big of a deal. The fitness apps I’m still kind of learning how to set up, but the data they give per workout is pretty useful, being able to monitor your intensity, and distance. I mainly use a treadmill due to poor air quality where I live so I haven’t been able to test GPS much. Overall, if your into fitness or tend to be more outdoorsy this is a great watch especially for the price.

title: I love this watch
text: I love this watch. I wasnt sure if i wanted the one with music on it. I decided that since i am mostly on the trails, it is safer if i have my phone with me, so i decided on the one without music. It is easy to use. I like the notifications on my wrist for stuff. I also like that i can block some of the notifications. I can scroll through faces while gps is on to see different things, elevation, climb, pace, time, heart rate. The gps doesnt seem to be as accurate as my older model Garmin. When i use gps/glonass in the run settings, it's more accurate than gps only. When i am on the road it is very accurate with gps only. The trails in my area a very curvy, i know that it can shorten the distance, by making straight lines, instead of following the curves. There is a way to link to other peoples gps on the same routes to be more accurate. I had an update that allowed you to do that and didn't click yes in time. I am sure i will have another chance.

title: Long Wait for GPS before working out
text: I bought it to mainly to run outside. Sometimes is annoying that takes so long waiting for the GPS. It can be 10 minutes. I connect it to the phone every day (another thing that keeps your attention) Other than that is ok.

title: Reliable personal tracker
text: The ability to track all daily activities with one device is very convenient and beneficial. Great for tracking daily calorie intake & caloric burn, water consumption, various exercise activities, sleep and other valuable metrics. Sleep scores are helpful but the nightly calculation of "deep sleep" is, unfortunately, not as consistent as I would like it to be. Sense model has additional features not found with the Fitbit Blaze model, previously used.

title: Garbage. Avoid this product. Uninstalls my chosen clock face and apps every time.
text: After about 24 hours of apparently normal use, it started freaking out. It uninstalls our clock faces and the ECG app. When we re-install them, they work fine for about two minutes, then disappear. In the Fitbit app, it gives us the option to re-install them, but only after showing a screen saying that there is no internet access (this house has almost a dozen other wireless devices that do not suffer this problem). We will be returning this cursed thing at the earliest opportunity. 0/5, would not recommend.

title: For those who want to know what's going on
text: Although I don't use my Fitbit for exercise in general, I do like to know how many steps I take how many calories I'm burning and how much sleep I'm getting. There are many options and anyone serious about exercise will love this smart watch.

title: Don’t waste your money😭
text: I’ve had this watch for 4 months and have taken great care if it. Battery doesn’t last past 2 days. Heart rate tracker is not accurate and very poorly developed. If my heart rate goes past 160 it stops reading it and shows a drastic down peak to like 90bpm. On top of that. You have to pay 10$ a month for features that should be included with the watch.

title: Amazing
text: I’m in love with this watch and mins you I had other watch in the past from Fitbit .. so yes the best watch ever .. finally it count my stair step properly

title: best fitbit yet
text: Accurate! ease of changing bands! provides multitude of health facts! I can even log blood sugar readings in app! would buy again

title: I’m mostly happy with my sense.
text: Overall I’m satisfied with the performance of my Sense. Only thing that I find odd is that it often thinks I’m asleep when I am reading or watching TV. It is attractive, but I only give 4 stars because overall I feel that my Surge performs better and is more accurate

title: AVOID: Inaccurate sleep, SPo2 and even steps
text: Avoid This Watch: This watch is inaccurate right out of the box. The first thing after you enter your height and weight is you have to calibrate your steps. The sleep monitor is a joke...seriously...a joke. I keep a dream journal and I know with 100% certainty that I entered REM sleep and the watch can not pick that up. When I compare what I know about my sleep with the Sense....well, bottom line is IT JUST DOES NOTWORK!!!! The EKG function is kind of cool. There is a $10 fee if you want all the functionality of the watch. Cons: Initial cost of watch plus $120 per year. Steps inaccurate from the go Sleep monitor is a joke SPo2 is ONLY during sleep. You can't just take a reading. Battery life is no where near what they say. Heart rate is kind of hit and some miss Pros: It tells time :-/ It can sense when you are exercising and your heart zones All the major functions work on the surface

title: Geared for workout / upsell on health
text: Sleep is working as intended. However their stats are fairly useless particularly the oxygen levels. Still haven't got the tapped and go pay to work. Receive an error on all machines. Really not many useful apps for it outside the limited health results. Here's a tip Fitbit: You can continue to focus on data gathering and service gouging (which is why Google bought you..) or you can build an affordable product that actually helps people with health concerns. This POS is going back.

title: Very Comfortable Smart Watch
text: Really enjoy this watch. Purchased to keep track of steps, but does so much more!! This is by far the most comfortable watch I have ever owned. Little tricky to get use to different items available. Will often drop my phone connect and have to reestablish network again. Other than that, Great Watch!!

title: Charging
text: Bought 2 after 3 months very difficult to charge. Place on charger and have to move it around sometimes will charge and sometimes not. I bought new charger and same problem. I’m very disappointed. Works great when I can get it to charge.

title: Love it!
text: This is my 4th Fitbit and it's awesome...except for the battery life. Because I use the "always on" feature, the battery life is 2 days even though I use sleep mode at night which turns the always on function, off. Still, it's the best Fitbit I've ever owned. I'm still discovering the many new features that my old one didnt have. I highly recommend the Sense!

title: Weak Construction & battery only lasts 2-3 days
text: I have had 3 models of Fitbit with no issues until I got this Sense… not only did the battery not last even half the time advertised but it cracked on a really light bump on the table after 2 months. We contacted Fitbit and they wrote us off with a 35% discount. I had ordered the premium services so I’m out of luck getting that cost back. Very disappointed in their customer service so switching us out of their ecosystem.

title: Counted steps I didn't take
text: Counted steps I didn't take, sub par tracking sleep, battery life very good, informative otherwise and shouldn't enforce a fee to be more informative

title: Great for us.
text: We have fitbits and apples, and it just for what you want your watch that they are different. I feel that Fitbit (for what I need) is better for sport. It was easy to set it on, maybe because we already had an account and we just needed to upgrade it. The watch itself is comfortable to wear. The battery life is good. Last a lot. We connect it to the Alexa, easy and fast to do it. It reads everything we need/want to know, calories, steps..... to be honest we wanted it for those readings. And for those readings it works great. Just like all other fitbits. I recommend it. As I always do. For sport info I prefer 100% Fitbit than apple.

title: Even a great watch isn't worth much if you can't charge it!
text: II bought two of these from Amazon in 12/21. Five months later one of the charge cords has failed with a "pushed in" charge pin issue (do a search). This is apparently a frequent issue and the replacement cord costs about $20. Until the issue is resolved ie. more robust charge cord construction, you might think twice about your purchase. Aside from the cord, I am satisfied with the watch. It was an update for my Fitbit Pulse. I had that watch for many years with NO problems. Update 08/22 Fitbit sent a new charge cord under warranty last December. THAT cord is no longer working, same issue "pushed in pins" on the charge head. I have been VERY careful of this cord. Do I have to buy one every year? I'll contact their support again but this time I'm technically "out of warranty" I'd advise another product.

title: this was a gift
text: I bought this for my gf because her old fitbit had broke & the warranty ran out. she really loves this fitbit. definitely recommend 👍👍👍👍👍

title: Love my Fitbit Sense!!
text: Took a chance with the Sense…had previously used the Versa 3 which had a lot of glitches. I am super happy with the Sense!! Works flawlessly, looks sleek and accurate. Only issue I have is the battery life isn’t as good as the Versa 3.

title: Love my Fitbit
text: This is my 5th Fitbit. I love it. I would highly recommend to anyone. I love I can wear swimming.

title: One Major Drawback - The Exercise Selections
text: My wife bought this for me as an upgrade to my Versa 2. A great thing about the Versa 2 was the ability to arrange the selection and order of Exercises on the watch, albeit via the phone app. I was expecting this feature to be the same (or improved) on the upgraded watch. But on this model, you do NOT have the option to change roster of exercises on the watch, or the order in which they appear. Wow, hard to believe that a watch that's intended to help you track your exercise would loose this feature. The very clumsy workaround is use the button double-click option to select up to 4 exercises (only) if you don't want any other apps in double-click. And you can't add any exercises to the roster. Rowing (one of my frequent exercises) is not included. Fitbit designers - these are BIG MISSES for a health tracking device!!

title: FITBIT SENSE IS FABULOUS
text: I got this watch to monitor my sleep patterns, blood oxygen, and heart. This is the best watch I've had to date, it does all the things I love! Plays music, has a Starbucks app, text messages, the app has calming and meditation programs. With COVID-19, I need all the relaxation, breathing techniques, meditation, and exercise I can get. The watch is light, sleek, and comfortable to wear. I'm truly impressed with Fitbit and their dedication to advancing technology.

title: I like it but it can be improved
text: I like that it tracks my steps but it has issues with tracking my sleep. Also it would be better if Alexa worked even if the app wasn’t open. Right now it only works if the app is open. Oh and another thing… it would be great if you could answer a call from your watch but as of now, you can’t. So yeah, I like it but it can be improved.

title: waste of money
text: I've had it a month and I am very careful with it, removing it for showers, not doing yardwork with it--just wearing it to work and while I attend to my kids. It is already cracked in two places. But, my least favorite thing about it is that it is NEVER synced! I have to constantly pull out my phone, open the app and manually sync. What's the point of a smart watch if you have to pull out your phone anyways to use the features on the watch? I wish I would've just bit the bullet and got the apple watch. I would return but amazon says I am past the return window.

title: Device I received did not work properly
text: Purchased around 2/23/2022. Had previously purchased one for my wife which seemed to work fine; however, my device, the button never worked right. It had difficulty being activated and frequently disconnected from my phone amongst other issues. A few days ago, after removing the watch from charging, it began flashing the Fitbit logo, and now it will not factory reset or work any longer. Very disappointed in the performance.... It barely lasted 50 days..... Worst $250 ever.

title: Excellent tracking watch
text: Tracks sleep, steps, and my runs using GPS. I depend on it and it motivates me to improve my health 100%. I use the food log. I had the Fitbit Ionic before which I liked better for three reasons. 1) The look/design 2) It was more accurate with my steps/active minutes. 3) I could download my mp3 playlist on the Ionic and did not need to bring my phone on runs. My new sense has some great features and works great. The sleep data has helped me and my family physician solve my insomnia (that alone is worth the price and premium subscription). The food log and exercise logs have helped me lose over 40 lbs in 2021! With the premium subscription, there are some great extra tracking, features, and programs. Premium subscription is NOT necessary for the watch to be useful. My wife and kids have Garmin watches that they love and they claim those are better if you do a lot of hiking or are more serious than me in training for running/races. Fitbits are better for those wanting to improve health in my opinion. In the end, I would recommend the Fitbit Sense if you need something now, however, since Google bought Fitbit I believe the next higher end iteration will be better (and hopefully more accurate). If you are not in a hurry to get a new watch,, then wait then wait for that otherwise you won't go wrong with the Sense. I'll likely upgrade to the next generation when it comes out (hoping for improvements, more accuracy, and music playlists downloaded to the watch

title: not perfect, but some good improvements over Versa
text: This watch is a nice step up from the Versa. A few random improvements: the band is MUCH easier to change; the snore detection and other sleep features are great (IIRC you must have the premium subscription to get this, but it's free for 6 months); the always-on watch face is very handy; the sp02 and hr detectors are good info to have (haven't tested their accuracy, though!). And the battery life is much better than, say, the Apple Watch -- even with all the battery-eating functions active, I still get around 36 hours out of the battery (I charge every morning while I read the news, so this is plenty). OTOH, the pedometer is still useless. This thing actually measures ARM movements, not leg movements -- so, for instance, if you're walking down a store aisle pushing a shopping cart, you won't earn any steps at all because your arms won't be swinging. And if you're lying in bed petting your cat, you may earn hundreds of steps even though you haven't even stood up. So don't count on that being accurate! Also, the band that comes with the Sense is horrible -- it gave me a bad rash even though I'm not allergic to much of anything. Get an after-market band!

title: Cool phone if you like receiving invites for adult activities and not dressed ladies
text: Two days in receive an invite from a User ending in 93Q4ML and told Fitbit support, chat, emailed them, its still online for any child to view many days later. No way to be anonymous or private so make sure you don't connect any real email to the account. No option to hide or go invisible, so beware. To verify this active user, go to Fitbit.com add a slash user then the number above. Pretty pathetic. The watch is ok but having to pay for features in the future with poor filtering and outright laziness on their part is not good.

title: Face off
text: The face fell off. It’s crap. Go to google and search for Fitbit face fell off. It’s a persistent issue.

title: Update…thought it was great but…
text: Updated Review-have had it a few months now and now wish I had gotten an Apple watch. The Fitbit keeps losing my Wallet settings, can’t get one setting in the watch to work and the phone app will ding you at 10 pm every night to go to bed, even though that setting is turned off and it dings through the phone’s do not disturb setting. Very annoying and Fitbit can’t seem to fix or they don’t care. My old Fitbit Charge 3 got too dim to see outside, so had to replace it. It was a toss up between Fitbit Sense, Apple or Kate Spade's. I went with Fitbit Sense and LOVE IT.

title: Great watch
text: I went from a Fitbit Versa to an Apple Watch Series 5 and ended up getting rid of that after 6 months and purchased this. I missed Fitbit's data and simplicity. I love the battery life and the tracking. It's a lot less glitchy than the Versa was. The watch itself is beautiful and there are some good faces you can get. I ended up getting one from Lignite and it was a few dollars but I got access to all of their creations. There's some good free ones too but I liked the customizable features of the face and watch itself. I really love it and so happy I switched back to Fitbit.

title: Some great features added. Some unwelcome changes
text: Switched to the Sense after my Versa 2 bit the dust (weird screen issues). The Sense looks great and serves every function that the Versa 2 had and then some. The added built-in GPS and Google Assistant features are great. I like being able to receive calls on the watch as well. The couple of issues that drop this watch below a 5-star rating for me are: 1. The lack of a physical button. I personally prefer having an actual button to press to wake up the screen. The Sense still responds when you press the side of it where the button would be, but it's not as reliable as a good old-fashioned button. 2. The vibration seems weaker. I use this as my primary alarm in the morning. The vibration is still enough to wake me up, but it's a noticeably weaker vibration than the Versa 2. Sometimes I don't even feel my hourly reminders to get up and move at work. I have messed with the settings and set it to the highest vibration, but it is still weak compared to my old Versa 2. In addition to issues with the tracker itself, the Fitbit App needs work. It doesn't connect reliably to the tracker throughout the day, and additional features within the app would be welcome (more virtual trails, for example). Personally, I don't care for Fitbit's bands that come with their trackers, so I replaced that with a nylon band right away. I will say the band replacement was WAY easier than previous Fitbit models. Overall, though, the pros outweigh the cons for me. I'm happy with the tracker and would recommend for anyone looking for a smartwatch or fitness tracker.

title: Screen is not as durable as other models
text: This is Sense #2 for me. #1 slowly slid off a chair on to the floor and left if with several cracks in the screen originating on the bezel, less than a month in. I previously had a Versa for a number of years and it only managed to pick up a barely noticeable surface scratch in that time. Thankfully my cc reimbursed me for Sense #1 and I got a wrap around screen protector for #2 before I wore it. title: Stopped Charging

title: Don't RELY on the numbers if they are important to you!
text: I ware my Sense 24/7 and charge it while showing daily. It's fun to watch the trends... The main issue is with the SpO2 measurement. It is clear to me now why the FDA would not recognize the Fitbit SpO2 accuracy. Compared to my O2 Ring, FDA Recognized, the nightly saturation levels are way off... I use a cPAP machine as I have OSA. With the ring, which I have compared to hospital oximeters, it is within ~0.5%. My nightly averages run 98% - 99% with no drops below 95%. The Fitbit has me all over the place... Sometimes as low as 92% average with drops into the 80's. Without the ring, I would be really concerned. The sleep tracking is fairly OK except it does sometimes drop an hour of two and gives me a really bad score. The HR monitor is very slow in calculating the current HR. They appear to be using some long-term averaging that does NOT match the real time reading of my Polar Strap when walking. However, the average sleeping HR does match my O2 Ring. The GPS does not match the reading I get with my Polar strap / Pixel 6Pro for my nightly walk. 1.32 Mile Fitbit / 1.42 phone. Comparing the maps, it appears the phone GPS is more accurate. The speaker quality on phone calls is quite poor, but it does work. The ECG monitor does pick up Afib and matches my Kardia Mobil ECG monitor most of the time. However, I have had instances where it shows "inconclusive" while I am in Afib as indicated by the Kardia. Maybe wait and buy a Sense 2 if Fitbit improves the accuracy...

title: Wrist band is faulty. All in all....I'm very disappointed!
text: I so loved this. But there are sad issues with it. First off the band kept popping off. And the 3rd time it popped off it hit the tile floor and cracked the screen in 2 places. title: Really love this watch!
text: Once I got through the learning curve I really love this watch! The app on the other hand.....not so much. Getting through the menus to setup all the features and permissions is not a consistent single logic approach. I wish app developers would use a more user friendly approach. ie...list features in one location with a click here adjust permission by feature you want turned on. My second gripe is charging. With so many comments on no charge I got worried I had a problem. Once again it was that I misunderstood the process. The first time charging before setup is different than after setup. First time before setup whenever you touch button or screen the charge status shows up. AFTER SETUP, when you put your watch on charger it shows status of charge for a few seconds then goes back to your selected watch face "so you can use your watch while charging". I found this info in the downloaded manual. So if you miss this brief charging message you might think the watch is not charging. The app is little help in this regard since it only reports on state of charge when it last synced. Other than that the features on this watch was well worth the pain of learning the logic in the software!

title: Potentially solved the Low heart rate.. It's all about the band.
text: I have been a fitbit user for many years. Starting with the Fitbit Flex and then the Charge 3, 4 and now Sense. I wanted to try and stay in the same family of products to be able to compare to existing historical data and considered a few options before settling on the Sense. Now when I ordered the Sense I also picked up a cheap set of wrist bands from amazon to replace the silicon band that it come with. I always hated the silicon bands on previous models and I found a set that were similar to the ones I had for my Charge 3/4 that I enjoyed. I didn't think much of it as I didn't think it would matter. Well, I was proven wrong. The bands I got worked just fine for fit and my heart rate seemed normal when at rest or just doing daily tasks. However, when I would work out. My heart rate would show in the 80-90 bpm range under heavy aerobics. I could check with my pulse oximeter after a brief rest and still show 120+ bpm and show in the 70bpm rage on the sense. I switched back to the terrible band the sense comes with and it was better. bpm ranging in the 100 - 120 mostly. Peaking in the 130 bpm range. Closer to normal that I got on my Charge 3 & 4. But still low. no matter how snug I made the included band fit. The included band also would chafe where I didn't have that problem before. I really dislike the included band. I ended up ordering from Fitbit (Because I couldn't find any other sources for official Fitbit bands in my area). The hook and loop band. Now it is picking up my heart rate much more on point with what I was getting before on the Charge 3 & 4. My conclusion is for me, the included band and a cheap woven band off amazon sizing was just not right for my wrist. Thus not making the optimal contact to measure heart rate. I seriously don't know why they choose such a uncomfortable design for the included band. It is terrible.

title: Inaccurate data tracking - Pay wall - Battery issues - Fragile / Shoddy Materials
text: Don't waste your money on a fitbit, buy the Apple watch instead not just for the obvious digital connectivity/functional superiority of the Apple watch, but as a health tool my now 6 month old Fitbit Sense did not met my expectations for several reasons: (1.) The algorithm by which Resting Heart Rate is calculated is horribly flawed, especially for more athletic people who train at different intensities. Fitbit thinks my low intensity workouts represent my “resting” heart-rate. (2.) Useful features like Sleeping Heart Rate is hidden behind a monthly subscription “Premium” membership. Too bad because one of the few things fitbit guesses with better accuracy is when I am sleeping. (3.) The battery can drain entirely in less than a day rather than the several days it was supposed to last. The reason is accidental turning on GPS, which clicks on at various times without any reason nor my being aware of it, at which point the battery promptly drains to nothing. (4.) The watch construction is fragile and shoddy. The watch band disengages from the watch face without reason at the weirdest times. Normally it feels very tight and secure, then without any reason it just disengages and the watch comes loose. Caught it each time, the watch has not yet fallen to the ground when this happens, but if it did fall I am sure it would break the watch. A crack mysteriously appears completely across the face of the screen without any reason or cause last month. At first I assumed it was a scrape as I have reached into things like a gym bag and could have scraped against a zipper or car keys, but no, the screen is completely cracked through it's entire thickness, and now I am afraid to use it in/near water which partially defeats the purpose for buying a waterproof smart watch. Fitbit had no comment when I complained several times recently, they just reply in emails of garbled english saying things like “We have reviewed all the information and we'd like you to know that this type of inconvenient is not covered by fitbit.com, “ or “We understand your point of view in regards of this issue, for it, we have reviewed the warranty and it is not covered by the warranty.“

title: Check out the return policy before you buy
text: CHECK OUT THE RETURN POLICY BEFORE YOU BUY! I wore this for 1 hour and found it too big and bulky. No feature set is worth its ugliness. And, now I can't return it. I really wish I hadn't purchased this. The information should make clear that the only condition under which you can return it is if it's not functioning.

title: Not Waterproof!!!!
text: I bought my Versa 2 less than 2 years ago (from Costco, so I'm not a "verified purchaser" on Amazon) and there are many features I like. However, the first time I wore it in a swimming pool, it died immediately. The one-year warranty had expired. Fitbit offered me a 35% discount on my next Fitbit product, but that's not much of a consolation when you spend $150 on a watch that lasts less than 2 years. Apparently that's what I get for taking Fitbit at its word that the Versa 2 is "swim proof."

title: DO NOT Buy if you want SPO2 Monitoring! FALSE ADVERTISING!!!!
text: I upgraded to this model because I needed the SP02 monitoring. First I couldn't get it to connect to my Home WIFI even when I created a Specific Dumbed down portal. Then when I went to a second location I was finally able to connect to the WIFI and Download the App and the SP02 faces however I have Not yet been able to get a single reading! I have tried the original band, 2 different leather bands. Uninstalling and re-installing my Fitbit app, Resetting the Fitbit itself. Everything I can think of and it does not work!!! Furthermore, Fitbit blames my WIFI for the problem or has just written me off since I never got a reply to my last email (They replied that they were working on it but then nothing after that.) Additionally it seems to have battery issues. Some times it will have battery that lasts for 2-3 days and other times I can't even get a full 12 hours!! I wish I had returned it instead of trying to fix the problem. Interesting Note: In their advertising they have removed the Sp02 notice. The reason is that MANY people have defective devices that CANNOT or DO NOT ever measure the Sp02. I have been in contact with them since JUNE and in addition to taking anywhere from 48 hrs to 3 weeks to get back to you (Which means you cannot return it because they will take over a month to answer you!!) this is their latest response to my question on when they expect to get this KEY feature working: "we would like to apologize for the inconvenience that this issue has caused you. We would like you to know that we don't have any updates on when this issue will be resolved or the exact time frame, we are working the fast as possible to find a fix soon." Lots of pretty word to say... It doesn't work and we don't know how to fix it or even if we can ever fix it!! Well, that's $200 I'll never get back!!

title: Clock is constantly off (5-20 minutes)
text: I purchased the watch a couple weeks back, and I might have just got unlucky, but unfortunately the clock consistently gets behind (5-20 minutes). When you get the watch connected to your phone and sync it manually, the clock catches up, but not for long. I reached out to Fitbit's customer support and they confirmed that the device is most likely defective, and promised to reach out to me over email with the instructions for how to proceed with the return or replacement, but they never did. So, I am returning the device via Amazon now. That is quite sad because I have been a happy owner of Fitbit Charge 3 for 2 years, and have never experienced any issues with that one (also bought on Amazon back in 2018). But based on my experience with the Sense and Fitbit's support, it's probably time to try something else now.

title: Great upgrade!

title: Broke immediately, no repair/replace options

Mine broke from being set on the counter too hard… My family owns 6 Apple Watches and have never had this problem. Don’t buy this trash product.

I find it super annoying. Also, I bought clock faces on their app and hot dang are they a pain in arse to download, use codes, pay for and then use. What a rip. But it makes a decent watch.

title: Device failed 4months later.

Something is totally wrong and I do everything to prolong the battery life. Yesterday evening was still 56% and in the morning 5%!!! That is rediculous for a price of $200 (special offer). I'm looking for a better one!!!

title: No comment. I’ve not yet used it.🤔🙈
