title: It's what I thought it would be
text: If you read my other reviews, you'll note that I *rarely* give low marks and that's very relevant here. I had specific, narrow-focus interests defined for this purchase, researched that interest with as much care as possible, made a purchasing decision based on those interests and got exactly what I expected. Reading reviews like this are one small part of making that decision, which is why I'm posting mine. Doing that is why I so rarely buy something I don't like. Due diligence. I'm not rating the app or the sleep tracking because I don't use them. No idea if they work. I don't care about how it interacts with my phone, because I don't want to be seen talking to my wrist and with eyes well over 60 years old I'm not reading my SMS on a screen this small, tyvm. The specific features this model offers which *are* relevant to me over other models - you can infer them from what I haven't mentioned yet - work well and cost less to have than the offers from competitors, most of whom also think you want to be Dick Tracy. The white/gold aesthetic is minimalist while at the same time receiving compliments from casual observers, and I agree with them. If it gets dirty, I run it under the faucet and clean it. No biggie. Special mention should be made of the included bands. I'm a man of small stature - 170cm - and did not have to resort to the "small" band, instead using the "large" band on its' second-smallest setting. Fits my particular wrist better that way, although I can also fit the "small" band with less overlap than the attachment regimen (excess band under rather than over) allows. It fits better that way for me, but the important point is that it's difficult to imagine many human beings exist who can't leverage one or the other. On the wider settings the darn thing falls off my wrist. *Major* adjustability. It struck me as intelligent design and packaging. It's what I wanted, and what I thought I was going to get. YMMV if if you want a crossfunctional, true "smartwatch," which case might justify spending more money on the main competitors' (admittedly quality) offerings. This one works for me, because I did my due diligence.

title: ECG not available in my country
text: The only reason I decided to buy this dollar store knock off version of an Apple Watch was because of the ECG functionality. I have an elderly family member that was close to dying from afib related heart issues and needed to monitor her heart health. So I bought this Fitbit and brought it to the other side of the world to give it to my aforementioned family member. Turns out, the ECG functionality is not available in some countries. Why they didn’t make this more apparent is a poor choice on their part. Best part is, my trip back to the states wont be until after the return window closes so maybe I’m stuck with this POS.

title: Missing charger
text: Just opened and found box was missing charger, return window has closed.

title: 5 years user
text: I have been using Fitbit for about 5 years now. My latest model is Sense. I monitor my sleep, my heart beatings and steps. I am currently on a 400+ days of walking streak (10,000 or more steps). The great thing is that I only have to charge the battery once every three days.

title: A little disappointed.

title: Decent smart watch

text: I loved the watch for the first 8 months. But now the watch band keeps detaching from the watch- several times a day! It has fallen to the floor many times and it is just a matter of time before the watch itself breaks. This is not what I expected from a watch I paid this much for!

title: Totally died after 14 months
text: It totally died after only 14 months (and not covered under the Fitbit one-year warranty). Got it for my 40-year-old daughter who went into heart failure after Covid. Got the best Fitbit for heart that was offered at the time, and it failed way too soon.

title: WAS a great Watch but is no more
text: I was very happy but will charge no more have not had it for a year. I put numerous chargers and as each quit I bought another. Now I see why they sell two chargers at a time. I highly recommend a warranty. I am very disappointed I have had FitBit Watches for years and this one is a loser. I bought it November 3rd 2021 and it is only June 15 2022 today.

title: Love it - but daily restart and connection issues...
text: I love Fitbit; been using them for years. It would be 5-star if I didn't have to restart it on a daily basis. I've never had as many sync issues with any of the earlier models as I do with this one. The daily 250 steps-per-hour tracking does not refresh daily so I have to restart it every morning. Annoying. Especially because it took a while to even figure out the exact spot my fingers have to be to get it to restart. 🤷🏼‍♀️ I constantly receive the "connection lost" alert... With the big red button that I have to press to get main screen back. Not sure what that is. A little annoying. Also, I never really had to have a protection screen with the others; this one tends to hit everything (maybe because it's larger; sticks out more from wrist?) and I had little scratches already a few weeks in. I did get a protection screen after that. The Versa 2; no screen protector and not one scratch. I kid you not. See pics. Thought I was getting slate grey protector... 🤣 So it's silver... 🤦🏼‍♀️ That being said; I still love Fitbit and will most likely upgrade again in future. Been using these for at least 8 years now and I'm a sucker for the upgraded watches. 🤣 I also have Fitbit Premium (took advantage of the free trial); took the advice to raise my daily steps goal from 10,000 to 15,500 to get to my goal weight and it worked! Oh, the main reason I upgraded to this one was to detect A-Fib... Turns out you have to go to an app on the watch to then place your fingers on the watch on certain spots on corners and then it detects it. Well, when I feel the weird heart beat skips/speed-up/slow-downs and I get to the app and try to catch it, I never can because it's over! I hope in the future it just dectects this right from the wrist! More of a curiosity than a fear for my health; I'm very healthy, not overweight or anything like that. Doctor told me not to worry about it. Anyhow, still recommend the Sense, if you can get over having to restart it daily... And don't want it to detect A-Fib in any effective manner. 😊

title: Does the voice does not keep accurate track heart rate.

title: Love!

text: Bought this for my wife for Christmas. She loves it. She had the Charge 3 I think before this. The battery life is better than I expected(I have an Apple Watch). It easily lasts longer than mine.

title: Disappointed
text: Daily use, however it is not available for return or refund. I knew within a week that this was not what I wanted.

title: Can't go Phoneless
text: After reading quite a few reviews I was misled that I could add my own music to the device, but it has become very clear that you cannot (without subscription to Deezer, which I don't want). So, you can't use the 2.5GB for your own data, just the data you upload through a subscription service. And then, you can have a GPS on the watch, but not a simple MP3 player. I prefer to listen to music while I run, it would be nice not to have to compromise so much on such a simple feature. I even attempted to develop my own MP3 player for the watch, and it is clear there is no way to do so (limiting app storage and no audio API).

title: Beware, this is a sealed unit and you can not replace the battery. 5 month throw away
text: Many of the features were borderline in accuracy but the most alarming fact is regarding the battery. I should have read reviews on that. For the price, you would think that this watch should last a few years. But, it is sold as a sealed unit and when the battery goes, you toss it. I have had mine less that 6 months and the battery is already having problems taking a charge. A Rolls Royce is a "sealed" engine, but at least you receive the value paid before something has to be repaired on it and it can be repaired. This is a joke.

title: Cool Idea, But Doesn't Work
text: If all of the features this thing is supposed to have worked, it would be great, but they don't. The biggest annoyances right now are the slow charging and the SPO2 not working. The slow charging is a crap-shoot; sometimes it will charge normally, but most of the time it gives a warning that it is slowly charging, and it doesn't matter what USB charger or port I use. The battery only lasts about three days between charges, and I don't use notifications, quick-look, or most of the other battery-draining features. The SPO2 worked for a few weeks, and then stopped reporting. Support had me uninstall and reinstall the app, and restart the watch in between every step and after completing. It takes several nights of data gathering before you know whether it was successful or not. It worked for a few more weeks, and now it hasn't reported SPO2 data for several days, so I just went through the process of reinstalling again. This sucks. For several hundred dollars, I expected it to work.

title: Definitely not their best
text: I have had Charge 2 & 3 over the years and loved both. Never missed an alarm. This thing, however, died in less than 24 hours requiring a charge. title: Absolute TRASH...if you actually want something that works, look elsewhere
text: So I got this on Prime Day based on the reviews and it was a stellar deal. Boy, was that a mistake. The FIRST watch's Sp02 monitor just up and quit working. The REPLACEMENT watch was way worse: it kept disconnecting from Bluetooth, it turned itself on and off - usually, when I was in the middle of exercising, it's a FITNESS WATCH, so my stats were gone, the screen wouldn't come on 3/4 of the time unless I basically shook it even though it wasn't on "Manual mode", it didn't consistently send me "reminders to move" throughout the day as I had it programmed to do, it didn't send me reminders to get ready for bed as it was programmed to do, the silent alarm never once worked on either watch, the sleep tracking is pretty iffy, there were many nights I was up and down multiple times and tossing and turning and it gave me a "great" sleep score. Yeah, according to who??! Then nights when I felt reasonably rested even though I didn't get a lot of sleep, it said it was only "good". So basically, it goes off the amount of TIME you're lying down to "score your sleep". Do yourself a favor and HARD PASS on this piece of junk until Fitbit goes back to the drawing board and corrects the flaws in this hot mess. But hey, at least it looks nice.

title: Great smart fitness watch.

title: Third fitbit sense in 2 months, faulty battery life
text: ***Update*** My sense is lasting less than 24 hours with out charging it, the batter is once again breaking, after less than a month of having it. This is the third fitbit sense I have had to return. I purchased this smart watch five days ago, and I have been using it for three days, almost continuously. I have enjoyed some aspects but disliked others. The major issues that I have with the device are as follows: I have to repeatedly re-sink it with the app, and it doesn’t always accurately read my biometrics accurately, and lastly, it seems to drain my phone battery more quickly even when I have the settings state not to run in the background. I have an iPhone 10. Its frustrating to always have to re-sink my phone, but if I enable background refresh it will more quickly drain my phone battery. And as for the biometrics it is having problems recording my base core temperature and heart rates, as well as steps I have taken (I have a phone app and basic pedometer to base this around). On the hand, there is a lot of praise to give this device, as well. For starters, I greatly enjoy the access to countless apps at the reach of my wrist, it is helpful when I need the help of Alexa, and listening to Pandora as I work out. I also enjoy how it looks, the sleek design, and the third party accessories make it fun to change around and play with. I also enjoy the strap far better than I did with my Fitbit versa 3 I purchased a year ago. Overall, I am neither satisfied nor disappointed with this product with less than a week into utilizing it. As time progresses I will be more concise with my review.

title: Ended up buying 3
text: My wife liked hers so much I had to buy one for the grandkids too. They are all very happy with it. Would definitely buy one again

title: LOVE IT
text: It's amazing does everything it says it does, I had an ionic, the only thing that I miss is the fact that I could just send my music to the watch. I guess I'm okay with paying for Deezer because you can upload your own music to Deezer and then download it onto your watch and then you don't have to have your phone with you when you run just pay the $6 a month. (And these are not that bad of a service)

title: Not a good product if you're actually active
text: When the Sense works and charges properly it's pretty cool. Loads of neat features, I love earning the stupid little badges and I like seeing how active I am during work. (I'm in Construction) The bad part? This device is ridiculously frustrating to charge. It uses this magnetic charging pad with 4 tiny pins on it. The pin holes on the back of the device constantly get clogged with sweat and oil from your body. It's worse if you are actually {GASP} ACTIVE! I have to keep a bottle of Isopropyl Alcohol at my desk and take it when I go out of town to clean the ports. Sometimes it takes several attempts to finally get a successful connection and even then, you come back an hour later only to find out it lost connection and isn't charging. What's even more frustrating, these types of issues have been around and complained about for a very long time. I'd love to hear why this can't use a form of inductive charging as so many other devices can. I'd even rather have a plug-in-type charger with a little rubber cover for the port. This is my second Sense and it will be my last. Time to look at other manufacturers, I hear Garmin makes good stuff. Buyer Beware!

title: Fitbit Sense
text: This is my 4th Fitbit in 8 years.They usually last about 2 years. This alone is a bad outcome. I liked the new Sense design. It is sleek, band is velvety smooth and a lot of watch faces to choose from. My biggest problem is sleep tracking. I don't know what they did to mess up but my Charge 2 is better. On average, it shows that I logged only 1 to 2 hours every night, which I know is not correct. If you nap less than hour, the chances of getting that logged in is pretty slim. Two days ago, I exercised about 90 minutes and my day step count was over 10,100. When I synced it with mu iPhone, my step count was stuck at 1868 steps. I quit sense and restarted. I quit my iPhone and restarted. Nothing changed. If I look at the chart there is definitely a big activity between 10 and 12 PM but my tallied daily step count was 1868, I called customer support. The person on the phone confirmed that my step count for February 1st was over 10K but he had no clue as to why the numbers did not match or Sense did not sync properly. He sent me a few emails which were totally irrelevant to the issue. in summary Sense is full of bugs and the company is clueless as to why they are happening. A new update: Now my Fitbit Sense is counting from 20 to 50 stairs climbed each day. I live in a two story house and go upstairs maybe twice a day. I rarely go outside due to pandemic. I have reduced my rating from 3 stars to 2 stars, I has Fitbit Versa, Charge and Charge 2 in the past. Sense is the worst of all Fitbits. Update: There is nothing that works properly on this device. Sleep tracking, number of floors climbed, steps taken all produce wrong results. Microphone is so weak, you can barely hear incoming calls. The worst Fitbit ever designed. This is the Boing 737 Max version of a watch.

title: Terrible warrantee service.
text: I bought the Fitbit Sense to replace my Fitbit Ionic which overheated and caused 2nd degree burns on my arm. I stayed with Fitbit mainly because of its Android compatatability, otherwise the Apple warches beat it hands down. The main features I bought it for are its steps, o2, and sleep monitoring none of which work very well. From day one the sleep record was wildly inaccurate and undependable, as was the steps feature. Steps uses both gps and arm motion to sense them. But can not differentiate other arm motions like raking the lawn or sweeping the steps from walking or running. Since I do a lot of work around the yard its misinterpretation of the mild exertion of everyday activities as long walks or runs gives false fitness info. The O2 sensor requires an extra $10 a month subscription and frankly doesn't work very well the watch also has a sensor that is used as an on/off switch and for other functions. From day one it was quirky and after a few days stopped working entirely. I phoned customer service numerous times and they could not solve any of these issues. The authorized a warrantee replacement which seemed punitive. I had to wait for a return box and label, another week of transit time, assessment time at fitbit and another week for them to get the replacement to me. Please remember this watch was defective from the gitgo, and was reported to them the second day I had it. After arguing with the rep and waiting on hold for well over an hour, I spoke to a Supervisor for another long session. The finally agreed to replace the watch immediately. It took most of a week to get it. The replacement had exactly the same issues! I had to jump through the same hoops, only more so and will be without a watch for another week. If you have an iPhone, buy Apple, if not try a Samsung watch, but avoid Fitbit like the plague.

I basically just wear it and check out the stats later. After a convo with customer service they informed me the advertised battery life is without all the apps running. Once I start running apps (which is the reason I got the device), it cuts down the battery life significantly. On the plus side, it charges extremely fast. Under an hour to charge the whole thing. I had a Samsung watch that I thought had bad battery life, but this is probably twice as bad. Granted the Samsung watch didn't have all these sensors. The other bummer is some of the cool features are only available with fitbit premium. They give you 6 months free but if you want the full capabilities of this device, be prepared to pay for that. If you don't want these features, you're probably better off buying a cheaper/different product. Overall, I am satisfied but hope they can improve the battery life with some firmware updates. title: If you're going to use this for hiking, read this first
text: I've been waiting several years for a wrist-worn GPS device that I could use while hiking, that I could use to navigate routes that I designed in BaseCamp, with high quality maps that worked similar to Google maps. When the Fenix 5X was released, I purchased one of the first units. For the most part, it works the way I would want, with one very large disappointment: while navigating a route, the Fenix gives turn-by-turn alerts (via a chime, vibration, and large black banner on the watch that takes up one third of the screen). These alerts can not be turned off without turning off all alerts on the watch. Turn-by-turn directions are great while driving, or biking, or even running, but I don't see the use while hiking. Most hikes are along established trails, so I'd like to be alerted if I'm off course, but that's it. You'd think you'd be able to reduce the alerts by reducing the number of waypoints, however when a route is uploaded to the Fenix, it takes it upon itself to add a bunch of additional points to the route, and with the watch alerting for each point, it doesn't take long for it to get annoying. If I were hiking with someone that had an electronic device chirping every few minutes, I wouldn't want to hike with them for long. I'd like to think this is a bug that will get fixed, but Garmin has released several versions of the firmware and it hasn't changed, and they haven't given any indication it ever will. Other than this issue, the Fenix is a great product, but this issue is a huge one for me.

title: This is a commitment watch. *** Added Pictures of 5 and 5s demo unit***
text: I've been rocking the Fenix 5 for about 3 weeks and I am very pleased with it. I came from the Nike Apple Watch Series 2 and have no regrets. I previously used the Garmin 235 but returned it due to the crappy back light and switched the Nike Apple Watch - (just to save my Nike Run history). I then purchased the 935. The back light was fantastic but was afraid of the plastic built quality and went for the Fenix 5. Fenix 5 feels great! Sturdy, reliable (unlike Apple watch, too many Nike run crashes), ridiculously long battery life, awesome backlight. I have three comments for the watch though: 1. Too expensive and pricing scheme is all screwed up. I would think 5s, 5 and 5x would have three prices due to size differences, battery life and minor feature (ie 5x with 16gb maps storage). 5s should be $499, 5 - $599 and 5x-$699 with sapphire default. My opinion. 2. Size - I'm a small guy with small wirst. I should really get the 5s, but extra screen real estate and battery life for the same 5s price made me go with the 5. 3. Should have included onboard memory for music storage for the price. At the end of the day, do I really need the Fenix 5 and do I really use all the features? Probably not. This watch is more of a commitment watch. Keeps me active and helps me train. I am also a watch enthusiast and surprisingly the Fenix 5 competes well for my wrist time against the SeaDweller and GMT. All in all great watch and fun watch to own. See pictures - added 5 and 5s comparison on my small wrist. Demo units at local store

I wanted a purely Data analyzing beast of a watch to monitor my heart rate, VO2, recovery rate, training performance, and historical record for cycling. I have a Polar heart rate monitor with a chest strap and the Fenix 5 doesn't capture the peak levels as accurately, the averages over a 10,20 and 40mile ride are exactly the same. I love the data collected by the Fenix watches but the battery life on this watch was not as advertised. I put in 3 rides (10,20, and 40) and 1 walk and the watch was drained after 5 days. This is very disappointing for such an expensive watch. Will charge to full again and test another week to see if the numbers remain the same. Overall love the data disappointed with the battery life. UPDATE (11/24/2020) -- wrist heart rate monitor stopped working. I even went to settings, sensors and accessories, wrist heart rate monitor, and set it to auto. No green lights showing up on the bottom and the heart rate monitor is dead.

PRESET PROGRAMS: the Jumpmaster for skydiving cannot be modified to be used for paragliding or hangliding; it has the most complex functions for going down, but cat be modified for updrafts? An incredible shame... 3. FACE DISPLAY: likewise, the "homepage" can display all sorts of things, but NOT the heartbeat which would be a primary function in my everyday life 4. MUCH TOO COMPLICATED: there's a predfined "hike" and a "climb" function but no indication as to when one goes from one to the other: I rock climb, ice climb, mountaineer, and occasionally walk up to 8 hours in cities...when should I use which function, and what is its purpose? 5. HEALTH STATS seem bogus: Fenix says I have 24/7 stress with zero rest, while recording up to 11 hours of sleep. Inconsistent! A nice yuppie toy perhaps a bit more useful for hyperathletes in training - but then again only for pretty standard activities. Definitely NOT recommended for adventurers.

title: Another Amazing Garmin Watch
text: Looks incredible, software functions well and is easy to use.

title: My 50 year old son LOVES this
text: My son is training for a triathlon , he loves this watch for that reason, works perfectly, and he likes the size, and light weight.

title: Watch band holders break regularly under normal use; buy a 12-pack when you order watch.
text: I like this watch a lot, BUT -- the garmin connect app is not as reliable as it should be. It's glitchy, and can go down for several days at a time. The watch HR is not accurate nor reliable -- the chest band is the only reliablly accurate way to track HR. But mostly, the biggest problem is a small but inexcusably recurring one -- the watchband fastener ring -- the little thing that keeps the loose tongue of your band from flopping around -- breaks about 2x per year. It did the same on the Garmin watch I had before this 5 version. I rinse my watchband daily. I don't have "acidic" or "corrosive" skin oils or perspiration. I'm not one of those people whose sweat stains or discolors clothing. Yet, the band fastener breaks like it was designed to self-destruct twice a year. Garmin -- please include half a dozen free watchband fasteners with every order of watches. The quality control on them is horrible, and there's no excuse for it except being cheap and indifferent to customer satisfaction.

title: Amazing fitness watch
text: I love this watch! Helps me track my exercise and my steps! Love the challenges with my friends! Strongly recommend!

title: Good, but still wanting.
text: Works well as a GPS watch. Still a bit off the mark as a fitness device. HR tracking can lag actual rate if doing other than steady state work. Sleep tracking lacks spO2 measurement like the newer devices have.

title: Great for 1/2 price, meh for full
text: I bought this while on a deal here on Amazon, and I don’t regret it. Would it be worth full boat price.....no. It’s nice, burly, and has great battery life. It’s screen isn’t great quality. Very large pixels, and not as great looking by any means as an IWatch. Also no touch screen like an iWatch. But 12ish days of wearing between charges if used as a watch, unlike the iPhone (you’d be lucky to get 2 days). It had tons of fitness tracking feature which are great if you have nothing to track your fitness. I primarily bike and have a bike computer and chest strap heart rate monitor for it. That is how I know the heart rate on this is solidly 20-25 beats off when out exercising, which kinda sucks. I would hope for closer (my chest strap is also a Garmin) readings. So it looks impressive, the screen is underwhelming, it does a ton if you don’t have anyway to track, but isn’t crazy accurate for heart rate (gps tracking is spot on). For half price totally worth it, for full price.......

title: Five Stars
text: I absolutely love my fenix. Use it daily to track everything.Great motivator.

title: Meh...
text: Watch is pretty good but overpriced and the battery life is horrible. I only get 5 days before it dies and that is doing nothing with GPS. Garmin has not answered my email either. I would not recommend it. I would say look around because there are many alternatives for way less money.

title: amazing watch
text: if you got this watch you will never think to change it ever. i have fenix 3 used it for 2 years and i got fenix 5.

title: Not working
text: I used this for a couple of golf rounds. It's hard to find the golf course. Sometimes it finds the golf course but it doesn't show the golf course name. Thus it shows the wrong distance to the green.

title: Worth $129 not $600
text: It was great but for two weeks then Garmin did software update and the watch became the worst fitness tracker ever. It was off on a wrist based heart rate by 50-70 bpm. Didn't count all my steps. It does not register all the raps and can not figure out which exercise I am doing. The new update won't come out until four months from now according to Garmin rep. Then if you travel to a different time zone, the phone needed to be reset and set up again, loosing any data you had on the phone or watch. The screen is hard to see indoors unless it is lit. $600 for this crap? No thanks. Bought the watch in August, it stopped working properly in September, no update until January 20. This is unacceptable for a device that costs $600.

title: Way too glitchy
text: This watch seemed like it had everything, but it ended up being very “glitchy” and not very functional. Toggling between features is very cumbersome and it’s seems to steer me toward shutting down once it gets “confused”. Would not recommend.

title: Best smart active watch ever!
text: This watch isnt for everyone, but it's perfect for me! Just watch the reviews on you tube. You won't be disappointed if you are the right person for this watch. And even if you think your not, still give it a try if you want an upgrade from that fit bit or Apple Watch. I came from a pebble watch.

title: Best sports watch
text: Very good and premium watch. It has nice fit. Should have gotten this early rather that waste money in getting the fenix 3 HR

title: Great watch - wish the battery lasted longer
text: This is my first Fenix - I upgraded from a Forerunner 230. I primarily wanted a watch with a longer battery life that you can charge during an activity. After I bought the watch, I was disappointed to realize the Fenix 5X has a shorter battery life than the Fenix 5. (20 hrs vs 24 hrs). I am assuming it is because the Topo maps are a battery hog. I had a chance to try this watch out at a 100-mile race last weekend. I turned off a few features to extend the battery life including the HR monitor. I recharged the watch after running for 18 hours - it was at 25% battery life, so I guess it could have lasted for about 24 hours total. It did take a while to recharge. I was charging it for about 2 hours and it got up to 57% battery - note that the watch was still running during this time. The watch was very accurate - the course is measured at 101.85 miles and the watch measured 101.8. It might have just omitted the last decimal, so for all I know it could have been exactly right. The watch looks really cool and I like the feel of the buttons - they are easy to press while sweaty and are hard to press by accident. The watch is bulky, but I am getting used to it. All in all, it's a great watch. As an Ultrarunner, I recommend it.

title: Amazon has sent me two defective out of the box
text: My first one, the battery wouldn’t charge over 30%. This includes leaving it on the charger overnight. So the “9 day” battery life only lasted a couple of days before another all day or overnight charge. I ordered a replacement for the defective one that arrived right before a busy few days at work. Left it on the charger for 3 days before I was able to get back to it. 70% battery. After 3 full days of charging. A $300+ fitness tracker shouldn’t be this bad out of the box. And I shouldn’t need to charge it for over 8 hours every other day. Disappointing.

title: Amazing Watch!
text: The Garmin Fenix 5x Sapphire is an amazing watch to own! I've had mine since April 2017. A lot of the activities are programmable to tailor your data screens for when you work out. Battery life is great! I've gone 2 weeks on a charge, but mostly lasts a week during heavy use. Perfect! Well done Garmin.

title: After six weeks I have really grown to like this watch
text: After six weeks I have really grown to like this watch. Best hybrid of sports monitor as well as smart watch. Moved to it from a traditional android smart watch. It is a little clunky (no touchscreen, so you need to navigate via buttons and no microphone--so if you like to Dick Tracy texts into your smartwatch, this won't do it for you), but after six weeks, I am fully used to it. Better than my previous Forerunner in terms of pre-loaded sports as well as satellite reception. Gets push notifications and has several hundred apps that can be downloaded from Garmin IQ to add customization. I got the 42mm size, which is perfect for an every day wearer. In terms of sturdiness, the thing appears to be a tank (I have sapphire model). And battery life is outstanding--a week plus if I am not running the GPS. As for sports activity monitoring...it is perfect. Has every sport imaginable, so you set it before starting and it is there on Garmin Connect/Strava/MapMyRide almost as soon as you finish. Great all around choice if you are trying to decide between smartwatch and sports-monitoring watch. I do wish they had more variety for the "quick-fit" straps on the 42mm. The only choice for dressing it up is the grey suede, which I may end up ordering.

title: Great purchase so far!
text: I waited almost a year to buy the Garmin Fenix 5s and did a lot of research on this watch and others with similar features. I love this watch! It's a great size for a woman, still a bit bigger but not nearly as bad as the regular unisex version. It's easy to navigate and the battery life is great. I did need to do a workaround to get only certain notifications to my watch instead of all of them. I would love to have that feature in the app but unfortunately, it's not available yet. Otherwise, I love the color and the ease of switching bands. I just recently bought it so I haven't used all of the active features yet, so I don't feel comfortable speaking to that at this point. Overall, I'd recommend!

title: Very very happy
text: The Fenix 5X is a great fitness watch. I wear it all the time. Awesome app and great utility. I bought this instead of upgrading my Apple watch. I'm so glad I chose Garmin!!!

title: Impressive watch
text: Garmin has hit a home run with this model. Its everything and so much more

title: App is deadware
text: The watch is awesome. The Android app is pure garbage. You've been warned.

title: Not great exercise features. No swim
text: Ad says swimming and does not have a swimming Option. False misleading adverts. Otherwise the watch was nice but didn’t have what I needed and why I ordered it.

title: More (fun) options in the Health App!
text: First off, this is a great fitness tracker and you get the top quality of exercise and sleep tracking (much better than Xiaomi band 5). After setting the region of Health app to China, I get to add new watch faces and participate in various fun activities (love the world road map game!). The way to change the region of the app is as follows: 1) Re-download the Health app; 2) Turn flight mode on; 3) Open the Health app; 4) You will be prompted to set the regions; 5) Choose mainland China; 6) Turn off flight mode and connect to the internet; 7) Optional: register for an account; 8) Now we get to download new watch faces, etc. in USA! Hope this helps!

title: Avoid seller. Defective product

title: Great tracker - is it for you?

Pros: Price Light and comfortable Great battery life – talking 1-2 weeks, even with gps use 3-5 days. Nice display Simple to use as is Huawei health app. Accurate features Cons Does not pick up steps if pushing a cart - I would assume the same for a stroller. No altitude Limited watch faces in the US A few words about the Huawei health app. I like it, coming from Samsung Health. Everything is ready to find. There was so much on the Samsung app, this is simple. No forum, work out . You can share info. Basic and ask info right there. Think about that part. I am very happy with it.

title: Made with real Cheese
text: Watch Looks nice but as soon as you pick it up you feel how cheap it is made, Im pretty sure the watch face is plastic and not glass, it sounds like it anyways when you tap on it. It weighs 99 grams which is 5 grams more then my Apple series 2 watch but the apple watch definitely feels a lot more solid. It took a couple of tries to get everything to pair up but it was good after that. My biggest complaint is that I have to raise my wrist several times to get the display to light, its just easier to push the top button to activate it. I never used the workout feature and the weather feature keeps saying its not paired, you shouldn't have to repeatedly pair a watch over and over. Im used to wearing much more expensive watches, I have two Breitlings and at least six citizen watches, 1 oakley watch and an Apple watch and all of them feel really solid and have some weight to them except the apple watch which is pretty light too but still feels like its put together well. This watch seems to work ok and so far the battery has been good on it but to be honest I have only worn it for maybe a day and a half and slept with it on once for the sleep app which isn't as accurate as the Apple watch. If your short on cash and don't mind how plasticly it feels then maybe it will work for you. For the price you do get a lot of features though. Having to re pair over and over for the weather to work and shaking my wrist to get it to light is a deal breaker for me so Im returning it. Hope this helps someone out.

title: Adequate for the price
text: This is a good watch for the money. Tracks your steps, blood pressure, oxygen level just fine. Not so great for making calls, but it's only a $58 watch so if you want more buy a more expensive watch.

title: The connection with bluetooth
text: As long as the watch is connected to bluetooth there is no problem, but if you disconnect the bluetooth you cannot reconnect it you have to restart the watch again

title: Keep looking

No other app notifications on it. Battery dies fast. Doesn't always light up when turning the wrist to see the time.

title: Yes, it is worth a try.
text: I haven't broken it yet, which is a compliment coming from a clumsy brute who wrestles with folks for a living.

title: Ladies, not sure which size to choose? Please read my review for answers!
text: The biggest issue I had was to decide which size to choose, the 40mm or the 44mm. I did plenty of research, watched videos (96% were done by guys and only showed bigger wrists), read reviews, checked reddit etc, but I still couldn't make up my mind. My wrist is barely 6 inches in circumference, so it is small. I first purchased the 44mm because of the better battery life (so they say) and it did fit on my wrist. It looked however a little "cartoonish" due to the big size. It also felt heavy and since it was so big I would have bumped it against things a lot, because the watch was basically the same width as my wrist. I played around with it for a day and while the features were fantastic, the size just didn't feel right. So I returned it. I now received the 40mm one and I LOVE the size. It's big, but not humongous and HERE is something I haven't seen in other reviews: I was worried that my older eyes would have trouble with the slightly smaller watch face, BUT if you quickly tap 3 times on the screen, it magnifies the letters/numbers (if needed) which is awesome! You can see the difference it in the 3rd and 4th picture. So the 4mm difference really does not matter when it comes to reading. That's a fantastic feature I must say! The watch comes with a shorter strap than the 44mm which fit my small wrist perfectly. I replaced the black strap with a wine colored (small) one I found here on Amazon (Brand is NANW and it comes in a 3 color pack). I love the color combination. The shorter battery life doesn't bother me since I charge my phone once a day and do the same with the watch. A full charge lasts about 1.5 days, but I prefer to charge it daily... just in case. So if your wrist is 6 inches or smaller, go with the 40mm watch. If your wrist is 6.5" and you really love huge watches then go with the 44mm. For wrists 7 inches plus I would definitely recommend the 44mm. If my review helped you with the decision please click "helpful". Have fun with your new smartwatch!

title: Great for tracking sleep and heartrate
text: So far so good. It can hold up to my on the go style. I'm appreciative of the water proof feature. It even expels the water. While the screen has remained scratch free the edges of the bezel has a couple of scuffs. The screen is clear and easy to read. The vibration is perfect as a silent alarm.

title: Meh
text: I'll start by saying that I'm a harsh critic of smart watches since I look for very specific features so take what I say with a grain of salt. I look for the following in a smart watch: - at least one day battery life: this watch succeeded at that but in offline mode + GPS it lasts at most 2.5 hours so not great for marathons - offline mode GPS: I want to be able to run without carrying a phone which means the phone should have offline GPS mode for Strava and for offline Spotify listening. This watch has both but it's extremely unreliable. That is, both of these apps (and most others tbh) will crash randomly. This is particularly annoying with Strava since you can end up losing a 6 hour hike's worth of data. - a good UI and OS: while the watch has a beautiful UI, the Samsung OS is pretty invasive and annoying to use. It requires a half dozen apps to connect to your phone and even once it does it forces you to get a samsung account. Then the app store is filled with a disgusting number of virus looking apps and watch faces that mostly have 1 to 2 star reviews. Overall, pretty unappealing. - comfort and look: pretty good in this field Overall, I wouldn't buy this watch again. Not that there're many out there that would beat it, but as of now this watch is too unreliable.

title: Horrible step counting!
text: These watches suck at counting steps. I have already sent one back for repair, it still didnt work so bought another one, and it sucks at tracking as well. Not sure what the deal is, but I am definitely not satisfied with step tracking. Also, the second one I purchased didnt even have a charger with it. Not satisfied at all. Will be looking into a different brand.

title: Great product but check phone compatability if looking to use ecg feature.
text: Purchased this mainly for the ecg function. Like the watch. Comfortable, easy to use, but returned because my phone was not compatible for the ecg feature. But if you are just looking for a reasonably priced, comfortable, and easy to use smart watch I would gladly recommend this one.

title: Doesn't use heart rate to calculate calorie burn
text: For an active workout watch, it's difficult to believe it doesn't use your heart rate/effort to calculate calorie burn. Just uses a generic calculation. Wrist strap needs more smaller size holes.

title: Samsung Galaxy Active 2
text: My husband pur hased one first. He loved it, so I decided to get one. It doesn't disappoint. Great purchase !!

title: Great watch. I recommend
text: I use mine everyday and track my steps . I love this watch telephone. I even bought one for my friend .

title: This is just a watch not for fitness
text: I was using a fitbit before my husband bought this for me as a gift. I was making great progress with the fitbit because of how it tracked calories. It would calculate intake vs burned. This will calculate both but separately. I researched online and it used to have more fitness functions (including calculating calories) but samsung removed them. It also doesn't sync with the alarm app and the alarm sound settings can only be changed for alarms set on the watch. There are also fitness goals that don't sync with the samsung health app. Like you set different goals on the watch vs in the app.

title: Battery Wouldn't Hold A Charge
text: Bought for my daughter - she told me the battery wouldn't hold a charge more than a few hours, no matter what she tried. Software updates didn't help. As this is apparently a common problem with this watch, we returned it.

title: It was great! Until... not so much
text: This watch was amazing in the beginning. I could charge it and use it moderately for two days. I didn't really spend a lot of time on it, but I used it to give me notifications for texts and apps, when my phone was on vibrate and I didn't notice. It seems constructed well, and worth the buy... but that changed about 2 days ago. I haven't even used this watch for 3 months, and it's broken. I was walking and touched a wall (I didn't intend to touch the wall, I just hit my hand when I was walking.) Sure enough, small crack appears. Then less than an hour later it spirals across the whole watch face. Now I got a huge crack on this thing. I had many close calls, but I didn't expect lighting tapping a wall would be the end of this thing. Samsung makes great products in general, but this watch needs to be way more sturdy... for people that aren't sitting at desks all day.

title: nice
text: The health app works pretty good. I only wish the battery would last longer and that it had a BP option.

title: OMG!
text: We bought two of these. We were Fitbit people. But, Fitbit has lost ground and become very difficult to use. We were about to upgrade to their Sense from the Versa series, but became so frustrated we began looking for alternatives. We researched and researched! In the end, we took a chance on Samsung and went with the Active 2. We bought two of them. Now, there is a learning curve...we are not the most adept people with smartphones etc., but we're getting the hang of it. These smart watches are absolutely over the top! Truly, as we explore, I'm expecting to find a button we can push allowing this watch to jump off our wrists, vacuum the floors, empty the cat box and cook dinner. Well, maybe that's a bit high of an expectation, but they are unreal! The Galaxy Active 2 is not even their top of the line (I think the 3 and now the 4 are out), but they are just amazing. We got a good deal--great discount and I see very little difference between the Galaxy 3 at $350ish vs. what we paid ($179) each. Pros: ECG, Sleep is much more accurate than Fitbit, Steps are much more accurate than Fitbit; You can get the LTE version which gives you more accessibility/freedom from bluetooth/wifi set ups (as I understand). We went with bluetooth. Easy to charge, high quality band; made peace with the round watch face vs. square; awesome bezel, voice activation is available; many watch faces (via google wearable); O2 feature, B/P feature and on and on. Cons: battery not as long lasting as Fitbit, but easier/faster to charge; Samsung "community" not as accessible as Fitbit; it takes some focus to learn to use the features--thankfully YouTube is available; Wish they had compatibility with PC's and not just smartphones, but all the smart watches are abandoning Windows (it would appear). Galaxy Active 2= highly recommended--especially if you are using Samsung android phones.

title: Awesome watch highly recommend
text: Awesome watch I can do anything on it working out biking even check your heart ecg you just gotta download the app from galaxy store

title: Love it!
text: Upgraded from a Gear Fit2 Pro, fitness watch before that was a FitBit. FitBit died/fell apart, & had never really given me full satisfaction. Samsung Health app paired with the Gear Fit2 Pro gave me the reports I needed. After 2 years - became more & more difficult to charge, thus my excitement over the release of the Active2. Improvements I considered worth paying for: Wireless charging, charging through my Note 10+, audible alarms, more features. I am still learning more about what it is capable every day. JUST ONE negative comment... if you have continuous heart rate monitoring on - battery simply does not last. I need to recharge daily. As heart/sleep are my top 2 reasons for a fitness/smart watch, I understand the drawback to continuous monitoring. Just wish the battery stood up to this better.

title: Samsung lies about water resistance
text: Samsung touts this watch as having an IP68 and 5 ATM water resistance rating. The watch has a swimming tracker mode designed to track swimming. The watch also has Water Lock mode you are supposed to enable when planning to go underwater. The first time my wife ever used this in a swimming pool she enabled the water lock mode and got into the water. Within 2 seconds of her gently putting her wrist about 3 inches under the water, the watch made a strange series of sounds and then died. The screen will not turn on and it appears the electronics are completely fried. Samsung will not honor the warranty on the device even though it was used in accordance with all of their instructions and specifications. They claim the device is not meant to get wet despite their advertisements clearly showing the watch getting wet as well as advertising the swimming tracker mode. In fact, the official Samsung website for this device has a picture of the watches bobbing up and down in water. What a joke.

title: I like my watch alot
text: I like my watch a lot. I wish they had a better way to customize the watchface.

title: all right for the price
text: much better than garmin except for the battery life. very sleek and good performance

title: Terrible "active" watch
text: This watch does not accurately track calories burned. You can select a specific exercise, start it, then sit down in a chair and it would show the same amount of calories burned as it you actually did the workout. Samsung support with run you in circles and never actually fix the watch. They had me send it in once, sent it back, then it did the same thing and they told me to send it in again. Don't waste your money on this watch if you want it for more than just telling time.
