title: Not the greatest battery life, but great apps and functionality.
text: Love everything about this watch! I was worried about getting it wet after reading some of the comments. I forgot about taking it off before getting into a hot tub. After getting in and the watch vibrating, I got out and dried it off and checked it and it's been working great ever since. Would recommend this watch to anyone.

title: Good Hardware, Poor Software
text: This watch is probably the best option for an Android user so I bought it. But it's Samsung at the end of the day so expect poor product support after purchase. The watch has the hardware for an ECG but didn't activate it for a year after the launch. Even now the ECG works only for Samsung phones and not for non-Samsung phones. I bought this watch for the ECG only to wait for a year with still no guarantee that the feature will ever roll out. Also now that the Watch Active 3 has been released, I doubt Samsung would bother with updating the software for an older model. Samsung's continued efforts to sabotage their hardware with their pathetic software makes their product not worth buying or recommending. Will probably never buy a Samsung branded mobile or accessory again.

title: Does many things poorly and zero things well.
text: It's pointless. Just stick with your phone. The watch is extremely inefficient at everything it does. Most of the time the screen doesn't turn on when you want to look at the time, but turns on when you don't want to look at it. The strap that comes with the watch is infant sized. I took 2 steps and the watch counted it as 10. It told me I was stressed out when I was completely relaxed. It constantly harasses you to get up and walk around when you are working. I got mine for free from tmobile and still feel like I got ripped off.

title: Love the watch, battery life could be much better.
text: I love the watch but you have to charge it almost every other day. I don't have any apps running which would drain the battery. I guess it's just how it is!

title: Wife liked it so much she bought me one.
text: I bought my wife one for Christmas. She liked it so much she bought me one for my birthday. I gave it 4 stars for durability, we'll see how long the plastic strap lasts.

title: It's an excellent smartwatch
text: I normally don't write longer reviews, but I'm super happy with this watch. Yes, the sleep tracking works great, as well as the pulse feature and it's super handy to be able to get notifications from your phone on your wrist. Charge time and battery life are both really good. The more crazy you go with the apps the shorter the battery life will be. On rare occasion, I've used it to answer my phone when driving or my phone is in another room and it works well.

title: Don't swim with this watch!
text: watch broke after 1 month of use and Samsung wouldn't replace it or fix it due to water damage that voided the warranty. I went swimming once with the watch in "swim mode". I would not trust the swim mode on this watch and Samsung has really bad customer service.

title: Good watch!
text: Overall I'm happy with the watch because it does what I need it to do. The battery life could be better. I am also concerned I may have gotten a product that had been open because there was not a clear safety sticker on the face of the watch or back. But there was a clear safety sticker on charger??? I was given a month to return if need be.

title: This watch is okay.
text: It has more features then my previous watch....fitbit but they are harder to navigate and I don't like that it only tracks fitness when you activate it, unlike my previous watch. So, a few times I forgot to activate fitness and then had no data on workout. The texting and using for phone calls is cool and have no issues with that.

title: Overall a nice smart watch
text: This watch is a good blend between a smart watch and an activity tracker. My only complaint with it is that the battery does not last very long. I usually have to recharge it every day.

title: Useful and efficient!
text: I am REALLY enjoying this, and it's my first smart watch. I got it for the sleep tracking as well as stress checker, reminders and calendar. It is so cool all this watch can do! Syncs up with my phone. Lets me read and send texts and show off pictures of my cats. Easy to set reminders and calendar events. I didn't think the alarm would wake me up since it's quiet and I usually set my alarms max loud and obnoxious, but it does! Very useful when you and your partner keep different hours and you don't want to wake each other up. The customizable faces are a lot of fun. Can be as creative as I want.

title: I lost my money. Don't buy this product and this re seller
text: Terrible product and re seller. After 4 months the watch broken with any reason. It just stopped. I wrote them but they said is out of warranty because it was a used watch. Never nobody explained to me why the watch broken and who covered this problem. Very bad experience. I lost my money. I don't recommend them. I think the battery life dead. The broken was while I took a shower. Maybe entered water.

title: I LOVE THIS WATCH
text: I swirch from a Fossil Gen 2 smartwatch to this and what a HUGE difference!! I highly recommend! The battery life is amazing! I can go 2 days without thinking about a charger! I can track my sleep too! Couldn't do that with my Fossil. I love how affordable the protection plan is too with this one.

title: I use it primarily for workouts and it is great!
text: Not sure what all the hubub is about calorie counting. For my workouts, I have the calorie count on the watch and the elipitcal machine. I also compared it to sHealth app on my phone for the exact workout time and intensity. The watch had the lowest of all three. Ya know what, that is ok. I always thought the machine was unrealistically high anyhow. This thing tells me my heart rate when I am working out and I don't have to hold onto any sensors. I get the stats, I get them synced, I am working out more with the watch, etc. What more can I ask for from a watch? I really like how it tells me to stretch throughout the day and then gives me suggestions on which to do and then how many reps I should do. I also like how I can set my phone in my workshop plugged into the stereo and make a call from 30' away when I am on a ladder that I need an extra hand from my wife. I can control my music player too! I can respond to Messenger messages from my wife too. Again, it is great. The one down side, and perhaps I just have not found the feature yet, is that at nights when in bed it turns on every so often. Once I am asleep it is no big deal though.

title: Excellent
text: As good as advertised. Its high rating is well deserved.

title: I regret the purchase but can see how others like it.
text: This watch hits the okay mark on my needs. It doesn't seem to accurately count my steps or miles walked. It's sleep tracker assumes my laying down and relaxing is sleeping (I definitely don't get 10 hours of sleep per day). The text feature is okay. It works but is not very user friendly.

title: Samsung Pay is hopeless
text: I bought this in part to track my running (which it does well) and partly to use Samsung Pay (which it does not do well) I will be sticking to my debit card chip or my OnePlus phone and Google Pay Batter life is ok, but sometimes dies after less than 2 days.

title: Very fun!!
text: Has ALOT more features than my GearFit2. I like it a lot - has a lot more features,apps, settings, and enhanced sleep/workout tracker. Even the band feels more secure and I purchased a "scrunchie" band for it. I have a bumper and screen protector on it as well.

title: I love it.
text: Ok. People. I love this watch. I got the 40mm Aqua Black. I also purchased other bands and a gold bezel ring (it doesnt move,fyi) to give my watch some femininity. I am a review reader through and through so I understand it when people oversell something and its underwhelming. Ok, this watch though. Its super light weight. I have tiny wrists so I was afraid the 40mm would be clunky but it is very comfortable to wear. I read a previous review that said the Aqua black was more of a dark navy, and i totally agree! It is very neat and with the gold bezel, fits my ovarian needs. I wouldnt classify myself as super sporty but i am active. This watch is perfect for me and my lifestyle.

title: Subpar in Nearly Every Way
text: The only good thing about this watch is the screen. If you don't own a Samsung phone, the watch's advertised features and functionality will be crippled. Samsung launched the Active 2 with spo2/pulseox sensors enabled, then removed them from the app. Samsung requires multiple app downloads to use the device, and the apps are a buggy mess. The rotary touchscreen concept is brilliant in theory, but Samsung's user interface makes the watch difficult at best. While Android users will have slightly better luck using the watch for messaging, iPhone users should avoid this sloppy product altogether. Additionally, as noted in numerous other reviews, Samsung's warranty support is negligible and the company rarely honors claims it stands behind its products. Apple and Garmin, while higher cost up front, offer far superior products that will stand the test of time.

title: A great purchase
text: I love this watch. Synced to my phone easily. Keeps track of my activity when working out. So glad I bought.

title: Samsung Galaxy Watch Active2
text: This watch worked well for about two months. Then, without warning, the watch just quit working. It was always kept charged; was never abused, never subject to water, or any other inappropriate treatment. Attempts to contact Samsung were useless. Their support website simply doesn't work. All in all, this watch is an expensive ripoff. DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY!!!

title: All around a great watch
text: I'll keep it simple (Positives:) +Beautiful +Shows notifications +Can respond to text +The time and date + Tracks workouts +Tracks sleep (idk how accurate) +Tracks heart rate/ stress levels (idk how accurate) +Tracks steps and calories (idk how accurate) +Lots of widget choices +Charges fast (Negatives) -Ive been able to cancel and accept calls but not actually have the phone call on my watch (could just be me) -Horrible battery. It last a day or two. A day and a half maybe

title: Always enjoy Galaxy devices
text: Nice watch, haven't messed around with it much but it's comfortable, perfect size (40mm) for my wrist. For the people with tattoos on the wrist, the heartrate monitor will not read through the ink for some reason. I've tested it on multiple areas, new and old ink and right outside the ink it will read. That's one big drawback for me because I bought the watch mostly for that. Other than that so far it's great, more features than I'll utilize for sure.

title: Samsung Galaxy Active 2 40mm smartwatch is a great buy!
text: Before I get started. I am not by any means an expert on smartwatches nor do I even use all the features. I recently used a Samsung Frontier S3. I really like the size of it and I liked the dial around it that spins to move the screen around and I felt the dial or bezel whatever its called added a layer of protection. Here we go! Pros. I bought this watch for one reason only! The ECG which if the FDA doesn't mess this up will be activated via software update to detect irregular heart rhythms. Because I have Atrial Fibrillation and the Fall Detection because of Hypoglycemia (in cas I pass out from low blood sugar) I am hoping this will be beneficial to me. If not, Ill have a cool watch! Battery Life is amazing! Cons: 1. The 44mm looked to big or just weird in my opinion which it should have compared to my Frontier S3. 2. The 40mm looks a little small on my wrist but I can live it. 3. The apps don't seem that much different than the ones on the Frontier. I don't use the apps often just timem date and heart rate so don't take my word for that. I will say it was nice that the icons and all looked nearly the same so I didn't feel like I was learning a whole new system. 4. I miss the bezel from the Frontier but this watch was designed for Activity so I can live with it. Don't take all my cons and think this isn't a great watch. 1. I don't know much about smartwatches. 2. I really loved the Frontier S3 design. 3. If Samsung comes out with a watch like the Frontier with ECG, this watch will be for sale. I think its a great watch for those who are using it for the reasons it was designed for. The sale price I got this one for on Amazon made it hard not to buy it. All in all its a great watch despite my bias towards the old Frontier. EDITED TO ADD THE FOLLOWING: The battery life on this watch is amazing! I wore it all day and around 10:45 pm I took the watch off and still had 74% battery life left. It was connected to my phone the entire day.

title: After 2 months won't pair
text: I loved this for the first 2 months. It easily paired with my Samsung phones health app and worked well other than the sleep tracker, because it's dead by then, so there's no way it would make it 24 hours to actually track sleep. Now, 2 months later it impairs with the phone and the only way to re-pair is to reset the watch only to have it unpaired after a few hours. With a Samsung phone and pre-installed Samsung health app, I made the mistake of thinking a Samsung fitness watch would be seamless but it's anything but seamless. UPDATE: The beauty of Samsung and their product team is they listen and make adjustments as needed. I've had this for awhile now and after a system update or two, it's my favorite fitness tracker. I recently upgraded to a different phone and the connection was quick and easy.

title: Lasted 9 months
text: The watch worked for 9 months and then stopped suddenly. Although under warranty, with no damages by customer. The manufacturer refused to repair the watch. Disappointed!!!

title: Not bad, needs improvement
text: I have to charge the watch every other day. In my opinion, that is not long lasting as described. It also doesn't seem to record my sleep well, and I know the watch it tight enough, because when I take it off the strap is indented in my wrist.

title: Ditched my Versa 2
text: I ditched my Fitbit because I got tired of being technical support and rifling through forums for what seemed like constant connection issues. The walk tracker thinks I ran through neighborhoods for half the distance I went, or nothing at all, etc. This is fantastic. The screen is great, the app works perfectly, the watch is very snappy, it looks like a regular watch, and everything just works without fiddling. Set-up takes just moments. I guess you can't go too wrong using samsung products with a samsung phone.

title: It's not new!!!
text: It's beautiful even when I ordered in black and get a navy blue. The sleep tracking and mobile app are good, the battery life sucks. I can't use others health care apps instead of Samsung health. It's not new! it came without the plastic cover on the screen or on the sensor... A little disappointing...

title: great fitness watch!
text: if you are looking for a smart watch, then this is not for you. however, if you want a fitness watch, then get this one! the gps tracking is great and accurate! it takes a little bit to get used to the buttons and where all the settings are, but i love that i can customize it to do just what i want in terms of display, audio outputs, etc. the band is comfortable and the watch face is a good size to see my stats while working out without being overly cumbersome (i'm a small 5'0" female). i love that it can play my spotify playlists! the only thing of note is that it will not be able to get any data such as weather, sms notifications, calendar updates, emails, phone calls, or send emergency assistance notices unless you have your phone with you and connected via bluetooth. the point of this watch for me was to keep my phone at home so those features don't work during my run, but it does do the fitness tracking and play previously setup spotify playlists, so it's exactly what i want and need. i don't use it for sleep tracking since i only wear it during workouts. love the heart rate monitoring too!

title: great looking watch and great for running and biking
text: I really like this watch. I replaced and old forerunner. (many generation old) It feels great and looks good since you can download and tailor the watch faces. I have downloaded music to it using MediaMonkey and it worked fine. So far, synching with earbuds Jaybird Tarah Pro and Vistas, has been good. The availability of watch faces and activity widgets is nice. But Be warned, it takes a little bit to set it up and understand how to understand how to download and update activity widgets. Updating of watch faces isn't too bad. Be patient and read the user guide, there is a lot of functionality you should be aware of whether you use them or not.

title: Great purchase
text: Great, does all of the stuff running nerds love. Spotify is a hassle to sync when i want to adjust my playlists. This is especially annoying for podcast listeners such as myself. For this reason, I could have gone without the music upgrade and just used my phone but I still use the music feature a good amount for my shorter speed runs where I need the running jams! But obviously I didn’t take a star because Garmin is the GOAT

title: Sleep Tracking and Incoming Call Notification (on android) are EPIC failures
text: Overwhelming 5 start reviews really make me skeptical that the reviews themselves are genuine.... Overall the watch is not bad but really needs functional work. The Android Dev/QA team should have some re-training/structuring after releasing this to the general public... Sleep tracking shows me as sleeping if I am in bed relaxed watching tv during sleep hours, making it useless. I only receive an incoming call notification on the watch if my phone screen is unlocked... missed calls come in every time.. no problems with GPS, Battery Life, Music , Bluetooth, feeds to 3rd party athletic tracking apps. all those work fine. Not sure I would buy this again.

title: Great watch
text: I bought this for my husband, an avid runner, for our anniversary. He is super into tracking, numbers, stats, etc. And he loves this watch! He previously had the Forerunner 235 Garmin but it was probably close to five years old. He had done alot of research on this one verses the newer models and this one still came out ahead and did not disappoint!

title: Good watch, good battery life, passive tracking functions are very poor. Active functions are good.
text: Nice big face, easy to read. I can charge it once a day while I am in the shower and it keeps it charged enough that I can wear it normally. I got this for SPO2 monitoring. When I'm sitting up it seems to match the finger monitor For the bad... Passive monitoring. The 245 is very poor at accuracy for sleep monitoring (a big factor in sleep monitoring is what you have configured for your sleep/wake times). My prior Fitbit was much better at sleep analysis. The 245 is very poor at passive heart rate monitoring, auto identification of activities has failed to identify any activity on it's own. Just for an idea of what to expect. My heart rate can be 160+bpm when I'm cycling, if the 245 had not been told I'm riding the bike it will register around 90-110bpm. So if you actually do something like climbing a bunch of stairs during your day, you cannot look back at the data and expect to see a real heart rate. Active monitoring, so if you remember to tell the watch you are working out the heart rate monitor becomes much more accurate. GPS is very good for a watch during exercise. Unfortunately the SPo2 monitor is almost useless during activity, as you have to be very still for ~10 seconds for it to take a measurement. I bought this to be a bridge between a passive monitor (like a fitbit) and a backup activity monitor (while you are performing a structured exercise event). It looks good, but is really only good at the Active monitoring. That is probably the trade off for battery life... I can only hope the next version of the Apple watch has SPo2 and better battery life, because I've basically just bought a pretty watch.

title: lighter than my old Garmin 305. easy to use.
text: This is watch is fairly easy to use and comfortable on my wrist. I wish it gave the time of day on the same screen as mileage but it's still easy enough to see while running.

title: Dead pixels in 6 months... Very common issue with this model.
text: Bought the watch on October 4, 2019. Fantastic watch, amazing battery life, zero complaints until... In March 2020 I noticed a few dead pixels right next to the Light button and next to the Back button. The dead zones got larger by the day. I decided to look into getting a replacement. I did a simple search for "Garmin Forerunner 245 dead pixel" and found thousands of others with the same exact issue and the dead pixels are all just about in the same spot. I've been using Garmin devices for 20+ years. This is the first one I've seen fail like this. There was obviously a manufacturing issue with the screens on this particular model of watch. I've submitted a warranty replacement through Garmin. Depending on how they handle the issue I will update my review.

title: Awesome for runners!
text: I waited almost a year before reviewing this watch to make sure it truly was as amazing as I thought. I upgraded from a Fitbit and it was an awesome decision. I use this watch for running but also everyday and all day wear. It has the smartwatch functions that I wanted so I can see calls, emails and texts for convenience. The accuracy for the GPS and mileage is fantastic. The watch is also durable yet not bulky on my tiny wrists. I love the buttons as opposed to the touchscreen that was on my fitbit that was way too sensitive. This watch was also super easy to learn how to use!! The Garmin app has so much info and also simple to navigate. This watch was money well spent.

title: Good for running!
text: If you love to run, this watch is enough for anyone. I have been using it for half marathon training, and the information that I’m getting from the watch is been very helpful.

title: Like many others, serious button quality issues
text: I opened the box, and tried to set up, but I noticed that buttons have very different feel for clicking. Some buttons are hard to press, and do not come back quickly. I search internet and found that many many people complain button quality issues. Too bad such a well-known company cannot even make buttons work smoothly. You should check the buttons and if they do not work perfectly (the chances are, if buttons do not work smoothly, they will get stuck soon), you should keep sending back until you get functional buttons.

title: Birthday gift
text: My son wanted this for his birthday. He had a watch in the past like this. Now he will recieve a new one.

title: Battery lasts 4-5 60 minute workouts or at least 7 full days if not in use.
text: I am so happy with this watch, I wear it even though I haven't been training. Its a really good looking watch. The software updated on its own, and it now tells me my Respiration Breaths Per Minute which it did not do when I bought it 1 year ago. You can read a full line of text messaging as well as news headlines, see who is calling, etc. Highly customizable watch screens. I am happy I bought the 345Music, I did for the battery life - I could never deal, charging an apple watch daily. But I learned from a Garmin rep that if you uploaded your music onto the watch and used it to Bluetooth your music while using GPS on your run - it wouldn't last a full marathon.... which means I always run with my phone for music even though the watch has GPS tracking. I beleive I have used my phone for music, but used the watch to skip a song a was surprised it worked. Like Strava, you cannot look up the status of a workout in the Garmin Connect app while in the middle of the workout. You must begin a workout on the watch, otherwise, you will need to enter the workout into the app manually. (With other trackers I've used, the software would intuitively add the heart rate and calories burned, steps, during the time that I told it I was working out...Garmin Connect doesn't do this.)

title: Battery and heart rate SUCK
text: I bought the 245 for the music even with reservations about crappy battery life. I have the 235 that i bought only 18 months ago and it is far superior with regards to heart rate. I understand the wrist is not as accurate as a chest monitor but the 235 wrist heart rate is far more accurate that the 245. seriously considering returning this!!! **Edit to add: I also forgot to mention the safety alert features which alert one or more of your contacts via text and live location tracking in the event you fall during a run and don’t get back up. Seems like an awesome feature; however, you must be in range of your cel phone in order for this feature to work but WHY would I have my phone on me when THE reason I bought this model was for Spotify music so i don’t have to carry my phone!!!!

title: Upgrade from my Apple watch
text: In my opinion, this was a better option for me than my Apple watch. The GPS is pretty accurate and was pretty intuitive to use. The emergency contact notification feature was really neat. It'll be good to have peace of mind that I can send a notification out with my exact GPS coordinates (if needed) when I'm on hikes or trail runs in areas without reception.

title: best running watch
text: seems to be tailor made for runners. it shows every stat you can think of for runners. mileage, pace, intervals, tells you how goos your doing, when to rest much more than galaxy watch that i had.

title: Didn’t Work Out of Box
text: Not sure why but didn’t work. Then I had to send back to Garmin. Not sure if this is an Amazon thing or a Garmin thing. Replacement works great but it was a pain.

title: Solid Running Watch
text: Good running and biking watch. Accurate, responsive and concise form factor.

title: Love the Garmin 245 Music
text: I have had several Garmin devices over the years and this is by far, the best. It was simple to set up and easy to find all the latest features. I’m looking forward to getting the Run Dynamics Pod to pair with it for more data. The sleep tracker is not so accurate, but it never is on any device. I’m looking forward to using it while I train for my first ultra.

title: It's an elegant smart watch: beats the Apple, Instinct, and Corous Pace watches for me
text: I am not a runner, but I am quite active and walk, ride a bicycle, and hike quite a bit. Thus, having a sports smartwatch is important to me. I have had a Garmin Forerunner 235 watch for quite a while, but at some time felt like it was time for an update. To make a long story (sort of) short: - Apple Watch was not for me - its biking and walking interfaces felt too small and I did not feel like charging it every night. Also, these day every kid seems to have an Apple Watch - I wanted something sportier and more special. - Garmin Instinct is a good watch, but I could not stand its small black and white screen, even though I admit it was pretty crisp. The Forerunner 235 is an older model, but the size of its screen is noticeably larger. - Corous Pace 2 - I ran into this model while watching smartwatch reviews on YouTube. On paper its specs looked great (most importantly, it has a barometric altimeter), but it looked like a toy when I got it - may be because I chose the "sport" strap. May be not exactly like a toy, but definitely not something one would wear as a dress watch. - Garmin Forerunner 245 Music - I was hesitant to get this one at first, mostly because I felt like this time I wanted to get an altimeter for my mountain hiking trips and the 245 does not have it. I even ordered a Forerunner 255 at some point, but then canceled my order after realizing that not only I would have to pay almost twice just to get an altimeter, but would have to wait for 3-5 weeks. In the end I decided to keep the 245 - it does lack the barometric altimeter, but the Gaia GPS app on my iPhone provides elevation profiles and paying twice as much for a watch just to get this additional feature on it felt silly. Most importantly, the black 245 Music looks very elegant - it's round, it's black, it's face is very crisp, and I can adjust it in various ways (one of the reasons I did not like the Corous Pace 2 was its choice of preset faces). I got myself a screen protector to keep this beauty safe and could not be happier!

title: Keeps texting at bay
text: Unlike a smart phone, hard or not possible to text call etc. Takes away the distractions. Provides ultimate training data. Thank you

title: Great watch
text: This watch is amazing! I am training for a marathon and it's been very helpful so far. I wear it 24/7. It's also really nice that I can reply to texts

title: Damaged Background at the top when received
text: During the set-up of the Garmin Forerunner 245/245 Music, I noticed a defect at the top of the watch's background. I saw it and immediately asked for a return and replacement. I rated it a 3 star because I was disappointed and wanted to use it, but I realize things happen, and I have another on the way.

title: Amazing fitness watch
text: If you've been researching all the Garmin watch brands comparing them let me save you the time. This is the one you want. It offers almost everything the top of the line does but for a third the cost and is slimmer. The one thing that isn't great is the sleep tracking but otherwise this is an amazing watch for health tracking and especially running.

title: Too complicated, too many features...
text: The watch is insanely complicated to operate. You need to graduate degree to figure it out. And to change anything while you are running? Forget it. You would have to sit down on a bench and play with the watch for 10 minutes. I wanted to track my steps. Searched in the list of activities for "walking" and it was on the list, but about 1,200 items into a list of 1,400 exercises. What I want: the time of day, steps, an exercise timer, intervals, maybe the ability to listen to music or a podcast, and a big legible screen. I have no doubt that this watch has the ability to do all of that, but it does thousands of other things too and picking through the menus using five different buttons in order to get it to do a few simple things is extremely daunting. Also, after using a Fitbit that I charge once a week, a watch that runs out of power after 8 hours (when using GPS, Spotify, always-on screen, and other battery-draining functions) is unacceptable. I'm returning it. Overkill for me.

title: Nice product
text: Nice features for running much better than cheaper products as to be expected. Quite happy with it.

title: Better than Fitbit for active people
text: I have had the following Fitbit products - Blaze, Ionic, and Charge 4. After having this Garmin Forerunner 245, I won't be going back to Fitbit. I feel like Fitbit is for people that need nudges and nagging. Garmin is for people that already have a good workout routine. I fit into that latter category. And you don't have to pay extra for more in-depth stats. I don't run as much as I used to but on the runs and bike rides I've done so far the Garmin GPS has been much more accurate than any Fitbit I've used.

title: Picks up GPS signal for outdoor exercises fast
text: Great at picking up GPS signal quickly. Excellent battery life, and very durable. The find my phone feature was a nice added bonus. Just wish with the amount of options and configurations this has, the menus would be easier to navigate.

title: Does NOT work

title: Good for price

title: so bad

title: Great little watches

title: My son loves his

title: very affordable and nice toy

title: If you want a smartwatch that works, find one that costs at least twice as much as this one.
text: Spotty cell phone connection. No texting. No internet. Can't even check voicemail because there is no touch-tone keypad after dialing. 10 contacts can be added, but you can't give them names: The first two are always "Dad" and "Mom" and the remaining eight are numbered 3-10. title: 18 months later and still works great
text: I’ll be honest, I bought this think it’d be a cheap way to see if I’d like wearing a watch - thinking I’d upgrade to an Apple Watch since I have apple everything. Been using it since April 2021 and I see no need to get a different watch or Fitbit. I shower and swim with it - at first I didn’t wear it in salt water but I forgot about it a couple times and it’s been fine. Worth every cent of $40, no doubt. The best part is that I only have to charge it once a month!! Apple can’t compare to that, and I rely on the sleep metrics with this watch. They’ve really helped me understand what gives me more hours of deep (restorative) sleep and what doesn’t. My friends all have to charge their apple watches overnight so that alone is amazing to me. The key to extending the battery life is to turn off the “life wrist screen sense” feature so the screen only turns on when you want it to. I like the alarms and fitness features, the app can be a little tricky at first but it makes sense once you learn it. I’m not all that gentle with it and I’ve never cracked the screen. I don’t use the message feature because I have enough notifications on my phone and computer that three would be overkill.

If you're hoping to track all your sleep, this won't. It takes all night, but won't track again for a nap.

text: This watch is exactly what I needed/wanted. I have always desired a smartwatch, but the high price tag of most with a bunch of features I knew I wouldn't need kept me away. The tracking features work super well, the app on your phone shows everything with graphs and numbers that are super interesting to look at. It's awesome also that it's waterproof because it gets sweaty often and I don't have to worry about it getting dirty or damaged. Highly recommend for anyone who wants a smart watch but doesn't need something super high tech.

title: Great except when Garmin accidentally kills it.
text: The Venu is a mixed bag: The screen is fantastic, I got reasonable battery life and the HRM is accurate even when swimming. The tracking is pretty good. The swimming tracker isn't all that great at stroke or distance recognition, but the biggest problem is that auto-rest is good at determining rest... but doesn't show your heart rate during it, so you can't drop it correctly. But the deal-breaker is, this is largely dependent on the Garmin Connect service. Which goes down frequently, or at least did in August and the first half of September. And is behind CloudFlare. Which blocked my IP address. Nobody, including Garmin, can figure out why, and Garmin can't unblock addresses, so the Connect website and the service on the phone/watch when in my WiFi range are broken. No other vendor has this issue. I've never had this issue with any site before or as of yet since. Avoid Garmin; the device needs at least some cloud connectivity and they don't know how to make that work.

title: Great value alternative to Apple Watch
text: I have the black with gold trim model Venu and feel the overall style is an upgrade over Apple Watch offerings. The only function I miss about my Apple Watch 4, which shattered on its first drop, is the text/reply and call options from the watch itself. The Venu does everything else I need it to do, activity tracking, HRM, phone-independent music apps with downloadable content, sleep tracking, and it display texts, calls, & voicemail notifications. It charges fast and the battery lasts longer than my older Apple Watch did.

title: False specs on webpage

title: Very happy with the Venu!
text: I haven't had a new Garmin in many years - my last was a Forerunner 205. I had a Fitbit Ionic, then a Fossil Gen 4, then the Garmin Vivoactive 4s. I loved everything about the VA4s except the display - it felt like such a downgrade from my previous two watches. The Venu solved that problem! What I use this watch for: Fitness - tracking outdoor runs/walks, day hikes, and indoor workouts like using the elliptical Smartwatch - notifications of texts and calls, 2FA logins, Garmin Pay, and having fun with the cool watch faces General health - the stats of things like stress, heart rate, body battery are fun, but I consider them to be kind of anecdotal; that's a lot to ask from a wrist-based device This watch doesn't feel rugged to me, like a Fenix would, but it certainly is capable of tracking the types of workouts I do and can handle my level of "adventure". I spend most of my week indoors at a job, and so I really appreciate that colorful display to look at. The display is also plenty readable out in sunlight, too, so it isn't like it is a trade-off to have it look good indoors, it looks good outside as well. Battery life for me has been really good; after the first few days of updates and me messing around with the settings quite a bit, it has settled down to using about 12-15% per day, which includes tracking either a 30-60 minute GPS activity or a non-gps activity. All the functions work as I'd expect; vibrates when it should, responds to wrist gestures when it should (and I like the fact that it is slightly delayed, it avoids false activations IMO), AOD looks nice if you have watch faces that support it. I have not tried the music function because I always have my phone with me (in case of emergencies) and just listen from that. I'd buy this watch again without hesitation and would recommend it to anyone looking for a nice looking watch that is a capable smartwatch as well as a decent fitness watch.

title: Features Do Not Always Work
text: This watch is a real disappointment. Many of the features only work sometimes. If you get on a plane and change time zones, good luck getting the watch to sink back up with your phone to show the correct time. I had to restart the watch and phone multiple times for it to finally show the correct time. Swiping to show features only works once in a while. You have to wildly shake your wrist for the display to show you the time. This is not a very smart smartwatch!

title: A Major Step-Up from a Simple Fitness Bracelet, does everything better at a much higher price.
text: I had been using a Fitbit Surge for several years. When the integrated band failed they provided a refurbished replacement unit. I found the Sleep and Movement tracking very motivating, but the proprietary band and unstable synchronization process frustrating. When the second band began to fall, I considered the Fitbit Charge 3, but then the Google acquisition was announced. I looked at several pure trackers but decided to give this smart watch a try. My initial impression is it does a lot more but has a bit of a learning curve. But my main complaints about my prior Surge are not an issue, since uses standard bands and syncs automatically without being asked. As an avid walker, I was thrilled to see a much more extensive list of trackable activities. The unit itself looks very clean and stylish, and it is lower profile on my wrist so it interferes less with my sleeves. The sleep tracking is more detailed and shows time in each perceived sleep level: deep, REM, and light. It also shows your breathing rates and movement. Adding more monitors reduces battery life from excellent to something less, but doing a regular charge while you shower keeps you topped up. I try to walk a 10K on days I am not at the gym, and Venu has many activities to track including walking. You can use the Garmin website to join a casual group of similar interest, track your activity and post your results. The leaderboard can be a motivator for many. I am very pleased with this Venu and will take some time learning how to use it and will update topics like battery life, Bluetooth and Spotify playlists.

title: My wife loves it
text: I can't personally attest to the features of this fitness watch. I bought it as an Xmas gift for my wife. She loves it. I find it a bit large and clunky on her - but she loves it and uses it all the time.

title: Just too much going on....
text: I thought it might a fun idea to update my Garmin Forerunner 35 and try the new Venu. I use the watch primarily to track my runs for mileage and timing, but thought the many added features would only make the Venu more appealing. Pros: beautiful watch faces, nice big watch face, tracking for menstrual cycle, any type of workout, stress, sleep, and much more. Cons: The mobile app gave me nothing but trouble. The watch would sometimes sync and sometimes not. This was the biggest turn off - the admin required to enjoy the darn thing! Had to return it as this watch simply became another item for me to 'manage' in my already busy life. I wanted it to do the work for me, instead I had to keep troubleshooting it. Not where I want my priority to be.

title: Great idea, but lousy implementation
text: I bought this to track my SPO2 during sleep. Here's why I'm returning it: 1. SPO2 sensor is inaccurate. Constantly gives readings that are 5% lower than what is measured by multiple other devices. As a result, this devices failed the primary purpose for which I bought it. 2. Poorly designed UI. Both on the watch and in the app, it behaves like a device that was designed in the 1990s. The features are all there, but the UI makes it difficult to find and/or navigate to many of them. The icons on the watch are so small, or the watch so insensitive, that I often found myself having to press the icons 3, 4, or even 5 times before they would activate on the watch. 3. Not Wear OS compatible. This wasn't a dealbreaker since I knew this in advance and the watch wasn't advertised as such, but I include it for anyone who has read this far and wasn't aware of the fact.

title: Keep looking...

title: really happy with my Venu
text: This is my first smart watch or fit watch or whatever you want to call it. I already had a garmin edge that I used mostly for cycling. Always hated using the heart strap it came with since its just a pain to put it on for each ride. So I've been using the venu to track my rides and it seems to work just as accurate as my edge and the heart rate seems to be very accurate and consistent. I've also loved the other stuff it tracks (sleep, steps, body battery, etc) more than I thought I would. I've had a couple issues with it syncing up to my garmin connect, but ez phone calls to garmin solved that and it has been problem free for three months. My battery seems to last about a week even when I have it track my sleep so I'm happy with battery life so far.

title: Durable
text: I've had this watch for going on 3 years. My husband and I do group personal training at our local club 3 to 4 days per week. Our classes consist of treadmill, weight lifting and lots of floor work like burpees and planks. I've banged this accidentally many times on the treadmill rails, scuffed it along the floor mat, and I'm sure it's come in contact with heavy dumbells as I struggle to lift them for various sequences. It's gotten sweaty...very sweaty! It's also been splashed with water while washing up in the locker room. I mainly use it to track my calories during class and don't wear it all day like some may. It tracks my heart rate and shows which zones I go through, also recording my resting heart rate. It does track steps for those that find that useful. I'm not a super tech savy person, but I find it easy to use as it pairs up with my phone to track all workouts. Another favorite feature is the downloading of spotify playlists. I can leave my phone in the car and pair my wireless ear buds to my garmin watch. When I get back in the car near my phone, the watch automatically syncs up to the phone again and transfers my workout info. My husband and daughter have similar garmin watches and have had equally positive experiences. Our daughter has changed out the wrist band to different colors which is cool if you're into that. I would definitely reccomend this watch. Oh! If you use the my fitness pal app, garmin and my fitness pal can link together to track your food and activity. We use that function daily.

title: Love my watch
text: I love my watch. It took some time to learn to use it and the set it up but I am happy with it. I wish the apps in the marketplace were better but it is ok. The only thing that bugs me a bit is the fact that I have to make a quick turn of the wrist to activate the screen. If I do it too slow it won't turn. I hope it is fixed in a future update.

title: This is a fitness watch, not a modern smartwatch
text: If you are looking for a fitness watch with GPS and exercise features, this is a good option. If you are looking for a smartwatch with a modern operating system and integration with your phone, RUN away from this device. My wife purchased this for an early Christmas present for me this year, and we're going through the return process now after using it for a few weeks. All the reviews we read before purchasing said this was a fantastic smartwatch, but it absolutely is not. The operating system is clunky and insufficient for today's world to say the least. Garmin would do well do ditch their OS and go with Wear OS or Tizen. Phone notifications (I have a new Galaxy Note 20 Ultra) may show up on time, or you may get them hours later, if at all. The interface/touch screen experience is trash. Something as simple as setting a countdown timer is a journey into frustration. There's almost nothing you would expect from a smartwatch here. No ability to answer calls, no replies for messaging, no photo viewing, etc. If those features exist on this phone, they've never worked for me. It may be a decent fitness watch, but compared to my previous FitBit Ionic that I rocked for three years, happily, it's useless. Don't even bother trying to compare it to a current-gen Fitbit, Apple or Samsung smartwatch. This feels a decade old by comparison. But hey, it can play music...

title: LOVE LOVE LOVE
text: does everything I want it to and more! so light but durable at the same time. great purchase and easy to use. battery like is really good

title: Buggy and frustrating
text: 8-month's in and extremely disappointed. Extremely buggy every time they push an update. Sleep tracking is completely inaccurate. It says I'm sleeping when I'm sitting on the couch watching TV. The latest software update causes the device to fail to reconnect to the Garmin Connect app on my phone if the Venu and the phone are out of connection distance for several hours. The only solution is to remove the device from the phone and to factory reset the Venu, which then requires you reconfigure all of your settings. Stay away unless you like being frustrated and angry.

title: Great for the price
text: I bought this watch 3 months ago and have been using it every day since. It is by far the best watch I have used, even in comparison to the Galaxy Watch series. The look, size, features, and feel of a watch are vital when it comes to using it in everyday life. Garmin got it good. The size isn’t too big, but it's not super small, it is lightweight and feels great when you wear it for any use. The battery life far exceeds any of my expectations, I will get on average 5 days per charge, and charging it only takes 30-45 minutes. Fitness tracking is one of the main features of this watch and it also exceeds my expectations, it has everything from rowing to running on a treadmill. My previous galaxy watch suffered a sudden quick and sudden death after a few times of submerging it in water, I feel confident with the Garmin Venus water resistance that it will continue to work in the near future. However, my only complaint so far is the watch band. Most of the time it feels good, but recently after a few months of use I’ve started to get almost like a rug burn on my arm from the band. Overall, if you are a very active person, like the outdoors, and want a that will be able to withstand everything you throw at it, this is a great watch for the price.

title: I just think Garmin gets it. Great watch/tool.
text: I resisted a smartwatch for a long time. But now that I've ditched cycling after 12 years, and taken up running, I needed one. I decided on a Samsung Active2... and used it for a week. The Samsung interface wasn't that intuitive for me and seemed to have quirks. Perhaps it was MY quirks, but the last straw was Samsung Health app not even having a web interface. I don't mind doing most interactions by phone, but sometimes I want to see it on my desktop. I returned it. Grabbed this Garmin Venu and haven't looked back. I just prefer the Garmin way. And they nailed all my needs with this one. The display is great. The battery life, for me, is phenomenal. Every couple days, I charge it while taking a shower. No worries. I'm not doing any long epic runs or anything, but I do use it for music while running. And have display "always on" during activities.

title: Everything I'd want in a G-Shock but it falls short
text: The goods: -A lot of functions and functionality, many sport modes to track/record -Very vivid and spacious display, many official and custom watch faces to choose from -Looked rugged, could rival G-Shock (not tested but G-Shock does not offer anything at this level. Their best fitness watch is the Move which is very basic) -On-watch software is responsive / app is clean and easy to navigate -Decent battery life; excellent price for the package The bads: -The watch case is bulky. I have relative small wrist and the watch/band combination does not sit comfortably. Comparatively, I have never felt uncomfortable wearing a G-Shock albeit in smaller watch case. -Functions and metrics are more like novelty than valid. The watch captures a handful of metrics but they don't feel accurate after monitoring them for a few days. I simply don't find them useful but they feel highly gimmicky to me. The step tracker algorithm suffers the same flaws as every other brand. It's a number, but not an accurate one. Bottom line: The Amazfit T-Rex Pro is a mixed bag in my opinion. There are a lot to like but the few quirks ultimately tipped the scale.

title: Not a good product if you’re serious about your fitness.
text: This watch only tracts calories by steps. It doesn’t track elevation (stairs climbed), or heart rate burn during your daily activities. It’s counted about 33% of what my previous watches would. I’ve had Fitbit, garmin, and now this. I deeply regret this purchase. I’ll end up having to buy a better fitness tracker soon. The battery life, and sleep tracking is cool, and I do like the minimalist approach, but it is no where up to par as a fitness tracker. You’re better off buying a low end Fitbit.

title: Really light weight and durable
text: I’m a mailman and I tend to beat the bleep out of watches. Catch them in boxes or whatever. But so far this is holding up! Let’s see how well long term it does. I bought the protection plan just in case! But it really looks good and I don’t miss my Apple Watch or old Fitbit at all!

title: A must have watch
text: I'm enjoying this watch so much. I'm really motivated to use it during my daily workout routine 💪😤. I love its looks too because even if I'm not workingout my watch is perfect to wear when I'm relaxed. I like it because it tracks important things about my health: heart rate, what type of activity I'm doing, 💧resistant, and much more. I love it on my day hikes and the overall information it gathers.

title: Amazing watch for the money (Updated)
text: I received this watch today and the ONLY thing I don’t love is the light weight. All plastic parts. That aside, the watch was easy to set up and pair with my Apple 8 IPhone. It update the watch with new software and everything is easy to understand. I sent back a Citizen CZ smartwatch because it wouldn’t stay connected to my IPhone. This watch seems to work very well. For only $127, I was not expecting much. So far so good. Very impressed with all the faces. The only other thing is I don’t know if it will show Apple text messages. It says it will show SMS but I have not been able to get the Apple messages to show up. Update: battery lasted me 3 days before needing to be recharged. Not close to what the claims are (9-18 days) but beats I have seen in other smart watches. Love this watch!! Can’t connect Imessgae but love everything else about this watch!! Charges very quickly.

title: No body temperature or blood pressure
text: I wish there were more screens, like a blue digital one would be nice. Also if there was a body temperature and blood pressure option as well.

title: more than I expected.
text: Build quality is solid. I mainly purchased to watch Heartbeat data during workout. I also thought it would be nice to view O2 during exercise. The O2 function requires sitting still while "measuring" so real time is not possible. App download and watch setup was a breeze. Data sync happens pretty much automatically. Even though the watch seems rather bulky, the watch is very comfortable. Having a choice of downloadable watch faces is awesome. Very happy with the purchase. Oh, and the battery life is awesome especially once the setup of keeping functions off when not needed. Recharge is fast.

title: Great watch! Easy to crack screen!
text: [[VIDEOID:171d604d6ed5ea83dc4b8269fd73604f]] Love this watch. Not even sure how I cracked the screen but it still functions so I will wear it till it dies. Sleep tracking & battery are excellent. Mobile app is easy to navigate & use.

title: It does what they say it will do
text: Initially, I was charging the watch every night, like I did with my Samsung S2 Smartwatch. Then I noticed I could go for DAYS without charging. I have worn it all day and night for three days running, and the battery is still above 90%. That surprises me because I know the display turns on and off throughout the night as I turn over in my sleep, and also during the day as I work around the house. It has all that I need in applications, and I am sure there are more. Excellent purchase. Most pleasing after owning the Samsung with its 24 hour (if lucky) battery.

title: Amazfit T-Rex Pro Smart Watch
text: The Amazfit T-Rex Pro Smart Watch is great. I was hesitant to purchase it because of the brand even thought it has so many reviews. I researched and was convinced. I took the risk. The watch is very well constructed. The size is big enough but not huge. The screen display is big and sharp. There are so many features that can be useful for those fitness gurus out there. It tracks sleep, steps, SPO2 (blood oxygen level), heart rate, many exercises, etc... It states to be IP-69 waterproof to 100m. So far mine has been submerged in shallow water (10 ft) with no issues. The only downfall is the app. I could not get it to allow the watch to provide notifications. I researched and even follow tech support with no joy. I downloaded another additional app for messaging that supports this watch. It works but often goes off line and drains the phone battery. My issue could be the phone (T-Mobile Revl 4). Overall, for it's price is comparable to higher priced branded watches when compared based on quality and many features that the Amazfit T-Rex Pro Smart Watch has to offer. Highly recommend if you want a customisable watch with many features.

title: Just arrived and app will not download
text: Do not try calling tech support or emailing. They suck. Sent it back.

title: Ok watch for the price

But it does not tracking swimming accurately. Now it has stopped receiving messages even though my phone shows its Bluetooth connected to the watch.

title: My favorite watch I barely wear anything else. I'm very impressed with the battery and the app
text: I stopped short of five stars because a few functions napping, body temperature, blood pressure has to be stored manually but I do think it's perfect the ban could be a little longer but that's personal.

title: Very difficult to set up.
text: The app is confusing at best. It took quite a bit of searching the app to figure out how to pair the watch with the phone. Since it’s only been in use a few hours, we have yet to see how well it works while wearing the watch.

title: Wow.
text: Amazing watch. Light weight. Tons of functions. Countless sports trackers. O2 and pulse sensor is accurate. Going to take a year to try all the features in this watch. Always on display option is a plus for me. Works better than the Amazfit GTR I was using. This watch is my everyday watch.

title: Battery life is great for a smart watch. Rugged and great display
text: Lol another reviewer here had a complete melt down in his review because the battery didn't last the advertised 18 days. He's apparently never had a smart watch before. Mine with display always on during waking hours and slightly turned up brightness will go about 4 days which is great compared to others I've had. With even more conservative power settings my old Samsung had to be charged much more often than that. You might get 18 days out of the T Rex with a much more conservative power use profile. Anyway the watch is rugged and has a great display. It does way more than I need - for the price I'm happy.

title: Very unimpressed with this watch.
text: Read my initial review below...... I continue to NOT be impressed or even enjoy using this watch. The biggest annoyance is that the watch does not "wake" when you lift your wrist as designed. I have contacted customer service and even completed a factory reset. It still will not "wake" when I raise my wrist. Too many screens to scroll through for simple features such as the timer. This Smart Fitness watch is nothing special. There are so Many irrelevant features. I got this to track My workouts with GPS and monitor my vitals. Even with reading glasses, it is not easy to see the numbers and characters. The workout program is not intuitive. The buttons are not even intuitive and too closely spaced especially when one is working out. I bought this because of a positive review by Consumer Reports (CR). I am not at all Impressed with the watch or CR's review

title: Little glitchy
text: Sometimes it needs to be restarted since it doesn't sync well with the phone so I wouldn't get notifications for calls or texts. I like the variety of faces available. Very bright and so far good battery life.

title: Inaccurate step tracking. Off by 100%
text: This is incredibly over priced for it’s lack of accuracy. Major regrets trying it.

title: I love this watch
text: I had the Original Samsung smart watch. Sure it was cool that I could get calls (even if I left my phone at home), read text messages but the battery needed to be charged at least once a day. I got away from the Smart watches and bought the Basis Peak which was an amazing watch. It was more basic but tracked my heart rate 24 hours a day and went 30 days between charges. Too bad there was a thermal run away issue with it and it was recalled whereas I then received a full refund. I then bought the Amazfit BitPim. I had it about three years until it just started malfunctioning and died. Having lots that watch, I was going to buy it again only to see it went up in price. So I bought the T-Rex Pro. I have had it over a week. I don't keep always on display but have it set to turn on when I raise my arm. I changed the watch face to one I like and average about 10% battery loss per day. The SPO2 is pretty cool.. I swam with it and it detected my stroke as well as distance (someone the old BitPim couldn't do). With 10 ATM, the upgrade over the non pro version which is 5 ATM is worth the extra 10 - 15$. Yes I have been diving well over 120 feet.

title: Cool tough watch, with THAT LOSES CONNECTION TO PHONE multiple times per day
text: I've been an Amazfit fan for a long time. Had a GTR before the T-Rex Pro, and had no issues with it. First off - this watch is really tough, and is truly one that can give a G-Shock a run for the money. BUT... my biggest complaint is this.... it CONSTANTLY loses its connection to my iPhone (using an iPhone XS with the most recent IOS). An example would be this... If I've synched the phone manually (by swiping "down" on the Zepp app), it synch up, and the watchface I use shows the temp/weather. Typically within an hour or two, where the temp/weather should be.. I get a "--" with no updated info (or even the last info). I have to then open the app up again... and swipe down to re-synch. Again. Additionally, I have my iPhone set to go to do-not-disturb from about 11pm to 6:30am. I set the DND ont he watch to do the same. BUT... in the morning.. if I get a text or Facebook message AFTER 6:30am, once the DND is no longer on..... I don't get the notification on the watch. I literally have to shut off my phone, restart the phone. Go to the Zepp app.. and swipe-down and re-synch. Again. This watch has so much potential, but for these connectivity issues, I'm going to recommend you DO NOT BUY IT. I also have a Fitbit Sense, which I stopped using in order to use the T-Rex... but, I've never had these issues with the Sense... So, I'm now considering moving back to the Fitbit watch instead. Sad that I have to, but the reason I wear a smartwatch is so that I get notified of txts, etc. Given that I've got to go thru multiple steps daily - I cannot recommend this. Maybe if they update the software, that will fix it.. I don't know... but for a watch that LOOKS cool... to have to re-sync it multiple times per day (as compared to an apple watch, fitbit, or Garmin that you don't have to - I definitely DO NOT recommend, and I wish I wasn't outside of the return-window, I'd send this clunker back)

title: Great watch
text: Like everything about this watch with one exception, would like to be able to turn off automatic Wrist flick and see time by tapping the watch to save the battery. Great price, very good smart watch.

title: Excellent Watch
text: Nice size, very durable, 5-7 days battery life, and tracks data very well along with a concise app. Added the Super Shieldz glass screen protector and it is great at keeping the scratches at bay.

title: Great except for a few
text: Watch is great but lacks a few. Can't get correct weather. Always way off. Can't feel vibration on alerts or notifications. Very weak vibration..Hard to see display in bright sun light. Limited watch band replacements.

title: So far so good
text: Over the past weeks I've owned this, it has performed very well. I've charged it after 4 days and purchased to mainly track steps and monitor heartbeat. The other functions are great as well. I just ordered the watch face protector and might change bands in the future....more to come!

title: I LOVE this fitness tracker!
text: After a few days of research, including asking friends, online reviews, and the Consumer Reports fitness tracker ratings report, I decided on the Amazfit T-Rex Pro. I am EXTREMELY satisfied with this tracker! The SPO2 (Blood Oxygen Saturation measuring) meter is one of the features that locked down my decision. The sleep tracking and analysis is EXCELLENT and pairs perfectly with the Apple Health app. The watch face store offers numerous options and can't wait for the release of more. The watch is extremely light and I rarely notice I'm wearing it. The band feels durable. The battery life is EXCELLENT! I record three to four workouts a day and I only have to charge every three to four DAYS. The only issues I have with the T-Rex are the confusing customization of the workout menus and lists. I have to go through a few menus to get to my most-often used workout types (I'm a CrossFitter and primarily use the Cross-training, HIIT, and Strength Training options). I hope that the app developers will eventually include the options for a favorites workout list AND the ability to customize the menus via the app. One more thing I'd love to see the ability to make minor changes to completed workout data, primarily the stop times. There have been a few times after the end of the workout, I've forgotten to stop the workout tracking. I'm not concerned with the connectivity features of messaging, phone calls, and music (although you can!) -- sometimes there's a thing as being too connected. All in all, the T-Rex is a fitness tracker jam-packed with features with a phenomenal price point hundreds less than an Apple Watch. You can't go wrong with this watch!

title: Didn't meet my needs, but battery life is exceptional
text: I really wanted to like this watch! Looks rugged and appears that it will stand up to some hard use. That said, it had two faults that wouldn't suit my needs to keep it. Pros: 1.) Crazy battery life. After (9) straight days, it still had 50% battery life. 2.) Rugged construction. 3.) Neat watch face graphics. 4.) Convenient and easy charger. Cons: 1.) While the time displays were easy to read, the HR/step displays were too small for my 64 year old eyes. This was a major reason for my decision to return. 2.) Watch wouldn't count steps when pushing things around, such as a lawn mower or shopping carts. Lots of steps going on there. Just too much $$ for what it lacks for my wants. Maybe overly picky, but going to try another route.

title: Nice aatch
text: I like the sleep tracking feature. The battery lif us excellent. It is a bit thicker on my wrist but not bad. You can select many faces.

title: Great smart watch!
text: This Amazfit T-Rex Pro smart watch is really good for it's price. Monitoring features are pretty precise and battery life is excellent. Very satisfied with this purchase.

title: Keeps track everything
text: Like the many different faces you can pick from. Easy to set up and battery last 10 days so far.

title: Exceptional Watch
text: I've seen the reviews claiming inaccurate HR and O2 sat. I'm a retired Biomedical Engineer and imho their expectations are unrealistic. HR varies from second to second and is computed based on a few heart beats and extrapolated to a minute value. Beat to beat time can vary significantly. May I suggest that you establish a baseline then evaluate based on change. O2 sats also can vary based on algorithm and site perfusion. It might be valuable to know the precision of the watch but for what it is being used for that's not necessary. This watch has many features that do not appear on anything I am aware of at this price point. GPS on my watch is highly accurate. I have used the watch for a week and there is still 43% of battery remaining. I have been using GPS minimumly. IMHO an excellent watch especially at this price point.

title: Not waterproof as indicated
text: Great watch until it got wet. Wasn't in the water for more than 5 minutes before it stopped functioning on full charge. For the price I paid this is unacceptable and I would want a full refund. If you're planning on getting this thing wet, look elsewhere. Not waterproof even up to 1 meter

title: Bought to replace Garmin Vivoactive 4 very disappointed
text: Out of the box it looked like this watch was used, it had what appeared as dead skin or some residue on the backside of the watch. I purchased this as a replacement for my Garmin Vivoactive 4 which died after 18 months. The battery would not charge properly and when it did it went dead in about an hour. App was horrific Sending back, a definite POS. Very disappointed.

title: Although this is a Beautiful watch I hated the operating system
text: I ended up having two of these watches in the space of about four days. The first one didn’t work at all and the second one didn’t offer a text notification. Amazon sent out the second watch in one day but I just wasn’t happy with the no text messages on a $130 watch.

title: Update:
text: I probably got a bad one, but it still will leave a scar, the plastic casing does not dissipate the heat from the battery and leakage could occur from the battery causing a chemical burn. It takes awhile for customer care from Amazfit to respond but they eventually do. In my case they made it right with a new watch, but still, this should not have happened.

title: Great applications, great look, Solid smart watch.
text: After a bunch of research I opted for the T-Rex. I really, really like this watch. I love the rugged looks and it’s surprising light weight. I have the steps and sleep monitoring on permanently, and I use the workout tracking daily and I have about 12 faces saved which I will rotate. I will not get 18 days of battery life, After 3 full days I was down to 57%. However, it only took 15 minutes to fully recharge and I am happy with that. I went with the grey color scheme, the strap is super comfortable. If you like the look of the watch, you will love it and all that it offers. 100% vouch for it.

title: Worth the price
text: Edit 10/11/2021: I am thrilled with this watch! I changed numerous settings and as a result, I go up to 12 days between charging. It's data continues to be accurate and it's waterproofing holds up in the shower. Life is great! I love this watch. The data that it presents seems consistent and more believable than other fitness trackers I have used. Having said this, I wish it had a higher capacity battery. The only plus with this small battery is that it can be recharged quickly. I could get longer spans between charging if I stopped logging everything but I feel that the data is essential to log. My sole concern is will it last and is the battery replaceable.

title: Lots of Function in One Smart Watch
text: Cheaper Smart Watches on the market but went with this one due to the functions that the cheaper ones don't offer. I mostly use this for general activity tracking but like the other features for sleep tracking, blood oxygen, heart rate, etc. So far the battery life has been good. 18 days on one charge is about right but figure I will recharge every 14 days so it doesn't run too low and lose any functions. All in all would recommend and happy with the watch so far.

title: NOT very user friendly!

title: Good watch but not 100% suitable for pool swimming
text: I'm a everyday lap swimmer and need watch measuring distance and laps. I had Ironman before. This watch reads distance inaccurately like showing 20 laps and distance 508 meters in 25m pool. ((( Also you cant engage chrono and pool mode simultaneously. and if using stop watch separately because of touch screen it stops and starts by itself during exercise. But those are good watch for everything else.

title: My husband loves it!

title: Pros and Cons
text: I ordered this to replace my Samsung as this seemed more versatile and had a longer battery life. I returned it because it did not have the features that I thought it stated it had. Here is a short list of things I liked/disliked: Pros: battery life. Samsung lasts max 2 days whereas this lasts well over a week even with the always on screen. Always on screen, didn't turn off. I could always see the time. Waterproof. No worries in rain or taking a shower. Cons: Button configuration was odd. Wasn't the easiest to navigate. Could not respond to text, only read them. Alarms, meetings on my phone did not transfer to the watch when the reminders went off. Always had to have the app running on your phone. Pros/Cons: It was very lightweight which was nice, but also made it feel cheap. The band stretched so the fit was good, but since it stretched sometimes it would get to tight. Find the hole for the correct fit, and mark it.

title: Awesome but not a Garmin

That makes this brand seem clunky. It is just as durable as my Garmin and has taking a beating and looks new. It is Tough!! I don't like app though. Just too busy. Good watch

title: Not bad
text: [[VIDEOID:ec778b1883c2207d68119538f647a56c]] So far not too bad, I got it June 24th charged it and lasted me exactly 2weeks. I slept w/it a few times and the tracking isn't great I work overnight and when I'm not moving it says I'm sleeping when I'm actually watching a movie lol so I wouldn't trust too much of that but the nights that I do sleep I think it does okay. But I can't sleep with a watch so I care less about it. Music works fine, there's no adjustment for volume bc I just tap on my headphones idk why Ppl want volume control on the watch. Also I can see text & call on my watch and glad it doesn't have reply option bc can you imagine answering a phone and it's not even within reach. Hahaha, I would have to run to find it so I'm okay just seeing who's calling me or texting me w/out replying/answering. The rest of the features are fine, idk how accurate they are but I guess it's a good estimate. I don't use the rest of the stuff so I won't give my opinion on it. The app is simple and easy to use. I just notice the weather doesn't connect but I care less about it 😅. It's funny bc the app says it's connected so idk why it says that. Steps can be a little off but not so much vs my Samsung note 9 tracking my steps. It's always between 100-200 steps different (less or more each day is different from my phone). Also, those who get skin burn, make sure you give your skin a break! Bacteria (sweat, dirt & dead cells) builds up and develops an infection. We see this a lot at the hospital for those who things you're not supposed to take it off or worse clean your watch at least few times a week if you use it outdoors or gym. Anyways above all its a good watch to track time at work. I have no complaints

title: It's great customer service. Definitely 5 star service. I love my new watch!

title: Too many bugs
text: I wanted to love this because of the answer/call feature but I ultimately returned it. The watch continually disconnects from the phone (this is a built in feature to conserve battery) so I will hear my phone ringing and see it on my watch but I am unable to answer it. You have to keep reconnecting it through the Bluetooth on your phone. I also only received about 70% of my call/text/message notifications. I don’t know if I got a faulty watch but it also didn’t securely attach to the charger. I have another fitness tracker and it strongly magnetically connects but this one would spin off it not placed just right. Also, when I would make a phone call using my phone, it would default to put the sound through my watch and sometimes during a phone call the audio would switch mid conversation and start coming through the watch. The health features matched my other fitness tracker pretty well though the step count did seem low.

The app and watch does not notify me unless I am manually trying to sync the data from my watch to the app (even then it doesn't always let me know). I like that I can manually tell the watch I am working out so it will monitor my workout while I am working out. It let's me know what my heart rate is at and how many calories I am burning. This is great stuff that I love being able to monitor. However, sometimes I forget to tell the watch that I am done with an exercise and a 30 min exercise appears to be a 2 hour one. I get busy or distracted because life and I don't remember to let the watch know i am done exercising so I end up have this really long exercise in my exercise history and no way of editing it after the fact. Also, there is no way to change the type of exercise afterward. If you accidentally select treadmill but you are just working out, you can not go into the app and change it. Other helpful features that I would love to depend on are just plain unreliable. It almost never stays connected to my phone so I have to go through a whole annoying process to be able to control my music from it (I normally give up and just don't). "Find my phone" rarely works. The meal and calorie tracking feature in the app is super broken and limited in feature. I am not going into it, but I would just use another app for that.

Surprising since I only set it for steps, walking, calories burned, and sleep. No GPS, music, sharing or other settings that shorten battery life. And because of the battery issue, it is not worn at night to track sleep. Finally, it is only worn when leaving the house. My previous Fitbits did have a 4-5 day battery life but this Versa dies by the third day. The watch is stylish and easy to read. Also, I like the charging dock. The Fitbit app is easy to set up and use. But the poor battery life is disappointing. Therefore, the watch which the Versa was meant to replace, is still the watch to wear. title: Nice Entry Level Smartwatch with all my Fitbit tracking
text: Previously owned a Charge 2 HR for several rough years and wanted to switch out. I was looking at the Versa Lite or the Charge 3 and waiting for one to go on sale, Prime Day came through with the Versa Lite on sale. It was a quick and easy change to disconnect my Charge 2 from my app and connect my Versa Lite. I am still playing with the apps from the Fitbit store which are limited but still have good options, free and paid. Uses the same Fitbit app. I love that it is waterproof to 50m which I would only use in the rain, splashes or reaching into the sink. But now I don't have to panic if it gets wet. I don't like that it does not have stairs or SpO2 monitoring which is on the Charge 3, but these were not make or break options, just my preference. When shopping for 3rd party accessories realize that the only difference in Versa Lite and regular Versa is there is only one side button on the Lite and three buttons on the regular Versa. they have a 1 year warranty, which I have not personally had to use, but everyone I have met has had a great experience. I do worry about scratches and damage so I did get a cover and a leather band for work use. Switching bands it fairly easy, just slide the tiny metal lever on the band down and pull out. It takes a bit of playing with to get your apps, notifications, and responses to meet your needs, but I like that it has more options and apps than a Charge 3

title: No luck here. Died the first day.

That’s why I called it quits and started the process to return to amazon. The Fitbit app is NOT very intuitive, hard to navigate and like noted above would not sync with the iPhone. title: Save your money
text: I purchased this product in May, it was broken by august. Upon first impression, the watch is pretty good. The battery last for days, it tracks your sleep, exercise, it’s got a little social media hub for like minded folks on their fitness journey, overall it’s pretty neat. However, the actual product isn’t worth the price. My Fitbit worked fine until all of a sudden it started counting thousands of false steps(40,000 steps in one day?), the battery would sputter out in les than a day, & the heart rate monitor just stopped working. I called their rude support, who seemed annoyed at the time of my phone call and got no where with him but I spoke to their chat support and they shipped me out a new one after a few troubleshooting efforts. I get the new one a week later And it didnt work at all. I gave up, not worth the frustration. Say what you will about the price of an Apple Watch, but they tend to last at least a full year before you run into problems. Also FYI chat replies only work on android, their website could’ve been more forthcoming on this.
