title: Broke in less than a month, customer service no help at all.
text: This was a gift for my birthday/our anniversary from my husband before he left for two months for training. I had been wanting a smartwatch for a while and was hoping that I would be able to use the interval training for data collection at work. (I'm an ABA therapist and sometimes I need an interval timer.) I had a Fitbit a long time ago that I liked except it was pretty basic and the band made my arm break out after extended wear. Fitbit seemed like a decent enough brand and it did have interval timers. Husband switched to Fitbit after jawbone trackers kept breaking on him. I got this watch on April 8th. The morning of May 1st I woke up to a watch that said it was 30 April. After syncing it, it still had the wrong date, so I turned it off with the intent of turning it back on again-it's an IT cliche for a reason-and it just displayed this message. I contacted Fitbit support; first guy tried to tell me that I couldn't use the Fitbit with my Google Pixel and that if I looked it up on their website it would show that it wasn't supported. This was a lie. I pointed this out to him, politely, and he then escalated my case to a specialist support team that would only deal with me over email. Ok, whatever. They reached out later that night asking me where I lived, whether it was a gift, and where it was purchased. Ok, fine. Supply that info. 22 hours later, I get an email from someone else on this team asking me to take a picture with my case number written on a Post-It next to the broken Fitbit. Kinda weird, ok. Sent that within 10 minutes. That was two days ago and I have heard nothing from anyone. I have no idea if they are working out how I can fix this, or if I have to send this back for some kind of replacement, or if they've all just gone out for tea and forgotten about my email. $159 down the drain at this point. I'm so sad about this. Also the interval timer doesn't work for my purposes.

title: Great watch, much better than my old "smart" watch
text: I got Moto 360 several years ago when smart watches first came out and it was nice, but annoying. It was tied into everything and kept giving me alerts and so eventually I got tired of it. My wife also had a first generation Samsung Gear watch and that was about the same as the Moto. Well, fast forward a few years and now my wife, daughter, son and daughter-in-law all have newer smart watches (Apple Watches and Fitbit) and they all love them. It was time to get a new phone, so I got a Samsung S20 FE and then decided to get the Samsung watch. I saw on the reviews that it really works well with Samsung phones and so I decided to get the Watch 3. I was looking at the Watch 2, which had a few less features and then I found the Watch 3 in the 41mm size and then found a refurbished one so I ended up paying about the same for the Watch 3 as I would have for the Watch 2. I'm very impressed with the watch and really love it. I didn't get the one with a cell phone, it just connects to my phone with bluetooth and/or wifi, but it's really amazing. I get my messages, and can turn off the ones that I don't want and then I also get all the health apps. So, now it tells me to get off my chair and walk around and does EKG and stress tesing and Oxygen levels.. I was concerned that the 41 mm might be too small, but it is a great size for me as you can see from the pic. I have had a Citizen Echo Drive for more than 10 years and it is a little larger, but I like the size of the Watch 3 better. If you are thinking about getting a watch, this one is a good deal right now and I believe it does work best if you use it with a Samsung phone.

My S22 Ultra figured this out immediately, so did my wife's iphone. However the watch still tells me the wrong time. title: Renewed Was Good - Review The Seller
text: Since Amazon lumps all these reviews together, you'll see widely different experience because the seller is a big factor. My renewed item came from "SELLER: Edge Cellular" so factor that in. My watch arrived in original factory packaging albeit it was not pristine, but everything was in the box. The only sign of being renewed on the watch was the band that had a kink or obvious strap position mark where the item had been worn. That has subsequently disappeared with my own use - it was on the end and apparently I have a much smaller wrist. Otherwise, everything looked new. As the instructions noted I fully charged the watch before using it and then tested it. Everything seems to be working well and I was able to pair this with a Google Pixel 6 phone using the Galaxy Wear app. I'm not a heavy user but my main function I wanted was SamsungPay because my preferred card isn't allowed into GooglePay that I have on the Pixel. This worked fine and the watch works fine with contactless payments using SamsungPay. I don’t wear the watch while sleeping but I have used the heart rate monitor, the Samsung Health and blood oxygen measures and they all seem to work OK. I have used the audio/media control – mixed results but mostly OK. Having only recently ditched a Samsung phone for the Pixel I was already setup with many of the Samsung apps. I am not a heavy user during the day and seem to get 4-5 days of use between charges. Again, this is excluding 8ish hours of sleep time per day. Net a good experience we a renewed item, the Amazon guarantee was a comfort and as my first smart watch I’m happy, mostly because SamsungPay works and lets me pay with my preferred card.

title: Battery life is unreal. Excellent! Steal of the century for this price !
text: This battery is flat out amazing!!! Nothing can beat it. I've owned Apple watches, and Samsung. I recently broke my Samsung Galaxy watch and looking to replace it, I thought I would give this a chance and if I didn't love it, return it. Both other brands mentioned need charged either daily or every other day. This thing is unbelievable. I left town for 5 days and didn't bring my charger. I knew I could charge it if needed but thought it would be a good time to test it. Let me state that it's not in battery saving mode or anything like that. It's regular brightness , turn wrist to display , and notifications from text, calls, emails, snap, etc... enabled. I'm currently on DAY 8 !!! AND NO CHARGE YET !!!! From the pics you can see I have about 25% left. Unreal, I've slept, showered, exercised, worked, played in the ocean and sand, and it still works great and the battery is still kicking out the juice. Cons : don't like the app, the limited watch faces, and the band is a little cheap. Can be replaced though. Need a better app and have the watch faces interchangeable in the app like Samsung does. Tweaks like this would make this watch a true competitor. Also, I've had numerous people ask me about it when seen. They say it looks really nice and expensive. I don't tell them any different. Just said, I got it on Amazon. The price and the battery gives its 4 stars alone. $40? Gtfo of here.

title: Works okay
text: Is comfortable , good size, my only issue with it is the steps tracker and the sleeping tracker For example my phone says 5,243 steps & the watch says 6,626 steps Also I slept 7 hours and the watch says 5.35 hrs besides that works fine

title: Needs improvement
text: Liked it until got wet. It says waterproof and barely got soray on it and it quit. But while it worked it was good for health tracking and messages.

title: Great smart watch on a budget!
text: Great smart watch for anyone looking! Good place to start if you don't want to spend $200 on your 1st watch. Easy to set up and use.

title: Great performance and value
text: Love this watch! My previous digital watch was good, but this watch is much faster and has an analogy face option and displays the current temperature, date and steps on the analog face

title: Nice watch
text: Nice battery life, gives me an idea of what text or notification I got, doesn't seem to track sleep though. I do like it.

title: Great Watch
text: I have had a couple of Tinwoo products in the past years. I have found them to be most reliable. The product service from Tinwoo is great. I would expect this product to be no different, a great value and reliability.

title: Only 3 stars
text: Good price for what it is. Won’t display notifications for texts but notifications for calls come up. I had to go thru a lot just to set it up u have to download an app. Doesn’t stay connected sometimes no matter how close the phone is.

title: I like it for the 100 exercise and sport modes..Oxygen level, music, weather, heartrate.
text: The steps are 1,200 off on the watch from Healthmate App on my Android Samsung. I notice my heart rate stays low when there's an update. The user is not notified of an update. The user has to update the app, Turn off the watch and turn it on again.

title: Sleep monitoring
text: This really helped me get my sleep in line, seeing that I barely got rest was amazing. The battery life lasts long and charges fast.

title: An Awesome Watch!
text: I like that this watch is so light that I'm able to keep it on ALL day and sleep in it! I normally don't like to sleep in a watch but I can't tell that I have it on! It tracks my sleep pattern really good. I Love my Amazfit GTS3❤

title: Great product
text: Got it as a gift for my girlfriend an she loves it. Great battery and health track

title: So happy with this fitness tracking smart watch!
text: I wanted a fitness tracking smart watch that was accurate. This is the 3rd brand I've tried because of returning watches that stopped working or weren't accurate and this is BY FAR the best one yet! It has so many different exercise styles that it can track and it seems to be accurate. I love how smoothly and quickly it responds and how easy it is to navigate. There is even haptic feedback when you toggle with the side button thru a list. I love that I can get notifications when my phone isn't right next to me, however it doesn't have the ability to make or answer phone calls, but you can decline a phone call. I actually didn't want a watch that made calls, it's just not a feature that I need. The battery life is amazing! I always forgrt to check how many days it lasts before I recharge it again, but I'd guess about 10. I've had a good experience with their customer service when I needed help setting it up. I am so happy with this watch, I'd definitely recommend it, and if anything happens to it, I'll get another!

title: Unable to get notifications other than phone calls, disappointing battery life
text: Not performing as expected for a smart watch. Notifications and SMS messages do not work despite following all instructions provided by the manufacturer. Only receive notices of phone calls. Changing to imperial setting from metric doesn't affect barometer/altimeter. Inaccurate weather info for my location or not refreshing. Battery life much shorter than expected. Sleep tracking was terrible claiming I wasn't asleep when I was deep in dreamland. My previous smartwatch that cost a lot less was much better at sleep tracking. The only nice things about this watch is the screen size, always on display option, and the ability to set a custom watchface. The custom watchface options are limited to time/date only with a custom background image.

title: No continuous Heart Rate
text: Advertised as capable to do continuous Heart Rate monitoring, but it does not! It will tell you to turn Automatic detection on if you want the continuous HR monitoring. However, with that turned on it still does not. What it does is it sample the HR at intervals and displays it where you expect to see you instantaneous heart rate. What you will see is the HR at say 80 and will stay at 80 for a while and then it will change to another number say 76 and would stay on that. So it is always lagging. I checked while having a pulse-ox on my finger and watched how the heart rate was changing on the pulse-ox but not on the Amazfit GTS 2E.

title: Great!
text: It seems to be accurate in the info it gives me.

title: Light, Long Battery Life, but syncing and app are not good
text: This is a light watch and the battery lasts a long time. Great number of options to adjust performance vs battery life that other watches don't give you. Reasonable number of watch faces you can download onto it. The app, however, doesn't do a very good job of keeping the watch in sync with your phone. I'm on an iPhone 12 mini, and the temperature on the watch is usually off by 4-6 hours. It's 95 out now, but watch says it's 89 - WRONG! if accurate/timely information from your phone is important to you, then this watch probably isn't. It's great for long battery life and good looks, and getting alerts from your phone, but you can't clear message alerts or respond to messages from the watch, you have to pull your phone out to quit getting alerts from your phone.

title: Does Not Sync Consistently with App- Updated
text: This watch has to be worn very tight which is problematic when putting pressure on the arms and hands. More than half of my bike rides don't record properly. I don't know if it's from sweat or movement. Last time I wore it so tight, my fingers tingled and it still didn't record 20 of 28 miles. It also does not seems to calculate paddle boarding miles accurately. The watch seems to work well only for walking and steps. Now I have to take my phone AND my watch in hopes of capturing workout information, but then it does not consistently sync. Way too many bugs and cannot be relied upon. Choose something better. Update: After comparing between my iPhone, a Garmin, and this watch, there is is nothing to recommend with this device. Exercise data are often laughable inaccurate. I actively hate this thing. It's now dying a slow death in a drawer I have for terrible buys to remind me how easy it is to waste money. It was very hard to set up compared to my new FitBit which took about 5 minutes to set up via BlueTooth. This watch is old tech with little regard for accuracy. Don't waste your money or be misinformed.

title: Battery Life Is Poor
text: This is a cute watch and has some great features, but it falls short on battery life. Battery only lasts about 2 days, and I don't use any notifications. Also the step count is not accurate seems to miss alot of steps. I am returning this item and will try a different brand.

title: So much value for the money!
text: I am pleasantly surprised. I bought this watch mainly because I love the green wrist band. I have been a loyal Garmin watch wearer for over 10 years. The price and the styling made me give the Amazon watch a try. Wow! So much value for the money....it is great for tracking what it tracks...it doesn't have as many multi sport activities, but it does an excellent job tracking what it has. The battery life is good considering the colorful screen - I love this watch.

title: Poor App but watch is OK
text: I could not find additional sports to track my indoor cycling . After looking at help on Amazon and I restarted watch then it was there. The app won't let you add excersise time to track which I don't like . I also wish it had kayaking as an option

title: Good device
text: I like this device compared to others. I lost the first one that my wife purchased for my birthday because the strap tends to come out of the two catches that are supposed to hold it in place. Either way, the functionality and options are very nice so I replaced it with another. I waited until prime day and saved about $30 on the second one. Overall, I'd recommend this over others.

title: Disappointing
text: I wanted to love this watch. I mostly wanted basic features and sleek design. It has both, however the quality is lacking. After just 3 months of use the watch band broke. Additionally it spontaneously quit syncing with my phone and could not re-sync without restoring to factory settings and losing all the data. When I reached out to customer support they were not helpful and did not address any of the issues I asked about. Just get one of the basic apple watches or other brand name watches.

title: Love my GTS3
text: I just recently purchased this watch for me and my husband. It took a while to get it set up but no biggy. I did some research and found this adaquate for our needs. Great product.

title: Would not initiate
text: A beautiful smart watch and I was anxious to use it but nothing I tried would complete the initiation process.

title: Great smartwatch
text: I have an apple watch and compared it with this watch. This watch is much more affordable than my apple watch and is still impressive. This smartwatch has excellent battery life - I have to charge my apple watch on a daily basis but didn't have to charge this watch for over a week after using it! It has a very soft, comfortable, and light wristband, and a large screen that is easy to see. It's great for use during workouts and hikes as it monitors lots of data, such as heart rate, exercise time, steps taken etc. I'm very pleased with this product.

title: Was looking for more.
text: I want to love this watch but it's kind of hard to. For the price i paid you would think it would do a little bit more. If you want this just for fitness tracking i wouldn't spend the money on this just for that. The functions are pretty comparable to a cheap smart watch. Idk what we are really paying for but i feel like a cheaper smart watch can do it all the same.

title: Broke after three months
text: I was very excited to get this watch and I was using it every day. And then one day I plugged it in to recharge and it did not recharge. Since I was long past my return date there was nothing I could do about it. I will not buy from this company again and neither should you.

title: Good option if you are looking for core functions sleep, heartrate, O2, etc. with great battery life
text: I will also add this works with standard third party watch bands (if you get the proper size). Wanted a watch to be able to check my heart rate and blood ox, features that were built into my previous Samsung phone. Plus I wanted to be able to monitor my sleep. This seemed to tick those needs well without having to spend hundreds of dollars. While there is not a large selection of additional apps, I don't need my watch to do everything, there are definitely useful ones that can be enabled. What it does for me - vibration to notify of incoming calls and texts and ability to read that text and even reply with a canned response. Tell time. Check vitals with a one press. Control music on phone - play/pause and skip tracks. Alexa control has come in handy in rooms where I don't have an echo device, but I do want to control my AC and other connected devices without shouting to another room. My only reservation was having to use the Zepp app instead of the Samsung health app, but it hasn't been an issue so far. A huge plus is the battery life. I'm not getting 14 days, but I am easily getting about 10 days. Charging is quick, so even if I forget to charge it, I can connect it while I am doing my morning routine and I am good to go for another week.

title: Not worth it, waste of money
text: Bought it as a gift for my husband for Xmas, been 5 months & it doesn’t work anymore. Doesn’t really have any useful features, can’t txt or answer calls from it. A bit complicated for something that should be easy to use. Don’t recommend at all.

title: Wife's best gift ever
text: This little guy has everything someone would like. Long battery life, beautiful design and great functionality

title: Love it
text: So far so good!I upgraded from a smaller one and so far I am loving the bigger face. Love the sleep feature and the notifications from my cell. Worried it will get scratched tho.

title: Quit Working
text: Watch doesn’t track steps accurately so if you are purchasing for fitness, don’t waste your money!

title: Finally picked up a smart watch! Couldn't find the app in the Google ...
text: Finally picked up a smart watch! Couldn't find the app in the Google app store so had to go to the website provided in the instructions, go to the website from the Firefox mobile browser and it tells me that my device is not compatible...um...excuse me?! So then I double check the compatibility, just to be sure, and then go the factory installed web browser and try again...SUCCESS! Once I got that figured out it's been smooth sailing ever since! Pedometer is not exactly precise...shake your arm like a mad person and you will jump 100's of steps easily! Note: While you do receive call and text notifications you cannot answer calls (only reject or decline with a text stating you will call them back) or respond to texts (other than pre-programmed short messages).

title: Pretty design, poor execution.
text: Oh Samsung... I had such hope for you, but then you let me down. The screen on this is BEAUTIFUL - it is a curved OLED screen. As beautiful as it was, the face of this tracker was still too wide for my wrist. Wearing this correctly, it had big gaps between the edges of the face and my wrist. I hate that! Also, the wide screen was odd to use. The app left a lot to be desired too. This device is ultimately a let down - spend you money elsewhere! I just got the Fitbit Surge last month and it was the tracker I have been waiting for.

title: Does your Smartphone need Smartfriends?
text: After using a clip on FitBit, which promptly fell off and got lost, as well as another high end fitness watch that was a bit too complicated for my simple little brain, I decided to give this one a go. As it turns out, those of us with little brains can breathe a sigh of relief, now that we can have a smart watch to talk with our smart phone. So easy to set up, they are like buddies that soon chatter back and forth about everything their owner is doing. The display is large and bright, and the watch itself is stylish and fun. Great way to get in touch with your health and your body.

title: Nice but VERY limited
text: Worked nice but the information it provides is very limited. Get a Gear 2. ATT has them NEW for $199 no contract. You can reply to text messages and talk on your phone from your watch. The Gear Fit is too limited.

title: Love it.
text: I love my Samsung Gear Fit Smart Watch. I wear it all the time. I only have to charge it every 3 days. It tracks all my steps better than the one i was using before. I don't have to worry about where I left it because it's always on my wrist. I have recommended this to my friends. =) Good deal.

title: I really like my gear fit
text: I really like my gear fit. I love that I can get notifications so if my phone is in another room I can read the notification and decide if I really need to get my phone to reply. I really like being able to control my music with the gear fit especially when I am working out. I have blue tooth earbuds and with the fit I don't have carry my phone all around the gym. Could the fit part be better - yes. That said most of the fitness trackers have some kind of issue. Other reviewers have stated they lost their fit because it came undone and they didn't realize it. Samsung could have made the clasp much better especially for the price. My solution to that concern was to go to Walmart and buy the tiny rubber bands that are in the hair care isle and wrap it around the band twice. I move it up when I take the fit off and then back down past the clasp when I put it on. Easy fix for .98 cents. And it works today mine came partially undone and the rubber band kept it on my wrist.

title: Five Stars
text: my wife love this smart watch, does every thing she want it to do.

title: I do love it. However my fit bit HR read Mt ...
text: I do love it. However my fit bit HR read Mt heart rate better.

title: Think hard before purchasing.
text: I loved this device for the 1st 2 months. Then randomly, it stopped connecting to S Health. The next day, it wouldn't send notifications from my phone. Now, it is basically a bulky watch. The return window was 1 month. Hardly a sufficient amount of time for bugs. I googled all of the methods of reconnecting to no avail. I am sad and angry.

title: Don't Get it Wet, and Needs a Better Band
text: The water resistance of this watch is pathetic. I went into one of those small swimming pools about 3ft deep. I didn't do anything crazy. When I got out, I noticed the watch wasn't working. Upon investigation I saw that water was inside the watch, which could be seen from the back of the watch where the heart rate monitor is. Looking at the specs, Samsung states a water resistance rating of 30 minutes at no more 1 meter which is about 3ft 3 inches. Simply unacceptable considering the price I paid for the watch. It is a fitness watch, I should be able to swim all day with it if I want to! If a $20 cheap watch can be waterproof to 50m, why can't this $100+ watch do the same. I am completely unsatisfied with my purchase. The other downside to this watch is the watch band is not made well. It is only held on by two studs, and there is no band loop, so the watch can come loose. You better be prepared to spend a few bucks and buy one, or you will lose this device! Aside from that, if you promise not to get it wet, it is pretty accurate in counting my steps. Connected to my phone great. If I turned off the bluethooth, and synched it up once a day the battery lasted 5-7 days. A lot shorter with the bluetooth always on. Of course if you turn the bluetooth off, you loose the ability to find your phone, or receive vibrations when a text or phone call comes through.

title: Poor Hardware
text: Started out fine but soon it, became faulty and went it some administrator mode and wont get out of it, Horrible equipment barely lasted a month before it started acted funky. Samsung dept wont do anything about it because it doesn't recognize their own devices serial number, Like I went and bought a knock-off or something c'mon man, horrible customer support on their part becareful purchasing this device if you want it to fizz out after a month of use.

title: good quality, love the features and that you can ...
text: good quality, love the features and that you can add apps to it. However the only negative is the battery life. I upgraded from the Garmin Fit which the battery lasts for a year without charging. This one requires charging every few days.

title: Great fitness watch
text: Pretty cool watch with limited function control. The fitness tracker works great but for more function you're better off with the gear s3 or s2.

title: Great product as long as you don't need continuous heart rate reading.
text: I've had this since August. It seems to do a good job tracking steps. Since buying it is seems that there have been a couple new apps added that seem to be useful. My only complaint with this is the heart rate monitor. You have to be standing completely still in order for it to read. But you can use it to show your continuous heart rate with an additional chest heart rate monitor through Edomondo. I still recommend this watch, but if the heart rate monitor is the only reason you're getting this over another activity tracker you may want to look elsewhere.

title: Great Smart Watch!
text: I bought this smart watch for my wife and she loves it, her main compliment is that she can check messages and also see who is calling without looking at her phone, I guess that's why she never answers my calls.

title: I wear it every day!
text: I wear this everyday! It records my steps and then synch's up with my Galaxy phone when I get home. Now I no longer have to hold onto the smartphone or stick it in my bra when I don't have pockets. I can simply wear my light watch and gather all the information that way. As an added bonus, I put a picture of my grandson on the wallpaper. It's nice to be able to change the bands and wallpaper to coordinate with an outfit.

title: This watch is better than most "newer" 2016 models.
text: This, of all the sport watches i have owned, seems to be the best "all-around" package. Here's the problem "most" sport-watch / fitness trackers can't get past: They seem to think that, to get style you have to give up on functionality and vice versa. This watch has changeable watch faces, a pedometer, and a heart-beat sensor. I know most everyone wants to get every possible sensor into a watch but it's just not possible. You can't have weight or blood glucose readings in a watch and, in ALL honesty, the speed and cadence (for bicycling) is best left to the independent unit you would mount and just sync with your phone via Bluetooth. This watch also gives notices of calls and messages via vibrations and it can be used to control your music via the watch. It also has a stop-watch and timer that work decently well plus some people have coded a new "nifty" apps to install on it. It's best NOT to over-tax a watch with features because companies start skimping on quality when they do. Now, if you were like me, you might have to go to an "older" version of Gear Fit manager to get the watch to "sync" with your Samsung phone. Unfortunately, Samsung's "Gear" Manger....it's getting crappier as they continue to code it.

title: Syncs well with S4 Galaxy for S-Health or other pedometer \ life activity
text: My wife really like getting this for Christmas!!! She wears it every day and syncs well with S4 Galaxy for S-Health or other pedometer \ life activity apps. Battery life seems at 2 days with light use. I hoped it might last a week. Kind of annoying , since regular watches last months and month on a button battery, but this is doing a heck of a lot more I get it and know how this is always talking blutooth near field to the phone.

title: Swine
text: It does exactly as its supposed to do. The drawback is that it is limited (i.e. chained) to only Samsung products. I enjoyed it for the month I wore it. Though I believe the pedometer overestimated frequently, it still was great. I ended up going back to my Flex because in syncs with my food diary app, while this one doesn't. It is an excellent smartwatch; but not so great fitness watch. When Samsung unchains it, i will try again.

title: BAD REVIEWS ARE MOSTLY WRONG
text: I bought this at my AT&T store along with the S5. I have to say I mulled over this purchase since the release of the first Gear smartwatch. I initially purchased a FitBit, and then really researched the Gear Fit once it came out. I have been wearing it for a week and it is much better than what I expected, namely since the reviews have been so bad. The first thing to know is that many of the people that supposedly reviewed this product after trying it simply didn't take the time to figure out how to use it. For example, there are reviews out there complaining about the smartphone pedometer reading having discrepancies with the Gear Fit pedometer reading. They are wrong. You have the option to set which reading you want, and even with what frequency they sync. The other common complaint is about the orientation of the text due to the orientation of the long screen. If bending your wrist to read what is on the screen of a smartwatch bothers you......DONT GET A FRIGGIN SMARTWATCH!!! You will have to bend your wrist to look at any smartwatch. It is not awkward in the least. In short, any complaint I had I was able to resolve by either doing a quick web search or by clicking around. At this point, I would like the battery to last 3 days instead of 2.5...so I am not running out of charge in the middle of a day. I would also like the sleep tracking feature to be automatic. I don't know if this is possible, but it would be nice since you sometimes snooze and forget to set it. Other than that, I am really, really, really happy with my purchase. It is as good or better than the Fit Bit. It is much more stylish than any other smartwatch out there. I had actually decided not to get it because of the poor reviews, but am glad the AT&T guy talked me into it when upgrading to the S5.

title: Samsung Rocks
text: l don't know a lot about the features for a fully personalized review because I bought this as a gift. And the receiver loves it.

title: Don't waste your money if you want a heart monitor. Screen has failed after 10 months
text: I like everything about it with the exception of the heart monitor. The monitor is a joke. It can only be used while resting, even then is doesn't work well. If you are sweating, it simply will not work. I'd of given it 5 stars if Samsung actually put effort into designing a heart monitor. Don't waste your time if you want a functional heart monitor. After owning it for a few months, I have to say it is a complete disappointment as a fitness tracker. The sleep app is useless and you have to charge the watch oevr night most nights anyway. The battery has 2 days tops from normal use. The charger is weird and hard to snap into place. The software is a joke, there's no place to put height, weight and age. There is no social media apps to accompany this product that I found. There have been no decent software updates since I purchased this device. I'm pretty sure Samsung abandoned the platform. TOTAL LET DOWN, I WILL AVOID SAMSUNG IN THE FUTURE! UPDATE: The display failed after 10 months. This thing is an absolute disappointment.

title: Works for Me.
text: Fits. Certain. Situations. By this I mean that if you WORK in a facility (like a hospital) where you are not permitted to use your smart phone, then perhaps this is for you. Assuming that you OWN a Samsung smartphone the you might enjoy this little device. So... it's nice to NOT juggle your smart phone but leave it somewhere on your person (pocket/purse) and still be able to monitor texts & emails. I have only had this device less than a week so I need to use it more to provide a better evaluation. Here's a typical day for me and why this device works for me. I ride my bike to work and home again (exercise/heart rate/mileage). I walk a LOT at work (steps per day). I have a life OUTSIDE my work where my significant other or family likes to contact me (texts/email). I would rather NOT be handling my smart phone constantly. I hope this helps me keep my phone in my pocket and not out in my hands but still able to monitor texts and emails with less OBVIOUS smart phone use behaviors. I hope it tracks my bike commuting effectively as well as my steps. I hope you enjoy it too.

title: Great!
text: works good, pedometer function works automatically and is very accurate software is clear cut and easy to setup, the unit itself looks futuristic, very light and very comfortable, the device makes you look good. heart rate function works well but it should be on 24/7 to monitor your heart rate, manual intervention shouldn't be necessary battery life is only 3 days...

title: I love this Gear Fit
text: I love this Gear Fit. I am very motivated now and I totally love this product! There have been complaints that you have to turn the pedometer on to use it. This is true but only the first time. Big deal! It wasn't a show stopper for me.

title: First watch worked great for several months
text: First watch worked great for several months, then went into a cycle of rebooting. I checked on the internet and this seemed to be one of the more common problems with the Gear Fit. After struggling with the support web site I finally got through to someone, heavy accent and all. That got the repair process started but there were some errors due to language difficulty which I finally got figured out with the on line chat. Watch was sent in and returned promptly. Actually it was a different watch that was returned, I don't know if it was new or refurbished. That watch worked for 2 months and now I have the same problem. I just spent several hours over 2 days attempting to get some help on their ridiculous support site. I have finally given up and am going to junk the watch. It's a pity because when it was working I liked it a lot, well, other than the heart rate function which was kind of a joke but it didn't really bother me that it was not accurate. I did like the notification of incoming calls and texts when it was working. Over all, great when it works, not so great when it breaks. Having two fail with the same problem indicates to me they have a faulty product.

title: But this product is excellent at what it intends to do
text: The only reason I dont give this a 5 star rating is that would mean there was absolutely no room for improvement. But this product is excellent at what it intends to do. It worked for me immediately after charging, which was quick, and with easy set up; it stays charge for about 3-4 days and I look at it frequently. it is very handy to see messages as they come in and i am missing fewer calls as a result. the fitness tracker is very good and compares nicely to my wifes fit bit flex but is handier because I can view stats without having to get out my phone. the pedometer/running accuracy is about as good as any accelerometer I have used and so needs to be viewed within a range of accuracy. When I simply walked and counted steps it matched perfectly. when I run it slightly overestimates my pace and distance. I wonder if there is a way to program ones stride length. seems like a simply software fix if not. For the price and since I have a samsung note 4 this is the best deal out there for the present time.

title: I'm getting myself one now!
text: My wife loves it. This is our first smart watch, and although it's not officially Android Wear, Samsung did a great job on this device. Battery lasts her 2 days, when she forgets to charge it overnight. It's got a lot of great features for a sporty watch. My only gripe is that the Samsung Gear software on the phone occasionally freezes up when trying to change the background picture on the watch.

title: Okay
text: You get what you pay for I guess? Sensors don't work at critical times. Glitches cause reboots and the watch doesn't retain my prior settings when it does. No quick way to adjust for difference in lighting, which can be a challenge if you step out into the bright sunlight and have no hope of seeing the screen to brighten it. Special adapter required to add to a micro-usb for charging - very easy/likely to get lost. Glad I didn't shell out for a full-on smartwatch. But I'm hearing from friends and colleagues that this isn't all that different from their FitBit experiences, so at least I have one that works with my Samsung phone S-Fit app. Pedometer seems to be pretty accurate as these things go.

title: I love love love love mines
text: I love love love love mines! Monitors my heart, knows my steps finds my phone and when I am working out or away from my phone this thing tells me who is texting or calling so I don't have to answer! love it!

title: ... know where I was in my life before thiswatch! I absolutely love it and it's extremely easy ...
text: I don't know where I was in my life before this watch! I absolutely love it and it's extremely easy to use! It's great that it can read my HR and also accurate steps taken. I love how it fits and looks. Several people have asked me about it and where to get one. It's also nice having control over my music when walking as well as calls. I also love the fact that I can read text messages from it. It helps me to know if i should stop what I'm doing to respond or if it can wait, all without skipping a beat. i was worried that the band would be too small as I have very large wrists (measuring just over 8 inches) but these bands are perfect.

title: I find it very comfortable. Fall asleep wearing it every night
text: I have a nasty habit of forgetting to take my watches off when getting in the shower. Can't tell you how many I've broken them this way. I've already done that three times since I got this watch. That waterproof thing is no joke. I find it very comfortable. Fall asleep wearing it every night, no problem. Works great and has been extremely useful. And I have not gotten one fingerprint or smudge on the screen. And the battery stays charged for days. Loving it so far!

title: This Watch is an awesome product.
text: I love it. I love it. I love it. I wear it all the time, it allows me to shut off alarms on my phone even if I am several rooms away from the device. It works just as advertised, and there are a lot of 'extras' of which I was unaware when I bought it that make it even better than I had hoped. I would recommend it to anyone as a companion device for an Android phone. Again, I love it.

title: Good watch, but doesn't last long.
text: This was a nice watch. A lot cheaper than most. The battery lasted quite a while at first, then started only lasting a couple hours. After having it for two years it went completely out. It gets hot when charging and when I turn it on it says it is rebooting. It reboots for a few minutes, shuts off, comes back on to rebooting. It does that in a vicious cycle until it dies. All in all, it worked great but not worth it to only last a couple years not wearing it full time.

text: New out of box the screen is burned out in one corner. Not sure if this is the brand to get with these issues showing bad quality control. Processing return as I write this.

title: Really nice high quality screen
text: Really nice high quality screen, very nice and clear, easy to traverse through the menu system. Easily adjust settings via the samsung phone or tablet device. It is a one star product because I was really disappointed with the heart rate monitor. The heart rate function worked really well when I used purely for walking, but as soon as I tried to use it for working out, it completely fails. It gave me really wildly low values. There is not any on board function that strictly for a general cardio workout, so I tried some of the other pre-programmed workout functions (walk, run, hike, biking). More specifically I used the running and walking functions since they did not try to access my GPS but like I mentioned before the heart rate values were ridiculously off. I also gave it a one because they used cheap cobalt or nickel in the retention clasp, I had a really severe allergic reaction to this clasp.

title: It's exactly what I wanted!
text: It's exactly what I wanted! At my job I very rarely have my phone on me, so this is a very convenient and simple way to stay connected to it while I work. The notifications and ability to send a quick text response are great, and the media control is perfect for changing a song without having to go to my phone! I also use the pedometer and sleep monitoring functions. The battery life is long lasting, I can usually go a few days before even thinking about charging it. I will say that if you have the 'wake up' function on it will drain your battery faster.

title: Not the US version, not a fan.
text: As others have said this Gear Fit sold by AmericanTVAppliances is not the US version. I got it as a gift & noticed that the outer box is all in Chinese. So is the main screen of the Gear Fit when you turn it on, but most of it is English when you get past that. But since everyone else was having issues & saying the serial numbers are not supported, I am returning it to possibly get the Garmin Vivofit. After trying it out, I am not a fan of the sideways screen that you can't really look at when it's on your wrist. & to measure your heart rate you have to have it super tight & it was uncomfortable. It also said I only burned 12 calories on a 20 minute walk. Doesn't seem accurate. It is a neat device but I am afraid it will have issues like many others.

title: Has potential
text: I originally purchased the Samsung Gear Fit over both the Nike Fuel band and the FitBit, because of advertised capabilities. The number one thing that I wanted from this that both NIke and FitBit do not offer, is setting a goal time with a specified distance. Samsung advertised this capability, but you can only set one or the other. In addition, the distance is not accurate. I ran on a measured track for 2 miles, and the Gear Fit only said that I ran 1.7 miles. Lastly, the Samsung does not fully monitor sleep like a FitBit, you set the Samsung when you go to sleep and it starts a timer, it does not monitor you while you sleep, it merely keeps a running time. We had high expectations for this considering it was $200, in the end we decided that we will wait until fall when the Moov is released and get that.

title: Love it! Well worth the price!
text: After watching several YouTube videos between this product and the Samsung GearNeo and Gear2, I finally decided on the Gear Fit. I mostly purchased it because it's more geared towards fitness, which is what I will be using it for. I've been a user of the Nike Fuel Band for years, and I've been so unsatisfied with it. I love the notifications, being able to check my heart rate, record my sleeping pattern, track calories and count my steps.

title: yes - good product
text: I do like this one especially if you have a Samsung phone. Works great.

title: Small, bright, and handsome!!!
text: I have used the Gear Fit for 3 days now, and I have absolutely no idea where all the negative comments are coming from. It took me about 15 minutes to install the software on my Galaxy S 3, including the Health S software, the Gear Fit Manager Software, and the time it took to pair the device with my phone. It has worked as expected since then, including monitoring my sleep, notifying me of missed messages and calls, allowing me to control the music I am playing on my phone when I exercise, and counting steps, heart rate, etc. Unlike other people I am not so much concerned about EXACTLY how many steps I have walked or the precision of the heart rate monitor -- both cases it is consistent, i.e., my heart rate increases in proportion to the duration and intensity of my exercise, and my the steps counted are roughly the same as those my wife (and I) get from her FitBit. I think it is naive to expect perfect precision from a wrist-worn device. This device is light, attractive, easy to use, and very versatile, as well as being priced reasonably. I myself try to match brands in my stereo components, video equipment, etc., and so I would probably not have chosen the Samsung if I had had another brand of smart phone -- but that's just me. And since it was a gift ( I asked for), I have absolutely no complaints. P.S.: Reading the ( in this case brief and concise) instructions always helps -- I try not to blame technology for my own shortcomings :-(

title: Died after 85 days.
text: When it works, I love it. I've had it on my wrist for almost 3 months and have become very attached to it. The screen stopped responding to my touch and the only button on it also stopped responding after 3 months. I REALLY liked it but it HAS to work! Samsung support is horrible. It starts out very pleasant. I created the initial ticket request online that allowed me to upload my Amazon receipt, describe the issue, put in the model number and serial number...etc... it even allowed me to upload a video SHOWING them what the problem was. I thought this was going to be a great returns/RMA process. Boy was I wrong! I've spent 2 hours on the phone with them this morning after THEY CALLED ME. They asked me every question that was on my initial ticket request leading me to the conclusion that I wasted my time on their support site. I was transferred to 2 other technicians that ALSO asked me the same questions. Finally, I'm told that my serial number isn't in their database and that it will take 2 days for them to sort that out!!! 2 days!!! This is 2015 and one of the largest technology companies in the world needs 2 DAYS to sort data? Where is this data? On a notepad in the top drawer of someones office??? Very disappointing. I'm an avid fan of Samsung products. A bad device every now and then is excusable and it happens. Bad customer support is never excusable!

title: Nice little fitness/smart watch - Entry level gadget

text: Bought this for myself, but the strap is just a touch too small for my larger wrist. So the Fiance took it, and loves it. We both have S6's and the sync was super easy. The monitoring works well, as we can tell for the first week. Running and walking is her primary workouts, and it keeps great track of both. The sleeping monitor is neat, but more testing before I can say more. Sync with the phone is almost instant, bluetooth needed to be on always. Fit will last a few days easy. It was at 74% charge on day 1 and is still around 50% on start of day 3. I found a post about a method of extending the strap a bit more, for me to use it... title: Very NOT Glad I purchased this Gear fit.
text: My husband has a Fit Bit Charge which he likes very much. I had only an activity tracker and needed a heart monitor (because heart Doctor doesn't want my heart rate over 134 during exercise). I tried his Fit Bit for my aerobics class and it was ok but I had to stop what I was doing and push buttons. of course the heart rate went down before I could get a reading. I saw this Gear Fit before Christmas and read the reviews and thought I would like this better than the fit bit.Of course it went on sale, which was great. I absolutely love it. It is an encouragement for me to keep moving. I check it from time to time, especially if I am sitting down. If it looks like I will not walk the 10,000 steps, I get up and walk. There are some things about it that I didn't know, but really like. It was very easy to set up and syncs very easily with the Samsung S4.It works with Bluetooth. There is an exercise mode, when set provides continuous heart rate, I only have to look at it, or at most push a button, which I do without stopping. I like having the text messages and phone call notifications. I also like that I can "find my device (phone)" with this. I haven't explored all of the features, like controlling music, I don't listen to music on my phone. But I plan to try later. I do use the timer and stopwatch. I have colorful bands on order to change it up a bit. Also, I am purchasing the little clasp covers, they are very inexpensive and will help protect the gear fit from coming undone.(this seems to be a slight problem with the colorful bands) At first I was not too crazy about the very large face, it looks manly to me. I changed the wallpaper to something dark and it is not so bright. I think the new bands will make it look more feminine for me. All in all, I am very happy with this product. March 2016. The paint began rubbing/flaking off shortly after I started using the watch (see photo attached). I work in an office and this watch is gently used on a daily basis. I have been in touch with Samsung. This watch is well within its warranty period and I expect the company to send me a replacement. If I had known about the cheap paint around its face, I would not have purchased this watch. I would not recommend this product.

I like the steps on the main screen, more information that the flashing lights on the FitBit. I change the wallpaper often, daily to match what I am wearing, and have even used some of the pictures taken with my phone as wallpaper. One downside. It is waterproof, but it doesn't register information well in my water aerobics class. The other downside is I'm not sure it records anything when it is out of bluetooth range of the phone. title: Great Watch
text: Nice Smart Watch. I wear it all the time. At work, I keep my cell phone on silent. As a teacher I can discretely respond to calls and text without drawing attention to a cell phone. Setup is easy. With a glance I can see my grandson's picture as I check how many steps I've made or the time. I can also call my phone from the watch and check my heart rate.

title: I love it!
text: This was listed as used, but came just like new (box was opened, but everything inside looked untouched and pristine). I like it a lot, as far as this price range goes. I'll probably be looking to upgrade soon, but let's talk about this product since you're considering it: The display works both vertically and horizontally (I was concerned about that when I bought it, but vertical view is awesome and well-designed). When I'm wearing it, a lot of people call it a fitbit. So that's kinda funny. It's very obviously more of an exercise watch than a "watch"-watch, which is something you might wanna know before you buy it. It's really good to wear while running or just walking around. I hardly notice it's there anymore. It takes about 45 minutes to go from 10%-ish to 100%, and then it's good to go for another 48 hours (for me, at least), so I'm impressed with the battery life overall. I don't use a shield or screen protector, and it hasn't gotten scratched yet. I do a ton of stuff like gardening, running, assembling furniture, with this thing on, and it hasn't gotten a mark. Impressive. In this price range, I'd definitely recommend this. I've had it for about 6 months now. Samsung is awesome and so is this watch!

title: Better Products Out There
text: I find the Samsung to be very inaccurate. It is off by large margins on distance and steps. The heart rate is not accurate either. I walk two miles on a treadmill and the gear fit records 1.25 miles and is consistently wrong. The heart rate is usually off by 20-30 bpm. In addition, it doesn't sync to S health which is why I bought it. So, you have to use multiple applications to track your data. The fit gear manager doesn't record any dietary or weight data and basically just puts your gear fit info on your phone. I was much more satisfied with the fit bit and using a separate heart monitor. The Samsung does look cool and that's about the only positive for someone who is looking for serious fitness equipment. Boo Samsung.

The only draw back is the silverfish rim of the watch has come off in places and I have had it since August. I am in the process of arguing with Samsung because they said it is cosmetic and not covered under warranty. I feel it is defective. title: Good fitness tracker but also consider the Pulse HR at less cost
text: I should have saved a few dollars and bought the next model lower down. I don't use VO2 Max as my idea of excercise is walking and not running. I find that this watch and the app are really good. The step counter is accurate during a workout but it does not update the count much if you are just puttering around the house. I mostly wanted this watch for the heart rate, sleep function, and the exercises it monitors. Much of the watch concerns the "watch" itself. Personally, I find it very difficult to see the hands. I tried the white watch and the black watch. Both are not much for being able to sneak a look at your watch to tell the time. I always have to push the button to tell the time. It has something to do with the slender and shiny hands and the many reflections on the crystal. Really hard to see. Having complained about that, let's talk about battery life. It is fantastic. Almost a month of life. Maybe only two weeks if you press the buttons a lot but that is still excellent. The app is fantastic and integrates well with all the Withings device I own. It reports on every bit of data it collects. I like that the sleep function works well and that heart rate is recorded while sleeping. The smart alarm for wakeup is also nice and it works. Some have complained that the watch buzz is too gentle but I am the type of person who is almost always awake when the alarm goes off, anyway, so it does not matter to me. I also have a fancy and expensive Galaxy watch 3 which does all sorts of fun stuff. However, when you boil it down to the basics, the Withings does all the exercise monitoring as well as sleep monitoring better, in my opinion, than the Samsung. Bear in mind the Galaxy watch is a full-fledged smartwatch while the Withings is basically a fitness tracker. I do recommend this watch but if you want to save money and stay in the Withings domain, just get the Pulse HR instead.

title: Pleasantly surprised
text: I have many watches and was attracted to the clean face of this smart watch. I like it from a fashion and function standpoint. I chose the used/like new option at half the retail price. Very pleased, extremely comfortable silicone band. Recommend this one.

title: Beautiful time piece.
text: I have been using Pebble products for several years and loved them. I have been looking for something with a better display and a nicer look. This watch is a beautiful time piece, it doesn't do anything close to what the Pebble did but is way more accurate. Step count is way lower, the Pebble counted many extra steps during the day. My normal day with the Pebble was 12000 steps, with this more accurate step count I'm around 7000 a day. It has actually made me take more steps to try to get my number back up. Battery life is amazing! I'm getting about 25 days between charges. I play volleyball and don't even have to start the activity, once I did it the first time it asks me if I just played and will automatically track it now. Really good health mate app. I would recommend to people looking for a great looking time piece that is a fantastic activity tracker, with the added benefit of getting notifications and alerts.

title: Hmmm
text: Ok I will be subjective here as it not my first smart device. I did buy it to track my sleep and heart rate and it did meet my price point for a wearable device, given my previous adventures into way overpriced smart watches. That said, below are my comments. Pros. Smart looking watch that easy to set up out of the box. Dead simple actually. Looks quite good and the band has a lot of adjustments to it so should fit all wrist sizes. The watch face is not over the top so you can use it for most occasions, which is a good thing If you have a large wrist however, it may look like the watch your mum got you when you were young. Small face. Cons. Battery life at best is 2 weeks. Whilst it’s still good versus other smart watches, it’s not even close to 25 days. I’m assuming you only get that if you don’t look at it, press the mode button (which after a month is getting sticky) or do anything unusual. Sleep tracking. Best used as a guide as even though I wear the watch as suggested, it just doesn’t seem accurate by way of sleep length. Often I need to go in and manually adjust the results. Syncing to google fit is a complete joke. Now I know there are better fitness apps out there than google fit, but I have been using it for a very long time. All my other smart watches have over the years managed to sync up without issue. But, this little guy is totally random as to what data is sent to my main fitness tracking app and often requires some manual input into the google app to keep score on what you have been up to. Sorry Withings, but there are a ton of people out there having the same issue and you simply need to fix it. No excuses these days to say your products can sync up but only offer a half hearted attempt. All in all, the watch is fine and for the money (there are more expensive product out there) I’m ok with it. A few fixes to the sync up and this review would have gained an extra star or two.

title: One of if not The Best on the market
text: By far this is my favorite smart watch on the market. I have had the Wirthings steel for almost two years now and it has withstood the test of time for me. The new Sport HR brings in a beautiful classic style to a eligent and sleep smart watch. I was very reluctant with the strap being as it was the weak link on prior watches but this one is quite positive. It holds up well and has a very nice modern style. With this new Sport still the watch face has been given a elligent and updated red tip for the minute and hour hands and a completely red activity dial hand. This gives much more contrast than the previous watches stainless on black background. But the most important two features of this watch is its battery and water resistance. Unlike any other watch of its class in its market the battery can last some time without being recharged. I’m still on the factory charge of about 35% after a week of use and it has only dropped to 20% (this was with use of the new sports mode.) I have ultimately choose wirthings for there eligent stile, water resistance and outstanding battery. There app is streamlined and just as smooth as the watch itself. I’m hoping for another two years out of this classicaly designed smart watch.

title: Zero Support
text: I honestly love the watch. Looks good, functional, good app, and an amazing battery life. But as you can see, my screen broke and I’m having a heck of a time finding anyone at Withings who can tell me where to take it to get it fixed. Withings forum boards are ghost towns and I can’t find a phone number for them. Fingers crossed they reply to my email. I did feel like the glass broke a little easy but it could have been me wearing it when I shouldn’t have been. So conclusion, buy it but be gentle. Because if you break it, you might not be able to find anyone to fix it and you likely won’t be able to get ahold of Withings.

title: Exactly what I was looking for, if the features worked
text: [[VIDEOID:7454ac17efbcc2ad8d9dfa1eb7991478]] I really wanted to like this watch. Aesthetically very pleasing and it has exactly what I was looking for and the battery life is impeccable! I just wish the features actually worked. I thought I maybe have received a faulty watch but after going to their website, it seems these have been an issue for over a year with no solutions. Four issues (all that have been on their website forum for over a year without any solutions from the company): 1. My biggest gripe is that they report it works with MyFitnessPal. I use this because their healthmate app doesn't have food logging. Their Withings app does not automatically sync the step count to Myfitnesspal. You have to open up their app, refresh it, then open up myfitnesspal every time. This should be done automatically like every other watch. If you don't do this, then your steps will be logged incorrectly every day (see video) 2. Step count from their app vs watch step count off both off somehow. I don't understand this since their app should be getting the step count from the watch, but the app always reports more steps (see both pictures) 3. Gets email from my Gmail account widget however it does not send notifications from the iPhone email widget. 4. You have to unpair and pair every morning if you have your iPhone set to DND overnight. Otherwise, you don't get any notifications. Also, the increased the prices on their watches. I purchased this for $150 and they are now selling it for $200. For that amount, I’d suggest the garmin vevomove 3 (which is what I replaced this with) or the fossil HR. Also, I still have my heard back from their customer service. Terrible product and service

title: Not impressed
text: I really liked the idea of a tracker that actually looked like a watch. Also the steel backing is very nice and not irritating to my skin. That being said, compared with my Fitbit this watch is somewhat lacking. Yes, the heart rate works well, but the step tracker is nowhere near accurate! I have been walking and pacing today and the watch says I have only walked 260 steps. I checked it last week, counting the steps I took to get to my kitchen and back. 25 steps and the watch said 0. Apparently it will not count the steps if my arm isn’t moving. Wish I had bought a new Fitbit instead.

title: Watch is of No Use Without the App
text: The watch itself is well made and is probably comfortable to wear but I can't truly say as I returned the watch for a refund. Sadly, Withings has a policy that in order to set up the watch, you must agree to all the terms to open an account before you can even download the App. I would have no objection to the account, if the workout data was stored on my phone rather than the cloud. Withings and partners have access along with potentially 3rd parties. Called Withings CS and no work around to set up and account unless all terms are agreed to. Poor business practice.

title: Great battery life, good app integration, nice looking
text: I had 5 criteria for a smartwatch: battery life, heart rate tracking, sleep tracking, integration with Google Fit, and aesthetics. This watch does well on each of those. I'm 9 days in and the battery is at 60%. The HealthMate app works pretty well, and syncs easily with the watch, and offers configurable integration with Google Fit. Sleep tracking seems pretty accurate. Heart rate tracking is accurate but only sample's intermittently AFAICT. Finally, it looks and acts like a normal watch, and I like that. As noted by others, there is no backlight on the watch face, so you can't see the hands in the dark. And you will want the white watch face to be able to read it easily in the light. Update 10/2021 4 months in and I am still very happy with this watch. I've charged it 5 times, so battery life is staying consistent. The HealthMate app is pretty good. The watch reliably syncs with the app. Definitely the best smartwatch that I've tried.

title: Smart Fitness Tracker
text: Sometimes the key to fitness is accountability. This watch can be your personal accountability coach. It keeps track of all of the important factors like sleep, heart rate, and stress. It may help you notice small changes that could prevent serious health problems. The app is easy to navigate even for the tech challenged. It's an important tool that you can use to improve your health. I highly recommend it. Thanks so much for taking the time to read this review. I hope the information that I've provided helps make your decision a little easier.

title: Excellent sports watches
text: These watches provide you with so many options, you will be amazed. It is even more amazing how long the battery will last. You get all around health tracking, which includes 24 hour heart monitoring, sleep monitoring, blood oxygen saturation monitoring and more. You also get 90 built in sports modes, stress load monitoring, anywhere from 12 to 45 days between battery charging, voice control and water resistance to 5 atmospheres. When a watchmaker indicates water resistance, that is not the same as water proof. So, follow all guidelines when it comes to water. This watch is stylish and has more utility than many other watches of this kind.

title: Easy setup
text: My first "smart" watch, so far it is working perfectly. Had to pair with my phone, and an initial charge. The battery life is lasting through the day, with a charge while I work. The settup was easy and was able to fully use it. Really makes living on the go a little easier.

title: Great battery life but that's it
text: I was so excited about this watch because of the great battery life and it really was great. I used every setting I could ever need like always on display, tilt to wake, full brightness etc and I still easily got 7 days on a single charge which is pretty much unheard of for smart watches. The issue that I had is with the software. The app notifications were not great and there were very few options on customizing them. For instance every time I played a new song on oandora it vibrated and flash the song name which became pretty annoying. I also couldn't get Alexa to work no matter how hard I tried and I even reached out to customer support and they never answered me. I wish this ran wear os or another software that was better but the hardware is great. But sadly not great enough to make this the watch I'll wear every day.

Battery life is good so far. Any smartwatch that you don't have to charge every day or throughout the day is a plus. You can change the strap with any quick release 22mm strap. That way, you can use the silicone band for sport and switch it up to a leather band or even a link band to dress it up when you're out on the town. The price is phenomenal for what you get compared to other smart watches. It can be found on sale here on Amazon from time to time. It works with both iOS and Android. I recommend giving it a try. title: Great, fun watch for a better price
text: To truly get this watch to track your exercise, you need to set it to an exercise mode whenever you’re active. For me, that means while at work I set it to “walk” exercise mode, and then it accurately tracks my exercise for the day. Otherwise, it really doesn’t monitor heart rate well. The sleep monitoring works well for when I sleep, even with naps, but I don’t believe it’s various ratios of light sleep vs. deep sleep, number of times awake, etc. it seems sketchy at best. And again if one doesn’t have it set to an exercise mode, it doesn’t accurately track your heart rate throughout the day. Having it operating for exercise mode also drains the battery significantly- I tend to charge my watch every other day. This doesn’t bother me because it charges fast (20%-100% in 15 minutes) but just note-worthy. The gps tracking was impressive to me. I like to hike mountain trails, and it accurately showed how far my walk was, altitude, etc. (of course only if I had it set to exercise “hike mode, but still). Was fun to see the map of my walk, how intensive certain parts were, etc. Have worn it while kayaking and brief swims and it hasn’t had any issues with water. Batter charging nodes haven’t worn down at all (I have a cheaper old smart watch and it’s battery nodes corroded over time and it sucked, this one hasn’t had any issue)(plus I sweat a lot so it’s impressive how little this one shows any wear at all). Overall love this watch. Has withstood the tests of time, constant wear, and has been a fun way to check on my health, just taken with a grain of salt.

text: Bought this for my wife for Christmas. Everything was fine until now, two months later, it says her heart rate is 30 beats per minute. It's normally 70 to 80 beats per minute. Hope yours lasts longer!

title: Tiny Display
text: This watch is so cute, and I really wanted to make it work. However, the display on it is super small. The text is tiny, and it looks like it's 8bit. I had to return it.

title: Careful of mesh band
text: Pretty watch, easy clasp, nice displays. A filament came loose from the mesh band and catches on clothing. I’ve tried coating it with clear nail polish, but it’s wearing off. Annoying.

It would not allow me to select imperial measurements which would mean I would need to convert my weight each time I weighed myself. After that there was very little communication between the watch and the app.

I wear my fitness tracker a lot but sometimes it looks a bit too sporty for my outfit so I decided to get a watch that’s complimentary to jewelry and dresses but still can offer the modern technology of a smart watch. This thing is the perfect solution! It looks pretty, but not too bright and shiny. Just a nice muted silver band and a pretty design on the face! Looks great with all my boho jewelry looks and minimalistic looks too!

I like how it looks but still learning what it does it does not stay on like a original watch you have to keep touching the screen but to me that doesn't matter. title: A nice, beginners watch.
text: My wife loves it and that’s all that’s important! She likes the light blue watch band and it’s ‘smart’ enough.

title: Love it for what it is
text: The watch is very good for what I want to use it for. I love how it looks (like it isn't a fitness tracker) and the price is decent for this type of watch! It's not too thick or heavy and I love the color (silver/blue). The good: the menu on the watch is extensive and it took me a few days to go through it and get used to how it works. Once I learned my way around, it's good. Remember to start activity tracking on the watch before you finish! LOL. Others: Battery life. Charging. Fast synching to phone. Message and email alert and can read most of them right away on the watch. The fine: App. I would love a way to delete some of the options but haven't found it yet. It's a bit confusing to find the main screen after leaving it and is there a way to stop it from tracking flights of stairs? This isn't something I do right now and it's just too much. APP is sometimes too much. It does sync with phone/watch no problem and updates quickly. The bad: As other reviewers have said the strap it comes with does start to irritate after 1-2 weeks of consistently wearing it. I had to remove it at night or leave it off for a day. I didn't wear it in the shower. The wifi connection alert :( . I had to disable watch wifi when my phone was IN THE NEXT ROOM. This is the most annoying feature EVER. Imagine waking up by a buzz saying that the watch wifi connection is broken and then 2 minutes later another buzz saying the watch is now connected. This goes on and on and on. I started to turn on 'don't disturb' on the watch and set a sleep schedule (sleep and wake) on the app. These seem to help. Overall, I would recommend this watch to someone who wants to track fitness (time, HR, calories, distance), a good price, a known brandname, and a stylish looking watch.

title: Three Stars
text: I love the watch face but wanted more functions. Paid the extra money for the VivoActive 3

title: Not for me but good customer service.
text: After trying this for a few months i have too many dislikes unfortunately. I have the silver & white face. Can't read it, especially outside or in any bright light. Syncing problems, too expensive for what it does. Hot & uncomfortable especially to sleep in. Going back to a less expensive one that actually does much better. Also, in case you didn't read, it does not do blood pressure. The $40 one does everything including blood pressure & the app is more user friendly to me. That said, Garmin does have good customer service.

title: Stylish
text: I really like this watch/step counter. I have got so many great compliments on it and how its so stylish compared to other smart watches! It does everything! Surprise it measure stress throughout the day, it was an eye opener! You won’t be disappointed!

title: Can this tracker be fixed?
text: I like the size and the style of the watch. I especially like the fact that I can wear in the pool for water aerobics. However today it stoped tracking. Not sure why. I ordered a new charging cord. I am surprised that it didn’t tell me it was going out. I like the fact that it tells time.

title: Really good first smartwatch
text: This was a gift for my husband for Christmas. He takes pride in remaining as lo-tech as his family and work will allow, but I just KNEW he'd appreciate the text notifications, step-tracking, and weather features of this watch. Making it a gift, he felt obligated to at least try it. LOL. Happy to say, he really likes this watch! It doesn't LOOK like a smartwatch, which is important for him, and it really is good at the very basic things you might want from a smartwatch. He's not a fitness geek, nor does he want to be super-connected all the time; just wants to know when he gets texts from family and colleagues, and since he doesn't always have his phone at the ready, the watch is great for this. Response time to my own texts has improved dramatically. ;) His only complaint is that it's hard to wake the screen up at night to check the time. He used to have a backlit watch that he wore to bed, and that's been an adjustment. He has a clock next to his bed now. Not a huge change, but it's annoying (to him especially) that he can't easily check the time on his watch in the middle of the night. It's strange that they took the features of this watch so far and then were like, "Screw it, we can't possibly add any more (simple) features to this watch." You could've added that one! Still ... it gets a solid 4 stars. It's a good-looking, stealthy smartwatch that has 90% of the basics down pat for your typical user.

title: Not great
text: Battery runs down quick. Watch does not always tell Tim correctly.

title: Love the style!
text: The sleep tracking is not very accurate, but love the style and works in tracking steps. Battery life is great.

title: Slick, Light, Good Battery. A good hybrid.
text: I did a lot of research and knew what I was getting into. The tiny screen is not very sharp, it's black and white, and you can only read the first few words of a message. That's all I needed. I wanted an analog watch with basic fitness tracking and the ability to see my notifications without pulling out my phone. This does the trick perfectly. I've coupled it with a few leather quick release straps and it looks nice enough to wear to the office. You don't get all of the functionality of a full lcd smartwatch, but if that's what you wanted you wouldn't be looking at a hybrid. This seems to be the best of both worlds as of 5.10.18.

title: Garmin customer service is a joke
text: I went to charge my watch that I've had for a little over 2 weeks and I notice the little sticker to the left has fiber optic strings that were under the sticker before and attached at the top of the little sticker box area, customer service for Garmin was rude overall and said the watch looked to be in bad shape and I asked how given the item was basically 2 weeks old, he said nothing should be there my picture wasn't the best and just return it and no sorry for your time etc.. I don't know what that area is for and he refused to answer ..truthfully I thought they would be more reputable but clearly not... let the buyer be wear

title: Love it!!
text: Really love this watch! I’ve been using it for a long time! A lot of people have complained about how hard it is to read... I think the only issue is when you are outside, but it doesn’t bother me! Great watch!
