text: I really enjoy this watch and it's features. If I could I would rate it a 4.8 for 2 reasons: though waterproof, this activity tracker cannot tell me how far I have swum and it is VERY difficult to read in the sun or while wearing sunglasses.

title: amazing
text: Bought this for my wife and she loves it. Fits amazing she was a bit worried at first cause most watches are uncomfortable to her but this actually have several fitment holes that allows for great adjustability. Tracking for pedometer is very handy and the message reading display works well also. Only issue is the battery life isn't as long as it states but my wife's job does require a lot of motions with her hands so it was probably constant on and off due to wrist motions. I highly recommend this and color is very good as well.

title: Excellent watch and activity tracker heart rate monitor for daily use
text: This is what I wanted: a watch that also tracks activities and monitors heart rate 24/7. It has a nice quality and is easy to use as an activity tracker. The optical heart rate sensor is the first one that works for me for daily activity and heart rate tracking (I tried fitbit charge HR, garmin forerunner 235 and all gave nonsense results all the time) and as such it provides a much more relevant picture of daily activity than the ones with motion sensors only (2hrs of XC skiing or rowing and you don't meet your daily step goal). It's very practical (waterproof, battery lasts about a week and charges really quickly) and my style advisors say it looks good. If you want a smart watch (check emails, answer texts etc.) this is not it. Similarly, if you want a sports watch, this is not it: it has limited built-in selectable activities (no cycling???), no way to integrate heart rate strap and the built-in heart rate monitor is useless for real-time guidance during training (e.g. interval training, mountain bike XC skiing). Also, I found the VO2 max on this particular unit useless.

title: Has two significant shortcomings
text: A nice looking watch with good features; however, two issues made it essentially useless for my wife. First, and most importantly, we bought it to notify her of calls/texts while she is busy with little ones in her preschool room. The vibration notification is too weak, even on high, for her to notice. Have seen several others with the same issue on Garmin chat. Second, the watch face is hard to discern - must stop and look very carefully to figure out time - no quick glances here. After a couple of cheap imports with similar features didn't work, I was willing to spend the money for a name brand, but, alas, it doesn't do the job either. If anyone knows of a step counter/watch with phone pairing and a good vibration notification, PLEASE let me known - I'm sure Amazon is getting tired of my returns.

title: So far, so good
text: I just received this today and first impression is that I like it a lot more than my vivoactive, which broke a few months ago. The look and comfort are great. I also love how it is so slim, no buttons, and it looks like a classic watch unless you activate the notifications. I'm hopeful the battery life and tracking matches up to my last garmin!

title: Expected a lot more
text: Bought two of those - one for myself and one for my sister and both have the same issues. First the good thing: it looks really nice and you can wear it also when dressed up some. Negatives: Step and stairs count doesn't work. I have my stair goal set on 10 and some days, when I max climb on the second floor, I hit the goal and sometimes, even though walking up to the 5th floor three times, I never hit the goal. It only shows the phone number, when someone is calling, not the name. So, can't really pick up the calls from watch. According to the sleep track I seem to be sleeping much more than I actually do.

title: Not what I expected
text: The product is good, but there is a flaw in it which is dealbreaker for me: it attracts fingerprints incredibly fast. The entire design of the watch is based on touching the screen and the screen gets dirty and blurry even after a few interactions! The screen does not have a good resolution and is not responsive enough. Also, the watch band is not comfortable (at this price I expected something more elegant). Anyways, the bottom line is that it did not work for me.

title: Great buy!
text: Great watch! Just what I was looking for. The band is a little tough now because I forgot to take it off before a shower.

title: I really loved the concept of this watch
text: I really loved this watch the short time I used it but wish I would've gotten the premium version. I'm a bit of a watch buff but gotten the cheaper version and it definitely didn't feel like it would withstand too much of an everyday beating after prolonged use. Wound up returning but was definitely an awesome original idea! I'd recommend, but the more expensive, more solid premium version (unfortunately).

title: Pretty fitness tracker.
text: I've had about a month to use the watch and am neither impressed nor completely disappointed with its performance. I wanted a watch that looked presentable, had a heart rate and step tracker and could track my workouts (I mostly run), I had no interest in getting any type of notifications to the watch, so after a few days I turned this feature off. THE PROS - The watch does look presentable, as do both bands it comes with - Set-up time was probably 5 minutes or less and I have not had any connectivity issues - I am satisfied with the battery life - Heart rate and step count are accurate - The automatic workout tracking is great once you get the hang of it. THE ANNOYANCES - The screen is not as responsive as I would have liked, which is incredibly inconvenient when trying to start or stop the timer during a workout. - The screen can be hard to see when outdoors. - Sleep tracking is off (I think it kinda just goes by what you say your bedtime and wake time is and often confuses sleep for when you are stationary/sitting/laying but awake) - The display part is too small to really be able to get anything out of notifications, so if that is what you're looking for, this is probably not the right device for you REASONS I WOULD NOT SPEND $350 ON THIS DEVICE, IF I COULD DO IT OVER... - It is completely useless if you are a runner. I understand that it does not "have" GPS, but I would have hoped that it could use the GPS in my phone to at least track my runs with some accuracy. Yes, I should have done more research. I'm happy that I can track my heart rate, but when the pace/mileage is nonsense, it's more work going back and trying to correct it. So if you are looking for a device that will track your runs accurately, this is probably not it (unless there is something here I'm missing, so if anyone has gotten this device to work with strava, please tell me your secrets) To summarize, it is a $350 ($299 now) heart rate and step tracker. Neither impressive nor completely disappointing.

title: Love the look and size
text: Love the look and size. Smaller and more feminine looking then the Fitbit Ionic. My Fitbit died and I did t want the big square look again. This looks like a real watch. I love the alarms as I have to take medicine 5 times a day and I can set it to alarm at those times. It goes off every 10 minutes until you clear it. Just like my Fitbit did. Hard to see the lit up area I. The day like like others have said but I can see the watch hands so that’s fine to me. So far seems up track everything well. Took a little setting up but finally got it to connect with my fitness pal app. So far I am in love with this Garmin ❤️ I did turn off the display when I turn my arm as you can easily double tap and get that to display. Otherwise the watch hands are always moving out of the way. I did have to calibrate the hands twice so I hope that does not remain and issues. Otherwise I love this watch tracker.

title: Not as accurate as Fitbit, but prettier
text: I’ve had this watch for about 6 months. It’s definitely nice looking - I appreciate that it’s not sporty and I can wear it to work. However, the tracking in general (especially sleep) is not nearly as accurate as a Fitbit. I frequently hit the stair goal while driving... I also am annoyed by the notifications, as you get EVERY notification from your phone and can’t limit whether you just want texts or calls. If Fitbit ever offers an option for a watch face tracker, I will absolutely switch back.

title: nice smatwatch
text: only have it for a week so far I like this watch it looks good and it is easy to use so far it it keeps really good time all the functions work good steps and mileage are almost right on. Would give it a 5 stars if you would not have to get screen protector for it.

title: Not as advertised
text: Watch was clearly worn for a while even though it said it was new. No other damage or signs of wear so we will keep it.

title: Dont buy, Garmin is a great brand with many great products, just not this one...
text: Don't buy. Go with the one with buttons or stem. The watch hands are constantly need to adjustment so it points the time correctly. The capacitive touch sounds cool at first but after 2+ years of using it, it was a pain in the a$$. The lack of buttons or stem and relying on a small touch area makes the UX really frustrating when you need to adjust somethong, especially hands.

title: Can’t see the digital display outdoors
text: The digital display is unreadable outdoors, making the sport hybrid part of the watch completely wasted.

title: So far so good
text: I’ve had this thing for a total of 6 hours now, and I really like it except for a few small things. 1- I can’t see the digital part of the display in the sunlight, and considering I live in Los Angeles, that’s kinda important. I have to make sure I’m in the shade when I start an activity, just so I can start it correctly. 2- there’s no quick start icon for biking. It has walking, running, weights, other cardio and something else that I can’t remember because I’ll never use it. I can go into the app and edit an activity to be biking, but I can’t have it set to that automatically. 3- in the app there’s a hydration tracker, but there’s no way to do it on the device at all. I can’t speak to the accuracy of the steps counter, but I like that there’s a custom step thing where I can change the length of my stride. That’s be nice because my distance is always off. I have long legs and I never get credit for my full distance because I’m just not taking as many steps as someone shorter. Also- it’s pretty. That’s probably the number one reason I got this one and not a different one. I’ll admit to that. It’s a bit bigger than I expected, but looking back at the pictures, I should have expected this size.

title: JUNK
text: What a waste of money. The hands show the incorrect time. I love this watch, but after reading all the the issues online with this thing and keeping time, I CANNOT RECOMMEND buying this. What a waste. This isn't the Garmin I've been using for years. Their quality control is slipping.

title: Love this watch (former Apple Watch owner)
text: First let me say, I briefly had a Series 1 Apple Watch. Hated it. And we are Apple people (iPhones, iPads, MacBooks, Apple TV’s, the works). Apple Watch is crazy dorky like you have a computer on your wrist (a small step up from a calculator Watch). And I do not need to talk to my Watch like Dick Tracey or call Ubers when my phone is in hand. But I wanted a smart watch which tracked fitness, sleep and had alerts. I looked at the Samsung Frontier and LG but then found this. I wanted a watch to replace my 20 year old Tag Heuer and I wanted one that looked good. Love this Garmin. The day I bought it someone on my team went and bought one. It’s awesome looking and just works. All my phone alerts come through the watch and it is much more subtle that the Apple Watch in how they appear. If you want a watch that looks like a...watch, this is it.
A movado look a like smart watch amazing features iOS compatible , water proof

title: This is my fourth Garmin!
text: This is my 4th Garmin watch. Every few years I upgrade. I've been very happy with all of my past watches, but this watches display stopped working after 5 months. I guess it's time to try a different brand.

title: Good Hybrid, lousy battery life
text: I’ve had the watch for almost a year. Ivr had fossil and withings hybrid watches as well. Battery life started with about 10 days, then a week, then 5 days. Now, it’s about 3 days. The digital display is not as clear as the Withings Hybrid, (which sucks for those of us who need reading glasses) but it’s a cooler looking watch. My favorite part: when I get a spam call on my cell phone (in my pocket), I can decline it on the watch. Also, I’ve used the “find phone” several times to find my phone in my house. The audio allows to play/pause/forward/back but no volume control unlike the fossil watches. I like that it’s waterproof and I can swim and shower with it - unlike the withings watch. Overall, it’s a good watch, but not perfect. Not yet.

title: Attractive BUT...
text: The watch is really attractive and fits good on the arm. There is a little difficult understanding the fitness icons on the watch and some difficulty selecting the actual fitness icon that relates to your activity. The only thing that really really bothers me is...the watch scars my arm leaving dark spots and then my skin peels. I wear it loose and it still scars my arm. I'm thinking its the light that flashes on the backside. I'm likely going to get another watch.

title: inaccurate tracking!
text: I'm on my second one due to my first just being replaced because of the inaccuracy of its sleep tracking. well this one is doing the exact same thing. it says I'm sleeping when I'm doing anything from watching TV to reading to literally walking around my house! when this dies I'll be going back to fitbit.

title: Simple but Annoyed
text: At first, I loved the way this looks. It is simple and does what I need it to. The look and ability are exactly what I was hoping for. The ability to use the touch screen is nearly impossible. It is hard to touch and tap the screen. The worst part is that this watch ONLY works with IPHONE! Literally. I bought this watch as I moved back to Android and was highly disappointed to learn that the apps for Garmin are only on iphone. Don't say I didn't warn you.

title: Yeah cool so far
text: Yeah cool so far. I've been waiting on this guy for a while. No silent alarms...maybe they can add it? (Either I missed the settings or it is added. Nice!) Also is the brightness time adjustable? You check the time, the display pops up but dims in a nanosecond...why so dim so quickly?(Same here. Found the setting for brightens control time out. Nice!) Super light weight. Not too big. Functions well.

title: Easy to work with
text: Bought replacement watch band. The grommets were out. Garmin replaced it strait away!

title: Loved the Watch - Won't Pair with New Android Phone
text: i'm returning this for the same reason I returned my fitbit versa. Love the Analogue watch, but it only pairs with Iphone, won't pair after the first time with any android phone. This is a huge bug, if it had worked, i would've kept the watch.

title: Customize the watch face!
text: Someone asked about rose face possibilities-I took a sunset photo with gold color and up loaded it as my watch face! Fun! You can add a photo of you sweetheart, dog or grandkids!

title: WOW I love it!
text: I have a higher-end Fitbit which I also love. The only thing is I wanted something that looks like a classic dress watch. This does it! As a smart watch, it's not as full featured as my Fitbit, but it's still packed with good smart watch features. I especially love reading text messages from it and checking my heart rate. The music control feature is good also. When not using smart features it looks like a regular, nice dress watch!. Mine came with the Italian leather light brown band which is beautiful; however, I bought dark brown, black, and also a stainless steel band for it also. The bands are easy-release so they are easy to change from one to another, so it's like having several watches. EVERY band looks beautiful on this watch, and because I got the silver stainless steel color the silver stainless steel band I bought for it looks amazing - it looks like it came that way. If you want a very powerful smart watch you may want something else - the display on this is small and features are limited. But if you want a watch that has average (well, slightly above average in my opinion) "smart" features but has the classic look of a dress watch, then this is the watch for you! Battery seems to last around 5 days which is better than my Fitbit. Oh, and I'm not throwing away my Fitbit - I will still use that a lot, but this will be great to wear to the office or to formal functions. Prior to this I was wearing my regular watches for the good looks but this really is a great solution to have both dress watch looks and smart features. The price is good - I honestly might not have bought it but it was an amazing discount on Prime day. I have always had an eye out for something like this but was not really looking to buy one when I did, but the Prime day deal really induced me to buy it now - I even had at the back of my mind to jump on the deal and then debate later whether to return it or not, but once I got it I was excited to see if it met my needs and boy am I glad I opened it, it is fantastic!

title: Advertised as new, but it was clearly worn before
text: I have not tried the product yet. I am too grossed out. Upon opening the box I discovered that the product appears to have been previously worn (despite being advertised as new). There is skin or something on the back of the band and the box did not have any seals or any of the typical plastic pieces covering the glass and such. Very disappointed!

title: Impressive
text: All of the features you could expect from a Garmin fitness/activity watch but with professional class and style. Compatible with any 20mm quick release band, accurate tracking on all metrics, and notifications for everything without a lengthy set up process. I like that I can customize the quick cards on this watch and how the analog hands move out of the way when using the touch screen. The best feature for me is that this a true blend of analog and smart fitness technology. As an active sales professional in a high volume environment it was important to me to discretely stay in connection with my incoming notifications while with a client. High volume sales is often a stressful position so it was equally important to have a system to monitor my general health and activity. The steps and calories counted match closely to my phone's on-body tracker and the sleep tracker is spot on. The charging clip is an interesting variation from the regular plug or wireless charging options which guarantees my cat won't disrupt the charging overnight while still giving a water tight seal to the device. I haven't tested it in the hot tub yet, and I may not simply because of the heat, but I was in the pool for half an hour last night and it did great. Customizing your screen settings can drastically effect battery life but you have the option to control the brightness and how long the screen stays on among other things. I have owned a couple different smart watches over the years and this is by far my absolute favorite overall so far. Comfortable, confident, stylish, and accurate. Glass screen shield fits perfectly in the bezel, leather band is breaking in nicely... I couldn't be more pleased, especially for the price!

title: Worst screen on a fitness tracker
text: I was so disappointed. This watch has nice features, which is why I gave it two stars instead of one. But the screen was so dim I could not even see it! It was worse if daylight where I couldn't see it at all. I asked several people who gave me the same feedback. So, essentially worthless. I've had fitbit and apple which are golden compared to this one.

title: Also if screen freezes it may mean the screen is dirty or the screen protector needs to be changed
text: Works well. Have some issues when I wear it swimming. Screen sometimes freezes & I power-off then turn it back on & it erases past activities but saves past records? Will try locking screen when I swim & see if that helps. Also if screen freezes it may mean the screen is dirty or the screen protector needs to be changed. I wiped the screen a few times & suddenly it un-froze. Freezing may also mean watch needs to be recharged. HR Monitor works well as long as watch is securely on above wrist bones. Adjusting the light to dim & turning HR monitor off saves the battery also. Like the color & strap is comfy.

title: Five Stars

title: I love this Garmin!

title: YES -- a great upgrade from the other brand

Much more info available than past generation F*tbits, easier to read for...um... aging eyes, comfortable, and it's doing great despite some contact with water. Been using a few months, and he is still quite happy with this purchase. He believes it is more accurate considering he is in and out of heavy equipment all day -- a problem for the other brand.

title: Battery life
text: Works great, after six months I'm having to charge the battery every day. Not good.

title: Very nice band. It's very accurate in steps count
text: Very nice band . It's very accurate in steps count, also monitor your heart rate and sleep. You can get your notifications on screen and you can read them or dismiss them, see weather forecast, control music player, etc. Some downside is that the app has to be open on the phone to these feature to work. But overall is a really nice band. It's ot as slim as a fitbit, but it has gps integrated so you can go outside without the phone and your activity will be recorded completely

title: Don't waste your money
text: I received the Garmin HR+ for Christmas. By the beginning of February it was already malfunctioning. (Just past the 30-day return window, hmmm). 1. It doesn't record steps properly; after a particularly busy day of housecleaning, running errands, going to the mall (walking the entire mall twice), I come home exhausted and see that my Garmin tracked 865 steps for the entire day. I usually get almost that much just getting ready to go out in the morning. I am up and down stairs at work, yet Garmin thinks I take the elevator, I've never had it record steps. 2. Time and date won't sync properly. I have to set the time manually. Who knows what day and time it is, I need to check my phone for that info. 3. Battery life is terrible. My old Garmin had a changeable battery that lasted almost three years. This one has to be plugged in and charged constantly. I had it on the charger all day yesterday, and all night last night, it's 10:00 am (had to check my phone for the time just now )and the battery is half-empty, or half-full if you're so inclined. You also have to have a special Garmin charger, it won't work with a micro-USB like every other electronic on the planet. So when I travel I have to remember to bring that charger along with my phone charger. The band is awful clunky and hard to put on, the upside is, I don't need to put it on, because is doesn't work most of the time (there's the glass half-full upside to that.) Bottom line, I'm switching to another brand if Garmin won't let me return this piece of garbage.

title: New to fitness trackers-this one hard to learn
text: This is my first fitness tracker and I chose it because I can record heart rate and I can wear it swimming. I'm by no means tech ignorant but I found the lack of documentation and learning support from Garmin super frustrating. I had to just figure it out myself basically and that took a while and I'n still not completely up to speed. It has tons of features and so I will keep this-just wanted to let people know it's not easy to set up if you're a neophyte to fitness trackers. The material it's made of for some reason gives me a rash under the band. Also the heart rate sensor only works if you have the strap relatively tight against your skin.

title: So glad I got this and not a FitBit!!!
text: so glad I got this and not a FitBit. At this price, you can't find another watch that is water proof, has it's own internal gps, and will control your music. I also love the app. I love being able to see all the graphs. There is a learning curve to using the app, but that's what you get with any device or programming that can do a lot. the only thing I don't like about it (minus 1/4 a star) is that it has a high profile, but most other smart watches at this price with these features do as well. Just be prepared to struggle a bit with tight jacket cuffs. Having a heart rate monitor has been instrumental in better calorie and sleep tracking. It is fairly accurete (not perfect). Sometimes the stair climber counts other things as climbing stairs. But, this is to be expected with a pedometer - it tracks things like that with arm swinging and such.

title: Five Stars
text: great for keeping up with the HR and many daily and weekly activities.

title: Pros: Lots of options -- Cons: Lots of options
text: The device itself is easy to use... that is until you explore the garmin connect app. Lots of information and data to geek out on, excellent flexibility for workout configurations, but the cluttered graphics are nonintuitive as your attention does not know where to focus on the multitude of information provided. In fact, just setting up notifications from iPhone to the vivosmart HR+ device was... well weird. I had all the options to notify selected yet nothing worked. After 10 minutes and no changes made either on the device or app it just started worked properly. Backlight is a joke even when level was turned to full illumination. After beginning to understand the flow of the device and app software I decided to return the unit. I realized spending my time playing with unit consumed time for my workout; inevitably a config won't work as intended and before you know it 10 minutes has passed without beginning a workout. At the moment smartphone and activity trackers have too many bugs - sticking with a dedicated running watch or my Apple Watch and Seconds Pro app.

title: Nighttime screen look not so hot
text: The app works fine, watch works for everything. The only 2 things I did not like is the screen brightness at nighttime, it has to be set at level 4 which is the highest setting to see it. Doing this eats up the battery. The other thing is when I am not walking it still counts steps because of arm movements. So I only wear it when I power walk and I try not to wear it at dark hours.

title: This is a great motivator to keep you active
text: Bought this for my girlfriend and she loves it. Tracks her workouts as well as steps. This is a great motivator to keep you active.

title: Garmin product did not live up to its claims.
text: I had hoped that this tracker would work for me since it was a Garmin product. I was very disappointed. It was the exact same as the cheap one, with the exact same product I had purchased which did not work either. Garmin products should be more helpful but are not.

title: I like the HR+ but its only as good as the ...
text: I like the HR+ but its only as good as the app that serves it, for the first six months it worked fine. But the next two months have been nothing but trouble. problems withe it connecting garmin even replaced it under warranty thinking it was the HR+. and still the same problem it will work sometimes (not very often) it also will sync with one cal. count and five min. later the cal. count will be less then half of what it first showed. Example 1.6 mi walk at first it showed 175 cal.after down load five min. later it showed 73 ca. By calculations it should have been 132 approximately. I have been talking with garmin and going in circles for the last two months.

title: What's Not to Like?

title: I bought this one thinking it will give me more ...

title: This has been nice upgrade for my 14 year old that was a ...
text: This has been nice upgrade for my 14 year old that was a religious Fitbit user allowing her now to receive her text and not have to have her phone on the runs to tack mileage.

title: Easy to use and accurate
text: Easy to operate, Does what i bought it to do

title: Tested this against my Garmin Fenix 3 with chest strap and I have a tip
text: OK: I have tested this against my Garmin Fenix 3 with chest strap and I have a tip. The Fenix 3, I do trust very much the HR readings I get..... so I did some workouts while wearing both the Vivosmart HR+ and the Fenix. While doing road biking, elliptical and spin. What I learned was this...If you wear the Vivosmart HR+ down on your wrist near the hand the HR readings will be off as much as 20 + beats. You need to wear the Vivosmart HR+ at least two inches or more above the wrist firmly strapped(not tight just firmly strapped). When i did that I practically got identical HR readings from both the Fenix and the Vivosmart HR+. Which is great...but it also means that when I wear it daily just at work or casual low on the wrist, the HR readings recorded i do believe are suspect, I also think that nobody else is manufacturing a wrist worn that is more accurate as Vivosmart HR+.

title: Perfect!
text: Love this, some issues with documenting stairs or energy used, but overall a great product. GPS works perfectly for me.

title: Tracking my progess made easy
text: I fricken love this watch!!! No issues with the batteries, or the band. It fits well and tracks my heart rate as well as a wrist HR monitor could or should. The customization of the interface is wonderful and allows for the addition or removal of widgets that are better suited to your needs. The best part is the DETAIL that is given after each workout. Elevation, HR, pace, a map of your route, rest periods, stride, etc. I mean... how could you not improve with such a detailed account of your workout. I did, however, find that I didn't get as much detail out of a gym session lifting weights and doing calisthenics, but it was still detailed with calories and heart rate and rest periods. Oh and have I mentioned the sleep tracking? I love it! I can see why I feel the way I do in the mornings and it matches up with the tracking. I feel crummy and see that I didn't get a lot of deep sleep and vice versa. It even lets me know the times I woke up (bathroom trips) and I get to see how it affects my sleep there after (guess I need to cut back on the heavy drinking before bed). I will say that within the two weeks I've had this item, the only flaw is the fragility of the screen. It has a small scuff (not scratch) on the face. But it's not bad and hardly noticeable. I've had this for 2 weeks and have had no issues with it besides the screen. Love it!

title: Great deal
text: Great product.takes a while for it to adjust accuracy to my steps. But very happy with it

title: Good quality
text: Bought as a gift for my mom. She is technologically challenged but can use this!

title: Needs some more work
text: I have used and owned a lot of Garmin products and this has the worst and most incomplete user manual of any of the Garmin products. Normally you will find screen captures and clear instruction. This one is very unclear whether changes and customizations are done online, on your mobile app or on the device. You will get better information by going on Youtube. The device itsself works well, the band is the most comfortable of the field and it has a long battery life not using GPS. The automatic backlight does not function nearly as well as the Fitbit, but the device does surpass comparable Fitbit models in performance and durability.

title: and I love that it's waterproof so I can wear when I'm ...
text: I've had many other fit bands before and this is my fave! Accurately counts steps, and I love that it's waterproof so I can wear when I'm swimming or in the shower so it doesn't get all smelly like my fitbits used to. :)

title: Too Bulky, iirregular syncing, poor tracking, but it does keep the time!
text: I've been wearing the Garmin Vivosmart HR+ since Christmas. Pros: It keeps the time Cons: It's too bulky and actually hurts the top side of my wrist. It doesn't track my steps or the use of the eliptical nearly as well as my old fitbit did. It continually syncs and unsyncs with my phone all day long. I usually have to manually sync it at least once per day. I am either switching back to a fitbit or the apple watch next christmas. my old fitbit lasted 3 years. This garmin will probably last 10 years sitting in my drawer!

title: I like the app - easy to read and understand
text: I'm really enjoying this tracker. I've had two FitBits in the past, but this seems to be more accurate for steps, although slower to measure stairs. I like the app - easy to read and understand.

title: Best GPS watch I"ve had and the least expensive.
text: I've worn this watch for well over a year and I still love it! The GPS for hiking in the mountains is more accurate than the other Garmin's I've had in the past. They were double or more the price of this, plus this one has lots of other useable apps. The battery holds a charge well. When it gives up the ghost, I will replace with the same!

title: I love this thing
text: I love this thing. My Fitbit dies exactly 4 days after my one year warranty expired, so I am never buying another Fitbit product. I am very happy with the Garmin product - it is very comfortable to wear, much more comfortable than the Fitbit. The interface is intuitive and the GPS feature works great. Very accurate heart rate measurement and recording. This is a great device.

title: Heart rate works great, even during my workouts
text: Heart rate works great,even during my workouts. steps are good, works decent for a casual runner. However, I can't get it to sync, and it won't shut the 0540 alarm I set on it initially. So now, I have to shut it off at night, which defeats my purpose of getting it to monitor my resting heart rate. Activities sync, just not the alarm.

title: great idea. terrible execution
text: great idea. terrible execution. the screen gets scratched even by your running hoodie sleeves. it is impossible to use because of the cheap material garmin chose for the screen. no tempered glass protector is available yet either. the product is too new. the ones offered for sale by 3 party sellers have bad ratings. none will stay attached if theres humidity. so, no to swimming pool, trails and try not to sweat while running:) ive returned mine and will be waiting for garmin to come to their senses.

title: But it functions great. The GPS isn't thrilling but I also dont ...
text: It's bulky for sure. I can't spin it under my arm either or I can't type. It gets caught taking clothes on/off. But it functions great. The GPS isn't thrilling but I also dont have great cell service in the boonies. It synced really easy with myfitnesspal.

title: Not your average tracker
text: I’m a former long time Fitbit user! I’ve been through 4 in 4 years. They don’t last long but it’s all I’ve known & they’re so user friendly! This one took a good week to grow on me! I honestly almost sent it back. It’s not user friendly at all. Just try setting a silent alarm! However it’s slowly growing on me as I learn & figure out how to navigate it! I’m starting to really like & realize it does so much more than the Fitbit! Happy to have finally graduated!!!

title: Almost Perfect
text: I love this thing, syncs fast and easy and tracks my steps and bike rides perfectly. One complaint is that the "low battery" light comes on way too late. Only gives you about 20 minutes warning until it dies. Only other complaint is that the stair counter seems off. One day I walked up 7 flights and it counted as 2 and another time I was riding around in a truck and it counted as 10...I'm guessing most people aren't buying this for that reason though.

title: Great tracker and support app
text: I have been really impressed with this tracker. The GPS on this device is astonishingly accurate. This was a welcome feature after coming from a Fitbit Charge 2 that seemed to merely estimate your location. In addition to the accurate GPS, the heart rate function seems spot on. I particularly liked the way that you could set heart zone alerts so that the device would alert you if your heart rate went outside of a pre-set zone while you are training. This is a great feature. Overall a great fitness tracker.

title: no need to worry about it getting wet
text: I bought this thinking it would track my laps while I swim, but it doesn't. those have to be entered manually but it is water proof and that I like.

title: I really wanted to love this product
text: I really wanted to love this product. It looks like it has some good features. Unfortunately, I found the screen all but unreadable in almost any light. Even when I could actually see the screen, the printing on it was so small it just wasn't worth the trouble. I give it 2 stars because returning it was really easy.

title: Great watch and both my wife and I have one
text: Great watch and both my wife and I have one. Very accurate on the GPS. Doesn't always synch readily and I have to figure out how to make it so my wife's watch won't symch to my phone and vice-versa. From my wife's point of view, not as stylish as she;d like so she won't wear it all the time, including to work. However, we tried the smaller Garmin model, it was inaccurate on the gps and did a lot less. The battery life is excellent though the snap on charge clip is a bit difficult.. Pulse sensor seems to be accurate. The band has some elasticity which makes for a comfortable fit. I can swim with it and have had no problems. For most apps, there is a choice among only 3 fields, a 4 field option would be nice. I got the extra screen protector and it has little problem sensing my touches; glad I did, our puppy already cracked one.

title: Does not track swimming. Comfortable and Simple to use - Garmin Support Center was WOnderfuL!
text: Love the smaller size compared to others out there. I did have an issue with an error code the first week I had it. Garmin Support was very responsive. We solved the issue together. They had not seen the error before. I deleted a recently added fitness app and the error went away. Some type of Bluetooth interference with their app. I have had it for about 6 weeks now. I picked this one for its ability to be in a pool. Even though this is advertised as being able to swim with, it does NOT track swimming activity. I have to run the “Cardio” selection to get the activity credit. The mobile app has swimming as an activity but the devise will does not track it. I wish that was more clear in the description. When speaking to Garmin they said the next model up has that ability. It am not able to get it to connect to GPS yet. It gives the option to but it wont connect. The band developed a small rip this week. The rubber material is very comfortable and there is just enough stretch in it for comfort. A drop of super glue seems to be working. I do not wear this for sleep for I can not report on that function. I compared the pulse rate to a monitor during a recent doctor visit. It was spot on. Easy to use once familiar with the order and location of things.

title: Bluetooth shuts off and then you are screwed.
text: I bought this last July 2017 it is now May 2018 the Bluetooth is off and I cannot turn it on. Not very happy. I looked that up and it appears to be a very common problem as a result, I cannot recommend it.

title: Disappointed in this watch’s performance.
text: I purchased this watch for the HR monitor and GPS specifically. Well, I got the GPS to work twice before a run outside. After that it does not connect and all I get is “wait ‘. I went on Garmin website which is not helpful at all. The Garmin connect app is not that user friendly for a non- techy. So frustrating. I really was excited for this watch. Major let down.

title: Piece of garbage!

But unfortunately the heart monitor is really bad. Does not pick up my heart until I was 25 minutes into intense exercise. The floor counting is a joke! And it does not count the steps correctly. As you can see in the picture, after 28 minutes on INTENSE exercise, my heart monitor was showing 168 while this watch was on 96 only. Impossible! I wrote for the costumer service and they did not even replay. The costumer service phone does not work either. Terrible! But Polar!

title: She's been using it for 2 weeks and it functions great. It's comfortable and looks great on her

title: Nice for running

title: Never again

title: Very reliable.
text: I purchased the Garmin to replace the one I accidentally broke. I have always been happy with its performance.

title: Great but not perfect
text: I would LOVE this thing so much if I could customize the app a bit... the default activities need to be changeable -- what if I never run, but do miles of inline skating every day and hours of climbing every week? It'd be nice to be able to have those activities readily accessible and to have their stats highlighted instead of diving through the menu. GPS tracking works great. Flexible/stretchy band is a plus. I've recommended it to friends.

title: Nice watch with abundant features.

It is a nice size for a fitness watch, I have small wrists and was afraid thay it would be too bulky and wouldn't be comfortable sleeping with it on but I barely notice it. Charge lasts 6+ days without using the GPS feature which will drain it faster. Heart Rate and Sleep Tracking seem to be pretty accurate with only minor discrepancies. I haven't used much of the other features so I will try to update later on.

title: Avoid PNR Sales. Watches don't appear to be New
text: Update: Still 1 star. 2 months and the battery won't hold a charge. The watch was put into service about November 16, 2020. It's now January 22, 2021 and it won't hold a charge. Even after resetting the watch per manufacturer troubleshooting steps it only look lasted 2 months. I don't know where PNR sales is acquiring these products from but they obviously aren't brand new. Amazon "Fulfilled" order but couldn't confirm the correct product. NEVER order anything "Fulfilled by Amazon" for a seller other than the mfgr. Sounds petty but this was for the 56th birthday of a woman with stage 4 metastatic breast cancer. For the price, you'd figure that Amazon could get it right. Thanks for nothing Amazon & PNR Sales.

title: The Perfect Tracker with GPS

title: Garmin customer support told me it has to do either with a bad sensor, or an issue with the tracking algorithm

title: prefer garmin over fitbit

title: Starting with Garmin Express Version 6.19.2.0 this no longer works with your Computer
