Tried multiple computers (all Windows 10) not one worked. Thanks, Garmin. Update: It just died, a piece of junk, I'm done with Garmin.

title: A bit disappointed
text: Initially everything worked great. Within a month my battery life became shorter (without using the GPS or having all types of notifications on) and it seemed to lose bluetooth connection. Now into 2 months it is constantly losing and reconnecting with the bluetooth and it is not recording the number of flights of stairs I have gone up or down not to mention having to charge it every 3 days. I followed all the tips and directions in Garmin Connect and on blogs; nothing seemed to help. I did end up returning the Vivosmart. On the plus side, I liked the weather feature and the clock!

title: END OF LIFE - Do not purchase - No updates since 2017 per customer service on 2/9/20
text: This model is outdated and at End of Life. No updates since 2017. And you had to download the desktop app to update the software. Why another app?? it's bluetooth! Pros: Seems sturdy. I have only had to send it in for service once in the first year; A few setting adjustments on website; Quick charging, which is important b/c the battery does not last more than 2 days. Cons: No updates since the year I bought it in 2017, per Andrew this morning on CS chat. HUGE. Sticks out on my wrists, making it susceptible to scratches; (buy the screen cover from the 3rd party) Cannot adjust the vibration, which is strong, and drains battery. A lot. And I need the text, phone alerts; Cannot add steps on website NOR app, and wearing the watch is not sexy with dresses! (haha, a rare occurrance, but point is, why can't I add steps!); Overall: I'm now 100%against buying another Garmin. The cons outweigh the pros. . This is not an easy watch to wear daily on my small wrists. Best for runs and walks, not all day use. BUT it does the tracking I need. So I'm a good enough purchase for my first wrist-worn fitness tracker. Do NOT pay more than $50 for this. It's outdated. Garmin does not tell you that.

title: I was fairly happy with my Garmin (much happier than I was with ...
text: I was fairly happy with my Garmin (much happier than I was with my Fitbit) except for a few things: #1. The vibration/buzz was SO LOUD!! I’m a teacher & when it would buzz to alert me, my whole class would hear it. I couldn’t use it as a alarm bcuz it would wake up my husband too. I wish u could adjust the setting/strength of this feature. #2. The metal fastener has fallen off randomly 3 times in the last few months. Luckily it will snap back on. #3. I was putting on a jacket & the wrist band ripped from the watch face. It will not just snap back on, so I am now without a fitness tracker. Very frustrated because I don’t know if I just had a ‘bad egg’ or if all of the products are like this.

title: She loves it
text: My daughter loves this so much she's so happy it was her birthday and christmas gift. She can't stop bragging about it and showing all the things it does .

title: Runs large
text: Wristband was too wide for my wife, had to ship it back.

title: Like this tracker.
text: Nice tracker. The sleep tracking isn't completely accurate. The mobile app is great. The GPS mode for walking and running is great. Overall it was worth the money.

title: An all-round well performing tracker in everything but sleep.
text: I really appreciate having the vivosmart HR+, and it was a great choice for my first fitness tracker. Having GPS tracking independently of a phone is a plus, for me, if I go on an occasional run or hike. Also, I like that it is waterproof, because my previous sports watch stopped due to water damage. At first, I was concerned that it would be too large for my thin wrists. However, I've found that it fits and stays in place, even though it looks chunky (which I don't mind). Also, the watch band is surprisingly comfortable and flexible. The Garmin Connect App is well organized. My biggest peeve with the vivosmart HR+ is that its automatic sleep tracking can be so inaccurate. Almost every day, I have to reenter the time that I fell asleep and woke up, which then changes the calculations for Sleep Levels. Fortunately, viewing the movement tracked during sleep helps me guesstimate those times, if I don't remember exactly. Furthermore, Garmin should look into distinguishing time awake from REM sleep, as Fitbit has done. If sleep is the main activity you are looking to track, I'd look for a different device.

title: Slow to find gps signal, and requires internet to see data - both are deal-breakers for me
text: Good: easy to read; intuitive interface; light weight; comfortable to wear. Bad: takes about 2 minutes to sync with gps, in wide open field with no hills/trees/buildings nearby; must have internet connection to see data; loses step count when you start a new activity; intensity minutes didn't "trigger" (device asked if I wanted to get active for 20 minutes for better data, I said "yes", it looked like it was starting to measure, but nothing happened)

title: The Band broke at the screws LESS than four months ...
text: The Band broke at the screws LESS than four months of use. I was in a leg cast and was hardly active, then rehab, so it has not been used and abused.

title: Also great that text show up and I can scroll through ...
text: Wear it every day. I work an off schedule so my sleep is not always at night. With the App I can set my own sleep times to coordinate with the move/sleep tracker. Also great that text show up and I can scroll through who has text me and what they said. Can only set 1 alarm which would be nice to have at least 2 or more. Worst of all is the music player. It worked perfectly when I first got the watch but they did a software update that made it work for Apple products and now it does not work at all for android. It seems like everyone has this issue and its been this way for about a year with many updates coming out since then and no fix for android.

title: Get a running watch, a Casio G-shock, or an actual watch instead
text: It's relatively not comfortable to wear and I can't imagine sleeping with the thing on. The step counter seems largely based on distance traveled and not on how many actual steps one takes. The heart rate monitor is not very accurate and is largely only useful in knowing when one's heart rate is up or down. It seems to get in the way when weightlifting. It's not stylish enough to actually replace a watch. The Fitbit is probably no better and the Apple watch largely seems for fashion rather than actual useful function. Fitness watches are decent for cardio, but it'd suggest getting a running watch and get a chest strap for heart rate. Even then, unless one is an athlete or bodybuilder, it's not necessary.

title: works ok until it doesn't which happens very quickly
text: I purchased this, my first fitness tracker expecting Garmin to be more accurate and reliable than fitbit based on the reviews. While it works it was mostly accurate for my steps but frequently doesn't register when you 'start' the exercise time so it only records your steps. I very quicky had issues with the screen freezing and found on youtube that you have to completely turn it off then back on to reset. Well when you reset it you have to set the time and date EVERY TIME (it will sync to your phone automatically but can't detect the time/date). You also have to do this when the battery dies and it will cause you get very little notice that the battery is low and it drains Very quickly because you can't set it NOT to receive text and email alerts from your phone. After about 2 months it quit charging at all. I called and they sent replacement power cord. I had hooped that might help it charge in less than 5 hours (it did not). It is now about 2-3 mnths since the replacement cord was sent and today, plugged in, the device once again is not charging. I AM DONE WITH THIS! I got the item with a credit for signing up for the Amazon store and paid $30 for the warranty. I am now going to eat the $30 loss because I have spent WAY too much time dealing with this sub par device. I don't know if the problem is again the charging cord or if it is the device and I don't care. I definitely expected better from this company based on my experience with my GPS. I will not buy any other Garmin tracker and I will make sure that anyone I know looking at them is aware of the issues. It is pathetic that an item at this price point couldn't last 2 months without issues an more than 5 months without causing this level of frustration. If i could I would give it zero stars but as we all know, these systems are set up for that

title: Undecided. Wristband could be an issue.
text: My new vivosmart HR+ arrived today and I couldn't have been more excited - until I opened the box. This is my third Garmin vivo fitness tracker and they do get better with each version. This one, however, is really big on my tiny wrist. It needs to be this size to accommodate all the new features and I'm sure if I put my mind to it, I'll adjust. More concerning - and this is why the preliminary three-star review - is the wristband. Other reviewers have complained that it broke after a few months. Holding the device in my hands, putting it on and taking it off a few times did not inspire my confidence in the wristband. It's made from a comfortable material that seems rubbery and stretchy, but I don't get the a sense of its tensile strength. I haven't charged up vivosmart HR+ yet because I may return it tomorrow. I am a heavy user of these devices because I run or walk five miles a day. The vivosmart devices have been a key tool in maintaining my fitness discipline. My trackers come off my wrist only to bathe and sleep. Your thoughts and experience would be much appreciated.

title: Great Tool To Remind Me but...
text: I enjoy wearing my Vivofit 2. I love how it tracks sleep and let's you know if you are in a deep sleep with movement or deep sleep with no movement. That helps me to figure out why I am a bit tired some days. I like the little blip that reminds me to move. Everything is terrific, but I have discovered I am allergic to the band. I have tried other replacement bands and have come to the conclusion that I must be allergic to silicon or the combination of ingredients. Is there another replacement band made out of something else other than silicone? For now, I taped the band up with medical tape to protect my skin, leaving the device free of tape of course. But I only wear it around the house because it looks so awful. Any suggestions?

title: I think it's a pretty good alternative to some of the other similar items ...
text: Got this for the wife. She loves it, and even though she's a bit in the stone age as far as technology goes, (she got her first smartphone 3 weeks ago), she was able to hook up to her phone, and download her activities. She's been following the activity logs, entering her nutritional info, and monitoring her sleep patters ever since she got it, and really likes it. I think it's a pretty good alternative to some of the other similar items out there. I like that it has a watch display on it.

title: Love it...but not for what it does but what it doesn't need!
text: I love this tracker! Why because I don't have to charge it...yippee. To all you techie's out there that hate to take it off, put it in the computer and then try to remember to put it back on or visa versa, here's the product for you. It tells you all the good stuff, links to My Fitness Pal and so gives me all I need to push me into moving a bit more. It did fall off and I did find it a few days later so be careful of the accessory bands they don't always do as they say! Not so sure of those little bands to hold it on, mine slip up and down.

title: Stopped syncing after a month, otherwise great product, wish it lasted longer.
text: Stopped syncing after about a month, once I updated the software. Garmin tech support says I have to restart my computer before syncing each time. Even this doesn't always work. If it does work it takes several tries of syncing and restarting. And even then, parts of the data are missing. For example it may say I only walked a few feet a certain day, when I actually walked many miles. The vivoifit2 will have the correct amount, but it never sends the right data to the software any longer. Actually really loved this item when I first got it. It worked great - accurately counting my steps. Wearing it made me push myself to walk further each day and also made me mindful of eating healthier. It used to sync fast and correctly. I wore this kayaking - which I do several times a week and found it to be totally waterproof. Sleep feature nice, but I don't really need that data. The plastic band is a bit sweaty. I wore it super lose because of this. Even so, I bit uncomfortable to always have a perspiring wrist. I ordered the silver watch band, but after three weeks it still hadn't even shipped out. Glad it didn't since the Vivofit2 no longer works. So in short, if it is OK that it only functions a few weeks, then this is wonderful item.But, if you plan to use for a longer period of time, this is not good.

title: Almost perfect!!
text: The circumference of my wrist is 5 1/4 inches above the bone which is fairly small and the small wristband fits perfectly, there are still 5 holes (1.5 inches) left to make it smaller. The two reasons I went for this activity tracker are it is waterproof and the battery lasts one year... for me these are the most important reasons because I really hate all this constant charging of gadgets. Syncing is easy, at the end of the day I just press one button and it syncs with my smartphone, it also comes with a little blue-tooth USB attachment if you want to sync it with your computer. I've read they will add autosync with the next software update which is supposed to arrive shortly. You get to choose what to see on your screen when you press the button, I went with steps, goal, distance and time. You can also add the date, calories and heart rate if you are wearing a strap. I absolutely love how it feels, it doesn't bother me at all, you don't have to wear it real tight and the silicon is very soft. The reason I took one star off is that the beep sound which comes on after one hour of inactivity (when the red warning line appears) is way, way, way too quiet. I set an alarm just to check on the beep sound and it was so short and subtle, if there would be any kind of background noise you won't be able to hear it at all.

title: Love it!
text: I love this. I haven't taken it off since I got it 3 months ago. I have alot of health issues, and I'm the type of person that if I know I should be doing something, I will do it, regardless of how much pain I'm in. Walking is difficult for me, but so is sitting. I started out with only 500 feet and increase by 500 every week. This has helped me stay somewhat active, I won't stop until I get my required amount of steps in for the day.

title: garmin vivofit 2
text: Small fits perfect on my wrist. Comfortable. Forget I am wearing it. Office worker so it beeps at me if I have been up and moving in a while. Keeps me on task. Lets me know how many steps I have taken and also sets goals for me.

title: Allergic to battery
text: I loved this watch. Wore it religiously for a few months, took off to shower tho.. then I developed this rash.. contacted the company they told me I was probably allergic to the battery and to stop wearing it. It's been off for 3 months. I took this photo today. My dr told me this will probably never go away.. so thanks garmin for damaging my skin !

title: Great product
text: I've had this for about three weeks now and it's working great. So nice to have it right at my fingertips to see my steps etc. I didn't want to spend that much money like some of the others were so this was a good cost. I give it five stars.

title: Had one before and loved it..
text: Works great so far.. for a while wasn't sure it was water tight in the pool this summer, but it still works.

title: Display Fades Away
text: I had one of these for over 2 years. It was great. I loved it. Then the display simply faded away. Garmin customer service was of no help. I know another person whose vivofit2 did the same thing. It should last longer than that.

title: A few days in and I like it so far
text: A few days in and I like it so far. My sister and I purchased together (when her Fitbit bit the dust randomly) and we've been comparing our results. Even when we do mostly the same thing in a day hers tracks more steps than mine - I think perhaps I hold my purse with the hand the Garmin is on and it doesn't track properly as I'm not swinging my arm naturally as I do when walking without holding onto anything. I like this because of the battery and no need to charge and that I can wear it in the pool up to 16' (5 meters) deep (which I've not tried yet). I have switched it to sleep mode each night I've slept with it, so I am unsure of what would happen if I didn't do that. I like the product, I wish it counted the steps a bit more accurately. I think the miles walked is right on, however. When we tried to download the Garmin app for our iPhones we could not log in right away, and I was impressed when I called Garmin and I got an American worker almost imemdiately. She was kind and helpful (servers were down, but within a few hours we were back in business). The red line can get annoying as it seems like I need to take a lot of steps to make it go away. However, with all being said, this makes me more aware of my activity level and I think that is what it's all about.

title: Worked great until it last week
text: Worked great until it last week, the display started blinking then went out. it still works, but without the display. Not so good.

title: One year batter, constant time display and waterproof - no other device does that
text: Super device - I had a UP and my wife had a fitbit. Each had to be charged every week - vivofit 2 has a one year battery. Those other devices are not waterproof - I sit in my spa 5-6 times a week and the watch is not adversely affected. It shows the time all day - so it is not in addition to your watch - it is your watch - and it lights up so that you can see the time at night. The sync to iPhone or iPad can be a little clunky but that is a very small price to pay for all the great features of this tracker that others simply don't have

title: Great until you have to replace the battery.
text: Worked great until needing battery replacement after about 13 months. I originally thought I bought a bad batch of batteries, but I have tried 5 different brands from 3 different vendors. Amazon, Walmart and Batteries Plus. All batteries now fail at a rapid rate, and because of this I want to warn people in the market for this tracker. Know that your investment will last thru the factory installed batteries, after that good luck. I wish I could say this is a personal issue with only one, but after looking at my past purchases I found that this was actually my 3rd Garmin band tracker, first of the Vivofit 2 model, but they all exhibited the same behaviour. Worked great on factory battery until that wore out, then no matter brand or where purchased from all replacement batteries died fast without warning. Pros: fully waterproof, keep it on in the shower, while you swim or even at the beach. Doesn't need charged, one less thing to worry about, and screen can be read in bright light or even dim light with the new backlighting feature. Cons: Only lasts through factory battery, unless you enjoy changing batteries often and enjoy dead spots on your tracking stats because of no warning on low batteries that die quick, also random synching issues that I believe are app based, usually resolved by restarting PC or Phone being used to Sync, sometimes Bluetooth togggle helps also.

title: Excellent!
text: Basic fitness tracker. Like the simple style and easy readability. The Garmin Connect app has a lot of tracking options ranging from sleep to steps, and types of exercises.

title: Made well, steps seem accurate, and battery life is outstanding
text: My wife loves this watch. This watch has a light on it now so you can check your watch status in low light conditions. This is an improvement over the previous revision of the product, which my wife also owned. We gave that one to my daughter when I bought this one. Shows your steps so far for the day, the time, calories burned, and the number of steps before you hit your goal. Once you hit your goal the watch emits a short beep, and a plus sign appears, so you know how many steps over your goal you went. Has a sleep function which she doesn't push any attention to, so I can't comment on it's effectiveness or accuracy. I personally like that the watch can run months before changing out the battery. This is in contrary to a lot of fitness watches where it requires charging every couple days, or weeks. The downside to this is that the bluetooth is only connected when you open up the app and sync it. Some of the battery guzzling watches sync all the time, so you don't have to remember to do it.

title: Popped out
text: My tracker popped out after 3 months and i lost it???? Has this happen to anyone else? Will Garmin send a replacement piece? Thanks

title: Get fit
text: Keeps track of everything for me ance it's comfortable to sleep in.

title: Worthless
text: I owned the original Garmin Vivofit and liked it, so when it finally gave up the ghost I decided to replace it with this one. What a freaking disaster... First off the band is virtually impossible to keep on my wrist during any vigorous workout. Secondly, the sync function worked fine until they pushed a software update, now it does absolutely nothing. And, it's not horribly accurate even when it does work. Garmin makes great GPS units but I'll never purchase one of their fitness trackers again.

title: It motivates me
text: Since I bought this I'm walking 3-4 miles every day. I didn't think I could do it but I built myself up and now I want to. I'm also posting my food for the day online with My Fitness.

title: Count me in
text: I just wish it counted when my arm is still, like when I'm holding a purse or using a shopping cart. That sounds so lame :) but when I'm running errands all day, it looks like I've been sitting. Other than that, it works great. Waterproof. Monitors my sleep patterns and best of all...It doesn't have to be charged at all! That in itself is worth it.

title: Love my vivofit 2
text: I love my vivofit 2! I wanted to get an activity tracker that had a watch included, but didn't want to spend 100's on one. I was also concerned about the syncing, as some reviewers said they have problems. I had problems, at first, but I am pretty sure it was my error. There was one other time that it wasn't syncing, but we live in the country and our wireless isn't always working properly. Other than that, I have had no problems with the syncing. I like that it gives you subtle reminders to get moving after being inactive. I am really intrigued with the sleep activity, however, I wonder how accurate it really can be. But it's neat to compare it to how I feel after a nights sleep. I didn't really have any problems setting up the vivofit 2. I haven't really immersed it in water much, did go down a water slide a few times with it, but took it off to make sure it wouldn't get ruined. I don't shower with it on either....it's strictly my personal choice. They say it is waterproof...I'm just more cautious with things than probably necessary. I went with the 2 instead of the orginal because the original one seemed to fall off a lot, and the vivofit 2 has a lock on the band. For the price I paid, I'm very happy with it. It's good enough for me! :)

title: It looks and feels nice. My other one was a fit bit which ...
text: I bought this for my son for Christmas and he hasn't used it so gonna wear it . It looks and feels nice . My other one was a fit bit which I lost . And that one I could complete with others on my phone . I lost the papers to this one . How do I get the instructions?

title: Screen Accumulates Scratches
text: While the pedometer function is generally accurate, it picks up dozens of phantom steps while I am shampooing my hair. The bigger flaw is that the screen is plastic and scratches quite easily. I'm dinging off two stars for not using glass- as small as the screen is, the extra cost would be trivial.

title: Inactivity
text: I received this as a gift for Christmas. I am for sure that the step count must be inaccurate. I just spent 2 hours walking the mall, got back in the car and the inactivity bar is all the way across. I should have worn another pedometer to compare it to however I have walked for two hours… This model was purchased for me because of its underwater capability. I am anxious to see how it does when I try that activity again. Do you have to walk at more than a slow walk for it to activate?

title: Four Stars
text: Seems pretty accurate.I really enjoy it. The app is very helpful

title: Garmin Activity Tracker Vivofit 2
text: One of the main reasons I purchased this was because I didn't have to recharge it. There is a battery that is supposed to last a year. So far, it works fairly well. I do get the reminders to get up and move every hour or so, though I find that you have to walk several more steps than expected to reset the arrows. The sleep tracker works well, recording all the movements when I sleep. One thing is that I do not find that the tracker automatically syncs to the Android app, and I have to manually sync each time.

title: I did not realize how much I sit around working ...
text: I did not realize how much I sit around working, chained to the computer. Now I monitor my steps, and am feeling stronger and have more energy.

title: Not accurate.
text: This is my first activity tracker and I had high hopes for it. I have used and love Garmin products so felt confident in this purchase. I have been very disappointed in it. I have used it for about a month and find it to be very inaccurate. It's supposed to track sleeping, but when I leave it on overnight, it always says that I have done steps. One night, it said I made 38 steps while I was sleeping. I'm also a musician and play guitar. Every time I play the guitar, it adds on steps...like a lot of them! If I'm short on my steps, all I have to do is play the guitar to catch up. I don't know if this is normal for activity trackers, but I will be returning this one and not buying another one.

title: Not accurate. Probably slightly more useful than a dumb watch unless you pay a lot of attention to it.
text: It's nice when it's working, but their software and algorithm is kinda a joke. Frequently fails to sync for days and lose data. When I am playing games, it thinks i am sleeping. Walk tracking is fine, except if I am waving my hands, or washing my hair, etc, they are all counted as "walking". So one has to monitor the numbers and manually adjust a bit. However, at least I don't have to charge every month or week. That's a huge plus for me. It's at least a competent watch, just a bit too expensive for a simple watch.

title: If you don't mind having a fitness tracker that doesn't track fitness because there is no app or computer records of your exerci
text: Does not sync with computer or phone app. Originally it synced 2 times but never again. If you don't mind having a fitness tracker that doesn't track fitness because there is no app or computer records of your exercise than you might like this. I should have gone with a fit bit.

title: Accurate and easy to use!
text: I ordered this as a gift for my grandmother who loves to walk everyday. She has heard the hype of all these new fitness bands and wanted to try one out to count her steps so she can stay on track everyday. I feared she would learn how to use it being technology illiterate, but she had no problems at all figuring it out! She loves it and always shows it off to family!

title: Great buy
text: Bought this for my wife and she loves it. Has worked flawlessly for a lost a year, and the best part is that you don't have to charge it everyday like other brands. She wears it all the time, even during water sports and it has held up perfectly. Do yourself a favor and click buy it now!

title: Great product
text: I have had the jawbone up, the Fitbit flex and zip. So the selling point to this device is no charging, or no pushing a button to see the time and waterproof to 50 meters. I can hear the audio alarm when I have not been active and that is inside a noisy classroom.The interface on the iOS app is not as good as Fitbit, but the recent update was a good improvement. The only con is you are not able to manually set alarms, which I was able to do on my flexI am disappointed that it went on sale a week after I received it.

title: perfect, works great
text: I was not sure between vivofit 2 or fitbit.... Now I know.....perfect, works great, great apps, waterproof, one year battery, big nice display....and great price.

title: Nice watch/tracker combo
text: Was a gift for my wife. She is very pleased with it and wears it all the time (makes a good basic watch plus tracking) . The back light is a nice feature when its dark out (in daylight you really don't need it). The strap is sturdy but sometimes the clasp is a little hard to rotate (still a big improvement over earlier straps that were reported to not stay closed). Once yu learn exacly where to push the raised rib on the strap to change modes (the button is covered by the strap), is easy to use. Good value for the price vs more pricier options form other sources..

title: Perfect activity tracker
text: I am glad I chose this over the Fitbit charge. Works just perfect and no battery charging!

title: Two Stars
text: It counted steps when I was seated. Didn't work for me.

title: Don't waste your time
text: This is a revised review. I ordered this one a 14 months ago. I replaced the batteries last week. Now, half of the display doesn't work. I just ordered another one. This is the third one I've had to buy in just as many years. What an immense waste of money so far. I've invested nearly $300 just to track my fitness and sleep.

title: Get a cheap step counter instead
text: It doesn't pick up your steps unless your arms are swinging. So if you are holding on to the grocery cart in the grocery store, it doesn't pick up any of your steps. It is also very difficult to get on and off your wrist. It takes 2 people. I had mine on and my arthritis caused my wrist to swell. It was so painful and my husband and I had a great deal of difficulty getting it off. It also doesn't measure your sleep accurately. I go to bed and read and it says I am in deep sleep. Well, I'll admit some of the books I read can be boring, but I haven't been to sleep sitting up yet. A cheap step counter that you attach to your waist band is much better for counting steps.

title: This is a great product.
text: I never take this off. This is a great product.

title: Very Good Quality
text: Very nice. It does all that I needed it to, track my steps. The band is good quality. I'm reviewing late, and it has lasted me nearly a year now.

title: Very Nice
text: Works great! Got this for my daughter for Christmas and she has worn it every day since. It is strong and very nice. I think I like the Garmin better than the fitbit because it's basically the same thing just at a much better price and with much more options band wise.

title: Watch out for the infamous white dot
text: Never got to use it. It came brand new, with the infamous white dot covering almost half of the screen, and was returned. I have since bought another one, and it's fine. (So far)

title: Get moving, Chubby!
text: It does what it is advertised to do. Big reason I chose the Vivofit over the others is that it uses two standard watch batteries for power and not a rechargeable battery. Garmin says the batteries should last for a year. It is not step accurate but neither are the others. It is close but if you count off 100 steps the Vivofit may display 109, 112... I should adjust it for my stride which would make it more accurate but it's not that important to me. The main reason I bought it was to remind me to move. I write and produce commercial music and I am often sitting at my studio desk for hours at a time. I now can glance at my wrist and see that it is time to take a break and a short walk. I don't find the app that Garmin has for the Vivofit to be of much use. You can use it to sync with your computer or smartphone and keep track of various things like steps, calories burned, miles walked etc. by day, week, month. BUT... you must be connected to the internet. Garmin doesn't advertise that fact. I discovered it when I was at my cottage in the Northwoods of Wisconsin and after a good walk I went to sync the Vivofit to my iPhone. Nope. No internet - no sync. I would think that Garmin would have created an app that wouldn't require a internet connection to your phone. It also functions as a watch.

title: Garmin vívofit 2 Activity Tracker, Black
text: So far a superior unit compared to the Fitbit offerings. Very durable and stays put on your wrist. Will definitely buy again when needed.

title: Is This A Defect?
text: It would be nice to communicate with the seller, then perhaps I could find out why this Tracker can't keep time. It is synched to my iPhone and my MacPro but it is TEN MINUTES SLOW. I don't know how to adjust the time, there is nothing to tell me how to do this. I'm wondering if this just is a defect, and if so, I would like a replacement.

title: Love it! Better and slightly cheaper than it's biggest competitor!!
text: Love it! The best parts about it: -You don't have to charge it but once a year (my friends with the fitbit are super jealous about that). -It's waterPROOF (not just water resistant - again, better than the fitbit) to 5 feet. I wore this to the beach and it did just fine in the ocean and in the pool. I wear it in the shower every day. I've never taken mine off except for to clean it or switch bands, and I've had it for several months. -It automatically syncs several times a day without me having to tell it to. -I don't have to tell it when I'm sleeping for it to track my sleep - it automatically knows. -The Connect app is pretty good and can join with the My Fitness Pal app to track calories. A couple very minor cons: -The sync button is hard to get used to and sometimes hard to push. But I never have to use it, so that doesn't really matter to me. -I wish it would track my route like a GPS would. I think I have to pay more and go the next product up for that ability. Definitely recommend!!

title: Gets me off the couch
text: I bought this to remind me to quit sitting at my computer for too long. It works! I do not have a problem synching with my IPad. It is very simple. The only issue is the button to press for modes is not easy. The software is easy to understand and there is no issue I have found that other people have whined on about. Maybe some people had not updated the system they use? The synch happens as soon as I go into the mode. I am amazed at how it tracks sleep vs. not sleeping. You can tell if you got up during the night by the chart it creates and what time by the spike of activity. It knew I stayed up late (watching television in bed) and when I actually went to sleep. The steps may not be entirely accurate, but an approximate amount is good enough for me. Overall, this works to get me moving and that's what a lazy computer geek like me needs.

title: So far everything is good! I don't like that it must be removed ...
text: So far everything is good! I don't like that it must be removed from the band to access the main button for options.

title: She has been very happy with it and so far it has been very ...
text: Mrs had been wanting one of these and received it for Christmas. She has been very happy with it and so far it has been very accurate and has worked flawlessly.

title: Great choice for being informed and keeping it simple.
text: I love my vivofit because it tracks my sleep, accurately tracks my steps, does not come off, and has a light. In conjunction with the "My Fitness Pal" software, I have an accurate picture of what is happening and what I need to do. I must actively engage in entering meals and some of my unconventional exercise activities, but this is necessary for me if I want to be in control of my progress. I like that I can wait until the end of the day to sync and enter my data. I am not attached to my phone to track steps and steps needed. Great choice for me. The 5th star will be added after more time. I love not having to charge it, like I do everything else I have!

title: Entry Level Fitness Watch Offers PC Connectivity
text: Although the Vivofit 2 lacks a heart rate monitor and GPS (understandably in this price range), it's reasonably waterproof, provides fairly accurate step counts and displays mileage, as well as time in a very secure, attractive band. Additionally, you have the assurances of a strong brand. A major advantage of this activity watch is it will not only sync with a smart phone, but with a PC through Bluetooth and is uploadsble to Garmin's free software, available online for free. A Bluetooth dongle for the PC is included. Those without a smart phone will love this feature to record a history of their activity. Best of all, you won't need to recharge the battery every day or two -- the battery is good for 1 year! The band has a secure locking mechanism, making loss unlikely. Two bands are included -- a small and large. The large band, no doubt, would fit 99% of larger persons. It lacks all the bells and whistles of an Apple Watch, but is an economical entry point into the world of fitness watches to see if you really want to use this tool to motivate you to exercise.

title: Three Stars
text: Sometime does not sync with phone. I would not buy it again.

title: Great Tracker. I need to study its reports more. App works on either smartphone or computer. (I chose computer)
text: Randy Cassingham, who writes a wry news commentary column every week (Google "ThisIsTrue") raved about this combination watch / activity tracker. His words about it were enough to get me to try it. It is comfortable, it is waterproof so I don't have to take it off when I take a shower. (It even gives me credit for steps taken while I'm moving around in the shower, which some people might call a defect, but I don't.) It synchronizes itself with my computer automatically, but if I wanted to, I could do it simply by holding the button until I saw the word SYNC on the band. It also has a timer, but I don't use that. It also keeps track of sleep patterns, but I don't like the fact that it assumes that I got up at 10 am on the weekend. I need to figure out if there is a way to simply tell it when I go to bed, then have it decide that I've gotten up by quantity of movement, or simply telling it I got up. That way, my varied schedule doesn't confuse it. BUT that is my problem, because sleep experts say that you should go to bed the same time every day and get up the same time every day. (I've always hated that advice, I always looked forward to sleeping in on weekends.)

title: She Loves it!
text: Had for over a month now and she loves it. App works great with her phone.(Android)

title: This item has changed my life
text: So far so good. This vivofit keeps me walking. I love this item. It was a little difficult to learn to use in the very beginning but now that I have the kinks worked out it keeps me walking and in shape. I love all the various features it offers. I would highly recommend this item to anyone who wants to keep heart healthy and fit.

title: Amazing product without a charger
text: Love the Garmin Vivofit. This band is great to keep you motivated. Connects easily to Garmin Connect. This is an upgrade from the Vivofit. It tracks steps, sleep, calories, date, and clock. It also has a back light. The best part is that it doesn't need to be charged for one year. I love my Vivofit2 and plan on getting the Vivofit3 soon.

title: a little difficult to see
text: But is typical for a Garmin product … No complaints at all

title: Good Tracker, but syncing issues with mobile app
text: I really like it, but just like some of the reviews I've read, if you have the mobile app, it takes several tries before the info syncs up from the tracker to the app. I also realized that I should have ordered the heart rate monitor since I do more than walking as a form of exercise. I ordered the HR monitor this past week and will review that after using it for a month or so.

title: I loved the 1st version but this 2nd one is great
text: I loved the 1st version but this 2nd one is great. I like that you can push the button at night and the info lights up. also it's super water-resistant, never take it off, during showers and even in the ocean.

title: This is a great unit - particularly for the price

title: No charging needed!

title: Good Sleep Tracker
text: I bought this at BestBuy. I traded an UP3 for the Garmin Vivofit 2 (the UP3 didn't fit my arm properly - small wrist). I went with the Vivofit 2 because it is waterproof up to 50 meters and I would be able to swim with it. It also came with two sizes of bands to ensure a proper fit (I went with small). I have had the Vivofit 2 for 4 days and most of the features haven't worked properly. 1) The audible alerts do not work. I occasionally see the move bar on the screen when I look down at the faceplate, but I have never heard an alert. I double checked device settings within the Garmin Connect app on my phone to ensure the alerts were enabled. They are enabled, but no alert. 2) The device has yet to automatically sync to my phone (iPhone 5). I have had to sync it manually every morning when I get up. 3) The active calories are incorrect. I went camping this weekend and hiked for several hours; the vivofit 2 registered that I had burned 1 active calorie. What I do like about it: 1) Monitors sleep automatically. 2) Keeps correct time. 3) Backlight comes in handy and I used it quite a bit while camping to check the time after dark. 4) Comfortable band and fits well (this was the reason I returned the UP3 after only having it a few hours). I have not had issues with it falling off, as another reviewer suggested. It seems like it would only fall off if the band wasn't locked properly. 5) Additional band color choices available. 6) Garmin Connect app works with the My Fitness Pal app. The main reason I purchased an activity monitor was to get a more accurate calorie count throughout the day. I may end up returning it since this feature doesn't seem to work well. I have not tried to pair the device with a heart rate strap though - I didn't really want to wear a strap around all the time, but it could be useful during exercise or for short amounts of time. I may try this before I decide to return it. The sleep feature is "neat" but not a necessity for me. If you are looking for a cool sleep tracker this may be a good device for you.

title: Garmin Vivofit 2 Logs Substantially LESS Steps in a Side by Side Comparison to a Fitbit One
text: I previously owned a Fitbit One which by virtue of the "belt clip" had met its demise by being left clipped on my pant and going through the washer and dryer. I recently purchase the Garmin Vivofit 2. I’m over 50 and one of the majors selling points on the Garmin over the Fitbit was the constant display of steps and of course being able to see the display without glasses. The Fitbit display is somewhat smaller and you have to press a button to have the steps displayed. When I received my Garmin, I did notice immediately that it was very delayed and logging steps and sometimes didn't seem to appear to log any steps at all. I used the Garmin Vivofit 2 on an elliptical for three miles. When I observed the number of steps, it fell below the number of steps that I had expected. I quickly decided, this was not acceptable and sucked it up and purchased another Fitbit One as well as a wristband. Using both the Garmin Vivofit 2 and the Fitbit One on the same wrist, I did three miles on the elliptical. When I finished the Garmin reported 3712 steps and the Fitbit reported 4736 steps. After a bit more comparison, the Garmin consistently logs in excess of 1000 steps less than the Fitbit. If you are looking for accuracy, I’d look at the Fitbit.

title: Nice, but doesn't sync to my Pixel phone consistently
text: I wanted to start walking more, now that I have retired, and bought my wife a Fitbit Alta. She liked her fitness band so much that I decided to get one, too. This Garmin Vivofit 2 seemed like a good deal and, when I got it, it paired easily with my Google Pixel phone's app. The band is a little uncomfortable initially to get strapped to my wrist. This gets easier after a couple of days and the device itself is great - it has a series of red markers at the top of the display, gently reminding me to get off my keester and start moving. The device is somewhat basic in what it records, but totally adequate for my needs. I'm not running triathalons - just walking and sleeping - and the Vivofit 2 records both. What's really great about this device is that the battery lasts about a year - it uses watch-button type batteries, so it doesn't need charging every 3-5 days like my wife's Fitbit does. HOWEVER, I noticed after the first three days that the device would not sync consistently with my Pixel phone. Somedays it would - somedays, despite six or seven tries - no dice. I tried pairing it with an older Nexus 6 phone and had the same result - initially, it worked great, but after a couple of days, it would only sync about every ten attempts. I don't know the cause of the sync problems - I suspect that it doesn't create a sufficiently strong signal to connect to my phone in order to save battery life. But after a couple of weeks of this, I'm done... moving to a Fitbit, like my wife.

title: UNBELIEVEABLE
text: I really love my Vivofit 2, except that I think it's a little too wide, But that's just me. I'm attracted to the fitbit alta for that reason. So, you say...why don't I get that? As I walked from the parking lot to the store, I put my Vivofit into my pants pocket. Well, one day I left it in my pocket, and after my shower, I wondered where it was...then shock! I left it in my pants, came home and washed a load of clothes, and yep, my tracker was still in my pocket. I knew it wouldn't, couldn't still be working and was heartbroken. I looked at the screen and yep...there it was...with the red line across saying, move! IT STILL WORKED. It's been two weeks since that happened. title: I'd even go so far as to say it can be mildly painful. The clasp really sticks
text: Its an ok fitness tracker, but it had enough drawbacks that I eventually returned it. First, the clasp device they've come up with to keep it from falling off your wrist is TOO effective. The first version of vivofit apparently popped off people's wrists a lot, so Garmin wanted to design a secure clasp. They definitely did, but I'd say they overshot the mark a bit as its a real pain to take it off and put back on. I'd even go so far as to say it can be mildly painful. The clasp really sticks, and jerking it free sometimes means that your fingers get the wrong end of the plastic edges. If you never plan to take it off, maybe it won't be an issue for you. I like at least a few hours a day of freedom. Second, sleep tracking is weak. I found it not very accurate at determining when I went to sleep, or woke up. And when I woke up in teh middle of the night, even if I was up for hours, the tracker would still show me as being asleep, and count that time as sleep time. Its a shame because the readout I found attractive, better than any other wrist device I've used (including charge hr). Everything else was fine, steps tracking was reasonably accurate, the website I thought was not too far off of Fitbits, and of course the year battery life is phenomenal. The red "non-movement" lines were fun at first but then just became tedious. Garmin, fix the clasp (why not use a watch clasp?) and improve the sleep monitoring, it'll make a big difference.

text: This is my fourth Vivofit. I had two of the previous versions. The functionality is relatively basic but I really only want to track my steps/mileage and don't need more sophisticated features. There's no back light, heart monitor, stairs readout, intensity monitoring, or other nifty features you find on many more expensive products. The one year + battery life and water resistant design enable you to leave the device on your wrist full time. No charging, worries about forgetting to put it on, or losing it. To me, that's well worth the tradeoff for having less teatures I never really need. The reason I'm on number four?? The units' readout screens begin failing after about 8-12 months and two of them just plain died on me. I'm OK with this given the relatively inexpensive cost but I would ever call these durable. title: Lost my Fitbit, and now have a Vivofit 2
text: I'm struggling with whether to give this device 3 or 4 stars. It does what it is supposed to do and I have no problem with the accuracy of its step tracking, which some people say is a problem for them. I had a Fitbit Charge for a couple of weeks that fell off my wrist during Christmas shopping. I was just sick about it and felt like I lost a good friend. A band that comes undone easily is Fitbit's weak link so I decided to replace it with the Vivofit 2 for three reasons. 1) The band has a lock feature that keeps it from falling off, 2) It was $30 cheaper, 3) I liked the idea of the inactivity alert feature. Unfortunately, I can't hear the audible chirp that is supposed to remind me to get up and move, unless I hold the device very close to my ear. I realize I have some hearing loss, but I didn't think it was THAT bad. There is a visual reminder; I just don't remember to look. I agree with many others that a vibration feature, like the Fitbit has, would be a huge improvement. Unlike the Fitbit, the Vivofit 2 does not give any indication of having reached a goal, and I miss that positive reinforcement, and it's not as sleek and attractive as the Fitbit. It's bulky on my small wrist, but not uncomfortable. It is more water resistant than the Fitbit Charge which is a plus. The battery could be an advantage over having to charge up, but I'm wondering if missing features like an LED display and vibration is the trade-off, as well as its bulkiness. Maybe those features would wear the battery too fast. It's a good product for sure, and if I had not started with a Fitbit, I would probably love it. A Fitbit charge has other advanced features like text and call notifications via bluetooth and it stayed synced with my phone much better, so there is a reason for the higher cost, but that band problem is a huge flaw. Okay. I started out with 3 stars for the Vivofit, but as I write this review, I realize it's a solid 4-star product considering the price I paid. If a vibration feature is added in the future, I'd upgrade in a heartbeat.

The sleep tracking seems to work really well, too. Cons: The button is pretty hard to press down until you get used to it. When I first got it and was trying to "long press" the button, I kept missing the Sync and opening the Stop Watch and couldn't get back out of it. It was a mess. title: This is my second one. I love my first one so much I bought a replacement IN CASE something happens to the first one!

I know how companies frequently discontinue items when they come out with a newer version, so I got another one "just in case" something happens to my first one! That's how much I like this item! What I love about this is: it's a watch - and one that is EASY TO READ. (That's one of the reasons I got another VivoFit 2 instead of going with a more current version!) I like that it's simple to use and I can see my status at any moment with just a press or two - I don't have to download or sync or whatever. My data is right there on my wrist all the time! (I do sync, which provides more detailed information, but it is absolutely not necessary in order to find out my status at any given moment.) I also love the AUDIBLE reminder to move. It's a small, chirpy noise so it is not annoying at all. I also like that it chirps every 30 minutes during an activity so you know how long you've been going. The only complaint I have is that it does not accurately track my steps when I use my elliptical - but I understand that NO fitness tracker "understands" those steps because they are zero impact. I love that it's easy to put on and take off - and I have a bunch of colors of replacement bands so I can coordinate with anything I am wearing, if I so desire. I love that it's waterproof, and that I don't have to take it off to charge it because it has a battery - which has gone something like 3 million steps and almost a year without needing to be replaced! As with any activity tracker, the sleep and calorie monitors aren't very accurate - it's just the nature of the beast. However, when I compare the sleep activity with my smart bed, it does accurately track my movements during sleep - but sometimes it interprets those movements as awake time when I am actually still asleep. In addition to all the other great things about this tracker is it's affordability. BONUS!

The accuracy for sleep is difficult to get; sometimes it starts me sleeping when I'm just sitting in the chair watching TV or if I dont take it off and get up to read in the morning it extends my sleep hours.

title: Great watch. Terrible manufacture.
text: I bought it over two years ago. First year it worked perfectly. Second year I started having some battery issues. Contacted customer service and had the watch sent to their repair center very quick. New battery, but same watch, it was fine for maybe 4 months. Than same issue. Contacted Samsung again, same procedure. Sent it over. Got it back. But at this time the problem was not fixed. So called them again. Again. Again. Then sent the watch again. At this time I was asked to have the watch and charger sent together. So they could run tests. After whatever tests, they informed they would be replacing for a new watch. After TWO MONTHS waiting, I received in my house just the watch body in a ziplock bag, with no charger, wrist band, and wall power plug. Pretty much a pocket watch. Or eventually a paperweight, as I would not be able to charge it to use. Called them again and they sent me a new charger in TWO WEEKS, but no power wall plug or wristband. I bought at amazon new band. And being using a standard usb wall plug. After one month of use, again problems with charging. Called again, and I’m sitting and waiting for the escalation team to get back to me. I use it with my iPhone. I don’t like the Apple Watch looks. And I was planning on switching to a Samsung Galaxy phone. After this experience. Samsung is not seem my money ever again.

title: Buyer beware of "certified renewed"

title: Great.

title: Amazfit GTS - Great Smart Watch
text: Purchased yesterday and although I have only had this a day I can tell this is a great watch. The screen is amazing and is very bright and vibrant. Text is clear and notifications are easy to read. Touch capability is very responsive. Sleep tracking works well and provides lots more data than my prior Smart Watch (Wyze Band). Lots of information available. There are lots of available watch faces but I found the default screen is fine as it shows the time, date weather (current and forecast) heart rate and battery power. Highly recommended.

title: A bit disappointed
text: I had a couple of fitbits before I tried this watch and definitely can see the difference between the two watches. I thought it’d be nice and track well my steps and sleep at least but it doesn’t perform as well. My steps are always much lower than what’s typically recorded on my Fitbit, the app is just ok. Sleep features are just ok.

title: Good smartwatch with several compromises, see below
text: Pros: Good battery life (if you don't use the GPS) Good selection of watch faces (if you days wait for Zepp to populate copies to your app or hack third-party sites) Lightweight (you'll not notice you're wearing it) Incredible display with auto brightness (even readable in full sun) Cons: Distance tracked using watch GPS can be off by an order of magnitude. This might be an app problem, dunno, but I cycled 10 km and the report in Google Fit (auto exported by the Zepp app) was 0.7 km. Useless. Countdown timer only works as dedicated app, you can't switch to exercise tracking or anything else and have it continue to run. Almost useless since you can't even tell the time when the countdown timer is running. Only one downloaded watch face can be stored on the watch (why?). You have to sync any other choices, very slowly from the app. The watch has enough memory to store a number of .bin files, but it isn't addressable. No third party apps or add ons other than watch faces.

title: Replaced my Pebble Time
text: My Pebble was only lasting 3 days and getting harder to read with my aging eyes. This is physically the same size, much brighter, always on display, and the text is easier to read due to it being brighter. The app and watch menu have many options and settings I will need to play with. Likely though, I will not ever use it. I was hoping for a watch that can tell me the time, alert me of texts and phone calls, and last a week between charges. This fits the bill. Still working on the settings to give me optimum battery life. About 60 watch faces avail without going to a 3rd party, many are ugly. Hopefully that will change.

title: Fantastic (Basic) Smartwatch!!
text: This is a great entry level smartwatch. I have to admit I don't use notifications and the like. I primarily use this as a watch and fitness/sleep tracker. First off the BEST feature is the battery life. Yes, there are longer lasting fitness/watches out there (several from Amazfit). But, this provides a beautiful display, GPS, Sleep tracking, etc. with long battery life. IMPRESSIVE!! This is my third Amazfit, first being the Bip. I will step up in the future. A big improvement would be the ability to port over data from the mifit app to the Zepp app, to have continuous data from one device to the other.

title: Touchy screen, but good watch!

The only issue I had was the band but my wrist is very small and I did end up finding new a band that tucks in the additional length of band on Amazon. Love this watch.

title: THE DISAPPOINTMENT BRO!
text: I bought it with great expectation. I saw videos with pros and cons in abundance, but I did not think I would be very disappointed. Its app and battery (14 days) is good and complies, its packaging and construction is appropriate but not too much. The experience with it has been bad, its notifications send useless msgs like "2 msgs of 2 chats" instead of showing the text of the msg. I have an SG2 and SG3 with amoled, at a cost of $ 50 and a robust construction and better user experience, and faster than this. I can't believe that a $ 100-150 smartwatch like Amazfit GTS has Lags in its system, no option to control the camera, bugs in notifications, no option to turn on the screen by touching (SG2 AND SG3 have it and are worth $ 50 ),among other things. I had so much expectation, and I was so happy waiting for a better performance, that I ended up so disappointed. I do not know if it will be only my unit that is like that, but if it saddens me. title: Great value and excellent functionality
text: I recently upgraded from the Amazfit Bip to the Amazfit GTS. This watch has a much easier charging cable, a beautiful resolution on the screen, many more fitness tracking functions and exceptional battery life for the watch. The price was excellent for the value. The overall design and fit of the watch and especially the band are an upgrade from the Bip and feel sleek and you barely notice the watch in your wrist. The upgraded screen and display makes it easy to read emails, texts and other notifications.

title: Great battery, but not much else
text: It has a good design and the battery life is just great, but it goes down from there. The app just isn't that great, the watch interface childish and I had to install other paid apps to get the control I needed. I'm likely to purchase something else and resell this watch.

title: Great battery life
text: The most important features of a smartwatch to me was battery life and readability, especially in daylight. This watch meets those expectations. I put a bit of effort into extending battery life by changing some settings. I turned off constant heart rate monitor and set the display to turn on only when I push the button. I've had the watch for almost a week now and this is day 5 without charging. Battery sits at 91%. Looks like I can probably get an easy 20 days out of the battery. GPS is a real battery hog and very inaccurate. I use my phone for more detailed walking data. Step data seems to be right on. Weather info is only updated while running the app on my phone. Many many watch faces to chose from especially using third party apps. Like other folks mentioned, the app is a mess but can be figured out. There's a lot of data to be had and the watch can be customized extensively. Update 1 - Currently on day 35 on the original charge and the battery is down to 12%. Step count appears to be accurate but distance calculation is way off. I surmised that stride length was calculated by height so I adjusted my height from my actual (6') to 4'8" and the distance is now spot on. Found a watch face that has the info laid out the way I want so the watch is a definite keeper. Update - 3 1st year in and I still really like the watch. Can average 35 days of charge (I have a lot of stuff turned off of course)

title: Great Watch for the Price!
text: This is a great fitness tracker for the money! The screen is bright, easy to navigate and it does everything I need it to do. I have an older version of this same watch and was happy with it, but this updated version is even better! It can track your heart rate, steps, sleep patterns, calories burned and stats from workouts, as well as alert you to notifications received on your phone for things like calls, text messages, Facebook notifications, etc... You can also control the music on your phone from the watch with a basic play/pause and skip forward/back. The touch screen is easy to use, the design is sleek and looks as fashionable as some of the name brand smart watches. I'm honestly quite impressed for the price point. My one complaint is that I have freakishly tiny wrists for an adult and even on the smallest setting this watch slides all over the place, so I would appreciate a smaller band, or at least more holes in the current band. Overall though, for the price I'm impressed and would definitely recommend this watch!

text: Using the product as intended. It is slow to get a reading,, such as heart rate. No BP info. No ekg info. Step counter offers no correlation to distance. During set up there is no way to determine stride length, thus no correlation to actual distance.

title: Just what inwanted

title: A lot of promises and very good effort but not well executed
text: The first impression out of the box is solid nice hardware a bit on the chunky and clunky side. The unfortunate thing about it is the clunky design. The screen is nice. The real problem lies in the user interface. The software is foreign? Even to an android and iOS power user the icons on this thing are cryptic at first and aren’t enjoyable to look at. The default watch faces included and what I saw available in the app didn’t impress me. Here is where the watch gets destroyed. Data. Data capture, for a smart watch is the most important thing. I could care less if it has a screen at all! The heart rate tracking is accurate but data resolution is abysmal. Only able to collect every five minutes at the most frequent continuous sample interval. The sleep tracking function? Well it sure didn’t catch a cat nap I took that I sure as hell detected that I slept for a half hour. Do yourself a favor, save the $40 for a different smartwatch. Better yet, skip the whole smartwatch fad and go with a smaller tracker unit or forget the eFitness trend entirely. Bottom line, whatever option you pick of the above. Buying this watch shouldn’t be one.

title: Much better when they first came out
text: (I have roughly 46 Wyze devices, so I have value for some of their products.) I pre-ordered this from Wyze Watch 47, and when I first got it the features were worth a $20 watch. One of the features was you could set the heart rate monitoring to 5 minutes, 20 minutes 45 and 60 minutes (I believe), which was nice for battery life! Then China released a new firmware for the watch, they called it an "upgrade", now you can only do every 5 minute heart rate, which depletes the battery pretty fast, or you just went without it to make the battery last longer. I also used notifications like email, phone calls, etc. for a short amount of time, because it drained the battery within a day and a half. Sleep tracking was so-so but it wouldn't auto sync with your phone, you had to manually sync. I liked checking my heart rate at night while I'm sleeping so therefore it checked every 5 minutes and my battery lasted maybe two and a half days, tops. Having to charge it all the time just wasn't worth it so I stopped wearing it a few months back and it just sits in the drawer. If somebody would like it it's theirs they can have it! I also bought the smaller Wyze watch for my wife (RN), to tack her steps, it was worn about a month. I would not recommend this watch to a friend. As you can see from the pictures, the watches were made by two different companies, not Wyze. The chargers are different, the OS is different. Wyze buys gadgets and integrates them into the Wyze app. That's all they do. They're tech support is somewhat worthless, prices are low and they make up the difference in they're shipping cost. The products have to have access to Chinese servers, I have a firewall and I log all outgoing traffic, I turned off the access to Chinese servers in mainland China and suddenly my wyze products no longer work. So, keep that in mind. I've read that the access is only to check to see if there's new firmware available, but still it's the principle of of it. Lastly, all wyze products have to have internet service to work. I have an off-grid cabin and I cannot use any Wyze products there.

title: Only one language!

title: Easy

We did replace the bands with black stainless steel magnetic clasps (and wish WYZE offered that as an option). Recently one of the watches stopped being able to do the top row functions (exercise, stats and O2) but I figure that is due to user abuse).

title: For the $$$ Wow
text: Neat addition to my iPhone …. Amazing value …. Seems very well made Could use a little better documentation

title: Some features are simply not real.
text: I received this from the Wyze pre-order program after waiting many months. It has nice features for a $25 investment, but several key failings. 1. Since the first firmware update, the battery life has become miserable if you activate the "Raise to Wake" setting. It lights up randomly when you hardly move your arm. As a result, battery life is about 3 days max. 2. The SpO2 tracking simply does not work. Never has. You only see the latest measurement. 3. Sleep tracking is inconsistent. Sometimes it starts counting "Sleep time" at about 11:30 pm if you are not highly active (e.g. watching TV). If you get up at about 6 am for a few minutes, sometimes it counts this as temporary time awake, sometimes not, and today it indicated I stayed up when I returned to sleep after about 5 minutes. 4. Step tracking is unreliable. It counts me as taking a hundred steps by the time I wake up, when it should be about 20.

title: Not worth it at all
text: The company advertises that the watch lasts several days. Using it for about a month and it has an average life of 14 or so hours with no activity. My return window expired, otherwise I would return it.

title: Great watch! Really great watch so please
text: [[VIDEOID:69116333c69466722360c02aabf04a14]] The watch is really good looking. It really is nice. Big face. So I get about 20 days of essential mode with battery life. Understand it turns off all the other functions and you just get a watch with your steps. Date and time. But if you have it on dual screen mode, you get a good 3 days. I've gotten three and a half days if you really run it to the limit. My only gripe is all the pre-loaded tick watch apps. I wish I didn't have to have them. The top button is for going back and if you long press it activates Google Assistant. I really like the Google pay. It's the best. So much better than my Garmin any of my Garmin watches. It's probably on the level of my Sunto watch. Only $500 cheaper. But definitely has great battery life. Great functionality! It's super fast. I have no issues whatsoever with to watch. I wish. Like I said earlier, I wish I could just disable some of these bloat apps that the company has. It's got heart rate monitor It's got sleep tracking It's got blood pressure. Oxygen level. There might be more But overall I'm very pleased. Very happy. It's a great running performing watch. It connects to Google fit, Strava and their own personal app might be more. You can download apps directly from Google Play store on the watch. The the ability to be able to take a phone call and talk to someone on your watch is really nice. Oh did I mention the Google pay is awesome. You know you can leave your phone in the car and going to a store and use Google pay and come back out with no problems. Would I get this watch again definitely

title: More than likely the best of 202
text: Mobvoi hit it out of the park with this one. Insane battery life... optimized wear OS with a faster somoother experience and a new launcher. I went on ahead and sold my Samsung Galaxy watch 3 on swappa and will be keeping this one. The galaxy watch 3 doesn't even come close to the battery life the Ticwatch offers.
