title: Good but not great
text: It is a good watch. Would be better if I had android phone. iPhone limits it. Already screen cracked. Not sure how and not covered under warranty:(.

title: great watch, but useless if you want stats
text: i had the watch for only a few hours and it is going back. It has lots of features, some really cool watch faces, tracks so many things. However, you need Google Wear app, which is fine, but that app does not show any stats. you need the Mobvoi app, and that no longer connects with Google Wear, so if you want a history of steps, you are out of luck. Want low and high heart rate along with resting heart rate? Sorry. My purpose for this watch was that I spent quite a few dollars and 5 knock-off fitness trackers in the last few months. Each of them had their own issues, so I went with an expensive one, so wouldn't you know it, it made no difference. Still can't track my info. Fitbit Versa 2 was great, but stopped connectivity after one year. It happens to almost everyone, so I will go nowhere near any fitbit again. Looks like this is a no go too. Too bad.

title: BEWARE and READ THIS From a longtime Mobvoi customer BEFORE YOU PURCHASE...
text: I really wanted to like the TicWatch I bought the E and in about 11 months it quit charging. I had it replaced gave it to my nephew and upgraded to the Ticwatch pro. In about 2 years or so it also quit charging, but I figured perhaps my fault somehow although I never went above the recommended 5v for charging. So I bought the pro 2020. I was EXTREMELY CAREFUL charging since the internet is full of people complaining thier watches quit charging...and lo and behold 2 months past the warranty and it quit charging same as the previous 2. I love the watch I really do, but the company is terrible especially with customer service I mean they really just do not care at all about thier users at all and if you talk to them it is very apparent. Plus the fact it appears you will have to buy a new watch every few years since they apparently all quit charging at some point.

title: Great balance of price and quality - would buy again
text: I was the last person I knew who hadn't tried a "smart watch" yet, so decided to dip my toe in the water. After researching all of the non-Apple options, I decided that Mobvoi's TicWatch had the best balance of price and features. About the same time (9/2/22), I saw that they were reducing the price, likely in preparation for a release of new models in late September 2022. I chose the TicWatch Pro 3 GPS model and paid $150. After two weeks of use, I am pretty happy with the build quality of the device. It is not overly large, it is light and unobtrusive. The silicone watch band feels nice and looks nicer with the actual threaded stitching. I go on an hour long walk every day and the GPS has been flawless so far. I especially appreciate the "dual display' that allows me to see the time, date, and step count without actually waking the full screen. That's all I need 80% of the time. I have never used a wearable prior to this, so I cannot compare health tracking data from device to device, but I feel like the heart rate, step counts, and oxygen levels are accurate. I take it off at night, so I have no info to share about sleep tracking. I cannot honestly review the Mobvoi software, as I have opted for all of the stock WearOS options and Google apps (WearOS, Fit, Keep, Wallet, Maps, Messages, YouTube Music.) These Google apps work as expected. In the end, I am very happy with what I got for $150, even if they release something whiz-bang in a few weeks. It does what I need it to do. In fact, my wife plans to but a different TicWatch in the next few weeks based upon seeing mine in action, and she has been a Samsung and Fitbit wearer for many years.

title: Writing this review after less than 2 years of purchase
text: My original broke after going swimming. The replacement one broke after swimming. They are marketing this watch for swimming. Now the watch is out of warranty and I'm stuck with a dead watch.

title: Sent it back
text: Initially I was in LOVE with this watch. Ultimately after 2+ weeks I had to send it back for a refund. 1) I couldn't buy a spare charger because they literally don't sell them. I even contacted their support on their website, which confirmed they did not have them for sale (mid-December 2020). 2) It wouldn't *actually* charge 3 different times in the 2 weeks. The charger clicks when you set it in, so you know the connection is there. I always charge watches overnight, but this one wouldn't indicate why it wasn't charging, just wouldn't. 3) Support couldn't resolve #2, and I just gave up and got my money back. Maybe it'll improve over time. The watch is WAYore responsive than the Fossil one I have that's just over a year old, I imagine thanks to the newer processor.

title: Not a quality replacement
text: If you want something like a Samsung watch or other Android type watch, this is NOT a replacement. This is something I would buy my son to get used to a watch. The app is very clunky to use and the customization options appear more graphical than functional.

title: Best watch I ever had!
text: Best watch I ever had!! Battery life for me is about 3.5 days with moderate use.

title: Superb performance and battery life!!
text: I've had many Android Wear watches and every TicWatch I've owned has always been at the top of the game when it comes to features, performance, and battery life. The dual screen technology is superb and the price point is excellent. If you buy a TicWatch Pro 3 GPS and compare it to other Android Wear watches you'll be greatly impressed. This is the best watch I've owned so far.

title: Excellent battery life and very responsive
text: I get more than 2 full days of battery life during normal use with all of the health monitors enable. The display is crisp and clear and very responsive. It's a huge step forward from my ohinal Ticwatch Pro. Using the new essence features I am easily able to get 3 plus days of battery life and still have roughly 30% battery remaining. Once Wear 3 is a 3, it will be perfect.

title: Wear OS champion!
text: Finally...Wear OS shines on this watch! There is no lag whatsoever thanks to the new Snapdragon processor, whether scrolling through the apps or swiping through notifications. Even switching watch faces through facer is very fast, which is something that has always lagged for me on previous watches. Battery life is pretty good...not AMAZING, but I'm getting up to 2 days which is good enough for me - I was barely getting through the day with previous smartwatches. The LCD layer is very handy since it's always on, I just wish it was a little brighter because it's pretty hard to see (no backlight if turn-to-wake is enabled). Overall highly recommended.

title: Nice watch
text: I used to collect watches and had dozens. I had wanted a Wear OS watch for a while but terrible reviews on most of them kept me away. Since this one has the 4100 chip, I took a chance. I was worried about the size, but it isn't too big...some of my other watches are very similar in size. Don't worry that the body is plastic, heck, plastic is everywhere and is tough. It has some great features and I haven't even messed with a lot of them yet. The connection to my phone is strong and everything is intuitive. I'm pretty happy with my purchase.

title: An excellent upgrade over the original.
text: The original Ticwatch Pro was my first smart watch. I basically refused to upgrade from an old fashion dumb watch because I didn't feel like charging a watch every day or every other day was a paradigm I could get behind after going literal decades between batteries in normal watches. Then enter TicWatch and the dual screen. Getting a couple weeks worth of battery suited me just fine. It feels like I have dumb watch battery, with option smart watch features whenever I want it. The downside of that watch those was that it ran like absolute garbage, to where I really got tired of using it after a year or so. This version solves that problem. It runs buttery smooth and is very snappy. And on top of that not only has the dual screen been improved, but they added a backlight! Something sorely missing from the original. The buttons also don't feel near as cheap. In short, this is the first smart watch I've actually fully enjoyed. However, it gets just 4 stars because of a lack of a rotating crown or a rotating bezel. Also, the new charging cradle is step down from the puck of the original. Don't get me wrong, it works just fine, but not having the watch lay flat while charging is a bummer.

title: Disappointed in quality
text: I purchased the watch in Oct 2020. Was very happy with the battery life and the functionality. In December 2020 had issues with the watch the top screen data was not matching the oled screen. tech support was very helpful and I returned the watch and they promptly shipped a new one directly from Amazon. In February of 2021 I had another issue with the watch. It started vibrating and would not stop without being shutdown and restarted this would keep happening. Again tech support was helpful again shipping a new watch. In June 2021 the vibrating issue started again same symptoms. tech support again was helpful and shipped a new watch. After getting 3 watches in under a year the issue started again in Jan 2022. Now the watch is out of warranty and tech support offers to repair the watch or give me a discount on a new watch. It is unacceptable to spend $300 on a watch that more than 3-6 months. I am not going to accept a discount and spend $200 on a watch that won't last more than a few months. My son has had a Fitbit for 2 years and never had an issue. Time to get a Fitbit or Garmin. I recommended his product when I first got it. but after having 3 brand new watches die in less than a year I would not.

title: Best Wear OS watch on the market
text: Never liked watches, this however changed my mind on many levels starting with look and feel, battery life and features. This is an awesome watch

title: Sleek Device - Battery doing better than expected
text: A couple of days in and I am very happy with this: > device is as sleek as it looked in the pictures > battery is doing much better than 1-2 days - currently at 3 days without charge > love the faces available > Band is fantastic - is waterproof and easy to clean, but it looks real nice and feels really good. Million times better than the Fitbit bands I have used before. A couple of things I am less than happy about: > Wear OS (unrelated to the watch ~ but FYI) doesn't support Work Profiles, so the watch doesn't show my work emails\meetings > Nest notifications do not show video (Apple Watch does) - not sure where the blame for this should be > Can't get watch to play Spotify from its own speakers (yet - still early days)

title: Excellent!
text: Moderate use & by the end of the day you still have 60% battery. Snappy performance and extremely comfortable. BRAVO!!!!!

title: Amazingly functional

title: Pending Review - 1st Review! NO BAD reviews at all for me
text: UPDATED REVIEW*** YES! Yes! and Yes! It's fine! You'll Love it. Watch still going strong. Took off the charger in the morning, but 10am still 94% with "Always On Face"!, by 4pm it was at 74%, whuhhh! wow!!. I highly recommend this watch and for the price it's pretty darn amazing. With "Hey Google" it works great. I can also answer my phone via the phone, reply to text messages, etc! I don't have one bad comment or review of this item. Just to be clear, this is made in China but appears to follow the vendor specifications to a "T" so you won't regret buying this watch for sure. Pros: Easy setup Good looking watch Fits nicely and comfortably on your wrist. No bulky issues or sharpness of any type App allows you to remove notifications and choose only the applications that you want to have notify you Took off charger at 6am and at 10am 94% still and that is with "Always on Face" chosen. Brightness is nice, easy to read Notifications are working fine once loaded. Plenty of choices for watch display type. Cons: Nothing at this time. **UPDATED** Still no cons do date! Overall: The watch quality is nice, looks like a high class chronograph. I was expecting a more detailed chronograph watch display screen but it looks 3% corny but close to realistic. Hope to see better choices soon. Watch has been great so far!!! For the money, great watch! Also lightweight and very form fitting on ones wrist. The band looks leather as well, however is flexible plastic/rubber, that does not stink at all. I will update this review if I see any other good points or bad points....more to come. Have fun and hope you enjoy the watch!

title: Great watch
text: Great watch but use the google wear app and ignore all tic watch stuff. When it does work it’s meh, but you can do all of the same things using the google software so there’s not really a need for the proprietary junk loaded on it. It’s a reliable and useful watch. Bought one for my dad and he’s worn it for 5+ months with zero issues. Bands are easy to change and compatible with quite a few out there. It also lasts for days at a time so unlike apple watches, it isn’t begging for a charge at the end of every day.

title: more of a fancy toy, really...but cool, none-the-less
text: 'twas a total impulse buy (stimulus check made me do it!). it's an awesome watch, with a ton of features (that I already have on my phone, so did I really need it? no.) if your just looking for a new toy, and have $300 to throw around, this watch is for you. if you're looking for a good fitness watch, i'd probably steer you towards a better tracker such as something from the fitbit lineup. my old fitbit charge seemed much more user friendly and accurate (as far as fitness tracking goes). overall, it's a nice watch and has some cool features. it isn't perfect, but it's just what I was lookin' for (me, not caring so much about fitness tracking anymore).

title: no 4100+ but a great watch
text: Ok I was upset when I got the watch and the 4100+ was not there. Note that the add has already been changed so others probably got upset also. I was going to send it back but after trying it out I will not part with it. This is an awesome smartwatch. Fast, long battery life. I've owned a number of wear OS watches and this is the best. I just hope it is upgraded to 3.0 when it comes out nest year.

title: works much better than my old wear watch
text: Depending on which display mode, I can get 3-4 days or 20-30 days before I have to recharge. Display is very readable, love the step tracking.

title: Good watch, NOT hypoallergenic.
text: This is my third TicWatch. And this one, so far, seems to get most everything right. Great battery life. The dual-layer display with low-power backlight is a pure pleasure to use. Best approach I have seen in any smartwatch so far. Sort of like the old Indiglow backlight. Very easy to see at night. The speed, capacity and battery life of this watch is what all Smartwatchs should have been from the beginning. The O2 sensor is a really nice addition too! The phone app could use some significant improvement and debugging. Not sure if TicWatch or Google gets the blame for that. It would be nice if I had more control of the backlight settings and display settings of the ambient mode. UPDATE- The buckle on the band is NOT hypoallergenic! I have a metal allergy (nickel) and when I perspire a bit, the skin under the buckle develops a rash. I can no longer wear this watch. ARGH!!!

title: If you love Google WearOS get this watch!
text: I have been using the Ticwatch Pro 3 for close to 4 months now and I am very happy with my purchase. After doing some research on WearOS powered watches, Ticwatch was a consistent winner with everyone referring to the Qualcomm Snapdragon chip. I was also coming to this watch from a Fossil Gen 2 and with the latest WearOS updates, the speed of response on my Fossil Gen 2 was just painful. Enter Ticwatch Pro 3, and what amazing response time this watch has! I use it for pretty much everything, from using the fitness app (Ticwatch one and Google Fit), to paying on the subway or at stores, thanks to its NFC capabilities, to tracking my sleep. My only complain is that the watch is shipped with a fairly cheap rubber watch band which did give me a skin rash after using it for a prolonged period of time. For geeks who want to monitor their sleep every night, I'd recommend getting a metal band or anything other than rubber.

title: Great hardware. Wear OS is still lacking
text: So many disconnects with the watch. It was driving me crazy. Sleep tracking was great, but doesn't feed into Google fit while steps and heart rate tracking do. I cycle indoors and outdoors alot and couldn't pair a bluetooth cadence or speed sensor for indoor cycling so I couldn't use the watch for indoor cycling workouts (third party options like ghostracer didn't work for me). Having to track in multiple apps is annoying! (mobvoi app for some stuff, sleep as android for sleep so it feeds into Google fit, and stilling using my phone wahoo app for tracking cycling so I can see it all in Google fit) Notifications weren't great and you can barely feel the vibration (when it does work). It will be nice to see what google does with wear os 3.0. They need to get it together and if you're going to keep pushing google fit, it needs to be competitive. Bummed to return it because I actually like the look, feel, and battery life but it's let down by wear os.

title: If I could give it zero stars I would
text: I emailed the company 8 times about the watch not connecting properly to my phone. It will disconnect on its own multiple times. Now it has got to the point it will not even connect to the internet. I have reset it 10 times and it still will not reconnect to the internet and will not update. I have tried to connect it to the internet through my phone and on the watch itself multiple times with zero success. I am highly disappointed in this watch. It also doesn’t track my exercises or locations. I have tried to update it multiple times and reset it to update it and it still will not. At this point the watch is just a $300 paper weight. I am constantly bounced around from person to person saying email this place or call this number and not this one, only to start the same process over and over. To be talked down to as if I am stupid and do not know who to manage the watch when in fact it is the watch that is a piece of junk. I also reached out to Amazon to get feedback from them since I purchased it through them and they said the reach out to your company in regards of the watch since their knowledge of it wasn’t that deep (not Amazon’s fault). After this experience if I could give them negative ten Stars I would. No one should have to go through this experience especially for the price of $300. We are hard working people and money is important especially during the pandemic. Buyer be wear.

title: Got to struggle to make this watch track anything

I have replaced my watch once, i have to reset or restart my watch in SHIP MODE once every 2 months for the sensors to start working again. The water resistants in another scam with so many extra conditions that i take it off even if it just pool or shower. title: Absolutely Fabulous Watch!
text: I had put off buying a watch for a long time and decided to finally purchase one. This watch is fantastic! Answering calls and receiving text messages right on the watch is incredible. The sleep tracking is amazing, as well as keeping track of physical activities. I use in when at the gym while lifting weights and keeps good detailed information. I have received many compliments on the look of the watch, and being able to choose from over a thousand watch faces is a joy. I can't be happier with this watch. Has more features than I expected.

title: Best Wear OS watch
text: I've had so many Wear OS watches, and inevitably sold them quickly because of the sluggist, unreliable performance. This is the first Wear OS watch where the performance is excellent, thanks to 4100 processor. Not as slick as Apple Watch, but now it's close. Google Assistant also works so much better with new processor. I also love the secondary screen. I only charge this thing every three nights. Definitely worth the money.

title: NO COMPASS... are you kidding me..
text: wow... one the basic things you think you get in a smart watch is a compass.. yet they did not include one... sad.. you have a GPS.. and no compass.. come on man...

title: Dual Display Battery Saver and works with EUC World
text: The dual layer display is a terrific battery saver. You have both a digital face and an analog style face. To further save battery life you can also lock the watch onto it's analog face. Doing so also deactivates the backlight. To reactive you simply press the function button and it's back into digital mode. You have the option of staying on the digital face 24/7 if you choose. Step tracking, sleep monitoring, oxygen content and heat rate sensors all work great. With normal everyday operation the battery last about 2-3 days. Package contains the watch with a stylish sylicone watch band and a magnetic mount charge cable. The speaker on the watch is loud and clear. The microphone also works good for phone calls. There is a keyboard function for texting. When i first saw the keyboard i thought it was so tiny. However, the screen is so precise i had no problems typing on the tiny keyboard. There are multiple controlling apps that work with the phone. The Mobvoi App and the Wear OS App. These apps give you full control of the apps that send notifications to your watch. I use this watch for daily use and for use on an EUC. The watch has no problem running EUC World. With the data stemming between the phone and watch i use about 20% of battery life every 6 hours while on my EUC.

title: This is hands down THE best WearOS Smart watch.
text: I am switching to this watch from the Fossil Gen 5, and the difference is night and day. The always on screen that is on by default lets you see any of the information you would want to see on demand, all the while still being able to have a custom watch face. So far I went 2 days without a charge and still had 48% battery remaining (this was with pretty heavy use). Very happy with my purchase!

title: IMPRESSIVE
text: I usually read the BAD reviews first, that sort of gives me a better idea of the problems I may face with a device, and so I did with the TickWatch pro, most complaints were not significant, a few worrisome so I took a chance, BOY I AM IMPRESSED, this watch blew my expectations, Samsung is a little close with this one taking the advantage of using WearOS, watch battery is more than impressive, 3 days on a single charge, and took around 30 to 40 minutes to fully charge, the speed is just way better than the samsung, watch faces are a million thanks to WearOS. I had my doubts, but after wearing this watch all of them are gone, this is my watch, I'm returning the Samsung [sorry but this is way better], I will revisit this review after a month has passed.

title: Display doesn't come on when arm is raised. Have to shake arm to see watch.
text: Display doesn't come on when arm is raised. I have to shake arm a few times for display to appear. Heart rate monitor is inaccurate, e.g. doctor's office measured heart rate as 75 bpm whereas watch showed 135 bpm. I have to charge watch everyday after a swim or workout. Watch will indicate 100% battery life at 9:00 AM, and after a 3hr workout, battery goes down to around 50% and then 6% by 9 PM. If I don't move much or workout battery life will stay above 90% and last about 2 days. I do a lot of water aerobics. I have to charge watch afterwards. I'm usually exhausted and doze off after a strenuous workout. If I doze off before watch is charged, I don't get any sleep quality data. Watch needs a better battery, heart rate monitor and sensors to turn on display when arm is raised.

title: Very nice watch
text: This is a very nice watch. It’s very comfortable to wear and has lots of good functionality. This has nice functionality - I’ve used a lot of fitness trackers and smartwatches, and this was accurate for my heart rate. The other functions are nice. The watch is responsive and seems to work very well

title: Easy to Read At a Glance
text: I like the size of the face and it is super easy to read because everything is sharp, clear. I really appreciate that, with the aid of the app, I could customize the watch face (put my dog’s face on it). I only use it for time and steps though I do occasionally check my heart rate just for the fun of it. I did it one day during a routing annual checkup and the heart rate was very close to what the nurse said. The band is easy to fasten and unfasten, though it is a bit too long for me, but I can live with that.

title: This is a little better than okay - not bad, but not great, either
text: This is the third smartwatch I've ordered and reviewed from Amazon in the past month or so. The first two stunk on ice and were returned. One was completely non-intuitive to use, which is the entire point of a SMARTwatch - that you be able to figure out how to get it to operate. That was the Bovrou for $25.99. The other wouldn't light up and show me the time when I flipped my wrist, which is the other entire point of a smartWATCH - to tell you the time. That was the Portzon GL2 for $65.99. This one is both intuitive and it works when I flip my wrist. So, immediately, it's better than the other two models. The steps, heartrate, and blood pressure measures are all accurate. I also LOVE the metal snap-on wristband - much nicer than the regular rubber wristbands that these smartwatches usually come with. So why only three stars? Well, it might have to do with the size of the numbers on the screen, which might relate to the size of the screen itself. The screen here is a little smaller, a little lower resolution than other watches - 1.57" versus 1.8". The selection of watch faces is relatively limited, so that there aren't any selections where the subsidiary information - date, heart, calories, steps - has a large font size. Sure, the time is in big numerals, but that's it. And I'm old, and I can't read the small font easily. If you've got young eyes, this is a nicer watch - I'd rate if four stars for you, because it does do all the regular things pretty well. But for me, with old eyes, it's not a very smart watch if I can't read the smart info it's giving me.

text: My wife really likes this watch. This is the one with the glittery watchband... It comes with a magnetic charger that just attaches to the back - no fidgeting. It paired on the first try and seems to be working just as it should. She's now got it set up to check emails and can generally do anything on the internet that she would do with her phone. title: It could have been so much better.
text: I have so many feelings about this watch. First off, set up was a breeze. You just open your app store and get the Google app directed. Pairing and synching up your info is very easy. The watch is very beautiful! I was scared the crystals would rub right off like glitter, but I have not had any issues so far. Now for all the bad stuff.. first and foremost the battery life is terrible. I would give it 9-10 hours max. I'm not much of an app person either, so if you are then that means your battery life will be even lower. It has its own charger, so that means you'll have to carry it around with you, especially big your planning to go out after work or school which is very inconvenient. I with it was a standard C USB charger so I can just use my phone charger, but sadly that's not the case. I did an experiment to see how long the battery would last. I charged it to 100%, and left it in my desk right before bed. In the morning at 8 am, I am at 15%. Whoa. Yeah, the battery is just really really terrible. So I thought I'd just change the battery settings..well there is only one other option and that is to go into battery saving mode where all it will display is the time. That in my opinion defeats the purpose of a smart watch. Other than that, I love how I can customize watch faces by using my social media, or pick from a pre made list by Michael Kors. You can also get email notifications, download apps like Google keep to take notes by speaking into your watch, as well as use Google pay, activity tracker, weather, and pause and play music without taking out your phone. So yeah, if your okay with a short battery life, then everything else about this watch is awesome. Just giving you the real tea. Hope you found this review helpful.

title: Still Searching

The lack of this feature makes the watch unsuitable for me, and that makes me sad, because the iPhone is a begware spamming disappointment machine these days, and I really want to move to android.

text: I've not owned a smart watch before, so perhaps my impression is a bit naive, but as soon as i received it, I charged it as the quick start guide said to do. The other end is a traditional usb plug, but this does not come with an outlet plug, though I'm sure it can attach to a laptop and/or tablet with a usb port. I happen to have purchased an extended outlet that also included four usb ports, so I plugged it in and waited. The watch told me when it was done - it had, "Tap to Continue," on the face. I followed the instructions - already had the Google OS on my phone, it just needed an update. Once done, the watch came to life and took me on a tour - I played with the included watch faces on the phone app - chose the moon and stars face which shows my time just above center and in the circle of the moon, I can choose another time zone. My pulse/heart rate was set by my height and weight, my appointments/calendar were syned and when a notification is sent to my phone, the watch face shows it. When I first saw it, I thought, this is going to be clunky - I may be a good-sized woman, but I have fairly delicate bone structure, meaning I have very small wrists and big watch faces usually don't work well on me. Maybe because it is so light-weight, but even with the larger watch face, it is quite comfortable and the "rubber/silicone" band is very smooth and comfortable. The band would be my only wish - that the surround (around the watch) wasn't the same material as the band since there will probably come a time when I want something different in a band. Other than that, this is one cool watch and of course, I'm still figuring everything out since I'm old and new tech takes me longer than younger folks to learn. I do really like this watch!

title: A decent Android smartwatch but with bad battery life
text: Michael Kors' MKGO is their latest and lightest smartwatch to date incorporating the Snapdragon Wear 3100 processor giving it a bunch of power. It makes use of Googles Wear OS rather than just be another fitbit type watch and so is a full smartwatch for Android. The watch itself is very clean and elegant with a pink silicone strap. The bezel and the rest of the watch is also pink making this great for your wife/daughter. On the right hand side there are three buttons, one of which acts as a sort winder which allows you to scroll through the apps the watch has. It connects to your mobile phone through bluetooth and is simplicity to setup. Just download the google app on your phone, tell it which gmail you want to use and link it to your watch with bluetooth. The watch face is of course touch sensitive. You can choose which face design you want the watch to display from a wide variety of choices. By default the watch will turn its display off to save on battery usage but when you twist your wrist to look at it, the accelerometers built it detect the movement and turns the face back on again. The bottom button gets you into fitness mode with guided workouts and breathing exercises, heart rate monitor and all the other stuff you would expect from a fitbit type device. The middle and main button takes you into the apps which range from weather checking (you must have GPS turned on in your phone for this to work), calendar appointments, alarms, contacts to find my phone which comes in handy and also a small flashlight app although it isn't very bright. Once hooked up with your phone, any alert that your phone displays will get mirrored to the watch. Facebook alerts, news items, emails, phone calls etc. My main email account is not a gmail account but because the phone gives me an alert whenever I get an email, the watch displays it and will let you read the contents. The MKGO is not quite yet at the standard of the Apple watch but close. The only slight downside is battery life. You will get roughly 36 hours on a full charge for average usage, less if you let the watch constantly check your heart rate.

title: Simple and functional exterior is surprisingly elegant -- & battery lasts longer!
text: The thing I was least prepared for with this watch was how much I would like the utilitarian case and band. Waterproof and minimalist, the matte finish makes it easy to mistake this for an elegant evening piece. It is, indeed, lighter and slightly thinner than previous generations of smart watches. It is still very large for a slender wrist; I wear a size 8 glove and the watch looks generous but not over-sized. On my friend who has a 5.75" wrist, the watch looks enormous. The applications are those that work with Wear OS. The one new one is the Michael Kors Access menu, a striking linear design that works surprisingly well when swiping through. The heart rate tracking will sample and record heart rate automatically periodically throughout the day, but there is no recognition of arrhythmias or tachycardia as there is with the Apple Watch (not FDA approved, of course!) But, most important, I think is the new Qualcomm processor and the claim of improved battery life. It's true! I was dismayed when I ran out of battery within 8 hours on the first day. However, it must have been doing updates or something, as it has been terrific since then, with 20 hours and more, a huge improvement over previous generations. The accompanying watch faces are a bit repetitive, lots of big "MK" over startling colors, but I do like a couple of the "glam" faces, especially the animated stars that "fall" across the dial as you change its orientation. And it is SUPER easy with this watch to push a social media (Twitter or Facebook) photo to the face.

title: Interesting Gadget, Works as Advertised, But Tied to Smartphone
text: This SAMSUNG GEAR S2 SMARTWATCH (Dark Gray) is an interesting gadget, and works as advertised. It's kind of fun to make and receive telephone calls from your wristwatch (just like Dick Tracy did in the comic strips with his 2-way wrist radio). However, to be able to make calls, you need to register it with your cellphone network (on Verizon, this entails a $30 activation fee, plus $5 a month thereafter). You can use the Gear S2 for lots of things without activating the phone, of course. There is a fitness tracker app, and there are interactive watch faces that can keep you abreast of your favorite teams' real-time game scores, the current stock market numbers, and other things. However, I like my [[ASIN:B00N2BW2PK Fitbit-Charge-Wireless-Activity-Wristband]] much better for telling time and for activity tracking--the Fitbit is easier to use, and does more things reliably. The biggest drawback regarding the apps, is that they are tied to your smartphone. All of the Gear S2 apps use Bluetooth for running the app from your phone. This means your smartphone has to be turned on, within the Bluetooth range, and charged, for the apps to work. One problem that I never solved with the NBA watch face, was that the real-time scoring updates would stop when my Samsung Galaxy S7 Edge went into sleep or dormant mode after about an hour. Finally, the Gear needs frequent charging--every day or two. This means you can't really treat it like a watch that you leave on your wrist 24/7. You have to treat it like a cellphone, and take it off for charging every night. A negative about activating the phone--boo to Verizon!--is that my assigned phone line had been previously assigned to someone who had a lot of people still looking for him/her. Thus I got a lot of unwanted calls from the moment the Gear S2 was fully activated. My Gear S2 was free (from a Samsung/Verizon deal with my preorder of the Galaxy S7 Edge). I'm very glad that I didn't pay a couple of hundred dollars for mine, as it turned out that I have no need for a smartwatch.

title: In the immortal words of Ferris Bueller: "It is so choice. If you have the means, I highly recommend picking one up"
text: Bought this for my son for his birthday. He is head over heels in love with it. Syncing it with his Galaxy S7 was completely painless (well except for his impatience) but it really took less than 10 minutes. The fact that it had interchangeable bands was a huge selling point for me, I liked the fact that he would be able to get a dressier band if he needed it and change the display appearance to match the occasion. The charging dock is great- he can sit it right on his nightstand and still see the watch. Texting on it is obviously tedious, but it isn't meant for you to write a novel on it. As a mom- my favorite option is the fact that he can find his phone with it! He says the very best thing about it is that it has features that he actually use for example: The S Health is so user friendly, he can add right activities and food on the watch and not have to dig out his phone. He love the fact that he can see his steps right on the lock screen. He also loves the fact that he can see if he gets texts or emails immediately.There are the other typical options that people want at a glance- such as weather. He is not a big user of voice commands, so he can't comment on that. But he does love the remote control option- especially for music, you can skip songs etc without stopping what you are doing to grab your phone. He hasn't found a smart remote app for the TV but that would be a game changer- no more lost remotes! The camera remote is great too- he also has a Samsung Smart Camera so it won't be long before he learns how to sync that too. It's a little pricey, but you get a lot of bang for your buck. As a parent, I know I have wasted thousands of dollars on the latest gotta-have it gadget, that ends up being nothing but a dust magnet in a few days or weeks. But this is one gadget that you probably won't feel like you were duped into buying.

title: Loved it for 6 months, then it was "unrepairable" due to sweat... Seriously?
text: Let me start by saying that I wore this watch every day for 6 months. My husband got it for me as a Christmas present December 2015 and I absolutely love the bevel and the apps and the step counting. I LOVED the watch and told my friends about it and encouraged them to get one as well. That was until 2 weeks ago... Here is why I give it only 2 stars... after 6 months, the watch stopped counting steps, stopped reading my heart rate, and no longer responded to the "wake up gesture". I called Samsung and they sent me to a Samsung repair shop close to me. The result of the repair was that it was deemed "unrepairable due to extensive water damage". I swear I never EVER emerged the watch in water, pool, tub, anything. I was even careful when I washed my hands to not get water on it. The "extensive water damage" came from my sweat. Seriously? Isn't the point of the watch to be worn at all times? The watch even encourages getting up and moving and working out. Here in Texas, it's hard to not sweat while doing such things, so this"water-resistent" capabilty they claim is NOT true. Additionally, Samsung will not repair, replace, or discount another watch due to this damage. Needless to say, I won't be buying another one. How could I? Within 6 months it is unrepairable due to sweat from day-to-day activities and working out. Hope this helps!

Google Now cards show 1 card, and launch on phone. I was hoping for the watch to handle it. S-Voice is dreadful, my 4 syllable command would open svoice 1 out of 10 times (maybe). Texting etc was decent, but not great. Battery life is around 1 - 1.5 days, far far far short of 3 days. Charging from 0 takes hours. I could get in the habit of charging overnight. In summary, to have another item buzzing that I have an email/text/call that all necessitate using my phone for addressing the notification defeated the purpose. I know text or email can be read without pulling out the phone. For me, it was just easier to deal with notifications coming in on my phone. That left me with a $300 watch/pedometer that buzzes. Maybe with some updates I'll look again, but as it is, its too costly for what it added to my life.

title: Interface Not intuitive. Inaccurate SHealth data. Battery isn't that great
text: This review is after 2 months of use. The watch is a replacement for a Fitbit Surge ... mainly so I didn't have to carry my phone when out running. The watch connects to Verizon and that works well for taking calls. So why the 2 stars: First, the watch is extremely in-accurate as a sports watch: 1. Distance tracked is usually off by 15-20%. (Run/Walk a mile and watch will show .85) 2. Heart rate is sometimes off by a factor of two (Watch shows 194, Actual is 97). If I take the watch off and put it back on, this resets the heart rate and it's usually accurate after that (although I've occasionally had the problem recur during a single workout). If I don't do remove the watch to reset the HR, it will stay inaccurate for entire workout. 3 The watch has restarted the workout stats a few times. So in the middle of a workout it, will reset the mileage to 0. I haven't determined why this happens yet...but it's obviously pretty annoying. What's interesting is that it will continue to track the workout duration (time) and steps. I did try a hard reset the watch to take it back to the factory setting. Also, trying clearing running apps before a workout. Neither worked. Second, Battery isn't that great. Just using it as a watch it might last a full day. But, plan to recharge after a workout or taking a few calls. It in no way lives up to Samsung batter life claims. Third, the interface isn't very intuitive. I do software development & IT Project Management. Designing an intuitive User Interface is critical to the user experience. The Samsung watch apps are not intuitive and sometimes you have to go through a number of screens to get something done. Follow-up: I sent the watch back to Samsung to have them look at the sports watch functionality/issues. They sent the watch back saying there where no hardware problems found. So, reconfirms the Gear S2 is a buggy/immature product ... at least from a firmware/software standpoint. It should spent more time in the Quality Assurance/Testing department before release.

title: Works great, looks good
text: IMO smart watches shouldn't overstep their bounds and try to do everything, the thing I like about the Gear S2 is it's a watch first. I have the screen in always-on mode, so it feels like a high-quality digital watch, and it has the added bonus of being able to: Track my steps & heart rate Play music through Bluetooth headphones Get notifications Send short text messages (pre-made reply or emojis) Show weather alerts, news stories, or stock prices It also has a calendar and maps, but I haven't tried those After wearing it for a few days, I only have a couple of minor complaints: No speaker, so the alarm is vibrate only (it did wake me up though) Not Android Wear, so no apps from Google Play - there's a small Samsung Gear store for apps and watch faces After about 6 weeks of use: I use the step-tracker every day, I like not having to wear an extra fitness tracker I like having the temperature on my watch, good for when I'm about to walk out the door on cold nights I like being able to see who is calling so I can decide whether or not to answer I like listening to music using only the watch & bluetooth headphones After 6 months: I still use it everyday, great for setting alarms, glancing at texts & messages from FB or IG, and seeing who's calling. It looks brand new, no signs of wear. Battery lasts two days in always-on mode connected to bluetooth. Wireless charger cradle and fast charging.

Since my oxygen had been so low, they sent me home on oxygen and I’ve been on that and a nebulizer since. I bought a pulse oximeter and that is accurate. I ran the heart rate along side the watch and am happy to say that the pulse on the watch is accurate. Pros: battery life is great. The pulse message notification is great. The watch fits comfortably. The blood pressure seems to work well. When I’ve stood up quickly and felt dizzy, I’ve checked the blood pressure and as expected it reads a low blood pressure. title: Great Battery Life, good watch, but will leave you yearning for more.
text: While I did return this watch I will say I was very impressed with the battery life. I went about 16days before I decided to recharge it, and even then it was at about 14% and it could have possibly lasted another day or two. The main reason I returned it was because it was not accurately keeping track of when I slept. I work at night so I sleep during the day and (unless I missed the setting) I couldn't get it to measure or record any data when I slept during the day. The other issues I had with it was the connection to the phone. It was almost always behind when receiving messages or phone calls. More than a few times a message or call would come in, no notifications would happen on the watch, but after I answer the call or start to respond to a message the notification would come in for me to answer the call or that I received the message. There is no way to reply to the messages on the watch, so if you are looking for that feature, this is not the watch for you. If you are looking for an entry smart watch with a very long lasting battery, good/basic health tracking features, then look no further, but if you want something with more advanced features, keep searching.

title: Sometimes it works!
text: The main selling feature of this watch, by far, is the built-in Alexa functionality. When I got my watch, I followed all the steps, downloaded the app, upgraded the firmware, got it all set up and... it didn't work. So I notified Amazon and asked for a replacement. When the replacement came, I did everything over again, careful not to leave out any steps, and it didn't work either! I called Amazon, they couldn't offer much help. I called Amazfit, they walked me through several troubleshooting steps, and it started working. After I got off the phone with them, it stopped working again. I went back through the steps again, and it started working. But it would never stay working for very long. Sometimes the steps to reconnect it wouldn't work at all. Sometimes I didn't need to do anything, it would just work. That's when I realized that this is actually a feature! The brilliant minds at Amazfit have developed a device that changes the way that people see technology. We take for granted that things should just work when we want them to. We never consider for a moment if our technology even WANTS to work for us at that time. How inconsiderate! This watch DOES work, but it works when IT wants to work. That may be the first time that you ask it something, but more likely when you try back in about 25 minutes. Sure you could probably do what you're wanting instantly by using an app on your phone, but then you will never learn the lesson that the good people at Amazfit are trying to teach you about just having a little common courtesy towards the devices that serve you day-in and day-out. So how about having a little patience, give your device a break, and let it decide when you really need to talk to Alexa. Is that really so much to ask?

title: Get the 1st gen instinct
text: I bought this watch (not from Amazon) as an upgrade from my first generation Instinct that I had for almost 2 years. However, at best this watch is only marginally better than the first generation Instinct. The only real "improvements" are the SPo2 meter, the ability to track heart rate while swimming, and the solar assist. Frankly, none of those improvements justify the price difference between the Instinct Solar and the first gen Instinct. To start with, calling this a Solar assisted watch is pretty charitable. The solar power generation is negligible. I left mine out in the full Texas sun in August, off my wrist, for two and a half hours from 11:30 am until 2:00 PM and it only increased the charge by 4 percent. You could get that much charge in less than two minutes plugged into the wall. So don't expect to get any kind of significantly longer battery life from the solar assist. Second, the heart rate while swimming is so inaccurate as to be entirely useless. Indeed, the watch tells you this when you turn the feature on. Finally, I guess its cool to have SPo2 and VO2 max, but frankly, I don't care much about that. Save a hundred dollars and just get the first generation Instinct.

It was exactly what I was looking for. Just right amount of smart watch features combined with solid connection and fitness tracking. Loving the battery life of this watch. The "old school tech" screen combined with the solar charging gives amazing battery life. No more charging the watch every 4 or 5 days. Super happy with it.

title: 3 months in: Good but not Great
text: First and foremost, this watch is perfect smartwatch alternative for someone who would typically wear a G-Shock watch. The battery: The battery life isn’t quite as good as advertised. I would guess I could get about 15-18 days on smartwatch mode rather than the 28 days advertised. Doing exercise doesn’t put as much of a drain on the battery life as you would think, but the cold does. Heart rate: This is why I’m not giving the watch 4 stars and not 5. I don’t trust the wrist based heart rate at all. I will wear this watch while cycling and have my chest based heart rate strap synced with my Garmin 520 cycling computer. I trust that heart rate. When I compare that with what’s on the watch, sometimes it’s perfectly aligned, sometimes it’s off by as much as 20%-30%. However, this watch will pair to any Garmin HR strap for exercise if you’re using your watch as your main tracker. So I’ve done that. The only con is that it won’t remember my chest based heart rate strap so I have to forget it and re-sync it for every exercise which can take a few minutes. Also, the heart rate feature doesn’t work for swimming, which is a common thing for smart watches. Exercises: -Running: Seems to work great for running as long as I can get to an area that is wide open. -Cycling: I won’t be replacing my 520 with this for cycling anytime soon. I depend on the heart rate while cycling and I can’t trust this. -Swimming: While pool swimming it works pretty well with freestyle, but doesn’t count the laps accurately if you’re doing a different stroke like breaststroke or butterfly. I haven’t tried open water swimming yet. Elevation: It doesn’t do great finding and holding the correct elevation unfortunately. GPS: Works well as a compass and in expedition mode. Would recommend. Solar: Takes way more sunlight than I thought to actually make a difference in the battery life. You would need a full day of being outside in the middle of the summer for it to actually increase battery life. The sun in the winter doesn’t do anything for it, especially in Northern climates. Notifications: They come through 100% of the time. Usability: 10/10. This watch is super user friendly and easy to set up as someone without strong technical competency.

title: Really bad for people with nickel allergy!
text: I love this watch so much but after having my daughter, I developed a pretty severe allergy to nickel. Though the back says it’s “Aerospace Aluminum” The charge port connector on the back (below the heart rate monitor) is nickel as are the pins from the watch band that they provide and they have caused my wrist to break out as if I got poison ivy! I have found a work around to cover it with packing tape every time I take it off the charger but it’s lame that I have to do this! You’d think they wouldn’t use a common allergen in their products! I filed a complaint to the company and depending on how they respond, I may change my review but please know that if you have a nickel allergy this is not for you! I don’t know about the other models. Update- I contacted Fitbit and they explained that I’m not washing my watch well enough! I am not a chemist, but I’m pretty certain that soap and water do not remove nickel from metal! I’m definitely knocking more stars off due to their apathetic response!

title: Never buying a fitbit again!

title: I love the Versa!

title: Great Gift.

It tracks well but never wants to sync with app. I spend hours trying to get it to sync to wifi but it doesnt. It goes days without syncing then randomly syncs a few times then never again. Im done with it. Back it goes. I will continue to use my Charger 2 version until I find a better brand.

title: Great fitness tracker for the price
text: Great fitness tracker for the price...and it alerts me for incoming phone calls and text messages. The battery life is great, too. I would recommend this smartwatch to anyone. Did I say easy to set up? Yes it was super easy!

title: Mostly good
text: A great tracker, but on my wrist it tracks things like when I move my hand too much. My last Fitbit tracker was kept in my pocket or on a belt loop, so non-walking steps hardly were counted. This one makes it look like I walk more than I actually do, but I suppose it isn't a huge exaggeration. Otherwise, very nice, especially the sync with strava for my bike rides.

title: Really like it. Beeen wearing for about 4 months
text: So far love it - have had it about 4 months or so. Works well! Water resistant which I love and it holds a good charge! Definitely better quality than my Fitbit HR charge I had in the past. It’s a quality touch screen smart watch but much better quality than previous models!

title: Great motivator quits after 8-9 months.
text: I've been wearing this watch for almost a month now and I'm impressed with the overall quality of the versa. The only issue I have is that I do not believe the calories burned during workouts are necessarily correct. I wore this watch along with my polar ft4 heart rate monitor ( HRM ) and chest strap to see how they compare. The heart rate was near perfect when compared to the HRM. During the same 75min workout my HRM said I burned 692 calories, while my Versa stated 976. This alone is not a big enough issue for me to warrant returning the watch. I love my versa. Its attractive, motivates me to move more to hit that step goal, and helps remind me of my overall goals. It is waterproof. I was skeptical and nervous af first. But I've worn it in the shower and swimming with no issues. I was worried about the band fitting since I am a large woman. Im 5'9 & currently 302 pounds...However the s/m band fits with 4 extra slots. The watch comes with a large band too so I wouldn't worry about the fit. Remember to clean the band as it can get smelly if you dont daily or every other day. I dont use the watch for "smart watch" purposes so I can't comment on that aspect. The battery lasts about 4 days for me. The watch Is very attractive and the app it syncs to can provide a lot of really good insights when it comes to sleep, workouts, and daily activity Update. It's been almost 9 months and the heartrate sensor is shot. I contacted Fitbit support and they told me to factory reset and now the watch is basically useless as all it does is flash the fitbit logo and a few languages telling me to download the app. I really hope they'll replace it, I'm calling again tomorrow to get things sorted.

title: Love it!
text: This is my 4th Fitbit. This one is the best yet! I compared it to the Apple Watch, and I feel this is a much better value. I love how quickly it charges up and it is easier to connect to the charger than any previous model. The band is much better than other Fitbit models have had. I love being able to customize my display as well. Super awesome device!

title: Mine was hacked and customer service does not care.
text: I have the Fitbit special edition with rose gold. My first review nearly a year ago was denied by amazon, probably because of my lower than 5 star rating. But now after having it even longer, it is an even lower rating from me (so maybe they should have accepted it the first time). Fitbit knows what’s up. You can’t leave reviews on their website and mine gets denied on here. Someone bought me this as a gift via Amazon. I’ve had this since maybe June of 2018. Fitbit has the worst customer service I’ve ever dealt with. I’ve had to call them twice so far. Also, my Fitbit was hacked probably bc you can enter your credit cards and Starbucks cards on there to pay with your watch. Customer service said i had to wait 48 hours for them to email security and then security would email me. Why can’t they just transfer you to security that day? Now my watch is stuck in a different time zone and It doesn’t recognize my email. Unacceptable. The syncing with your phone constantly turns off, pretty much daily, and it’s a hit or miss if I’m able to receive texts through it. I’m so over Fitbit. Next time I’m getting the Apple Watch. I don’t care if I have to charge it every day. They simply do not back up their product.

title: Love it!
text: I love my Fitbit Versa! Works great, tracks everything, is stylish, and is the perfect size, not too bulky.

title: Inaccurate
text: I had a Surge for three years which I really liked but I had to replace it when the wristband broke. The Versa is more versatile and has better graphics but it is incredibly inaccurate. I wore the Surge and Versa together and the Versa is too sensitive (also counts a lot of steps while driving in a car - which the Surge didn't do) and the sensor for the stairwell is way too sensitive. Update: Wristband cracked after just two months ...

title: nightmare to set up/update
text: Wow where to start. Well, first, if you are set on getting this Fitbit, be warned. It has taken me 4 days, including contacting Fitbit support, to get the thing set up. This is my 3rd Fitbit and I have never had issues before, and I'm not that big of a tech dummy. If it doesn't like your wifi network, it will NOT connect even if every other device in your home has no problem. So how do you set up/update the Fitbit without wifi? Well, it gives you an option to skip it but trust me, that will not work. Your update will fail over and over, sometimes after hours of waiting to get to 37% and bam! update fails. **TIP** If it won't connect to your wifi and the update continually fails, save yourself the trouble and use your phone as a Hotspot and connect to that for wifi, save yourself the grief of restarts, unpairing, starting over, waiting, and frustration of multiple failed attempts. It finally worked that way for me. Now that it's finally up and running, let it be known that the bands are a pain in the rear to change, especially in comparison to the Charge2 that had a fantastic easy way to replace bands with no pins. So, ease of setup and band replacement gets an F. The functionality seems OK, time will tell. I'm not sure if this was worth $180; I'd feel better about it if I had paid the $150 sale price before Christmas. I hope I like it in the end as much as my Charge. If it gives me any more grief it's going back to JB.

title: when it works
text: When it works it works great. Every so often it stops syncing with my phone. Sometimes shutting off and turning back on the Bluetooth works. However, sometimes you have to reset it back to the factory settings when it starts losing time or you can't get it to sync at all. Unfortunately, when you reset your versa you lose some of the data.

title: Bluetooth syncing issues still not resolved.

When I contacted fitbit, they seem to be aware that the versa's have this problem and that there may be an update at some time. My husband has a blaze, which they have discontinued, and an Ionic, and both work great. Neither the Ionic or Blaze have this problem. I would be hesitant in buying a Versa until a fix is found.

title: Fitbit needs to fix many issues with this watch!

title: Good and Bad
text: Edit: 07-21 Shipping back for refund. Lack of GPS and poor data mgt makes it nearly useless. I will continue to use map my walk until I find a better app/device combo. Sorry FB. Edit: 07-17-18 Had to set up a guest 2.4GHZ network at home to connect this, and once I did, setup went smoothly. Pros: great styling smooth functioning touch screen, lot's of face options. Great battery life, getting 5-6 days, but I don't use GPS too often...yet. Cons: Really poor integration between FitBit and Map My Fitness (under Armour) app(s). Very common workouts are not included, including Elliptical (treadmill doesn't work well as substitute) and water sports like canoeing, kayak, or paddle board. Very disappointing. This whole "must have a 2.4GHZ wifi network" to complete setup should embarras FitBit. Spend $200, it should work out of the box. Will update if I can get this thing rolling

title: Awesome fitbit

My only beef is that sometimes it un-syncs from the app and it's a pain to re-sync about half the time. I'd buy it again though and recommend it to others.

title: Works for at least 3 years
text: Bought this for my wife's birthday in August 2019. She wears it almost daily and it's still going strong now in September 2022.

title: Didn't last long enough for the money

title: I really love the watch
text: I really like the watch for the most part, it is the sleep reporting that is not reporting correctly (after multiple resseting of the watch) all else works great. Some days I wake up after I know I slept more than 8 hours and my watch will display one hour of sleep? Really? title: I love this watch
text: I love this watch! It is awesomely intuitive with exercise even if you forget to put it on that mode. It doesn't have all the bells and whistles (or price tag) that the Apple Watch does, its a fitness smartwatch-not and entertainment watch. But people do mistake the design for an Apple Watch. It has a nice look! My wrist is small and it is a little big on it, but I really like it. You can see texts (but cannot answer them) and you can see and answer (if you have bluetooth) incoming calls. Guided breathing and coaching sessions. Timer (stop and countdown) and alarm. Weather, including extended forecasts. Reminders to move if you aren't on target to hit your goal. Calories burned. Miles and of course steps. You can also download songs onto it ( I have yet to do this) Its like a power packed motivator on your wrist!!!! I absolutely LOVE this watch! It does scratch easily, and I would recommend a protector purchase immediately.

title: decent watch for a decent price, please read
text: The watch is great for the price, easy to set up, various notification options available, but beware 2 things, the more things you enable on the watch, the shorter the battery life; my watch battery life went from 5 days to 2 days between charges as I enabled more useful notifications. The other thing to be aware of is, my watch's usb charger cable melted at the contact pins next to the magnets that attach to the watch. The magnets will attach to anything metal thats near by, they attached to my nail clippers while the other end was still plugged into the usb port. I can no longer charge my perfectly good, but dead, watch.

title: It's so close...

Turning battery saver off (Android) does help, but I disconnect multiple times daily still. Notifications stop, it can't update the temperature, or do much except track steps and read the time. *notifications don't show the source, like email or text, or group me, etc so you have to know the context. title: fun and productivity wrapped around my wrist
text: This watch is exactly what I hoped it would be. I used to have to carry my phone around with me in case coworkers needed to contact me which was often inconvenient. With this watch, I get all the notifications I need without the bulk of the phone. A pleasant surprise is the distance I can go from my phone and remain connected. I am still learning about it - finding exciting new ways to utilize it. It is fun and productivity wrapped around my wrist... can't go wrong with that.

title: You can't beat the price, it has a lot of utility and great battery life.
text: I'm honestly quite pleased with my watch, particularly considering its price and utility. It's as waterproof as I need it to be (I've taken it swimming and in and out of the shower). Its battery life is fantastic, it does everything I need it to do (send and receive text messages, remind me of things on my calendar, tell me how long I've been sleeping, how well I slept) and a lot of bonus things! I use the timer, the alarm, and the pedometer every day. I used to use some apps, but the pebble health feature made those unnecessary. The only features I would additionally like is a way to respond to my google chat messages, but I can't really complain, it was less than $100. I'm highly anticipating the next version of the pebble time when it has a heart rate monitor, until then I'm quite pleased with its functions.

title: B&W Pebble vs. Color Pebble Time.
text: I owned the earlier B&W Pebble smartwatch, but after a year the display became an unusable blur. I decided to take a chance and upgrade to the color Pebble Time smartwatch. The basic operations and apps are very similar, but the color display makes the watch face more fun. Furthermore, you've got to hand it to the Pebble folks. They've improved the basic firmware so it now includes many "must have" apps pre-loaded, such as: "find my phone," "phone ringer," "Music Boss," alarm, stopwatch, timer, weather, health, notifications and "send text." I just discovered it even contains a microphone so you can reply verbally to incoming messages. All this in a watch that is waterproof to 30 meters for under a hundred bucks! The color pebble Time doesn't last a full week on a charge like the old black and white version, however--more like four days. This is still light years beyond other smartwatches, though you don't get that gorgeous display available on the fancy rigs. At the reduced price, the Pebble Time is a real bargain.

title: A Wonderful, Functional Smart Watch
text: I purchased this watch primarily to use as a display device for my Dexcom G5 (a continuous glucose monitor). It works great for that purpose but I also got a great, functional smart watch and fitness tracker. This is NOT an Apple watch. I looked at those and while they are beautiful, they are expensive and not that durable. I wanted a watch that really functioned as watch, something that was always on, had solid battery life, and could withstand daily punishment from me. The Pebble Time is NOT a touchscreen device. But it is a waterproof (I've tested this thoroughly, spending all last week wearing it at the beach and in the ocean) and the battery life is great even with heavy use (getting several days out of it easily). I use this with my iPhone 6S and all the notifications, voice text response capabilities, and fitness capabilities work perfectly. I have replaced my FitBit with my Pebble because the Pebble system integrates nicely with Apple Health. If you know Pebble and understand what you're getting, this is a fantastic device. Definitely recommend it as a display device for anyone using the Dexcom G5 or G4 on Nightscout. For my diabetes management, this has been incredibly helpful.

title: Great purchase!!

I am 69 years old and our sight begins to deteriorate so I need a watch with large numbers, this is perfect for this. Some of the reviews complained about short battery life. Mine has lasted about 2 weeks and it only takes about 1.5 hours to recharge to 100%. There are 6 light intensity settings, I keep mine at the lowest setting witch works just fine for me unless I am outdoors in full sunlight, which is only once in a while. I just put it at max intensity and have no issues seeing the display. Others complained about not being accurate on Heart Beats Per Second or blood pressure. Why would you expect a $29 device to give you an accurate reading on these items, buy a high quality blood pressure device for 3-4 times the cost, your health depends on it. Others complained about the walking is not working or not accurate enough. Then spend the dollars on a higher priced device. Remember this only cost $29 and some change at the time of this review. I bought it to tell time on these tired eyes, and this it does in spades. I bought an extra charger and put it in my car just in case I need to charge it, cost $10. The wrist band is very soft and comfortable. Yes the instructions are way too small, you need a microscope to read them. But since I am not born with a chip implanted in my brain like my kids and grandkids are I am not too computer savvy so I only need to tell time I didn't need to read them, but yes the seller should rewrite them with larger print and provide a PDF for us.

If I put them in my snowpants pocket near my waist, it would continually cut out so I couldn't enjoy a full song. I don't have a pacemaker or any other electronic device on my person or near me, and the snowblower is a mechanical gas-powered device without bluetooth, so there's no real reason why the earbuds would be acting oddly under these circumstances. I can't wear them while mowing the lawn on my (gas-powered) riding lawnmower because they cut out all the time. Can't wear them while cleaning in my basement unless I am always in direct line-of-sight to my phone at all times. I haven't even tried using them while exercising but I anticipate another frustrating experience. It's too bad because they fit well, the sound is good, and the charging case is super well-designed and convenient. But I can't rely on them to deliver good sound continuously. I'll probably only use these at my desk (if possible -- haven't even tried that yet) and use my Soundcore bluetooth earbuds for all my other activities. Disappointing experience!

text: *Update* after trying to use these for a few days, I'm disappointed. They are great except that they won't stay in my ears. There's nothing to hold them in place. They are okay for emergency use, but only if I'm using just the right one and I'm laying on my left side so it stays in. I've got several versions of Samsung wireless earbuds. I get a new set about every other year. The case on these is about the size of two samsung charging cases put together. It's just massive. But it charged quickly and the wireless charging works just fine. I called my mother to test the call quality since she is the most discerning about my earbud call quality and she was impressed at the quality for the cost. My galaxy buds were a refurbished buy from Best Buy and she could never understand me when I used them (no one else really had a problem hearing me with them). The galaxy buds live has good sound and call quality, but very poor battery life and comfort in use. They always popped out of my ears if I smiled or laughed and they pushed against that little flap and caused pain. So far, these little things are doing pretty good. I have weird shaped ear canals so the left one didn't hold in very well (but it almost never does with any of these) but, the right one is holding in good. I'm not thrilled with the shape because it's hard to know where to line it up, but for the money, I'm sold.

I'm so frustrated that I can't find something like that without spending $200!! Crazy! I guess most people must buy these for working out, but some of us have other needs. title: Not great.
text: Update: I've been using these for about a month now. Bought two pairs and my wife has bow stopped using them because they fall out of her ear. Battery life is not what they said it is. Especially true if you are in the heat. I got two hours out of them before having to recharge. Below is my original review and still true. I have plenty of other headphones to compare to include wireless dre beats, wireless jaybirds and base, but don't have experience with off brands. I purchased two of these for my wife and I to mainly be a comm asset when participating in online meetings. The good: First, they did the intended purpose of sounding clear on the line and meeting participants heard me loud and clear. Amazing for the price...considering the fact that I almost bought the pair that I actually wanted at $185 x 2. Another great feature is the wireless charging which comes handy for us. Music came through better than dre beats, but worse than jaybirds with nice clear sound and decent base. The bad: My biggest gripe is how big and how much they stick out of your ear when wearing them. Its awkward to see it sticking out so far vs some of the others I have seen at the gym. Wouldn't be a big deal but the heaviness makes them slightly bounce when you run with them, therefore making them fall out. I tried all of the buds that came with them but didn't find a solid fit. My wife was even worse, they all either fell out of her ear or were way too big! I purchased an $8 set of new buds with wings and they worked a little better, but you have to pull them off every time you put the headphones back in the charger. Overall, I think I made a decent purchase for the price but with all the negatives probably wouldn't recommend to anyone. I like the sound, case and look, but the design features fall short vs some of the competition. I honestly didn't want them sticking out that far, but now I have to deal with it. Kind of looks and feels like I'm wearing a Bluetooth headset vs an Avenger's or Navy Seal communications piece.

title: FINALLY !!! Ear buds that WORK as promised
text: 1st off let me say these are my 5th or 6th try at getting great sound out of ear buds. I was thinking that it just wasn't doable. Ordered these earlier today and they showed up early evening, wow and wow. Went with white as I am tired of losing things in airplanes and gyms. Nice change. So, sound quality: WOW. I listen to a lot of Latin: Prince Royce, Romeo Santos, Aventura.... things with lots and lots of harmonies and mid range percussion, bongos and crazy things. To FINALLY get buds that bring out that myriad of sound is an answer to a prayer. Clear, crisp highs, clean drums and mid ranges, clear voice. The base is just right, very present but not overwhelming. Listening to Daddy Yankee Dura, holy crapioly, amazing percussion.... I feel like breaking into Zumba!!! I would say just about perfect sound. The best I have heard this side of my $1,500.00 Alpine Audio in my Nissan Z. I like that they are waterproof, not that I am going to go swimming with them in to test it, but still kind of cool. More than able to handle sweaty LA Fitness trips. Gotta love the wireless charging feature too. All this for $49.00 is CRAZY. So glad I kept trying and returning until I found these gems. I will be looking no further. My only suggestion would be to include Comply foam ear tips. That would be a huge win.

title: Overall very good, but come out of the ear too easily
text: Reviewing "TOZO T10 Bluetooth 5.3 Wireless Earbuds with Wireless Charging Case IPX8 Waterproof Stereo" I've had these Tozo headphones for about a year, and I use them almost daily. They sound great, charge well (I've had them for about a year), and have withstood endless sweating and even falling into water. The bad part is they are bulky and fall out of my ear unless I have a tight skullcap (warm hat) or sweatband covering them. I literally bought a sweatband (which I'd never use otherwise) to wear even in warm weather only for the sake of keeping these things from falling out of my ears. You can try different ear bud size attachments (yes, I know that), but I think it's the bulky design that just makes them want to pop out. I've never had this problem with any other headphone--at least not to this degree. When I run or ride without any head covering, I'm continually having to push them back in, or lick them a thousand times and push them in for a little longer lasting stick. But hey, they've fallen literally into water and survived, so I have to give them that. Overall, I would buy again, BUT I would also be open to looking for a different product.

If $30 earbuds are this good, why would anyone want to pay more for brand names? That's my thinking. I've been listening to You are the reason by Kodi Lee, Scott Calum and other AGT, BGT songs over and over to test the quality and compare on different earphones and speakers, and the sound quality of this product is really good. The base is deep, the stereo great. Simply great.

title: UPDATED Tough little buggers
text: UPDATE: I stopped using these because I got a different brand, but began using them when I left my others in my car. They don't stay in my ear as well as my other ones and hurt after a brief time. It doesn't hold a charge and keeps connecting & disconnecting out of nowhere. Issue from the water exposure 6 months later or just a "you get what you pay for" product? These stay in my ears pretty well and I'm usually only using one at a time so I can't really speak to the noise cancelation. I've worn it in the shower to keep listening to a lecture for school before. What really made me love these is that I accidentally washed and dried one that I left in my pocket. It still works! I thought for sure it would've crapped out but it's going strong. Would definitely recommend although I wish I had controls on the buds themselves. Small issue though.

text: I purchased these after trying a similar set in the same price range. The sound on these is quite good, and the positioning in the ears can further isolate the ambient noice. They have proven to be waterproof, and secure when placed firmly in the ears. The charging case can charge the ear buds at least three times. I had to remove one star because the range is a bit limited, and the battery life on each charge is pretty low, at about 3 hours of playback. However, at this price point, the sound is comparable to ear buds at three times the cost, so the battery and range issues can be somewhat forgiven.

But the battery life has deteriorated quickly, and now they only last a couple of hours, sometimes less, even on a full charge. I would be still be disappointed but really not mind that much if they at least lasted long enough to be able to charge during my lunch break, but since they can't, they are almost worthless to me - I have to keep another set of earbuds to switch to while these charge, and honestly, the other brand's battery lasts a full day so why would I use these. They are at best a backup pair that can be used in a pinch for a short while, which for $50 is absolutely ridiculous.

title: Lightweight, fast charge, easy to use, solid bluetooth earbuds

Couple that with the sleek charger case, which gives you multiple charges on the go in a short period of time, and it's really a no brainer. The size and weight of the earbuds are great.
