title: Tozo T6: a fine true wireless earbud for the price
text: The Tozo T6's are good "cheap" basic buds. They lack high-tech noise cancellation, pass through ambient sound, and some other features of top models. BUT, the T6's are OK/satisfactory for 90% of most peoples' needs (listening to music and taking calls, right?). When I'm planning to be in a situation where losing an earbud (or getting an earbud wet) is likely ( or whenever it would make me nervous to take "expensive" buds); I'll absolutely throw the T6's in my pocket "just in case" and leave my expensive buds safe at home. I have virtually no fear of losing a T6; for the cost of one "expensive" bud, I could lose multiple T6's (and I haven't actually lost one yet, only saying that T6's aren't a monthly rent payment). Music on the T6 not like sitting in symphony hall, but it's not "bad." People talking to me on the phone (at least when I'm in a reasonably quite space) can hear me well from my T6. Overall, FOR THE MONEY, a very good earbud! The buds you actually have with you, sound better than the buds you left at home!

I probably should have bought another pair of the T10s, but the T6s had pretty amazing specs, so I took a chance. First, the pros; AMAZING sound, noise isolation, fit, and sensitive fingerprint controls (no pressing). I have over ear Bose, and Beats, and these could stand against their sound quality any day. Now the cons: you can't roam far from the phone, computer or iPad you're connected to, or the bluetooth will drop you. In fact, if a butterfly farts in the amazon, these earbuds will drop their connection to your bluetooth device. The other stand-out con is battery life. I don't know if mine were defective, but they NEVER had the battery that I enjoyed with the T10s, and they seem to be getting worse. The case will hold a charge when stored for well over a week, but the buds last about four hours with music playing in them. If you're just wearing them at the gym for an hour or two, they're fine, but if you're wearing them to drown out office noise, you're going to be out of luck after lunch. I am considering handing these off to one of the younger people in my family who need a spare pair to use while their primary pair is charging. If TOZO comes out with a new model, I may wait to see if the folks reviewing it have the same issues. I'm actively looking for the old T10s in the meantime.

text: I originally never thought I’d own these.. I have several Apple products and try to buy other brands just so I don’t come across an an Apple fanatic (I'm actually somewhat critical of them).. I also always want to know if the grass is greener, I want to own the best gadgets regardless of who makes them :) I own Bose Soundsport free and a couple pairs of Zolo liberty plus. I also have used an Anker set with the wire between the buds. The AirPods, while I have experienced bugs over the years.. they are the most robust Bluetooth connection I’ve used. They literally NEVER cut out when using under normal conditions. I bought the first generation ones because I like that they are small and white, fits perfectly under a hair net that I have to wear in clean rooms for work. Can listen to my tunes and most people won’t even notice I’m wearing em. I have put dozens of yards of space between me and my phone, several tall metal machines that one would think should interfere with the connection. It amazes me how solid they are. Now, I won’t use these for working out as I sweat quite a bit and I’m certain they’ll fall right out. I think the Bose ones are the most secure for working out. Battery life is pretty good when they are new. After a year or two you will notice that it declines (based on my experience with the gen1 version). The battery case could definitely have more juice. When compared to the amount of charges you can get with the Zolo’s, puts the AirPods and the Bose to shame. People like to complain about the sound quality and sometimes about the lack of noise cancellation. But I find that they sound really good, granted I’m not really a sound snob.. easy to please.. IMO neither the Bose or the Zolo sound any better.

If you do want to do fancy things like skipping a song or going back or even adjust the volume, you have to memorize a series of long and short touches switching between right and left ear. title: Inexpensive but not well suited for swimming
text: These are inexpensive earbuds and advertised as waterproof, which pretty much sums up these. I bought these for aqua jogging for which they work fine because you don’t submerge them underwater, but because they are bluetooth, they will stop playing if your ears go underwater, so they are not good for swimming. Furthermore, you need to be within range of your phone kept by the poolside. It won’t work well with music playing from your cellular-plan capable watch, which is again because your watch would probably be submerged under water most of the time. It’s fine for aqua jogging at one end of the pool with my phone by the poolside, which is what I bought them and use them for. I use them instead of my airpods just in case they fall into the water. The design could be improved by adding a hook that goes around the ear to minimize the likelihood of them falling out. With aqua jogging, they mostly stay in place, but if you do any other water activity involving more head movement, they will almost certainly fall out, so even though they might be waterproof, you will still have to go fishing to the bottom for them.

title: Comparable with the Samsung Buds Plus- $123
text: These are equally good as more expensive Samsung earbuds! $123 Pros and cons in the comparison are: - S8 has slightly better bluetooth range - S8 sound mixing adds a bit more volume on the bass and high notes; Samsung equalizes across the timbres. - S8 is a tiny bit less snug, while also lighter. Overall it stays in the ear just as well. - S8 noise cancellation does help a bit; Samsung Buds Plus don't offer that. -S8 battery life seems a little shorter; still plenty. Overall, the S8 ties the Samsung user experience. While costing about 20% compared to Samsung.

title: Incredible value
text: This is my first pair of wireless earbuds, and my first thought is I wish I had not waited so long. They used to be all fairly pricey, so when I saw these for around $20 US I had to get them. The sound quality is amazingly good. You will want to tweak your source to fit these earbuds. I had my bass set very high and too much will (understandably) cause these to buzz as the bass tops out. But when you get it right, these will be very close to a nice pair of inexpensive earbuds. But it's the comfort and freedom from wires that's the big change for me. I can listen to these easily for their whole 5 hour charge time and not feel weary from either the sound or the weight of the earphones/headphones. It's also incredible to me to have a pause function available by just tapping on one of the earphones. Have a conversation, then just tap to start up the music again. I think these are for everyone, if you already have an expensive pair of wireless earbuds get these as a back up, and if like me you've never had wireless before, this is the perfect pair to start with

title: Absolutely great product
text: Great sound....easy to set up. Carry/charge case is very good quality.

title: Better than the price
text: These work and sound great. You sacrifice some of the low end bass and noise canceling of the more pricey brands, but these sound so much better than they should at this price. I also never had anyone on the other end of a phone conversation mention they couldn’t hear me or vice versa.

title: Works exceptionally well and at a bargain price
text: Short opinion: I would not hesitate to recommend this over the VERY expensive Apple product. For about a quarter or less of the cost of the Apple brand product, these simply work. I opted for the black version to use with an iPhone 7. Comes with several different size ear cups, so you can fit it just right. Works every time. Once you've paired this initially, it connects quickly every time. Even in the middle of a phone call, you can take the right earbud out of the case, and in a couple seconds, you can switch over. Like the Apple version, this has a charger/case for storage or recharge on the go. I've had these about four months now. I use these for phone calls, podcasts, and sometimes music. This week I had an opportunity to see how long a charge would last on a continuous phone call: One long call 2 hours 45 minutes, and then I heard a voice "battery low." I switched my call to speaker phone and continued my call. My wife uses the Apple Air Pod Pro--over $200. In my opinion these work just as well--certainly well enough for the price! One weakness maybe. Connecting to a computer with Bluetooth and using GoToMeeting, the connection is unreliable. It will start OK, but when someone else joins the meeting, it drops off. I can't fault it too much, though. My wife's Apple product does the same thing. GoToMeeting is really finicky about audio, though. Other Bluetooth products I've tried have been unreliable as well with that service. I've pretty much given up on wireless audio with online meetings, where nothing seems to work as well as a USB headset.

title: Not a great headset for phone calls.
text: This Bluetooth headset is definitely low-quality. It's alright when listening to music as long as your phone is in your pocket. But when making a phone call people on the other end cannot hear you. And the sound Cuts in and out. I would definitely look elsewhere for a Bluetooth headset.

title: Get what you pay for.
text: Good pair of noise cancelling earbuds. Worth what you pay for them. The fit is a little weird in the ear.

title: Wow! Finally.
text: This is my 4th set of blue tooth earbuds. I have finally found earbuds that really work well and do what they claim. Very good battery life along with exceptional range, comfort and fairly decent noise cancellation will make these my favorite set so far. I will most likely buy a second set of these- they are that good.

title: Good buy
text: Lived up to expectation! Sounds great! I've had a few friends complain about my sound but rarely. I love that it comes with multiple sizes rubber covers. They hold a great charge! The charging case is great too. I've had air pods users want them for the color.

title: TERRIBLE FOR STREAMING.....ALSO connection is NOT STABLE....breaks up repeatedly
text: They're comfortable and pair well but the connection breaks up repeatedly. When streaming a video the timing is off between the speaker's/singer's mouth moving, and when the sound actually arrives. Also, the directions are totally unreadable (light blue text against a white background and the letters are extremely small) and don't really explain what some alleged different lights mean. I say "alleged" because I have yet to see any of these lights. The case is supposed to have an indicator light but it doesn't. I'm considering returning them because of the repeated sound interruptions.

title: Awesome
text: Anker always makes great products. This is no exception love them.

title: Unimpressed
text: I was looking for a cheaper option for wireless headphones and came across these. They overall looked great and connected with no issues, however, they had zero bass when I listened to music and the mic quality was absolute garbage, so I can't use them at work. Returned after a week

title: Bad
text: I bought this as a gift and the receiver didn't like it at all. Terrible sound quality, it's going back.

title: Hard to justify $100 + more on any better
text: I've tried a couple of other wireless earbuds. These are my first fully wireless and they sound much better than any thing else I've tried. Seems I never have to charge the case, and I've never worn them long enough to run the individual earbuds down. They fit my ears comfortably for long periods. I won't soon be trying any others! The charging case is pretty bulky for carrying in my pocket. Otherwise perfect!

title: Good value for the price
text: I had no desire to spend a bunch of money on a pair of AirPods, but I needed a wireless solution. Took a chance on these and they work well with my iPhone. They pair up right away, sound quality is good, battery lasts a long time, and noise canceling is great. I was also surprised at how great the range is. I can leave my phone in one room and walk around the house and the bluetooth stays connected. I mostly use them for listening to audiobooks or music. When I use them for phone calls some people tell me the sound quality is fine, others tell me they can't hear me very well and I have to go back to my regular headphones. They pair to my MacBook with no problems but if I try to use them for a Zoom call the person I'm talking to tells me they can't hear me. I'm giving these 4 stars because they do what I bought them for, but others would probably rate them lower if they expected to use them to talk on the phone.

title: Ear buds keep falling out, don'tpair with two different phones
text: These earbuds are just not made for everyone. They easily fall out of your ears just talking. They don't automatically pair with one phone when both are turned on, let alone tow phones. Not what I need. I have a Bluetooth earpiece that costs $10 that pairs with my two phones better than these.

title: Poor sound long battery easy to pair
text: I thought I had hearing loss. Honestly, poor quality sound and dropped connectivity on and off all the time. Easy to pair, good battery life, poor sound.

title: So far so good...
text: After a few tries they seem to be of good quality. Let's see how long they last.

title: Great value for solid wireless earbuds
text: These have been great so far after a few weeks. Pair easily with iPhone. Great battery life. Good noise reduction with great sound quality. I like them as much as my wife’s AirPods

title: Heavy sweater? Not for you
text: Sound distorts. I use these while I am drumming and working out and after a month, max volume has already gone down in quality. Do not recommend

title: Good starter ear buds
text: Great product at a great price. Sounds great. Multiple tips for ears for different size ears

title: Difficulty pairing with computer
text: Both ear buds are their own devices so you have to pair both with your device. For whatever reason my computer also gives me like three different volume controls for these and whenever I first turn them on to use, the volume is always at full capacity so I'm scrambling to find the correct volume control for this thing. This may be a windows issue, idk. Very inconvenient none the less.

title: Awesome! So glad I got these vs. paying up the wazoo for a more expensive brand!
text: These are so dope, and a fraction of the price of some of the more "trendy" brands out there. They stay in my ears when working out (running/walking/jogging, weights, stretching, yoga, etc.) and, sometimes, I even forget that I'm wearing them. As far as noise cancellation goes, I have to take 1, or both, out of my ear(s) in order to uphold a conversation with someone. Otherwise, the other person's voice is too muffled and I often miss or don't understand what he/she is saying to me. So i'd say that's pretty good as far as blocking out noise goes. I have yet to run out of battery life with either the ear buds or charging case, and i've had them for about 3 weeks already. Sound comes in crystal clear when answering phone calls, and sounds good to the person on the other line, as well. I usually end up putting people on speaker phone a lot and I was told that I come across much better through the ear buds. Lastly, I don't have to get tangled up in cords anymore! 🙌 As a bike commuter and walker of my dog, these make a HUGE difference. 👍👍🙏

title: Doesn't work well
text: Now for the second time it does not connect as pairs only one at a time . The left now does not stay connected when the right is charging. Very disappointed. Very disappointed. Not good

title: good battery
text: Just expected better quality, have another pair of 20$ ones that do everything these do except in battery quality

title: Falls out of my ears
text: I tried every size of the ear adapters and none of them worked. They were always falling out of my ears. I don't like that the only way to turn them off is to put them in their charging case. I will be returning these as soon as my replacement pair comes.

title: Nice
text: Excellent for the price. Not for audiophiles. Battery life is top notch.

title: Good battery, okay audio, terrible audio desync
text: The battery life is good, lasts the full 8 hours of my shift without having to recharge. The audio quality is okay, decent to listen to but lacks bass and sounds very tinny at higher volumes. The thing that annoys me the most is the audio desync or delay. It's incredibly noticable while watching videos, half a second to a full second behind the speech in the video. Sometimes it catches up and is barely noticeable, other times it makes it unwatchable. Wouldn't be an issue if you're just listening to audio, but if you're watching videos, these will not work for you.

title: Great sound quality
text: These earbuds are so easy to use and take care of. The sound quality really blew me away when I first inserted them. I have hearing loss so this was a big plus for me. They charge up quickly and the charge last a long time. Highly recommend them.

title: Great for Conference Calls, Fine for Music
text: I use these primarily for my excessive meeting schedule via videoconference (Microsoft Teams). I end up wearing these for 6+ hours a day with no discomfort. Audio quality is great both ways. My wife has these, too, and I hear her loud and clear. If phone and conference calls are your primary use, these are excellent. For music, they are fine. They block out some noise, but are certainly not active noise canceling. Note the "noise canceling" in the produce description refers to blocking out ambient noise from the microphones during phone calls. Not blocking noise entering your ears like Sony or Bose. They are light on bass. For the price, I would still rate them good for music. If music is your primary use, these are fine but not excellent. I still use them around the yard and in the shop.

title: works great... if you can make it stay in your ear
text: I tried all sizes. they will only stay if you have no head movement. i was at the golf driving range and they kept on falling. I walk.. i'd be happy they just get loose and not fall, and they have fallen at least once. Lucky for me I catch it on my arm/sweater. I was cutting branches.. they fall! If it wasn't for that, I'd say it's a great product. Heck I clean my ears first to make sure no ear wax is there to make them slippery. Yeah, TMI but anything and everything to prevent a return and give the product the as much chance.

title: Not worth your money
text: Really don’t believe these are worth a whole lot. They don’t stay in my ears, And if something doesn’t stay in your ears it’s really not worth anything to you. I have Apple earbud pros and they stay in my ears just fine. But they’re 200 bucks. Really wish these were made better. And the sound quality was better to

title: Great for remote work
text: One of the better Bluetooth earbuds I have received. I was them for remote meetings. Holds battery for a very long time, good and clear microphone. Sometimes a little crackly. The biggest issue is getting it to switch blue tooth devices. You essentially have to shutdown one (computer) to get it to pair to another (phone). Generally not a problem unless I’m on a call all day and need to move between devices.

title: Keeps falling out of my ear.
text: These do not fit securely in my ear no matter which bud size I use. I’ve ready other reviews with the same complaint. The slightest move of my head will dislodge them from my ear. I wish they came with wing tips. Too bad because they sound great. The sound is very well balanced.

title: Ear buds no longer pair together
text: Up until recently I was in love with these headphones. I was recommending them to all of my friends because they worked AMAZINGLY. I could put them in and they would last an entire work day without needing to put them in the case to recharge. I am serious. A solid 8 or 9 hours without a low or dead battery. and the case holds enough power to recharge them so that i only have to recharge it once a work week so I don't have to worry about forgetting it each morning. it's been great! But then the earbuds stopped pairing to each other. They will pair (separately) to my device so i will get sound out of one ear bud at a time but never both ear buds at the same time. so if i am on a plane or in a situation where i might want to watch a movie or youtube video on my own... i can only listen with one ear bud. I have tried ALL of the tricks. i have tried resetting both ear buds individually. I have tried resetting them together. I have tried unpairing them from my device. I have tried letting them run dead... I have quite literally tried everything. I am really disheartened that after just 6 months, they are essentially one of those bluetooth headset people used to wear to take phone calls... not ear buds.

title: Terrible pairing function..
text: Average sound quality, the pairing function is terrible, if you have more that one device pairing with the headphones ...You have many problems to pair each time that you want to change beetwin them...

title: Good sound must speak loud for mic
text: Loved them only problem is the mic. I have to speak like the person is in another room for the person on the phone to hear.

title: No bass
text: I am a huge music lover. I listen to all kinds of it and for hours a day. The first song I listened to with these headphones was Pillowtalk by Zayn, which is a bass-heavy song. I immediately noticed there was no bass to speak of with these earbuds. That's just not acceptable for me, so I'm returning them.

title: Recommend
text: The battery life is great. I’ve read other reviews about sound quality and noise cancellation - I don’t seem to notice. They work for me.

title: Awesome.
text: Love these, but my kid stole them. We're good. He'll get more use than me.

title: Best headphones ever!
text: These are the BEST wireless headphone I have ever bought I will NEVER go to another brand EVER again

title: Very good sound
text: Easy to use, easy to pair, great sound, it comes 5 pairs of Ear Tips to choose the one that fits you better. Very good value for the price you pay.

title: Excellent sound
text: Update(year+ later) still working great, the only downside is that the individual earbuds no longer hold a charge as long as they use to...my left ear still seems to hold well, but the right ear doesn't make it more than 4 hours before needing to be recharged. But on a plus side the ability to pull one out and charge while on a call and no one noticing is pretty amazing. I'd been debating going full wireless. Finally decided on these since they were charged via USB C. So far the only complaint I have had been with the ear piece sizes...I just haven't figured out the right ones that fit my ears.

title: Amazing earbuds
text: Use these everyday, the battery life is what the box says and they do noise cancel some but nothing like earplugs or active cancelling.

title: Bogus charging cord.
text: Sound is great and long lasting battery too. But I don’t like the fact that the cord has to be the one that came with instead of a standard charging cord. Inconvenient.

title: What a mistake
text: I have given it a few days. Here is my review The sound quality is not too bad. I had AirPods and was looking for a cheaper alternative since My AirPods stopped working. The phone sound quality when taking a call is terrible. Staticky, the buds alternates back and forth the entire time I was on the phone. The ear buds have to be manually turned off or paused when taken out of my ears. The casing is ok. Lid is very loose and it’s worrisome that the buds would fall out. It holds along long charge. I would not be ordering them again and will return the earbuds. Not worth the money apent

title: Great fit for a variety of ear sizes!
text: Bought these for our daughter and she couldn't be happier. They hold a charge for a lot time and sound great. The cost is amazing too and we're huge Anker fans.

title: Started great but did not last even a month
text: These earplugs started great buy after less than a month they both worked out of sync...and the rattling noise began. Also..the battery started dying soon. Sad because i really like Anker

title: Quality product, comparable to AirPods.
text: Gift for my daughter. She loves them, they fit her ears well. I tried them and I like them better than my AirPods. The case is on the large side so they don’t easily fit in your pocket like AirPods.

title: Worth every penny
text: Started ok. After a few hour and adjustment to my Iphone the sound improve a lot. True enough is deserve a 4 star. Eric Clapton - wonderful tonight Love music with sting and bass n vocal

title: Great product, amazing customer service
text: Great sound quality on a set of buds that work great. The best part is the customer service and warranty though. 11 months after purchase I was having some issues with connection and the microphone on the left ear bud. I was bmed out because I loved them so much. But I reached out and they quickly sent a replacement. I will definitely be purchasing from them again!

title: Seem great so far
text: Had them for a month or more and seem great so far. The case and charger is compact and convient.

title: I don't need anything else
text: These are so good. For those saying that they are tinny sounding without any bass then you didn't lock them in your ear as the image on this website shows. If you insert them, push them in and move them upward once in your ear then they pretty much lock into place. One downfall is that you cannot pair these to multiple devices unless you are using it as 1 bud per device. For the price it's worth it. If I want these on a second device then I'll just buy another pair. Anker has quickly become an industry leading brand. I own some of their other headphones and they are very good. I also own several of their powerbanks. Their customer service has always been top notch. I couldn't be happier with my first pair of wireless ear buds. Lastly, the charging case where these sit in act as a charger even when it is not plugged in. You only plug in the charger to charge the base. Once you have done that then you can carry the base with the buds in it and they'll charge. This is way to cool. I cant recommend these enough!

title: Great product, customer service
text: This product is a great value and so far am very happy with sound and connectivity. After an initial problem and contacting customer service (which they actually responded over the Memorial Day Holiday) they had me reset and explained the bluetooth pairing principal. Working well and for the money the sound is pretty, pretty, pretty good! Update: even though I mentioned customer service previously, I must say they REALLY do stand behind their products and are very easy to contact and resolve any problems. A-1 company.

title: Sound doesn’t sync between headphones.
text: Unfortunately can only use one at a time as the sound echos (delays?) between sides. + lots of interference when using both. 2ndly: When making calls, the ‘R’ side pod is the only bud am able to be heard on. 3rdly: Range isn’t very far. Am only able to step 3ft away from device when using. And if you go around a corner or door forget it, connection drops. So, these are fine for listening to podcasts, using one at a time, if your device is close. But if you want to use both at once, or for calls, or need to be more than 3ft away from your device. These prob aren’t it.

title: Best I’ve used so far!
text: Way better than expected! I’ve always wanted airpod style earbuds but it doesn’t work with my ear shape and always fall out. Then I came across this and I gotta say it’s amazing. Fits perfect, sounds amazing, and good quality all around. Def recommend this product!

title: I would buy them again.
text: I recently purchased these true wireless ear buds and I love them I have had other earbuds but these are winners. Update now almost a year later I would still buy them again.

title: Definitely get your money's worth.
text: They sink right up to the phone, the battery life is a couple hours. The charger case charges them up nicely and fits in the pocket. The base isn't all that strong but I'm not getting a very tight seal with the cups provided. Upgrading to better tips would most likely improve the base but for the price I can't complain.

title: Won't sync, but good battery life
text: I have never been able to use both of them at the same time, the buds pair one at a time with blue tooth with no way to sync them? Sounds qualities are great, battery life is great. I will always trust Anker with that at least.

title: Looks good but has zero bass
text: These earphones have no bass at all and I mean nothing. This will get old quick.

title: Great for price
text: Wanted a back up pair, these do the trick. Happy with overall product. Good price.

title: Anker honors their product quality!
text: Update: Back to 5 stars. After leaving the review that the one earbud no longer worked they contacts me and sent a replacement overnight. So very grateful For a company that still honors all of their products. I still recommend Anker and use many of their items.

title: Responsive Company
text: I thought they were great, but left earbud is already crackling. Boo!! UPDATE: I posted an earlier review of my first set with the title “Left headphone (earbud) crackles.” Anker, the company that makes them, contacted me right off and send out a new set and thus far they work great. I do love the quality of sound on the earbuds and anyone on a call can hear me find. It is great they have adjustable earpieces as I have small ear canals. Well, anyway. If you have an issue with them, know the company cares about its product.

title: Sound was awesome
text: Loved the sound, the crispness of the talk and music. What I didn’t like was controlling the volume with my device and after changing the extra ear covers, they still fell out of my ears

title: Great earphone!
text: A great earphone, comfortable for an extended period of times used and lightweight. Battery is good both on the earphones and charging case, has three battery charging levels indicator while charging. The case is not too big, good size that fits in pockets good. Good clear sounds, good amount of bass and treble, voice call is good. Good for listening to music, phone calls, YouTube and news. Easy to paired once taking the earphone out of the case and connection is fast, good amount of distance coverage without been drop signals. Overall, a good earphone with good sounds, clear and easy pairing with good battery life. Good budget earphone compared to other competitors higher prices.

title: Apple? Forget em!
text: Sound quality is awesome. Very sturdy and the price is perfect!. Who needs those expensive ear buds when this is just as good! Fits great in my ears. Came with different size cushions just in case!

title: Great Value!
text: Sure beats the Apple ones for twice or more the money I bought for wife and daughter, great product, even dropped one immersed in sink water once and keeps working.

title: Excellent Quality Earbuds
text: The item was amazing, I've had lots of earbuds and this is the only set that allowed for me to use it through out my house. I could even walk to the mailbox and held the connection. I called in had an issue and Rochelle helped me so much, excellent customer service.

title: Started Out Fantastic
text: These were so awesome when I got them! I would have given 5+ stars if I could. Then one day they didn't turn off when I put them back in the case. I didn't know at first, I just knew I couldn't hear anything on my phone including calls. I was fidgeting with the phone as I walked past the closed case and heard everything coming from there. But even though I now knew the problem I couldn't stop it. So I ended up shutting off my blue tooth. That worked. When I turned it back on everything else synced right back up, my Fitbit, my car, but not these. It shows them available but won't connect. But they were great for a couple months.

title: Love love love 💕
text: Wish I would have ran into these sooner. Soooo good! I wasted my time and money on a pair of sony earbuds that cost more than double of what these cost and no where near the same sound quality. They are comfortable and the battery lasts my entire work day. Absolutely love and recommend to anyone looking for good quality earbuds.

title: Started Great.. but one week later...
text: My son loved these at first. He got some razzzing at school for not wearing apple-white ones, but he was cool with that. Until.. they would no longer pair together. At present he can only get sound out of one side or the other. He's tried resetting, repairing, etc. Hasn't tried support yet, so I'll update this if we fix it, otherwise, Amazon return policy here we come.

title: I Hate Them
text: So far, I hate them. 1) the cord to case is too short 2) You need a magnifying glass to read left from right 3) The stupid button sequences are ill defined… I tried to adjust them and suddenly my phone was calling my congressman from my contacts! WTF???

title: 2 major issues with the earbuds
text: I have this earbuds for more than a year. I had good experiences with the quality of sound and buttery. Meanwhile I had 2 major problems: 1- sometimes it disconnects from my laptop and takes more than an hour to recognize the Bluetooth and reconnect. I have to restart it more than 4-5 times till it gets fixed. 2- after using the earbuds I feel a pain in my right ear. I tried all of the sizes but none of them made the pain better.

title: Overall a great buy - a few cons below
text: I have SUPER tiny ears - and the smallest bud cover size isn't small enough, which I kind of expected. I do adjust them pretty often though, but I have this issue with all in ear headphones. I do wish they had more bass level and sometimes the battery life level seems like it's not consistent. I really like the case, the cord it comes with, and the overall design. I do think that you have to tilt the ends more toward your mouth to pick up good mic audio more than other brands on the market, but I'm ok with doing so. The noise cancellation is a huge plus, and I feel like they're a great buy for the cost. I do alternate them with my Sennheiser over ear headphones because I work a lot/am constantly on calls and listening to music. I charge the case about twice a week, but I haven't had it die so far. I do wish the coating on the headphones was a bit more textured and they had worked in a way to control volume from them though.

title: high pitch
text: I should have read the reviews that complain about high pitch sound that's coming out from these earbuds. It's impossible to even talk (or listen to people talk) on the phone for longer than 10-15 minutes without having ears hurt and migraines. These really have no bass in them and this company has no app to control sound issues either.

title: so far so good
text: Fit is excellent - sound great - battery life much better then iPods

title: Solid earbuds. Surprising long range.
text: Sounds great, stays in ear and easy to pair with my iPhone. 👍🏼 I was 100’ away from my phone before the sound cut out.

title: Fer listen'n to music and podcast
text: I wanted to like these. They just don't fit in my ears and they don't stay in just sitting still. I couldn't imagine moving around with them. Back to Amazon they go.

title: Not the quality I expect from Anker.
text: Sound quality is ok. Not great. If the microphones weren't so terrible, I would probably have kept this. Noise cancellation during calls is abysmal. So you won't be using these to talk to people unless you are in a silent bank vault. The case on mine was apparently defective. It doesn't stay open and just flaps closed unless I keep my finger in the hinge. I'm not a huge fan of the knockoff airpods look, but I could have gotten over that if it wasn't for the other shortcomings. Usually I'm a fan of Anker products. But these definitely didn't impress me.

title: Worth the purchase
text: I do enjoy these earbuds. They are quite comfortable and they fall out when I am working out.

title: My everyday audiobook earbuds
text: The best sounding wireless earbuds I had for under $50. Works independently, easy to pair, easy to play/pause. Long battery life, now I use this for my audiobook every day, 6 hours a day without ear pain, unlike those expensive one I had.

title: Poor quality
text: The earphones stopped working in the first 45days. It’s a poor built product

title: Excellent value for phone calls but lacks booming bass
text: I've had issues with every pair of ear buds I've ever tried that I could afford except for these. The sound is clear and crisp, perhaps lacking a bit in bass but frankly I need these for phone calls not intended for listening to music. Anker makes good, if not great, products and gives you tremendous value for the money. The only reason for the 4 in sound is lack of pulsing base, the battery life is absolutely amazing. Another solid Anker product.

title: Very nicely made and work well
text: I was looking for a 'headset' replacement so I decided to try a set of ear buds with a mic instead to see how that would work. In my case, these do not make a good replacement for a headset. The 'head' sound is far too annoying as I suspected. For making general calls and listening to music and videos, these work very well. The pairing process was painless, the sound quality excellent and the charging case where you magnetically snap the buds into is nicely made and seems to be very high quality. Good job Anker, you continually impress me with your products.

title: Great sound quality!
text: They sound really nice! They have good range too. I haven't listened for extended periods yet, couple hours maybe, so can't say I've tested the battery life. Fir the money, I'm happy.

title: Not worth more than $20.
text: People kept on complaining about my mic that they couldn’t hear me properly. It doesn’t connect automatically to previously connected devices. No bass at all. I’m very happy with jabra 75t.

title: Very good for phone calls.
text: I bought these earbuds primarily for phone calls, and for that purpose, I can say that they are exceptional. Callers sound loud and clear, and they tell me that I sound fine on their end as well. I also tried listening to music with them, and while they do sound fine (I'm no audiophile), I have a pair of Bluetooth over-the-ear headphones that are far superior for music (immersiveness, bass, richness of sound, etc.) - link below. These buds paired easily with my phone (Galaxy S20), and I haven't had any issues with them disconnecting accidentally, and they reconnect instantly when I remove them from their case. I haven't tested the battery life to the max, but I have been in online meetings or conference calls that have lasted 3+ hours, and the buds still reported the battery charge as "high" (there's a convenient little voice that gently tells you the battery status of each bud in each ear). text: I bought these headphones as a cheaper alternative to a more robust pair of wireless headphones, like the pixel buds or airpods. My main gripe is the in-ear feel. They encompass your whole ear canal with sweaty, grippy plastic. The bad kind. Like the kind that makes it really hard to talk while wearing them, or when you move you hear a muffled rumpling with every step. I personally can't stand that and would prefer a more open ear feel, but that's just me. Just be aware of what you are buying, I find it hard to take calls wearing these as my voice seems to reverberate all throughout my head. I keep them in my bedroom, where, if I want to doze off to some tunes they provide a decent option. The sound is pretty great for the cost of these things too... I would put them equal to my JBL tuned or Harmann tuned earbuds crisp clear, and ample low end for casual listening, the fit is quite good at passive noise exclusion as well. UPDATE: I own both the Soundcore Life P2 and the Soundcore Liberty Air 2 headsets, and I have to honestly say that I prefer the sound quality and comfort of the less expensive Soundcore Life P2 headphones. The essential issue is that the Liberty Air 2 earphones attempt to create a channel of air between your eardrum and the driver, the theory being that with no leaks the sound will be truer, but instead what happens is that the sound is muted and dull because in order to seat the headphones securely the channel of air requires a negative pressure, otherwise they fall out. The design of the Life P2 earphones appears not depend on this suction tactic to stay put, and thusly the driver isn't impacted, and the sound quality stays the same every time you put them in your ear. A year on from my initial purchase and the Soundcore Life P2 earphones are still my favourite Bluetooth device.

title: Great battery life, great price point
text: I bought these because my old model of Bluetooth earbuds gave up the ghost – the design where the two buds are connected through a single wire allowed for the wire to fail and I lost all treble in one ear. I was hesitant to go with the "airpod" design due to fear that they'd fall out during exercise and I'd lose them. I can't say for running yet, but they seem to fit plenty well for exercise. I've taken them on a 5 hour bike ride, no concerns about losing them, and the battery was going strong the whole time (at full volume). My old earbuds by comparison only got about 3 hours of battery life. They come with a variety of rubber tip sizes, I'd recommend that you use the smallest that will fit without falling out. They might have quality control issues. The first set I ordered would not pair together, no matter how many factory resets I performed. Returned them for a replacement and they've been working flawlessly. So if you have any pairing issues, get a replacement. I've read a few reviews that complain about the design of the push button, causing them to press into their ear in an uncomfortable manner. First, it sounds like they might be using too large of a tip. Second, I simply hold the earbud in place with my thumb and middle finger while pressing the button with my index finger. No discomfort. Update: 2 years in and these still work flawlessly. I have dropped them while cycling, crashed while cycling, they're scuffed and scraped - but they still sound great and have no issues. I use them anywhere from 2-6 hours a day and the battery life is like new. Update: Alright, after 2 years of daily use for 1-6hrs a day, many drops and impacts, and rainy runs/bike rides, the treble driver in the right ear finally failed. I placed a new order immediately for a $20 refurbished pair, and they're like new. I'd say that's a more than acceptable lifespan for some earbuds!

title: Quality for the price
text: The headphones themselves are nice. They pair easily, and can easily use one or the other, or both. They pair automatically with the last device upon pulling them out of the case. You can easily go from pairing both, to one, by putting the other back into the case. The earbuds themselves are made well and the recharge case is nice and recharges plenty of times. I typically go about two weeks between case recharges. They sound good, but not studio quality or anything. If you're in an office and want some music in the background they work excellent. I find that as I move frequently, they often feel like they are going to fall out and I have to continuously reposition them in my ears. The biggest issue though is that I find these to be incredibly uncomfortable in my ears after an hour or more. I've tried all the different ear pieces on both, and they just get annoying after a period of time. I'm not sure if this is a personal issue due to my ears, or by the nature of true wireless buds themselves. However, I use wired earbuds and have zero issues wearing them almost the entire working day, sometimes for three+ hours without any pain in my ears. I believe the discomfort comes from the weight of the battery, bluetooth, etc, tech, all crammed into a tiny earbud and the weight of that resting solely on your ear canal. Wired buds don't have nearly as much weight to them. If you can overlook that or know that isn't a bother to you, I would definitely recommend them.

title: Its a great for the money
text: First off, I have decent Sennheiser and Sony headphones and I like to think I know what I am talking about but not really. I am not an audiophile. I got this for my job after hours of closing. These earbuds have excellent noise cancellation. Also, I'd like to note, there is no noise cancelation it's just the side effect of sticking these in your ear. It's really hard for me to hear anything while playing music with both earbuds in at the same time. They sound actually really good for 40$ at the time of purchase(it's currently 50 right now). They have decent bass not, unlike Raycons which is completely bass and destroys mids and especially the highs. There is nothing to complain about except the one weird quirk. The buttons force activation force is crazy high. You push the button on either bud and it registers but you have to push in the bud deeper in your ear. It's not a problem for me as I do not skip songs often or pause it. I truly believe that these earbuds are an awesome affordable gift you can get for someone during the holidays and the person will actually use it and not throw away. Considering these 210$ cheaper then the industry standard apple earbuds these things are killer for the money and I like them a lot. I would buy again if I lost it or a gift for someone during Christmas or any gift-giving holiday. 8/10 -1pt reduction for the button force and -1pt for missing the ability of using the microphones to hear what is going around you without either pausing it or taking one ear out.

title: Great all around ear buds!
text: Really love these! Sound quality and low end punch is good for the cost. Almost perfect all purpose ear buds. Several fitment adjustment ear pieces help you get a good fit. They have stayed in during walks and runs well with only minor adjustments and neither has fallen out so far. Works great with either L or R stand alone or both in atthe same time. Definitely great bang for buck on these. I've had these for around a year now and they are still going strong. Actually buying a second pair today to use for work. There are only two l areas for improvement that would make these a solid 5 star for me. The ability to connect multiple devices at once without re-pairing.(which is why I am buying another pair, got tired of swapping) and the ability to do a triple press or an extra long hold to raise or lower volume directly from the units. Fortunately it looks like the Bixby software interface has improved over the S9+ and volume can now be controlled via the voice assistant activation even while the device locked now on the S20. Even with out those two capabilities I'd buy these repeatedly. Battery life has been great. Probably still getting 5-6 hours even after a year of use. I like the overall setup and features of these even with the physical buttons. A lot of the other newer versions have a different control layout and do not have the ability to maximize control from the ear buds. These have single press play/pause double press to manage track and long press for voice assistant. This setup seems to be as good as it gets for control options and my activities.

title: Satisfied and Happy Customer (but read this first)!
text: When I listened to the ear buds for the first time, I was a little disappointed. The music sounded what I can only describe as distant. The frequency range from top to bottom was, in my opinion, somewhat thin. The first thing I did was go to the equalizer function on my iPhone and experimented with various presets. I found one I really liked and can honestly say that the sound was much improved, but still not entirely satisfactory. Now, for my most important discovery. As an average sized guy, I always assumed that I’d have an average sized ear canal. Boy, was I wrong! I went to the next size smaller bud and, holy cow, it was a whole new listening experience! The soundstage was greatly improved, I could hear all frequencies clearly, the bass was punchy, but balanced and the highs and mids shone through beautifully. Now, I am an extremely happy customer and to think that the difference came from a bud that was less than a millimeter smaller than the original. Amazing! As a former professional musician and headphone fanatic, I was thrilled that I wasn’t going to have to send them back. Be sure to experiment with the various sized buds and don’t forget to play around with a variety of EQ settings. It made all the difference for me. Great product! Great sound (finally)!

Like just about any Bluetooth device, when the battery starts to get below 50%, there is an echo, but this is not unique to these earbuds. The good news is that the battery lasts through multiple calls, back-to-back if necessary, and they seem to charge very quickly in the charger/storage container. The noise canceling is OK, but not great, for instance, if outside with a little wind, but not bad for indoors. The biggest problem I have with them is that I can't get them to stay in my ear if I'm moving around much at all. I've tried just about every different ear bud that come with them, which are several, and they always work out of my ear when I'm moving around. A second problem is that the button to hang up is right where I naturally put my fingers on the ear bud to reposition them securely in my ear and if I'm not extremely careful, I accidentally hang up the call. This happened 3 or 4 times when I first started using them but I've learned to carefully grab the sides of the earbud in a pinch-type grip to reposition them in my ear. I've tried wearing them on my daily 2 mile walk and I have to push them back in my ears constantly throughout the walk. They just don't stay in very well. I don't know if it's my ears or these ear buds. Overall, they meet my primary needs in my office, on video calls, so I'm fairly satisfied with them given the reasonable price.

title: Excellent Performance at a fantastic price point
text: I purchased these earbuds in December and I have to say that I am very impressed with the overall sound quality and performance considering the $50 price point. For the money, I don't believe that you can find a better pair of wireless earbuds in terms of sound reproduction, fit, and overall quality. Sure, I could have paid more for Apple earbuds but the marginal increase in performance is not worth the extra cost. The pairing is simple, steady, and reliable. Battery life is about 3 hours on a single charge when I listen to music, which is on par with other earbuds and what I'd expect from a device that I wear at the gym and for short periods of time. Midrange and highs are good (letter grade = B+), but overall bass performance is decent (letter grade B-) which really is as expected. I am not sure how you can engineer solid bass performance into an earbud, so my expectations are modest and given that, the Anker product is a success. My thoughts on overall sound quality are not curved to reflect earbuds as a class, but rather what this device sounds like in reference to any audio reproduction. I have sampled Beats and Apple earbuds and honestly, none of them can replace true over the ear headphones, but that is not their intended purpose just as earphones cannot replicate the sound of reference speakers. Calls are clear and the microphones do a great job reducing background noise (letter grade = A-). In short - I strongly recommend this product and don't believe that anyone would have any reason to be disappointed with the purchase of this product. In short - This is an excellent product with very good sound, solid build, easy Bluetooth pairing, comfortable to wear, and nice quality. You could pay more, but why?

They used to make CD players for Pro DJs which would advance read a few seconds in to a track and play them basically in "delay" so that if the decks were jostled at all, it wouldn't matter because the laser had already read further in to the track and the computer was programmed to auto correct the skip, thereby effectively eliminating skipping on non severely damaged CDs. Maybe there was another way, but I couldn’t find anything online to say otherwise. - the carrying case is too large! They are suppose to go into standby mode and not use up battery, not the case! When I went to use them they were completely dead. Overall NOT worth $200+. Don’t waist you money unless $200 chump change or something, then maybe waste your $

text: I wear glasses, and these fit comfortably over my ears and frames. title: My perfect…
text: As you know, these are wireless earbuds. They are not wired audiophile headsets on an amplifier. This may seem obvious, but some folks like to take reviews as opportunities to share their “vast” knowledge of what they think earbuds are supposed to sound like. After buying many wireless earbuds specifically for working out and running, these are my perfect set. First, sound quality…. Many of the sets I’ve used can handle sound on varying levels, but start to show distortion in the lower bass levels. These are solid. I need some thumps to motivate my lifts and footfalls. This gives me what I need without sacrificing midrange and detail. Secondly, and this is an enormous one, security…. They sit securely in my ear and the hooks hold on appropriately. I have no worries at all of losing these at whatever activity I perform. Third, comfort…. They are light, tight, and all around alright. I don’t experience fatigue wearing these at all so far. Finally, functionality…. This one’s for the folks who compare these with wired headsets. These offer super quick connections to Apple devices. Within minutes I could use my Powerbeats Pros with my iPad, iPhone, and Apple Watch. I can receive calls well through these with good call quality. I can use Siri easily with these as well. I didn’t want these for the greatest sound quality available. I wanted these for the best sound quality for wireless, workout earbuds. Again, these are my perfect set. Drawbacks? Yes, a few. A lack of a wireless charging case was an oversight that definitely shows the age of these earbuds. It’s slightly inconvenient as compared to my other devices that can charge wirelessly; however, the hours of charge and the additional charge from the case helps to mitigate the inconvenience. Also the price tag. It’s really a good product, so I get it, but I feel like the price tag is more about exclusivity and less about a fair price for the type of technology offered. On the other hand, my wife bought me these and I’ve been like a kid at a candy store since I received them… Folks they are good and if you are getting them for sound, security, comfort, and functionality, you won’t be disappointed.

title: Poor Quality
text: Right headphone stopped charging 2 months after my purchase. Now I have to play the troubleshooting game with Apple customer service.

title: Disappointing
text: I had high expectations for the Powerbeats Pro, and have ended up highly disappointed. Fit If there's one good thing I can say about the Powerbeats Pro, is that they don't fall off like AirPods, EarPods and most wireless and wired ear buds do. The Powerbeats Pro come with four pairs of ear tips in different sizes. Too bad none of them actually fit my ears. I wish Apple would just make their current AirPods with an ear hook to prevent them from falling off our ears. Anyway, the ear tips included with the Powerbeats resulted in either flat out pain or discomfort. After trying out all four pairs of ear tips, I ended up going back to the medium ones that come installed out of the box. Sound Sound quality in ear buds is directly related to their fit and how well that fit can create a seal. Needless to say that I cannot get good sound with the ear tips that don't cause me pain, and I can't get good sound quality for too long with the painful ear tips. The end result is ear buds that sound like the cheapest earphones you can buy, except that the Powerbeats are not cheap at all. Battery life If the Powerbeats Pro are supposed to have better battery life than the AirPods, I seriously don't want to imagine how awful the AirPods can be. The Powerbeats Pro can't even stand a whole day without needing to recharge, and that's regardless of whether you use them a lot throughout the day or barely at all. Yes, even in Standby these ear buds suck a lot of battery. Don't forget to take the oversized case with you, because you are definitely going to need it before you come back home.. Pairing Don't be fooled by the super quick and simple iPhone pairing process the first time you use the ear buds. If their batteries reach near 0%, the ear buds lose their pairing and you have to re-pair them by long pressing the pairing button on the case. I'm seriously debating whether or not to return these ear buds. They are not worth the money I paid for them. I'm already talking to people I know against buying them.

title: Ok, for Android
text: I bought these last December and use them 8 hours daily at work (mostly podcasts). Battery still lasts about 8 hours, which is notable. These pair much better with iPhone, interaction with siri, etc. With my android, it disconnects about every 4 hours (for no apparent reason) and I have to repair it. Not a huge deal, but a little annoying. Never did try the Beats App on the playstore, but lots of bad reviews there. They rest nicely in the ears...I often forget which ear it's in if I have to press the pause button. Never had one fall out, and a little light rain is no problem for them. A little expensive, yes...but, for me, well worth the cost.

title: Garbage
text: They are the absolute worst. Biggest problem is that, while they'll pair with your phone after some fiddling, they are unreliable - the left and right buds frequently lose pairing with each other. When this happens it creates strange sounds and gaps and means you have to stop what you're doing to try to get them paired again. Try doing that in the rain when you're out running. So I gave up using them in both ears, meaning they're not at all suitable for music. I had let the return period run out, so I'm stuck with them, so now I only use them one at a time and only for phone calls and podcasts, although even for that, the max volume is variable and is often not adequate. The microphone doesn't work consistently either. Batteries don't last long on a full charge after the first month or so (maybe 30 minutes). Sound is only so-so when they do work. Crappy workmanship - one of the earbuds on mine falls apart repeatedly, and the silicone seal doesn't seat right so it's for sure they're not waterproof. Frankly, I have a couple of pairs of generic-brand totally wireless earbuds that cost about $30 or less (with coupons) from Amazon that work and sound much better and are more predictable about pairing, and they stay connected and hold a charge for a decent amount of time. Another big problem is that the manufacturer doesn't seem to feel any need to distinguish among different models or updates/versions of this product. Prices online range from about $80 to $250 with no clear distinction among them to explain the differences or why the prices are different - they're all called just "Powerbeats Pro Wireless Earphones".

text: Not impressed at all.. I'm on my second pair of Apple Airpods and have used them almost exclusively for the gym. Sadly after about 14 months my first pair was shot. Not willing to see what Apple could do I went ahead and purchased a second pair, this time careful not to throw them back in the charging dock immediately after each workout. Well after about six months now I've started to experience the same issue I had with my first pair... Which lead me to bite the bullet and pay through the nose to get these water-resistant Beats wireless headphones... As soon as I fired up Spotify I could not believe how bland the sound was.. Wow, paying $100 more for these I foolishly believed the Beats moniker would at least have a slight upgrade over the Airpods but nope, not to my ears..Listening to Podcasts sounded exactly like Airpods too.... All that said, I realize I'm a slave to Apple so am willing to pay the $$$ for what is often an inferior product just to stay in their eco system.. So it's on me... I just hope I don't have any issues with sweat degradation and if that turns out to be the case then (gulp) the price will be less cutting.

title: Avoid the reviews, buy the product
text: Reviewing after clocking 40 miles, 30 days of use. I spent hours searching for a earpiece which won’t keep falling off my ear during my outdoor and treadmill runs. I tend to focus on listening to my body while long distance running but felt the need for music during my speed workouts, purely for motivation. After reading the bad reviews, I was doubtful if this Device will meet my requirements but then I decided to give it a try and not get influenced by the bad reviewers. The battery lasts long enough and you don’t need to charge often. One full charge gives 2 weeks of full use. The device doesn’t slide into the ear and the video clip on detail page is misleading. It does take a bit of manual adjustment to tuck it nicely in your ears but once it does, it stays there. Speed workouts or long distance, I never had any issues with the fit. You also get different soft buds to perfect it with your ear hole. The volume buttons on the device works well but the change button is a hit and miss. Sometimes it pauses and sometime it changes the song but the mechanics of single and double click is mostly faulty especially when you are running. While walking or static it tends to be more accurate as it reads your inputs from finger with more stability. The connectivity is simply and seamless, you open the box, connects to your iPhone automatically (except the first attempt when you manually connect the Bluetooth). Lastly, the Bluetooth range is adequate but not great. I see the sound break as I move away from phone but no issues upto ~20ft. All in all, I am very happy with this purchase and worth the price.

text: If you lead an active lifestyle, these are king. Only these have independent rocker button volume controls in each side; the newer Beats Fit have awkward single button volume control which is awful. I enjoy these so much, I bought a second set. For running outdoors, I use Shokz (formerly Aftershokz) Open Move and their newest premium model since they are bone conduction. But for treadmill, weight training, use in a stadium, a loud gym, these are wonderful. I do not like active noise cancelling headphones as it’s a battery drain and, frankly, you need to hear someone screaming and sirens. These have no ANC, but have four ear insert choices to keep sound essentially out. Nothing will top these genuine full ear hooks to keep your devices in your ears when you are sweating, hiking, bodybuilding, driving your car (unilateral), hitting golf balls and baseballs, this is the beast.

text: I wanted wireless headphones mostly for running, but also to use casually for conference calls and listening to music/podcasts. From the outset I assumed the Powerbeats would be the best for me and got those. While they are very good, it didn't blow me away. It wasn't so much better than the $30 bluetooth headphones I got 3 years ago. I also struggled to get a good fit in my one ear. What made me send it back though, was that it is just too bulky. The carrying case is huge and even the earphones without the case are big, and I didn't just want to put the headphones without the case in my denim pockets, as they have protrusions that might get damaged or break off. Bottom line, you can't just keep them in your pockets "just in case". Every time you want to take it somewhere you have to make space for it somewhere. So I got the Airpods. I was very skeptical that: 1. They would fall out when running 2. They would not survive the sweat I generate in the Atlanta summer during 13 miles jogs I watched some YouTube videos testing the Airpods water tolerance and I was surprised that people reported them fully functional after a wash/dry cycle (obviously not recommended). I pulled the trigger and bought it and am happy to report that they work perfectly for running. The Airpods' sound is good (not quite as great as the Powerbeats), and they don't fall out at all while running. I thought I'd might need an after market silicone casing or ear hook, but found I didn't need it. Overall, the Powerbeats are great product, but the Airpods won me over due to their portability and the fact that I can carry them on me all the time.

title: Good, not great - updated
text: These are ok. The sound quality is good, not great. Probably as good as you can expect from true wireless earbuds. My biggest complaint is that you cannot tell if the earbuds are charging. My left earbud will not charge unless it is seated just so. I wiggle it into position, but cannot tell if it is charging or not until the next time I go to use it. 50% of the time my left earbud is dead and I have to put it back in the case and hope for the best next time I want to use it. I should have returned them right away. Updated - after three months I would recommend you stay away from these. When I first purchased these I had intermittent connection or charging issues with the left earbud. Now the right one only connects 50% of the time. I am using these in an office environment, so they are not really subject to abuse, just going in and out of the case on a daily basis. If I want to use these for a Zoom meeting, I have to pop them out of the case 5 minutes early to make sure they pair. If not, back in the case and try again 20 seconds later, repeat as necessary.

title: Best wireless earbuds I've ever had
text: Like many other women in this comment section, I've been looking for a pair of wireless earbuds that do not slip out of my ears on a long run, in a heavy sweat. These are the fifth pair I've tried over the last two years, and they're the only set I've ever had that stay in no matter how far I run and how much I sweat, and as a bonus, the sound is incredible. They're expensive but worth it. Incredibly easy to set up and have had no technical difficulties. Only drawback is that you can't pair them with any device unless they're in the case, so just remember to bring the case with you in the car in case you need to re-pair before a run.

title: Great earbuds for active individual

title: My experience
text: I will be totally honest, these things gave me a really hard time out of the box with pairing. I spent about 2 hours trying to figure out how they work. I even started contacting customer support within the first 20 minutes of unboxing. Every time I would go to pair, it would connect, until I went to play music, it would drop. No idea why it did that. THAT being said... I have had no issues with these at all since. I pair them to my fire TV, my MacBook Pro, my iPhone, as well as my Mighty Vibe that I use for workouts (check out my review for that, it's like a wireless iPod shuffle). Some people I read on here talk about the music quality being poor, but I guess I'm not from LA and work in a music studio, so I thin the sound is what I would hope for from any of my music devices. If you are worried at all about these falling out of your ears (I also had trauma from the skull candies before I decided to spend big boy amounts of money on my earphones, which would constantly fall out) THESE WILL NEVER AND COULD NEVER FALL OUT, unless you somehow broke them or you have elephantiasis of the ears. I won't wear these things for more than an hour and a half to two hours, because I just want my ear canal to breathe a little every once in a while and it can get slightly uncomfortable (as would any other earphone). I use these for runs, and they are great! I don't have to hear my terrible heavy breathing, and with a Spotify subscription, these earphones, and the Mighty Vibe music player, I have already lost about 10 pounds in the last 3 weeks. I also prefer to use these when in lecture with my college over zoom sessions. I bought the moss colored ones, and if you are at all like me and don't really like the idea that the beats symbol is too gold colored, don't even trip. They don't really show as super bright gold, and no one would see the gold in your ear anyway. Hope this helped you! :)

title: Great headphones!
text: These are great. I’m a runner- and I like the fact that it’s completely cordless! Also- on mornings is dark outside- I can take just 1... and feel safe Bc they work with both or one.... also, they are easy to control Bc both sides have a button you can push or volume control. Can also up or lower the sound in either ear. The only thing I felt was cut short- was the bass. I had beats3 before these. Those had a lot of good bass. These are good but if I have to suggest a change- I’d say allow users to change the bass or treble etc. so if someone wants it more bass they can do it. Apart from that they are good. They stay in place as I run and feel comfy. The ones I got were ivory. I’m wearing white sunglasses in the photo. You can see the difference in those vs the earbuds. They are ivory but a pretty ivory. I wanted white originally but these don’t come in white. So ivory was next best. They’re fine as that color. Def stand out more than the other colors they have. Get them. Oh and the battery life is also great. U pull them out of the case and they’re fully charged for days...!! And when you pop the lid ope - your phone lights up - and it shows you the percentage of battery life. Super handy. Overall I give a 4 out of 5.

title: Amazon Renewed and got Screwed
text: [[VIDEOID:b779bafe29b2fdc9c08e29ebc78a4a6b]] These sound amazing I'm sure - just not the defective pair I bought through Amazon renew. They were still close to $200. When I paired them and went for a run I wasn't that impressed. They sounded good - not great. Two months in, I'm out on a run and the left bud suddenly glitches and for the next few minutes I experience what non defective beats sound like - Incredible! I've had to "forget device" and re-pair them several times because the left one will not work sometimes when I put them in. The battery life is great - I work 11 hour shifts Monday - Friday and use them to communicate with Dispatch or listen to music and they last all day. They were returned and registered under someone else’s name when I bought them and I should’ve sent them back. Will probably buy another pair eventually but not through Renew. Update: A few months in, a full charge lasts about 6 hours which isn't bad , they still charge quickly. The sound quality doesn't live up to the hype. I'm hoping the new pair I bought won't have the issues. NEW PAIR UPDATE: I’m so disappointed with the Max volume. I use an iPhone 11 Pro, so it’s not my phone… They’re not loud enough. They’re great for running, charge quickly, last for hours but at $200/pair I don’t understand why their max volume isn’t higher. They’re nice but they’re not worth the cost for that reason alone. UPDATE: I now own 5 pairs of these ,3 work. The oldest pair (Less than a year) only the left one will now connect. ALL OF THEM have THE EXACT SAME FLAW. The left head phone will cut in at times- the sound is amazing when this happens. I listen to a lot of reggae, which has percussion instruments in the background. I've heard a awwpercussion, in songs I've listened to for years, that I never heard before - when both head phones are working as they should. I've read that Beats are currently being sued and this is one of the reasons, along with not holding charge in one ear piece (which is exactly what happened to 2 pairs)

title: Think Avatar
text: You know how in the Avatar movies the people, animals, and plants connect to each other so easily? That is how these Beats connect to the iPhone. I have an iPhone 14 Pro Max, and the connection with these earphones was perfect and instantaneous. I have a set of AirPods Pro which also connect the same way. Seamless. However, like many of this style, they are not always comfortable or if I'm really busy (cleaning house and bending over the bathtub for instance) they can feel like they are going to fall out. I needed something behind the ear so that I wouldn't have that problem. I have a couple of cheapie behind-the-ear buds, and while comfortable, they can be a little touchy and the next thing I know I'm five songs ahead when I didn't mean to be! That doesn't happen with these. They are far sturdier than the less expensive ones, and they're actually quite comfortable for me. The attached silicone tips fit my ears perfectly out of the box (YMMV), and while it took a few adjustments for the ear wire, I finally got that dialed in as well. No pain even after hours of wear. I listen to podcasts, YouTube videos, audiobooks, and music, of course, when I'm busy. I am not an audiophile, but the sounds have been more than satisfactory for my needs. I happily give these five stars so far, but Apple accessories have never been a problem for me, so I doubt that I will change my rating. Oh! While the battery life is good, one pair of my cheapies can go even longer. These are nine hours, and the others are 12 hours. The difference is these feel much more substantial than the others. That being said, either pair can work fine with just one earpiece in at a time. Highly recommended.

title: Life Changing
text: These headphones are INCREDIBLE. You can control the volume, pause, skip, and repeat songs ON both earbuds. They have a great range and battery life, too. I can't stand AirPods because they never fit comfortably for all-day wear. These are perfect. Figuring out how to put them in my ears took some getting used to, but the three sizes of ear plugs (provided in the box) are helpful in getting a good fit. These are not noise-canceling. Beats says they have "noise isolation," but it is still difficult to hear what's happening around you when you use both earbuds. I bought the red ones (not sure why they have a price markup). They are orangish-red in person, so if you are looking for bright red, you'll be disappointed. My favorite thing about them was pairing them with my iPhone, iPad, and Mac. The headphones communicate with the device and basically set themselves up. Super easy. They sound great, too. In typical Beats fashion, the bass is on point. It has to be noted here that these headphones do not come with the correct cable for connecting to an iPhone 11. You must add your own adapter. Fortunately I came prepared and had the adapter needed connected to a pair of Ear Candy ear buds I had been using. Plugged in and ready to go, I found the sound quality terrible. Immediately returned them for a refund. Think I'll stick with my ear buds thank you. Why the one star? Maybe you could use them as ear muffs during the winter months? Don't know.

The other problem is when I place a phone call, the person I am speaking with comes in clear, but I sound muffled to them. I read this same complaint from other people's reviews as well. I am keeping the headphones because I want to use them to listen to music or podcasts while I clean. I’ve not encountered any noise cancellation type of situations when using these so I can’t speak to how well it would cancel any outside noises but if I’m wearing these in bed at night, my wife will have to tap my shoulder to get my attention to say something. Finally, the sound quality: wow! For headphones under $30 I wasn’t expecting very much but I was surprised that these have excellent sound. Whether it’s bass in tv show intros, sound in random YouTube videos, or listening to music, you’re covered very well by all ranges of sound. The volume gets very loud at its highest so I usually keep them set on about halfway. The other potential cons are the questionable build quality and they could’ve added a bit more padding to make them even more comfortable. They aren’t uncomfortable but my ears are very sensitive so I prefer thick padding so the sounds don’t do much damage to my hearing. But again, when you consider the price of these, I wasn’t realistically expecting the Cadillac of headphones but they are definitely a nice and safe Honda Civic.

title: Terrible audio.
text: I researched reasonably priced earphones and finally put these on my Christmas "Wish List" and my wife of 50 years obliged. Fortunately I could blame her selection on myself, so there were no hurt feelings when I exchanged them for a set of even cheaper earbuds after less than a week of trying to make them work. The main problem was that everything coming through the speakers sounded like I was underwater; very dull with a very narrow sound range heavy on the bass. As the battery began to lose its charge it was even difficult to understand spoken words coming through the phones. The second issue was that the charge didn't last; they could be charged up overnight, but after 3 or 4 hours the "low battery" warning would begin to interrupt whatever I was doing. And it's not a gentle reminder; more like a claxon or a very loud busy signal on the old land-line phones. I got these because I was tired of dealing with the wire from my computer speaker jack to the earphones I was using; the cord just managed to be in the way of my mouse most of the time. So after 12 years I made the leap to wireless, but I'm much happier with the Boltune earbuds for which I exchanged this set.
