title: Work great for podcasts and phone calls; muddy sound quality for music, but fine for price point
text: My old bluetooth earbuds took FOREVER to pair and were a daily headache. They also fell out constantly. So just about anything would've been an improvement. These are TREMENDOUSLY better on the points that mattered to me: - they pair with my phone in about 5 seconds, and then stay connected - they're comfortable (though they can be a bit hot, since I usually wear them while walking and it's currently 90+ degrees) - they stay put no matter what I'm doing (not that I'm doing extreme sports, but for ordinary walking, running, mowing the lawn, or doing chores around the house) - they sound fine for podcasts and talking on the phone - the microphone seems to work well for phone calls - they block out enough sound, and have enough volume, that I haven't had any trouble hearing phone calls or podcasts over road noises - the color (black and orange) is vivid; it looks just like the ad picture - I've only had them a few days but the battery life seems fine If you start listening to music, you'll notice immediately that the sound quality is not great -- it's a little muddy and indistinct. But for the price point, what did you really expect? If you want crystal-clear sound, it's going to cost more than these. These are solid headphones for day-to-day use, with the bonus of a functional microphone for calls. Plus apparently they can pick up FM radio?! Very satisfied for the price.

title: If They Fit They'd Still Have Problems
text: I didn't buy these here. Got them at my local T-Mobile. First off, the sound is good. Really good. Maybe a little bass-y for me but not enough to send them back. It has paired up easily with a wide variety of devices. My iPad even shows me a picture and tells me the battery status. And now for the cons. The fit isn't great. A little tight over the ears and then the strange part. There's a gap between the top of my head and the headphones. I always thought that's why God made adjustable lengths on these things. But since they held on so tight I let it go. But it really does seem like they'd only fit well on a girl with a very long very thin face. I am smallish and this is the first time anything has ever been anywhere near this tight before. But I usually buy Bose. Then there was one annoyance too many. The faux leather or whatever it is that covers the ear pads started coming out of the seams it tucks into. Within a month. This is a few too many faults. The design flaws were bad enough, but a failure in quality control on something this expensive is one fault too many. I freely admit I probably should have returned it. There were others to choose from. I just didn’t manage to find the time to go to the store and T-Mobile only gives you two weeks. Plus you have to wait in line. But I also think fair warning is needed here. So there you have it. There's a reason they still have these around. I hope this is helpful to someone

title: Probably the worst Beats headphone I've ever owned
text: I've owned previous Beats headphones in the past and I've never had any problems with them. I figured I wanted to get a new pair so that I could use for work since I work remotely. Let me start off by saying, they're following in the footsteps of Apple, smaller boxes means less things you get in the box. They didn't even provide the aux cord for direct connection to devices. So you basically either have to own one from previously or just spend extra money to buy one if you need it. The case that they give you now are just a complete downgrade from what they used to give you. They used to give you a sturdy case for the headphones to where you wouldn't have to worry as much if you accidentally dropped it or something fell on top of it. Now, they give you cheap soft case. Okay, enough about that, let's get to the headphones. The moment I took the headphones out of the case, I knew instantly, it wasn't even going to be comfortable and it would hurt. I was right. Once I put the headphones on, it already started to hurt my ears, the padding on the headphones are extremely stiff and they're just small. So that definitely do NOT fit around the ears comfortably because after 10 minutes of having it on, I had to take it off because my ears were hurting so much. The headphones are also really tight around the head. No, I don't have a big head and yes I've adjusted both sides height and all that stuff. It was so tight that it actually gave me a really bad headache. So honestly, with that being said, these are the worst Beats headphones I've ever owned and for the price, it's not even worth it anymore.

My right ear bud died at 5 hours in. And it kept saying “low battery” in another language. * My left ear bud was fully charged still in the case, which I then went to use, and realized that this side spoke in English. At this point they started to hurt my ears, so I took them out. * these are not noise cancelling, but they do have good sound quality. *read before you buy; just because it’s inexpensive doesn’t mean it won’t come with a headache or two and I decided mine weren’t worth the headache. I need earbuds I can depend on and these were not it. I listen to music throughout the day at work and occasionally will power up my wonder-boom to give my ears a rest. I work in a closed door pharmacy, so when I need to tune things out, I can. I’ll be grabbing something else & giving this away to someone who only plans to use these for short periods of time. *the breakdown shows the right ear maintaining a charge of 3.5hrs and the left 8.5hrs for a total of 12Hrs. It’s much shorter than the average wireless earbud, hence “DIME” *I got the black pair. Cute & compact; just not for me. I’m incredibly picky; things have to stay in my ear (even with the smallest ear grip and these being a smaller ear bud themselves, I still struggled; so I flipped them up longways and tucked the tip into my upper ear area instead of swinging it low.

title: Great Sound, Good Range, Most Awful, Obnoxious Ear Buds I've Ever Owned
text: I like these a lot. The battery lasts about 3.5 hours. But the range is amazing. I can leave my phone in my office and walk to the back of the plant and still get the sound. That's about 50M through 4 or 5 layers of drywall, wood, and sheet metal. Nice. 3 Month EDIT: Any time I bump the headphone case it nudges the earbuds and they connect. It messed up my other headphones, my Bluetooth speaker, my car stereo... I hate it. I hate it so bad... The earbuds perform really well in their price range, but the fact that they connect if I look at the case wrong is just infuriating. 5 Month Edit: I just threw these away. If I look at the case wrong they connect to my phone, so my video, disconnect my car stereo, etc. I hated it. I hated it so bad I couldn't even believe it. It's just so obnoxious. I guess I got my $20 worth of use out of them, but I would rather die than but another pair

title: Great starter set of Bluetooth wireless headphones
text: This is such a great starter set for anyone. We are an Apple family but their earbuds / headphones are so expensive. Before buying some for my 12 year old, I wanted to make sure that he could be responsible enough for something like this. So I purchased these for him to try out and put them in his Easter basket. They are his favorite gift!! He hasn’t asked for the Apple branded AirPods since! My older son has them so it’s not an out of sight out of mind type of thing. He loves these things! The battery life seems to last time all day. He really enjoys the sound quality and while he plays his music and shows loud sometimes, I can never hear it when sitting near him. This set is super compact and easy to carry around in your pocket. We love the red color because it’s easy to spot them when you drop them or forget them somewhere. With everything being black and white lately, my son looses things. The red color is a huge selling point for us. Overall, we highly recommend this set! I’m not even sure if I’ll upgrade him to AirPods or stick with this brand when he’s finished with these headphones. They’ve at least bought me some time to figure that out.

title: Impossibly Good Cheap Earbuds
text: After the first time, it pairs IMMEDIATELY, from your car to your ear to your car and back. I had 150$ buds as a gift that drove me nuts with pairing. Losing them was a godsend as I bought these; and all my problems vanished. I was primarily audiobooks and podcasts; 90 minutes a day of lines, exercise, drudgery, some phone calls. Charge every night like the phone, never go wrong. I hate Airpods every teenager has to have but I got sick of wires.

title: Pretty good earbuds for the price

Comapre to my old Tozo which had battery for 5 hours, the Skillcandy lasted for about 2.7 to 3 hours max. Its ok for me since I use it mainly at home. But if i am traveling, I would prefer to have longer battery life.

title: Perfect little earbuds
text: I have bought 4 sets of these now, one for me for running and the gym and a set for each of my kiddos. They are cheap so if they get lost no big, they work fantastic for both running and being at the gym-haven't had one pop out on me yet and I've used mine for almost 2 years straight, and the battery life is just fine for a little set. They are the same price as other no name sets so why not get a name brand with a good reputation? The only issue I would have with these is that for phone call use, they are worthless. It doesn't matter to me as I don't use them for that and never would (I hate hate hate hate hate using earbuds for calls, just a preference), so don't expect that out of a pair of 20 dollar earbuds.

title: Great sound but falls out of my ears
text: These have become my favorite ear buds but I have to adjust them frequently when wearing them because they slip out of my ears. The noise canceling doesn't completely work for me because the outer round part doesn't sit all the way inside my ear right. This has been an issue for me with other earbuds too so it's not just Skullcandy earbuds. The sound is great and I like the bass. I listen to a lot of heavy beat styles of music like EDM, metal and Trap music to run to because the beat helps me keep pace. These are good for that. These charge well. Make sure you remove the little plastic guards on the earbuds before charging. I haven't had the battery die yet and I have worn these for a couple hours at a time. I always charge them after I use them and I haven't had any issues with them. You can turn them off/on by quickly pressing on either ear bud. This is great for pausing music quickly like when I'm wearing them at work and someone talks to me or when I'm running and I need to be alert. These ear buds come with a case and USB connector to charge them. I use the USB port on my laptop to charge them. I've used these every single day for the last month and they still work great.

The bass is a bit low (compared to other Skullcandy earbuds I've tried) but overall the sound quality is very clear especially with phone calls, the battery life is decent considering the size. You do loose a few functions compared to higher priced earbuds (wireless charging, USB C, ANC) but taking into account the price these buds are well worth it.

title: TLDR; These sound good, especially for what they cost
text: This is a $20 set of ear buds. If you're wanting audiophile quality sound, you're not going to get it from these. But if you want better than average call quality, and good sounding music playback, these will give you both. No, the bass isn't booming, and the highs aren't in the stratosphere, but the sound is better than acceptable. Especially at this price point... Maybe there's a better sounding set out there that's available for $20. Maybe there isn't. I can't say. What I can say is, there's no way you should be disappointed with the sound these put out. Not if you have reasonable expectations. These are worth the $20. Back in the day, I had a $179 set of Motorolas, and these sound every bit as good as those did. More recently, I had a set of off-brand BT ear buds that didn't sound as good, and made my ears sore. These are comfortable. I've got wired JVC, and the wired buds that came with my iPhone. These sound a little better than the JVCs, and are roughly on par with the ones from Apple. TLDR; These sound good, and are worth the money.

title: A cheap intro to true wireless
text: I got these to replace the Jib True. I’ve had two sets of Jib true. Sounded great and fit well, but after a few weeks of daily use the right bud would lose volume significantly. The magnetic attachments to the charging base would lose strength and allow the buds to disconnect from charging and auto connect to my phone at inopportune times. Dime has a lid that SHOULD push the buds down onto the charge points, and they’re less expensive, so that was what made my decision. After a week of use my ears hurt and I kept having to reach up and push them deeper into my ear, even with the biggest tips installed. I ordered an aftermarket memory foam tips and that fixed the fitment issue but now they’re not staying connected to the charging points, and they auto connect to my phone when I don’t want them to. Sound quality is a 4/5, controls 4/5, aesthetic 3/5, price 5/5. All in all, spend more money on a better true wireless earbud if you want something that isn’t annoying.

I had to size down the ball on my lower conch barbell and use my triangle lobe plug so I could maneuver them in a way to make the earbuds to fit securely. They still try to fall out when I bend over or sweat too much, but they are still my favorites. I haven't had connection or battery issues at all. I only use them for a couple hours at a time, but I've never had the battery die in that time or after three days of use without recharging the case. Haven't had any cutouts or glitches. Case is super tiny and fits anywhere but is hard as heck to open if closed all the way (snap shut vs magnet). Physical button controls are a PITA since you have to hold the stem while in your ear to press in which takes a bit of pressure so you may prefer to pay more for touch sensitive controls & wireless charging. The main flaw... they are short meaning they don't go far enough into the ear canal. As a result, for me, it sounds ever so slightly lower on the right side and it hurts my ear a bit pushed in as far as it will go. Thing is this is easily solved by replacing the rubber caps. I've tried both rubber caps from my wired Skullcandy's and the caps off a Blackberry earbud set and both solve the volume and ear pain problem *BUT* with any other caps other than the included on they won't sit and make charging contact in the case but they do make contact and charge once you close the case as it pushes them down. Overall though for $22 color me impressed. Definitely keeping them.

Case is mildly difficult to open one-handed (not good/bad depending on use). Default eartips don't secure well when running so make sure to test out which ones fit best. title: NC9s are exactly what I was looking for!
text: First of all the customer service from Tozo is outstanding. I bought the T12s, but I was having an issue with phone quality. I reached out and they said it isn't an issue they were aware of, but thought maybe the NC9 would be a better fit and helped me out with a free exchange. They were 100% correct. No issues with call quality. I was looking for a relatively inexpensive pair of earbuds I could use to workout and make phone calls. These fit the bill perfectly. They stay in my ears when I'm running, and the ANC is surprisingly good. I will say to set expectations accordingly. I have the SONY WH-1000XM3s, and these are not that, but for this price point the background noise these knock out with active noise cancelling in addition to the passive noise cancelling is very impressive. Just as important to me as the sound quality is the USB C charging. I got a pair of Skullcany Sesh Evos that I thought were USB C but they actually only charge with USB C to A. I've tried these NC9s with a half dozen chargers from C to C, C to A, and even my desktops USB C port. All of them work perfectly with the case. Definitely would recommend these. Pros: * ANC is good and has a transparent mode * USB C charging works with all chargers I have tried * IPX6 rating * Impressive sound quality for this price point Cons: * Touch controls on headphones in general can be a bit wonky sometimes

title: Nice for the price
text: Overall I like these ear buds but they have room for improvement. What I like: The sound quality is good. The highs are clear and not bright. Mids are spot on. Bass is great. It’s not overdone. The battery life has been good. I haven’t pushed the limits but I’ve run them as long as my Ear Pods and they were still going. The case is holding a lot more charge than the Ear Pods but it’s also larger. The controls are easy to use. The audio is good on phone calls. What I don’t like: There is no vent in these so it’s like putting in ear plugs. I can feel the little bit of air pressure created when these are seated. When used for phone calls there is no audio feedback. It’s like having a conversation with ear plugs in other than being able to hear the other party clearly. The whole side being touch sensitive means I pause audio or video when I have to push them in occasionally. There are voice messages telling which bud is primary and secondary, when they are linked, and when pairing. It’s not necessary and slightly annoying.

title: Best TOZO wireless earbuds so far
text: I owned TOZO T6, T10, and T12. This product is by far the best one. # Pairing The pairing experience is similar to other similar bluetooth products. There is voice hint to tell you whether the earbuds have connected to each other, waiting for pairing, or has been disconnected. I found that the pairing speed of T12 is faster T6 and T10. With T6, sometimes when I turned the power back, it will drop the connection. But so far it never happens to me with T12. # Sound quality The output quality is similar to other product. However, the input quality is slightly worse than the Macbook built-in microphone. IMO, it's good for casual use, but bad for voice meeting. # Charging The charging indicator is much helpful on T12. It shows both the progress or the cases and each earbud. It's nice that it is using USB Type-C cable, which saves me the trouble to have multiple cables. # Battery I used the earbuds continuously for 6 hours straight until it warns me low battery. # Design I like the shape of T12 better since I could clearly distinguish the right and left earbuds instantly. Compared with T6 and T10 where the two earbuds are identical, I often have to take second look to make sure I have the right one.

title: Excellent sound quality
text: These earpods sounds very good. Deep bass. Easy to use. Takes time to get used to the sensitivity of the touch control. It's very easy to unintentionally pause the music when you're trying to adjust the fit of the buds. Nice charging case. I like the wireless charging capability. An Ap to adjust the sound would be a nice addition. Initially I thought the bass was inadequate so I contacted customer service.. They were very responsive and were willing to do whatever they could to resolve the issue. I later discovered that changing the ear pads produced the bass that I was looking for. Luckily Tozo provided a wide variety of ear pad sizes. Very happy with the Tozo earbuds.

title: Touch controls trigger constantly
text: I had some issues with T6's, and TOZO offered these as a replacement after leaving a review. Unfortunately the replacement pair was stolen by a package thief, so I decided to buy them. When working out, they are unusable. The capacitive touch button, particularly in the left ear, will trigger itself randomly and pause, reverse, and lower the volume, and then just repeat "minimum volume" in my ear until I turn them off. Using them for work, this is slightly less of an issue but still a common occurrence. They should at the very least remove " for Sport" from the title, but I still wouldn't recommend them for home/office use either. Honestly, the one thing that makes me happy is that the thief will presumably be suffering with the most frustrating pair of headphones in existence. TOZO customer service is good, but it's so proactive that I can see how this product has good reviews even though there are serious design flaws. I will not be removing this. They need to kill this design and promote their better ones. The T6's aren't perfect, but I'd take them any day over these.

title: For me: better than AirPods or Beats
text: Over the past 4 years I have probably owned 10 different sets of Bluetooth earbuds. I like to spend under $100 in case I lose them or they get ruined in the washing machine and fortunately this is a pretty big market segment. Over the past two months I gave in to the hype and purchased AirPods Pro 2nd Gen for over $200 and 3 weeks later I returned them for the simple reason that they wouldn't stay in my ears. They kept falling out. It seems this is a common problem with AirPods! A few days ago I got Beats Fit Pro for $200. While they fit much better and have a lot of very cool features (Siri will read my text messages to me, Spatial audio, Transparency mode) the bass is really quite weak, and there's no Qi charging for them, only wired USB-C. So that brings me back to the Tozo T12 which I've owned for about 6 months now. These little earbuds sound amazing. The bass is great as is the rest of the spectrum. They don't fall out of my ears! They stay in place just fine. While they don't have a lot of the Apple-specific features, they cost almost 80% less than Airpods Pro. Great sound, great price, and Qi wireless charging. These are my favorite right now, and if I lose them or send them through the wash I'll just buy another set because they didn't cost an arm and a leg.

title: A lot to like and one don't like.

I tried the T12 because their shape gave a large base that would prevent the rubber tip from going in too far. The T12's had a lot of pluses and one deal-breaker negative. They're comfortable in the ear. Good controls. The pillow did not mess with the control functions. Batteries lasted the night. I set my books to stop at the end of a chapter or after a set time so it's not running all night. I could easily pause, back up, skip ahead once I got the "tap" commands down. Sound and volume were excellent. Although I do use my graphic equalizer on my phone. The one negative: The metal contacts on the underside of the buds touch my skin on an ear fold. This left burn marks on my skin. The burn marks line up with the metal charging contacts on the bud. Maybe if the metal were more recessed the contacts would not touch my skin. I really wanted to love these. I could just roll over and enjoy my book. But I'm returning them. I might try the T6 - those look like they have contacts in a different place.

title: Another great Tozo earbud!
text: This is now my 3rd set of Tozo earbuds. I have both the T6 and T10 and now the T12. The first thing I want to bring up is the sound quality. I have to really emphasize the importance of making sure these buds are snug and fit inside the ears. That is probably the single most important factor in making sure you get the best sound quality possible. Tozo knows there are many sizes for the ear so these come with 4 different bud sizes. Personally, I had to use the 2nd to the largest one to make sure the fit is snug but not too much. Once you got the fit and snug, the sound quality is just amazing. The bass hits deep and low and vocals are clean. However the highs are just a tad bright for my personal tastes. Music sounds great and movies are loud and clear. Also, the noise cancellation is passive but if you got the buds fit right, it does a really good job stopping external noise, much like a quality earplug. Ergonomics and control. The touch control is identical to the T6. Tap once to play or pause, tap twice to skip song or previous song, hold for volume up or volume down. What I like about the T12 is the touch is not super sensitive to slight adjustments and movements. When I used the T6, adjusting the earbuds in my ear sometimes caused an unintentional touch command. The case is perfect. I prefer the flat case over the tall airpod clone. The T6 has the tall case and it was slightly difficult to take the earbuds out. I think ergonomics should be the primary factor and the T12 case is perfect. It is small, has wireless charging AND it is easy to remove the buds. I use these primarily for working out and I get sweaty. The IPX8 waterproofing gives me assurance that the buds won't break from sweat. I might even wear them floating around the pool but I still get nervous using them around deep water. Can't comment on battery life, I've never used them long enough to actually run out. Overall, love these buds. You just can't beat the value.

title: Great sound quality but not workout approved
text: 3/22 update:: I have been using these headphones almost exclusively for the gym. Maybe these just aren't a good fit for my ear shape but the design of these earbuds is just awful. I've tried every single size variation the ear buds came with and these ear buds simply will not sit in my ears like they should. I am constantly adjusting the ear bud back into my ear so it won't fall out (falls out frequently while lifting weights). I can't stretch doing toe touches without them falling out. I can't lift weights without them falling out. I can't sit on the exercise bike without them falling out. The button on the ear buds is so incredibly sensitive that every single time I have to adjust it so it doesn't fall out that it causes whatever I'm listening to stop. So then I have to touch it again, which can cause it to fall out of place yet again no matter how gentle I am. These are the most frustrating ear buds I have ever owned. The sound quality is EXCELLENT! But the shape & design of the ear bud itself is so incredibly disappointing considering the price. Con:: I bought these mainly for the purpose of working out. I hate how large they are, they portrude way too far from my inner ear. So much so that my arm often bumps them when I'm lifting weights above head. Even when I am not lifting weights, I find that in constantly having to readjust them because they're falling out of my ears. I've tried using the different sizes ear bud covers but it does not help. I've had a little bit of static from the Bluetooth connection every now & then despite my phone being on me. It doesn't happen often, it was just odd it happened at all as my phone was sitting right in front of me. Not even a foot away. Pros: The sound quality is exponentially better than any other ear buds I've owned. They definitely cancel noise. The battery life is great. I've only changed them twice since I began using them in December...I like that the case recharges the ear buds even if the case itself isn't fully charged. The case charges very quickly too.

title: Nice addition to the Beats wireless line
text: These are a solid addition to the ever growing true wireless market. Although this is a Beats branded pair, it is markedly different from the Powerbeats Pro. First, it’s a smaller form factor both in the buds themselves and the case. The buds in particular are very tiny. See pic comparing to the AirPods Pro. It has no stem but the bud itself sticks out your ears a little more, so they are uncomfortable to lay on if you were to watch a movie in bed or so. They look like bolts in your ears from afar. With that being said, they are comfortable for regular use, at least for me. Although the silicone tips are less pliant and soft compared to the Pro’s. Sound quality is where it shines, with a nice resonating low and crisp highs. Mids is where these fall short. Battery lasts pretty well, about 6 hours with ANC on, haven’t tested with them off but it claims to last up to 8 hours. Now the case I believe should have been a little smaller since it doesn’t house a wireless coil, so not sure what the large body is for. Overall battery life with the case is similar to that of the Pro’s and the Pro’s case is much smaller. Another pro is that it works better with non-Apple devices but may be a con for Apple users. There’s no proprietary H1 chip, so you won’t get the auto-connect to all your synced devices. There’s no spatial audio for video although I believe it supports audio on Apple Music. Now for the ANC and the ambient pass through. It’s ok, for the price point. Both pale in comparison to AirPods Pro or even other similar priced competitors but you do pay extra for the brand cachet. All in all, nice pickup. Hopefully the successor will be more tuned towards the iOS ecosystem.

title: Nice Sound, Great Design!
text: For the last two years (May 2019 to June 2021) I've owned BOSE Sound Sports as my ear buds that I use at the gym. Sadly I lost them recently and needed a replacement. The Beats Studio Buds looked good and were a good price point. I was pleasantly surprised that the Beats were quite a bit better than the BOSE and at a better price point. 1. Sound: Just as good as the Bose Soundsports if not better, good volume amount. 2. Button Controls: Very nice light touch buttons on both the right and left buds. Unlike some other reviews that I have read pressing the buttons did NOT push the buds into the ear. I found the buttons to be a nice lite touch when compared to the SoundSports buttons, which were about 3 times harder to press (or more, really took some pressure). 3. CASE: Very well designed case, sleek, durable. Really liked the magnetic lid and charging ports, well designed and thought out. 4. BEATS APP: LIke that the app shows how much of a charge is in each bud right and left. Useful. 5. Comfort: Felt like the fit (For me) was perfect, never fell out, a good interface with the ear. A better fit than the Bose for sure. 6. Aesthetics: The Beats do not stick out as much as the BOSE Soundsports (They really stood out quite a bit). The BEATS are much smaller and have a very nice profile to them. Overall am very pleased with the BEATS, so much I got the white ones to! Ironically after I ordered the Black ones I FOUND my BOSE soundsports, but after using the BEATS, I found them to be superior in many ways to the BOSE buds. Sorry Bose BEATS is the new BUDS for going to the gym for me! Update, 8.27.21 Having no volume control on the actual Buds was no big deal to me (Some reviewers really didn't like that you couldn't adjust the volume on the actual Buds). You'll always have your phone with you anyway and it's just as simple to press the volume control on your phone.

text: These buds are awful. They're way over-priced considering their very low sound quality. They sound very much like the low quality of AM broadcast radio from the mid-20th century. It's especially difficult to get the buds in and out of their case, as the magnets that hold them in are pretty strong, so the magnets pull them out of your fingers. Basically you have no control over your hold on the buds because they're so slippery. There's nothing your fingers can grasp onto. In order to pair w/your phone, you need to have the case open, and be in close proximity to your phone. Because the case has no flat surface, and the lid has a spring mechanism that snaps itself shut far too easily, you'll need both hands on the case itself to pair. This is a *really* poor design and I absolutely hate it. Matter of fact, I absolutely hate both the buds, and their case.

title: Not great.
text: Got these at half off to replace my AirPods that stopped working. Overall, these weren’t nearly as good as I was hoping based on the $150 price and relatively good reviews. Pros: They do fit very well and stay in easily. Really comfortable to wear and I haven’t had them fall out while moving around. Battery life is fairly good, definitely outlasts my older 2nd gen AirPods Noise cancelling is nice, not up to par with over ear headphones but that’s to be expected. Cons: Sound. Out of the box these really lacked bass. Everyone has different preferences here so maybe that’s just me. Figured this would be an easy fix through their equalizer. Nope. The Bose app doesn’t support these earbuds, only the more expensive variants. Pretty unacceptable to have a pair of earbuds at this price range be intentionally hindered this way. And yes, they are sealed correctly. Connectivity. I use these with an iPhone and getting them reconnected is always a pain taking them out of the case. I often have to “forget device” and reconnect. They also stutter regularly (every 5 minutes or so) while no other Bluetooth headsets I’ve used have this problem. The play button is also very easy to press when putting them in, a pretty minor inconvenience compared to the above points. The case is incredibly cheaply made for something in this price range. Not a huge issue, but I could see the lid breaking in the future. Really not impressed with these, I’ll be returning them. Regular AirPods are cheaper and have vastly better sound quality imo.

title: Cheap, compressed, bassless audio from a $25 pair of cheap buds
text: I am absolutely blown away at the low quality of these earbuds. I have an audio engineering degree and own some $2500 headphones including Stax headphones and a pair of lovely flagship AKG 701 headphones... in addition to Amphion & Barefoot monitors. These are by far the cheapest, most lifeless earbudds I've ever experienced and are below my $50 cheap in ear buds I replaced these with. Brand apparently means everything to half asleep American consumers because these are shockingly bad and yet they have 5 star reviews. Sheesh. I am blow away actually, at how poor the mid range and bass response on these are. Thin, hyper compressed, small soundstage, boxed in and completely lifeless. The audio is poorly compressed and missing a massive amount of frequency range needed to minimally enjoy music. I do not recommend this product to anyone looking for quality. I suspect Apple bought this company and the average unsuspecting consumer has no idea the difference between quality and "loudness" of these buds. However. I can assure you the quality is on level with any other $20-40 pair of entry level buetooth buds.

text: So I lost one of my other ear buds and had to buy a new paper. My older ones did not have the ear wrap and would fall out. HOWEVER, I have been wearing them all weekend and my ear canal HURTS. I have tried various placement in my ear canal and haven't found a good placement. So I am wondering, do I have these actually IN right?? Possibly not. It would be useful if there was a clear demonstration on the proper placement of these devices. I almost returned them but decided to research more .. cause I don't want to go through the hassle of returning them. The 2nd issue I have that I didn't notice is that the included buttons are iffy. They turn on and off OK but you have to press down on the button more than on my other ones that is just via touch. WHICH probably is a good thing as I would accidently fiddle with my other ear buds and it would turn them on and off and mess with them. THese you actually have a button. The volume seems fiddly and doesn't seem to be working as well as I would like Again, they are buttons so you have to press down harder rather than just touching the device. That again, could be good or bad. the other issue that may be the biggest problem is that there is not a forward 10 seconds or rewind 10 seconds. It is Next Track, previous track. That is less useful for me as I listen to podcasts rather than music. So Just something to consider. I may actually eventually replace these as I don't think they are perfect but I am hoping they will work for a bit more time until I can afford a better set for myself.

I also like they way that they feel on my ears, very solid and doesn't move or slip out. Sound quality leaves something to be desired, although you should keep in mind that is a very personal choice. For those of you who are in the know, the way I'd describe these is "scooped". In other words, in a standard EQ range, the mid ranges are de-emphasized for in favor of the low (or sometimes high) ranges so the the EQU range looks like it's been scooped out. I don't generally have a problem with this for certain kinds of music, but it can get a little annoying at times. Podcasts/spoken word doesn't need booming bass, and vocal ranges usually live in the center range so you're dulling it. Most American ears probably won't even notice since everything these days is heavy bass, but it bothers me. I'm not looking for reference EQ, but the emphasis on the lower ranges is enough to bother me. Still, I'll keep these. They're good enough.

Obviously would buy again UPDATE: After spending some time with the different sized earbuds I can say the sound quality on these is far better than I originally experienced. I know Anker makes good audio products, but this product needs a little more work to make it a little more durable. UPDATE: Anker has excellent customer service. They sent me a replacement, unfortunately the replacement died after one use. It just did not turn on, despite being fully charged, I have no idea why, so I'll just chalk that up to being a fluke. What did they do after that? They sent me another pair! (with the caveat that I send the non-working pair back so that they can have their QC people have a look-see). The third pair works like a charm, and just like above, the sound quality is great, they work just fine, and have a very long battery life. title: Super comfort, Best distance for Bluetooth connection
text: The headphones are really nice. They are very comfortable. The ear cup cushions are soft, and form nicely over the ears. Combined with noise cancellation, they pretty much completely isolate the user. I have to lift an earpiece if my husband is trying to talk to me! The foam on the over-the-head band is also very soft, and does not hurt my head if I binge-listen to a whole audio book all day (9-10 hours). The ear cups are large enough that, even when I wear them all day, they don't squash my ears and leave them aching at the end of the day. The whole headset is quite light-weight, which contributes to the comfort too. The distance range for the Bluetooth connection is by far the best of the several (3 different mfrs) previous headphones I've owned. I can walk out into the yard, or go upstairs, and still get a clear signal, thru the walls of the house, so I get the full 30 feet range, even with obstacles. The listening time is also amazing. I can use it all day, and charge it when I go to bed. The only down-side, for me, is that the headset is slightly too large for my head (60F). With the earcups fully pushed in, it's just the tiniest bit too long. My grandson (20M) tried them on and he had to drop the earcups, so they fit him fine. Maybe it's better sized for a man's head. So, I just have to be careful if I bend over, because they occasionally slip a little. They stay in place fine as long as I'm standing or sitting, it's only an issue if I bend over to pick something up off the floor.

text: Muffs are soft, headset feels solid, buttons work good/has all the ones you need. Sound is solid, sounds clear. I would recommend if you’re just a basic user looking for a nice headset.

title: Amazing
text: These things are a amazing, especially at this price. I bought these for my 5 hour weekly lawnmower ride, and the noise from the 60” mower almost disappears. In the past I tried using earbuds but the noise was just too much. I can understand those that may not like these because you can’t hear the mower (should something break), but the noise cancellation button allows you to turn that feature on or off. Even with the NC deactivated you can hear the music. They have decent bass, probably a little better then average, but I do wish the ear cups were a little bigger as my ears hurt after a day on the mower. I really couldn’t justify taking a star away in my review even though they’re not perfect. When reviewing a product I feel it important you consider what you paid. I gave these $40 headphones 5 stars, but had I paid $300 they would have gotten 3 stars. You really get what you pay for but for the money these are amazing and you just can’t go wrong.

title: Love the fit!
text: These have a great fit and feel to them. I haven't used them to travel given I have small kids I shouldn't tube out, but I do use them at night when everyone is asleep and I can watch my movies/shows. Sound quality is great. Noise cancellation really reduces surrounding sounds. I used them for conference calls during work and it works well. People hear me well and I don't hear much outside of the conference call. A bit large to travel with, but that's personal preference. These are for sure a great buy! Update 6/9/2022 So unfortunately these headphones broke! I grabbed the earphones part, pulled out to place over my ears, and heard a snap and crack. A piece of plastic chipped off and now are rendered unusable. I contacted customer service (very quick response) but their warranty is for only 18 months. I purchased mine 20 months ago! They should have at least a 2 year warranty!!! In the end, I was told there was nothing they can do. No replacement. No discount coupon to next purchase. Nada! I'm removing 2 stars from my rating. 1 star for shoddy material and another for limited warranty. Item was still excellent to use and sounded great! My next purchase will be one with less moving parts-less likey to break I guess.

title: Worth it (:
text: Everyone's gonna ask about the sound cancellation. It's like an 8/10. It definitely quiets everything down. Making outside noises doable for me. Screaming, loud noises, are all on low. The fit is great. I have two helix piercings, one on each ear and these headphones don't cause any issues or pain. The battery life is AMAZING. My AirPods die within like 4 hours & these headphones last so much longer! I've used them 2 days in a row over 4 ours each day and the battery is still on "high". Sound of music is just the same as it is with my AirPods. I was going to buy beats, or Apple headphones but I'm glad I bought these instead.

title: Great dupe for bose
text: Cancels noise just like I wanted and works as great as the 400$ bose noise cancelation headphones. Great value for the money

title: Awesome headphones
text: I really actually love these headphones, connected easily via Bluetooth to my TV, gives battery percentage on all devices, sounds amazing and does an awesome job of noise cancelling. My only issue is that they broke two months in, but AnkerDirect was super awesome when I contacted them and took care of replacing them. Excellent customer service. I would definitely buy from them again. Supet happy customer!

title: worth the low price for the quality
text: So far so good. The audio quality is good. The battery last a long time. This doesn't give a thumping base but I was looking for an above average bluetooth headset so I'd stop accidentally choking myself on wires and this is it. I've never tried fancy headsets like Bose or Beats so I can't say how those compare. I don't have the money and I don't think they're worth it. This sounds better than my previous wired earbuds, blocks out noise, allows me to walk away from my device, and has a great battery life. The functions on the headset are easy to control so that's also a plus. It serves me well. Worth the price for sure.

title: Great quality and a reasonable price
text: These are amazing! The overall quality Dow not match the price I would think these are $100+ headphones. I have bought a few other products from anker and so far I have been happy with their stuff.

title: Piece of Realistic-Looking Garbage For $60....Looking Elsewhere
text: Here is the skinny on this 'noise cancelling' headphone: off the bat, the instructions that come with this headphone should definitely be returned with the rest of the package for a refund. There are no instructions on the Soundcore website either. Not too much thought has been put into the user interface of this headphone. I don't know when it is fully charged. There is no indicator for 'charged'. I am not sure if it is in noise-cancelling mode or not. There is no way to know if it is in noise-cancelling mode other than there should be no noise, but there is lots, therefore it is not in noise-cancelling mode, if it is at all capable of noise-cancelling as a stand-alone feature. At this point I am not convinced at all this headphone can do noise-cancelling without having to be connected to a noise-producing device via bluetooth. It might not even do the hybrid it claims. My hunch is that like a lot of consumer products from China the basic technology was ripped off of some western company (probably Bose) and it was then Chinesed down but made to look shinier than its original Western counterpart. I am returning this headphone pronto.

title: Not durable, but covered under warranty.
text: Edit: I contacted customer support and they are sending me a replacement. I improved my rating since their 18 month warranty is being honored. I hope the replacement is more durable, but have my doubts. The headphones operate fine, but they are not physically durable. The plastic broke apart on both sides. I glued them back together which worked for a while, but they broke again in a different place. The plastic is just too thin and cracks into pieces.

title: Overall Good Noise Cancellation and Sound Quality BUT BROKE after only FIVE MONTHS of use.
text: I really liked these headphones. The sound quality is good, but the Noise Cancellation is fantastic. I wore them often to drown out the TV while studying and listening to lectures or videos. Worked like a charm. However, just after 5 months of normal wear, the plastic parts which held on the right earpad SNAPPED! Very disappointing. I couldn't believe it. Not fixable, as far as I can tell.

title: Work great! Can barely hear my children!
text: In the days of shelter in place with a 4 and 6 year old, I was desperate for a little quiet. Even with my door shut and earbuds in, I could hear them arguing and their elephant feet stomping around the house. These work great. They aren't so noise cancelling that I'm senseless of my surroundings, but they eliminate and muffle plenty. They eliminate nearly all road noise, and mute the kids and their movie in the car. I can clean the kitchen or work in peace, without overhearing all the "momma! momma!" they pretend whine when they play babies. The first pair I had, one of the earphones had an odd pulsing. It wasn't a sound so much as a pressure. Like ears popping but softer. They helped me troubleshoot some options, but when those failed, they sent a new pair without any hassle. These soundcore headphone shave made 5 months home with my noisy children bearable!

title: Excellent, except....
text: Love the sound and noise cancellation. The headband is slightly too big for my head (average female size). Indoor use is no problem, however if you are outside walking on a windy day, a headwind can be very loud despite the noise cancellation. Wind can be heard blowing between the earpiece and the headband, and because of this, they work best when worn on a day with no wind or with a hat worn completely over the device. They sound as good as my Bose, if not better. I wore them all winter, every day, great battery life, great comfort with glasses, great sound.

title: Too many issue for people trying to hear me
text: I recently bought a few types of headphones for various different reasons. I was actually most excited about these. As someone who has a handful different Anker products I have never been let down by them..... until now. These look amazing. They have a really nice build that is great fitting. Super adjustable. Fits all hat sizes from children to size 8 very comfortably. Nice ear pads that rotate, everything you could want in design. I attached them to my computer via Bluetooth (super easy) and tried out videoconferencing. I can hear the people on the other end (we tested in the same house a hundred feet away) awesomely - but they hear cracking noises every few seconds so they can only make out every other word essentially. I go to switch places with them and yep, cracking noises. You can’t make out the person on the other end really. Okay I think, let’s try using with the phone instead. I plug back in to charge (even though it was fully charged already) and wait until the next day. The next day I try them again when making a phone call via Bluetooth. Again, setup is easy. I can hear the person on the other end of the line perfectly. They actually ask if I am driving because they are having a tough time hearing me. Like I am going through a tunnel. I am sitting on a couch inside. I switch to another headset and they can hear me perfectly. Unfortunately these are great in design, and great for listening to things. If that is all you are primarily doing these might be good for you as the noise canceling was pretty good. Could hardly hear people yelling from 10 feet away. However, if you are going to use them to talk on a phone or use to videoconference then these will not work for you, and was why I specifically bought these as they were supposed to be able to do that. For those reasons they need to go back.

title: Poor Build Quality in My Pair
text: I bought these and am impressed by them. The good: Comfort - These fit well and I've been able to wear them for periods over 5 hours without a problem. Noise suppression - I wear these while walking in a busy gym, on a treadmill. These work well suppressing the mechanical noises in this environment. They also reduce surrounding conversations that I have no interest in hearing. Sound quality - I am not an audiophile and usually listen to audiobooks. That said I have been very happy with what I hear using these. The bad. Build quality - This is where I have my problem. On the 2nd use, I noticed that if I handle these in a certain way, if there were any sort of impact to them (inadvertently bumping them, jumping during exercise or just putting them on and letting the ear cups "hit" my head) they produce a loud pop noise. Initially, it was am infrequent irritant but is now to the point where I cannot use these. The sound is loud enough to be painful. I suspect there is something loose/improperly soldered inside. If it weren't for this I would highly recommend these.

title: Kinda Blown Away
text: First, I’m no audiophile. Second, this is my first pair of ANC earphones. That said, I’m very impressed and think this is an amazing set of earphones for the price. The first thing I did when I got them (after pairing them) was try out the noise cancellation feature. I happened to have a lot of laundry running so I went in my laundry room (closet, really), closed the door, and tried them out. The noise in the room when from a loud rumble to an almost imperceptible hum. Really amazing. I turned off the ANC just to make sure it wasn’t just noise isolation and it wasn’t, though the noise isolation is good, the ANC is what really does the magic. I’ve tried these on plane trips as well, and they do a very good job; sitting at a window seat (where it’s loudest) the din of the plane went from a loud, low ruble to a higher pitched soft rumble - not quite a hiss but perhaps what one might get from a white noise maker. Not bad for noise cancellation alone, but when listening to or viewing media, the difference is amazing. Finally, I can hear the full efffects of a movie without turning the volume all the way up. Honestly, after using these earphones I don’t think I can ever go back to being without ear protection on a plane, for me or my family. That said, I won’t say the audio quality is outstanding. It’s good enough, with good range, adequate volume and decent base, but it’s not at audiophile level. But because they have ANC it’s actually possible to hear music or other audio in situations where normally you wouldn’t barely hear anything, and that’s the big difference. Does Bose do a better job of noise cancellation and audio quality? Probably. But I’d never spend $200-$300 on a pair of headphones just to use on the plane, especially since paying that much for for every member of my family would break the bank. But at the price of these Ankers it’s a no brainer to get a set for everyone.

title: Okay, these headphones are great
text: So I’ve become a big fan of Anker products over the years including their Soundcore line of products as well. I was looking for a new, quality headset that wouldn’t totally break the bank. I decided to give these a shot. I think there’s a notion that high quality sound is only accessible when it breaks the bank and that’s just not true. Unless you’re a hardcore audiophile or work on audio in a professional capacity, those $500 headphones aren't necessary. I can’t gush over these headphones enough. They’re reasonably priced, have balanced, excellent quality sound. They’re great for hobbyist audio/music production. Not to mention the noise cancellation is definitely on par with a lot of the more expensive sets. If you’re on the fence about these headphones I’d say go for it. I’m very satisfied and my next pair might also be a Soundcore if they continue down this path.

title: Comfortable and ergonomic, great noise cancelling, sounds a little thin
text: I like these headphones. I did a side-by-side comparison with the beats solo and found a few key differences. The soundcore headphones are more comfortable and flexible than the beats. The ear cups are also large, which made me almost forget I was wearing them because they fit so nicely on my ear. The controls are plastic buttons, rather than the touch sensors on the beats - so they are not quite as sleek. Soundcore more than makes up for it in comfort though. The noise cancelling is also far superior to the beats. When I have these on, I cannot hear someone talking to me from 3 feet away, even when the volume is only at 50%. The only advantage that the beats have over the soundcore is depth of sound, the quality and crispness of music is definitely not as good in the soundcore as it is in competitors. If I did not have another set of headphones to compare it to, I probably wouldn't notice. Overall I would recommend these, especially for people wearing them for long durations or in especially noisy areas.

title: All Ears
text: So comfortable. The best sound and base. Glad I came across these and can add to the rating, so you all out there can get you a pair also. The best.

title: Noise cancellation useless for exercising
text: Headphones are comfortable. The only issue I have is the same that a few reviewers mentioned already; sudden movements when the noise cancellation is on cause a static burst of sound. I can reproduce it by just tilting my head to the side. Bass isn’t the best unless you turn on the bass boost. So every time I use these, I turn off noise cancellation and turn on bass boost. I haven’t spent any time to see if I can have those settings remembered. UPDATE: 2/19/2020 Anker customer support reached out to me and offered to replace my headphones. The replacement headphones do not have this same issue. I am happy to say that it's been resolved. I have bumped this product up to 5 stars.

title: Inexpensive but mighty
text: These are an incredibly competent set of headphones considering the price. I needed a pair of noise reduction headphones to use for conference calls at work because I work in an industrial area with lots of machinery noise right outside of my office. I would love a pair of Sony or Bose headphones but I am not bringing a pair of $300 plus headphones to an industrial area where they will likely be damaged or stolen. I found these and was skeptical, but pleasantly surprised with the performance once trying them. They cancel the loud humming noise of the machinery and the people on the other end of the call can hear me clearly as well so perhaps the microphone has a noise canceling too but it's not advertised as such so I am not sure. I just know that the people on the line say my voice is clear on their end. The sound of music is impressive too. Lots of clear bass is present which seems to be the primary basis of how headphones are rated these days thanks to Dr. Dre. These may not be a pair of Beats, but they definitely give Beats a run for their money for a fraction of the price. It also has a bass boost option which takes the already ample bass and turns it up to eleven. No need for that, the normal mode bass is more than adequate! My only minor niggle is that in order to hear all the nuances in the music I listen to, I have to max out the volume. This could be due to my hearing going bad (did I mention I work un a noisy industrial environment?). It may also be in part due to the volume capabilities on my phone, so I want to be fair and say the dynamic range may be fine for most people, however, I have had other headphones that are capable of being much louder for better or for worse. Ultimately I think these are an amazing value compared to the rest of the market offerings and if I lose or damage them at work I can replace them 5 or 6 times and still be under the cost of 1 pair of bose or sony headphones.

title: Big sound, big comfort, but small price!
text: So I have to say, I am very impressed with the quality of these headphones. I've used a few wireless headphones in the past few years, but I haven't used any of the big name high dollar ones so I'm not sure about an exact comparison. However, I feel these could be up for the challenge. So first thing I noticed was the light weight feel of these. They fit well and aren't too noticable, but the light weight didn't mean cheap plastic like some of the others I've used. The head strap material has some flex so they don't feel like you're going to break them putting them on. Also if you have trouble remembering which ear goes which, they have a big L and R on the inside of the muffs. Speaking of the ear muffs, they are extremely comfortable and seal well to keep out noise. The ear muffs and padded head band allow for hours of comfortable wear. Battery life has been excellent and I like how the headphones will audibly tell you charge level when you power on. This is my first set of active noise cancelling headphones and I wonder why I never got a set sooner. I love how I can have a low volume to relax with music rather than having to crank them up to drown out other noise. The controls are within easy reach on the bottom of each ear. For the price, I definitely recommend these headphones!

title: I love these headphones!!!!
text: I have always loved Anker products and these headphones didn’t disappoint. Extremely high quality noise canceling headphones for the money. I refuse to spend $300 on headphones and for the price I paid for these, I think the sound quality is almost to par with them. You want some great headphones for the money, buy these Anker headphones.

title: Best I've had in a long time
text: Audio quality is very decent. I wanted headphones I could use for gaming that didn't sound terrible, so you know what I did? I stopped looking at headphones that call themselves gaming headphones. I had been so disappointed by the audio quality on the Arctis 7 headset, but also spoiled by the wirelessness. So this Life Q20 thing looked like an ideal replacement, and it is. The noise-cancellation is on by default and you only really notice it's there if you turn it off; it's not as powerful as, say, a Bose product that has noise-cancellation as its main selling point. The comfort of the headband is fine. There was a lot of creaking in the plastic where the earpieces connect to the headband, for the first few weeks, but that's gotten better. Update: Almost exactly one year later, a piece of plastic has broken off the left side of the headband, just above the earcup. Considering how often I've put them on, taken them off, and put them back on every single day since I got them, I'm neither surprised nor disappointed, and I'll probably replace this headset with another just like it when tape stops being enough to fix the break.

title: iMac connection fixed!
text: EDIT 24 May 2021: i have finally gotten these things to work correctly with my iMac! the problem is that the iMac by default connects to these headphones with Bluetooth's built-in audio CODEC, SBC. however! you can tell the system to use AAC or AptX via the command line. i am using Mac OS Mojave 10.14.6, so i do not know that these commands will work in other versions of the OS. to use AptX, open the terminal and copy the following command: sudo defaults write bluetoothaudiod "Enable AptX codec" -bool true to use AAC, use this command: sudo defaults write bluetoothaudiod "Enable AAC codec" -bool true if you want to revert it to how it was before, change the ending from -bool true to -bool false. i used AAC, and now my headphones work exactly the way i expect them to. when i adjust the system volume, the volume of the headphones changes. they even sound better (hardly surprising, as AptX and AAC deliver superior audio quality). --- i usually use these with my iPhone, where they work beautifully and as expected. but when i connect them to my iMac, things go wrong. when i try to change the volume via the keyboard, using the media keys, nothing happens. and depending on which app is playing audio, sometimes the sound gets very, very bad. i have to use SoundSource to keep things consistent. and even then, when i change apps (going from playing a video in a web browser to listening to iTunes) i have to tell the app to send the audio to the Ankers. otherwise it starts playing through the iMac's speakers. this does not happen with my VMODA Crossfades. i don't know if i'm missing some setting on the Q20s or if there's an app for it i need to install to make it play nicely or what, but for volume control, low, low marks. :( it's a pity, because these things sound amazing. guess i'll just start saving my pennies for the AirPod Max.

title: Great sound quality and amazing battery life

At first I used it with my phone, and was terribly disappointed, but on my computer and other bluetooth sound systems, they sounded fantastic. I later learned I would have to re download my entire Apple Music library to enjoy higher bit rate music, so I primarily use these with other devices. The battery life it amazing. I have not had to charge them in almost a month after daily use of an hour or so. When the battery does get low it takes only a few minutes to get hours of use thanks to its quick charge technology. They are lightweight, comfortable, and the sound quality is surprising decent for an inexpensive set of headphones. About my only complaint would be that the controls are not as intuitive as I would like, but overall I am very pleased with this purchase, and would highly recommend them.

title: Good for podcast and audio books and the price can't be beat.
text: The noise canceling with this set is better than any other I have used. I use them with my Mac Book Pro 13 2020, iPad Pro 12.8 2018, and my OG iPhone X. I use them for podcasts, audio books, YouTube, video calling, and audio calls. I have been told that the quality of my voice over this set's microphone isn't as good as with the Air Pods Pro, but that it is still good. The bluetooth, while not as seamless as Apple's, works better than any non Apple product I have used. It automatically reconnects to the last device used, but I have to go into settings to reconnect when switching devices. Occasionally I have had to manually disconnect them from the previous device before connecting them to the next one. I don't listen to music often, so that is not an issue for me. I lowered the star count for the sound quality because I can't recommend them to folks who are really into their music and need a less bassy and better range. That being said, I can't believe what you get for the price. Before Covid19 stopped me between Peru and Mexico, I had spent two years as a nomad, living in Airbnbs around the world. Between flights, airports, and exuberant neighbors, noise canceling headsets are very important to me. I have tried many types of Boise devises over the years, before finally settled on Apple Air Pods Pro. I was missing having a good set of over the ear ones. Normally I don't travel with over the ear sets because of the added weight. (I travel with only 15 kilos total gear, including what I wear.) Right now I am in an airbnb in the US not traveling for the foreseeable future. Everyone here is trapped by Covid19, no one is working, so TVs and conversation cause a lot of noise at various times of the night and day. For the night I have an excellent pair of earplugs. During the day, I switch back and forth between this headset and my Air Pods Pro. The difference in form factor gives my ears a rest, so I can't stay insulated from my neighbors all day long.

title: Does Not Handle Device Switching. Destroys Your Ears. And It's Difficult To Switch Between Devices.
text: When you switch devices you'll have to Disconnect on the old one and Reconnect on the new one. It's a hassle. And then once you've done that, since the volume doesn't pair and adjust on the system, the headphones will destroy your ears. Regrettable purchase honestly. and the music isn't that nice from the headphones and the noise cancellation has high pitch tones sticking out. You could save your money to buy something more expensive and hopefully better than this. It suffices though so 2 stars if you're ONLY looking for something basic at this price. It won't blow you away.

title: Not durable at all. Earpiece connection to the headband is destined for failure.
text: I bought two of these headphones for my teenage daughters about 6 months ago. They seemed to have decent sound when I listened to them, although a bit bass heavy for my liking. The noise cancellation was almost entirely ineffective, but that's to be expected at this price point. What's not expected is material failure in half a year.... One of my daughters came to me today to show me that the left earpiece on her headphones had completely broken off. The joint where the earpiece connects to the band is made entirely of extremely fragile, brittle plastic with one tiny metal pin. I looked at the right earpiece and see that is cracked as well around the same joint, and would likely fail soon too. I asked my other daughter to see her headphones, and sure enough she has the same cracking around the same spots on both earpieces. On this 2nd pair, it is again the left earpiece that is showing the most damage to the joint with a piece of plastic already missing. I'm sure it is only a matter of time before the material fails completely on this pair as well. So that's a complete failure in 1 of the 4 joints, and visible damage to the other 3 joints on 2 headphones used for 6 months. I've included pictures of all 4 of those joints. Looking at other reviews, I see multiple mentions of nearly identical cracking at the same location. This joint is poorly designed given the brittle, weak materials used and it is destined to fail. Anker really needs to use some metal in this connection to make it more durable. An extra dollar in materials would go a long way towards durability. UPDATE: June 2021 - As expected, the left earpiece has now completely broken off my other daughter's headphones. That is complete structural failure at the exact same spot on both headphones less than 10 months after purchasing. I recommend you avoid this product if you are looking for something that will last more than a year.

title: Fantastic ANC and Sound
text: Amazing ANC performance, sound clarity and quality. I don't own a $300 or $400 headset but can't imagine how one could improve enough on these to make one of those a better value. These are very light weight. I listen at low volume with a TV going in the next room and I honestly can hear as though I'm totally alone in "pin drop" quiet.

title: These came today and I am loving them!
text: Only comparison I can make is against my TaoTronics Soundsurge 60s. Review is not finding fault with the TaoTronics, I've been enjoying them for around two months. Thing is, in every aspect, the Anker Soundcore Life Q20s are better! Better sound, tighter bass, lighter, more comfortable. I am happy!! Play on John Maus, play on!!!

title: Very good for the money
text: Very nice headphones. They do not fell cheap. The ear cups feel solid. The sound is loud (I tried an other brand for a similar price and the sound was very low at highest settings). Base is also solid. Let's see how long they last.

title: Can’t beat them for the price.
text: Works well so far. A little much bass for my taste, but not enough to go messing with the qualizer on my phone. Phone call quality fine, no complaints from my callers. A little warm while exercising, but not extreme. I’m sure $300 headphones would be better, but I’d rather pay $50 and get good enough. Noise cancellation is fine at low frequencies, but the highs are mostly blocked by the padding.

title: Good headphones
text: Overall I am satisfied with these. They are comfortable and sound pretty good. The look nice. They fold flat for storage. They come with a bag for storage which is okay but will not protect them. They don't connect smoothly and powering them on is a little glitchy but not a major hindrance. Overall these are good. I have had better and I have had much worse.

title: This product doesn't last
text: I dont trust this product line of headphones! This is my second replacement due to poor materials and construction. First pair lasted a few months then the headphone covers came off! The replacement broke apart at the swivel assembly while wearing around my neck! Very thin plastic parts and cheap design engineering. Sure, they sound good and Anker has an 18 month warranty, but im tiring of getting replacements that WILL break with daily use.

title: Headphones
text: I really like the look and color of these headphones. There is a large letter "L" and "R" on the inside of the headphones. They adjust about an inch on each side. The top and the ear piece are padded and very comfortable. The ear pieces rotate about 90 degrees, and they can be folded in. There is an audio jack, a mini usb port, a volume increase and decrease button, pause button, noise cancelling activation button, and power button. The volume button controls the volume on the device you have it connected to. When you press the volume button, for some reason the media stops for a second then adjusts. When you turn it on, it makes a noise and tells you the status of the battery. The headphones are pretty loud; I was able to hear what was playing clearly while holding the headphones in my hand. The sound is good too, all the bass from my sons came through and sound the same as if I was in a car. The noise cancellation comes on automatically when you turn them on. I feel like when the music is all the way up, it is noise cancelling and I cant even hear myself yelling what (not at the top of my lungs). As I turned the music down, I could begin to hear myself a little more, but I couldn't hear things outside of that (this is with the volume at about 80%). The true test was turning on my tv with my sound bar on (and it's a really good one) and I kept turning it up and didn't hear a thing. I took these headphones off and my tv was blaring, so much so that my sub woofer was vibrating the bed, but I didn't hear a thing. So, these are DEFINITELY noice cancelling.

title: Wow!
text: I would love to write something positive about these headphones. But, all I can say is that they are lightweight and comfortable. However, this is the second pair that I have had trouble with and I am extremely displeased. THE BLUETOOTH CONSTANTLY DISCONNECTS... THE HEADPHONES WILL TURN OFF (wtf) ... EVERY NOW AND AGAIN THE SOUND "FREEZES" AND STOPS PLAYING WHAT I AM LISTENING TO BUT IS REPLACED WITH AN ANNOYING BUZZING SOUND. Needless to say, I am going to get a different pair of WORKING headphones.

title: Guess I never truly experienced "noise canceling" before
text: Was getting sick of using ear buds on airplanes that despite being right on the ear and also claiming to be noise canceling could barely hear shows on my tablet. Decided to give these a try and I'm very happy I did. I finally experienced true noise canceling that you can notice when you turn it on and off and not only makes watching Netflix on a plane more enjoyable but also sounds great with music and even found the quality of making calls was decent as well! Highly recommend!

title: Excellent headphones!
text: I was tired of using ear buds. They were expensive, uncomfortable, and always were falling out. I was doing research on noise canceling headphones and always got results for the high priced ones (Bose, JBL, Sony, etc). After more research, I came across these Anker Soundcore Life Q20 Hybrid headphones. Price was fantastic, and the reviews were excellent. I was skeptical, given the price was so low, and didn't know what quality I'd get. It showed up today. I unboxed it and let it charge. It was simple to pair with my phone (though it comes with a wire if you don't have bluetooth). I fired up my Amazon music app and the sound quality was FANTASTIC. The true test would be hopping on my zero turn mower, which is the main reason I bought these. I was blown away at the noise cancellation! I sit in front of a 26HP Vanguard engine, and literally couldn't hear it when using these headphones at full volume, which isn't all that loud. Now I can mow my 20+ acres while listening to great quality music due to these awesome headphones. All the other functions work as expected too. Very easy to volume up/down, skip or go back to soundtracks. I found no need to adjust any equalizer settings, the music sounded great as is. The only thing I haven't tested was when receiving a phone call but expect that to be simple too. If you're on a budget, and looking for great quality headphones with great quality sound, you need to buy these.

title: Who Needs Beats???
text: ... bought 3 sets of these for my boys, 4th, 11th and college freshman for virtual learning during this Pandemic of 2020. They all love them and say they work great. Sure beats spending hundreds on one pair for each of them!

title: 💯 So worth the Money
text: Greatest noise cancelling headphones on the market, and after 9 hours of play, charge remains at 80% remaining. I hear nothing around me, and no one hears my music banging from these headphones.

title: Sounds the same as the Beats I bought
text: I thought they had better noise cancellation than the Beats I bought. I tried three different types of Beats and I just decided to keep these instead, since they work as well at half the price or less. I would’ve liked to have a hard carrying case. I had to buy that separately.

title: Muffled

title: I got these for study, but these are all purpose
text: I have many lectures I need to listen to for school, I got these Bluetooth headphones thinking they would be just OK...Boy was I wrong. They pair up fast, and have about a 60 foot range but the big news is the sound quality, and the noise cancelling ability. I watched a movie and paired these with the NVIDIA Shield, better than home theater, and comfortable to boot. As far as battery life, I have charged them once and have been using them for several days they claim 40 hours, so far it seems right on. Once unpaired they auto shut off to save the battery so well done there. Going over seas later this year, and I am sure these will have enough charge for the long flight. Comes with a carry bag, and the ear pieces turn sideways to pack flat. CON: If I have my cellphone too close, or between the Bluetooth transmitter there is intermittent chatter, other than that crisp connection. I also purchased from Amazon the ASUS USB-BT400 USB $14.95 at time of purchase, the two items are very compatible with each other. Good purchase, Get two to keep your roommate from taking yours when you need to study.

title: Works great

text: I bought these for my husband for Christmas. He loves them. The sound quality is great and they are comfortable. However, we noticed that plastic is breaking off the headphones which shouldn’t be happening, especially when these are less than 4 months old. I am guessing I received a defective product. title: Comfortable, and decent value.
text: No, they're not Bose. Nor are they Beats. They are simple, affordable, and comfortable budget-oriented headphones. I've owned a couple Bose headphones, and the Anker's don't really come close to a new set of Bose. But, even Bose headphones will wear out with time and use (and sometimes even without use). Comes down to how much you want to spend, and what you're using them for. Do you need a $300 pair of headphones to listen to audiobooks or cancel out the noise of the neighbor's kids playing in their driveway? I didn't.

title: Hurts ears after a while
text: I'm really enjoying them, but there ear cups are to shallow and press against the center of my ears (cartilage? Whatever it's called). Gets pretty uncomfortable after an hour or so. If the were deeper I'd buy a second pair for work.
