title: Anker stands behind the warranty
text: I've bought Anker products for ages because of the quality and price. I have been really happy with these headphones but I am posting this review because of their great customer service. The headphones have an 18 month warranty and recently I noticed that the ear cup had split on one side after 16 months of use during the COVID-19 pandemic and sharing a home office space. Anker sent replacement ear cups in a matter of days.

title: Good value and here's why
text: My sound preferences: I own the Bose Soundlink Mini, JayBird wireless ear buds and cheaper Anker ear buds-all excellent poducts. My usage for Q20: travel on airplanes, at home for music or tv via streaming device. The SoundCore Q20 are solidly built and comfortable. Sound quality is good and there's a bass boost button. Not as good as an equalizer app like JayBird but that's a cost trade-off. In listening to a variety of music I did not feel the Q20s made my listening experience bad. True, they don't have the articulation of Bose where you can hear every plink of an instrument, but overall the sound experience is good, satisfying and full. NC is okay: they will lower the noise of a dishwasher, for example, to a mild hum instead of an annoyance. There's no case, just a rubbery bag which has an unpleasant odor, so plan on an extra $13 for a case which is fine because you can choose your preferred configuration of folded or flat layout. Very good value. Recommended for people who want the function of wireless with a sturdy build and price point that doesn't make you worry about traveling with them.

title: Didn’t last long
text: This was an overall good buy at first but, after 8 months in, they started to fall apart. I’m very good about taking care of my electric items. I’ve never dropped these or anything like that. The day before yesterday I went to pick them up and the left earpiece fell apart. This was the 2nd piece to break on these. Last month a piece of the hinge covering the earpiece broke off. Had to glue it back on. Now the whole earpiece… In addition, it would lose connection from time to time with my computer during Slack and Teams meetings. I have to check the warranty as to what my next course of action is? I’d say as performance goes they’re decent but, I would be hesitant to buy these again.

title: Worth the money
text: The battery life is great, the NC works astoundingly well as my first NC phones. The quality in music is there or even for casual use. I weedwack wearing these and it blocks it out well enough for me to enjoy podcasts. The only con for me was the adjustable head strap isn't firm. We've all had those headphones that grow weak over time and stop holding an adjusted setting that slides open. I'll be outside yard working and they'll come undone ever so slightly that will pinch if I take them off and rest them on my neck. This is hardly a problem for me because they're comfortable when they are on your head. I just figured this review would help people consider something more like 3M's line if they're outside moving around. I'll wear these all night on the computer or take them on a trip.

title: Great value, works well for phone calls
text: I've been using these for about 6 weeks as I work remotely from home. They are the first pair of noise cancelling headphones that I've ever had and maybe my expectations for the noise cancelling feature was a little too high. For consistent noises they are very good. For my three kids running around the house yelling, they are helpful but definitely don't block out most of that sound. I think if you need the noise cancelling feature to be awesome, you might have to upgrade to a different price range. That said, the battery life has been great. And most of all, the phone call quality has far exceeded my expectations. From reading reviews prior to purchase, other people made them seem maybe okay for listening to calls, but unusable for speaking on calls (i.e. the mic was bad somehow). I'm not sure if they upgraded mic components or what, but I've asked a half dozen people that I've spoke with about the call quality and everyone has said it's been great. Overall, very pleased.

title: Great sound and noise cancellation, but plastic has already broken
text: These headphones are fairly comfortable and produce a good quality sound - deep bass and high treble, good active noise cancellation that cuts down on external low-frequencies. My only problem with it is the plastic piece that is at the end of each side of the faux-leather headband part. One of them broke off entirely, and the other is on it's way. This doesn't really interfere with the functionality of the headphones, at least not at this time, but it does make me nervours that other parts of plastic will eventually break as well. I'm not super gentle with my headphones, so if you are, this may never happen to you. They've probably slipped off my bed a few times and fallen on the floor from a couple feet up, which is probably what caused this. But for the plastic pieces I mention are either at a particular angle or are made with a particularly brittle type of plastic such that they would be the only parts of the headphone effected - at least so far. If this is all that breaks, well, the only real downside is that they don't look as nice. Given their relatively low price, I guess this is not a huge shock, so I'll only dock them one star, but if you want something that's a bit more durable, you might look at some higher-priced headphones that don't have this potential issue.

title: Failure is like peeling an onion
text: How can a product with all these 5 star reviews be so bad? First, did I accidentally order the child size? Nope they're really that small. These are built to look like an over-the-ear headset. They're not, the ear piece is way too small. These are on ear sized, no adult's ears are that small. They're way to heavy to practically be used on-ear. Second the sound quality of the microphone is horrifying. I'd describe the voice quality as underwater in a steel drum, drowning. The noises can't be recognized as human speech. While the headset easily paired with my desktop, they didn't even show up in either of two android phones. Finally when connected by USB they cause the PC to continuously connect and then fail to recognize the headset. This repeats constant;y every few seconds. So you can't really charge these by connecting to a PC.You have to use a power brick. Pros: Decent sound playback. Cons: Can't be connected to a USB port for charging. title: Good Headphones but has Limitations
text: Overall, the LifeQ20 is good, but it has limitations that are not clearly listed in the Amazon product description. For example: 1. if you want to use the headphones to listen to TV, they cut off the sound from the TV, so no one else can hear TV. 2. if you want to use them with a computer (tried with new iMac), you need to use the enclosed 4' cable. 3. if you want to use the headphones with a phone, there is no built-in mic

title: Great Headphones!
text: I'm not tech savvy..but these headphones are great! I can block out my grandkids playing while I'm on my laptop.

title: So far so good
text: I bought these partly because I wanted some noise cancelling headphones and partly because my new phone and tablet require bluetooth. These seem to work really well. I haven't used them much outside of the house nor have I really put the noise cancelling technology to the test but so far these seem comfortable and durable. The price is affordable so it was worth taking a chance. If you are looking for a reasonably priced set of headphones with Bluetooth and noise cancelling ability, maybe give these a try. I do have to admit that this is my first pair of noise cancelling headphones so I don't have a lot to compare them to.

title: Excelent price and quality!
text: This headphones are AMAZING! I bought it for my 11 years son, and he loves it! Good price, perfect size, lightweight, amazing sound!

title: High-end headphones at a reasonable price!
text: These were a replacement for a 5-year old pair of Anker headphones that had some sort of short. These are even better than what I had, and I really like them! They are lightweight, comfortable, and have great sound quality -- all with noise cancellation. Right after I got them, I took them on a flight, and they cut out ALL the noise of the plane's roaring and the overhead announcements -- it was wonderful! Highly recommend these headphones. +++

title: Will not charge
text: They sound really good but I only had them for a couple months and used them a few times. The second time I tried to charge them they will not charge anymore. I bought them for wireless capabilities so they are useless to me.

title: Loves them
text: Bought as a gift for my teenager. He really likes them, sound quality is good, crisp. The noise cancellation isn't as good as others he's had. However, the quality is great for the price. Battery life is excellent! He wears these about 70% of his day.

title: Okay, Not Great
text: I have a number of Anker products at home. Their products are bargain priced and good. However, I was not particularly impressed with these headphones at the price. When I buy headphones, I want them well-made, comfortable, with good sound. I travel for a living. ANC is important to me. I normally use Bose QC35s. Granted, the cost is a lot more, but if you are in need of noise cancelling look somewhere else. These cans are relatively comfortable, but you don't want to wear them for 5+ hours on a plane. For the price, these are good if you want pretty good sound and noise cancelling.

title: Noise cancelled
text: I had several headphones claim “noise cancellation” with these you can 100 percent tell the difference. I drive a truck, and they cut down on the road noise tremendously.

title: Great Value
text: These headphones are a great value. For the price, you get a sturdy feeling set of comfortable over ear headphones. The sound quality isn't super amazing, but for the price is very good. The sound could be a little crisper and bass a little deeper. The noise cancellation isn't comparable to some of the higher end products out there, but compared to other headphones I tried in this price range, they outperform the competitors. I stood in my living room with the dryer running and TV on, and the noise cancellation is noticeable, although not complete. I could still hear the dryer and TV, but their sound was muffled so with music playing I could barely hear the TV or dryer. I think this is a great buy for the price. No use going out to buy fancy Bose or Sony noise cancelling headphones, these work just fine.

title: PS5 Owners Beware
text: If this works with PS5, it’s not trivial to pair it. My guess is I need to spend more money on an adapter. Not sure if that will work. **25-APR-2022 Update** I was contacted by customer support and they have been very helpful in offering to help and/or assist with a full refund. That said, I stand by my statement that anyone purchasing this to work wirelessly with a PS5; beware. I am in the process of exploring adapters to achieve this, but I do not believe this product will work (sound and voice) with a PS5 out of the box. I am not getting into the discussion of whether this is an issue with the design of these headphones or the design of the PS5. My intent here is to ensure that anyone looking for headphones to work with the PS5 may be better served by other products.

title: Great Value

title: Very comfortable!
text: I use these to listen to my books. I can even vacuum and not be disrupted. Lol. Very comfortable and good sound quality.

title: Sound Amazing - Construction Not So Amazing
text: I bought these back in March, so have had them less than a year. The sound is amazing and the comfort is great. The noice cancelling helps alot when there are sounds in the house I don't want to hear, even if I'm not listening to music. I can easily connect them to my MacBookPro, as well as my iPad and iPhone, even my Amazon Fire TV stick. Even using them for phone and Zoom calls is great. Overall they are great headphones....except fore one thing. The plastics around the hinges suck. I had seen a crack in the plastic above the left headphone about a month ago, but this morning piece of plastic fell off, I wouldn't have known about it had it not hit my chest or I had eventually seen there was missing plastic. Turns out that when the headphones are on my head, the way that they adjust causes the hinge to put undo pressure on the outside plastic and thus weakens it to the point of it breaking. I still have full functionality which works for me but makes me wonder if sometime soon the hinge is just going to fail altogether and then I'm out a great sounding pair of headphones, for which I could probably do a warranty claim for, but then I'll end up with a refurbished pair as a replacement which will probably be someone else's problem that got replaced. Doesn't appear that Soundcore did any QC testing on this design, otherwise they would have known that there is an obvious design failure with the hinge assembly. I'm no engineer but even I can see the design flaw with these. I don't throw these headphones around and I very rarely fold them up, they usually just hand off the corner of my desk or are laid down when I'm not using them, so there has been no stress put upon them other than when I use them....it comes down to this....I baby the heck out of these headphones. But considering I paid roughly $50 for them, it doesn't surprise me that they are already breaking.....the sound is great for $50, but you need to have just as good of a shell to make the headphones wonderful, otherwise customers will just go somewhere else

title: Horrible support , no support for defective units
text: I am changing my review to F. Anker has the worst outsourced support I have encountered in some time. I have had 4 pair of these headphones. So far 2 have been defective. Noise canceling fails when you plug into the Aux jack. Support is out sourced to India and they just ask the same question over and over about the Invoice. You send it and they keep asking for it. The communication is horrible. You can't talk to anyone in real time and the response time is in days not hours. Anker seems to have horrible quality control as these are not the only products I have had that failed in the last few months. For this reason I do not recommend this product as greed has yet again killed another company.

title: Almost awesome, but returning....
text: For the price, these are absolutely brilliant, with one huge major exception that caused me to return them. First the good: - Price! - Comfort! - Sound! - Actual physical buttons instead of magic swipy controls. I hate capacitive headphone control. Everyone hates capacitive headphone control. It's a cute idea for a demo, and a terrible way to actually use headphones. - Carry-bag + headphone cables included. Yes a case would have been better but....50$. - I liked them more than my Wyze headphones, which are closer to the Q30 price point. The pretty good: - Call quality. - Noise cancellation (except....). - Decent battery life. The less good: - Micro-USB charging; but hey 50$. - The lack of app support The bad and cause for return: - Noise cancellation in my set had a dealbreaker bug. Under some conditions it would generate a rattle/wind-buffeting sound. This would only happen under some conditions, and it would go away if I rebooted them, and it didn't happen with noise cancellation turned off. However this would happen many, many, many times a day, and made these otherwise awesome headphones unusable. Pity. I don't know if my specific sample was defective, or if this is a general issue, but for me this was a no-go.

title: Works great for the $
text: Just as good as the 10yr old $150 Sony over-ear noise cancelling headphones it replaced. So what if it’s not the $500 Bose units, it’s good enough for me. Mainly use it on planes as it allows me to sleep. For those not schooled in noise cancelling it does not eliminate noise. It only cancels out noises that are constant like an airplanes engines. Does not cancel babies or talking. But if you connect these to a music/sound source it will mask the talking and babies.

title: Great sound quality, terrible mechanical quality
text: I have had these heaphones for about 4 months. I really enjoy the sound quality, and the noise cancelation. Unfortunately the mechanical strength of the headband is not up to the same standard. I noticed some cracks by the joint of the headphones a couple weeks ago, and today the right ear cup fell off. I do wear the headphones for 6-8 hours a day five days a week, but I would expect that to be well within normal usage. If I can get a replacement or get them repaired, I will update this review. Update: After reaching out to Anker, they sent out a replacement set of headphones. The communication with the customer service was a little confusing as I think they mixed my case up with someone else's, but it got sorted in the end. I got my replacement, and everything is working great so far. If these end up breaking, I'll do another update.

title: INCREDIBLE SOUND AND COMFORT..... bad construction.....
text: CONS: So this will be my third pair, 2 were replacements. I only use them inhouse for gaming and for walks. The hinge area, where the cups fold is VERY WEAK. The construction doesn't keep into consideration that when put on the ears it creates stress particularly to that area. So the more you wear it the more tension is placed there. It creates micro cracks. Eventually it cracks. PROS: AMAZING SOUND. Very nice midtones and treble with balanced bass. The customer service for this company is TOP NOTCH.

title: Brilliant customer service by Rochelle @ Anker.
text: I bought these two months ago. They feel great and sound great too. But every once in a while the headphones just turned off. I brushed it off and just turned it on again, and repaired my phone to continue listening. But now my headphones turn off every two minutes or so, which is really frustrating. I'm talking to a friend one minute and the next I'm trying to repair my headphones to my phone because it just randomly turned off mid conversation. TLDR: PROS: sound and feel good. CONS: they turn off randomly every two minutes, rendering them useless. EDIT: Brilliant customer service by Rochelle @ Anker. Anker really tried to make me happy by sending out an alternative product at no cost to me, I would recommend you give Anker a fair chance to work with their nonconformances on the product.

title: Geat Value!
text: I've own a set for about six months and couldn't be more pleased. They're an incredible value, it seems to me. I say "it seems to me," because this is the first set of noise-cancelling headphones. I'd considered buying a set before but was discouraged by the high price. Hence, I can't make comparative judgements about their audio-quality. I can only report on my experience. I use them when I work in my shop, mow the lawn and drive in my somewhat noise truck. They do a fine job blocking out enough of the ambient noise that I don't have to crank up the volume to levels that would surely damage my eardrums. Sure, I can still hear the background sounds, so it's not like walking into a padded recording studio. They do tend to slip off when I'm bending down, but that's a minor irritant. They haven't shattered or been damaged despite the many times they've hit the pavement. They're very durable. For the money, they strike me as an incredible value. I wouldn't hestitate to recommend them to all but the rare audiophile in the pursuit of perfect sound in the middle of hurricane.

title: A purchase you won’t regret!

title: Finally some peace with my loud family!
text: These are great , definitely make noises less loud around me. My kids are always loud and my husband blares the tv bc he cant hear. These headphones help a lot and the sound for movies and music are great. I believe these are a good price for quality.

title: Not my favorite but they sound good.
text: I bought these to replace my $300 Bose quiet comfort 35 headphones which crapped out on me. I LOVED my Bose but I could not justify another $300 for something that didn’t last long as it should have. (My uncle also had to replace his also. That spells quality problems to me.) For $60 these Q20 are not bad. The bass on these is ridiculous. I like more bass but I have to keep the “bass up” turned off - there’s more than enough without the bass up turned on. Only thing I don’t like about them is they are slightly too tight on my very average (maybe slightly smaller) head. (I wear a 7 1/4 size military camo hat if that tells you anything.) I get a headache from the squeeze. I just got them today so I’m not sure how that is going to work over out time. That being said, the foam ear cups are very comfortable - like the Bose if you’ve ever tried those on. It loses a star for the tight fit and because the instructions are horrible. I had to search the internet for a few things because the makers apparently can’t spell enough to write things out. Im of an older generation and appreciate instructions *without guess work.* They can only draw very light blue pictographs that are hard to see on white paper with all the explanations in symbols. I don’t know if I would recommend these or not. The tight fit would be the reason I would advise against.

title: No one seems to make good-quality earbuds any more.
text: My wife got these for me for Christmas because my old, $16 (like 25 year old) Sony ear hook buds finally fell apart. I've been writing a book and using Speechify for editing, using these earbuds. Initially, I liked that there were different sized silicone pieces to fit different size ear-holes. The sound quality seemed fine, and they were a bit bulky, a bit loose, but seemed not bad for $20. So now (1/10/21, or 17 days later) the charging port broke loose from the solder joints which affixed it to the little printed circuit board inside. Anyone who knows anything about wiring and electronics can tell you that a solder joint on a circuit board is inadequate to secure something that is going to have pressure put on it repeatedly due to plugging and unplugging. Obviously no one at Senso thought of this, or cared enough to put it into practice. This is all part of a larger problem which is what is known as 'planned obsolescence' or put simply 'making things cheap so they break quickly (usually just after warranty expires) and you have to buy another one'. It's happened to phones (buy a new iPhone every 2 years), audio equipment, cars, televisions, and computers (don't get me started on the crap Dell sells, and forget getting any support from them). AMAZON, if you're LISTENING, stop selling CRAP from SHADY SELLERS! Stop allowing companies to bribe customers for 5-star reviews. It makes reviews worthless and untrustworthy. Also, your buyers are obviously getting kickbacks, or if not they are terrible at judging quality. Either way, I cannot find good Bluetooth earbuds anywhere on the site. Even the Beats audio ones you sell for $110 are lousy with quality issues. Disappointed, AMAZON. You own the internet but you can't sell quality electronics to save your lives.

text: This review is for the ActivBuds S-250. I like these earbuds very much. They have a long playing time and have a pleasing sound quality. I use them with Comply foam tips which greatly improve the comfort and sound. Comply tips come in a variety of sizes, shapes, and sound isolation and are a positive addition to any buds. One improvement I would like to see would be cloth braided connecting cable between the two buds. The rubber cable sticks to the back of my neck sometimes and it will dislodge the buds from one or both ears. I usually wear them with the cable in front of my neck and flip it to the back if I am going to take them out. I like these earbuds because the controls are easy to use and are ergonomically designed. The charge plug is easy to put in and the buds hold a charge for a long time. The playing time is quite good and is at least equal to the time claimed by the vendor. All in all a comfortable set of buds with sweet sound. (I also have a set of the S-255 buds and am not happy with the flimsy ear hooks. Fortunately, the Comply foam tips keep them in my ears as the hooks are quite useless.) I have several pair of these buds because I have a number of Bluetooth sources and the buds, like most Bluetooth devices will only pair to two at a time. Bluetooth 5, which will be released any day now, is claimed to allow several devices to pair.

title: Excellent audio for meetings, good overall sound for everything else
text: My primary use for these headphones is for meetings using Skype for Business. I've had these headphones for a week now and have used them for over 15 hours of meetings in that time, paired with my laptop. The most important thing for me was whether my audio was good enough according to the other persons on our group calls, and they agreed that the sound coming through was very clear. I also could hear very well, so I am pleased with the end result and the quality overall. Pairing with the iPhone was a snap; the Kindle Fire HDX was not as cooperative, but eventually it paired well and the sound is very good. My Windows 10 laptop is a bit more challenging to pair and manage, BUT that's not the fault of the headphones, it's just a bit tricky to figure out which setting controls the levels for my audio. Once I found that among the Windows settings, it was fine. As soon as I turn on the headphones, The ActiveBuds connect promptly to the laptop. As noted by another reviewer, the placement of the On/Off button is a little awkward; you do feel like you're pushing the right earbud further into your ear canal. But with a lighter touch and a slightly different angle, you can power on and off without difficulty. I found the volume up/down tricky because you press the front of the toggle switch to turn it down rather than the back end. But both of these are minor, and once you get the hang of it, they're not an issue. I have watched and listened to TV and movies on my Kindle and my iPhone, and the overall sound quality is quite good. I'm not listening to music with a great bass beat, so I can't comment on that, but I am an audiophile. For the price and ease of use, these headphones are everything I need. When I want to listen to classical music, I put on my big headphones anyway. These SENSO headphones fit neatly in my purse, and I'm very pleased with them.

title: Battery issues resolved through a reset
text: Great sound quality and I enjoyed them until a week ago when they stopped charging. It doesn't matter which charger I use, they charge all night and notify me of "low battery" as soon as I wear them. They lasted almost 3 months :/ *** UPDATE: The customer service from Invotek is prompt and outstanding. They were willing to do a full refund if a reset didn't work, but gave me instructions on how to do it, and the issue has resolved. In case you have the same issue or any other malfunction, here's the snippet from the email with instructions on how to do resolve it: "Let's try a factory reset for your Senso headphones which usually fixes most similar issues related to the issue you are facing with your headphones. 1. Reset the Senso headphone to factory settings (while plugged into a power source, press/hold the power button for 7 seconds). 2. Unplug the headphone from charging cable and power them on. 3. Enter the earbuds into the pairing mode and follow instructions for connecting. Also, the issue you have described is common all Bluetooth devices as the connection between the two devices gets "corrupted" and needs to be re-configured. In order to do that, please `Forget the Device` on your mobile phone for the Senso headphones and try pairing again. In your Bluetooth settings on your phone, you will see all detected Bluetooth devices. Click on the Senso ActivBuds option and click on Forget this Device. Next pair your headphones to your mobile device once again as shown in the instructions manual. I am confident that this will fix your issue. Also, you are covered by our 1 Year Warranty, so you have nothing to worry about in case these don't work." I have many pairs of Bluetooth headphones and these are my favourite due to comfort and sound quality. So happy they are working perfectly again!

For me, as every day headphones, this is totally fine. For an airplane or a loud situation, I'd probably still opt for higher end headphones (bose, etc), but these are very good for day to day stuff. They stay in place, don't shift around, and all of the controls are easily on the headphones, so you can turn them on/off, adjust the volume, etc. without having to touch your phone. For the price, these are great, comfortable headphones for blue tooth enabled devices.

text: I bought these over two years ago and they have held up with no issues yet. The sounds quality for me is fine. If you're expecting audiophile SQ, these aren't for you but if you want to enjoy your music while on a run and still be cognizant of your surroundings these are great. I am a heavy sweater when I exercise and have never had an issue with these crapping out due to moisture. As a comparison in the past I had two pairs of Sport? Power? (can't recall exact name) Beats that broke from sweat/moisture. The earbuds still charge quickly and hold a charge for a long time. I had a pair of Jaybirds that suddenly would not charge or even turn on after less than a year. One thing that I did notice with these, the Bluetooth sensor must be on the right side and you will want to run or carry your phone on your right arm or side. Otherwise you do get some cutting out of the music. It took me a couple of runs to figure this out. And the more stationary (use an arm band vs keep in pocket) the better. But overall these earbuds work like champs at a fraction of the price of the other big names out there.

title: Update: Does not work anymore (Was: "They keep going even when wet")
text: Update: They only lasted a few months. They simply just don't work now. Wasted my money. Look elsewhere. Original Review: I did really well with this. I kept accidentally going underwater with it during deep water exercise. Just below the surface, but the first time, the USB jack was not closed up and nothing went wrong. I should mention that I wasn't swimming laps with it. It did come off a few times, but not to the level of being annoying. Unfortunately, I've lost it. I now have to figure out if I am going to buy that waterproof MP3 watch for a few hundred bucks or buy another one of these. One thing to note: I did use this outside and the range is limited to 15ft if the mp3 player is not with you. I used my phone which I kept on the side of the pool. If you do use a phone to stream music, attach the phone to a portable battery charger or your phone will start skipping the stream in about 10-15 minutes. It's just trying to conserve battery for all the tasks it's performing. This is an argument for getting the mp3 waterproof watch, btw.

title: All around a fair quality for the price.
text: I've bought several of these over the last year. It seems that each one lasts at least a few months before issues arise, but that's nothing new for earphones, at least in my experience. The sound quality is great, and it fits comfortably in my ear. The package comes with different-sized earbuds, so anyone concerned by that should rest assured; it is possible to change them out for comfort. The battery life is about 10-12 hours on average which is nice. The range is around 8 feet if the right earbud(where the signal is received) is pointing to whatever the Bluetooth is connected to such as your pc, phone, etc. If not, the signal will cut out fairly quickly which can get annoying. Another thing that may not annoy you, but it certainly did me, is the part that loops around your ears. It gets old fast, and the earbuds stay in your ears regardless of the loops being there or not so I always decide to cut them off. As far as I'm aware it does not damage them in any way, and I certainly have never seen a reduction in listening quality because of it.

title: Decent sound, but....
text: These Senso wireless earbuds had surprisingly good sound for such an inexpensive item. They were so loud, in fact, that I actually kept the volume on my iPod turned down to the minimum while I used these for working out. That said, I always found the flat cable between them a little awkward, as it would never lay flat and always seemed to want to move to one side or another. It also, because of the nature of it being flat, would hold the shape from having been in the (nice) hard case, which also prevented it laying flat. The most disappointing thing was that, after less than a year of use, it suddenly started just skipping songs randomly. A song would start, and just a few seconds in, my iPod would jump to the next song, as if I had pressed the button on the right earbud. It would sometimes do this multiple times in a row and then stop on its own. As well, the volume up button on the earbud now seemed stuck (and I don't abuse these - just normal use during workouts) so that it doesn't press in or click like the volume down button does. Unfortunately, customer support was even more disappointing. I contacted them in November and they promptly replied apologizing for the trouble and asking for pictures to be passed on to the warranty department. I sent the pictures the same day and have not been able to get a response from anyone there since. Needless to say, I will not be recommending nor buying any Senso products in the future.

title: Never knew what I was missing
text: These are phenomenal headphones. I didn't realize the kinds of ambient noise I had around me until after I used this for a while. I bought other fancy headphones in the past, which usually had cables and ended up broken when I tripped across it. These are wireless, with a volume control built in. (You can still plug them in if you like, but I never do that.) When I got them in the mail, they worked perfectly. Then, after an update, for a while, the software was a bit glitchy and would randomly beep. But at some point they must've fixed that in another update, after a year or so. Because they work perfectly again. One downside is that the microphone isn't really worth having on it. In order to use the microphone, you have to put the headphones into "headset" "communications device" mode, which doesn't properly do sound cancelling. Worse, it sounds like someone is playing back the audio from outside the headphones. I never use that mode, because I can't stand it. I also wish that I could stream (mix) two wireless sources at once. While speaking on the microphone. I often want to listen to a show on one device, and a video game on another, while possibly talking into a microphone. There isn't a solution for this. For my purpose, I connect to a small bluetooth adapter, and plug that into the line-in jack on my PC. Then I check the "listen to this" button for that line-in, so that I can hear the second audio source. But despite any and all drawbacks, I am very happy with my headphones and would buy them again.

title: For comfort it's Bose, for sound it's Sony.
text: I purchased the Sony headphones and the Bose QuietComfort 35 (Series II) set because the reviews were so close and I wasn't sure which ones I would like better. While the Bose were definitely more comfortable and the case was large enough to fit the charging cord and headphone jack, the sound did not quite measure up. I did like the on/off switch of the Bose headphones better and the Bose app, but I love the Sony headphones for the following reasons. The sound is phenomenal...it's transforming. I took them on a recent flight and it was like being in another world...no noisy discussions or engine noise, just a beautiful series of sounds that volleyed from one ear to the next. It's easy to change tracks, adjust volume, or stop play by simply swiping or tapping the outside of the right earpiece. The Sony app is fairly easy to use, too, including a way to adjust if your connection cuts in and out. I didn't experience that with the Sony, but did with the Bose. If I could have chosen the comfort of the Bose with the sound of the Sony (and the convenient swipe feature) I would never take them off!

title: NO USER MANUAL IS AVAILABLE FOR THIS PRODUCT!
text: Everybody should be aware that this is a complex, sophisticated product which is shipped completely without instructions. Also, it is shipped without a charger, and nowhere mentions that the battery needs to be charged. Is it in fact rechargeable? - I am guessing so but there is no information about battery care. The only clue is a link to the Bose website, whereupon under this product it says "There is no user manual available for this product". By the way, I am a Ph.D in electronics of the kind who builds his own computers. The dissatisfied, desperate purchaser of this product can download snippets of information on how to achieve various objectives. For example there is quite a useful one which tells you which control button is which. But for $349 Bose owes the purchaser some instructions instead of leaving him/her to flail around trying to find by experiment and trial and error how to use it. I feel insulted! I wanted a product, not a research project - I have better things to do with my time. In my opinion Bose are trying to turn off their customers, and are succeeding at least as far as this customer goes.

title: Excellent product, but wired users may not like the 2.5 mm audio jack.
text: I selected the Bose 35ii after extensive research and am very pleased with comfort, audio quality, and performance. A key aspect of my selection was the wired connection that I often need, as with in-flight entertainment systems. (I would have bought the Bose 30 earbud design but, amazingly, it lacks a wired connection). My only disappointment with the 35ii is that the audio jack is not the standard 3.5 mm (1/8 inch) style that we have known and loved for about 50 years. Instead, the phones have a 2.5 mm jack. I did not see this noted in any of the many reviews that I read---they all mention a standard audio connection. The phones come with a cable that plugs into the 2.5 mm jack and provides a standard 3.5 mm plug on the other end. But for the life of me I cannot even guess why a 3.5 mm wasn't used on the phones themselves so that any standard cable could be used. So if wired connection is important to you be advised that you may wantto buy an additional (more robust and longer) adapter cable, and I do see some on Amazon. Apparently the smaller jack is used on other headphones as well. But why? Makes no sense to me.

title: What kind of idiot would pay $300 dollars for headphones? Me.
text: Back when I used to spend my days fumbling with earbud wires, I wondered "What kind of idiot would pay $300 dollars for headphones, when you can hear your sounds perfectly fine for less than $10?". Even as these products rose more and more to popularity, I scoffed and resisted. Those days are long gone. After I borrowed them from my friend for a day and tried them myself, I knew why. After getting them, these quickly became a non-negotiable part of my life. I use them to: - take and receive meetings - freely go pee, refill coffee, and wash my dishes while listening to a meeting - go on runs while listening to music - ignore noisy people around me - get myself into a state of focus - calm my anxiety on airplanes - show people I am not interested to talk to them - as a fashion statement Seriously, I wear these so much I think I am developing a bald spot. Maybe that's why all the engineers are bald. The sound quality is superb, and so is the bluetooth range and connectivity. I have since tried the Sony's, Dolby dimensions, the newer model of these, but these are the best one. I have bought a pair for my whole family, and replaced my old pair when it got old without a second thought. One time, I tried my friend's airpods and almost threw up at the sound quality. Not to mention, with this size, they are much harder to lose. These are my favorite product of the last several years (this, and the divacup) and I would wholeheartedly recommend!

text: Received the headphones today, removed them from the case, zipped the case shut. I then realized I had left the audio cable in the case. Went to open the case and the zipper stuck. Had to wrap the headphones in bubble wrap to send them back to Amazon because I couldn’t get them in the case. Update: I’ve updated my rating from 1 star to three...why? I decided that since I had them I might as well listen to them. I wasn’t so interested in noise cancelling as I was the sound, so I tested them with NC turned off. I thought they sounded very good - excellent. I wasn’t impressed with the volume though. I only turned them up to around 2/3 rds volume and they seem kind of low for the price plus I noticed the bass got pushed back at that volume, I assume to stop distortion. They have a large leap in volume around 60 - 65% up. Too bad about the zipper getting stuck the first time I zipped the case. I tried everything to get them unzipped but I was afraid I was going to damage the case. But if Amazon/Bose wants the audio cable back (its in the case) they will have to destroy the case to get in it. UPDATE 2: The first pair I had did not have good Bluetooth range. I would move about 15 feet in any direction (a wall was between the headphones and iPhone) and they would cut out. So I decided to buy another pair but silver this time. The logic behind silver is that I read that different colored iPhones are made at two different facility’s in case there is a disaster at one facility they can continue to make iphones at the other one. So my logic was that maybe the silver QC35 ll was made at a different facility with slightly different parts (Bluetooth module). Not sure if that is correct but the silver headphones goes anywhere in the house without dropping the signal. The house is 2800 sq ft upstairs plus basement. UPDATE 3: Returning. I've tried various ear plugs, but those haven't been effective enough for blocking the noises, so I figured I'd try active noise-cancelling headphones. These do not work for that purpose. I have the noise cancelling function set on "high," but I can still hear the TV downstairs, footsteps nearby and chatting a few rooms away. It blocks has blocked out a very limited range of background road noise (noises like revving engines are still heard), but simply isn't doing what it claims to be able to do: cancel noise. I'm desperate here - does anyone happen to have suggestions for headphones that actually cancel noise? I've been playing brown noise in the background when I try to sleep, but the constant auditory input in my life is driving me crazy and I want to be able to simply block out the noise. I just need some quiet time while I'm trying to rest. :(

title: 'Pure heaven, now that my smart phone EQ is set to 'Off'
text: While I don't have the audiophile's experience and passion I know what I like when I hear it, and I value great sound. I received my silver Bose QC 35 Series II wireless headphones yesterday, free of charge, courtesy of a bank card rebate (so is it really free? a debate for another thread...), and paired them with my iPhone 7 Plus. Based on my experience yesterday I would have granted the Bose QC 35 Series II just 4 stars. They sounded OK... still, while they lacked the high end sharpness/contrast/clarity/depth I value in premium sound they have a number of tech features I enjoy. Today it occurred to me to adjust the equalizer on my iPhone to see if I can get more out of my Bose QC 35 IIs (on my iPhone the pathway to EQ is: Settings-->Music-->EQ). My EQ was set to Late Night. I turned off my iPhone EQ, and, holy c&@p! Now that the EQ is off I could live in these, seriously. I enjoy using them with Roku, using the headphones setting on the Roku app in my iPhone 7 Plus. My fave TV programs, movies and music sound like magic to my ears. 'Pure heaven.

title: First time buyer
text: This is my first time using a noise cancelling headphone. I picked Bose because I own other Bose products. The price was what kept me from buying them sooner. Sound quality is fantastic and they're amazingly flexible. What impresses me the most is the noise cancelling, it works fantastic.

title: Great heaphones, Bluetooth needs help
text: Let me start off by saying, these are the best headphones I've ever had. I love them. They sound amazing, fit great and are very good for an active lifestyle. I have only one issue with them: One of the advertised features is that you can connect to 2 devices and the headphones will intelligently detect which device is sending audio and sound it to your ears. This has been very glitchy for me. I have a Macbook Pro and a Galaxy S7. When it is connected to both devices, it will always prioritize my Macbook, even if no audio is coming from the macbook and audio IS coming from my galaxy. This is my only gripe with the product. Other than that, I love it. Send me any test products that you would like me to test and review.

title: Completely died after a year and a half.
text: These Bose headphones were the joy of my Dad’s life, until the padded right earphone completely came apart. Then it just died! And Dad died without being able to listen to orchestral music for the last excruciatingly painful month of his life, which happened two months before he was once again able to hear his Beethoven, Brahms, and Mahler, sounding SO magnificent!! In addition to that, he could have been comforted with a much better product. Don’t get me completely wrong; I was grateful for the amount of money you gave us. But $200 for a product that was $329.00 plus when I purchased it? And nothing else made him at least partially comfortable for the last month of his life. I just thought you should know that he suffered greatly! I’m not looking for sympathy….but a little empathy and a replacement for a man who was a great physician for 65 years, a man whose skills saved hundreds of lives, would have transitioned much easier with a much more decent product. Customer service shouldn’t die, especially when a product as good as a Bose set of headphones dies a month before it could have been worth it. A mega-wealthy company like Bose (and you) left us both with nothing but a pain-filled month of death and sorrow.

title: Amazing comfort, crisp clear sound, and absolutely no background noise. Superb!
text: Bose more or less invented (with other companies working in parallel) noise cancelling headphones, and while there is an emphasis on style, marketing, and hype--these are legit. No weird sound, eerily free of background noise, and supremely comfortable. If you want the best noise cancelling headphones--these or the original QC35 are it. The box was surprisingly small--so much so, I wondered if these weren't full sized over the ear headphones. They are, albeit with a very justified focus on folding compactly. The box opens to a minimal experience with the nearly fully charged headphones in the included case. Accessories are the case, a bizarrely shorty micro USB cable, and an analog cable. The included instructions are absolutely minimal (unless I missed the larger one I found online) and basically direct you to the app. This created a modest issue, as I was diligently charging the headphones, and lo and behold, they cannot be paired when charging. They cannot do anything but be passive headphones while charging--no wonder they have such a short USB cord! Problem solved either with holding off on charging (as noted they were nearly fully charged) or via the analog in. They sound OK with analog in, but great with NC (available via Bluetooth or analog in, but not while charging). The Bluetooth quality is pretty darn good, though it's not really clear what codec is in use. I use these largely for audiobooks and podcasts, but they hold their own for music at common sound levels with some issues at loader levels or with more demanding tracks. Bose isn't known for an unaltered sound profile, neither are most noise cancelling headphones, so I wasn't surprised to hear the somewhat sculpted sound, which many won't notice and most would like anyway. All in all, I love these for work. I had a frankly better sounding pair of Audio Technica studio monitors, but they lacked noise cancelling, had a cable, and weren't as comfortable (I have a giant head). I'll save those for at home. They're great headphones, but these are the perfect set for the office. I've been known to proclaim "No highs, no lows, must be Bose!" in relation to various Bose speaker systems, but I've always enjoyed their noise cancelling products (alas from afar, never owning any), and I love these.

title: Great Headphones
text: I really like these headphones. The sound is awesome. The noise cancellation is excellent. I especially like that they are wireless.

title: Best headphones I have ever purchased
text: I was frustrated with a cheaper pair of headphones, so decided to invest in these, despite the outrageous price. I fell in love the very first use, and knew I made the right decision! I only use these when I fly, but I could not imagine flying without these. The noise cancelling works so well I wear these even when not listening to music to block out all of the noise of the plane and passengers. They also have great sound and I can wear them for 10+ hours without any discomfort. These are the best headphones on the market!

title: Comfort with a blast
text: The headphones arrived within three days. Setup up is completely dummy proof (thank goodness). The quality of sound is better then any other wireless systems I’ve tried before. Well worth the money and made this music buff very happy.

title: Ok but a little over rated
text: I feel like they're a little over rated, yes they cancel out noise better than most of the competition but the sound hasn't exactly blown me away. Also, im always Taking public transportation to get to work, the bus goes through the freeway and as soon as the road gets bumpy I start to hear stutters of air which ruins the sound and cuts it off.

title: Damn thing works great!
text: I bought this because my family was too noisy. Once I put it on, I forgot I had a family. It made me miss them so I had to take it off. But yeah, damn thing works great at cancelling out noise you don’t want to hear.

title: Impressive
text: These aren't specifically for base sonthe base is good. But I've had base booster headphones that had better base. The house cancelation is very impressive and adds to the sound

title: A bit expensive for sound quality
text: It blocks out low frequency noise like a plane engine but I could still hear a baby crying in the background. The sound is good for music when listening via Bluetooth but the sound is only ok for movies and shows with the cable. With the rumble of the plane engine, it almost wasn't loud enough to hear the dialogue. I had to turn the volume on my tablet up all the way.

title: Worth every penny.
text: These are amazing. Almost balked at the price, so glad I didn’t.

title: Love love love
text: Love them. Use them on noise-cancelling at my damn loud gym to keep my sanity and hearing. Would caution against using them outside though. Couldn’t hear the world outside my own head.

title: Meant for phones, not computers
text: Pretty obvious when the user manual states "how to connect to your mobile device" I spent all day struggling to get it to pair to my computer or bluetooth transmitter, but it didn't work. I can only recommend if you're only going to be using this for your phone. Ears hurt from having sound cancelling on all day with no noise. Audio quality not as good as when using an audio jack, but it's wireless so I can forgive that. Works seamlessly with my phone. Voice saying that you're connected/not is loud and not controllable, but at least I can disable that almost immediately.

title: Comfortable and noise canceling works great
text: These headphones are made really well. I bought these so I can study for my CPA exams while I’m at home with my kids. The noise cancelation works very well. Sometimes I find myself wearing them with no sound, just the noise canceling and it really helps me focus. I’ve even used them to watch TV when my boyfriend is sleeping at night and I don’t want to have the TV too loud. I can connect them to my FireTV and it works great. They are very comfortable to wear for long periods of time.

title: Not cheap, but you get what you pay for
text: Easy blue tooth setup, good noise cancellation, excellent sound quality, and the battery lasts a long time. I'm very happy with it

title: Witchcraft Involved in Noise Cancellation?
text: I am forced to the conclusion that witchcraft must have been employed in the creation of the noise cancellation in these headphones. Just now I had nothing playing on them while lying in bed and out of curiosity I turned off the noise cancellation. I was confused when I suddenly heard a loud rumbling. I took off the headphones and realized it was my white noise machine on my bedside table. I keep it pretty loud to drown out noises from outside the house. I turned the noise cancellation back on and the sound completely disappeared. How in the world can it do that? I mean, maybe white noise is something particularly easy for them to cancel out, but that is still incredible. Is someone playing a prank on me and just turning the noise machine off as soon as I hit the noise cancellation button? I might think so, but if I lean in really close to it, a bit of the sound gets through. A seemingly unrealistically small amount... and yeah, yeah the headphones sound amazing when you play stuff in them or whatever too.

title: First minute was good . . .then ouch! Not for big (or medium?) head sizes.
text: Well I put these on and at first it was great, super quiet. Then about a minute later my ears began to pop. Then I began to feel a somewhat painful sensation on the sides of my head, right around the ear area. It was if the headphones were exuding an uncomfortable internal pressure on my inner ears - perhaps a combination of the tightness of the fit with the sound-canceling technology. How do they fit? Quite snugly. I am a medium build male and I believe my hat size is medium as well. I didn't think much of the tight fit at first but it sort of feels like two suction cups on your ears. Somewhat uncomfortable. These headphones are narrowly built and not for the wide of head. After about fifteen minutes and googling how easy it is to burst an eardrum under pressure, and getting tired of a legitimately painful sensation in both ears, I gave up. Given the narrow profile of the headphone crest, I doubt how much they would break in to potentially alleviate the issue. Weird that this wasn't an issue that came up in any of the reviews I looked at. Basically unusable for me.

title: Works mostly as expected but with silly issues.
text: The headphones work well and replace an older set. The internal battery is a positive step and battery life is good. Noise cancellation is only marginally better than the old version. The 3 settings is useful but only functions with Bluetooth connection. A cable connection does not allow the same flexibility which makes little sense. I find the cable connection to be quite sensitive requiring care connection at the headphone socket. The biggest problem is the BT app on an iPhone at least. Connectivity to the app is easily lost forcing an on/off routine to connect but even that often does not work and a new pairing is required. It’s annoying.

title: Good value & won't be disappointed
text: I did a lot of research on a solid pair of noise-cancelling headphones and it came down to these and another pair. I knew that these were significantly more expensive than the other, but based on a few reviews indicating that the quality of the other could be a hit or miss, I just ended up going with these because I knew they would be a solid purchase and love them. I also went to Best Buy and tried on several in the same category, and loved the lower profile of these and the lighter band around the head (didn't feel too heavy). It was a plus to have the Google Assistant function with the series ii since it went along with the rest of my environment. I love the cordless and bluetooth feature, and I can be connected to my phone and computer at the same time. I also kind of like the robotic voice that tells me how much it's charged when I turn them on (though I think you can turn that off as well). It has high, low, and off levels of noise cancelling and also comes with a smooth and solid app that helps with the pairing process.

title: Most comfortable headphones ever.
text: Noise cancellation is somewhat better in next gen headphones, but I still wear these most of the time because they’re so comfortable! In comparison, AirPods Max have superior noise cancellation and are reasonably comfortable (but subpar battery life and portability). I kept them, but I returned the Bose 700 and Sony MX4 headphones because they were uncomfortable to wear. The 700s have a rounded headband, and they slipped to weird angles too easily. The MX4s rubbed on my ears and made them itchy. I wish Bose would keep the QC35 form factor and release a third series with the next gen noise cancellation. I’d buy two pairs! In summary: Comfortable, foldable, portable, great battery life (even after three years). You’ll have to replace the earcups yearly, but it’s worth it.

title: Fantastic !!
text: Because of price, I purchased a headset for $79 that had ANC and Bluetooth. I returned it as the ANC didn't work and the Bluetooth kept cutting out. I then decided to go to the other extreme and got the Bose headset. The difference was like night and day. ANC is almost perfect, sound quality is excellent. Bluetooth has not cut out and phone calls are crystal clear. Alexa works very well. I highly recommend this headset.

title: Top tier headphones
text: Amazing Noise cancellation and sound quality to match. Quite the increase in the listening experience with the addition of noise cancellation.

title: Nice headset but broke after 7 months
text: Worked great for about 6 months. Then one dat I was in a meeting and everyone told me they can hear everything around me. Just stopped working. I would not purchase again.

title: Only works with music app, upgrade bricked it
text: These things only work with the music app. The pause feature will always revert back to that, no matter what app you were actually using - YouTube for instance. Then it took forever to download and install a firmware upgrade. After that, it won’t connect to anything. It’s a brick now. I didn’t buy them here, but at the Apple store. Hopefully I can return them. I am done with Bose.

title: More comfortable than the Sonys // After 1 year Stitching FAILED exposing right ear foam
text: Edit: Changing to a 1 star because the stitching on the right ear has failed after 1 year from purchase - product is already out of warranty. Light weight, doesn't hurt your ears (irritation) or top of your head, can wear for long hours. Sonys are heavier and squeeze too tight. If you're debating between the Sonys or the Bose, get this one. Easier to cycle through the 3 noise cancellation options Can also connect to two bluetooth devices at once

title: Wonderful Hardware Let Down By Poor Software
text: This review would be 5 stars if not for one very bad flaw in these headphones. The moment you make a call, the noise canceling turns off and you (and whoever you're calling) will hear everything around you – amplified – while you're on the phone. It's so bad that I have to use my old QC25 wired headphones for calls (which work perfectly for this), and only use the QC35-S2's for wireless listening to music/podcasts/tv while doing other things. This is beyond ridiculous for headphones of this price. As for their performance purely as listening devices, the noise canceling is slightly (but only slightly) better than the wired QC25's, but the tonal range is slightly worse in the base tones. Their ability to connect to multiple devices is great, but suffers from a tendency for them to want to connect to multiple devices AT ONCE (iphone + something else, for instance), which about half the time causes no audio to be played through them at all, even though the source is muted when they're selected. You then have to remove them from each device you've paired them to, and start over to get sound back.

title: Not great for sensitive hearing
text: I get migraines and because of those, I am easily annoyed by noise. I was thrilled to get these as a present. They're comfortable (not too squeezy for my head that hates things that are too tight). As for the noise canceling, I'm underwhelmed. With these on and my music playing, I can still hear a fair amount of what's going on around me, even when I'm at home and not out someplace loud. For the price, I expected these to be a lot better at noise cancelling.

title: Blows Beats out of the water!
text: The perfect set of headphones. Amazing materials and playability. Outstanding sound easy to link up to 10 devices through Bluetooth. Fantastic. Would highly recommend

title: The best headphones ever made
text: I am now a long-time owner of the Bose QC35 - I bought my first pair in 2016. They are extremely lightweight and comfortable, I regularly wear them 8+ hours a day with no discomfort. The battery life is extremely good, with a single charge typically lasting me 3 days. The noise canceling is excellent, with ambient voices typically reduced to barely-noticeable level in my shared office, and loud sounds (think jackhammer right next to you) reduced to a comfortable listening level. All-around the best pair of headphones ever made, even Bose has yet to surpass their own creation.

title: The BEST value! Couldn’t live without them. (6 month review)
text: I’ve been using these for 6 months and they are invaluable to me. They are quiet enough for doing loud chores like mowing the lawn or vacuuming. I also use them while I commute on the train. Even with the noise of the train cars and other people around me I’m still able to make phone calls while listening and speaking clearly with these headphones. I love music and they are also loud enough for my taste (I’m moderately picky about audio). Battery life is great it’ll last me all day listening to podcasts, music, and making calls. They seem to charge back to %100 very quickly The buttons are easy to use. They make answering calls or pausing/skipping songs easy. They also come with a very nice case that I use often. Overall these headphones are great and well worth the money in my option. I would absolutely recommend these to a friend.

title: Excellent
text: There were a surprise Mother's Day gift, and I LOVE them! Airplane travel is so much more comfortable with the noise drowned out, and music is so much more enjoyable with the sound quality for which Bose is famous. The bluetooth connectivity is a nice upgrade, too, allowing me to move around the house a bit while listening to podcasts, web conference calls, etc.

title: My boyfriend loves it!
text: Got it as a gift for my bf, he is SOOOO happy ;D Been using them for a couple months now, couldn't be more satisfied.

title: It’s Bose - of course it is great.
text: Is a review really necessary? It’s Bose. Of course it works well. Love how soft the ear pads are.

title: It’s Bose or nothing.
text: I purchased mine refurbished from Bose after purchasing and returning 3 different sub $100 headsets here on Amazon. These check all the boxes, great sounding, comfortable, lightweight and noise canceling that really works. I tried to save money but everything else had one or two major drawbacks or flaws. The only other product that sounds as good were my AirPod Pros. I’d say the AirPods are slightly better at noise cancellation but I couldn't get my right one to seal in my ear canal so they’re history.

title: Incredible Technology
text: I have owned several cheaper noise cancellation headphones. The all had this background buzzing noise that was not tolerable. These headphones have the most incredible noise cancellation I have ever heard. Very soft earmuffs for long flights and great sound quality you would expect from Bose. Worth the investment for traveling.

title: Very good for Music, but not for TV
text: Nicely finished, comfortable, and I wanted to keep them. However there was too much latency for TV listening . Very good noise canceling also. Overpriced.

title: Amazing Headphone
text: These headphones are amazing. The noise-blocking feature is so good to the point where someone has to jump around in front of me to get my attention. The sound quality on these is great as well. My music sounds so good and I feel like I'm immersed in every part of it. They are also comfortable to wear for an extended period of time.

title: The incomparable Bose does it again!
text: Bose has been and remains the best headphone maker. I’ve tried at least a dozen different products on amazon, with perhaps a dozen more in my life, and in all those experiences, the Bose name always stood far ahead of the crowd. First, their noise cancelling technology remains the best. Eerily effective, especially on airplanes and in cars, trains, or buses, you put them on, and the world becomes quieter, making you realize how terrible the ambient noise was! These have the added benefit of adjustable noise cancellation, unlike previous models. In comfort, these are built for long-term use, remaining wearable for hours. Most other headphones I’ve tried tend to make your ears sore, but not these! They feel soft and lovely everywhere they land on your head. With or without Bluetooth, these offer exceptional clarity of sound, powerful bass, and clear crisp treble, none of which turn to distorted noise, even at high volumes. Yes, these are very powerful! And they offer the option for wireless battery-operated use or plug-in use. They sound equally good in either setting. As for battery life, these won’t let you down. They last hours and hours without needing a charge. My partner has the QuietComfort 30, I believe, and I always loved borrowing those, so it’s great having a pair of my own (in an even better version, no less!) Fantastic! No product compares to Bose.

title: Great for air travel.
text: I travel almost on a weekly basis and this is always in my backpack. Reduces the engine noise significantly. Use it both via Bluetooth or connect to the seat outlet to watch movies. Nice case for travel. My first Bose headset broke at the hinges after few years so hopefully this one will last. Still feels like cheap same old plastic but time will tell. It is an expensive product to buy every few years if it doesn’t last. But I am happy so far. Makes long flights little better.

title: Really great hardware, but the worst software I have seen.
text: I bought this set of headphones to have some noise cancelling while gaming in the same room as my wife. The noise cancellation is great, and the sound quality is great. But the connectivity is absolutely horrendous not to mention the non-existent software. The product says it has 40ft range of Bluetooth connectivity, but if I walk out of the room I completely lose connectivity, if I lean back in my chair so my head is about 3-4 feet from my PC I start losing connection. This results in an extremely choppy listening experience which is pretty bad. I have updated all the firmware and drivers, disconnected and reconnected multiple times as their online instructions suggest.

title: Sooo quiet!

title: Bose. Never disappoints.

It will not block the totality of the abuse that modernity seems to accept as normal. So, for my purposes so far very disappointed for the price.

title: Not good for Noise cancellation.

title: I am in LOVE. These have changed my life and my marriage
text: I'm a writer and my husband plays his tv shows and sports or music which really detracts me. I must have ADD or something because I get distracted so easily. In the room I have this ceiling fan that does not know how to move air quietly, the "special silent" motor isn't silent anyore—unless I put on these headphones! I have no idea how they work, but bluetooth connects them to my computer and my phone so I can use them like regular bluetooth speaker headphones. It's summer now and my neighbors always have bbqs with lots of beer. I like to sit by my pool with a glass of wine and write. I can't even hear any of them unless someone shouts I got the silvery ones and am glad I did. They sort of disappear on my head easier than big ol black ones. I have never had pain from these either and wear them all day. When I bought them, I also bought the Sony Noise Cancelling Headphones WH1000XM3 which are actually just as amazing but Bose was just one tiny bit better. But mostly, I didn't like the dull finish on their silvery ones. Looked cheap. sooooo happy with these I'm going to buy my son a pair who is starting college and gets way too distracted by his roommates. His grades are going to improve so much!

title: Excellent headphones
text: I LOVE these headphones. I’ve had them for a year and 8 months and they’re still working great. I got them to help concentrate in a loud, open floor plan office and they do cancel out a lot of noise. Now I wear them while walking my dog and I really don’t hear anything around me. They connect easily, I wish they didn’t connect to multiple devices at once because that only makes things more complicated- you can only really be connected to one at a time or another device might interfere. I’ve also had a few instances where the headphones have worked improperly and started picking up ambient noise from my surroundings, or the audio gets fuzzy, but that is not a common occurrence. But other than that, they’re very sturdy and durable and worth the money.

title: If you will NEVER need this to have a mic, then it's great
text: If you don't use your bluetooth headphones to make calls or talk on Discord or anything, then these are great. Good sound quality, comfortable for long periods of time, and the dual device pairing is amazing. Lord help you if you want to answer your phone with them. The "hear-through" technology in horrific. It takes any background noise (like crinkling plastic or paper, keyboard clicking, mouse clicking, breathing, your neighbor's voice through the wall, breathing, dishwasher, ANYTHING) and turns the volume of that background noise up to 11, blasting it into your ear canals. Oh yeah, and this "feature" CANNOT BE TURNED OFF OR ADJUSTED. I can't keep a thought in my head while talking it's so bad. It is MADDENING. It's honestly an embarrassment for this company that it hasn't fixed this problem. Also, it sends that background noise through to the person on the other end of the line as well. It's literally anti-noise canceling to both parties in calls. My solution was to buy a $20 3.5mm to 2.5mm audio cable (because for some reason they thought a non-standard plug was a good idea?) with a boom mic on it. This removes all Bluetooth capability but makes them function how they should have out of the box. I use them Bluetooth usually, then plug in the cable every time I want to take a call (I use them for work calls).

title: I have not been able to get them set up.
text: There were no directions for set up, and what I did find did not work. I am going to the Bose store to see if they can help. There was no one to call for help. If I can not get them to function, I will return.

title: Great Headphones

title: Love mine
text: I love these headphones. I am 65 and I so enjoy listening to books on mine. They fit well and are very comfortable. I use them at the gym when I am on the treadmill. Makes time go by much faster! Easy to use and I'm so glad I got them!

title: Perfect Sound

They are AWESOME!! I wear these daily because I work next to a very loud machine, when I put these on I actually had to take them off again to make sure machine was still running!! Bose is always worth the money!

title: Incredible Sound!!
text: I can’t write anything that hasn’t already been said. These are excellent headphones. Expensive but worth every penny.

text: What can be said that already hasn’t been said, nothing. These aren’t the best headphones in

title: Great sound

title: Great sound
text: This is the second pair I bought in a month time. One for me and one for a friend. The sound is excellent. Highly recommend. JG

title: Great quality
text: I enjoy this product mostly when I fly. Most of the time I forget I'm surrounded by people.

title: Expensive but does the job
text: I wouldn’t spend my own money to buy these but received it as a gift and it works great. Sound cancellation is high quality. Doesn’t cut out sound completely but it would cut out traffic noise or office chatter pretty well.

title: Upgrade
text: Had an existing pair and purchased these as a gift and upgrade. Very pleased with ongoing noise cancellation, sound and bass quality are great .

title: Not an original Bose product!

title: Best I’ve ever experienced
text: These headphones are awesome. I cannot hear my girlfriend snoring and I can also make phone calls with them without any additional devices. I am blown away at all that these headphones can do and the sound is amazing. Sometimes I think the sounds from the headphones are actually noises in my room until I take them off and realize it was the headphones that sound so realistic, not from outside them. Lol

title: Good headphones!
text: I sleep with these on listening to sleep sounds for insomnia on YouTube it plays all night. Drowns out the snoring going on next to me. They connect with Bluetooth. One charge lasts me two full nights.

title: Awesome!
text: I work at a machine shop where it's a very noisy environment. I occasionally like to listen to music every now and then so I was looking into different noise canceling headphones. I had originally tried the new Sony xm5 and the Bose QC 45 which have the transparency mode but being that the environment I was in was too loud I feel like those earphones did more damage to my ears because of the transparency mode that they have rather than good. I decided to try these headphones and they work perfect! I love that these are true noise canceling and don't have any other gimmicks such as the transparency mode and all that new stuff. These are perfect for what I need. It doesn't cancel 100%, but neither do any other noise canceling headphones out there.

The buttons are easy to find, but don't do what they are supposed to even after programming, so can't work this right without the phone app. Overall, if they weren't so expensive, I would give maybe more stars, but for the price they have just too many problems.

They keep directing me to the "discounted" price, and not actually doing anything to provide support because of a one-year warranty. I'm sorry, but your $300 headphones should last longer than two years without breaking on their own accord. I am absolutely disappointed because I really love these headphones, but I don't want to shell out another small fortune just for them to break like they're made of glass.

title: Overrated, especially by youtubers.
text: I didn't get it from Amazon. But still want to publish this review here. This headphone is overrated partially because of the social media hype. Is it good? Yes. The ANC feature is awesome. It is comfortable in cool weather. The sound is better than average headphones. It supports multi device connections (2 for normal usages, 3 if you count the google assistant) which is super convenient comparing to 1000XM2. Is it great? Not at all. First of all, when people talk about this headphone people say how comfortable it is. But it is not that much more comfortable than other headphones such as 1000XM2. Prepare to have a lot of sweat around your ears in summer even in a room with AC. Second, the sound quality is good only when compared to the "average" headphones/earbuds such as the one that comes with iPhone. It sounds like a disaster even when compared with a JBL Everest 300: flat resolution, messed-up bass. and tasteless overall performance. Third, the connection range is not far enough. My kitchen is just Last but not least, the featured "Google Assistant" button is such a waste. When connected with iPhone, you must keep the Google assistance open to use it. Otherwise, you won't get any feedback from time to time. Also the supported features are limited on iOS. On Android, it is surprisingly slow. I tested using my Galaxy S8 with the newest firmware updates. It is not only slow in reaction, it is also not functioning properly. For example, if I ask "what's the status of xxxx flight?", it will say "Sorry I cannot/don't know how to help with that". But if I ask the same question directly on the phone, I will get the answer promptly. Interesting to mention, if you set up the google assistant on an iPhone, then connect to 2 other devices, you can still use the Google Assistant key to make queries. It seems the hardware is capable to connect to more than 2 devices at the same time, but somehow Bose chose to limit the number to 2. Overall, I still recommend this headphone if you don't care much about sound quality and like its look. Unlike most social media puts it, the comfort shouldn't be a reason you chose it. There are headphones which sounds great and feels comfortable with the same price tag.

title: Disposable!!!
text: Bose used to make their noise cancelling headphones so that they could accommodate a standard AAA battery. The QC 2, QC 15, and QC 25 all used a single AAA battery and would last for 15+ hours. When I went on a flight, I'd carry two Eneloop rechargeable batteries with me, and if one died, I could just remove the dead one and put a fresh one in. Now, they use an internal, non-replaceable lithium ion battery. So, when the battery reaches the end of its usable lifespan, you must throw the entire product away. What a waste! Even worse, if it happens while you're on a flight, that's just too bad. No noise cancelling for you! Oh, and let's not forget that lithium ion batteries occasionally catch fire, and sometimes even explode. It's definitely not a good idea to have one next to your head, or on an airplane for that matter.
