title: Work Very Well, Excellent Sound Quality
text: Replaced my old Wired Bose Quiet Comfort with these wireless phones. (the old phones noise cancellation just quit working.) Read many reviews and most were spot on with these wireless headphones. Bluetooth had no problems connecting to my Samsung TAB A (2017.) Could even walk into another room over 15 ft away and connection held just fine. Use for music and some other programs on You-Tube. Fit well on my head, very comfortable. Pads are replaceable. Cancellation is outstanding. When on, everything is extremely quiet. Music quality is very good to outstanding. Can tell the difference between recordings (classical music), which to me is a real test. A few minor downgrades - bass is OK, not great. Not a major issue. Battery is only rechargeable through a micro USB port. The prior model ran on one AAA battery. However, when connecting, the headphones tell you how much battery life is left. Does appear to hold a long charge. Wish they had made the charging port a "Type C" to keep standard with other devices. Also, no way to control volume except using the tablet. The wired version had a volume control on the cord. Summary, if you want a high quality noise-cancelling headphone, you won't go wrong with these.

title: Fantastic Headset
text: I work in a data center and my amazing boss decided to use part of his budget to buy these for the team after noise concerns arose a few months ago. Hence why my purchase isn't verified. They've been so good that I wanted to come leave a review. I had to get used to the noise cancellation at first. It was such a shocking difference between my Sony MDR-7506 set. These are the first $300+ pair of headphones I've ever used and "impressed" doesn't begin to cover it. The lab I work in gets pretty loud, to talk to others you have to raise your voice no matter the distance. More than 10 ft away and the best you can do is shout "HEY!". Not only do these cancel out a good deal of it, the sound quality is also superb. I was also surprised to find that I could make phone calls in this noisy environment and without complaint from my conversation partner. This headset really is a step up. The battery life is superb as well, it charges quickly and I can have my headset on for the entire 8-hour workday without even a full charge. It's able to connect to multiple devices simultaneously so I can be watching something on youtube on my laptop (not at work, of course) and then get a phone call and swap straight to the call without having to pair / unpair. The only negative thing I can possibly say about these is that after months of use, the power button on the side doesn't "snap" like it used to. It's still perfectly functional and it doesn't affect the operation at all, it's just a little bit of that tactile-ness is gone. Overall I couldn't recommend these more. I'm going to have to turn them in if I ever leave this job, and I don't ever want that day to come.

title: Still A Top-Tier Choice
text: The QC35II has been around a long time, and offerings from other companies and even from Bose themselves would seem to have eclipsed them. But first, comfort is subjective. If you expect to spend hours every day wearing your phones, trying on several different designs will reward you. I've been wearing headphones for work and pleasure for more than 50 years, and these are simply the most comfortable over-ear phones I've ever owned. Your head may vary; mine is a giant Irish one. These are more comfortably, to me, than the newer Bose 700 or than any Sony models. Second, value varies with price. These are still premium phones, so if you see them on sale at a really low price they could be a true bargain. I've seen sales recently offering these for close to half the price of the 700; that's a deal I'd jump on. Third, they sound great, and I say that without qualification. They are within the window of accuracy and naturalness that, IMO, anyone can acclimate to. They are clear, balanced, full-range, and don't change the character of the music. They don't do sonic tricks, either, so if you want your headphones to somehow enhance or exaggerate your music, look elsewhere. I know Bose uses active equalization and that some purists turn up their noses at that, but the real-life effect is more natural sound. Dozens of independent third-party tests confirm this. Fourth, they do all the basics of BT headphones quite well. They pair and connect with my OnePlus 6, my iPad, my Windows PC, all easily and repeatably. They stay connected when I walk into the next room. They hold a charge for many hours, and recharge quickly. Finally, this is still world-class noise cancellation. Put them on, turn them on, start your music, and the world goes away. Of course, no ANC can filter non-repeating, staccato, or very loud sounds, but these do the best that can be done. The cans themselves are effective sound-deadeners. Bose marketing, combined with some over-hyped, poor-value products, has made the company a favorite target of some commenters on the industry. I even agree with them about most Bose home-entertainment products. But Bose makes some very good pro-audio and architectural equipment, and they make some really good consumer headphones, too. These may be the best of them.

title: Worth the money over cheap brands
text: I'm not an audiophile, but I am a bit of a cheapskate. I bought all the cheap noise canceling headphones first, then bought the Bose when it went on sale. Battery life is great. I listen to it a few hours a day, and a charge lasts nearly a week. Included case is nice, with interior and exterior pockets for accessories. Easy to pair, and connects quickly when turned on. Fit is light on the head, but secure enough. Ear cups are big enough to go over my big ears. Noise isn't completely gone, but sounds distant and muffled. Noticeably better noise cancelation than the cheap brands of headphones and earbuds I have bought over the years. There is also very little high pitched static hiss, my main gripe about the cheapies. Sound is also better. Bose seems to favor the low end of the spectrum, but it doesn't sound unnatural or distorted. The app is easy to use and intuitive, if you want to customize your listening. I looked at it, but knew in my heart things would only go downhill if I touched it. So far they haven't broken, but I tend to treat expensive things a little better. Favorite unexpected features are L and R printed inside the ear cups, and that the ear cups rotate a little forward as well as backward for storage. I would buy again over the cheap alternatives, but I would probably wait for a sale to do so.

For the very high price it charges you, Bose should provide a better support. I do not recommend the purchase, with so many other similar options in the market. Update: I could make the headphones to work without glitches by disabling a couple of Bluetooth Services, namely ARfcomm, AudioWear, AudioWear Voice and Handsfree Telephony. It still presents glitches, but now it is less frequent. However, now I have another issue. The earpads began to wear off. It is way too early for this to happen (I bought about 10 months ago). I again asked for support, but Bose is very inattentive.

These came up and had excellent reviews. I left them laying around the house for a few days and he took the bait. He can't resist trying a new gadget (he's 80). He tried them a couple of times and promptly ordered his own pair (which ironically had gone down in price $60 since I bought them the week previously). It's a dream come true for all who live with him. We no longer have to hear podcasts blaring all over the house, and he claims he can no longer hear the traffic go by or the airplanes over head. We are a happy household now. They were worth EVERY penny (and yes...I kept my much more expensive, identical set).

I don't do any telephone conversations with these as a rule but a time or two and I did receive a call while using them and it went OK. I don't use the Google or the Alexa silliness but I suppose younger folks might like that. I do like that I can control the volume very easily with the control. Also, I have no problem with connecting via Bluetooth with my iPad and my android phone. It just works. I wish I could pair more than two devices at a time, but I can't say it's really a problem. Things stay connected, too. I've had no communication failures. The radio link is really solid. I maybe should say that I am updated to the latest firmware and had no trauma. It simply worked. I've used these on airplanes and they really cut down the noise. Sometimes I'll just wear them and turn them on and I'm not listening to anything. I'm just using the noise cancellation. Certainly better than the constant noise of the plane, especially if you fly cattle class like I do. To me, Bose is very over priced and they drop products and move on to the next newer thing so in time you end up with an orphan device. Still, they have the market pretty much to themselves with these nifty QuietComfort headphones so props to them for that.

title: Pretty much had it with the cheaply made Bose
text: If you think this headphone is superior to the Sony WH-1000xm2, you must be deaf, dumb, and blind. Tried both back-to-back and the Bose seems like a flimsy toy, with half a dozen screws visible. The Sony is beefier, with plusher ear cushions, and just more classy looking as no bolts or screws are visible. The headphone cable is twice as thick as the thin, cheap-looking cable that comes with the Bose. Even the marketing of the Sony product is superior, with a thicker cardboard box and nicer advertising graphics. The Sony isn't as comfortable because it fits tighter than the Bose, with massive earcup cushions compared to the Bose. The Sony headphone is larger and feels more solid but can fold up about as compact as the Bose due to one headphone being able to swivel. I found the Bluetooth was quicker and more consistent in hooking up with my laptop. The Sony is quite irresistible due to it's high-tech features and quality build. In regards to the noise cancellation, they are close but the Sony has a slight edge. What I really like about the Sony is being able to undo the noise cancellation by placing your hand over the right headphone. What it is comes down to is musical preference. The Sony is detailed and neutral to the point of being clinical whereas the Bose has it's signature warmish sound. The Sony is more accurate while the Bose is using some sort of equalizer to alter the sound, similar to the Maxx Audio Pro software in Dell laptops. Well, I guess it has the 'Bose' sound. I might add that all the Bose QC headphones I've owned crapped out within 3-5 years, so I kept buying new ones at a 50% discount from Bose. My last pair died on me on an airline trip to Japan, so I had no headphones on the 7 hour trip to Japan and the 8 hour trip back - I WAS NOT A HAPPY CAMPER! That is why I tried the Sony and quit Bose. Both are the same price. Note: As a frame of reference, I am an audiophile and the headphones I own are: Sennheiser PCX250, Audio Technica ATH-ANC7 (both are noise cancellation), AKG K701, Beyerdynamic T1, and the headphones I use on my 300B tube amp are $4,000 Focal Utopias.

The earbuds themselves are not great. Sound quality sounds like $30- I only hear top ends, no bass and low mids. This can of course be changed in the EQ, however I’m writing regarding my experience out of the box. Taking the buds out of the case will yield one of two results: the buds turn on and pair, or they don’t turn on at all which means you’ll have to put them back in the case and take them out again. The worst part of the earbuds (I’ve found): if the case dies, the buds turn on and drain their battery, while in the case. So if your case isn’t always full, forget about it. Overall, I’ve had infinitely better experiences with other budget earbuds. Skullcandy’s Jib Trues are just one example.

I've worn them while in the shower with no issue, so they're waterproof enough, and the built in charge cable is great. The noise canceling is pretty good, drowns out leaf blower and people, especially if you're listening to something. The battery seems long lasting too, I use these for 5-8 hours a day and charge the case every other day or so. Cons: The case sucks. It's open, so I'm worried about the earbuds falling out or getting damaged. It's also built so that the left and right buds have to be put into their correct hole, so I always have to check for the "L and R" engravings on an otherwise symmetrical and minimal design. Also, and this is just me, I find myself really missing my mechanical push button on my old pair. I've had to rewind so many podcasts because I put the buds down for a second and bumped the touch feature. These are fine. I plan on moving to the next price point for my next set of earbuds, so I don't think I'd buy them again, but I'm definitely not upset by the purchase.

The biggest issue though was the fit, or lack thereof - nothing I did could keep them from falling out of my ears, even if I so much as yawned, and of course I tried the different bud tips. Perhaps I received a defective set but I doubt it. Which brings up the question - what's so inconvenient about wired (ear-to-ear) BT phones? title: Another new favorite set of earbuds? Looks like it.
text: A while back I fell in love with a set of Panasonic wireless earbuds. (They’re “wireless” but still connected to each other.) My wife loves her AirPods but they didn’t satisfy me (and they're ridiculously expensive), although I remained open to the possibility of using separate earbuds. Then I got the opportunity to try the Soundcore Anker Liberty Air True earbuds and I absolutely fell in love with them at first listen. Of course, I remained open to the possibility that another set of earbuds could knock them off the throne. Enter Skullcandy Sesh. They were already mostly charged and easily paired with my iPhone. The sound is clear, with rich, velvety bass. Almost too much bass at first, but I adjusted my EQ settings on Spotify and I think they may have broken in over the past few weeks. Listening to music on them is a delight. I primarily listen to podcasts (with the left earbud in only); while the Anker earbuds allow only the use of the right bud by itself, these are completely independent: Listen with one ear, the other, or both. (The ability to switch comes in handy when the single bud inevitably runs out of juice, which it tends to do within about two hours.) I can also make and receive calls with excellent clarity on my end. They are comfortable all day long and stay in my ears. The range is not very good (you can get maybe two rooms away before they start cutting out) and they're extremely sensitive to microwave use, but for the most part these are winners. UPDATE 11/14/19: Tragedy strikes! I misplaced the left earbud and can't find it. A few weeks ago I was unable to listen to just the right earbud, something I was able to do before. Then the left bud went missing and according to the Skullcandy support website, I'm SOL because the left is the master and the right bud alone can't be paired to devices. So I have a nice charging case and earbud that are completely useless because the buds can't be paired independently. Not a big fan of that. Meanwhile I'll keep looking for my missing bud and watch eBay in case someone loses their right earbud and case.

title: [Life Q30] very good travel headphones
text: These are very good travel headphones. Over-the-ear style is very comfortable when worn for hours at a time. The headphones are relatively lightweight and compact. They fold nicely into the included EVA soft-shell case, which fits easily into my carry-on bag. The headphones pair easily with my Android smartphone. The Soundcore smartphone app is required for upgrading the headphones' firmware. The app also lets you customize the equalization to one of the presets or you can design your own. Depending on the kind of music you are listening to, the equalizer can make a noticeable difference in clarity and balance. Unfortunately, the app spams me with notifications about unrelated Anker products. Hopefully this will not be frequent. Noise cancellation works well. There are 3 modes: on, off (normal), and transparency that lets you talk to people around you without taking the headphones off. Noise cancellation can be toggled both from the app and from a button on the headphones themselves. Overall, sound quality is good. More of a balanced sound than the boomy default effects that some headphones give. I mostly listen to acoustic music, so this works well for me. Clarity is good. Bluetooth connectivity has been great so far.

title: Effective noise cancelling. Good value.
text: NOISE CANCELLING There are three noise cancelling modes: Transparent - You can hear everything around you. Normal - Blocks out most of the street noise, but you can still hear your kid ask for milk. Noise cancelling - When you want alone time, but need to be aware when you're kid screams for help. The active noise cancelling is very effective. I live over a busy street, and the headphones complete block out the typical noises. SOUND QUALITY I've spent literally thousands of hours playing Animal Crossing, using cheaper noise cancelling headphones, and difference in sound quality is very noticeable. With these headphone I can hear the hollowness of wood floors when I walk on them, and the way the rain sounds different depending on the surface it falls on. Also in Animal Crossing, when using the active noise cancelling, it's easy to hear shooting stars without having to make the volume louder than usual. EASE OF USE I'm not particularly tech savvy, but it was easy enough to figure out how to charge the headphones, and use the various controls, without reading the instructions. I was also able to connect to my Switch, and iPhone easily. I only looked at the instructions when trying to figure out how to fit the headphones in the case, and then I noticed the (cheat sheet) label in the case that shows you how to use the case. It's helpful that the headphones make different sounds when powering on and off, announces the battery level when turning on, and notes the different noise cancelling modes when you switch between modes (although the differences are obvious). USE DURING WORKOUTS The headphones stay in place when I workout, even when start sweating a lot. The places where the headphones adjust don't make any squeaky noise. When I'm done I wipe the padded parts with a wet towel and dry it with a tissue.

title: Good product for the price
text: I've purchased two the Q30 models. One for my wife and one for me. I'm a fairly avid headphone user with my favorites including HiFi Man, Beyerdynamic and Sennheiser models. The Q30 is no sound quality rival to any of those and is "muddy" in comparison. However, the Q30 is only $80 whereas the others are several hundreds of dollars. You get what you pay for. With that in mind, the performance of the Q30 is quite satisfactory. I found the sound quality acceptable for the price, the controls easy to work with and the wireless range very good. If you want the best wireless noise cancelling headphones, look to Sony but be prepared to spend $400. If you want to spend less than $100, these will serve you well.

title: Solid headphones for the price
text: Noise canceling is on par for the price point. Wouldn't be fair to compare to Sony and Bose because they are a fraction of the price. They don't cancel out everything, but they cancel out enough of everything. And sound quality is fine. Again, remember the price point. The main loss of a star (4 down to 3) for me is when I connect them via Bluetooth to my receiver (Yamaha), there is frequent cutting out. My other headphones don't do this unless I go too far away, these do it frequently and it gets super annoying. They are the main reason I wanted the headphones, so it is a big deal for me. They are the newest headphones I have with the best Bluetooth technology, but maybe it's not backward compatible enough with a 5 year old receiver? Results: I donated them to my wife because she connects to her phone and ipad without issue, and I look like a good husband.

title: Nice headphones
text: Bought these so I could listen to music while I work. These are really good quality and I'm happy with my purchase. Price is affordable and I like the pink color!

title: Great headphones
text: Great headphones!! The clarity and sound are awesome! Noise cancellation is fantastic compared to other headphones I’ve purchased for this price.

title: Love these headphones
text: I love everything about these headphones. The sound is great, they're very comfortable, and the noise canceling is awesome. You can change the noise canceling by just touching the earpiece. They pair easily and I love how long the battery lasts. The app is great as well. The case is well made and protects the headphones really well when they're not in use. I'm very pleased with my purchase.

title: Edit January 21, 2022 - After 10 months of use... plastic is breaking/cracking
text: Edit January 21, 2022 - After 10 months of use... the plastic is breaking/cracking (see attached photos), which appears to be spacers between the earphone slides on the headband and the soft foam lining on the bottom side of the headband. These plastic pieces keep the different parts of the headband aligned and now that they are broken the various bands are separating. It makes me wonder if these plastic pieces are of such a low quality to last less than a year, it makes me doubt the overall quality of the product. To be honest, I expected more from an Anker product. ⬇️⬇️⬇️Original Review⬇️⬇️⬇️ I like mine, they have a decent battery life, sound is good, noise cancellation is decent, and I like the transparency (amplified outside sounds, NC off) and normal settings (NC off).

title: Falls off
text: I like these for music, but I bought them for more than that. I wanted noise cancellation, these do an okay job at it, just about the same as putting anything else over your ears. More disappointing though is that they do not stay on your head if you aren't sitting upright. I tried laying down with these and they fall right back. Lean forward, and they fall forward. There isn't much security in keeping them on your head if you aren't just sitting still. So no gym, yoga or anything. Walking should be fine, but not running.

title: Wow.
text: I bought these for my wife and was blown away. Technology has come so far to allow such a great product at such a cheap price

title: Updated
text: I’ll first say Anker makes some great sounding products. I had a set of their ear buds that were an absolute design failure and didn’t receive good customer service from them at all, so I was reluctant to try these. I’m glad I did. These things are absolutely great. They cover the ears well, are comfortable, and sound much better than they should at this cost. I deducted one star for three things. First is they’re kind of a pain to turn off and on. A simple switch would have been better than button holding. Second deduction is because they randomly switch modes too easy from the touch controls. Lastly, they have to be fast charged. If it’s not a fast charger they literally won’t charge at all.

title: Amazing!
text: I was very skeptical but they have been amazing so far! Better than the higher brand name product I had. The perfect gift!

title: Try en you'll like them
text: OK these things are awesome.. I'm a good judge of sound, who cares right. It's my opinion.. But I've watched YouTube vids, read reports and reviews.. They sound great. Easy to connect. Build quality is great. Great company with customer service. Here's what I feel is wrong..... 1 makes my ears sweat... OK it's because it surrounds my ears.. Verdict exceptable because of sound..... 2 buttons are hard to get use to unless these are all you use... Skipping is holding the volume I stead of just skipping.. That's it... Perfect if it could cool my head and 2 more buttons for skipping and going back... Really, they're great a d well worth the price, you're goofy not to buy these.

title: Decent quality
text: Good noise canceling. Wear while lifting. Blocking out loud family.

title: Hard core headphone
text: I've own Grado Lab Prestige I 80, Sony MDR Series, Sennheiser And Koss HD Pro series(Koss light weight best over ear ever for sound). All these head phone are corded. I play and write music so you need to hear everything. Branching out I found these SoundCores. WOW!... 1. If you want loud You got it with these. 2. If you want quality you have it with these 3. If you want easy pairing you got it with these 4. If you want to hear everything you got it with these. 5. If you like Noise cancelling it's ok. 6. For the price buy..buy ..buy..Sorry Cramer for using that. 7. Enduring had mine for many years...Just can't remember how long... Too many beers. Ok 30000 beers at least. 8. Sound is killer. 9. Better than the high priced competition 10. I review because We were poor and I fought everyday to get were I am...And I love YOU. You deserve the best.

title: Don't buy if you plan to talk.
text: Sound and comfort were fine. Sound Cancelling was OK for the price. Having to listen to someone talk into the microphone during meetings was painful. Can't recommend getting these for Teams, Skype, Zoom etc. etc. Not sure if I got a bad one. Anker stuff is normally great.

title: Good with some flaws
text: Pros-sound is generally nice Decent noise isolation Good app Long battery/fast charge Cons-pretty warms. Ears will probably sweat Phone call quality could be better For the price I am pretty happy

title: Very poor
text: There are a number of good things about this, the batter life is excellent, and range is amazing, they have zero latency, lots of great stuff, and none of that matters because they just sound absolutely terrible. There are no highs, everything is muddy. Honestly the quality is below what I would expect from an entry-level device, much less this mid level model.

title: Poor Noise cancellation
text: Normally I would have given these speakers a 1 star rating but the sound is very good. I bought these NC phones to mow the lawn but the noise cancellation is terrible, if not useless.. I couldn't tell if the NC was on or off since I didn't notice any improvement by turning on the NC. Another issue is wind noise. When it's windy one can't hear anything but the rumble of the wind through the earcups. I did receive an email from the manufacturer offering me a discount on a future Amazon order, so I'd say they were responsive to my problems. They need to hire new sound engineers to design a product with good noise cancellation. If noise cancellation is not a consideration they make a very good inside headphone. I very much like the sound so they're relegated to the indoors.

title: Extraordinary value for money
text: They pair easily. They are light. Their noise cancelation is superb. They are cheap without compromising quality when compared to others at 3-5x the price.

title: Arrived on time .. No Damage- worked right out of the box. Great Product . Would recommend it
text: Daughter uses it to watch streaming programs and music. She is very pleased with it

title: Huuuuge step up from Q20
text: These Q30 replaced broken Q20 and i must say they are in another sound quality universe. Everything sounds just perfect. Bass is not crushing skull but quality of it is just soooo good warm and melodic. Mids and highs are just so pleasant i want to re-listen to all my favourite tracks again. Anything from Iya Terra to Van Hees to RATM sounds clean and transparent. Noise cancelling is boss. For 60$ this is no brainer. Buy it.

title: Perfect gift for casual listeners!
text: I purchased this gift for my father, who was in need of new headphones and I'm extremely satisfied with the purchase. Both my father and I agree, the sound quality of the headphones are very good for the price. Setup to connect to your device or computer is pain free. Switching from noise cancellation and sound isolating is a breeze with an easy access button on the side of the headphones. I love the look and finish of the headphones as they feel very durable and long lasting.

title: Awesome headphones
text: Great price for a pair of superb sounding headphones. I have zero complaints with the headphones and very pleased. Anker continues to make great products

title: Not good
text: I’m very disappointed with these headphones. They looked used and the noise cancellation was the worst

title: My neice loves it
text: Well these are awesome for the price killing known brand names that cost a lot more. The bass is amazing! Now no these dont have a booming bass if that's what your looking for. The bass is crisp to the point where you are like damn let me hear that part again. Paraphrasing my niece these are the best sound headphones she has ever had. As i have seen she had owned beats, low level Sony etc. Now i personally own the black ones and they do have build quality issues. I had to exchange my first pair abd my 2nd pair is showing the same damage. Right below the cushion headband section there is a plastic section before the adjustment part and that part cracks or chips off. I hope anker fixes this. Otherwise these are top notch.

title: Lacking in one way
text: Soundcore by Anker has great products for the price and the Q30's are no exception. BUT the Soundcore app lacks the most important (to me anyway) feature. NO adjustability for the ambient/transparency mode. The EQ settings are awesome. The ANC settings as well. BUT no adjustability on the Transparency/ambient mode is a deal breaker for me. And when it is on (according to the app) the hear thru is weak and marginal at best. WHY can't Soundcore make the Transparency mode adjustable? I need to occasionally hear my surroundings. Update-- I have lost a lot of my hearing so I invariably turn my headphones up loud. Sort of. Well the Q30's DO produce a lot of sound but my Wife complains that SHE can hear a lot of the "music" no matter the volume. I don't experience a lot of passive noise isolation with the ear cups. Sigh.

title: Great headphones!
text: I got these as a gift for my daughter. She was very happy with them. She wears them when she's mowing the lawn and she said that they work fabulously

title: thus far, thus good
text: I've admittedly not used these a lot, as they are playing backup to a V-Mode equipment that looks to fall apart in the next year. But I've tried them out and am impressed. Easy to set up, light on the head, and the sound is quite good, within the constraints of Bluetooth connection. Good value, as everything I buy from Anker seems to be.

title: Updates
text: Decent music sound and great noise cancelation. However, very bad sound on phone calls. Battery is good but not even close to be what they advertised. In full battery mode the sound is great but as soon as you drop you battery level to Medium the sound quality drops drastically, making it impossible to maintain a phone call. UPDATE: SELLER OFFERED A REPLACEMENT UNIT. CUSTOMER SERVICE WAS DILIGENT AND EXTREMELY NICE AND SEND UNIT TO REPLACE THE OTHER HEADPHONES. EXTREMELY PLEASED WITH THE ENTIRE TRANSACTION.

title: Only used on spin bike and I sweat like I’m in a shower
text: I have done what you should not with these. I have ridden solely on a spin bike when sweating like a mad man. I sweat like someone is hosing me down. They have survived well except the right noise canceling doesn’t work now. The normal and transparency settings work fine. I do not fault Anker for this as I know they are not sweat proof or water resistant. It is my fault, but this is what I bought them for. As for the headphones, they are comfortable, have good sound, and pair easily. I will definitely buy them again when these succumb to my drowning them in sweat.

title: Decent headphones for the price
text: I do appreciate a good deal when I find one. When I purchased the Q30's, it was for international air travel (Can't stand crying babies of any age lol). After a year of hard use, the ear pads on both sides started to split open and allowing the foam to escape. I contacted the manufacturer (Apparently cannot name them for the review) and was able to get a replacement set on order under warranty. I recommend these headphones to those with a limited budget as they are great for the price.

title: Blown away
text: I purchased these headphones for a week long IT boot camp for my job that I’m attending at home. I was skeptical at first given the price and I had never heard of this brand. Am I ever glad I made the investment. Today 6/6/2022 is the first day of class and the first time I’ve used these headphones and all I can say is THESE HEADPHONES ARE THE TRUTH!! Even with my tv playing in the background ALL I can hear is the instructor! I just can’t believe these are under $100. What a freakin steal deal! They are so comfortable and the sound quality is mind blowing! And they paired perfectly with my iMAC and iPhone. I’ll provide an update in about a week.

title: AWESOME!!
text: My husband got his first, I needed an upgrade on my old headset and wanted a good quality noise canceling system. The color the soft pink is great, the sound quality and easy to connect to my devices. Also will be great when traveling, carrying case is nice and easy to handle.

title: This is my second review within a week from the first one
text: I am liking this product more and more everyday I use it. The battery life is superior comparing with the other brands that I know of. I like to change my previous rate of its ANC from 6.5/10 to 7/10. The default bass is near perfect to my taste.

title: Solid buy, dope quality *At First* -AGAIN-
text: [Post Customer Service Update] I decided to keep trying to make them work to no avail, but saw Anker provides an 18 month warranty! So I reached out with all the details to their customer service email and within two days! BOOM! They're sending a new set. :) Very happy! And still set on buying a pair for my wife! pobody's nerfect! But these headphones are great! [3.5 Month Update] These were great and perfect~! Until last night. They were working fine until I put them to charge for a little bit and the right ear stopped working. The buttons on it still work, and I have to use it 'cos it's all I have now. BUT. Yeah, kinda sucks that randomly after taking care of them for this time that they stop working due to... charging the battery? :( Sad times. from 5/5 to 3/5 'cos I feel bad doing lower. [Update] So I wore these on a trip across the globe. The noise cancelling function did WONDERS on the plane to drown out the engine and people sounds. It helps when I'm in public spaces, because it cuts down on sensory overload. :) BUT. I was on my trip for 14 days and I didn't need to charge them once. I used them for NC on the plane, with earbuds under them for watching movies. Absolutely worth the price! I'm getting a pair for my fiancee! :) [Original] They not only fit my massive head, but aren't MAX EXTENDED to do it!! There's room to spare! I can blast music and no one else can hear it until i take them off. This is my first intro to noise cancelation and it is really an incredible thing! Uhhhhh... They're good headphones man. Battery life is incredible. I didn't download the app. Aaand it works almost simultaneously on laptop and phone. Though it does bug out a lil. But no biggie to do one at a time. :)

title: Battery life & sound quality & mics
text: The battery life is beyond amazing + great to use for video chats and phone calls.

title: Good headphones given the cost
text: I've gotten other Anker products before and have been generally satisfied. The noise cancellation isn't the best when I'm working in the office and people start talking, but works good enough with respect to other background noise.

title: Good qualitybasic phones
text: Good sound quality for mid price phones. Comfortable. Build quality is good.

title: Not the top of the line. But works for me
text: A perfect headset. Great for the price. I'm very happy with it.. it took me a few times wearing them to stop hurting my ears. And it was a little confusing finding the buttons while wearing the headset. I recognize it by sending the bottoms and I feel the charging port on the right side so I know the power button is on the left.

title: Fantastic headphones! Finally!
text: 1. Comfort. They cover all of my ears and fit snug, but comfortable. The pads are very soft and conform perfectly. 2. Noise cancellation. Five stars. When I first put them on I was sitting under a loud fan and the sound just disappearing. I'm an idiot so, for a second, I thought the fan broke. lol! 3. Sound quality. For $80? WONDERFUL! I'm sure there are better out there, but this is absolutely the best bang for the buck. 4. Bluetooth. This was the primary reason I was looking to replace the last two pair of headsets that had failed me. Apparently my study is located in a bluetooth black hole and I needed to find something - anything - that could make it to the primary living space of my home without cracking up. This one did it. Frankly, this is such a relief. 5. Clarity of instructions. This is the worst part and it is bad. The print on the instructions is ridiculously small. Fortunately for me, I collect magnifying glasses, so it was nothing but a walk to my bookcase to fix the problem. 6. Bass. It's actually pretty good. Four stars only because I know that much more expensive headphones could do better. But it sounds as the artists intended and that's plenty good enough for me. I haven't played with a equalizer with it yet, so it might be better than I realize. But I'm really not complaining. All-in-all, this solved all of my problems. I couldn't be happer.

title: Quality headphones!
text: Best headphones I've had for a while. Good price, great sound. It connects to two systems well, auto connects to the one you're using if it's not connected elsewhere. Battery life is amazing.

title: Comfortable, long usage on single charge
text: I have tried other over the ear headphones and they ended up hurting my ears as they weren't big enough. This headphone is perfect sized for me and extremely comfortable. I have tried ear buds that are similar to ear pieces, but they died after about 6 hours. This phones has yet to die on me and I tend to used them 14 hours a day on weekends. I have always liked Anker products and I am very happy with this purchase.

title: Like Bose Headphones, only 1/3 the price
text: I think the headline of my review sums it up all. This is an excellent headphone. Very high value for money. The transparency mode is excellent.

title: Doesn't work
text: The headphones are more like a speaker than headphones. Even on the lowest volume people not wearing the headphones can still hear the music.

title: They really work
text: These headphones really do cancel most of the ambient noise, and the audio fidelity is pretty good. Much better performance than I had expected for the price.

title: No ANC when using the AUX cable...on an airplane.
text: I bought these to use on flights. However, the AUX cable disables ANC and the headphones won't power on. The do work passively, but that is of no use. Why have ANC phones that don't work when you need ANC?

title: Solid ANC headphones
text: Used them on a two week road trip in a van with kids. The ANC worked so well I couldn’t hear my wife in the next seat. I did have the volume cranked up but I’m not sure if it’s the movie or the headphones. The transparency mode seemed interesting but I didn’t use it. The carrying case is slid. The supplied charge code is short but good enough.

title: Seriously Amazing Headphones
text: I've had these headphones for a couple years now. These have been the best pair I've owned in quite some time. Especially considering the price, there isn't a better set of headphones around. These make Beats sound like the cheap, over priced garbage they are. 10/10 will buy again.

title: Decent sound and features, but weird fit
text: The sound and features of these cans are solid for $100. Effective ANC, consumer-based, V-shaped sound. Don't expect audiophile performance, but these shouldn't be bad for most people. But there was a problem for me with the fit. Every time I walked while wearing these cans, there was a distinct popping sound in the left ear cup when I was using noise cancellation. Maybe the cabin pressure of the ANC is really high with these cans - not sure. But the popping sound and pressure with every footstep was unbearable for me, so I returned these.

title: sound quality?
text: I think the sound is better than the Cowin E7. I bought it 4 years ago and sadly it still works well so I just bought the q30. I don't know if this is any better than the E7 except for being lighter.

title: Very Comfortable!
text: These are my new go to headphones for airplane travel!

title: Unbeatable value
text: Comfort: 5/5 Sound: 5/5 after making adjustments with a custom EQ (recommend dialing back low frequencies, slight boost to mids) ANC: 3/5 - lacking compared to other, higher priced products. But Transport mode is a major difference in ambient sound when travelling, especially on an airplane. Solid budget buy for travel headphones

title: Great sound, decent build, meh durability
text: They have great noise cancelling for the price. Sound quality is awesome, but not quite amazing. I love these headphones but I have to baby them as the materials feel cheap. I’ve already had them break in one spot although they are never out of the case unless on my head. Would definitely buy soundcore again if they can make their products more durable

title: The weirdest and most inconsistent pair of headphones I've tried
text: I wanted to test these out in a variety of different settings before writing this review. Thus far I tried them in a coffee shop, at the gym and also at home. First the good : these do,have some noise cancelation capability. However, they don't hold a candle to my Bose noise canceling 700s that I refuse to ever take out of the house. The price on these headphones is also a plus. For the most part, they're fairly comfortable as well(more on that below). The battery life is also good and a single charge did last me through hours of listening. The bad: I wanted these to totally block out sound around me while doing whatever I was doing. I understand that most heads won't block out 100% of sound however, these definitely let through a decent amount of noise which is surprising and also disappointing. The fit is also a major complaint of mine: the ear cups are fine but, I find the band of the headphones slip and this leaves a feeling of them sliding and not being secure. Recently, the pair of headphones also started to make a very odd shaky/reverberating sound when I wear them and if I tilt my head down which I can't figure out. There is also a button on the left side of the headphones that controls the option of the sound setting to normal, noise cancelation or transparency. Soundcore couldn't have picked a more irritating spot to place this button as every time I try to adjust the left headphone, my finger or thumb seems to touch this button changing the setting. I wouldn't repurchase these headphones personally. They're not horrible but there are better options out there.

title: These are great, Make sure you order ANKER brand and not one of the cheap knockoffs!
text: I almost ordered the cheaper knockoffs until I fortunately noticed the slight spelling change. The Anker headphones are everything and more, can't wait for my red eye flight to put these to the ultimate test. Super comfortable and very light weight, can't go wrong, worth every penny!

title: Sound is great as long as you have special charging cable
text: Not real happy with proprietary 5v charging receptacle and needed cord. Sound is great as long as I don't have hearing aids in my head which cause feedback, but is NOT due to the headphones.

title: Great Headphones
text: I really enjoy these headphones. They are well built and have a great sound for the money. I would buy them again.

title: Not noise canceling enough
text: I can still hear my annoyingly loud coworker 3 or 4 cubicles over. The sound is nice, the battery life is good. The noise canis just meh.

title: Great sound quality.. but the right earcup has less padding
text: Great headphones, great sound quality and battery life too.. But my only issues that I'm having are the right earpad having a little less padding..

title: Great set of headphones except for the plastic clips that hold the top pad in place.
text: I use the headset daily for work. they work wonderfully, but a few months back I found the clips to be broken. I just applied electrical tape to hold the clips in place. the design does need to be rethought for the clips or make them using a nylon reinforced clips.

title: Well worth the price! Great value!
text: These are the BEST headsets I've ever owned! Lots of features! I love the app. It has equalizer and sleep functions. Awesome bass response! The noise cancelation is the best I've ever experienced and the transparency mode is very useful. You use that function if you want to talk to someone in the room and you don't want to remove your headsets. Battery life is great!! 30 to 40 hours depending on whether you're using the noise cancelation mode.. I would recommend these to anyone!

title: Great noise cancellation and sound
text: I wear these to listen to soothing music and to cancel my husbands snoring. The noice cancellation works great. The price is right also.

title: They SLIP OFF HEAD over and over and over and over and over again
text: These are awful, when I adjust the ear buds on my ear, the buttons get hit and I turn my headphones off. These are very slippery, I spend all my time adjusting for comfort ( there is none) and they are continuously slipping off my head.

title: Total winner in price range all around should have.
text: I own the 10.20 and now 30 with each version they have improved. The Q30 is to me an excellent piece of versatile communication / entertainment value. Phone calls seldom get complaints, loudness is excellent for me on calls as well as music. I fall asleep often with noise cancelation as I do not hear the constant window ac unit anymore. YouTube videos are nice and clear, concerts sound good and on top of it if I need to, the integration of the soundcore app make this a winner for all sorts of customizable settings. Hands down a five for value comfort and usability. I have no need for my older headsets. I am not sure that I need to go for their latest offering, this set works great for my Oculus as well, enough room even for my big head. Battery life is outstanding seriously beats everything else I have by a long shot AND these charge extremely fast as well.

title: My new everyday over ear.
text: For the money you are not going to find a better set of wireless headphones. I own multiple wireless headphones by Soundcore and they all serve a purpose. These are great for videos, confrence calls and music. The battery life lives up to the hype. Get them while you can. Nice ANC for the money. I know it’s not “Bose ANC” but honestly these sound better than Bose.

title: These are very good for the price, but...
text: ... the one valid complaint I have is that they are very hot on the ears. I only knocked off one star for this, because many headphones are hot on the ears. It does seem to me that these may be a little hotter than others, but I can't prove it. The noise canceling is very good for the price. If you want to pay two or $300 you can surely get better ones. But at this price point, I don't think you can do much better than these. The audio quality is also very good, and they can be used without Bluetooth, but you do not get the noise canceling without the Bluetooth. The last pair of headphones I bought broke apart where the earpiece meets the headpiece, and so I gave them a bad review. I have only had these for a couple of months so I can't be sure yet about the quality of the device itself. If they break apart like my other ones then I will come back here and lower my review appropriately. Otherwise, assuming they last a year or two, they are a good buy.

title: Worked great sometimes.
text: Worked great with my phone but with my computer it would constantly clip. Tried to reset the headphones and now they wont connect at all. Otherwise the sound quality and noise cancellation were awesome but I guess I'll try a different brand for actual connection quality.

title: I like these headphones, q40 coming out soon though
text: I like these. Bought them to replace my old Sony MDR XB950BT headphones. The ear cups fit and feel better on the Soundcore q30s. I preferred the on board controls of the Sony’s, but the q30 controls are not hard to get a hang of. I’m not a huge stickler for noise cancellation, but these do a pretty okay job at it, and has transparency mode which is a huge plus. The sound is a little bassy at first but you can easily create custom EQs through the Soundcore app. All in all, I’m glad with my purchase, though I’m a little upset because Soundcore is releasing an updated model, which I’m assuming will be the q40. I’m interested in the newer model, but I just recently got the q30 so I probably won’t get it for the time being.

title: So far, amazing for the price
text: I've never owned over ear headphones before. My daughter has the Sony WH-XB700 Extra Bass headphones and I thought they were ok. No NC capabilities though. Came across these on Amazon and figured I'd take a chance, especially since they're 50 bucks cheaper than the Sony's mentioned above. So far they're awesome. And I love the ability to change things up via the app. Well worth the money. And having the app makes it worth spending the extra 30 bucks for the Q30s over the Q20s.

title: Incredible noise cancellation for a steal of a price
text: You absolutely won’t find a better price to performance ratio in a pair of noise cancelling headphones. They just plain work. Air travel without these is absolute torture. We wound up buying a pair for the whole family and I won’t be caught traveling without them. The ability to quickly switch the pass through mode and hear outside sounds is a game changer for me while working from home. Audio quality for music is very good, but nothing like a pair of Bose or Sennheisers. But for the price, you won’t be disappointed. The microphone function works pretty well and the array of microphones does a good job of keeping background audio to a minimum. Highly recommended!

title: Very Good
text: The sound is very balance, it is not too heavy and can be used for a very long time. The battery live is very good. I used it for an 11 hours international flight and served me very well.

title: Awesome battery life, great sound, superior service!
text: I bought these on a deal through WOOT. The noise cancelling is excellent for the price. Yeah Bose does a better job at 3-4X the price. The sound quality is very good and the Bluetooth works great with my phone. The only down side is the instructions that come with them are less than stellar. Other than that they are great. **Update** It is said the measure of a company is how they handle adversity. Using this metric Anker Life is a stellar company. The foam ear cushions needed to be replaced under warranty. I contacted their support. I was treated like I was the single most important customer they have ever had. Don't believe me? Check this out. They asked me for the serial number to process the claim. I sent it in on Thursday evening. Bright and early Friday I had an email from support thanking me and apologizing that they might not be able to ship on that day, and asking if Monday would be OK. (WOW!) Then on Monday I got an email saying it was shipped. Then another asking if it arrived. Then another asking if I had any issues installing the new cushions. Finally I got a final one thanking me for my business. (If anyone from Anker reads this please thank Cookie and May for me, they both rock!) I am super pleased with this headphones. I wear them all day and sometimes at night so I can sleep better. I also use them on airplanes. I am very happy and fully recommend them.

title: Really good value for what you get
text: I have a bunch of lesser headphones and a higher end set with the Bose QC II. These probably sound 90-95% as good as the Bose but come a little short on the multipoint connections. Noise cancelling is also pretty good but doesn't block out quite as much. They are way ahead of all my other sub $80 headsets though. I have been working from home a lot multipoint is a major factor for me. The Bose will connect to both my PC and phone simultaneously whenever I turn them on. These will only connect to one of the two and I have to connect to the other manually every time (but will stay connected to both). It's a bit of an annoyance so hopefully they can fix that with firmware. The other advantage the Bose have is a hardware switch to turn them on instead of a press and hold button. The switch is significantly quicker and works 100% of the time. On the other hand the Q30's have a few advantages over the Bose. They can adjust active noise cancelling with a button. You can only turn Bose off with the app. Also passthrough mode can easily be activated by a button or cupping your hand over an earcup (which I always forget to try). Bose needs the app or it will do it automatically with a call. Comfort wise it is a close call but I would give the edge to Bose because the earcup shape fits my ears better and they are a little lighter. The Bose also fold down a bit better, with a smaller case, so better for travelling. All in all though I was impressed and keeping my fingers crossed for a firmware update on the multipoint.

title: Excellent budget headphones with ANC
text: There is a lot to like about these headphones and a few minor changes. Likes: BATTERY LIFE! Mine came charged up at 60% and they lasted through four 8-hour work days with 15% left. I was using the indoor ANC setting so I'm sure it would have lasted a lot longer with the ANC turned off. Active Noise Cancelling! Through the app, there are three different modes - Indoor, outdoor, and travel. I have tested all three and each behaves slightly differently. Indoor and travel are very similar, but I noticed that the outdoor mode seems to let in a bit out outside noise so you're able to be aware of your surroundings. Transparent mode: this mode works very well, it seems a natural volume level and mixes audio well so you can hear your surroundings while listening to music. You can activate it through the ANC button or by resting your hand on the right earcup. The touch mode is convenient, but I wish it was quicker. Sound Quality: These are very nice sounding pair of headphones with good bass, good stereo separation, a wide range of adjustability through the in-app settings. I found the flat setting a bit lacking in bass and trebles, so I used the custom setting to adjust it to my liking. Companion App: Normally I don't install apps that come with products because they're filled with useless features or don't add many features. In the case of these headphones, install the app!! It allows you to fine-tune the equalizer settings with many presets or the ability to customize it to your own tastes. You can change the ANC setting between the three modes, normal, and transparent. You can also use a unique sleep mode that allows you to mix your own soothing sleep sounds that automatically turns off after a certain amount of time. Overall I'm very pleased! I was fortunate enough to preorder and get these headphones for 20% off, but they are worth the full price.

title: Very clear sound if you plug in the auxiliary cord

I compared it with my 7 year old Sennheiser Momentum. The sound is much clear. If you can, plug in the auxiliary cord. The headphone is very good.

title: Quite good for over-the-ear Bluetooth headphones
text: First I do not prefer over-the-ear (aka. circumaural) headphones because I wear glasses which makes the ear cups uncomfortable. Second, I am happy to say that reviews of these Anker Life Q30s which say they are comfortable for glasses wearers are correct. The ear cups are soft and forgiving. I still am not quite used to having my ears completely covered, though. I have been using bone conducting headphones -- which do not block the ear canal at all -- for a few years and I had forgotten what rich, full sound was. These Q30s have a much richer sound, more bass (NOT annoying extreme bass, although you can choose to increase the bass level if you wish). The active noise cancellation works very well (not the absolute best I have heard, but nearly as good) however I think that blocks out the world a bit too much. I prefer the normal mode or, if I am listening out for deliveries or a phone call, I like the "transparent" mode which effectively turns the ANC around and lets you hear the outside world in addition to whatever you're beaming into the headphones. Battery life so far has been incredible. Again, I'm coming from tiny wraparound bone conducting phones with a tiny battery, so these chunky Q30s last much, much longer.

title: Good for music, not great for phone calls *UPDATE 1 call quality* *Update 2 long term durability*
text: I was hoping for something I could use for listening to music, gaming and working from home. Comfort: I have large ears, and can easily wear these all day without discomfort. Stays on my head fine with short hair, but it tended to slip a little with long hair. Noise cancellation: Good but not perfect, felt a little uncomfortable pressure since it was my first set. Got used to it quickly. I can slip these on and its dead quiet in most situations. Music: Very good sound for the price, no complaints. Gaming: Using the included cable, not Bluetooth, for gaming. Replacing a set of AKGs that had a busted channel. These are more comfortable and I didn't have any issues (tested in Cyberpunk and a few others) Work/Phone calls: Can't recommend these for working if you use the built in Mic. After switching to these, I got significantly more complaints from clients that they had difficulty hearing me. Usually they said my voice was distorted, or that it sounded like I was in a box/can (compared to a cheap wired apple earphone) *SEE UPDATE* Battery: Haven't tested the 40 hour claim, but below 20% it starts to give off a "battery low" warning which interrupts my work/listening so I usually don't run it dry. But I can get by with charging these just once or twice a week, and it charges really fast. Sadly, I'll have to look for something else for work due to the poor mic performance, which is a shame because I like using these otherwise. Update: Since the most recent firmware update, I am no longer getting complaints about the audio quality during phone calls. There is an issue where sometimes the audio gets really distorted on calls, but quickly changing the audio device from the headset to the phone and back fixes it. An annoying glitch, but its rare. Update 2: After about 2 years of ownership, the ear cup padding cover started to deteriorate. It's mostly a cosmetic issue. Eventually, the inner and outer half of the cover has started to separate, exposing the foam pad inside. To be clear, I used this headset constantly and extensively 40-100 hours per week during this period. I have decided to upgrade the earcups to some thicker, genuine lambskin which which should hopefully hold up much better. (Comparison photo attached)

title: Great value, but after 1 year, broken—
text: My office decided recently that cubicles were the way to go, and with that, my misophonia grew. I have a set of wireless Anker earbuds that I have a love/hate relationship with, but after wearing for hours, my ears would be in agony, so I thought some over-the-head style would be better suited. For a year, these have been terrific for what I need. I love how easy it is to switch from NC to transparency. The sound is just good enough for sitting in an office. The NC feature works well enough. If it worked any better, then I'd probably never use the feature. Being in an office, I still sort of need to be able to be aware of my surroundings, even if I don't want to, if that makes any sense. Anyway. I didn't buy these for their superior sound quality. I just needed reliable and within budget. These fit that bill. But, now I have to bandaid them because the headpiece broke above the right ear. Not the clip where the band slides where most folks have had issues. No. Mine broke further down. It doesn't affect the quality of sound or functionality, but it's annoying and actually pretty sharp edged. So I have to tape it. Which is not the look I was going for. Not that I had a look I was going for at all to begin with, but this equates to tape on the rails of eye glasses, and I just do not approve. Either way. They're good headphones, but not at all durable, unfortunately. I'd have probably broken them a long time ago if I used them outdoors. I figured they'd be safe indoors in an office environment. Guess I was wrong. Bummer.

title: I have a giant head, legit hat size 8 1/4 and these are comfortable
text: I have a for real giant head so I don't get to just wear any ol' headphones I want. The few I have had that I was able to stretch around my giant melon failed quickly. Some faired better than others but I could always tell that they would fail eventually because they were all tight feeling and uncomfortable. These Q30 phones are not tight, they are totally comfortable. I wear them about 8 hours a day with no discomfort whatsoever and they don't seem to be strained by the massive girth of my cranium. This is truly miraculous. I have tried quite a few of the "big head friendly" headphones and these are the only ones I think will last more than a month or two before they break. If they do break I will be back to update and take away as many stars as I can. So you might be wondering - if these fit your giant skull, mister actual big head person on the internet, then why - pray tell - aren't you giving them 5 stars? Seems a bit odd, don't you think? You have seen the first glimmer of hope for a pair of totally comfortable head phones in your entire life and you are only giving them 4 stars, what rubbish. But the fact of the matter is, dear reader, that these headphones basically sound like crap at anything above half volume. So there's that. In the big scheme of things, all headphones considered, they sound pretty bad. I have heard good headphones and these are not it. I wish to whomever has the power that I even had the option to buy good sounding headphones that were also comfortable atop my magnificent dome. But guess what, if these hold up I am seriously going to order about 10 more pairs just in case they stop making them. So they can't sound THAT bad, right? Right. But they don't sound good, either. title: Decent entry level ANC Headphones under $100
text: For less than $100, I got an ANC headphones with App support for firmware updates and customizable EQ settings. That and a hard case was worth the extra dollars spent over getting the Q20. I previously ordered the black Q30 which had a compartmentalizations rectangular hard case. The blue one I re-ordered during the Valentines Day sale ($59.99) is a smaller oval case with no compartmentalizations inside (no accessory pockets or grooves for the ear cups). The customizable EQ was a must for me as I listen to a wide range of music and don’t like heavy bass drowning out the music. It’s not audiophile level of crispness and separation of frequencies (low frequencies/sub bass not reproduced cleanly) but the 8-band audio helps. The Soundcore EQ setting is too muddy for my listening and use a custom version of the Piano EQ. This is my first ANC and for my work from home needs during the pandemic, it’s passable. The right cup touch toggle for ANC is hit or miss and ALWAYS interrupts the audio with a spoken notification (You get multiple beeps during phone calls). The Bluetooth range is great. I’ve had no issues with dropouts when walking away from my device at @20 ft between several walls/rooms at home. It does connect to multiple devices at a time. HOWEVER, the headphones have some switching issues which can be annoying. There is also a considerable volume drop off when toggling (perhaps intentional) between devices (when it works!). Honestly this get fixed by a firmware upgrade as I find it wicker disconnecting all devices and reconnecting manually. Despite the shortcomings I’ve listed above, they are little quirks as the majority of the headphones suits my needs. If you need an ANC headphone that cuts out most of the noise at home (read: kids!), this is a no brainer especially if you get it for the price I did.

title: Fine for price range
text: I purchased these solely for use when traveling and on airplanes. The only thing that really matters to me is the noise cancellation and it was below par. They were decently helpful with the fuzzy/turbulent airplane noises but that was it. I did not help with other sounds or voices at all. I actually tried to ask someone a few rows away to speak more softly because I could still hear them clearly with the volume up and noise cancelling on. I also purchased Beats Studio3s and the Anker Soundcore Q30s. Each of the three models were marginally better than the last (as the price went up) but none were worth keeping. I recently used my husband’s Sony headphones and I’ve finally accepted that only Sony or Bose will have good noise cancellation and nothing under $300 is going to really very well for what I am looking for.

title: Tl;Dr Solid 4.5 stars
text: I love these headphones. The lows are heavy which, is great for someone who likes heavier music, enjoys listening to lower tones for sleep, or for playing video games. Most people want will want to adjust the tone quality and they can do that by choosing a preset or customizing the equalizer. However, there are times you will need to be corded (like a call or if plugged into a ps4 controller) and you will end up with the default sound. You can still listen to music while on a call. These aren't gaming console compatible. The app has settings for sleeping and will even play sounds like "white noise" or "rain." The headphones will make your ears warm/hot and it may cause you to take them off after a little bit of time just to cool off. I don't mind the heat because the noise canceling is simply phenomenal and there are alternate settings for noise canceling in the app. The spatial quality makes it feel like the sounds are in your head instead of speakers on your head. The volume is controllable with the buttons on the headphones themselves or through any connected device. The volume is loud enough to be loud without blowing your eardrums or creating distortion. They're a solid build and they have a little bit of weight to them. The padding is thick and kind of gives it a luxury feel.

title: I love these.

They're very comfortable to me and I like the pink color :) They're great at work for helping me focus and even better when I'm at the gym. They also come in handy when I don't want the sales people at the front door of the gym to try to pitch what ever 'great deal' they have. I just put these on and pretend like I can't hear. I know it's a little rude, but I just want to work out lol.

title: Nice headphones for the money!

title: Don't waste money on a Bose
text: I've owned 2 Bose quiet35 noise cancelling headphones over the years, but after awhile either a speaker goes out of or the foam padding breaks down and disintegrates. So I thought this time I would try a cheaper alternative. I admit I was skeptical and had almost convinced myself that I would be sorry for spending a lot less money on ear cancelling headphones that would end up not working. I was wrong. These Q30 headphones, in my opinion, are as good as Bose quiet35 in both hardware and performance. Again, these are only my opinions. I find little to no difference in the noise cancelling performance, the sound quality is the same for both brands, carrying case and accessories are the same, comfort and fit (covering the ears) is also the same, in fact for me the Q30's are more comfortable that the Bose. I read other reviews that say your head gets hot after you wear them for a long time. I put no stock in comments like that, because every body is different. Some people sweat, some don't. Some like spinach, some don't etc.............. So far, after a month of use, the only real difference between the two is the prices. $80 vs $240+

For the battery longevity, the product lasts a very long time and if ANC is turned off, you will maybe charge them once every two weeks on heavy use. Supposedly a manual is available on the web - but the provided url just takes you to the marketing web page. Would it really add that much to cost to provide instructions in readable type (at least 12 point, black on white paper?) Don't buy this unless you have the eyes of a sharp-shooter!

title: Amazing
text: I've had these headphones for about a year and a half now and I absolutely love them. I'm verrrrry rough on headphones and usually buy cheaper ones just because I know they won't last. I decided to spend a bit more on these and I'm glad I did. At first, I was worried about their durability, because they seem to be made of a relatively brittle plastic. However, I have sat on/dropped/rolled over them in my sleep and every time they're just fine! I attribute this to the way they swivel and fold, and all the joints there being nicely reinforced. But that's not the best thing about these headphones! Despite using a weird usb type (and I had to buy a longer one because the included powercord is like 3') it does charge REALLY QUICKLY, and you really can get hours of use from a 5-minute charge. I also listen to obnoxious bass-heavy edm at full volumes, and the battery lasts a genuine 40+ hours, it's kind of crazy! This is all while using active noise-cancellation, which is also pretty excellent on these headphones. It's touch-activated, too, which makes me feel like I'm in the future and works flawlessly. To note, even after 18months of use, I don't sense any significant battery degradation with daily use. I've had ZERO issues connecting the bluetooth to my laptop, tablet, or phone. Works easy every time. Apparently the mic works well too, I've never had any complaints so long as I have the cups on the right ears. Music quality is, in my opinion, excellent, and while I'd always like MORE bass, it definitely registers. The cups will shake around your ears at all the right times and that's good enough for me. Note that I'm not exactly an audiophile, but it all sounds great. Would recommend these to anyone and would love to buy more from this company in the future.

title: Believe The Hype!!
text: I traded my Bose QC35 for the Sony XM4 (pictured) and I thought I had the very best headphones. Well, that is until I received the Soundcore Life Q30. I purchased the Sony's for $350 and I purchased the Q30 on sale here on Amazon for $69. OMGosh, the Life Q30's exceeded my expectations. Not just hype. These are the real deal. The sound is amazing and without exaggeration the noise cancellation blew me away. THEN, to cap if off, when listened to with the Soundcore App, the sounds goes to a whole new level. Do they get loud? ABSOLUTELY YES!. I can turn the Sony's fully up, but the Q30 will blow you away at 75% of max volume. In my picture you will see the Sony's in their case and that is where they have been since I purchased the Q30. I enjoy bass but not the kind that distorts. The bass on these is smooth and made me smile with every note. I listened to them for 5 straight hours as I cleaned the house. walked from room to room and never lost the signal and I never experience ear fatigue, although they did get a little sweaty. Bottom line, Believe The Hype. Believe the 4 and 5 star reviews. Best on the market!

title: Fantastic purchase.
text: What can I say? These things are impressive! The value is insane. I have used other "brand name" headphones in the past and are they nice? Absolutely. Do they sound good and feel good? Absolutely. Are they outrageously priced? Absolutely. These bad boys on the other hand are all of that at half, and sometimes a quarter, of the cost. I have a different Bluetooth speaker from Soundcore and I love it so I thought I would give these a try. I wouldn't say that I'm an expert by any means, but I have spent time in the audio industry so I'm not completely clueless. You don't have to have the app that partners with this product but I highly recommend it. It's free and easy to use. The noise cancelling is above average and the headphones feel great overall. Very solid but not cumbersome or heavy. Bought these to replace an old pair of earbuds for a 4 hour flight to Vegas and I literally wore them the entire flight. If you're looking for value price but top quality, look no further.

The cable catches easily if you put it behind your neck, and if you put it in front it looks goofy. Seem to have much worse connection than the Phaiser BHS-530 as well. title: You won't be disappointed
text: At this price point, these rival competitors who charge double to triple. My first impressions enjoying classical music was a very solid yet responsive Sonic stage with a warmth at the bottom end. Then I switched to jazz. The highs seem crisp without being brittle. The mids, as I progressed through a jazz playlist varied from great definition to a small but detectable distortion. However, to clarify, this distortion was not from these ear buds as I initially thought but were part of the recording itself. The ear buds were faithfully reproducing content like they should. Do they reproduce content like my studio headphones and tube amplifier? No they don't, these are not designed for that application, however, considering the engineering tradeoffs for portability and affordability these ear buds set a very high standard indeed. Buy several, you won't be disappointed

They’re good for gym headphones. You may not be looking for music quality but just something to pump you up. Additionally they’re very convenient and light. Wireless and Bluetooth gets rid of all the wires and tangles. The material feels good and sweat resistant and I was able to pair them easily without much hassle. Additionally I haven’t heard any drops yet. For less than $20 there is understandable compromises. Sometimes it’s build quality other times it’s design. title: Great Bluetooth headset for a great price
text: Feb 20, 2019 - There's isn't a whole lot I cant say about this headset that hasn't already been mentioned by countless others, they're just that good. Battery life is great for how small they are, hours of listening time and days of standby. The fit comfortably on my ear and do not slip out despite any exercise activity I've thrown at them. They're also comfortable to use for prolong periods of time, unlike previous in-ear headset I've used in the past. I would have no issues recommending or re-purchasing these IPX7 Bluetooth headphones. UPDATE: 08/14/2019 - Battery life is still. I use them nearly ever day during the week, twice a day during my morning and afternoon commute to work, 15-20 minutes per use. I charge it on Sunday and pretty much leave it unplugged throughout the week. So far, it lasted all the way through Friday afternoon without any needing to be recharged. As for the performance, that a different story. Not sure what happen when, but depending on who the cable rest in the back of my head, the audio might cut off one of the ear pieces for a second or two, or come across with a bit of static. It doesn't always do it and it doesn't last a long time, usually shifting the cable is enough to reset the issue, but it has become noticeable over the past couple weeks. Again, I do not think this is a fault of the manufacturing process, more than likely a result of one of the kid messing with it, but felt it should be noted. It is advertised as a sports headphone, so I expect it to survive a bit of rough housing, but I also don't expect miracle when it comes to it being kid proof. Overall, still very happy with this purchase.

title: I've loved these little earbuds for four years! Still going strong.
text: My Otium beats will be four years old in July. I've tried to upgrade earbuds (nothing too pricey) and have always been disappointed. 🏋🏼‍♀️ I wear them while I work out. They have a great sound and block outside noise pretty well. They help me get in my zone in my own little world, and I love them. 💦 I tried to swim in them, and while they're waterproof, they stop playing as soon as my head is underwater. 🎧 The plastic ear tips, which are super comfortable for my tiny ear holes, eventually broke down — as aging plastic will do. I replaced them with BLLQ Replacement Ear Tips, which are nearly identical to the originals [[ASIN:B07FF9DN5K BLLQ Replacement Ear Tips]]. 💵 They're $20. BT 4.1. So not the newest Bluetooth, and I'm sure Bose sounds better. But at this price point, I love these little guys. 🏆 Actually, I got them on a lightning sale for $13, so even better! So I paid $20 for the earbuds AND replacement tips. 🌚 I still want something new because I just want something new, you know. But knowing the disappointment I always feel with my attempted replacements, I'll probably keep using these sweet little babies. 🔊 I don't know what the heck they're talking about with the "noise canceling" in the product title. There is no ACTIVE noise-canceling, but the earbuds do form slight seals, which have a passive noise-canceling effect. I think I actually bought them for noise-canceling, but whatever. It's overrated as a feature unless you are willing to pay hundreds of dollars. In sum, these are great earbuds, especially if you're prone to losing things and hate to feel heartbroken about losing something expensive.

title: Great value!
text: For the price you can't go wrong. I had a pair of Powerbeats wireless earbuds for about a year and half. I used them 5 or 6 days a week. They stopped working. After some research on Amazon, reading reviews I decided to purchase these. I've had them about 2 months. They work great, the sound quality is decent. The fit and finish aren't quite as nice as the Beats but for $20, it's great! I'm only using them for 45-50 minutes at a time and then re-charging them. Sometimes I forget to re-charge them and use them again the next day. Haven't run out of battery yet. For the price I can buy at least 3 or 4 pairs of these compared to Powerbeats wireless earbuds (refurbs). If you want to spend $20 on wireless ear buds, these are them! Update 3/27/2019 Had them about 5 months now. I have been wearing them on longer runs, close to 2 hours. No issues. Saw a coworker in the gym with the same earbuds. We compared notes and you just can't go wrong for ~$20. As I write this they are selling for $16.89. Are you kidding me? Buy them. Update 12/31/2021 3 years. Still working, no issues. My teen age son has gone through multiple pairs because he's hard on them (swings them around by the connecting cable, etc) but mine are like the little engine that could or the Energizer Bunny, they keep going and going. Love them.
