text: I will start by saying that, like most people, I am not a sound aficionado and am not paying hundreds of dollars for earbuds. title: Bluetooth is laughable and quality is low, but they get the job done in a pinch
text: Yeah, theres a few things I don't like about these. Here are the cons: - Once it gets to 30% volume, they repeat "Battery Low" couple minutes until they die completely, interrupting what ever it is you're listening to - Sometimes it has issues connecting, especially if your content is playing before you turn them on. For some reason, having music playing when I pair them causes them to not remember my phone, which makes my phone not remember it, which requires me to turn them off, reset the Bluetooth on my phone, turn them on in discovery, discover them, pair them, and then start the song again. Tedious. - The Bluetooth range is laughable. I have a clear connection when my phone is in the arm sleeve pocket of my running shirt, but it's choppy if it's any further. This makes keeping it in my shorts pocket less than ideal. - They shorted out on me and turned off when I was running in some moderate rain. I know they're "water resistant", but my iPhone headphones keep up better than that. - They're not as sturdy as I'd hoped. They've popped out of my ears a few times due to sweat. - They don't have a resting mode out of ear. Some headphones have magnets that connect to each other when not in use which makes them function like a necklace. These just dangle and flop around and fall off of you. Here are the pros: - Cheap - They get the job done (but they do it badly) Analysis: - Spend $15 more dollars on something more serious. Bluetooth technology is becoming less costly to make these days, and you'd be surprised what you can find in some proper $30-$60 headphones. If I was on the Price is Right, I'd put the value of these things at $15 total. If that's your cuppa tea though, go for it.

title: Lots of attributes, excepting the actual sound
text: I wanted to give these a two- or three-star rating, but to be fair, for $25 bucks, the build quality is very good, the comfort and fit is good (and the relatively high pressure they exert on the ears really helps with sound isolation), the battery life is good and the Bluetooth connection to my iPhone and computer is good. The sound though ... it's fairly bad. I've had some cheap headphones that punch far above their weight clas, but these are not among them. To me, they're a bit out of balance, with too much mid and upper bass, making the mids sound a bit recessed. That's not necessarily bad because these headphones are seriously lacking in clarity and detail. Back to back with a set of wired Philips Fidelio M1 Mk2 headphones (which I bought "refurbished" for $40), the JVCs have a bit of a murky transistor radio sound, and you don't want that right in your face. Better to have the pounding drums. There's not a lot of low bass, or a lot of high treble (that I can hear, at least) and cymbals entirely lack detail--just a hiss. Still, it's not so bad you can't get most of the gist of whatever you're listening to. These work for playing music when you're doing something else, like cleaning the garage or mowing and don't want to deal with a cord, or worry about destroying something expensive if you sweat too much. The couple calls I had on them seemed fine, nothing notably good or bad. I'm sure they'd be fine for listening to spoken word programs.

Watching TV - I sync them to my Apple TV and listen to TV when I'm doing things around the house and so I don't have to crank up the volume on my TV 3. Ultimately I get the sound I want, so it's not a big deal 2. They sometimes move a little bit, where they drop down in the back a little so I just readjust them All in all a great buy, definitely worth every penny.

title: These are AMAZING!
text: I LOVE my AfterShokz Aeropex. They are better than I expected. Design is comfortable to wear all day. Stays in places. Sounds great! If you are in the market for great sounding headphones that are awesome for music and great for conversations than you must get a pair.

title: Beast earphones Ive owned.
text: I keep them on 8 hours a day. Comfortable. Great sound. I use silicone plugs when I'm in the shop and the sound quality goes down but not too bad.

title: AMAZING headphones ever!!
text: Update: I love mine so much I bought another pair for my sister. I absolutely love these headphones. I didn't think you could get good sound out of a device not stuck in your ears, but sure I was wrong!! I have small ears and regular earbuds are too big and never, ever stay put in my ears, which means I drop them on the floor constantly which requires cleaning...big inconvenience. On top of that, while I like listening to music, books, podcasts I can't do it while walking because I can't stand not being able to hear what's going on around me. A friend told me about open ear AfterShokz and it took me a few months to finally take the plunge. I got them a few days ago with 60% battery... I listened music for ~4 hours before I got a low battery notification. I recharged them and I had them on every day since, so battery life seems good. Other Pros: They are very light, fit well and I can wear them for a few hours without being uncomfortable. The sound is very clear and the bass is good. Noise cancelation is not big, but that's the point!! I like that I can hear what's happening around me. I can have a conversation and listen to my stuff. I can go on a walk and hear cars coming and people getting close. The mic is good for taking calls- the other person could hear me clearly. The Bluetooth pairing was very easy. The controls are easy to master. The packaging was great, with clear instructions, 2 charging cables, a rubber storage pouch, a waist travel pack and a pair of noise cancelation ear plugs. Cons: It would nice if you could adjust the width of the connecting band, but it's not a big deal for me.

title: LOUD BEEPS!!!!
text: I'm taking off a couple stars because I'll never be able to use the on board buttons for skip and volume control (without removing the speakers from close to my ears first). They put in STUPID G*D D*MN LOUD beeps on every function, when they could have had no beeps at all. Why do you need to hear a beep at 100% volume to confirm that you've hit the volume down button? The beeps cause me physical pain, and create sensitivity which lasts for minutes. These headphones already sound very crisp and sharp, and the aftereffects of the beeps make me too sensitive to the sharp sound quality of my media. The sad thing is that this hardware has no capacity to connect to a computer for data, so there will be no chance to fix this error with a firmware update. This is really unforgivably stupid. I don't know how this made it through the development and testing process without being caught.

title: Comfortable to wear.
text: If driving long distance I like to lister to audiobooks, can hear the books as well as everything going on around you. Also use at home every day.

title: Most comfortable headphones all day long
text: I bought these specifically for my all day long virtual learning sessions. I produce sessions for corporate trainings and needed headphones I could comfortably wear all day. I tried normal speakers (did not work well for me), I tried ear phones (hated the wire connections), I tried over the ear headphones (uncomfortable all day) and then I got these. They are perfect for me. I needed the 8 hour battery life for all day sessions so I paid a bit more for this model. I use the speakers only (my mic is a separate table top mic) in my classes held in Zoom, Webex and Teams. Sound is good (used use for talking sound only, not music). Comfort is the best of all methods I have tried. Noise cancellation is not applicable since these sit on the jawbone and not over the ear--so the ear is open and can hear all background noise (although one can insert supplied foam ear plugs to block outside noise and still hear sound from these headphones). My only recommended improvement would be someway to change and reduce the headband size so the band around the rear of the head would fit more snug against my head. The headphones stay in place well yet because the band is not snug against my head (see photo), the band hits against my collared shirts, car headrests and even my bed pillows if I lie down. I knew this from the product listing but because I needed the 8-hour battery life, I ordered these rather than a youth model that may fit more snug since the other models do not have the 8 hour life. Because this was not a surprise to me, I still rate these 5-star since they fill the advertised description, do it well, are well built, sturdy and most of all, are the most comfortable headphones I have found for my purposes. I love them.

title: they work perfectly
text: Bone conduction does not give you the best sound quality! But, open ears is better when cycling and just plain comfort. I have worn these all day, 12 hours and no pain. I wear a lot of headsets, earplugs, and these are my go to for most activities. If you like to hear your environment, there is nothing better.

title: Make sure you know what you are getting before buying these.

I want to be aware of my surroundings, but also listen to my music. I also wanted to be able to listen to my music without it bothering others around me. If that is what you need, these are the ones that meets your needs. The music quality takes a hit because of the way it is being delivered to you, but in my opinion isn't enough to warrant me throwing them out. I hope this helps anyone who is unsure about these.

BUT GUESS WHAT Breakage at the same spot as the others. I don't sleep in them or lay on them or anything. I generally take good care of stuff. I've had them almost a year without much visible wear. My kid crashed into me the other day, and I heard a pop. Same spot as my other ones. I'm done with this brand for now. Maybe their next generation will be more durable. Oh, and the charging cable design is garbage. The connection isn't solid, and the magnets in the cable mean I can't just leave my cable plugged in. Once, a cable fell into a cat water dish and did some electrochemistry. Another time it tried to charge a necklace. You can't leave the live cable anywhere near ferromagnetic materials. title: Great! For What They Are
text: These are not the highest quality audio you will ever hear, but they are not engineered for the audiophile. What they do do they do well. First, sound quality is good, especially for something not in or over your ears — its actually pretty cool when you think about it. They do leave your ears open but the sound does tend to drown out the other sounds, but you have the volume control so adjust accordingly — on high you will hear very little else, on low you can listen and have a conversation. They do vibrate on your ears with high bass levels, but nothing you won’t get used to if you have mastery of your id. What these do really really well is allow you to comfortably listen for long periods of time without headphone fatigue; I wear them for hours with no discomfort, including when not using them, and while wearing glasses — they are, bar none, the most comfortable headphones I’ve every used. I mainly bought them to listen to audiobooks but find myself using them to enjoy sound when otherwise I’d have to avoid it... Now I can pretend to listen to my wife complain while I really enjoy a nice song in the background. These just might save my marriage. I’ve set all of my other headphones aside and honestly see no need for them now. My one complaint is the light never turns blue when they are supposedly charged (annoying), but I’m not returning them. Ever. I give them 5 stars because I never want to take them off. I may buy a second pair so I always have a pair charged (that’s how much I use them).

title: Great little device!
text: Amazon is getting more than a bit daft, they asked me to assign a star rating to these for "noise cancelling" abilities. They're going senile if you ask me. The whole point of these is that you aren't cuddled up in your own private little space, oblivious to your surroundings like the trendy lemmings with their earpods and such. I'm getting to the point of needing to lobby for a ban on earpods / earbuds in my office, because none of the kids can hear you when you speak to them, because it cuts them off from the world. They seem like they are literally deaf in the head and you can't see that they are wearing them (no cords anymore!), it's really pretty rude of them. On the flip side, it is rather funny, as you do get to see just how jumpy '20 somethings are these days, so many of them freak out when they get startled while "rocking out" or whatever they're doing. But I digress... The Aftershokz are amazing, they deliver crisp, clear sound, while allowing you to not get snuck up upon by bears, a mugger, a Tesla, or God forbid, your Boss. I've not used them for phone calls, but an identical pair that my girlfriend uses, sound a bit tinny (like an OK speaker phone), not terrible, but also not amazing. We didn't buy them for use as hands free set for phones, we got them for music and for that they sound great. The controls are easy to use and somewhat intuitive. Now I just need to figure out if you can force YouTube to play media when the display is blanked. I understand it would be counter intuitive, but for me it would be a useful feature. Battery life is acceptable, they last at least the whole day at the office and into a workout session. Overall a great purchase. Would buy again, but I hope I won't need to for a good long time, or else I'll need to come back and significantly lower my rating on account of a lack of durability. We do both have hard shell cases to store them in. Aftershokz provide a case for them, made out of what seems to be neoprene, but it doesn't really make me feel confident that it would protect the device from damage.

text: I bought these Aftershokz in search of a great sound quality sport earphone that doesn’t fall out of my ears, willing to pay good money for the set that satisfies all needs and durable. The physical design of these are top notch feels like nothing at all, unless you’re going to lay your head back on something. And then I have to acknowledge that it is state of the art technology, the bone resonance, 2000 Tom Clancy stuff. Like other reviews, the lack of bass is a draw back... I don’t think I hear ANY base. I can feel some lower frequencies vibrating on the contact point and that’s it. I tried the ear plugs and that didn’t help. If i put my fingers all the way in my ear canals I can hear the bass and then there’s other frequencies that sound muffled. I would say the sound totally lacks good frequency range, vibrance, or anything , just as you would expect with jammers if they’re not in the ear canal well. The manual it comes with has the sound specifications. I usually check these like frequency range if I can first. 20 hz- 20khz is super basic. 8 hz would be some good bass. 22khz would be a little more decent treble. But against i feel my connection with the sound just sucks. I know it’s different bypassing my ear drums and I’ve put these on very open minded. SO, other than the novelty of the rare technology, the sport comfort alone is not worth $160.

title: Great concept, painful beeps and pops
text: Update: dropping from 3 stars to 1 star. 6 months after purchase, battery life has dropped to under 2 hours per charge with 3-4x/wk usage. Again, unacceptable for a premium priced product with modern battery technology. Original: This is my first set of bone conduction headphones. I bought these to be able to hear my wife, kids, and surroundings while listening to stuff. They work great for that. I love the open ear concept. The physical design is really attractive, but it has very irritating operational issues. As other reviews have mentioned, the beep is loud, and always at the same volume level. If you put pressure on the sound piece, and press it to your head, it becomes unbearably loud. In addition, there are random, painful, vertigo-inducing pops occasionally, usually when connecting, playing/ pausing, incoming call while playing something, powering on or off, or opening an app. Not all or even most of the time, just every once in awhile. Probably not Aeropex's fault, but they should have a limiter. It feels like my ears are being boxed when it happens, and makes me dizzy and nauseous for a moment. I literally have to find a wall or piece of furniture to stabilize and recalibrate. Pressing these to your face (if you lie down on them) increases the perceived volume. The single multifunction button on the left is difficult to find by feel. There is no texture to differentiate it. if you haven't used these before, it takes a bit to get used to them. They feel buzzy on your head at high volumes. Even at low volumes they felt strange. Other people can't hear them, and you can barely hear them when removed from your head. If I use them for a long time at higher volume, they can cause my back teeth to hurt. With the beeping and popping, it doesn't feel like a premium product that justifies the higher price. If I lost or broke these, I would probably buy a cheap pair until Aeropex worked these issues out, but I would definitely buy an open ear headset again, even with the compromises inherent in the design.

title: Great for background noise while working, but don't expect much more
text: I've been using these for about 160 hours per month since I got them a few months ago. Initially I was very impressed by the novelty of bone-conduction audio, but now that I'm used to them I can provide an honest review. I bought these using a company stipend. The reason I chose these over conventional headphones or earbuds was because I have to be able to hear my surroundings at work. I'd like to keep this review concise for your sanity and mine, so here are some things I like and don't like about these headphones. The good: • Reasonably lightweight • Astounding battery life. These last me an entire 12 hour shift without a charge, after months of use • Acceptable microphone quality for meetings/phone calls • Good voice clarity in calls or listening to podcasts • Fairly simple, easy to find controls • Low profile. You'll sometimes forget you're wearing them and they don't stick out much (I can wear a half face respirator + safety goggles with these) The bad • The audio quality isn't all they advertise it to be. Expect the same audio experience as cheap $20 earbuds. The mids are fine, but the bass and some high tones suffer from severe distortion at volume settings higher than 50%. This is expected from bone-conducting headphones. If you want great audio, shop for conventional earbuds/headphones. • After a few months of use I find myself having to readjust their position on my head every hour or so. They tend to slip/move around a little when I turn my head side to side or up and down. Pretty sure the spring material in the band is wearing out over time That's about it. Would I spend my own money on these? Probably not, but I do not regret the purchase. There are MUCH better headphones/earbuds available for a lot less money. But, as I mentioned, I need to be able to hear my surroundings. Not many headphones offer that. It's a good compromise if you're willing to spend the money.

text: I was thrilled to find that this product existed very recently at the Oregon Ducks bookstore in Eugene while I was traveling. I think this is a great feature as you can carry on a conversation with a flight attendant without having to adjust your headphones or take them off, you can hear bikes/runners/people/animals coming up on you when on a community path, and in general, you can hear the outside world and you have the safety of knowing your surroundings. title: If this is what you need, it amazing while it lasts.
text: I have had aftershokz headphones for the last 4 years and have used them almost daily First I had an air which I purchased shortly after release. I ended up getting another set on sale but gave it away to a friend. That first set of airs I still have and they still work, but battery life has faded predictably. I have used them in the shower, cycling on my commute to work, doing chores around the house. Probably in the 1-3 hours per day. 2 years ago I upgraded to the aeropex and the difference is marked. 1) The sound quality is excellent for open ear headphones. Read some reviews of the sound to understand what you are getting. Base is not a forte here. 2) Voices are clear, call quality is excellent and the microphone is a real standout feature. 3) The fit is excellent and light and it is very easy to forget you are wearing them. Far more comfortable than wearing a mask. 4) The bluetooth range is among the best I have ever had. It can actually be annoying because if you don't turn it off, they will reconnect in my front yard when I get home. 5) Waterproofing means I shower with these on. Have you ever watched a movie in the shower? It's awesome. 6) The ability to hear is perfect. 7) Battery life is better than stated, and standby is measured in weeks. The bad part. If you use these alot they will break. The transducer breaks loose after about 6-8 months of daily usage. I am on my third pair in 2 years. Warranty is excellent with quick replacements, but I am back to using my air set 1-2 times per year while I wait. I hope they come out with a newer more durable version soon.

title: Great set of open ear headphones
text: If you're looking for a pair of open ear headphones, this is a great option. I have pretty frustrating eustachian tube dysfunction that makes keeping in-ear headphones in all day very painful. I didn't realize there was another option until I discovered this pair. They are perfect for avoiding this discomfort and are generally very comfortable to have on my head all day (they don't squeeze or pinch like some over ears tend to do). Overall, I have to say these are a solid 4 stars. They charge quickly and retain a charge for quite a while (I've used them for several days in a row without charging with no problems - easy to plug in for a quick charge is necessary, though). However, there are a couple reasons I'd take away a star. The audio quality for video or audio calls is great, works perfectly for working from home, but the audio quality of you're trying to listen to music is not that great. It's a bit flat. Still works fine, but you're definitely not getting a hifi experience. If you're planning to simply listen to music, these might not be the best option for you. The second reason to take off a star is that while they can connect to two devices, the process is extremely cumbersome. In fact, the pairing itself is a bit frustrating at times. It works well if you have it paired to one device, but if you're trying to switch between phone calls and virtual calls on your computer, it can be annoying. All of that said, I'm really enjoying these headphones, especially given my ear issues. Definitely recommend for anyone who can't tolerate extended periods of time with in-ear headphones.

title: Exactly like the aeropex, but for smaller heads.
text: This is a smaller version of the aeropex, which is an excellent headset for every day use. If you have a smaller head, (distance around the back of your head is 9 1/2" or less) then these would be a good option to try. They obviously hug tighter than the original aeropex, but this minimizes interactions between the headband and things like collared shirts, or anything that you might lay your head against. I absolutely recommend the aeropex in general, especially for listening to spoken word content, like podcasts while going about daily life. They're also great for teleconferencing and phone calls. They don't sound the absolute best compared to conventional headphones, but what you give up in sound quality is more than made up for in usability and convenience. The headlining feature for bone conduction is the ability to listen to music as well as your environment at the same time, but they also work with earplugs (which are included) if you're trying to block out loud noises. If you use earplugs though, just make sure to hold both the volume up and volume down buttons to switch the eq. This makes them sound a lot better with earplugs. Like the og aeropex, It uses a proprietary magnetic connector to charge, which i wasnt so happy about at first. After using it for a while though, I'd rather have this than a usb connection with a flap (like on the titanium and the air). Plus, they give you two cables out of the box and spares don't cost too much. Finally, the water resistance is no joke. I've been wearing the original aeropex all day, every day since it came out and they've held up to showers and rain just fine. Just know that the mic will take a little while to work well after the headset gets wet. I think this is because the mic hole gets water in it and needs to dry out. The aeropex is an awesome product, and absolutely worth a try. If the regular one seems a little too big, the mini is also worth a look.

title: Nice concept and execution with shortsighted flaws
text: I like the open concept of bone conduction because I wear hearing aids and I can use these without covering the microphones in my hearing aids. They pretty much work as advertised, but with a few annoyances. The vibration takes some getting used to, but is really no longer an issue. The fit and flexibility are good and they produce a passable quality sound, but not anything close to immersive experience with high and low range sound. My biggest complaint is the charging cable and connection. The included proprietary magnetic charging cable is woefully short and as a result if the headphones get bumped slightly while sitting and charging, the cable disconnects enough to where no charge is flowing to the battery to recharge. Interesting concept, but clearly not well tested in the real world. Also, as a proprietary cable/connection, if you lose your cable, replacements are not easy or inexpensive compared to a regular USB Micro or USB C cable. Thankfully, they include an extra, but that has little to do with the flaw in the design. This design is well suited to keeping electronic components dry, but otherwise has no practical use. I would have bought the lower tier version, but it lacks flexibility and that is important, so I had to choose between annoyance and convenience and comfort. I do wish these were available in a low latency version with an APTX codec. I watch TV with headphones due to hearing loss and the sync is awful although my transmitter and headphones are supposedly BT 5.0

title: Excellent product for many reasons. See below.
text: I like to use these when I’m working in my shop or outside. I frequently want to wear ear protection, but still hear music and be able to talk on the telephone. Sound is not as good as earbuds, but it is reasonably close. The huge advantage is that I can use them while still physically blocking my ears. My wife and one granddaughter wear hearing aids, and they can use these to listen to music while simultaneously having their hearing aids in place. When used as a telephone outdoors, there is no wind noise to disrupt conversation. Recharging cord magnetically snaps into position, and works better than any other charging port I have ever used. Battery life is very good. I can use them through an eight hour day without running out. In summary, if you are a true audiophile, these probably will not give you as good as sound as you would like, but if you want your ears to remain available for situational awareness, or if your ears need to be blocked with some other thing, they are outstanding.

title: Really impressed
text: I've been running with the older Titanium model for years now without any real drama. I have to say the incremental changes added up. They're noticeably lighter, the audio is definitely improved. In theory they're more waterproof, and that makes sense with the new charger, but I run pretty regularly in storms with the old ones with no problems so I'm not sure what prompted that. Too early to say how these will hold up - my titaniums did break at once point but they replaced them immediately so I'm not super concerned, but they're so thin hopefully they've thought all that through.

title: An Audiophile Review
text: The packaging deserves mention...beyond anything I have ever bought. Superb! I unpacked the headphones very carefully as I thought there was a real probability that I would return these headphones. I am keeping them. The headphones will change the sound quality depending on the exact position you have them on, so you can move them around a bit to get the sweet spot for you. The comfort like others have said, is amazing....I too forgot I was wearing them at times. The sound will also depend on the volume you set them at, for those of you familiar with the Fletcher-Munson Curve. The midrange is STUNNING. Perhaps as clear as it gets. The detail is far beyond my expectations. For you base heads out there, you will be disappointed. Compared to a very good pair of headphones, it lacks dearly. There is severe roll-off of frequencies below 500 kHz. That being said, these headphones give me a good listening experience to classical, and most music that is not bass heavy. While I was listening, a phone call came in, and the audio on both sides was excellent. I am keeping these for casual listening, and also when doing certain sports. If you are looking for high fidelity headphones, look elsewhere, but for me these are a keeper for what they are made to do, and they do it well. If bass response was improved, they would be perfect...and I would pay more for the full bass to be there.

title: Solid performance, but only ok sound
text: Unlike the others in the reviews section, the beep from my unit is not too loud (ordered July 2021) so AfterShokz must have modified the firmware. Regardless, I tend to use my Apple Watch or iPhone to adjust the volume anyway, so I rarely hear the beep from pressing buttons on the headphones. The sound is about what I expected for bone conduction headphones: a little lacking in bass unless you turn it way up. If you do that, others can hear your music coming from the headphones faintly. I don't have any other bone conduction headphones at the moment because I've always returned previous models after hearing the sound leakage and lack of dynamic range. However, I will be keeping these ones because they are the best I've used so far. I've compared the mic in the Aeropex to the one in the AirPods Pro on conference calls, and the Aeropex mic sounds acceptable but slightly more muffled and flat (less treble, less bass). Overall, a good purchase if you're tired of having things stuck in or over your ears for most of the day, especially during the hot summer. However, now I have the problem of sweat forming under the contact pads of the Aeropex where they touch the skin in front of my ears.

title: Perfect for me!
text: I've been searching for earphones that would work in a particular situation. I normally wear hearing aids... I'm not deaf, but I have some hearing loss in the same frequencies as my wife's voice. That's all I have to say about that. I prefer wireless earbuds, but it's a hassle to have to take out my hearing aids, be sure to store them in a proper case and then not accidentally misplace them. I've tried the over ear headphone style... great sound but bulky and bit too obvious for my tastes. And of course, both earbuds and headphones tend to isolate you from ambient sounds... such as my wife's voice. I also have the type of hearing aid that allows you to bluetooth your music directly, and while that works great for phone calls, music doesn't sound that good and it kills the batteries to the point that hey won't even last a day. So I decided to try the Wireless Bone Conduction Headphones and I'm very pleased that I did! At first I tried a cheaper brand, but they weren't very comfortable and the buttons weren't very ergonomic. Then I switched to the AfterShokz Aeropex, oh man, what a difference! Very comfortable, ergonomic buttons and they sound great! Not as good as proper headphones, but plenty decent. Plus they allow me to keep my hearing aids in my ears and be able to hear my wife's voice! My only caveat is the charging cable. I absolutely love the ease of the magnetic connection, it's so much easier to use compared to typical usb micro cables! But, if you ever need to replace it, it's going to be a lot tougher to find than a micro usb cable. In summary, they're perfect for me. ,

title: not what expected
text: not all that clear. hurt the skull bone by the jaw after a while. Would advise trying before buying

title: Excellent quality
text: Love these! I returned 2 other headsets before finding these. They fit well, you don't even know you are wearing them and some quality is excellent. Bought these for a remote position to use on calls and zoom meetings. Highly recommend.

title: Best for people who love to hear their music while being able to hear what's important around you.
text: These are my first pair of bone conduction headphone and so far I am impressed. My hearing has always been important for me and my job but I never wanted to make the jump until my last pair of regular headphones broke. The quality of the construction is excellent, the sound is superb compared to what I thought they would be. Noise cancelation isn't like its going to be with regular headphones as these are around the ear and not in or over. With that being said I can still hear my music or videos even in the loundest areas. The company sends not only the headphones but a nice carrying case and two charges to go with it.

title: Where has this been all my life?
text: I always disliked headphones. They made my ears hot or itchy or both. I didn't like the muffled external sound. And I couldn't hear my little one near me. These Aeropex are FANTASTIC!!! It solved all my headphones issues. I can listen to my music and still hear the neighbor saying hello on my walk. Or I can hear traffic passing by. My little one calling for me. My ears are no longer itchy. I am in LOVE with Aeropex.

title: Our third pair
text: I originally bought a pair of these for my husband who runs marathons. He wanted a set of hesphones that would still allow him to hear traffic when he's out running marathons. He loved them so much, he bought me a pair. My son tried mine and loved them so much he wanted a pair. So we now have three pairs and we all wear them frequently. They are NOT noise canceling, but that is kind of the point. Also, when played at high volumes, you might get a headache. But otherwise, we love these things!

title: They really do the job
text: I time using them was very impressed I do construction work and I love them why didn’t I buy this one before.

title: Great bluetooth head set
text: I like the way you can hear such good sound without haveing it in your ears. I wear hearing aids like a lot of seniors and on some I have to take one out then its hard to hear conversation. Some ear buds just hang in your ear and it makes my ear sore after a while. I only wish the head band was adjustable as it hits things and the multi function button is not raised enough to find it quickly. Otherwise I love it.

title: The design is amazing!
text: My sons said "Wow"! They want them. Since their birthdays have passed they will get them as a Christmas present. I'm so happy with them. I also love that I can answer my cell phone on them. I can use them on my tablet or my Apple cell phone. I can also hear what people are saying because they sit very comfortable in front of my ears. I have not been able to wear the ones that go in my ear. I just wish I had learned of them sooner.

title: Great bone conduction earphones
text: Lightweight and with excellent battery life, these are the best bone conduction earphones I have seen to date. I tend to use the Aeropex all the time, even when I might otherwise use a straight in-ear headset. Sound quality is good (but not exactly the same as traditional earphones). I prefer having my hearing unimpaired when I am listening to music so these are perfect for me.

title: Very comfortable & crystal clear
text: I’ve never been a fan of in ear headphones. I heard about these headphones from my audiologist. My hearing dramatically improved in the sound test with this bone technology. I like how ear wax will not impact these earphones. I can listen to something and still allow my situational awareness to be around me. These are comfortable and there are 2 chargers.

title: Not Eye glass friendly
text: sounds good, works for awareness of surroundings. Only problem is when wearing glasses...Last a good 10 hours for me

title: Great for work and exercise
text: These Aeropex are well worth the money. I wear them for exercise and for work. Not only are they hidden by my hair (I got the grey version), but they allow you to hear the world around you, which is important if you’re on a bike or walking in an urban environment. The sound quality is great and, unlike the Titanium version (which are more like speakers placed close to the ear), these seem to be real bone conducting. I’m very pleased with this product.

title: I wasn’t really sure about them till I used them for a week
text: I waited over a week to write my review and I have to say I am quite happy with them. After owning more then 2 pairs of air pods, and loosing one, and one sounded blown out I decided enough was enough. I use headphones occasionally and I find these very comfortable on my head and the way the music plays through the bone conductivity is really nice. The best way to describe them is it’s almost like having background music wherever you are. As the sound quality for phone calls is really good. Music sounds good until you crank up the sound. I find the bass to be lacking and vibrates which I have read out in other reviews. However after using them during the past week I decided they really are what I wanted. The magnetic charger works great, battery life per charge is around 5-6 hrs and I like when you turn them on it announces the battery level. Overall I am pleased with them. If you happen to be looking for headphones Strictly for music not sure these are the pair for you. But the “Coolness factor” is there for sure and I really love the open ear concept.

title: Excellent Headphones- bone conduction is spectacular
text: These are truly spectacular earphones especially if you can't have your ear canals covered. With these on you can have a conversation with someone nearby and never have to take them off. The bone conduction works great. I've never had that type of headphone before, so was surprised of how well the sounds work- I typically use them for phone calls, so I can't speak to the music quality- but can say that voice quality is great. Would definitely recommend them for anyone that can't have their ears completely covered.

title: No more sweaty ear canals!
text: All said and done I am enjoying these headphones/buds very much. In the ear buds no matter how good a fit become irritating to the ear after couple hours. I can wear these as long as I want with no effects. Bass not wonderful but also not non-existent a fair trade off for comfy ears in my opinion. People do look twice and think it's a medical attachment lol...screw em! They work with my glasses on too guess ear piece on glasses would matter if there real thick, I just like these that's all. Very happy

title: Get them!
text: Perfect for podcasts or audio book listening. Amazing battery life. So light, almost forget they are on. Music is decent, but don’t expect hifi sound. Worth the price!

title: Great but defective
text: These mini headphones are great. They’re as advertised. But I had to send them back because they kept shutting off when I lifted my high collar jacket, or taking off a shirt, which both were touching the back of the headphones and causing the headphones to automatically turn off. Hopefully only my headphones were defective, because I would like to re-order them again.

title: Light and Convenient, and I Can Hear My Wife!
text: These are open ear, so there is no noise cancellation. The bone induction works very well. The telephone conversations are clear for both speaking and hearing. I am on calls for nearly 4 hours a day, and the battery lasts for two days in between charges. You will hear everything going on around you - no one needs to shout to get your attention. That’s a big plus for my needs.

title: Excellent sound quality!!!
text: Comfortable lightweight headphones with amazing sound quality and excellent noise cancelling and well over 8 hours of music and phone calls. I love these headphones!

title: Good product but needs longer battery life
text: The sound is pretty good but they are fairly loose on my head and I need them to fit a little snugger to get best sound quality. I definitely cannot lean back against some thing with them on or it’s uncomfortable. Really wish the battery would last at least 12 hours since I have them on all day. But overall pretty decent product

title: Love these!
text: I was very pleased with my headphones/earbuds. I can’t tolerate buds in my ears so decided to try these. Great sound quality as a listening device and my husband says I sound fine on his end. So great product. Glad I bought this device!

title: Loses connection constantly and shuts off for no reason
text: My headphones keep randomly disconnecting and shutting off when I still have 60% + battery life. It has happened multiple times a day for the past week or so that I have owned them while listening to audio books or on phone calls. My phone (brand new pixel 5) is in my pocket or within the same room and should not be having connection issues. This is very disheartening, as I had my previous pair of aftershocks for over 4 years and loved them. I plugged them in last night and this morning I can't even get them to turn on. I will sadly be making arrangements to return. The headphones themselves, when they are working, are most excellent and I love the smaller design vs. the old.

title: Aeropex at 3 weeks
text: I'll include complaints. But really, these things are great. The issue with other choices for me are comfort, stability and battery life for all day bike rides and hikes. Oh and the headset must fit under a helmet. I keep trying to find something stuck in my ear canal that's comfortable. But they're always painful. The battery life on the Aeropex is way more than 8 hours. That may be because I mostly listen to podcasts. With music it's fine too. It's a little tinny. Yet it's still better than airpods, which I would never wear biking or hiking. I was concerned about the "tickle" issue I kept hearing about. I feel it. But it doesn't bother me at all. When I'm not listening, I can leave them on and the battery will last for days. When I'm biking and turning my head frequently, the contacts shift around and sometimes loose contact. But that's usually temporary. Even if I have to use my hand to adjust them, it doesn't bother me because I'm so happy with the comfort, stability and battery life. 2 complaints: #1 - Phone calls: Best I can tell, there's zero noise canceling on my mic. All the other person can hear is wind. It's not like that for an Apple wired headset or airpods. #2 - Aeropex fits under all my helmets including my ski helmet. But there is no way I can adjust the volume with my gloves on. Even thin gloves won't work. The buttons are way too tiny and hard to distinguish from the charging port. What were they thinking?

title: Was ok until it died.
text: Cool product that give a new way of listening to music but died within 7 months. Can't charge and can't power up. Also this product sometime give me headache. No adjustment. For the price I was expecting it to last at least a couple of years.

title: High Quality Product!
text: I don’t like writing reviews but this one deserves it, I read a lot of negativity mixed with good. I was impressed from the packaging, to the actual product quality and the sound delivery. Look if you want that studio sound go get some Beats over the ear. These are great! Great for cycling, commuting and being aware of your surrounding while enjoying some beats. Plus less damage on your eardrums. Great product, I waited too long to finally buy. Glad I did. You will be also.

title: great for office or workouts
text: Hear the outside and your own music while not blocking your ears. Great product. My complaints are when there are bass sounds involved they vibrate my ear too much making my ears itchy and there are barely any mids and no bass whatsoever in the audio.

title: Best set of headphones ever
text: I love these headphones. At first I was skeptical, but after trying them I love them. I like the long battery life. I love the quality sound and the fact That I don't have to put them in my ears is awesome.

title: Would recommend! Comfortable, great sound, long battery, water resistant
text: I tried an inexpensive bone-conduction headset to see if I’d like it. It was terrible. But this headset has been fantastic. It connects so quickly when it is turned on. The controls are limited but very simple. The main play/pause button is accessible and reactive as are the volume controls. It’s comfortable when working out, under my helmet when riding, and even in the bed if the neck strap is pulled up. It is stable and doesn’t slip off. And, unlike the earbuds, it never hurts and I even forget that I even have it on. The sound is really great, much better than I expected and worlds better than the cheap pair I sampled. This is probably not for the audiophile and doesn’t compare to a Bose-over the ear set. It’s for working out or being active. These aren’t intended to cancel noise so you can still hear your surroundings, unless you have the volume up high. When I’m riding my bike, I keep the volume at about 50% or I can’t hear a car from behind. The battery lasts a very long time. I can’t say exactly because they have never died even after 6+ hours of continuous use. None of my earbuds have lasted this long despite their claims of 8hours of listening time. They also charge pretty quickly. The charger is a USB to a proprietary magnetic attachment which is easy to hook up even in the dark. But it is a separate cable that is not universal. Water resistance has been excellent so far. I’ve been caught in the rain, dropped them in the tub and they were fine. I’ve tried wearing them in the shower and have had no problems. The only area that looks exposed is the charger port and it still looks sealed tightly. Pros: comfort, stable, sound quality, still aware of environment, battery life, water resistance Con: proprietary charging cable(that works great!), awkward storage

title: For runner and bikers who like music, these are great.
text: I was looking for music head gear that was NOT noise cancelling. As a biker and runner, I need to hear what is happening around me but I also love to have music to train with. These are PERFECT! I am able to run outside without being a hazard to myself and other around me. They are also sweat proof, and as a person that drips perspiration from my head, that feature is a must. The battery life is great as I've been able to run 5 hours without even getting a low battery promp. How log is the battery life? For sure 5 hours plus. I've had them for over a month and have not had a single hiccup from the beginning. They pared super easy with my samsung 10, they don't fit snug but I've tossed them over my pony tail each time and haven't had any staying issues. Also, for not being in my ears, I think the sound is pretty great.

title: Unique design
text: Unique design, great sound. If u want “noise cancellation”, just use the ear plugs that come with the unit. Plus there water resistant/proof

title: Great, except for one unforgivable flaw.
text: Both of the Trekz I got from. Aftershokz have been great I use them so much I need two pairs to recharge one while I use the other. They last me over 8 hours but I use them constantly. One finally had too much abuse and I so I replaced it with this model. It's really good. An improvement all around, and I don't even really mind the specialized charger due to the water resistant design. But the beep from on/off or volume adjustments. The beep. The BEEEP!!!! It is painfully loud with no remedy on my Samsung Note. I often have to remove it to use any of the buttons. This is a very, very serious and stupidly easy flaw to avoid for an otherwise perfect headset. Disable the beep. Entirely. I don't need any beep to let me know I pressed a button Turn it off. Disable. The. Beep. Update Nov 13, 2021: I bumped this up to 4 stars due to the way a replacement was handled. The battery stopped accepting a charge blinking red, and they replaced it. Also of note, the replacement is not deafening me with the button pushes. Same phone, so I have to assume something different with the current stock.

title: Great Headphones for Jacuzzi
text: I use these headphones when I'm in my Jacuzzi. They charged up fast, are very comfortable, and this sound quality for this technology is pretty good! If you want noise cancelation you can input any ear plugs.

title: Don't buy if sold by woot
text: I bought this thinking it was me, but I'm pretty sure it was refurbished even though it wasn't stated on the page. One of the ear buds died out and i haven't had that issue with soundcore. IF IT'S SOLD BY WOOT DO NOT GET IT, IT'S REFURBISHED ITEMS.

title: Single Ear Sound
text: Sometimes you may want to listen to music or podcasts, but want to keep one ear free to listen to ambient sound. These earbuds allow you to choose to hear either from the left or right side. You also get quick charging and long playtime. The earbuds are water resistant in case of accidental falls. I highly recommend this product. Thanks so much for taking the time to read this review. I hope the information that I've provided makes your decision a little easier.

title: noticeable step down from the Soundcore A2 earbuds
text: I got a chance to try both the Soundcore A1 and Soundcore A2 earbuds. The price difference between these 2 models is relatively small, but I think additional features on the A2's is more than worth the price. The A1's might be a little over-priced at $60, while the A2's are a bargain at $80. The A2's have noise cancellation, many more equalization settings that are easy to set via the smartphone app, upgradable firmware, and larger speaker drivers. The Soundcore smartphone app does not work with the A1's. All the extra features give the A2 earbuds noticeably better sound quality while also being easier to use. The A1's have decent sound quality, but there are a lot of $50 wireless earbuds that are just as good. On the other hand, the A2's feature and sound combination is better than any other $80 wireless earbuds that I have tried.

title: Extended usage review
text: I wear these earbuds between 40-50 hours per week while working (auto body and painting). I have had zero problems with these earbuds. Never fall out, comfortable, lightweight, always connects, and I like the EQ option. Battery lasts approx 8 hours. Highly recommend.

title: Excellent sound quality and noise cancellation
text: My test of the noise cancellation was being able to listen to a podcast while cutting my grass without turning the volume up so loudly that my ears hurt. I am very satisfied on both accounts.

title: Buds
text: Good sound for the price, easy to pair. Instructions are way to small to read.

title: Its for Christmas
text: I have no idea if these work well or not. It's a Christmas gift.

title: Does not work for long
text: These were my go to work headphones for about 8 months. The earbuds needed to be charged after about 6 hours of wear. If you are wearing these and trying to take a call without them and you don’t turn them off, mid call it will connect to your earbuds and you’ll lose the person. The microphone is also crap and is not good for calls. Occasionally, even after turning the buds off and putting them in their case, my phone will still connect to them which is annoying. I’ve never had this issue with any other Bluetooth devices. Now, not even after 9 full months of ownership, the battery in the carrying case is shot and the earbuds only last about 3 hours. Really disappointed since I’ve had great experiences will all my other Anker products. This one really falls flat. Buy different earbuds.

title: Very good
text: These earbuds are comfortable enough, block sound well, and are good sound quality for the price. I did have to change the earpieces out to slightly smaller pieces but they were included in the set.

title: Updated: Customer service is just as important as quality
text: These sound great, but I had the same issues others had with the rubber ear pieces constantly falling off and stretching out. This is both a quality and design flaw. Keep in mind we’re talking about rubber pieces that probably cost a few cents but wildly change the experience. Anker said they are not able to replace the rubber pieces under warranty. They offered to exchange the entire set up out for a new one, but being a design flaw in my opinion, I asked to pay the difference to upgrade to a different model that used a different attachment system. They stated no, and offered a refund if I send them back. I said I would just take the loss since I didn’t want to be troubled with driving all the way to the post office to send them back. At that point they offered me a partial refund with no return. I can’t say I’m pleased but at least they tried. I had a pair of JBL ear buds years ago that the case zipper fell off. JBL discontinued them so they sent me a completely new set of ear buds free of charge. Just keep in mind you’re buying the company’s customer service and not just the product. If I could have paid the difference to swap out for a model with better design I would have been satisfied. Anker is far from the worst, but now I have to buy a new set of ear buds minus $15. Not optimal considering the situation, but now I regret not going straight back to JBL since they take such better care of their customers.

title: Really nice!
text: I was worried in the beginning because they did hurt my ears after 20 minutes of listening, but after taking some time to try every ear tip and rubber ear.. wing flap thing, I found a match that was pretty comfortable. I fell asleep a few times just listening to stuff and woke up pretty comfortable with the music still playing! The button controls have a bit of a learning curve as they aren't the most intuitive, and the case is a bit bulky for tighter fitting jeans' pockets, but there's really not too many drawbacks I can see as someone who's using this as their first pair of true wireless earbuds. I'm not an audiophile either but the sound is good for me, though the EQ is a bit of a gimmick as the other options than the first one just don't sound that great for what I listen to. Good stuff though!

title: Great, but wish they came with basic instructions.
text: I’m very happy with the quality, but have had to guess a lot, because there wasn’t a single instruction with them.

title: good buds!
text: I tried the galaxy buds a while back, and wasn't too happy with their performance for the price. I saw these on sale, so thought I would give them a try, not expecting much. But they have a great sound and last for hours!

title: Too many moving parts
text: There are three pieces for each bud. The ear cushion, the bud and the part that helps keep them in. Once that last part comes off that’s it, it will keep coming off. I’m also tired of my audio continuing to play when the buds are placed back in the charger. Why the hell are these the only ones that don’t automatically shut off? Why would I want to keep playing media while the buds are seated in the charger and it’s closed?

title: Perfect fit for me!
text: I like that they aren't touch type. I use my ear buds to sleep in and these are great. They stay in and provide music for a long time...

title: Excellent sound quality!
