title: Really good for the money.
text: Ordered these to replace some wired headphones that I was using for Zoom calls. My wife has the more expensive pair and while hers are truly nice, these are truly inexpensive. If you are on the phone all day, you may want to consider letting go of more cash for the nicer phones. However, for the calls I do, these are fantastic. My goal was to free up a USB port and start using Bluetooth. These work great. The sound quality is fantastic, they are lightweight and most of all, they are affordable. There are some negative points too. Here is my assessment. Pros: - Price, for the money, these are great little headphones. - Sound Quality, again, the sound quality is really good. - Pairing is very easy - Weight, they are very lightweight. - Microphone, it is built into the right ear pad but people say they hear me just fine, as good as my wired set I was using. Cons: - Ear pads are too small. I am a larger man and they do not surround my ears. - Cheap construction. Feels very "Plastic-y". I am hoping they will be durable enough for what I use them for. - Controls too close to the microphone. Now there is no need for this one. Adjusting volume during the call is done with buttons on the ear piece themselves. So everyone on the call can hear you fumbling with the volume controls. Way around that, mute to adjust volume I guess. But they could have put the mic on the other ear piece. Unknowns: - Battery Life, haven't had them that long so I am not sure on battery life. I charge them each night and they last for at least 2 or three calls per day. Conclusion: - These are actually great little headphones for the money.

title: Makes a noise when you fast-forward, plays ambient noise into your ears.
text: If you fast-forward or rewind it plays an alert noise over what you're listening to, a noise that sounds like a death-dialog just popped up on Windows 3.1. Who thought this was a good idea? Never connects to my phone automatically when all my other headsets do. And forget about using it for phone calls: it has the opposite of voice-cancellation, where everything you say, every breath, every room noise, every slight sound on your end is played back into your ear while you're trying to talk. Useless for phone calls for that reason. And according to other reviewers it can go into that mode when listening to content, though I have only heard that intermittently. So what did the engineers do? They hired a professional voice artist to record the voice prompts in a smarmy voice appropriate for a TV commercial, and they even put reverb on it. That's what they put their effort into: putting reverb onto the voice prompt. I'm actually old enough to remember when Sony was a reputable brand name. At least these are comfortable.

text: I honestly think many of these 5-star reviews are fake. I thought Sony would be pretty decent quality. I bought these to replace a regular pair of cheapo $19.95 Bluetooth headphones (cracked the headband part after a year of OK use), expecting a slight upgrade. I also have Apple air pods, some knock-off air pods, Jabra earpieces, and Beats by Dre headphones I’ve had for a few years. So I’m pretty into headphones. Of course these don’t stack up to $200+ headphones… but they’re not even as good as $20 headphones. Cons: -Expensive for poor quality in calls -Painful on the ears, after 20 min. The earmuff part is too small. It’s also tight, and not enough padding to offset the poor ergonomics of it. I have an average-sized adult female head. They would only be comfortable if you only wear them for a short time, like 30 min a day. -Impossible to use for phone calls, due to the super awful “echo feedback.” I could hear myself breathing, loudly, as it was magnifying sound on the mix and feeding it back in my ears. All my words echoed back at me. I looked up how to change this, and it can’t be changed. Said move mic further away” which is impossible to do while wearing the headphones. -I called my friend, who reported the audio quality wasn’t good and didn’t sound right. The feedback was so much I could only talk a minute. Pros: -Cheap looking and plain. Nobody will want to steal them from you! -The earpieces swivel, I guess that’s good? -Stay on your head well. I could do sit-ups or bend over and they don’t move. I like snug fit in headphones. -Not to big or heavy -Sound quality is just ok, but not worth fifty bucks or so, considering you can’t make a phone call and they hurt. -I didn’t get them expecting noise cancellation, so no comment on that. They don’t have that. -can’t comment on durability as I am returning them.

title: Solid choice for cheap earbuds!
text: For the price, I'm pretty impressed with these Bluetooth earbuds! The sound quality is decent (not spectacular, but better than expected for the price) and they are comfortable. I shook my head all around trying to make them fall out of my ears and they didn't. Pairing was simple. I was able to connect to both my computer and my phone (separately, not at the same time) without problems. On one occasion I only had sound from one earbud but it was easily fixed by turning it off and then back on (long press until you hear "power off"). Phone calls are clear and no on had a problem hearing me. I even used them for a Zoom meeting on my computer and there were zero issues. Battery life of the earbuds themselves seems good but I haven't put them to much of a test. The charging case seems like it'll recharge the earbuds several times before needing to be recharged itself. I haven't had them very long so I cannot comment on durability but the earbuds are lightweight, as is the case, but neither of them feel cheaply made. I buy a lot of cheap stuff, and the cost tends to align with quality. That doesn't seem to be the case with these which is great. If you have reasonable expectations for a low cost item, I think you'll be quite surprised by the quality of these earbuds but if you're expecting crazy high quality sound from $25 earbuds, you're going to be disappointed so be realistic and you'll be more than happy with these.

text: I use ear buds mostly to listen to podcasts, so I only use one ear at a time while the other stays in the case stay charged. When I shop for headphones it's important for each ear to be able to paired independently. I have a Soundcore Liberty Neo isn't able to do that. The Rumixi H01 meets the criteria even though works somewhat differently. In other headphones each ear would show up as its own Bluetooth device (for example, E18 would show up twice in my iPhone Bluetooth settings, one for left and one for right). With this device I only have to pair one of the ears, and the other ear is also automatically paired. At any given time only one H01 shows up, but it's intelligent enough to know which one is in my ear and which one is in the case. So far so good! One other characteristic I like about this is that the left bud and right bud are exactly the same. Some ear buds are designed so each fits left or right better. With H01 I can use them interchangeably and wear them comfortably.

title: Worth every penny!
text: I was hesitant to get these, but I needed a cheap set of buds with the absolute most battery life possible. While I was hoping the buds themselves would have more, the way I intend to use them, they serve the purpose. So day one, I charge them up for about an hour (they recommend at least 30 min before first use.) I use them to listen to podcasts mostly so I decide to use one then switch when it dies, so the other will be charged when the second dies. Also they transmit their remaining charge very well. Many BT devices just say full all the time. I believe they claim 90 min per charge for the buds? One con is the manual is in dire need of spell and grammar check, because some parts are hard to understand. Anyways, pairing, powering on, all that is auto which I love. The first bud lasted about 4hrs. Switched to the second seamlessly and finished my shift and probably after 30 min to 1hu (didn't really time it) the first was charged and ready before I needed it. I tested the range also, and I forget what they claimed, but I know it surpassed it. I was getting a full connection with no cutting out at almost 30 yards with a bunch of metal, computers, and other BT devices between us. So for the price, I am very pleased with these boys. Time will tell with durability, and battery longevity. (Update) So after a few months of daily use, the buds only last about 2 hours before needing charge. Also, one bud suddenly got like 60 percent quieter.. I went to clean the tips one day and pushed the mesh a little bit and that solved it.. meaning the connection to the actual speaker is not super solid. But I mean for the price you can't expect absolute perfection. Technically I could attempt to disassemble them and fix that.. but if I just have to push on it once every few months.. why do that? title: Completely disappointing sound quality; no bass, and tricky to pair BT
text: We bought these with high hopes because we love the sound quality of our SkullCandy Crusher headphones. We paid about $70 on sale, and these aren't even worth half the price. There is a constant white noise in the background that becomes evident when you listen to music that is mixed left to right. The bass doesn't even exist - you can almost get the low end if you max out the volume, and in fact, you have to max out the volume to hear the music and block out extraneous noise at all. The bass has an unpleasantly crunchy sound that detracts from the music. The high end is less annoying, but there is little depth and character to the music when played through the Indys. We tried these paired with an iPhone 8, an iPod nano, and the FiiO M7 digital audio player. Pairing was tricky and unpredictable across devices, requiring multiple tries. Not fun at all. The sound quality was just meh across the board. We even tried high-quality music files on the FiiO, augmented with EQ to help, but the sound was so unimpressive. We switched to $10 wired Panosonic earbuds and the sound quality was significantly better. We then compared the same songs across players using the Tozo T10 BT earbuds that sell on Amazon for $50, and these were also of significantly higher quality than the SkullCandy Indy. These just aren't a good value for the price. I am shocked at the poor sound and fidgety BT connectivity. I expected so much better based on my previous experiences with the higher end SkullCandy products. Save your money. There are so many better options available right now.

They're really touch-sensitive, and I have a long pixie cut, and I sweat a lot when I run, even if it's cold. When my hair was just very sweaty, but I didn't have any headgear, the earbuds would change volume in response to my wet hair. title: Updated review: GARBAGE
text: My initial review for these was fairly positive, however now, just a bit over a year later, my opinion has drastically changed. First, the biggest issue: After a year, these earbuds will no longer hold a charge. From a full charge, I get MAYBE 5 minutes of listening before one or both buds go dead. Second issue: Although these initially fit pretty well, over time the rubberized shells -- which aren't attached, and are more like just sleaves on each bud -- have completely lost their firmness. The shells are now so flimsy that the buds just sort of sit in the ear rather than actually FIT in the ear. Activity on the level of merely walking up the stairs is enough for them to just fall out. Third issue: The touch controls are so ridiculously sensitive that it's impossible to adjust the ear buds without pausing what you're listening to, restarting it, or just shutting the buds off completely. But really, those other two issues don't really matter given the absolutely garbage battery life. All in all, these are junk and I 100% regret spending money on them.

I don't think this problem is peculiar to Skullcandy/Indy Fuel alone; it seems to me that all Bluetooth gadgets are glitchy and temperamental. title: Confusing but worked fine, for about a year
text: I purchased these earbuds 14 months ago, in May 2020. They were the first wireless earbuds I've ever owned, and were my faithful pandemic companion when I went on walks, cleaned the house, and took phone calls. It's always been hard for me to find earbuds that stayed in, so I love the "wing" on these that holds them comfortably and securely in my ear. The battery life was good and sound quality seemed fine. There were a few instances of the two units getting slightly out of synch, but other than that, I didn't have any major problems for months. Something I didn't realize was a consideration with earbuds, but now know, is that the right one is the "master" side, and if you only want to use one, it has to be the right one. Then they started not pairing with my phone on the first try, so I had to keep putting them in and out of their case to reset them. I got a new phone without a headphone jack, and it became more important than ever to have a working bluetooth option. Finally, when I went to use them a few days ago, the left earbud just wouldn't pair with my phone. The right one works fine, but the left one just says "Power on ... Pairing" (I'm not sure what it's pairing with), and no audio actually plays. This seems to be a common and frustrating issue, and though I've followed all the tips on how to reset and re-pair them, nothing seems to work. If this is the typical lifespan for earbuds, maybe that's fine, but I figured I'd be able to get more than a year out of a name-brand product. Instead, I'm about to replace them with some no-name earbuds. They might not have as many controls, but actually that's fine with me because the tap controls on these Skullcandy earbuds were also always confusing and never seemed to work. It was almost as if the user guide sometimes mixed up what you were supposed to use the left and right sides for, and there was no way of knowing if each tap in a series had registered. tl;dr: I was happy with these for about a year, the experience slowly degraded, and now they're getting replaced.

title: Burpee Proof Fit and Fantastic Sound!
text: I love true wireless earbuds but have small ears and struggle to find pairs that have a good solid fit, with the exception of Bose. Every pair I’ve tried from Bose with the wingtip ear tip design stays in, and stays solidly. Even with my small ears, I have no concerns about these falling out, which I would consider vitally important in a pair of sport earbuds. I ordered both the sport version of these earbuds and the Quiet Comfort version, and honestly, despite the $100 price difference, the sound quality is so similar I almost can’t tell a difference. They both have a crisp clear, sound with booming base, fantastic surround sound, and crisp treble. I’m quite impressed sound wise. The only big difference is the active noise cancellation of the Quiet Comforts, which is phenomenal, and in my opinion, worth the extra money, especially if you travel or work in a noisy environment. But with the lack of notice cancellation in these earbuds they are significantly smaller and lighter than the Quiet Comforts, so it just depends on what is more important to you as to which headset is a better fit for you. They are both fantastic earbuds with great sound quality and a solid, “burpee proof” fit and I would recommend them. 👍🏻

title: Perfect for my running and fit much better than Jabra 75t
text: These fit in my ear perfectly and stay there in running. The sound quality is good for what it is, and one of the best among true wireless earbuds. Sound stage is okay, highs are pretty good, for bass I wouldn't want a bit more than what it already has. I also used these to make phone calls, and sound quality on the other end was also good. My main use: working out, including running. Features I need: staying in ear while moving, stable connection, quality mic for phone call Features I don't need: ANC (bad for running), complex touch control (tried Sennheiser True Wireless and it was bad) What do I already have: Jabra 75t, Shure 845 with M2BT1, a few other wired big/small headphones, etc I was worried reading other early reviews, but I'm so relieved after getting mine. People compare with Jabra 75t and complain about these. I have both and on the contrary totally prefer Bose. Sound is more open and clear. Jabra is not bad but the sound is too closed and gives an even smaller sound stage. Jabra don't stay in my ears despite I have a few different foam eartips to try on. For bass, I can say these have the signature Bose kind of bass, deep but not heavy. It touches the low frequency a bit but does not not go boom. I personally prefer this though others may want more bass. Overall, these are better than Jabra in every aspect for me. They don't sound as nice as my Shure, but they are for different purposes.

title: Excellent for listening (even on Linux)! But, not good for calls.
text: I got a set of these as an out of warranty replacement for a pair of Sound Sport Free headphones that had some battery issues. The out of warranty expense to replace was $60 IIRC. The old ones were about 3 years old. The support from Bose on this was just perfect. They sent me a replacement set of SSFrees that had issues with the bose updater application. I sent those back and they sent me these. These sound great but they don't sounds as full as the SSFs. The battery life on these is excellent better than the SSFs. The audio is excellent. Compatibility for these has shocked me. I've paired these with EXCELLENT results on my iPhone, iPad, MacBook Pro, Windows PC, and Linux PC. The fact that there were zero issues pairing these with Linux blew my mind. The only drawback on these is the using them for phone calls (on the iPhone) is a bad experience for people on the other end. I've tried using these to talk to others and they say the audio is really bad. Not sure if it's something I'm doing wrong or if it's these headphones. Either way I don't use these for phone calls. title: So glad I chose Bose wireless
text: I have had three previous sets of Bose headphones, 2 were the wired Soundsport and one noise cancelling full headphones for flying. Recently my last set of SoundSports needed to be replaced so I began looking into wireless options. Although I like the Apple functionality and fit, I’m a music buff and the sound quality of the Apple product, in my opinion, is inferior to any Bose product I’ve listened to. I mostly listen to music with my headphones, I like it clear, loud with lots of bass, I’m very fussy about the sound quality. I hesitated with these for a couple of reasons, 1. There were many mixed reviews and 2. My son in law has a set and commented that he did not care much for them because the microphone for voice calls wasn’t good. He said sound quality was excellent but Bose placed the microphone in a place where when he is on the phone, his customers can’t hear him and he has to switch to other headphones. Well after agonizing over what type to buy, I finally decided to take the plunge and try these. I don’t talk on the phone much with headphones and mostly wanted these for walking an hour day listening to music or books. Well a month after having them I can report I’m so happy I decided to stay with Bose and selected these. The sound quality as always with Bose is exceptional. I have no problem with anyone hearing me when I’m talking on the phone, I don’t know if Bose changed something in the microphone but mine are perfect. They are sturdy, very comfortable and easy to set up. Battery life is longer than expected or previously experienced with my wired Bose headphones. Would definitely buy again.

If I’m not paying close enough attention, sometimes adjusting the EarPods will pause/play (should adjust them via the bottom not top). The tips provide a secure fit like earplugs do; they’re not open which might bother some people. I haven’t had any issues with connectivity, they’ve paired fine with both my iPhone 10s and iPad. I haven’t used them for working out of any kind so I don’t know how they’ll work with lots of movement/sweat, but they do work great for music and watching shows on my iPad. The volume can be set to very loud, I only put it at like 1/4 of the full volume and its sufficient enough for me. The reason for the lower stars, is because In terms of phone calls, The sound quality is just okay, not great (and that’s the majority of what I use EarPods for). The person on the other side of the call had trouble hearing me at times/clarity wasn’t great, but nothing horrible. Overall, I would recommend; there’s some nice features, sound quality is good for music and shows, call quality is just decent- if you’re looking to purchase mainly for calls, I would not recommend. But for the price, it’s a good deal- the EarPods work pretty well.

Also, these earbuds last for hours listening to music or podcast. I only use one earbud at a time, so when one gets low on battery, I put it back in the charging case and use the other one. The only negative thing I have to say is that when I'm using the earbuds, they will disconnect a few times each day momentarily, and then will reconnect itself within 10 seconds. So the first time I had to replace them was because the left earbud would not sync up with the right side at all. I tried multiple times but they just would not sync. I can listen to the left or the right side by themselves but just not together. The 2nd time I had replacement is because of the battery on the earbuds. I use them from battery full (100%) til it tells me that the battery is low (10%). BUT I noticed that every time it tells me its low. Its always the left side and never the right so I put the left side earbud into the case and found that the right side is still at 40%. I full charged it again to test it out again and same a few times and once the right side was at 60%. Not sure if its the left side just drains the battery more or if the battery bad? I seriously never had earbuds that had that of a difference in battery drain if the left side does drain more. So I'm waiting for my 3rd pair to arrive. I will be updating this review once I test this pair. I'm hoping it is just my bad luck that I'm getting these issues since I do like the feel as well as the sound of these earbuds. 'crossing my fingers' that these are keepers.

I really like these earbuds though because most of my listening time is spent on podcasts or video webcasts and for this they are phenomenal. They're lightweight and the charge lasts a really long time. The case also serves as an external battery so you can recharge them on the go without messing with cords all the time. title: Update: Support helped with some issues
text: Rating: 4/5 (was lower, but their email customer support is actually helpful and responsive and made a difference) Pros: +Comfortable fit (though they may not fit well for smaller ears) +Decent sound quality for earbuds in this price range +Built-in volume control (a must-have for me, as I use it on PC) +Reasonable battery life (see cons for the other side of this coin) +Passthrough mode works pretty well at lower volume levels, ANC works great for white noise sounds Cons: -Advertised battery life is misleading. In my testing, they only last 3-4 hours when used together. Used only one at a time they seem to last a lot longer (probably because they don't have to communicate with each other). -They aren't that easy to get out of the case for me, and they are slippery - easy to drop -Typical latency of Bluetooth earbuds means a slight delay compared to video / games. -Bluetooth range is okay, but it struggles to perform at maximum distance where other devices do well. -Occasional ~1 second audio drops (not enough to bug me, but it does happen) Like many things, there aren't a ton of perfect options - ear buds have been like that for me. Pick what matters to you, and maybe this one has what you want. Maybe not. With my newer issues, probably not.

title: These are the earbuds you are looking for! 10/10!
text: I've owned dozens of headphones over the years. This is likely my favorite pair for general use! 10/10! I'd expect them to be $150. Tozo is generally a fantastic brand. I loved the T12, but consider these an improvement over those. I didn't care for the shape of the NC2 and Tozo sent me the NC9 as a replacement. A+ Company support! So what's better? Everything really. I've only had them a day, but I'm super impressed. The case has a ridge which makes it easier to open and close. Improved over other brands and previous TOZOs. The earbuds have a ridge making it easier to insert into the ear without accidentally interacting with the touch controls. The included earbuds have a better shape than the normal round ones which sit in my ears better. The transparent mode is clear without hiss of other microphones. It's very useful and easy to activate. The ANC mode is super effective for broad noise like fans and steady tones. Turning it on and off is as easy as touching the left earbud. The audible notifications of the headphones are much quieter in a great way as well. Just loud enough to hear without being too loud or annoying. My comply foam tips didn't quite fit snug on these so I'm still looking for a foam pair as they are generally even more comfortable. A tip, your ear canals may need different tips for each ear! Try the included ones then adjust each ear so it's snug. You'll know it's right when electronic music kicks and subs feel centered with punch. Outstanding value, quality, and will recommend them to every person I know needing a pair on the go.
