title: By FAR, the worse Bose product ever
text: Update 10-04-21 I received my 2nd pair of these headphones after the 1st one all of a sudden didn't want to turn on after charging them. They just simply died and stayed that way. Luckily bose replaced them very easily. The 2nd pair is absolutely just as garbage as the 1st. It loses connection at least twice for every 30 minutes that I use them. I found that you actually need to go into the app and make sure they're connected through the app so they don't disconnect as often but they still disconnect. And yes, they continue to make a very loud buzzing sound every time that disconnects. The biggest disappointment in the bose lineup of amazing products. I've had about 6 different bose headphones and ear buds throughout the years along with a speaker, and a home sound system. You come to expect amazing quality for what you pay and you get it. Absolutely NOT the case with these. These things are an absolute joke. The noise cancelling is amazing, the sound clarity is amazing, but only if the headphones stay would stay on. Ever since the very first time I connected them they've had issues every single day. They disconnect and make a horrible, loud sound as they disconnect right in your ear. It's loud even if you don't have it on high volume. Worst of all, after less than a year they just died. Yup, plain and simply just died. I called bose and they are sending a replacement. But if I could get my money back I wouldn't think twice. The last pair of noise cancelling headphones I had from bose never gave me issues but it was time for a replacement. Do some research and completely pass on these. I'm not the only one having issues read all the negative reviews.

title: Not worth the cost but is good.
text: It is not bad, but for the price, I expected better from Bose. It’s heavy, drops off your big head at certain angles, and touch control is not as good. Not worth the cost.

title: Terrible size adjustment
text: For the price I give the noise cancellation and sound quality a B+, but the mechanism for adjusting the fit of the headphones is unacceptable: essentially sliding levers attached to each earpiece. You cannot lock them in place at any given time which is imprecise and annoying.

title: Excellent product
text: Used while flying, mowing and just relaxing by the pool

title: Very Impressed So Far
text: These are beautifully constructed headphones. I chose the silver color. Bluetooth sound quality is getting close to excellent. I had no problems setting these headphones up and running right from the box using the Bose Music App. I set mine up after their first update. I see that today 8-7-19 they have made a second update to the app. These headphones are on par with wired units. I also own a pair of Bowers and Wilkins P7 wired headphones Using a Sony DAC with it. Up until now they were my headphones with superior sound. These Bose headphone match it. I also have the Bose Soundlink II headphones. They are lighter than this unit but no noise counseling. I really like this new design. Bose put some thought into this unit with design and quality. No more of that fabric material on the headband that disenegrates over time. The ear cup material is soft and appears sturdier too. They function well. The app is not perfect but adequate at this time. I haven't had time to test the second update. They really need to add an equalizer to the app with presets and customization like the Sony units. The unit has crystal clear highs, very good midrange and decent bass. The noise cancelling is great. I think the app will get better and better. So at this point I am very pleased with them. As a note, the luxe silver is beautiful but the black will probably look better aesthetically in the long run from showing normal wear marks.

title: Ok
text: Work good have some problems connecting with one of my Bluetooth

title: Great headphones....but just a few issues.
text: So I bought these headphones because I travel a lot and would love to not hear the airplane engine noise or crying babies. Overall they are great, the quality is supreme. The only 2 issues I have with these are the touch controls are not the best and can accidentally hang up calls. The other issue is that when you don't want to wear them up on your head/ears and just leave them around your neck they pretty much choke you and it's very uncomfortable so the only option you have is to wear them or put them away in their carrying case. Lastly, this one is not a big deal and is not relevant to everyone, because I have a shaved head they seem so bulky.

title: Noise Cancellation not great
text: This headphones are good, but they do not cancel noise like I'd like them to. I can pretty much hear every sound from around me, just a bit quieter. Disappointed, as other Bose headphones I've tried block out noise much better.

title: Love these headphones
text: I only use this on an airplane for watching movies or noise cancellation. They work great for this purpose. Very comfortable.

title: Noise Cancelling Heaphones Are Difficult to Use
text: I bought these as an upgrade to my Bose QC-35 phones that I had 3 years and loved. Thought they were going bad. Decided to try the Bluetooth feature with these phone and was hoping for a convenient wireless set. Unfortunately, I was very disappointed and returned. Here's why: 1. Buttons on the phones are very tiny and almost impossible to use or feel in the dark. 2. Difficult to connect to my Samsung android tablet. Sometimes connected, other times not. Very inconsistent. 3. Noise cancelling levels are nice, but rather than put a switch on the phones, this had to be activated by using your phone or tablet. I found that very inconvenient. 4. Battery is built in and had to be charged using a 2.5 to 3.5 mm cable (included.) If it goes bad, then I think you have to get the battery replaced at a service center. I found it an annoyance. 5. Volume control was completely non-intuitive. Had to press and swipe upward on the right ear-pad case. I couldn't tell that well if sound quality was as good or better than the QC-35s I think for the marginal improvement, I would pass on these and wait until either Bose re-engineers this model or look to another brand.

title: Initially disappointed, improved after update, still needs a bug fix
text: I was really excited to get these cutting-edge headphones and found them to be, unfortunately, unusable. I connected them to my iPhone 7. The Bose Music app failed to connect at least half the time; photo provided here. In addition, the bluetooth settings screen shows two connections at the same time; I have no idea why. The app frequently throws error messages indicating that the update failed, and the connection failed. It's actually connected, but the app does not know it. The headphones' hardware buttons for switching favorites and activating voice assistant sometimes worked and sometimes did nothing, even when pressed repeatedly. Otherwise, the basic form of the headphones is good: reasonably comfortable-- though just slightly less comfy than my Sony WH-1000XM3-- and with good sound. The touch controls seem fine, though I wish I could disable the battery status control, and this is currently impossible. Overall, for me, this is a real dud-- defective product. Update 03 Aug 2019: I reassessed after updating the phone app. Most of the earlier problems appeared resolved. I took a 4.5-hour flight where I sat next to the jet engine, which was quite loud. The Bose noise cancelling was outstanding. I could hear my music very well with hardly any outside sound. I'm not a sound engineer, but I found the music to be exceptionally pleasing in its tone and quality, with clear and balanced sound. I did not have any issues with volume. The touch-based sound controls worked well, though they take a bit of practice. I still wish I could disable the battery notification. Comfort was better than expected: I had no discomfort from the headband even after 4 hours, like I do on my Sony. Battery life seemed great. The case is slimmer than Sony's, adequate for the airplane seat pocket. Overall, I was favorably impressed and will stick with them for now. There is still an app bug that prevents the app from consistent connections with the headphones. The biggest problem with the app, as noted by others, is the required Internet login to use it!

title: Must have for airplanes
text: I’m no headphone expert; this is my first pair of pricey, noise canceling headphones, but I’ll say after my first trip it was worth it!! I travel a lot for work and plane noise is a huge irritation for me (people and loud speakers). I turned these on for the first time when boarding a plane and I couldn’t believe how quiet it became in the jetway! Works great if I want to watch something on the plane and I can finally hear it without hearing my seat mate fumbling with his bag of pretzels! I also am sensitive to pressure on my ears, so devices like earbuds usually cause soreness or pain after an hour or so. Not these babies! I love them. I’m just sad it took me so long to finally invest in a good pair. App/software isn’t a priority for me, so I can’t say anything on that, but that wasn’t anything that was relevant to why I was buying. Totally recommend!

title: Good idea, bad engineering
text: Pros: Great noise cancellation performance. I can block out sounds of a conference call conversation right next to me. Sound quality is good. Light and comfortable in wearing. Cons: Multiple-connection does not work. Often falsely decide one device is playing, thus blocking sound from the other device. Blue-tooth link not stable. Once you get out of the range and get back in, reconnection would fail. The Bluetooth thinks it is connected, but the sound does not come through. You have to manually disconnect and reconnect the Bluetooth to get it working. The microphone is not usable, based on feedback from my phone partners. I can only use it as a pure headphone. The voice announcement at power-on is long and annoying. I want a device that can be used as soon as I turn it on, not waiting for several seconds listening to the predictable voice announcement.

title: Worth the money
text: I'd been considering buying these for quite some time. I'm more of a beats gal, but after my last beats studio broke I decided to try something new. Bose are a bit more expensive but, I'd heard great things. After reading what seemed like an endless amount of reviews, I made the plunge. I love them! Super comfortable, great sound, great nose cancelling. Highly recommend.

title: Do not buy
text: I got this in October and they do not work anymore . This thins atrash do not buy

title: Excellent sound, lousy design
text: Spectacular sound quality, but functionality was scrapped for a more stylish design. The headphones won't stay tight on your head and the touch controls work about 50% of the time.

title: Very good sound and a great, slim fit
text: I read all the high tech reviews suggest the new Sony XM4s were better. I tried those first and was not impressed compared to my old Bose noise canceling headphones. The Sony's were large and clunky, and didn't sound superior. I then tried the Bose 700 and they were noticeably better than the old Bose and the new Sony in terms of sound richness, shape, and fit. My biggest gripe is the placement of the buttons on the headphones. You can't touch them without accidentally hitting one and changing something. Overall, glad I went with these as the upgrade to my old set.

title: Surprisingly Good...
text: I had taken time out from bluetooth headphones and have been on a wired to my iPhone via dac/amp, dongle and whatever that wasn't bluetooth. My preferences in the sound of music is what I consider to be on the neutral side. For example I like and have owned a number of cans from Sennheiser HD700, Fidelio X2HR, Audio-Technica ATH-AD700X, Shure SRH1540 and SRH1840 and for bluetooth I had gotten rid of all but my trusty Plantronics BB Pro2 which is bass heavy but still pleasant to use when I'm mowing my lawn for their NC function and I kept my ATH-DSR7BT because to me they present the music the way I like it. The ATH-DSR7BT was my go to can when I wanted to cut the cord for a minute or two. In comes the Bose NC700, I guess that's the name. I purchased the QC35 when they first came out and was totally turned off by the lack of NC control and the way they made my ears feel like the were in a tube or some type of enclosure, needless to say they went right back. I tried the Sony WH-1000XM3 and WH-1000XM4 and still can't hear or determine what all the hype is about other than the NC which the BB Pro 2's did alright, but I can control it although it's very limited. It doesn't matter anymore now because the Bose NC700 check all the boxes for me. This is the first bluetooth can I wanted to bring out of my house and listen while I'm in my car. As far as using them while cutting my lawn the Bose NC700 does an excellent job at cancelling out the noise from my 33" Cub Cadet walk behind mower as well as various power tools I'm using in remodeling my bathroom. I'm hooked and totally impressed. BTW, I go back to the old Bose 901 series corner facing speakers. Never stop trying is my way of life too. Good job on this one Bose! I like these.

title: Not a good match for me

title: Best noise cancelling headphones I have owned.

The battery life is also very good, I have yet to drain the headphones in my normal usage (5-6 hours) in the office or when traveling. I only have a couple minor complaints. When I first started using these, I wished the ear cups were bigger as I was not used to using over the ear headphones vs in ear buds, I have gotten used to this but something to be aware of. Second, I find it annoying to have to collapse the headphones to get it to fit into the provided case. This means you need to readjust them every time you use them. I live next to a busy intersection where people constantly pass by in the summer with "boom cars" playing loud music, and Bose noise cancellation makes that all disappear. They also work great to block the sounds of idling trucks, cars, and motorcycles. When I show these to people, I tell them to put them on with the power off and pay attention to the background noise. Then I tap the power button and their eyes open wide as everything simply disappears. There is no music playing, so they know the background noise isn't simply being covered up, and the power was off before, so they know it's not just an expensive pair of ear plugs.

title: Superior ANC to Sony and All Others, but Lo-Fi sound beaten by QC35II
text: ***UPDATE 9-17-2020*** I just did an A-B with Bose QC35II and found the older headset to have similar ANC (i.e. better than Sony), more comfortable (cushier headband), and better sound. The 700 looks more modern and 'cool' but QC35II is a much better value at 50%+ off (I paid $100 on ebay). Multipoint Bluetooth connecting 2 devices works well on both headsets. It all boils down to looks and USB-C. So I'm returning the 700. ***** I did A-B comparisons with Sony XM3, XM4 and Bowers & Wilkins PX7. My findings: ANC - Bose > Sony > B&W. The difference is more than subtle; in fact, with my portable a/c running at full blast in this weekend's CA heat wave, the Bose puts me in complete 'pitch black' silence. Some high frequencies comes through the Sony; a bit more still on B&W but still very good. I use the highest ANC setting on each headset. B&W has the best passive noise isolation (ANC off), Sony less so, while Bose has zero passive noise isolation. I do not feel any mid-ear pressure or headache wearing the Bose as others have reported. In terms of comfort, Sony is #1 among the three. Bose's narrow headband could use thicker, softer padding (the earcups are great, however) MUSIC - B&W > Sony > Bose. For this comparison, I used hi-res audiophile tracks of classical music and opera. Both B&W and Sony are clearly audiophile quality, comparable to my $1000 flagship wired cans, with B&W having a wider soundstage and warmer richer (but not exaggerated) bass than the Sony. (Listen to the sustained low-C in the bass and organ of the Karajan/Berlin Phil "Also Sprach Zarathustra" to know what I mean.) The Bose 700, on the other hand, sounds embarrassingly lackluster and distinctly non-audiophile: the highs are tinny and the piano sounds metallic. The thumping bass is a bit exaggerated to my ears. Soundstage is wider than Sony's. I guess Bose is best for electronic music, not really my cup of tea. The only saving grace is, by turning down the volume to below 60%, the Bose 700 actually sounds half-way decent and does not offend the ear. But audiophile quality it is not. Even my Sennheiser Momentum True Wireless earphone with its tiny 7mm driver sounds better than the Bose.

They don’t have a hear through function but if you do not put the earbud firmly in your ears, you can hear through a bit. Once they are snug in your ear, it cancels out most noise - depending on volume. I take my walks around the neighborhood so I do not want to not be able to hear my surroundings, but, I’m happy for the option. I haven’t had a phone call yet while wearing them... I’ll update this after I have had a chance to talk to a few people. I haven’t run out of battery yet? Cannot really comment on this as I need to let the charge run out, though, I can see the battery status on my iPhone XS Max when I swipe right on the Lock Screen. They were super easy to pair by the way. I could hear my incoming text messages too while wearing them (phone sound on mode). The only thing I’m not a fan of it how hard you have to press the earbuds in order to give a command. I can see the benefits but it needs to react to a softer touch. Currently, it’s such a hard press(es) where I find myself almost taking them out of my ear so I don’t damage my ear canal trying to skip a song while walking. This disrupts the flow of the walk as well for fear of dropping it and losing it in the street. I found it easier to pull my phone out and change the song on the screen rather than the touch function. Thank goodness for leggings with pockets. Otherwise, these are better than my last economical earbuds and a great alternative over airpods for the price. I got green. I love the vibrant color.

title: Great audio and the battery case is extremely convenient and easy to use
text: I've been extremely impressed with these headphones. I was a little worried at first since the headphones wouldn't turn on automatically when removing them from the case, but that was my fault. Don't make the same I did. Remember to remove the little plastic covers on the headphones then everything will work great. The battery case is by far my favorite feature of these headphones. I take the headphones out and it syncs to my Note 9 within a couple of seconds. This is great when I am on the phone and want to quickly use one of the headphones as a headset. Putting it back in the case also immediately causes them to turn off and start charging. Now I don't have to worry about charging the headphones every single time I use them and only charge the case once in a while. The audio quality is pretty good as well. Music and voice have been very clear. I wouldn't say it has very heavy bass, but turning on dolby atmos sound definitely turned up the bass and the sound on my phone. The range is pretty great as well. I can probably get about 20+ feet away from my phone until it starts cutting in and out. Even when it cuts out it will immediately reconnect which is great. I have started using these as my primary headset when talking on the phone since the audio and microphone are so much clearer than my dedicated headset. The volume and fast forward/rewind buttons are a little harder to get used to. Fortunately I usually just use my phone's buttons for volume and skip forward/back so it doesn't really bother me. The other features definitely make up for it.

title: NOT for people with little ears

I don't use headphones much for calls, and I wanted something I could use when working the lawn that wouldn't get tangled up or that I wouldn't have to crank my volume up to drown out tools. What I'd forgotten about from the first time I bought them was how tight they are in my tiny ears. Even with the smallest adapters, they create such a tight seal that my ears end up itching and swelling for 2-3 days after just a few hours of use. So, sadly, they're getting returned and I'm going back to my wired Google buds.

I must say, I finally found earplugs that work for my ears! I believe the major benefit to these, besides the quality sound, is the adapters. These come with SEVERAL different attachments for one's personal preference, and I was able to find the perfect combination that worked really well for my ears. They fit, they stay in my ears securely, they seem to block ambient sounds really well, and the music sound quality and the balance of all frequencies is really good! text: I was as skeptical with the sound quality as the rest of you. I recently purchase Airpods 2 so my standards were stupidly skewed. But actually... it's ok. It's better than you would expect, not great but not too bad. The earpieces are tucked within the ear mask so you can position it so it rests over your ears as loosely or tightly as you'd like it. You can set up some white noise and it'll work just fine. The blackout quality of the mask is very good, blocking out any light when I have it on comfortably on my face. My primary cheap face mask has a ton of light leak, but this one I would use for sensory depravation or sleeping in the daytime. One of the features to rate is noise cancelling - it is noise cancelling insomuch as holding a loud pair of speakers next to your ears, drowning out anything softer than it. There isn't any. Now why it's my secondary and not my primary. The design resembles that of a headband that goes over your eyes and ears - and my ears get warm quickly. As someone who prefers earbuds over headphones, having my ears covered just changed my comfort level too much to fall asleep. If you can't fall asleep with headphones or earmuffs on, this won't work for you. If you live in a cold climate with no money for heating, it'll help your glasses-holders warm and cozy. The other goofy design is that the power, forward and back buttons are around the bottom of your forehead when you have it on. The buttons are clicky too, so pick your playlists wisely. Otherwise you'll be the day-napping person who occasionally jabs at a button against your forehead. The tube-top like design also means it will slip off your melon head during normal toss and turn. I suppose if you secured the mask securely enough, it won't budge and I won't judge.

That is exactly what I got with the Tiksounds Wireless Earbuds. I have a set of Airpods that will only last for 3 hours or so before I have to charge them. With these, I can put them in and listen throughout my workday without having to worry about charging them. The case holds a charge well and I have only had to recharge it once in close to a week. I am more than pleased with the quality of the audio and the fit comfortably in my ears. There have been times that I forget I even have them in. For the money, these are a great set of earbuds and I highly recommend them.

title: LOVE these headphones !!!!
text: These are fantastic headphones! What I noticed first is that they are very lightweight and you really don't feel them much on your head at all, MAJOR plus especially if you wear them a lot like I do! They are very comfortable and fit very well. They cover your ears nicely and fir just right. I had at first some issues pairing them but I think that was a user issue more than anything else. The sound quality is very good and the volume can go up pretty high if you want to so you have quite a range there. The noise cancelling feature really brings it home though and will come in very handy if you have either some noisy coworkers or when I really like it is on the plane. It really blocks out all the annoying noise out there. These are really cool headsets and will be my go to ones going onward I think, especially because they are just so light but also small. This will come in handy when traveling. The ones I have used to date have always been a bit heavy and bulky and used up a good amount of space when traveling. These are thinner in profile. They did come with a carrying case that is also very nice and a lot thinner than others I have had in the past. They did come with the necessary accessory cables (charging and an audio cable). You get everything you need for a pretty good price at $60 (but they do have a $15 off coupon), so not too bad and these are pretty darn good so I am not complaining since I REALLY like these. I believe these are my 4th or 5th noise cancelling set and these are in my top 2. Only downside, I think they will "only" last like 16 hours in comparison to another one I have that will last 40+ hours from the same manufacturer, but they are also bulkier ... so you have to pick one over the other I guess ..... They are the smallest ones I have so for traveling they beat their slightly smaller brother the NC75 pro, so with that size vs battery .... tough battle

On a fresh charge, I ran them over six hours without running out of battery using Bluetooth. I had to stop listening at that point and don't know how much longer the battery would have gone. Overall, I think they are a good value for the price. Update Dec 2022. After four years of casual use, the ANC has failed. The headphones themselves still work when using Bluetooth or the 3.5mm jack. title: Pairing is tricky, sound is Good.
text: Update 2023/02/15: Got a follow up email from the seller, but I had already returned them. The sound is **very** good and sad to see them go but the Pairing drove me nuts. Update: Just found that the ANC LED (green) will stay on even when the main system OFF. Make sure when turning them off you visually check the LEDs. That ANC LED waste battery between uses. "OFF," does not mean All-Off. Weird stuff. Original Review: Very comfortable and true over the-ear-fitting. No discomfort when wearing glasses and used over extended listening time. Love that aspect of them. Terrible instruction leaflet for this price-point. It has no instructions only icons to guess at their functionality. Pairing is not an easy thing. The Pairing button is also the On/Off button. The Power On/Off takes about 3-seconds hold-down. The instructions suggest to Pair, hold it down for 3-seconds. This becomes a struggle between turning it Off and getting it to Pair. Using the On/Off button for Pair makes little sense, perhaps if they made the ANC button to Pair, it would be easier. The ANC seems to work OK, but also makes the sound quality dip a bit. It seems like the ANC is mostly just clipping the Dynamic Range rather than active ANC circuitry tracking and blocking the actual "noise" frequency excursions. The Volume control buttons are strange, they seem to need a second or so for each step Up/Down. It's a bit of a balance between getting one-step or a bunch of steps all the way Up or Down. Once set it seems to retain that level between turn Off/On, so that's good. I am at the crossroads on keeping them, but they do have good quality sound, excellent bass without booming, but the upper-highs of Classical Music get a little muddy. Not bad enough to return them, but just saying they are not super-crisp highs throughout the full audible-range.

You can disconnect them, but they seem to just reconnect without your knowledge, or just stay on with the green light. I have found that they only way to completely turn them off after use is to connect them to the charger. Since it takes me about 4 hours to mow, they can usually use a partial charge when I'm done, so that does the trick, however, the designers really should come up with an actual OFF button. It makes NO sense to NOT have one! That's what you get when everything is made in China! But the sound quality is excellent, so I'll just plug them in every time. title: What do you expect for $20?
text: When I received them, I charged them and paired with my phone ASAP. On my first use with my Pixel 6, the phones connected and then separated after about 15 seconds. I did the stuff suggested at the Amazon tech support page and got the same result. Finally, I connected with the company. They suggested some of the same "forget" "pair" stuff. Same result. They said "we're sending you another set." Meanwhile, I connected another of my headsets and the same thing happened. I then googled "Pixel 6 bluetooth headphones" and discovered a recent update had caused widespread problems. I followed the suggestions there and the headset connected and stayed connected. I then emailed the company to say "don't send another set!" They said "they're on the way. Enjoy the backup!" So, for overall sound quality, OK for a very low price. For Customer Service, outstanding.

title: I'd recommend. Detailed review.
text: I-phone 6s Plus-Phone battery 100% Bluetooth headset fully charged. (Takes about 1.5-2 hours to fully charge.) Youtube off and on all day. Headset kills my phone battery 3 times faster but that's with all bluetooth products. The sound is good and clear. Disconnected from bluetooth settings on phone. Waited a good minute or two but the light on the headset kept flashing so just be sure to turn the headset off by holding the power button down. 3 hours of non-stop use and my phone battery was down to 20%. I decided to keep phone my plugged in to charge while working. (Not a big deal.) Volume- Only 2 clicks and it’s comfortable for sitting in my office cube on Youtube. Phone calls= Easy 1 press answer/hang up. Voice/Hearing= Had good call quality on both ends. (Our backgrounds were both quiet settings.) Earholes a bit sore by mid-afternoon. I just needed to turn them inward a bit more. (My fault.) The case is handy. I like it. The carabiner clip is small and broke within 2 days though. *Sidenote I wear glasses. I have HD blue light blocker lenses. (Helps protect eyes from the glare of screens. Phones, tablets, pc’s.) The slow flashing on the headset reflects into my right eye thru the inside lense of my glasses. It’s not bad but just something to take note of. I wouldn’t be able to keep the right side in my ear if I were driving at night. The company reached out and offered to send me this headset for my HONEST review/opinion and I’ve done just that. Overall, they work well. They stay put and the sound is great. (Especially for the price.) I’d recommend them and will purchase a pair at a later time for a friend of mine who works out daily.

title: Still noticeable audio delay :-/
text: Update: Added one star. Otium contacted me and sent a replacement unit for the current model I'm reviewing. The replacement unit has a stronger BT connection over distance than the previous one I had which is great (both this current model, and the previous model, the one with the red flat cable). There is still some audio delay, but not as bad as with the current model of the headset I had initially reviewed. The previous model (red flat cable) has zero audio delay, so that's what I would have liked to see here too. Otium customer support acted very quickly (kudos on that!) to send me a replacement, but they were also incredibly persistent, so much that I ended blocking their many e-mails. I have other things going on in my life, esp over the holidays than testing a BT headset, I realize they are concerned about their ratings, but still ... - so their "responsiveness" works both ways. ----------- There is a very noticeable audio delay when watching videos on my laptop (which has Bluetooth 5.0). I thought this also had BT 5, so the connection should have been even great and I definitely didn't expect an audio delay. This was disappointing. I didn't see anything in the instructions that might troubleshoot/help this, so I will be returning these. This is the first BT headset where I've ever experienced any delay. I had a previous version of this (with the flat red cable) and it worked much better. That unit had version 4.2. I also have found that the various descriptions on Amazon don't' seem to be consistent re BT versions, so it's hard to say what headphones has which version.

title: old version was great, new version has easy to trigger redial feature that ruins these
text: I owned the previous version of these, lost them, and bought these (at the time the "new" version) to replace them. For the price, the sound quality and battery life is sufficient. Obviously they're not top-of-the-line headphones but they do the job well for a $20 pair. I use them primarily for working out, they stay in my ears fairly well for most activities, but any sort of sprinting or jumping and they come flying off. Here's the bad part though... there's a big button on the side which you press and hold to turn the headphones on and off (that's fine), or you can press it quickly to play/pause your music (also fine). BUT there's a weird middle-ground where you press and hold that button for just long enough and it auto-redials the last phone number you called (assuming you have it hooked up your phone). There have been several times when I have tried to pause my music or just turn off the headphones and it had started calling someone. This is a huge problem, especially since I work out late at night. I have accidentally called my boss and a client at an obscene hour because the headphones seemed to think that's what I wanted to do. I've done a fair amount of research on trying to disable this on my phone's end but it seems the consensus is that it's built into the headphones and cannot be changed. I'm not sure if this was a feature or not on the old version, but if it was I never once had an issue with it accidentally triggering like I do with this version. At this point I have to make sure that every time I hang up the phone with someone, I immediately call my own number, this way if the headphones trigger a redial later it will just call my voicemail and I don't have to deal with the awkward situation of someone asking me why I called them and hung up after one or two rings at 12:30am the night before. If this is something that might be an issue for you I highly recommend looking around elsewhere.

title: Very Clear Voice Sounds, Good Noise Cancellation, Comfortable to Wear
text: This 2022 Wireless Earbuds, Tribit 150H Playtime Bluetooth 5.2 set has a sturdy feeling and slightly weighty feeling charging case, five extra sets of ear silicone covers in graduated sizes (a lot), and a USB-C charging cord. There are little blue stickers over the ear bud charging metal prongs, so take those off before charging- I didn't notice the stickers before charging before first use, so I had to re-charge the actual buds (vs. just charging up the battery pack/case). These are not tiny ear plugs, but their slight thickness out past the plane of my ears makes them easy to take in and out of my ears by holding their sides without accidentally pressing on their faces- which are not super sensitive, luckily, but responsive. The sound quality of this set is definitely in the upper tier of earbuds I've tried in this price range, and I've tried many. I use these primarily for audiobooks while I walk around. The voices in the audiobooks I listen to sound soothing, clear and full, and there are no sharp or painful sounds when speakers suddenly speak loudly or laugh or yell. I can still hear the ambient noise in the room around me, but this doesn't actually interfere with the clear voices reading my audiobooks, so I believe the noice cancellation works pretty well. The only minor criticism I have is that I need to turn the volume up a bit more to obtain the same sound level as some of my other earbuds (but still within range). These immediately started pairing the second I put them in my ears, and they connected easily to my phone. I have not had any loss of connection within about 30 ft. Overall, I'm pleased with this set, which are comfortable to wear for a few hours at a time (a bit shorter battery power than some others), and I think the sound quality is very good.

title: Incredible sound!
text: I'm replacing pretty good earbuds that I have had for a couple of years, and I'm a musician, so my standards are pretty high. These come in a nice little white charging case, which includes a short USB-A to C charging cable. It has both USB-A and USB-C inputs, so you can give it a charge with whatever is at hand - as long as it is not USB micro, which is probably the most commonly available option right now. Oh well, you can’t have everything. The case itself holds a charge, so you do not have to have it plugged in to charge your earbuds. The earbuds themselves are very small and inconspicuous, and they come with 6 different-sized ear tips. I have not experimented with the different tip sizes yet, since the ones they came with worked and felt fine. It’s easy to forget you have them in... Except for the incredibly good sound. I tested these first with some Hawaiian slack-key guitar music, which has a very wide and delicate tonal range. They sounded beautiful, with good bass to clear, shimmering trebles. Then I switched over to some rock music; Aerosmith, Allman Brothers, Led Zeppelin, and so forth. Outrageously good! The stereo separation on “Whole Lotta Love” was perfect, and once I EQ’d the phone (iPhone 13 Pro) the bass of John Paul Jones was outstanding. You can do better with professional over-the ear studio headphones and a high-end preamp, but there is nothing to complain about with this sound. If I had to find one shortcoming with these, it is that I initially had some problem getting the tap control to work. After a few tries, however, I guess I got the touch, and now they seem to work fine. Just as a test, I made a phone call with a simple “Hey Siri...” The volume of the call was a lot lower than the music I was playing at the time, but that may be on the other end. I’ll update this review if there are ongoing issues with phone calls, but I don’t really use ear buds that often for talking on the phone anyway. For now, I’m giving these a solid 5 stars - highly recommended!

title: Decent sound quality for price, but terrible build quality
text: I've had a pair of these for just shy of a year, and at first I loved them! They rested in my ears nicely, and barring being very active always stayed in. The sound was really great, not top of the line, but really good without spending much more. Battery last forever. However, as time has gone on, these earbuds are showing their true colors as cheap headphones, priced much higher than they should be. It's no wonder they are always on sale. As many others have said, my number one complaint is the silicon cover on the tip (part in the ear) no longer sticks. It's completely peeled up and will completely fall off in a matter of days. With out it, the earbuds will be unbearable to use and fall out constantly. This started happening after 5 months. After continuing to deteriorate, around the 8 month mark I decided to contact JBL since these have a 1 year limited warranty, and was promptly told it doesn't cover most physical damage, even though it's from a design flaw. I wouldn't waste your time on these. At their sale prices, you can get other products that better, and at regular price you might as well spend the extra for airpods or something else. I have a bunch of JBL products, which is why I was draw to these initially, but I would not recommend to anyone.

title: These are garbage.
text: I bought these earbuds because I have difficulty using the kind that you have to jam into your ear canal. The positives is that they are relatively inexpensive and fit well but that's about it. The sound is decent and there are a few functions available via the buttons on the earbuds, such as pause, forward one track, and back one track. There is no volume up or down, which is kind of annoying. The Bluetooth is great and works better than any other Bluetooth earbud set I've ever used on my Samsung phone, when it connects. Other BT earbuds have cut out when my phone is in my back pocket or did not have direct sight to the phone, oddly. I would not purchase a second pair of these if/when they break or get lost. The design of the earbud includes a rubber material that covers the inner part (see pictures). The rubber piece is not flush with the plastic moulding, which makes putting these in your ears uncomfortable, as though someone is sticking your ear with a pin. UPDATE: After 3 months, the little rubber seal has completely disengaged itself from the earbud, only being held on by a tiny bit of glue. I don't use these earbuds to do anything besides sit and stare at the wall so if that is normal wear and tear, I'd hate to see what happens if you try to use them regularly while exercising or doing anything besides stare at a wall like I do. Secondly, the battery life is not great. If you are using these consistently, you will only see about 3-4 hours of actual battery life. Total garbage. Review updated to one star.

title: The only way they could be more uncomfortable is if they came with embedded glass shards. OUCH.
text: I received these as a gift. Straight out of the box, the instructions are markedly light on info. I think I figured out the basics using the insert, but these (allegedly) have a lot of functions, so you'd think that warrants a much better manual. Unfortunately, outside of the quick start guide, you're pretty much on your own as there's no additional detailed guide included. I charged them and got ready to try them out. Pairing was lightning fast and seamless. The sound quality seems good, but I have to qualify that with a really important point: I can't truly be certain. Let me explain: These are so horrendously uncomfortable that there's no way for me to get an accurate user experience. They're hard. Really, really hard. Just sitting softly in my ears in what's shown to be the correct position, they're actually painful. PAINFUL. There aren't any silicone sleeves to help you get a comfortable, more custom fit, so you're stuck with exactly how they're designed. The tips with the speakers are sharp. Forget using them for listening to podcasts or watching any kind of streaming service in bed. NOPE. I came here to check out the reviews because I'm 100% certain that I'm not the first person to think these are the most uncomfortable things you could shove into your ears (a rusty knife being an improvement over these), and another user suggested they were better with the stems up instead. I tried, still a hard no. I even thought that maybe some silicone inserts from other headphones would help = negative. Maybe these are okay for someone with much larger ears, but it's not like mine are freakishly small. (I'd call them average with no deformities). As much as I hate to send them back, I gave them as good of a chance as a person could. They're awful, and life's too short for painful earbuds. From what I could tell without a good fit, they did seem to cancel out some noise and the audio quality sounded promising, but comfort is a high priority for me. Back they go!

title: The charging method is flawed
text: l do not review things often, I have to when it is a product I use everyday day for work and home life. I have run it through my personal obstacle course and they have failed. I am not easy on things, but I do treat them with respect as to not break them. I had two pairs of these and one pair died in a scenario that was completely my fault (I take full responsibility, FYI: they cannot go through the washing machine and survive.) The other pair is alive and well. The sound is good and battery life seems ok if you shut them off when you are not using them. After a few hours they hurt my ears a bit, but I do have them in for hours. My biggest issue (this is the deal breaker) the charging apparatus is flawed. Three tiny holes on the stick portion that sticks out of the ear, if not set properly they will not charge. It will look like it is in there right, all the little lights light up but then something happens when you close the lid and the charging stops on one or both ear pieces. I think the depth of the little holes are too deep and the tolerance distance between the charging contact points is inadequate. They needed to have a little more wiggle room and make sure the charging contacts would contact even after a few weeks. For the record both sets had this problem even before I washed one pair. I hope this helps someone.

title: Most disappointing Skull Candy's I've owned
text: I have been a faithful skullcandy fan for over 15 years. I've owned many of their wired sets including Skull Crushers and now Skull Crusher wireless, which I am super impressed with. I received these Jib True earbuds using a credit from my Wireless Provider and would have to say they are the most disappointing skullcandy headphones I've owned. --PROS-- 1) Color Options 2) Sound quality above expected for their MSRP 3) Compact and easy to take with you 4) Each bud can be used independently (see cons) --CONS-- 1) Battery Life: 2) Bud Design: Of the four or so wireless earbuds I have owned so far this set is by far the worst design for staying in your ear. It is constantly coming loose or falling out with simple actions like talking or chewing food. This also leaves it very prone to getting knocked out when you bump your earlobe or pull your hoodie over your head. 3) The Case: It doesn't tell you how much battery remains. The lid is a PITA and constantly closes as you're trying to get your buds out or in. The right earbud charges correctly but rarely registers when I take it out of the case, thus I have to drop it back in to get it to register and turn on when I pull it out a second time. 4) Independent Right/Left Bud Use: When using one bud standalone is that friends have a hard time hearing me on calls. I have also had numerous issues getting them to connect automatically to my Windows 10 PC. It's like whichever earbud I initially connected with will automatically pair, but the other one won't without resetting the connection or manually telling it to connect. This may be attributed to the bluetooth on my computer as it seemed to be working fine with my phone. 5) The headphones randomly disconnect from my Windows 10 PC as well. Sometimes it will stay connected for hours. Sometimes for two minutes. You never really know. Sometimes it reconnects automatically. Sometimes it doesn't. --OVERALL-- For the price I think they are decent. The sound quality is above some $40+ pairs. The battery life is short, but not so short you can't tolerate it. They are okay as an entry level wireless earbud. Just don't expect any extra features.

title: Great commuter headphones
text: So there are quite a few 1 star reviews on here, but I get the impression they either spend their time in too many headphones and are over critical OR they just spent more than $50 on a pair of headphones for the first time and expect XM4 quality. Anyhow, I don't consider myself an audiophile, but I do have a weird compulsion towards buying headphones and these frequently pop up on sale which put it on my radar. What I use them for: I have a pair at my office desk, they're comfy (for me male, average size head with glasses), they're comfortable, great noise cancelling, and the noise bleed is minimal which my co-workers appreciate. Thoughts; Yes, the audio is no where near as crisp and full as the XM series from Sony, but if you're looking for something to run around with or throw into a carry on that you want decent noise cancelling this is a good choice. Specially if you're like me who struggles with earbuds. Yes, they're plastic, which does hold durability issues, but it does make them light, which I like as I sometimes struggle with my XMs on a 4+ hour flight due to the weight. Added note: I'm actually purchasing a 2nd pair of these to keep at home as I've found the mid tones hit right for ASMR and they have a similar comfort my Bose Soundtrue which keeps me tethered to my desktop.

title: Hate For No Reason
text: I'm not sure why so many reviewers have knocked these headphones. I paid about $45 for a Like New pair and they are more than adequate for my needs. I bought these to use at work when I return to the office. I wasn't looking for Bose level sound quality, just a decent pair of noise cancelling headphones. I saw reviewers mention these aren't loud enough. Unless you are hard of hearing, or want to become hard of hearing later in life, the volume is more than enough. I also saw reviewers mention how uncomfortable they are. I, admittedly, have a large head. I didn't find these uncomfortable to use at all. I gave these headphones a 4 out of 5 for two reasons: 1. Build Quality - As many have mentioned, they are plastic. They definitely feel flimsy. A carrying case of some sort would have put me at ease. For now, I will keep them in the box they came in. 2. Noise Cancellation/Ambiance Mode - The Noise Cancelling works fine on these. Not the best, but they do a fine job if you have music going plus the NC mode. Ambiance Mode is where they lose me. Both are tied to the same button. From the description, the headphones are supposed to be able to detect what is going on around you and auto adjust accordingly. I didn't find this mode to work very well at all and it certainly made my music sound worse. Overall, I'm happy with these headphones. If you've ever owned a pair of Sony headphones, you know what you are getting. They aren't going to blow other headphones out the water, but they will sound serviceable for most people's needs. The main draw is the noise cancellation feature, which it does well. I can't recommend these at $198, but if you see a pair for $50 or less via Amazon Warehouse, they are worth taking a chance on.

My daughter said she heard a little bit of a high pitched feedback sound when she would talk. That might be because the microphone and speakers are so close to each other. But she said the feedback wasn't loud. On the upside, going back to my original Sony SBH70 headphones (which I love btw), was like listening to old favorites for the first time again. There's no beating quality sound. Sadly, you just don't get that here. I even tried fiddling with the equalizer, but it just couldn't put out decent bass. So, I will continue with my Sony headphones for music. I got these earbuds specifically because the microphone on the Sony headphones sometimes gets buried in my collar or scarf. I'm used to 9-10 hours of play time on my Sony headphones. It's difficult to find an affordable pair that has long battery life while in use, and good sound. I was thinking I'd have to get *two pairs* in order to get the maximum play time I require. But if I have to pay through the nose to get good sound quality, there's no way I'm going to be able to afford one pair let alone two! 🙄

text: I’ll start off saying that I have received zero compensation to write this review. We just like these so well at my home that I had to write a review. My teen wanted bluetooth earbuds for Christmas. He’s terrible at keeping up with items, so I want buying the pricey big-name ones. My husband had a wireless set of earbuds that have the connector cord made by this company that he really likes, so we read the reviews on these and decided to give them a go. Kiddo loves them. They stay in his ears while lying in bed and he often wakes up in the morning with one still in his ear! They’re just bulky enough to see when mixed in the sheets, but not bulky enough to be intrusive. I have a great pair of connected Bluetooth earbuds by a big name company, but was tired of the cord getting in my way. I frequently only wear one bud so I can hear what’s happening around me, and the wire on that pair are in the way when worn like that. I jumped on board and ordered a pair of these for myself. I love them. They are incredibly comfortable. I can’t wear apple’s buds because they hurt my ears. These are so comfy you have no clue they’re in your ear! Good noise cancelling, good sound. The best part? Super easy pairing with your device! Literally just hold the button down and they connect. AND some genius made them actually read as “sound peat” in the bluetooth menu on the device. Not a single other bluetooth device we own actually says what it is in that menu- they’re all a string of letters and numbers. My Sony buds are like wic2000, my car is U2, my bluetooth speaker is “bts” but we have 2 so I have to guess. These are a no brainer! They hold a good charge, the case is sturdy and they clip in there well with the magnet. I marked my headphones with a dot of nail polish and my case with a sticker to differentiate them from my son’s. I wish they came in fun colors, but that’s not a fault. (I didn’t want to do white because of grunge potential.) So far these have been a great product. I’d def not hesitate to recommend them!

title: Great sound at any price
text: After my Lab chewed my $180 Bose SoundSports, I decided to minimize my financial loss in case she got a hold of another pair of ear buds. After reading reviews, I settled on these $30 SoundPEATS. At 1/6 the price of the Boses, I wasn't suspecting much. Wow, was I wrong! These buds pack a better punch than the $180 Boses and has better sound. The bass is deep, but not overpowering. The highs and midrange sound true as well. They are sometimes a bit fiddly to firmly place in your ears, but after finding the right ear tips and the proper orientation, they sealed well and didn't loosen, even after a 3 mile run. These are amazing ear buds and are worth way more than their price.

title: So far these are the best true wireless headphones I’ve come across
text: I’ve bought about 5 pairs of these, no try y don’t last forever, but pretty long considering the price. And more expensive brand won’t last much longer. I either lose one or I’ll have them for so long that they’ve just gone bad, I’d say longest I’ve gone was 10 months or so. But keep in mind I wear them all day at work and then a few hours outside of work too, so they may last a lot longer if I didn’t always have these in my ear. The quality of just fine, best sound quality I’ve heard so far, and the fit well I can’t say for other peoples ears but for mine they fit pretty perfect. They may slip out sometimes if I’m very active but they all do that. When they’re in their properly they work better than ear plugs for sound cancellation for.

title: Great once paired

title: Awesome! These stay put while I work out
text: These are the perfect lower cost ear buds so far. I have been on the HUNT. I went through 4 low cost ear buds and bluetooth headphones. I run about 10-15k each week and need ear buds that will stay put and not cause pounding in my ears with my steps and will hold up to sweat. I'm also a small woman and I cant use clunky gear because it just fits me differently. These so far do all of it. They don't cancel much noise. Personally I didn't want that because I run outside and need to listen for traffic and things. The sounds quality is just fine for me. If you need pro quality sound these aren't that.. but I am personally not going to shell out for expensive ear buds. For the price these are super.

title: So Far So Good. Love the independent pairing!
text: I am NOT rating these for stereo music use. I have other, better headphones for that. I wanted ear buds that would stay in place. Another major consideration is pairing with two different devices. I have the right bud paired to my phone, and the left paired to my computer (both Bluetooth capable). In mono mode, both work great! So Far! I've only had them a short time, so I can't speak to long-term performance or battery life. Be careful if you want two devices connected at the same time. MANY of the products sold in this category do not offer that capability, but the descriptions don't make it easy to find out. These WILL pair to two different devices at the same time. Left to one, right to another.

title: these are great

The only problem is the other day he dropped one outside and my husband ran over it with the car. Can I buy one replacement?

title: Great Wireless Earbuds at a Great Price
text: This is the 2nd set of wireless earbuds that I have purchased within the span of a week. The first pair was the True Wireless by TaoTronics. Having used both pairs now for about 2 weeks, I like the SoundPeats much better. Here are some of my reasons why: 1) SoundPeats fits my ears better and are more comfortable to wear 2) Better noise cancellation vs the TrueWireless TaoTronics, even w/out music on, I couldn't hear mom who was talking to me from the kitchen while I was in the living room (we don't have a big house). 3) SoundPeats simply sounds better. 4) Both earbuds clicks in and out, frequency is seldom, I can look pass this. 5) Simple to pair with Samsung Galaxy S10+

title: I love my SoundPeats, best
text: I have had these for over a year now and I can still safely say I use them every day and I LOVE them. I don't have any luck using them for phone calls, but I prefer holding the phone up to my ear anyhow. The bass is lovely, the sound is clear, and the noise isolation is impressive. They are comfy enough for me to wear in bed, I listen to soft sleep sounds and they still block out my neighbors screaming at 3 AM. I get several hours of play time (4-5 times from one charge of the case) even after a year of heavy use. Any time (like 3 times) I have had a weird issue with them I email customer service and they reply same day or within a day or two. They always provide a video or clear instructions and I end up feeling silly haha even months after buying they offered replacements if the issue wasn't solved. It's always something that is easily explained as a connection/reset issue. So sure, they aren't as 'attractive' as some ear buds. But I recommend these to everyone. If you are looking for buds as just awesome audio and noise isolation (not calls) these things are out of this world. Thank god I found these before the 100th YouTuber tried to sell me RayCons.

Considering they are much cheaper than the Apple AirPods, they are a good value and an acceptable option for those who don’t want to spend a lot of money for good wireless EarPods.

I don't hear a lot of separation between the different frequencies. But they are $30 headphones. title: Defective upon opening; hours to diagnose due to inconsistent responses
text: The manual makes the activation and pairing of these earbuds seem very easy - enters pairing mode right out of the box, simply factory reset if this doesn't happen. Well, I have spent an absurd amount of time even trying to get these to factory reset. The only time I have ever been able to get these to enter pairing mode is one at a time, at which point only the Left bud will connect. This isn't all that helpful, because the left is supposed to connect with right which connects to the device. Unfortunately, the right bud has been unable to connect to any device at all. The factory reset process worked, I think, but sometimes the buds won't turn off or respond at all to touching, sometimes they do but only one works, sometimes they only respond when one bud is docked and the other is loose. Which can lead to the buds being disconnected from one another... Preparing to return these. I am assuming I got a defective pair (or single defective right bud) but the difficulty of use and lack of coherent support beyond one step of problem solving (what happens if the factory reset doesn't work?) makes me eager to get away from any Soundpeats product. Probably a good idea to shell out enough for a brand that isn't only ever found on Amazon.

text: I'm surprised more people aren't complaining about the hiss in the background. It would be easier to ignore if it was at least consistent. The staticy hiss starts with any music or video and stays for about 10 seconds and then goes away. Though I've had these earbuds in while navigating around on my phone with nothing playing and the static periodically comes back. They're also very loud. I can only tolerate the first 2 volume levels on my phone before it's painfully loud, so that doesn't give me a lot of options. As for fit, they're incredibly uncomfortable. It's like putting rubber earplugs in, it creates a seal in my ear that feels like I've got earwax stuck in it. I can feel them moving and popping when I move my jaw or head, and my hair brushing against the earbuds creates a lot of feedback noise, similar to moving the cable on a cheap pair of wired headphones. It's not like any earbud I've used previously. Even my husband didn't like the fit and he has a similar pair of Bluetooth earbuds. The sound however, is very good for this price point. It has decent bass, although highs cause a little ear fatigue. But it sounds much better than I expected it to. Pairing was easy. Despite what most reviewers are saying, there IS audio lag. It's not terrible on WiFi but it's noticeable if you're watching videos of people talking. It's like half a second or less. Overall I'm probably going to return these because the background hiss is annoying and the fit is invasively uncomfortable.
