title: I did a lot of research... These are the ones you are looking for.
text: I did A LOT of research on wireless bluetooth headphones. These are the ones you want. I use them with my Samsung Galaxy S7 which had some audio settings that can boost sound quality; this pods sound great and super simple... just pic them up and they connect automatically. Use one pod at a time or both. Call clarity is great; no issues. Intuitive multifunction button allows you to pause videos/music, skip forward or back; answer calls and hang up. I can't speak tot he noise cancellation... I guess it works because I have to take a pod out to hear someone speaking to me. No issues with moisture but I haven't tested this either. Surprisingly long battery life. For $30, this is totally worth it. I compared the sound to my wife's airpods and they sounded very similar!

title: Good overall
text: Not the most comfortable earbuds I've had. Maybe my ears are a bit small for them. But it is a solid product considering the low price. Volume is a bit low but the sound quality is fine. Sometimes they (or just left earbud) disconnect, but work most of the time.

title: Nice headphones
text: Awesome headphones I've had 5 different pairs now and these by far are the better ones. I've bought my family all a set so now I have 4 of these guys. The fact they have a physical button and not just a touch sensor is what sold me as well

title: Recommended
text: These are honestly really convinient. The charge lasts a whole day (for me) and the noise cancelation is amazing. They also look cool :)

title: Good sound quality, bad battery life, video playback lag
text: The sound quality is good for the price. Unfortunately the battery drains quick, within a few hours, and the audio lags when playing videos. I will continue to use the previous wired version instead of these.

title: Great Fit
text: I use the product for working out but if jaw or ear movement earbuds fit loosens. Other besides this great product.

title: Only good for listening, not phone.
text: There was no noise cancelling, and the quality was worse as the battery started to run down. I returned them after 2 weeks.

title: Great value.
text: The earbuds come with a nice charger. So far so good. Comfort fit. I use them while running on treadmill and I like them so far.

title: Worth it!!Long battery
text: I've been using these since the 29th of June and today is the 16th of July. I have used them for several hours each day and I have not charge them yet. Highly suggest if you're in the market for real cordless headphones this is a good option.Its now Agust 26 and still have not charged..SoSo impressed definitely the best purchase I've made in a bit.ty UPDATE: I've now had these babies 15 MONTHS!! Ive seriously only charged these 3 times and only one time did it go into the red alert to charge, the other 2 was because I was going somewhere and I wanted to make sure they were good and even then they didn't really need it. I use them at least 5-8hrs a day...they are very comfortable as well. I'm getting another pair to gift to someone. These are EVERYTHING!!!

title: SoundPEATS hit the sweet spot of solid performance at a comfortable price.
text: My wired ear buds were driving me nuts at the gym and I'm too stingy to pay Apple's price for myself. I'm extremely happy with my new SoundPEATS. Admittedly, my wife's Air Pods sound a little richer, but my SoundPEATS sound plenty good enough. They work great and for 1/5 of Apple's price they are an outstanding value. Please note that SoundPEATS' well made recharging/carrying case is significantly larger than Apple's.

title: Amazing!
text: Excellent product! I use it at the gym and it works perfectly.

title: The Battery Life Sucks
text: The battery life on the buds are not that great. I have to charge it every hour and 45 mins. So I bought me some more from another company.

title: Poor Noise Cancellation
text: The noise cancellation on these earbuds is very bad. You have to speak too loud for the other person to hear you. Sound quality is good though for the given price range. And the battery life is not bad either.

title: Best Buds!
text: These earbuds are fantastic! - Great sound & noise cancellation. - Charge lasts a really long time. - Comfy fit. They come with several different-sized cushions, so they'll fit anyone. I can even sleep comfortably on my side with them in my ears. - Best distance range of any wireless headphones/earbuds I've ever owned. They still work when I go upstairs & leave my phone downstairs. Friends of mine who own more expensive airpod-type earbuds agree that these are a superior product.

title: Keeps signal even when you walk away from the phone.
text: I use these on the ranch, I leave my phone in the front office of a large primate barn and have perfect sound quality while in the barn itself. Works through the wall and about 159 feet away from the phone.

title: Awesome
text: Connected easier then expected! Sounds great and able to work out and they stay in the ear!

title: Never again!
text: I hate these things. I have literally spent hours trying to get the left bud to pair with the right. I've watched all the tutorials and read all the comments. Once in a blue moon I'll get lucky, only to find that they have disassociated again a few days later and I have to go through the whole frustrating hit or miss process again. I finally gave up and bought the TRANYA earbuds again. What a relief! What a difference! These are now going in the trash.

title: Amazing sound for the price!
text: First, the Bad: The case is HUGE, and feels like it is made of the cheapest plastic known to humankind Next, the Good: Phenomenal sound with decent bass from a $30 set of BT headphones! the AirPods originals can't hold a candle to this sound! I was blown away! Battery is decent, and the noise cancellation is fairly effective due to proper fit and insulation from outside noise I had to take them off to cross a street!) I guess touch functions are all that this set is missing. But for $30 and great sound, who cares?

title: Pretty Good headphones.
text: I am really enjoying these headphones so far after a few months and I got them earlier than expected so that was great.

title: Best value for the price.
text: These work very well. The fit and sound were excellent. This is my second pair. The first pair had a charger meltdown because of European electric surge.

title: Disappointed
text: One bluetooth works great the other sounds muffled. Received replacement with the same problem😏

title: Beautiful sound!
text: Impressed with the sound quality!!! I don’t know how to say it but you won’t be disappointed!

title: LOVE
text: I bought another pair of Soundpeats wireless earbuds earlier this year to use at the gym but decided I wanted some to just keep at home. I considered just ordering a second pair of the ones I had, but decided to give these a try. I haven't used them much, but so far I'm very pleased with them. The battery life is advertised as being the same as my others, which is absolutely outstanding. These actually fit a little more snugly in my ears than the others, which I like, though my one minor complaint is that they're a little hard to take out (my others have kind of a stem that makes them easier to grab onto). At first, the sound quality was really tinny and weird when I connected them to my laptop. I disconnected them and then tried them with my phone and suddenly they sounded great, so I tried them again on my laptop and they were fine. Not sure if they just needed to be calibrated a bit or what. I do have to turn the computer volume up higher with these than I do with regular corded earbuds for some reason, though I discovered that when I disconnect them, my laptop volume goes back to normal, and then when I connect them again, the volume jumps up to whatever I had them set at last time. So that's kinda handy. The sound quality is pretty great, and they sound phenomenal with Windows Sonic enabled. I've been really impressed with both of my Soundpeats products thus far. They're definitely good earbuds for the price.

title: Too bulky for my ears and volume sux.
text: I had to give these to my man. They were too big for my ears. They pop out and were uncomfortable. I also didn't like that the volume level wasn't loud enough to cancel out the music at the gym. He likes them so at least it wasn't a total waste of money.

title: Just ok
text: I think you can forget using these for good quality phone conversations. For music they are pretty good . The fit in and staying in the ear is somewhat questionable . They are a little bulky. Some other brands may be better but these are the only ones I have tried so far,

title: Just what I was looking for
text: I have been looking for ear buds that will both connect individually. I generally only use one at a time and it’s great to be able to have one charging while using the other. They say in my ears well and were easy to connect.

title: Good earbuds
text: These are not the top of the line earbuds but for the price these earbuds are well worth it. My son paints houses and I bought him a pair. He loves them. I have bought many cheap earbuds and always had issues with one thing or another. These are perfect. They pair well good sound and fit great.

title: Doesn’t pair both channels with my iPhone 10.
text: Only one channel works when paired. What good is that? Tried every solution I could find online.

title: Good buy for the price...
text: Had these for about 3 weeks now and so far I’m happy. Haven’t really used them while working out or sweating, so I’m not sure how good they’ll hold up with moisture. Will update if anything changes.

title: Even my GF isn't as true as these wireless headphones
text: Mind you, this review is only after a week of use. I give the product itself five stars but I give the CEO of the company only one star because there is no way he is making the company any money by selling these high quality items at such a low price point. Someone, somewhere, has to be going hungry. All jokes aside, SoundPEATS has become a brand i can trust to provide a product I will be content with. If you're new to True Wireless and are uncertain if it's for you - these are a safe and affordable option.

title: Great sound
text: Wow. Great sound quality. Very surprised. These are awesome! Wish battery life was longer... If they come out with a version with longer battery life, I'm upgrading. Nice job soundpeats!

title: I'm impressed
text: So far I'm very impressed the sound quality is some of the best that I have heard the carrying case is light and very easy to use headphones turn on when you take them out of the case pairing was very easy used these headphones under my full-face helmet while riding a Harley at highway speeds and the sound was completely locked in

title: Great Quality for the Modest Price
text: I use these ear phones to listen to podcasts or SiriusXM on my phone. I’ve been using them daily for about a month. The initial pairing was easy (Pixel 3xl). The sound is clear and balanced for my needs. I use the medium sized ear plugs and have had no problems with placing and keeping them in my ears. I love how the storage case charges them so that the earphones are topped off and ready to go when I need them. I really can think of no negatives for these, especially considering their low price point. The first set I ordered took 6 days to arrive because they had to be ground shipped due to the lithium batteries. I just ordered a second pair for my husband which are arriving “next day”.

title: I like these a lot!
text: With the whole AirPods craze, I figured I should test out the wireless earbud trend. For about $30, these are a great deal and seem very high quality. It's cool that the storage case is also the charging case. Easy setup too! The only annoying thing is that there's no option to control volume. UPDATE - these stopped working 3 months in with light use. Not a fan...

title: Excellent Sound Quality
text: Love my new Sony Earbuds! They hooked up to my bluetooth so easy! Easy to charge! You can go into the App and change the touch sensors to your specifications. Sound quality is great and I love the noise canceling feature! The only downside for me is I must have a little ear canal because I can't find an ear cover that's small enough so they don't fall out!!

title: i found the active noise cancellation to be ineffective
text: i bought this hoping it would be a good noise cancellation set of earbuds, but it isn't. otherwise it works fine, just not worth the price.

title: Disappointed returned.
text: I own multiple pairs of wireless earbuds. Apple pro, Samsung buds+ and these. I wear a headphone nearly 24/7. I sleep with them in to cancel out my partners snoring and to listen to something while I do everything. I decided to return the Sony pair. Unlike the other two, these were the largest devices. Even though I could fit them to my ear, after an hour they would be drooping and falling out. I could never get them to stay in my ears. There is nothing to keep them inside my ear and they are not balanced weight wise. The sound was comparable to the AirPod pros. Because they droop, they would initially do great canceling out noise, but would fail as they fell out. Overall I thought they were just ok in comparison to the Samsung for fit and apple for sound quality. The case does not have wireless charging unlike the other two. The Bluetooth connection was less reliable in comparison. It frequently disconnected when worn throughout the day and dropped the connection at a shorter distance. Disappointed.

title: Pretty good but still cuts out from time to time
text: These earbuds are the best set that I have bought yet, but they still cut out from time to time when I'm moving around. The noise-cancelling is okay but not the best.

title: Don’t buy Apple!
text: These are far more comfortable and work way better than the Apple ear buds. Also, the tackiness of the Apple ones are appalling, while these fit snugly and perfectly in the ears. I highly recommend these over all other choices.

title: Fantastic wireless earbuds
text: Very impressed with these earbuds. Sound quality is probably the best for any earbuds that I have owned, wireless or otherwise. Noise cancellation is good, but I haven't had an opportunity to really see how well it works in various settings. For me at least, they are also remarkably comfortable. Battery life compared to some other options on the market isn't as good, but for me it hasn't been an option. I usually have an opportunity throughout the day to throw them in the case and let them charge for a bit. No reservations about these and I have recommended them to several of my friends.

title: I wish I liked them more than I do
text: The sound quality and noise cancellation of these earbuds are amazing. The hear through option works relatively well. I just can't find a good fit of ear tip for my ear. I was able to find a moderately comfortable fit, but I could not be fully active while wearing them. They often fall out of my ears. I really want to like them more, but I just don't.

title: not good on calls, but great for everything else
text: they would get more stars if they didn't pick up so much dang background noise! when on calls there's this echo and people on the other end of the call always say they hear the background more than me or that the background is so loud that it's a distraction. I cant use them for calls like I'd like to but I use them for music and audiobooks. batterylife is insane!

title: I can not use this for phone calls.
text: The noise-canceling works well. But the Bluetooth connection is really bad. I can not use this for zoom meetings nor phone calls. There is a huge electrical noise sound when people talking.

title: Truly noise cancelling!!
text: These headphones are amazing. I am usually not a fan of headphones that go in the ear, but these are very comfortable. They give you the option to then on/off ambient noises/noise cancelling or nothing. I have 4 loud children and a husband, so I decided to see how truly noise cancelling they were. Popped them in while my husband was on the phone, tv was on and toys were going off and could only hear my music. That right there won be over. They also have the ability to take phone calls. Connecting via bluetooth was extremely simple and they charge right in the case via USB-C. Do yourself a favor and buy a pair, you won't be disappointed.

title: Excellent in-ear head phones
text: They are comfortable to wear for hours, connect to my iphone instantly, sound great, and stay charged for many days. I highly recommend them.

title: Poorly thought out.
text: These are the most annoying things ever. They sound fine (a little quiet), they are great to wear, and their charging case is good... But every time you need to take one earphone out because someone is talking to you, it just stops playing music, and there doesn't seem to be a way to disable this on the app. It's really frustrating to have to use them in public, which is of course the only time I actually need to use earphones. Given all the positive reviews I'm really baffled as to why this doesn't seem to annoy everyone else, maybe I'm just difficult 🤷‍♂️

title: Meh, money is better spent on jabra elite
text: Meh, minimal noise cancellation. Adds white noise with added ambient sound. Ok sound for wireless. Rather big & bulky. No volume adjust on ear buds is unacceptable. Unable to skip or forward. What is the use? I’ll stick with my Jabari elite 65+. Smaller, more comfortable, decent sound and basic noise reduction, and Darn near Perfect for the gym & running.

title: Keeps disconnecting
text: Great noise cancellation, as long as you use the proper size bud for your ear. Sounds is great when it works. My left earbud keeps dropping connection for a split second then reconnects almost immediately. It does this 3-5 times per song. Extremely annoying. Made sure firmware was updated, but that didn't fix it. Talked to Sony and they walked me thru resetting them, but that lasted just a few songs, before the problem reappeared. I've reset them myself dozens of times, but that doesn't fix it. Now the LED on the left earbud doesn't work. All in all, for the money I paid, I'm very disappointed in Sony. Now past warranty, so I'm stuck with them. I'll be looking for another brand after this experience.

title: Wife loves em
text: Wife picked these up for work and she absolutely loves them. She researched for months and finally decided on these, she could not be happier with her choice. Really good sound and great for phone calls.

title: Absolutely horrible call quality
text: Really disappointed in these headphones. I was super excited to get them after reading and watching great reviews. However, the microphone is terrible so if you're buying these to make phone calls, I'd stay far away. Using them to make cell calls is adequate as long as you're not having more than a 1-2 minute conversation. VOIP calls through skype or teams is 100% unusable. the only thing these are good for is getting fired. the rest of them is fine. great sound quality, battery life is good, build quality is good. just zero function as a headset hoping sony will issue an update as i don't think it's a hardware issue but if it doesn't come before the return window closes, these are going back for sure I use airpods, beats and a variety of other bluetooth devices and can safely say this is a product specific issue. Samsung S8, windows 10 pc. 9/3 update: Sony issued an update to fix the microphone at the end of august and it did zero to improve call quality. return window on these ends in a week and i'm almost positive they're going back. really disappointing since music quality is outstanding

title: They fall out too easily.
text: I tried these at an airport demo and was impressed by the noise cancellation. But I could never replicate the experience. I tried nearly ten different ear tips to make these work. If I used a pair that gave good noise cancellation after about 20 minutes my ear canals hurt. If I used a pair that I could wear for a longer period of time they either fell out on their own or the sound was tinny. Part of the problem is the weight.

title: Great Sound Quality With Problems
text: In terms of sound stage, these earphones are, hands down, the best wireless earphones I have used. My most recent pair was the Klipsch T5 and I really liked them despite their connectivity issues. That being said, it was time to retire that pair so I decided to give these a try. Design looks great but the rounded bottom on the case makes it a hassle when taking out the earphones since you can't set the case down without closing the lid. Sound quality is awesome after a couple tweaks on the app. There are a couple things that I find annoying though. To properly connect these, you need to take both earphones out of the case. This makes it difficult to use just one side. The workaround is to take both out and leave the left out while listening to the right. However, this only works temporarily as the lair shuts down after a couple minutes due to the left earbud being taken out. This may seem like a little thing but since I like to switch ears every now and again with only one earbud, this was a major annoyance. Another issue that I found was the battery life as they died after only 2 hours of use. Really want to love these but these issues make this a complete no-go for me.

title: Didn't work, bad instructions, didn't stay in ear.
text: Scan thing didn't take you to the instructions just a Sony page to type in their words which didn't work. I went to youtube and watched a video that told me how to use it very easily from Sony. Watched another guy on how to install it. After 30m of testing everything it didn't connect to my phone. I never got the blue tooth to even go into pairing mode. I can handle all of the above because it's Sony. But it gets one star for failing the most important priority test..... it kept falling out of my ears. I literally couldn't get them to stay in no matter how I did it. Super disappointment. I only buy Sony products too because they almost always excellent. My TV, 4k player, receiver, speakers are all Sony. I was really looking forward to these. Returned same day I got them.

title: its off white...rosegold ish
text: I ordered color white and it came with a really nice rosegold/off white charging case. The actual earbuds are also off white, not true white. The set up was very easy and it came with 6 pairs of replacement eartips, ranging from small to large. I have texted them in the gym and it survived. The design and quality is really good and my favorite part is the ambience control, it gives you option to turn it on when you still want to hear the surrounding sound when you are working. My only comment for this product is the single tap function. I wish it could be double tap instead, because whenever I am adjusting my earbuds, it would accidentally turned off or turned ambience sound on, etc. Or if I am tapping too soon every 2 second, it tend to freeze. So far it has been working great with my Galaxy S9 and there were no connection issues, and I wish soon this line will have more color options.

title: I love these things!
text: Even though the battery doesn't last as long as I'd like, these still get 5 stars.

title: meh ANC and connectivity issues, don't waste time
text: These earbuds look good and have great sound quality thanks to Sony's DSP and EQ functionality. However, two issues caused me to return these earbuds. First, the noise cancelling is at best mediocre. I tried all of the included tips as well as my own Dekoni foam tips which created the best seal and the noise cancelling still was not nearly as good as my older Bose QC-20 and QC-30s which don’t even require such a tight ear canal seal. For a better example, when washing dishes, the running water is much more audible on the Sony’s than on my older Bose ear buds. The other major flaw is that the right earbud would sometimes just stop playing sound, often if I pushed the play/pause “too quickly” (never happened on other headphones I’ve owned). The QC20/30s are still the best I have experienced. The QC 20s, though, are wired, something which I am trying to avoid in 2020, and the QC30s had a major decline in quality, i.e. basically started falling apart after a few months of use. Altogether, there has yet to be a satisfying ANC earbud released. The Bose 700 earbuds set to be released in 2020 could be it, but their quality control has plummeted recently, so I have doubts.

title: Great sound for when was made
text: Was great when it came out but there's bettee now plus they are bit bulky and noise canceling is meh. I've been using Samsung buds 2 and they work great

title: Nice at a renewed price
text: I felt that $178 was a little pricey for a new set of these but the renewed price was ~ $70 less and easier for me to stomach. They work fairly well but noise cancellation isn't all that and a bag of chips. Sound quality is good but you have to utilize the EQ settings through the Sony headphones app to get them where they should be. Had trouble connecting to my Mac - just had to put them on and hold both sensors for 7 seconds before they paired.

title: The best sounding true wireless buds I’ve tried, but....
text: I am by no means a sound snob.. but wow these things sound fantastic. However, for the price tag.. I’m pretty disappointed to report that they have frequent cutouts. Sometimes it’s just momentary sub-second blips here and there, sometimes one earbud will cease to play music.. Often this is while connected to my iPad sitting 2 feet in front of me. it's not acceptable. They also don't seem to want to work when answering a phone call. I can be on a walk listening to music, phone call occurs, I answer it.. nothing. Have to take out the earbuds and use the phone itself for the call. I have experienced several different true wireless earbuds over the years, including Bose Soundsports, Apple AirPods gen 1 & gen 2, Anker Zolo liberty plus and now my first Sony buds.. I wish another company could match the insanely reliable connection you get with the AirPods (quite literally don’t believe either gen has ever cut out on me) These Sony buds are definitely the best sounding ones though, so there’s that

title: Constant connection drops. 😑 Decent sound though.
text: These wireless Bluetooth buds constantly have drops no matter what settings I use on the app. It's very annoying and honestly not worth it. The competitors from Jabra, JBL, Plantronics, and Bose are all better. I've tried them all too. The cheap Ankers I have don't lose connection as much as these Sonys, but they don't sound as good. The Sony's sound good, not great. For the price, go buy any of the other brands I mentioned.

title: I have 30 USD earbuds that perform better.
text: This is one of my worst purchases on any electronic device I have ever made. The call quality is terrible almost impossible to have a conversation (no problems at all when listening to music or videos). They drain my phone's battery to 20 % after 3 hours of being connected (not in use) just connected and the phone overheats to a point in which I can't keep it in my pocket. They are not water resistant. Ohh and every time I dare to walk or stay still a beep sounds off which mutes whatever I am listening to. It is a huge disappointment coming from such a recognized brand.

title: Great product
text: Love the ear buds as the music sounds perfect and they are comfortable to wear.

title: Good for the money.
text: A little shrill for my tastes. Battery life is average.

title: No bayyerulife
text: The sound and noise canceling is great for me but it disconnects from my phone from time to time and the battery life is 3 hours and getting. Shorter.

title: Sony WF-1000XM3's
text: Let me say that these XM3's are the Truth! I love the sound that the in-ear headphones put out. They have great bass and give an amazing sound experience. I really haven't tried the noise cancelling feature yet, but I'm sure it works fine. I'm still getting used to the touch pad though, as I sometimes can't find it on my ear (large hands). Pro's: Great sound Sound Isolation (Even with noise cancelling off) Con's: Sometimes falls out of my ears Battery life

title: Earpads tore the first week. No support from Sony.
text: These earbuds are pretty nice. They are only useful if they fit in your ear properly however. Choosing the correct size of ear pad is absolutely imperative. When the earpad that fit my ear tore the first week it rendered these earbuds worthless to me. I contacted sony yet they refused to send a replacement (these likely cost Sony $1-2). Its unclear to me where to even find these replacement pads, so the earbuds are worthless after only 1 week. And Sony has lost a future customer over a $1-2 cheap part.

title: CHEAP!
text: Owned the first gen appple AirPods and eventually they wore out. These EarPods by Sony are extremely cheap. Right away I noticed the case was made of flimsy plastic. The actual pods were made of the same cheap plastic. When I tried them on, the sound quality was horrible. At least compared to the AirPods. It took me all of 5 minutes to realize I was sending them back. Right away bought the AirPods Pro. Best choice ever!

title: Major issues.
text: I was initially impressed with the sound quality, only to have a major issue where it suddenly drops in sound quality for a few seconds randomly when listening to music. This is with an iPhone X and newer devices. This is a widespread issue, search Reddit or head-fi and you'll see more people complaining about this strange problem - which is either due to defect or can hopefully be fixed with a firmware update. I also have serious issues with the microphone - during calls I am told my voice sounds almost robotic and cannot be understood whatosever. Not sure if I have a faulty pair or what, but I will be contacting Sony support. I cannot recommend buying these until these issues are resolved!

title: Great noise cancellation
text: The noise cancellation works well; finished listening audio book during a lawn mowing session.

title: Simply Blown Away (iPhone user)
text: I won’t make this very long but I just have to say that The Sony WF-1000XM3’s are the AMAZING. I’ve had products from Beats, Bose, and Apple and nothing even comes close to matching the sound quality of these earbuds. The noise canceling is on par if not slightly better than my first generation Bose QC35’s. The sound stage is incredibly broad with sharp definition for all frequency ranges. I’m no audiophile but even my untrained ear can tell these earbuds are a massive cut above all others in this price range. I simply cannot recommend this product enough. To clarify I’m an iPhone user (iPhone XS running iOS 12.4). At the time of this review I have experienced no problems with the Sony app (which you need to make use of all the features of these bad boys). While these are made to be used with primarily android devices the loss of Siri is not enough of a deterrent for me. If you’re an Apple user and you’re considering the AirPods with the wireless charging case just do yourself a favor and spend the extra $30 for a set of these. I promise you will not be disappointed. These loss of wireless charging is a minor inconvenience for a truly life changing audio experience. AirPods in comparison sound lifeless after spending a session listening to the Sony’s. I hope this helped any Apple users with their decision making.

title: Worth the money
text: Great noise cancelling alternative to bulky over-the-ear headphones. Case slips easily into a pocket. Earbuds fit better and more securely than others I've tried. Sound quality is great and app includes an equalizer function.

title: Would buy again
text: Very impressed overall, sound quality is excellent for a Bluetooth headphone. Noise canceling is better than expected given they are in ear. They charge quickly.

title: I swear they won’t fit in most ears
text: I absolutely love the sound quality and functionality of the headphones, but I hate absolutely hate the fit and how awkward they feel , you can’t go up one step without behaving to readjust them, and no one makes Accessories to fix this issue. The batter life is above and beyond the apple counterparts, but the fit isn’t worth it

title: Amazing sound quality and snug fit
text: Design:⁣ - The design of the headphones are very classy. Even the rose bronze colored cover on the charging case exuded class.⁣ - The in-ear pieces themselves, while large, fit beautifully and neither felt heavy nor over-sized.⁣ - The charging case itself was much larger than I was expecting, due to the ability to provide 24hrs of playback charging, and I would have taken a case that was 20-30% smaller at a sacrifice of 6-8hrs.⁣ - The red charging LED was noticeable yet understated. Pairing & Interface⁣ - Pairing was fairly simple once I installed the 'Sony | Headphone Connect' app. I could not pair via the normal method I was used to.⁣ - Customization via the app was very detailed. There are four environmental/activity profiles that you can set different noise cancelling levels for. I did enjoy how as the slider moved an image of people, cars, and buildings would transition from 100% transparent to completely solid, giving you a visual representation of the noise cancelling setting.⁣ - Answering calls and changing tracks was simple and effortless. ⁣ - I am very disappointed that there is no volume control on the ear phones, especially as I had planned on using them for activities that generally do not allow easy access to my phone.⁣ Audio:⁣ - I have owned about six (6) pairs of wireless in-ear headphones and without a doubt, these are the BEST sounding ones I have ever used. The bass response and power are unreal. I set the equalizer on the app to 'Excited' and it raise all levels a little and made the treble a little brighter, which really made these headphones shine.⁣ - The noise cancelling was quite impressive. I ran a miter saw a few times while noise cancelling was turned off and then slowly moved to full cancellation and I was amazed at how well it suppressed the saw noise. At full cancellation I could barely hear the motor spin up.⁣ - Every now and then where people on a call state that they cannot hear me. I switch to my phone I come through clearly. For those that just want audio quality, buy these. If you are looking for headphones with a full control feature set, these are not them.

title: Good sound, mediocre noise cancellation
text: I got these to use while sleeping, primarily, although I have also used them during the day and while walking. The sound, which is adjustable using the app, is good and the flexibility of the touch controls on the R and L earbuds (also customizable via the app) is a plus. Battery life is also excellent. Negatives: noise cancelling is barely noticeable and far inferior to both the Apple AirPod Pros and (my gold standards) the Bose QC-20 and Sony's own over-the-ear WH-1000XM3 (which useless for sleep and not as comfortable for long periods of time). Unlike the AirPods, it's pretty much impossible to sleep with these if you are a side sleeper like me. I also have had no luck getting ear tips that provide a comfortable and secure fit, either Sony's or those from third parties like Comply. Even the largest size won't stay put. So for now I stick mostly with the AirPods despite their much shorter battery life. At least they charge very quickly.

title: Good not great sound with EQ tweaks and otherwise disappointing...
text: I wanted to like these and thought because they were so expensive and were made by Sony that they would be better but I was really disappointed. I bought 4 different pairs of headphones to try and have a few others at home that I compared with. 1. Sony WF-1000XM3 2. Anker Soundcore Liberty 2 Pro 3. Anker Soundcore Liberty 2 4. Anker Soundcore Life P2 I ended up with keeping the Anker Soundcore Liberty 2 because they stayed in my ears a bit better, had decent sound, and were only $100. I would have stayed with the Sony headphones but I was not impressed the the non-EQ tweaked sound quality. It was good but not good enough for the price. That noise cancelling was a joke as well. There was almost no difference with it on and off. The NC/ANC button didn't do anything. It would just beep and occasionally it would have a voice prompt that would say Active Noise Control on/off. Most of the time it just beeped. PROS: - Better sound quality than others I have tried. - Fit well and stayed put pretty well. - Light and comfortable. - NFC pairing - I wish more companies did this. - Auto pause feature when you take one out is nice. CONS: - Sound quality was lacking for the price. - ANC/NC button functionality was very inconsistent. - Noice cancellation did almost nothing. - Case is on the large side.

title: Adaptive sound control works great
text: These Sony WF-1000XM3 headsets are pretty nice. The adaptive sound controls successfully detected all my movements whether I was standing still or moving around. I was able to set the noise canceling to allow more sounds through the headset as I needed it to be while I was at work and changed the settings to block out more sounds when I was out for walks or I was in noisy environments. I was really impressed with how well the adaptive sound controls worked and they are probably my favorite part of these headsets. In an office environment, they worked great, blocked out all the ambient noises and muffled out a lot of voices as well. When I was out walking, again it blocked out most sounds, except wind noise. Wind noise seemed to be amplified with these on, but I'm guessing the wind was able to enter my ear from a lack of a good seal from the headset since the noise sounded a lot like what I hear when riding a motorcycle and the wind entering the helmet. Sounded a lot like a wind tunnel in my ears. These are a little bulkier and heavier than some of my other wireless bluetooth headsets, but they weren't too bad really, but that might be a reason I had a little issue with the fit. A few times the headset fell out of my ears when I just looked down or if i barely touched it on accident, they would fall out. I almost lost the left side when I looked down over a sink full of water and it fell out of my ear. Luckily i caught it in mid air before it fell into the water. The sound quality from the headsets are pretty good and the sound quality improves a little when you turn on the DSEE setting, although it does drain the batteries faster. With the Adaptive sound controls turned on and the DSEE turned on, i averaged about 3 1/2 hrs of use before they needed to be recharged. With DSEE off and adaptive sound controls on, I was regularly averaging 6 hrs of use before recharging. This headset was a good buy for me and I have no regrets. They have become my go to headset for daily use. :)

title: Great headphones!
text: To start, I am very satisfied with these earbuds. However, there are a few things that prevent them from a 5 star rating. Im sure these issues could be fixed w/future updates, which is a good thing. Sound: This is where these really shine, the noise cancelling is superb. Once you enable the full noise cancelling effect, you are locked in! Full bass, crisp highs, no distortion from what I can tell. Comfort: It is imperative you spend some time messing with the different earbud tips or else you wont get the proper sound or fit. At first I was using the incorrect size and was not impressed with comfort, sound or fitment. But once I messed with the different bud sizes, it was like night and day. Battery/pairing : I havent run into any issues even running them almost at full volume, plus the case doubles as a charger so thats pretty sweet. Pairing is super easy, just open the case and youre almost instantly connected. Features/app: This is where the buds get dinged a little. So the recommended app is kinda limiting I think and needs a little work. The auto-noise cancelling feature is a bit gimmickey and doesnt always work nearly as it should. I find that just turning the feature off and manually adjusting the amount of noise cancelling needed. Touch controls are a bit hit and miss. Registering touch isnt always on point. Water/sweat resistance is another big deal for me. I primarily use these at the gym and not having water/sweat resistance is a bit stressful. I like the Google Assistant feature and it works surprisingly well so thats a plus. Switching songs can be frustrating sometimes bc of touch sensitivity. Overall these are bad ass and I would recommend them. Small firmware/software tweaks can address all but the water resistance issue.

title: Man these sound GREAT

title: "Why do you sound like a serial killer?" or "Are you a mutant robot?"
text: I really want to love these. I actually do love parts of these earbuds,but there is a huge problem that is likely going to result in me returning the earbuds. I keep having problems with my voice during phone calls. I've heard "why do you sound like a serial killer", "Are you a mutant robot", "It sounds like you are chewing on rocks every time you speak" and other complaints about the sound quality. Now, I don't actually hear this problem, as the people on the other end sound perfectly normal to me. This is the truly upsetting thing about the earbuds because everything else works pretty well. I originally bought the earbuds to wear while using my riding mower. The mower is loud, and I wanted something that could cancel some of the sound out and save my ears from unnecessary loud noise. These earbuds do the trick! They do make mowing the lawn a more relaxing experience, but I can't overlook this problem I keep having with my voice during calls. I say headphone because normally I use only one at a time and this meant that I would not have access to the application as it would think I had none in. The sound was clear with a good amount of bass but even after a couple of days was weak and not loud at all, even having a hard time keeping up when I was running down a busy highway. I want to note that I have a larger tragus and these were downright painful after just a little bit of tune because the front of the headphone pressed down hard on it just so I could maintain a good seal. No matter how I turned it it always ended up pressing hard on some part of my ear. I hope this helps some people as I wanted to love these but with the bulk of a huge case, overly large size of the headphone pressing on soft body parts and causing pain, a terrible application and sound that did not boom I would not recommend these for anyone looking for anc headphones. The AirPods pro are an example of the best of these kind and just work, small form factor and easy to use app interface. (I do have an iPhone).

title: Audiophiles prospective.
text: Having tried many high end headphones, these sound honestly surprisingly good. If you care much about sound over ANC get these over the mk4's. To those who have problems with the fit. Go with comply ear tips on amazon, they never fall out with these. The sound is really nice coming from the 6mm dynamics with sonys classic tuning, but they have an amazing app and a good EQ. THE ANC is good as well as the mic quality, one drawback I'd say is wind noise, but if you're listening in a windy environment you get more than enough cancellation with comply and the ANC turned off. I HIGHLY reccomend these over the m4s unless you care that much about the 20% better ANC or ldac codec. I love the codec on my btr5 and wh-1000xm3 but AAC is a strong codec for these to have. title: Really disappointing!
text: I have (I think) every Sony headphone made, love this stuff. So of course, I jumped at the XM3's. Sadly, they went back to Amazon within the day. What was wrong? I love my WH1000XM2 headphones and the simple push a button and recalibrate. Easy enough, but this XM3 feature is WAY overdone. Simple, Sony, make it simple! title: Meh...

title: Been working great for me
text: I wanted to use these for a couple of months before passing judgment and after 3 months I feel I can now say that these have worked great for me. I use them with a 2018 12.9" iPad Pro and XS Max iPhone and have not had any connection issues at all. Noise cancellation works very well - not as of course as my Bose QuietComfort 35II headphones, but close. I am quite happy with this purchase and have zero regrets.

title: Hardest thing to keep in my ear
text: It absolutely won't stay in my ear. No matter which ear piece I put in it. Having to return because of the difficulty

title: Sounds is great, fit is mediocre, features need work
text: There are a lot of true wireless earbuds available. They all have one thing in common: by their very nature, they are heavier and bulkier than wired earbuds. These Sony buds are no different, but unlike others I have tried, they make little attempt to contour the bulk to the shape of a human ear. They have an oblong shape that I, at least, had a hard time getting to stay in my ear (they do come with a set of tips in different sizes, but none of them gave me what I considered a good fit). The sound: This is where Sony can't be beaten. These sound great, with a really nice range for all types of music. I also tried them with an audiobook, and again I have absolutely no complaints. They seem good at blocking out ambient noise, though I guess you'd need to be on a plane for this to be essential. All earbuds give decent noise reduction. Given that I love listening to audiobooks, a lot of the content I choose is mono. Other earbuds I have tried let me remove one bud and continue listening with the remaining one, which is the best of both worlds for outdoor exercising. I don't want to block out traffic sounds if I am walking along the side of the road. When I removed the left bud, they both stopped playing. You need to use both of them or they don't work. Pairing with my iPad was effortless. I just removed them from the case, opened the Settings app, and chose these buds off the bluetooth list. I had no connectivity problems. I will likely save these for traveling, where movement is minimal and noise reduction is needed. For everyday use, just for walking, these will not be my first choice.

title: Why pay so much for a deeply flawed device?
text: Not good for outdoor use, or while hot, or android phones. A light breeze creates a ton of wind noise in my ears, very destracting. Any sweat at all causes them to slip out. I tried all the tips, and even some aftermarket tips. Even if not sweating, if I am in odd positions, (working on car) they wiggle out. While the audio and the noise canceling is better on these, is is not worth the pain of them falling out. To top it all off, these do not work correctly with Android phones. The Google assistant intergration makes the buttons on these not work, and make notifications fail. The notification problem is well documented on some forums.

title: Battery issues after firmware update V3
text: The sound on these is amazing, have owned it a couple of years now. After an update the battery on one of the ear buds drains extremely faster than normal. Sony can't deny not knowing this as the internet is literally littered with these complaints. What's the need buying a beautiful earbud you can't use?

title: Disappointment
text: Based on how high this product has been reviewed by the experts it is a far less superior product to Apple air pods. Noise canceling is non existent. Product is large and bulky which causes it to fall out of your ears constantly. Don’t buy it. Save yourself from buying two and just got straight to Apple.

title: Will not stay in my ears. Noise cancelling not as good as Airpods Pro
text: I read a lot of glowing reviews about these earbuds. I have owned a lot of true wireless earbuds, including every generation of the Airpods and the previous generation of these Sony earbuds. I got a good deal on these, but I had to return them for several reasons: 1) They will not stay in my ears. I have always had issues with earbuds that have tips that "seal" in your ears. Airpods actually work great for me because they just sit in my ears, but anything that has a rubber tip that squishes in works its way out while I'm wearing it. It's annoying and frustrating. The difference is, the previous generation had little tips that rested against the inside fold of your ear. Wingtips, if you will. These do not have those, so the only thing holding them in is your ear canal's ability to grip them. With that, they would never stay in my ears. I tried every single tip size and they all just kept popping out. 2) Noise cancelling: All of the reviewers seem to be praising this. These have been declared the best noise cancelling ear buds on the market. I'm hear to tell you that, for me, that was not the case. The Airpods Pro did a much better job. That could be because these things wouldn't stay in my ears, but even right after twisting them in, the noise canceling was pretty weak. Definitely not what I was expecting. 3) They are huge and the case is huge. It's really good quality and I like how they magnetize. It's much better than the previous generation, but it's a big thing to carry around in your pocket and the earbuds themselves are pretty large. Lastly, Sony please learn to name things. No one is talking about your WF-1000XM3 earbuds because no one knows what that is, even people who own them. Learn to name and learn to market. You want people to get excited and talk about your products? Name them so that people can remember what they're called. Thanks.

title: Worth Every Penny
text: I’m a big Sony fan in general and these did not disappoint. I have some wired ones that are exactly as advertised, so when these became available on the Amazon Treasure Truck, I couldn’t pass them up. They were cheaper than my AirPods!

title: Great sound but some drawbacks

If you want more of a conceal get the JABRA 75t. Sound is not as great as the Sony headphones however. App takes a bit to get used to but overall, easy to use, great sound, I am glad I bought them and I would recommend them.

They are not for everyone, but if they get to working for you it is a 10/10! I’ll have to wait out and see if they have new models with a different grip in the future.

text: Great sounding headphones. Some of the user controls that the application allows would be useful if you weren't required to pair the headphones and your phone to a third party app. 1 application is Tidal (the failing music service) the other 2 applications have a half start rating between the two of them. title: Good concept but has many flaws
text: I was able to use these for a 12 hour flight and I was through disappointed. The concept was great but the execution was poor mainly in battery life, comfort and usability. Battery life: 3 hours into the flight, I was getting notice that the battery was low. Had to take them off to charge. I’m so used to the wired Boses lasting 40+ hrs, I’ve never once had to hear the loud airplane engine noises. This was disappointing that I had to take breaks in between. Comfort: After 3 hrs in the ear, these felt extremely uncomfortable and my ears started to hurt. Aside from the battery recharge, I would’ve had to take them off anyway to let me ears heal from the pain. Usability: I was wearing these with a headrest pillow, when I took my pillow off, I had accidentally knock one of the earpieces out of my ear and it fell under the airplane seat. I struggled for 20 minutes trying to reach and find it without success until I asked my seat neighbors to get up so that I can crawl down to find it. I ultimately found it but it was such a pain with it’s small size and how it protrudes out of your ear to be knocked off easily. I’ll be returning back to my wired 40+ hr headphones

title: Sent me used Earbuds

When I removed the earbuds they were full of scratches, the ear tips were cracked. Some of the additional ear tips had ear wax in them and very nasty. The whole thing was just so disgusting that I couldn't really bring myself to test them out. I am disappointed that a reputable company like Sony could let this happen. title: Easy to use once you get it set up.
text: At first, I thought the left headset wasn’t working. It wouldn’t light up, and no sound came from that one. After following the instructions from the user manual on how to reset the headset, they both started working. Before using this headset for the first time, I had to download the Sony Headphones Connect app from the App Store. Once I started utilizing the app to control the headset, I found it easy to use. This comes with a charging case, a usb charging cable, and additional earbuds. I like the built-in microphones because I can talk, handsfree, while my phone is in my pocket. The sound quality of voice calls is good. I can clearly hear the other party, and they can clearly hear me. The sound quality of music is good, but there’s not much bass. Noise cancellation is decent. These stay in my ears without falling out.

title: Disappointing
text: I did a lot of research before buying these, and every review I found said how amazing the sound quality is. What I wish anybody had thought to mention is that the sound is amazing... for Bluetooth headphones. This isn't Sony's fault, I'm sure it's true they've done the best they can with the limitations of a Bluetooth connection. But while the sound that gets through is good, with almost no compression artifacts, it's like something's always missing. Like entire parts, or instruments or voices have been removed. It makes everything sound like an unfinished demo version. It makes all my music sound flat and uninsteresting and just OFF somehow. Switching from these back to my relatively cheap, 15-yr-old, over-ear wired headphones, music sounds STUNNING in comparison. The noise cancellation works well as promised, though the earbuds fit so well and naturally block so much outside sound I almost never need to use it. Sitting right next to my window unit AC they turn the roar into a low hum. They stay connected to the source pretty well, though the left ear sometimes drops out for no apparent reason. The phone mic works fine, I can be heard perfectly without raising my voice. I have yet to run out of battery, though I haven't really pushed it. Comfort is fine now that I've gotten used to them. At first they made my neck tired and sore for some weird reason. If you want true wireless earbuds, and you're mainly concerned with blocking out your surroundings and don't care what your music sounds like, these will do the trick... but if that's the case, you can get it done a lot cheaper. If you NEED true wireless for some reason, you probably can't do much better, just like all the reviews say. Personally I won't be buying Bluetooth headphones again, at least as long as there are still phones with headphone jacks being made.

title: For my ears, a big pain and a noise cancelling fail
text: I normally use Bose Q35, which I enjoy, but I tend to get ear fatigue from the pads and they tend to warm up my ears after a few hours so I did a significant amount of research into in-ear options. These Sony’s got consistently good reviews however, to me they were abysmal. I can only chalk it up to the fact that some products work for some and not others. First off, I tried all the ear plug sizes and could not find one that fit my right ear. I guess my ears and maybe my head are not symmetrical. The closest one I could match to my right ear caused me pain since the buds rely on the fit and seal to hang in there. The way that this hung out of my ear caused me a noticeable headache. So I had one side sealed well, and the other not so well. Even with the left bud sealed in my ear, the noise cancelling was non-existent. Maybe a 1 out of 10??? I still have a hard time understanding this. All the online reviews raved about the noise cancelling but they weren’t remotely close to noise cancelling I’m used to. Even my Jabra 65ts, which don’t have noise cancelling but a solid seal worked 5x better at blocking out noise. I looked online to troubleshoot this and didn’t find much. I made all the adjustments on the app and with the buds. There is a possibility that my unit was defective. Since my last ventures with Sony have been lackluster, plus the right ear pain I decided not to try another pair and returned. Very disappointed but the search continues.

title: Mediocre for the price
text: This is a rather ambitious product and I enjoy the improved sound quality and active noise cancellation compared to the other wireless earbuds I own. However my experience has been marred with weird quirks and glitches that makes it hard to justify the price. It's possible I have a defective unit but some of the things I've experienced so far include: 1. Bluetooth connectivity feels too unreliable. Compared to my other wireless headphones (Raycon and Bose) I find that audio playback issues ranging from small hiccups to one earbud losing connectivity for multiple seconds. I've experienced this in different environments connecting to different bluetooth sources (including a high-range bluetooth adapter for my TV). 2. Weird charging issues. Last night I tried to use my earbuds and the right earbud was fully charged and the left earbud was at no charge when I thought the case had plenty of charge left. Tonight, after charging for another day the left earbud is now fully charged and the right earbud is out of charge. This is the fourth or fifth time now where I've seen this weird behavior where one earbud is not properly charging while in the case (after verifying the charging indicators were on when I left it). 3. Blue LED lights. I use these earbuds at night when watching TV. They have brilliant blue leds that blink every 2 seconds to indicate bluetooth connectivity. I find it to be incredibly distracting and excessive.

title: Amazon Warehouse purchase was not worth it. Like new was anything but
text: Purchased these earbuds from Amazon Warehouse. Listed as Like New, but unless you consider non working, scratched, body funk, and ear wax - "like new", these are probably not for you. I did not get a chance to use these, so one star it is.

title: I liked it. Best noise cancelling than Apple.
text: Noise cancelling awesome. No complaint about noise cancelling. I have used Apple AirPods Pro but comparing with AirPod pro this one definitely wins Incase of noise cancelling. I even don’t know when someone said in the review here that no noise cancelling. Ugh. If someone just looking for best noise cancelling earbud this is the right choice. But My complaint is about sound quality. Definitely Apple wins here. Sound quality not so good. Design is also ok. I like Apple case very small than this one. The most nightmare about it is pairing it on because it needs separate app to download. Apple wins here very easy to use but this one isn’t very easy to use. Incase of battery Sony wins. Apple needs to charge very often, lame. Also it’s almost 70-80$ less than Apple. So for price, battery and noise cancelling I will say Sony definitely wins over Apple.

title: Bulky but work as advertised
text: These earbuds and charging case are *considerably* larger than my 1-year-old Anker wireless buds (which sound like garbage, btw -- maybe the new ones have improved) I also have the over-the-ear Sony XM3 for direct A-B comparison. Comfort: the big headphone definitely wins, the earbuds feel heavier and less comfortable inside your ear canals Sound quality: the earbuds are about 75% of the big headphone, full warm well balanced sound but a little tinny in loud orchestral music or chamber music. ANC Noise Cancellation: also about 75% of the big headphone, but remarkable for these little guys. I tested ANC on my neighbor's loud muffler exhaust noise (don't you just hate those??) The big XM3 headphone cancelled it down to a whisper, while these earbuds cut it to a running-fan level, not bad. Overall, pretty impressed with these ANC earbuds. Bluetooth paring/reconnection works perfectly every time. I haven't tested phone calls but I have my trusty old Plantronics Voyager for that. I guess time will tell how long they can comfortably stay inside my ear without causing discomfort. So stay tuned for update.

title: Bulky and doesn't stay in ear.
text: The sound quality is off the hook!!!! They sound better than most over the ear headphones. That being said, I could not find any set of foam buds to fit my ear. They also lack some of the integral advantages that the air pods I have with my iPhone. If I just move my head too quick or eat moving my jaw, they come out and fall to the ground. Not cool, easy to lose one. Although I love the sound quality, I would not recommend these if you have weird ears and want total integration with your iPhone.

title: Annoying to Use

They're telling me something that I have no patience to figure out. Battery is almost 0% at first use. Most headphones give you a courtesy 30% so you can use them straight out the box. Requires an app to pair. Every time the headphones connect, the app pops up a notification "transferring", then "connected". The headphones then say "battery fully charged"....."bluetooth connected", EACH ear, one after the other. Why so much drama for such a routine task?! All my past headphones could connect via the regular bluetooth menu and maybe give a couple beeps. Done.

The companion app adds on to the features of being able to button map and also look at the battery percentage of not only your earbuds but also the charging case!

title: Good Sound, Poor Fit, Tricky Functionality
text: I purchased these based on reviews of others both on Amazon and elsewhere on the internet, but they did not live up to my expectations. First, the fit was not good. Sony does provide two different "feels" for the tips, and multiple sizes for each, but none worked in my ear. They either hurt after wearing for a short time or started to slip out. They also did not pair well with my computer (2019 MacBook Pro), and one of the main purposes for using these was for virtual video calls during COVID. There was a lot of interference, and it was not always easy to hear people through them. The controls were also very tricky to use when wearing. Despite the app that paired with my iPhone, the adaptive noise cancelling did not always respond to touch of the ear buds, and it would often stop music, hang up on calls despite not pushing for that to happen. On the plus side, the noise cancelling was very good, and the sound quality of listening to music via my iPhone was excellent.

title: Does Wireless Noise Cancelling Work?!
text: Good: The design of the Sony WF-1000XM3 Earbuds is undeniably great. The sound quality is also amazing so I sincerely enjoyed listening to music or podcasts with it. I find the noise cancellation feature decent enough, and the battery life good as well. Not so good: For me, the major drawback of this model is the poor quality of calls, so I don’t recommend using them for calling. Another thing that might need a big improvement is the touch controls, and others might find it inconvenient to adjust the volume on a separate device. Moreover, people who love to sweat might not be happy to know that the Sony WF-1000XM3 is not water-resistant. Read the rest on my blog Girl On The Reviews. com

title: Excellent

title: Almost exactly one year in and one bud won't hold a charge
text: Loved these buds while they were functional. Case is kind of large especially in conparison to airpods. One year in and the left bud wont hold a good charge, tried every fix from cleaning all contacts to resetting etc. No luck. Will claim to be 100% charged in the app but a minute or 2 of use drops it to 20% with a couple more minutes of use left. Disappointing for the price, I would have expected a good 2 years of use at least.

title: The sound quality is astounding
text: I have a pair of $350 over the ear bluetooth headphones and I'd be hard pressed to tell the difference in sound quality. It is shockingly good. There is very little to no noticeable latency. Battery life seems as advertised and they easily pair to multiple devices across OS's. Active noise cancelation is impressive and the passthrough feature is a nice touch (especially adaptive passthrough). Passive noise isolation leaves something to be desired. The tips that come with the buds are high quality and have the option of foam fill in the empty space but I just couldn't fine one that fit right. I like the tips to flair out and then back in (like a mushroom) in order to apply a sealing force against the canal without an outward force pushing the buds out of the ear. The stock tips didn't do the trick for me but I swapped them for the ones on buds I already have and the passive isolation was a lot better. I'm sure if you invested in some high quality tip replacements like Comply, the result would be even better. Overall this is a really, really good pair of buds, probably the best I've owned.

title: Sounds good and mic works well for using assistants

title: Must be comfortable as they are permanently attached to teenager's head
text: Gave these to my 14yo as a Xmas present, and I don't think she's taken them off since. Thankfully, blue is her favorite color, and these seem to go with all her outfits. She walks all over the house and even into the backyard with them, so I assume the bluetooth range is stellar! But don't fret, it seems easy to turn that off, because mysteriously there are times when her hearing is absolutely perfect - even through walls! - especially when conversations are not meant for her. The couple of times she's insisted I listen to her latest fave emo song and stuck them on my head, the sound has been super clear and I have to say I was impressed. I try to buy electronics of medium quality that can hold up but when they break it's not a huge hit to the bank account (she is pretty rough on her stuff). These guys are still going strong after 3 months with something like 3-12 hours of use a day and she seems to love them. I'm happy with this purchase.

title: Great sound for an excellent price
text: Having grown tired of dealing with a cord for my headphones, I felt it was time to go with a Bluetooth set. However, I didn't want to spend too much. These Tuinyo Bt headphones seemed to fit the bill, coming in at $30 with Prime (apparently $40 without Prime?). There is an independent volume control on the headphones, as well as an "EQ" button with about 4 equalizer presets. The battery life is very good at approximately 40 hours on a single charge (I have not yet had to recharge them). When I received the headphones, I charged them up right away (took about 2 hours for that first charge). Pairing with my phone was a breeze, I simply turned them on, waited for the tone saying the headphones were ready, opened the Bluetooth device listing on my phone and the headphones were there - clicked and I was good to go. I tried a variety of music (industrial/techno, rock, country, blues) and everything sounded great. The headphones are very comfortable (I've listened for up to 8 hours strait to an audio book and they were still comfortable. So, great sound, nice look and comfortable for a very reasonable price. I definitely recommend these headphones.

title: Certainly lives up to hype
text: So after my last earphone broke, I decided to the Raycon earbuds I’ve seen a lot of YouTubers we follow pitching them. I was skeptical, because I’ve tried equivalently priced wireless earbuds before, and they then to just boost the bass to copious levels to try and cover up the fact that they actually suck. With one such pair, I actually had to pull the bass down to its minimum level, while pushing the treble to it’s max, to make the music even remotely enjoyable. Now I’m no audiophile, but I do know that balance between bass and treble is necessary experience the full speed trim of music, and I’m happy to report that the Raycon Everyday Earbuds do indeed achieve a good, balanced sound. So yes, I approve.

title: Bad build quality
text: The sound is fine, the bass is overemphasized which might be beneficial in some situations. I had fitting issues which caused me to constantly fiddle to make sure they were fully in my ears, regardless of the rubber insert size used. Mainly leaving 1 star because while cleaning one earbud, the cloth driver screen came out, quite easily. This causes the sound in one earbud to be much louder than the other, also allowing your lovely wax down into the driver chamber. I contacted raycon customer service to which they replied the earbud would still work perfectly fine, they offered no solution. I dealt with it until I ordered a pair of anker earbuds (which have metal driver screens) & the ankers ended up being better in every practical way while also being less expensive. Raycons are very expensive for what you get, I didn't realize that until I tried other earbuds.

The earbuds themselves have a very long battery life, but I find that the charging capsule itself isn't actually capable of charging the earbuds 4 times from dead unless it's just my charging capsule. I heard that it could from a YouTuber who was sponsored by Raycon, because what YouTube isnt?, and he said it could charge them 4 times, but for me that's not the case. None the less the everyday E25s are amazing and sound pretty high quality for less money and I love them. Also just a little FYI for people. DONT LEAVE THE CHARGING CAPSULE CHARGING ALL NIGHT! It uses a lithium ion battery to charge the earbuds and in case you didn't know in some rare cases, when lithium ion gets overcharged or gets too hot it can and will explode. It's in all of our phones, it's in every power bank, and its in the charging capsule for these earbuds. It doesn't take long for the capsule to be fully charged either so theres no reason to charge it all night anyhow.

title: Good, Not Great, But Serves its Purpose
text: The headset was 100% charged upon receipt. Pairing was very fast and easy, and I like that I see the percentage of charge available in the bluetooth menu on my phone. I tried the headset out at the gym during my weight machine workout. They were very comfortable. I normally use in-the-ear noise-canceling earbuds, but I figured I'd get better cancellation with an over-the-ear headset, since the gym is very noisy. I was listening to a podcast, and as soon as I entered the gym floor, I placed my cellphone in the pocket of my workout capris. Suddenly there was a lot of static with the podcaster's voice breaking up. I immediately withdrew the cellphone from my pocket and the static ceased. I couldn't understand why a pocket would interfere with the operation of the headphones. Since I do not wish to keep my phone on the gym floor while working out, I started experimenting. I learned that if I keep my cellphone in my left pocket, that the headset controls have to be on my left ear. When I switch the cellphone to my right pocket, I turned the headset around so that the controls were on my right. As long as the controls were on the same side as the cellphone, I had clear sound. I reached out to Tuinyo about this issue because I find it hard to believe that I would have to maneuver the headset in this manner to maintain a clear signal. Everything else with the headset is great. Bluetooth connected immediately, was 100% charged. Used it at the gym for 1 hour which used 10% of the battery in that time. The seller responded to my inquiry with the suggestion that I charge the headphones and don't wear them while working out as they could fall off my head. What a joke! Bottom line is that, of course, you get what you pay for. I have a Bose headset which is the best there is but they're so old they don't have blue tooth capability. Rather than spend $300 for a new Bose, I'll stick with this low-cost set, since I only want them to listen to podcasts at the gym. I would not recommend this headset for playing music. The sound quality just isn't there.

title: Excellent sound, frustrating bluetooth and terrible mic
text: Sound and noise canceling are best-of-breed, if that's all you need: this is a pretty good buy. Comfortable, charges quickly, battery lasts, and the touch control is actually fairly nice. Especially the "cover an ear to hear the outside world" "gesture", that's a stroke of brilliance. If you want to hook up to more than one device at a time though, it's a surprisingly painful experience. Generally speaking it only connects to one thing at a time, and *does not accept connections from other devices*. So if you want to switch from your phone to your computer, you need to explicitly disconnect from the phone, then connect from the computer. And do the reverse to go back (it'll happily reconnect to your now-sleeping laptop, and will refuse to switch to your phone). It also has a bad habit of either being (much) too quiet or (somewhat) too loud, with no volume steps in between. My phone volume is only at 20% or 30% while listening to music, and I need to go into an EQ to turn down everything so 30% isn't uncomfortably loud. And I've needed to do that for everything I've connected it to. On a PC it's fine since there's much finer-grained volume control, but wow. Frustrating. It feels like I'm dealing with a bluetooth device from 10 years ago. Shockingly bad, especially since it's clearly software issues that could be fixed (but haven't, a full year after launch). Coupled with a $300 price tag and it's simply inexcusable. The microphone has been covered at length on youtube - do yourself a favor and listen to to the examples. In a quiet environment it sounds like you're speaking from another room, and anywhere louder it's almost unusable. The microphone is bad enough that I'm very strongly considering returning it and getting a Bose instead, it might as well not exist.

title: Amazing ANC
text: When I was first thinking about writing a review for this product, I was going to start picking apart the sound quality. Then I realized, is it really fair to compare these to open-back audiophile headphones that cost four times what these do? The answer is no. That's not what you're getting here, and that's not what these are meant to be. These headphones (and headphones like these) have a specific use case, and it is not critical listening. So instead, I'll review based on that use case. The noise cancellation on these things is outstanding! I'm typing this on a mechanical keyboard right now, and I only hear music. To be fair, I have spent very little time listening to Bose headphones, so I would not be the best person for a direct comparison. What I can say for sure, however, is that these work really well. A couple of negative points: They could be a little more comfortable for someone with a head and ears the size of mine, but I'm used to that by now. The bass is very present, but it's a bit loose and sloppy (not tight or accurate), and mids take a definite back seat. It is very easy to accidentally change tracks when trying to adjust the cans. These things being mentioned, these headphones are good enough at what they do (in context of what they are meant for - private listening, airplane listening, etc.) to be worthy of a five-star review. If there are better ANC headphones out there, I have never tried them.

title: Great At What They Do --But Not What I Expected
text: Nothing on the Amazon Vine listing indicated that these headphones were specifically designed for use with a phone. My assumption (oops!) was that since it came with a cord that it could also be used on my laptop and desktop with equally good sound quality. Unfortunately this is not the case -- and that should have been mentioned in the description. Using it on my desktop provided a muddy and distorted sound, easily surpassed by any of the other 10 pairs of headphones I have. Even my desktop speakers provide a superior listening experience. Looking at the Amazon product page now it is still difficult to find any information stating that it is not for use with those two devices. I will say though that they are VERY comfortable, easily adjustable for fit, and I like the 'desert' color which differentiates it from the typical black headphone. The fit itself is conducive to noise cancelling even without the electronic gizmos. More comfortable than my Bose unit and just as good as providing clear sound quality. Good product for the price point.
