title: Sony versus Bose- my experience
text: Quick Summary: are the XM3's the Bose QuietComfort killers the reviews have made them out to be? Yes. Having used the Bose on a long flight to Europe, I liked the noise cancellation but the comfort dropped a bit after several hours. I did the same test with the Sony's, and when positioned correctly on my head- I was able to wear them longer. Also the noise cancellation seems more effective as well- including the killer test of commercial lawn mowing and trimming gear. Note both basically require that you use their smartphone app. But Sony's App is more full featured and really changes how the headphones sound. Which is good, as the default was waaaay to base heavy for me, but with some simple adjustments to the app, I got my preferred sound. The Bose has less features and adjustments in my experience. The Bose does update MUCH faster though- the Sony took forever to update its firmware and wanted an update straight out of the box. That minor quibble aside, when it come time for my next flight- I am going to reach for the Sony's over my 4 month old Bose Quietcomforts. Now just make these in throwback Walkman Sport livery Sony!

title: Such mixed feelings about these!
text: I'll start by saying that I'm not an extremely tech-savvy person, otherwise I might not have been so dismayed to learn that my favorite feature of these headphones is rendered useless when they're wired. Evidently it has something to do with digital BT vs. analog wired technology of the headphones, but that's not something I'm schooled in. And I'm so incredibly bummed by this discovery. First off, the NC feature on these is stupendous. If that's all you're going for, and don't care too deeply about sound quality, then these are your cans. When you're connected to Bluetooth, and you've got the Sony headphones app up and running, you can customize the sound in an amazing array of ways (there are Reddit, and other, threads, dedicated to sharing such customizations). Several of the 'stock' EQ options are okay; others not so much. But when I got my headphones tweaked just right and saved the setting as a 'Custom 1,' I could not believe the sound quality: crystal-clear, highs, lows and midranges that all popped yet complemented one another. You can also adjust the 'direction' that the sound is coming from. So yeah, this is all great, unless you want to wire yourself to your laptop, the (quickly disappearing) back-of-seat entertainment on planes, or an old-school iPod that doesn't have BT capability (waves hand here). Plus, my vehicle is telling me that the headphones are not compatible with its entertainment system, so BT car audio is out as well. Also, as someone one of the aforementioned threads complained, if you're listening (with the subpar audio) to a movie on a plane, and then unplug the jack at either connection point, the headphones announce loudly that they're turning off, and then they turn off. That's ridiculous. For $350 you'd think that these major sticking points could be addressed and resolved, but until then I'll stick with the inferior noise-cancelling but superior stock sound quality of the Sennheiser 4.50s.

I was thinking of trying the Bose competitor version for myself to see if the treble is better because I also love the noise cancelling aspect of headphones like this.

title: Good to go

title: Better than my Bose QC25
text: I really didn't think wireless headphones could beat out my old Bose wired QuietComfort 25 headphones, but I find that I like these headphones much more than my Bose. I just got back from my first flight with these headphones and will be happy to bring them on many more flights to come. The sound quality is fantastic. I can hear more musical subtleties than with my Bose. The Bose are also great, but I can hear more of the music with this pair of Sony headphones. The noise cancelling portion also works a little better than the Bose. More sounds are cancelled out. I find that these cancel outside voices better than the Bose. With the Bose, I can still hear the advertisement that American Airlines plays on every single flight. I used to have to turn the music up very high with the Bose to be able to cancel out the horrible advertisement. With this pair of headphones, I can still hear that the advertisement is happening, but it's much quieter and I can't make out the words. The feature that controls the music by swiping the headphones is wonderful too. It works well. I can control the music without having to look at my phone (Samsung Galaxy S8+). I was easily able to pair the headphones to my phone. These headphones are comfortable. So far, I've worn them for 6 hours straight without them becoming uncomfortable. I'm not sure if they will start to hurt my ears if I wear them for longer. The ambient mode is also nice when wearing headphones at work. I can still hear what's going on around me without having to take off my headphones. My one quibble is that the advertisement shows people walking around the city, wearing these headphones. Even with the ambient filter, it is not safe for city walking to wear these headphones. If you're crossing streets, you still may not hear the cars. I wish Sony would add a feature to turn off one of the headphone sides for use when walking around in areas with traffic. Overall, I very much recommend these headphones. These headphones really improved my flying experience. They are expensive and they take up more room in my bag than is ideal, but they are so worth it.

title: these headphones work very well with the new 2020 Sony 65in oled master TV.

title: Better ANC than the Bose QC15s
text: I can only compare these to my Bose QC15s. The noise canceling is much better than the 1st gen Bose, and less fatiguing for long flights. There was no noticing hiss when using ANC. It handles voices and other noises quite well, where the Bose was only good at cancelling steady, droning noises. There is also a button to turn noise cancelling off or down if you don’t want, or need it. They are comfortable and fold up very compact into the case that they come with.

title: Great Headphones Android/Windows/Linux
text: These are my introduction to $200+ headphones and my introduction to ANC. My first impressions were quite high when I received these. They come in a nice case that carries everything you need. After reading all the reviews on here, I was expecting to put these on and totally block out the outside. This simply is not true. When there is no music playing, you can hear almost everything. Though sounds are muffled. However: with virtually any music playing (or movies), even at low volume, everything goes silent and you mostly hear nothing but beautiful sound. The app works great with my S9+, Fire tablet (side loaded), windows pc via bluetooth, and Linux desktop. I tried Linux today and it was as simple as pairing via bluetooth then selecting the headphones as my speakers. So these work with everything, wirelessly. I've been able to get about 4 days of listening before having to charge them, which is great. The sound is fantastic. I would highly recommend these.

title: Outstanding Headphones - must try
text: I am a headphone addict. I have Bose QCs Nuraphone, Sennheisers, etc. I got these for a trip to try them out and am amazed. Noise cancelling and sound clearly beat Bose with amazing comfort. Outstanding product.

title: Excellent noise cancellation and long battery life!
text: I have purchased several noise cancelling headphones over the years in my effort to find the best combination of sound quality and noise suppression, mostly for travel. Until I bought these, my favorite was the Bose Quiet Comfort 25's. Yes, they're wired, but their combination of comfort and noise cancelling is hard to beat. The WH1000XM3 isn't nearly as comfortable for long periods as the Bose (so I won't be wearing them in bed), but that's not surprising in an on-ear vs. in-ear design. Their noise cancellation and customizable sound are major pluses, though, along with the long battery life. I haven't had a chance to test them in the air yet, but I expect they'll do a superb job of blocking aircraft noise. That makes them my favorite so far.

title: AMAZING noise cancellation!!
text: OH MY GOODNESS!! We originally bought one pair for my wife who had suffered a severe concussion and was having difficulty with doing her job with all the background noise. We were almost to the point that she would have to quit her job. I chose Sony as they were rated #1 in noise cancellation on a couple of websites. Sony completely solved the problem for her. They were so good that she insisted that I get a pair for myself to help with distraction in my office. I don't even have to turn on any music, the noise cancellation gets rid of the most annoying background noise without it. There is a phone app that has a noise cancelling "optimizer" that I run every time I put it on so that it accounts for any little differences in the background, things like atmospheric pressure. The difference between 0.8 and 0.9 atmosphere has a big effect on noise cancellation effectiveness. They are also extremely comfortable to wear for long periods of time. They are a stupid amount of money, but they work amazingly and you are paying for a lot of high tech to make it work so well. If you are already looking in this price range, I would highly recommend them.

title: Highly recommended
text: I highly recommend these if you’re looking for great sounding noise cancelling headphones. They’re cheaper than the new Bose headphones but they don’t sacrifice quality. The noise canceling is amazing and with the app you unlock the customizability of these headphones. The app gives you control of an equalizer with preset audio-styles as well as setting a Custom profile. You can adjust noise cancelling level from a full 12 ambient sound down to wind reduction or full noise cancelling. There’s also a neat adaptive ambient sound that will adjust the level of noise cancelling based on whether you’re sitting, walking, running or on transit. All of which are customizable to what ever level you want. Another amazing feature of the ambient sound setting is being able to filter out only voices so that background noise is cancelled but you’re still able to communicate with those around you. The headphones themselves are also very comfortable I wear them for about 6-7 hours a day with no discomfort or pain like my older over-the-ear headphones. My only complaint, which is less of a complaint and more of a small annoyance, is the touch controls. What I do like is the level of control you have, there is forward track back, play, pause, volume and Siri. My problem is it can be kind of finicky, it not horrible but it’s not perfect either. One wish I had would be wearer detection, in that removing the headphones would pause and putting them back on would play. All around I highly recommend these headphones other than some small personal complaints, these headphones are amazing and well worth the money

title: Ridiculous that it only connects to 1 device at a time
text: A $300-350 "high end" pair of headphones that only connects to ONE, I repeat, ONE SINGLE DEVICE at a time. Good luck switching from your computer to your phone. HOWEVER, It will Always try to reconnect to the last device you used. If that was your computer, then even if you go into your phone and select the headphones from the pre-paired list... it refused to switch!!! You literally have to go to your computer and turn bluetooth OFF to get it to switch. The only other way is to turn the headphones off, unpair the device from your phone,turn them back on and go straight into pairing mode, then repair the headphones with your phone. This is a LUNATIC procedure to use headphones. Absolutely returned. I wouldn't even consider using any headphones with such a pitiful design. title: The Best

title: Deal Breakers: Uncomfortable and No Multi-Point Bluetooth
text: I purchased these headphones after weeks of online research and even tried them on in-store along with other options. The general consensus around the internet is that these Sony WH1000-XM3s are the market leader in high-end active noise cancelling (ANC) headphones. Because they're my first pair of ANC headphones and are fairly pricey, I wanted to make sure I was getting the absolute best that would last for years. However, I'll be returning these headphones for two reasons: 1. They're simply painful to wear for more than an hour. The ear cups are too shallow and the ear pads are too small, which causes the hard plastic driver to physically touch my ear while I'm wearing these headphones. The headband also provides too much clamping force and really fatigues my head after a while. You could maybe get around this by adding aftermarket ear pads, but for the price of these headphones, that's not acceptable. 2. Lack of multipoint Bluetooth is a huge pain during day-to-day ownership. These headphones can only be connected to one device at a time, so going from my laptop to smart phone requires turning off the headphones, and turning them back on in pairing mode, then pairing them with the device I want to use. This is so tedious and backwards, it's a major flaw that makes the headphones feel years older than they really are. In the Sony WH1000-XM3s defense, they have very effective noise cancelling. I used them on a cross-country flight of 5+ hours and hardly heard a peep from the droning engines and crying babies on the flight. Sony's app has detailed EQ and noise canceling settings for customizing your experience. And, subjectively, I think the styling and build on these is nice! But, the fatal flaws of comfort and connectivity are a dealbreaker on these for me. Hopefully Sony will improve on these aspects in the next iteration of this model.

title: Real deal headphones all around
text: These headphones sing! Lows get Low! Highs soar, and the mids sing. Great pair of headphones. Find the sweet spot on the ear pad for gestures and it works great. title: Great NC headphone
text: This is a great NC headphone. Very comfortable to wear. I don't have problems with wearing it for a few hours. Although it is heavier than QC 35, it's hard to notice the difference (unless you intentionally want to feel which one is heavier). * Noise cancelling Unfortunately, in 2019 there isn't a headphone that cancels human voices perfectly. With NC on without playing music, I can still hear people talking. But it's difficult to tell what they are talking unless I concentrate on the conversation or the people are talking in a sharp voice. Some music can easily cover people's voice. * Comparison with QC 35 I first tried QC 35 and got a headache after wearing it for minutes. Then I tried XM3 and felt that it was better (could be that I was already getting used to NC headphones). Anyway, there are more levels of ambient sound you can choose from compared with QC35. title: Peace in the heart of the city.

title: NOT FOR THOSE WITH BIG HEADS!!!!!!!!!!! Honest Review from an ANC-Loving Misophoniac

title: Noise cancellation is great, but only 4 starts due to a collection of minor stuff
text: These have been a surprisingly massive upgrade in terms of the effectiveness of the noise cancellation. Most semi-consistent sounds simply disappear a few seconds after power-on. The effectiveness does vary slightly depending on conditions, but you can generally adjust out this variance using the free app to adjust. Perhaps the best example is that the characteristics of air pressure and such vary by altitude, so the right formula for noise cancellation is a little different at 35,000' than it was on the ground - you can use the app to sense the needed adjustment and make it. While the actual noise cancellation is fantastic, there are a series of small items that collectively make it seem a bit short of a true 5-star item: 1). The app is clunky, and, for me at least, is currently entirely broken (even with a re-install). It usually gets the job done, but it really could benefit from some usability work, and the recent issue with it locking up after the "accept newe terms" page has made it useless until the next update. 2). The case is mostly solid, but the slots for putting in cables can be a bit challenging. There is a clear fit for the airplane adaptor slot, but the headphones and charging cables do not fit as neatly in as I would expect for this level of product. 3) If you unplug the physical cable from the headphones, it automatically turns off. I have not been able to find a way to disable this, and just because I stop being plugged into something doesn't mean I want to lose the sound cancelation vs. my current environment or that I'm not wanting to simply switch to using my Bluetooth device. The result is that I pull the cable, wait for it to power down, and then have to press and hold the power button to get it turned back on followed by the brief delay before the actual noise cancelation begins anew. Overall, I'm pretty happy with this purchase. Were I to do it again, I would probably go for the QC35's from Bose simply because they fit me just slightly better, but I don't have any real regrets.

title: Excellent noise cancellation, mostly great sound, some issues.

Either too echoey, or the voice was too muted in comparison to the instrumental track. There is an option for quality vs using the options which is kind of crazy to me. It sounds so much better when you choose sound quality. What's the point of having equalizer options when you can't use them unless you set it to lower quality? That makes no sense to me. The Ambient sound features work well and I like the controls as capacitive finger movements on the exterior right side of the headset. However, in actual use, I found that sometimes I advanced a track rather than raised the volume. It's a case of remembering how you have placed it on your head and getting used to it. Overall a very comparable offer to the QC35. I imagine it would be up to a few personal preference features.

title: The Best Pair of Headphones I’ve ever owned -- worth EVERY Penny!
text: I have been in a search for the perfect pair of headphones seemingly forever. I’m not an audiophile or a purist, but simply have a 1.5 hour commute everyday and like to hear good music on my commute. Over the years I have purchased numerous headphones from different brands and time after time, each one lacked something. Recently, I purchased the Sony WH-CH700N, which were on sale for half off. They sounded great, but the noise cancelling isn’t as great and I’d always have loud talkers on the train creeping in to my music listening. So I began to search for yet another pair of headphones that had better noise cancelling. Time and time again, reviewers were saying that the WH-1000XM3 had the best noise cancelling of any headphones, even better than Bose; however, I could not swallow that $349 price. Fast forward to Black Friday and the WH-1000XM3 were on sale, so I took the plunge – WOW!!! These are the best headphones that I have ever had!! They sound great, with great balance between the highs, midranges and bass. And to my surprise, the reviewers weren’t lying, the noise cancelling on these headphones is out of this world! I’ve only had them for a couple of days, but its like I’m on the train by myself. It pretty much drowns out the world and you’re in your own, just you and your music. And once you set up Sony’s Headphones Connect App to personalize the equalization of your music, you’re in music heaven! My only issue with these great headphones is that they seem to be able to be charged by the cord that came with it, and its quite small and easy to lose. I've tried a couple of different USB-C cables and none of them seem to work (so just to be safe, i'm going to order another one as a back-up.) Now I know the price of these headphones is steep, but trust me, if you’re really into your music, and want to tune out the world while you’re listening, then Sony WH-1000XM3s are definitely worth every penny!

title: Worth the Price
text: Being an occasional cheapskate, I first bought a $100 pair of Cowin SE7 noise cancelling headphones, and thought they were "good." That pair was serviceable, but after they broke (my wife dropped them) I decided I wanted to splurge for a set of Sony headphones. I'm glad I made that decision. The sound produced by the Sonys is FAR better than the Cowins. There's a deep richness the Sonys produce that the Cowins didn't have, and the variety of sound directions you can choose from via the Sony app is impressive. The Sonys connect to my phone immediately when I power them on, and I like that they have button-free controls that work well. A touch and swipe in different directions controls the volume and forward/backward tracks, and a double tap plays/pauses. Battery life has been really good. I haven't timed it, but I know I've gone beyond 20 hours of use before charging. The noise cancellation eats up the battery faster, but it's worth it to keep it on since it does such a good job. The headphones are really comfortable on my ears and scalp, but sometimes slide off the top of my head if I'm wearing them during garden work. Overall, this is a very impressive set of headphones that are worth the price.

title: Great ANC headphone with a major flaw
text: This is a great ANC headphone. Has great noice cancellation, great sound but it has a major flaw. Unlike the Bose QC35, this headphone does not support active pairing with multiple devices. Let me explain with an example. Let's say you are sitting at your desk at work, watching a video on your laptop, sound coming out on your headphones. You get a call on your phone. What happens with Bose QC35: You answer the call on your phone, QC35 automatically recognizes that it's a call and automatically switches the connection so it's between your headphones and your phone and you start talking through the headphones. When you hang up the call, the headphone switches back to your laptop to resume watching the video. What happens with Sony XM3: You answer the call on your phone, you disconnect your XM3 from the laptop's bluetooth menu, you wait for XM3 to pick up the new connection to the phone, and then choose XM3 from your phone's output menu to use the headphones for conversation. When you are done with your call, you go to your phone's bluetooth menu to disconnect it and then reestablish a connection with your laptop and the XM3 through your laptop's bluetooth menu. To summarize, this is a perfect device for those who use it only with their phone but if you have more than one device such as a laptop, tablet and a phone, the user experience is pretty terrible.

I like the sound and noise cancelling more than my Bose Quiet Comfort 15s that I have had for years. I may have to put those in the drawer. What I don't like: the app you need to load to use this headphone set is nothing special. I have also not figured out how to save my equalization settings so they stay (maybe user error). title: 11 Month Update
text: Update after 11 months of use 6-10 hours per day. All systems are failing. Not taking a charge most days and powering off frequently—bluetooth works sporadically. I am returning to SONY, but their customer support is foreign, apathetic, and difficult. I stand by the audio quality being one of the better options, but bluetooth connectivity is difficult (you have to 7 second re-pair across different devices), and call quality is not acceptable. I have Bowers & Wilkins PX and B&O H9i's coming in the mail. I'll let you know my thoughts on those alternatives. ——————————————————————————————————————————————————— I have tested the Bose Quiet Comfort 35s, Bose 700s, Beats Studios, VModa Crossfade II Codex Editions, Sennheisers, Harman Kardons, and several other over-ear headphones in the $300-400 range. The Sonys have the edge in regard to sound quality. If you’re into diverse frequency music with a blend of bass and treble I can guarantee you they have the best sound on the market. I was impressed...going from a heavy pair of $400 VModas to this lightweight, almost cheap feeling pair, Sony absolutely stood out as more satisfying. That aside, noise isolation is decent. Sony’s proprietary system crushes ambient sound and you’ll begin to wander how you ever lived with that horrific white noise in your life. But voices are still audible, they really only cancel out the humming and not all frequencies. Still one of the best on the market and a must-have, but the technology is obviously still in development. The call quality is poor. I actually can’t use them for phone calls because the people on the other end complain.

title: Yes yes yes!
text: First off, I ordered them on a Saturday evening and the order was processed Sunday. I was supposed to receive them on Friday, but they arrived Monday! Not even late Monday, Monday morning! I'm not sure why it was so early, I didn't pay for two day shipping, but I'm very happy that they got them to me already. I'm assuming it is all based on your location and the location of the item, but I'm amazed! Okay, now in terms of quality, I'm coming from $15 earbuds from Target, so the quality seems extremely nice in comparison. The sound quality is very good, I can't really compare sound quality to other headphones on the market. The noise cancelling is amazing, as well as the gesture controls. All of them have worked flawlessly. I have not had these headphones long enough to really rate the battery life, they are supposed to be 30 hours of battery life I believe, which is unbelievable. Overall, extremely satisfied with this purchase!

title: Good but not perfect
text: I’ve been using the Sony wh1000xm3 for two months now. Overall, I like the the headphones. The highlight of the headphones is it’s noise canceling. The noise canceling is excellent. It took me a few days to get used to the cabin pressure. The sound quality is good but not amazing. The microphone is terrible. The battery life is excellent. The headphones are comfortable. I’ve been wearing them a few hours at a time. The depth of the the cup of the earphones is about .5 inches so if your ears stick out this may be a problem. I wasn’t to excited about the touch controls at first but I can live with it. The two buttons on the left cup are easy to accidentally press when grabbing the headphones. It would’ve been better to have them recessed. It comes with a 8 inch usb c charger, 4 ft headphone cord, airplane plug adapter, and storage case. I guess it is geared towards traveling but for daily use at home I find the charger cable way to short. The accessories are low in quality as out of the box the cord supplied has a loose jacket around the plug and the charger has a bad fit. Initially I was having a hard time deciding between the Sony and Bose. The reason I chose Sony was because of the complaints about the QC35’s firmware updates comprising the noise canceling on the Bose. I have tried on both Bose QC35 and 700 and both are more comfortable than the Sony. At almost two months I don’t have too many complaints. I expected more from Sony in terms of quality on the supplied accessories. The headphones do creak a little. I’m wondering if this will get worse as time goes on. I don’t think there’s a perfect set of headphones. Both the Sony and Bose have their pros and cons. Overall, I recommend these headphones depending on your needs.

title: Can't hear a thing except my music
text: As someone who has gone through at least dozens of different headphones and earbuds over my lifetime, I think I have found THE one. As a musician, my ears are one of my most important tools, and as such I like to take care of them. These headphones have the perfect over-ear fit to ensure you don't have to blast music to hear every detail. With noise cancelling, I can play music at around 25-40% of max volume and not miss any note. The ambient sound control is a cool gimmick, but I tend to just pause my music and take my headphones off if I want to listen to my surroundings. Medium and treble sounds are clear and crisp, even at both ends of the volume spectrum. The bass could be a tad stronger, especially at low volumes, but I suspect that just may be the fault of the actual recordings I am listening too. The companion app is very intuitive and includes some interesting features to enhance your listening experience. I know I am just some stranger on the internet, but I highly recommend these to anyone who is in the market for quality, over-ear, noise-cancelling headphones. The price is a bit steep, but you get what you pay for. I don't think I will need to purchase new headphones for several years.

title: Astonishingly good
text: In the short time I've had these I've come to associate them with a renewed ability to focus at work. That is easily worth the price. I'm a nit-picker and there's just nothing to pick at. The sound quality and comfort are excellent. The noise cancellation is amazing. The battery life is never going to be something to worry about. After a couple of hours with them on you'll hear the noise that is all around you freshly (with fresh annoyance). NC anecdotes: People around me talk all day at work which is fun, until I have to write some wall-of-shame SQL that requires my limited brains to not be constantly task-switched. Put these on, everyone is almooost gone. The loudest person sounds far away and faint. All the fans/hums/ambient sounds are gone gone. Add some low volume chill electronic music and it's perfect. Did I mention these sound great and can do LDAC (if your device supports it)? Anecdote 2: I just fired up a motorcycle to warm it up and charge the battery some while listening to an audiobook at low volume. A faint murmuring. Doubling as earmuffs? The audio quality really is superb. If you are bothered by Bluetooth limitations you can plug them in. I have not had a single dropout, and in LDAC 990 kbits/sec mode. The Android app also has more things than I'm going to use. You can personalize the sound, you've got EQ, virtual space stuff. Setup is painless. You can prioritize between stability and quality. I may kick the Beyerdynamics out of the house, I surely haven't been seeing them lately.

title: I'm so disappointed but they're still phenomenal
text: I got these from Best Buy after reading the glowing and praising reviews, assuming these would compliment my heavily-bassed up music (which is easily more than 3/4 of what I have- I'm literally all about that bass). Honestly, they are terrible when I listen to anything pumped with bass (ie Kesha, Die Antwoord, Zedd, etc). I can't explain it, but something about the sound makes me cringe- it's so distorted and just not good. HOWEVER, I then tried listening to other genres like rap and rock, and oh my god those songs sound FLAWLESS on these headphones. They just compliment each other so well. It's just so unusual because I thought these headphones were going to bring a whole new positive experience to... well.. bass-y music? Instead it sounds like, well, close your eyes and picture sitting in your car at a red light and hearing one of those annoying people pull up beside you who have a terrible quality radio and speakers and all you hear is distorted and muffled "BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM BOOOOM BOOOOOOOOOOOM"s. That's legit what these Skullcandys sound like and that's only when the bass booster is at MID POINT. I tried putting it all the way up to the highest setting and it sounded like pure garbage. I'm not an audiophile, BUT I am obsessed with bass and can tell when it's good or not- and Skullcandy definitely dropped the ball on these. I would highly recommend finding another pair if your most listened to genre is heavy dance/electronic/pop/club, BUT these are breathtaking if you listen to genres or any music in general with minimal bass. Other positives- SO comfortable (I used to have other Skullcandy Crushers and they gave me head aches), sleek (old ones were bulky and imo ugly), VERY easy to use (literally took seconds to pair and figure out), feels durable and like it's made with high quality materials, and had absolutely no connectivity issues. Overall I'm giving this a 4/5. I'm extremely sad that I'm returning them but they just aren't for me. I hyped myself up so much only to be let down by distortion and overpowering buzzing thumping. I won't lie or give these 1 star because I'm sorry but that's just ridiculous. These headphones are wonderful, just not quite on the money.

title: Spring gimmick will likely cause ear damage.
text: So these headphones have a great battery life, and feel decent for consumer headphones. The main gimmick is the "haptic bass"... the haptic bass is just two springy metal pieces that resonate at specific frequencies making the sound much worse and likely hitting decibel levels of ear damage! If that isn't bad enough just taking a step or moving or tapping near the headphones causes the metal to resonate in a weird way. I opened them up, and cut out the spring part of the headphones, and now they're decent isolating consumer headphones. Beware, the slider haptic bass gimmick sounds bad and is likely harmful to your hearing so I'd go with another pair without that!

title: Solid headphones that are fun to listen to and have great battery life

I use them mostly for listening to music around the house and while traveling and they sound very good. Obviously, they are extremely bass-heavy headphones, but the vocals still come through well (assuming you don’t have the bass slider turned up to 80%). The battery life of these is incredible. I’m not sure exactly how many hours they last, but even with heavy/daily use I only have to charge them every 2 weeks or so. Build quality is good, and everything feels well made, with the exception of the bass slider, which feels a little cheap but still works fine. They’re not noise-canceling but they do block out sound pretty well. They are heavy and take some getting used to at first but after that they feel fine. As for the microphone, it works well if you need to use these to make phone calls, although I don’t. Overall, they’re a nice pair of headphones that are fun to listen to and last forever on a charge. Just keep in mind that these are headphones with a ton of bass, not exactly balanced sound.

text: These headphones are as close as you can get to having a subwoofer in your headphones. The bass feedback is not perfect by any means, but pretty darn good. There is no delay in the bass response as I saw some other review mention. The bass just cuts out when it doesn't sense that bass needs to be amplified or if it senses that the frequency of the bass is too low for the headphones to reproduce. I will mention that if the bass slider is up too much, it might sound muddy depending on the song. Luckily it's easy to adjust. Good pair of wireless headphones even without the bass feedback feature, though definitely glad it's there. Pretty comfy, looks good. I've always been a fan of skull candy. title: Skullcandy "Crush-Your-Ears" Wireless Review
text: For me, bass is everything. The sensation of low frequencies puts you in an audio trance and doesn't let go. This is the review of the Skullcandy Crusher wireless headphones. I seriously don't know where to begin. Design is like usual headphones but they feel amazing on your head, even with extended use. They feature high quality materials and memory foam padding for a relaxed experience. The average battery life is about 40 hours and charges very quick. Now, let's talk about that bass! Three words: Oh. My. God. Folks, the 40mm drivers paired with the haptic vibration is seriously the most insane bass to come out of a headphone. When I cranked these up all they way, my head literally shook and my mouth was wide open like "What just happened?!". The bass is SO heavy! I'm not kidding. Best way I could describe it is when your in a car with multiple subwoofers. Words can't describe the bass. Also, it's not a distorted type of bass. Whatever technology is in the haptic vibration meter, it makes a one of a kind experience. And coming from me, it's BASS HEAD approved 100%

text: These are the best headphones I have ever had (or ever tried) and they are half the cost of many other similar products. The bass is absolutely insane. Music just sounds better, it feels like it's coursing through your body. Even streaming Twitch channels I can hear the intense vibrations and you really get sucked up into the game. (I use it for work, so can't comment on the gaming side itself yet.) The charge seems to last forever--sometimes I forget to plug it in and leave it on for a day or two and it still runs the whole next day. Setup was a breeze. It's comfortable--took me a little getting used to because I had the soft wired Bose earcups before but these serve a different purpose as they sort of engulf your ears in bass. Two things to note: It doesn't seem to fully connect, bluetooth-wise, to my phone. Calls can come in through the headset when it's synced and nearby but other audio like alarm testing or videos or apps don't always go through the headset. I am gonna guess that this is a phone issue and not the headphones because other people don't seem to have the same problem and I have a pretty weird phone (Blackberry Keyone). The ear cups don't fold flat so if you are wearing them around your neck your chin might hit the edges. They fold in on themselves for portability (at the groove right above the skull logo) but the cups are not super flexible. However, sound is still phenomenal, as is the battery life. These also fully function with low-latency bluetooth transmitters that plug into a standard audio jack (if you need to use that for some reason--my work locks USB functionality for security, so we only have access to headphone jacks). 100% recommend.

title: Comfortable, easy pairing, good battery life... but shuts off in the cold :(
text: I have a little armada of bluetooth headphones, mostly in the $20-or-under category from Mpow, Photive, Anker, and the like. Some are clunky but serviceable, with decent battery life but uninspired interfaces (MPow), some are convenient but don't stay in the ears well (Photive), and some are just baffling and make you want to cry because of poor design decisions (I'm looking at you, Anker). I haven't usually invested in pricier headphones because it seems like these things tend to die within a year or so. However, after seeing various positive reviews, I finally decided to give these a whirl. At first, the left ear was comfy, but the right ear wasn't a great fit (it tugged/pressed in a distracting way). I don't know if my ear has been trained over the last week, or if maybe the headphones molded a bit to my ear shape, but they're perfectly comfortable now. The real advantage, though, is pairing. I can seemlessly use them across multiple devices by simply choosing them in the airplay settings, rarely needing to go to bluetooth preferences to manually "connect". Other bluetooth devices require lots of manual connecting or disconnecting to micromanage which source they're listening to, but the Powerbeats just stay paired with whatever device you select them from. The sound itself is, well, OK. I'm using these mostly for exercising, wandering around outside, and doing chores in the house, so they're fine for that. And the mic seems to be OK, but not great. (It's hard to tell what is a problem with the mic, and what's a problem with the quality of my cell connection, though) The only drawback (and, actually, it's a pretty big bummer) is that if you walk outside in them in modestly cold weather, they shut themselves off after a little while. You can be walking along and suddenly get the "disconnecting" sound, and if you try to turn them back on, the white light just blinks. I haven't tested it extensively, but it seems to happen most when the temperature is below about 25°F out. If you live somewhere warmer, this wouldn't be an issue, but sadly, it makes them useless for running or walking around in colder climates :( Overall, if they last a reasonably long time, the extra money seems to be worthwhile in terms of convenience, but don't ditch your cold-weather back-up option.

title: Poor sound and fit
text: I got these because I wanted to find a better sounding pair of headphones to replace my Backbeat Fits when running and working out. The Backbeat Fits are very comfortable and fit great, but their open ended design lacked bass and made it difficult to get pumped up when listening to music. I got these headphones because I thought that the Beats brand would produce better sound and have an acceptable fit when exercising. Unfortunately, these headphones failed in both regards. As it turns out, the earbuds are open ended and not meant to seal, just like the Backbeat fits that I have. However, the sound produced is far inferior to what I have in the Backbeat Fits. There was a very minimal amount of bass and the mids sounded muddy. If the earbuds are sealed into the canal, the sound is pretty decent (but still nothing special), but the design is not meant to keep them sealed in the ear. As a result, these headphones get a 1/10 from me in terms of audio quality. My second issue was with the fit of these headphones. The clips to keep them secure around the ears (like the Backbeat Fit), but I could not find a way to get the earbuds in the ear to not move around during my runs. As a result, with every step, I get the sound of the earbuds sticking and unsticking from the inside of my ear canal. It was very annoying and distracting. Since the earbud part of the Backbeat Fits is more rigid, I did not have this issue at all. Ultimately, I returned these Powerbeats 3 headphones even though I really wanted to love them because I got a decent deal on them and I liked the idea of having 12 hours of battery life. I ended up paying full price for a pair of Bose Soundsports and loved them immediately. The fit is great and the sound quality is magnificent. The bass is wonderful and the although the mids are a little warm, I couldn't be happier with them for my runs and workouts.

If ou can find foam ear plugs to put on as covers instead of the ones provided - you'll get much better sound. The MAIN thing is, my Beats3 also just straight out stopped suddenly. I pulled out the charging cord and the light went completely off - hasn't come back up again since. It was very rainy the otehr day so i can only imagine that is what happened (but it was fine and the light was on charging overnight...) Other gripes - the provided chord is not comfy. The Bluetooth mic is horrible (i have to ut the cord in front for it to have a chance to work). The controls are unreliable (start/stop for me) as others have said. I really wanted these to work and when i saw all the other reviews - it hit me that - no.. this really is how these are. I didn't just get a bad "set". Going back to bose.. they have an actual noise-cancelling bt for similar price. Bose noice-cancel is phenomenal.

title: Wireless forever
text: Packaging was beautiful, product is a definite upgrade from previous versions. The charging port is accessible without having to move a flimsy rubber piece out of the way, and the materials look and feel great. The best part though is not having to connect your phone with these head phones. Bluetooth connection was easy to use, they connect quickly and sound awesome. When jogging or running they don't tug nor fall out. Sweating doesn't seem to phase them, and they seem to be lightly water resistant, based on a quick jog through a light rain. The worst part are the accessories, or lack of, that come with the powerbeats 3. The case was a terrible feeling rubber material that looks like a Pacman. No zipper making it surprisingly stressful to place the head phones inside, will they fall out, will they stay in, nobody knows. Additionally there was a distinct lack of charger, thanks for the cable, but I'd really like to be able to plug them in from the get go. Overall these are a fantastic buy. The Apple store was selling them for 199.95 and when I looked on Amazon for next day free shipping it was 129. The Apple store associate told me they could price match up to 10 percent, quick math led to not purchase then through the Apple store. Though I did technically purchase then in store with the Amazon app. I doubt I'll ever purchase wired head phones again, though I hope they'll up their accessory game in future iterations.

title: Do NOT buy for workout - died on first use after 15 minutes of running because of sweat
text: My wife bought these for our son because of the current discount on Amazon ($79). It seemed like a great deal on a brand that has a good reputation. I guess there is a reason for the steep discount. The first time my son used them was after charging them to 77% he went for a job with them. After only 15 minutes it disconnected. He tried to reconnect it to his iPhone XR using the Beats both the beats power button as well as the iPhone settings app. He tried many times, using both methods. When he tried using the button, the light would blink red, which means it needs to be charged. When he used the settings app on his iPhone, the phone gave the message "make sure your Beats are charged or in range." The charge went from 77% to presumably 0% (he could not see the charge amount for the Beats on his iPhone because it would not connect) in 15 minutes. My son researched online and found many complaints that this specific model had an issue that sweat caused the battery to lose its charge and not reconnect. It seems to be a widely reported issue with this model and I regret not doing some basic research before purchasing. Despite its advertising stating that this is sweat resistant, it is not resistant enough to withstand 15 minutes of jogging. We will be returning these and will do our due-diligence research on the next earbuds we buy for working out, rather than relying on Brand names.

title: Worth every penny
text: Sure there are better noise cancelling headphones available for a lot more money, but at this price point these headphones are excellent value. If you have a long international flight, or a coast-to-coast flight coming up - do yourself a favor and just buy these. They are great at removing most of the engine and cabin noise from the airplane. This means you don't have to blast the volume in order to hear anything - and you can even turn them on without music playing just so that you can get some sleep on the flight. I prefer that my kids use these on road trips to (vs regular headphones) so that they don't have to play their tablets too loud in order to hear over the road/engine noise. At this price point, they are the best "creature comfort" you can add to flying or even commuting on the bus/train.

title: They really do reduce jet engine noise
text: They really reduce noise on an airplane. I have used them on several flights. To test noise reduction I turned the switch off while listening to music on a flight. The difference was amazing. They fold up to take less space. Sound quality is good. Earpieces are soft and comfy, but there is no padding on the part that goes over the top of your head, which isn’t too comfy on my bald head. Wearing a cap helps. They’re not perfect. The battery cover came off the right headphone once for no reason. It is easy to put back on but I’m concerned about losing it. I have already run down one battery before it’s time by either leaving the switch on, or it got turned on by movement inside a bag. I carry a spare battery. 80-hour battery life doesn’t mean much if I forget to turn it off! I have yet to be on a screaming baby flight (which is really quite rare) since I bought them, but will update the review if that happens.

title: Nothing fancy, but they work
text: I owned a pair of the previous model, which is what prompted me to buy these. I had been researching more expensive noise canceling headphones priced between $100 to $150. However, my research just made me want to splurge on the Bose noise canceling headphones (which are supposed to be the best for noise canceling, not necessarily the best sound). Since I do not have $400 for the boise, I figured I would save the extra hundred dollars on a fancy pair of headphones and just get my old set again. And, I'm glad I did. These headphones are good enough. They're comfortable to wear with glasses since they are on-ear, rather than over the ear. Lastly, they're sold at a great price point. The work well at canceling out monotonous background noise (airplane noise, heavy winds, etc.). You can still hear other noises that are high pitched, but if you're working and in the zone the noises are quite enough to tune out. Overall, I'm glad I didn't buy anything else. I'm very happy with this headphones and they work just as well as the older model (although they don't fold nearly as small as the older model). Would recommend.

title: You get what you pay for
text: Everytime I bumped the cable the sound would go out .

title: it reduces noise so you can listen better. I love it
text: It doesn't block all the noise. However, it reduces noise so you can listen better. I love it !!

title: Great bang for the buck.
text: I needed some headphones to deal with noisy co-workers in an open office environment. This was the ticket. These do have a battery for the noise cancelling portion and if you aren't listening to music you can almost hear some higher pitch white noise but once the music is playing they work fine and you can't notice the noise. The switch also does amp up the music a little bit which isn't a big deal. I used them outside one and had the noise cancel feature turned on but ended up turning it off because the wind noise was the only thing that got louder and very annoying. I'm sure this is common to a noise cancel feature when using them outside.

title: Excellent.
text: Sony MDRZX110NC is fantastic and beyond comparison. Sony MDRZX110NC Noise Cancelling Headphones vs Sony MDR10RNCIP Wired Headphones. Sony MDRZX110NC is a winner.

title: Sony, there is no substitue!
text: I love Sony products and these head phones are another example of the best products out there! These headphones have a booster that enhances the volume. They are loud enough to drown-out my very noisey neighbors!!! Thank you! I will continue to purchase Sony. I bought two of these head phones. I am a very saftisfied customer. I highly recommend Sony, head phones!

title: Solid headphones
text: These are solid headphones for the price. They may start to make your ears sore after longer stretches which is to be expected from on-ear headphones.

title: Better with sound quality than noise reduction
text: Better with sound quality than noise reduction. Am using these in a noisy household but unless I use radio or cd/mp3, I still hear the noise around me even with switch on. Once I activate with sound or music though, they are really good. Would not recommend to block out ambient (airplane cabin for example) noise unless you bring along something else to play.

title: Affordable quality headphones
text: Very pleased with these headphones especially at the price. They look nice and feel like a quality product. Sound quality is great, And noise cancellation is better than I thought it would be.

title: Dampen noise, small muffs
text: These work well. They don't cancel out all of the sound but take out annoying high frequencies, softening and dampening the surrounding noise. Audio quality is good. They are also small enough to fit my tiny head, which has been a struggle with past headphones. The muffs are small, so I wouldn't recommend them if you have large ears. My only complaint is that they don't come with a case.

title: Develops loose wire connections
text: Wires/sheathing started to come out from the plug and the headphones after a couple of months of use.

title: They look good, but sound awful!
text: These things look nice, and are fairly comfortable to wear, however, the sound quality is TERRIBLE! Everything sounds muffled, and it's really weird how these headphones seem to highlight some sounds, while dimming others, making them sound like they're in the background. I tried messing around with my EQ settings as much as I could, and just could not get these things to sound clear. Compared with my Sony MDR-NC7's, these MDRZX110NC's belong in the trash.

title: It's just okay.
text: It's all about perspective. Back in college I would have thought these were the best headphones ever! But now that I have money, of course my standards are a little higher. Bass is good, but at the cost of a not so good treble. The noise canceling is there, but it's faint. Don't expect Bose level of noise canceling here and you shouldn't for the price. I took these with me at a laundromat and it cancelled the low rumblings of the dryers next to me. But you can still here the higher pitch sounds. That being all said, for $30 this are a good throw-around headphones. If they break or you lose them, no biggie. For students who only have Top Ramen budgets, these will be fine. But for me, I think I'm moving on to the Sennheisers.

title: They work well!
text: I bought this for my latest vacation. They were very well at canceling out all of the airplane noise while I watched a movie. They are more comfortable than the previous ear phones that I used. So happy that I bought them!

title: Cheapest price ok. But quality...
text: Sounds good, but quality of the headphone... need better one...

title: Keep looking, these arent the headphones you are looking for
text: More like noise muffling instead of noise canceling. My cheapo corwin ones do much better..

title: Sound Great but not noise cancelling
text: Sold as noise cancelling. They aren’t. I can hear everything unless they are pretty loud. However they sound great!

title: the cable is hardwired into the headphones so if the cable goes bad you can't replace it without somehow splicing it
text: This is a decent procuct for the price. Compared to the more expensive set this has replaced, these fit over the ear and do not surround the ear. Also, the cable is hardwired into the headphones so if the cable goes bad you can't replace it without somehow splicing it. But they do the job fairly well, at least until I decide to spring the money for a top quality product.

title: They don't cancel noise...
text: These headphones are fine if you don't need the noise-cancelling feature, because they only slightly muffle sounds. I'm sorry I spent the $35 on them. They certainly won't be of much value on an airplane.

title: Great Low Price Wired Headset.
text: Not blue-tooth, but wired allows low price for high quality.

title: Poor sound quality, poor noise cancellation
text: I bought these and promptly returned them. The noise cancelling is VERY subtle. I was disappointed in the quality from Sony. The quality of the music reproduction was also very lackluster. They are cheap, poor sounding headphones with not very good noise cancelling.

title: Great on a budget
text: It came with a battery but died after 5 minutes. Put a quality one in there and it hasn't died since I got them months ago. I wouldn't say they're completely nose canceling, it mostly just dulls the noise slightly but it does help me focus in on work. Ear pads are comfortable if not worn for a long period but I suppose that might depend on your ear shape and size as well. These are definitely killer for the price. But at the end of the day they're still budget, lower end headphones. I do love the portability of these and sound quality is good enough for what I use them for which is listening to music while traveling and working. Update: The nose cancelling feature no longer works at all.

title: They're ok, but not true noise cancelling.
text: I have owned very good Sony noise cancelling headphones in the past, but these basically just increase the volume to drown out the background noise when you turn the noise cancelling function on. They do sound good and they are reasonable priced, so I am giving them a 4 star review, but make no mistake they are not high quality noise cancelling headphones.

title: Fine for the price
text: As headphones these are probably up to the low price. But the earpieces are fairly small (on-ear instead of around ear), and the top head piece is hard, making these uncomfortable to wear for a longer period. I added padding to the top. The audio is fine, but not comparable to headphones that fit around (fully enclosing) the ear. They are worth the money as second or occasional headphones.

title: Noise cancellation does not exist
text: These are great sounding and have a good level of volume. The noise cancellation is non existent though. With the battery installed and the headphones turned on, there is no difference in sound. This doesnt bother me as I didnt really need the sound cancelling anyway.

title: ... would rather spend a bit more to get a better one. This headphone is not Noise Cancelling
text: I would rather spend a bit more to get a better one. This headphone is not Noise Cancelling, it just jet up the volume. And the ear cover hurts your ears after putting on your ears more than 30 min. Spend a bit more to get a better one.

title: Worth the money
text: I was looking for good quality headphones with a noise cancelling feature and came across this. I wasn't expecting the quality to be nearly as good as the bose models but I also wasn't willing to pay over $75 for headphones so these seemed feasible. The fit is nice and quality of audio is great but I wouldn't necessarily say that they cancelled out noise when no audio was in play. I could still hear noises around me but to a lesser extent. These are great if you are looking for a cheap alternative to the bose but if you are looking for headphones that truly do cancel noise, these may not be the best. You get what you pay for!

title: You get what you pay for
text: I ordered these based on reviews. They are OK but I wouldn't classify them as noise canceling. Even with the white-noise I hear my co-workers. I wanted to buy headphones that would help me drown out the conversation and unfortunately these don't do the trick. They're fine for listening to music but I think I'll have to pay more for what I'm looking for now.

title: They work for my office.
text: They are perfect for the office. if anyone is actually yelling my name i can still hear them but it blocks out all the conversations in the surrounding offices.

title: Good sound & comfortable
text: I really like these - good noise canceling & they are very comfortable to wear.

title: Well worth the money
text: Wear them at the gym. Can not hear people next to me talking for an hour. Can not hear the loud music over the sound system. Can not hear the guy vacuuming all around me. CAN hear the music from my I-Phone loud and clear!

title: Good while you save for better ones
text: Bought these for airports so I could get some relaxation. Couldn't afford Bose. When not playing any music they cut the air conditioner noise in my hotel room by about half. With the noise reduction off they sound terrible. Which makes me think half of the noise reduction is just the increase in volume and fullness by a booster.

title: Noise cancelling
text: for 1/10th the cost of a BOSE QC. This is an amazing value. It cancels out the white noise. If you are near a loud fan and put on the headphones and turn on the noise cancelling. You will notice a difference.

title: Excellent quality for price point - comfortable and works
text: I just used these on the plane. While the cancelling noise was not that efficient it did work to some degree. The clarity of the sound for watching movies on the plane was great. On the trip to New York I just used the headset for cancelling noise so I could sleep (it helped). On the way back I watched movies and the sound was excellent. The headset was very comfortable. I have already recommended them to family members. Obviously not as good as Headphones that you would pay a lot more for but very good for the money.

title: Pretty good but not $40+ good
text: I bought them for $20 used from an Amazon seller and they're worth $20. They're not very good at noise cancellation but they are good headphones and better than the earbuds I was upgrading from.

title: Saved hundreds of bux
text: For the price, can't go wrong. Tested on riding mower. Cut sound of mower down considerably. Used on flight, could hear voices somewhat, but definitely lessened the sounds of flight. Sound quality average. Saved me hundreds of dollars and works fine. A little uncomfortable but acceptable.

title: Save your money...get the $300 model.
text: Noise-cancelling? They do, somewhat. After trying the Bose models, I can say these don't come close. They do cancel out the 'white' noise from A/C units, nearby quiet conversations and generic transportation noise. For the $36, you get a small taste of what noise-cancelling tech can do. With this model, I will concede that they have GREAT audio drivers and the sound is impeccable. I won't send them back, but I would not recommend these over the $300 models that actually do cancel external audio.

title: only one complaint but important to me
text: Noise cancellation isn't great. That was the main reason I bought these. I do like that its controlled by a switch so it's not on all the time. Thats an awesome feature. Theres just not much of a difference when the switch is on or off. And yes, I did put new and fresh batteries in them. This isn't user error, its just not a great noise cancelling product. The sound quality of the speakers is great though! They are super light weight too! For the price, I give it 3/5. I wish it came with its own case, I had to buy one separately.

title: Not good
text: Didn't like them at all. Sound quality... meh. Noise cancellation... didn't notice any.

title: Great sound!

title: For a Sony they were cheaply made!
text: For the Sony brand, I expected something a little better. they were very cheaply made and they were worse sound quality than my $14 headphones!

title: Great value for the money
text: I lost my first set that were a gift from my hubby. I took a flight and thought no biggie I flew forever without them I'll live. WRONG I ordered a set the second I landed. I'll never fly without them. I found the set I lost almost a year later and now my hubby uses them on the lawnmower to listen to music.

title: Noise cancellation feature requires using a battery
text: Havent gone to the trouble of putting a battery in it. Not exactly what I was looking for but they work well enough. The padding is good except when I fall asleep on them for 8 hours.

title: Sound was ok, but the battery compartment cover kept ...
text: Sound was ok, but the battery compartment cover kept popping off at the slightest touch. I returned them for my money back.

title: Quality for money.
text: Quick easy headphones used for a vacation for both children. They are smaller ears so I did not care for the headphones but they seemed to not mind.

title: Don't want to drop $250 on headphones for airplanes? Buy these!
text: Just purchased a pair of these for watching some movies during a flight. They didn't remove all of the background noise, but they certainly made a big dent. Comfortable to wear, collapsible and easy to use. I did take a spare AAA battery with me, just in case, but I didn't need it with a good 10 hours of watching movies. Though I've never purchased the high end $250+ headphones, I can't imagine that they would be THAT much better. Very happy with my purchase.

title: Nice but tight on the ears
text: Sound is clear. Seem to work fine. Only complaint is they begin to feel tight around the ears after wearing them for a short time. There is no manner in which to adjust to relieve the tightness.

title: Excellent deal - used
text: These are excellent headphones for the "used" price. I would say they're good headphones for the new price. Initially the noise cancelling does not seem that effective, however once you get lost in the music/podcast/video turn off the noise cancelling and you will be stunned at how much background noise is being blocked out. Easy to use, simple on/off switch. Powered by a AAA battery with a long life span so no fumbling with extra chargers. The noise cancelling works well on its own if you just don't want to hear the things around you as well. Sound quality is good with responsive bass and clear highs. They're comfortable for extended wear - for example a 7 hour flight to London. Though the material was warm on my ears causing them to sweat a bit. What would give it 5/5? Built in microphone and a more breathable material on the ear pieces.

title: Good Noise Cancelling, Poor Sound Quality
text: If you are buying these as a grab-and-go headset for Noise Cancellation, they are good. If you are buying them for sound, you will not like them, unless you are not very particular about sound quality. The battery installation can be confusing, but dedicated directions are available on Sony's support site. The cords are hard wired, and come from both cups. Since I don't use these for listening to anything, only for Noise Cancellation, it would be great if you could have a plug instead. Also, the more you use these headphones, the more tangled the cords become.

title: Not good for moving around too much
text: Kind of flimsy pivot connection for folding them up. Not good for moving around too much, they do not stay firm on your head. Noise Cancellation (with battery) use is more of a booster than just NC, the sound is much fuller with NC. You'll want to use NC all the time to get the best sound.

title: Good
text: Used this on airplane to hear entertainment and to block noise so I could sleep. Worked great.

title: Great headphones!
text: I bought this for my partner, but tend to swipe it often because I love it so much. It is foldable/compact without compromising its sturdiness. The padding fits comfortable on your ears and feels pleasant to wear. I live in the heart of a big city and use these when I sit in my stoop and work on my laptop. It eliminates all of the background noise and the sound quality is GREAT!

title: they are good but won't cancel out even the guy talking 2 ...
text: For the price, they are good but won't cancel out even the guy talking 2 cubes away. Turning on the noise-reducing feature definitely helps but they aren't as good as the top line products, naturally. If you read reviews before purchasing like I did, you aren't finding a hidden treasure here

title: Expected better from Sony
text: Flimsy plastic headphones that don't sound that great. Noise cancelling feature is almost non-existent. It removes less than half of ambient noise despite it's claims of 95% - and that is due to the passive noise isolation from the foam earmuffs. You can detect a hint of noise removal on the right side because that is where the battery operated component is. Since the ANC unit is not centrally located on the wire before it splits to left/right sides, your left side does not benefit and you can still hear background noise in your left ear.

title: Stick with Bose
text: Nope! Tried these for the kids to wear on road trips while watching movies. No real noise reduction. Should have sticked with Bose!

title: Great for the price

title: Great for Studying
text: I got these headphones so I wouldn't hear my family when doing homework. For the price, these headphones are AMAZING. The only thing I don't like about them is that even when the volume is fairly low those around you can hear your music.

title: Pretty good for the price

title: Works great

title: Great for airplanes

title: Don't buy, READ this first!
text: Don't buy it if you want noise cancelling feature. I used it on a plane and it was absolutely worthless. I would say approx 2/10 feature in noise cancelling. Even one side of the speakers has stopped working, i barely use the product. It'll go in the junk. I bought the Sony mdr1000x from bestbuy on discount, for $299, usually $350. Those are real noise cancellers and I should've gone with them at first. Compared then to Bose qc35 and found the Sony relatively better. I don't know the nitty gritty specs if the audios, just my simple opinion.

title: Five Stars
text: Daughter loves them for studying ,cuts out distracting noise !

title: Good for price, but not as good as I hoped
text: I ordered these on a co-workers recommendation, but they may go back. Though comfortable for my couple hour long testing, the sound quality doesn't cut it for me. With power off the sound is dull & flat. Turning on power boosts the volume & adds a little clarity to the sound. I compared power on & off in various levels of constant background noise from a running fridge to a loud bathroom exhaust fan. With or without music playing the noise reduction was minimal. I don't expect them to match high end/priced models, but these don't cut down enough steady sound to stay in my bag of headphones. I hate to spend the money, but the $350 Sony phones did wonders to almost all the background noise in Best Buy... If only there were a middle ground for $100 to $200. Update 2018.04.27: I've used these at work for a few days now. I rotate skiing these, old Bose, and new Mpow 059 phones. The 10 year old Bose sound better than the others, but let in too much external noise. We have a wire noise system at work that these Sony phones can't overcome. They got a bit uncomfortable after 6 hours or so. Still good sound for price though a pad where they sit on top of the head would be a nice addition. Update 2018.04.30: The most maddening thing about these that I somehow neglected to point out is that the battery cover falls (fell) off almost daily and today I didn't notice and lost it somewhere. Now what?! Wish I returned them while I had all the parts.

title: Very good headphones for flying
text: Got these as an upgrade to the same headphones, but they are five years newer and markedly improved. Very good headphones for flying.

title: No noise cancellation
text: They work and by that I mean you can hear music through them. But they don't block out conversations at all. The only noticeable difference when turning on the noise cancellation is that the sound from my music got better. They're 30 bucks, didn't expect much but thought they would be better than this.

title: Fit well, but noise cancelling not great
text: These fit well but after a few hours they will start to feel like they are clamping down on your head. Because they don't fit over your ear, the noise cancelling feature doesn't do a great job. When you turn it on it just sounds like the audio gets much richer, but doesn't help a great deal with surrounding sounds.

title: Great for the price point
text: I got these as an open box discount and paid 22 dollars shipped. With that said, these are just what I was looking for. Pros: *didn't pay much. Even new they were budget friendly *name brand confidence *noise cancellation works well *folds flat for transport or storage *ear pads are durable and comfortable Cons: *Ear pads are pretty small in diameter. They don't fit around my ears or even come close, and I have fairly small ears. Consequently, I wonder how much sound is escaping, reducing the noise quality *runs through batteries quickly. The first battery lasted for about 5-6 hours of use. I don't remember replacing the batteries in my last pair for months at a time. Overall, I certainly can't complain for the price. 300 dollar Bose or Beats headphones just seem ridiculous to me. These cost me two 6-packs of craft beer.

title: Great for kids going to school on Zoom
text: Comfortable, good price, good value for a good brand. Pretty entry level but perfect for a 13-year-old going to school on Zoom everyday.

title: Product Lives Up to Sony reputation
text: These headphones are of nice quality and live up to their Sony reputation. They are collapsible and portable and lightweight for transporting.

title: A great headphone for the money
text: A great headphone for the money. I rely on these at work to keep out the background noise and better concentrate on the project at hand. I recommend these for an inexpensive solution and the sound is exceptional, they get the job done at an affordable solution. And they look nice too. The only thing is the batteries run out pretty quick but for me they really don't make that much of difference so I don't use the batteries. If your hearing is a little more sensitive than mine, you might need to use the batteries. over all very satisfied and I recommend these to anyone.

title: You are getting what you pay for

title: perfect bang on your ear, for your bug

title: Decent headphones

I feel like noise cancellation just makes them louder, can't really comment on that aspect. With that said, I prefer over the ear rather than on the ear. Comfortable for the most part, good clean sound and dont feel fatigued after an hour or two of use.

title: Comfortable, decent sound cancelling.
text: I got these because I live with my sister in law who works from home, (as many of us do) and she has a rather... enthusiastic and unique retail voice. I'm a writer/editor, and it's rather hard to concentrate with her voice in the background, so I gave these a try for price and rating. They're comfortable, and I was able to wear them all day without issue, which is important- I have chronic migraines so I worried they be an irritant. Not the case! Lightweight and comfortable! The sound quality is good- no thumping bass or ridiculously over the top quality from more expensive sets, but good quality for the price, and I'm content with them. The sound cancelling is not 100%, but it does help tune out my sister in law's unnatural, saccharine retail voice enough that when I'm listening to music, it's a non-issue, and that in of itself is a form of migraine prevention. Definitely a good purchase for the price!

title: Replacement
text: My son bought me a pair for Christmas that I mistakenly left on the airplane. I loved them so much I had to replace them. Would be lost taking a flight without them!

title: Sony fail.
text: These were cheap and they’re Sony so I expected value. For the most part, value is there BUT the design of this unit is stupid. Every time I take them off and set them on my desk, the battery cover pops off. The battery cover release is part of the hinge. Any light bump releases the battery door. So you can’t even set this thing down without the cover popping off. Very frustrating and poorly designed.

title: The noise canceling does virtually nothing
text: This product requires batteries in the headset itself, and has a power switch. As far as I can tell, the noise canceling did little did nothing. Either quality control is slacking and I got a defective unit, or the noise canceling in this product does almost nothing. Either way, I cannot recommend this product.

title: So so

title: Good Bargain Headphones

I have trouble remembering to turn them off so every time I use them I have to put in new batteries if I need the noise cancelling. The work very well as regular headphones too. I feel like the ear piece needs to be slightly bigger to make them truly comfortable. But for the price, they are a great bargain.

title: Meh. Cheap. Tired of stuff being lousy.

title: Overall good and affordable but with some fairly big flaws

The controls are terrible. You control them by simply pressing your finger on them, with no immediate physical or auditory feedback on whether or not it registered the touch. Turning them on/off requires touching and holding them for like 5 seconds and many times I have to release and press again for whatever reason, this is pretty annoying. Also, getting them to properly sit in the charger so they will charge is a huge hassle. I often need to shut the case or even knock on it several times for both red lights to show that it is actively charging. Another peeve I have is the low battery notification, it will tell you "low battery please charge", except it practically SCREAMS it into your ear. It may be possible to turn this lower by using the volume controls on the ear buds themselves, so this may be a fixable issue I haven't tried that yet. All being said, I would recommend them.

title: Nice earbuds but I decided swapped them out for Bose QuietComfort earbuds
text: I went on the search for a set of ear buds that would stay in my ears better than my Airpod Pros but with the same level of Noise cancellation. It seemed like the Sony WF-1000XM4 and Bose Quietcomfort earbuds were the top picks in this space. After a lot of research i went with the Sony earbuds. Besides their sound and level of ANC. i liked the fact the Sony earbuds still had a lot of playback control available from the earbuds and you can use either earbud individually. I also felt like the fact that they sit in your ear canal rather than on the outside would contribute to the noise cancellation. The earbuds felt and sound good and the accompanying app was nice but the case had a cheap, almost cardboard feel. My main issues were, although the earbuds never actually fell out of my ear, I think their top-heavy design made them feel like they were always about to fall out. The bigger issue i had, which won't apply to everyone, is how much effort went into getting them to sit correctly in my ear. Even with twisting, and pushing, I could never get the right earbud to fit securely in my ear like the left one did. After a day of wearing the Sonys i decided to pick up a pair of Bose Quietcomfort ear buds as i already had a pair of Quietcomfort 35 over the ears that i loved, i figured I'd give Bose another shot. As soon as i opened the Bose, I immediately fell in love. Besides the unboxing and charging case feeling more premium, the earbuds went into my ear effortlessly and securely. I wore them the first day and they stayed in place all day and sounded great. Although the Sony WF-1000XM4 is a great set of earbuds, The Bose earbuds have the same functionality, sound and ANC but are designed in a way to comfortably fit a wider array of ear shapes and at a cheaper price. The Sonys are going back and the Bose are going to be my new day-to-day earbuds.

title: Love these! DETAILED feature review.

The noise cancellation and sound are both above average though. I like the charging light on the container. It communicates with color and flashes what the status of the product is, and isn't bright or hard to locate. USB-C charging makes the base station charge up nice and fast. It holds the earbuds securely, and doesn't rattle or fall open. It's also a nice pocketable size and shape with no sharp corners, making the whole product especially portable. Controls are gesture, rather than button. I'm not a fan of this because I end up doing a lot of swiping and hoping. A click button interface, I can just click it the number of times I know will do what I need, and move on. I've got a few Sony audio products that I use every day and am very happy with, but with earbuds, I'm sticking with jabra for now. It's a competitive market right now for earbuds.
