title: Better than they were, but not there yet
text: These are great upgrades to previous generations. I've been using true wireless earbuds since they were just a kickstarter thing. And they were AWFUL back then. These are great in most areas! The sound quality is definitely better than my Galaxy Buds+ were. The noise cancellation is relatively good. Top notch for current generation true wireless earbuds, but still not nearly as good as Bose over-ear headphones of yesteryear. There's no multi-point bluetooth connection, but it's pretty easy to switch them across devices (they don't have to go through the whole re-pairing process for devices that it's been used with before), just a couple clicks in the bluetooth menu of your computer/phone each time to switch. I enjoy them for Teams calls on my laptop and everything under the sun on my phone. My complaints are as follows: -They hurt my ears fit-wise. They're just not perfectly comfortable for me. There's just plastic pushing in the wrong place somewhere. It's not bad enough for me to return them, but it's not a perfect fit for everyone yet. -It's tricky to get the noise cancellation to work well. They have to be cranked into your ear at just the right angle to get maximum cancellation. Twisted a bit to the side, the cancellation is minimal. -Pass-through noise is ALWAYS on for phone calls (at least for iOS). I even reached out to customer service for the device, and they just gave me the run-around. If you're listening to music at a comfortable low volume with noise cancellation on outdoors, and you answer a phone call, suddenly it will switch to pass-through mode with the microphones AMPLIFYING external noise, which you have to talk over and listen to the other person over. I find it highly annoying, but, again, not a dealbreaker. For $300, I think they're top of the line for the generation, but still not worth the money. Worth the money more than those old kickstarter generations, but still not there yet. I'd recommend getting a previous generation galaxy buds of some sort and upgrade more regularly in order to get a better bang for your buck. You'll likely get the better features of tomorrow at a better price point. If you want the best of today, though, you're here.

title: Sony vs. Airpods
text: I'm not an audiophile, but I was looking for great sound, noise cancellation, and fit. I got the Airpods first, but was a little disappointed with the sound quality so I got the Sony's since I love the sound on my WH-1000XM4 headphones. Sound-I bought the Sony's (WF-1000XM4) second for one main reason, SOUND! I have the Sony WH-1000XM4 headphones which are amazing. The Sony earbuds sound very close to the headphones. The Airpods didn't quite have the same sound although they sound great. I was actually surprised that the Airpods sounded very close to a pair of Mpow M30 earbuds that I got in 2020 for $30. The Sony's seem a bit louder with richer sound. Also, the Sony buds have the ability to change the sound profile using the equalizer app. The Airpods rank second to Sony in my opinion. Noise cancellation- Both Sony and Airpods do an amazing job, but I think the Airpods beat out the Sony but a hair. The noise cancellation does not disappoint on either one. Fit- The Airpods are way more comfortable for my small ears. The Sony feel big and like they are going to pop out. I find both comfortable, but the Airpods feel more natural in my ears. The Sony's take a little getting use to. Controls- I prefer the Sony controls. The Airpod controls still feel a little awkward to me. Matter of preference. Voice/Calls- LOVE the Airpods!!! I haven't tried the Sony's on calls yet simply because I automatically go for my Airpods. They connect quicker. The calls are clean like the person is in the room with you. Battery Life- Airpods lasted a bit longer. Overall, if you mainly make calls or workout, I would go with the Airpods. If you are looking more for music listening, then the Sony's are way better. Noise cancellation...either one, but because of the better fit of the Airpods on small ears, I would default to the Airpods...although the Sony headphones beat out both. If you can afford both, then I'd say go for it!

title: DO NOT BUY! Horrible distortion
text: There is a lot to like about these buds. Sadly they have an extremely bad flaw which is not getting enough attention by Sony. They have horrible "tinny" or "metallic" echo, commonly heard in the higher vocal range. This is most noticeable on calls, and podcasts. It's impossible to ignore. Amazon will not allow me to post a link, but you can search around and find people complaining, there is a good thread on their forum. Search for "Sony WF-1000XM4 metallic echo". This happens on ANC and. non-ANC modes. Using "hear through" does make it less noticeable. By the time I noticed this, the return window was closed (didn't use them much for the first month). I have since returned two units to Sony for repair. The second set was even worse than the first, which leads me to think it might be a manufacture defect, rather than a design issue. I will update the review if this gets resolved. Meanwhile, stay away from these! The good: - comfortable for IMEs - excellent battery life - when distortion is not present (see above), reasonable sound quality - good ANC - a snowballs chance of replacing the battery in a year so they are not just e-waste - decent app The bad: - distortion (see above) - capacitive touch controls are a bit annoying; prefer the tactile versions on some other deigns - app has some gimmicks that are not that useful

title: These would be great if they had ear hooks to secure them in place
text: Use Case: Needed a pair of noise cancelling headphones/earbuds to block out loud annoying techno music at the gym. I ordered the over the ear version of these originally for maximum noise cancellation, but they would fall off when I would lay on a bench and they were really hot when training hard, my ears would sweat. So then I tried these ear buds. These ear buds were not quite as good at noise cancelling as the over the hear ones, but I just had to turn my music up slightly more to accommodate that, but still at a very acceptable listening level. Liked the noise cancellation Sound quality was fantastic Liked the app, had a nice setting that auto turns off the noise cancelling when you talk. Liked how the case had a battery in it, so when you put the buds back in the case they continue to charge. However, these earbuds don't work if you train hard. I had never used ear buds before without some sort of an ear hook and these, which don't have that, didn't secure well on the ear. Had to keep re-setting them in my ear every few sets. Never realized this before, and this sounds funny, but if grit your teeth during a hard set, that makes your ears move slightly. And all it takes is a small movement and the buds lose their seal and start to wiggle loose. I just got in the Bose Quiet Comfort, which are the only noise cancelling earbuds I could find, doing more googling, that had some sort of an earhook on them. It's a small hook that goes inside your ear, but is significantly more secure. And because of that, the noise cancelling was even better because of the secure fit. If Sony could produce this same earbud with some sort of ear hook, I'd give it 5 stars. But because they functionally didn't work well, just give them 3.

Sony has outdone itself on this iteration. Waiting on the XM5's now!

title: Blah, disappointing
text: I bought these to try out as a replacement for the Galaxy Buds Pro. I tried these one and they fit fine. They are comfy with no issue of staying in during workouts or walking, running, etc. The app itself is loaded with features that are mostly useless and do not work. The Google or Alexa AI would be great, if it worked. The 360 audio wants to to subscribe to a service for it but does not work when playing a native 360 audio mp3 file. Also, the sound is sub par and mono. There is no rich bass or bass sound. The bass is mid range and not deep. I lacks the punch in sound that it should have for that price point. Also, the noise canceling is fair, but not as good as other earbuds and not worth it. Even with it on, I can still have a conversation, even though ambient sounds were off. I would not purchase any of these ear buds.

title: Quality not great
text: I wanted these to be awesome. I'm on my 2rd pair and the first pair wouldn't keep connection in case so they would activate Bluetooth when they were in pocket out of nowhere. 2nd pair sounds horrible at work in loud warehouse. Girlfriend says it sounds awful and better with just phone. I'm so disappointed. Listening in bed the sound is great. Bass kicks.. Volume is extreme.. Sounds like movies should.. I'm no audiophile or expert. I got them for phone calls too and I don't know what to replace them with because these are supposed to be good for calls.

title: Like a 4x4 in the ear; good sound, scant documentation
text: Would not buy again. Good sound but very awkward fit. Documentation severely lacking in detail. No plain list of what does what.

title: I prefer apple AirPods than this
text: I did not like the setup of this song since I’m using an iPhone. The integration isn’t the best but is good enough. I hate the memory foam ear plugs, I use it for a few hours and then get so tired of it expanding in my ear. I don’t recommend this.

title: Great set of earbuds
text: I wanted to purchase a good set of wireless earbuds for a long time and decided to go for these. I did a lot of research and thought these would be the best fit for my use. They are pretty darn good. Sound quality is great as is the noise cancelling. Once I dialed in the equalizer, they sounded great. The noise cancelling really cuts down the high frequencies and the pass through works well. It is kind of fiddly to get in the ears sometimes and I have a tendency to touch the sensors while doing said filling, but it is what it is. Not to big of a deal. The only downside is the stock tips would start to hurt after about an hour. I ended up purchasing some Comply replacements and it made a world of difference. I can pretty much wear them for as long as I won't with no discomfort, at all. Recommend these, for sure. Great earbuds.

title: sony's new ear buds
text: I ended up returning these earbuds. I had a lot of trouble getting the left earbud in my ear even with the smallest tip. Because of that it was hard to get a good seal to test the noise cancellation. It seemed very good but not as good as my Sony WH 1000xm2 headphones. The audio sound was better than my sony headphones. Overall I just couldn't justify having to force them in my ear to get the proper seal

title: BEST WIFI EARBUDS
text: They say third time is a charm....and it sure is with this pair of Kurdene WIFI earbuds.....I had just about given up to the idea of owing a pair of WI FI earbuds. I tried twice and both times was a very negative experience. The major issue I had with the previous two brands was that it was very difficult to keep a connection...and in one brand one of the earbuds stopped playing period....so I had pretty much given up to the idea of owing WIFI earbuds and kept using the wiring type....So...tired of being tangled by the wired earbuds...I decided to give Kurdene a try and glad I did.....They are super simple to connect and no worry about turning them off....just remove them from your ears and place them back into the small charging box they come with..and they will turn off automatically.....I am not an expert in sound..but both music and speech come out very clearly with a nice bass sound to it.......One more thing I need to share with you and this is no fault of the Kurdene's earbuds....I downloaded them on both my Samsung Galaxy Tablet and my Samsung Phone...they both work perfectly...BUT...YOU MUST MAKE SURE to turn off the bluetooth in one of the two devices in order to listen to audio, or they must be more than 50ft apart......I was puzzled at first why I was not able to download my Kurdene earbuds on the Tablet...it would not connect to the Bluetooth. Then I found out I had to turn the Bluetooth off on the phone first in order for the Kurdene earbuds to download on the Tablet.....Problem solved...and you are welcome.......I hope they will work fine for you as they are for me. So make sure both devices the tablet and the phone are not close by when downloading the earbuds to either, if so..then turn off the Bluetooth on the device you will not be using...

title: $250+ for non replaceable battery earbuds???
text: People need to wake up. These have internal batterys. When they no longer hold cgarge (a yr, maybe less!) these are throw aways. Buy some wired headphones if your spending high dollar. Or at least a wired/bluetooth set so you can still use them when the battery dies. If you want earbuds, buy good budget ones under $50 so you dont have to feel bad tossing them in the trash when the battery dies.

title: The headphones are the king, which probably makes these the queen
text: Short and blunt, the XM3 headphones were easily the most recommended headphones in my office a couple years back. I loved them, absolutely fantastic on every front. These WF-XM4s are literally everything I like about my phones in a smaller size. Noise cancellation is basically the key factor in these, they cut out so much sound. In my living room I set the cancellation to max and I can't even hear my AC anymore. Mix that in with great sound quality and these effectively became my golden travel earbuds. I especially take them to the gym every day to blot out the sounds while I work out.

title: Revolutionized my desk life
text: Since covid started I've been one of few who has stayed in the office the entire time. However many people are coming back to the office now and it has led to a lot of noise particularly as they continue to take meetings at their desks online. The noise canceling on this headset has made it so I can do work again! Not only that the sound quality of anything I am actually listening to is wonderful very crisp and pleasant. I will absolutely continue to use these and would buy another pair of these died.

title: Vast improvement over the WF-1000XM3
text: I had the WF-1000XM3 and constantly had problems with it. The touchpads would not always work, it kept shutting off, etc. etc. I sent them in twice and finally they just refunded my money, The new model, WF-1000XM4 work great. The touchpad works every time. The wind reduction is not as good as on the prior model, but they fit better. The only reason I gave them 4 stars was the ridiculous price, which is $100 more than the prior model.

title: Don't waste your money....
text: I'm so disappointed with these. I expect far more from Sony. The noise canceling is solid...best I've experienced with ear buds. But after that, nothing but sadness. The buds are heavy, fall out routinely (just while talking, definitely if eating), the voice cancel seems good until you hum or sing with your song, then it cuts the music off...so useless. The quality of calls are AWFUL! My wife could hear people 15 feet away from me but could barely make out anything I was saying. Background noise in general was atrocious, regardless of the setting. The music sounds ok, but not spectacular (which for the price, I'd expect). Overall, really disappointed, can't recommend, and can't imagine how Sony will recover from this crap of an expensive ear weight.

title: Doesn't connect to Amazon Fire tablet
text: These are good, but will not connect to my Amazon Fire tablet, which is the main thing I wanted them for

title: Awesome!
text: First...Sound Quality is fantastic. I'm a Bass head. Once you set your EQ settings, and there are a few. You can really customize this the way you want. I am blown away by this system. Sony has nailed it!! For this to be totally wireless is awesome. Noise cancellation is outstanding!!! Nobody is going to satisfy everyone with battery life but, I'm super happy with what Sony has done here. Outstanding job!!!!

title: They don’t stay in your ear
text: I’ve tried multiple tips - followed instructions on how to perfectly insert them into your ears, but no matter what I do, these IEMs always pop out of my ear, especially when wearing a mask. Sound quality wise, these are solid compared to other Bluetooth wireless IEMs… but the fact that I can’t get these damn things to stay in my ear makes them hard to recommend for the use cases where I’d imagine these would be best for. There’s been multiple times where I’m walking down the street and they just pop off. Hate to say it, but the AirPods Pro are better simply because they actually stay in your ear… for the most part….

title: Awesome headphones but..
text: Great sound and ANC but the huge issue is the fit , if you dont have a great fit than you won't experience the best sound and ANC , moving the earbuds over and over till you find the perfect fit does get annoying.

title: Don't think about. These are the real deal.
text: Amazing. All around great ear buds. No negatives I have noticed. Buy with ko worry. Look at my photo for a comparison to a quarter to gauge the real size of these awesome little things.

title: Love!
text: Researched, researched and then did it again. First time moving to wireless and wanted something dependable and quality. Hands down best choice. Not a fan of some of there software like tracking but it all can be declined and turned off. Wish the carry case was textured, already had a few drops but quality is great and hold up to waist level drops both earbuds and case to hardwood floors. Love the sound and calls video conferencing are superb.

title: Confused as to good reviews
text: I'm a little stumped as so many people, as well as Consumer Reports, said these were the best noise cancelling ear buds. I tried Apple AirPods Pro before this and wasn't too impressed, so I chose what were supposed to be the best. Huh? Sound quality is thin and tinny. Noise cancelling is non-existent. The little voice tells me noise cancelling is on yet I hear no difference between on and off. It also does not seem to work well with iPhone. If there's more to setting this up than I know, I tried to find any and all instructions and couldn't. Printed instructions had links to online tutorials, most of which were unhelpful and non user friendly at all. Bottom line, as a fairly educated person, I could not figure out how to make these work. And the sound was simply bad. Am utterly confused about good reviews.

title: The best noise cancelling
text: These have become my go to headphones. The fit is comfortable. They will not fall out of your ears. Highly recommended

title: This bud fit my ears well. BUT the ear tips do not last long.
text: The sound quality is fine. I wish it had more bass. I have customised it and yet I am not satisfied. The noise cancellation is awesome. I wouldn't wear this to jog on the road. You wouldn't hear any car that blares it horn for u. The ear tips tore and wore off so fast especially the left ear tip. The battery of the least ear tip goes down very fast too.

title: I Hate these garbage headphones
text: Can only use both buds, or the right bud only, the left one alone wont connect to the phone or computer. seems like a basic function. Also can't change volume via gestures, for some reason your phone volume is separate from earbuds. Also why are there so many unnecessary notifications? Also nearly impossible to use the touch gestures without just pausing every time. Seems to not work at all with google assistant or it doesn't detect anything. Also the charging case is terrible. Half the time it isn't even charging because they designed it so poorly

title: Excellent sound quality
text: I love these earbuds, however I took off 1 star because they were useless until I found some longer ear tips. Before that, the earbuds fell out of my ears all the time. The other star came off because the charging pod is so small that it is really hard to fit my longer ear tips in it. As far as I can tell, no one makes longer ear tips for this Sony model because they would not fit nice and neat in the charging pod. Some people just take off the longer ear tips during charging, but for an older person with reduced manual dexterity and arthritis, that is just impossible. I got the Comply ear tips B00RRD7XJE. I get someone to help me manhandle them on the posts of the earbuds. They are a kind of foam that can be crushed but then they expand afterwards. I push the earbuds with these tips on them into the charging pod and either clamp it or velcro it shut. Then another problem I have with these earbuds and charging pod comes into play. My poor old arthritic hands have a hard time prying the earbuds out of the charging pod with or without the long tips because the magnets are so strong. All this trouble is still worth it to use the earbuds because the sound it so clear and now they seldom fall out of my ears.

title: No title
text: These are pretty good earbuds. Tips need to be replaced with better ones. The sound is good for Bluetooth earbuds.

title: Metallic Echo with noise canceling turned on.
text: Music and audio books sound great. Noise cancellation for the wearer of the device is good. That being said, call quality is ok until you turn on noise cancellation. With noise cancelling turned on, metallic echo is present and sounds horrible. I have heard this sound in several units, so not isolated to just one set. Also googled it, and seems like a common problem.

title: Excellent True Wireless earbuds
text: I came from Sennheiser Momentum True wireless gen 1's, I really liked the sound quality of those but battery issues were annoying. These sound great and do just about everything right. They're more comfortable than the Sennheiser's, and the controls are appropriately responsive. Really happy with these.

title: high quality
text: high quality but did not fit my ears...I have weird ear canals so not the fault of Sony

title: The one you can sleep with - when the batteries last
text: UPDATE 1 year later. It seems that we are a lot; first the case was blinking red, charging bad or not charging at all. Now they charge sometimes but 100% last 1 hour (8 hours when it was new). The case is empty after 1 false charge, even on the ac, it is not charging well. So i ve bought a replacement battery for the case and finally found the button li-ion for the ears from china.. When i'll have everything, i'll tear everyhting down and change those damn batteries. I'm very upset for the price/lasting ratio. Those are my expensiviest earbud i have ever bought. From what i found on the net it is a recuring problem. BEFORE You may already know that the sound is excellent very detailed, surrounding, and everything. You also know that the battery last is long, the case is small, the buds are so light you barely feel them. The foam tips are peculiar, still you can order regular silicon tips. But for me after 1 week I'm really used to it. And it is part of the noise cancellation trick. With foam and the buds off, it is already so silent. What you may not find is if you can sleep with it - of you are like myself used to fall asleep with music. The answer is yes - and maybe not. Sure everything depends on your anatomy. I fall asleep with it nearly everyday and it is really okay, the ball shape cover the lobe of the ear so in between the pillow it pushes on the entire surface of the inner ear. Sure it not recommended, but for me it is really okay. Still better was my triple more earphone and the best is nothing..

title: Left side does not hold charge total garbage after warranty is done.
text: So without a doubt these are/ where excellent earbuds, everything everyone says about them is/was true, but after a year of owning these the left side will not hold a charge I might get 30 minutes if I'm lucky an hour sometimes less than 15 minutes. So honestly I'm disappointed in these because when you buy a premium product like this you expect it to last. Update left earbud goes for 100% to 0% in minutes now total garbage. Ended up buying Bose QC, hopefully they will last much longer.

title: These are great. Wish I could turn them up louder!
text: Wish I could turn the volume up louder as I do like the volume to be up a bit more. Do I need the extra volume? No, but would be nice. The noise canceling is fantastic and I love that you can talk to people without take it the buds out. I did have a hard time pairing them initially, however once they were paired they have not had any issues. The battery life is great and so far they are holding up well.

title: amazing earbuds
text: I have an iPhone and had the airpods but they really bothered my ears. I liked the design of the airpods better BUT these sony ones are AMAZING. they may be a bit larger and clunkier but they are a solid product and I'm very pleased with them

title: Good, but is it $270 good?
text: I bought these a couple months ago to replace my powerbeats pro, and while the sound quality is slightly better, they don't work well with my watch. I'm not sure if it's Samsung's fault or Sony's, but listening to any music through my Samsung Active 2 is incredibly quiet with these earbuds, and they were not with the PBP. So now I've had to take my phone with me to listen to music, which kind of defeats the entire purpose of having an LTE watch. Will probably get a new watch and see if that fixes the issue (or see if an firmware upgrade fixes it soon). As far as quality via the phone or anything else I pair these with? Very nice. Once again, the earbuds could be louder, but they are rather balanced. The tech on these things is unbeatable. The noise cancelling is rather impressive, but if you're jogging, remember to turn ambient noise or noise cancelling off or you will just hear every footstep in your ears. I'm not sure if the quality is worth the price though, because they aren't that different in sound from the Powerbeats Pro. Perhaps a bit more balanced and clear, but not by much. Bass could be heavier.

title: Excellent in all respects
text: I have tried many high-end ear buds and these take the cake! Superb sound, with deep base, clear mid tones and highs. Nice and compact. Great feel in the ear and in the hand. Touch functions work very well. They feel so much smaller than the earlier XM3 and they are more comfortable. I have only had them for a day, but they are my new favorite. So long Bose, Sennheiser, etc.

title: Wish they came with silicone tips
text: I have used these and the Sennheiser Momentum 2 wireless buds. As far as sound quality between these two, they are very similar - both very good. I probably prefer the Sennheisers a bit better. However, there is no comparison between the ANC of the two. The ANC on the Sonys is amazing - it works extremely well. I almost can’t tell any difference between the sound isolation and ANC modes on the Sennheisers. Both headphones have ambient pass-through modes that work really well. I do really wish the Sonys had silicone ear tips though. The foam feels a bit rough to my ears, and after several months of use, the foam is starting to get a bit icky.

title: Nice in-ear noise canceling earbuds
text: Worth every penny. Sound great. Great battery life. Easy to set up and use (on Android and my Peloton). App has a lot of great features and controls. The voice detect work pretty good, no more popping buds out of my ear to chat with someone. Noise canceling is good. The wind canceling could be a bit better, this is where the over the ears Bose do a better job. Fit well in my ears. Nothing to complain about. UPDATE - I bumped this down to 4 stars because the rubber/foam on the buds that secure this in the ear have already started to fall apart. I am not wearing these every day. The Shure buds I replaced lasted for many months before I needed to buy rubber/foam.

title: So far, very good, if not excellent (Updates)
text: Firstly, I've only had these a short time so I will very likely update this review over time. I don't have a lot of comparison earbuds but initial impressions are very good, but I wouldn't say outstanding. The sound quality is very good with many customization options in the app -- some of which I'll never need. Build quality is also very good and the foam tips give excellent fit. Noise canceling is -- you guessed it -- very good, but not as magical as some claim. All other aspects: connection, battery life, comfort, portability, etc. are similarly what you want in quality earbuds. I'm still happy with the purchase, but as of now, they seem a little over-priced for very good earbuds. BTW, I purchased the "silver" model and the color is really beige. Not a bad color, just not silver. UPDATE 1: Unfortunately, after less than a week, I'm going to have to return these as the right earbud discharges over 20 percentage points faster than the left. After a few hours, the left bud is at 53%,the right is at 32%. I'm going to try a replacement pair once and hope it's just bad luck. Lowering rating to 2 stars. UPDATE 2: Here is the solution for low battery life in the R earbud: Don't use most of the features! I did get a quick response from Sony support and they said this happens if you use wind noise reduction, voice assistant, speak to chat, adaptive sound, quality over connection priority, EQ, etc. Since these are features I paid for, I had them enabled. When I disabled most of them, battery drain was indeed much lower and balanced between L&R. So, if you want the extra features listed above and are willing to have MUCH shorter battery life, I say get these. If you only want great sound, you can likely get very close to these for a lot less money. Bottom line, these sound wonderful, but are over-priced if you just want great sound. Back to 4 stars.

title: Using on my Harley
text: I using these on my 2015 Heritage with a Half helmet and a windshield that is way lower than my eye level. Getting plenty of wind and noise. I must say that I’m pleasantly impressed with these earbuds. I’ve tried many but I always had to put the volume quite loud, not with these ones; around 50-60% riding at 100 Km/h (60 Mph). Don’t expect miracles but with the ANC and Wind suppression on, they are the best by far. Airpod pro are horribles on the bike. For people on budget (who owns a Harley and are on a budget?!?), try the TOZO-T6 and ComplyFoam ear tips, simply amazing.

title: I hate them.
text: The seller was great. They arrived faster than expected. These things are huge. though. They don't stay in and they look ridiculous. They're really heavy. I wanted something smaller and subtler. I ended up buying the Soundcore Space a40s. I love them and they fit very similarly to the Galaxy Buds +. These went back immediately. Customer service was excellent. I had no problem with the company. I just didn't like the earbuds.

title: 4.5 definelty growing on me.
text: Overall these headphones are Amazing, as cam be expected from Sony products. I'll start with cons and then the pros... Cons*: These take a few minutes for me to feel like they are secure, it took a whole to get a feel for them. They sometimes feel a little big, but you get used to it. Even I shake my head aggressively I hear something moving, but normal wear and treadmill running were great. As you can see they aren't dealbreakers for me, just not perfect. Pros: the sound can get loud if you want loud music, I can only listen to them to about 70% volume before I feel they are too loud. Base is punchy in a good way. Battery life is great. Touch sensors work very well for me, although not always 100% of time. The best thing I can't really explain a reason for is that my ears don't feel like they sweat, I think it may be the foam earbud inserts.

title: Great except...
text: The pros. These are fantastic. Really they are probably the greatest earbuds available. Noise cancellation is top of the line for ear buds, the sound quality is great and improved by the equalizer function allowing you to have two custom settings. The design is great and I haven't charged the case in a week with about 2 hours of usage each day. But... The reasons why they are only 4 stars. The cons. After about an hour I get what I'm calling ear fatigue. My ear canals start to hurt from the hard tips that enable the seal for the noise cancellation. Secondly, the case is extremely slippery. I have dropped it 4 times in the week I've had these buds. While I have been extremely cautious about where I take them out of my pocket or even open them they sometimes go flying out of my hand just from the force of opening the case which scatters the earbuds across the floor. I feel like every time I open the case I risk losing an earbud.

title: Incredible
text: Truly remarkable earbuds. I was kind of expecting a lot when I got these. Not only for the price but also because of all the hype, and I have to say, they exceeded my expectations. Fit: I know others have had issues with fit, and apparently I must have larger ears because they fit me great. In fact the roundness of the inner and outer surfaces made these more comfortable for me than my Galaxy Buds+. If I had to ding them on fit it would just be that they are heavier than my other earbuds, though it hasn't bothered me through extensive (hours-long) wear. Sound: INCREDIBLE! I have the Soundcore Q30's and the Sony M4's and I got Beats for my daughter as well as a few other buds, I have to say the ANC rivals anything on full-sized headphones. The sound is dynamic and rich, and much much more spacious than my Buds+. The Buds+ sound fantastic, but the sound comes from inside your head. With these Sony's the sound isn't spacious when compared to actual speaker, not by a LONGSHOT, but I do have some sense of space that I've gotta say, I've never experienced with earbuds in my life. Features: This is where it's not all positive. The app is just ok, and I am not going to use a bunch of the features. I like that you can select options for the earpad interface and you can turn them off as well, but I'd say, really, just ok, sometimes you can try to do too much, and I think that's what happened here. Battery: The battery is incredible, with ANC on it's still comparable to my Buds+ in practice, maybe a little less life with ANC on, but with ANC and transparency off they just go and go and they charge fast! It never seems like they get less than 60% charged in my usual usage unless I'm in an epic work session and I'm using the ANC. Others may disagree, but in many way I ALMOST prefer these to my M4 headphones. No, I DO prefer these to my M4's in every way except in just sheer high-end sound quality. Not that these are bad, as I've said, just come on, you can't ever compare sound quality from earbuds to full headphones.

title: High Quality Sound, Uncomfortable earbuds
text: Used it for over a month. 5 days per week. 1. Sound Quality (5 out of 5) - Absolutely the best wireless earbuds in terms of sound quality. (July 2021). If you can stream high-quality music and if your system supports LDAC, these are the best sound-quality wireless earbuds on the market. (At least at this price point). I have not tried it on iPhone but since it only supports AAC codec, I believe sound quality may not be the same for iPhone users. 2. Size (3 out of 5) - They are big. Yes, they reduced the size compare to version 3. However, they are still bulky when you compare to Samsung, Apple, Jabra, etc. Unless you have big ears, these will stick out. 3. Comfort (2 out of 5) - Some people feel comfortable using the product. However, for me, this product is not comfortable at all. Most of the weight is at the top of the product which is the very furthest point of your ear. The foam tip constantly fights for the position in my ears because of the high center of gravity. If you ever used other popular earbuds like Samsung and Apple, their center of gravity is very low. So the earbuds sit in the ear comfortably. However, for this product, the heaviest point is at the very top of the earbuds. (I believe the battery is in there) So the product is not stable at all. The whole point of being 'wireless earbuds' is to use them more freely. If I have to correct to position all the time, it's just not a good product no matter how good the sound quality is. 4. Noise Cancellation - Great. It is almost good as Sony WH-1000XM4. Due to the noise isolating design, it blocks most of the noise even without the noise cancellation. Overall, I could not give them a great score. I have used them for a month almost every day since they sound so great. The sound is very clean and gives you typical very soft and warm Sony sound color. However, the earbuds are big and not comfortable. I do not recommend this product if you are looking for a pair of earbuds to use while working out, running, and walking long distances.

title: Great, but …
text: Great sound quality but do not stay solidly in my ears, do fall out if not careful. Also sound canceling cuts off whenever my phone gets a notification, no idea why. It won’t stay on permanently. Cuts out and I have to tap to reinitiate.

title: Best earbuds I've ever owned
text: I wasn't happy with the fit, so I changed tips with another set of earbuds (see photo). I can insert these all the way into my ear tightly, and what a sound! Great bass for earbuds, noise cancellation, wonderful stereo / surround sound effects. After a month, they still carry a full charge thanks to the charger. Trying to charge the charger now, we'll see if it charges. As of this writing, I couldn't be happier!

title: Expensive! They are great but not loud enough!
text: These are really good just Not loud enough. I’ve never had headphones that I wanted to turn up the sound up constantly. I kept going to turn them up and they are on the loudest setting 🥲. I just can’t believe they would make such great headphones with great sound quality but with a limit the amount of sound output. When working out and running on a treadmill they need to be louder than they are, still in Disbelief. Next version please make the sound go higher especially for 300$ that’s a must! I’m not a teenager I am 50 and I hear really well but I really need the music louder. I’ve had them for three weeks I’m going to give it one more week but most likely will return. Great sound quality and noise canceling is really good! The battery life is great! The app is cool, you can change the settings for someone but not for someone who wants to hear music nice and loud. I have another pair of Sony they fit better these they are large, so people with small ears they will fall out here and there. Should have stuck with the ear design of the Sony C500 they rock. You’ll have to try these for yourself, they are great earbuds it just depends on exactly what you want. I want my music louder 😬

title: Terrible call quality
text: The call quality was terrible. Heard repeat voices and static no matter where I was. The initial voice upon placement was so faint and no way to turn that up.

title: Worth every penny!
text: Hands down the very best wireless ear buds if have ever owned.

title: Noise cancelling is awesome
text: I work in a very noisy environment with other music being played over big speakers overhead. These guys shut that right out and I don't have to listen to the same stuff being played over and over. The sound is clear and it is easy to adjust the way you like it using the app. The only thing I find annoying is that the places that you tap on the outside are very hard to zone in on and I have had a lot of issues finding just the right place to tap to pause the music. It can take quite a few taps to find it and then when I hit the exact same spot again, it doesn't work. Very frustrating when someone is waiting to talk to you.

title: Wanted to love them! But OH that FIT!
text: Just like several others have stated, I really was hoping that these were the perfect earbuds. So close but the fit just bugs me. Squeezing the foam turning the earbuds to get a seal, takes a few times to get them perfect but after 1hr or so they hurt. I wear the medium size but just couldn't get them to the point I forgot I was wearing them. Switching between devices is a bit of a pain too. Do they sound good? OH YES, they do. Noise-cancelling is awesome. I love the talk and stop feature so much. I am sticking with my BOSE quiet comfort buds. So much more comfortable I forget I am wearing them. I have several earbuds, iPod pro's, Jabra 75T, Beats Pro etc. I think Sony missed the mark by not including silicone earbuds for people who just don't love the memory foam.

title: Don't stay in ear!
text: These do not stay in my ears. Constantly falling out and getting lost. Won't be able to use these when I go back to the office because I will lose them. I tried the feature of in the accompanying Sony app that allegedly scans a persons ears but that did not help. At a complete loss. Wish I had returned these but missed the return deadline by 1 day.

title: Pretty great overall! First pair of case charged buds.
text: These rock overall and work well as advertised. I wish they had a volume control and and off switch however. I often use them in bed and don't want to dig for the case when I'm done and sleepy. That means they're dead in the AM. I leave the case on the charger though so it works out pretty good.

title: Average, especially compared to Apple
text: Average sound quality. The do fit your ear fairly well. But, nothing like the Apple ear pods.

title: Perfect for listening to audiobooks but fall out of my ears
text: Comfortable fit, noise cancelling works well while husband listens to sports and I want to listen to audiobooks. Update: After a few days of using I’ve had the buds fall out of my ears as I walk around the house. Also I may be allergic to the material since my ear canals have started itching when I wear them. Love the performance of these buds but they just aren’t compatible with my ears.

title: Not that great
text: Pros: Comfortable. Great sound quality. Lots of audio control in app. Cons: LOTS of connectivity issues with iPhone. Can’t use right earbud by itself only left. Bad Bluetooth range. Battery life. Bulky case. Definitely would not recommend them for someone with an iPhone. I really wanted to like these but honestly they are a waste of money.

title: 100% great
text: Great sound with clear and deep bass, adjustable buttons. 6 hours listening on battery.

title: 5th dimension level of sound!!
text: By far the best quality of sound and sound cancellation in compact ear buds...something you would find in full ear muff type of headphones.

title: Best set of wireless earbuds.
text: This was a Father's day present to me. After getting my youngest son the Sony over the ear headset and seeing how it performed, I wanted the in ear version. The noise canceling aspect of this head set is phenomenal. When cutting grass, it blocks out the noise from the lawn mower without having to crank the volume up. The ambient setting allows sounds to pass through when driving. The quality of sound when playing music or a movie is outstanding! Of all the in ear head sets that I have owned, these by far the best. You can hear the lows without it sounding tinny and the highs do not sound muted. The tips that came with this headset have also out performed all other headsets I've owned. When inserted properly, they don't move around and I don't have to worry about them falling out when I'm moving around. Now for the downside. They can only be paired to one device at a time. I wish I could pair them to two devices simultaneously. The charging case feels flimsy and somewhat cheap. Battery time, for the cost, could be somewhat better. I'm not sure if I am doing something wrong, but when using only one earbud, it has to be the right one. Unable to use the left by itself. There needs to be a way to control the volume without having to pull out my phone. The tips seem to pick up any random piece of dirt and are somewhat difficult to clean. Even with those little complaints, I highly recommend this set above all others. There are many more good reasons than bad to buy these. Just the exceptional quality of sound justify the cost for those who really enjoy music.

title: Uncomfortable & Ineffective
text: To be clear, I have misaphonia and need to use ear buds to block out my upstairs neighbors throwing things on the floor and coworkers typing at my office. I cannot function otherwise. I might eventually get used to the feel of the ear buds (which are too hard and heavy for me, even with the smallest coverings), but they are not nearly as effective for noise-cancelling as my cheap corded ones. Like, not even close. You can toggle between “noise-cancelling” and “ambient sound” but if there’s a difference between these settings, it’s extremely subtle. Maybe in comparison with other Bluetooth ear buds they’re superior, but they don’t stand up to corded ear buds at all. I was really disappointed because it would have been worth the money had they been comfortable and effective.

title: Great noise cancelling Wireless Buds
text: Nice rich sound, if not a little bass oriented. I would recommend tuning your EQ preferences for a better experience than out of the box. Even with EQ optimization, the treble still feels slightly lacking. But, overall a good sound. Comfort is a little bit to desired. After wearing the buds for more than an hour they start to get a little uncomfortable. The noice canceling is excellent with no inner ear pressure. Ambience mode sound a little artificial at first but, almost natural after you adjust to it.

title: 1 Major flaw is keeping me from keeping or recommending
text: Amazing product but with a major flaw. Wish I would have ignored the YouTube reviews and on a couple of them paid more attention. When you go above 50 % on volume the quality goes away and you lose bass and quality of sound. Volume is not that loud also. This is a deal breaker for me but maybe not for you.

title: Not what I expected.
text: Before I bought these I had bought the Samsung Galaxy Buds pro and was very disappointed. I decided to try these, because I have the Sony WH- 1000xm3's and love them so I thought these would be as good, nope. The anc isn't as good, but it is good enough for me. The sound is good and I have no complaints. These would actually be great if they were more comfortable, stayed in my ears and didn't have so many connection issues. The first day of wearing these my ears were red and they hurt. I thought, my ears will get used to it, it's been a while and I'm still waiting. I don't like the fit. They have fallen out multiple times. I have tried different size tips. I could live with this though... The worst thing about these for me is having the connection drop out multiple times durring one song. I have to keep my phone in my right pocket in order to not have as many interruptions in my music, wich is not okay. If you pay this much for a well known brand of headphones you shouldn't have to deal with this much crap. I have Skullcandy headphones that cost 20 bucks and have no connection issues at all. I can't recommend these to anyone unless you can deal with all these issues and can get them at a very low price even then not worth it.

title: Buyer Beware: These have a defect that Sony refuses to acknowledged
text: Many people who have bought these earbuds, including me, have an issue with them where one side produces a strange, metallic echo when ANC is on. It's especially noticeable during podcasts when people are speaking or when you click your teeth. It's hard to describe the sound, but it completely ruins the experience and makes these useless. It almost seems like a hardware defect rather than a software one as you can reproduce the effect with your teeth, as I mentioned earlier. For me, the sound was like nails on a chalkboard -- there was something about the sound that made me feel uneasy. It's not just me. If you go on Reddit you'll find tons of people who have had the same problem. Entire threads are dedicated to people expressing their frustration, some of them on their third pair. The worst part is that the defect has been around since these buds launched nearly a year ago and Sony hasn't acknowledged it. The sound quality seemed to be good and the ANC was effective, but the metallic, tinny echo was a complete deal breaker.

title: Rumbling in left earbud
text: My left earbud makes a moderately loud rumbling noise at random times when ANC or Adaptive noise is enabled. Apparently this is not an unheardof hadware issue for these. For the price they are, I expect significantly better quality control than this. I'm not your quality assurance division, sony. I'm the customer. I'll be returning for a refund. If they worked they would be good earbuds, but not the improvement over the XM3's I was hoping for. Keep in mind, they're probably one of if not the best premium wireless earbud options out there. Unlike the XM3's these have LDAC, which is nice if you can notice it. The comfort is a big upgrade over the XM3's. But the noise isolation and noise cancellation is just not that much better than the previous gen. Best in class, maybe, but in-ear earbuds have the potential to offer excellent isolation in addition to active cancellation, which would be an amazing combination that these just did not accomplish.

title: I am not a raver. I need to rave about this product for a minute.
text: I have many pairs of earphones and earbuds. I've been pursuing excellence in fidelity over forty years. Music is maybe tops on my priority list. My hearing is keen and discriminating, I am a musician, audiophile, mimic, and merciless critic. I kick the tires hard when I make a purchase. I had hoped the Sony WF-1000XM4 earbuds were noticeably better than the last phones/buds I bought. I am still blown away and immersing in every dimension of these earbuds. Isolation, bass, mid-tones, higher tones, comfort, fit, battery life, ambience, soundstage. I have never been this impressed by something I've purchased

title: Amazing sound but extremely painful to wear
text: Oh sony. Im not sure how to rate this product. The sound is phenomenal, but the earbud itself is extremely uncomfortable. It's heavy, it's big, the material used for noise cancelling is best on the first use then it deforms and becomes less effective. I also wonder how much they plan to charge for replacements because it's definitely not a material that lasts long. The longest I can wear this without it falling out or become painful to my ears is about 1 hour. 30 min is usually when it starts to get lose. This is my experience of sitting on my couch and working with earbuds. I can't imagine what it'd be like at the gym.

title: Broken, do not purchase
text: The performance is great but you lose the ability to switch between sound modes, noise cancelling, ambient sound or off. Something in the software or firmware is broken, and Sony refuses to acknowledge the issue. Using the latest Android 11 and latest firmware and Sony Headphones app. Don't purchase until sony fixes the issue because the headset is essentially bricked, and gets stuck in whichever mode it gets stuck in with no way to change it.

title: Not worth it- I had 4 sets of them
text: I have run the gamut of ear buds/headsets, from a $600 Jabra headset, the AirPod Pros 2nd, these Sonys, and $30 Amazon specials… and these are not worth it. I have owned four pairs of the WF-1000XM4’s and they all stopped functioning before six months. I would start to notice one ear bud randomly disconnecting at around 90 days, then by six months that bud would be totally dead— on all four pairs. I thought that these would be top of the line at noise cancelling, but I’ve now decided that a lot of the review websites must be owned by Sony. The noice cancellation was impressive until I bought a pair of AirPod pro’s 2nd generation… holy cow… what a difference!!! In my AirPod pros, I feel like I am in a spaceship. Not only that, but you can’t turn on noise cancellation in the Sonys when you are on a call… BUT YOU CAN IN THE AIRPODS! The foam in the Sony’s hurts my ears if I am wearing them for any extended period of time. They are also bulky on my head, and the case is super bulky in my pocket. When you are accepting a phone call, these ear buds take a few seconds to connect (at least to my iPhone 13), so you have to repeat yourself as soon as it connects or ask the other person yo repeat themselves if they spoke first. I also hate that these buds and the case don’t have any way to track them if you misplace them. I’m serious when I say… get the AirPod pros 2nd gen over these. The one area where I think the Sony’s win is in battery life. And considering the giant hunk of real estate that they take up in your pocket and on your ears, they better have an ample sized battery in there!

title: A much improved upgrade to my older Jabra Elite 65Ts
text: I had been using the Jabra Elite 65Ts for quite a while when I would workout and do yardwork. After the battery started to degrade, I began looking at options. I was already used to the WH-1000XM3s from Sony, so I decided to give their matching earbuds a try. Sound quality wise, these are a huge improvement compared to the Jabras. The clarity is great, as is the bass response. I did opt to buy silcone ear tips for these, which improved the fit but may have detracted slightly from the overall quality. A worthy trade off to keep them in my ears though. Noise cancellation is great. Not as good as the over the ears, but still better than any other earbud I've used. They also are easy to pair, and have multi device support, which comes in handy!

title: Don't waste your money
text: The biggest reason I wanted these earbuds was the "great reviews" on here for the active noise canceling... I had the product set up correctly (which takes 20 minutes, 2 apps, and photos of each ear!) After all that, the buds are not as loud as my Bose and I heard EVERYTHING around me!

title: Perfect buds
text: Sure, they are pricey. But for on the MTB (not in traffic), they are perfect for listening to podcasts or music. Noise cancellation is great, and easy to turn off. They stay secure 100% of the time.

title: Absolutely incredible headphones, kinda regret not buying another pair
text: Used the WH1000XM2 for a while and also had the AirPods Pro but was really unhappy with the sound quality. When I heard these are coming out I just HAD to try them and I was not disappointed. Stellar sound quality and build quality, great controls. Super happy with the purchase.

title: Great quality
text: I've always had issues with in ear type earphones and always chose to have over-ear. Buying this i can say the fit is great and overall quality in sound and noise cancellation exceeded my expectations, highly recommended!

title: Love these as upgrade to WF-1000XM3's
text: Better fit and more comfortable These have outstanding audio quality, noise isolation/cancellation, and battery life. They are pricey but for me the quality is well worth it. For comparison, I still have the XM3's, Bose QuietComfort 35 II headphones, Bose QuietComfort 20 earbuds, and Bose SoundSport earbuds - but these are what I pick up and use.

title: Very Nice
text: This is my first Earbud and the sound and app are great. At first they felt fun in my ears and like it would all out. I highly recommend reading the instructions. They fit fine now. It's a lot of money, I hope they last. So far so good.

title: Do not cancel noise
text: I’m very disappointed with the noise canceling, it is very ineffective.

title: Not bad but certainly not perfect.
text: Don't stay in ear well and ear starts to get fatigued fast.

title: My favorite pair compared to Apple, Bose, and Soundcore
text: This is a tough category as people's ear shapes and sizes plus sound preferences can be so different. Up until I bought the Sony XM4's, I had been using the Apple iPod Pro's for calls and noise cancellation and using the Sony SP800N's for music. The goal, of course, was to be able to get down to one pair of earbuds for all scenarios. My testing criteria for Sony vs Bose vs Apple vs Soundcore: -Comfort: I have small ear canals, so most earbud types hurt my ears --The Soundcore Anker Liberty 3's were hands down the most comfortable to me -Sound --The Sony's just edged out the Soundcore's -Bass --Same here, the Sony's just edged out the Soundcore's --For me, this is where Apple earbuds suffer the most -Call quality --I think Apple is probably the best here, but the Sony's were "good enough" -Noise Cancellation --I think the Sony's are the best here, even better than Bose --This is one of the reasons I returned the Soundcore's -Pass-thru sound --Again, I think Apple is the best here. In my opinion, when you turn on the pass-thru sound, the Apple's sound the most natural to the point where it doesn't seem like a mic is picking up outer sounds and passing them thru the speakers. I feel like the Sony's are very close to getting it right, perhaps with a future update. -Battery life --Sony and Soundcore are both up at the higher end of the pack If you don't want to spend $250+ on a pair of wireless earbuds and are mostly interested in comfort and sound, I would highly recommend the Soundcore Anker Liberty 3's. But, at this price, for me, the Sony's are the way to go. I'm very happy with them.

title: Simply Incredible
text: These sound absolutely incredible. Noise cancelling is amazing, bass is amazing, clear as crystal, fit well, I only have 1 complaint. The ear tips it comes with seem to wear out and crack I've been using daily for about 2 months. Sony support was great sent out new tips no questions asked. However I have discovered Spinfit cp360 and those work as a great silicone alternative. Are they worth the price? Absolutely! Best sounding earbuds I've ever owned Battery life is incredible too they push me through 8 hour work days without any issues

title: They hurt my ears
text: After about 10 minutes these start to hurt my ears from their shape. It's unfortunate because i spent so much on them and really hoped they'd be more comfortable. They work great. Noise cancelling isn't as good as my over ear ones.

title: Thank god for prime day deals :)
text: Got these 80 bucks off for prime day - helz ya! (these were sitting in my save for later queue forever and there was some sticker shock on original suggested price) These headphones rock!!! I did get a defective set where one headphone side was staticky, but I got a replacement that worked as expected so I'm not going dock anything star-wise. Lemons happen, not going to get butt hurt over it. Thank you amazon customer service for being awesome (as I have grown accustomed to) :) The good: All my songs sound like listening to them for the first time with these. Even old 80's stuff sounds new. The bass reminds me of the beefy deep bass and crisp trebles you had when you used the good high-priced cassette Sony Walkmans back in the day when I was young so the sound brings me back to the good old days (but much clearer!) and it's quite nostalgic. I'm very brand loyal to Sony headphones because of the warm full sound. The bass is such a star of these headphones. Clean and deep, not sounding like a wave file that was recorded too loud and is wave clipping. Their connecting app is completely user friendly and makes paring a breeze. Not always a fan of their proprietary software, but this was done well. OMG these charge fast in the case! It's sick actually The only negative - the included ear pads suck. I've learned I'm not a fan of the memory foam ear buds they make. The good news is Sony's rubber tips are totally compatible so I took some old spare rubber tips from wired headphones and they lock in my ear canals as I expect and the sound is superb.

title: Not worth the price
text: Noise cancellation is great! Having an app connected to them was also nice. Other than that, I expected sound quality to be much better for a Sony product. They are difficult to take out of the case, I guess that can be a good thing since my old ones would fall out too easily, and they were extremely uncomfortable. They irritated my ears. I am returning and hopefully trying out the Bose earphones.

title: Nice sound but that is all.
text: The sound quality of these is 2nd to none of any of the other earbuds I've owned. I had lost my Galaxy pro 2 earbuds and decided to go for these after reading the reviews about the sound quality and some other items that intrigued me but once I got them really the only thing I like about them is the sound quality they're not comfortable they're very big, If you use one at a time and the battery goes dead in it you can't pull the other 1 out and start using it. It has foam for the ear plug portion which I don't care for it started hardening after only a couple of days. Using them to talk on the phone is absolutely horrible, If you're not directly in front of your phone and within 10' it feet it cuts out constantly doesn't have a very good range at all. Overall for the price I would rather just have Samsung Galaxy Pro 2 they can be used independently battery life is way better And the Bluetooth range is really good. I will be returning these and buying new Galaxy Pro 2

title: Outstanding tech
text: I hadn't bought new headphones in quite a while. The features of the WF-1000XM4 are so intuitive and for buds without wings, these stay in my ears just fine. The sound quality is nearly as good as the WH-1000XM4. There's even a feature that tells you if you have a good fit with your chosen tips. Sony knows how to do sound.

title: Best noice cancellation earbuds I’ve tried.
text: Bought these specifically for sleep. My husband snores something fierce. I’ve tried more headphones/earbuds than I’d like to admit. I was extremely hesitant because of the price. But a good nights sleep is more than worth it. Amazon does offer a payment plan that is reasonable. The noise canceling works well even with no music on. The sound isn’t the best thing I’ve ever heard, but you can adjust the equalizer with the app. I’ve only had these for a few days and so far they have met my expectations. I am still curious about the Bose sleep earbuds, but these are more than okay for now!

title: LOVE these earbuds!
text: I LOVE these ear buds. I got them today and charged them up. It didn't take long. I have them in now, and they are so comfortable that I barely know I'm wearing them! A little pricey, but worth every single penny. The sound quality is great. I'm so happy with my purchase!

title: Amazing sound, great for travelers, not so great for phone calls.
text: Sony absolutely nailed it with these ones. The sound quality is greaty, the noise cancelling is amongst the best. I fly frequently, in the week I've had these, I've taken 7 flights now comfortably without issue. At times I wish they could be a little louder, but I think for 99% of people these will suffice. The only complaint I have is the phone call quality, I'm not sure why, but every person I've spoken with on the phone has complained about static, sounding like a robot etc. Maybe this will change with firmware updates? But for now these are unusable for phone calls.

title: Great when working but connection is intermitten
text: Great sound quality and excellent noise cancellation. Honestly, I think it exceeds airpods in every way with the exception of call quality. With that said, connection often disconnects for no reason making it unusable. Will have to return but may give it another chance.

title: Not what I was expecting
text: Ok, I do like these. The sound is quite good. But I was expecting a lot better noise cancellation. I have the Sony over-the-ear headphones and those are absolutely amazing. The earbud equivalent pale in comparison. I feel like I could get a much cheaper pair without NC and be close to what these provide. I’ll keep them, but would definitely not buy again.

title: Very underwhelmed
text: Sound quality is mediocre and the noise cancellation is not very good.

title: DOA
text: Left earbud was dead on arrival, it worked to pause and everything else, but I couldn't get sound out of it. I'll wait for the replacement to update the sound when both work.

title: Great Quality
text: Very clear and accurate when optimized. I have a number of different brands and these have the best fit. The battery life is poor. The right bud lasts 4 hours with no ANC and ambient turned off. The left bud always shows 40% remaining battery life.

title: Was not impressed
text: I received today and returning today. I just don’t like these earbuds at all. I got these to try and just wear around the house. They are not very comfortable, the foam buds are kinda ridiculous honestly, I found it impossible to get a nice sealing fit. I was going to order silicone replacements but nah shipping these back. I am not impressed with the noise cancellation, by far not as good as Bose quiet comfort 1 earbuds. The sounds quality isn’t horrible, but not the best. Sound quality compares to a 40$ set of ear buds I recently bought. You can adjust EQ with app. Higher bass setting isn’t impressive. Left ear bud would electronically buzz and would just shut off or lose connection with in the first hour of trying. I have 2 pair of Bose quiet comfort 1 that I wear at work (power plant/ noisy environment) and at the gym. the noise cancellation is amazing, comfort is crazy awesome, and sound quality is way better than the Sonys. I’ll just stick with what works and order another pair of Bose for the house. The only thing I like about these Sonys compared to the Bose is the size of the charging case, Sonys is smaller.

title: Don't buy used
text: This was my second pair of these Sony buds. I loved my first pair so much, I bought a second pair to bring to my office. To save a few bucks, I bought this second pair used, in good condition. These used in good condition buds never sounded quite as good as my pair purchased new but they were still very good. Now, less than four months after purchase, sound fades in and out, and the buds repeatedly disconnect from bluetooth. Meantime, the pair I bought new performs great, just as they did from Day 1. I've never bought used or reconditioned electronics on Amazon before, & I this will be the last time I do. The savings wasn't that great and in the end they're a total loss.

title: Pair flakey - bad instructions great battery good NC
text: [[VIDEOID:fb77de6709880e263355d529cac14978]] Eventually the app finally paired and trouble free but for price I expected better pairing than the dozen $20 bluetooth buds I've used and certainly having better instructions. Noise Cancellation NC is good but ambient sound setting is like amplifying outside sound more than normal buds. Biggest selling point is very good battery and reasonably good NC

title: Amazing noise cancelation, meh sound
text: The noise cancelation on these earbuds are great and the app is very intuitive, but my problem is the sound quality. These things are not bad, but they are certainly not good for the price point. To compare, my last earphones were the Jabra Elite 75t which are the best I have ever used. These Sony earphones cost triple the price have worse sound, base, and make music sound flat. They are great for phone calls and podcasts, but if your looking for quality sound for listening to music there are better and cheaper options out there. Edit: the foam tips do not stay on well and can fall off when you take them out. I had the misfortune of getting the tips stuck in my ears.

title: They crackle
text: $250 for headphones that crackle nonstop? Returned them, going to try out the Bose.

title: Great sound but went back to the AirPods
text: Updated my review after a couple of weeks of use. I have the Sony WH 1000XM3 headphones and love them. Thought these ear buds would be the same but they are painful. The sound and bass is good but after about 30 mins it starts to get painful. I’m gonna have to keep using the AirPods. The sound quality and call quality is top notch, but not being able to use them is a 1 star rating. I don’t even know how good the battery life is cause I never wore them out.

title: A Classical Audiophile's Review
text: Having done some extensive A-B comparisons of orchestral, choral, opera and lieder tracks, here is my take on the Sony XM4 vs. other popular earbuds: With stock silicone tips, sound quality = Sennheiser MTW1 > MTW2 >> XM4 > Bose QC; With Comply foam tips: sound quality = MTW1 > MTW2 > XM4 > Bose QC ANC quality = Bose QC >>> XM4 >> MTW2 > MTW1 (where more arrow ">" means much better) In conclusion, the Sennheiser sounds good regardless of eartips, whereas the Sony is highly dependent on them and sounding best with Comply foam tips. The Bose earbuds ANC performance is so good it even surpasses my QC 35II over-the-ear and almost same as Bose 700. It's that good. In terms of absolute HiFi sound quality, regarldess of earbud or circumaural, it has to be the Bowers & Wilkins PX7....it completely destroys the above-named earbuds and headsets in all the classical genres. I based my HiFi evaluations on my 30+ years of attending live opera and symphony concerts.

title: Good sound
text: Audio quality is everything and for ear buds this is pretty good sound

title: Decent batter and sound quality. Frequent audio drops
text: Pros: Pretty comfortable Decent battery life Good audio quality Cons At least a few times each day, audio will suddenly drop from one ear bud and then return a minute later Audio prompts are very long. If you join a Zoom meeting, you often have to sit there for almost 10 seconds starting at your coworkers in silence while the ear buds announcing things like batter levels Don't expect any sound cancelling except for some low level background noise.

title: Incredible Sound, Noise Cancelling & Battery Life
text: Update: these headphones batteries have suddenly become so bad & can't last up to 1hr of audio playback. Just terrible & I can't believe it! Not certain if this is just a bad update issue or if this is a hardware issue. I'm dropping my rating to 2 stars pending a fix or replacement. Great sound quality, noise cancelling & battery life. Takes some time to get used to them in your ears & I won't be surprised some folks aren't able to see it through. The ear tips require time to soften as they are quite stiff on 1st use & soften up over time thereby increasing the comfort. Overall a very feature rich earbud & one of the best for the price. If you can wait I bet the price will drop in time for Christmas.

title: Thin and Hollow
text: Stuck with these as I had my Bose earbuds in my pocket in the ocean in Mexico. These were the only option at the electronics store. Compared to the Bose these are terrible sounding. Very thin with little low end and the ear pieces are not comfortable.

title: Amazing Sound! Amazing Battery Life!
text: I used to own a pair of Samsung Pro earbuds until they crapped out on me randomly the other day. I then upgraded to these and have never been happier! I'm sure you've read a lot of the reviews that have praised the amazing sound quality. They really need to be heard to be believed! They just sound absolutely jaw dropping! In addition to that add spectacular battery life and a comfortable fit and you have the perfect pair of earbuds. You gotta give these a try! You will not regret it!

title: Didn't like, the case too small
text: I bought these buds for the noise canceling feature. Either I didn't know what I was doing or the feature was too difficult to maneuver. Either way for the amount of money they were charging it should have been easier. I have last year's model and they worked right I out of the box . I have never had a moments trouble with them. I bought these because I wanted a second pair to watch television. Not good.

title: Volume control pretty low. Hard to hear.
text: Is very excited to receive these. I am deaf in one ear. When using it, it wasn’t strong enough for me to hear very

title: Noise canceling, auto lower of volume during calls or conversation with someone and fit.
text: I really wanted to like these Earbuds as its definitely superior to my older, non-noise canceling Sony ear buds. Unfortunately the 3 ear piece sizes that came with the product (Small, Medium, Large) just doesn't provide the right "fit" or snugness - Size Small - too small and inhibits full noise cancelling capabilities; Size Medium - fits fine but I really have to "push and rotate" them into my ear to get a good fit that makes the noise cancelling effective but unfortunately it hurts my ear after less that 15 minutes using them; Size Large - too big to get the proper fit and actually the left on keeps easing off my ear to almost come off. So after 1 week of trying to make this work, I've decided to return them as its just inconvenient to use daily and frequently. I am a Sony headphone fan that owns multiple headphone/earphones/earbuds but this one just didn't work out for me.

title: Stopped syncing via Bluetooth after 2 months
text: Ive been using headphones and at the 2nd month, i wont appear on any Bluetooth that wasn't saved earlier. Now i have a pair of expensive headphones linked to 2 old phones. When i, eventually, update the phones, then the headphones will be useless. And yes, ive tried all the options to solve this (even closing and opening the charger 10 times to reset it) to no avail.

title: Fun, detailed, punchy, comfortable!
text: These are better than the XM-3s (which I own) on all fronts. Extra detail, battery life, and less glitchy. The connectivity part is huge - they connect flawlessly now, whereas I had some issues on/off with my XM3s (apple products), and those are now all resolved. I find the connectivity with my iPhone really good. Ear controls are awesome. Pauses instantly when you remove a bud. Tap to start playing music without picking up your phone. I also own the Airpods Max. I know they are very different animals, and the Airpods have a lot more spatial details, but I find myself picking up the Sony's for most of the day because they are so comfortable I forget they are there, and I only hear the music. Re: the Airpod Pros, the XM3's already sounded better and the XM4s clearly trounce them.

My one gripe tho is the foam ear tips all break apart and rip for no reason. I take my earbuds out often at the gym to put on/take off a weighted vest and these eartips somehow always rip. Makes no sense if your fingernail isnt touching em. For the price you would think the eartips of all things would be such low quality rubbish

title: Rediscover music
text: Wow. I am a huge music listener. I feel like I am hearing music for the first time again. Albums that had sounded flat and wore my ears out are ALIVE again. Distinguishing cymbals, drum rolls and frankly hearing things i haven't noticed in albums I've played a hundred times..the price made me question my sanity but after breaking the wires on 4 sets of $30 wired earbuds and knowing that phone mfgs are ended ear jacks i relented and all i can say is i regret i didn't buy them sooner

title: Horrible Microphone
text: I bought these to replace my Airpod Pros, and to primarily use them for phone calls. I ultimately had to return them for the terrible built-in microphone, which was almost unusable. Call recipients couldn't understand me, and said my voice is muddled, and that the sound quality got worse as the call went on. Not sure if my headphones were defective, or if the product itself is bad. I know the Sony's put an emphasis on listener noise cancelling. I have the WM-1000XM4 (over-ear) headphones, which I adore, and why I wanted to give the buds a try. For comparison, the ANC on these are good. But so are the Airpod pros. But it seems that the microphone feed is just sent raw over the call, as the Apples process it to cut out background noise for the person on the other end. Going back to the WMs for over-ear music listening, and my Airpods for calls.

Out of the box, I couldn't get her new iPad to recognize them so I emailed customer support and they were very helpful and friendly, and even followed up after to see if their instructions worked. They did! So here's a useful tip: just turn off the Wi-Fi on every device in the house first. After I did this, the iPad picked them up immediately. Then you can turn the Wi-Fi back on the other devices and you shouldn't have to do this again.

text: These are very well packed and overall nicely designed. I like that they went with a type C cable to charge them. After pairing with your phone you can simply put the one you aren't using in the case. When you want to switch back to two you take is out and you will hear powering on and the sound will sync. The one downside I have found with earbuds in this price range is they don't offer the ability to sense when it's removed from your ear. This means when you want the earbud to turn off you'll need to put it in the case. The manual does a good job of explaining what tapping the side will do and you can also power them on and off holding down the side of it. Overall: These are great set of earbuds and are being used as my daily pair at the moment. I will update this review if I have any issues.

title: Love These
text: I purchased these after reading a review (CNet, I believe) about the best earbuds. I'd been looking for wired ones because I've bought nice, top-end Bluetooth earbuds before and have never been happy with them. Usually, they don't work consistently, are subject to interference, drop the audiobook/podcast/call, and are too finicky. These, though? They've exceeded even my highest hopes. The sound quality is excellent. They have a wonderful case that charges them until its battery dies, which then recharges quickly with its included USB-C charger cord (no plug, you need a regular USB port to plug it into). They're super comfortable, they stay in my ears impressively well, you can wear one at a time if you'd like because they connect independently and each has the pause/play button on it. They have an impressive range, too. I've accidentally walked away from my phone and made it 4 rooms away without losing the sound (it does get a little fuzzy). I've used them frequently since I purchased them 3 months ago and I'm still super impressed. Reliable, excellent, and I'm no longer looking for wired earbuds. I highly recommend them. The one downside for me is that they're noise-canceling. I'd love it if there was an option not to, but to make up for it, I just wear one when I'm out walking or need to listen for something.
