title: Great for music but terrible for calls....
text: Overall: Great for listening to music but terrible for calls. Sound: They sound great! They have a pretty nice and even sound stage with a slight emphasis on the bass. The mids and highs are clear even when turned up and with the bass kicking pretty hard. I wouldn't mind slightly crisper highs but are pretty good considering I am not using any apps or EQ of any kind. They sound a lot like a few good pairs of 3.5mm wired headphones I used to use and miss. Calls: Hearing others is not an issue however others hearing you is a problem. Every time I used these for calls I would have to switch to using the handset or speakerphone because every time people would say my voice was breaking up and not clear. Fit: They fit really well and feel light and comfortable. At first I almost put them in upside down but then realized how they go in and they fit great. Because most of the bulk sits up higher it feels like it helps push them down into your ears and helps them stay in. Comparing to others that have the same design as the AirPods where they go out and down, the EarFuns feel much more comfortable and stable. Controls: The controls for these are buttons on the outside. When pressing the buttons it is easy to press the earphone into your ear and cause discomfort. I think this is the only downside. It would be great if it was touch, or if the button was on the bottom or somewhere there you can grip/press it using 2 fingers that didn't involve pressing into your ear. Even with this design if you use a finger to support the earphone while you press the button it is not terrible. Issues: The only thing I noticed that happened a few times is the left and right didn't start playing the song at the exact same time occasionally. Right would start and left would start 0.5 seconds after. Definitely not a deal breaker.

title: Great sound, battery life as advertised, great features, nice ergonomics.
text: Wireless charging, USB-C, good battery life, awesome audible cues, 25% battery audible warning, charging case is not water resistant but I can wear the buds in the shower at the very least. I like the ability to listen to either L or R side independently for continuous podcast listening (one charges while the other plays). I think you can take a phone call on either one independently, but can't confirm. Volume/track has to be controlled from the device if only using one side. Audio quality is great, delay is low. The passive noise cancelling is solid. Active noise cancelling with a listening feature like the latest Bose have would be nice, but definitely not expected at this price point at the time of writing. I use an app that uses the phone's microphone and pumps that sound to the headphones so you can hear your surroundings when necessary, and the delay is less than non-BT 5.0. The ability to be paired and broadcasting to the headphones and another device at the same time can be useful as well. The case feels a bit cheap, but is acceptable, especially given the features/specs. I've used a few other similar wireless ear buds at multiple price points, higher and lower, and I am calling these a favorite when it comes to a balance between the latest features, both build and sound quality, and price.

text: This is my first pair of TWS earbuds. I cannot compare them to any higher end, $150+, TWS earbuds, but after reading various reviews, I bought these. They work fantastically. The wireless charging case is awesome, battery life is great, longest I've used them for was 6 hours nonstop while I cut down some trees. Sound quality I think is very good, clear. Pairing is easy, took them out of the case and paired them to my phone immediately, simple. I use them for phone calls often and sound is great and everyone says they hear me clearly, each earbud has a mic so you can use the earbuds individually on calls. Overall I would highly recommend them to anyone who wants to try TWS earbuds without dishing out $150+. Great bargain considering all the features it has.

title: Best sound from wireless earbuds that I've heard!
text: These headphones are excellent! They're a little bigger than normal wireless earbuds but that allows them more room for drivers. Sound - The sound quality of these buds is exceptional. Rich low ends, kicking mids and clear highs all come through on these. Battery - The battery life is awesome as well. I've been using them several hours a day consistently for about a week and I haven't had to charge the case at all - in fact, the indicator light for the case still shows a full charge. I haven't reached the limit on how long the buds last on a charge but I'll update if I hit it. Connection / Setup - Connection couldn't have been easier. Pop them out, search for BT devices on your phone and connect. The connection has always been very solid as I've been using them - haven't experienced any dropouts. Fit / Comfort - As I mentioned, these are a bit bigger than other wireless earbuds. That works perfectly for me since I've got pretty big ears. Not sure how it would work with someone with smaller ears. I wear them for several hours at a time without any discomfort. They seal out ambient noise very well too - again, probably at least partially due to the bigger size.

title: I really like these earphones but...
text: I love these earphones because they are comfortable and the sound is fine for my purpose which to listen to books, videos and articles while working in my studio. They fit well in my rather small ears which is unusual. They don't have the new feature that causes the slightest touch to turn them off or on or various other things depending on how many times you touch them accidentally or annoyingly get your finger in the wrong place. ( I don't like the earphones that have this at all because even getting them into your ears causes unwanted stuff to happen & I cannot lie on my side and listen to a book or article which helps me get to sleep - without some "feature" or other accidentally occurring.) That is - gratefully - not the case with these and I like that. There IS the ability to turn them on and off by clicking once which is great. The main reason for 3 instead of 5 stars is that I have now wasted close to 45 minutes of my time trying to get the warranty. After going through the whole process of filling out the form, I am stymied at the end because the visual code given to prove I am not a robot does not work and another code is not provided. Emailing has not worked so far. either I have not explained the situation adequately or they are refusing to understand what I am saying. None the less I would buy these again if available - knowing that I may not be able to get the warranty.

title: Excellent Earbuds

title: Incredible value!
text: These are amazing. The sound quality is pretty average, but the bass is there if you want it and the volume can actually get pretty loud. I feel like the sound profile is perfect for the intended uses of these, wearing them while being "active". The included rubber ear tips actually work for both decent sound and holding power. I usually switch my buds to comply foam, but I think i'll stick with the rubbers on these. I wear them in the shower all the time, no problems with waterproofing! The case is nice, showing it's charge status with 4 LEDs. USB-C is very appreciated here as I can just use my phone charger to charge the case. The buds fit snugly in their spots and always start charging right away for me. Connection is easy and they always pair right up when I remove them from the case. I have heard the left ear go out occasionally, but really only when I'm sitting next to my 2.4ghz router, which is probably causing interference. Generally I hear no interference. Only cons would be the left bud can't work independently if you are trying to stretch the batteries, it's a "slave" bud only. I'd pay a little more for the functionality for sure. So far battery life and charge speed has been good enough that this isn't really an issue though. I've been on the fence about truly wireless earbuds for a long time, instead using semi wireless earbuds for the much better battery life. I thought the case would be inconvenient and just be another thing to charge, but I've found it's actually more convenient as you don't necessarily have to bring a charger with you. title: Excellent Sound and Top Notch Customer Service are Second to None
text: First let me say that while I am an Amazon Prime member, I purchased two pair of EarFun Free TWS earbuds through their Indiegogo Campaign (before they were offered on Amazon) for the same price as sold here on Amazon, so my review will not be labeled as “Verified Purchase.” I had been researching TWS earbuds for close to 2 years. Either they cost an arm and a leg for mediocre to reasonably good quality, or they were cheaply made and reflected that in the reviews of so many YouTube reviewers. I did audition a pair of Bose SoundSports. And while the sound was good, they were so large and bulky, and hurt my ears after a short period of time. And the connection between the earbuds was unstable. So I kept waiting, and waiting—until Oluv introduced the EarFun Free TWS earbuds on his YouTube channel. He got me interested in this full-featured set of TWS earbuds. And they received his hearty approval. The EarFun Free TWS earbuds use the latest 5.0 Bluetooth for super-quick and stable connections, are completely waterproof, use advanced 6mm graphene drivers, use the latest USB-C charging in addition to wireless charging, last for 6 hours between charges, and are so comfortable, they can be literally be worn for hours without ear fatigue. This pair met all my expectations! Buttons: These earbuds do not have capacitive touch controls. The jury is still out on the overall positive-versus-negative benefits of capacitive touch controls, and proponents are on both sides of the issue. I do not have to push hard at all to operate the push button controls. I quickly learned how much is enough, and I have never needed to push harder than that. Some users might think that they have to push harder than they really need to. But rest assured, just push the amount needed and you’ll be fine. I write, arrange, record and mix music using Apple’s Logic Pro X DAW, so audio fidelity is critical to me. These earbuds are so accurate, that after working on a song, I will bounce it as a high-quality MP3 and then listen through these earbuds to help my evaluation for end use. Customer Service: Just like their incredible earbuds, Customer Service is top notch! Couldn’t be happier! Bottom Line: The incredible feature set of these earbuds—and for the price—is second to none!

title: Solid Earbud w/ a Major Case Design Flaw
text: I'm a fan of Earfun as I also have purchased their waterproof Bluetooth speaker which has great sound for $40. I was really excited to receive these earbuds since they checked everything on my requirements list. They have good sound, an ergonomic shape that fits my ears, a reliable bluetooth 5,0 connection, and a USB-C charging case. Battery life has been solid so far as well. The downsides of this product are: 1) The button interactions on each earbud are not intuitive. Skipping backward and forward between tracks is handled by two or three taps on a single earbud instead of a long hold or double taps on both earbuds like most other manufacturers. 2) There is no way to change between EQ presets or modify the EQ to your preferences. There is also no mobile app for interacting with the earbud settings or to make firmware updates. 3) If you swap out the included rubber tips for something slightly larger like Comfy foam tips then the earbuds will not fit in the case anymore. This has been a real pain for me since I basically cannot charge the earbuds in the included case unless I remove the foam tips first.

title: Doesn't live up to the bone conduction hype
text: I wanted to try bone conduction headphones so I could hear what's going on around me better while listening to music while out riding my bike. I could tell these headphones were not up to the task within 2 minutes of trying the out at home. The placement of the drivers on your head matters significantly. Just a fraction of an inch too far away from your ear causes the volume & especially any bass frequencies to drop precipitously. The drivers are attached to the band rigidly meaning that there is no room for adjustment or better placement. Worse, the arms felt like they were competing for the same space where my eyeglasses go. The final straw was that just tilting my head up & down was enough to cause the perceived volume to rise & fall...it just created an unenjoyable listening experience. There was no way that these were going to work for me while out riding trails on my mountain bike...as I'd be constantly moving my head & getting jostled while on the trails. While these headphones appear to be made quite well, the manuals are typical super tiny print & only explain how to turn on/off, connect to your devices, and play/pause. Nothing is said about how to wear them properly and/or achieve optimal results.

Now, with my Aftershokz, the audio connects once and stays connected and I can listen all I want to my laptop and, as a bonus my hearing aids can concentrate on doing what they do best - picking up the conversation in the room. text: Overall I would say they are pretty good but they are a bit overpriced for the features that you get. These should be $60. They are nothing special. Cons: - No multipoint (no pairing/switching between multiple devices). - Cannot use the right earbud on its own (only the left one or both). - Matte finish isn't the greatest feeling (makes them feel a bit cheap). - Earbuds are on the larger side and stick out a bit.

title: Very Clever
text: I think this product is very clever. The case serves not only to keep and protect them, but to charge and turn them off and on. When you remove them from the case, they turn on. When you put them back in the case, they turn off. For those who haven't seen them, that's because they make electrical contact with the case. Charging is as simple as plugging in the USB C to standard USB cable. There are three red LED lights in the case. One for each earphone to indicate that it is charging, and one as an indicator that it is receiving power. When either earphone is fully charged, its corresponding LED goes off. When I first put it in my ear, it was too big. Fortunately, I had already looked at the rubber earpieces that came with it and noticed that there are different sizes. After exchanging the rubber earpieces for smaller ones, it fit just right. I just popped the rubber part off, and forced a new one on. It didn't break, but there is a better way to do it (with a twist) that is explained in the directions. Just a warning so you don't risk breaking them like I could have done if I weren't careful. It's easy to transport, charge, and use. The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars is because I was expecting extra bass "as advertised". But to me, it sounded good, but no different from what I would consider normal. For me at least, there wasn't extra bass, and I could find no way to increase it. I'm undaunted because I like everything else about them. There is one thing to consider. I don't use earphones normally, so I have nothing to compare the bass to, except my speakers, which have stronger bass in my opinion. Try to find someone who uses earphones regularly. Such a person might say, that these do in fact have extra bass - compared to what they are used to.

When they finally died on me, I assumed I was trading up by spending more and buying a good brand. I don't know if it's something that's wrong with these earbuds specifically (are they defective?), But I would consider the sound quality inadequate for mainly listening to music. UPDATE- I've been using these for about a year at least and they have developed the problem of one bud dropping out during use. The right earbud frequently turns itself off and I have to re-pair it to get it working. Sometimes the act of the earbud switching off will cause the app playing music, podcasts, audiobooks etc to switch off entirely, sometimes it keeps operating as though nothing is wrong. I just suddenly can't hear in the right ear anymore. I know it's foolish to expect electronics products to last longer than this, but if this is the beginning of the end of this products lifespan, I won't buy Sony earbuds again. I would probably just buy the cheap ones with expectation of them not lasting.

title: Easy Set Up & Use
text: As someone who has yet to find a wireless headphone that works and stays put these definitely check those boxes. But first - setup was easy! Looked for bluetooth and it synced. Easy breezy! The bass is great, the volume is good, and buttons worked well. Accepting calls was also very easy and the caller had no problem hearing me and I had no problem hearing them. Battery life is pretty decent. Lasted about 8.5 hours the first day and over 12 hours every time thereafter. I love that the storage case can help charge in between needing to actually plug them into an outlet/battery charger. The only flaw was the size. I'm use to smaller earbuds and these are pretty big. They help up well working out, but I was so paranoid about them falling out and they did shift in place a few times and needed a lot of adjustment. Love the product, but not sure they will replace the tried and true little white, wired headphones I use on a daily basis.

title: Wow. Love these buds.
text: I have owned dozens of earbuds and use them for hours everyday. I am a huge fan of wireless buds, but the problem has always been how long the charge lasts. That is no longer an issue with these. Pros: 1) These buds have the best BASS range I've ever heard for under 100$. The BASS booms and the music experience is powerful. 2) Awesome battery life. These buds have never run out on me on a single charge, so I don't know how long they actually last. The packaging says 9 hours, and I have used them around that long with no issues. The case charges them super fast and holds 2 charges. I honestly have never had the charging be a factor with these. 3) Comfort/Fit. These buds are a bit more clunky than my old favorite Jabra buds, and while they are a little more tenuous than their big brother buds (Sony WF-SP800N Truly Wireless Sports In-Ear Noise Canceling Headphones) I haven't had them fall out while jumping rope or lifting. If you are a runner, these may not be the ones you want. I feel like they would fall out too easily. But the other Sony buds I mentioned are more secure. 4) Connectivity/Ease of use. These buds are easy to learn to operate. I haven't had to look at the instructions more than a couple times to get going. Overall, easy. Cons: 1) The only issue I have is that they stick out a bit farther than other wireless buds and that is to provide the rich bass sound. So, this isn't really a con to me. Overall, these earbuds are my new favorite and Sony's other set (mentioned above) is my second. But if you are looking for great sound with excellent charging numbers, this is the pair you want. Highly recommended.

title: Sound quality

title: Great clear sound, nice microphone for clear calls
text: Sony always makes good products, this is no exception. Comes in a nice charging case, with 9.5 hours of power use, the earbuds, though a bit larger than some, fit quite nicely in the ears. Setup was easy and thanks that Sony doesn't require some app to go with it to use it. So installation was fast and easy. Once on, the sound was crystal clear. But here's the thing: I found the bass response to be on the medium end. Not some "Extra bass" as it says, however it was CLEAR bass and sounded fine. I just didn't find it with any real extra push. I have other earbuds that for sure showed the bass off more. The earbuds come in a very nice case, with the usual USB c cord for charging. Easy on and off, easy setup, the "usual" ear pushed as most buds have for skipping over and turning up the sound. Comfortable, easy setup. You get what you pay for with earbuds. These are top shelf for the price, I would ignore the "extra bass" thing and just go for "excellent sound quality"!

title: Much worse quality sound than before!
text: I've had a Senso S-255 headset for a number of years ad have used it several times a week, mostly at the gym. When my first one died after just a few months the company immediately sent a replacement, which was great! That one lasted at least 2-3 years until I accidentally pulled the earpiece off the base on one side and broke the wire connecting it to the speaker. Battery life was excellent--I never measured it but it was several hours. And the sound was remarkably good at this price point. I hade compared it to 4 others, none of which were even close. Bass is probably the main shortcoming of cheaper headsets and the Senso was terrific, with well-balanced sound. Unfortunately, my recent purchase, with the same product designator (S-255) is night and day worse than the prior headset. I kept the old one and was able to compare directly with the one side that was still working. Now the sound is tinny with little bass and poor balance. You can tell just from the tinny tone of the voice that says "Power on...Connected.), Very disappointing to see them degrade an excellent product. I returned it and got the Lakukom BH690A for $17.99(!!) vs $26 for the Senso. That one has the best sound I've ever heard in anything within double of this price point I can't believe how rich the bass is and how fantastically balanced the sound overall. They had me dancing in place with every song. Seriously, get them!

I could probably go a week's worth of use before the battery conked out. So, great battery life, it was sweat-proof, the ear hooks that come out, up and over-behind the ears were sturdier than the previous model. The only annoying thing was the flat cable, which, when sweaty, stuck to your skin enough that when you turned your head, the ear piece(s) pop out. Fast-forward about 9 months in, i started noticing that the battery life was shorter and shorter to the point where I could only get by barely after ~75-90min. Over the last 2 months (Months 11 & 12), when the battery charge has been depleted, it does not want to seem to charge. Once or twice, i just left it plugged, forgot about it for 3-4 days and it resuscitated from zero charge, but it will not 'top off'. No lights turn on if I try to charge it. title: Not Audiophile, But Listenable.
text: One has to understand that these are very inexpensive buds. So I have adjusted my expectations to accommodate this fact. First, I found the ear hooks to be useless. My Hopday buds stayed in my ear better (note: Each person's ear hole is unique and this weighs heavily on how well a bud stays put!). I did try different sizes. I am using these with my Apple SE phone. Note: The sound tends to be on the dark side with good very low bass extension. I actually found them more open sounding as they started falling out of my ear and stabilized in that position. I found that choosing "Electronic" in the EQ settings to help the sound balance a lot. All this is, of course, personal preference. The bluetooth strength was reasonable. Found them to work best on the right side of my body with the phone back facing out. Helps reduce dropouts (the receiver is in the right bud). This tends to be common with buds. Battery life is excellent if you're not blasting the ear wax out. I tend to save my "drums" by keeping the sound quieter. Bottom line: yes I like them. I would be more satisfied if they sounded a bit more natural and crisp instead of dark and a bit muddy. My Hopdays were better in that area.

text: For the price, you can't really beat these earbuds. I own several pairs of the different models, and i've yet to have an issue with any of them. These aren't audiophile grade earbuds, so don't purchase them expecting sound lab quality, you'll be disappointed. The bass is decent as are the mids and highs. They can be further dialed in if the device you're using them on has an EQ. I can't comment on the Bluetooth 5 spec portion as i haven't had a chance to test the actual range (Bluetooth 5 is supposed to have a range of about 800 feet or almost 3 football fields) but i wouldn't expect that to hold true of any device currently on the market. I can pair these with my phone and easily walk around my entire house without losing a signal. Battery life is consistent with what's advertised, and i typically get around 7.5 hours. What i like best about the Senso brand of Bluetooth headphones though are the hooks that hold them to your ears and the different ear tips. Not everyone can wear Apple earbuds, they simply don't fit my ears. I have had other BT earbuds and while great, they fall out from time to time which can be a hassle. These stay put and the fact that you can work out with them and even shower with them after the gym or whatever you're doing is a huge plus. I stocked up on these purchasing several extra pairs as losing or breaking more expensive sets are costly to replace, when for a fraction of the cost you can simply buy another set. You should be able to get 2-3 pairs of these for the cost of a comparable higher end product. I Could not recommend them more.

title: Disappointing fit and features, Dead in less than a year
text: Update May 2020 contd: Customer service to the rescue. After doing a factory reset, it's working again: Here are the instructions for resetting the headphones: 1. Reset the Senso headphone to factory settings (while plugged into a power source, press/hold the power button for 7 seconds). 2. Unplug the headphone from charging cable and power them on. 3. Enter the earbuds into the pairing mode and follow instructions for connecting. Also, the headphones may not connect to your devices after you perform the reset. The previous connections that you had established between the headphones and your devices become "obsolete" after the reset and needs to be re-configured. In order to do that, please `Forget the Device` on your mobile phone for the Senso headphones and try pairing again. In your Bluetooth settings on your phone, you will see all detected Bluetooth devices. Click on the Senso ActivBuds option and click on Forget this Device. Next pair your headphones to your mobile device once again as shown in the instructions manual. Update May 2020: less than a year later, dead. I can hear the 'too loud' tone, I can hear it say it's turning on/ connecting off but no sound otherwise. It stopped in the middle of an audiobook so it wasn't damaged in the wash. I needed a wireless headset for exercises (HIIT) and while doing housework. I only listen to speech (news and audiobooks) so I can't speak to the music sound quality. No noise cancellation. Washing dishes? Can't hear a thing. Low battery message is loud and seems to start at anything less than 50%? It links to the phone, shows 70% battery then 20 minutes later low battery! It's loud alert. Then done. The fit: it falls out during side planks and jumping jacks. Stays on when I'm walking at least. For calls: likely due to the placement of the microphone, callers have said my voice is very faint. At least this isn't my main purpose for the headset.

title: These are great.
text: Bought these for my husband, who has pretty high standards for audio products. My only complaint is that if you don't get a case for them right away, the case that comes with them is very prone to scratching. Keep these out of your pockets until you can find a case for the case to go into!

title: DOESN'T GIVE ME MIGRAINES! And great design
text: 20 min usage review. I will update if anything changes. I've tried 3 other much more expensive pairs of ear buds (bose, apple, Sony) before landing on these. The others would hurt my head, L ear, and trigger migraines, which I rarely get. Some you couldn't turn noise processing off. These samsung ones cause a very small amount of pain near the left ear, but it is bearable, which I'll take for the convenience of buds. You can also adjust the ambient noise volume, and turn off processing completely. The ambient mode sounds natural and there's next to no latency unlike I noticed on higher end buds. Controls are intuitive. Additionally, the design is sleek and feels well built. The material feels like airpods through and through, which I love. It's portable and not clunky, easy to open and close. The small size is very comfortable and easy to insert. The audio quality is great. It has crisp highs, decent lows. It's better than my bose soundlink, although those have literally been dragged through the mud multiple times, so take that with a grain of salt. Small complaint: it didn't come with a USB c charger like it said. (I ordered refurbished) Update: still love the buds. Some minor complaints: ears get itchy sometimes, buds get warm occasionally, buds may play music when you're adjusting the bud due to the tap, but these can be changed in settings. Tap is on both sides (annoying for adjusting). Mic works well as far as I can tell. Great battery life. Buds kind of stick together due to magnet which is good if you're setting down.

I can only have 1 in because I need to have an ear free to hear around me so I knew it wouldn't be 100% but something was better than nothing. But you cannot even activate the noise cancellation with only one in. On top of that, they constantly fell out of my ears. Just bending over they would pop out. I get about 30-35k steps in a day so I walk a little bit. Every couple dozen yards or so I have to push them back in my ears because they're sliding out. But not just once, when you push them in it thinks you're trying to pause the music so you have to hit it to push it in and then once again after a couple seconds of waiting to un-pause the music. I have been loyal to Samsung brand for well over a decade now from Laptops, TV's monitors, PC parts, cell phone, they make it I'll usually try and buy their version of it. title: Ok for price
text: The quality of the product is excellent. Case is solid and seems like something that would cost more. Ease of set up is as good as you can get. They were half charged when I got them so I was able to try them immediately. Took out of box, paired, listen to music. The cable being integrated in to the case is super cool. Nice and compact really cool tech. I definitely like the true wireless design. I have others that wrap a wire around the back of your head and it is annoying. These are true freedom. I'm not versed in audiophile language so... I'll just say they could use a much more powerful sound? Edit.. Went back to my Jaybird freedoms which I only paid $20 more for than the Jlabs. When I listened to the Jaybirds after spending a couple days with the JLabs, I realized they simply blow away the JLabs in sound. I mean it's not even close. I really want to lose the wire that goes around the back of my head, but the sound tradeoff isn't even close to being worth it. I will switch to completely wireless buds one of these days, but it looks like I'll probably have to spend a lot more than 50 bux. However, I do stand by my review of the quality of build. text: I listen to music almost constantly and have several sets of headphones and earbuds. These became my favorites when I heard the first song through them. I never have had them in long enough to see if they will go for 6+ hours but they easily hit 5 1/2 hours and are still comfortable when I take them out. I really like the touch sensors for volume control and track/pause/etc. The Bluetooth range is average - nothing special but good enough. When I first used them I would have occasional drop outs from one or both ears but that has vanished. I highly recommend these for their good audio quality, comfort, and battery life. title: Nice earbuds for the price
text: I just bought a second pair. These are really nice ear buds for this price. I listen mostly to audiobooks so I don't worry too much about audio quality but I think the quality of these buds is very decent. They come with a wide range of adapters so nobody should have a problem with fitting them. They also come with small "fins" which make a real difference. Not sure if this is intended but I found them to provide outstanding (passive) noise canceling. The charging case works great. In my use as ear buds for listening on audiobooks while taking my dogs on walks I found the batteries too last forever. The buds connect to each other and my iPhone Xs rapidly and without fail. Couple of issues: The USB connection attached to the case looks a bit flimsy (but then again I actually prefer it over the need for a separate micro-USB cable). I found the controls to take some getting used to. You have to press the ear buds in just the right place to get the desired effect. And I'm having a hard time trying to remember which bud to press how many times for which function, but I guess that's just me getting old...

I haven't worked out with them yet to see how they hold up to sweat. The sound is not spectacular but I'm also not an audiophile that needs a perfect performing device. So, I'm very happy with the sound, which can be adjusted. They sync up pretty easily with my fitness watch and my phone. My only complaint is that they are advertising 14 hours of battery life. I haven't gotten anything near 14 hours out of these things. Currently, my battery life record is about 4.5-5 hours.....that's pushing it. I'm not blasting them in my ears. But, they're not of a quality that you get a good sound at low levels either., so I had to find a happy medium volume. If you're looking for a quality, budget wireless bud I would recommend the J-Labs.

title: They plain didn't work well for me.
text: I live in the middle of the Chicago loop, and after buying a cheap pair of bluetooth earbuds that had connection issues, I wanted to find a pair of truly wireless earbuds that would hold a connection in the heart of the city. title: Love 'em!
text: I honestly love these little things. I've been eyeballing them since Wired posted a rave review about them online a few months ago. For the past couple of years, I've been searching for a quality, affordable pair of truly wireless headphones, but it hasn't been until recently that manufacturers have seen the demand and started producing them at affordable prices. I was less-than-enthused about spending several hundred dollars on Bose wireless headphones when they're extremely bulky-looking, and the reviews for them aren't exactly positive. I can't say enough good things about the JLab ear buds, they fit great out of the box, and pairing them with my Android was a breeze. I also love the adorable little charging case they came with, and it's so convenient that they instantly pair with my phone as soon as I take them out of said case. Also love the little included "cush-fins" that secure the buds in your ear a little more securely. Only downside to these is there are a ton of commands for button functions (pause, play, skip forward, volume up/ down, etc.), and it's hard to remember which earbud does which thing, and how many times to press said button for which function, etc. I love that it does so much, but it's almost a little too complicated. I really like how registering the earbuds was super simple, too. All I had to do was forward an email from JLab to a registration email address, and it was pretty much instant. I don't know about anyone else, but I find registering items for warranties to be a hassle, so it was really nice to be able to do that so quick. I'd recommend these to anyone in the market for a great quality set of wireless headphones that do double duty at moderately canceling out background noise, especially for my fellow runners. It's really nice not to have any cables or wires or big, bulky headphones bouncing around on your neck or head when you're just trying to focus on getting a quality workout in.

title: Safe buy, fair to middling sound
text: I actually got these wit the intent to use on my pc, as I use my Airpods pro on my phone. Pairing on the PC is actually VERY easy, and was almost done without realizing it. Place the buds in the case, then put both in your ears, then go through standard pair on the computer, boom. They are recognized as both a sound and communication device. You want to make sure they're registered as the sound device, as communication strips all of the sound quality from the audio stream. The device being push-button instead of capacitive isn't as much of a factor for PC sound, but having the right bud control volume up and left control volume down is fairly intuitive. Comfort-wise, I've gone through both extremes on the pre-installed eargels. I've had scenarios where it feels like it's slicing into my cartilage, and I've had several hours where I'd forgotten that they were even in. I use these primarily in concert with my Oculus Rift, as the built-in speakers stopped working. They work perfectly in this case, as they're low enough profile to not interfere with any of the hardware, and I don't have to worry about them getting knocked out or jostled with adjustments. Sound-wise, they're a little weak, but that's setting the expectation against tests with more premium TW earbuds. For the $50 paid, I'm more than satisfied.

Good for podcasts and music but probably not for phone calls. --- There are only two issues I see with these earbuds as mentioned in the title of this review. The max volume being a little low is personal preference technically. My girlfriend says 80% max volume is almost too loud for her but for me, 100% max volume needs about 20% more volume for my "rocking out" mode. I like to be aware of my surroundings when I'm in public so listening to 1 earbud is super important. The right earbud works just fine by itself but not being able to pair the left earbud is a major flaw. In a scenario where I'm on a long flight, I was hoping to get 4 hours out of the right earbud, put it back in the charger and then get another 4 hours out of the left earbud while the right one is charging so I'm never without my podcasts. After reading the Q&A and trying multiple times to only pair the left earbud, I realize this is not an option now. Outside of these two flaws, the earbuds are very comfortable, lightweight and the sound quality is great. Bass boost is VERY good compared to other wireless earbuds I've tried. title: Terrific commuter headphones
text: I take the bus downtown to work, and like to muffle the sounds of ambient conversations, bus and other city noises. I also like listening to music and audiobooks to boost my spirits and occupy my mind. In-ear headphones are uncomfortable and typically fall out of my small ears. Over-ear headphones muffle better and have better sound quality, but are bulkier and heavier to wear and store. These on-ear headphones muffle enough so I am not so irritated by the environmental sounds, and provide acceptable sound quality for my music and audiobooks, especially for the price! They work fine for hearing phone conversations, but I have not had success with a mike on these phones --not sure there is one-- so I just hold my phone to my mouth to talk. I like the way they look--the muted gray does not attract too much attention, but the subtle purple trim on the inside of the headband and earphone cups makes me happy when I look at them. They also fit better around my neck when I don't have them on my ears, and take up less storage space in my locker or commute bag. I appreciate the modest price. I figure people can pay as much or as little as they want for a product that will meet their needs, and I prefer to pay less.

text: My work bought each person in my branch a pair of QC25’s from Amazon. I also own a set of QC2’s. I have to say, whether I’m wearing my QC25’s or QC2’s, I love my Bose QC headsets and will not travel without them. I also use them for work, not just at work. Since I have both a pair of the old and new, I thought I’d do my own comparison: 1. Equally comfortable 2. In a quiet environment, where noise cancelling isn’t really a factor, I think the sound quality (even of the older QC2’s) is pretty comparable. If I were thinking about upgrading just for sound quality, I don’t think I would. 3. Noise cancelling has definitely improved in the QC25’s over the older QC2’s. In a noisey environment where noise cancelling matters, the difference is noticeable. The QC2’s are good, the QC25’s are clearly better. 4. The QC25’s will work w/o a battery. If the battery dies in the QC25, you will have music, just not NC. In the older QC2’s, the headphones would not work at all w/a dead or no battery. 5. QC25’s have a mic for taking or making phone calls. The QC2’s did not. 6. The case is smaller, but just as protective for the QC25’s. The QC2’s do not fold up as small. 7. They both look good. 8. The prices really haven’t changed over the years. The bottom line, I love my Bose headsets, both of them. I would absolutely recommend buying a set, particularly if you have a need for a set of quality headphones at work or for travel. For me, after reviewing the older and newer QC headsets, I don’t think I’d upgrade until the older QC2’s stopped working. I think that Bose headsets are built so well, that time doesn’t diminish the quality and utility of Bose’s older products.

title: Bose QC25 Headphones
text: This is a tremendous product, as fit for purpose as a product could possibly be. There are some better headphones out there in terms of audio quality, but for noise cancellation, nothing even comes close to the Bose 25s. I had the Sony equivalent, which were about 2/3 of the cost (hence my purchase of the Sonys), and they were NOTHING compared to the Bose for noise cancellation. In addition, the QC25s are extremely comfortable for my large head and ears, and I can wear them as long as needed with no fatigue. I use the QC25s to work out on a treadmill and watch a small TV while my wife uses a rowing machine and watches the main room TV at full volume. With any other headphones, or even with the QC25s and noise cancellation turned off, it's a cacophonous madhouse - a giant TV blasting, exercise equipment and fans running, etc. - I can barely hear my own TV at all no matter how loud I turn it up. But when I turn on the noise cancellation, almost all of the noise in the room just ... disappears, and I can comfortably listen to my own TV show at a low volume. It doesn't eliminate "all" background noise; for example, you can still hear voices and some higher-pitched sounds. But it almost entirely eliminates low frequency noise, background hum, buzz, fans, and other constant/ambient sounds. These headphones are nothing short of phenomenal. The price seems ridiculous, but they are worth every penny if you can afford them. In case it's ambiguous, just to be clear I ***love*** this product. I wouldn't even consider getting on a plane without these.

title: Great update to QC15s
text: A friend had these headphones for a review, and was nice enough to lend them to me for a week to see what I thought. I have owned the QC15 headphones, the SoundLink around-ears, and the AE2i headphones. I also have a half dozen or so cheap over-ears of various makes that I use for recording. My go-tos are SkullCandy Aviators. I found the QC25s an improvement over all the other Bose I've used. First, the noise-cancellation is just great. The real reason to get these headphones is the cancellation. The previous Bose I've had were fine, but these are far, far better. I noticed no hiss, no distortion, no real change in frequency of the source sound. I was really impressed, even when comparing it to older Bose headphones. And, crucially, they still sound great with noise-canceling off. The headphones were very comfortable as well. They were good for wearing for at least a couple hours, unlike the QC15s, which I found to be irritating after an hour or so. They were maybe a little less comfortable than the AE2i, but that's a pretty high bar. The sound was great, but like all Bose, the bass was boosted significantly. Most people like this. I prefer something a little flatter, but I can't fault the Bose sound, either. The bass boost was particularly useful for spoken content, which was clear even in noisy conditions. The headphones come with a nice case, into which they fold up very nicely. The cable is detachable, which I think makes them last much longer. They also come with an airplane adapter, which I suppose is a nice touch. There are two version of these headphones, one for iOS and one for Samsung/Android devices. The Android version controls do NOT work with iPhone.

title: Most comfortable flight ever

title: Great, as advrrtised.
text: Still fairly new, but thus far amazing, especially while flying. Work as advertised. Aids relaxation. Easy to use.

title: Love it for what it is !
text: Love it for what it is ! Well, I mean, be aware you are paying mostly for the fancy noise cancellation. I ride BART here in SF bay area every day and this changes the way the commute feels. It is now far less tiring and much more tolerable. First it "blocks" a lot noise. Just by putting them on without even turning the noise cancellation on you will see a significant difference. Once you turn the noise cancellation is it near quite. No, it will not completely eliminate all noise but majority of it. It blocks most low to mid frequency noise. You will still hear some hiss. And I like that I can still hear when the train operator makes announcements. It is also very light weight and very comfortable to wear for extended periods. My primary headset before this one was an Audio-Technica M50x. The M50x is bit heavier and slightly less comfortable in comparison but sounds much better than Bose. And I still prefer to use my M50x over this Bose when I am sitting at my desk without much noise around. One strange thing I noticed with the Bose is that even when I am in bedroom with no noise the music sounds better with the noise cancellation switch in on position. (don't tell me it is the white noise from home appliances and such, I know the difference) And lastly for any Windows Lumia Phone users out there, you'd be happy to know the control functions (play,pause and volume) on Android version work with my Lumia 640.

title: Winner in comfort and noise canceling, hands down
text: To be clear: I've never owned QC15 headphones before. I'm coming from a pair of AudioTechnica Studio phones. Main reasons for purchasing: Comfort and noise canceling. My previous over-ear headphones have ever-so-slightly better sound quality, but after wearing em for an hour or so my ears would start to hurt. Also, I didn't enjoy the fact that I needed to crank the music to drownout background noise when on a call or just working. I can wear these headphones all day without any pain (And are REALLY comfortable) as well as being able to play music at a lower volume. Will noise canceling block every single noise out? No... it's not a vacuum! That said, it does pretty well with reducing noises that it doesn't eliminate, so really, a non-issue. Only improvement would be with sound quality. Don't get me wrong, it's still pretty darn good. I guess quality is affected by construction of noise canceling aspects in headphone. So right: if you want a headphone with pretty good sound AND noise canceling - this is your winner. If noise canceling isn't your draw, probably should look elsewhere.

title: Works great in our new "Open Office"
text: We moved to our new office, from a private SCRUM room with just my team to a brand-spanking-new building with an "open" floor plan. Basically this means there are no walls, high ceilings, low cube walls and no offices. Everyone is practically just out in the open. And i knew that meant lots of noise. Don't get me wrong, the new building is beautiful, spacious, and has a lot of new fancy gadgets and features with nice, modern materials. But we have no drop ceiling, and my team sits right under the air handler, and you constantly hear people walking around and talking all day. Plus they are pumping in white noise on top of all this, so it honestly gets a tad annoying. These headphones have been a life saver. When I have had enough of the constant noises I simply pop them on, flip the switch and it's like zen...total silence. So much to the point that people usually have to tap be to get my attention, which is fine by me because it means I get left alone a lot more when I have them one vs. off. Sound quality is good. By this I mean the actual audio when listening to music or movies. They are not heavy in the base department, but that suites me and my tastes in music quite well (mostly classic rock, Radiohead, 90s alternative, etc). If you like bumping to the beat these might not be the pair for you. Movies sound good to me as well...nothing to brag about, but definitely like cheap sounding at all. Materials seem of quality. I can't speak to how long they will last as mine are not really that old. I have read reviews of people complaining the headband broke, but it seems well enough made to me that if you take good care of them they shouldn't break. Fit-wise I think they are perfect for my head. I am a 7 1/4 hat size, and don't have like huge ears or anything, and I keep them adjusted all the way down and can wear them all day with no discomfort at all. In fact, other than the silence, I sometimes forget I have them on at all.

title: Excellent noise cancelling
text: Good sound quality, and nose cancelling is surprisingly good. It works especially well for 'steady' sounds, like airplane engine or train.

title: Literally one of the best purchases I've ever made!!!!!!!
text: Literally one of the best purchases I've ever made!!!!!!! When I'm really stressed (or traveling) noise makes me rage! Granted I live in a big city, in an apartment with annoying downstairs neighbors that love to bang and slam everything and the annoying neighbors across from them that have a one year old. They also love to bang and slam every door they have and are just overall obnoxious thanks to their outdoor patio that's right outside our living room windows. If I'm slammed with work or have to write a 25 page paper last minute because I procrastinated a bunch, annoying people really annoy the crap out of me! And then my frustration goes from the stress of whatever I'm having to do to a rage. Pure rage. Sounds are a big trigger of mine. And traveling is even worse. Duh, I don't need to even go into it. Not only do these do an amazing job at just drowning out noise by themselves, when you turn on music you can't hear anything else but that. I don't know how they do it. I read something about an algorithm. And I've literally wanted to buy these forever since they came out. But then I went on a 3 hour flight with a screaming, screeching, crying 3 year old (with fully developed lungs). Never again. I was a ball of anxiety for the rest of my trip. Never again! Instant purchase. Instant success. Best thing ever. I would love to even buy the in-ear ones. This shouldn't even have a price. They should just say "PRICELESS" or "LIFE NECESSITY" or something like that. Would buy again. Like 5 times over.

title: Audiophile ... not even close.
text: These are decent headphones for MP3 or compressed old style iTunes music and as such get 1 star, but when I compared them to a pair of headphones from any of several other true (no gimmick) headphones, these fall to sub par and not even close to being worth the money. They isolate you like so many others like those from Sony and other companies (Grados are really good if you don't need to be isolated), but in terms of real "life like" sound, forget it. The bass, especially, is not close to being accurate. Noise canceling headphones in general do so by sending your ear a signal that is opposite from what it picks up outside. Right there they have changed the music you hear. These may work for people who don't really care about the quality of the music, but with the new style music players, like Pono among others, and the big move to higher quality downloads and AIFF files on an iPod, Bose falters big time. For MP3 or basic old downloads they are reasonable, but not if you really like your music. If you want to hear what is good, at least go check out some of the ones from the better audio companies so you can make an honest decision. One listen to one of the better brand names at an audio store was all that was necessary for me.

title: High quality sound and extremely comfortable
text: I've used these daily for the past 6 months and my only regret is not buying them sooner. The sound cancellation is top-notch and the sound quality is better than anything else I've owned. When the sound cancellation is turned off, the bass is less distinct, but the sound isolation is still great. I particularly like how comfortable these are. I wear glasses and they aren't painful or annoying to wear over ear portion of the glasses. They go over my entire ear nicely without touching or annoying them. The price is high, but so is the quality. I highly recommend purchasing these from an authorized dealer like Amazon or Bose direct because there are a large number of visually-convincing knock-offs. Be very wary of buying second-hand.

title: Good earphones with a minor flaw.
text: Here goes. For starters, the earphones are comfortable, very comfortable. The quality seems good I'm pleased with that. Noise cancelling works, although it seems as if you're on an airplane but it works. I don't think it's meant to cancel out all of your loud close up noises but it works pretty darn good. I do t hear people talking when they are more than a few feet away, few meaning 3 or more feet. Now for some reason the lows at times get kinda weird. Sometimes it seems like the bass is too much and I get a rattle and then at other times, it's ok. I know songs have different levels of bass but I'm talking about on the same song just played at different times. I can't figure that one out. Now if you're looking for smooth mellow volume earphones, these are it. If you want loud music in you ear, then may may want to go for another set of earphones. I listen to a lot of jazz so it's not the banging bass and loud music people want to listen to. Just mellow music. I'm not a earbud type of guy. These are just fine for what I need. I have other BOSE speakers that handle bass when I want to hear it loud, just not in my ears.

title: How QC25 quality after 2 years heavily usage
text: I bought QC25 2 years ago. Now it is the good time to provide a unbiased review based on my daily usage. I almost travel every week to some cities. Use QC25 during my flight, that headset never failed me a little, excellent noise cancellation and super good quality. However few weeks ago that headset broke, right ear side did not work at all. It failed after extremely 2 years heavily usage, I am not surprised. Called BOSE support, they offer me a new QC25 headset as replacement for 68 dollars. No need to spend 350 dollars for a new QC35, I am quite satisfied with BOSE support. But let you guys know no matter QC25 or QC35, it has design issue with right ear side, most likely it will be broken in 2 years. I strongly suggest you use the credit card which cover 1 year extended warranty to buy Bose headset to cover future replacement costs.

title: Good value at $100
text: I bought this as a gift for my wife as she likes Bose. She had an old Sony noise cancelling headphone that was falling apart. I have quite a few headphones and earbuds. My reference is an AKG K240; the downside is that it is difficult to drive due to its high impedance. My next in line is an Audio Technical ATH M50. I also have a BlueTooth Audio Technica ATH AR3BT; it is not in the same league as the other two. This Bose has excellent noise cancelling performance. It cuts out surrounding noise very effective. It is also very comfortable to wear; my wife is very picky about this. In terms of sound quality, It ranks clearly a distant third. Both my AKG and Audio Technica sound more open and airy. This Bose is better than the ATH 3BT though. My experience with noise cancelling headphone is that they do take some quality away, which is why I don't own any right now. This Bose is a good value at the BF price but not at the regular price.

title: Very nice.
text: These are great headphones with good noise cancelling. Keep in mind noise cancelling will not cancel out ALL sound but designed to tune out common undesirable frequencies such as rumble from a jet or a car engine. The tuning on these is much closer to natural...another popular brand is purposely bass heavy which is a matter of taste. I have a set of studio speakers I enjoy more if noise cancelling is not required but these are very nice on their own and for flights are amazing. If wanting more bass go with Beats (though I can't comment on their noise cancelling), if want pure and don't need noise cancelling check out Shure.

title: Best noise cancelling headphones on the market. Just not great in sound.
text: Before you make your purchase, you have to ask yourself how important the noise cancellation feature is. If the feature is up there on your list of needs or wants, you won't go wrong with the QC-25's. Bose sets the noise cancellation bar real high. They're the leader in the industry. No other headphones can match it. In fact, these totally outshine the next headset in line by a lot... the next being the QC-15's. These are far better than the QC-15's, which were already great, but the QC-25 outclasses the 15's in both sound quality and noise cancellation. They do it while making the headphones more attractive and with a higher quality feel. It's still plastic, but you can twist and turn these with little creaks or feel of it breaking. The QC-15's didn't feel like that. At least not the ones I had. So why the negative review? Well where these headphones fail, is in the audio quality department. The bass and treble seems to be on one linear line. The sound is just really really flat. I'm sure on a plane ride they'd serve you fine, but if you want just a little more oomph, you might find it elsewhere. For $300, that's why I'm left disappointed. Yes they sound better than the Beats, which have almost too much bass, but they don't sound as great as Sennheiser Momentums. You almost always have to have the NC activated. Believe it or not, they sound even worse with the NC turned off. 1 star might be a little harsh, but again, for the money spent to get a pair of these, Bose could have done a lot better with the sound quality. Look at the Sennheiser and don't look back. Pros: *Best noise cancellation period. No hiss or under water feeling with them on. *Attractive design. *Comfortable. You can wear them for hours and no feel fatigue. Cons: *Expensive. *Sound is very uninspiring.

title: Best damn noise canceling out there.
text: This is the 3rd pair of noise canceling headphones I have tried and there is no contest, these are absolutely the best. title: Works great (in the right environment)
text: these work great--as long as your expectations are realistic. They are very good at canceling background sounds that are constant and even. Any sounds that are momentary come through loud and clear. I use these while driving a tractor which (due to the hydrostatic drive) runs at full RPM all the time. These headphones cut the engine sound by about 2/3. However, any other sounds are still just as loud (rocks being hit by mower deck, etc.) Listening to music is super clear, even in that loud environment. In fact, i'm hearing words in old songs more clearly than I ever have before... (Apparently, Benny and the Jets have electric "boots"... Who knew?) My wife tried using these headphones while mowing lawn on a zero-turn mower. They did not do as well in that environment because the background sound changes so rapidly (engine sounds, hydraulic wheel drives, etc. are not smooth and even levels or pitches.) for that environment, she prefers to use drummer's headphones. Those don't have active noise cancellation, but they are better at passive isolation. I had a pair of bose noise canceling headphones about 5 years ago. I didn't like them--when active, they audio sensation felt like a kind of 'pressure' in my ears. This new model doesn't feel/sound anything like that. Much better technology.

text: Unfortunately these are not as good as the model they replace (the QC15) My primary use for noise cancelling headphone is long haul flights - they save my ears and allow me to sleep. The problem lies in their construction - the flimsy plastic headband transmits noise from your average seat headrest which defeats the noise cancelling. The noise cancelling itself seems no better than my QC15s although sound quality might be improved. I did consider the QC35s however the bluetooth performance (range and battery life) is unimpressive. In addition, at a similar price-point I get better overall performance, utility and (in particular) battery life from my PCX550 (Sennheiser) headphones. Overall, if you are flying, I'd recommend finding a pair of QC15s (they are discontinued but can still be found on ebay) but regardless these are very good noise cancelling headphones and I'm not planning to trade them in!

title: Great but not for Me
text: First I want to start off by saying that I do not own these headphones but I tried them on several times with many different songs. Pros Sound amazing (but their Bose so don't you except that) Amazing Noise Cancellation Cons Expensive (but you pay for quality) Uncomfortable Bulky Amazing noise cancellation that takes awake some of the quality I tried many different Bose Headphones on as well as a few other brands. I ended up buying the Bose Soundlink Bluetooth on ear headphones. I was standing in a very busy Best buy when trying these and when I put them on and took them off I couldn't believe how well they worked to cancel all the noise in the store. Your ears get used to the noise I guess but these blocked out the fork lift, the chatty customers and children running around and this was before I started playing music. When I started playing music it sounded amazing until I tried on the Bose Bluetooth headphones and realized how much dimmer the active noise canceling makes the music. I didn't care for the around the ear headphones because they were pushing my earrings into my skin and it was painful - and I was just wearing slightly large studs. In the end I chose the Bluetooth version because I don't need the complete noise canceling even though the Bluetooth end up canceling the noise by blocking and with the music playing. Also I hate being tethered to the wire.

title: Still best ANC i’ve seen
text: At $120, it was too good to pass up. Very comfortable, very pleasant sounding with amazing noise cancellation. Nothing like going through an airplane ride without the constant hum of the jet engines.

title: Broke within a week!
text: Within a week the noise cancelling function stopped working completely. Before that, they were great.

title: Great Sound at a Great Price
text: I purchased these at about half the list price because newer models are here, but at that price it was an incredible value and the sound is excellent.

title: BOSE - Absolute "BEST"
text: I've tried most of the top brands in headphones and no one comes close to the quality,sound & durability of Bose Q25. The noise canceling on these headphones is unbelievable, know matter if you're on a plane or in your home. When you turn on the noise canceling switch on the headphones all outside noise disappears. By far these are the best sounding headphones on the market, some may say the price is too high but if you want quality then price is not an issue.

title: Five Stars
text: These work great for home schooling. Helps my son stay focused from small noise distractions.

title: Buy some extra double A batteries!
text: I wanted some "wired" headphones specifically for my table computer. They are so good my wife has to physically tap me on the shoulder to be acknowledged....scary! My test for great headphones uses the "Good Morning" into "Sgt. Pepper's reprise" from the most recent version of "Peppers." Using this model allows me to hear Lennon say "Good Bye!" plus something that sounds a lot like "break neck" repeated about three times along with "Ahhh, Dig it!" Bad thing? They can absorb some batteries!

title: Flimsy Cable, Again!
text: I have used a number of Bose headphones through the years because I like how they sound. Now half of my collection have broken cables and the other half I have to be very careful with them. Two of the headphones actually had their replacement cables broken again. Look at the Bose spare parts offered on Ebay and you can well see the flimsy cables is the number one problem of these otherwise wonderful headphones. Why Bose won't switch to thicker, tougher and better-looking cables as used by Beats is a complete mystery to me. May be they make good money replacing cables. I have not used this new headphone, but it apparently is keeping its flimsy cable. For that I have to give it a one-star. May be someone at Bose will listen.

title: The leather pads are hella comfortable, they are very soft and do not hurt ...
text: These headphones will change your life! I purchased these to use at the office, since we sit in rows and during the day it can get kind of loud. Typically I listen to it with active noise cancellation off. When it gets loud I flip the switch on. The leather pads are hella comfortable, they are very soft and do not hurt your temples at all, even if you are wearing glasses. The headphones are also very lightweight. The only drawbacks are that after prolonged periods of listening to it with active noise cancellation on, I get a little bit of ringing in my ears. I have also experienced slight amounts of nausea with active noise cancellation on. However, given my trance playlist and my copious amount of morning coffee, I do not know whether the ringing/nausea are caused directly by the active noise cancellation, and I have yet to do a rigorous scientific study.

title: Their Bose what more do you need to say?
text: Great product use them every time I fly which is several times a month. So happy I finally broke down and bought a pair of silencing headphones. When you wear them be realistic they don't block everything because nothing can.

title: Excellent product!
text: Best purchase I’ve made in a long time! A blessing on long international flights.

title: Product Review
text: Bought on sale. Very nice. Quiet and rather than bluetooth, I really like the cable. It is medium weight, not like the thin ear buds or huge like the sonys studio version. These are quiet and the battery seems to last a long time. I did a 13 hour flight from Moscow to Los Angeles recently surrounded by young kids and stinky babies. Couldn't do much about the kicking and stink but the basic crying and constant chatter was blocked out by noise cancelling and 100dB Rolling Stones. These were a life saver. Not mine, theirs. One thing I really like about these is they use a aaa battery. They are small cheap and available anywhere. And the battery is only for noise cancellation so when it is dead and you put your spare battery in checked baggage, the earphones still work. So now I am keeping my 6S no matter what OS apple comes up with My QC-25 and my full frame camera. I have no reason to migrate to equipment that renders all my accessories useless.

title: My son is very pleased with them
text: Gave as a gift. My son is very pleased with them !

title: Junk!!
text: Right ear cutting in and out. This is same problem that others are having. Bose answer is to sell replacement unit for $225. Bose is aware of manufacturing problem but wants me to buy new one to replace their defective product. Buyers beware! Mine going in trash and never buy Bose again.

title: Mutes sound, plus other great design features
text: I work in a lab where we have alarms going off all the time. I can still hear the alarms but they're significantly muted. In that environment I like to use the noise cancellation without listening to music, so there's no need for the cable, giving me freedom of movement. When I first put them on I got a little dizzy -- maybe because my inner ear/balance mechanism was confused? But after a short while that problem went away. I've noticed that it seems to completely block out continuous background noises like fans for example. Otherwise, it just really mutes noises. I cannot overstate the value of having the extension cord unplug from *both* ends -- I've walked away from my computer before and forgot to take off my headphones and it just unplugs from the headphone side instead of ripping the wire out like on other headphones. These are also the most comfortable headphones I've ever owned -- I can wear them for hours straight. I cannot wear them all day long but I can wear them for about four hours before I feel a need to hear stuff.

title: Love this headset with my iPhone 6
text: IPHONE 7 WARNING: Love this headset with my iPhone 6, but when I got my 7 today, the mic is not working through the adapter into the lightning port. Hopefully there will be a resolution, as I really love these headphones and use them for conference calls from my home office all day long.

title: Great noise reduction earphones, work well.
text: I mow my 3 acres of lawn, plus a neighbor's lawn every week These earphones cut the mower noise down so low, I often look down to be sure the mower deck on my zero turn mower is working. I have a 24 horse engine and it sounds like a low purr. I have them attached to my iPhone. I listen to internet radio music. I also listen to internet radio old time mysteries when I mow. All sound great. They are comfortable. My ears don't hurt after several hours of waring them, unlike other non noise reduction earphones. I answer the phone with them on. I have to turn the mower off for that. The mike picks up well. The caller can hear me well. I can hear the caller very well. These are worth the money. I should have gotten noise reduction earphones years ago for all my loud noise jobs.

title: Great sound, comfortable, and unmatched noise cancellation
text: So far, I'm very impressed with the quality of the sound and the construction of these headphones. I read other reviews of others having problems with build quality and functionality, but I haven't experienced that. These are relatively pricey headphones, but the noise cancelling quality is the best I've experienced. Other pros: - Sound quality is very good, after initial burn-in - Very comfortable even after long listening sessions - These come with a really nice carrying case and an airplane converter plug I would recommend these to anyone wanting a solid set of 'phones for travel or everyday use.

title: Works but eats batteries
text: It works, but it eats batteries (it does not shut itself off, so if you forget, it's all over)

title: Five Stars
text: My husband loved them and the noise canceling is awesome! They were a winner Christmas gift here.

title: Comfortable and effective.
text: Comfortable to wear for long periods. Blocks low frequency noises like the "humming" sound from breathing and office chatter. I can hear notes in the songs I never heard before. Keeps me focused while working with all the office noise, even without music playing. Built-in mic to answer calls on my iPhone 6.

title: great noise cancelling headphones
text: Bose are the best - wouldn't want to go on an airplane without them

title: Amazing Sound Cancelling
text: The Bose QuietComfort 25 Headphones are well-crafted, fairly light weight and have rich, broad range sound. The real moment of truth is when you place them on your head, and with no music playing, activate the sound canceling switch on the ear piece. The effect is immediate and striking...quiet. One doesn't realize how much ambient noise there is until the sound canceling is activated. The carrying case is well designed and relatively compact. There is a space to carry a spare battery and a two pronged aircraft plug is included. One thing a wish was also included is an adapter for a full sized receiver plug. The over earphones are comfortable.

title: Amazing sound and keeps out surrounding sounds very well
text: Amazing sound and very portable. Perfect for flights or just needing to have some quiet time.

title: Noise cancelling works great! Sound is phenomenal
text: Noise cancelling works great! Sound is phenomenal, as to be expected from a Bose product. I'm not used to headsets over my ears and I found after an hour or so that they were not comfortable for me. They felt tight over my ears, even though they're nice and padded and soft.

title: Great sound, horrible design flaw!
text: Originally I gave this headset 5 stars, but now 2 1/2 years in and I'm revising to 1 Star. I still love the sound, quiet, comfortable, but there is a major design flaw that Bose seems to care less about. My first unit had the right ear speaker start cutting out 6 months in. Now just over 2 years with the replacement and again the right ear starts cutting out. There is some connection in the ear cups that fails over time. It's a well known problem with posts all over the Internet about it. If i tap or move the ear cup I can get it working for a time till I move my head. My current unit is now out of warranty and Bose offered me a replacement for $220. It's available brand new for $170 on Amazon right now! If you decide to buy I'd highly recommend an extended warranty!

title: No sound from right side right out of the box
text: The only positive comment I can come up with is that the Bose QC 25 headphones are attractive. On the other hand, I just got these 2 days ago and opened the box today; looking forward to trying them out. Put in battery, connected cable and plugged into my iPod Touch. There's zero sound in the right headphone. Tested iPod with my on ear Bose and sound is fine. Tested QC25 with multiple audio cables and none of them produced any sound on the right. I should have given more weight to all the 1/2 star comments about right side failure. I've used Bose speakers for years and they are exceptional & reliable - but they seem to have a real quality control/design issue with headphones. I suspect the unnecessarily tight wire connection to the individual sides is stressing connections. I'm returning and looking at Sennheiser and Beyerdynamics now.

title: Several upgrades from previous model makes these worth the price.
text: These are comfortable, sound good, and the build quality is great. A battery is included (and the case has a place for an extra, which is nice - there are several upgrades over the old model: The cord is detachable if damaged, and you can continue to use the headphones (with the same sound quality and volume, as far as I can tell) when the batter runs out on the noise-cancelling function. Worth the price for the quality.

title: Good noise cancelling, ok sound quality
text: I had the original noise cancelling Bose headphones and really liked those. On a trip this year the headphones died and never came back to life. Knowing I had some long flights coming up over the summer I picked up the latest headphones, the QC 25. The noise cancelling is great on these, as it was on my previous model. I can't say I noticed any improvement in the noise cancelling but I wasn't looking for any improvement over my last ones as they were already very good. I'm still not 100% happy with the music sound on these, compared to my original Bose headphones. The sound is good with regular music but they seem to struggle more with Heavy Metal and Hard Rock. The base sound seems to be bit off and I find myself having to turn up the volume more to get better sound, then I did with my other Bose headphones. The QC 25 does seem to have better clarity as I can hear individual instruments more clearly on these than other headphones. It is just overall, the sound isn't what I was expecting.

title: These are the best. They completely cancel out all sound
text: These are the best. They completely cancel out all sound. The best on the market.

title: Nice but expensive
text: Great headphones, but they are not completely noise canceling and very expensive. I take the train to work everyday and walk through busy city streets and can still hear a lot of what is going on around me. For example, I cannot hear nearby conversations, but I can hear sneezes, horns, and sirens. I recommend this product.

title: Noise cancelling very effective but not perfect
text: Noise cancelling works very well no only on white noises but also on speech and music. However, at high frequency the cancelling is less effective. Music playback quality is good. The frequency response is different when noise cancellation is turned on or off. Overall, high frequency response is lacking, making the sound a bit muffled. The headset is light and comfortable. The carrying case is a plus. However, mechanical design can be improved to make the headphone more compact when folded.

title: Wow!
text: These work so well that I'm having to fight my son for them! I've used them extensively on a road trip. Kept all external sound out and made spoken words very easy to hear. Music/video is also awesome! Typical Bose quality! I have not gotten them before because of the price but I couldn't pass at the Cyber Monday price! Glad I got them!

title: Great sound!
text: This is one of my favorite products from the BOSE brand, they are perfect for me because I use them on a daily basis while I take my three-mile walk around my neighborhood listening to my favorite music from Placido Domingo, Luis Miguel, Frank Sinatra using my old Sony Walkman. The sound is amazing, I can hear all the instruments used, perfect interpretations, perfect silence from outside noises. Very happy with my purchase, with great value.

title: Perfect for gaming & works with all consoles
text: By far one of my sons favorite Christmas gifts. He loves using it for gaming and it works great with his xbox one and Nintendo Switch. The mic works great for gaming and the outside noise is completely blocked out. I’m going to order myself a pair

title: Wonderful at making air travel pleasant
text: Great addition to airplane travel. They dramatically reduce the background noise that I perceive on a plane trip.

title: Too dollar for poor quality
text: From the day I’ve bought these the headphone jack had to be plugged in just so (plug all the way in then back out 1/32”) or it would lose sound in one or both ears. Also the noise cancelling aspect stopped working several years ago. Also the foam ear pads don’t hold up well to use. From now on I’ll be buying less expensive headphones, I expected more from Bose.

title: Don't go on a plane without these
text: I don't ever want to go on a plane without these. Makes any trip so much better.

title: I work in an office with an open architecture. ...

title: Five Stars
