title: MUST HAVE HEADPHONES!!!!!!!!!!
text: Literally the best headphones on the market not to mention the best noise cancelation over the ear headphones. They are a little pricey it is so worth it!!! Definitely get these headphones if you are thinking about it. Just what i would expect from Bose just better with a new modern look!

title: Does the job at an OK price
text: I work with some industrial noise and the damage and stress is felt at the end of the day. These are helping, but feel like I am underwater. If not for that strange feeling would say 5 star. I will be better able to concentrate, but wonder if I will get used to the clam shells.

title: The only headphones you will ever need
text: Amazing headphones, amazing noise cancellation, quality of the foam cushions is extremely soft. I recommend investing in some rechargable AA batteries. Ikea sells a great pack of 6 for $7. Love the headphones and have been using them daily for the past 4 months with absolutely no issue. I may get a pair of the wireless headphones (QC35) for lounging around the house when those drop in price!

title: Great sound, great suppression!
text: I use these al the time. They do a great job of sound suppresion and with music playing I am not disturbed at all. I really like the sound as well. You can crank these if you want and the sound does not distort. Only complaint is it goes through the regular triple A batteries. I would use recharables or get lithium batteries if you want more than 1 days worth out of the battery.

title: Awesome set of headphones !!!
text: Comfortable fitting over the ear. The noise cancelling is nice but it won't block 100% of ambient room noise. It does a nice job of blocking out ambient noise from a car or airplane seat. You won't hear normal conversation in the same room while wearing these headphones while playing music at normal volumes. If the battery dies or the noise cancelling is turned off you can still listen music but much of the bass will be lost. There is a compartment in the bose headphone case for a spare battery along with airplane headphone adapter (nice!) . Overall , I'm very please with the sound quality. I would prefer to have the bass heavier and punchier but I can adjust with an equalizer. For good clean sound as it was meant to be heard it is near impossible to beat Bose without paying over inflated prices on brands that perhaps millionaires only have access to.

title: Powerful noise cancelling, sounds like Bose
text: These are the strongest of the noise cancelling headphones. If that's your primary concern, you can't do better - big reduction in outside noise, and an even frequency rejection balance. Headphone amp inside is a little hissy, but you won't notice on a plain or in a loud room. They're also incredibly light and relatively compact, battery life is great. Unfortunately they sound like Bose. No LF, hyped upper midrange, not much HF. Great for speech intelligibility. If you listen to a lot of NPR they're perfect. If you love music keep looking.

title: Major disappointment
text: I don't mind paying big bucks for a quality product from a company that has a good reputation. These headphones are not worthy of the name BOSE. The electrical circuitry either has cheap material or has a bad design flaw. The connection to the left ear must be constantly repositioned to bring sound to both ears. When the first set failed after 10 hours of use, I returned it to Amazon. They replaced it quickly with another set. Now this one also has the same problem with the connection after just 10 hours of use. Don't buy it, you'll be sorry you did.

title: I love these!
text: I love these headphones! the noise canceling works very well. they are comfortable and light. The sound quality is good (as long as you have it turned on). and the battery lasts a long time. I have worn them for almost three weeks of work and the first battery hasn't died yet.

title: Improvement over QC15
text: Was waiting for the price on the QC25's to come down so I could upgrade from the QC15. Everything is better. Sound, comfort, noise cancellation.

title: Daughter loves them

I personally don't think any noise canceling headphones block out enough noise without the music playing, but I will admit, the music sound great though these. The low hum of the noise canceling without music playing would give me a headache, but perhaps that is just my sensitivity to white noise.

title: High quality!

Great sound quality, superb noise cancelling qualities bar none! and most of all, very, very comfortable to wear. Sincerely, Mike.

I go through a lot of headphones and these are the most comfortable that I've owned and over three years of having them and still function like new

title: Great quality!
text: These headphones were great! Though, I no longer use them, they were ol reliable for a long time. Upgraded to the 35s. Still one of the best headphones I've owned to date

title: Wish I Bought them Sooner
text: Finally pulled the trigger and bought a set of Bose noise cancelling headphones. I opted specifically for the QC25s vice the 35s for the fact they didn't have Bluetooth built in. I've had other noise cancelling headphones and ended up not liking the fit or the function of them. I decided I needed something over the ear to get the full benefit of the technology. After a bunch of research, I begrudgingly opted for these. I was more than a little surprised by how much better they worked than any other noise cancelling headphone I've used to date. Even in the noisiest part of the plane, they were able to completely mute the engine noise. The only exception was when the engines were at full throttle. At that point they do appear to get overloaded a give a crackling noise. Amplified sound seemed to be clearer and I could hear the overhead announcements without issue. While the sound quality in a noiseless environment doesn't compare to others, they do outperform anything I've used on a plane. Normally when I get off a long flight, I feel wore out and just want to get to the hotel and sleep. The last two flight when I've been wearing these, I've felt rested, in a better mode and had more energy.

title: Best sound, best noise cancelling on the market (while working)
text: Nicely packed, excellent unboxing experience, includes the AAA battery to operate the active noise cancelling feature. As soon as I put them on, I can notice the excellent passive noise isolating of these headphones. But Bose seems not to care much about the quality of their products. My headphones lasted less than 24 hours. I unplugged the cable in the headphones end and this damaged the internal female connector THE FIRST TIME! This is the extreme of bad quality Bose! Oh come on! I can't believe this just happened with a $200 headphones! I am very unsatisfied with this purchase. I bought this because of my excellent experience with a SoundTouch 20, wich sounds amazing. But now I figure out its not just about sound quality, its also about QUALITY! Bose, thumbs down for you.

title: Nice noise canceling
text: Purchased these for a UFlyMike setup. Haven't flown with it yet, but the noise canceling is great.

title: This thing is probably my favorite pair of headphones so far
text: This thing is probably my favorite pair of headphones so far. They sound better than my B&W P5, Sennheiser M2, and Master Dynamic MH40. Bass is well defined, midrange is open, treble is airy. The noise cancellation function works extremely well and I can't heard the ambient noise once activated. I can't do a review of these headphones without talking about comfort. They are the most comfortable headphones I have ever used! The build feels plasticy, but from what other people are saying, it should be durable. Time will tell. Works well for now.

title: It would be a good choice if you like light music and just wanted ...
text: It would be a good choice if you like light music and just wanted the noise-canceling. However as a headphone it is just a mediocre one, or even below average for the price.

title: Way better than QC15. I have both.
text: These are indeed much better than the QC15s. The only thing I could complain about is that the wire is a bit short. The wire on the QC15s was longer and thinner and the wire for these is thicker and notably shorter which can be kind of annoying. Other than that these totally rock. Keepers!

title: Very nice for the price
text: Price great and I use wire for Samsung phone, works great.

title: DO NOT BUY! They are great headphones...if you only have ONE EAR!
text: Just like the numerous other people out there, I had one side of my Bose QC25 headphones go out. I was lucky I guess that they lasted for about 2 years. From what I've read in these reviews and on Google searches, most people have them fail long before that. I handled them very carefully, always stored them in the case, and only used them on long flights a couple of times a year. So I guess I spent $300+ for maybe 6 to 8 uses. Sigh. Not a great return on my investment! The saddest part is that my backup pair are some Bose QC 3's that have been going strong since 2009! Obviously Bose is cutting some corners these days because the quality is dropping fast. I was going to replace these QC25's with a new QC35 model, but looks like those have the same problem with one ear going out. I will have to try Sony or Sennheiser instead, I guess. I have multiple Bose products and used to trust them as the gold standard, but I don't think I will ever buy Bose again.

title: ... friend of ours who came here from Sweden and hated being on a plane with all the noise which ...
text: These were for a friend of ours who came here from Sweden and hated being on a plane with all the noise which made it very hard to sleep, this was the answer he is very pleased...

title: Quality is Declining
text: This is the 3rd set of Bose headphones I've purchased. The first set (purchased in 2008) lasted 5 years. The second set (purchased in 2013) lasted 2 years. This set (purchased 2015) has conked out after 16 months. See the trend here?

title: Great product if you can get one on sale
text: Quality isn't the best but it's good. Sound is typically Bose, need more work. But noise cancelling basically class leading. Got it while on sale, which made it a good buy, other QC20 might be better.

title: GOOD NOISE CANCELLATION, POOR MUSIC REPRODUCTION
text: I've always been put off by BOSE's claim as being the most respected company in audio. Great marketing perhaps but not accurate. I bought these headphones for one purpose--air travel. For that that purpose their active noise reduction qualities work well and certainly better than other brands of noise cancellation headphones I've owned. I would rate them one star for music reproduction and four stars for noise cancellation. Unfortunately as an accurate audio reproduction device they are a fail. Bass extension is poor, upper high frequency reproduction is poor. Directly compared to a pair of Sennheiser HD 380 Pro (same price range as the discounted BOSE), the BOSE simply aren't in the same league. Subtle nuances on voices, reed instruments, are lost, with no depth. The BOSE make a plane trip tolerable but on the ground I won't be using them.

title: I don't understand the critical reviews.
text: I don't understand the critical reviews. I take consumer reviews seriously, and try to avoid products that have more than about 8% critical reviews (I recognize that some people have experiences with products that are either dead on arrival or don't last by more than a few months. I've had this item for about 6 months and have been very satisfied. I bought them directly from Bose after my earlier model broke (due to my own negligence). Bose offered this replacement for a relatively modest discount. The earphones are comfortable and seem to have better noise cancelling characteristics than the two prior models I had purchased. I especially like the clever way the phone fold for storage in the convenient carry case. Perhaps my only disappointment is that the product doesn't offer blue tooth capability, since it would be great to "cut the cord". On the other hand, I recognize that Bluetooth has its own issues. Perhaps Bose hasn't embraced the technology for its earphones because Bluetooth could create its own issues. Regardless, if you can afford them, I recommend the QuietComfort 25. Incidentally, the AAA battery doesn't seem to last as long as on my previous model, but this isn't an issue, since AAA batteries are cheap and plentiful. There's even a "bay" built in to the carry case to store an extra, along with an adapter for those annoying two-pronged connectors that still prevail on older airplanes.

title: Fantastic! Love my headphones
text: Fantastic! Love my headphones. Makes air travel a lot more enjoyable.

title: Great for recent trip.

title: Falling apart
text: Purchased this in 2014. Not even after a year the noise canceling stopped working even with fresh batteries. Now the foam is exposed around the ear. Pretty bummed about this and wondering if there's anything Bose can do to help out.

title: Perfect for airplanes.
text: Blocks all engine noise, but can still hear overhead announcements.

title: Best noise canceling headphones money can buy.
text: These are the best noise canceling headphones money can buy. I've tried several other brands and kept wanting the Bose. I like having the best and not settling for anything less. Once you get past the sticker shock you realize you get what you pay for. Completely satisfied with this purchase.

title: More than 1 year and best headphone ever
text: I am a software engineer and I use my headphone every day for at least 4-5 hours. It is comfortable to wear even if I am wearing glasses. The noise cancellation is very good for open space. The battery is impressive but I do not use the noise cancellation more than 1h-2h per day. I would say that I have to change the battery about every month, so probably about 20-30h.

title: I can listen to my music and not hear any noise from where I am (usually a subway or a commuter train). I can listen to the most
text: Better than the Beats Studio . I bought the Beats Studio about 5 months ago. They sounded good but they added a lot of clumsy noise in the top three volume bars. Felt like all the music was just being thrown at you at once without proper clarity. and I use my beats for work out and at work only in 5 months the head band had broken and I fixed it using a tape and my wife is using them. they are soo expensive and not reliable at all. But just today I bought these Bose QC 25 headphones and they are a class apart. They produce crystal clear music with precision to each and every note. Even at high volumes you can hear every note very clearly. And the best part is the LFE channel. I tried the dolby 7.1 channel test (video in youtube) on both the Beats studio and the Bose QC25 and guess what.....the Beats headphones could not even produce the LFE channel sounds at all where as the QC 25 totally nailed those effects. The 10.2 channel effects tests also sounded awesome. I can listen to my music and not hear any noise from where I am (usually a subway or a commuter train). I can listen to the most subtle instrument played and enjoy my music. QC25 is very reliable and sturdy, just to check them i tried to twist the hadback almoy 90 degrees and nothing happened. they are very light weight, i use for 4-5 hours at work and i do not feel i have something on my head. The only reason I bought Beats instead of Bose QC15 earlier was because I am a bass lover and the QC15s are not the best for bass. But the QC25 totally conquered that area too! The bass these produce is quite amazing. I am off to return my Beats Studio headphones! The Bose QC25 headphones are too good to be true! Definitely another masterpiece from Bose!

title: One year and one month
text: My husband bought these headphones for me, and they lasted one year and one month before the right earpiece started going out. The headphones have worked like a dream, as everyone describes them, and I had the previous model of these as well. But for $300, I expected to get 3 years of use out of these headphones, like the last model before its ear cushion wore out. Buy the extended warranty when you purchase these in case you're as unlucky as me. I'll be buying another pair with warranty once smacking these on the side of the headphone doesn't restore the functioning anymore, or if I can't find someone to repair them.

text: I'm probably not adding a lot to the thousands of reviews, but these have some of the most effective noise cancelling I've heard - comparable if not better than some of the top of the line current models from Bose and Sony. I also find them more comfortable. If you can still find them new in the $120 range, you can get top of the line noise cancelling and comfort for about 1/3 of the price if you don't mind a wire. The sound is acceptable (particularly for an airplane or transit), but I don't love it. I don't find the Bose QC35 particularly compelling either, but I've liked what I've heard from them a little better. The sound with noise cancelling off is terrible, but I guess it's better than nothing if the battery is dead. I prefer the sound of Audio Technica's similar models (ANC7,ANC9), but those are less comfortable and the noise cancellation is not as good. If you don't need noise cancellation, most normal headphones in this price range will sound better anyway - so for travel or needing to occasionally block out some noise in the office or at home I kept the Bose QC25 and got rid of my pair of AT ANC9.

They are great for work when you are stuck in the cubicle world and there conversations going on everywhere Music sounds crisp and clear when using the noise cancellation. The Bose QC25 has good range of sound but do not expect to get too much of the lows. The mids and highs are fantastic. If you like Jazz music then will love listen to Jazz with the QC25. Without the noise cancellation on music is just OK. My only issue is after wearing them for 30 to 60 minutes my ears get a little sore. I need to take them off for a while. I have tried re-positioning and adjusting then and I did find the sweet spot for the ears but they still get sore. I do not own the QC15 so I cannot comment on whether QC15 owners should move to the QC25. I did go try the QC15s at an electronic store. The noise cancellation seemed to be on par with the QC25; however, that was only having them on for a couple of minutes. My rating is 4 ½ stars. I am removed ½ star because of the soreness I get.

title: An awesome headphone gets better!
text: Bought these as replacement for my original Bose QuietComfort 15. I used the original Bose for over 5 years on many international and national airline trips. I passed those down to my daughter and picked this up as a Christmas gift for myself! So how does Bose improve upon something that was already very very good? It did so in the following ways: 1. The biggest change is that you don't need to turn on the noise cancelling feature to listen to music. So what, you say? Well, if you are on a long plane ride and you run out of batteries, you are out of luck on the older Bose headsets. But on the QuietComfort 25s, the show doesn't stop! 2. The case is a little bit more compact and symmetric than the previous one. Why does that matter? It fits well inside backpacks and or large purses. The inside of the case has a nice holding rack for the airline plug adapter and an extra battery 3. The headband has a softer cushion which makes it a bit more comfortable to sit on your head. 4. The cushions over the ears are also made of softer material and make for comfortable long-term use. There are times when I use these for over 2 hours straight and they are quite comfortable. 5. The cable is a bit thicker than the older one. This means fewer tangles when taking it in or out of the case But most importantly how do they sound? Are they an improvement over QuietComfort 15s? I think so, but the 15s themselves were so good that any improvement will be marginal at best. That being said, these sound absolutely amazing.

title: Performance vs Price Ratio not good
text: If one buys these headphones, do it for noise cancellation. At that task, they do a good job. Otherwise, the headphones are mediocre when it comes to music or video sound tracks. I have pair of $100 Logitech Bluetooth headphones that sound better than these $300 gilded lilies. The Bose 25's don't have much dynamic range, and the highs are just not there. And no, my Logitechs aren't put together as nicely as the Bose are, but I've had them for 3 years, banging around in my laptop case, my desktop, occasional drops to office floor and everywhere else and they still work fine. Others mileage (and hearing) may vary, but in my opinion, Bose isn't worth the price. Me thinks that lofty price is mostly to pay for marketing and advertising. Fine, but where's the beef? And we don't even get Bluetooth with the Bose 25's. What is that??? More wiring to screw with.

title: Noise cancelling earphones
text: Got these for my husband for Christmas and he loves them!!

title: Excellent Headphones
text: These head phones have excellent active noise canceling in them. I work in a very busy and loud office and with the noise canceling on, I can barely hear anything except voices when the music is low. I am autistic and these head phones are the only reason I am able to work in this environment. I would recommend them for someone who is autistic that must work in a loud environment that is distracting. If I put ear plugs in and use only the noise canceling feature, with no music, it greatly makes concentrating at work more tolerable. I can still hear voices, but they are muffled and sound more distant. They are on the high side, as far as price, but I couldn't find a pare cheaper that worked this good. Bose did an excellent job on making these headphones.

title: I bought it brand new and it took a while ...
text: I bought it brand new and it took a while to figure out why the noise cancelling wouldn't work, only to realise it was because the Right side of my headphones did not work. Thanks a lot! Just figured it out, the seams around the foam were ripping. Poor craftsmanship.

title: A Necessity for Flying
text: When flying and using in-ear headphones, I found that I had to have the music at full volume which I would never do in every day use. And listening to music or a movie at full volume in addition to the jet noise did not eliminate the tiring effects of the noise on a long flight. The Bose noise cancelling headphones do an excellent job of eliminating the jet noise and allowing me to listen at a volume I like. I wear them for the entire flight even when not listening to music or a movie. The only thing wrong with these is the AAA battery.

title: disappointing sound quality
text: Very comfortable. You can wear these for a long time. The cord is the perfect length. The noise canceling works great, but it chews up batteries pretty quickly, which is annoying. The reason for the 3 stars is that I'm just not crazy about the sound. It's not bad at all, just not great. Something is missing and I wish I could explain exactly what. I feel detached from the music. Update: these do get considerably better with good amplication (despite having a built-in amp). One of the problems is that the Mac and iPhone - as well as every other PC and phone - don't have great analog output. Using optical/HDMI/USB digital output to a good amp will make these sound better, and you'll still want to keep the switch on. I'm leaving the rating at 3 stars though because I've found significantly better sound with the AKG 712 Pro. The search for better sound never ends.

title: Right side goes out when listening to music, but noise cancellation is top notch
text: Got these, and the noise cancellation is great! I didn't even hear the cleaning lady vacuuming while working late. When I saw her, I pulled the headphones off a bit, and yep, it was loud! Unfortunately, for music, the right headphone goes out. I wiggle the cable, and it comes back... for awhile. I suspect that the cable (which goes into the left headphone) is coming loose. I take it out and put it back in as tightly as I can, but it's still an issue. Also, it makes my head hot... actually made my head sweaty. Not sure anything can be done about that, but the right headphone thing bugs me. I may exchange them for another set soon to see if maybe I got a bum pair.

title: Purchased them twice. I am convinced.
text: I purchased the Bose QuietComfort 25 just before Christmas. The noise canceling was nothing short of amazing! The sound of silence blew me away. Then like a nut, I started reading reviews about other headphones having a better bass sound and such craziness. I returned the Bose and then went on the hunt for affordable, "better than Bose" headphones. Like a dingbat, I bought the new Beats Studio (great bass and comfortable) Audio-Technica ATH-M50x (great bass and soooo uncomfortable, heavy), and then the August Bluetooth Wireless (ok is sound, comfortable and light) Outcome: I still have the Beats Studio (put away in the box), I returned the Audio Technica as quickly as I could, and every now an then I like the freedom of the August Wireless, so I still use them. I have since received my new purchase of the Bose QC25. YES...I bought them a second time and absolutely love them, just as I really did the first time around. The sound is great and the comfort level is an A+. They are very light and it is as if you have cotton around your ears. I have learned that it is all about personal taste. What I find comfortable and pleasing to my ears is what I like, not particularly what others recommend. In this case, make me the exception. :-) I highly recommend the Bose QuietComfort 25. Take my word for it. It may have taken me 2 times to believe my ears but ....this is the best $299 I have ever spent. Worth every single penny.

title: These are a must have.
text: As with anything I have ever owned from Bose, they are exactly what they say they are. These are the perfect headphones for airplanes will never travel without.

title: These are the real deal, sound quality, noise canceling and comfort.
text: Best yet! I have owned all of the various iterations of the Bose (and many other brands) of noise canceling headphones. I fly a lot and music is a passion. These are by far the best that Bose (or any other company) have come up with yet. I have the "on ear" and cup style (over ear) versions as well. I would never buy the on-ear again, regardless of claims that might be made. You just don't get the same sound quality and no even close to the same noise canceling effect. Buy these, you will not be disappointed, save your money on the cheaper ones or on other brands. It's a waste... these are the real deal.

title: Excellent for Long Flights
text: Wow. Noise cancellation is truly superb -- and it is VERY comfortable to wear. Used it on a trip to Japan -- can't believe I've never bothered to have one on my previous trips -- it made a WORLD of difference. Having this on and off is night and day in an international flight. I was actually shocked at how loud the cabin is during a flight. HOWEVER -- while the noise cancellation is great, I have to admit that Dr. Dre's Beats (the original) has 100% better bass, bar none (and is much MUCH louder). Maybe because the Beats I have uses 2 batteries? But noise cancellation and wear-comfot wise, these are 100% better. Maybe I'll try to find one that's 100% in re bass and noise cancellation so I don't have to carry around 2!

title: Right ear broke after 18 months
text: The right ear stopped working after only 18 months. Not worth the money.

title: DOESN'T WORK ON MANY ANDROID DEVICES -5 Star Quality Sound but 3 Star Compatibility
text: As you will read from others, these are great quality headphones. Unsurpassed. HOWEVER, that being said I am disappointed with the remote. I bought these ones in particular (instead of the Apple compatible) because I own an android phone/computer. For the price, I wanted all the features to work. But to my dismay, the remote isn't compatible with my phone( I have a NEXUS 4). The remote does work for pausing a song, but the volume control does not function. After going to the Bose website and reading on more, they do state that is item is made specifically for the SAMSUNG GALAXY and MIGHT work with other android devices. So buyer beware, if you want 100% compatibility for your android device, you might not get it. But if the volume feature isn't an issue for you, then these are the headphones for you! I hope that Bose will come out with an All-Android remote so that their customers aren't forced into owning a Galaxy or Apple device.

title: I'm sold.
text: I am impressed. I thought the Audio-Technica (see prior review) was great, but I got tired of the fact that my ear was hurting after a few hours. But with recent Bose price drop to $175, I went for them and boy am I glad I did. Outstanding Quiet when the switch is flicked. Dead quiet. Outstanding Comfort, wear for hours, cross country. Great sound, again better with jet audio/Bongiovi apps, together less than $10 and worth it at this level of quality and cost. You are not going to stop flying, and you're going to have these for a long time, Bluetooth to me is still not quite dialed in, these are great. And that surprised me.

title: What else could you ask for?
text: I'm not and audiophile. I just like to have a decent pair of headphone to listen to music and watching movies/videos on my devices. Pros - Comfortable. I can wear this for hours and won't feel any strain on/around my ears. - Quiet. It dramatically reduces low frequency noises like airplane hums or background noises in coffeehouse. - Detachable cable. If the cable fails for some reason, all you have to do is purchase just a new cable, not the entirely new pair of headphone. - Crisp & clear sound. Usual for Bose, sound profile is leaning more towards mid and higher frequency while giving out a very nice/tight base. - AAA batteries. No more proprietary battery like QC3. - Looks nice. I prefer this look over the older QC15/QC3. - Smaller case. Easier to carry around when traveling. Cons....I can't think of anything. Honestly, I can't find anything that I'm not happy with. Unless you like a bass heavy stuff, QC25 should give you everything you want. A crisp and clear sound with decent amount of bass. The noise canceling that block out background noises (not everything though). Again, since I'm not an audiophile, I can't really critique the sound profile of QC25, but as an average consumer who cares about sound quality, this was a great buy. PS. The box redesign is also amazing.

title: It depends.
text: Reading through other reviews, it seems that your satisfaction with these headphones will depend on your expectations. Yes, they are expensive. In terms of pure sound reproduction, the discriminating audiophile may do better elswhere. In terms of noise cancellation,these headphones are worth their weight in gold on any flight over a few hours..especially if you are seated to the rear, anywhere behind the wings where the engine noise is greatest. If I want to watch a a movie while my wife watches a cooking show, I just plug into my tablet or laptop and the room noise evaporates. The new model 25's are, to my ear, no better than the older model 15's which are now discontinued but are still available on some websites. If price is a consideration that might be your best bet.

title: AMAZING!
text: AMAZING! I don't think I've ever had such a nice set of headphones. I treated myself because I really want to start doing meditation apps my phone. Well, we just flew on an airplane, and I brought these. The difference between having the noise cancelling feature on and off was like night and day. I don't think I ever realized just how loud airplane noises are until I was able to magically turn that noise off! Just amazing.

title: Annoying and un-initiative power on/power off, kills usability
text: Sound quality and fit is perfect but the power on process kills it. You need to hold down AND release the power button to turn the earbuds on, but the problem is there is no sound/light that gives you feedback on when you can release the button. And if you hold down the button too long, it won't power on at all. Not only that, the power-on sound only plays a couple seconds AFTER releasing the power button. Essentially, these ear buds are a pain to turn on especially if you put them down for a little bit and you don't know if they're already on, or already off.

title: Neck Pain - Less Functionality With Android and PC
text: First of all this is a more functional with Apple devices. If you use this with a PC or Android device you will not be able to how much battery life it has. But on a Apple device you will an animated video clip and you will be able to see how much battery life the buds have. I wore these for a few hours a day around my neck and I had the worse neck pain I stopped wearing them and the neck pain went away. Coincidence maybe. But there is a lot of hardware on these that was just about in the area where I was experiencing the pain.

title: good mid-range wired buds
text: Based on its price, it's pretty easy to tell these aren't meant to be top-notch earbuds. And they're not. They aren't as rich sounding or richly featured as my AirPods/Airpod Pros. And my Powerbeat 3s also sound more full (though not as good as the AirPods). If you know that going in (and you should, since you're paying sub-100) and your expectations are set, then you should be fully satisfied. They do sound good, just not great. I'd say they're rough akin to my several-years old Jabra Elites, though these are more bass-heavy, so I actually slightly prefer the Jabra. they're comfortable given that have a neck wire (obviously if that bugs you don't get these) and there lighter than my Powerbeats. all the basic controls are here in-line and work smoothly. Pairing was, as always between Apple products, fast and effortless. Immediately paired with all our phones/iPads fine. call quality was good, microphone worked great. they click together magnetically, but the wiring isn't super flexible, so I don't feel comfortable storing them in a small space. They come with 4 eartips for sizing. As always with Apple, packaging was nicely minimal I got these either for myself to have a pair of cheap earbuds to take places I don't want to have to worry about losing or to send to my son at college so he doesn't have to worry about losing them. They're budget earbuds but still fine sound, just not as good as the high-end ones, as should be expected. That don't come with a charger (just a cable), which I'm fine with as by now I've chargers up the wazoo, but something to be aware of. excellent product for its niche

title: Great features, excellent battery life
text: Pros: great sound, and has amazing battery life. Little magnets click to hold the earbuds together around your neck if you aren't using them, and the audio stream automatically turns off in this position. And, the stream turns on again when separated, if the earbuds are still on. Pairs easily with other devices, unlike other earbuds that I've tried, which seem to get very confused and would only turn one ear on, or was finicky and didn't want to connect, etc. These connect quickly and surely (I don't know how else to put it!). Cons: none really. The only (mild) complaint I have is that the light that indicates whether or not the earbuds are still on after they've been hanging around your neck without being used is in a spot that's hard to see. You kind of have to skootch the whole thing away from yourself so it's not directly under your chin where you can't see it, and even then, you have to angle the switch toward you to see whether the light is on. (Such First World Problems.) Beyond that, no other complaints!

title: Meh
text: I've been on the look out for an earbud headset of this style (wireless, but connected together, with controls, that charges with a USB-c cable) to replace my beloved but discontinued aukey ep-b60. i am still on the look out. they seem ok, but fall short of my expectations. there's a lot of cord noise. not as bad as if they were wired to your phone, but the rumble is amplified compared to my old headset. they seem to fit my small ears well ('ve had a TON of trouble finding earbuds that don't just fall out) but they were very uncomfortable. while my old earbuds i barely noticed (i often wore them until the battery ran out, sometimes forgetting i was wearing them all together. they has a small nub that would nestle into your ear curve so you didn't have to shove the whole cap into your ear canal.) these are pretty uncomfortable and hurt after twenty minutes of use, regardless of the size of caps i used. it might be the material. i found the audio quality a little harsh and tough to balance. voices were too piercing and any effort to mellow them out made them too quiet. little bass to music. just over all not ideal. i have no idea what the app is for. i thought it would help with EQ? but i guess not. i am giving them a little more time but i have a feeling i may need to return them (if i can. can you return items you've stuck inside your ear? lol.) it sounds like they work well for a lot of people, which is great. it's a good price, and if you aren't into true wireless, this is a winning design (seriously, more options like this please. i don't want three things i need to charge and lose.) i am not an audiophile, but i have something very specific in mind for my next headset and this isn't it unfortunately.

title: Almost had it, but compromises had to be made
text: This is a direct successor to the Beats X, and in some ways its better, in some ways, its a step back. Being a newer product, it should use the newer Apple H1 chip instead of the aging W1 chip, which this has. That diminishes the bluetooth range and sound clarity. The components, although feels nicer, is made of cheaper plastics than that of the X. It's more smaller and now uses usb-c, which is great, but it now doesn't include a carrying pouch. For half the retail price, corners have to be cut.

title: Short battery life, high expectations ruined
text: Based on experience so far, the only thing I’m glad about is they were ‘on sale’ at half MSRP. Battery life is less than six hours listening to spoken word audiobooks at low moderate volume. Rocking/rapping out and I’d expect a shorter life with high volumes and full spectrum music, but under 6 hours for words only? Might be that the ‘cyber Monday’ sale units are leftovers from the initial release several years ago and the batteries deteriorated in the warehouse. Might also be why the cable is so stiff and inflexible. Haven’t noticed sound cancellation qualities. The interface and cable are both clunky compared to some other brands - is the button I want on the left or the right (it is usually opposite where it is supposed to be). Not having a way to charge them without buying a new charger cable was also a disappointment - they include a usb-c to usb-c cable. The cutesy sounds and on screen animations are wastes of battery, which does one quiet tinkle before dying.

title: The BEATS go on…..
text: These earphones are EXCELLENT! I chose to have the wire connected ear phones, as opposed to the EAR BUDS! I use my BEATS* while I am working outside, and that is usually shoveling snow @ my home in Lake Placid, NY (6-10 inches expected today 4/19/22), and if I lose a BUD, even if I find it, they will be ruined…….next week I will be mowing my lawn, if I lose a BUD, good chance it will be turned into mulch; however having them connected, NO WORRIES! My BEATS* have an excellent full sound, and and GREAT noise canceling capability. A feature that I really like is the Magnetic Ear Buds. If I want to stop listening to my BEATS*, unlike most, I don’t have to fumble around trying to turn them down, and/or off…….nope, just remove the BUD from each ear, let them hang around my neck, and usually they will connect without me needing to touch them, but either way, they magnetically connect, and no fumbling around trying to figure out how to stop them. I KNOW there are much MUCH MORE EXPENSIVE earphones than my BEATS*, however with a Lawnmower or Snowblower engine running, I doubt they would justify the EXPENSE, and would there even be a noticeable difference? In closing, in case you are interested, they also were outstanding lying on Daytona Beach Sand the first two weeks in April! So my advice? IF listening to music that is LOUD, CRISP, and keeps the beat, then BEATS* will make your ears happy, and the money you saved not buying over priced garbage……remember, INEXPENSIVE IS NOT THE SAME AS CHEAP!!! BEATS* ARE INEXPENSIVE AND OUTSTANDING!

title: Poor sound quality
text: Avoid these if you want to enjoy music. I used these headphones for 60 seconds before repackaging and sending them back. I use the apple headphones with a wire that came with my phone, and I never went wireless because I was reluctant to spend the money for AirPods. I’m a painter, and I hate the idea of dropping an ear bud into my bucket or off of a tall ladder while working, so I’ve stuck with wired headphones. I finally decided to try something new, and these seemed great because they are made to work seamlessly with apple products. However, the moment I started listening, I was incredibly disappointed with the horrible sound quality. After years of apple headphones that are not the greatest, but have nice sound in my opinion, these sounded like they were filtering the audio through a tin can. Zero low end/bass, just metallic, tinny noise. I’m not a headphone expert by any means, and I’ve never owned any “Beats” products, but they should stop selling these with their name on them. I assumed the name was synonymous with great sound quality. Not this time. Avoid these if you want your music to sound good. I am giving two stars because all of the other features seemed pretty slick. If you’re just using these for communication, I imagine they would be fine. Phone calls, hands free voice assistant, etc. should be fine, but if you want to listen to music and enjoy the sound, pick anything else.

title: Simple, form fitting usb-c earbuds
text: Finally! A wireless usb-c earbuds that fit. I've been through so many different different usb-c earbuds - aukey, huawei, boltune, Mpow, Soundpeats, even aftershokz bone conduction earphones - but ultimately, they would eventually all fall out of my ear. I know, there are numerous earbuds out there to try from but for me, there are 3 features that I look for: 1) Usb-c. It has to be usb-c. Both my phone and laptop are are usb-c. 2) Convenience and Security. I don't like separate individual earbuds that don't attach to each other. I lose things easily. With these type of earbuds, I can easily secure them around my neck without worrying about losing one piece. Plus, unlike other detached, individual earbuds, I don't have to constantly take them in and out of my pocket when answering calls. 3) Magnetic. I love that the earbuds magnetically attached to each other. Not having any of these 3 features are automatic deal breakers. The Beats wireless have all three but what makes it stands out from the rest is that it actually fits my small ears. All the other ones I've tried fit at first but would eventually fall out during a workout. Even switch to the smaller rubber ear pieces would not help. Beats wireless are the only ones to not fall during my jogs and work out sessions. My only 1 complaint is that I wish the earphones would pause whatever it is that's playing when putting the two ends of the magnetic earbuds together. This is a common feature among other devices. Instead, the on/off button has to be pushed to pause. Minor annoyance but by no means is this a deal breaker. Kudos Beats!

title: They aight
text: For $40 bucks I guess they are good but if you think you are going to get something with a good sound, look elsewhere. The volume is not very strong and the bass is low but I do believe a lot of this is attributed to the poor sealing of the earbuds in your ear canal. I noticed that when I pushed in the earbuds just a little bit to make the seal tighter that the sound was richer and the bass was fuller. Its just a poor design on the earbuds themselves and not the actual sound components. The mic on the phone actually sounds really good. I was impressed with it and I actually thought phone calls sounded really good as well. I have a pair of earbuds that the sound when watching videos and music is phenomenal but phone calls sound atrocious. Another thing that was really good was the Bluetooth antennae. You can walk really far away and have lots of walls in between and it stays connected perfectly. It also immediately connects back on if you happen to walk out of range. It doesn't work well if you have it attached to multiple devices as it will just disconnect from one and you have to hit connect when going back and forth between the two. Most headsets just smoothly work between the two. Battery life is really good. No complaints there. The wires though are a bit too long IMO so that if you want the mic and controls within reach you have this long curl of wire in front of your face which can be annoying. (see attached pic) You can just unseat the wire from the back of your neck and let it hang back there but the controls go with it. They probably could have cut at least 4 inches on the wire. conclusion: If you are looking for long battery life and are not too concerned with having loud volume and if you have particularly small ear canals, then these are good. But if your main concern is loud, bass rich, and you have particularly big ear canals then you should pass on these.

text: The Beats Flex earbuds are, I think, at the bottom of the Beats line of earbuds. It's not surprising that they're there. Unlike many earbuds, these are tethered together. Charging them was easy. Pairing them to my phone was not a problem. The sound wasn't impressive. Noise cancellation was average, and they weren't very good for phone calls. Still, if you want a low cost, somewhat acceptable BEATS earbud, these might be good enough - until you can get something better.

title: Great headphones for an affordable price!
text: I read the reviews, and I didn't expected much from roughly $50 (I paid in $30 range) headphones. Many mentioned about the microphone, and yes, it is bad. However, I did not buy this for a conference. My main use of this is to listen music and videos. So, I really do not care much about mic quality. In case of audio quality, it is surprisingly great for the price. Considering that this is a wireless headphones with W1 chip from Apple, it is well built with better than expected sound quality. I highly recommend this headphones if you just want a wireless headphones with good sound quality. (Don't expect much of the microphone)

title: Decent ✅
text: These are ok but it’s kind of short around the neck. Also the battery life could be longer. The sound is excellent!

title: clunky
text: I had to return these. The wires were thick and clunky and it kept falling out my ears.

title: Loudest setting is similar to medium setting on my old LG around the neck BT headphone
text: Sounds good, but beats Loudest setting is similar to medium setting on my old LG around the neck BT headphone. Disappointed. Should have read the reviews before ordering

title: Arrgh!!! No Lightning cable port!
text: Totally useless to me since it only takes USB-C. If you read the description carefully it does indeed say USB-C, but it's buried way, way down in the description. Nothing worse than having to lug multiple cables to get something done. For mobile devices, Apple needs to stick with Lightning until the input on its iphones changes to USB-C.

title: Decent headphones for the price
text: Decided to go with these since my old BeatsX headphones dies. Think the battery went out and wouldn’t turn on. In comparison, the sound quality is not as good as the BeatsX. It lacks highs and mids in comparison to the BeatsX. It seems a little muted in comparison to the BeatsX. There is plenty of Bass with the Flex. Another thing about the Flex is that they don’t have a separate control switch for play and volume control. It’s just integrated on the left battery pack area. So in order to adjust volume or play/pause, etc. You have to reach next to your neck in order to access them. It takes a little longer find the location since you have to grab the cable and slide your fingers down the cable until you find the switch location on the battery pack. The old BeatsX had a separate area higher up on the cable closer to the side of your face which was easier to access. At least it has the W1 chip so you can share music with multiple headphones and you can use Find My app to find your headphones(only if it’s on.) Or see the last known location while it was on. The main reason why I went with the Flex is that it has a much longer battery life than just the separate ear buds, plus you can easily take if off and let it hang around your neck without having to stick it back in case. With the 12 hour battery life you can take it on an airplane trip and it will last pretty much the whole flight from the time you are waiting to get on the plane and while you’re flying. Overall it’s a decent entry level product. It’s the only around the neck ear buds that Apple now makes. It’s good enough for what it is. But it would have been nice if they still sold the older BeatsX headphones which cost a little more and had better sound quality.

title: Nope
text: I bought these Beats with reasonable expectations: Their price was a fraction of the price of the AirPods Pro, so I didn't expect them to have the same sound quality. Still, they disappointed me... what a horrible sound! Completely flat sound, music is just lifeless... I already returned them.

title: Very Good Earphones but…
text: For the price and its compatibility with the iPhone, nothing beats the Beats. I love its functions and how well they work with the iPhone. I love the magnets that stick together the ear pieces, turning the earphone into a collar. My only bellyache is that the earpieces themselves are of that type that won’t stay out in your ears. They keep popping in and out. I wish they were shaped like the regular apple earphones.

title: No way to charge them

title: They work and if they fall out I don’t lose them!

The quality of the sound isn’t anything different from my $20 headphones. Returning. Also like everyone else said they need a special charger. I was able use my daughters chrome book.

title: Nice headphones, neet magnetic feature.
text: The cool thing about these Earbuds is the fact that the back of the earbuds are magnetized so they click together, then automatically disconnect the bluetooth and shutdown. Then you can pull the earbuds apart, put them in your ears and they will reconnect to whatever you're listening to at the time. Nice feature. Sound is good, not amazing, but good. The ear buds fit my ears, I can lie down on a pillow with them for 30 minutes or so with them on and not have any discomfort. Past 30 minutes and I need to lie on my back. I have used them for about 6 hours without a charge, they recharge in about an hour. They connect quickly. There is no built in noise cancellation, but the ear buds do block most sounds, including in a aircraft. This is one of several types of earbuds that I have and I like this sort of necklace format, because they are easy to use and keep track of unlike the separate earbuds with a case. Happy Trails.

title: Best thing I ever bought on Black Friday weekend
text: I’m not a connoisseur of music technology (though I’m pretty familiar with music), and I have tiny ear canals; I usually go with over ear headsets of good, not great, quality. I had wired buds in the past for walking, nothing fancy, and when these were on sale, I figured it was a good purchase. It was an *amazing* purchase. They’re easy to wear if you’re used to the wire, and the features are awesome—I use the magnetic feature all the time, the controls are easy to use compared to the cheap stuff, and the sound is excellent. They’re comfortable to wear on the go and around the house. I have no complaints, but I had the USB-C adapter already. There is no noise cancelling to them, but they’re the least expensive of the line, so I’m not faulting them that. I don’t do calls in them, so I have no experience with the microphone. I don’t really understand why the controls need to be ergonomic, according to other reviews? I guess I’m used to mid-range quality, so if these are the lower end of the best, I accept. I also got them on sale, so I’m basically blown away, honestly. Other humans with tiny ear canals, yes, they are great and I actually find all of the tips comfortable. title: Great price for the quality!
text: I’ve been looking for some new earbuds and didn’t want to pay for the super expensive Apple AirPods. I stumbled across these and the delivery was SUPER fast. These are exactly what I’ve been looking for and I love them. The sound and the noise cancellation are amazing and they don’t move too much while around my neck like my old pair of off brand that resembled these. It does just like it says and once you take them out your ear and put them back together (they’re magnetic), whatever you’re watching or listening to pauses which is awesome. title: Jabra doesn't support this headset being used on a laptop
text: I bought these to use at work with my laptop. The range is horrible; as soon as I walk out of my office, the calls go in/out. When I started researching the issue, I found out by a Jabra tech support person that these headsets are designed for use on smartphones only so they do not support any of their claims when using them with a laptop. I returned them.

title: Love these things
text: Bought these specifically for the 'hear through' feature. Its is very nice to be able to hear whats going on around me when I go on walks I have started to use them as earplugs for when I put my toddler to sleep at night, he is a screamer very comfortable if hard to get used to putting in your ear just right wish I had bought them sooner. work great on android and windows 10(somewhat iffy at times) and I use them for zoom calls daily now. Bluetooth range and connection can go pretty far. the charging case is nice and small and fits in my pocket quite well, though I have the back one and it can be hard to find at times, and would recommending putting something reflective on it they recently added a simple ANC which I haven't really been able to benefit from but I appreciate Jabra keeping the past products updated the only complaint is the buttons themselves are too easy to press sometimes, and if I am laying down with them on they often get press. maybe jabra can make a capasitive touch version in the future.

title: Overall good earbuds but a little expensive.
text: The big problem with budget earbuds is that they tend to not work for too long. The Jabras are clearly better quality in terms of build and sound over cheaper true wireless earbuds I've owned. The case is compact and the hinge has a really nice feel to it (I know that's kind of a weird thing to point out). For music and podcasts these are perfect. From a non-audiophile's perspective the sound is pretty well balanced with strong bass, clear highs, and strong mids that aren't muddled. The smartphone software equalizer is pretty nice, but only offers a few inflection points. Useful but not impressive. These are also very comfortable and generally stay in my ear. I get a little worried running in them but they've never fallen out. That was my biggest fear getting expensive earbuds. But I often wear them for hours at a time with no issue. They do have Android Assistant integration but I haven't really figured out how to utilize that too much. I do miss my Google wired earbuds with the assistant button built in. But I can't really fault these for not being as seamless as a Google product. I do have a few issues. Primarily call volume can be a little low. I'm not really sure why this is the case, but I have noticed that sometimes I switch to my handset because I just can't hear the person on the line too well. I know there's a ton of variables at play here, but I've never had this problem with wired earbuds or the handset. I wish I could overboost the call volume somehow. And my BIGGEST complaint is that often the earbud just does not charge in the case. I have had problems where I have the charging case plugged in, and put my earbuds in overnight, and in the morning they're not charged. I've put the earbud in, seen the red light blink indicating it's charging, and STILL have it not charge. So that gets really annoying. Overall these are really nice and I use them daily. But I'm just glad I didn't spend the money on them.

title: Great until they die on you.
text: These have been great little earbuds. The ANC function isn't anything to write home about but the sound quality, ease of pairing and battery life were great. Unfortunately after a year and a half of daily use, the left earbud gave out and none of the fixes Jabra support offered have worked. If you're the type to always buy a new pair of earbuds every 12 months then they're great! If you're like me and expect high end earbuds like these to last 2-3 years then I'd look elsewhere.

title: Disappointing sound quality, wouldn't stay put
text: I really wanted to like these earbuds. I have a Jabra Speak 710 conference device that I absolutely love (rock-solid), and I hoped for the same with these earbuds. I am aware that not all earbuds fit all ears, no matter what you do; these just wouldn't stay in my head. My husband has gone through dozens of earbuds trying to find the right fit, so I don't fault Jabra on that point. But I was disappointed with the sound quality overall -- it seemed tinny to my ears. I'm a classically trained musician, but I wasn't expecting to listen to music with these earbuds, just hoping they'd work well for my daily-dozen videoconference calls. People couldn't hear me and the sound just wasn't that great. Like most things, it's better to pay more and stop wasting time on lower-cost versions. I returned these for a refund.

title: Nice Product

I think the sound quality is very good, but I don't have the ears of a concert musician. For the price I am really happy with these and will get a few of these to give as gifts to my friends.

title: Bass heavy with clear sound quality! My go to earbuds
