I actually don’t know what would I do if I lost them or something wrong happens to these! Using them for the past 2 years and I felt I should write a review for my 75t. You won’t like any other earbuds, once you use 75t. They are very comfortable. Comparing other in ear headphones. Apple AirPod pro would feel so less audio quality when you compare them with 75t. Powerbeats has less base than 75t. Only downside is they are bit low if you are using for calling over phone. Active noise cancelling is just fine not great as Bose qc35 or AirPod pros. Hearing music, watching movies no audio delay, can be used along running, they won’t fall, and jabra app is also great where you can customize. Also a great fan of jabra’s buttons instead of touch sensors.

title: Bad Company with a Decent Product
text: One of the buds stopped working after a month. Contacted them about the warranty and it took filling out multiple forms and sending half a dozen emails to get a warranty replacement. I had to spend my own money to send it to them before they would send a replacement, and then they said they were out of stock and it would be 2-3 weeks minimum before a replacement was sent. They did not offer an alternative product or solution. I can not recommend this product based on the customer service. This space is far to competitive to put up with such poor customer support. Stay away

title: Call audio unstable; Left earbud connection problem
text: Same issues as many other reviewers. Left earbud keeps cutting out or never connecting in the first place. And on phone calls, the headphones regularly both cut out even though they are still connected to the phone. I have to tell iphone to switch call audio to phone and then back to the earbuds to get them working again. They are incredibly unreliable. For important phone calls, I end up shelving these and using the wired headset that came with the iphone. Jabra's only support is to tell you to unpair the device and pair again. I have to do this multiple times a day to keep them remotely functioning but more and more I just don't even bother because of the constant issues. Short return window so it was a waste of a purchase. Jabra replaced my headphones under the warranty and I'm having the exact same issues right out of the box. Garbage product.

title: connection issues
text: THE GOOD small size earbuds are very discrete small charging case is very easy to carry around awesome battery life very secure fit in ears, don't have to worry about them falling out THE BAD sound quality is too bass heavy, poor performance on the mids and highs left earbud plagued by severe connection issues, apparently this is common as other reviews mention the same problem CONCLUSION despite many good things to like about these earbuds, severe connectivity issue and bass heavy sound signature render these earbuds useless. very unfortunate.

title: Great Earbuds
text: Tried several cheaper wireless earbuds... some couldn't hold a connection while others required the charging case to be within bluetooth range of the earbuds. The Jabra 75t's have excellent sound and the battery life so far has been outstanding. Able to use the earbuds on bike rides far removed from the case. Jabra offering free upgrade to new software that provides noise cancelling features.

title: Battery life is poor and warranty policy is horrible.
text: Battery life is horrible otherwise great. After the update my left earbud was extremely low. They were covered under warranty. The warranty process is a horrible experience. I would not recommend jabra. Just received an email stating my new product was ordered. I returned the item 2/17 it is 3/11.

title: Serious Reliability Issues, Very Limited Support
text: I've owned two sets of Jabra 75t. While I like the sound quality, voice quality, and fit/comfort, the reliability of the product is severely lacking! ... My first Jabra 75t lost its battery life (down to 30-60 listening on zoom call) in just one year of use. My second Jabra 75t lost its left earbud (completely dead, cannot be charged, no LED lights) in just 3 months of light use. (Usually, I only use the right earbud). While I resisted buying the white airpod/pro, and really wanted a non-apple product, I don't think I can keep throwing money away on Jabra now.

title: Mostly good
text: Overall I really like these headphones. They connect to my phone effortlessly and stay connected even when I'm away from my phone (within reason). The sound quality is good but the headphones let in quite a lot of ambient noise. I have other headphones that make more of a secure connection and make for better noise cancelling.

title: Would be 5 stars, but I had issues after 3 months
text: I purchased these from a different retailer as soon as they were available and used them with an android phone and an ipad. The sound quality, noise cancellation, battery life, and call quality were all fantastic. However, 3 weeks ago I started experiencing an issue where there was an audio imbalance between the left and right earbuds. The right earbud would get quieter and quieter over time until you couldn't hear anything unless the volume was turned all the way up. This of course would make the left unusable because the volume would be so loud it would blow out my eardrum if I left it in. I did extensive troubleshooting on my own and the issue did not get any better, so I opened a support case with Jabra. After a few conversation over the course of a week, they sent my case to Tier 2 support. I didn't hear from them for about a week, when they finally reached out and told me there was a firmware update addressing my issue. I updated the firmware on my earbuds and they were fine for a day before the issue returned. I updated Jabra on the issue and asked about a replacement set and referenced the warranty, but have not heard anything back from them since.

title: Good Quality Sound
text: The sound quality from this system is very good. I was initially uncomfortable with the units in my ears but I have become accustomed to using them.

title: Blows AirPod pros out of the water.
text: I’m a bit of an audiophile so I expect good quality when I spend upwards to $200 on headphones. Jabra never disappoints. They’re treble and bass are balanced and they stay in my ears at the gym when I’m doing HIIT training. Phone calls are crisp and clear. I’ve tried soundcore and anker and the AirPods are awful. Honestly if you have the money don’t bother wasting your time looking at other brands.

title: Work Wonderfully! Fit Not So Good
text: I've been using these Jabra Elite 75t Earbuds for eight months now and first let me say they work beautifully. They sound great, good battery life, and I like the hear-through feature. But maybe they're a bit top-heavy? Because unless I am sitting pretty still, like while behind the wheel during a long car ride, I just cannot get them to stay in my ears. I've tried all three sized Silicon EarGels, and once in my ear I turn them and I twist them, I try to jam them in, I try NOT to jam them in...but when I move much or even look up or down, I can hear and then feel them as they slip out of my ears. Maybe it's just me, but I am 6'1" and have normal shaped ears. Otherwise I like these.

title: My best earphones yet
text: I already had a Sennheiser HD 4.40 BT (headphones) and a JLAB EPIC 2 (earphones), but ordered this one (my first true wireless set) for better microphone quality over phone calls, and I'm very happy I did. As advertised, I no longer get complaints about my voice not being audible over the other side, and a lot of times the person on the other end is not even able to figure out if I'm calling over some earphones or my phone itself. Apart from the primary feature for me, the music sound quality through the earphones is also unmatched to anything else I've ever listened to. The connection is pretty effortless as well. Overall, this one appears to be the perfect earphones for me.

title: The right earbud stopped working. Appears to be a common issue
text: The right earbud stopped working. Appears to be a common issue

title: Smaller than the 65s
text: Sound just as good as the 65s but smaller. Lots of features. You can just use one if you want to.

title: Spotty Bluetooth Connectivity - RETURNING
text: Very disappointed. I had no problem connecting, setting up and installing the noise cancelling software. Then, I went for my first walk. With my LG V60 phone in my pants pocket, these headphones could not maintain connectivity. I had to move the phone into my shirt pocket. Even then, it was only about 95% the product also asks you to install noise cancelling software. In my case, I couldn't get it to work reliably. It appeared to be going on and off. I could easily hear cars going by, with ANC turned on. Basically, these are JUNK... Chinese junk!

title: Almost perfect but......
text: I had wanted these for a while. While they can be great for some in my case they missed the mark and hopefully will improve. I'll skip the fluff and give the pros and cons. Pros: Great fit out the box. Form fitting and doesn't protrude much at all and looks stylish as can be for ear buds. Sound reproduction is incredible. Not to much highs or lows in my opinion for my taste. Charging case is very minimal and almost forgot had them in my pocket. I do like the jabra app let's you know battery of both the buds and case, by percentage, so you know when you can or need to charge. Three features I like is.. 1)pressing left ear selection can be set to pause audio with background noise pass through or mute with pass through. This comes in handy when someone wants to talk to you, you don't have to take them out. (2)you can leave the pass through on, that way when working or outside you can still hear what's going on and the music, not on or other. (3)when you take one out of ear it will pause the music for 1 minute or when you put them back in, it will auto resume. Cons: Unfortunately the big con for me is, in my opinion not "true" wireless... Meaning you can use both or just the right....but you can not use the left solo. That was a deal breaker for me. At times I need a longer battery life so when they can operate solo, if need, I can use one and charge the other... You can't do that with this. Other con was sound volume. I don't need ear drum busting loudness or base, but it sounded like was about 20-30 lower than other earbuds. If you don't need them solo or to be independent, like the sound volume decent then you'll love these. Otherwise I would suggest others. I personally am keeping my Anker SoundCore Liberty Pro 2 as my everyday driver still. Only thing it lacks is the pass through option.

title: Not perfect, but... The best compromise among all my devices
text: The ability to connect to two devices at the same time, decent audio quality, stable connections, and reasonable comfort. While I have earbuds that have better audio quality (Sennheiser), more stable connection (Anker), and better comfort (Samsung) - this is the set I use most for their versatility.

title: Great AirPod competitor
text: Overall great earbuds. Cutting to the chase I would recommend these right up there with the AirPods and other competitors. They will not break the bank the way the AirPod pros do. Also never had connection problems that some have stated having. Pros • Fit like a glove in your ear vs the iPods which just don’t feel secure. • Battery life is awesome much better than I expected it would be. I listen to podcasts most of the day at work and on my commute. The charging case has to be charged every week or so depending on use. • Connects immediately when they’re pulled out of the charging case • The app is nice for customizing your settings for different audio. • Water and dust resistant. • The hear through feature is nice to have Cons • They’re not as loud as I’d like them to be compared to the beats or AirPods. • Also name recognition isn’t there as much as it is with its Apple, Sony, or Samsung competition. Which is sad cause how good they are. • For some people. Not myself even though I do have an iPhone. Having to use Siri can be frustrating there isn’t a way to access it without having to physically use your phone.

title: probably great buds, but they didn't fit my ears
text: even with all the different sleeves, they would fall out when I exercised so I had to sent them back.

title: fix the left earbud issue!
text: These wireless buds have the potential to be the best in this price range. They’re packed with very cool features. The app needs an over haul, but I like how the app tells you the battery status of the buds and also the case!. The find my buds feature is cool and will also allow you to play a noise on the buds so you can help find them. Also the hear through mode is awesome and works!, it allows sound in from your surroundings using the ear buds mics in case if you converse with someone or run-near traffic so you don’t have to take them off (very cool). I have tried the Bose soundsport buds and the jaybird vistas. Although these jabras sound awesome and are packed with features and battery life that surpasses the Bose and jaybirds, sadly I will be returning them. The left ear bud is a real issue. It cuts in and out often. Tried troubleshooting but no use. At times you get through some music uninterrupted and then bam it does it Again just when you’re thinking...hey the problem is fixed! Lol it’s very annoying. Between the Bose wireless soundsports and jaybird vistas, Jaybird vistas wins because of the case (usb-c) longer battery life, more compact and light and the App with eq settings is miles ahead of Jabras and Bose! They compete with Bose’s sound quality and bass no problem! I really wanted these Jabras to be the one! But sadly they will not till they figure out how to fix the left ear bud issue.

title: Goog quality for the cost
text: The ear buds are east to lik up to your system and have good sound for the price. Fairly good fit with moderate noise cancellation For the price these fit the budget well. If you are a critical music listener probably need to sped a little more

title: Says what it does, does what it says
text: Sounds great, fits great, good battery life, not heavy in your ear, decent price

title: Most under rated earbuds out there!
text: I purchased these headphones earlier in the year and bought my son a pair for Christmas. I love the fit of these, their small and fit in my ear, have buttons so I don't have to worry about fiddling with touch controls, also the case is nice and small. I prefer the sound signature over the AirPods and possibly the Pros as well. The way they're designed they close off most noise from outside, but about a month ago Jabra added ANC via a software upgrade, even though they were selling a new pair the 85t, that promoted ANC. These were on sale for $119, which I consider great value.

title: Great Buy! Couple Small Cons
text: Ive had these head phones for about 4 day and so far they are great. Below are some pros and cons Pros: Great price Nice compact case App allows for easy setup and updating Customize your music experience easily Noise cancelation is just enough that you can still hear loud noises Sound is good, about what i was expecting, crisp clear and punchy Cons: Buds are very small, i can see myself losing an earbud if i am packing quickly or if one falls out of my ear Volume doesnt get very loud. At full volume, i could still use another couple clicks of volume then again maybe its saving my hearing App is usful for setup and customizing your sound but unless you are constantly changing your preferences, you are in and out of the app once maybe twice My biggest complaint is the hear through doesnt really work that well while music is still playing. Used it and could still not hear my wife talking right next to me. Once i paused the music, i could hear her fine.

title: 75t is better than the new design.
text: The sound quality and balance is fantastic. Easy to pair, long battery life, sound design, comparable to Sony, Beats, and Bose and the best part it's less than half the price.

title: Had nothing but problems
text: I had no issues pairing with my Windows laptop or my Samsung phone. The issue was that the left earbud would randomly cut out and cause my music to pause. I found that if I moved the earbuds more than about 6" apart from each other, the left bud was unstable. Loosing signal and reconnecting. You can see the connection meter in the Jabra app. A simple google search showed this is a HUGE problem with these. I used all the "official" and "unofficial" fixes found in online forums and from Jabra tech support. Long story short, I returned them.

title: Eh over the 65t
text: The battery on my 65ts was fairly degraded, and was only getting around 4 hours of play time, so I decided to try these. While they are good yes, I think the 65T sound just as good, if not better. I like bass, but the bass on the 75T are VERY STRONG. So I suppose if you're a bass head, and are contemplating these as an upgrade to your 65t, you'll enjoy them. Regardless, the case is much slimer, opens much easier, and the magnetic lock to the buds are very much appreciated too, also the decision to go usb c is very welcomed. Though with the case being this slimmer, the top feels kind of "cheap", I don't think it will last, it does not feel durable at all. Overall, I would get these on sale.. otherwise get the 65t. They're not as comfy, but that's alright.

title: Great sound and comfort. The basis awesome
text: These are by far the best sounding ear phones that I’ve ever used.

title: Sound good. They fall out with perspiration.
text: They fall out when you sweat. They sound good. Noise cancelation is ok. The hear-through is nice. Comfortable for the first hour bluetooth connectivity is terrible. If I put my phone in my pocket while connected, there's constant interruption. Who wants that while listening to music!?? Last Jabra purchase. going with Samsung buds very soon.

title: Lovin my Jabra’s
text: My first pair of wireless air buds. Love them. Excellent sound quality. Don’t know what I was waiting for.

title: Great Sound Quality
text: Easily paired on my phone and my Versa 2. Great sound, I love the 'hear-through' function.

title: Static noise after 6 months
text: I use only for working out and running. Left ear gets loose when running but never feel down but it is annoying to have to ireadjust once in a while during running. Static noise after 5-6 months of use (5x a week for about 1hr, total of 5-6hrs a week) with low volume level, not the bass heavy stuff. I am quite disappointed with the static noise given this is a mid-high end earbud that costs more than I wanted to pay. I like the fine tuning app but once I set up, never touched it again. Battery life…well, I didn’t hardcore tested it but found myself having to charge every 2-3 times of use (see above) and leaving off the case after each use. Hear through is nice, but it sounds more of an amplification of the surroundings. Noise canceling feat is not great, but decent, you really have to tuck it in to have a good cancellation. I like it along the hear through.

title: Jabra
text: Sound is great and noise cancelling is best I have ever had. Still have a small issue with fitting in my ears. Just trial and error trying to get the right fit.

title: The best u can get
text: Wow great wireless earbuds the sound is amazing good. Just pair it with your phone 📱and the app let's u set the sound u want...you will not be disappointed with these ..they are a 10 for me ..beautiful

title: AWESOME EARBUDS
text: My boyfriend LOVED these. He won’t stop wearing them. Also the app that goes with them is pretty cool.

title: Pretty great headphones
text: I originally purchased a set of refurbished 75t from Jabra on eBay. Unfortunately they were riddled with issues but I loved the fit, finish and sound quality, so I bought a new pair on Amazon. They have been my go to headphones. I have a pair of Sony WF-1000xm3 earbuds that have been my main buds for a couple years. While I love those the fit never was my favorite. I also have tinnitus, and the Jabra's have soundscapes inside the app which does an awesome job at masking my symptoms. The overall fit and sound quality and other features like great battery life make these my current faves. I do wish you could use left or right independently, but not a deal breaker for me. I recommend these to anyone who is looking for some great earbuds.

title: The most amazing wireless earbuds I have ever owned. Bass is FANTASTIC!
text: Let me start off by saying that I have tried lots of different brands of wireless earbuds over the years. I have tried apple, boltune, sony, samsung, and lots of generic off-brands. These are by far the most comfortable and best quality sound wireless earbuds that I have ever used. The bass is FANTASTIC! The closest to bass and sound quality that even came close were the Sony WF-XB700's. Those really hurt after wearing them for a few minutes though. These Jabra's don't hurt me or bother me at all. The sound is wonderful. I'm so happy that I finally found my perfect wireless buds. I highly recommend these, especially if you are a bass head like I am. Even without the bass they sound awesome though. Just a tip: If you want to maximize the bass out of these, you need to use the Jabra app to turn up the bass on the equalizer. Without this the bass is mediocre at best. The good thing about the app is it lets you customize the EQ to your own liking.

title: Great ear buds
text: I use these everyday and like them a lot. The noise cancellation is quite good (not as good as my Bose headphones, but, hey, they are very compact). I use them for doing yoga (they do sometimes drop out when I am sweaty). I also use them for watching movies. I prefer headphones if I am really LISTENING to music, but I use these in the shop for ear proctection plus music.

title: Fall out of my ear
text: I bought these earphones from Costco (Amazon has them beat on price tho) and I’m returning them sadly. EVERYTHING except one thing makes them the best but the one thing is a deal breaker. Maybe it’s because I’m used to wearing earphones that wrap around my ear but for some reason these do not sit securely in my ear. I can feel them start to slide out and I’m constantly pushing them back in. I’ve tried really pushing them in and making sure my ear is dry, but if you’re used to running with earphones that wrap around or inside your ear, you may not enjoy these as they are not as snug as the alternative. I use these specifically for running so as I start sweating is when they slide. If you use AirPods or something else that youre used to adjusting them, you probably wont even notice this with these earphones. Sound quality, hearthrough, comfort when not exercising, and everything else is top notch though.

title: Average
text: I was expecting more out of these considering how expensive they are. They aren't loud enough for me; I can hear my treadmill when the music is up full blast. The music shouldn't have to be full blast and I definitely shouldn't still hear my treadmill. I have had one fall out if my ear at least 3x so far. Battery life is awesome and no connection problems, love the case too. Just not as impressed as I thought I would be.

title: Great, while it lasts, but it will fail eventually
text: Loved these when I got them but then it unpaired itself from my phone every few weeks. I suspected there might be issues with it but ignored it and lived with re-pairing it when it did this every few weeks. But after a few months the dreaded volume-imbalance problem started. The right bud's volume was muffled and lower compared to the left bud. Getting a replacement sent was an awful experience as you had to go through 2 layers of customer support to get the replacement shipped and they gave conflicting information about the process. Got the replacement and after a few months I'm getting the same problem with volume-imbalance. Another problem is the fragile bluetooth connection. When paired with my Fenix 6 that I wear on my left hand and when I go running you get music cutting out every few seconds. If I wear my watch on my right hand then the connection is much more stable but still not perfect. I wanted to like this ear bud because of it's great form factor but this experience had put me off buying another Jabra product. I have a Jabra Active Elite 65t that's still going strong so will use that for as long as I can until I upgrade to a non-Jabra earbud.

title: Awesome bang for buck
text: Way better than AirPods. And they stay in your ear. no matter what you’re doing. also very sweat resistant.

title: Awful pairing with Apple products
text: Unfortunately, I've had nothing but problems with these earbuds. They never pair smoothly with my iPhone or macbook pro. I go through all the steps of looking at my bluetooth settings and clicking on the Jabra device, but it doesn't connect. I'm at my wits end. It shouldn't be this difficult. I'd say that 85-90% of the time the earbuds don't connect. I love the way these fit into my ears because I couldn't stand how the Apple airpods felt. I just wish they'd work as promised.

title: Great sound and comfortable
text: These are a wonderful pair of earbuds. Previously I had a pair of Samsung galaxy buds, which sounded amazing, but were not comfortable so I had to return them. Thankfully, these earbuds not only have great sound, but they are very comfortable! I believe the ANC and hearthrough feature are superior to the Samsung buds. I like the feature where I can connect multiple devices at once, which enables me to watch videos on my laptop and pick up incoming calls on my phone. My only complaint is that these buds do not support mono mode for the left earbud. These buds were made so that the left bud connects to the right bud, not the phone; consequently, the left bud can't play music if it's more than a few inches away from the right, so I can't share my earbud to someone else and listen to music unless we're butting heads. Overall, if it was just me listening, these various features these buds bring to the table make them great for the price.

title: Warranty replacements are not comparable to original buds.
text: Original buds functioned well until the right bud abruptly failed at 5 months of ownership. Warranty department was disorganized and took 25 days to make the warranty replacement. Replacement buds arrived yesterday. I discovered that the replacements don't have the noise cancelation feature and are merely "hear thru" or on with no noise cancelation. I called the warranty department, waited on hold for 15 minutes, and was told to call back on Monday. The representative indicated that they do not replace defective products with ones comparable to the originals and to accept what they sent. Buyers be ware!

title: Tops!
text: These are the best fitting ear buds I have found. Superior quality sound. Love them more than my AirPods.

title: Fantastic battery life. But, having issues 3 months in
text: Started cutting out on the left bud, reconnecting would fix. But now it's constant and bass is super bloated. Left cuts back in and bass returns when I open my mouth. Super weird. Probably a connection issue. Anyway, unusable at this state. Fine buds otherwise. Bought at best buy for 80$. Battery life is awesome. Charge the case maybe once a month. Moderate / light use. Slip out of my ears, but I can't ever find a perfect set of buds. Except for Panasonic eardrops. Those are *chef's kiss*

title: Great Sound and secure fit
text: LIked it a lot and secure fit while working out and running. Sound is awesome. Connected them to Samsung GS10, very easy setup.

title: Not ideal for cycling
text: For those hoping to use this while cycling / bike commuting, the “hear through” feature amplifies the wind to the point of making the feature obsolete. The AirPods Pro seem to be able to isolate this sound so it’s not a problem. Hopefully this is just a software issue that they will resolve. Otherwise, hearthough works great, conversations can easily be had. ANC and other feature through the app are all well designed.

title: Best tws Earbuds I've owned
text: Great earbuds. Quality control issues. If you plan on keeping I suggest a warranty. My left earbud did eventually fail. But... Best earbuds I've owned.

title: Pathetic...
text: Pathetic product, I didn't buy this for great sound quality or great ANC ...I wanted one thing and only one thing from this....be able to stay paired to 2 devices and be able to switch between them seemelessly. But everytime there is a stupid notification on my phone the paly back on my laptop breaks and then starts again .... irritating and also did I mention the pathetic battery life...stay away people.

title: Jabra customer service is worthless
text: I liked these headphones, they fit great and the sound was pretty good, the battery life about what you'd expect, the "hearthrough" feature with my phone didn't work well at all. After seven months however, the one headphone stopped working well. So after a week of back and forth they told me to send the headphones back. It's been almost three weeks since they asked me to send the headphones back, it's been over a week and a half since they have gotten the package from UPS and yet I haven't heard a word from Jabra. The track and trace number they gave me only says that they sent an email and nothing else. If this is the quality of service you get for spending this amount of money on headphones, go somewhere else Update: I have finally heard back from Jabra and after they have had my headphones for a month, they've finally agreed to replace them. But of course, it's on back order, and it'll ship in 2-3 weeks, and try in their words, "it may get delayed further", don't waste your money with these guys, unless you are ok not having headphones for at least two months if something goes wrong.

title: Two pairs, same problem. one of them stops working
text: Just like others have said, the right one stopped working after only a few months. I was able to get the pair replaced under warranty. but that second pair did the same thing after just a few months again! Bought some Tozo brand ear buds and have loved them! the only thing I miss is the Jabra app. Also, without features like wireless charging and the ability of using left OR right independently makes these ear buds total failures compared to others that literally cost a tenth of these. Now I am looking at Anker's Soundcore line.

title: I love these ear buds
text: I am very happy with my purchase of these earbuds. I like the fit and I've worn them while biking and exercise, they fit great and have never felt loose. I like the sound quality, and I feel that the battery life is very good. As for noise cancellation, I feel that it's pretty good. They don't block all the wind noise while I'm biking, but I'm not sure that any earbuds would block that much noise. In fairness I would add that turning with noise canceling on or off there is a big difference. I would recommend them to anyone.

title: My Raycon ear buds are better.
text: My Raycon Ear buds are much better and cost less. Sound is just a little better but with a battery life half of Raycon... I'll stick to Raycon.

title: MY HUSBAND LOVES THEM!
text: Bought these as a gift for my husband! He loves them , and says the sound quality is great! He wears them everywhere with no issues of falling out.

title: I like these a lot but the noise canceling is mediocre
text: I bought these for my daily walks near a highway with a lot of traffic. I've had them about 4 months. I usually listen to podcasts while walking but occasionally listen to music. Pros: 1. Sound quality is very good 2. The app is great! I customized the button controls exactly the way I wanted them and they work great. 3. Has a button on each and no touch controls. I hate touch controls. These do not require much force on the button. Perfect for me. 4. Good fit for me, but limited bud tips so they may not fit everyone. Cons: Active Noise cancellation is not good. Honestly, I toggle on and off and hear no difference at all. Transparency mode is nice if you're talking to someone but I really don't use it much. Because of the isolation from the buds fitting well, I can use them by the highway, but my Anker buds have much better noise cancellation. 2. Noise cancellation is always off when I connect. They don't remember the previous state. So I have to turn it on each time (I know, why bother if it's not good anyway). Overall, I like them but wish active Noise cancellation was better. I rotate between these and two others. The custom controls make these the favorites, but during rush hour I use one of the others because of the superior noise cancellation.

title: Rubbish
text: Do NOT buy this. It will fail for no reason and Jabra customer service WILL NOT CARE. It's literally a piece of junk and Jabra knows it fails for no reason. Just search it up in Google. The right earbud has a known issue that causes it to fail and Jabra will not replace it no matter what. You've been warned.

title: I was originally disappointed out of the box
text: It also took time to get the earbuds connected to the app. But once I was done with the setup process the sound quality was remarkably better. Now, I love these earbuds. Update: My biggest gripe is that the software is not available on other platforms. Not on Amazon Fire tablet or Chromebook.

title: The Best
text: I has the 65T version before the 65’s came out and loved them. These are similar, but more expensive. Ive had many different manufacturers in my ear and these are better than Bose or Plantronics for sure. Highly recommend. They made many significant improvements over the 65’s especially with a new improved case.

title: Buggy
text: Update: The right earbud completely died 53 weeks after purchase just outside of the warranty (doesn't even make the boot up noise when taking them out of the case). Jambra likes to charge a premium price for a buggy product with poor quality. Next time I will buy from a brand with a better reputation. At the price point these were sold for when they originally launched I could have bought Sony or anything else. Original review: For a premium price you get to be a de facto beta tester for these buggy things. Earbuds lose connection all the time and will not pair again. title: Persistent issue with left earbud going out. Seems to be widespread problem w/Jabra.
text: A friend of mine received these from her company as part of her work-from-home package. However, she had already purchased another pair of earbuds and did not need these, so she gave them to me for free. It's the ONLY reason I am not harassing Jabra or Amazon for support/replacement/refund. Pros: * Great audio * Great noise cancelling (blocks out the train that goes by my house a million times a day) * Great hear-thru (blocks out loud noises but allows you to hear conversations) * Easy-to-open charging case. My husband has the 65 version and his case is a real PITA to open. Cons: * Terrible battery life (~5.5 hrs) * Easily fall out if you're eating/drinking or doing cardio or get sweaty ears. And by far, the MAIN REASON I am giving this product a 2-star review: They are unreliable! I have had consistent issues with the left earbud randomly going out and not wanting to connect at all to any device. I've tried various devices to see if it was just my phone, but that's not the issue. I even launched the Jabra Sound App to see if there was a firmware update I was missing. Nope. It shows the left earbud is "online" but there is no audio coming out at all. This is an intermittent and consistent issue: one day it will be fine, the next day it won't. I have tried all the troubleshooting tips and tricks and most of the time it doesn't work. I've had these less than a year and have had this problem since day 1. If you look online, this seems to be a consistent and widespread issue with their products, especially this particular model. I'd stay away if I were you.

title: Multipoint bluetooth earbud that actually works
text: Awesome! I was looking for multipoint Bluetooth earbuds connecting to 2 devices simultaneously. Most Bluetooth earbuds don't provide that (unlike over-ear headphones) but this one does! It connects to my phone and another device (Samsung tablet or Facebook Portal) effortlessly. Pairing is easy (press and hold the left and the right button). Sound quality and noise cancellation are very good. What I also absolutely loved about this model - is the fact that earbuds controls (Play/Pause, Skip, Answer, etc) rely on *clicks* rather than *taps*. With clicks - you don't have accidental presses as I have with all my other tap-based earbuds. USB-C port for charging, so all is well. One can only use the right earpiece without wearing the left one. Too bad it doesn't support wearing the left earpiece only - that would effectively double the battery time, would be so much better if they added it! Overall, very satisfied.

The control function with the different L/R ear pieces works well. The connectivity is a little tricky, they say these can be paired to 2 devices simultaneously but I can only pair to 1 or the other and have to turn off my device bluetooth in order to pair to the other device which is a bit of a pain. Playback quality is good, battery life seems good so far. I've used these around my home, office, and travel and overall am very pleased with the performance of them. I tried using sharp objects, pushing from below, sticky tape, and exacto knife, gorilla glue on a toothpick , you name it. Keep in mind, I had to disassemble the sub woofer a little to get the circuit board out to do all this. When I contacted Vizio for help (specifically that I needed a new subwoofer board since the chunk of metal was stuck inside mine) they referred me to three outside vendors who sell their parts. First of all, if you supply s***ty cables and they break apart, you should just give me a new board and be glad I'm not just returing the whole shebang. Secondly, if you're going to be a douche about it and just expect me to pay for the parts myself, at least refer me to a vendor who actually sells the part that I told you I needed - none of the sites sell the subwoofer board. So much for that. Eventually, by some act of God, I got the second metal tip out and when I tried to gorilla glue that one back on , the plastic tip broke off in my hand. So now I at least have a working subwoofer board but will have to buy new RCA cables. I certainly won't buy the OEM ones but will get some better quality ones off Amazon. It's too bad that they dropped the ball on this, because the sound (when I can actually use it) IS really good.

title: Great value, terrible bug.
text: Got this Soundbar, expecting to be underwhelmed due to the price. Sounds pretty good for the price, however there is a critical flaw: sound lag/non-existance for the first 2-3 seconds of audio on optical in sources. Basically, if the audio from the source has stopped (say a paused movie, or inactivity on an XBOX / PS3 dashboard) and then you start the audio source up again, there is a significant (2-3 second) delay during which time the video plays but there is no sound. The sound then fades back in (in sync with the video, so it's not a sync issue) and continues on as if it never happened. I reproduced this from several different sources (PC / XBOX / PS3 / TV) using several different cabling schemes. The issue was always reproducible. I spent an enormous period of time trying to track down what, exactly, is going on here, and I think it has to do with a design flaw in the soundbar itself. I eventually reached level 2 technical support at Vizio after describing the problem in excruciating detail to them, and they came back and said "This is a feature of the product, and there's nothing wrong with it". I messed with every possible setting on the sound bar, including "Eco mode", which I initially suspected as the auto-off culprit, but could not fix the problem. A sound bar that fails to play short sounds at key moments (ex: feedback from clicking a button on a computer or selecting an item in a console dashboard, or unpausing a movie)? Some "feature"!! Sadly, while I like the audio performance for the $$, I will have to return this until they fix this very annoying problem, as it makes it very annoying to use with a game console (e.g. PS3/ XBOX), a PC attached to the soundbar, or even pausing a movie. Note: This problem seems to only occur on optical in, tried it on bluetooth and it worked without any delay problem.

Battery life and charge time is excellent. I charged using an Anker setup, which was able to minimize the charge time, but still, the headphones have been left on for hours with no power loss. 3. Range is very good. I mainly use these paired to my phone and walk around the apartment with them on. 1400 sq ft and dropped signals nowhere. Cons: 1. The ear cups could be deeper. This is one of the only ways the build falls short of my Sony studios--the fit on the ears is not very comfortable. 2. Mic is average. This has been mentioned in previous reviews. 3. Sound is Good to Very Good. I mean, they're bluetooth headphones, I'm not using them to spin Led Zeppelin 4. Bottom line: If you are looking for good sound and wirelessness at an affordable price, these are the headphones for you.

title: Disappointing
text: UPDATE 11/25/2014: Upgrading to 4 stars from 2. The manufacturer sent me a free replacement - they said the issues have been fixed, and the issues I mention have. No more chemical smell and the sound is pretty good, better than I remember with the original set. The annoying hum is gone as well. I was able to use it to watch a movie, the sound was enjoyable, with no annoying hum. I like all the buttons. The one issue I had was the size and material of the earcups. I wish they were bigger and softer. My ears hurt a little towards the end of the 80 minute movie. If the earcups were improved this would be near-perfect. UPDATE 4/4/2014: I wanted to add that these have the nasty chemical smell just like the BTX6, but again it's probably in the packaging/case not in the headphones itself. ORIGINAL REVIEW: I ordered these after being disappointed with the BTX6, hoping that the lack of bass emphasis would help the sound and be more comfortable - I was partially right. Pros: - More comfortable that the BTX6 - Clamping force is moderate, swivels front to back as well as up & down, but the ear-cups are still small Neutral: - Mids & Highs are better than the BTX6, while the bass still has presence. The sound is not spectacular - not as good as the Creative WP350 or Harmon Kardon BT, but ok for the price point, I guess. - Construction is not as solid as the metal BTX6, but acceptable Cons: - The big letdown - there's an extremely annoying hum/whine in the background when there's silence in the audio. This makes it especially unusable for movies or shows where there are periods of silence. This wasn't there in the BTX6, making me wonder if it's just my unit.

title: Great value!
text: These are some of the most amazing bluetooth headphones I've ever had. First off, they're some of the most reasonably priced bluetooth headphones I could find on Amazon. 2nd, the sound is absolutely amazing for the price (no disappointment there). If I had to write down at least 1 con for these headphones, I think it would have to be the comfort. I have sensitive ears, and after long hours of use my ears will tire from most headphones. Like I said though, that's only if I had to write down 1 con. These headphones are actually pretty comfortable. I'll wear them anywhere from 6-8 hours a day sometimes, and even though my ears will tire from wearing them long hours; I know a lot of other headphones that would be way worse. Okay, my final comment about these headphones is one of my favorite features. The amazon listing for these headphones is saying that these get up to 12 hours of use. I'm getting much MUCH more. I use these headphones every single day of the week at work. I literally charge them once a week, and that's using them at least an average of 4 hours a day... Now, one thing I did when I got them is read the instructions on initially charging the battery and followed them to the letter. I can't remember those instructions now, or I would list them here, but you get the point (follow the instructions!). Bottom line, I couldn't be more satisfied with this purchase. These headphones are a GREAT value, and if I could go back to when I made the choice to purchase these I would make the choice to do so again again and again.

title: Good if your expectations are reasonable - decent sound, inexpensive, and not visually distracting
text: Make sure your expectations are reasonable. In my case, I came from a pair of Klipsch Reference series speakers which I had to get rid of when we reorganized our living room and wall mounted the TV. The difference is night and day, but I also didn't expect this to sound better than my old speakers - or even comparable. What it will provide is passable sound, which is still a major improvement over basically any TV, at a low price, without being visually distracting - particularly if you've wall mounted your TV. That said, there are some caveats... For one thing, try to avoid putting the subwoofer in a corner - especially if that corner is next to where you sit. Because of the long wavelength of low frequencies and the reflections from the walls and floor, being in a corner makes the sub significantly louder in a distracting, boomy sort of way. Besides the boominess, being close to your seating area also makes it easier to localize the sound (low frequencies are less directional, but the soundbar doesn't play low enough so you can tell that part of the sound is coming from the soundbar while part is coming from the sub). If you put the sub in a different location it will reduce this effect considerably. In my case that meant putting it on the sidewall, and using RCA extension cables so that I could still place the surround speakers on either side. It also has been exhibiting some weird issue where sometimes when I turn it on and then switch inputs, hardly any sound comes out of the soundbar but the sub works normally. It doesn't always do this, and I have yet to determine if there's any pattern. It's definitely a software issue though - playing around with it a bit (such as rotating inputs again) causes it to correct itself eventually. It's a bit annoying, though nowadays many things are subject to software glitches (some low end receivers I've seen similar bizarre issues). On the up-side, Bluetooth pairing is remarkably easy, and I do find myself playing music from my phone through it while I work downstairs. It was also easy to setup and get running.

title: This is a fantastic solution to the receiver and huge speaker system it ...
text: Before I nit pick on this sound bar keep in mind I purchased this from WalMart for $198. This is a fantastic solution to the receiver and huge speaker system it replaced, I am not an audiophile. It comes with all the cables necessary to hook up. All the mounting brackets for hanging. Basically everything you need for an easy install. Sound quality is good and variety of settings is abundant, probably too many. Complaints: The biggest issue with this device is its grainy volume control. It is not jut bad it is poor. They need to make the volume adjustments finer. This really huge lacking in my opinion. The lack of fine volume adjustment is a result of the bars method of volume feedback indication. They use LEDs on the front of the bar to indicate volume level, as well as other levels, bass, treble, subwoofer level, etc., There are 12 LED indicators, 13 if you include 2 for midscale, which is clever. The volume has 24 adjustment levels and uses the 12 sets of LEDs plus a high and dim setting to generate the 24 levels of feedback. 24 levels of volume may seem like plenty, it is not. Keep in mind that your typical listening level will be at the first 1/3 to 1/2 of the sound range so your adjustment decreases to 8 to 12 levels, not good. Not sure if higher end bars have connectivity to the TV other than the audio output. This device only has input form the TV so there is no visual feedback on the TV screen for what is going on, just those LED's. My guess is that higher end bars have a better user feedback system than this system. All in All this package is GREAT for the price. If Vizio addresses the volume control I don't think you will find a better soundbar for the price.

title: I just know what I like and when I think the purchase was worth the ...
text: I am not an audiophile or an audio expert. I just know what I like and when I think the purchase was worth the money. I am extremely satisfied with this purchase. I had read a lot of the reviews and must say that most of the problems have been fixed with the firmware update. I did not have to do this update as my unit had already been updated. Set up was very easy and took less than an hour. I ran the optical cable from my DirecTV Genie directly into the optical cable on the sound bar. The digital cable I ran from my Blue Ray player into the digital cable input on the sound bar. You will have to change the sound bar input when you switch between devices but that is not that big of a deal. Only negative is the remote. Very small screen for old eyes but with enough light you can see. I would recommend you go the Vizio web site and follow the manual posted. I used my IPad and it made it much easier to follow the instructions especially for the remote. Settting my DirecTV remote to control the sound was very easy and also balancing the speakers. I placed my two back speakers on speaker stands at each end of the couch turned in a little toward the center of the room. Units come with brackets if you want to mount on the wall. Now I am sure there are better systems but what this one does for the money is what I want it to do. It adds to my viewing enjoyment. There is a whole world of hidden sounds that come alive. Dark Knight when Joker blows up the hospital, sounds start to the left and comes toward you. Saving Private Ryan when they are coming into the beach the sounds are a whole different world. Distant explosions, bullets pinging off the hull ect. Das Boat the water moving across the hull and creaking of the boat as they sink deeper. The sound of the destroyers propellers coming closer and the sudden explosion of the depth charges. The thing that surprised me the most was watching football. You hear behind you fan noise, not enough to be irritating but added to the environment. The system enhances my viewing enjoyment. What more could you ask for?

text: The best headphones I have ever owned. I have a large cranium/head/noggin' and buying hats or anything that goes on my head is always a gamble, but these are adjustable, comfortable, and sound very, very good. I have absolutely no problem wearing my set for hours at a time. They have an amazing battery life - I listen to them at a lower volume and only plug them in to charge over the weekends. The battery lasts 35-40 hours (the general 5 weekdays at work). Amazing! Another plus is that with the 4.0 bluetooth technology, incoming calls don't switch my music to my phone's speakers to allow the headset to ring, which was a problem with earlier versions on my phone. Speaking of calls, the microphone picks up my voice fine, even when talking very softly: it works better than my phone! EDIT: It took over a year but they finally broke due to being extended fully and worn that way all the time. Slightly disappointed, but I am used to this from headphones in general. title: Amazing batter life
text: I don't normally write product reviews, but these headphones are so surprisingly great that I really wanted to for them. My new laptop came with horrible, horrible speakers. And I hate cords with headphones, so I wanted to try bluetooth headphones. I've had success with bluetooth speakers, but they often run out of battery life pretty quickly. I've had these for four months now, and I love them. I'm pleased to say that these headphones have an amazing battery life. I can use them hours on end all week and only have to charge them once or twice a week. If I had to guess, I'd say the battery life well exceeds 12 hours. I use these a LOT. The headphones trill a certain beep to remind you to charge them when the battery is low. Its battery is so long that I sometimes forget they even need charging in the first place. The sound is decent. If you're a very serious music listener or gamer, I might look elsewhere. But the bass is really decent for the price. I really enjoy the sound. They're some of the better headphones I've had over the years. The headphones rotate at the base so they can go into the provided carrying case, which is great. I use the case every day, because I take the headphones with my laptop with me to work to use on my lunch hour each day. It's a soft case, but rigid enough to protect the headphones. The only downside to these is that you have to use a regular sound cord while they charge. The one provided is really short. I charge the headphones over night so I don't have to deal with it.

title: Amazing headphones for the price: Quality sound, comfort, and convenience
text: As others have claimed, there is slight sound leakage, but it was not bad by any means, especially if I was listening to something at a reasonable volume level (which was always because they block out sound rather well), and, to get no leakage, I would have to spend far more money on much more expensive headphones (I got these on sale for about $30). I have been using these regularly for a couple years now and they have never let me down. I used Amazon's most popular bluetooth connector, and these headphones produce amazing sound quality even from ~30 feet away, or about ~20 feet away through a thin wall. This means I can bring it into my bathroom and continue listening to whatever was playing without cutting out at all - incredible!! Definitely the only headphone I've encountered that can do this consistently in this price range. Beyond this, the buttons on the headphones are well-placed and well-defined, and I almost immediately adapted to and started using them with ease. These also hold a charge for a very long time: Using them about 4-5 hours a day, I would probably only need to charge them about once a week. Obviously, there were periods during this that nothing was playing, but I'd say sound was playing about 80% of the time, and still sounded great and were extremely comfortable even on my somewhat large ears. At most, I would only have to take them off for a few minutes and just rub my ears a little bit or adjust them to put stress on a slightly different spot to continue with complete comfort. Again, in this price range, I have definitely never found a better set of headphones, and though the resulting build quality might not be top notch, I find that simply being as careful with them as you would with any electronic device has kept there from being any issues with breaking whatsoever.

title: very good headphones. Great sound quality
text: These were very, very good headphones. Great sound quality, great comfort, great battery, you name it. But it did fall in certain areas. As noted by other reviewers, these headphones experience sound leakage. Someone next to you will likely be able to tell what you're listening to a certain degree, but it won't leak into another room and disturb your housemate. So as long as you are in your room, you're fine. Another area it falters in is durability. I knew about this coming in to the purchase so I treated it gingerly usually, but I did occasionally rough it up (i.e. tossing to the bed, accidentally dropping on the floor). Mine lasted a year and a half, before the right fell off, dangling by its wires. It still works, if that's any consolation. What it took to break my set of headphones is accidentally falling asleep in them. So with that in in mind, I think it lasted a fair amount of time for the price I paid, which if iirc was 40 dollars, and that it had great sound while it lasted.

title: Works okay, just really uncomfortable for people with small ears
text: I have owned these for a little over one month and they seem to be holding up fine. The sound quality is average for this type of earbuds, the sound output/volume for spoken word podcasts is a little better than average, the battery life is accurate as advertised, and I have had no connectivity issues. The touch function is finicky and delayed, but for me, it's better than a super sensitive touch pad that gets pressed if your hair or sleeve brushes against it -- if you're using these for a lot of phone calls, I'd say to look elsewhere. But the shape and stiffness of the ear hooks ultimately made me stop wearing these, and I can definitely never keep them on for any extended period of time. I have slightly small ears. The large, thick ear hook doesn't bend or flex at all. It presses on two different parts of my ear & pushes the in-ear portion out and away from my head. I end up with very sore ears and can't get a snug fit. There are a LOT of smaller, lighter, and more streamlined designs out there -- that being said, if you have bigger ears than me, they might not cause you any issues. I've been burned by random off-brand wireless earbuds dying right after the return window is up, but I don't think I'll be able to see if these ones stand up to the test of time, because they just don't work for my ear shape.

text: This is my second pair of JLabs earbuds — I lost the first pair, which didn't have the ear hooks, and got these as a replacement. They are a big disappointment. What are the problems? The volume, at maximum, is so low that I can barely hear a recorded book; ok in a quiet room, but useless in the gym or while riding a bike. The "button" is no longer a button but a capacitive touch device with no tactile (or audio) feedback, so you can't tell whether or not you have pressed it. I find that I go forward a chapter when I'm trying to pause playing, or change the mode. There are no instruction, so I never found out what "music mode" or "movie mode" are, or which I should use when listening to a book. "Customer service" could not even give me the instruction manual. But the worse issue is that there is no adjustment of the position of the speaker with the spect to the ear hook: if the hook is around my ear, then the speaker isn't pointing into my ear canal, and if I put the speaker into my ear, then the hook sticks out and the whole thing falls off. title: Fantastic for the money
text: I just got these a few days and used them for about an hour on the first day. The sound quality is awesome. I love the Jlabs Signature EQ Setting. It's the perfect balance of bass and treble with good mid levels. The ear buds are super comfortable and will be great for long term use. I first used them while helping my young daughter with an online pre-kindergarten course. The "Be Aware" feature is super cool. I was able to hear my daughter ask questions and hear the audio coming from the laptop through the earbuds while still being able to hear my music. Later, I needed to quickly vacuum the house so I turned off "Be Aware" to completely block out noise from the vacuum. Since then I've used them while doing miscellaneous chores around the house and going shopping. They stay in the ear really well. They charge in the case really fast and the case itself charges quickly as well. I've only used them for one phone call. The description states these feature stereo phone calls - I only noticed audio coming from the left side. I will continue to watch this. The person I was talking to had no complaints about the audio quality coming from me even though I was outside and talking quietly. I love the the touch controls. I had considered the Jlab Air (non-sport) ear buds but after watching reviews, the thought of having to push physical buttons and thereby pushing the ear bud deeper into my ear turned me away. text: I'm usually not this effusive....but these are the best ear buds I've every had. They are all the things ear buds should be: nice quality sound, easy buttons on the buds, good mic, comfortable, stay in place (as good as any earbuds I've used), pair easily. Two things that set these apart: they stay charged an amazing length of time AND they recharge in their case which also holds a charge for a long time. Only con, and not a deal breaker, they are very smooth and difficult to get out of the case if you have big or clumsy fingers.

title: Charges quickly
text: I use it about an 1-2 hours a day for my morning walks.

title: Finally found the last earbuds I'll ever buy!
text: I am absolutely in love with these earbuds. I've gone through so many pairs from many brands and these are my end game buds! First of all, the packaging is very nice, very fancy and boxed up very well. The case itself is awesome, it closes and stays closed... shows clearly how much battery is left and charges quickly with its charging cable. Being able to use my wireless charger on the case is pretty neat as well. They connect automatically and super quickly once I take them out. They're connected before I'm even able to stick them in my ear. My absolute favorite feature is that whatever I'm listening to pauses when I take them from my ear and it starts playing when I put them back in my ear. I love that you can use just one at a time. My calls are very clear. The people who I have talked to also sya they can hear me just fine with no background noise and they wouldn't have known I was on earbuds if I hadn't told them. The battery power is great also. I'm just beyond happy that I purchased these. I almost lost one the second day I had them and was about to buy another set just because I did NOT want to be without them now that I know what they're like lol! They are absolutely worth the money and I'm very surprised they're not more pricey!

title: real and the best earbuds
text: EarFun Air True Wireless Earbuds, The voice quality and long battery life really worth for the purchase. They are so comfortable to stay in the ears , much more comfortable in my opinion. The headphones usually fell if I had to pick up something from floor and created a mess. I have been so happy to use the Earbuds to enjoy music and phone calls

title: Lacking Features
text: Hello! Just a quick note to say these work pretty good. They sound decent, and the price point was pretty good too when comparing to Apple Airpods. Just one really weird lacking feature is there is no way to repeat a track after it has ended. You either have to use your watch to do it, or grab your phone and do it on there. I find this really odd and was convinced I missed something, so I emailed the company. Just an email back that said it doesn't have that feature. I am still considering returning these as I have a pair of $35 Anker Soundcore headphones that sound great and do have all of the necessary features. Just my two cents!

title: Compatibility problems, and bad in-ear detection.
text: These earphones seem to have some serious compatibility problem with Windows. The sound cuts in and out on one or the other, and there are glitches, distortion, static, looping sounds, and other problems The in-ear detection is a pain. It's nice that they pause your media when you take them out, but they invariably detect my hand, or the tabletop if I set them down, and start playback again. They do sound good, and the battery life is good, so if not for these other problems I would give them a much higher score.

title: Controls didn't work right. Sound OK but distant.
text: Bought these to replace a dying EarFun Free set. The shape is comfortable, and they charge fast, but that's all I could recommend. Sound - Distant. Didn't matter which ear tip I used, or how much volume. Everything still sounded distant in my ear. Controls - Finicky. To use the play/pause function, you tap on an earbud twice. This did not work right. Even when I found the 'right' delay per tap, it would only respond half of the time. Ended up returning them. Maybe I'll get another EarFun Free set instead...those at least work properly.

title: Worth more than the price!
text: If you are looking for wireless earbuds at a bargain price these are what you need. They are the real deal when it comes to everything you need in earbuds. I'm always skeptical of reviews but if you do your research you will find plenty of positive reviews all over the internet. They have worked perfectly since day one!

title: It's ok but not great

title: Excellent

Four sizes of tips should provide the correct size to fit almost anyone's ears including those needing a different size in each ear. Sound quality is very good. The touch controls are excellent. Touch the right earbud to increase volume and the left to reduce. Having tried several brands of these discount earbuds I find these to be the best yet and easily worth their price.

title: AirPods alternative !
text: [[VIDEOID:a2335e8c422a7181a877303741d6191]] These paired easily and quickly. When you open the case, you can confirm that there’s power and it pairs automatically to the iPhone. title: Great Earbuds
text: I had a problem with my first set of earbuds losing connection, so I contacted the EarFun customer service. I tried the suggestions they gave in hopes of fixing the problem. They did not work, so I followed up with customer service, and they provided a new pair with free shipping. The new earbuds arrived quickly, and I've experienced no problems with the new set. The earbuds provide excellent sound, do not fall out while riding my bike and maintain a connection even when I walk away from my phone. Customer service alone is reason enough to buy these earbuds.

title: Perfect to get the job done on a budget
text: These are fantastic substitute for EarPods. If your not a brand snob or an audiophile, save yourself $100 and just buy these over Apple’s version. Despite lacking the magic W1 Apple Bluetooth chip, they have worked flawlessly for me so far. Volume is good. Sound quality is adequate (way way better than expected for the price). I was ready for these to suck, but I took a chance on them because they were cheap and got extraordinary reviews. Glad I did. If you’re a super audiophile you probably won’t be happy with AirPods either anyway. If you’re buying these just for phone calls or to workout like I did, why spend $150-200 on the Apple ones? These even come with the little charging box. Yeah they are a ripoff of Apple’s product. So is 30% of the stuff in Amazons electronics section. Who cares? You’re getting 80% of the product for 30% of the price. I believe in paying for extra quality when it matters most. I wouldn’t settle for a janky Android phone with a wannabe iOS skin interface, but when it comes to these, the value is there and the difference is negligible. My biggest concern was reliability and it’s been stellar. They pair up to my iPhone 12 Pro instantly, flawlessly every time. The controls work as advertised. The battery life is sufficient. What else could I expect for $50? These have been a really pleasant surprise. I’m telling everyone I know about ‘em. Buy them.

title: They sound great....

title: Sound good BUT no 'Previous Track' option!
text: Sound good BUT no 'Previous Track' option! Seriously - not even mentioned in the manual. To skip a track you tap 3 times (too many!) on the right one - but the 'previous track' is not, as I had hoped, simply tapping 3 times on the left one. Plus, they are very hard to get out of the case. I am returning it.

title: Second time is the charm!
text: First set I purchased had problems. Left earbud stopped working after 2 weeks. After finally hearing from customer service they did eventually replace the set. The new set is working great so far, no issues. Happy with the new ones.

title: Awesome Earbuds!
text: I am surprised these are so good for $50! I bought these to replace my old Bose ear buds, I forget what they were exactly called but their wire was stripped white and black and I LOVED those.. the bass was beautiful and they fit wonderfully. The EarFun is a close second to my old pair I mentioned, the bass is there but not quite much of an "oompf" as the others. They definitely do a great job though and they fit perfectly as well. The sound quality drops off a bit if you have these on max volume, might even hear a crackling sound but that is not really a bother to me. I am not really a fan of the "ear bud" types, you know those ones that violate the insides of your ear. These don't really do that surprisingly. I am also not a fan of bluetooth ear buds, but technology is moving forward so I gotta make do and see how these really last, hopefully a long time. So far I recommend these highly, I'll update my review over time to see the longevity of these.

title: Great Value
text: Very good product and is similar to brands that are around $150 For the money, it is a great set of value earbuds. Good sound, water resistant, and good battery The only downside that I have noticed is that at higher volume levels, there is a warble or distorted highs. It's like cheaper speakers in a car, when it hits the highs, it kind of becomes distorted I bought and returned a $150-$175 pair of Samsung Galaxy buds maybe a year and a half ago, and these are just as good, with the exception of the distortion that happens at loud volume I would highly recommend this product, if you want good wireless earbuds and you want to save about $100

title: You get what you pay for

title: Update! OMG aggravation central
text: Update! Am upgrading this to three stars because their customer service is exceptional. They reached out to me and sent me a different style which work so much better!!! Old review: I have small ear canals. I thought these ear buds that tuck in and lock down would be the key. Except they refused to stay in my ears. Threatening to fall out every 5 seconds was only part of the annoyance. Here I am at the gym strength training, listening to my workout playlist and every 30 seconds I have to reseat the buds in my ears. Uh-oh. You've touched the ear buds. This means you must want to command your music streaming app to pause playback! No? You didn't? TOO BAD. You shall not listen to a single song without halting playback multiple times and having to pull out your phone and restart it. By the end of my 60 minute workout I had to remind myself that I was too poor to stomp these things into the ground rather than return them for credit. Would not recommend.

title: Worth the money
text: This is an absolutely crucial purchase if you work in a shared space (crowded coffee shop), fly for longer than 30 minutes, or if you just appreciate hearing the nuances of a song. I was hesitant to buy them after reading about the condensation issue but I’ve worn them now for several weeks and have only seen condensation once, which came during a marathon writing session. The carrying case is a joke but if you’re spending this much for headphones, I suppose you know how to take care of nice things. Buy the headphones, you won’t regret them.

title: Still forming an opinion
text: I see people raving up and down about the perfection and wonderfulness of these headphones; I’m not as completely blown away by them as those people are. Quality of construction does seem to be excellent (although because Amazon doesn’t lower all prices at the start of Prime Day but only lowers some of them well after Prime Day has begun, I had to send back the first pair I bought and purchase another pair to get a discounted price, and the piston things for extending and compressing the size of the headphones was smoother on the first pair I had) and they’re comfortable enough to wear for extended periods, but while it may be a limitation of Bluetooth (I don’t know), I haven’t noticed myself being amazed by their bass response. No, in fact I just now watched the video for Shake It Off and listened to a couple of Lana Del Rey tracks and these headphones are definitely lacking in bass response – as in, there’s very little, and what there is gets completely lost under any midrange and high-end sounds that may be playing at the same time. They’re tinny-sounding. I have to wonder what the people are listening to with these who are praising the sound quality so enthusiastically. On the other hand, I don’t ordinarily listen to music anymore, but only to talks and lectures; While I’m watching movies is probably the only time I’m going to really want big bass, and I watched The Revenant last night and didn’t feel like I was missing anything… So their construction is much more solid than that of probably most other headphones on the market, they’re comfortable to wear, and there’s a nice ecosystem of accessories out there, but I personally find the sound quality quite lacking and I’m going to have to decide whether to hang onto these or return them.

title: Best headphones ever
text: They’re Apple, so they’re pricey, but worth it. Comfortable to wear, turn on and off by themselves, have transparent mode which is important when walking outside, and the sound is great.

title: Best Headphones but Hurts My Ear Lobes
text: They are very excellent head-phones. The spacial audio is phenomenal. Noise cancellation is great. With all that said -- I had to return them because they start hurting my ear lobes after 45 minutes, which totally interferes with my full enjoyment of listening to BAND-MAID for hours and hours. When Apple redesigns them for maximum comfort and where I can wear them for a full day without hurting my ear lobes, then I will buy that pair.

title: Great audio quality but mic quality not up to par
text: I used a Bose 700 headset for most the pandemic, and was hoping these would be an upgrade. Alas, for calls, the microphone in these is inferior. I did random tests, switching between the two headsets, with coworkers, and every single one said I sounded far better on the other headset. The AirPods Max has a mic that’s about on par with standard AirPods, but nowhere near as good as what Bose currently has. I hope Apple fixes this with a future AirPods Max 2…

title: Love these so much — great if you have several Apple devices
text: These are really well made, quality headphones. The build is perfect, just like an iPhone everything fits perfectly and is well finished. There are clever little design touches like the removable earcups — you can buy new ones when you get grossed out by the old ones. The spinning knob feels great and can be used to get exactly the volume you want, perfect when you are trying to fall asleep. I find these comfortable enough to wear almost 24/7. The sound transparency is top-notch, actually helps me understand people as I’m hard of hearing. They don’t have an off-button but they go into a very low power mode automatically so I don’t miss that. Using this with many different Apple devices is the best improvement over my old headphones, I used to spend ten minutes switching my other headphones in an app and in settings — having more than two Apple devices is probably the best use case for this product. Well, that and also I can use these with the Apple TV, there is no lag and it connects quickly. Drawbacks: 1) apparently these are not for really high-end listening to lossless audio, but they sound great compared to other Bluetooth noise canceling headphones 2) they are heavy (actually made of metal) and might put too much pressure on the head for some (less comfortable than Bose 35s) 3) too fragile for workouts and not a bit water resistant 4) case is completely useless. 10/10 would buy again.

title: Great headphones but overpriced (by quite a bit)
text: I’m giving these a 5 rating because they really are great headphones, but $550 is a big overreach. Sound quality = 5 stars; comfort = 3.5 stars; noise reduction/transparency = 5 stars (really you could add a star!). My favorite thing about these headphones is how how easily they pair and transfer from one apple device to the next. These are definitely for Apple universe people. All in all these are really good headphones but from a bang-for-your- buck perspective, definitely not worth the price tag. The only reason to buy them is because you want them.

title: I’m so happy!
text: I’ve read hundreds of reviews. Let’s face it, time well invested at this price point! I was prepared for all the bad. I purchased silicone covers for the ear pieces and the headband before the headphones even arrived (less than $20 for 5 pieces). I expected monumental disappointment with the included case. But I waited to purchase something different. The headphones arrived (I purchased from a big box store brand new - better deal for me). First, the charging. I’m deep in the Apple ecosystem so I just plugged them into my iPhone charging cord. Simple. After charging I thoroughly enjoyed a good hour of music. Sound wise, I’m in love with the experience. These are comfortable and perform as I would expect. I placed them in the goofy included case. It too performed as intended. Absolutely zero battery drain. But I decided that my shiny new purchase required a better case. I purchased mine from Amazon. My headphones were instantly recognized by my all my devices so I had zero connectivity issues. Devices include: phone, laptop and tablet. I easily switched between all three. These are loud. I don’t understand why anyone would complain about them not being loud enough. You’ve got undiagnosed hearing problems if you can’t hear properly even at 50% volume. I haven’t mastered everything these have to offer but now that I’ve spent the money and enjoyed the listening experience, I regret nothing! And that’s coming from someone who has never ever spent that kind of money on headphones. Bottom line: these headphones are expensive but amazing! They’re user friendly and everything you need to know is available on several platforms for you to make an informed decision (ie: what comes in the box and weather you need an adapter). Save your pennies and purchase them new from an authorized Apple retailer. If you’re going to drop over $500 on headphones, you should not squeal about the extra expense of maintaining their care. I’ve spent years purchasing Apple products and out of the dozen or more products, I had one bad experience a la my wireless carrier, not Apple.
