title: Absolute unreliable junk! (TWO different purchases)
text: I returned the first pair after having connectivity issues with my Apple devices (MacBook, iMac, iPad, iPhone). Being the Apple Fanboy that I am, I later caved and purchased another set after reading more rave reviews. But then I ran into even worse connectivity issues. I have to manually connect to a device EVERY time I switch. And the instant I switch, I see the AirPods Max disconnect from the previous device. It's a time-consuming hassle. So much for the Airpod Max working with the Apple ecosystem, huh? Interestingly, I've had a pair of Sony XM4s that have worked superbly. Granted, they remain connected to no more than 2 devices simultaneously. But they do it REALLY well. I upgraded to the Sony XM5s recently and like them even better. So the bottom line for me is that Sony works better with the Apple ecosystem than the AirPods Max do...which is kinda nuts, huh? Two different sets of AirPods Pros have worked extremely well, so I have no clue why TWO pairs of the AirPods Max have been utter junk.

title: swing and a miss, status symbol?
text: I was pretty excited when apple decided to come out with these but they left me disappointed enough that I returned them. For startes, the cloth is not comfortable. Having had incredibly comfortable quiet cloth it's what I expect for a premium set of cans. The noise cancelling is rated quite well but because of the design and padding if you turn your head, gaps form which destroys the noise cancelling. Thirdly these are HEAVY for headphones. The padding does a surprisingly good job helping but the fact is they are needlessly heavy. Having them this heavy both creates strain on the user, and makes it so they don't track head movements well unless exaggeratedly slow. The benefits are the same you'll get from other apple products (within their ecosystem), with the exception that the sound is clearly superior to AirPods which they frankly have to be. The battery life for it's class is meh.

title: Very nice headset. Great noise cancellation. Battery does not last long.
text: I was enjoying this headset. It fit in well with all my Apple items. Noise cancellation was excellent... best I have experienced. But, battery life was horrible. Even when you put them in the case, which puts them to sleep... you can't turn them off otherwise. I would put a fairly charged set in the case and sleep it went then took them out the next morning and the dreaded red light came on indicating the battery was in dire need of charging. In doing some research I saw that many others were noting this issue on Apple talk boards. One other issue, the controls on the top of the ear pads often got activated when trying to take off the headset... I found them to be awkwardly placed. I found the Bose 700 controls much easier to use and less obtrusive, for instance. Very awkward placement. So, I returned them, sadly. I really enjoyed them otherwise.

title: Better than my Bose headphones
text: Got this for the wife for Christmas. She was using my Bose headphone and loves the AirPods Max so much better. Has a lot of functions and design she loves.

title: Nothing better at its price.
text: Impressive sound quality -- these reveal the space and air around instruments; are detailed without being strident; reproduce deep, tight bass; kill extraneous sounds very effectively; and are the most comfortable headphones I've ever used. A plus: Apple TV users can employ them as a quite effective surround-sound system for viewing Dolby Atmos content -- offering sound that would cost thousands more in front/center/side/rear speakers/amps. I and my wife each have a pair for such use.

title: Apple build, Apple UI, Apple sound -- best-in-show quality
text: I could wear this headset all day -- its design distributes their mass equally over/around the head. The earcups seal well, seemingly without pressure, but with excellent effect. Noise cancellation is close to perfection. Treble and mids are detailed without being aggressive; bass goes seriously deep without artificial boominess. Listening to TV content with Dolby Atmos over my Apple TV 4k is ear-opening -- a solo viewer could replace home theater speakers (two headsets can also be paired to an Apple TV 4k). As is usual with Apple, the price reflects value received (still, I waited for a 100-dollar-off sale). Particularly for those with an Apple-centric household, Airpods Max deliver an easy path to audiophile quality from Mac to iPad to iPhone to Apple TV. Their case, while unusual (maybe even amusing), does present a compact solution to packing for travel (if you're not wearing them to the train/bus/plane).

Pairing to the iPhone and iPad are quick and seamless. Dollar for dollar, the Max outshines the 5909. title: Awesome if you’re an apple user!
text: I solely use apple devices, and was looking for a noise cancelling headset that could easily work between multiple apple devices. The apple AirPods max does exactly that. I have used other headphones in the past like Sony and Bose but honestly I didn’t like the white noise sound they’d make, and how frequently frustrating it would be to connect the headphones between various apple devices seamlessly. The airpod max are a little overpriced in my opinion. The headphone’s storage case is pretty useless, it offers zero protection to the headphones. It’s not a hard case just a soft one that doesn’t even cover the top band. When I stick these in my bag I’ll actually put them in an old hard camera case because that protects them more than the case apple provided for them. Despite that though it does a very well job of smoothly connecting to my different apple devices depending on which one I’m using. Almost 2 months in on using it and I’ve never had an issue with them randomly disconnecting or not pairing properly, even with non-apple devices like my gaming PC. The noise cancellation is pretty great too, it doesn’t cancel out 100% of the background noises depending on what that noise is and how relative it is to you. It has multiple modes (2 or 3 depending on the device) so you can switch the noise cancelling off if needed. For example, it does a really great job of cancelling the loud construction noises outside my apartment, barking dogs, loud cars (including the construction vehicles) and people talking in the background but it doesn’t do as well as job of cancelling out the noise of my boyfriend streaming sports on the background. It cancels a good amount of the game and his “enthusiasm” but it doesn’t cancel as much as I wish it would. Overall I would highly recommend this to anyone who owns multiple apple devices, wants seamless connection, and is looking for a better noise cancelling solution than what the normal air pods offers. I would not recommend this if you don’t have apple devices or only have one but use android/other operating systems. Yes the noise cancelling feature is great, but at this price point it’s not worth it in comparison to other noise-cancelling headphones priced similarly.

title: Excellent headphones for those in the Apple ecosystem; decent for those who are not
text: I consider myself firmly rooted in Apple's walled garden, but am by no means a zealous fanboy. That said, I would not buy these headphones without an iPhone and without an Apple Music subscription. The only way to justify the price tag is to make full use of every feature it offers and without those two you'll be out of luck. The soundstage is absolutely brilliant, and coupled with Dolby Atmos it will change the way some of your favorite tracks sound for the better. The sound-cancelling is first in class. Build quality is amazing and although I have experienced condensation during extended listening periods, they're easy to clean and it doesn't happen often. It's easy to gawk at the price tag if you compare them to other noise-cancelling headphones on the market, but none of them offer the seamlessness these do. Make sure to spend time learning how to get the most of this pair before buying!

title: Battery drains no matter what
text: I really wanted these to work. I'm pretty invested in the Apple Ecosystem and am very happy with all of my Apple devices (iPhone, Macbook Pro, Airpods Pro, etc). I was never willing to pay full price for these, but when they finally went on sale, I pulled the trigger. The noise cancelling is good. I like the physical controls. The touch controls on my Sony XM4s are horrible to deal with. I often turn them off on accident or pause the music just by shrugging. That's about all the good I can say about these. I'm not sure if they didn't quite connect to my iPhone correctly, or it's just the way they work, but even in their "bra" case, these headphones drained completely dry overnight. I tested this over 3 days, charging them to full, using them for about an hour, then putting them in their case (the right way) and setting them down. When I got up in the morning they were completely dead. I did not try unpairing them and pairing them again because, it's Apple and I would have expected them to work properly out of the box. Even if this isn't normal and they usually drain at a much slower pace, the fact that you can't turn them off is such a horrible design decision that I can't even fathom how this is an Apple product. My Sony and Bose headphones can be turned off and as a result, will last for weeks on a charge. These will never last you more than a few days because they're always draining. The battery will degrade from the daily charging within one year. The best headphones from Sony and Bose are half the price, the Sony's have better noise canceling over all, and they sound comparable. I can't see any reason to buy these at this price, even if you're heavily invested in Apple like I am.

I was unsure how I would like the mesh headband area, but its actually very comfortable. The ear pieces sit gently area the ears and have a nice cushion to them for comfort. A thing I would love to see improved would be the case....I nearly always put it in backwards and can't plug them in if they aren't in the correct way. It could stand to be a little more user friendly. It's just sort of clunky. You really have to pay attention to put them away the right way. So at first I didn't put them away. If you don't put them away, every little bump or rattle wakes them up (great if its on purpose, annoying when its not) and will slowly drain the battery long term. Honestly if the case was something you could use without having to think about it, these would be perfect imho. Battery life is great. Even with forgetting to put them away and accidentally bumping them on a lot, it still takes a long time to drain the battery. They really last when you properly store them in the case between uses. Best level of reliability, comfort, and sound quality so far out of four different brands and designs. Initial pluses: tactile controls - I am so sick of touch-sensitive controls which create difficulties when your skin is dry or when wearing gloves; intuitive controls - everything is located where it makes sense to have them (for a right-handed person, at least); and comfort - the arrangement around the neck is surprisingly comfortable and the ear buds stay in place I think because of the lack of weight dangling on them. Initial minuses: rechargeable - Lord knows how long this will last - where is the genius who makes one of these w/ disposable batteries?; battery level indicator - you have to put the unit on and listen to know the battery level (low, med, or high - what that means in runtime remains to be seen); and sound quality adjustments - the tone function has three preset adjustments (lots of bass, some bass, and tinny). This is an updated review - I'm happy with how these are performing. People I call have remarked on the improved sound quality over previous devices. I've used the set for several extended phone calls and the battery level remains "high".

Would recommend just buying these in store at a place that does price matching.... Amazon, is really letting go of itself and it's product quality.

title: Good product, but sometime it is hard to connect the left side
text: I don't know why, I bought 2 of those and both units have problems syncing the left side sometimes. I would still recommend it as the sound and microphone are good.

title: Desent
text: A little disappointed in the bass. Not near enough have to jam the ear buds in deep.

title: Don't buy!!!
text: I bought these and for a while they worked great but after a few months I could only connect the right ear. The left ear would only turn on if the right ear was already on and paired. I like to use on at a time and switch them when the battery died I don't not recommend buying these. Also it was always a hassle paring them I always had to manually do it on my phone.

title: Ghetto AirPods
text: They feel and sound a little better than Apple AirPod Pros but these JBLs had endless connectivity, battery, sound and range issues the entire time I used them. They would turn off for no reason, disconnect to the point of having to 'discover' the bluetooth with my device again, or just disconnect for one second resulting in constant pausing of my content. They also have zero features like Noise Cancelling or Transparency. I hated these for four months until I got AirPods. Then I only used the JBLs as backups but I just tried to use them and failed for the last time, trash time. The JBLs just feel and sound a little better, will save you some money, but drive you completely insane. Treat yourself to the AirPod of the Pros.

title: maybe a lemon pair?
text: They lasted 4 hours fully charged. the sound was very good. Didn't even have 9 months and they stopped charging and got an awful burning smell and super hot. Like i said, i may have gotten a lemon set.

title: Don’t buy them. You will regret it.
text: Very disappointed. One headphone did not work. The other one sounded very bad. I have some $25 wireless headphones that sound better. Very disappointed JBL.

title: Sounds great stays in ear
text: As advertised, I run in them and they stay out.

title: Wont stay in my ear
text: I'll be walking along and one or the other just pops out.

title: Not good for cycling
text: I have tried using different ear wings and bud and they have excessive wind noise coming through. I had jaybird vistas and jabra 75 that had no wind noise at all. These are definitely not good for cycling. The sound is fine when you are indoors are just walking. Decent amount of bass and treble. My husband could hear me talking to him through the mics while riding my bike but I couldn't hear him well due to the aforementioned wind noise.

title: More Bass
text: I'm serious about my music. I want to hear every single note as it was intended. These earbuds are for people like me who care deeply about sound quality. The bass is amplified to make your favorite songs sound their best. You also get quick charging and long playtime. You can use the app to customize the sound. I HIGHLY recommend this product. Thanks so much for taking the time to read this review. I hope the information that I've provided makes your decision a little easier.

title: excellent sound quality and features for the $80 price
text: The first couple of generations of Soundcore headphones were pretty mediocre. I'm glad the company keep improving their products. This year's models are really good for the price. I got the Life A2 model. For $80, these earbuds come with features that I usually see on earbuds that cost more than $100 like equalization, noise cancellation, and upgradable firmware. These features all work great. I especially like the equalization that noticeably improves sound clarity. Overall, the sound quality is great for earbuds that cost less than $100. Bass is not boomy, but great if you like a more natural sound. Stereo separation is excellent. Clarity at the higher frequencies is excellent when I set the equalizer to type of music that I'm listening too. Volume is better than average for true wireless earbuds. These earbuds are on the larger side, but they don't stick out of my ears too much, so I don't constantly knock them out like I do with Apple-style earbuds. They are comfortable and secure enough in my ears. I'm using an Android smartphone and the earbuds pair easily with my phone. Bluetooth connection has been solid. The Soundcore Android app is necessary to manage the equalizer and upgrade the firmware and both features work great. The app also shows your battery levels. Unfortunately, the app does spam me occasionally with unrelated Anker product announcements. I wish they wouldn't do that. Anker spams me enough by email.

title: Good microphone
text: I have a few other Bluetooth earbuds. When I use them to call my father, who is hard of hearing, he can't hear what I'm saying on a phonecall. He hears me just fine on these. They work well for video calls, too.

title: Pairing Issues
text: Purchased due in large part to Advertisement re " EASY PAIRING" .. I could not pair with my Galaxy S10 Phone. Called customer support ..... on phone 25 min. no success . Advised to return for replacement.

title: They made a great product and I made a great decision.
text: My last earbuds were destroyed by a rogue grocery store fridge door. Upon searching for replacements, I found a ton of options - too many. I decided to go with Anker because their products have always been so impressive. It was a great decision. The sound is great. The fit is great (the pack comes with several sizes of fittings, from x-small, small, medium, large, and x-large). The ear lock piece was firm and uncomfortable at first but after a few wearings, the rubber softened - but they still hold the earbud in. Battery life: Seems to go on forever. BT connection: Lightning fast. My last pair (a different brand) were so much trouble trying to connect. Volume: They can be turned down to a whisper or up too loud - every time. My last pair had a lowest setting of 'too loud'. Button customization: you can download an app to customize the controls - It works great. I love it. I recommend these. I'm not usually a brand loyal, but Anker has proven to me time and time again that their products are legit.

title: Great earbuds, but not for me.
text: For the most part these are very good earbuds and should serve most people well. I drive for a living and have to deal with constant road noise. The noise cancelling worked well enough but they don't get as loud as I would like them. The microphone is decent. I would also prefer there be Voice notifications when pressing the buttons. Especially when switching between noise cancelling, transparency, and normal. The app is great. It would be better if there were more control options available. I understand why it was done this way but I would rather have the option to single press if I wanted it, even if the occasional accidental press was inevitable.

title: Great sound, but NOT Bluetooth Multi-mode!
text: My old $40 GeeKee buds started acting up & I shopped for a Bluetooth multi-mode set, which my GeeKees are. Meaning I can connect to my laptop & my phone BOTH AT THE SAME TIME. Watching a video on my laptop with the GeeKees, when I get a phone call I just tap an earbud to answer or reject the call. When I answer, once I finish the call I tap to hang & the audio & video from my laptop auto restart. That does not happen with the Anker Life A2 NC buds. Pity, they do sound great. Lawrence

title: High quality sound
text: High quality sound ear buds that work well with noise cancellation. The battery life is spot on especially with the charging case.

title: Good
text: This set is not very expensive but does the job.

title: Outstanding TWS buds
text: I’ve been an Anker fan for a long time and these earbuds do not disappoint. Sound quality is excellent and the ANC is also excellent. I had to discard the wings for better fit but that’s due to my large ears! I’m very pleased with these earphones (and in very picky).

title: Decent Headphones, worth the purchase
text: What can I say, I do like these headphones, the noise isolation is great. The Active Noise Cancelling could be better as well as the Ambient Sound. There are multiple setting for each mode, Transport-Indoor-Outdoor for Noise Cancellation and Fully Transparent-Vocal Mode for Ambient Sound. For me personally, if they had focused on making one great setting for each mode, I feel they might have sounded better. Now listening to music and watching videos the sounds is great, you get just enough bass to not overwhelm whatever you are listening to, and I love bass, so while I wouldn't have minded more, these are good enough for what I purchased them for. All in all, these are some decent true wireless earbuds for the price, I just feel they fell kinda short on two of the features.

title: Punches above its weight!
text: these buds rival those double its costs, to say the least. What I really love about Anker is the app support. If you check the app store ratings, its one of the best, compared with Sony's, Bose's, Jabra's, etc. Soundcore knows how to build a nice app that supports its products really well. The buds themselves feel nice to the touch, has good texture and a good fit. It does stick out a little more than I'd like, so definitely not to fall asleep in. The case is a matte finish, no fingerprints. Small enough, although bigger than most for this category. Also has usb-c, which is a nice touch, but expected nowadays. Only thing missing is wireless Qi charging, but forgivable at this price. Now, the sounds. First things first, you can use either independently. Much appreciated since others more than twice its cost (cough: Jabra) can't do that. The ANC is ok, nothing compared with the higher end ones. More like a gimmick in my use case. Barely works. Transparency as well. Has a hissing sound when turned on and have no music or low music on. I tend to just turn both off. Now, the sound itself. This is where the buds outdo themselves. Great soundstage although gets a little muffled when lows kick in. The bass is deep and you could feel it thanks to its 11mm drivers. The different EQ settings help as well, and you can tweak your own. I would say these rival the sounds of much higher end and higher priced buds. I've also paired them up with my work PC (a Dell) using a bluetooth dongle and used it for meetings on different platforms like Teams and Amazon connect softphone and works fairly well. Only one person stated I sounded distant. Sounds from their end comes crystal clear. This is a higly recommended pair of buds that punches above its weight!

title: Excellent value
text: Although I wish the noise cancellation was a little more robust I really like this Anker product. Anker has never let me down with other products I’ve purchased from them and this is no exception.

title: Just ok.
text: These are just ok. The volume is not that loud and they tend to fall out when running.

title: Great sound!!
text: Noise canceling is top tier!! Better than my Bose! Long battery life. Love the.!!!

title: ridiculous, clients can't hear me when i make phone calls on this
text: This is ridiculous! I bought it because had great reviews! I tried to return and they said they couldnt take it back (amazon) that it should go to the manufacturer! either way, people can't hear me when i make important calls on here! very very frustrating. they were expensive! where is the quality?

title: So wanted to like these
text: A great pair of headphones in all departments other than the basics, unfortunately. No matter of what combination of loops/inserts I tried these just wouldn't stay in my ears. Even the slightest motion makes them fall out. No way these would work for someone doing exercise. It's odd because old pair of Ankers work great. Ive contacted customer support and they were nice enough but no help with this issue. Touch controls are not sensitive enough and it takes multiple attempts to go to next track or change volume. Definitely will give Anker another chance when they come up with something good but these earbuds werent.

title: Don't buy
text: Wouldn't pair with my android phone returned for a refund!!

title: These headphones are amazing!
text: Amber always makes great products, and these didn’t disappoint! I bought them to replace my Beats because one of the earpieces broke off. These pair so easily - just like Apple’s, and the bass response is the best I’ve ever heard in an earphone. They stay in my ears at the gym and the battery life is awesome!

title: Almost perfect... Had to Return
text: First off let me tell you where I'm coming from. I started off with the LG Tones. Then upgraded to Jabra 65t Liberty Neo (after 65t's broke) Jabra Active 75t Life A2 NC (these) Life A1 (for now) The 65t's fit bad (couldn't use foam tip with them) and were pretty disappointing, but they have a great app and customization Liberty Neo's - Great fit and battery life but lacked control 75t Active - Almost perfect but had to use right bud and it finally died These - New app added sooo much usefulness, but with only 4 total controls they just fail. No single or triple button press. The second part is the fit - they simply don't fit well. So I ordered the A1's. Life A1 - Fit is amazing! Lack of app support is making me think about returning them as well. You can't change what button's do what and there's no previous. So these are good with the app, the ANC is only barely passable. The fit stinks. The button control is garbage. But you can make them work... They just didn't cut it for me... I'm still searching because the A1's don't have app support and blink continuously

title: PRETTY GOOD
text: These are not fantastic, as they are not completely sound proof. The fit is great, they don't slip out. Sound quality is pretty good. Battery life so far is fantastic.

title: It’s good but don’t get it wet not even a mist
text: Had them while working out worked fine for the day but the day later the left earbud had noticeably lost power in sound hopefully I can get a replacement

title: I may have gotten a dud but my people can't hear me and they don't work inside
text: I may have gotten a dud but my people can't hear me and they don't work inside . So I only tried them a few time gave up and ordered wired ones 🥺

title: The Controls are Awful!
text: The controls on these are terrible, and it's so hard to get from one song to another, or back. The noise cancellation was ok, and one weird thing was putting them back in the case almost seemed backwards. I am almost always please with Anker products, but returned these.

title: By far my favorite pair of ear buds
text: My job requires TONS of con calls and meetings and customer phone calls. I've been putting off buying a pair of Bose, Samsung, or Apple ear buds due to the insane price point. So I decided to purchase 4 or 5 of the cheaper sets and test them all out. These are by far the best. The battery life is awesome. USB-C charging. Sound quality. The big thing for me is the mic quality. Customers on the phone cannot tell i'm on a set of earbuds. The voice quality is the big winner for me. The noise cancelling i'm more interested in is that of the mic. There is limited background noise that comes across on the mic. It's not perfect, but it's way better than the others I tested. I tested taotronics, sound peats, hexdeer, phaiser, etc. I've recommended these to coworkers and friends. Do your self a favor. If you want good quality phone ear buds, get these. If there is a negative, it's that I haven't found a set of the rubber ear pieces that fit my ears like I want, but i'll sacrifice that for sound and voice quality.

title: Disappointing in a multiple ways
text: First, they don't connect as well as my other Bluetooth devices. I got them to use with online meetings, but often when the 'connect' with my PC, i.e. all indicators say they are connected, I still don't get sound. Once they do connect the sound is good. However, after wearing them for a while they become uncomfortable - I think it's because the battery charging connector space at the bottom - where they rest on your ear - has a little ridge, isn't completely smooth. That makes my ear sore after time. Then, my final point is that they aren't really secure in the ear. The little wing things they provide aren't large enough to really secure them in the ear, even after I put on the largest ones they provide; they have fallen out multiple times. I would certainly never exercise in these! All in all, I wouldn't buy these again; I'd look for others. I find it interesting that the features they ask for ratings on are sound quality and noise cancellation - if they don't connect and won't stay in my ear and I can't stand to wear them long, those are irrelevant!

title: Great Value
text: Sound audio quality was surprisingly good for a lower cost ear bud. While I have been a big fan of Ankers charging products for at least 5 years and expected a good value and quality built product , this is my first headphone product from them so I was happily surprised that their quality extends to other non charging accessories. ANC is a bit wanting compared to higher end over the headsets like the WMH-1000 3&4 and equivalent Bose headsets but at 15% of the price and close audio quality including good bass response, it's a fantastic deal.

title: Junk
text: These worked for about a month. Volume in left earbud just kept getting quieter and quieter till there was nothing. The right is doing the same thing. Phone volume is all the way up. There was zero noise cancellation I have only had these for a few months and they were not used excessively. Very disappointed.

title: I watch movies, noise cancellation is nonexistent
text: I mainly watch movies, not music and the noise cancellation function is nonexistent. WTF? What good is noise cancellation that only works with music, even this I cannot verify. sometimes you just want to use them without any media just to make noise go away. they are utterly useless in this mode of operation. there is no difference between settings for noise cancellation, transparent, and off. I’ll ambient noise is just as loud as if the earbuds we’re never there. Earbuds you can take the air pieces out of your ears and the ambient sound are the same as with the earpieces in. On top of that the controls that operate through the app are awkward to use. these are the worst earbuds I have ever tried; they are going back.

title: WOW. Superior product at an affordable price!
text: Far more impressive than I'd expected! Sound quality and noise cancelation is quite stellar. They are also comfortable and came with five different sizes of ear buds to ensure a proper fit. I would recommend giving these a try for their price.

title: Good fit in ear, and good sound quality for money
text: Like title says... typically just wear one, when I did wear both had good options for noise canceling settings. Good headphones for the money. Honestly just use these for work and use airpod pros the rest of the time. Got these so didn't risk losing/damaging my good ones but these fit the bill for their intended use perfect and really like them. They fit snug and have never came lose nor fall out.

title: The best!
text: Love these headphones! Work amazing and last forever. They do fall off my ear every now and then so just be aware of that

title: Not buys Apple again
text: Well, I bought these to substitute a pair of apple pros until next pay day. But after using these for two weeks, I’m no buying pros now. These earbuds sound fantastic and the battery life is amazing. The sound suppression is okay, not amazing but it does the job enough to satisfy my needs. For the cost vs pros this is a massive deal and I’m happy I came across these before spending more than 3 times as much for the pros.

title: True 5 Star Earbuds!!
text: At Home with Lucas YouTube Channel is where I did a review on these earbuds. I love the sound quality and bass! These are 5 stars in all aspects...but the case is very big.

title: Anker is one of the best
text: So I have a few sets of Anker earbuds because I listen to music and stories constantly because I'm easily preoccupied. Most of them have their highs with only a few lows like the one model requiring me to constantly disconnect and reconnect to get just the left ear to work. I was excited when I ordered the Anker Life. Remember though, more expensive doesn't always mean better. Is the sound quality good? It's phenomenal. Great bass and very clear. Noise cancellation is wonderful with several settings. Then why only 3 stars? Battery life on mine are abysmal. Not sure if it's a bad batch or all of the excellent additions but battery life on my nanos are insane, these dropped to 60% after a half hour. I thought it might be the noise cancellation but I kept it off and same issue. They are also a lot larger than I expected. To get the premium sound, you need bigger drivers but these things almost fall out of my ears. I have tried several way pieces by the way. They just don't seem as comfortable as I thought they would which is a shame because I fall asleep with earbuds in all the time. Definitely wouldn't with these. For any audiophiles, this one may be to your liking but I hope your battery life is much much better than mine. *update 01/20/2022* A customer service specialist reached out to me about the poor battery performance. I explained my concerns and they were able to address the issue and the replacement that was sent has been working perfectly. The charge holds for a considerably long time before needing to go back in the case. I am still getting used to the larger size but with the correct ear piece, they are absolutely comfortable. As listed above, the overall sound is incredible and noise cancellation offers so many options for different environments you may find yourself in. Absolutely the best take away from this review is that Anker honestly does have customers service representatives that care ad strive to make your experience five star.

title: Very comfortable
text: These are one of the most comfortable earbuds I have used. In addition the "wing" does a great job of holding the earbud in place. The sound quality is good for the price. There are better sounding earbuds at a higher price, but I doubt you will find more comfortable. Battery life is also good as well as the noise cancellation. The one thing I have not been able to figure out are the flashing LEDs on the charging case when plugged in. They flash many different patterns, not what you normally see with more lights lit the more charged it is ... but when it is fully charged all the LEDs are lit ... so I ignore the rest.

title: Great Sound_Bass
text: Just really like these for the quality audio they output.

title: Wonderful Sound Quality; Battery So-So
text: I asked for these around the holidays so that I didn't have to deal with wires while I work from home. Reading about the product, I was intrigued as to whether the microphone would hold up to its potential. According to people I've chatted with or have spoken to on the phone, it sounds great. Take that for what you will. In my opinion, the company has prioritized phone users over computer users. To my understanding, the active noise cancellation and EQ options are only available through the app. That said, the sound quality with these is excellent compared to my other earbuds and headphones. It was a shock to put these in, turn on some music and YouTube and hear things that I hadn't heard with my other devices. Unfortunately, unless I'm listening to people talking, I tend to only get about 4-5 hours out of these per charge. I was hoping they'd last me the majority of my typical shift, which I can achieve with other lesser earbuds. The reason I'm rating it 3.5 stars instead of higher is because I have no idea whether these things charge to their potential when they're in the case. The only battery indicator is triggered by pressing down on a button on the case, and that's a basic system of 1 to 3 dots showing you how much battery the case has. I know the earbuds have controls on each ear, but they haven't registered for me. I tend to use in-app shortcuts or my mouse to mute myself to cough, shift through songs, etc. Because I received these as a gift, I can't return them and honestly, this product is hit and miss. The sound quality is so much better than my other earbuds, and the microphone is certainly more than serviceable, but the fact that I can't rely on the battery of these in and out of the case over the course of the week really knocks them down a few points for me.

title: The best headset for the price!
text: Great headset and it fits great in the ear. ANC is still not where it needs to be at, but it is OK. Overall, I am happy with these and I strongly recommend them.

title: Preliminary and updated review, straight out of the box and 3 weeks later
text: I just received these today and I basically took them out of the box, paired them, and listened. I studied the manual prior to receiving so I knew basic function. Paired easy and fit was very good with wings and nipples that it came with. The sound is breathtaking. Going to fine tune and trick them out, but I just had to share first impressions. Impressive to the extreme, kinda scary. My whole being is full of outstanding sound. Together with Prime music HD these will rock your musical world. Update: In the second week I received a notification that a firmware update was available so I downloaded. The connection between buds and phone became disrupted so I contacted Soundcore. I did a reset as described in the directions and reinstalled the app prior to hearing back from Soundcore which came within the same day. They recommended the same action. I had asked if there was a way to delete the update as the problem came after the download but they suggested that the buds may be defective and replaced them for me. I received in 2 days and am back to enjoying superior sound and seamless operation. NC is great as is the transparency mode which I use while riding my bike. I can enjoy great sounding media and calls and still hear cars from behind, dogs barking, etc. You can be reassured of a high quality product and stellar customer service for a reasonable price.

title: Meh. Just ok.
text: Pros: Sound and ANC quality is decent. ANC is not nearly as good as the Bose quiet control 30's but probably not fair to compare to them. Cons: The tap and hold feature does not work. I have to keep constantly pulling my phone out of my pocket to adjust volume or fast forward. This is a deal breaker. The rubber parts are super thin and cheap. I do not see them lasting very long. I have tried various combinations of the different sized rubber parts but can't find a combination that keeps them tightly in my ear. If I am just sitting still they will usually stay in. As soon as I start walking I have to constantly push them in. Definitely can't run with them. Very disappointed.

title: Crackle loudly in left earbud
text: I really want to love these buds so bad. The battery life is excellent. The fit is perfect. I've honestly forgot they were in my ear. I love that I can program what the controls do. They have alot of good going on for them. The one very bad issue I have is that the left earbud has a very sharp crackling sound at all volumes. The right bud is great. I use it all the time. For music and it's also flawless for phone calls. But the left bud is completely unusable.

title: Excellent!!!
text: Finally found what I was looking for with good quality and it anounces my incoming calls.

title: Great!
text: I work in a clean room environment and I have purchased multiple earbuds and Bluetooth headphones and these are the only one that I have bought that not only can I hear everyone on the phone but they have no issue hearing me. I would highly recommend them to anyone who works in a noisy environment.

title: Serviceable but not perfect
text: The updated model from the A1 version features more and better microphones for calls and much-improved noise cancellation. Yet the battery life remains the same, something I would have hoped they'd improved, and this time around it features a quite overly large, awkwardly shaped case to hold the earbuds in. TBH, if you wanted to save $20, the A1 model is still more than serviceable. The A2 model doesn't feature enough bang for your buck to warrant paying the extra money.

title: Excellent budget true wireless earbuds.
text: These are an excellent bang for your buck. They sound quality is very good for this price point and the noise cancellation is exceptional. My only gripe is that the battery life in the earbuds themselves is a bit spotty and this results in some connectivity issues. But this only happens rarely (and they charge fast) so this is only a minor inconvenience. Also, as with most of these style earbuds these days, the microphones are pretty terrible -- often have to talk louder for the folks on the other end to hear me. But I didn't buy them for this, so, no stars lost.

title: My daughter lovees them.
text: After she was disappointed with her iPods dying after 6 months, I bought these for her and she said their much better. I strongly reccomend, especially for teens considering more expensive options.

title: Love the product but..
text: I love Soundcore products, I have a few of the can headsets and I bought the earbuds and was immediately in love. The only issue I have come across almost had me sending them back. I have a problem with one of my Life A2's that it continually disconnects once I connect any other soundcore product to my phone. The right earbud just stops transmitting and will not allow any new info to download to it to update buds, unsure if its the bud or the pod. But its too late to return the broken one and the new one doesn't have the same issue (I thought it did but a the update and a re-pairing to the phone fixed it fully for awhile now). Unfortunately I'm not stuck with the first set having busted after only a few weeks but its still a one earbud use. Only complaint/issue would be the first pair.

title: Really great
text: I bought this for my daughter. She’s a runner, and this headband works perfectly for her. It stays up, stays charged and is very easy to clean.

title: Good product
text: I like this Bluetooth headband a lot. I use it to sleep mostly, but I can also see using it other times. The sound quality is good.

title: Comfy Headband Headphones
text: This is a nice comfy headband headphone that has decent sound. This is my first headband headphone set so I don't have anything to compare it with, but I am very happy with this. I wanted this for sleeping and it seems like it will work great for that. The headband is comfortable and not too tight, which I like. The material is soft yet thin enough that it won't make your head hot. I was able to pair it easily and I'm not technically inclined. The sound seems fine. I like that you can remove the hardware to wash the headband. I'm going to get a lot of use out of this!

title: Very comfortable
text: Very comfortable to where I love it and would highly recommend it.

title: Can’t adjust volume.
text: First I want to say the fabric of this sleep headband is delightful! Unfortunately that is the only positive thing I can write. Don’t have this on and next to your ears when you power it up because a woman yells in your ear “Power On” and “Connected”. My ears are ringing and I’m awake now! But no worries, I’ll just put on some soothing sleep music and fall right asleep…. Nope. There is absolutely no way to turn the volume low. At higher volumes, there is fine control of how quickly you want your hearing damage to happen, but once you get to the halfway point heading downward it is just all the same volume. Also, the +/- buttons don’t control the volume, they advance the track or go back. Seemed an odd feature for sleep headphones.

title: I use these to sleep.
text: Can’t speak for the gym, but these allow me to listen to a book or white noise over my ear plugs and not wake my snoring husband! Still can hear the alarm, but not keeping him awake with my book either! More pleased than I expected.

title: Very comfortable, great sound, long battery life
text: It doesn't so much cancel out noise, but it is perfect for background noise while you sleep. The battery life is ridiculously long! Longer than 12 hours of continuous play. It is infinitely more comfortable than the headphones that fit in your ear. I'm seriously considering getting another one as backup.

title: Wonderful wireless headphones without buds
text: Remarkably comfortable to wear and even fall asleep, no pesky earbuds falling out, no wires hanging out for pets to grab, great sound quality, you can even answer phone calls. This will be your greatest buy to replace earbuds.

title: The inner wires move around
text: I’m not thrilled. The inside parts move around constantly. The wires/ear parts get tangled. I have to charge it daily. I don’t know how to wash it.

title: Hurts my ears!
text: Do not get the old ones, get the new padded ones for side sleepers!! These are so incredibly cheaply made! The flimsiest headband ever. Impossible to take out the electronics to wash it. There is no padding at all, so lying down with them on is super uncomfortable and hurts my ears. text: i bought these thinking they had a noise cancelling feature, but they don't. oops, that's my bad. they dampen but don't cancel. but for me, this actually worked out fine! i wanted them for a red-eye because i realized that the noise is what makes it so hard for me to sleep. these block out just enough sound to make the general sounds of a plan a low hum. they made me realize how loud planes really are, actually. i wasn't surprised that i couldn't sleep anyway, but these still made a huge difference. the comfort level of these headphones is very high. i really like the soft top and the soft cups--they fit well over my ears and they don't dig into my head. the sound quality on these is also really great! i've been using airpods for years now, which sound fine! but these are soooo much better. sound is clear and crisp and the bass is just right--not too heavy or light. compared to airpods, it's to be expected that the bluetooth connectivity isn't as stellar with an iPhone. if it has other past connections nearby, it'll try connecting to them. my girlfriend borrowed them once and then i couldn't get it to find my device without her removing them on her own device. a small hiccup, but it can be annoying. these are in the mid-price range and i think they're a good value for the quality. im happy that they come in a small case to protect them and come with a cord to connect to a device the old fashioned way. i use it rarely, but i do use it! overall, these were a good buy and a reasonable and stylish alternative to the popular sony headphones.

title: Comfortable headset with personalized sound
text: This is the best headset I’ve ever used hands down, and I’ve tried a lot of them over the years. They’re super comfortable, even for longer periods of time, and don’t make your ears feel hot. The sound quality is fantastic. The companion app allows you to customize the equalizer settings or choose different modes for podcasts, music or movies. One of my favorite things about this set is the Personal Sound technology. It’s completely personalized. It will play a bunch of different tones and ask you if you can hear it. Once you’ve gone through the process on both ears, which takes just a couple minutes total, it creates a sound profile for you. Everything sounds so nice through this headset. The noise cancellation is great. It’s nice to be able to focus on what I’m watching or listening to without any outside disruptions. I’m a huge fan of this headset and how much it has elevated my listening experience.

title: Outstanding
text: This is my second one, the first, I past on to my teenage son. We both agree that the sound is outstanding!

title: Super Bass
text: If you like deep throbbing bass that shakes your bones, these are the headphones for you. I bought them as a gift for my husband because he has hearing issues (from playing drums with no ear protection). I thought that the customized sound would be good but I’m not really sure if there is a difference. He is happy with them though. I took the hearing test and tried them with and without the customized sound and didn’t notice much of a difference. However, I do not have hearing issues and my left and right hearing was pretty even so I may not be the best judge for that. The sound is nice, clear and crisp top notes and the bass is easily adjustable from mellow to bone rattling. I still prefer my Bose quietcomfort but these are definitely just as good and maybe better if you enjoy super heavy bass. One complaint I have about them is you can only connect them to one device. To sync to another device you have to manually disconnect from the first device and then connect to the second device. I have Skullcandy earbuds and they do the same. My Bose and my Beats Flex do this automatically so I know it’s possible.

title: Sound great, not noise cancelling, prepare to replace
text: These sound great, bass is amazing. Unfortunately they are not noise canceling, they slightly muffle outside sounds the same as any over ear headphone but are by no means noise canceling. The most disappointing part is that the hinge for the headphones disintegrated after approximately 6 months and seems to be a common occurrence. These were my favorite phones in terms of sound but I unfortunately will not be purchasing this cheaply made product again. Spend the extra money and get a quality product.

title: Best of the Best!
text: This is hands-down the best set of Bluetooth headphones that I have ever used. The headphones provide a great balance of weight and comfort. I sometimes forget that I even have them on. The construction quality and materials are awesome and the product looks fantastic. Everyone that sees them wants a pair and everyone that hears them wants them even more. The bass reproduction is outstanding, especially for Bluetooth. You get as much bass as you can handle without distortion. The quality carries throughout the entire audio spectrum. I have owned Bluetooth headsets that costs 3x as much and did not match the quality of these. So glad that I got them.

title: Worst Headphones I've Ever Used
text: Returning these immediately. SHOCKED at all of these good reviews. I love bass. What I don't love is constantly being aware of my headphones, because they are literally vibrating off of my ears. The bass vibration on these is ridiculous. Sure, they've got the bass you want, but while using these with a TV to watch a movie, the treble (people speaking) is actually not very loud at all, even on the highest setting. I truly, truly can't believe how many people apparently like the feeling of their headphones jumping around on their ears. My ear canal hurts after ten minutes because of the air being forced into my inner ear. You ever hear those cars going down the road with the subwoofer in the trunk and the music blasting, the whole car vibrating so hard that you don't know how every screw on the car isn't unscrewing itself? Well, imagine placing your ear directly onto the hood of one of those cars, and you've got these headphones. I bought these to use with a TV, and the sound is awful. Voices are super tinny, sort of echo-ey. I am so disappointed. Both in the horrible quality of the headphones I just paid $150, and the fact that so many people like these crappy headphones.

title: Oh My...

Headphones look and feel superb and are not too tight. Sound quality is excellent and identical to my Audio Technica's (if you use no bass). Has an EQ mode via an app but I don't use EQ. Also has Tile for tracking where the headphone are. Kinda cool, it has GPS numbers on headband. Great buy for $150 and worth the regular price of $200. title: Wow
text: I bought couple of good ear pieces, and they served me well for what they're for. But I CRAVED Bass - started searching and ended up here. Pros: 1. I like the Matt finish with lack of logos - Also this surface is pretty good at keeping fingerprints off 2. Very comfortable - fits my big ass ear well 3. I like all the controls - especially the bass adjustment. It's good to have physical buttons for this sort of things 4. It's light - Light as it can get without using CF or Ti. 5. Bluetooth 5.0 is amazing! I can go downstairs with this thing running in my apartment 6. It's quick to charge 7. It's fast connect - no issues so far connecting to devices - laptops, tablets, and phone And finally 8. HOLY BASS! My skull reverberates after using this for a while. It was little weird at first, but man... I can't go back to anything I have. 9. You can barely hear anything, besides the reverberation of the bass, when you have this on - and it's not as distracting if you have it on not to distract others around you. 10. enough space on the headset for stickers. 11. The bass tested, for me, for 11 hz for bass - skipped the treble, because I thought my head was going to explode. 12. Holds on to your ear very well - Doesn't shake, slip, or anything. Good strength there. Cons: 1. It gets little hot after a while 2. The Skull Candy app is garbage - I did their patented "personalized setting" and it took away the bass and everything else, and it told me my hearing is for "podcast." I don't listen to podcast. 3. The design is remarkably plain. It's so plain, it's boring. But I honestly don't care. 4. Adjustment for the ear piece is infinite, which I like, but I wish the adjustment was little lower - I keep hitting the metal piece - this is very small gripe. 5. I guess if they can make this for $50, we'll be living in the future. EDIT: I just listened to the old music where I didn't understand the lyrics. Now I can hear it clearly. I'm not sure if it's just me, or the headphone but I can say I heard it clearly with this headphone.

title: Sound great wireless! But wired…
text: These headphones have really good wireless sound and especially bass quality. Microphone quality is also pretty good. Unfortunately, if you ever want to use these headphones with a wired connection while turned on (so you can enjoy the heavy bass), they fall pretty short. While plugged in and turned on, there is a constant, soft, high pitched noise going in the background. It doesn’t completely ruin the sound, but it’s present just enough to irritate your ears with prolonged use. The sound is especially apparent/irritating between songs, when no other sound is playing. It’s a bummer because part of the reason I wanted these was to use them with my Quest 2 for Beat Saber, which requires a wired connection. Alternatively, you can use the headphones wired while powered off to avoid this issue, but then you don’t get the heavy bass support, and they just sound like regular headphones. I tried returning my first unit, but the second unit also has the same issue. Both units were the black model, and I’ve read in other reviews that the grey model seems to not have this issue as often. Not sure if that’s true, but it might be worth a shot if you plan to use these wired with the bass support.

The Bose have a better sound but cost me 20 times as much. —Noise cancelling is only from the ear muffs. I see no evidence of active noise cancellation. —Comfortable fit for my large head. The only detractor I see is the tightness or the headset on my ears. After wearing these headsets for a couple hours your ear lobes hurt from the pressure of the headsets. The other thing that works but not as operationally sound is the location of the on/off switch on the left side of the headset. It is very small and almost in line with the frame so you have to focus on it to turn the headset off. I have also used this for phone calls and the sound from and too my caller is crystal clear. Furthermore, I have connected these to my computer for videos and music and the sound is just as good in my opinion. So if you're looking for a reasonably priced headset that works, this one's for you!

text: There isn't anything wrong with these headphones per se, but they were unable to serve my purposes and I had to return them. I wanted a pair of headphones with a mic as well as a removable AUX cord for gaming on the PS4. The bluetooth will not connect to the PS4, as I expected. However, what I did not expect was for the mic to lose functionality when the AUX cord was plugged into the headphones and controller. The sound would come through, but the mic would not work. title: Absolutely horrible for voice
text: I got these headphones to use for work meetings, now that COVID has forced me to work from home somewhat permanently. I didn't need anything fancy - like high fidelity or deep bass for music - just something to use for my zoom calls. So I figured, well, these seem good enough and people in the reviews like them. What could go wrong? Well. These headphones may be good for other things, but they are absolutely HORRIBLE for voice! My zoom calls sound like my coworkers are being suffocated with a pillow... underwater!!! I thought maybe it was the quality of the connection, but then I listened to a pre-recorded professional instructional video - so, higher quality - and the voice sounded muffled and garbled again. The headphones just suck. Switching back and forth between these and my old headphones (also cheap and off of Amazon), you can clearly hear the obvious difference. With my old ones, the voice sounds totally fine. The reason I'm replacing them is that they have a very short cord that gets tangled in the cat, kids and whatever else I have in my lap while trying to pull of this work from home thing. So I wanted something cordless. What a huge disappointment this set has been.

text: I use it for exercising, particularly running or high impact sports, calls, music whilst I am doing the housework, listening to audio books whilst heading out to do my essential shopping. These buds are snug [3 different ear sizes] and cuts out a lot of external noise, although there is a hear through to bring some of the outside awareness, but it sounds more like static. I leave it off. They are so tiny compared to my other ear buds, and I have no worries about them coming off when I am running at all. The app gives some manual adjustments , but not a lot. It stayed connected with my tablet and phone and will connect to the item nearest to me. It you take one bud out to talk to someone, the music stops, and starts again once you have the bud back into your ear. Instructions are on the website, and as there are no protruding buttons, you need to learn And practice how to take calls, adjust volumes, connect via Bluetooth. I love Them and a huge step up in technology, design, comfort at this price point.

title: Nice sound with classical music and audio books
text: As a rule, I prefer over the ear headphone style for comfort. But there are circumstances when ear buds are safer and more practical - like riding horses. These buds are better than expected and suit my needs pretty well. The case is the actual charger and you can charge the buds without the case being plugged in as long as it has residual power. You do need to put the buds into the case at the precise angle or they don't charge. These do come with small, medium and large ear pieces so you can get the correct fit for your ears. I do wish the right and left markers were more obvious and easier to see. I listen mostly to audio books and country, 80s or classical music. I don't use or care about heavy bass in earbuds at all, so I cannot speak to that performance quality. The do fine with the 80s pop and hard rock and behave nicely with classical music as well. There is an option for noise cancellation - called Through Sound. It actually works and there is a very noticeable difference when it's on. I'm pretty impressed by that. I do not like having to put yet another app on my phone to set these up and get full functionality out of the ear buds.

title: Mixed Bag
text: Pros-- -Very comfortable and secure fit even during high intensity exercise -Solid Bluetooth connection -Good noise canceling -Hear thru mode is useful -Sleek, low profile look -Decent battery life, charging case is nice -mic works well for calls or voice commands -LOTS of bass (I consider this a major negative, but some people will like the bass heavy sound) CONS- -Below average sound quality (WAY too much bass, even after using the EQ to turn down the bass its still more than I would prefer for most types of music, the default out of the box sound is the worst I have ever heard on a pair of headphones in this price range.. but that said you can make them sound pretty decent after a bit of tweaking with the EQ) -Not loud enough, the maximum volume is barely adequate for high external noise situations like airplane (even with the noise cancellation which works pretty well) -Sealed design is not good for 'active' pursuits because of microphonic effect amplifying internal sounds whenever you move around -software can be buggy, occasionally when I change settings and they appear to be changed in the software but do not apply to the buds I think there are certain people who will love these buds, especially if you listen to a lot of rap/hiphop or other bass heavy music as the default sound seems to be tuned for that kind of music. Personally I just can't really get into the sound of these, even after tweaking with the EQ there is too much bass and the soundstage is flat and lifeless. I do like a lot of things about them though, the fit is comfortable and very secure, much better than airpods or galaxy buds on that front.

title: Decent price and sound for this newcomer to the market

ANC works great on a plane or vacuum, ok for random noises though. Battery life isn't close to 8 hours advertised unless you listen really quietly- the closest I've got is 6.5 hours with ANC off. These are not $200 a pair, nor do they sound like it, however if you need something that won't blow your eardrums, last over 5 hours, sound decent enough, won't break the bank, work well on a plane, and fit into your pocket then these are a great choice. You can customize the sound experience to your preferences and I absolutely love that feature (especially dealing with multiple sound/music apps)

title: I didn't know an earbud could be so good.
text: UPDATED REVIEW: Had these for well over a year and they really are my favorite earbuds ever. They stay put and the music and sound quality is excellent. When I have them in I cannot hear anything around me, which makes them excellent living in a small house and trying not to hear important, private calls that my husband takes. When I have these in, I just tune the rest of the world out. Their charge time lasts seemingly forever. I have had no issues in the last year. ORIGINAL REVIEW: These are perfect for my lifestyle. The color I chose is perfect too ... I have medium cool skin tone and they just blend right in. This is the first wireless earbud headphone that has ever stayed in my ear. EVER. They never feel like they are going to fall out. They just stay in effortlessly. Setup took a little longer than expected. One must download the Jabra app first. It is not just a simple pair. But once they were paired, it was all easy. Take them out of the case and they are on and for me, paired to my phone. Aside from the fact that they stay in my ear during walking, running, and whatever, the sound quality is very good and music is so pleasurable and crisp. I also like that my husband can have private calls while on the couch (we are in the Covid year after all) and I can put these in and play music and not hear even a smidgen of his conversation. I can just immerse myself in my own little world and he can trust that he is having his space. I didn't know an earbud could be so good. No regrets here. Would very much recommend.

title: Great Sound. . . Great Experience
text: The Jabra Elite 75t has exceptional battery life of 7.5 hours of constant use, which also helps with wireless connectivity. I used these in the gym where I experienced almost no Bluetooth hiccups when I traveled several feet away from my connected phone, which is notoriously difficult on true wireless earbuds. Even though these earbuds do not have active noise cancellation, the sound quality is of high quality. The option of a button press on the left earbud allows you pause the sound to allow someone to talk to you. The Jabra Sound+ App allows you to customize the hearing experience, also has EQ settings that allow you to tweak the sound to your liking. The snug fit really helps buds stay in your ears securely and also promotes the best sound out of them with improved bass performance. And these do have very good sound quality for true wireless if you can get that tight seal. Having volume controls on the buds is a great option which you can press and hold the button on the left earbud to lower volume and press and hold the button on the right earbud to raise the volume. Overall, the Jabra 75t is a great earbud with quality sound for the much more reasonable price than the Apple Airpod Pro. I highly recommend these Jabra 75t earbuds.

title: Initially seemed very solid product, seemed good value for money, but...
text: Not quite perfect. Small gripes. I'm coming from airpod pros that sadly went through the wash. Overall the apples were great, although did have some auto-pairing issues. The Jabras pair well, set up is easy but does require a downloadable app (as does practically everything anymore). Sound quality is maybe even a little better than my airpods, in a quiet room at least. Good seal. Small airbuds are hard to hold on to, these are no different. Getting them into your ears can take a little patience. Fit isn't quite as good as the airpods pro, but that could easily be a personal experience just based on anatomy. They stay in well enough for most things, but do jiggle a bit when running and have to be adjusted. Also, with a tighter silicone seal, you also get the subtle "pressure" phenomena when running. Found that bothersome. The ANC on the airpods is better no question; here it's merely adequate. For $150 this is a good product and I will keep using them for now. Will I look closely at the next evolution of the airpods pro? Heck yes. Update: 2 stars I think now based on living with these for a little while. They do great, so long as you aren't very active or don't connect to anything other than a phone. Unfortunately, Jabra put "active" in the name of the product, so when measured against this--for me, at least, they are barely adequate. Lots of wind noise, when you resettle the buds in your ears when they jiggle out, it's very easy to push a button by accident. Biggest issue, are the random interference or rapid disconnects/reconnects from my watch, which are several orders of magnitude worse than my old APP's. Nearly unusable with running. Seems to do better when connected to a phone. Not buying this brand again.

title: Even more of a bargain in late 2021
text: Still high quality earbuds for 2021. I recommend them for their great sound quality, fit, and cost. I wrote everything below this before I realized I had forgotten a critical selling point of the Jabra earbuds -- The app which accompanies it. It includes an equalizer which provides presets, as well as the ability to customize and save your own personal sound settings. Granted, some media players have an equalizer included.¹ However, that doesn't help you much when you're streaming music or watching YouTube. What I found even more impressive is how they DESIGN THE SOUND QUALITY SPECIFICALLY FOR YOU. The app runs you through a simple hearing test for each ear, asking you to tap the icon when you hear a tone. Based on the frequencies and volumes you can recognize, the app creates a personalized sound profile!! And this is one reason so many find the sound quality to be exceptional. The physical buttons are big and soooo easy to use, for those having difficulties with the touch sensitive earbuds. You can't miss pressing them, they're the elegantly designed circle ◎ with "Jabra" writen in the middle.² I often go back and forth between these and other brands with the touch activation feature. And one thing I can tell you… thanks to the actual button, I have never had to press my Jabra earbuds more than once to activate a function. 👂👈😏 As with many earbuds which have ANC³ these days, I have found them to be quite good at passive noise cancellation. So much so that I rarely use active noise cancellation, thus increasing my battery life. But, when I do need it (e.g., when I'm 3ft from the air conditioner), it works very well. ··•✺•·· ¹ ─ There's also an EQ embedded in the settings of newer Samsung phones. Sadly, not at all easy to get at given how often one might need to when playing music.🤷🏼‍♂️ ² ─ Also extremely helpful if you wear gloves often. 🧤 ³ ─Active Noise Cancellation
