title: Not at all happy
text: I'm 6 weeks into this product and the sound quality is bad, volume reduces after a few minutes and I have to turn volume up to max and right earbud sounds lower than left.

title: Skip this brand, not reliable.
text: Second pair of high end Jabra earbuds w/ major issues less than a year after purchase. Skip this brand, not reliable.

title: Great earbuds with one major flaw
text: I really like these earbuds and use them for work......1/2 the time. Lets start from the beginning, I returned a set of Sony's and bought these due to all the great reviews, plus they're known for their strong bass, which I wanted. Initially, I thought these were the perfect earbuds, comfortable fitment, great sound quality, nice button controls (instead of touch, which I hate), good battery life. They were perfect for walking around outside because there was very minimal wind noise (the main reason I returned the Sony's). My main usage was for work. I work in a laboratory and need earbuds with enough juice to last ~6hrs and are comfy. I also spend a large amount of time at work working at a hood (for sterility). That's where the main flaw is. When I work at the hood, the left earbud crackles and then dies out. This happens every time and with every type of hood with negative air flow. Not sure why but none of my other earbuds do this. So now I use my Airpod Pros (which hurt after an hr) at the hood and only use the Jabras when working at a table. I've also read that some frequencies will cause these to crackle. So I'm still on the hunt for the perfect earbuds because these didn't cut it due to 1 issue.

title: Get the right fit
text: I just bought these somewhere else.At first I tried the tips that were installed at factory..the mediums.And then the small tips.I thought the sound was not close to my Bose wired buds.BUT then I tried the largest tips.Big Big difference!! The earpods must be tight to get the bass and mid range. If you can handle the largest tip, you'll be rewarded..

title: Best I've used. No good in small ears.
text: I'm generally more of a over-ear guy myself but you can't argue with the portability of buds. My wife primarily uses these though in the testing I've been doing for the review I've frankly been blown away at the performance you can get out of such a small package these days. I'll get straight to the point and let you know the sound is as good as I'd expect out of everything. Crisp and clear across the board and even the lows come through perfectly smooth. Comfort being the other import ant thing I'm happy to say I can wear them for quite a while without issue and they stay in. The one complaint we have about these is that my wife has a hard time keeping them in. While in my ears the entire body just nestles in the larger part of the ear and the tips aren't there to hold them in; they just provide a good seal. In her smaller ears however she can't get the body in to be able to seat the tips in the ear. She ends up having to tilt them at an odd angle and jam the tip in as the only way of holding them in. Don't get me wrong I understand it's impossible to get a design that would sit well in every ear on the planet. I just bring it up as something to consider as it's a drawback to us. One thing my wife did mention she liked was that she's able to adjust these without accidentally activating one of the controls; something that's been a problem on others for her. I did notice I really can't manage to turn the volume up. Supposedly the left side is a multi-position button but it only seems to work as one for me. Another thing that bears mentioning is the charging case. Being able to get multiple charges out of it and the pure ease-of-use in that after a month we can pull a bud out of it and it immediately pairs can't be beat. It just always works. So in the end we have had a few things wed improves but it sounds so good I wouldn't hesitate to bring it up as something for friends to consider.

title: Nice Buds
text: These Jaba EA 75t true wireless ear buds fit so well into my ears and the NC is awesome, all I hear is the music pumping into my skull clear & loud drowning out all the noises, like the power washer, lawn mower and the shrill of the voice coming from the other half

title: Perfect fit… for 46 mins. Battery Awful.
text: I Always wear headphones and have tried about every wireless pair I can find over the last decade or so. These are By Far The most comfortable pair, they have great sound quality and the Bluetooth connects to my phone a great distance. The only issue is they literally last 46 mins before the low battery warnings and about 56 mins before they die. I want to love them and i place on charger, allow to charge overnight and try again but each time it is the same- no more than one hour play time before dying :( the last three days i have gone straight from plugged in charger to my ears to see if any difference and one hour is Max time they operate. Super sad because i love them, aside from terrible battery life :(

title: Love em, but just didn't work!
text: I really wanted these to work for me. 1) I like the fit of the buds in the ear 2) I like the size - they didn't stick out to far from my ears 3) Overall they just seem extremely good quality. My biggest issue - sound. When having conversation with numerous people, they all complained that they could not hear me and I sounded like crap. They said I sounded like of "talking on speaker phone but way away from the phone", so both muffled and distant.

title: Stopped working in 90 days
text: OK, sometimes the products fail. My Jabra elite active 75t earbuds failed after 90 days. It took 4 weeks for them to authorize replacement. Now they say that there is no inventory and it could take weeks. Further, notwithstanding that they cannot provide working replacements, they will not refund my payment. Disappointing support (good luck getting a support person on the telephone) and failure to honor the warranty. Off to Bose

title: Charging case melt down
text: Six months after purchase and the Usb cable and charging case had a disagreement.

title: Pathetic product. Just buy the Airpods
text: These will NOT stay in and there are no ear hook products that fit these to help them be secure. Such a horrible concept to not even have an ear hook option. Customers have complained to the company about them not staying in but they still don't provide an option. Anther really stupid design is the button placement. I was constantly clicking it on accident. It's really touchy and since you are constantly having to secure these damn things in place you will constantly touch the button. I'm returning and spending a little extra due the Airpods which are so much better.

title: Great workout earbud
text: Love them, great for working out. I usually use just one when running outside. Noise cancellation is not great on a plane compared to an over the ear headphone. Comes with different ear bud inserts to fit your ear. Most importantly I have not had an issue of them falling out and I sweat a lot.

title: Love them
text: Works great with my phone. Great battery. Good at noise canceling. Good control of volume. Would recommend.

title: Not designed for small ears.
text: I love the quality of these ear pods. Great sound and phone app is awesome. But only short coming is not meant for small ear canals. Only way they would stay in my ears was no foam on ear tip.

title: Pretty decent headphones, not the best for calls, not very loud
text: I love how easy these are to connect and the fit is great. they are great for jogs, never come out of my ears. my main complaint is that the overall max volume is never really loud enough. I dont have damaged ears and I dont listen to music terribly loud, they sound great but never really get loud enough. Also, calls can sound distant sometime and the mic does a great job of amplifying every little noise around you too.... still decent reliable bluetooth headphones for the price i guess

title: Light weight durable with big sound Biiiigggggggg
text: Very small in comparison = very little ear fatigue (they’re comfortable). Great in app custom equalizer among other features. And what I believe to be the most important, the sound. I’ve tested a a few besides these(power beats HP, Sony wf-xb700,mpow x3, soundcore liberty air 2). Imo . they’re the best of these. I know my ears don’t need it but I would have liked to see a hair more volume from them. But they really are an awesome set. Update 12/14/20 : really so effing good. Get the app for them . I’ll continue testing but these are the best I’ve listened to by a fairly large margin, all features accounted. Awesome awesome awesome.

title: They do not care about selling broken products
text: The left earbud stopped working, there are no official troubleshooting methods just an extremely long reddit thread with people having the same issue, if not other issues. Light shows green but app says it is disconnected and it wont connect.

title: The good, the bad and the ugly
text: The sound is excellent! The fit is ok, I have to constantly tighten them up and when not seated well in the ear the sound is only fair. Tried all 3 sizes of ear pieces, the medium fits best but they still constantly work their way out of my ear. Noise cancellation is wonderful even when using while on a huge zero turn mower. Batteries last for a 10 hour work shift if put back in the case during my two 15 minute breaks. Really like the small case size, easily fits in a pocket and I forget it's even there.

title: These are so great - why didn't I buy sooner?!
text: Most earbuds to not fit me well-enough for physical activity. These are amazing, not only in fit but sound quality!

title: Terrific ear buds.
text: A bit pricey but worth it. Be sure to try out the different ear adapters - I found one that fits nicely. Good bass for music.

title: Customer service is nonexistent
text: Quality isn’t the best. I had a pair for less than a year and the left ear stopped working completely. Tried all the troubleshooting step on the site, nothing worked. Tried calling and just sat on hold, decided emailing would be easier. I got a response and was told they’d send me shipping label via email. They never emailed me. I call back a week later and they had nothing saying I contacted them. After almost 2 months I decided they didn’t care and tossed them. I absolutely will never buy another Jabra product, they do not care about their customers and trying to actually talk to a human is impossible. When the headphones were working, they were great. The only issue I had was if I had to bend over for anything like picking something up they would cut out. It have a pair of the I think 65 and it’s the same, which really isn’t horrible. Product (when working): 8, longevity: 1 (especially for the price), customer service: absolute 0

title: Great for sound, not for calls
text: Good sound quality for music or video. I was hoping they would work well for calls. Sadly no, volume at max on a call is to low for me to hear even when I am in a room by myself.

title: Do not use the S-hook to hold the charging case outside of a bag.
text: I love them. They have all the features I wanted. The size, the fit, the ANR. The battery life was fine for my runs. The bypass mode was awesome. I miss them. Why? Darn recharging case magnet. It gets weak over time and it popped open while I was dealing with the dog at the Farmer's Market. Lost the left unit. Well, that's it! Need to spend $100 or so for a refurb set or $180 for a new set. You can't buy "just one". My credit card protection policy was only good for 120 days, not 390 :( So, I love them so much that I'm going to buy another set, and add a rubber band like you get with celery to the mix to keep it closed. Jabbra - GIVE US A LATCH OPTION ON THE CASE!!!!

title: Love them
text: These are awesome. They connect to 3 devices all at the same time. They were great and the sound is really good. Can not wait to run with them.

title: Unreliable - do not recommend!
text: Left earbud stopped playing after several months despite no trauma to device. Support from Jabra nonexistent. I have seen from various chat groups that this is a common problem. Don’t waste your money on this company’s products.

title: Great sound quality when listening but the mic quality is awful for calls
text: I bought these to use to listen to music while hiking, driving in my older truck with no radio, and for casual calls while on the go. I have no issues with the quality of the sound they produce for the wearer but am seriously disappointed with the call quality. Any minor wind and background noise is amplified to the person on the other end of the call. When its moderate to windy out, forget about trying to have a call with these. It's terrible. Another issue I do not like is sometimes when connecting to a device that is already playing music, the first second during connection can hurt your ears with strange pitched, distorted sound, before it stabilizes. Not worth the super high price tag in my opinion, and I regret not returning for a cheaper option within the return window.

title: Strangers Ear Wax Included!
text: Shipt and sold my Amazon and arrived used (with ear wax) TWICE. Ordering direct through Jabra. Amazon needs to pull this product and inspect it. I've seen 8 other reviews in the last two months (May/June) with the same problem

title: Work better than u would expect
text: Are water resistant get them wet on daily basis and have flammable bass

title: Took me a few days to get it right
text: When I first got these, they didn't feel secure in my ears so I switched to the smallest earpieces. I couldn't figure out why the ANC didn't seem to do much. Last night I put on the large earpieces and that made all the difference! I could watch TV on my phone in the same room with the NBA playoffs at maximum volume and barely hear my husband yelling ;->. The battery lasts for many hours, and they recharge fast. The fit is better now too, much more secure. A huge improvement over my last pair.

title: Good but not great
text: So I have a pair or two of knock-off Bluetooth earbuds. The hardly stay connected when the phone is in my pocket. The Jabra Elite Active 75t have very good connection, even when two floors away on an old house. Sound quality... well they are not great. They don't sound that much better then the knock-offs at 1/8th the price. The base and deepness of the sound is lacking. Lots of high notes but not much more. Now grain of salt... I'm in my mid-50's with plenty of time around very load music (worked in a concert hall when Heavy Metal and Punch was cutting edge). I got these to use with Zoom meetings and I cannot find a way to mute and unmute the mic on the zoom meeting. So, might as well be at my computer on a cord.

title: The earbuds hardly work after 2 months of ownership
text: I was very excited about getting these and after much comparison, I narrowed the list to the Jabra 75t and the Airpods 5.0. Now I wish I had purchased the Airpods. Initially, the Jabra earbuds worked very well. The buds were very comfortable and I enjoyed using the hearthrough option for surrounding awareness. The Jabra app also allowed me to customize the sound quality and depth to my own hearing. From the start, the buds battery power only lasted, at most, 5 hours. I used them daily for my office phone and Zoom calls. Battery power time decreased to only staying charged at most for 3 hours after using them for 6 weeks. Now, they may stay charged for an hour, the sound starts breaking up after that. I can't return them now because it has been too long. I was hoping that after the positive reviews and how expensive these were, that I would use them for quite a while, but no, that was not my experience. I currently work from home and I need a reliable headset or earbuds that can provide great sound quality, have at least 5 hours of use time, and last. Too bad my experience was not great with this product.

title: Great quality
text: Awesome sound quality and phone calls Have been using them for over 1 year and have nothing to complain about Love them

title: dont work independently
text: You can't listen to just the left earbud. Either the right or both. INCREDIBLY disappointing that it doesn't have this feature nearly all 20$ cheapo-s have. Otherwise a nice headset. I'll probably be returning. If you're going to spend that kind of money get a pair that will work independently.

title: **BUYER BEWARE!!!**
text: I bought these Aug 2020. Started with great sound as others have noted. Within a few months the right bud went suddenly mute with no way to adjust the volume. Left bud worked fine. That began my ordeal with product support. After multiple rounds of trying everything they could think of to "reset" the buds, they finally had me ship the set back to them. They included the shipping info to print and include in the return. I do not have a printer, so I hand wrote all the pertinent information and included it in the return box shipped USPS. THIS WAS THE WIN for them, claiming they can't find the buds and there's no record. That's when the communication ended. In summary, I spent over $200 for about 3 months of decent earbud usage. I now have NOTHING!!!

title: WOW BASS NECTAR!!
text: I tried Beats, Airpods, and Google Buds+, and these are by far the best! Great for sweating at the gym/sauna, and outstanding equilizer balancing app included. And bc it's Jabra, you get EXCELLENT customer service....you get crappy customer service with the Beats.....which is not surprising.

title: Almost perfect
text: Sound quality is good. Noise cancelation is fair. Nice option for a hear through option if in an office. Color is great! The recharging battery cae is great too. Cons If I get sweaty at the gym and start running I've got to occasionally push them back into my ear. If you don't use the right ear piece then you can't use ONLY the left. The right earbud is what connects to the phone and that's a bummer because it would be great to use both independent of the other. If I could use only the left then it'd get 5 stars

title: Not Made for Athletes
text: These earbuds are not designed for runners. If I move my head slightly the music cuts out. The connectivity with my phone is spotty. And this is the biggie, you will hear every step very loudly on your run as your foot hits the road or ground and it drowns out the music. I would not buy these again. The Elite 65+ unit was way better and did not act like this. But, the battery lost its ability to take a charge and I had to discard them. Please don't waste your money on these. I know what I'm saying. I am a seasoned triathlete and these earbuds are pitiful and way over priced. These are my personal opinions and not conjured up for affect. I wish they had been tested by athletes so the engineers could make a better unit.

title: Amazing Battery Life and Top Notch Sound Quality With Latest Firmware
text: I have a pair of the Jabra Elite Active 65t earbuds so was very excited to get my hands and ears on the new 75t. There are some considerable differences between the two. For smaller ears like mine the 75t fits much better. However, I will say that the ONE thing the 65t did better was provide less ear fatigue after 2-3 hours of use. That said, it was hard to wear the 65t for much longer than that because of the battery life. That has changed with the 75t where I am able to stream music at a decent volume for well over five hours. I could probably get seven without an issue, but I haven't gotten quite that far without popping them back into the case. Other benefits: * They are magnetized so you can connect them when you lay them on your desk, table etc. This makes them much more difficult to lose. * The small size looks much better and fits much better in many more ears. * The sound quality was really good, but got a LOT better with the 3/31 firmware update. There are also some enhancements with the case charging, but I am not aware of what those are. I also own over the ear Bose headphones. I would say that the sound quality and music coming through the 75t is as good if not better. The noise cancellation is not even close (Bose is amazing) but it works well. The hear-through technology on the 75t works really well, so if you're on a run in the neighborhood you will easily know if there is something coming up behind you or around you. Again, great earbuds. So glad to see the wire free technology continue to evolve with this great set of buds!

title: Excellent product!
text: These are the business, just returned Apple AirPod pro since they lost on the shootout. Better than the 65t. Fit is perfect (no losing your earbuds here) and water resistance is perfect for exercise etc. The bass response is phenomenal and I love the app, lots of ways to configure your sound and controls. Jabra is doing things right, only request would be for wireless case charging but the usb c charging is super fast so no biggie!

title: Still pretty good in 2021
text: Bought these originally for work on MS Teams calls and ended up liking them a bit more than my Power Bears Pros that I used for personal stuff. The added ANC through an update is pretty sweet. Loving the thump in bass even before messing with the EQ. I can FEEL the music way better than the Power Beats Pro. Call quality is good. These are really good in terms of call quality, sound quality and comfort. Recently purchased the 85t earbuds also and ended up returning them as I can’t find any reason to prefer them over the 75t.

title: The sound quality is great, but not while walking or running
text: So I like the app. The sound quality is rich on the earbuds. The feature that customizes the sound in each ear is nice. What I absolutely hate is the thudding noise that occurs while walking and running. Thud, thud, thud… with everything foot step. I really wanted these for running, and this problem makes this a terrible buy for active runners or walkers. I wish I had spent more for a better brand.

title: Almost there
text: I like these earbuds. They sound good and you can customize through the app. The sound cancellation is not as good as my AirPods and I wish I could use either earbud individually. You can only use the right earbud by itself.

title: Great buds plagued with a design flaw, just get something else
text: These suffer from the exact same problem the 65t's had. Over time the air channel will get clogged and the affected bud's volume will drop to almost nothing. I had to return my 65t's 3 times over this matter (they lasted ~6 months and after 17 months with my 75t's, while I haven't had to return them I've had to clean these area's multiple times (and likely damaged them in the process, but I'm doing whatever I can to avoid dealing with their support.) It seems not every suffers from this, maybe it's due to use case (exercise vs just listening around the house) or some earwax thing. Either way just go with a different brand. Jabra's support works but it's a nightmare dealing with them and the return process can take over a month, since they don't cross ship that mean's you're without your earbuds. TLDR: Great earbuds, design problem likely to eventually cause them to fail, support is helpful but nightmarish to deal with.

title: Overall great with some room for improvement
text: The sound quality for listening to music or podcasts as well as call quality are great. The battery life is fantastic and the app is easy to setup and use. The only complaints that I have are that after about a half hour of use, they start to slip out of my ears no matter I do. The other problem I have is that I like to wear just one earbud while working so that I can have one ear free. You can use just the right earbud on its own, but you cannot use the left one on its own. The left bud can only be used if you are using both of them.

title: Defective product.
text: The connection is spotty most of the time. The longer they're in the worse the connection gets. Randomly drops the connection. Microphone quality is inconsistent, with excellent quality at the start of a power-on session to horrible quality randomly through use. I Will update this if it turns out to be defective, but if this does not change, then assume I returned/trashed these and got something better. Edit: After much time I've decided to just throw this in the garbage. No amount of repair or replacement has helped. No tech support from Jabra helped. This device is garbage.

title: Jabra when only the BEST will do!
text: Jabra is definitely the way to go! I had another brand earbuds and they can't touch the quality I get with jabra.

title: Love these
text: Very nice sound quality. Stays in the ear without falling out. Easy to connect to blue tooth products.

title: WOW I am really impressed with these!
text: I love the app, the equalizer allows you to customize your profile perfectly. I just got these so I am not completely familiar but there are 3 customizable profiles. The hear through feature works so well for me! I haven't used all of the features yet, but thus far these are the best headphones, earphones, earbuds I have ever owned. I have an old pair of BOSE noise cancelling earphones that are great, but pale compared to these.

title: Morning PT
text: What can I say but perfect. I have to be at morning PT ever morning and no matter what workout I do I've never had one slip or fail on me somehow. The quality is amazing. The only downside is you can either wear both or only the right side. You can't wear the left by itself.

title: An excellent less expensive alternative to Apple AirPods
text: These are an excellent alternative to Apple AirPods, and much less expensive. They have a lot of features, and they work great with my Iphone 12 pro. I have had no issues with these earbuds. The only disadvantage of these ear buds, are when I sweat a lot they tend to fall out of my ears. One of the earbuds fell out of my ear on hard concrete, and it broke. I was bummed about this, but I still bought a new pair to replace.

title: Losing the left ear was a deal breaker
text: So many issues with these earbuds. What broke the camel's back is I kept losing the left ear. I continually had to place then back in the case to get the left ear back. Bass wasn't there either. It was acceptable but it didn't stand out as expected. Maybe I got a bad set but I could not keep them especially with the constant drop outs.

title: Good for the average user
text: I got this product on Prime Day for $119 with the wireless charging case, which made it a great deal. I wish the noise cancelling (via software update) worked better, but the sound is pretty good. The build quality is really good.

title: Great sound and fit but lots of connection problems - returned them
text: Sound was quite good but lots of disconnects in use with iPhone 12 Pro Max and iPad Pro. Disappointed as I have had other Jabra wireless earbuds that worked well. So I ended up returning these and bought another pair of Sony WF-1000XM3 earbuds - they work extremely well but I was looking to save a few dollars on a second set of earbuds so I went with the Jabra's.

title: Good luck excercising
text: All the reviews say they have a nice secure fit. Im sure if youre like a painfully average sized person. They wont stay in my ears. They wont even go in my wifes ears theyll immediately fall out. Jabra customer service says “nope they arent any alternate tips or wings. You dont need them.” Love the confidence… but you absolutely do. Otherwise…. The sound is incredible i really want to love these. But i really cant if i cant wear them at the gym

title: I wouldn’t hesitate to buy again.
text: I use these while exercising or working in the yard. Great sound and a case charge lasts for several weeks.

title: AWESOME! Flawless...EASY 5 star rating
text: Flawless! I read about the Jabra Elite Active 75t's before I shelled out $150. The arived on time & well packaged. I followed the directions upon start-up. While the earbuds were updating, I watched a few Youtube videos about them. They paired flawlessly. Actually, I went out into my garage & paired them with my 2020 Polaris RZR Turbo S. The earbuds paired perfectly. I took these earbuds on the ultimate test in the RZR...a 6 hour ride in the Arizona desert. Not once did the earbuds come loose. I put on the Active Noice Control & I couldn't hear wind or the RZR's motor. Everything was totally cancelled out. Music sounds better with these babies out on the trail! I had my wife call me while riding. The call went great! My wife heard me crystal clear...no wind, no engine background noise. These earbuds lasted the entire 6 hour ride. I'm now a big fan! I'm super impressed with the sound they put out, their functionality, range, battery life, & ease of pairing and operation. They performed better than I expected. The Jabra Elite Active 75t earbuds are an EASY 5 star rating. I've already reccomended them to 2 of my friends.

title: DON'T FIT
text: I have had these Ear Buds for 1 Month now and tried everything !! They fall out cutting the Grass , Biking, and Running a constant Pain in the A$$ >>> I HATE THEM I'm in the process of STARTING A RETURN -- 30 days was June 19--- TODAY is the 24th OH BOY

title: Falls out too easily
text: I liked everything about them except they fall out to easily which shouldnt happen on sport earbuds.

title: Died on me 3 days after year warranty!
text: have never been really happy with these, overpriced, sound ok, overly complicated, don't stay in your ears while working out, really false adverstising to call them "active" as even when walking these fall out. Then they died on me recently, won't take a charge for more than a few minutes of listening and then they crap out, contacting jabra to see if they will warranty, probably won't ever buy a jabra product again!

title: Comfortable
text: Easy to set up and comfortable in your ears. Sound quality is lacking, but overall for earbuds it's probably pretty good.

title: One of the best sound for working out
text: Love the sound of the earbuds. Good bass and detail in the songs shine. The only problem I have is it disconnects frequently from my Apple Watch whenever I wear it on my left hand since the power earbud is the right one.

title: Don't Buy Left Earbud is defective, sound goes out
text: There is something wrong with the design of the left earbud. Sometimes the volume coming from the left earbud is much lower than the right. Then eventually there will be no sound coming from the left earbud, even though the left buttons work fine. If you google this problem, you'll find it that it is very common. Jabra troubleshooting will tell you to clean the buds, disconnect and reconnect to your phone, and update the firmware. Some customers have had success digging some glue out of a tiny hole in the left earbud. None of those options worked for me.

title: great product
text: I love these earbuds. Have had for a while now and they don't disappoint. Plenty of features.

title: Great Quality Earbuds!
text: I bought these because they were number one rated online and I am happy to say I am very happy with them! The sound quality is excellent, the bass is above what you would expect, and the noise canceling works pretty well too. I used them for both a Samsung phone and my iPhone. The Jabra “Sound+” app lets you customize a bunch of features for the earbuds too. All and all I recommend these. I could like to see some more color options however because the ones available are very few.

title: Jabra Elite
text: definitely works as defined. great product at a great price.

title: color me not impressed
text: i read the reviews and stuff and just am not impressed with these. they are water and sweat proof as advertised (because they would have failed by now otherwise). the high-end sound is pretty good and there is a decent natural pitch to the sound but the bass distorts to crazy levels. it makes listening to any music with any bass just not possible...which is of course all music. i have not tried to adjust them with the app yet though to be fair. the fit is just okay as well. the left one really doesnt stay perfectly in place while the right one does. the battery life is solid. i can do almost a two hour work out and not lose life most times so that is good. i dunno, solid but i am not sure they are worth the money given the sound quality. i can get the same thing with, say aukey, and those are a lot less.

title: Enjoy if they fit your ears!
text: I have no prior experience with ear buds, but these were easy to set up and use and to my inexpert hearing, they seemed great at first. The problem I have cannot be fixed--These buds just don't fit my ear "concha" (space where buds are meant to sit). None of the bud covers helped and the buds keep falling out. Try as I might, the pushing, twisting, and re-seating them only served to further hurt my ears. That's a non-starter from which I cannot give them a good testing and review. title: Jack's of All Trades..Master of None. Solid Product.
text: I will begin with sound quality and connectivity. I am very pleased with both. In terms of ergonomics, I'm a 6ft, 230 lb male athlete and I work in an industrial/ warehouse environment, so I have these in my ears for roughly 8-9 hours per day, 5 days a week. Though they are bulkier, and heavier than my Samsung Buds+, they are also vastly easier to put in and remove without dropping them. I have quickly gotten used to the additional weight. Only once have I had an issue with one coming out of my ear, but it may not have been in properly. As for battery life, meh. The case is rock solid and has literally never been at less that 50% charge. It is also stout and sturdy. I find that it charges up quickly. It also charges the buds quickly. However, the buds themselves are a bit too power hungry. I generally put them in to use as ear/sound protection at my desk, whether playing music or not. When at my desk, I will put the case on the charger. If I go into the office, I generally take the buds out and put them in the case. In that use case, I don't have any issues keeping them sufficiently charged to function properly all day for an entire work week. However, I am diligent about keeping them charged. If not, OR, if I used them on the ANC mode, or Hear Thru Mode, they would lose charge much more quickly. My use case is likely much more demanding than average, therefore I would not attempt to dissuade anyone else from buying these. I have no issues with phone calls or the mic. I have had no negative feedback from callers. The app provides a very easy to use and very useful suite of EQ and phone settings. I find the on bud buttons easy to use, though the latency could be better between touch time and function. I would trust these for sports, hard work, general everyday use. On a long flight, perhaps not. ANC is going to eat power, though I think it works very well. The hear through works extremely well for joggers or situations where you need high levels of awareness. I will often use that mode when running the forklift. I actually hear better. Overall a very solid product.

Sound is as clear as the wired headset I was previously using, and my colleagues tell me that they can't hear a difference with me switching to this headset (ie, that I remain clear to hear). I charge it daily (which may be unnecessary), and have had no issues with battery life. The controls that I use work fine (the MFB for on and off, and the volume controls). Of note, the mute button is effectively nonfunctional when used with windows, but for me and my purposes, this is not a deal breaker. It is no more or less comfortable than my old headset, and is slightly heavier than the wired headset that I was using, but it was easy to get used to. It is wearable on right or left ear, which is a nice option (and quite easy to switch mid-day if you choose, as there's no cord!). title: Great Headphones
text: My wife got me the silver and brown pair of these headphones for Father's Day. I used to have a couple of Turtle Beach headphones for gaming but the ear cups began to disintegrate so I had to get rid of them. I had purchased a wired pair for my son and thought they sounded really good so asked for the A71. The ear cups are extremely comfortable for me and my ears fit very well inside the cups. The sound quality is pretty good for the price point. The overall build quality is pretty nice but it is plastic. I have worn these for at least an hour and not been uncomfortable in the least. Included are two cables. One is a typical 3.5mm audio cable. The other cable has a 3.5mm head on one end and a 6.35mm head on the other. You can use either one, a 6.35mm port on the left side or the 3.5mm port on the right. The 6.35mm can be plugged into a soundboard, amp, etc. For fun, I have used both cables and plugged into 2 devices to get audio from both. I also managed to have bluetooth audio going from my phone and then used the 6.35mm cable and plugged into another device and got sound from both. However, it split the audio, bluetooth in the right ear and cable audio in the left ear. The capabilities of these headphones are pretty cool and , overall, the audio and build is great for the price point. If you are looking for some new headphones, give OneOdio a shot!

Similar with these headphones. The battery may last as long as stated on one charge. But these headphones shut down before the battery technically reaches zero. So the listening time is less.

title: Great ear buds
text: I purchased these a couple weeks ago. I wanted to write an honest review after using them for a while. I'm very happy with them. I tried a different brand but returned them after a couple days. These are heads and shoulder above those. I was concerned that they would fall out, but they fit snuggly, and they stay put without being uncomfortable. I use them when I workout, lifting, riding the bike or running, they have never fallen out. When I remove them, I have to gently tug on them for them to come out. Just make sure you are using the right size rubber attachments. I'm impressed with the sound quality. The app works well and you can actually hear the changes when you change modes. As far as noise cancellation--its more of the rubber inserts than the electronics IMHO. If I'm not listening to music or on a call they act like ear plugs. If you've ever talked wearing ear plugs, you know what I mean. However, when I'm walking the dogs or out in the wind, I can still hear the music with very little wind noise. It's almost as if I have over the ear headphones on. I'm still trying to determine the battery life. I wear them for a couple hours while exercising and a few hours after--I can wear them about 2 days like this until I need to recharge. I don't like to recharge until they are below 20%. The charging case will charge them up to about 75% in about an hour or less. I gave them a 4 because they are small and will sometimes slip out of my fingers when I remove them from my ears. I have the Bose noise cancelling over ear headphones and these are (almost) comparable to those for sound.

text: I like these headphones. 1. What's in the box?: You receive the headphones, plus the carrying case, a USB cable (USB-C) and the usual instructions and what not. 2. From the was of set-up and connection, these are very good to excellent. The connection is excellent without any problems whatsoever. Sony recommends using an app. The app is pretty good, but a bit clunky. You can turn the headphones on and turn the connection off. You do NOT have to use the app to use the headphones however. Sound? Pretty good. I am comparing these to my Apple AirPods Pros. I would say that these are a little less full and have a little less sound stage presence. Again, this is without the app, so with the app, this can be improved. The bass is not overbearing at all. However without the app and an adjustment, the sound can be improved. Compared to the AirPods though it is a little less stage wise. Comfort?: There are really comfortable to wear. There are some earbuds that can be used to adjust the fit, but once I changed these, they are very easy to secure. Overall?: I like Sony products, and this is no exception. The sound is certainly pretty darn good, though not great. On the other hand for the price point, these are excellent. The charge held lasts a while, a good connection. title: Great all around wireless earbud for a great price
text: I purchased these on daily deal from Amazon for $59 or so, and for the money I've been extremely pleased so far. Comfort: they fit well and are snug, they come with three sizes of tips so getting a good fit shouldn't be hard. They stay in place very well during intensive workouts Sound quality: For the money, I've pretty impressed with the sound quality. I own an amp and DAC, planar magnetic headphones, and a pair of wired balanced armature earbuds. So I love good headphones. These give my balanced armature earbuds a good run for their money. These don't have huge bass, but the bass is punchy and well controlled. Highs and mids are good, and there's decent separation and a nice airiness about these. Overall, these have a very well controlled sound profile and work well with most any music genre. These also isolate pretty well, so good that I see no need for wireless buds with noise cancellation, which I personally think is a gimmick that only causes increased drain on the batteries. Battery life: pretty decent, these don't have noise cancelling tech, so battery life is much better than buds that have that tech. One important note, I've found the right earbud will drain faster than the left if I use it frequently to advance or replay tracks. Sony headphone app: I'd recommend downloading the Sony headphone app as this allows you some equalizer features and let's you turn off the buds using the app. Also, the app has some other bells and whistles like an ear analyzer that takes a picture of your ear and optimizes sound to fit your ears. However, you'll need to download one of several 3rd party apps to take advantage of this feature. Overall, these are a fantastic deal for the money, with typical Sony quality and functionality. They work great with my Iphone and integrate with Siri, so you'll have that functionality as well.

Buds stay put. There's a myriad array of budget, mid-price and high end offerings on the market now. Reading reviews of the cheapo brands there's a lot of complaints regarding connectivity and durability. Sometimes when they are paused, I still communicate with others and when I'm listening to talking through them and there's someone talking in the room, I end up pressing them tighter to my ears as not to miss what I'm listening to. Also when you hook them up, you'll notice your device seeing D2 on the list. That's them, just pick it and pair and your all set. I put a fancy D2 on the case as to remember that. As Battery life, That was awesome from the start but now they die about twice a day if I'm constantly listening to them. As far as comfort, I forget there there and even slept with them in and found them where I left them the next day. I want to rate 5 stars but you did ask about battery. I think that after any ear buds, your going to have this issue. These affordable ear buds are worth your money and time enjoying them. I'd buy them again. Love them.

title: Updated. A decent headset for the price but...
text: I like these and they fit great, sound great, and do all you'd expect. My biggest issue is that I've yet to be able to get them to last longer than a year with little use of them (a few times a week while walking outside). I just ordered them again and it will be my third headset. I mean, at least they're inexpensive so there's that!

title: Good product for intended purchase
text: I like these a lot, but I can't use them for every activity. The rechargeable battery port/dock is the best feature. I can drop the ear buds repeatedly into the dock, to recharge them, all wk long. I have the flexibility I need, to skip songs or to turn each ear bud on/off, pause, repeat songs if I want, at the touch of a button. The only problem is wind. When I'm sitting at my desk at work, I can have conversations while the ear buds are installed in my ears. The real issue comes when I want to ride my bicycle, while listening to music. Too much air flow makes it hard to hear clearly, and the set dídn't come with different size options, to decrease air flow. Other than that, they're GREAT.

title: Great value and good quality

title: So far so good
text: I'm going to update this review with the battery life and whatnot. Out of the box: The instructions were easy to understand. I paired these up wrong with my phone and had to reset them because the left side crashed (hold left side button 12 seconds) and that worked quickly. Set them up properly. The warnings and troubleshooting are pretty thorough. The sound quality is pretty great. I've got them paired with my samsung s9. I'll have to report on calls later but I had a quick call with my mom and she didn't mention any issues hearing me. I like the options for different size buds. I have tiny ear holes I guess and the standard/medium size is super uncomfortable for me. I put these in and swung my head around pretty hard and they haven't slipped so it passed the head banging test. Noise cancellation isn't perfect but that's good. I don't want to be completely deaf outside what I'm hearing. I'm testing how they auto pair after the first time when I return them to the case to see if I'm going to have to reset them but it seems like I need to turn bluetooth on my phone on after taking them out. Edit: I dropped one in the sink and it worked like a champ once I fished it out. The recharge is fast and the battery life is unexpectedly good. Bumped up to 5 stars.

title: Won't charge. Complete waste of money💰
text: Sounded great until it lost life. The damn thing wouldn't charge with it's charger and a ton of mine that I tried. Disappointed 😞

title: Excellent quality with one minor quib
text: At first I was unimpressed with the lack of bass and having to turn my phone all the way up, but like everything involving earbuds, I just didn't have them in right. You have to find the right size, and pretty much grab your earlobe with your thumb and middle finger while you push it in at an angle with your index finger. Once that happened there was ample bass and tons of volume. Connecting and disconnecting is as simple as grabbing them out of the case, and then sticking them back in after; no need to hold buttons down to turn on/off like my previous 'neck hanger' ones.(after pairing of course) They don't fall out when running, and while the button pushing takes some getting used to, it's fine. Haven't made any calls so I don't know the quality of that. Not sure of battery life either as most of the time it's just for an The only bad thing is I get random split-second disconnects, usually a few in a row. Sometimes it helps to put my phone in my right pocket instead of left, but that's annoying for me.

title: Good product needs better microphone

title: Pretty good little ear buds
text: Bought these guys back in December as a gift for myself, and they have been clutch. For the price they are amazing! Granted that the quality of these little guys has diminished a little bit over the months. The battery life and sound quality are not as good as they were initially. They are still a great alternative to playing $100+ for any other pair of blue tooth earbuds. I personally have a slight problem with them staying in my (right) ear, but people I have lent them too say otherwise. They do look a little dumb sitting in your ear, but nothing a beanie can't fix. Sound quality and noise canceling is still pretty good after the last few months of heavy use (40+ hours a week). If for some reason my pair die or break in the next few months you better believe I will buy myself another pair.

title: The best bargain in town for truly wireless ear buds
text: First of all, let me just say complete wireless ear buds of any brand right now have poor battery life. So to rate these a 4 stars on battery life means: they meet and exceed other expensive brands, they’re actually pretty decent on battery life, and the nice little charger keeps you from running out juice. I’ve had beats, Sony, and JBL, all more pricier and expensive brands but these little things are my favorite. They actually sound better than my power beats and JBL truly wireless. They actually have better noise canceling features and they actually stayed out in my ear. Here’s the best part of these things: they’re $22!!! I paid an avg of 5 times as much for the bigger named brand headphones when I could have saved cash and just bought these instead.

title: Great wireless ear buds, you will regret it!
text: These are great, there's so many good things about them. First, they connect very easily via Bluetooth, no issues whatsoever with my Galaxy S10. They also fit very well in my ear. I used them both for music and for making a very lengthy call to unemployment for my employer. Both the call and music were extremely clear and the volume was great. The case appears to be black, but the top of the case is actually transparent. The benefit to this is that when the buds are charging you can see the progress and if charging is complete. There's also an LED indicator of how much battery is left in the case. I have recharged these several times and have not had to recharge the case yet. The instructions say that you can charge them 18 times without a case recharge, I'm not certain if that's accurate but I wouldn't be surprised if it were. The only thing I'd like to mention is just in case you haven't had wireless earbuds before (I haven't) while I was on hold on that very lengthy phone call, I used my finger to readjust one of the earbuds not realizing that there's a button on the bud that will disconnect a call..😳..I had to call back and wait through all the prompts and start all over. This however, is common for earbuds and I just want aware. They instructions and info are printed in tiny writing, which is my only complaint to date... So if you buy these and want to read the instructions, break out the magnifying glass. 😂 But don't let that stop you, they are really worth the price! Oh, I almost forgot, they came fully charged! A+

title: I'm Into It :}
text: On volume, my unit had little self direction in setting volume, even though it is apparently supposed to have Volume control is set from your device. On my mp3 player I went to settings - volume - slider to adjust. Then on player device itself is another volume control. YES - this blasts at 30 watts, no doubt about it! On charging issues: Ive noticed that these usb cables that are sent out aren't really that dependable. First if you have any issue with the Type C to DC plug itself or if the cable isnt attached firmly or if the usb end isnt seated well in your device you're going to have charging issues. Rather than assuming device isnt charging try another or new cable, they are super cheap. Im not using for waterproof needs so cant answer to that. I like the RGB 'breathe' feature but couldnt get mine to turn off, I dont really care. It may cause battery to discharge faster, whatever. This paired superbly with Bluetooth devices. The pairing was instantaneous. Have not yet experimented with range permissible - using in bedroom or living room so not really an issue. Well satisfied with this unit for now. Will have to wait and see on durability. Treat your devices well they tend to last longer.

title: Not impressed at all
text: First, I expected loud. Not! On my PC with both volumes all the way up and it's just what I would call normal sound. Second, it won't play sound thru the BlueStacks app. I get sound with Big Fish app, but not BlueStacks. I even set an Allow button in my settings that's supposed to allow apps to use that speaker. No luck. So it won't work for my PC. It's pretty expensive for it, but I decided I'd try it with my Echo. It does connect but the sound again, isn't that loud. And the Bass button does nothing. Or maybe it's more accurate to say I noticed no difference. Could be the songs, I tried it on several. And I can't tell when it's fully charged. A couple reviewers said it took an hour to fully charge. It's been on for several house and the light is still red. You are supposed to be able to double press the power button to check the battery level but, again, nothing happened??? I'll try it for awhile with the Echo but I will probably be returning this. For the money, all the buttons should work.

title: Pretty Solid
text: Came well packaged, Manual, USB, RC Jacks. It came charged but I plugged in anyways. on/charge light is Red turns blue when charged. I turned it on, in a few seconds it popped on my phone bluetooth (Iphone12Max). You control the volume from your phone and of course the songs you wanna play. The speaker it self you control "BASS" next or prev song. Battery lasted a good 9-10 hours and I'm sure it would've lasted at least 2-3 more hours, but I had to go and do stuff so I shut it off. It is built solid, lights at the ends. sound is crisp and clear with no distortion or noise, I had it in the Kitchen, and stepped outside on the Porch with it full blast and I can hear it good. I'm sure if I played it full blast outside the neighbors will complain. All in all it's a 10 out of 10.

title: Very nice speaker for enjoying my music outside.

Highly recommended!

title: Expensive but worth it.

title: Pricey, but good investment.

I used them daily.

title: Great idea Incredibly poorly executed...and with the worst customer service on the planet
text: These appear to be spectacular ear phones, much quieter than the previous models. The ability to use blue tooth to connect to iPads and iPhones is just fantastic if you want watch TV or proves while you are working out a an example. However there are two fatal flaws. First, you cannot really use the bluetooth for a phone conversation. They work for about an hour. Then the other party will think you are muffled then you won't hear them at all nor will they hear you. The other is that the connection between the earphones and the headband is incredibly and inexcusably weak and prone to breakage. I have three of the $1000 pilot Bose and two Comfort 35s. On four of then, tthey broke easily without any major force and with no possible easy way to get them fixed. I've just had to throw mine in a pile of junk. Consumer service? Don't count on any at all. They respond sporadically but will never actually help you. Appalling for such an expensive product. CUSTOMER SERVICE: So this is the worst customer service on the planet. My first pair broke months ago. They made me rip apart the headphones to get a serial number...then did nothing. The headphones are amazingly fragile for the price. Angelo from customer support wrote me a note about "support options" about three weeks ago. Then never followed up. They just don't care and they will leave you with a $350 piece of pure junk. Just appalling that they even have jobs since their main purpose seems to make customers go away!!!

title: Awesome!
text: Awesome! I have the QC25's and I have been very happy with them, when the QC 35's came out i was like Meh I dont need them boy was I wrong. The sound quality and build are terrific and they feel light on your head which is a huge plus for me. I have been wearing mine everyday and I do not miss have a cord one bit! I would say I have used them around 15 hours so far and it still says 40% charged! Well worth the extra $49.00 over the QC 25's

title: because they headphones are awesome! It was a little disconcerting at first when ...
text: I was in the TSA line and someone left these behind. Instead of leaving them there on the table, or taking them, I turned them over to the TSA agent. I really hope the person who lost these came back to get them and not have them stolen by some POS TSA agent, which usually happens, because they headphones are awesome! It was a little disconcerting at first when the noise cancelling kicked in and did exactly what it said it would, then the sound was great too. I would never usually buy something so expensive like this, but I've had a number of bluetooth headphones and they all suck. These do not, do I wish they were cheaper? Yes! But then they might not be as good.

title: Love these!
text: These headphones are amazing! I bought these a few months ago and have taken them everywhere with me. They are a bit bulky to carry around, but look very sleek and work wonderfully on planes and in the office!

title: Switch and breathability Issues
text: I'm on my second pair of these. The sound and noise cancellation is fantastic, although you can hear a white noise hiss when all is quiet. There are two problems with this headset. The first is that the on/off switch is cheap. It broke on my first pair, and now the second pair is ready to break as well. The second problem is how hot your ears get wearing them. My ears are practically sweating and I have to hold them open to get fresh air under the cups. I'm sure it's because they need a seal to do the noise cancellation so well. But it means they are not comfortable for wearing over an hour.

title: Awesome Headphones Way to go Bose! A++
text: I've had the QC35 headphones for about 2 weeks now and I love them! Sound quality is awesome and you are wire free! The Bluetooth pairing is super simple, and switching between Bluetooth devices is seamless. They are lightweight and very comfortable to wear for long periods of time, no itching or sweating. The noise canceling is amazing, just as good as the QC25 (wired) headphones. Receiving phone calls while listening is a breeze and the sound is clear, not muffled and easy to have a conversation. The charge lasts more than 20 hours and the on/off switch is very conveniently located on the side of the headphone with the volume and pause just below (if your phone isn't handy to adjust the volume). I absolutely love these Bose headphones! 5 stars all the way Bose!!

title: Worthy Investment
text: Purchased these headphones on a whim while in Hawaii just before my flight home. After many years of using my own in-ear headphones when on the airplane, I decided it was time to upgrade. I've always been hesitant to spend sooooo much money on headphones, but the aching from my ears after this last trip was enough to convince me that it was time to do myself a favor. Well, that and the 4.5% tax in Hawaii vs. the 10% back home in California. The Apple store has these in Navy, which was another selling point for me. The moment of truth came on the flight home. Just shy of 6-hours with these headphones on and not an ache or sore spot anywhere. Ear pieces are very comfortable, sound quality is great. Keep in mind that since these are wireless, you have to use the included cable to connect to an in-flight system. Make certain that you plug the cable into the headset all the way or you may have some sound quality issues. I was worried I had wasted $350, but once I double-checked the cable I realized I hadn't pushed it in all the way. Problem solved. I paired the headphones with my phone to test that connection, and the sound quality of my music was fantastic! Pairing process was fast and simple. The only thing I don't love so far is the Bose App. I'm trying to figure out what the purpose is, as it doesn't seem that critical and it doesn't seem to offer a whole lot. Other than that, I love these!

title: Amazing noise cancellation
text: These sound amazing. The ANC is second to none as expected from Bose. Battery life is excellent. They are perfect for what I was looking for and I couldn't be happier. The beats studio wireless sound better as far as powered wireless headphones go but their ANC was virtually non existent. If you want great sounding headphones with amazing ANC then get these now

title: Best wireless headset to work with.
text: Bose does not disappoint with this headphone set. I worked from home often and these noise cancelling headphones are a must. I tried multiple other vendors and got feedback from the people that they were not able to hear me, that is until I bought these headphones which are excellent. The sound quality is amazing and the other end hear me very clearly. The microphones work a little too well, I have have a customer tell me they could hear my tv from another room. It also comes with an airplane adapter and a very nice case. Well worth the money.

title: Bose continues to set the standard.
text: Tried & true on a couple trips on commercial jets and some military jets (loud compared to commercial airliners) and I love these things. Comfy, light, and the noise canceling feature is awesome. Super impressed with quality & performance from these headsets.

title: Good noise cancelling, good audio quality, loose fit
text: All things considered, I think these are good headphones. The noise cancelling is an improvement over the QC15s (what I upgraded from), and the sound quality is good overall. Where I disagree with most people, however, is in the area of comfort. While there are no pressure points to speak of that lead to discomfort, I feel the combination of the weight and soft cushions contribute to these headphones fitting somewhat loosely on the head. If I shake my head from side to side, the headphones slop around, and when I lower my head, gravity pulls the headphones down a bit. I wish they fit more securely. I don't have a particularly small head either. Another minor annoyance with these is that sharp bumps cause the noise cancelling to skip for a split second. I find that if I try and walk around with these on, the effect of my heel impacting the ground causes slight audio disturbances. I am not sure if I would buy them again as I feel they are a bit overpriced at $350.

title: Best Noise Cancelling Headphones.
text: I have been using this pair for 3 days and have nothing but great things to say. Comfort: These headphones are lightweight and ear-cushions are so soft and comfortable that I'm able to have them on for really long stretches without any discomfort. Noise Cancelling: I have used multiple noise cancelling headphones over the years and Bose QC headphones are the best when it comes to noise cancelling. In case you are wondering, yes it is as good as QC25. Music Quality: I'm not a audiophile and music sounds perfectly fine with this headphones. Connectivity: Connecting to multiple Bluetooth devices is very simple and intuitive. You can either do it directly using the headphones or companion app. Download Bose companion app from the App Store or Google Play store and it is pretty straight forward to connect and change between multiple devices. But, personally, I like to do manage devices directly from the headset. Pull and release the switch on right headset to toggle between different devices. Headphone voice prompts let you know the name of device connected to. You also get a backup audio cable and airline adapter for wired mode. Battery Life: Bose claims, on full charge you can run it for 20 hours on Bluetooth and 40 hours on wired mode. You only need battery to use noise cancelling feature. In case you run out of battery, you can use aforementioned audio cable and use the headphones without noise cancelling feature. Unlike QC25, this headphone pair doesn't have a slot for AAA battery. You need to charge it via micro-usb port. In my limited use, I have noticed it charges fairly fast. 30 minutes gave me roughly 40% charge. It is also very easy to see how much charge is left. Every time you turn on, you can have voice prompt tell you how much battery is left. Also there is small battery light indicator on the right headset. If you are using an iPhone, you can quickly check the battery percentage using Battery widget in Today view. Bose Customer Service: I actually bought Bose QC25 on May 28th from a local Bose store. When I noticed they released upgraded version, I went to the store and enquired whether I can upgrade by paying the price difference. Store manager was very happy to help me.

title: Bluetooth switching terrible, otherwise good
text: The manufacturer said in answer to a question: “So while you're watching video on the connected iPad, the headphones will automatically pause the video to answer a call from the connected smartphone.” This has never worked and irritates everyone who calls me. Even when I am watching a movie on my phone it still doesn’t work! Also, when I leave the headphones for a while and come back, they are always paired to the wrong device and take ages getting reconnected. Not recommended if you need more than one device to pair. I had to buy separate headphones for my iOS devices. The sound clarity is not good for podcasts. BTW the Beats and Apple headphones switch beautifully. However, these Bose headphones are particularly good for long-wearing comfort and noise cancelling. And the lack of voice assistant and finicky touch controls are a blessing. The ear pads are easily replaceable and while the battery isn’t, it is still fine after many years of daily use. They’ve been dependable. For a sale price of $100 these would be great. And I would buy another set.

title: If you fly alot, you simply have to cough up the $$$s and get these for your sanity.
text: Just got these after much consternation at paying $300+ for a headset!!! But, I am an audiophile who has spent FAR too much money on superiod sound eqpt, so why stop now. Yes, indeed. So I got 'em. Love 'em. First of all, very light! Never had such a light headset, you can move your head around and there is little inertia and little momentum in the headset so it stays put quite well. I think you could probable even jog with these on. The ear cups are very comfortable, but still you'll probably sweat a bit after a stretch of listening, but then again you want a good seal for good noise cancellation. The ANC isn't 100%, but wow it sure knocks out TONS of peripheral noise. You can probably do mindfulness meditation with these puppies on. The sound quality is 8.5/10. It's about as good as one gets for a bluetooth headset, as far as I have tested of all of them. Better than Beats, that's for sure. Not as good as the best B&W wired headphones that I've used. But more than adequate, and given the very low noise floor due to the ANC, I'd say it's a winner for an audiophile likeme. The bass is pretty killer, tight without being stupid boomy like Beats. Electronic dance music genre sounds very good on these. PLENTY loud enough, and my ears have been damaged from loud sounds plenty. Doing phone calls is quite good, too. I can hear enough of my own voice. The carrying case is nice and decently flat-ish due the way the cups fold flat. Accessories are an analog audio cable in case batt runs out, an airline dual jack adapter (for those OLD planes) and a MicroUSB charger cable. Pairs immediately with mini iPad 4, and Nexus 6P and Macbook Pro. I have to hand it to Bose. I pretty much dislike any and all of their other audio products. But these headphones rock it.

title: Perfect for what I use it for.
text: Love these headphones. My main use is to drown out the sound of the outside world. It does that perfectly when combined with some soft music. Battery lasts long, build is durable, and sound quality is great. Pairs easily with iOS (Apple) devices, and pairs even more easily with Android devices with NFC. I took it on a plane recently, and it drowned out about 90% of the noise. The sound quality is tuned more for bass-heavy tracks. It reminds me of sitting in a chamber when I use it. I use it for personal use and in my therapy practice. It helps the kids drown out outside noise. I just wish it wasn't so expensive.

title: Don't wait like I did
text: Being a frequent business traveler, I was always seeing these and being told I had to have them. I resisted for years. Didn't think I would like the pressure on my ears from the size or noise reduction. Ultimately, I was sold on the Bluetooth pairing with multiple devices and how seamlessly/ easily it transfers between these devices. I love turning them on and hearing the auto notifications as they automatically pair with any synced devices in range. I have a work iphone, personal iphone and ipad. The noise reduction took some getting used to but now I can appreciate why it matters on flights, i.e. white noise takes different forms and the plane noise is not white noise. The is probably sacrilegious but I use these for leaf blowing and while using my riding mower. Love them! Battery life is astonishing.

title: 18 Months Later: Battery and Earpad Replacement Needed
text: I was initially hesitant to purchase such an expensive pair of headphones (especially Bluetooth headphones with a battery that's not replaceable). But after having them for about a month I am in love. I rent a room in a house with a roommate who has a son who has severe autism. While I like his son he sometimes gets pretty loud. When I put these headphones on my head and get on my computer it's like I live alone. The noise cancellation is exceptional. If I have the headphones on without audio playing I can faintly hear him but if audio is going I can't hear anything. Even if these headphones cant hold a charge after a few years I feel that it's money well spend. No ragrets. Pros: Exceptional Noise Cancellation Solid Build Quality Comfortable (even after hours of use the only discomfort is sweaty ears which is inevitable with over ear cans) Great Sound Quality (no highs no lows yadda yadda, they have enough base and their very clean) Long Battery Life (I use them for 4-5 hours a night and charge them every 4-5 days) Cons: Battery Not Replaceable (unless they are serviced by Bose I assume, I can't score 5 stars because of this flaw) UPDATE: I have now had these headphones for roughly a year and a half. About two weeks ago I noticed that my ear pads were beginning to deteriorate, today both sides have stuffing coming out. Replacement ear pads are $40 from Bose. Last week my original fears were confirmed, the battery light started to turn on. I did some research and Bose DOES NOT OFFER BATTERY REPLACEMENT. From what I have read there is a third party company that will replace the Battery for $99 but these should have been designed so that the user could easily opened them and replaced the battery. I have used these headphones several hours a day since I bought them but they have always been well taken care of. While I love these headphones I am bringing my rating down to 2 stars because they are essentially a $350 purchase that has no solution for when their battery dies. I will contact Bose and update this review accordingly.

title: These Sounded So Good, I Bought Bose's Wireless SoundSport Headphones As Well
text: My new Bose QC35 headphones sound better (for the most part) than my Bowers and Wilkens P7 headphones, but without the cord-- and that impressed me. They also sound better than my MegaBoom speaker! At any rate, these are now my "go to headphones" at work since they're comfortable and sound great; when I first got them, I wasn't a fan of noise cancellation technology but the noise cancellation technology in these headphones is stunning and reminds me of LG's OLED display technology that produces deeper colors and deeper blacks. My original "4 star rating" was tied to not having an equalizer-- or any other way to shape the sound, but-- after a few weeks of use, these headphones have been nothing short of sensational, so I changed my rating to a "5." I can't imagine listening to sound with anything else; they also work great with skype and "goto meeting" since Bose's noise cancellation technology makes online audio experiences more immersive. In closing: this is the first pair of Bose headphones that I'll actually keep and, since they were so impressive, I bought a pair of Bose Wireless SoundSport headphones-- as well, for my workouts and they were really impressive too!

title: Awesome
text: They keep out the airplane roar and have a great sound.

title: Worth Every Penny!
text: As much as I liked my Sony 200D noise cancelling headphones from many years ago, it was time to upgrade to some over-the-ear ones because after many hours on, my ears would get fatigued due to the pressure of the headphones. I travel on average once a week every month, often times internationally on long-haul flights. These are the perfect noise-cancelling travel headphones: compact in size, great battery life and excellent audio output. I feel sorry for my passengers who are left listening to the deafening cabin noise, baby cries and coughing on our flights. This is not to say, these are miraculous because you can still hear the crying at times but the difference of headache-inducing cabin noise with and without these is dramatic. I don't know how people don't get headaches. They are great for in-flight movies, too. Add a great memory foam neck pillow and silk eye mask and I manage to sleep just fine everytime.

title: Best Pair of Headphones...Period
text: I've owned many pairs headphones. I've tried other noise canceling versions of this style. These Bose QC35s are supreme compared to any brand. The noise canceling is superior. I use them for meditation, airplane travel, late night TV watching when my fiancé is sleeping, at the gym and even at work. I can't even stress how multifunctional and comfortable these headphones are on my ears. Second and most importantly, the sound. I listen to music all the time from Hip-Hop to Classical Piano, the sound on these headphones is deep, rich, layered and clear. Everything I listen to sounds beautifully orchestrated. Third, a bonus feature is the battery is quick to charge and lasts a long time. I often forget to turn them off and the next day I still have battery life. Super great for a guy like me. Overall, these are the best headphones money can buy! They can be used to your benefit in many ways. A great purchase, probably my best purchase of the year.

title: Perfect noise-cancelling headphones
text: I got these for Christmas and OMG I love them so much! I wanted them for my commute to work on the bus and to drown out excess noise at work. I got to work and popped them on and I was instantly stunned by how much background noise was silenced - elevators running, the overhead ventilation system, construction work outside just GONE. I ran over to my co-worker's desk and told her to put them on and just listen and then take them off and listen to the difference, she was shocked as well. She now wants her own pair. Now, I'm not a headphone connoisseur and this is my first pair of noise-cancelling headphones so I can't tell you much about sound acoustics and what not. What I can tell you is that I can definitely hear more instruments than I could before and everything sounds much more crisp and clear overall. As for comfort, they feel like little clouds straight from heaven gently resting upon my ears. I have a small head and tiny ears for reference. They don't feel heavy or make my ears sore like other headphones tend to do. These are quickly becoming one of my most prized possessions. I would 100% recommend them! Absolutely love them.

title: Worth every Penny I paid...
text: Bose has truly produced a product that inspires the word "Awesome". After getting the headphones, I placed them on my head and over my ears then just listened to the ambient noises that filterd thru... Even without turning them on, the ambient sounds in the room were nicely diminished... Not completely, but enough to be much less distracting... After a few moments I decided to switch them on and observe the noise cancelling. AWESOME, that is the only adequate word to describe the total silence that ensued. After that, I picked some nice music from iTunes to play and it was so very soothing with nothing but music... I highly recommend these headphones to anyone who wants to escape the ambient noises of their life and be completely immersed in either music or videos or whatever sounds you truly want to hear... It is amazing.

If they did not make me ill I would rank them very highly, the sound is good and the noise cancelling is impressive. Just make sure to try them out for at least ten minutes before you buy.

title: Barely Heard Jet Engines
text: First and foremost, I do not get paid to write reviews. I also did not get these free in exchange for a good review; although, I wouldn't have complained if Bose sent these to me for free lol I've had these for a few days and they worked well at home. However, the real test came yesterday when I had two flights. I don't know how it does it, but the noise canceling on this is really good. No, it's not 100% effective, but it's pretty astonishing how little you hear from outside of the headphones. I could barely hear the jet engines and I certainly couldn't hear a word the passenger next to me was saying. The sound is what you would expect from Bose. It's clear with high trebles and soft bass. However, I do like how you can control some of this through the free app. Battery life is crazy good. I wore this for about 6 hours and only used 10% battery. Granted, that's on a brand new headphones and I'm sure it'll get worse with age. The one drawback is that the batteries are fixed within the unit. From what I've read, the battery is soldered which means you can either pay Bose to replace the battery when the time comes or you'll have to purchase new headphones. If you use this mainly for traveling, I expect to get at least 2-3 years before the better completely dies. At that point, since I have extensive solder experience, I may try and change the battery myself. Aside from that significant issue which won't be a problem for a while, I do love these headphones.

text: I love audio, and lately with the services you can get 320kbps or 256kbps. Additionally, I travel every week to South America or to California from Florida (5-6 hr flight time each way). Babies don't bother me, but I realized that I need peace and quiet to listen, watch or read my own media. I listen to all genres and wanted something practical and sturdy. These wireless Bluetooth noise cancelling headphones are the solution. Comfortable to wear for hours, long battery power and they come with their own case and necessary adaptors. Highly recommend these headphones. Alternate choices were the Monster Pro and Sony Extra-Bass but I was sold on the built of these. I have the black ones, the silver are OK, except that they "look" fragile and susceptible to scratches. I don't know yet when or how much it will cost to replace the internal battery, but for the overall package these are my best choice. From what I read it should take about 500 charges to find out.
