title: Spyware! Google "complaint filed by Kyle Zak in federal court in Chicago"
text: Was going to purchase another pair of QC35 after having lost my QC25s. I happened to come across an article about these headphones listening in on everything and uploading recordings, other media content from the phone, headphone's serial number etc., via the associated phone app. This is particularly despicable behavior from Bose. It's entirely expected from something like a random free app (i.e. if you're not paying for the product, you are the product), but I don't find it anywhere close to acceptable when buying something as trivial as headphones. Update: Went to the local Best Buy store and listened to the QC35 vs. Sony MDR-1000X and Beats Studio Wireless ... I bought the Sonys. The sound is clearly better and the noise cancellation seems to be very good, albeit somewhat different from the Bose. The QC35s have very aggressive ambient noise reduction, there's a lot of pressure on the ear drum as soon as you put them on and everything feels drowned out with a subtle yet annoying background "white" noise. Very effective, but uncomfortable to me. The Sonys seem to provide a similar level of noise reduction but you do hear a bit more of voices and other non-droning sounds around you. This is accomplished with less "white noise" pressure on the ear, providing a more comfortable experience, whether listening to music or not (at least in my opinion). If I may use a poor a metaphor, the Bose seem to use the sledgehammer approach to noise cancellation: take whatever sound comes in, generate a fat opposite-phase signal and shove it in. The Sonys seem to be a bit more selective with the spectrum (or perhaps just a bit more restrained with the amplitude) and the result feels a bit more delicate and less fatiguing. So far, from just half an hour of comparative listening, I much prefer the Sonys. In QC35's defense, the sound quality (even though still poor overall) seemed better than what I remember from my QC25s. I've tested them primarily with opera, and, as other reviews have noted, the voice region of the audio spectrum sounds OK. Not expecting Stax sound quality from this type of headphone, but I think the Sony is a better-rounded product.

title: Nearly perfect

This way the product would have a longer life span for when the internal battery eventually doesn't hold a charge. The noise cancellation isn't perfect but very impressive.

title: I love them
text: I love these! I bought a pair of very good in-ear wireless headsets, and they worked fine, but I found them deeply uncomfortable. So I bought the bullet and bought these. I absolutely love them. They're amazingly comfortable, and the sound quality is fabulous. I am at my computer far more than is healthy. I work as a computer programmer during the day and in the evenings, I write books. I wear headsets and listen to music for background to drown out other noises that tend to be more intrusive. I've tried a variety of headsets over the years, but I've never had a pair that felt so good and produced such rich sound as these. I'm on Mac. They work great both to my iMac and my MBP.

title: Great headphones.

title: Sound is good, but audio connection leaves much to be desired.
text: Noise cancellation is better than average, but I'm sick of the frequent cutting out of bluetooth audio streams. Sitting ten feet from my Apple TV, I get choppy audio. Also, any time a new device connects, it gets choppy as well.

title: Great Bluetooth headphones, Bose quality!
text: I have owned the Bose QC15, the QC25, and now, the QC35 and feel uniquely qualified to provide a review on these based on my past experience. These, I purchased locally due to reward points. The price listed are pretty much the same everywhere. I will say that I have tried multiple wireless headphones over the past year and simply did not feel that they were "up to par" as the Bose were. It wasn't until Bose released the QC35 that I decided to purchase a pair. I chose the black pair as they are more subtle than the silver/gray pair. The buttons on the right side are intuitive and easy to reach and use. I was very pleased with the placement of these buttons. After reading the quick start guide and the owners manual, I felt even more at ease with handling and understanding just how the buttons are to be used. It's intuitive and not convoluted. The ear cups, like the predecessors before them, are comfortable. Many assume that they are leather. In the true sense of the word, they're more like "pleather." They are most definitely soft and easy on the ears. I've worn mine for hours with no issues. I have also placed calls through my iPhone while wirelessly connected to the Bose. The other party have stated that it sounds "crystal clear." Last but not least - For people who may have a hearing loss - I paired mine up with a BT-compatible TV. In my case, I am now able to listen to the TV through my Bose QC35 headphones. It makes me appreciate these even more. PROS: Comfort, Bose quality, ease-of-use, quick recharging time, nice case CONS: Bose should include the same wires used on the QC25. I went ahead and ordered these through Amazon.

title: Great headphones and extremely effective with airplane noise
text: I have owned several Bose products over the years and these headphones are great. The price is high but the quality is amazing. I travel often and these make a huge difference with engine noise. I won't fly without them.

title: Good Earphones
text: I'm pretty new to quality earphones so don't have anything with which to compare my new Bose which I received yesterday. The earphone is very comfortable. The sound quality is very impressive. It connects flawlessly via Bluetooth with my iPhone, MacBook, and iPad. I'm not sure what I should have expected from the noise cancellation. I have found that when playing music via Bluetooth mild background sound does seem to be suppressed, but louder sounds come through. I tested the noise cancellation playing a variety of white sounds on my iPhone while playing music via my MacBook. The sounds do seem to be suppressed at low volume, but are easy to hear at higher volume. My conclusion is that noise cancellation is limited even in these highly rated earphones. They are superb earphones, well built, with great sound quality, but not sure they are worth the price. Since I submitted this review, I have flown overseas and back. These earphones are superb for flying. They completely block out aircraft background sounds.

title: Weird Issue
text: I have tried two pairs of this model and both exhibit the same weird behavior. There are times when I turn my head to the right, the sound drops out entirely. If I turn my head back it returns. The source device is in my left pocket so the range should be an issue, so I don't know why this happens. I have another pair of Bose wireless headphones that do not have this problem.

title: Best quality and most versatile Bluetooth headphones
text: For several years, I've been trying to find Bluetooth headphones that (1) provides quality sound with noise reduction, (2) don't cut out with during use with my Android phone, and (3) easily connect to a variety of of Bluetooth sources. My most recent failure was a Sennheiser MB Pro 2. This headset consistently cuts out during calls. The Bose QuietComfort 35 is quite a bit more expensive than other choices---but it satisfies all of my requirements. It (1) provides excellent sound with noise reduction, it (2) does not cut out during calls using my Samsung Galaxy S7 edge Android phone, (3) I use it connect for conference call, Thinkpad P50 video and sound, iPad Air 2 sound and video, and my Samsung smart TV audio---including while exercising on my elliptical. Several other features that I like: * I can easily switch from one connection to another, e.g., when I get a call in the middle of listening to music on my iPAD of TV. * They're comfortable * Built in microphone * Nice carrying case (can carry in on a plane for noise reduction) * Controls are easy-to-use by feel (not true of many other head sets) * Quick to charge * If desired, can connect wired

title: Exactly what I was yearning for.
text: After buying/returning a few different headphones from Amazon and brick&mortar stores, I settled on these as my forever-headphones. At least until something better comes out, which I'm predicting won't happen for another 5+ years. My headphone buying journey started cheap - with headphones from Amazon in the $50 price range. Each time I experience a dealbreaker with a headphone, I tended to return it and buy something more expensive. The last headphones I returned with the Plantronics Backbeat Pro ($159). Here's a bit about me: - My ear drums are hyper sensitive. Also I'm an introvert. These two characteristics mean loud sounds piss me off, and lots of different frequencies are jarring for me. - Most headphones, even light ones, hurt the top of my head after 30 mins. Here's what I love about these Bose headphones. - All elements of music come through crystal clear. You know they're truly great headphones when you can turn the volume way up and not a single frequency is jarring. All you get is loud, all-encompassing music... such a pleasant experience. I have only experienced this pleasant-clarity-at-loud-volume characteristic with one other pair of headphones -- my Audio-Technica ATH-M70x, which I use for music production. - These are the only headphones that I have ever worn that I forget I'm wearing. The other day I wore these at work for 4 hours. No pain. Only a jolt of realization, like, wow..... have these headphones melded to my skull? What a novel experience. Anyway, I'm in love. These are the headphones of my dreams. You probably won't love these headphones if: - You like a ton of bass. The sound is nice and round. - You like really loud music. Although these headphones get loud, they will never feel "loud."

title: These things are wonderful. I have used them for days with no ...

title: The sound quality is very good across the spectrum
text: Works well to knock out most plane noise. I also use the headphones at work to reduce ambient noise. The sound quality is very good across the spectrum, and I have been pleasantly surprised about how long the batteries last between charges. Overall, very pleased.

title: Microphone is useless for phone calls because it picks up all ambient/ background noise
text: These sound amazing and have incredible noise cancelling, but they are completely useless for phone calls. My stock wired iPhone earbuds work great for phone calls because they seem to cancel out background noise that could potentially be sent from my end of the phone call. The Bose QC35s do not do this at all. They send every little piece of background noise. This is a HUGE design flaw that Bose has acknowledged. This flaw basically renders these headphones useless for what I really need them for: Phone calls in airports and public places while I am working on the road. Bummer.

title: Good product
text: One thing I find annoying is how it automatically switches between connected devices, even if I turn one off in the app. I have it connected to my TV and my iPhone, and occasionally I'll want to use my phone and hear that alone, so I switch off the TV device in the iPhone app. After a few seconds it will automatically turn on the TV device. I gave up on that route (one of the reasons I bought this) and just stopped using my phone. Other than that, it's nice quality headphones.

title: Noise cancellation is just as good and also is bluetooth quality
text: I long anticipated this product. I have owned both the QC20i and Bose Bluetooth headphones. I would say that they have integrated both functions very well. It performs as expected. Noise cancellation is just as good and also is bluetooth quality. It also does well functioning with multiple devices which was a problem previously. For example. I can now listen to music from my laptop, take a call from my cellphone and the music resumes automatically from laptop when I'm done with the call without static or any delay. Build and quality is also good. They feel as sturdy as before. Sound Quality hasn't changed much (typical Bose, it sounds great at low and medium volume but at higher volumes you get the sense they are altering the music to maintain clarity) but the bluetooth is much better and now there is wireless noise cancellation. Battery life is also an improvement, lasts me a we before charging. They are fairly comfortable though I find myself taking them off briefly at intervals. Overall I am very happy. I have only had for a couple weeks. Once they don't malfunction I think it will be another great purchase.

title: Best wireless headphone on the market
text: Super awesome, love them so much. Bose is the best in my opinion. Sound quality is better than the Sony or Skull candy or Beats - hands down!

title: Worth it. Can't hear coworkers.
text: I got these as soon as I heard they were out and I am so glad I did. They are comfortable, the blutooth is quick and easy, and the battery life is solid, and the build feels very high quality. But what sets them apart is their noise cancellation. I have never owned noise cancelling headphones before, so I can't compare to other brands, but I am very impressed with these headphones. The noise cancellation itself will block out almost all low to medium volume ambient noise like air vents, fans, and just everyday noises around the office and home. It doesn't really block out voices or other loud sounds, it just muffles them. However, with a little bit of music, you can't hear anything! It's fantastic. All I have to do at work to not hear a thing my coworkers say is put these guys on and play some background music at low volume. I highly recommend if you are willing to spend the money. You won't regret it.

title: these work well enough and last long enough to justify the cost

He is very happy with them and feels that lessening the sound of the plane allows him to be more calm (he doesn't like to fly) and improves his ability to sleep during the flight.

title: Just buy and enjoy.
text: What Can I say about these great headphones that hasn't already been said? Battery life is amazing, really. Sound quality is very nice and extremely well balanced. Noise canceling is best in class, by a wide margin! BT connectivity is rock solid with my iPhone 6s and my iPad mini. It just works. Also, not mentioned enough, is the fact that the BT latency is very low. When watching movies on your device, the video is very well synchronized with the audio. Seems like a small thing, but if you watch movies on your device like I do when traveling, latency issues are really annoying. Yes, they are expensive. But, every Bose product I have ever purchased in still in service. Some for 20 years and counting. The Bose reputation for for high quality is well deserved. When you consider the real service life of the product, the cost is very reasonable. You will not regret the purchase, enjoy!

title: The best headphones for escaping noise at work and during air travel.
text: I use these headphones mainly at work and work related travel. I would use them at home, but I can't pair these with my PS4 (when playing video games late at night and surround sound would disturb everyone) so I use Sennheiser HD-598 headphones with my PS4 controller. At work, these are a great way to escape from co-worker conversations and focus on work. The only downside is they work so well people have to tap my shoulder to get my attention (or send me instant messages). If this bothers you, you may need to get a motion sensor or mirror in your cube. I pair these with my Samsung S6 edge at work. When I'm traveling for work or vacation, they work great on planes and completely drown out passenger noise and engine drone. On planes, these headphones are paired with an iPad 3 for offline Netflix downloaded shows/movies. After wearing the headphones for a few hours on multiple leg flights, your ears can feel a little sweaty, but it's not uncomfortable. I just dry my ear with my hands or shirt and put them back on. When not in use, I always keep them in the case which fits neatly into my laptop roller bag for work or a small carry on backpack for vacation travel. The sound from the headphones works for their intended purpose. They can't really compare to higher end Sennheiser headphones with amplification, but each headphone serves its own purpose. That being said, the audio range works for all genres of music and movies. It has enough bass that allows you can feel action movies in a small way which is fine for flights/travel. One other thing about travel, if you get lost in your own world, definitely take these off when it's close to boarding time. I almost missed a flight because I couldn't hear any announcements. The headphones hold their charge for a very long time. I rarely charge the headphones. It's nice that the charging cable for the headphones is the same as my android phone's cable.

title: Great Headset

title: As Good As It Gets
text: First, I did not buy these from Amazon as I do almost anything else, but, I am a frequent traveler and when I found out I could purchase these using Marriott points, I did. I fly about 130,000 air miles every year. So I spend a lot of time with headphones on my head. I have bought, oh, 10 different sets of Bluetooth headphone in the past 2 years. My go-to is my Bose Soundlink. sound, imminently portable, but not noise cancelling. I fly first class most of the time, and these headphones filled my needs. But then, a recent article on Flipboard talked about the possibility of allowing telephone conversations while in flight. I shuddered...3 or more hours of 200 people all talking. So, I saw that Bose had just released their first noise cancelling Bluetooth headphones. I waited a bit, and then began reading reviews, which were consistently good. I made a decision to get them, hurried along by the Marriott offer.They arrived today. Wow! These are by far the best headphones I have ever had. Now, I love Bluetooth headphones, but I am not expert. I am not an audiophile if that implies expertise, but I know what I like. I started with the soundtrack for South Pacific because one song was in my head. I don't like the term, "earworm" but prefer Theodore Reich's "The Haunting Melody." Rossano Brazzi and Mitzi Gaynor never sounded so good before. Then I went to a mix with everything from Claudio Villa, to Electric Flag, to Bob Dylan and Johnny Cash. To paraphrase Bum Phillips, if the Bose QuietComfort 35 headphones are not in a class of their own, whatever class they're in, it don't take long to call roll. I have not tried them on a plane, yet. This year's business travel is slightly delayed...an accident resulting in three broken ribs and a fractured knee cap have slowed me down. But, I will amend this review after my first trip. Highly Recommended

title: Bluetooth is easy to connect and they are so quiet
text: Wow, this rock! Third time is the charm. I had two different brands, were not at this quality and they both ended up hurting the top of my head after wearing for an extended period of time. Bluetooth is easy to connect and they are so quiet. Very happy with these.

title: Great sound quality and battery life
text: After first purchasing these headphones, I contemplated returning them because they pressed against the stems of my glasses causing discomfort. This problem ended up going away and they are now very comfortable to wear. I didn't realize how great the sound quality is until I went back to listening to music from a speaker. Now, I only enjoy listening to music through the headphones. I am also impressed with the battery life.

title: Always Superb!
text: So much better sound quality than my wireless Beats. I hear every instrument. Instruments in different ears, resulting in perfection. Bose has never let me down.

title: noise cancelling can't be turned off
text: I have used it for several weeks. I realize the worst "feature" of this headphone is that you cannot turn off noise canceling when connect via bluetooth. I don't like the base noise when the noise cancelling is on. It's much uncomfortable than the environment background noise.

title: The best noise cancellation I've used, including much pricier cans
text: After three months, I'm still quite enamored of this purchase. The noise cancelation is unparalleled in my experience. I've used noise-canceling headphones including the QC2 or QC3, I'm not sure which; Lightspeed aviation headsets; and Sony supra-aural cans purchased a few months ago. The QC35 surpasses them all, including the $600 aviation headset. I've only tried the Bose aviation headsets briefly in a couple stores, so comparing them isn't fair. I work from a home office, with my wife and our kid on the other side of a thin door. With these on, I can't tell if they are home or not. The hum of the various computer fans in my office completely disappears. This morning, the washer and drier were both running when I emerged to get some tea while I was on the phone, using this headset, and I heard none of the equipment noise except the occasional clink of a button or zipper -- the actual roaring noise of the washer and drier was completely eliminated. The person I was conversing with didn't even hear that. I haven't tried these in a commercial jet yet, but given their ground-based performance I have no doubt they will be excellent. (They don't have the connectors for GA aircraft, so whatever their performance they couldn't replace the Bose A20 or Lightspeed Sierra/Zulu2.) [edit to add] I've now used these for air travel, and they do indeed deal well with the noise of being a passenger in jet aircraft. Beyond the noise cancellation, this is an excellent sset of Bluethooth headphones. It pairs seamlessly with my phone, laptop, and desktop. Two devices can be connected at a time, and the Bose Connect app on my phone makes it easy to control which other paired device is active even with several paired devices are in range. Sound quality is better than I knew Bluetooth could do. I haven't used them with the wired connector yet, mostly because I hate wired headphones.

title: OMG the universe these headphones provide.
text: Truly, one of the best purchases I have ever made. They allow for me to truly lose myself in the music. And walk around the house (with Bluetooth limitations in consideration, of course). I was in the Apple store testing them out before I bought them. Could hardly hear a thing from the raucous store environment. And now that I have them in my home environment, the music with Spotify on my side...

title: Turns on by itself!
text: After two years of light use, I got the same problem so many people have had with their QC35's, the set will turn on by itself despite the power switch being in the OFF position. This is a disaster in the literal sense of the word and Bose tells us this is a hardware problem and can't be fixed with a software update. 350 dollars I paid for this and now I can't use it anymore! Bose CS says sorry yours is out of warranty and now you have to shell another 250 dollars to get a replacement! This is beyond outrageous! Such terrible quality control and customer service! The problem is so wide spread Bose ought to formally address the problem and straighten their mess! NEVER EVER WILL I BUY ANOTHER BOSE PRODUCT. Potential buyers BEWARE!

title: Best headphones I've ever purchased
text: Best headphones I've ever purchased! Very long battery life and comfortable to wear. Put these on and almost all sounds around you just fadw away. wonderful for airplane trips. Bluetooth pairs flawlessly with my Iphone and Ipad Pro.

title: Good audio quality, mediocre range, inteeface, and durability.
text: Decent enough product but falls short of what I would expect from Bose. The sound quality is great and the noise cancellation makes noisy environments more pleasant and safe for my hearing. The downsides are (1) the bluetooth range, (2) the controls, (3) the earpads, and (4) ultimate mechanical failure. The range is more limited than even very cheap bluetooth headphones I have. At just a couple meters the sound starts skipping. There are three control buttons: volume up & down and a multi-function: one press for play/pause, two for forward, three for back. Again, even cheap headphones have separate buttons for these controls, and it's very easy to hit this one the wrong number of times; it's quite annoying. The earpads are tearing after only normal use and could be more durable. Finally after about a year and a half the sound drops out of the left ear when the case is wiggled as if there's a loose wire. Would (will) I buy this model again ? Maybe, but I will shop around first, which I did not do last time.

title: Really nice headset, quiet and can stay on my head ...
text: Really nice headset, quiet and can stay on my head for more than 4 hours without hurting my ears, really comfortable and awesome sound effect. Worth the money.

title: Greatest headphones ever

When I reach office. When I go down for coffee. When nature calls. When I don't want to listen to my noisy neighbor. When I am in the airplane. Also charges very quickly.

title: Got a defective piece at first.
text: The bluetooth was flawed. The music would break up every few seconds over bluetooth when I am walking. There were no people around me and it was a fairly open area outside. I noticed this kept happening. Have started a return for them. EDIT: Second one I got was literally perfect. Have had it for the past 4 months. It's amazing!

title: So far fantastic
text: Oh my, oh my, these are the real deal. When I finally clicked the checkout button I was anxious. That's a lot of money. They arrive fully charged. They feel good. I put them on and turn then on, pre-connecting to Bluetooth so pre-music and wonder if my power just went out. Did the aircon on the fan just turn off? What happened? I take them off and the familiar drone of moving air and outside noises resume. This is noise cancellation at its very best. I pair and turn on the music and the audio is superb. I decide to push it further and play Streets Of Philadelphia by Springsteen to see how the bass is. It's lovely. It's rich. It's smooth. I am extremely impressed. I worried that I was paying for the brand but I was wrong. I paid for the best. These headphones are the bees knees. Flight on Sunday. I'm excited to report back on how they cope with aircraft grade noise!

title: Great sound, ear cushions are cheap
text: Bose ear pads are cheap and flimsy, I'm sure I'll have to replace these in a year or so like we did with my husband's set. Sound is good though, just wish for the price they would make more durable quality ear cushions.

title: Perfection
text: As a long time Bose headphones customer, I was elated that Bose finally released a wireless set with noise cancellation. I have been using pairs of QC15s (over the ear) and QC3s (on the ear). I also own a pair of Soundlink wireless on ear- which cause significant ear discomfort after lengthy use. My only concern with the QC35s was Bluetooth quality and possible audio/video lag. Some observations after two weeks of usage: the headphones are *INCREDIBLY* comfortable. I have worn them for hours on end and not the slightest discomfort to my ears. Also, compared to the excellent QC15s, the noise cancellation on the QC35s is a quantum leap - far superior to the previous wired sets. Like the Soundlink wireless, pairing and battery level is communicated via automated voice through the headphones. Paired with both my iPhone 6s Plus and iPad Air 2, there has been ZERO audio lag watching YouTube and shows via TiVo app. The sound quality is crisp and absolutely amazing. The noise cancellation alone is worth it. If you're a QC 15 (or older) holdout like me, don't hesitate to get the QC35s. They are comfortable, user-friendly, and the sound and noise cancellation features are incredible. I strongly recommend the QC35s without hesitation.

title: They music sound was really good but the noise canceling feature was amazing for studying

I'm a student so I usually used them in combination with ear plugs so I could then study anywhere! I highly recommend it! But unfortunately someone stole mine at the library and I can't buy another one yet because I'm still paying off my stolen one so careful with yours :(

title: Great quality, great music
text: Bose is know for it's great audio quality, and these QuietComfort are not the exception. They're comfortable to use, the audio is clear, the connection is fast, and I love that it supports 2 devices at the same time. The battery life is also great, given that these headphones provide noise cancelling and reproduce wireless music. I easily get the 8 hours of battery. They're light, and the included case make them easy to transport. I am 100% sure these are among the best wireless headphones you can buy at a reasonable price.

title: ... a skeptic of Bose products but I am in love with these
text: Generally a skeptic of Bose products but I am in love with these!! WHAT'S GREAT: - Super comfortable - Balanced soundstage, sound is good throughout tonal range, very immersive - Strong Bluetooth connection - Handles simultaneous connections to two devices without a hitch, unlike other Bluetooth earphones I've used. - The noise-cancellation is incredibly good, far exceeding other products I've tried. - Battery life is pretty good and they recharge quickly. - A (somewhat funny-sounding) voice tells you the battery remaining and devices it's connected to AREAS FOR IMPROVEMENT: - Noise cancellation can feel like pressure on your eardrums unless music is playing. It's pretty minor and you adjust to it somewhat. This isn't unique to Bose but some people are more sensitive to it than others. - Doesn't have thumping bass if you're into that. The bass is good, just not head-shaking. - Expensive, but I feel they're worth it, having gone through countless other pairs of earphones, these are the first I legitimately love. - Not super stylish (but not offensive looking). - Wish you could turn off noise cancellation, for instance, when walking around the city it's kind of dangerous because you can barely hear anything around you. - Not as comfortable when wearing them around your neck, kind of block your chin from going down. Overall, highly recommend. Have stopped using my other headphones and use these everywhere except the gym.

text: I don't know why I waited so long for the new ones. This year cold and flu has been so bad that i'm over listening to people cough and hack their heads off all day long in my office. Now that I've got these I can hear nothing around me and that's just the way I like it. I had an original pair of QC's and they lasted me for 10 + years so hopefully i'll get around the same life out of them. title: If you are on the fence about these...go ahead and buy them! I'm wearing mine right now!
text: My usual threshold for quality cans is around $100. But, after reading some of the reviews of the qc35, I decided it might be worth a shot and I am so glad I did. As you've heard many times, the noise cancellation is superb, just wearing the headphones with no music or sound is very relaxing. Also, to enjoy the music, I don't have to turn it up very loud. The sound separation (more 3d sound than stereo) is just excellent. I've been hearing parts in songs that I've never noticed before. Lately, I have been having to work in an office with lots of people and lots of chatter. Again, with music turned down low, I can really enjoy listening to music and I don't hear all of the white noise and chatter around me. It is true bliss! I did see a couple of complaints about them being warm after a while and it is true, the ears can bet a bit warm after extended use. However, these are closed headphones, so I'm not sure you can do much about that. Plus, I prefer there not being any outside noise bleed to a little ear warmth. Pros: Superior noise cancellation Superb sound Great for calls Great battery life Nice case (that actually protects the headphones) Cons: A bit heavy A bit warm for extended periods of time I've had a bit of an issue with the headphones connecting with two devices at once even with one of them 'off' in the app Expensive All that being said, for the sound quality, noise cancellation, and portability, they are well worth the investment.

title: I just bought a pair of the POWERBEAT PROS....

title: Great Headphones
text: I bought these headphones for work. I work as an Automation Engineer writing code most of the day. There's a lot of conversations and walk up traffic. I've had several headphones in the past, but these block out most if not all of the sound. Obviously they are expensive, but i got tired of buying $100 headsets just for them to break 5 months later. Go big or go home.

title: Worth every penny.
text: My first thought was that these headphones are too expensive. Recently, my brother brought a pair with him to our annual Guatemala fishing trip. He'd put them on just to cancel the drone of the twin diesel engines as we made the several hour journey out to sea. He let me try them and I was absolutely amazed at the amount of noise they canceled. I'd say they are better than advertised. Most of the noise I was still able to hear was coming from vibration induced through my body. Incredible noise cancelling ability, very good sound quality and very, very comfortable to wear. I wore these the entire flight from Seattle to Honolulu (6 hours) without fatigue, and the jet noise isn't nearly as loud as the boat engines were. Very nice to be able to listen to quality sound at levels that aren't blasting your eardrums out. My thoughts now? Worth every penny.

title: It’s great until the warranty runs out (1yr)
text: 100% junk. It’s great until the warranty runs out (1yr). Like everyone else says, it turns itself on and drains the battery. Customer service will try to get you to buy a new pair. Sorry, I’m not looking to drop $350 every year. I was a fan but i guess it’s time to move on. Also, there’s a lawsuit right now since the headphones illegally gathers data.

title: Bose, It just works !
text: All I can say is wow !! Let me give full disclosure by saying I am a Bose lover and have several of their headphones, ear buds and radio's. I have their products because they sound good and they have great customer service. The Quietcomfort 35's did not disappoint, they sound great and they eliminate outside noise. They work so good I would not recommend you wear them if you need to be aware of your surroundings. The sound is rich and the old saying "Bose, no highs or lows" does not apply here.. The sound rivals some very expensive headphones I have, almost as good, they just miss by a tad. The thing that separates them from the rest is the ability to block out outside noise. These use sophisticated electronics to eliminate outside ambient noise and block out sound they do. Just a great product that does what they say it will.

title: Good, but major design flaw
text: Overall these are great sounding headphones, but I discovered a major design flaw. Every night I got out for a walk around my neighborhood, so I decided to wear these headphones to listen to music. They do a great job of cancelling out the noise of passing cars and other ambient noises, but they actually amplify the sound of my footsteps hitting the sidewalk. Literally every step I take makes a "thud, thud, thud" sound that is amplified by these headphones. Even with the music turned up really loud it is still noticeable. The problem seems to be related to the plastic outer casing picking up the vibrations from my footsteps. If I hold my hands over the cups to stop the vibrations then the noise goes away. This is pretty annoying given that these are supposed to be noise *cancelling* headphones, but they actually *amplify* some noise like footsteps. I must have read over 100 reviews prior to purchasing these headphones and nobody made any mention of this phenomena, so I figured it was worth writing about.

title: Best headphones I've had near my ears
text: I'm not gonna lie. I had fixed myself a few scotches the night I ordered these. I began to research the best over the ear, bluetooth, noise cancelling headphones. I found several trusted sites saying that these were the ones to buy. So I started to look around in preparation for Black Friday. However, I started on Amazon, the price was the MSRP listed on the review sites, and the alcohol turned a research browse into a purchase. This purchase was pricey for an impulse buy. I REGRET NOTHING! These are amazing. First, I have a melon head. These fit my head diameter beautifully. I owned a wired pair of noise canceling headphones that feel like they're trying to squeeze my precious bodily fluids out through my temples. The QuietComfort 35 have no such pressure. I had a friend with a normal head try them on and they fit him as well. Second, I have dumbo ears. These fit over my ears wonderfully. My old wired set was tight around my ears, but these are super comfortable. Padding is great. My normal proportioned friend said they felt great around his ears - they weren't too loose for him or too tight for me. Third, this product has an app for Android and Apple. The reviews are...rough. I installed it on my Android device and it connected flawlessly. I used the Android device to connect it to my iPad. Boom! No issues. From reading the reviews on the app store, I was apparently experienced miraculous connection (not conception). But I can't find any issue with the app, it connected, installed firmware updates, and helped me connect to other devices. Finally, the sound quality is incredible. With nothing playing, the noise canceling is eerily powerful. It cut out the hum of the fridge, the whir of the HVAC, and even reacted to a human voice to knock it down quiet. These are great. In conclusion, these are pricey, but you are paying for quality and they deliver it.

title: Noise Cancelation is the best!
text: These headphones are the best, have been using them and they always work. The cancel the noise and let you enjoy the music so much it relaxes you.

title: Perfect headphones

title: Light weight, effective and amazing sound quality!
text: I have been using my Bose QC 35's for over a year now, and am just happy with this product! Even after a year, there is nothing as amazing as these headphones on the market. The battery life, sound quality, build and product design are all absolutely perfect! The battery charge holds up really well. I frequently travel to the UK and I typically use headphones only for the duration of the flight. I put on some music and go off to sleep. I usually charge these after 4 return trips (even then, I tend to have close to 30% battery power). Sound quality is absolutely fantastic and noise cancellation is superb. They are also extremely light weight.

title: Very Good Headphones but Disappointed a bit with Noise Cancelling
text: These are a very solid pair of headphones but the noise cancelling is slightly disappointing, at least in my opinion. I had never owned a pair of Bose before and expected to not be able to hear conversations around the office. Unfortunately that was not the case unless I turned my music to a very loud level, which obviously isn't an ideal solution. The battery life is incredible and the device does a good job of reminding you have much juice you have left every time you turn the headphones on. It's sometimes annoying because it also alerts you to when you have lost or paired with a device but overall I appreciate the reminder of how much battery I have left before I need to recharge. The best part of this product is that app that comes with it and allows for you to easily switch between two devices. I find myself in the app all the time switching between computers and other devices.

title: Great Headphones
text: Sound quality was better than I expected. I looked at the B&O highest end product but was unwilling to spend another $150 for what I perceived was similar sound. Product quality is very good. Battery life is very long. One issue with the case is that the 2 cords included (one to charge the headphones and another to use when power dies, have no place to go in the included carrying case. Also the included charging cord is too short to really be used anywhere. It's about 6 inches long or less. Important: It has just been announced via class action lawsuit that the Bose app to pair the headphones with your apple device has been sending private monitoring data about you and the music you listen to to Bose which they have been selling. Headphones will work fine without the app or only open it when you need to download a firmware upgrade. There should be no other reason to use it. Otherwise, I really am enjoying the product. It's great on plane trips and also works well mat home. I will say that the noise cancelling will not work well when the plane is landing, because the rumbling is not sound cancelled well and the noise canceling processor just duplicates the loud rumbling. Not really a big deal since it ends rather quickly. I would not use this during exercising. These are good for stationary use or light walking.

title: It's awesome!
text: If I can give this product a 6 star, I would. It's awesome!

title: Almost Perfect
text: Pros: - Noise cancellation (ANC). In my first 3 weeks of ownership, I've used these things in a variety of settings and they continue to surprise me. From a noisy warehouse floor, to airplanes, to noisy hotel room A/C units, to even mowing the lawn, these things do an exceptional job of filtering out the droning noises you don't want to hear without totally blocking out noises, alarms, and other things you may want to hear. The best part about them is that you can listen to your music at a comfortable level because the headphones block out the surrounding noise so well - Comfort. If you've never tried a set, find your nearest Bose outlet store and put a pair on your head. You'll be blown away. I've worn these on and off throughout a long day filled with work and travel, and my head never got tired of them - Weight. Despite the fact that these are wireless ANC headphones (consider the amount of circuitry, batteries, radios, microphones, etc, that that implies) these are still considerably lighter than my Sennheiser HD280s (and more comfortable too) - Style. Let's face it, these are a great looking set of cans. The controls are very sleek and intuitive also, and there was virtually zero learning curve to get comfortable with them. - Battery Life. These things handle 10 hours (if not more) of continuous use without breaking a sweat. Cons: - No aptX. If you're an audiophile (or just someone who appreciates hi-fidelity sound), you will notice a subtle quality loss from 320kbps MP3. That said, these still sound great over wireless Bluetooth audio. The quality loss is not nearly as noticible as it is in my 2012 Infiniti M37x, so I've trained myself to ignore it. However, if you're really picky about sound and have a sensitive ear, you may opt to use the supplied audio cable while listening to your collection of FLACs Other comments: - I've always been a bit skeptical of Bose's quality-to-price ratio but they really hit the nail on the head with these. I've only owned them for a few weeks now and they have already been worth every penny, and I get excited when I think about all the ways I'm going to be able to use these in the coming years

title: Best Wireless/NC headphones on the market... period... worth every penny. I would have paid more... :)
text: Short version... if you want the best Noise Cancelling Headphones, that are very comfortable, and offer top notch sound quality... buy these. Let me start the review by saying I am by no means an "audiophile"... I have a moderate setup for my home music listening. I use Sennhesier HD 580s with a Cambridge DacMagic - about a $400 setup in total. I was not expecting a wireless Bose NC headset to compete... but I have to say the sound quality of the Bose is on par with my desktop setup. In short, for the price point the Bose are about as good as HD 580's with a DAC. IMO at least. I travel for a living, so comfort is a key aspect for me. I would say these are again on par with my 580's, and maybe even a slight bit more comfortable. I have a HUGE head, so this is always a area of concern for me, but the QC 35's do a great job of flexing, without putting extra pressure on me. Padding is top quality. Build feels "strong". Now about the NC... my god... I don't know what type of sorcery Bose is conjuring up at their HQ, but the NC is unlike anything I have heard before. It's not natural... I tested this by turning up my white noise machine in my office to max, turned on all the fans, and opened the door to my office to allow my screaming children a chance to contribute to my test.... it was like someone hit a "mute" button to the world. It was one of those moments when you experience a new type of technology that leaves you speechless for a minute. Like seeing 1080P for the first time 10 years ago... I even let my wife try it on, and she literally looked at me and said "I feel like I'm 20 feet underwater", which I guess is the best way to describe it. The only "Con", and it might just be me... whatever they are doing for the NC, makes my ears sometimes feel like I'm changing altitude. Its like a small ear pop to adjust when you're flying. It can be a tiny bit disorientating at first. after about 10 minutes, this sensation went away.

title: Don't Think Twice On This Purchase
text: Honestly the best heaphones I've ever received. I was really into my beats, Solo 2 Wireless to be exact. But I've always ended up having problems with my Beats lasting. Powerbeats 2 Wireless not bending over the ear anymore and now my Solo 2's act up here and there. Leather is now coming off it, and I have only had them for some months, only stationary music recording/ listening usage and some gym. After my girlfriend surprised me with the Bose QC 35's it was a win! I tried the 25's in store but I do not like wired headphones especially on the go. These are very light weight for over ear headphones, not a lie in comfort and the quiet factor is just as good, if not better than the 25's. Compared to the Beats they are much lighter on the ears because of it being over ear I no longer deal with ear ache with pressure of foam against them. And with these headphones being able to connect to two devices, I can easily go from my iMac straight into my iPad Mini 4 without any hastle, reconnecting or lag. An amazing product I'd recommend to anyone getting wireless headphones, noise canclling at that and want to do it right! P.S. Many reviewers really downplay the bass. I can agree it doesnt hit heavy but it doesn't take away. I'm a bass head and have a Nyne Rock ready to knock on some doors at any time but these headphones do a good job on a subtle side. Testing it, I FEEL the bass rather than lose the voice, snares, and all other intricate details to make up for the overwhelming boom.

text: Have been using these for 4 days and probably 20+ hours and went from 70% battery out of the box to 20% finally today. title: Great Job Bose!
text: ABSOLUTELY FABULOUS!!!! I am 75 years of age and have purchased quite a number of Bose products during that time. Many years ago I purchased the first attempt by Bose to produce a background sound suppressor with their headsets. I returned them within a few days due to a background "hiss" sound that detracted from the audio output. Since then I have purchased 6 of their different series headsets, and completely satisfied. However, not one compares to the new Quite Comfort 35 Wireless Headphones. The design is classic Bose as very attractive, comfortable and lightweight. I can't feel any bulkiness or discomfort of any measure. The quality of the sound is FABULOUS, and second to none. I chose the silver ones, and am completely happy with the choice. Expensive...Yes, but totally worth it. My only problem is dealing with my wife's complaints that I can't hear her talking to herself (a trait that has been part of our 51 years of marriage). My only advise is to step up and invest, you will not be disappointed. If you are, you can return them.

title: A couple shortcomings that made me go with another
text: I'll agree with all the good things said in other reviews, mostly. especially regarding the comfort and the quiet! I'll keep it very short and simple: The headphone lacks features. You should be able to control the noise canceling, either to save battery or maybe mix in how much you want to block out or if 100% is too much (many complain about pressure sensation) Also, sound quality is just not that great. If you're coming from some cheap headphones or earbuds under the $20 mark or so, these will be impressive by contrast. I think it's their edge, marketing to that audience with all the demo aisles you see at your Best Buys or Targets. But it's not great! Any reliable headphone over $20 will seriously rival the sound quality you get, which is somehow both lifeless and exaggerated. Lastly, the build feels a bit cheap and delicate. But they are comfortable and the best as far as pure noise cancellation goes. But with no ability to control that in addition to very cheap sound quality in a very premium price point? I looked elsewhere. Trust me. There are headphones in this price range that come close to the noise cancellation and comfort while offering much higher sound quality, which will contribute more to your music listening experience.

title: Updated Review: Don't buy them. Too many problems 14 months after purchasing them.
text: SECOND REVIEW UPDATE: After rewriting my review here on Amazon, I copied my review and went to the Bose website to post it there. I pasted this review there, submitted it and answered the confirming email yet my review was not posted. You decide whether a strange website anomaly occurred or whether it was censored. I now trust Bose less than ever. I have purchased headphones, ear plug phones, speaker systems and more from Bose but I will never buy from them again. I'm an extremely disappoint former customer. IMPORTANT UPDATED FIRST REVIEW: I have been using these headphones for 14 months now and I am finding the quality is not what I expected. There are 3 problems with the headphones 14 months after purchasing them. First: The phones have developed an annoying hiss when connected to any bluetooth devices. If I am listening to something, the hiss is drowned out but if I am simply wearing them to try and block out a noisy environment, all I hear is the annoying hiss. Did I say ANNOYING HISS? Second: The headphones seem to be blocking less and less ambient noise. While using them listening to music or a streaming video, I can now clearly hear conversations in the room. They are muted but I can still hear them. The headphones blocked more ambient noise when initially purchased. Third: The lining of the right ear cup is ripped almost 2 inches. I do not abuse these headphones. Bose wants $35 plus shipping for 2 pieces of foam covered with a thin, easy to rip cover. Ridiculously expensive. NEW CONCLUSION: Don't buy them. They are much too expensive considering the problems developing. Couple that with a battery which cannot be changed, I cannot recommend these headphones. You know the battery will eventually need replacement. Save your money. Do your research. There are many more noise cancelling headphones on the market now. Just don't buy these headphones. ________________________ PREVIOUS COMMENT: I have been a Bose fan for several decades and decided I needed noise cancelling technology. They work and sound great. I bet they filter out 98% of the ambient noise in the room. I even sleep with them on with no music playing so I can have near absolute quiet when falling asleep. They are expensive but well worth it.

title: About what you'd expect for the price
text: When my much more expensive Bluetooth on-ear headphones broke I was a bit frustrated and decided to go back to something cheaper. As expected, this product is less comfortable and clearly uses cheaper materials and construction, but I can't really complain given the price. The sound quality is fine as far as I can tell. The battery life is decent but noticeably shorter than my previous headphones. Also, the low battery warning is a very annoying loud series of beeps that repeats periodically until you charge it. So if you just want to listen for 5 more minutes or get through the last couple of minutes of that video and then charge it, well too bad, because the beeps are going to annoy the **** out of you until you charge it. Also, the pictures in the instructions were not clear to me at all, and it took me a while to find the charging port (you have to tilt one of the earphones to reveal the port which is otherwise hidden behind the headband). Also, unlike my previous headphones, this one does not work well with my tablet's media volume sync (when the headphones are turned on they always revert to a default volume, they don't remember the last volume used), so I had to turn sync off to avoid constantly having to recalibrate the volume of the headset relative to the tablet.

I can see at some point adding a more expensive and better sounding pair. And I'll probably stick with the Harmon/JBL brand. text: I wanted to wait a month before writing this as I know it is easy to write a honest but less meaningful review withing a day of receiving something and I wanted to make sure I actually really do like them first :) I previously had BOSE QC15s for like 8 years that finally quit on me. I do still live bose but I knew the competition has come a long way in recent years and I didnt want to spend top dollar. Also, after owning fancy noise cancelling headphones...It is not as special/important as the companies make it sound. Is it bad, no, does it really make a huge difference, I dont think so at least when you are listening to music anyway. I can see if you fly a lot and dont want music but still want outside noises muted, it does help (it does not eliminate). Anyway, getting back the HDs, they have great sound (I am not an audio snob but I do know a bit). Some people complain about the volume being too low, these do not get as loud as cheap headphones and earbuds but they do get plenty loud. I really love music and if they were louder, it would be hard to hear and appreciate the quality of the sound and all of the different aspects of the music. The volume is only an issue if you just really want to JAM and dont care about quality at the moment (I get that way to at times and want to wreck my ears just for fun too). The battery life is awesome and the pockets for the ears are smaller but after breaking them in for a week or two they really soften up and get comfortable. There are plenty other reviewers that know a lot more about tech audio so Ill leave that for them. Overall these are well worth the money, if you want something fancier get ready to pay the twice the price.

title: Good Cans-Just Don't Fit Me Comfortably
text: I can't stand earbuds!! For the longest time I've been hooking my wired headphones, Sony Studio series, to my home audio system or in my iPhone with an adapter. My old phone died so it was 'upgraded' to a new apple phone, no headphone jack!!! I've been using a BT receiver jacked into my cans since then Not an ideal solution. My wife gave me these Sennheiser's for Christmas. They sound as good as my wired headphones pre-BT receiver. But, unfortunately, I asked my her to send them back. Around ear headphones are NOT a one size fits all solution Ideally the listener's ear should fit comfortably just resting on the padding. After a few weeks of trying every adjustment possible, I can't keep them on for more than 30 minutes. Either one of the earcups gives me an 'ears on fire' feeling or the padding at the top of the headband presses down enough to become annoying. I could probably ask if insurance would cover an ear bob, but I'm too chicken to put up with the pain. So short of plastic surgery on my ears these are, regretfully, going back.

title: Terrific sound, tight fit
text: These Sennheisers have very nice sound balance and soundstage. A bit more bass than an Audio-Technica ATH-M40x and way more bass than the reedy, disappointing Audio-Technica ATH-SR5BT but nowhere near the thump of Beats or Sony Extra Bass cans. These are excellent cans for those looking for balanced, true sound with just a bit of rich bass. Bassheads and woofer-thumpers can move on -- this is NOT your headphone. Great battery life, too. My only two quibbles are build quality and fit. These cans are all plastic and feel a bit flimsy. I guess that's the price you pay for excellent sound at a reasonable price. But I'm worried about the power button, as it already feels sticky after just a week. Lousy design. Finally, as others have noted here, the ear openings on these headphones are tight. If you have large ears, fit might be a problem for these otherwise-excellent over-the-ear headphones.

title: Pretty good for the price but not perfect
text: Sound quality is not comparable to my old Bose QC15s (wired). The sound is not as rich, although it's not bad. They can reproduce deeper bass than I expected but it's just not as full-bodied or satisfying as the Bose. I've only used them with a 2016 Samsung smart TV (KS series) and there is a slight hiss of background white noise while they're connected. Maybe that's a "feature" of all Bluetooth headphones, I'm not sure. Originally they would attach to the TV automatically when powered on but I paired them with my iPad once and now for some reason I have to manually connect them to the TV (in the TV settings) every time I want to use them. Probably fixable but I haven't tried yet. They are not as comfortable to wear as the Bose either. They're on-ear rather than over-ear which leads to sore ears after a while, and the headband presses on the top of my head making me have to shift them around every so often. I can wear the Bose for hours. All that said, I love that they're wireless, the sound quality is still pretty decent overall, they hold a charge for a long time, they seem well made, and for all that they seem to be priced about right.

title: Great sound but ear cup are too small
text: Sound I compared these to several other wireless headphones in the $150 to $200 range including the Sony Wireless, Beats Studio Wireless, and JVC wireless. For my taste, these headphones had the best sound hands down. I listen to everything from rock to hip hop to classical sometimes. I found the Sony and Beats headphones have way too much bass and not enough mid/treble. The JVCs were close; but, two out of three pairs were broken on the store display so I figured they wouldn't hold up. These headphones get plenty loud for my taste. However, I found that they are actually too loud. While at work, on the softest setting, I frequently find myself trying to turn down the volume. The minimum volume is just too loud. Controls The controls are decent. I have a hard time finding the "everything" button that does play/fwd/back. I have to feel around for it a lot of the time. Not a huge deal, but slightly annoying. I paired these with an iPhone 6 and they work great. If you walk away for a while and come back, just hit the multi-function button and they re-pair instantly. Stay away too long and the headphones shut themselves off to preserve battery. Activating Siri is a bit odd though, you have to stop the music, then you can hold to activate Siri. Build Quality Overall these are well built. I assume that they will last for years. The ear cups swivel in two directions so they are pretty comfortable there. Why I Am Returning Them All of that said, the ear cups are just too small; probably by a quarter inch. So either part of my ear is under the ear pad or I play with the thing for a minute until my ear is bent out of shape to fit in the ear cup. I tried these for almost three weeks and realized that every time I put them on, I sit there adjusting them for like 30-60 seconds to get them comfortable. Then after an hour or so I have to adjust them again because my ears hurt. I am also returning them because of the minimum volume issue I noted above.

title: These are hollow sounding, budget friendly, headphones.
text: This set of headphones was a disappointment. I use HD650 for online listening and the HD180 for the television. I purchased this because I upgraded the television to a Samsung Q6F and my ears are getting older from when I originally picked up the listed Sennheiser headsets. My thought process was, my ears are older so I might not notice. That was wrong. The ear cups are too small for my ears and my ears are what I consider to be normal sized ears. After a short while, the edges of my ears began to hurt and the headphones needed to be repositioned. I can use the headphones but in a normal listening position, they're far from comfortable. If the headband wasn't so tight, I'm sure the ear cups would be much more comfortable. This headset has a sort of hollow sound, poor bass and the sound field is very narrow. The HD 4.40 BTs are budget friendly headphones and in my opinion, should be purchased with the above thoughts in mind. My opinion, one is best advised, step up to better. The reception in front of the television is excellent and they're clear sounding in the kitchen. Clear and precise; no added noise. But the overall sound quality is middle grade. If wanting full, quality sound, step up a couple of classes to a $350.00, PXC 550 Wireless headset. If you want budget friendly cans that are echoey, a bit flat with bass that lacks punch with ear cups that are too small and hurt the ears, these will do fine. To all, sorry I can't give a positive review. Good luck with your blue ray, headphone hunt.

title: Long Term Review
text: Bought these at Walmart in the summer of 2019. So going on two and a half years of owning them and using them several times a week if not everyday. I understand that being a more budget based wireless headphone that not everyone will have exactly the same experience... But I have been overwhelmingly pleased. Mine still charge, sound, play, and last as long as they did the day I bought them. I get about 4 hours of constant play time with them before they die and the case will recharge them back to full more than one full charge before it too needs charged. These don't sound quite as good as a nice pair of corded headphones but they sound fine for the price. Especially since they do block out quite a bit of noise. The only con I had with them is the silicone ring that helps keep them in your ear tends to move around and fall off. A drop of super glue two years ago and they haven't moved and it's unnoticeable. These are awesome for working out doing anything active. They get the most play time while I'm riding my motorcycle. They fit under the helmet nicely and block out enough exhaust noise where I can still hear people and cars and traffic but can enjoy long rides without the constant wind and bike noise. Haven't soaked them but they are fine in the rain too. I bought them when they were $50. At $30 now that's a bargain.

title: Anker Q35 - Affordable Excellence
text: I'd been looking for a solid set of wireless around-ear headphones that weren't $300-500 type expensive. I don't do a ton of critical listening. I just wanted some comfortable headphones to have for quiet listening during study/work and occasional air/train travel. These fit that bill. They produce rich sound, excellent noise cancellation, are super comfortable, and have great build Quality. Are they the best in each of those areas? No. But they do all of those things well. If you're into cars, these are like the VW GTI of headphones. Jack of all trades, Master of None, but always better than only Master of One. I've tried Apple's headphones, Bang & Olufsen units, Bose's flagship NC-units, crazy expensive Sennheisers, and even the Aussie Nura units which modulate Soundwaves for your psycho-acoustics. I'd say these are just as comfortable as the Bose units, and the noise canceling is about 80-90% as effective as that of the Bose. The sound quality is similarly a decent 70-80% of the acoustically personalized Nura's. Bottom line: with Amazon Day discounts, you'd be hard-pressed to find a better set of NC-headphones for about $100-120. I heartily recommend them if you're looking for the absolute best bang for your buck. Audiophiles should look elsewhere; but these aren't designed for them either.
