The noise cancellation has 3 stages; normal, transparency (which lets through voices, door sounds, outdoors buses), and Noise cancellation (which suppresses all noise). If you run in normal mode you get the best battery life, 60 hours. The headset has several microphones so you can have clear conversation when paired with your phone. I have been very pleased with my purchase.

title: What a disappointment
text: Q10, 20,30 and now Q35 It is with great dissatisfaction to share my experience! The noise cancelation is virtually non existant, over Skype I have contrary to all previous models a massive negative feedback from all parties involved complaints about loud noise as if I was doing dishes water running fan noise etc. Terrible complaints from regular caller's and also from my side, so many calls not understandable as in digital disconnects. None of the previous models had this kind of negative feedback. Also for some reason the Dual connect on the Q35 auto connects to my Echo rendering my headset useless until I manually disconnect it. This does not happen on any other model?!. Sound in music was fantastic, loved the base drum clarity as if I was next to it. Battery life fantastic also. This is my first ANKER item that I had to send back, well out of 20 some gadgets I guess that's good?

title: Better than the Q20 IMO
text: I really liked the Q20+, but I wear for 6 to 8 hours a day and they get uncomfortable due to the ear cups do not fitting completely around my ears. That, and the headband is tensioned to press the earcups down. When the Q35 went on sale, I decided to give it a try. I like Anker and had no issues with the sound of the Q20. The Q35 solved the ear smash with larger earcups and possibly softer padding. And the sound is great and seems more immersive. Perhaps due to the LDAC my phone supports. Happy I made the switch. The Q20 seems better at noise cancelation however.

title: Best ever head set! Please try it, you will love it.
text: Love it! Bought to wear on planes. I travel alot. Excellent quality, works like a dream.

title: Nice headphones, bad bluetooth
text: I'm very disappointed. I'm a big fan of Anker products and when I researched noise cancelling headphones, I was excited by the Abker offering. Initially, I was very pleased. It had an annoying habit of the Bluetooth cutting out once in a while, but I thought it was just a quirk. However, after a while, it became unbearable. It was very intermittent at first, but then became more frequent and the outages lasted longer and longer. This came to a head on my last business trip. Several calls remained connected, but total silence and I had to keep shutting off Bluetooth to continue the call. Then, during the flight, the app with the background noise cut off and reset every ten minutes or so because there was no internet connection. Of course there was no internet at 30,000 feet. In general, I really liked the sound and the noise cancelling. Putting it into NC mode and activating the sleep sound machine virtually isolated me from the outside. The headphones themselves are comfortable. Unfortunately, the connection issue is just too much to deal with and I had to return them

title: So far so good!
text: Can't speak to durability over time but so far I love them! My first pair of noise canceling headphones bought for travel. Used for a road trip and didn't realize how loud the car noise was until I took the headphones off. The transparent mode wasn't great in the car, let in a lot of the droning tire noise. Transparent mode in the house worked great though. Curious to try on a plane soon, but I don't plan on using transparent mode much anyways, just noise canceling. Sound sounds great to me, I think I have the equalizer on acoustic mode, use it for all music and podcasts and shows. Didn't notice ears getting warm or achey like some headphones do after wearing them a few hours, so that's good as well.

title: Not made to last
text: Sound quality is decent. Noise cancelation pretty good. But if it's quiet, there is a constant electrical hum. They loosened up after a few days of wearing them. The ear pads are too soft and the adjustable head piece is not sturdy. I have a small head and leave them on the smallest adjustment, fit great the first day and a half. But I literally felt when they gave and loosened. Also, if you have gages or decent sized earrings, you have to take them out for them to fit properly. You also can't wear a hat or they don't sit flush on your head which ruins the sound quality and noise cancelation. I wouldn't spend this much money on these again. Which is a shame because the features and the app are pretty nice.

title: Not great for travel...constant video pauses
text: I bought these to replace a perfectly functional pair of Sony MDR-10RNC wired headphones that have been my trusty travel companion for many years. While the Sony headphones weren't the best dynamically, they were great for noise cancellation on commercial air travel. However, I bought a new iPad that no longer comes with a 3.5mm jack so I figured it was time to go wireless. After reading the reviews on these, I figured I would give them a go. I took them on a business trip that had me on 4 flights and also took them on a cruise vacation to watch some downloaded content when I was awake but didn't want to disturb my wife. While the noise cancellation is good, and the transparency mode is nice to have, the challenge with these is the auto-pause functionality. To say it was an annoyance is an understatement. Hit some turbulence? PAUSE. Look up from the screen for any reason? PAUSE. Flying in late spring through the Appalachians has some turbulence to be expected...these things would cause the video to pause every 2-3 seconds. I was thinking, there has to be a setting to turn off this functionality in the app...NOPE. Another thing is the touch sensitivity on the side of the headphones to switch modes, if your shoulder or arm comes in contact with the right side of the headset, the modes will switch. Sound quality - its OK. Not bad, not great. Lacking bass but clarity is good. Volume levels are fine to allow you to hear clearly on a commercial jet. But, they went back after my two weeks with them. The challenges I experienced were too much to live with. I instead opted for the Sony WH-1000XM4 which were on sale when I set-up the return for these. Yes, the Sony earphones are more than double...but the quality and functionality is better and more in line with my use needs.

title: High End Performance, Great Value, Big Upgrade
text: Great Active NC. Have you ever moved to a city where everytime you step out on your balcony, it sounds like you are standing on a highway overpass? This pair solves the noise instantly. Amazing and so superior to my aging high end pair.

title: Very impressed!
text: Very impressed! Soundcore has done it again. They sound great, look great, have great battery life, easy to pair, and a very nice case to boot. Very happy.

title: Good enough to sleep under a jet engine
text: I work on an aircraft carrier, and my bed is directly under the fighter jets as they warm up and take off. I’ve measured the sound levels at 103 decibels. No headphones on earth are going to block that out, but these made it bearable. Sound quality is fine, just fine. They’re not audiophile grade, but they are better than the ear buds I work out with. Features are pretty good (especially via the app). No regrets.

title: Super Impressed
text: I had an earlier version of the Soundcore by Anker Life Q30. This model is so much better. Very similar to the Q30, but tweaked to have better sound, noise cancellation, as well as comfort. Even the carry case has been improved. Update: I have a nice surround sound system costing many $k and I prefer to watch movies using these headphones over that. Such clarity and booming bass.

title: Anker headphones
text: These were a gift to myself and I haven't had a chance to use them yet. I dont believe in spending hundreds of dollars on a decent pair of noise cancelling headphones and I think these Anker Soundcores will do the job.

title: Not worth the price, on sale? Sure.
text: These headphones for 130 bucks left me disappointed. The ANC (active noise cancellation) was worse than their Q30 counterpart. The ear cups are made the same way and started to fall apart like the Q30s. They are less comfortable than the Q30s. I had weird audio stutter with Spotify on these headphones but it occurred with other headphones too so your mileage may vary. Sound quality and battery life were the best qualities. ANC effectiveness and comfort were the worse.

title: Life Q35
text: I bought these to replace an uncomfortable and lackluster pair of wired "gaming" headphones from a company I had high respect for. Comparatively speaking, audio quality is amazing for music and light/mmo gaming. I don't play FPS, so I can't comment on that. I didn't notice any audio lag from my PC, even when dual-paired between my phone and PC. There was a bit of audio lag when playing a mobile game, but switching from LDAC to AAC in the Bluetooth settings cleared that up. App has amazing EQ customization and the LDAC takes advantage of it. I'm still working through the break-in period, so I can only expect them to get better. ANC is nice, but I feel like the Life Pro 2 earbuds do it better. Definitely not to the level of a good/expensive set of Sony or Bose, but you get what you pay for. It will be sufficient for home-office working (I can't hear fans/PC/dog with ANC on and music playing) or traveling. A really neat feature is the customizable white-noise system in the app. I had it set to sound like a stormy night at the beach. Had some good memories come back. :) So far, for the price, these are excellent Bluetooth cans. I'm very satisfied and happy with them. That being said, if you're not concerned with having LDAC or a few other features, the Life Q30 is almost half the price. Definitely compare the two. Personally, I felt the features justified the price.

title: They're probably okay if you just want to use them while listening to music on your phone
text: I bought these to replace a Plantronics BackBeat Pro 2 set that i thought had died (it had not) and I was not happy with them. - The range is terrible. Not even 30 feet with clear line of site and I had audio dropouts and artifacts. - The battery life when not in use is not good. My Plantronics will last for a weeks if I'm not using them even if they're turned onn (they go into standby mode). These die after a couple of days. - The dual device functionality is very glitchy. I had them connected to 2 PCs and while watching videos they will randomly switch control to the other PC that's doing nothing, and never give it back. Sometimes they just wouldn't pair voice, sometimes they would just never let one of the PCs play audio. - Audio latency is really bad. I don't believe these support any Apt-X low latency codecs, so watching videos or movies is painful. - They would randomly paus whatever content I was watching, I think this was bad on-ear detection? - Not very comfortable compared to the plantronics. Now they're not all bad. The audio quality is definitely pretty good. The call quality was good enough. So if you're just using them to make phone calls and listen to music on one device while your phone is in your pocket, and you don't mind charging them all the time when they're not in use, they're okay, but I think you could probably do better at this price.

title: So Happy with These
text: I spent months trying to find the perfect set of headphones. I wanted quality, affordability, AND style. I’m glad I went with these! The battery lasts forever, the sound is so good, and I get tons of compliments.

title: Q35 headphones
text: Update*** I've had these for 3 months now and they've started to auto pause every 1 to 5 minutes. I've done some troubleshooting and unable to fix it. I attempted to replace these through the warranty but this Soundcore by Anker Life Q35 Multi Mode model is not found on the companies website in order to open a warranty exchange. This is disappointing. **** These headphones are exactly what I was looking for. I especially like the idea of the auto pause function since my kids are constantly interrupting me. The sound is excellent. Clear and crisp. Definitely would say "silky". I like that you can do a hand over to change from NC to transparency, or to normal. I also like to prompt Google, but that feature doesn't always work. It takes some getting use to for the pause and volume control. I am disappointed in the auto pause function because it only works maybe 30% of the time. It was what I was most excited about and what ultimately convinced me to go with these. All and all I would say these have the potential to be great. Really great -if only the functions were consistent.

title: Amazing! Although auto-pause is not working well.
text: I like it very much. The sound is surprisingly awesome! It's comfortable. I like almost every feature of it. Except when it's supposed to auto-pause playing music, most of the time it doesn't work, for example, I am listening to music, then, someone is talking to me, I can't hear him, so I take off the headphones, at that time, according to the manual, it should pause playing music but it continues playing it. Anker, can you help me with this issue?

title: Why doesn’t all features work?
text: I hope the manufacturer contacts me. I have iPhone 11 and just bought Q35 and trying it out now. The wear detection doesn’t work - when I take the headphones off my head, it doesn’t shut down. Also cannot connect to two Bluetooth devices at the same time, so forget about switching between two devices. Everything else seems fine. Will give further update once Anker answers me.

title: Great for the money
text: I will not go crazy and spend a lot of money for a headset that may sound a little better. These sound great to me and they are not overly expensive.

title: Great sound and comfort - bluetooth issues
text: The headphones fit well and are very comfortable and not too heavy. Can use for long periods of time without squishing my ears. I have a larger head. Sound is great, might be a bit high on the bass but can adjust that in the equalizer. I like lots of bass. Very high quality for this price point. The bluetooth multicast seems to be messed up. Maybe it is in general. I had an Audio Techca before this that had issues so I sent it back. With the Q35 listed, I have had issues with: 1. The volume buttons on the headphones was the only way you could adjust the level until I rebooted my phone. SamSung A52 newer phone. 2. The my phone won't pair with the headphones sometimes. I had to power cycle the headphones and then they paired. The button design is horrible. Controls are poor. The NCF button is HUGE and the power button is small. Have to hold 3/5 seconds power button to do most things. Why not add a Off button. I couldn't figure out how to skip a song, only to pause music. I am not sure I will keep or not, the sound is so good and these other issues are likely that bluetooth is just really bad, especially multicast. Want I want is rather simple it to cycle through 4 different devices. 2 computers and 2 phones. I only really need one device active at once, but I have to turn off blue tooth on all the devices that I don't want to connect to the headphone except the one I currently want to use. Otherwise if a different one connects first, I get locked out. Ok, current bluetooth issue is that I am on my A52 Samsung phone and also connected via Windows 10. Sometimes it works to switch between me playing music on my phone and being on teams in windows 10. Other times, it says I am connected on Windows 10 but I can hear anything. The same is true just being connected on A52 samsung phone. I have the soundcore app installed on my phone. I really don't want to send them back as the sound is so good but it's heading that way now. I am usually fiddling a few minutes to fix it everyday or talking to myself.

title: It’s good product, but ?!
text: I need more time to make a review, but in the first look , i think it’s perfect It’s good product, but it’s not have good mic in open areas, so I’m not satisfied with this product

title: Annoying as heck volume control
text: These headphones will completely disable the sound control of you phone. Even if your phone set to the lowest volume possible, the volume will be blasting at the loudest possible based on the headphone volume level. Not as big a deal, but why put the put the power indicator light right next to the power button? That's the one button you want to push and still see the light indicator at the same time (to see if it is turned on or off). With the button less then 1/4 inch from the light, I have to hold the headsate at a weird and uncomfortable angle to still see the light when powering off or on.

title: Fine for price range
text: I purchased these solely for use when traveling and on airplanes. The only thing that really matters to me is the noise cancellation and it was below par. It was helpful with the fuzzy/turbulent airplane noises but that was it. I did not help with other sounds or voices at all. I actually tried to ask someone a few rows away to speak more softly because I could still hear them clearly with the volume up and noise cancelling on. I also purchased Beats Studio3s and the Anker Soundcore Q30s. Each of the three models were marginally better than the last (as the price went up) but none were worth keeping. I recently used my husband’s Sony headphones and I’ve finally accepted that only Sony or Bose will have good noise cancellation and nothing under $300 is going to really very well for what I am looking for.

title: Great value!
text: Battery status notification needs improvement Sound quality is good. Noise cancellation is indiscernible. Great fit on my head! Super satisfied overall.

title: Meh! Unimpressive considering the price point
text: I own a pair of the Q20 headphones - which I have given to my daughter for her to use. The Q20 headphones are a perfect balance of price and quality. Based on my previous experience with SoundCore, I thought I'd give these Q35s a try. Bottom Line on Top: Meh! I have used the Q35s for about two weeks now and I have to say that I will be returning them to Amazon because there are simply better options available at this price point. At this price point (about 100 bucks) the Q35 begins to compete with mid-to-higher-end alternatives which might offer a better value and audio experience. For my grades below, I set the EQ to flat and turned off the noise-canceling features. Music Playback = B. Decent midrange to high range. The sound is clear and articulate enough, but the bass is a bit muddy. Phone calls or video calls = B. Call audio is not a strength. The sound is tinny and weak. Built-in mic for calls = B. Pretty clear mic audio pick-up. Pure Noise Canceling = B. Noise isolation and reduction are fairly good and effective at canceling out mid-to-high frequency background noise. The ANC mode also provides a very pleasant white noise. Noise Canceling with music playback = C+/B-. Not good. The audio is muffled and muted as you would expect. Phone App = Very basic control but easier to use than the onboard controls built into the headphone Battery Life = A. Charged it once and it has been going for a week. Wear detection function = It works but it is a bit glitchy. Yes, if you take the headphones off the audio will stop, the problem is that if you move your head too much (i.e. get up from a chair) it will also turn off the music. Comfort and fit = B. The synthetic leather feels a bit cheap and not as comfortable as I would expect. The headband fits fine. Bottom line. Save your money and go with the Q20s or spend a few bucks more for a better set of headphones. Simply put, the Q35 is not worth the extra money and at this price point, there are too many better alternatives. I am sending this back to Amazon today. Best wishes!

title: Great song, bass only OK. (For me.)
text: I was disappointed in these. The sound was very good, but it didn't meet a standard that I had in mind. Two things were missing, 1. Staging. The sound didn't seem to fill the the area around me with my eyes closed. 2. Bass wasn't nearly as predominant as I like my lows to be. I can see these phones being very acceptable for a lot of people. But when I spend the money and want to exercise, chill, listen to a podcast, I want the sound that I'm looking for, and these just didn't do it.

title: Good Value, Decent Sound
text: First of all, I like these headphones. I like that they were cheaper than competitors. I am enjoying them. All of these reviews are talking about the equalizer feature in the app being neccessary. Yup. True. The default settings are bad. Even my untrained ear can hear that. The other settings can make the sound good. It is annoying to have to use the equalizer in order for it to sound decent. One time I turned off my phone, and the speakers, and when I turned it back on, the equalizer settings had defaulted back to the signature sound. I don't want to have to keep changing / checking the equalizer settings to make it sound decent. If I want to listen to something on another device, I don't want to have to have my cell phone to double check these settings. It is awkward. The noise canceling is not as good as I have been used to with bose, but it is ok. My audiophile wife had some interesting reactions to listening to these headphones. The most unique thing she said was that the soundstage was different than anything she had ever heard, in a bad way. She listened to The Planets (Mars), and said that it sounded like she was at the front of the stage, facing the audience. She had this really weird confused/disgusted look on her face while she was listening. She tried "Staying Alive" by the bee gees, and said it was the same feeling. I was confused about which equalizer setting to choose (I hate choices), but I could tell that some sounded good, and some sounded bad. But it was hard for me to choose which one sounded "best". My wife's ear liked the "Classical" equalizer setting for both of the songs she played. So I am happy I got these, and I am going to enjoy them. Good luck with your decision to find a good pair of headphones!

title: SWEET DEAL!
text: Today I must say this item arrived in good working order, the box was sealed in cellophane and worked perfectly.

title: Great headphones with one problem.
text: Great sound and excellent noise cancellation, and love the fit can wear for hours with no discomfort. The one negative is the ear covers are already breaking down after only two months of use. Other than this one thing it would definitely be a five star product.

title: Great sound quality but too much bass
text: The overall build quality and sound quality of the headphones is worth the price in my estimation, especially if you are using a Bluetooth connection capable of the high quality LDAC codec and really enjoy bass heavy headphones. My only gripe is that the lower frequencies and especially the sub bass is higher than I would like. The EQ in the app does not allow you to properly adjust sub bass frequencies which can lead to some unbalanced audio in my experience.

title: Right Out of the Box Awesome
text: I bought these to replace my (still working) Q30 headphones. I didn't jump to 45 because I saw a review saying these were better so let's pay less for better quality, I said... Will be back to update later.

title: (Updated) Do not recommend
text: *Updated December 2022* Still using these despite the issues, but now I cannot because the plastic snapped - I was literally just picking them up and they broke. To say I'm displeased and disappointed is an understatement because I used these for sensory and sleep issues. *Updated October 2022* A few months ago I reached out to company support about my issues, and they had me mail mine back and sent me a new pair that are arguably worse. I followed up with them and they just wanted me to send them back and they would refund me partially so I could buy another pair... Uh no thank you. I am pretty disappointed. I still use them everyday because I can't sleep at night without the noise cancelation, but the odd noises in the right ear piece can be really frustrating to someone who has sensory issues and uses these for said sensory issues. I definitely wish I would have gone with a different brand, but it is what it is. I wish I could find an easier solution to finding noise canceling headphones for sleep and comfort. (Original) So I got these back in April, super impressed initially, until I started hearing weird noises in the right speaker and it also seemed like the noise cancellation was not as good. I did all the troubleshooting to reset and try different devices and all that good stuff, but nothing has helped. I contacted support when it started to happen, but decided to give it a chance to see if it'll resolve and it hasn't. I am not sure what else can be done at this point and if anything changes I'll update this review. The noise cancellation is pretty decent. I like the different modes as well as the features these headphones offer. They do lack comfort as far as around my ears go and that's disappointing. I bought this brand because I have a great pair of Bluetooth Anker earbuds, but earbuds really irritate the inside of my ear and I have been trying to find literally anything that is more comfortable. My ideal headphones would have max comfort around the ears, excellent noise cancellation and sound quality. I was hoping these would be it. I took the chance on these having read reviews of some having issues and here I am.

title: No problems! This is for the Q 35 model, not the Q 30
text: I mainly use them for watching TV at night without bothering anyone. I have had problems with other brands I like these so much I’ve bought another pair. Feel great, sounds great. Good price. I like that if you have to pause your show, all you do is take the headphones off and they will wait happily for you to return.

title: My kid barely takes these off
text: My kid has had these for a few months or so. Has not once had an issue. He takes them everywhere. Hardly ever takes them off. Sturdy.

title: Great
text: Great audio quality, and a functioning equalizer app. Works with mobile and desktop devices I own. Wish the sound was a dial instead of buttons, the buttons are easy to forget which is which when wearing. Sound quality is great. Noise cancellation is similar to the bose products I have previously owned. More features and buttons than I need, but maybe other people need them.

title: Amazing quality sound delivery, easy to connect easy to use
text: I bought these to replace a pair of Q30s that eventually broke due to my rough handling of them. The model up was worth the little bit extra I paid. I use these for work and personal use and the noise cancelation is top tier, the pass-through is just as good, even the 3mm plug/cable is a step up from the previous model. Sure you don't have the fancy name brand but it makes up for it in the quality being superb. I'm no audiophile, but I like my music, TV, and audio books like anyone else, and honestly wouldn't go with another brand.

title: It's ok
text: First the good. The headset looks good and are comfortable. If you are setting at home they sound really good. I have a soundcore speaker at home and I love the sound and quality of that unit so I thought I would try these. My new phone does not have a 3.5mm jack so I bought these to replace my old Bose headphones. This was not a wise decision. The noise canceling does not work very well at all. I guess I expected to much but these will not cancel the sounds in an airplane. It does reduce it some but even with music playing you hear the roar of the plane engines over the music. I am going to keep them to use around the house because I don't want to go through the hassle of returning them. But if you are looking to use these for traveling save your money and buy the Sony or Bose.

title: Great product
text: I have bought 4 items from this company 3 typed of ear buds and a pair of bluetooth glasses and the sound and quality is top notch but affordable prices will buy more items from them in future.

title: Excellent sound and easy to pair up
text: As a tech illiterate, I was worried about using these. But they were easy to pair with my device. They are comfortable, the sound is excellent and the freedom is great. Very glad I purchased these.

title: Just as good as my APPLE AirPods just less$$$$$
text: I love Podcasts and listening to audible books. I could not find my Apple AirPods and I really wanted to continue listening to all of my stuff. I bought this pair and I could not be more pleased!!!! I am totally blown away by how good they sound. I cannot tell the difference between my $250 AirPods and this $40 pair. The battery life is really good. I have since found my AirPods but I am still using my Anker earphones. I just love my new mint green Anker pods.

title: Custom fit
text: These are great...having custom silicone ear pieces is a added bonus.

title: Hurry Up n BUY!!!
text: Excellent product!!! In comparison at this price point, everything with regards to this product is excellent.! Im so impressed by it that i purchase a pink one for my wife and she loves them!

title: First wireless earbuds
text: I didn't know what to expect from wireless earbuds but i think this pair did fine. sound quality is good, noise cancellation is great. There are different size silicone earbuds to fit ears, I went a size down for a good snug fit. The Bluetooth connection is flawless so far, android phone, kindle, pc, they all hook up without issue. So far, I think I got a great bargain with these quality earbuds.

title: Excellent earbuds for the price. Super light and comfortable.
text: I seem to have trouble finding a good fit for my ears and I found these to be fantastic for me. They’re surprisingly light and don’t give my ears any sort of fatigue. The case isn’t huge but it isn’t small. When using a single bud, audio doesn’t seem to automatically switch to mono on my iPhone, unlike some other earbuds I’ve used. Luckily, I have a shortcut to quickly toggle mono audio. Besides this, the sound is great, decently loud with minimal distortion. Well worth the price point if you’re not interested in higher end buds. I can definitely recommend these.

title: Incredible for the money
text: Got these for my wife as she tends to lose or break earbuds. After another Anker purchase, I trusted these would be good. Nope, they are great. They have the tiniest case I've seen, sound incredible, are comfortable and handle calls very well. Would definitely recommend even if you don't lose or break earbuds often.

title: Not as good as the Curve line.
text: Used to get a couple Curves for when I was skiing. I miss the connected earbuds to help prevent losing them, but also missed what I felt was superior sound quality to these. Unfortunately they didn't last longer than a year either, both pairs. Maybe constant cold and wet weather was too much. Also unfortunately, looks like the line was discontinued. I got these expecting at least the same bass reproduction etc(I felt with the right fit, they sounded better than Airpods), since they were a similar price point to these, but I guess Anker felt that they needed to distinguish their higher priced ones more so made their budget ones noticeably worse, a shame.

title: It is not an Airpods but it is also hard to beat at this price point
text: Everything is decent but nothing is great. It is not an Airpods but at this price it is a very good deal.

title: Great pair of earbuds
text: Sound quality is excellent. They link right away. The battery life so far is really good. Definitely a great purchase.

title: Good quality
text: Anker product are amazing, I love anger, perfect for talking

title: Uncomfortable
text: These things feel like expandable earplugs, filling my ears to capacity and then popping out every time I move wrong. Tried every size of the earbud tips that came with and they still won’t stay, had one earbud fall out three times during the same song. Sound intermittently stops working in the right earbud, causing the stereo sound to flicker. Every time I take them out of my ears, they come unpaired with each other, requiring a restart. title: Great little buds

The price is great and the sound quality is really as good as any I have ever heard; but at a price that doesn’t hurt. Give ‘em a go!

title: Underwhelmed. Returning. Buy anything Mpow instead.
text: I have a lot of Anker accessories that I like, but having lost another Mpow M9 set at work and not finding them on Prime, grabbed these for a long drive I had to make today. I didn't listen very long. All of the negative reviews were accurate for me; they weren't as comfortable, they never felt as secure, they didn't sound as good, they were harder to handle (I have big, currently very dry fingers), more expensive... I started a return and bought some Mpow Mbits on the auction site for a good bit less. I would recommend similar actions, but If you don't have a big stupid head, and a different ear, this might be just fine. The case is impressively compact and it's a nice looking design, just too small for my head and fingers.

title: These things are great!
text: To be honest, this is my first pair of earbuds. I wanted them to use with my iphone, and I am glad I picked these. They are packaged in a nice charging container (charge by USB), and charge up quickly. The sound quality seems excellent to me, but I am not an expert in sound. For typical use, I highly recommend these!

title: Not happy overall

title: For the price this is a DEEEAL!!!
text: I got these for my boyfriend because they’re extremely affordable and replaceable if he loses or steps on them! My only beef is that you have to carry the case around instead of being able to put it in a silicone carrying case like AirPods, but less than a fifth of AirPods, he can certainly deal with it! I also like that there are different color options and different sized ear speaker pieces- a nice touch! Anker makes good stuff at affordable prices, can’t knock rhem

title: Should have listened, these things are crap

I tried all the instructions with repairing, in / out of the case, reset etc none of it works. The sound is ok, the bass is definitely better than anything else i have tried. title: Touch controls are garabge
text: Buy the button control version. The touch controls on these work about once out of every ten times. Extremely frustrating to the point I won't bother with them at work where I may have to pause to hear someone.

title: Good quality. One small annoyance...
text: It was frustrating trying to open the case for the first time, as the back hinge looks (to me) like it's where you're supposed to open it. I spent a stupid amount of time trying to open it from the back, and now the case has a couple small defects from me trying to pry it open with a tool. At least I accidentally figured out it was the back and not the front before I damaged it permanently. I feel like it should be a little better marked or easy to see somehow. Day 1 of use, I'm happy with these. The variety of earbud sizes to choose from make it easy to find some that are comfortable for my ears. I like being able to just use one earbud if I want to. So far, so good.

title: Impressive For The Price
text: For the price range this brand of earbuds is the best I have tried so far. I won a pair from the same brand that were a bit more expensive then these. Loved them but lost them. So I purchased this pair. The battery life is terrific. I have used them most of the day, fallen asleep with them in, and still used them most of the next day before having to charge them. The sound is good and I haven't noticed background noise as I use them. The sound can be turned up to be pretty loud, which isn't the case with many cheaper earbuds. I have had a few pairs around the same price previously and the quality didn't come close the these. I have dropped them multiple times and they are still going strong. They charge pretty quickly. Overall very impressed with these earbuds considering how cheap they were. I will be purchasing this brand in the future.

title: 1Star is too high a rating
text: This is the 4th sound core Bluetooth product I have purchased. To date, I have been unable to get ANY of the 4 to work for more than a very short time, if at all. And now I find out that my return window for the earbuds expired a few weeks ago. Anker should stick to the wires and connecting cords.

title: Hang up button
text: It's annoying trying to use the touch function on it... if I want to hang up or pause a video I have to tap the earbuds MULTIPLE TIMES😭 IT GEST ANNOYING! Plus sometimes if I have it outta the. Ox for too long it will disconnect me ....returning

title: Decent
text: Got these after the earbuds I'd been using at the gym crapped out on me. After reading reviews of these and the regular version, I opted for the "mini" ones because some people had commented about not wanting super long stems. After actually getting a look at these, I might have rather had the longer stems, but I think they'll end up being fine. Sound quality is decent—I can't speak much for battery life since I haven't used them very long, but if they're anything like my others, they should last a while if I'm only using them for a couple of hours a day and let them rest in their case. I like that there are indicator lights showing how much of a charge remains; another pair I've had didn't have that. Possibly my biggest gripe is that there's no real indication the earbuds are on. The instructions that came with them says they turn on automatically when the case is opened, but there doesn't seem to be any sort of indicator light. Other pairs I've had even have a voice that says "power on" and "connected" after you put them in. With these I just have to stick them in my ears and check my Bluetooth settings to be sure.

title: YOu get what you pay for
text: I use these when I paint and if I am farther than 15' from the computer, the sound goes away or is broken up.. Finally, I use them about once a week for about 1.5- 2 hours and they never go dead. The last draw was when one of the earbuds went dead and I couldn't get it to work. It was time for a switch. I may have been expecting more and was disappointed when they didn't perform.

title: Great ear buds
text: Love these earbuds. They last all day. Around 9 hours before needing to recharge. If I put both of them in for added concentration they do pretty well at blocking out other noise. They fit well in my ears and don't fall out.

title: My friend loves it
text: I sent it as a graduation gift for my friend and he loves it! The noise cancellation is so good and the sound quality is amazing.

title: Love these
text: They stick in your ear well. I have exercises with them in and they never fell out. One con I have with them is if you put your phone in your pants or jacket pocket it becomes scrambley. The other con is people say sounds in the background are very load even when you select the option to reduce background noise. Even with that I think they are worth buying.

title: Husband Loves Them
text: Hubby loves them and thinks they're fantastic. Grreat sound and quality. FYI- he let me use them or was going to, but I couldn't. My ears are smaller and they were too big to fit. If you tend to have small ears, you may want to try some out before buying. I have no problem with galaxy buds+ if I use the small tips.

title: Loud and Clear
text: These earbuds were a gift to my sister, and she just can’t stop talking about how good they are in canceling out background noise, and how clear the sound is when they are in use. They are worth the cost.

title: finicky and hurty
text: I bought mine direct from Samsung and ultimately returned them. I found that I had to fiddle with them constantly to hit the sweet spot for the music to sound like it should instead of like I was listening through a tin can, and while fiddling with them the touch controls become an annoying hassle because you are trying to get the fit right and the music is turning on and off and pausing and skipping, etc, because you are touching them. The buds can't seem to differentiate at all between an actual hold/grip to manipulate them in your ears, and a tap as you would do to actually use a touch control feature. Don't quote me on this because it's not like I counted every review that appeared male vs female, but I found that they hurt and I think it might be because they were designed by somewhat larger-eared males. I originally assumed the hurty issue was likely because they were designed by some 60 year old man engineer with huge ears (because ears grow our whole lives) and so they were only made to fit kind of older larger ears. I even wrote on my Samsung review that they should have made the fit for the age group of their customer. But now, reading these Amazon reviews, I am noticing that the people saying they fit great seem to mostly be male names and those saying they hurt seem to mostly be female-normative names, so I still think they were designed for larger ears, but maybe for males they will fit better - I truly don't know how different in size male vs female ears are though; it's just a random observation of these reviews of hurt vs feel great. Bottom line, they hurt my ears and were too picky about being perfectly aligned in my ear. On the rare occasion I hit that sweet spot they sounded great and never felt like they were going to fall out. Too bad it took so much effort to find that spot.

title: Look nice, but not comfortable.
text: I am still trying to figure out all of the functions for these earbuds, since it is all about how you touch or tap them. I end up just using the phone to control them since they don't react very well except for start and stop of audio. These buds look pretty sleek which is one reason I got them, and live up to the claims for sound and battery life. But they are not comfortable, and they take turns falling out of my ears when I am talking which is very annoying. And yes, I have them in the correct ears (L/R). Also, having to take them out and put them back in the case when I am not using them is inconvenient. I am going to return them and purchase my usual bluetooth headset, because at least I know they won't fall off and get lost. I paid WAY too much money for these to keep taking that risk, and to also be uncomfortable.

title: Light weight and quite accurate to the recorded sound
text: I'll start with the dislikes. They are a bit difficult to get a good fit in the ear canals. I've dropped them on the floor and it took sometime to find it. On the likes side, I love the long battery life as my old ones needed to be charged up on Thursday and Sunday. Sound is very engaging and true to what it sounds like on my $25K home system.

title: Still trying to Love these
text: If you place these just right in your ear AND you figure out on you tube how to increase the volume...There's not a better pair of ear buds other (in my opinion). The issue lies within the fit. There's no margin for error. You get a small and a large rubber ear piece attachment that are SUPPOSED to make the buds fit the anatomy of your ear. Problem...not everyone has the same shaped ears!!! Now, I would consider my ears as "average" for an adult male. Still, I cannot seem to keep these in the "sweet spot!" If I turn my head, oops, on move slightly and the sound isn't as good. I yawn, oops, the both pop out of place. I'm hoping I'll ultimately find a fix. I see these little rubber covings that are supposed to go over the part that sticks in your ear...I don't know. I might try those. Kind of expensive if you don't absolutely love them.

title: Good sound

I always seem to hit my ear. I like how the case will charge the buds without being plugged into power. Holding its own charge is a plus.

title: Works great!

text: The ear buds are quite unique in shape & size. Strong & smooth they easily slide into place & stay despite activities. And when you use the noise cancelation feature it drastically reduces battery life. Otherwise, battery life is excellent. I would recommend the ear buds only at a reduced price.

title: Don't expect it to charge unless you mess with it forever
text: Charging absolutely sucks on these. You have to wiggle it around forever to get it in a spot where it'll actually charge with the case open or find something heavy to sit on the case and keep it closed tight enough to charge, on top of making sure it's in the right spot to charge. Worst piece of junk charging solution samsung ever came up with, especially when they have wireless charging. Update: putting a little folded piece of paper or something where the bottom of the buds rest so they lay more flat instead of at an angle seems to work best. If I don't have any problems this way, I'll fix the charging case to make it a more permanent solution.

When I click to install it on my Samsung watch, it sits in “installing soon” mode. As far as battery life - long lasting battery is a joke. The battery MAYBE lasts 4 hours max. I use my phone for work for at least 8 hours a day. Don’t waste your money - you’ll end up sending them back too!

title: Fantastic sound, mediocre noise cancellation
text: I prefer these over my buds plus (lost one of them and thusly needed something else :( ) sound-wise. Everything else? Eh. Certainly a great earbud, especially if you get a sale, just in comparison to my previous Samsung buds, the only improvement I really feel is the sound quality. Everything else is take or leave. Some people find it more comfortable to wear than other earbuds, some don't. The buds plus offered perfect sound reduction because it worked similar to ear plugs. these beans are great for if you don't need or want to block out all sounds. the ANC will reduce things like electric hums and similar background noise, but not talking or loud things, due to the open design. I prefer blocking out noises, but they're still better sound quality than my buds plus, so instead of buying a single bud replacement on ebay (which I'm still disgruntled that Samsung doesn't offer bud replacements, I had my buds for only a few months, I was devastated), I've kept my shiny beans and I enjoy them a lot. The only thing I miss is the comfortable, sound blocking eartips/fit. And maybe the less accidental-touch-prone touch controls lol

title: The BEST I’ve Ever Used!!
text: This earbuds are AWESOME!!! My right ear canal is smaller than my left and I have always had trouble with earbuds, wired and wireless, fitting properly (and I’ve bought a lot of them!). Apple earbuds were my preference for a long time but even those made my ears sore after wearing them for extended periods of time...and fell out when I wanted to wear them cutting the lawn or walking. NO LONGER!! These Galaxy Live buds are a DREAM COME TRUE!! They fit nicely and are VERY comfortable! It’s like they aren’t even there! The sound quality is very good. The app comes with different equalizer settings. I have an iPhone and will play around with its equalizer setting to see if I can coax more bass out of it, but I am happy with the sound quality regardless (The iPhone equalizer does give me the sound I want!) Bottom line: you won’t be disappointed with these Galaxy Live earbuds. If you have a fit issue like I have, then these are THE PERFECT solution! They are worth every penny!!

title: Maybe take a pass...

These don't stay in super well, the mic is horrible, and the speaker could be significantly better. I mean, they work - kind of. They were a great patch for a moment until I just replaced my Pros. They are cute and okay if you're just listening to music (but not really moving). Other than that, they don't fulfill the needs that I have (as with everyone else - I do a LOT of Zoom calls and phone calls). If you're looking for something that is versatile - you can listen to music, make calls, and take meetings - these are not a win.

title: Love them
text: I absolutely despise ear buds that go into my ears. They make my inner ear "itch" and after 10 minutes or so I cannot tolerate it, plus they collect ear wax bits and that's just disgusting. The older Samsung wired buds were awesome, but I haven't been able to find them anymore. These are great. The larger of the silicone pieces really makes the earbuds very secure to the ear, the smaller ones stay put just fine for me as well, but with the larger ones it takes a bit of effort to remove them (in comparison to the small ones). My boyfriend thinks without the part going into your ear they're only going to fall out lol, but after months of use, while sweating, while sleeping, or bending and stooping frequently while cleaning and gardening, that's never happened. I like the function of "find my earbud" available with the Samsung Wear app. Also has equalizer and other control features I appreciate. I like that they look cool and discreet and not some awkward thing protruding from my ears also. Overall, giant win for my "sensitive" ears. Hope you find this helpful.

title: Good sound quality, bad fit
text: They hurt and make my ears sore. They don't fit well, seems like they're to big.

title: Great fit and sound.
text: Still liking these after having them a few weeks. They don't feel stuffy in the ear and I can hear stuff around me...the opposite of noise cancelling or attenuating, which can be good, but not what I want in these. One effect this sometimes has is that there will be a sound in music that seems like it's coming from the environment and not the earphones. A couple of times it caught me off guard and looking around to see where it was coming from. The best thing about these is they just sit in my ear with no pressure or discomfort and seem totally secure against falling out during vigorous physical activity. There's no squeezing a rubber or foam tip into the ear canal, and since they don't seal the ear, I can hear ambient sounds OK. Also, they don't protrude from the ear so there's basically no chance of getting knocked out of your ear mopping sweat off your face/head with a towel, donning/doffing a T-shirt or sweatshirt, getting hit by a helmet strap, face mask strap, combing your hair,etc. It's a very clever design. I find the sound quality to be really good. The app has 5 equalizer settings which make distinct but not wacky changes to the sound. Of course a lot of this will depend on how they fit your particular ears. I tried the noise cancellation and really couldn't notice much of an affect. That's OK for me as that's not why I got them. I couldn't notice any affect with ambient sound, which I would like, but since the ear is open, I can hear ambient sounds OK. I didn't try these on a phone call as that's not what I do with them anyway. Update. I just received an Android Wear update. I'm now getting noticeable effect from the noise cancellation and ambient sound settings. It's not huge, but definitely noticeable. I'm not sure how useful they will be.

title: Sound was awful

title: Horrible sound quality

title: It's not for everyone but it's Perfect

That's the deal with all the other same wireless earbuds, these aren't fully noise-canceling buds but they do work great and the bass boost is just sweet, definitely would be much better if they're actually paired up with a Samsung phone. Overall battery life is amazing and does get a case for the charging live case. I would have to say these are the best wireless buds I had so long, was worth the buy on a prime day. Definitely give these a chance If you want to go for em.

text: The photo with the X is the correct but worse way to wear these. Wearing it like this sounds no different than holding airpods near your ear. If worn the way Samsung recommends, the Galaxy Buds Live make my music sound empty and my ears hurt. The sound is exactly like if you held an Airpod close to your ear on full volume instead of jamming it in your ear like you're supposed to. There is absolutely no bass or distinction between instruments. My Galaxy Buds on the other hand have noticable bass and distinction between instruments when properly worn. The only way to get these to have okay sound, is by pushing the speaker part into the ear, which blocks the microphone and causes my ear to ache when the buds are removed. I have been able to literally wear any earbud from older corded ones to Airpods to Galaxy Buds and these are the first time I will not be able to comfortably wear them while maintaining tolerable sound quality. When worn as Samsung recommends, they fit just fine and stay in my ears but they have the worse audio quality I have experienced from headphones I paid for. I have been trying these for a matter of hours and with the pain I'm currently in, I'll be returning these. These have awful sound, no bass, and are terribly uncomfortable. title: Game changer for people who can't wear most budd
text: I've been looking for a good set of noise cancelling Bluetooth earbuds for a while, but the standard type that seals never fit in my ears, and on the odd chance I was able to pry open my ear canals and jam them inside with the extra small bud sets, they were insecure and wildly uncomfortable. I figured I'd give these a try, and they have exceeded my expectations. Fit - They're a bit tricky to fit at first, but are surprisingly secure. No issues taking them on runs or doing yard work. Comfort - I've worn these for probably 20-30h at this point. My ears do get a little sore after an hour or so, but that's standard for me. Sound quality - These are not sealed, so you're not going to get the same sound quality you would from a sealed bud or high quality over-ear headphones. That being said, I'm not an audiophile, and they're perfectly good for me. Noise Cancelling - Better than expected for an unsealed bud. There's a noticeable reduction in ambient noise, definitely not on par with an over-ear option, but much better than I thought was possible for an open bud. Looking forward to using these on a plane. Style - They don't stick out very far, and don't get caught on my hair, which is nice. I went with white so I could find them easier when I inevitably drop them, but the black option would make them almost unnoticeable if you have long dark hair. Mic - Callers don't realize I'm not using my phone, even elderly relatives who struggle to hear normally. Good call quality on both ends. Very impressed. Value - I got a fantastic deal and picked up a "used, like new" pair for about $60. Swabbed them with alcohol and disinfected them before using. I highly recommend keeping an eye out for options like this if you're on a budget. I've tried several other earbuds in the $120-200 MSRP range, these are still priced well but seem to go on sale quite often. If you're looking for impeccable noise cancelling and can wear sealed buds, you won't be happy with these. However, as someone who cannot wear sealed options this is a phenomenal option and I'm very happy.

title: Replacement for The Dash Pro by Bragi
text: I’ve been searching for earbuds to replace The Dash, as they are starting to fade a bit, and that Bragi no longer supports or sells the earbuds. I like the idea of the “bean” design. Form-fitting is something truly wireless earbuds have been trying to perfect, since becoming widely available. Sound quality is very very good. Deep bass, clear treble, with no distortion! A couple things that left me feeling let down: The water resistance is pretty much nonexistent. I honestly believe that with the direction that mobile-audio is heading, IPX4 should be the BARE minimum level of water resistance. IPX2 is just sad. The buds are pretty slippery when transferring them from case to ear. Moving forward, I’d like to see them with a solid, comfortable, material to reduce slippage. Both holding them in your hand and while in the ear. I’d also love to see a true “transparency” feature. Overall, for the first crack at this level of tech, 4 out of 5. text: Ok so let me start by saying that the "ANC" feature is garbage. Samsung should not have even included it. Makes no sense. Okay now that's out of the way. These earbuds are fantastic. They took me nearly a week (no seriously) to learn how to wear them right. The fit is AB-SO-LUTE-LY critical to the sound quality. Push them in too far? All of your high frequencies are gone and everything sounds boomy and muffled. Not pushed in enough? Bye to the bass. Seated in your ear just right? That's where it's gold. I'm inclined to say that the sound quality of these is more enjoyable than the Airpods Pro (I have them to compare). As for comfort? Nothing comes close. If you have these seated in your ear properly, you'll forget you're wearing them probably. They're lightweight and the open design completely eliminates the issue of plugged ears that most earbuds have. I can wear these for hours no problem. These are great all-day buds to carry with you. Samsung did it right. I rarely say that. But this time, I have to say that.

title: Amazing earbuds if noise cancellation isn't a priority
text: I've had my buds for a few days now and I'm really loving using them. I also own the Airpods pro and the regular airpods so I'll compare the two below. Good things: - Sounds really good. Better than the Airpods Pro and regular Airpods. There's a surprising amount of bass, and the mids and highs are very good as well. If you don't like a bass heavy sound, you can customize the equalizer in the Samsung Gear Wearable app. - They're super comfortable. About on par with the original Airpods in terms of not feeling them in your ears. - Multi device switching is seamless. I've used these with a Chromebook, my phone (Pixel 4), and my TV (Samsung TV). It pairs quickly and reliably with all of them. No issues so far. - Battery life is also quite good. With noise cancellation off (more on this later), I wasn't able to kill them in a day of solid use (I didn't put them back in the case). - The microphone is clear and sounds good for calls. - They don't force Bixby on you, you can customize the tap and hold gesture to launch Google Assistant. Not good things: - Noise cancellation is non existent. To be honest, I'm not even sure why they advertise this as a feature, it's that bad. The Airpods Pro is leagues above these in ANC. I guess that's the price you pay for having an open design. - The gesture customization is really bad. You can only set gestures in "pairs". For example, you can have the left bud gesture be volume down, but then the right bud HAS to be volume up. Why can't I make the left one do volume down and the right one launch Google Assistant? If I wan't one to control noise cancellation, guess what, the other one has to control it too. Very strange decision by Samsung. Overall I would recommend these earbuds to anyone that doesn't need noise cancellation. Almost everything else about them is fantastic. If you do need noise cancellation in a pair of fully wireless earbuds, the Airpods Pro is the way to go.

title: Loud & Bass Heavy (Not in a good way), and ANC Doesn't Work...
text: I bought these the first day they were released and tried them out at home for about a week. They were easy to pair with my Pixel phone, and sat relatively fine in my ears. I could shake my head back and forth without them coming out, which was a great change from other recent earbuds I've tried. However, because of how deep you need to seat these in your ears, you'll develop ear canal pain after maybe 10 minutes of wearing them, and it just gets worse the longer you leave them in. The bass-heavy sound is just too much and causes fatigue rather quickly. The ANC is a straight up joke, and it really just doesn't work at all... To combat outside noise, you'll need to increase the volume to drown out everything else, which will eventually cause hearing damage. No good. Battery life seemed good for the week I had these, and they never randomly dropped connection to my phone, either. The touch interface could be turned off, too, which was a huge relief. The move to touch-based interfaces is a big mistake, IMO. Every time you try to reposition an earbud because it unseats as you're moving, you inadvertently pause or skip your track / end your phone call... I don't understand why they got rid of tactile buttons on these things. Really dumb move (again, just my opinion). Samsung needs to get ANC built into the original Galaxy Buds design for a true winner. I've returned the beans and am, again, using my original Galaxy Buds that came with an old phone that I no longer use.

text: You can read a ton of reviews about sounds quality or battery life. I'm not going to cover that. I'm going to give my impression of these vs the Galaxy Buds Plus that I recently used. So I had the Samsung Galaxy Buds Plus that I purchased around April or May. I accidentally washed them and even though the buds still worked, the case wouldn't charge. When I bought them, I really loved them. I always only used one at a time though because wearing both made me feel cut off from stuff going on around me (even with the ambient sound turned on). When I would wear them for longer periods, I always got that clogged ear feeling. When I bought these and realized that they didn't really create a true seal, I was nervous that they would be terrible. I actually like them better. I don't get that clogged feeling and I don't feel cut off from the room around me. I think how well you will like these will depend on what you want out of them. If you want a true seal and to feel like you're fully immersed in the music / sound, I suggest you try the Galaxy Buds Plus. If you're like me though and you will wear them for long periods of time and want comfort and not to feel clogged or cut off from everything going on around you, you'll probably enjoy these. They are really comfortable to wear for long periods.

title: Good sound and battery, and comfortable, but can pop out.
text: If you are looking for a wireless headset that sits in ear but doesn't have the silicone "plungers," these are great. Some prefer the silicone plungers for more isolation. However for myself and many others the plungers are uncomfortable, and tend to lose seal unexpectedly. The largest issue is the the design can pop out. Culprits are heavy bouncing motions, things like hats or helmets brushing against ears, and the worst is covid masks. The mask band puts pressure on the back of the ear changing its shape pulling the buds forward where they can easily fall out. When removing a mask the band can catch and sling shot the bud. They are small and can bounce a considerable distance to their doom in a puddle, a storm drain, active street, etc. The result of which is costly as Samsung does not sell individual replacements buds, you have to pay full price for a complete new set. I do not recommend these for running, hiking, skiing, biking, or other vigorous activity. But for use at home or in an office they are nice.

title: Good headphones, worth the buy
text: Great headphones. They're worth the price and good quality. Comfortable. EXCELLENT at sound dampening. They're even decent to block outside sound when the power is off. Good sound quality - my only mild gripe re: sound is that the sound does distort somewhat at max volume, but I can still go to about 90-95% volume without distortion. This is for music, though - I haven't tried them yet for calls. I will update the review once I do. Other than that, I do like the ability to have no lights, all lights, just the ears, just the sides...but I'm not sure if it's possible to select just one color or not yet. I don't think so, which for me is a downside...but it's not the biggest deal in the world either. For the other things... They're easy to charge. I wish the buttons were more accessibility friendly re: 1. Sight - hard to see which button is which unless you're really looking for the symbols on them, you can't really tell with a quick glance. That may not be an issue once you get used to placement/muscle memory when in use, though. 2. Dexterity/strength/spasms or tremors. If you have issues with any of that like I do, the buttons may take effort to push. They may accidentally turn off if you or someone else adjusts them in a certain way due to the placement of the power button (also see the sight issue for this). The biggest accessibility pro, though, is that they don't easily fall off like some headphones do with having spasms. I know quite a few of my cons aren't exactly applicable to a lot of people, but I feel that it's a good thing to note regardless.

title: The best WiFi headphones I've ever owned!
text: These are without question the best WiFi headphones I've ever owned. They are as light as they are comfortable, and they are VERY comfortable. With my older headphones it is necessary almost all the time to manually connect the headphones. With these headphones, connection is almost always automatic and immediate - a wonderful convenience! Pairing is easier than with any other WiFi device I've owned. Very nice! Sound reproduction is excellent, and bass response is fabulous. Battery life is also fabulous! Unlike my other WiFi headphones, I do NOT have to recharge these daily. I recharge them only rarely! The battery life is amazing! The noise cancelling circuitry is more effective than any other noise cancelling headphone I've used. Ever. I frequently wear these headphones to bed, not to listen to audio, but because they are so great at eliminating ambient noise. I didn't realize how much low level noise there was in my home until I first put these headphones on and enabled noise cancellation. When you enable noise cancellation it is almost like you are in a soundproof vault! I could not be more pleased with these headphones. I will be buying more of them to replace my older WiFi headphones. Why? The quality of the sound reproduction is so good, for one thing. But mostly because the noise cancellation really WORKS!

title: The BEST features in wireless earbuds!
text: This is my 5th pair of wireless earbuds and I have to say; these are the BEST. Naturally, I paid the most for them. The reason why I kept buying various brands was because I thought I was highly allergic to "bluetooth." I even did research. Then, it hit me that the very first pair I purchased did not bother the insides of my ears at all. I finally deduced that the charging connectors located on the inner side of the buds must have nickel in them on subsequent purchases --which caused my ears to burn and become inflamed within minutes. It takes days to heal them with a lot of discomfort in the interim. To my dismay, these had the same effect but they sound so amazing and the features are so appealing that I figured out a way to work with them. I essentially made a plastic gasket to cover the charging connectors so that they don't touch my skin when I wear them. It is a bit of a hassle but I was desperate to have a good pair of wireless that fit into my small ears. I share this "silly" story in the event others find wireless earbuds to have the same effect. On a side note; I can wear wired earbuds all day and night long. The fact that they automatically turn down when they detect your voice is priceless not to mention the ambient sound adjustment feature. UPDATE: The extra steps taken to cover the connectors did not work. The saddest return I have ever had to make.

Well, they got stolen a year ago and I finally decided to replace them with these, the newer model (since I couldn't find the old ones). They started falling out of my ears immediately...while just sitting (not even working out which is the reason I use them). I've tried all the pieces to find a fit: large + medium are way too big, they just pop themselves right out. The small is the only thing that fits in my ear and it is NOT SECURE. I understand the thought process for making them sleeker, less fussy, less parts, etc....BUT you pair ultra-smooth with no security and it's a recipe for disaster...a disaster that hit today. While using the bathroom with one bud in, I turned to grab some tissue and that suckered just tumbled out if my ear, between my legs and into the bowl :( Why is it so hard to keep a design that actually works??!! You don't have to always change stuff- the old model worked beautifully. This model is like a Vegas slot machine: stacked against you to favour the house.

These buds do not come with (and were not designed to use) wingtips, which are used to keep them secure in your ears. This was a serious oversight by Samsung. These buds are super smooth and if any sweat is introduced then they will very easily slip out and fall onto the ground. This is very frustrating! title: These are the best bluetooth headphones you will find at a price point ...
text: Listen...no pun intended...These are the best bluetooth headphones you will find at a price point below those for "audio gourmets" (willing to spend above $150). I've tried 5 others under the $150 mark (that ended in returns). This was my 6th try, and BINGO, the best. Ended up buying a second pair. So the details: Clear, clear, clear sound. Deep, balanced bass (never sounds fuzzy). Midtones and highs are crystal. I typically test headphones by listening to a variety of genres of music (pop, classical, electro types, jazz, afro-cuban, "yoga music", hip hop, vocal ballads, piano and guitar solos). If the headphones can make all of these sound tasty, I know I've found what works for me. Don't be lazy. Take the time to try out the different size/types of earpieces. Doing this bit of customizing will make all the difference in your overall sound quality. When it's right, you'll know, because your ears will say, "Ahhhh...". Also, this is the best way to test out the noise cancelling. When the fit is right, nothing else gets in. That may be a good or bad thing, depending upon the activity you're doing, or the environment you're in. Comfortable, ear guards stay secure, not too heavy, easy pairing. Can't say much about sound quality for calls, as I haven't used mine for that. They go to the gym, cycling, and big chair sitting for streaming stuff (Netflix, Hulu Plus, CW, Youtube, Amazon Video...all sound great). Hope this helps!

title: Don't buy this for running
text: Yet another alleged "sports" headphone -- this one even has "running" right in their product title -- "TREBLAB XR500 Bluetooth Headphones, Best Noise Cancelling Wireless Earbuds, Waterproof Sports Running Earphones, Secure-Fit Headset w/ Mic" -- that is completely unsuitable for running. The 2 features that drew me to purchase this product for running were the over-the-ear feature and the cord tightener (on the cord that connects the 2 sides and runs behind your neck). Both of these features were a complete failure for running. The over-the-ear piece is nice and soft for comfort -- so soft, in fact, that it offers no support at all, allowing the earpiece to flop around completely unhindered. The "cord keeper", which is the feature on my last bluetooth headphones (Jarv Pure Fit) that really kept them in place, does no such thing with these headphones. The cord keeper isn't at fault -- rather, it's a fundamental design flaw with the headphones themselves. The cord attaches to each earpiece way too far forward, so tightening the cord behind your neck with the cord keeper does nothing to add to their stability as you move. I do not recommend this product to anyone who wants headphones for running, and would not really recommend them in general for use in any activity that involves moving -- at all.

title: Excellent fit for sports, excellent quality bass, not so great treble...
text: Pros: The fit on these is great. This is the first pair of wireless headphones that actually stay on/in my ears. I've been looking for 5+ years. The style is nice and quality of materials is high as well. The only other sport headphones that have been able to stay in my ears while biking, running, shootin' hoops, working out, etc. were some old school sony sweatproof/water-resistant wired headphones. Cons: The reason for my 3-star review is that of the sound quality. These are marketed as a high quality $179.99 MSPR pair of headphones that provide a "PERFECT LISTENING EXPERIENCE" and having "HIGH DEFINITION SOUND - Rock-solid bass, super-crisp treble." I was an audio engineer and music producer for about 10 years. I'll just say that the bass frequencies are boosted sloppily which muddles the mid-range to higher frequencies (treble). The bass and accuracy of the bass frequencies are excellent but they're not balanced thus leaving the "super-crisp treble" as something to be desired. If these headphones had half as great of sound quality as the advertisements led on, I would have given these a 6/5 star review. Overall they're a decent value for what they are at $50, but if sound quality is something you appreciate and understand, then unless the pair I received was defective, their are other headphones on the market for $50 and less with better overall sound quality and not just boosted and high quality bass. I'll probably still use these while working out until I can find another pair that fit as well with better sound quality. My other cheaper pair of wireless bluetooth headphones have better overall sound quality (not as quality bass though) but they don't stay in my ears.

text: I've been searching for lightweight wireless Bluetooth headphones and these are the ones. I can't stand in-ear headphones and I use these with the earpiece just resting against the ear canal. The only odd thing is volume control--it's opposite to every other set of headphones I've ever had. All in all, a very good set of headphones that have paired well ios 10.0.2. Update--11/03/2016 I've had to knock a couple of stars from my previously Five Star review. These are still excellent headphones EXCEPT that they won't pair with my iPhone 7 plus unless I delete the device from my bluetooth inventory and then reinstall it. I have to do this every time. I turn on the headphones and get the "Power On . . . Connected" audio cue. But when I start music from iTunes library or an audiobook with the Audible app, the sound comes out my iPhone speakers, not the headset. title: Excellent sound (with LDAC)
text: I like the sound of these earbuds way more than I expected: they're clean and clear through my hearing range, and I didn't even have to fiddle with the EQ settings to get there. I also have the Liberty 2 Upgraded version, and while those are very good, these are clearly superior. I did use the Soundcore app to update the firmware and enable LDAC: you'll definitely want to do this before you begin using them. Also, there are other settings on the app you might find useful. They are also very comfortable to wear for long periods (I use them at my desk while working), and even using LDAC (which uses a lot more power) the battery lasts as long as I've needed so far. The case is nice and compact, and of course charges the earbuds quickly. The only thing I would grumble about (and now I'm being very fussy) is that I have to turn the earbuds over to get them into the right position for the case. Another note: Anker was offering a "used like new" item for a much lower price, so I decided to try them. I'm very happy I did, since they really were just like a new product, seemed unused (probably a quick return). All the earpiece bits were new, of course. Highly recommended for excellent sound and comfort at a very affordable price (new or used).

title: I’d put these up against $400 buds!
