title: Better than Airpod Pros
text: I'm returning my Airpods Pro. These are better. They won't fall out of my ears like the Airpods do. You get more fit options, and no stems sticking out to catch on things. The sound quality is objectively better, the clarity is superior, as is the bass, and they have customizable EQ settings too. They send software updates, and have great software options. Overall I'm really impressed. They are not perfect — there are brief sound disconnects that I have yet to solve. They can connect to 2 devices, but it's not as good as an H1 chip for multipoint. They lack Apple's 3d sound feature (thought I find it disturbing to have artificial holographic sound sources places wherever Apple thinks it should be floating in the room....) They are slippery and hard to fit into the case — you have to rotate them to be opposite the position they need to be inserted in your ears, which is really dumb when transferring between case and ears, or ears and case. But damn, if you're an audiophile, you'll 99% likely prefer these for sound quality. I've had my Airpod Pros jump out of my ears in public bathrooms, on dog runs, and on dirty streets. That's bad design, and Apple should not be selling bad design. The 3 sizes of rubbery fit wings on these should help prevent such accidents. (though I might still drop them getting them in/out of the slippery case...). I spent hours checking reviews before ordering something better than an Airpod, and think these nailed it. Great job Soundcore!

title: What the ... HECK?!
text: I own a cheap pair of Soundpeats and an expensive pair of Google Pixel buds. For the money, the Soundpeats are good. The same can be said for the Google Pixel Pro buds, which are much more expensive but are also worth the cash. However, these Anker Liberty buds are surprisingly good. So good, they may set the bar in a whole new level. They are quite comfortable, which contributes to my criteria for a good fit (don't wiggle, good seal, don't fall out, don't cause ear pain). I spent several minutes completing the sound calibration in their app, which is slick and easy to use. After the sound calibration (which revealed my old ears are unable to hear certain frequencies), I was astonished how clear and clean the music sounded. I skipped around my library enjoying music from various genres and artists, enjoying the rich sound. The transparency mode is certainly better than the Google Pixel Pro buds. Don't get me wrong, I like my Pixel buds, but they are no longer my favorite buds. I only rated a 4 for battery life because I haven't had them a full 24 hours yet, so I can't rightfully evaluate the overall performance of the battery in either the buds or the case. I'll report back if I need to change that rating. Overall, these are stellar earbuds! I appreciate the app design, I love the form factor of the case and buds ... I'm going to carry these in my pocket as part of my EDC!

title: Sound quality is exceptional
text: Exceptional sound quality when using Hear ID and tweaking to my liking (added slight amount of bass manually). “3D surround sound” mode degrades the sound quality, but the earbuds have such good sound stage and instrument separation that you don’t need it. Lightweight and comfortable. The only downside is that sometimes one of the buds doesn’t make perfect contact in the charging case and the battery empties. This is rare, so I’m ok living with this flaw in design.

title: Best overall
text: Great app, great sound, great noise cancelling, great ambient pass-thru, and great "Hearing ID" (a hearing test similar to what they do in hearing aid centers)

title: Extremely disappointed
text: I really hoped these would be great. Based on the reviews, I thought I had purchased a solid and quality product, especially with Anker attached to it. Unfortunately, I was very wrong. Good: Sound quality, fit, comfort and overall look. Bad: Constantly having issues connecting, earbud randomly not charging despite contacts being clean and case being fully charged, and as of very recently, degraded audio quality. Sadly, these are being returned in favor of Jabra. Maybe these used to be good, but its clear they aren't good anymore.

title: What battery life?
text: I love the sound quality and the mic quality of the earbuds, but there are two problems with the battery. The first is that depending on the tips and wings you have on them you may not get them to charge properly in the case and not find out about it until it's too late. This can be incredibly annoying since I rely very heavily on my earbuds to work when I need them to. Even if you get them charging properly at first, they can all the sudden stop charging properly if you just bump the case barely. To make a long story short... It can be difficult to get them charging properly in the case because the case is finicky. The second and equally important problem is that I don't get anywhere near the advertised amount of battery life out of these. That's fairly normal but I get really short battery life with ANC on. Maybe 3 hours. For earbuds that I haven't had very long that is pretty bad. I drive on the road and the ANC really helps with the road noise, but only being able to use these for 3 hours is super disappointing.

title: Ear won't hold.
text: These work great. But the ears don't really hold it's position in your ear properly.

title: Rubber ear part ripped
text: I was at work and my rubber earpiece kept staying in my ear when I would remove my earbud. I looked at it today and it had a tear so there is no seal to keep it on. I’m disappointed because of the price I paid for these it should not have worn out so quickly. I will check the warranty to see what can be done.

title: BEST sound, without question
text: I tried so many earbuds between 2020 and 2022, and was tired of having to adjust the EQ with virtually every song or genre, particularly with the industry leading Sony WF10000XM4's. The Soundcore Liberty 3 Pro we're the best out-of-the-box sound I'd ever experienced. I even old my WF10000XM4's to buy a second pair of L3P as a backup while charging the other pair. No need to fiddle with the EQ anymore. I listen to Flac files with the ldac codec in the earbuds is an absolute delight! I believe that also has a lot to do with the personalized hearing ID provided through the Soundcore app. Though I also kick it up a bit by using the XTREMEMusic™ pro app as well. The battery life is solid when not using ANC. But I barely get 3 hours with ANC on. So my solution to this was to buy a third pair. After going through so many different ear buds, once I finally found the L3P's and experienced the sound they brought right out of the box, I was sold. I mention not needing to use the EQ anymore. However the L3P app provides a a 7 band EQ and several presets designed by award winning sound engineers (identified by each engineer's name) as well as a few other tweaks, of you need. Unfortunately, because we all have different shaped ears and we hear things differently, this may not be your experience. But hopefully with enough of us stating how great they are, one might find the confidence to give them a try. EDIT: These are absolutely the best sounding earbuds. I initially said "ANC kills battery, & LDAC Utterly Destroys battery Life.",) But Soundcore tells me this is abnormal. After suggesting a few tips, they ultimately offered to replace my earbuds. PHENOMENAL SOUND AND PHENOMENAL CUSTOMER SERVICE.

title: Excellent set of buds! Comparable with Galaxy Buds Pro and worlds better than Raycon Work
text: I paid the full price for mine 10 days ago and now they are $40 off. I bought them because I thought I lost my Galaxy Buds Pro. Then my wife found them and now I have 2 pairs of buds. If you are familiar with Galaxy Buds plus or pro, the Liberty 3 buds offer a very similar sound perhaps with more features. In the end, after adjusting the sound to fit my ears, they sound exactly the same as my stock Galaxy Buds Pro. Cons: they are bigger than the Pros, maybe a little less comfortable but a bit more secure in the ear. Everything else is the same which is a good thing. Bottom line: if you can get them cheaper than the Glalxy Buds Pro, get them. I don't need them anymore and I will not return them because I respect the quality that these people put into these buds. On the other hand, my daughter bought a set of Raycon Work buds and they are trash compared to the Soundcore Liberty 3 buds. Raycon Work buds sound terrible, right is louder than left, and have connection issues. Finally, the galaxy buds + I lost a year ago, were also fantastic. They were my first set of buds that I had no complaints about. My other daughter has Jabra earbuds and they are great too. Stay away from Raycon. Ugh...

title: Great Battery, Great Features, Universal Fit
text: For awhile I’ve been using the Raycon E55 Performer wireless earbuds and they were good. The main thing I liked was the shape, specifically the small bump on top that fit in part of your ear, making for a really nice fit for me personally. They unfortunately wore out after about 17 months, so I got these because it was recommended online. They don’t disappoint at all. I use an iPhone and the app works great and makes me feel like my product is very compatible, especially because it suggested a firmware update. The earbuds are independent, so if you want you can just use one. Battery life of both the buds and the case are as advertised, although for maximum battery life use ‘Normal’ mode, not ambient mode or noise cancelling mode. The noise cancelling mode is very good, the only reason I gave it 4 stars is for the very quiet white noise is has when nothing is playing. But if you’re listening to something at a normal volume and in a noisy area, you’ll hear the music or podcast perfectly. The ambient mode is pretty good too, although you have to be listening at a relatively quiet (but still well audible) volume to have any kind of conversation or acute awareness. The ambient mode claims to have a ‘Voice-Only’ mode, which is supposed to focus on letting voices through. There is no real noticeable difference between voice and regular ambient modes in my experience, but the ambient mode works just fine. Circling back to the fit, they fit very well, better than the Raycon E55s and with more customization options for bigger or smaller eared people. I have no doubt in my mind that with all the options available you will find a good fit. Nothing but good things, would definitely recommend these.

title: I really wanted to like these…
text: I’m a Soundcore/Anker fan from the start. Their quality, price and customer service can’t be matched. The problem with the L3P is the battery life! Even with ANC off I’m only getting 4 hrs! This is my second pair because I thought the battery might be better. It’s not. So disappointed.

title: Sounds good, noise canceling and battery life could be better
text: The sound quality is good, but the noise cancelation is only so-so. On a flight in a 737 sitting isles before the wings, the noise canceling still allowed engine noise and some nearby talking passengers. On the same flight, I switched to my older Raycon The Work wireless earbuds, which noise canceled/blocked out almost all noises, enough that I didn't notice we were landing until the attendant notified me to raise my tray table. The total battery life of case is good. The battery life of individual pods leaves a little to be desired at around 4 hours before they need charged in the case.

title: I only have them for a day. But...
text: Great sound , noise cancelling is very good too. When using them in the car, I can't hear traffic. Almost as good as my Sony over the ear headphones (910n). The problem is the battery, in ANC mode I only 2.5- 3 hours. I changed them 3 times today, and it is only 6pm. I discharged case too, it was showing low battery in the app. I don't use LDAC mode that drains battery faster. If this trend continues I will have to return them. 2.5 hours battery life is not working for me.

title: Not my first set of Soundcore earbuds
text: This is probably my third set of Soundcore earbuds, and not because there were any issues with the previous ones. I tend to lose them when I travel, which is all on me. However, I always replace them with another set of Soundcore earbuds. I appreciate the quality of audio they provide, the incredible assortment of attachments included, and the decent price point. I enjoy the personalized aspect of the hearing test/EQ option. When I first used the Liberty 3 version, I said aloud, "wow, that's really good!". I also like how these stay in place while at the gym, which other earbuds don't do as well. Obviously, I highly recommend these.

title: 20 minutes after fully charged, I get a "battery low" message
text: These were great for the first month. Now, I charge them overnight, wear them for 20 minutes for the noise cancelling feature only (no music, no phone). I then put them in their case, and the next day I get a "battery low" message. In other words, 8 hours charging = 20 minutes of use. Obviously other people don't have this battery drain problem, but this is the most expensive set of earplugs I've ever bought, because that's really all they're good for at this point. I can't speak to the music/phone features because I bought it for ANC feature only.

title: Don't expect the best battery life
text: These are great, amazing sound and quality Battery life, well, 4, maybe 5 hours tops, no more, so the 7 - 8 hours is not working for me at least Other than that amazing

title: Best earbuds I've ever owned.
text: Been a music fanatic all my life. I've owned Martin Logan, Magnepan, Legacy Audio, Gallo, Klipsch, Paradigm signature, and more. I've got to say these are prettt good. I had the pro 2 and returned them. To me they sounded terrible. These however were not too bad at their price of $80. I did have to go into the app and set these for custom eq, and all sliders to, max. Otherwise I couldn't get the volume I require for all types of music and recordings. The positive here is it didn't cause any sound issues or change the eq too much. Still sounds mostly even across the frequencies, but can now go much louder. I wish the default sound signature would have just been louder, but at least this works out. The good news it saves the eq settings to the earbuds, not the device with the app (phone,etc). Once programed you are good to go. I used them on a second device and they kept the seq max setting (downloaded app on 2nd device to confirm). I wouldn't mind just a tiny bit more bass in the 15hz-35hz range but that's just me being picky. I do like nuetral speakers, but I've always just liked that little extra bass kick in the 15hz-30hz range. It doesn't muddy the music down there and just sounds more exciting and full to me. The top end on the pro 3 sounds wonderful. No harshness, piercing highs, or anything that becomes annoying after time. Would I recommend for $100? Probably not. I'm a headphone over earbud listener. I'd probably try and but a m50xbt on sale and spend a bit more. Better sound, longer lasting battery, durable, and can still be plugged in when the battery dies. My issue with earbuds is they are garbage once the battery starts to go bad.

title: Went through quite a few pairs (beats also) and settled on these.
text: I went through Anker a1, Beats Fit Elite and a few others. These are solid headphones for sure. Out of the box they are not great. Take the time to try earpieces (larger better). Tweak the EQ in the app. Once you get a good seal on the ears and bass turned up these are much louder than the Beats were (at $210) and the noise canceling is better on these also. Noise canceling with a good seal on the ears is insane good. Whole world goes quite. Battery life not great, but that's due to the features running and it does last longer than the Beats Fit Elite did. I bought these for the pass through transparency mode. Transparency is OK. Works but the beats is better, more natural sound etc. These are louder and better than the more expensive beats with better noise canceling. Transparency mode is ok not great and the case is a bit funky to lay them into but I will learn that. (Weird angle they sit at). Beats are smaller in the ears which i liked. Beats wins on smaller size, look and transparency mode is better. Anker Liberty 3 elite wins on noise canceling, much louder, better app, pair better (beats sometimes stubborn), $70 cheaper, better EQ options.

title: I really enjoy the sound
text: I had the original liberty 2 pros and felt there were things that needed to be fixed although I did like them . The improvements have been made, these are excellent. Not sure the app can be synced on two devices having some issues. Maybe something I’m doing wrong I’m not concerned. Again awesome earbuds. Update: I deleted and repaired in Bluetooth settings on both devices and the app is only recognizing the earbuds on one device, it must be an issue only an update can fix idk.

title: My Experience
text: They fit very well in your ear. I have not had a single problem with them falling out. The sound is fantastic. The apps great. It's very intuitive so it's easy to customize the earbuds.

title: Amazing
text: After many videos, reviews etc., I decided to try these. Way better than expected. The app lets you customize everything from the way they sound to the touch controls (3 per earbud). I typically like the stem style earbuds but these work fine. They can be a little tough to take out of the case if you have bigger fingers. I don't care for the sliding top on the case but that's nothing to gripe about. Sound quality is great, voice clarity is really good, multiple levels of noise cancelling and passthrough, plus wireless charging. All this let's you know that the more expensive brands are just taking your money.

title: Great sound
text: Excellent sound.highs and lows are well defined, vocals are great, you could hear every detail of the instrument's. I love the case is very comfortable and well designed also fits in any Jean pocket. I think they did a great job on the APP for these ear bud's, you have total control, also you can set it to play through a the built-in DAC. I'm very satisfied and recommend them.

title: Multipoint does not work. Even multi-pairing does not work
text: These pods have amazing sound that beats airpod pros hands down, but you cannot reliably connect to devices, especially with the multipoint for connecting 2 devices simultaneously. It's a complete deal breaker for me since I have to switch from phone to laptop often. I just had a terrible experience using these headphones for a zoom call and no sound was able to come out from either my phone or the laptop! I reproduced the problem later and pinpointed that it was caused by the bluetooth connectivity of these headphones, not anything else. Avoid if reliable bluetooth connectivity is important to you.

title: Battery Life is the selling point here...
text: 8-21-2022 Update Anker reached out to me after I sent my purchase back and after some further discussion, they sent me another set to use. I did not ask them do to this and to be frank, I was very surprised at this. Most companies really do not care one way or another about one user or customer. I find that very refreshing and told them that in so many words. They stand by their products and I stand by them. Well Done!!! Comfort and sound were not.. I had to return them. I cannot recommend them for anyone who wants N/C or good sound.

title: Amazing. If you're looking for high quality all around these are it.
text: I've been struggling with finding wireless earbuds that meet my expectations. It's been challenging because I'm coming from using audiophile quality triple and quad driver in-ear monitors. The Soundcore Liberty Pro 3 are simply incredible. Fantastic sound quality that you can profile tune to your hearing curve results in really great audio quality. The noise cancellation is pretty good given how small these are. I've tested them on a commercial fight and they were perfect. Transparency is good as well. Can't believe I've been using earbuds without this capability for so long. As with all earbuds, a good fit and seal will greatly affect the results you get from them. I'm fortunate enough to have been using in ear monitors for so long that I know exactly how to get a great fit with just about any earbuds. I managed this with the stock silicone tips, but usually like thermal fit memory foam tips like the Comply tips. Get them. You'll be glad you did.

title: So Far,So Good
text: So far these ear buds have been great. I had recently purchased a pair of ear buds from Sony that would not only pair with my mobile but, they would't hold a charge. That, after letting them charge for nearly 12 hours, off they went, back to Amazon for a refund. These took a fraction of that time and, paired quite easily with my mobile. I used them for a couple hours and put them away. Over a week later they still had ample charge for me to listen to some 40's swing bands as I prepared dinner. I have not tried out the noise cancelling feature yet but, I do like them even though they're rather large. The medium tips fit my ears well and the time I wore them was not uncomfortable given they are pretty good sized. Just a bit of background on me; I'm in my 60's, use a smart phone and consider myself moderately technically capable. The app is understandable and I had no problems following the instructions. There, that's it in a nut shell. For me these work and so far, I'm glad I got them. Oh, they were purchased during the October Prime event so, the price was under $90 for them. Even at the regular price, if you're thinking about trying them I would give them a go.

title: Amazing sound and fit
text: I love how you can customize the sound based on your particular hearing levels and they are the most comfortable earbuds I've ever owned and over the years I've probably owned a dozen different kinds. My only wish is that you could control the volume on the earbuds themselves instead of co trolling volume from the source only.

title: misaligned charger
text: The magnetic connection is not precise enough. Most of the time, when I place my earbuds in the charger, the charging light fails to come on. The design and manufacturing of the earbud to case connection is poor.

title: Quit charging right earbuds after 4 months
text: Or earlier! I own 8 sets of earbuds, 6.Soundcore head and earbuds mixed. I was looking into the Liberty 4, so I took my 2 and 3 out to see if there was enough difference, I don't just buy cause it's new, it has to have new features. Anyways, I can't justify buying the 4 if my 3 is already toast. I hardly used them due to the charging process as is. I have to remove the tips every time to be able to charge. They are bulky for my taste. So, if I do not get support from Soundcore as a loyal spending customer, I will check out competition. Nothing worse than loosing your $ value within 4 months!!

title: Solid earbuds, but still waiting to find the WOW factor
text: A solid set of earbuds under $200, great sound quality and an accompanying app that out performs any other company. My only complaints pertaining to anyone looking into purchasing these; one being they are on the larger side, so if you have smaller ears they may get a bit uncomfortable. Unfortunately, that is the case for me, my Life P3’s fit my ears much better so i will be riding with those i think. The second complaint is one i’m surprised i haven’t read in other reviews and that is there is an annoying hissing white noise sound constantly. When music is playing it’s just not as noticeable, but it’s there and quite apparent in every listening mode. Wanted to love these as much as the rest of the world, but they’re just not doin it for me..

title: I didn't understand. Now I do.
text: I read so many reviews and these seemed to be the best bang for the buck. I had never spent more than $100 on earbuds before, but I was ready to see what I was missing. I was so excited to get these, that I waited by the door for the delivery. When they came, I immediately opened them and started listening. I was not impressed. Right out of the box these were no better than my last $30 pair. I downloaded the app and started three setup process. Setup was lengthy, but well worth the time. The sound was amazing. I was blown away. It was like watching 4K TV with my ears. I heard detail that had never been present before. Then I enabled LDAC. The sound went to another undescribable level of WOW! I now understood why the reviews I saw on YouTube where grown men giggled with delight. These are amazing!

title: Sounds decent
text: I'm comparing these to my Sony true wireless earbuds, 3rd gen. You know the ones that stick out prominently :) Anyhow, in short the Sony's emphasize by default the mids and these really emphasize the highs and lows. That said, the deph and quality of sound is better with the Soundcores, and LDAC pretty much gets rid of all the annoying AAC artifacts. Side note, I use the Sound Assistant for tweaking sound, and it does what the Soundcore app does by testing your hearing but does it on a phone level, not just for the Soundcores. Noise cancelling wasn't as strong as the Sonys. Overall I would recommend, but may hold out for LC3 support.

title: Fantastic.
text: Very pleased with the Soundcore products. As with all earbud type, fitment is crucial. Soundcore provides all sizes needed to provide the fitment. These do not disappoint.

title: Good sound, but won't stay in my ears. ((
text: Good sound, but won't stay in my ears. (( I got them for bike rides, but if they fall all the time at home, I won't risk to take it outside. Also, half of the times right one won't be charging. Have to push it in a bit.

title: The bet buds I have owned.
text: I've had these for one month and I am amazed by how great they sound. The app gives so many options to get the sound you want. They far outshine my Airpods. It took me a bit to get them to seal completely and it made a tremendous difference. These are equal to buds that cost $250 or more.

title: Best Ever
text: This is my 3rd set of earbuds. I'm hearing more depth with my music than ever before. The noise canceling feature is very effective and better than other earbuds I've owned. The fit is very comfortable. The price during early prime shopping was very attractive.

title: Ear speakers
text: I have to agree you get what you pay for if you buy the cheap staff. Over 100$ but the best sound and functions. Equalizer over the phone app. Very good product

title: DON'T buy the LIKE NEW Soundcore Anker earbuds! Warranty is 3 months! Update: from AnkerDirect CS
text: DONT buy a LIKE NEW product from Anker Soundcore. They only give you a 3 month warranty and if your buds start to fail like mine did have no recourse. FYI Jabra gives a full 2 year warranty on their refurbs. The buds were great. The sound was awesome. So if your going roll the dice and buy them ..... BUY the new ones! At least you'll get a 1 year warranty which is still NOT great, but it's something. Update: The Ankerdirect CS offered and given me a full refund for these buds. Better late than never I guess. I've given them 3 stars for making good on the buds in the end. They are not allowed and did not ask me to change or update my review. I still believe the 3 month warranty is too short and should at least be extended to 6 months or a year. If a Company truly believes they've refurbed or restored a product it should at least be good for 1/2 to a 1 full year IMO.

title: Charging
text: Charging still has the same problem as the pro 2's har to get a good connection with the case contacts

title: AVOID!!!! Terrible Battery Life, Decent Sound, Not Very Comfortable
text: I have some hearing difficulties so I was turned onto these buds because they claim to be much louder than normal buds, which THEY ARE! The loudness, clarity, sound quality, etc. are all very good. No complaints there. There are TWO major issues I have discovered: Battery Life - My old cheapy Tozo NC9s would easily last 6-8 hours (all day). With these I am lucky to get 2-3 hours of listen time before the batteries die. At least once a day I have one ear die in a meeting. My usage is NOT music, just web calls, etc. Comfort - No matter which set of ear adapters I use, I cannot get these things to set comfortably in my ears. They are CONSTANTLY shifting and falling out.

title: Can't go wrong with Anker.
text: These are some of the best ear buds I've ever tried. With the soundcore app you can fine tune these to get incredible sound! Blows Beats out of the water. Noise cancellation is pretty darn good IMO. I also like you can customize the tap commands on the buds to whatever makes sense to you. Comfort is pretty good. They come with several inserts and 'wings' to custom fit to your ears. The only thing I'd say is that they could have a bit more battery life longevity. They seem to charge pretty quick in the case, but wish they'd last a bit longer on one charge. I think I'm getting maybe 5 hours max. Other than that... amazing sound!

title: Keeps turning off
text: These lasted only two months before er had issues. One headphone piece keeps turning off. Says it's dead, then turns kin with a charge, and then turns off again. So basically you're left with one working ear piece, despite them being at a full charge.

title: Better than I expected
text: Feel in love with these. They solve a problem I have at work with 2 phones. They sound great, are comfortable and have become my daily drivers

title: I tried
text: I have the SLP 2 and wanted to really love the SLP 3 but the random disconnects and touch buttons rubbing inside my helmet made me return them. They're not as loud as SLP 2 and the upgrades are noticeable but inconsistent. I'm an iphone user so I decided to get the AirPods Pro. You will sacrifice sound quality but for iphone compatibility its umatched. Siri is awesome to use even while wearing a helmet at slow speed. I love this brand and use the LP2 for the gym. Your experience might be different but if you have an iphone AirPod pro is the way. For the Airpod you will have to upgrade the ear cushion or they'll fall out with moderate activity. I miss that soundstage though so I will wait til next upgrade. Main lesson learned here is your likely going to need more than one brand/set to fit your needs. Good to have a back up anyways.

title: Voice breaks
text: While use in zoom video conference, they say my voice is.breaking many times so I need to switch back wire earphones. Haven't used after that, $120 waste.

title: For the price, this is hard to beat...
text: For those of you that like a nice, clear, and deep bass, these earbuds are quite the treat. The one complaint that I've seen in other reviews that I also experienced was some harsh high-end frequencies. I will say that these are the most comfortable earbuds that I have tried and they are very light. My main problem with the earbuds was the ANC. For me, it was weak, and the ambient pass-thru sounded artificial to me. I already had a pair of AirPods pro and tried out the Bose QC earbuds as well as the Sony XM4 earbuds. Of those, it was a decision between the Soundcore and Sony earbuds. In the end, I decided to go with the Sony's because of the superior ANC and natural sounding ambient sound. I could go either way between the two on quality of music. Plus, it did help that the Sony XM4s price dropped at just the right time. I suspect that after a couple of more firmware updates, the Soundcore earbuds will be right as rain. Also, if they drop below the $150 mark, I say pick 'em up. Nice job, Anker!

title: Keeps disconnecting
text: So I tried these out today over my airpod pros and they keep disconnecting from my phone. Even though my phone is sitting next to me on my desk.

title: Touch controls are maddening
text: Double-tap, and it may register as 1 or 2 individual taps. Triple-tap, best of luck. I remapped the controls so single-taps are volume, long-press is skip track, and double-tap is for play/pause and sound mode. I did do a full reset, as their FAQ recommends for this issue, to no avail. I nearly returned these for this reason, but they sound better than any earbuds I've owned, and the LDAC connection is rock solid on a Note20. No fault of Anker, but be aware that if you choose to pair with more than one device AT THE SAME TIME, it won't be using LDAC on either device due to Bluetooth bandwidth issues. None of the silicone sleeves gave me a good seal. They never do. Order some foam sleeves from Comply. Excellent sound isolation, they're grippy so won't fall out in the gym, and the sound quality you get from a perfect seal justifies the price. I never even bother turning on ANC.

title: Most Reliable earbuds
text: Buy them don't question it. I switched from Beats to Airpods and now these and these are near as good as airpod sound but the build quality, feel, comfort all are superior to the other brands I used before. I say this about these 3 versions not the other ones. It tool them to make these versions to match apple quality. I'm now a customer happy with a soundcore brand built earbud priced at a very reasonable and competitive number.

title: Great sound in a small package.
text: Recently bought, just recently tried. Excellent sound quality. Comes with an array of ear pieces to choose best fit for your ears. Don’t know about battery life, yet.

title: I love Anker products; I wasn't impressed by these earbuds.
text: Short version: I returned the earbuds because the noise cancellation is almost worthless, and mostly comes from having one's ear canals blocked. The automated testing of one's ears is much ado about nothing whatsoever. I couldn't use the one that required a noisy environment, because I don't have a noisy environment. The audio is heavily weighted toward bass with little to no presence, and the amplification is radically weak. I had to use my music app's, BlackPlayer's, ability to ramp up amplification by around 50% plus use it's equalization to get a reasonable sound curve and volume of sound. And finally, the pressure required to get a good sound seal on the earbuds was uncomfortable fairly quickly. I also found the earbuds extremely slick and hard to pick up, though that could be because my hands are dry and/because I'm in an extremely dry environment, but still, having a super smooth/slick surface on a rounded object that has to be picked up with two fingertiips isn't a good ergonomic move. I seriously wanted to like these. The case is awesome, they look cool, and it's Anker — supposedly, Anker at it's best. YMMV

title: I like these so much that I
text: bought three pair so that I had one for each of my six ears. They're seemingly infinitely adjustable with the different inserts and what not that I sort of felt like we had somewhat of a Mr. Potato Head thing going on. Eventually the Mrs and I were able to figure things out and get these cooperating nicely with my other headgear and eye patches. One drawback is that when I have my retainers in there is some kind of resonance effect and I pick up WWV late at night when the ionosphere is highly reflective. Oh, well, take the good with the bad. Excellent audio quality overall. Nice triple stereo adjustment mode for those of us hex-eared listeners. Likely also good for those with only two ears, but you'll have to judge that for yourself.

title: Must have!!!
text: When I bought my first Soundcore earbuds, Liberty Air 2 Pro, after a week I returned it! They kept falling out of my ears and they were not steady. The app was great and that made me to probe more into Soundcore lineup. The Liberty 3 Pro holds a class of its own and there are very few ANC earbuds that can compete with this product. Hands down you are getting your hard earned money's worth by purchasing these earbuds. The app is one of the best interactions I've ever had with an earbuds manufacturer. It's totally customizable and delivers all the sound and tones that your ears desire. The built is solid and it doesn't feel cheap or inferior. The only thing that I hope they fix through software update is getting the ANC from 8 to 10 in my marking. This is of course my ANC ranking and nothing official.

title: Great When Customized
text: The audio is really good if you customize these to your hearing parameters. The battery life is about 3.5 hours if you use ANC and LDAC. It is about 6 hours if you don't.

title: Their okay
text: The earbuds are good, but there is a lot problems for the price. The touch controls are finicky and anc are that good. If you have the liberty 2 pro or the plus, I wouldn't upgrade. I also had connection problems. Everytime I reject a call, audio and media disconnect from the phone.

title: What did you say I can't hear you?
text: Best earbuds ever for the price. Good to use at work for those annoying coworkers tou don't want to hear. The battery life needs to be longer but the quick charge is good. Sound is awesome!!

title: Ok for the price
text: These sound good but there is a problem with anc. When sitting still in a room anc works great. As soon as the surrounding noise level increases the anc stops working. It amplifies the noise. Sometimes it a loud droning noise that comes through. Turn anc off and the background noise is far louder than with headphones that don't have anc. These need a software update to fix this. Also, if you take one out of your ear the audio stops and there is no option for the audio to keep playing. The touch sensors were working fine but now they are acting up. They need better tips. They are worth the price if you just sit around and listen to music or books but if your active look for something else. I'm going back to my Galaxy Buds pro.

title: I love the product but not this one
text: Got these in the right side didn't work faintly heard anything reset multiple times no luck ended up buying some brand new works flawlessly I love them now that's the only reason for the 3 stars

title: Battery life is very short
text: Sound quality is great but Battery life is very short and I will return it today!

title: Great sound to listen to the music
text: These play the music very nicely. It has amazing sound. However, they pick up all sorts of noise when they are used for conversation. I have updated the firmware but that did not fix the issue. I really like them, they are comfortable in the ear as well. So these will be returned.

title: Another great product
text: Anker releases another great product. Loved the earbuds while I had them. Unfortunately I lost one of the earbuds. Back to my old Liberty Pro 2’s. I broke down and bought another pair. Anker makes excellent products

title: Two much twisting, but good sound.
text: When you take it out of the case, you need to twist it 180 to actually use it. When putting it in the ear canal you have to twist them again. Plus the case was very slippery. Making it difficult to 1st begin to use. Overall it's a love and end relationship with this earbud.

title: Love these!
text: Great sound quality! And the look/feel is outstanding. Highly recommended! In fact I'm going to buy a second set - as a present for my adult son.

title: App Makes These Highly Configurable
text: The App gives you a lot of control over the sound of these buds as well as a what the touch controls on each bud do. The App offers an equalizer with presets and customizable settings. In addition, you can use the App to take a hearing test which generates a personalized profile which is surprisingly good. I especially liked how I could reset all of the buds' controls to the settings I prefer. The App is a big Plus for these buds. On the other hand, I'm not sure the ANC did much to block sounds, and even with all the tips and wings, I still couldn't get a secure enough fit for moving around at the gym. Probably you need that secure fit to fully enjoy the passive and ANC noise blocking. That lack of secure fit caused me to return the buds, but that is more about my ears than about the buds. If the gym didn't have a carpeted floor, these would have been history. I was sorry to have to send them back.

title: AMAZING headset!!!!
text: This one is my favorite headset, and I own I think 5 different noise cancelling headsets at this point. I actually also own the little baby brother the NC25 of this one which I also love. They are really close but this one I think wins because of the battery life but the other one folds up to a closer headset so for traveling it would win. A batter of 40+ hours of playtime is incredible, you just can't beat that since you don't have to charge it every day like you would have to with the other one. This headset has other amazing features as well. It paired pretty much instantly without any issues. The volume can go up very high if you really want to destroy your hearing but it allows you really to listen to your music quietly with very good sound quality. The noise cancelling feature works very well and allows you to block out noise you don't want to hear like coworkers or noise on the air plane so you can actually hear the movie you want to watch Not only does the battery last 40+ hours of play back, but also is the battery a fast charge, so it will charge fully in 1-2 towers. In 5 minutes you can get 2+ hours of battery life back into your headset! This is absolutely amazing. This headset will replace the one I have at work right now and will be my go to one for everything. These headsets are super comfortable and lightweight so you barely feel they are there, just like their little baby brother. I can't say enough good things about these and can only recommend them. At $70 plus currently they have a discount of $15. They come with a nice little carrying case, plus a charging cable, an audio cable and an airplane adapter. Just absolutely perfect! So the NC75 pro and NC25 are very comparable. The quality in both is fantastic. The NC25 is smaller but the NC75Pro has a better battery life and is slightly more expensive, so really up to you but you can't go wrong with either really in my eyes.

title: I am suitably impressed
text: These headphones are easy to operate, do a good job cancelling noise in the room from televisions, kids, dogs and husbands. They are also comfortable. They were so simple to set up. I set them up on my laptop. I held in the square button until I heard that the speakers were on. Then I checked my laptop system information and ran the Bluetooth device and there they were. Put on one of my songs and I had to turn the volume down quite a bit. They get plenty loud. I am very impressed with these headphones. I may be swapping out the ones I use nightly for these.

title: Super comfy headphones
text: I got these for working around the house, wearing around work and going for walks. The cups are super squishy and comfy, they sit outside my ears which is ideal to not put pressure on my piercings. I mostly control them with my phone, but the buttons are easy enough to figure out. Even without using the noise cancelling button I can barely hear people though they still try to talk to me. The headphones are a little uncomfortable if you put them around your neck, but that's not what they're meant for. There is a HUGE nonremovale L and R on the corresponding ear cups which is odd but not terrible, you will always know what side goes where. After nearly 3 months of about 5 days weekly use the fabric is pulling up from the cup part, but it should be glueable.

title: Comfortable
text: These headphones are comfortable to wear. The sound quality is not the best, but it's good for the price point.

title: Good for Travel But Bass Isn't Great
text: These are fairly decent for this price point (you can't expect perfection for something less than $100) but when you turn up the volume, the bass is not great and actually sounds a little muffled the higher you go. However, if you like to listen to classical music and soft rock, it's fine. It works using Bluetooth and syncs up easily. The battery power is fine and the controls are easy to use. My only other quibble is the crudeness of labeling the R and L sides of the headphone in can't-miss big print, as if they're made for older people or those with vision problems. I found this detail gave the headphones a slightly tacky feeling. I also like the fact that they fold up neatly inside the included travel case and it doesn't take up that much room in my luggage. It's something I would take on a plane or a train - good enough for a trip but I would use Bose or another high quality headphone when I'm at home listening to music.

title: Look no further then Srythem.
text: I absolutely love these headphones. The ANC works just like you would expect/want them to. Charge time is fast and battery lasts all day long. After I broke (dropped under a riding lawn mower) my last pair by Srythem I came right back to them and purchased another pair. You can't beat the price to quality of these.

title: Updated review for customer service!!
text: For the price, I am shocked at the quality of depth of sound. I listen to house music (edm, techno, trance), and it sounds much better with ANC on; more rich, deeper bass. Bass is just ok with ANC off. The left ear phone will occasionally buzz, even while music is playing but a few taps on the earphone makes it stop. I can put these on and roam about my whole apartment without losing the music. they're large enough to fit over my ears comfortably; I have many ear piercings and wear glasses, and can wear these headphones for an extended period of time, no problem. without the buzzing, this would be a five star product for sure. Edit: I upgraded this review to five stars after working with customer service. I initially contacted them about the buzzing, and they gave me some tips. They worked initially, but then the buzzing got worse period so I contacted them again, and they sent me a brand new pair headphones. They were very easy to work with, which is hard to find these days!

title: Great company
text: I had a problem with mine and they were replace with no hassle. The new one are perfect. Thank you

title: Not for computer
text: Worked fine with a Kindle or my cell phone but seriously wouldn't even work with my son's computer! What kind of headphones don't work for a computer?! Quickly returned.

title: My first pair of noise cancelling headphones
text: Found nothing i didn't like. But it's the first pair of noise cancelling headphones I've ever had. But love em

title: Pretty good, but stopped working
text: I purchased 2 sets of these headphones. One is still being used by the person it was purchased for, and when she's got them on, she hears almost nothing unless you're yelling or knocking to get her attention. MY pair, however, were also good until the left side just stopped working. I had to return them. Also, the volume is dependent on the device it's tethered to, so that was a bit annoying if you want to just use the headphones to turn it up or down.

title: Good looks, VERY comfortable, a bit less volume than some others
text: I got these for my daughter, who finds many headphone types uncomfortable. Not these--they're super plush feeling and among the most comfortable headphones I've tried. The controls are mostly logical and work well, though it is odd that the volume "up" button is below the volume "down" button. In terms of noise reduction, I compared these to my Bose QuietComfort 35's, and they perform about as well. Using white noise as a background sound, these headphones remove more of the low-frequency sound than the Bose. I can't say that one or the other is superior, but the ANC is impressive. Sound quality is fine. These do provide a bit less maximum volume than the Bose headphones. This is a slight issue for men, because I have significant hearing loss. I would think that for most listeners it would be a non-issue, but it did result in 4 stars instead of 5. These come with a basic but perfectly good hard case--a nice touch in this price range.

title: Noise cancellation just increases the volume
text: The noise cancellation button just increases the volume doesn't really cancel the noise

title: Weak construction but good sound quality and noise cancel
text: Something has broken in the left swivel joint and slips apart now from just a year of normal use right after warranty expired. I expected better construction for the price. UPDATE: The company reached out to replace my unit so good on them! The sound is good and cancels noise well enough to drown talking around me. Just be sure to connect to the "Stereo" device for music instead of the "headset" device which will not sound any good for music.

title: Works great for me.
text: Okay these are not Sony or Bose head phones. But these are perfect for what I need and if they get damaged or lost I won't sweat it. The sound volume is pretty good. The sound quality is good. Battery life is great. Noise cancelling is not great but better that nothing at all. Would by again for sure.

title: Great product for the price!
text: Just got these but did a decent test of them. They are very comfortable and appear to be made of good quality materials. The sound quality is decent and the noise cancellation is unbeatable for the price. Obviously its not Bose quality however it easily drowns out background noise while you can clearly hear someone who is talking to you. Great set would reccomend 100% for the price.

title: Revised review
text: New model sent to me at no cost. Works well.

title: Great product. Excellent value.
text: Very happy with these headphones. Right out of the box, I was able to connect via Bluetooth to my iPhone and immediately listen to music. The sound quality was really good. The power button is easy to find. Press for 3 seconds to turn on and a voice from the says “Power on. Connected”. Press for another 3 seconds and the voice says “Power off”. I love that they really took the guesswork out of this and I didn’t have a project to figure out how to use these. No batteries. Rechargeable. Comes with a USB charging cable (no charging block. Also comes with a short cord for powered devices that are not Bluetooth. Very comfortable ear pads! Easily adjustable for different size heads/ears. Also really like that the right and left are clearly marked on the INSIDE of the earphones (where it does not show from the outside) in a BIG letter L and R. There is also an attractive L and R on the outside, much smaller. Overall, a great value, good product. Very happy with it.

title: Impressive product!
text: Impressive product，the build quality was better than i expected. The noise cancellations only work for air plane engine like sound, normal talking you still can listen what people saying. Sound quality, mids and high were good, not a punchi bass headphone but is enough. The foam was comfortable, my ear was big and it can cover well for my ear. Good value product, highly recommended.

title: Noise canceling works great
text: Very helpful for autistic teenager, they love it. The ANC has helped them block out unwanted sounds, and the overall sound quality of the headphones is very good for the price point.

title: Got these as a present
text: My husband is a musician and really picky about his headphones. He absolutely loves these. Says it helps him hear more and crisper sounds. They arrived quickly and in a wonderful case. Great instructions.

title: Whoa, great headphones!
text: Im blown away at the quality of them especially for the price. Nice crisp sound quality. Decent noise canceling as well. Set up was easy too.

title: Mostly Good
text: Pros: Very very comfortable Pairs easily even with previous versions of Bluetooth Well made Sounds very clear and balanced with nice highs, mids and good bass Outstanding noise cancellation Cons: Does not sound good when Bluetooth audio streams from my TV ---- I have a feeling the audio quality issue I am having with streaming Bluetooth from my television may be due to a somewhat older Bluetooth transmitter I am using. My TV did not come with Bluetooth capability built in. The transmitter works great with my older headphones but they used an earlier version of Bluetooth and both had the same AptX codecs. I am going to purchase a new 5.0 Hi-Def transmitter and see if that fixes the issue. Will update if it does.

title: Pleasant surprise
text: Wow! I decided to take a chance on a cheaper pair of Bluetooth headphones. So happy I did. These have a great sound, fit my ears and head well, and I full submerged in the music. No problem with some of my more bass music like rap and alternative. It came packages well and with a lot of extra attachments if you decide not to use Bluetooth. I have not had them long enough to know if they will hold the charge over time..

title: Customer Service is Excellent
text: Update: Customer service reached out to me to replace the defective unit I received even though I was well outside the 30 day return window. I will review again if I have any problems with the replacement but so far so good. Impressive customer service makes up for a one off defect, I'm happy. Previous Review: One ear sputters in and out, bad enough to make these useless. Unfortunately past the 30 day return window. Poor quality, will fail. Please don't waste your money like I did.

title: Impressive for the price range.

I know I could buy more expensive / higher technology units but these do very well at this price range.

title: For the price, a great deal

This does come very close and for less than 100 dollars, is a very good deal. Easy to use, trebles and midranges are clear.

title: Great Gift for Collage Student
text: Purchased for my Daughter in college. She liked the color and the fit. Said the active noise cancelling works Great And Really liked the color.

title: Samsung fridge could not keep for 2 people

title: Only makes a little ice at a time
text: My review might be unfair as this is the first portable ice maker I've had and I have no basis for comparison. I'm not sure if I'm happy I got it or not. Bought for use in motorhome when camping. It takes probably 10 minutes or more to produce 7 or 8 small (the setting is for large) ice cubes. Then you have to remove them right away and put in freezer otherwise they will melt while sitting in the ice maker. So its alot of getting up and down to do this if you are making several batches. Kinda a pain in the butt, but if you need ice cubes for a couple of drinks, then I guess its a lifesaver. Maybe I didn't spend enough to get an icemaker that makes more cubes at a time? The red color is pretty snazzy though.

title: Very nice and simple
text: [[VIDEOID:eca310af931d29066fe6d85b77042b27]] I received this as a gift. Very nice works great ice comes fairly quickly I love how smooth the ice is , clean fresh taste, and easy to use, it makes noise but not to where it bothers you. Make sure to sit upright for 24hr before turning it on to make ice, clean with distilled water with mild detergent soap ( Read Manual For Directions )and use filtered water! READ THE MANUAL FIRST !!! title: Good ice maker but stopped working - 8 months old
text: Makes ice fine, gets icky / slimy within a few days. Quit working a few days ago, bought it in July last year so it has not even been a year.

title: Might work for you

title: Well worth the money

title: Did not work

title: Worked for 18 months..
text: I LOVED this for 18 months, but METAL parts in WATER = rusty ice. First I noticed a couple months ago there was orange residue in my tank. I got one of these for my dad, and his gets yucky because he uses tap water. I ONLY use filtered store bought water. I have a cup that gets ZERO residue so I know it's clean water. So I assumed I got bad water, cleaned it out and refilled it. I noticed orange dripping down the right 6 'arm' and AGAIN got orange residue. I watched a video and saw him take the thing apart and open up the motor in the right 'arm' and what do you know, it's metal and it RUSTED! It's RUSTING INTO MY WATER! And it rusted stuck and no longer rotates correctly! I do not have a garage of tools like the video guy, so I just have to BUY A NEW ICE MAKER! This is a HORRID design, metal in WATER?! I didn't give it 0 stars because it DOES work for 18 months.. but what a waste of money to be drinking rust water! PLEASE make one w/ a non-metal motor thingy! Anyway, it's not JUST rusty, the thing is rusted tight and doesn't rotate so it doesn't know when to make ice, and keeps thinking the ice is full.. But the machine still WANTS to work at times, but w/out the metal thing rotating it isn't able to. IF I had a garage I'd fix it, but I do not.

title: Works great!
text: So I was hesitant with some negative reviews. As with any mechanical thing, always a chance to get a dud so never assume they all are. This is not restaurant grade ice maker. All home ice makers will put out wet ice and store it in insulated area, not refrigerated. For that you need to look at restaurant grade.. and the price as well. No thanks. Here's the way to do this for best results. Before you need it, the day before, make ice. You don't want wet ice for your drinks. Use refrigerated cold water, not room temperature. After a couple of ice dumps put them in a large zip lock freezer bag and put it in the freezer until after another couple dumps, take it out and add to it, and on. When you need it the next day and it's stuck together, while bag is still zipped, a simple fist to it will break it up nicely. I use the water till it's not enough for more. I use viva paper towels and wipe it down dry. Then to prevent mold mildew possibly forming I put a nylon sock with raw white rice in it and put a sticky pad to keep the lid a little ajar. Love this machine. I don't have room for store bought size so I create 1 gallon size zip loc bags for my needs where I can place it where it fits in my full freezer.

title: Very noisy
text: Bought this in January of 2020 to replace a different manufacturer's machine that quit working after 3 years. It was much noisier than my previous one, but I finally got use to the noise. Today, September 3rd, when I went to get ice out of it, water was all over the floor. I thought the drain plug on the bottom had come out, but that wasn't the problem. It is leaking from the water pump every time the pump starts running. When the pump stops, the leak stops. Very disappointed that it didn't even last a year. The 90 day warranty doesn't do me any good, so this will be going to the bulk trash pickup. Time to look for yet another manufacturer. Update: Changed my rating from 2 stars to 3. I was able to remove the cover and found the leak. The water supply hose was rubbing against the refrigerant line, and created a hole in the hose. I was able to repair the leak, and now it's working again. The continuous running motor that fills the ice tray and releases the ice was making the excessive noise. I'm going to try and add some acoustic foam in the case next to the motor to see if that will eliminate some of the noise. 2nd Updtae: It is now March 6, 2023, and the ice maker has stop making ice. Sometimes it will fill the water tray, but the compressor isn't cycling on to make the ice cubes. Other times, it won't even pump water into the tray. I used it almost every day for 3 + years, so I guess I just finally wore it out. Worked really well, until it stopped working. title: This ice maker has paid for itself it 5 weeks and keeps working fine about 24 hours a day 3 or four days ...
text: This is as honest a review as you can read. I trust other's reviews on Amazon and have had alomst zero trouble with 99.9% of all of the items I have oredered over the last five years. The same can be said...so far...of my Igloo portable ice maker. I have had it running almost non-stop for over two months on a boat and it has performed admirably. It really does make ice every 6 or 7 minutes and every hour or so there is a full 1.5lb basket of ice. There are reviews which say that it is cheaper to go to the convenient store and buy a bag of ice. True, unless you need 2 bags a day for three months. This ice maker has paid for itself it 5 weeks and keeps working fine about 24 hours a day 3 or four days a week. The only thing I would say is that it is not , in fact, quiet. It can be loud and it sounds like it is working a little too hard with mechanical sounds which make you wonder how long this thing will last. BUT...so far so good. It has earned its price and I will get another one if this one fails. It is simply awesome to get 25 punds of ice a day out of this little cool looking machine. I love it and every day that it works, it saves me money!

title: So far sort of so good.
text: We owned a similar ice maker for a few years until it just stopped operating. I hope this lasts as long. There are a myriad of ice makers that use the same principle and we pretty much threw a dart at the board to decide. It does make ice as advertised. However, the ice basket fills well before it reaches the advertised two pound capacity. The "automatic shut off" works sporadically at best: It tends to freeze up (sorry) when it can't put more ice in the basket and it's annoying to clean out the supply tray and get it restarted. The say to avoid "cubes"--they're actually bullet shaped cylinders with a hollow core-- to use the small setting, OK, but then you get considerable less ice per cubic foot since the hollow core is the same size, but the ice around it is smaller. If you have patience and pay attention, this will churn out a good deal of ice in a day, but it requires a good deal of attention and it's pointless to try to make ice when you can't check the basket frequently. If you want to make the advertised 26 pounds in 24 hours, you had better not plan on getting more than 11 minutes sleep at a time. I'm glad to have it, but don't think you're going to get a mini-hotel-quality machine. BTW, Amazon's "rating features" in addition to asking about ease of use and noise, asked me to rate its "flavor." Sorry, I wouldn't know.

title: Broke after 7 months (and wasn't great to begin with)
text: This icemaker was mediocre while it worked, and didn't take too long to break. When we first bought the icemaker, the biggest issue I immediately found is that it's very challenging to clean. There's no easy way to access most of the internals that need cleaning the most, and I ended up buying a variety cleaning brush set just to work on it. Worse, even with filtered or distilled water, the system still gets gunky very vast, and mold will start to grow in the hard-to-reach corners of the system quickly. When it did run, I discovered several issues that made the system frustrating to use. First, it's noisy, draws a lot of electricity (equivalent to a mini-fridge three times its size), there's almost no insulation in the ice tray so ice melts very fast, runs out of water very vast, and worst of all, constantly clumps, resulting in nowhere near full baskets of ice; the system needs an agitator or something to knock down freshly frozen cubes or they pile up and stop with less than a quarter bucket. The biggest issue however, is that it broke irreparably after only half a year of use. The left-side spindle for the freeze bucket and paddle (a critical component) fractured and twisted, meaning that it can't fully cycle, and the machine errors out and flashes all lights. Resetting the device just causes it to immediately jam after homing again. As an engineer, I don't see an effective food-safe way to resolve this. I'm going to attempt to make a manufacturer warranty claim as I'm outside the return period but I don't have high hopes. Avoid this product and the thousands of clones that look like it; they're all the same product with different badges. EDIT: Manufacturer came through; they did honor the warranty and replace the device with a slightly larger and newer model, but I did have to jump through some hoops to get it, and it was a challenge to even figure out who to contact. The person I worked with via e-mail almost had an air of "ugh, this isn't worth my time", and we had to wait ~1 month for them to send a replacement. So still not recommended, but at least I wasn't completely SoL on this one.

title: UPDATED FROM 1-STAR (PLEASE READ)
text: Used this icemaker 24-7 for nearly a year until it began leaking water. Took cover off to investigate. Turns out an assembly defect or manufacturing defect. They routed the water hose around the cooling fan for the hot coils. Then the water hose rested on one of the copper hot coils which melted a hole through the tubing. Bought an 1/8" straight barb splicer fitting and re-joined the tubing and routed it away from the heat coil with some zip ties. All fixed and may now last many more years. Thing is built quality but then they dropped the ball and routed the water tube over the hot coils. Update: 9/2022. The manufacturer reached out to me after the bad rating and offered me $26 refund. They informed me that they reported the design flaw of routing the water hose near the heat coils and that engineering was going to be changing that. They seem to care about their product and will upgrade and improve it if they discover weak points about its design. One thing they could do to really make it great would be to offer a direct connection to pressurized water supply and use the signal that turns on the refill pump to instead or optionally open an electronic valve to a water supply that would automatically keep it filled with water. That would make this thing 100% complete. Works well but refilling it manually every day is the only usage drawback.

title: Broke after one ice cycle
text: 100% garbage, DO NOT BUY. Followed instructions to the letter. Made one (1) batch of ice, then it died. No ice at all was being made, even though it was being fed continuously by a 3 gal water bottle placed on top. Upon continued attempts at cycle activation, I could see that water was being pumped into ice-making tray, and it did fill up properly. However, 15 sec after the compressor turned on I heard the click of a relay that shut down the compressor. Removed plug, plugged back in and turned back on several times, all with same result...compressor kept shutting down. Then I noticed through the vent that the heat exhaust fan was rocking back and forth 1/4", as if it couldn't decide in which direction to rotate. Clearly the high heat safety shutoff switch was being activated because the fan wasn't removing heat from the unit. So this unit was essentially broken right out of the box. Awaiting UPS pick-up, on its way back to Amazon exactly ONE day after it arrived. Note: I purchased this exact same unit from Amazon three years ago, but it was distributed by a different Chinese vendor, and until recently it had worked great. The coolant finally leaked out and the compressor began shutting down due to high heat relay tripping, but not due to fan problems. The fan was still working great. So I know how the fan is supposed to run on this unit, and this new one was definitely faulty.

As a result of surface area (physics) it will cool a drink faster the more ice in the glass as opposed to larger cubes. I find it works great for smoothies or cocktails better (think margaritas) than larger ice cubes. It tends to blend faster and be a better consistency as opposed to cubes. I also feel that the blender isn't working as hard or dulling the blades. I am not going to lie, I didn't really need this one. text: I intend to update this review every couple months, as I've read plenty of reviews talking about the longevity of the machine. I made sure to follow all the instructions, and the one that almost got me was "Let it sit for an hour for coolant to settle before plugging it in", because the first thing I instinctively tried to do was plug it in; watch out for this, haha. I set this up in my garage because I wasn't sure how loud it would be. Turns out it is rather quiet - just the sound of running water and the occasional clatter of ice cubes. I was afraid it wouldn't work in the 80-90°F heat of the garage, but it has proven me wrong yet again. It works just fine, and dispenses ice around every 13-17 minutes. It's definitely wet ice - I believe that's due to the way the water runs. So my plan is to run it for a few cycles at a time, bag the ice, and store it in my freezer. Then I can bust it apart easier when it refreezes together. One of the reasons I got it was to put a container of water on top and not have to fill it manually every couple pounds of ice. I wish they would list a compatible barrel/jug, because that has been the biggest struggle. The way the cover folds out, it is in the way when trying to use standard 5 or 3 gallon barrels (I had 5 gallons on hand, and made a purchase of 3 gallon to test). With a little wiggling, the cover can be removed and the 3 gallon standard barrel fits, but only if the barrel has no lid. So I put the adapter (included) on the barrel and hoisted it on, and with only a little bit of spilled water and a few minutes trying to balance it, it's working. It is a little flimsy, and needs to be balanced, as it feels like it's bending the top of the machine a bit, but I've had it up there for a while and it seems to be fine. This is my second update, and update again in a month or sooner if it goes kaput.

title: Almost silent. Well built. Works much better than expected.
text: Retired EE, I bought this to 'cannibalize' for its cute little refrigeration system for another project. I was pleased that the factory packaging was so well done. Every scratchable surface was protected with removable film. Nice long cord with very high quality AC plug (right angle, so cord easily fits tight against wall if needed). So I had to test it thoroughly before taking it apart. Simple, clever, quiet. Made lots of ice. Very clever design. Here's how it works: 1. The controller opens a valve in the bottom of the upper tank, allowing a few ounces of water into the bottom of the ice compartment. 2. A little 12V motor pumps this small amount of water (from the bottom of the ice compartment) through a 'drip bar' over the top of the metal ice cube tray while the refrigerator/compressor chills the metal tray. 3. Ice starts forming in the square pockets of the metal tray. Any water that doesn't freeze and stick to the metal tray is recirculated by the pump back up through the drip bar again. 4. After 9 or 10 minutes (depending on the ambient temperature), when the ice has nearly filled up the square 'pockets' of the metal tray, the controller opens a valve in the 'high side' refrigeration line, allowing a bit of the Hot refrigerant to heat the metal tray, releasing the cubes which fall down into the collection basket; then closes this valve, restoring normal refrigeration of the metal tray. (Controller repeats these steps every 9 to 12 minutes). Neat! While taking it apart, I was impressed with every aspect of how it was built. All wiring insulation was of the highest caliber, every possible 'rubbing/chafing' spot was protected, all cabling tied down with cute high quality cable ties, all hoses and fittings of highest quality. I would expect this thing to last at least ten years. Well Done! The wires were all terminated with high quality connectors, all properly protected with heatshrink tubing, some of the wiring with high temp silicone insulation. Nothing cheap anywhere. All the molded plastics were of the highest quality. Impressive! These pictures show how well everything was put together. (The last shot shows the working "guts" I saved for my project.) Great unit! I'd buy another but I don't need ice. Great price for the quality.

It’s a nice looking unit to sit on your counter top and doesn’t take up to much room, but it does have to have some space to discharge the warm air from the unit. They have a button to push for 5 seconds to put the unit in self cleaning mode, and it runs for 20 minutes. But what does it actually do during that 20 minutes?? Because if you have owned an ice machine before they get slimy and smelly after 2-3 or 4 weeks of not cleaning properly. So in the instructions under Automatic Self-Cleaning program they post a “WARNING” that says Make sure the water tank, water filter, and the water separator pipe is not blocked, Clean Them. it tells you about 90% of what you need to do/know on how to clean the unit. During heavy use like parties and such you should clean the unit afterwards. Normal use about every 15-20 days if you want that clear fresh tasting ice. So besides pushing the self-cleaning button to run for 20 minutes, you need to manually clean the main places… Which is the water reservoir tank, the water filter and the water separator pipe. On this unit the hardest part I can see from experience is the cleaning of the water separator pipe. Getting it out isn’t to bad but putting it back in is a pain in the butt as described in the video. Also the drain plug doesn’t twist out and doesn’t pull out very easy either. On an igloo machine they use a soft gel plug that is easy to pull out and put back in with no leaks. The unit is ranked number 1 by some people, but not by me. I wish they would try the unit out themselves at home to see that they have a few more changes to do that would truly set themselves apart from the other units for sale

Anyway, the machine was a pain to install, but that's not its fault. First I hired someone because they had to move my fridge, tap a water line, and break through the wall to install the drain. They screwed all of that up and I ended up with a leak, a damaged fridge, and the drain line was leaking as well. They fixed two of the three a week later and now it works well (though the fridge is another story). The instructions were poor, that caused some of the problem (even the professional misread them). I mean, if you're selling a $500 product, can't you afford proper instructions with real pictures written by someone who speaks English? All that aside, there is one thing I took off a star for: The unit doesn't stay frozen! It makes ice and dumps it in a fridge. It melts because that is a fridge not a freezer. And then it makes more ice. This causes a lot of wasted water and electricity, and it means that you absolutely must have that drain line installed! I had another one of these some time back that cost a lot less and made about half as much ice a day. That one was insulated and stayed below 0, so the ice never melted! I didn't even connect the drain line and in 4 years of use, it never leaked. If I were to go back to the start of this project, I would have gotten that again. That's the reason I took off a star. title: Sonic ice? Sort of.
text: I'll get to the "Sonic Ice" part below. The ice maker required no assembly at all when it came out of the box, but instructions in two places said it needed to sit upright before use so that the refrigerant could settle into place. Instructions plastered to the maker said 24 hours; those in the manual said 1 hour. I let it sit overnight--it was fine. Instructions suggested cleaning out the maker with warm soapy water, and I'd say that's good advice since I found several hair-like strings of glue around some of the joints. There's a small plug on the underside to drain the water from inside once cleaning is finished. When the lid is lifted, you look in and see a plastic basket which sits towards the top of the machine in the front half. The ice drops in here when it is formed. (The back half is where the ice makes.) The "water tank" is just the area below the basket, and when you fill it with water, you have to be sure not to let it come up to the bottom of the basket. A pump pulls the water up into the back half of the maker to make the ice, which takes maybe five minutes or so. HERE"S THE CRUCIAL PART: There is no "freezer" aspect to this maker. Once the ice drops in the basket, it sits there until it melts back into the water tank if you don't use it. I think the maker must monitor the weight of the basket to trigger the mechanism to make more, as it will keep the basket full. SONIC ICE? Well, sort of. It has a different shape--that hollow bullet shape--but because the maker doesn't store the ice at freezing temperatures, it's 'softer' to chew than ice from a refrigerator freezer. VERY HAPPY WITH THE PRODUCT! It's quiet, except for those moments when the ice rattles into the basket. We turn it off at night. Keeps my wife in all the ice she can chew!

title: Am I on a different planet?
text: Based on most of the reviews everyone raves about the great taste of the water after installing this filter. I had the opposite occur. After installing I experienced no improvement in water taste. In fact, my water tasted salty. So I took TDS meter to measure the TDS of my filtered water and it was 401. My unfiltered water is 423. I looked through the installation instructions and under "Frequently asked questions" was the statement: "The main purpose of the Waterdrop filter is NOT to remove TDS." But the reason my water tastes so horrible is because of the high TDS! The customer service rep was very good and attentive to my needs. I give them kudos for that-- good customer service. And they did state clearly on the Amazon website what there filter would filter. Never did they say that the TDS would be lowered. I guess I didn't ask the right question... But if you are buying this filter to eliminate TDS, this is not the system for you.

The design of the "arm" that detects when the ice bin is full is nothing like the one in the original GE product that came with our freezer. This one regularly gets stuck in the "up" position when ice gets stuck behind it, which tricks the ice maker into thinking the bin is full, which in turn causes it to stop making ice. I have to constantly check it and remove ice to get the arm to snap back into place. It's really just an extremely poor substitute for the original GE ice maker." I was also appalled to find out it has only a 30 day warranty and Amazon doesn't give a hoot what happens after that period.

Our drinking water is pretty close to distilled water. I left the unit plugged in and opened the drain on the back of the unit. Once drained I refilled the machine with bottled drinking water. The machine is back to cranking out ice and all the bad noises have stopped. I think it is even more quiet than the first time I ran it. So far, I have made around 45 to 50 pounds of ice. Unit is working great now. WARNING! Do not use distilled water, or water from a reverse osmosis system. Can't say why but changing water made the machine run great. I would recommend this machine.

text: We read so many reviews and many spoke of how loud the machine was but others didn’t mention noise so we took the plunge. Big mistake.
