It’s expected that when dropping ice it would be loud, but the motor and fan running are ridiculous. We loved the convenience so tried everything to hold onto it. We moved it all over trying to find that one spot where the sound level wouldn’t annoy us. We even cleared a shelf inside our pantry but even with the pantry door closed the motor was loud. In reading reviews for nearly every counter top maker, the main complaint was the noise level. Even those priced well over $600. Our first intention was to spend more and get a different brand, but we now know it doesn’t matter. Noise is a global issue regardless of brand or price point. We learned that after watching tons of video reviews for so many models. In short, if you’re willing to live with the noise get it. We had to surrender and return it. I’m so disappointed because it’s a workhorse and pushes out ice so fast. Every counter top ice maker on the market today has noise level reviews that would allow you to rethink your purchase. When shopping you may also want to research how to maintain cleanliness and mold. I understand that’s a challenge too. In closing we did wind up returning it. I kid you not, the person on line at the UPS store in front of me had the very same box and was retuning hers. I asked her why. She said it was so loud they didn’t even give it a chance to make ice. They unplugged it, put it back in the box, and made an immediate choice to return it.

title: Worth Every Penny
text: There are undoubtedly cheaper ice machines on the market, but I consider this one well worth the total $160 or so that I spent on it. I'm physically disabled and living in an assisted-living facility where the aides are stretched very thin. I hate to ask them for little niceties like a cup of ice, and now that I have my neat little ice machine there's no need to ask anyone for ice, whenever I want it. The on-site maintenance guy was able to get my ice machine set up and working in literally minutes, and within a quarter of an hour I had my first batch of ice. I chose the "small" setting, which results in little hollow "bullets" of ice, per the product photo. The ice machine does make some noise, but I find it fairly easy to ignore, even at night. The ice machine does need to have water added to its tank occasionally, but that's very easy to do, and I've only had to add water twice this past five days. This little ice machine was a great purchase!

title: Works quickly but the ice is so wet is waters down drinks
text: The ice maker pumps ice out quickly. The noises it makes are easy to ignore in the background. The only thing that we really don’t like is how wet the ice is. Because the machine works so fast it doesn’t have time to freeze the ice hard. It’s like taking ice out of a glass of water and putting it in the bin. Not a problem if you’re just having ice water but if your drink has flavor (soda for example), it tends to get watered down quickly. We’ve tried using ice water to begin with hoping the few extra degrees would help it freeze better while being made and it doesn’t make a noticeable difference. If we dump it in the ice bin in the freezer it all just becomes one big block due to the extra water. We’ve resorted to putting a dish towel on a cookie tray, followed by a silicone baking mat. As the bin fills we dump it on the tray, put it in the freezer and then bust it off to fill the ice cube bin. The towel we use to absorb the runoff is usually frozen solid by the time we get the ice bin full. A lot of extra work for something that was supposed to make our life easier but we’re outside our return window so we’re trying to make the most of it.

title: The icemaker worked great for this use although the quantity of ice we ...
text: We bought this for use in an RV. It's worked flawlessly for 3 months now. We make several bags of ice to store in the freezer, then pull this machine back out when we need more. So we don't use it continuously. As they advertise, we get our first ice within minutes of turning it on. The tray fills up in less than an hour and we bag it for the freezer. We took the icemaker to Disneyworld and used it to make ice continuously for 10 days. That ice was used to keep drinks cold in a large 40-quart ice chest. The icemaker worked great for this use although the quantity of ice we could produce was a little low for such a large ice chest. Once we got the drinks cold, this icemaker made just enough ice to keep drinks cold. We use distilled water to keep particulates out. We primarily use the small "cube" setting because these are just right for drinking glasses. So it's all about the quantity of ice that you need. For relatively low usage for perhaps 2-3 people, this icemaker is what you need. It's produces a low hum which isn't overly noisy except when ice is plunking into the tray every few minutes. I'm very happy with this icemaker.

text: So far so good, although I'm not sure the automatic shut-off works. Basket was full this morning and it was still producing ice.... My one negative would be that the ice is connected and not cubes. But still functional! But if you are expecting individual cubes, that's not what you will get. More like a lump of ice that can be broken up.

title: Great little ice maker
text: Got this for my mom to use when guest come to visit. She loves it.

title: Five Stars
text: This thing works great. I have a small apartment, and doesn't take up much room.

title: Not really worth the price - very small ice storage
text: It does make ice. 28 lbs per day might be a stretch. You'd have to stand by and wait for it to fill with ice, empty the bin into something else and keep going. It does make ice relatively quickly but it only holds a small bin worth of ice (like a small refrigerator ice maker tray). I returned ours. Not worth the cost. I'll just save up for an ice maker that connects to a water supply and has more ice storage area. This might be ok for a camper or something like that but it's not a small unit so the space taken might not justify the small amount of ice produced.

title: Works great in Afghanistan!
text: Lack of ice in the "stan" was the norm, until I received the ice maker in just 5 days from seller. Ran a couple of batches through with a little lemon juice and put it into operation, makes ice as quick as you can fill it. It holds about six bottles of water and although it is not a freezer the ice remains for quite a while. Very quiet, requires very little electricity, worth every penny!!! Will purchase one for the deck when I get home.

title: Recieved just in time for 104 degree weather!!
text: We bought this because both my Hubby and I had a painful time trying to twist our ice trays. We unpacked this --an adventure in itself -- and Hubby cleaned it out and we started the ice making. We tried all three sizes and I prefer the small ones , he prefers the medium and large ones. One gallon of water fills the machine and equals about two gallon sized zipper freezer bags of cubes. Actually, the ice is more bullet shaped, being formed over steel posts. So the hollow part is fun, because they "burb" when they turn over! The unit is fairly quiet, and after the first time we hardly hear it. Recommended for anyone in a small household.

title: I like the choice of ice sizes
text: I have purchased two of these already because they last exactly 22 months. I like the choice of ice sizes. I love the size of the ice bucket. Other than their durability, it is a great machine. It is very disappointing because I had to buy a third ice maker this week and went with a different brand. It is much smaller but it was also half the price of this one. I can't keep buying new ice makers every 22 months.

title: Wonderful Ice maker for parties!
text: We have had this for about a month, and it makes lots of ice fast. I wouldn't want to leave it on all the time, just to make it last longer. Seems best to turn on the morning you will have a party for that night, or the night before for the next afternoon. It isn't a freezer, so it will not keep ice forever after it's made, but when I unplug mine and let it sit, it will keep the ice for about an extra day, and then it melts into the holding tank inside. We are thrilled with it and have used it several times. Really works great! Superbowl parties, clam bakes, crawfish boils, or whatever you are into. This thing is great. They even make a higher capacity one for sale on amazon as well. This one makes a lot of ice! Depends on what your needs are. Could work for big boats, hunting and fishing cabins, ski villas, tailgating if you have electric, and anywhere you need lots of ice for your friends.

title: First one worked the second one didn't!
text: I bought one of these in 2015 and it worked perfectly for over two years until two months ago when it finally died. Fortunately for me I bought the extended Warranty from Assurant and they quickly cut me a check for the full purchase price and I bought a second one to replace the old one. Unfortunately it only worked for one day and then it died. Regretfully the manufacturer is willing to honor their warranty but only if I will pay to ship the ice maker to them. I am trying to decide what I am going to do. Whatever you do get the extended warranty it is more than worth it.

title: Great for camping.
text: We purchased a second one for at home. Works fast and is extremely easy to use. Perfect for outdoor added ice needs.

title: Not for me...
text: D.O.A. Sent back, and from my experience, am not going to try another. Does take up counter space, which was kind of expected, but its just really not going to save that time or effort of filling up ice cube trays...

title: lasted about 1 and 1/2 years
text: was working great- used every single day- and last week it died- very disappointed for the amount of money it cost- going back to ice cube trays

title: A Worthwhile Purchase
text: In April 2014, we purchased the NewAir icemaker to use on our boat. We were on a 10 week Chesapeake Bay cruise between late April and early July. During this time, the unit performed admirably - we had to purchase ice only one time when we linked up with several friends. Otherwise our NewAir AI-100R was our sole source of ice for two people. A couple of times, during very warm days, the unit's production was a bit anemic, but tolerable.

title: Five Stars
text: I can't begin to put into words how convenient and fast this machine is

title: More than met our need
text: I bought this item for my wife, who every day would keep filling her big Nalgene container with ice and her combination of ice tea and lemonade (and our daughters were copying her). Even though we have a built-in ice maker in our Sub Zero, it was not keeping up, and we ended up buying bags of ice from the store to have enough. This new ice maker has solved the problem. It makes cubes every 6 minutes, and produces more than enough. We have not run out since. I have only two negative observations: one is that if we don't use the ice right away (like overnight), it melts into the reservoir (where the water is recycled into more ice cubes), and if we want to use the residual ice it is melted into small pieces or is stuck together. But that hasn't been a big deal, and when we are using lots of ice it doesn't have a chance to melt away. The other is that the ice did have a plastic smell/taste for awhile. That was lessened by running vinegar solution though it a couple of ice cycles, and it finally went away with time. The ice is fine now. We keep it near the sink for convenience of refilling the reservoir. I like the portability, and plan to take it to our family reunion this summer to increase our available ice, since we go through lots of it there.

title: We thought we would use it just in the summer and it is as good for the winter months
text: Our family fell inlove with tis item. We thought we would use it just in the summer and it is as good for the winter months.

title: Don't get too excited...
text: We bought this ice maker because we have burned out every ice maker that had come with our fridges in the past and we were having to buy ice and refill the bin every 2 days and it was getting really old. This machine sounded like the best (most affordable option). I knew it wasn't a commercial ice maker ($$$) but I thought it would do. I turned it on Saturday morning, ran it all day long and filled 1 and a half gallon size ziploc bags. If I keep up at that pace, I can always have a stash in the freezer but if we have a party or need to fill a cooler then we are back to buying bagged ice to meet the need. It spits out 12 ice cubes (in large setting) every hour or so. My other issue is that is is wet ice so when you freeze it the whole bag clumps up, easily solved by dropping the bag on the floor a couple time before loading in the ice maker or ice bucket but I wish it made more, faster and less wet. I found that I had to run over and get the 12 cubes in the freezer right away rather than letting the bin fill because the first batch would be melting. Sounds like a fun weekend? Overall opinion.... It's just 'OK', not great.

title: NOISY!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
text: It makes ice ok, but when it sucks up the wather it is so noisy the wall shakes!! I'm not kidding, you can hear it throughout the entire house. Basically, I turn it on when nobodys home, then store the made ice in the freezer and turn the thing off. Wish I had never bought it.

title: This is one of the best items I have bought for the RV
text: This is one of the best items I have bought for the RV. Its nice to have all the ice you need.

title: Works well indoors
text: I have used this at my camper a lot and found that if it is in an enviroment under 75 degrees it will work well. The storage tray is small so I bag the ice it makes and place in the frezzer and before the end of the day I have enough for my drink cooler for the next day. but for a big cooler would be hard to store enough ice to fill it but for me it works good.

title: BEWARE
text: This ice maker worked great for 13 months and then died. It came with a 12 month warranty. Too bad. BEWARE!!!

title: This thing is a WIN!
text: This thing works well and fast! We live in an older house and don't have the hook ups for a built-in refrigerator ice-maker. Everyone loathes refilling ice cube trays and the pain of trying to get the cubes out of the tray. Bought this ice-maker to solve that problem. SO glad we did! Takes up about the same space as a bread machine. Easy set up, easy use, easy maintenance and clean up! Indicator lights tell you when you need more water or when the ice basket is full. Keeps the made ice cold like a cooler would. As the ice melts, the water drips back into the reservoir to simply turn it back into ice. We use it to stock our ice bucket we keep in the freezer. We also just use the handy scoop it comes with and we grab ice straight from the machine. It's quiet and doesn't heat up the house at all with the motor's fan. Only sound we ever hear is when it drops the ice into the basket. You pretty much unpack it, plug it in and it's ready to go. Of course, I cleaned it first and threw out the first couple batches of ice in case of cooties, but that's just me. We tried the ice on the small setting and decided we preferred the medium. Haven't tried large yet. It's nice to know that if I go to the store and buy a warm beverage and come home to no ice, I only have to wait about 10 minutes from the time I press the power button on the ice-maker until we're good to go. Sure beats putting a can in the freezer and forgetting about it. My folks like it for their RV too.

title: Five Stars
text: The product arrived on time and set up was effortless. Works as advertised.

title: Five Stars
text: this is the greatest works better than my last ice maker!

title: Quit working after two weeks
text: Worked great for two weeks and then quit making ice. Seems to be cycling normally, just not getting cold enough any more. I have contacted the company for replacement under the one year warranty, I will update this review as we go through the process.

title: Paid for itself in the first month
text: I use this in my basement when having people over and it's a fantastic way to avoid running up and down the stairs all night for ice, or dealing with an ice bucket that melts the ice in no time at all. True to it's word, you can get the first cubes of ice within 9 minutes of turning it on. If hosting company, just turn it on an hour before anyone arrives and as long as you check on it periodically to add water (maybe a couple times throughout the course of an afternoon/night) you'll have a continuous supply of ice. We recently had 12 people over and started the machine roughly 1 hour before anyone got there. I added water twice during the evening and we never ran out. I've had this about 6 months and it's just an awesome product.

title: Not as good a value as plain white one
text: Uneven performance by this machine. Cubes not size they are programmed to be.. More noisy than expected. Cublesmelt pretty fast. I got a very similar one from Wal-mart for less money. I prefer Amazon more though better ethics.

title: A great ice maker
text: This is a great ice maker! It runs quietly and provides ample cubes. Be sure to let it set for 24 hours, the refrigerant needs time to settle. In shipping, the boxes are likely bounced around, turned upside down etc.

title: Great Machine!
text: Our old Nu Air Ice Maker worked like a champ. It finally broke down so I tried this version. Got the red one - love it! The small ice cube size works perfect for water bottles. When this arrived, I unpacked it and let it sit for 2 days before I plugged it in. It's much quieter than my last model, which I love. Works great - So happy - I love my ice cubes and this is money well spent!

title: Excellent portable Ice Maker
text: This little ice maker can make ice faster then my fridge ice maker.. you can't go wrong with it. I can't wait to take it camping.

title: Awesome Icemaker!
text: This does the job, we purchased an orange since it was the only color in stock but we were in major needs of an icemakers, not only does this not take that much space on our counter, we can move it outdoor and have it ready for people to grab ice for thier drinks. I would have given it a 5 star but we needed it at the exact moment. Would recoomend this product to family/friends.

title: We like to save money so we bough an open box ...
text: We needed an ICE maker for our Forrest River R-Pod 177 since the freezer is so small. We like to save money so we bough an open box NewAir AI-100BK 28-Pound Portable Ice Maker for 1/2 the price of a new one. So far on Amazon every open Box or refurbished item we buy is actually brand new! You can save a bundle and it there is something wrong Amazon will take it back and pay shipping at no cost to you. You can't loose! The NewAir AI-100BK 28-Pound Portable Ice Maker came in the original packaging. It had a few minor scuffs on the outside, expected with an open box item. Review: We LOVE it and it makes ICE very fast about 6 trays an hour. The ICE is not hard frozen but we like it like that anyway. We also like the fact you can use purified or distilled water and make perfect ice cubes. Highly recommend this unit!

title: I do not like this ice making machine at all and feel it is a waste of money
text: When I started making 'Large' ice after following the startup instructions and filled the reservoir about 3/4 and the round cubes that were delivered in my basket measured 1.2" by less than 0.7". I contacted the manufacturer via email and was informed via email that that 'size' was considered a Large Sized cube (what is a Small Sized Cube by their standards?)! I realized now that the initial batch or so of cubes experienced melting because there is no way for the receiver basket to be kept cold other than leaving it closed as much as possible. The cubes I later made increased in size however after a couple of batches. I then left the machine on overnight and after about 6 to 8 hours the basket was not full (which may have been due to low water in the reservoir which did not indicate on the display panel at all). I then filled the machine full of water as instructed and left it run when I went to work. I returned home to find that the machine had over made the ice, overflowed the basket and a dozen or so cubes remained in the delivery chute! I do not like this ice making machine at all and feel it is a waste of money. I am going to look for one that will perform properly and make Good Ice....

title: well worked but didn't last.
text: We did use it a LOT and it worked great while we had it. It lasted about 2 years I think and it did make great ice for us but gave out after a while.

title: Don't let the size fool you. It makes ice ...
text: Don't let the size fool you. It makes ice, but only a small buckets worth at a time, which means you have to constantly refill the water and empty the bucket. Additionally, it's not cold enough, so if you plan to put the ice in a freezer for storage after you're done making it, the ice will freeze together and make it hard to use it without breaking it apart with an ice pick.

title: When ready I plugged it in and have been amazed how much ice and how quickly this thing produced ...

When ready I plugged it in and have been amazed how much ice and how quickly this thing produced ice. Great buy!!

title: Excellant !!

title: great machine that keeps up in the summer for sports jugs and coolers
text: love this machine. our small ice maker in our LG refrigerator was not keeping up. rather then the big expense of getting it fixed we bought this machine and just love it. We put a nice size tub in our freezer and just fill it with this ice, we also fill the ice dispenser with this ice. it makes ice so fast that we can't keep up sometimes. we only need to fill the tub and the ice dispenser once a week. during baseball season when we use lots of ice for our boys water jugs and our coolers then we are using it a little more but this machine easily keeps up with our needs. i can honestly say, it's one of my top 5 purchases in the last 12 months.

title: Bad Experience turns out to be WONDERFUL

title: Great having the extra ice.

title: It’s soooo loud!!! Must turn off at night!

I've tried cleaners, vinegar, and even cycled a 75% solution of bleach water which initially helped but did not do away with the rotten smell.

Had to find it online.

title: It is compact
text: I love this. It is very compact and beautiful color. Makes ice in minutes. The quality is awesome.

title: It's pretty simple stuff
text: We bought the icemaker a month or so ago. At first, I thought it would be one of those products that you might regret buying but it's been anything but that so far. We've used the heck out of it. We seem to consume a lot of ice at this house. We're always buying ice in town to help keep up with the demands. That gets a little old toting bags of ice in from town all the time. So, we decided on buying the Igloo Icemaker. It takes about an hour or so and you can have a refrigerator freezer full of ice in the basket. The ice comes out in 7 piece intervals usually within 7 minutes of each other. It has a 3-prong plug in. You just lift the lid and add water as it says in the instructions, choose large or small ice and wait for the ice to fill up in the basket. It's pretty simple stuff. The best part is we purchased it for less than half price. It's been a pretty sweet purchase for us so far. The photo shows the SMALL size ice.

title: Total rip off!

title: Stopped working off and on 6 months in. Stopped working completly right after year return timeframe was up
text: Love it. It has a hard time keeping up with my family of 5. I have ice eaters and the ice is soft and great for chewing (don't tell my dentist '). You can not buy parts to replace anything when it wears out either.

title: Love this thing

title: Very easy to use. Makes the perfect sized ice.

title: Works fast and very well!!
text: We love it!! Had been buying bags of ice for years!

title: Reliable ice maker.

title: RCA portable electronic ice maker
text: Review is about RCA Portable Electronic Ice Maker. Model No: RIC-102-RED....Appears to be identical to Igloo & other labeled 102 ice makers. Importer and shipper: Curtis International Imports, Toronto, Ontario, Canada, made in China Item was shipped in original store shelf box as I neglected to specify plain brown box. Small ding from handling but with no visible damage nor apparent functioning. The form fitting styrofoam packing protected it well. WARNING The user manual contains several warnings that should have been printed on the outside of the box, IMO. (Paraphrased) 1. Ice maker should not be tilted more than 45° during transport or use. Do not turn upside down. (probably best not to turn upside down while unpackaging) Allow 2 hours for cooling fluids to settle before use. A youtube video by a seller suggests 24 hr rest after shipment. 2. Needs dry level stable surface. 3. Leave 8" clearence all around for ventilation and component cooling 4. Do not use hot water, room temperature or lower. Package should have supplied warning notice on film bag about careful removal of clear packing tape on ice basket, ice scoop, and mechanical ice shovel. As all interior components are white the tape is hard to see. Interior space was a bit cramped. Best to check nothing is left taped down to impede functioning with small flashlight. Tested the unit to see if it worked. Room temp 64°F, water temp 62°F Filled about an inch below max water line, which is indicated by very slightly raised lettering and dashed line, very difficult to see even with flashlight. Fortunately the line is about a finger width below the breaking slope line of the container, readily visible. From plug in time to first drop of ice bullets was timed at 7m 20sec with another 22 seconds before the ice shovel pushed the ice into the basket. Harvest was 9 bullets about 3/4" diameter and 1 1/8" inches long on the large setting. Continued test for four cycles with approx same time. I'm happy with the results, performs as advertised and at a very good price, less than $100. And the Candy Apple red color is way hot. ;>) ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

title: Ice Maker
text: easy to use - quick ice making - good value

title: Makes Ice very quickly

Within 15mins of putting water in and turning it on, it starts to dump ice. First few dumps are sometime thin but I have been very happy with the quantity and speed of ice production.

title: like the instructions said
text: I might have received a defective unit. I poured water into it. Turned it on, like the instructions said. Waited several hours, and still no ice. (The instructions said it would take minutes). This needs to be fixed... I guess you can say, I need justICE. (Excuse me for the bad pun) EDIT: they sent a replacement and works great

title: Makes ice cubes on the countertop, keeps the tray full of ice , and is easy to use.
text: We bought this same red Igloo icemaker early this spring. We found it for about $90 at Sam's Club, and purchased it there. Since our refrigerator does not make ice cubes, we were tired of constantly having to fill up the ice cube trays, and then empty them into the ice bin, and do the whole thing over and over again every day , all summer long. We just LOVE this icemaker ! As almost everyone else has mentioned, the ice does not stay chilled, and it is wet, as opposed to frozen hard once it has been in the ice tray for a while. However, this is just not a big deal, the ice is still ice, and it keeps itself refilled in short order. We fill the reservoir once or twice a day with the half gallon of water, and we do use filtered water to make the ice with. There is always ice when we want some, and it is wonderful to use in the blender for making iced coffee, or smoothies. The cubes are small (although there are two sizes possible), and they easily blend into frozen drinks in the blender. I have iced coffee every afternoon, and it is just like going to Starbucks, but way, way cheaper ! I would definitely recommend this ice maker, it is perfect for a family; but not enough for when you are having a picnic and have a lot of people using the ice. If you have found this review to be helpful in any way, please click the "Like" button for me.

title: Very nice
text: this is a very beautiful color, compact on the counter ice maker! it is super fast, like every 8-10 min produces ice ! I totally love it and will absolutely recommend it!

title: A-

title: small ice maker
text: This works great if you want ice for drinks but it would take days to make enough ice for a cooler to take to the beach or anything like that.

title: Awesome!
text: Love love love love!! I am absolutely in love with this little machine. I just moved... I had a 15 year old fridge that made so much noise and I was using ice trays. I would fantasize about getting a new fridge constantly. I found a great condo that came with a gorgeous stainless steel fridge.... no ice maker. I didn't even know they made countertop ice makers, and I am in love with this one! It makes a huge amount of ice in one round... you can choose small or large pieces, and it's quiet and cute. title: So far I'm in love! Made my mom jealous
text: I had to come back and edit my review. After less than a year of owning this machine, I can finally give a proper product review. This machine pretty much does what it says. It makes ice. But only sometimes. Some days it'll work great, popping out 9 pieces of ice every 8 minutes or so. Other days, like this whole past week, I have to fight it, turn it off and back on again; drain it; clean it; take out the catching tray; refill it, and turn it off and on again to get it to register that there IS NO ICE in it and that it is not FULL as the little red light indicates it is. Dear ice machine, You are a lying piece of crap machine. My ice maker is NOT full of delicious ice, it is empty. And this morning, after about 2.42 hours of sleep I needed my caffeine, and you failed me. You failed to provide the ice you so promised to have ready for me in the morning. It took me about 7 full minutes to finally get you to register anything, suck up that water that was ever so patiently waiting for you to be sucked up into your mechanism, and make the precious white gold I so desperately need to drink my morning soda. I am disappointed in you, and will not recommend you to my friends. Sincerely, An ice addict that can't afford that $500 ice maker that makes the delicious pebble ice like Sonic... I guess I'll have to keep a try of ice in the freezer again as a backup this summer :'(

title: like I am
text: The icemaker works up to expectations except once in awhile. The sensor doesn't shut off the ice making procedure when it should and the ice gets stuck in the freezer compartment, it's not a problem to fix the ice jam. Other than that, the machine keeps up remarkably well. It makes the right size of ice cubes and density for beverages and chewing. If you are trying to quit smoking, like I am, chewing ice works quite well.

title: So far so good. Arrived in two days
text: So far so good. Arrived in two days, unpacked it, let it sit for a few hours (something one should do with all refrigerators after moving) plugged it in, filled with water and let it rip. Now the question is to it's longevity. From what I can gather from other reviews, their warranty isn't worth the paper it's printed on, so I'm keeping my fingers crossed as to how long it functions. It's a great way to keep ice on my boat!

title: Love it!!!
text: Love love love this!!! We travel in our RV full time and usually spend a ton of money for bagged ice to use inside and to put in a cooler. We purchased this and it's great. To get the 25 lbs of ice you have to stay on top of it and empty the basket as soon as it's full each time and add the water when needed. My husband was skeptical at first, but he is a true believer now. You won't be disappointed.

title: One Star

title: ICE MAKER

title: Good Gizmo for $100 . . . loses one star for noise.
text: UPDATE 5/20/22 Unit last about four years. Still a decent buy for the price. Original Review: Right out of the box, the unit is easy to use. Very straight forward. Make sure you let your unit sit on the counter for a couple house after setting it up, and BEFORE turning it on. This allows the coolant to settle after being jostled about during delivery and set-up. Otherwise, you could end up with compressor issues. Set-up takes about 5 minutes, this includes unpacking, and initial cleaning of the unit (you don't want factory residue in your ice, yuck!). The unit has two ice sizes - the smaller ones obviously crank out faster (new cubes about every 5 minutes), so this setting is useful with a lot of people. The bigger size takes about 8 minutes, but the cubes last longer on a hot day. The system is a closed loop - pour water into the reservoir, that gets turned into ice. Auto shutoff if it runs out of water, or the ice bin is full. The only down side so far, is this unit is fairly noisy - louder than a standard full size refrigerator, but not as loud as a dishwasher. There are quieter units out there, if that is a concern, but for the price tag, this one rates as a fair price for a fair product. Does what it says it does, and does it well.

title: Initial Review: Day One
text: The instructions for this unit are not the easiest to understand, but the point gets across. Configuring this machine comes down to adding/subtracting time from the standard "+0 min" setting. In our kitchen, which is kept fairly at around 64 degrees Farenheit, this standard setting resulted in very thick ice with a heavy outer layer that fuses the cubes together. We've experimented with reducing the ice-making time, but even at "-6min" the cubes still push out mostly fused together. This isn't a real issue for us but if you're expecting a bunch of individual ice cubes every time, you may be disappointed. I'm excited about the self-clean feature, and also happy that you can partially disassemble the unit for deep cleaning. Our previous ice maker (what I would call a standard size—one of those ~$100 bullet ice makers) lasted about two years despite exclusively using filtered water. Time will tell if this lasts longer, but knowing that I can remove/replace some parts and more thoroughly clean the machine will hopefully translate to a longer lifespan.

title: and so far everything is fine. I keep the ice maker on the "large" ...
text: So I have had this about a week, and so far everything is fine. I keep the ice maker on the "large" setting which makes what I would call a medium chunk of ice. A bullet shape maybe a little more than an inch long and a little less than an inch in diameter. The ice comes out pretty quickly, especially if you leave the machine on. As it cycles water through the machine, the water in the reserve tank gets colder and colder and takes less time to make ice. So - once up and running it makes ice faster than I need for someone that drinks ice water all day long. It is pretty loud. It has a small compressor and a fan, and both are pretty loud. I use it in my office, and not a lot of noise escapes the door, but I need to turn it off if someone comes in to chat. It would be impossible to use in a cubicle. The instructions recommend using either lemon juice or vinegar to clean the machine for several cycles. I recommend vinegar unless you want to clean a lot of pulp out of the machine. Maybe if you can strain the pulp it would be better. That said - the hint of lemon for a few cycles after cleaning is probably more pleasing than a hint of vinegar. Now - many cycles in the ice tastes like ice should - which is no taste at all. At no time did it have a chemical taste - but I did throw out the first several cycles during cleaning. I use filtered tap water from the water dispenser in the office, and the ice is fairly clear and tasteless.

title: been wanting one of these for years!
text: I first saw one of these years ago in one of those junk mail catalogs that wind up in your mailbox all the time. At the time I saw it it cost $300. I thought, this would be a great item for parties and I swore if they ever came down in price I was going to own one. Well this one dropped to $100 and I pulled the trigger and bought one and I am glad I did. Every summer I Brew insane amounts of iced tea and I also work outdoors in the heat and need ice to fill my water cooler for work so I am constantly running out of ice. The Ice Maker in the fridge just can't keep up with the demand. The freezer takes 2 hours, this thing takes less than 10 minutes! When I come home from work I fill it up and it runs all night until I go to bed. Each day it produces enough ice for me to keep my summer beverages cool and at the same time make an extra bucket of ice that I use in my water cooler. Here are the only cons I have for this item. 1. before you use it you may want to give it a thorough cleaning with mild detergent.. I gave mine a quick rinse instead of a thorough wash and my first batch of Ice left a plasti-like taste in my beverage when melted. Cleaning it properly before the next use fixed that. 2. It judges the state of the ice by a timer not a thermostat. So 7 minutes for small ice 13 minutes for large (approximately). It takes a while for the chillers to get nice and cold so the first 2 batches or so it makes are pretty lousy little ice balls, but once she gets running up to speed, you'll easily get a pound of ice every hour. So if you are hosting a cocktail hour at your house, you might want to plug this guy in about an hour before your guests arrive. :o)

title: Great icemaker
text: This review is more detailed than most of my reviews for the simple fact that there is a lot of confusion on how this ice maker works. I love this icemaker. 9 donuts are made every 6-8 minutes depending on selected size. Two sizes are available--Small or large. Simply fill the reserve up with water and press "start"! You will have ice in as little as 6 minutes! The basket will hold quite a bit. Once the basket is full, a sensor is triggered and it does stop producing until either you empty the basket or the ice melts back into the reserve. I feel it is important to mention that there is no "freezer" to keep the ice cubes frozen and if the ice sets a bit it will melt back into the reserve to be reused but the ice stays frozen for awhile. I have noticed several complaints when dumping into your ice bucket in the freezer, the ice will freeze together due to it being a "wet" (but solid) ice. Simply take a knife and break it up after each time you dump in the freezer and it's fine.

It will make larger cubes if you dump some ice into the water reservoir itself, so it's freezing ice water instead of lukewarm water.

title: This has worked well for us so far. I ...
text: This has worked well for us so far. I bag the ice and leave it in our freezer and make more when we run out.

title: Broke one month after return policy expired
text: This ice maker broke shortly after the return policy expired. I did not mistreat, or even move the machine for that matter, before it broke. It just began making less and less ice until it stopped all together. When it did make ice, the ice was very wet and had a tendency to stick together. I was not very happy with the the ice that it did make when it was working but I figured that the ice was ok for the price I paid for the machine. Now that the machine has stopped working altogether I am very dissappointed. If I were you, I would save my money and look elsewhere for a higher quality product.

title: Five Stars
text: EXCELENT PRODUC. VERY EASY TO USE. I JUST LOVE IT!

title: Its okay once you understand how a table top ice maker works
text: just to set expectations for those wanting to buy one....I got mine today 6/8 and started using it. instructions state that once ouf ot the box and on level surface to wait 2 hrs for refrigerent to settle....just an FYI.....I selected small finger tip sized ice, large ones are a littlle bigger....it makes 5 cubes at a time and so far about 8-10mins to create the 5. The ice comes out "wet" so if you dump it into your refrig's ice maker ice holder they will stick together. you need to bag the ice and stick it in your freezer...once completed frozen...bang the bag to loosen up the cubes and you are off. I bought this unit because of the amazon reviews and the price...so if you are looking for something that makes a stream of ice...these table top units are not that.....but a good way to avoid having to make trips to the grocery store for bagged ice

title: Works well
text: Makes a little noise which is understandable but produces ice rapidly from startup. I turn it off at night

title: The ice tray isn't that big and the rate of product is fine for a small family during the summer
text: Not much to say about these ice makers. There must be a factory in China that spits these things out as a contract manufacturer as you see the exact same model under a dozen labels. The ice tray isn't that big and the rate of product is fine for a small family during the summer. It can't keep up for use at a party, think of it as an automated ice tray. I have had a few, they last 3 or 4 years. Cheap enough to replace but not a model of design or durability.

title: Pleased with this icemaker
text: I purchased this ice maker back in November of 2014. I use it everyday and have been very happy with it's performance. Recently the ice started to get really small. I looked in the back of the unit and could see that the condenser was full of lint. I took the back cover off and cleaned out the lint with a wire brush. It's back to working normally. I can't blame the ice maker for this problem. The only other problem I have had is the electric eye that signals the basket is full has stopped working so I have to manually shut it off or empty the basket when full.

title: Five Stars
text: Excellent product. Very fast ice production. Like that the ice can remain in storage bin quite a few hours.

title: Great little ice maker
text: Great little ice maker, does exactly what it's supposed to. If you're looking for something to pump out a lot of ice at one time this isn't for you but if you would like to have a glass or two of ice at a time for your home bar this is an excellent option for you. Good price. And it looks good, too!

title: Consistent Problems
text: The first one we received had problems. They tried to fix it, but ultimately had to send us a new one. The new one worked OK for a few months, but now it stops working and needs cleaned every day.

title: Ice maker

title: Great warranty support
text: Bought unit less than a year ago. Product started making noise while making ice. Contacted mfg and they replaced the unit quickly! Rep was very very courteous and helpful.

title: Didn’t work out
text: Ended up having to return. Machine rarely made ice due to constant self cleaning cycles.

title: If only it held more ice at a time
text: I love, love, love, LOVE this product. My only true complaint, besides not being able to use tap water, is that it doesn't hold much ice at once. Of course, this may be attributed to my husband and son stealing all my ice before I can get to it. My son fills a 1 gallon water bottle with the ice, I'm not sure if he fills it all the way, half way or some other way. And my husband uses it for his sodas and other drinks regularly. They are both very spoiled by this ice machine. As a side note, my husband asked me why I got an ice despenser in the first place, made a comment that it would never be used and then proceeded to take half my ice, if not more. Lol. Never be used indeed! Lol! Anyway. The ice tastes clean, even after it melts it still is delicious. If you can afford this, love ice and don't want to spend money buying bags of ice, I say get it!

title: Great Company Service
text: My kids and I love this thing. The pebbled ice is so good. I had a problem with the unit that was originally shipped to me, but when I called the number on the manual, Yvonne was so helpful. She quickly sent me an email for some information and I got a replacement unit sent to me quickly. The noise levels of the compressor in order to quickly make the ice is what I would have expected. You would have to build a bigger case with more noise absorptions to do anything about it, but it's in the kitchen when food prep and cooking is going on with much other noise, this isn't a problem. It doesn't carry all over the house, so no problem for me.

title: Garbage…

I have contacted customer support and received no help. When I open the front cover there is a ton of black that comes through a water dispensing hose. I cleaned the machine 3 times hoping that might help and I still don’t have ice.

title: Love the ice!
text: Love the ice!! Only dislike is refilling it so much due to our family using it a lot. I already had a Zerowater filter pitcher so that gets the TDS down to 1-2 instead of the 200+ out of the faucet. The plastic piece broke that holds the hoses on the back but customer service was awesome & sent replacement part quickly! Others complain about the noise but I didn't find it overly loud at all.

title: Love this ice machine! KBice customer service is awesome?
text: I ordered this machine during prime days for a great price. It arrived, I set it up, and we immediately had great ice just like Sonic! About 10 hours later, the machine was making an awful, grinding noise and would continually go into clean mode without my pushing clean. I unplugged it, drained it, refilled with purified water, cleaned it, drained it again and refilled. It started working fine, then in the middle of the night the horrible grinding sound starts again. My husband unplugged it and said it could catch fire so not to use it again. I called the KBICE CUSTOMER SERVICE. I was told that because this was less than 30 days I would need to go through Amazon to get help. Amazon kept referring me back to KBiCE. Less than 24 hours after my initial contact, and after I emailed KBICE a sound bit of the noise the machine made, they sent me a brand new one and didn't make me box the old one up and send it back! The new one works great and is very easy to fill and maintain. This is a large ice machine so make sure you look at dimensions. All in all very happy with this machine.

title: Only holds 1 lb of ice
text: I likw this machine. I bought mine off of the vendor website because they had a better price at the time and a 20% discount. Had been eyeing the Opal for a while. This one does not hold much water or completed ice. Its just me at home so it's OK, but I take two large insulated mugs of ice to work each day for water and this machine will fill one mug each morning when I get up and another before I go to work. If you are not careful to keep the water level full constantly then it will only make as much ice as you have water. So to ensure you keep that one pound of ice in the hold the water level needs to be topped up constantly. Additionally mine spits out random cubes more frequently than I wish it did. But I am really glad to have a machine and if you don't have large needs this one will work just fine. Freezing the cubes in plastic bags will change the consistency of the ice though, so if you need more than 1lb. at a time you might want to go with a different machine.

title: Not enough ice

title: awesome machine

title: It's not that noisy

title: Can be noisy. Customer support is a joke.

title: Great Ice!
text: It fits nicely under my cabinet on the counter top. It is rather heavy. It takes up a large amount of counter space so be sure it’s located somewhere you can easily plug into an outlet. Also ensure the space allows for the spout to be placed in the front to get water into the maker. The noise level is rather loud as I guess I expected it to be quieter. I don’t think it makes a lot of ice. It makes a decent amount of ice. I do wish it did have a larger capacity for water so the machine could make larger quantities of ice. I have noticed random ice pellets that have fallen out leaving wet spots on the floor. Make sure it’s something you really want because it can’t be returned. Overall, I’m satisfied. My grand daughter loves the ice so therefore, I like it for her.

title: Great ice maker just wish it was a little easier to fill
text: Bought this to replace an opal that kept shutting down on me. I bought this directly from the manufacturer and not through Amazon because they had a sale and also if you're not in California you don't have to pay sales tax, I ended up saving about $40 overall. It did take 10 days from ordering to delivery(ordered on a Saturday so probably nobody manning the sales desk on the weekend). I've only had this machine about a day. I think it makes less noise than the Opal did. This machine will auto clean with a manual clean using citric acid once a month and a disinfect with bleach once a month. Citric Acid is much cheaper than the opal cleaning kit. The dispensing feature is nice. Nobody has to reach into the ice bin. It has randomly dropped ice at least once that I know of but the machine was full (not making ice) so I don't know if it had overfilled itself and and settling ice shifted and dropped the nuggets but they landed in the provided tray. The front cover and the tray and both magnetic and very easy to remove when necessary. Might biggest gripe so far is that filling this machine could be slightly easier. It's difficult to get anything to big to pour into the reservoir when the machine is empty, and the funnel could have a better shape to it so that it's easier to pour in. I think this might be on purpose so you can't accidentally overfill the machine by pouring too fast/too much water through the funnel but it's something I wish was different. The only other concern someone might have is this machine requires distilled water. I went ahead and purchased a distiller after doing some research on the cost of making distilled at home versus buying. Making a gallon of distilled costs roughly 30 cents and you don't have the plastic jug to deal with. It is one more step in the process though for this ice machine. I don't think I would change the distilled water requirement. It will help keep the machine cleaner and easier to descale during the monthly cleaning cycle.

title: Garbage
text: This ice maker was a piece of garbage. Even after using reverse osmosis filtered water it would go into cleaning mode. After following their cleaning instructions it still would not make ice. We liked the idea of a self dispensing ice maker to sanitary reasons, however, this one is not the way to go. We returned this within 20 days of having it. Spend the extra money and get a GE Opal as we did that works perfectly for the last 8 months, it just isn’t doesn’t self dispense. KB Ice’s customer service was horrible, after contacting them they only advised to follow their instructions for cleaning which didn’t work. They would not replace the machine so I had to do it through Amazon. ***STAY AWAY*** KB ICE = useless and worthless GE Opal = Worth the extra money

title: Correct ice shape

title: Sonic Ice!
text: This is by far the most useful thing I've bought in so long. My mother is a hospice patient and chomping Sonic ice is sometimes the only thing that she can handle on her stomach. I was driving a half hour each way, several times a week with a cooler and losing half of it on the way home. And sometimes they wouldn't even have any... It was frustrating, to say the least. But I did it out of love. When I found this, a prayer was answered. It can be kept in her room because there is no water hookup required. It is quiet. It couldn't be easier to use. And it's exactly the same ice as at Sonic. To see her smile, everytime, is worth everything.

title: Does everything well except store the ice
text: This unit has a storage capacity of about 32 oz of ice at any given time, and can completely refill it in 60-90 mins. Typically this is more than sufficient for usage throughout the day. However, because of the unit's lack of refrigeration (melted ice recycled to reservoir), it is unable to keep the ice bin full in operating temperatures much over 80 degrees. And the amount of ice melt-off in temps over 80 degrees causes the unit to go into "cleaning" mode every day or so (while not making ice until it is cleaned manually). Also, the automatic Ice maker stops working automatically when the unit sets unused for several hours (but melt-off continues). I have reached out to the manufacturer to see if there is a fix for this defect, but have not heard back yet. The workaround is to hold down the Make Nuggets button to cycle it off/on whenever you see the light is not flashing. I do this first thing in the morning to make sure the ice bin is refilled, and it is then typically fine during the day while in use.

title: Good for office

The ice at my house is too hard on my teeth and I was spending money at Sonic and AM/PM for the "crunch" and "pellet" ice. I was apprehensive buying this machine but reviews were great and I have to say I couldn't be happier. The ice is delicious and definitely munchable. It's not pellet ice, but it's still very easy to eat. The best part it that it melts a bit in the tray making it very soft and pleasing, easy on the teeth. I use the small size setting. A few notes: The instructions say to let the machine sit for 2 hours and not to turn it upside down due to the refrigerant. I didn't realize this when unpacking it and had tipped it on it's side to remove from the box. The machine makes 10 cubes at a time. I expected more, but given that it makes them in under 10 minutes it's not a big deal, just something to be aware of if you're planning for more than yourself. You'll definitely want to remove the ice and freeze it in your fridge to be ready. The other thing is that it was hard for me to fin the max water line because it blended into the white plastic. I had to actually feel for it and once I felt it I could see it, but initially I didn't notice it. If anyone likes ice and is looking for chewable ice, but doesn't want to spend a fortune on the fancy machines I would highly recommend this ice maker.

title: Might Work for a Camping Trip, or a One Time Party...
text: Purchased this item and 8 months later it is useless. Was very excited to get this and hopeful that the days of buying ice would be over! For the first week it was so neat - a little noisy, and the ice cubes melted incredibly fast - but then, what do expect when they all have holes in them... So there are these rods, and they get super cold, enough to freeze the water around them - so you have these little playing dice sized cubes with a hole in the middle, where the rod was. Melted REALLY fast, and always kind of watery - the bin wasn't cold enough to keep them frozen for long at all, but it was okay for what we needed... for a bit... The bin and all the parts inside started getting moldy SUPER fast. We figured with constant use we could go maybe a week without shutting it down and doing a thorough cleaning - but no, we ended up just using the ice to keep the sodas cold. I wouldn't put ice from this machine inside my drink now for anything - there are too many tiny areas that are too difficult to get to and I could never get it completely clean. But still - it kept our drinks cold, we were okay. Then today - the red light indicating the bin was full went on, and the bin wasn't full. We've tried everything, gone online and researched it, and basically what we're being told is to just call it dead. While we might be able to get the manufacturer to repair/replace, we would have to pay the shipping and some kind of co-pay that would make it much more worthwhile to put the money towards a better one and call the bit we paid for this one - a valuable learning experience. Learn from our mistakes. :) Also, I encourage everyone to wait a year before reviewing appliance-type purchases. Lots of things that work great for the first while end up as doorstops, and I think a year is a fair trial to see if the item you bought possesses true quality or not. Just a thought. :)

text: I love This!!! I am not the type of person who always marks stuff as 5 stars. But I am so impressed with this ice maker and it really surpassed my expectations and is very worth the amount of money I paid for it. I bought this for my RV since l have limited space in my freezer for large bag of ice. After pulling it out of the box and setting it up, I filled the reservoir with water, selected the size ice cube, and hit start! In no time I had a full baset of ice! In a matter of a few hours I had a full gallon zip lock bag full of ice! I no longer need my ice trays and freed up a lot room in my freezer. The small ice will go into a soda bottle opening easily and will fit in the small opening of a Nalgean water bottle. The ice machine is very quiet and takes up very little space. To get the gallon bag of ice, it took 1 and a quarter fill up. There is no alarm to let you know the basket is full, but there is an indicator light that lets you know. will keep the ice in the basket frozen For hours. Also there is an ice scoop for use if your hands are dirty and you don't want to add mud to your drink! I am very pleased with this and would recommend to RVers who want ice, but can't just up and go to a store every time ice is needed or have the room to spare in the freezer for large bags of ice. I am, on the average. an hour or two away from town. I drive a full size I ton dually and am in the mountains with a high elevation gain, so by time I drive to town and back, hoping my cooler does its job and ice loss is minimal, I have pretty much spent the money it cost for the price of the ice maker. So as I said, the ice maker has paid for itself already. Could not be happier!

Its unmatched convenience, rapid ice production, versatility, ease of use, and durability make it an exceptional investment. Whether you're a frequent entertainer or simply want to upgrade your at-home ice-making experience, this portable ice maker is a notable change. title: Nice Ice, but...
text: I have a half-dozen ice-makers. This one is the Antartica Star, sold by different vendors, although this vendor did not use that name. I found out recently when I ordered from a different vendor and got the same machine. That vendor did not use this model's name, either. They all work fine for a few months, and then, some of them will display "Ice Full" even when empty. The trick that worked for a few months was to hold the Select button for at least 10 full seconds. The Ice Full message may or may not go away. Sometimes turning off and back on is all you need to get rid of it. Then you can make ice, but I recommend not leaving it on thereafter. I'll explain why now. I have three of these units, and the one I use downstairs now has the flaw that you cannot leave it on all the time. If you do, all the ice will have melted when you return hours later, and the Ice Full is red again. So, you have to start over. It's a pain in the ... well, you know. Other brands have this problem, too, but the Antartica Star model problem is among the most persistent. I wish I could tell you which vendors sell it, but you really can't tell other than by appearances. So, look closely at the pictures! Good luck!

This ice maker two sizes of ice — the large size is a nugget style cube about the size of a thimble and the smaller is slightly smaller. Both are hollow nuggets. Controls are intuitive. Water is added into a tank, above which is a basket to collect the cubes. The bracket is removable to easily dump it in a bowl in your freezer. There is also a small scoop included. Nuggets that melt into the tank will again be made into ice. There are indicators for “full basket” and “out of water.” There is a drain for the tank. The nuggets are “soft ice” by which i mean chewable. Because they have lots of surface area they will chill a drink quickly... which also means they melt fairly quickly. It does make ice fairly fast and within a half hour you should have ice for 2-3 tall drinks. The unit is fairly quiet with only the noise of a fan (be sure to have good air flow around the unit) and the sound of ice falling in the basket. One complaint with the vendor... shipping time was slow and then got delayed a couple more times causing a minor inconvenience for us. BOTTOM LINE... a nice ice maker for drinks. If you often need ice to fill a cooler or for churning ice cream you should look at a heavy duty ice maker or plan on buying ice.

title: Cheap and easy replacement for your ice maker!
text: I ordered this ice maker to replace the broken unit in our fridge, the first time it went out I tried to go cheap and just replace the thermostat. By the time I paid for the thermostat and special adhesive it was only about $20 cheaper than this whole kit and it only lasted about four months. If your ice maker has gone out, don't waste your time trying to replace individual parts that may or may not be a long term fix, just get this kit and be done with it. When I ordered it I thought was just going to be able to swap the ice maker part out and not mess with the wire harness(es) but I'm glad I read some of the other's posts about it since the new unit is an upgrade and requires the harness to be changed out. The kit comes with two harnesses and two plastic caps but you only use one of each (you match the old wire harness colors at the main plug to one of the new harnesses and that's the one you will use. This is an upgraded part so changing the harness is a necessity, but it's not difficult. Take a picture of all the where all the connectors plug in before you remove the original harness so you can plug the new ones back in the correct location. A word of caution since all the parts are loosely strewn in the box, check your unit before you install it, mine had a small metal clip that had worked itself under the ice fingers and would surely have messed something up if I had missed it. The whole repair only took about an hour, but in fairness I had taken it apart before, if this is your first time taking the ice maker apart, take your time and watch some videos before you start, it will be helpful.

title: Manage Expectations
text: A countertop ice maker seemed like a perfect solution for our situation of non-potable water city water, limited freezer space, and our general laziness about refilling ice cube trays. I made some incorrect assumptions about the quantity, quality, and storage features of this product. I don't think it's brand specific, but rather understanding that these machines are not quite what we expected. Quantity - the machine produces very small batches every 8 minutes or so. Really enough for one drink (and the ice melts fast). Quality - the size of "large" cubes is actually what I would call small. The cubes melt almost instantly when added to drinks. Their composition differs from freezer ice cubes, they are less dense and less cold. Storage - this doesn't really store quality ice cubes like the ice tray in your freezer, rather they just kind of melt back down into the water supply. I should've done my homework before making assumptions about this product's capabilities. That being said, it's easy to clean, it was easy to set up and seems to be working well. Hamilton Beach is a trusted brand and I've had great experiences with their other products. The ice maker, for us, will be more of a compliment to freezing cubes the old fashioned way.

I keep a fresh bag of ice in the freezer and when it starts to run low, I just turn on the ice maker and let it do its thing. It's so much easier than dealing with the ice cube trays and less expensive than having an ice maker in the door - traditionally they haven't worked well for me anyway. The bonus was the amount of space I gained in the freezer & I was able to toss the silicon ice trays that are fantastic when they're new but have a short lifespan. I'll admit, this was on my wishlist for a while. Let's face it, it's not a need - but we're enjoying having it more than I ever expected. An added bonus ~ if you have a "margarita machine" these small ice cubes turn into wonderful snow - the hardness is just right so the beverages have a smooth consistency. In terms of set up, it was very easy - I just followed the directions that came with the unit, let it sit for 2 hours for the refrigerant to settle, and cleaned it well. Overall, it's a great little unit.

text: We've been making ice everyday as our in door icemaker in our fridge is not working. There isn't a lot of difference in the size between small and large ice. The smaller ice melts really fast. I dont think it would work too well for a party where a lot of ice is needed. It is surprising how much ice can be made in a 24 hour period. For a party it would be wise to spend the day before making a freezing the ice. We have been using one gallon zip lock bags to store the extra ice. The operation is simple. A light comes on when the ice tray is full. Dump the tray into a storage device for the freezer and put the tray back in. A light also comes on when it needs water. Fill it up to the line inside the ice-maker and off it goes. Note: It would really be nice if there was a buzzer or a bell to let me know when the ice is done or the machine needs water. About the only complaint I have is the machine is noisier than I thought it would be, While making ice you can hear the machine working in the next room. I was expecting the noise of the ice dumping into the tray. I like that sound. Just not the operational noise. I would recommend this ice maker as a good place to start. I was skeptical about spending almost $200 for another appliance to sit on my counter that we don't use, but I have use this icemaker every day since it arrived. It's pretty easy to maintain and prep for making ice, and it makes a ton of ice. I think it could support a party of 20+ people as long as you continue to supply it with fresh water. It is simply awesome! Now with that being said, there is one major issue that Costway should address immediately. the screw that holds the ice-making section started rusting shortly after I received it. About once a week, I have to clean the rust generated by this screw as it starts to rundowns the side and would end up in the water supply if not cleaned regularly. I eventually had to dis-assemble the top so I could take that screw out and replace it with a stainless steel number 8-1/2 inch screw. I think this will solve the issue. It was not hard to do and well worth it, if it solves my issue. This is a design flaw that has an easy resolution even if it cuts into Costway profit, by 5 cents a unit. title: For all those times we needed ice and nobody wanted to leave the party to get it.
text: I've seen video reviews of products such as this BOSALY Ice Maker Machine. It promises to make ice in 9 minutes and I gotta say, it does just that. This ice maker can make two sizes of ice. In my testing, small ice cubes can be made in 9 minutes while the large one takes 11. I think it is necessary to set some expectations for this unit for those who are interested. If you know these things ahead of time, you will not be disappointed by your purchase: This ice maker is fairly heavy, but that is to be expected because of the compressor. Also due to the compressor, this until will not work with power from a car adapter so as far as portability, you'd need to make sure there is a wall outlet or a generator that you can plug it into or you'll be draining a lot of battery power. It must also be pointed out that the ice made by this machine is quite wet due to how the ice is made. It means that if you make ice with this machine, then put them into your freezer, you'll end up with one big lump of ice. With that said, this machine does EXACTLY what I want it to do: make ice during a small gathering without the need for much oversight. Just make sure the water tank is filled. Here are the features I like: -- Portable. Be the savior of the party by bringing the ice maker for a friend's party. -- Auto stop when the water level is low or the basket is filled. -- Plug at the bottom allows draining of excess water. -- FAST. 9 pieces of ice cube are made with each batch. That's enough for two cups. -- Convenient. Make sure the machine is filled with water and plugged in. Come back once in a while to dump out the basket to make more ice or to refill the water. -- Useful. This will definitely make a difference during a party. There are too many other things to worry about when preparing for guests. Overall, great product.

title: Awesome little ice maker
text: I absolutely love my little ice machine! Super easy to clean, relatively quiet, fills a gallon baggie overnight. I run mine at night because it’s summer, over 95° during the day, and I don’t have AC ~ this little guy puts out a fair bit of heat. Other than the ice dropping and a little *whirrr* there isn’t really any noise. I did follow the instructions and thoroughly clean it prior to using, and I use bottled purified water. The ice is clear and flavorless … PERFECT! I really wanted one that makes the *good* ice (you know what I mean, the tiny crushed cubes: perfect for crunching) but wasn’t willing to throw $250+ at one. The Small setting make the little cups thin enough that, either straight from the basket and after being transferred to the baggie in the freezer, they are easy to crunch (or whack the baggie on the counter and they’re smaller). It does NOT keep the ice frozen for long, but does reuse the water from melted ice. So if you forget about it, it’s okay. It’ll just keep on remaking the same water into ice. I do run a Clean cycle every few days, drain it each morning (I use the leftover water in the dog dish), and flip the basket so the machine can air out and dry. Weekly I wipe out the machine with a wet rag and one drop (half a drop really) of dish soap ~ then use a clean very wet rag to rewipe and remove soap, and finally run two clean cycles with fresh water each cycle (about half tank each time). Then I let it air dry for the day and fill and run again that night. It’s been a lifesaver and is the perfect ice for cocktails, iced coffees, teas, and water. Definitely worth the investment!

text: The ice maker in our kitchen refrigerator is very slow to make ice, and there is never enough to get through the day with our family. We were constantly running out to the store for ice, especially with warmer summer weather. We bought this in July 2021, and it has really made a difference for us. It takes about an hour to get a full bucket of ice cubes, which we then pour into the always-empty ice maker bucket in the refrigerator. Two full buckets = 5 lb. bag of ice and uses up a full gallon of water, so then the machine is empty and not full of stagnant water . We use the filtered water from the refrigerator, so the ice always tastes good. If we run the machine to get a single full bucket each morning, we usually have enough to get through the day. If not, it's just 10-15 minutes for the first ice drop. We unplug it and give it a deep clean every other month -- not too much to do for a constant and convenient supply of good, clean ice. Very happy with this purchase.

title: I Returned This Ice Maker - Not "Bad" Not "Great"
text: Since I returned this ice maker, I feel obligated to review it. It is not a "bad" ice maker, but it is not a "good" ice maker. I have owned 4 or 5 counter top ice makers and none of them have been a "great" ice maker. The biggest problem with this unit is that it does not completely fill the basket with ice. It is also quite noisy. The ice stays in a pile next to where it was dispensed and does not fall to the front of the basket to completely fill it up. It makes ice just fine, but you cannot just let it make ice and expect to find a full basket. You have to empty the half-full basket often for it to keep making ice. It does make lots of ice, has a stainless steel body and looks great. According to an A/C engineer, counter top ice units have oil mixed in with the coolant. You should always try to keep it upright, never turn it upside down, and only use the ice maker drain to drain unused water. If the oil and coolant are not properly mixed, friction can destroy the ice maker which is likely why so many people report that it never worked. After you move it, it is recommended you let it sit for 30 minutes before turning it on. I did some research and discovered that almost all counter top ice makers are made by the same manufacturer with many exterior designs and virtually identical inside working components. They all seem to make ice then just stop one day after 6 months or more. So I would suggest you sincerely consider purchasing the Protection Plan. Bottom line, counter top ice makers are fussy, do not like to be moved or cleaned, and make lots of ice until they just quit one day. So it is well worth your time to learn how to take care of them.

title: Review update
text: I spent weeks reading the reviews of dozens of ice makers. This one had the best positive reviews although they all have negative reviews. I'm going to address some of those problems. I have had the ice maker for several days now, and I'm very very happy with its performance. 1. Noise level - 15 feet away from the machine, I can't even hear it running. Seriously, it makes all the noise of one of those battery operated handheld fans. 2. Ice quality - some reviews of ice machines complain that the ice is all wet and mushy. This machine produces very good ice. Not mushy at all, but still nice and soft to chew on! I suggest after three cycles of ice, let it be transferred into the freezer in a Rubbermaid type container with a lid. The ice will be slightly wet so it will tend to stick once it's in the freezer for a while. Giving it a quick firm shake solves this problem. Also, some people complain about the ice melting too fast. The ice cubes are quite small and are hollow inside. This gives them a rather large surface area and they will melt quickly if placed in room temperature liquid. Best to use chilled products. 3. Breakdowns - these ice machines have several moving mechanisms. A water pump to transfer water to the freezing unit. A lift to raise the finished ice. And a sweeper to push the ice into the ice basket. Any of these mechanisms will break down with age leaving you with a non-operational ice maker. I strongly suggest you purchase the 5-year warranty to save you from any grief. Changing my stars from 5 to 3. The reason why is that the machine came with absolutely no instructions on how to maintenance clean it. Many ice machines come with a clean cycle. This one doesn't. I have no idea how to clean the insides or if it even can be cleaned.

text: It is easy to set up and easy to use - assuming you have instructions in English (and the electrical plug isn't a "Chinese" type. Note that the machine MAKES ice - but does NOT keep it frozen ! After the cubes drop into the holding bin, they will start to melt (hence why you need to hook up the supplied drain hose and have if drain into a bucket or sink or a drain). The idea is, you make ice in the machine, then bag it and through it into a freezer or use it immediately. You can set a time to start up (and shut down) so it isn't constantly making new ice to replace the stuff that has melted. (Which would cost you more in electricity and water of course.) Or you can simply turn the machine off when not in use. Takes a few minutes for it to start up again and about 20-25 minutes to make the first "tray" of ice (45 cubes) depending how thick you want them. I ran mine for an hour and shut it down as I had already ran out of room to store ice. (When I bought the machine I thought it would keep the ice frozen.) I'm using large (18l) water bottles now but I'm already thinking I'll switch to hooking up the filter and connecting the machine to a water tap. I suspect the design could also be a part of the problem. Vents go all the way down the center back. Usually they are at the top so you only have to watch the center of the top shelf for freezing. 4. I don't know if all refidgerators of this model are made by Daewoo (111 prefix) but ours was. Not good. Technician said parts are hard to get and he has fixed some ice makers multiple times. Fortunately we never hooked ours up and don't plan to. We have had good Kenmore appliances in the past but we are not pleased with this one. I know that multiple manufacturers make Kenmore appliances and I have learned more about the prefixes to know which ones. title: No Indicator When the Ice Basket is Full
text: I agree with most of the comments mentioned in the other reviews so I will not repeat them. However, there is one issue that I will, mention. This ice maker does not have any means of alerting you when the ice basket is full, it just stops making ice. Other ice makers have various types of indicators to alert you when the ice basket is full, a red light or some type of sound. This one does nothing. There have been times when it stopped making ice, and I did not know that the basket was full. The problem is, when the basket fills up, the ice maker stops making ice. If the ice in the basket is not dumped, it will melt. If it melts below the cutoff line the ice maker will start making ice again. There have been times when I have gotten up in the morning only to find the ice maker, making ice. It had been cycling through this process all night. The ice basket fills up, the ice maker stops making ice, the ice in the basket melts and the ice maker starts making ice again. This process will happen repeatedly until the ice is removed from the ice basket, or the ice maker is turned off

title: Counter top ice machine
text: Pros: esthetically pleasing, beautiful exterior design. It does produce ice at the rate advertised. It's not too loud. Cons: Unlike the popular countertop designs that produce "bullet" shaped ice around small fingers that then drop individual bullet shaped cubes into the bin, this machine fills a classic looking tray before releasing ice to the bin. Once the ice is full in the tray, the ice is released into the bin but does not break apart. Especially if the tray is fairly full, and the ice doesn't have far to fall, you will be left with large rectangles of 8 or 12 cubes stuck together and will require you to pick and break apart all the ice in your tray. Because you'll have large rectangles of many cubes fused together, it will not nest down in the tray but instead stick up above the sensors that tell the machine it's full. We are returning ours in favor of a machine that makes individual bullet ice.

text: Love having this product. It arrived on time and was well packaged.
