title: All ice makers are noisy. This one is less so than others
text: It is not particularly quiet, but the ice cubes don't seem to all fall at once. In general, it seems quieter. The pump isn't as noisy as the NewA*r we had for several years. And the ice cubes don't seem to get caught under the sweep when the water level gets low like our old one. I like the color. The stainless steel has been easy to keep clean so far, compared to the red one we had. It also looks smaller, in spite of being the exact same dimensions. The red one just seemed huge by comparison. I had to get out the tape measure to prove to my husband that the stainless steel was the same size as our old red one. Visually, it is that much less intrusive in the room. I can't say whether it makes more or less ice cubes or whether it meets the amount per day that it says but I did have one of the smaller versions for about a year, in a different brand and it could not keep up with our ice consumption, so by comparison to the 26 pound versions, this model churns out a lot more ice. If you make ice and try to store it in the freezer, you will be needing an ice pick. Like all ice makers of this type, the bullets (cubes) release because hot water is run back through the line to melt them off the tines. So these are wet cubes and will freeze together if stored in the freezer.

title: Absolutely Love This Machine!
text: Absolutely love this machine! This is a BEAST at making ice! I really, really love the ability to hook up to a direct water supply. This keeps me from having to continuously fill the reservoir with water. This thing makes about 45 lbs of ice per day, and I use almost all of it. I bought this (and the Emerson units) because my LG refrigerator has a built in ice maker in the door that has not worked right since I bought the frig new. When it does work, it makes about a glass of ice a day - not near enough for my household. Like any new product, it takes a few days to get used to it. Once you are used to the way it works, the noises it makes, and the look of the thing sitting on your counter, it feels like it belongs there as one of your most valued appliances! I have not had one single problem with this machine, and it runs continuously 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. I guess you can tell I really love my ice! UPDATE - Feb 4, 2017 I have now had this unit for about 17 months, and it died today. Unit comes on, but does nothing. After about 5 minutes of doing nothing, the "problem in unit" icon lights up. Machine is dead - been through enough of these countertop portable units to know that there is no fixing it at this point. For the cost, this machine should have lasted longer than it did. I have come to the conclusion that it doesn't matter what brand, or style you buy, they are all made of cheap parts, and have a limited life span. Save yourself some heartache and aggravation, and just buy a much cheaper version that fits your specific needs.

text: I looked up what part to use to replace a broken icemaker in my Kenmore (by GE) fridge. I wanted the whole kit, including the water valve, just to have every possible contingency covered. I was told the original part number was superseded by this IM6 unit, which is supposed to be universal. Unfortunately, the electrical connection is entirely different than what is in my fridge, so this will not work. I looked for adapters in the packaging, but found none. My advice is if you have a rectangular electrical connection in the fridge and it has male pins, this might work. If the connector is round(ish) and has 4 female sockets, with 4 male pins on the Ice Maker wiring harness, this will not work. I could have gone one star, but Amazon was good enough to allow a return, and made that quite easy too, so its difficult for me to say "I hate it".

title: Great icemaker, simple install. But . . .
text: The instructions are easy to follow, but the templates for trimming the filler tube are vague, and not correct. The filler tube has foil around one end and an angled slash cut on the other. The instructions require me to trim the filler tube, but they don't tell me which end to trim. Do I shorten the end with the foil, or do I shorten the end with the angled cut? If I'm supposed to trim the foil-covered end, do I trim it with the foil on, or do I remove the foil, trim the tube, and reapply the foil? The instructions don't say. Also, the templates for trimming the filler tube are incorrect. My refrigerator calls for the type M instructions, and if I follow the type M template for trimming the filler tube, it's at least one inch too short for my refrigerator. After trimming the tube to fit the template, I had to go to the hardware store and buy a new piece of tubing because the template isn't long enough. After all that, it's an effective ice maker, and that's what I was looking for. I just wish the instructions covering the filler tube installation had been more detailed and accurate.

title: Another Great Modern Invention
text: Our refrigerator broke and we got tired of using ice cube trays. A friend recommended we buy an ice maker (I didn't know they existed). After doing a product research, we decided on the Black & Decker due to its many features; i.e., price, variety of different size ice cubes, and brand name (Black & Decker). In about four (4) hours we have enough ice cubes to replenish our refrigerator's ice cube bin; we now have enough ice cubes to last approximately three (3) days. Please note the ice cubes are slightly wet when you take them out of the ice maker - the ice maker does not have a separate refrigeration compartment for the produced ice cubes. No problem; just put the ice cubes in a 1 quart zip lock bag and then into freezer for a couple of hours. This freezes the ice cubes; some will freeze together. After a couple of hours, take the zip lock bag and gently hit the bag against a hard surface to separate the ice cubes; I use a met tenderizer hammer to separate the cubes. Dump them into the refrigerator's ice maker ice cube bin and you are ready to use your refrigerator's in door ice cube dispenser. You can produce three (3) different size of cubes; we use the medium sized so our in-door ice dispenser will work correctly.

title: Refuses To Make Ice --- UPDATE....UPDATE!
text: I'm on my second Igloo now. It has failed exactly like my first one. It will make ice nicely all day but at night I turn it off so I don't have to hear the clunking of ice while sleeping (I'm a light sleeper). The next day I turn it on. The ice scraper moves up, then down, then back up and the "Ice Full" light goes on and there is no ice in the basket. I keep trying but it does the same thing. Until.....finally.....sometines it seems to find it's way and starts working the rest of the day. Some days I just give up. It won't work at all. I returned the unit to Amazon for my second one which fails the same way. Amazon will not send me any more. UPDATE.....UPDATE.....UPDATE I have finally figured out thge "secret" of making my Igloo work. My problem was the "Ice Full" light would go on with no ice in the bucket and the unit would stop operation.....even with no ice. The problem was simple to fix. With the lid open you can see two small (about 1/8 inch) bumps.....one on each side of the ridge on which the ice isn scooped over. The red bump is a LED (light emitting diode). On the other side there is a white bump which is a photo diode. When the ice bucket is full the ice cubes block light from the LED from reaching the photodiode and the unit shuts down until the ice cubes melt and it starts running again. This will continue this way 24/7 if you wish or just for a few hours when you turn it on. I got a small piece ofpaper towel and gently rubbed the two diodes to clean them. I then turned the unit back on and it worked perfectly! All that was needed was to clean the diodes of tiny dirt particles which were blocking the light....acting like ice cubes. Rub the diodes very gently. I do mine every two weeks or so. It works perfectly and mkes lots of ice as needed.

title: Best Ice Maker I've had.
text: I love this ice maker. It's easy to use, not noisy to me, considering that the ice has to be moved once it's made, into the basket, so it can make more, that should be expected. The flavor is great, and I've read a lot of reviews of people saying you can't freeze it, because it melts and sticks together, I've found that if you use COLD WATER out of the fridge, it makes ice faster, if you let it cycle 4-5 times and start putting it in a baggie with the sides folded down, so the air can get to it, it WILL freeze hard. I don't have a problem with it breaking into a bunch of little pieces, or sticking all together, because by the time I let it cycle 4-5 times again, the first ice in the freezer is frozen hard, and I shake the bag as I'm emptying the 2 in so it helps with the 2nd batch freezing faster. Then, I rotate the bag a couple of times open it back up, so air can get to it to harden it up, and it's great. I eat a lot of ice. I'm anemic so I *crave* ice. I LOVED Sonic ice, went through a bag in 1½-2 days. I like mine better. Especially when I'm not making ice to have in the freezer for bringing with me when I go somewhere, and the basket is full, and it stops making it because it needs emptied... And it's kinda melted, and *chewy* yeah, that sounds weird to say, but it's that texture that I like. :) Bottom line is... I love this ice maker. It's small, and compact compared to others, but don't let that stop, or fool you. It's fast if you use *COLD* water, and just try what I've suggested. Hopefully, you'll see the difference in it, VS not. Everybody's different, water is and tastes different. I don't think you'll be dissatisfied with this one. Definitely worth every penny spent to me. I've used it every day since I got it, and not 1 issue so far.

text: I bought this ice machine because we had to buy ice constantly when we had company over since our refrigerator ice maker only holds a a small amount of ice. I haven’t had any issues so far. I will run it all day and make a big gallon bag of ice to keep in the freezer. It can make ice in two sizes, I prefer the larger size. When it for the gets started the ice cubes are smaller, I think that they melt a little until the machine really starts to get going and it gets cold in the bin. It makes ice in about 7-10 minutes. I let it run a few batches then put in a bag and in the freezer, I don’t let the ice cubes sit in the bin too long. The ice cubes can be a little watery, I just make sure I let the excess water drip off before adding them to the bag. I store the gallon bags in the freezer until we need them and they still taste fine a few weeks later. One thing I didn’t know was that it shouldn’t be moved because of the refrigerant, or if it is, it should sit for at least 30 minutes before being used. Also, it needs to run in a very open area, due to the fan. I just move it by my kitchen sink and make sure there is nothing around it. It also makes it easy for clean up, since the water needs to be drained from the bottom. I could not get all of the sticker off from when it came out of the box, but I store it away, so no big deal.

text: I absolutely love this ice machine as our last one from Igloo broke. We went through 2 in the last 2 years. Hopefully this will last longer. It has a cleaning option which I'll be eternally grateful for. Our fridge doesn't have a built in ice maker and it's quite small so space for ice trays is not even in the question. My only thing about this ice maker is that it is a little louder than my last one. It whirs and revs somewhat loudly before making the next batch of ice. It's the only thing that gets me. The only good side to that is I know when a new batch of ice is almost done. Overall so far I love it. Instructions are also easy to understand but to be honest it's not hard to figure out even without the instructions.

title: works well, however it was obviously a previously returned unit that had damage
text: Ice maker arrived in 3 days after order. Packing was good, well protected. Upon opening, it was apparent that this was a returned product that had been reshipped. All accessory packages had been opened, and some missing. The plastic door track tabs had been broken, and the door stuck in the bin. It is such a cost and hassle to exchange or return, and virtually impossible to get replacement parts, so I opted to make new tabs. Time consuming, but successful. It works well, produces lots of ice. This is for use on a boat, and a plus is that it works with a list of +/- 10 degrees. Compromise review: 5 on function, 1 for resending a returned unit without ensuring everything was good.

title: Great Maker
text: This Ice Maker was a straightforward install. The only thing that was on my refrigerator was the electrical connection. This looks more difficult than it is, and one of the few projects where the instructions are better than a YouTube video. I do recommend watching a few videos first, and then using the instructions for the details. For the install a mirror and a work light makes this much easier. The electrical connection is directional and it's hard to know if you have it in correctly without the mirror. I wasn't sure there was a cap in there until I used the mirror and light. The instructions said to wait between 24 and 48 hours for ice. I had ice when I checked after 6 hours. After 24 hours, the ice bucket was 2/3rds full. I have my freezer on the coldest setting. This takes up as much space as an ice bucket and 4 trays. That's about how much I would need to keep up with the needs of my family. It's worth the cost, space, and convenience.

title: Probably the next best thing to an ice dispenser in the fridge
text: I bought the plumbing kit for mine since I didn’t like having to refill it all the time. With that being said, I still clean the reservoir out every once in awhile. Mine’s next to the sink so I put the front portion of the maker over the sink and pull the drain plug. If you have the water line to it, just make sure the ice maker is off (better yet, unplug it) so it won’t fill when draining. It is a bit noisy when it’s making ice, but it’s fun to watch! Once it’s done making ice, the maker is virtually silent. The water that is dispensed is chilled, but not cold. But that’s the way I like it. We never turn ours off. If any ice melts, it drains into the reservoir and “recycles” the water. We even take some of the ice out and put it in the ice cube bin in the freezer. Aside from the noise, (it’s tolerable but does add noise to the kitchen) I really like this ice maker! I wouldn’t hesitate to buy it again.

title: Functional, but not perfect.
text: Unit works as described, but take note of several items. The Bad: 1) The external casing is plastic, whereas the summary description might lead one to think it is metal. 2) The unit is poorly insulated, if at all so ice melts rather quickly. 3) The noise from the unit is rather disturbing; louder than a modern refrigerator. 4) The ice is frozen within a water reservoir, which causes the ice to be somewhat soft and wet. 5) The ice reservoir is not very large. It will fill about 2.5 glasses with ice. It would not work for a party. 6) The instruction manual is written by someone who does not speak English, so it is a bit hard to decipher in places. 7) As water is recycled indefinitely, fairly frequent cleaning would be recommended to prevent pathogen cultures from growing. The Good: 1) It produces ice fairly quickly. 2) It is very convenient. 3) The controls are intuitive. 4) One can feed an external water source to the unit. 5) It works for those occasions where is no other convenient source of ice.
